title: Sub-construct output must resolve by declared port, not reverse type-scan
description:
GH #17. A sub-construct's output is found by scanning branch state in REVERSE for the first value matching output=. That is a heuristic over a dict whose contents depend on unrelated declarations, and it silently returns the WRONG value when two share a type.

Reported: a branch declared context=['read'], which puts a Case into branch state, and output=Case because Case is genuinely the right domain type. The scan matched the INJECTED CONTEXT Case, not the one the branch produced. It did not fail -- every branch came back carrying the OPENING case, five readings and zero claims, and the run completed green. Found only by dumping compiled state and comparing against what the branch demonstrably computed.

The cost was a type invented purely to be type-distinct, whose docstring says 'the boundary type must be one that appears exactly once in a branch's state; distinctness is the whole of its job' -- against the codebase's standing rule about types that only move shapes.

Wanted: output='settle' -- the NAME of the node whose output is the boundary. Ambiguous or missing refuses at lint()/compile() like every other wiring mistake.

Note the action at a distance: adding a context= input can retroactively break an unrelated output=, with no error.
design:
## Root Cause (unchanged, CONFIRMED by the review)

`_scan_subgraph_output` (_subconstruct.py:47) walks `reversed(list(sub_result.values()))`
and returns the first isinstance match. `sub_result` is the childs FINAL STATE, which
holds fields the childs own items never wrote -- forwarded `context=`,
`neo_subgraph_input`, framework keys. `compile_state_model` appends context fields AFTER
node output fields (state.py:278-289), so reverse iteration reaches a HANDED value before
a COMPUTED one.

Sharpened by the review, and this wording decides the fix: the disease is not "reverse
iteration" and not merely "name-free resolution" -- it is that **state-dict order is
eligible at all**. Values the construct never produced are competing to BE its output.

## Fix Approach -- MAINTAINER-DECIDED 2026-08-24 (supersedes the earlier sketch)

Measured basis (review atom instrumented the real scan over the full suite):
    output-boundary scans : 270
    ambiguous (>1 match)  :  26  (9.6%)
    item-order rule agrees:  24
    item-order rule differs:  2  <- and both ARE this bug

### DECISION A -- ORDERED, not ambiguous. Eligibility is the fix.

Restrict eligibility to fields the constructs OWN DECLARED ITEMS write (via
`iter_with_arms`), then take the LAST in declaration order.

  • A forwarded context field is not an item, so it can NEVER win. The reported bug and
    the action-at-a-distance both die with NO public API change.
  • Measured delta: 2 of 270. The other 24 (review->revise, write->improve, the
    canonical refine chain) keep resolving exactly as they do today.
  • REJECTED: refuse-on-ambiguity as the acceptance criteria literally word it. It
    turns those 24 green scans into hard failures and pushes authors toward a type
    invented purely to be distinct -- the exact cost this ticket exists to abolish.
  • It CONVERGES with `_agent_spec_boundary.resolve_end_node_sources`, which already
    picks `construct.nodes[-1]`, instead of adding a fifth rule (review F11: that
    positional resolver is a FIFTH site my syntactic scan missed).

### DECISION B -- a SEPARATE field, `output_from: str | None`. Not an overloaded `output`.

  • `Portal.output` (_portal.py:83) and `ConstructSpec.output` (_spec_schema.py:152)
    already accept a str meaning a TYPE NAME via `lookup_type`. Overloading `output`
    to mean a NODE NAME gives one spelling two contradictory meanings on sibling
    boundary fields -- the same "one heuristic, two rules" condition this tickets own
    scan blames for the bug.
  • `output_from` is RESOLVED EAGERLY TO A TYPE AT ASSEMBLY, so `_declared_output`
    keeps returning a type and none of its ~10 type-consuming call sites change
    (state.py builds `sub.output | None`, `dict[str, sub.output]`, `list[sub.output]`;
    _schema_fingerprint hashes it; compiler.py/testing/scaffold.py take `.__name__`).
    `_declared_output(item)` takes ONE argument and cannot see the enclosing construct,
    so it structurally COULD NOT resolve a name -- eager resolution is what avoids
    touching that guarded monopoly at all.
  • The type form SURVIVES (review F9): `output_reachable_on_every_arm`
    (_validation_arms.py:119-133) deliberately supports a boundary satisfied by a
    DIFFERENT node per arm. One name cannot express that.

### Ordering of the two mechanisms

  1. `output_from=` present -> resolve that item EXACTLY. Missing or ambiguous name ->
     `ConstructError` AT ASSEMBLY.
  2. otherwise -> item-eligible, last-declared-item wins (Decision A).
  3. Portal mode-(b) dispatch (_agent_spec_dispatch.py:150) keeps the TYPE scan: it
     invokes a flow emitted at RUNTIME whose node names are unknowable at assembly.
     Eligibility narrowing does not apply there; it gets the ambiguity refusal instead.

### Carried from the review, all binding on the fix atom

  F6  Agent Spec export must ENCODE the port (a neograph-flavored marker, as
      `neograph/oracle_spec` already does) and import must RESTORE it. Without this,
      export->import drops the port and the imported construct silently reverts to the
      heuristic, green. `_construct_from_subflow` restores from Properties (types only).
  F7  lint `_framework_field_reads` (_lint_consumers.py:138) gates on
      `isinstance(construct.output, type)`; teach it the port so a declared boundary
      does not draw a false `output_field_unconsumed` WARN. CLAUDE.md: teach that ONE
      function. OPPORTUNITY: with a port it can name ONE terminal producer instead of
      every type-compatible one.
  F8  `ConstructSpec` needs an `output_from` key or the gap is stated -- 5suot needs the
      explicit boundary on exactly the spec-loaded/imported paths.
  F12 The SHARED authority the three deferred sites read is the ELIGIBILITY +
      PRECEDENCE rule, not "by-name resolution": `_scan_subgraph_input` reads the
      PARENT state for a value to FEED the child, so there is no producing child node
      to name. It can adopt the eligibility half verbatim; only the output half gets a
      port override.

### Test work the review found missing (all binding)

  T1  test 1 asserts only the boundary VALUE, so a fix that stops forwarding context
      into the child turns it GREEN while BREAKING context=. Add an assertion that the
      child node actually SAW the forwarded context. This is the tempting minimal fix,
      so the risk is live.
  T2  test 2 is not a standalone oracle (with == without passes if both are wrong the
      same way); say so in its docstring.
  T3  test 4 wraps Construct(...) AND compile(...) in one pytest.raises -- pin WHICH
      gate refuses.
  T4  no test for the AMBIGUOUS-name half (a name matching a context field; a name
      shadowed between a top-level item and an arm node).
  T5  test 5 pins the REJECTED criterion -- rewrite it for Decision A: two item-produced
      values of the same type must resolve to the LAST DECLARED, not refuse.
  T6  three-surface parity is entirely unpinned (all 5 tests are declarative). Add the
      @node route (`construct_from_functions`, _construct_builder.py:94-101) and the
      programmatic route; ARGUE the ForwardConstruct exemption (forward.py synthesizes
      `Construct(output=<inferred type>)` and cannot express a port) rather than
      assuming it.
  T7  add a tests/check_fixtures/should_fail/ + should_pass/ PAIR -- CLAUDE.md requires
      it for every new validation rule. Plus round-trip (F6), lint (F7), and an
      Each/Loop-modified sub-construct with a port (F10).
acceptance_criteria: output= accepts a node NAME and resolves exactly. A name that does not exist, or is ambiguous, fails at assembly. The type-scan path either goes away or refuses when more than one value in branch state matches -- silently picking one is what this bug is. A regression test reproduces the context=-shadows-output shape and asserts the branch's OWN value crosses the boundary.
notes:
## Why this is P0 alongside the portability work
It is the only item in the 0.8 set that returns a WRONG ANSWER with a green run. The reporter's every branch came back carrying the opening case -- five readings, zero claims -- and nothing failed. Same class as the invented tool argument fixed in 0.7.9 (GH #15), and by the standard applied there it outranks portability work, which fails loudly.

## Interaction to settle BEFORE implementing
neograph-iq4a3 (GH #16, accumulator channel) and neograph-5suot (native LangGraph subgraphs, P0) both change how a value crosses a sub-construct boundary. Decide the order deliberately:
  - by-name output resolution (this ticket) makes the boundary EXPLICIT, which native subgraphs need anyway -- a Pregel handoff cannot type-scan.
  - so this one probably lands FIRST and makes 5suot easier, rather than the reverse.
Confirm that reading against 5suot's notes before starting; do not assume it.
## Reproduction (atom neograph-ogk5i.2, 2026-08-24)

- Failing tests: tests/test_subconstruct_output_boundary.py (5 tests, ALL FAIL)
    TestContextMustNotShadowTheOutputBoundary
      ::test_the_branchs_own_value_crosses_the_boundary_when_context_is_declared
      ::test_declaring_context_does_not_change_what_crosses_the_boundary
    TestOutputResolvesByDeclaredPortName
      ::test_output_accepts_a_node_name_and_resolves_exactly
      ::test_a_name_that_does_not_exist_fails_at_assembly
    TestAmbiguousTypeScanRefusesInsteadOfGuessing
      ::test_two_values_of_the_boundary_type_do_not_silently_resolve

- Root cause: `_scan_subgraph_output` (_subconstruct.py:47) resolves the boundary by
  reverse-iterating the childs final state dict and returning the first isinstance
  match, while `compile_state_model` (state.py:278-289) APPENDS `context=` fields
  AFTER the node output fields -- so an injected context value of the boundary type is
  reached FIRST and silently wins over the value the child actually produced.

### Measured, not narrated -- the identical construct, one declaration apart

  context=None      -> boundary = Case(label=SETTLED, readings=5)   <- correct
  context=[read]    -> boundary = Case(label=OPENING, readings=0)   <- WRONG, run green

Nothing raised. Same nodes, same bodies, same types; the ONLY difference is a
context= declaration, which is an INPUT concern with no business re-pointing an
OUTPUT boundary. This is the reporters "five readings and zero claims" verbatim.

### One test was initially VACUOUS and was tightened before this atom closed

`test_a_name_that_does_not_exist_fails_at_assembly` first passed with
`pytest.raises(Exception, match="nosuchnode")` -- because `output=str` raises a
PYDANTIC ValidationError ("Input should be a subclass of BaseModel") whose text merely
CONTAINS the name. It would have kept passing if the feature were never built. Now
asserts neographs own ConstructError. Recording it because the same loose-matcher trap
is waiting for anyone who writes the by-name tests from the acceptance criteria.

### Ordering CONFIRMED against neograph-5suot notes (the ticket said not to assume it)

5suots only remaining unknown, #5, is `_scan_subgraph_input` -- the reverse type-scan on
the INPUT port. This ticket is `_scan_subgraph_output`, the SAME disease on the OUTPUT
boundary; the two functions sit adjacent in _subconstruct.py (lines 31 and 47) and share
the "reverse iteration so later pipeline nodes take precedence" rationale verbatim.

5suot measured the INPUT side across the suite: 186 port scans, 5 ambiguous (2.7%), in
exactly two shapes (loop re-entry, nested sub-construct). Its acceptance already
requires "the static input binding is documented, including what replaces the
reverse-scan precedence rule". So 35mur lands FIRST and 5suot inherits the answer --
confirmed, not assumed. Whatever rule this ticket picks for the output boundary should
be one the input side can adopt, or the two halves of one disease get two designs.
## Trace Similar (atom neograph-ogk5i.3, 2026-08-24)

Bug pattern category: **resolve a value by isinstance-matching over a BAG OF STATE,
first match wins, ordering decided by unrelated declarations.** Not "reverse
iteration" -- that is one symptom; the disease is name-free resolution.

Swept `grep -rn "reversed(" src/neograph/` plus the isinstance-resolution sites.
FOUR instances, all confirmed by reading, two confirmed by RUNNING:

| # | Site | Direction | Status |
|---|------|-----------|--------|
| 1 | _subconstruct.py:54 `_scan_subgraph_output` | reversed, LATER wins | THIS TICKET -- reproduced |
| 2 | _subconstruct.py:38 `_scan_subgraph_input` | reversed, LATER wins | already tracked: neograph-5suot unknown #5 |
| 3 | _input_shape.py:135 `_extract_single_type` | forward, EARLIER wins | NEW -- filed neograph-t1nbp, REPRODUCED |
| 4 | _agent_spec.py:387 export mirror | reversed, LATER wins | NEW -- filed neograph-t1nbp, REPRODUCED |

`forward.py:200 reversed(cls.__mro__)` is a normal MRO walk -- NOT an instance.

### The finding that outranks the rest: runtime and export DISAGREE

Same construct (a -> Case FIRST; b -> Case SECOND consuming a; sink inputs=Case):

    runtime: sink consumed FIRST     (_extract_single_type, forward)
    export : wires sink <- b         (_agent_spec.py:387, reversed)

The exported Agent Spec artifact wires a DIFFERENT EDGE than neograph executes. That
is a portability defect stacked on a correctness one, and neither surface complains.
Filed as neograph-t1nbp at P1.

### Three implementations, two contradictory precedence rules, no authority

  _scan_subgraph_input   reversed -> LATER wins
  _scan_subgraph_output  reversed -> LATER wins     <- this ticket
  _extract_single_type   forward  -> EARLIER wins
  _agent_spec.py:387     reversed -> LATER wins

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS TICKETS DESIGN, and the reason this atom exists: whatever rule
35mur picks must become the SHARED authority the other three read, not a fourth local
answer. Fixing the output boundary alone leaves a codebase where one heuristic has two
rules and four implementations -- which is how this bug was born.
## Codebase Disease Scan (atom neograph-ogk5i.4, 2026-08-24)

Pattern: **choosing WHICH of several state values is meant by ISINSTANCE-matching over
a bag, first match wins** -- resolution without a name, where the winner is decided by
declaration order of unrelated things.

Shape: SEMANTIC (four syntactically different loops: two reversed dict walks, one
forward state walk, one reversed IR-item walk) but small and fully enumerable, so a
single-executor scan was sufficient; no fan-out.

Scan commands (reproducible verbatim):
  grep -rn "reversed(" src/neograph/
  grep -rn "_isinstance_safe(\|isinstance(check_val\|isinstance(val" src/neograph/
  grep -rln "single_type" src/neograph/

Total instances found: 6 (4 real, 2 non-instances)

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | _subconstruct.py:54 `_scan_subgraph_output` | reversed(sub_result.values()), first isinstance | MIGRATE | THIS TICKET. Reproduced: context= shadows the produced value. |
| 2 | _subconstruct.py:38 `_scan_subgraph_input` | reversed(state.keys()), first isinstance | DEFER -> neograph-5suot | Already tracked as that tickets unknown #5, which must document what replaces the reverse-scan precedence. Same function pair, adjacent lines. |
| 3 | _input_shape.py:135 `_extract_single_type` | forward state.keys(), first isinstance | DEFER -> neograph-t1nbp | REPRODUCED: sink declared after b consumed a. Filed P1 today. |
| 4 | _agent_spec.py:387 | reversed(ordered_items[:idx]) | DEFER -> neograph-t1nbp | REPRODUCED: export wires sink<-b while runtime consumes a. Same bead as #3 -- same root, and fixing one without the other keeps them divergent. |
| 5 | _lint_consumers.py:267 | adds declared_type to consumed_types | ALLOWLIST | NOT an instance -- a CONSEQUENCE. lint must over-approximate ("resolved by TYPE at runtime, not by the producers name") precisely because #3 is name-free. It resolves nothing; it widens. Expect it to SIMPLIFY when #3 lands. |
| 6 | forward.py:200 | reversed(cls.__mro__) | ALLOWLIST | Ordinary MRO walk for class-attribute collection. Reverse iteration over a class hierarchy, not a value bag. |

Every DEFER row points at a filed bead: neograph-5suot (pre-existing), neograph-t1nbp
(filed by this ticket, P1, covering rows 3 AND 4 together).

### Scope decision this scan forces, stated for the review atom

Rows 2-4 are NOT in this tickets budget, but row 1s fix must be the SHARED AUTHORITY
they later read -- not a fourth local answer. Concretely: the by-name resolution and
its ambiguity refusal should land as a reusable helper, not as an inline change to
`_scan_subgraph_output`. Otherwise this ticket leaves one heuristic with two
precedence rules and four implementations, which is the condition that produced the
bug in the first place (AGENTS.md Portal retrospective, same anti-pattern).
## Blast-radius facts established by the orchestrator (atom neograph-ogk5i.5, independent of the review)

Verified by reading source, so the review can be checked against them rather than trusted:

### `_scan_subgraph_output` has TWO callers, and they are NOT symmetric

  _subconstruct.py:199        sub-construct boundary            <- THIS BUG
  _agent_spec_dispatch.py:150 Portal mode-(b) dispatch          <- different problem

Portal dispatch invokes a flow EMITTED AT RUNTIME from a spec. Its node names are not
knowable at assembly, so **by-name resolution is structurally unavailable there**. The
fix therefore cannot simply delete the type-scan path.

The coherent split, and it matches the tickets own acceptance wording ("either goes
away OR refuses when more than one value matches"):
  • sub-construct  -> resolve BY NAME (names are known at assembly)
  • Portal dispatch -> keep the type scan, but REFUSE on ambiguity instead of guessing

Reading the acceptance as "delete the scan" would break Portal mode (b).

### Concrete breakage sites if `Construct.output` widens to accept `str`

  compiler.py:407    output_name = sub.output.__name__ ...     AttributeError on a str
  factory.py:396     output_name = sub.output.__name__ ...     AttributeError on a str
  compiler.py:436    subgraph_metadata(sub.name, sub.output)
  compiler.py:469    passes sub.output positionally
  _agent_spec_boundary.py:236  _properties_for(construct.output)
  _agent_spec_group_import.py:97,166  output_types[...] = sub.output   (import side)
  _member_select.py:56  obj.output is not None  -- SAFE (a str is still not-None)
  _normalize.py:167    _declared_output -- the MONOPOLY; returns .output unchanged,
                       so every downstream consumer inherits the widened type

### Precedent worth reusing rather than inventing

`Portal.output` ALREADY accepts a `str` and resolves it via `lookup_type`
(factory.py:541). That is a TYPE-name lookup, not a node-name lookup, so it is not the
same semantics -- but it establishes that a str-valued output field is representable in
this IR and shows where such resolution is expected to happen. Do NOT overload one str
field to mean "type name here, node name there"; that ambiguity is a smaller cousin of
the bug being fixed.

## Architect Review (atom neograph-ogk5i.5, 2026-08-24)

Every claim below verified against source or by RUNNING, not from the write-up.
Verdict: NEEDS_USER_INPUT (two maintainer calls, stated at the end).

### Measured first, because it decides two of the findings

Instrumented `_scan_subgraph_output` and ran the FULL suite (5063 passed, the 5
TDD-red ones failed). Then re-ran with a second probe comparing today's answer
against a candidate "last DECLARED ITEM wins, non-item state fields ineligible"
rule (`iter_with_arms(sub)` -> field names, last match in declaration order):

    output-boundary scans      : 270
    ambiguous (>1 match)       : 26   (9.6%  -- vs 5suot's 2.7% on the input side)
    item-order rule AGREES     : 24
    item-order rule DISAGREES  : 2    <- and both ARE this bug

The 24 agreeing shapes are not exotic. They are the canonical ones:

    sub=loop-review-revise out=Draft  matched=[review, revise]        x3
    sub=refine             out=Draft  matched=[write, improve]
    sub=refine             out=Claims matched=[first, second]
    sub=researcher         out=Claims matched=[claims, researcher]    x2
    sub=inner-loop         out=Beta   matched=[inner_seed, inner_refine]
    sub=inner-sub          out=Beta/Gamma matched=[n0,n1,n2]          x17 (hypothesis)

The 2 disagreeing:

    sub=branch out=Case matched=[settle, read]  non_item=[read]  x2

### F1 Root cause -- CONFIRMED. LOW.

Reproduced. `_scan_subgraph_output` (_subconstruct.py:47-58) walks
`reversed(list(sub_result.values()))`; `compile_state_model` appends context
fields after node output fields; the child's `output_schema` is non-`neo_` so the
forwarded context field IS in `sub_result`. Root cause as written is right.

But the write-up names the disease one notch too narrowly. It is not "reverse
iteration" and not only "name-free resolution": the scan iterates STATE-DICT
order, which contains fields the construct's own items never wrote -- forwarded
context, `neo_subgraph_input`, framework keys. The value that won in the field
report is one the child was HANDED. Read that way, the 2/270 measurement above
is the whole bug and the other 24 are not defects at all.

### F2 The ambiguity-refusal acceptance criterion is not implementable as written. HIGH.

"the type-scan path either goes away or refuses when more than one value in
branch state matches" turns 24 currently-green resolutions into hard failures,
including `review -> revise` and `write -> improve`. A refine chain of two
same-typed nodes is the most ordinary sub-construct there is. Refusing on it
would be a large breaking change wearing a bug fix's clothes, and it would push
users toward exactly the type-invented-to-be-distinct that this ticket exists to
abolish.

### F3 A smaller rule fixes the bug with a 2/270 delta -- and it IS the shared authority. HIGH (opportunity).

Restrict eligibility to fields the construct's OWN declared items write
(`iter_with_arms`), then take the LAST in declaration order. Measured: 24/26
agreement, 2/26 disagreement, and the 2 are the bug. Properties:

- Kills the reported bug outright: a forwarded context field is not an item, so
  it can never win. The action at a distance disappears with no new API.
- `_scan_subgraph_input` (5suot #5) can adopt the eligibility half verbatim.
- It CONVERGES with `_agent_spec_boundary.resolve_end_node_sources`, which
  already picks `construct.nodes[-1]`, instead of adding a fifth rule.

`output=<port>` then becomes the EXPLICIT OVERRIDE for the cases position gets
wrong, not the only fix -- which is a much smaller public-IR change.

Note: under this rule the current test 5 (`settle` + `also_case`, both items)
resolves to `also_case` rather than refusing. That is the maintainer call in
Decision A below.

### F4 `output=<str>` collides with an established, OPPOSITE str convention. HIGH.

`Portal.output: type[BaseModel] | str | None` (_portal.py:83) where str means a
TYPE NAME, resolved by `lookup_type` (documented at factory.py:541).
`ConstructSpec.output: str` (_spec_schema.py:152) likewise -> `lookup_type`
(_spec_loader.py:237). Making `Construct.output=<str>` mean a NODE NAME gives one
spelling two contradictory meanings on sibling boundary fields -- the exact
"one heuristic, two rules" condition this ticket's own scan blames for the bug.

Recommend a distinct field (`output_from: str | None`) or a wrapper
(`output=Port("settle")`). This also resolves F5 and F10 for free.

### F5 Widening `Construct.output` to str breaks `_declared_output`'s contract and ~10 type consumers. HIGH.

`_declared_output(item) -> TypeSpecStatic`. Consumers use the value AS a type:

    state.py:136,143,146,156,168,173,182   `sub.output | None` -> TypeError on a str
    state.py:243                            Portal payload field
    _schema_fingerprint.py:84               fingerprint would hash the NAME
    _validation_types.py:111                effective_producer_type
    _validation_portal.py:201-209           identity compare across mesh members
    _construct_validation.py:381-382        boundary contract
    _validation_arms.py:121-127             arm convergence
    compiler.py:407,436                     `.__name__`
    _agent_spec_boundary.py:236             `_properties_for`
    testing/scaffold.py:84                  `.__name__`

`_declared_output(item)` takes ONE argument and has no access to the enclosing
construct, so it structurally cannot resolve a node name. Either its signature
changes (10 call sites, and the premise of `TestDeclaredOutputSelectorMonopoly`),
or the name is resolved to a type EAGERLY at assembly. The second is clearly
right, and it argues for a separate field over widening `output`.

### F6 Agent Spec round-trip silently reverts the declared boundary to the type-scan. HIGH.

`_construct_from_subflow` (_agent_spec_group_import.py:69-77) restores
`input`/`output` from `Flow.inputs`/`Flow.outputs` -- Properties, i.e. a TYPE. A
port NAME has no Property representation, so export -> import DROPS it and the
imported construct is back on the heuristic, green.

That module's own docstring records this precise trap already happening once:
"came back with BOTH set to None ... while still passing an is-a-Construct plus
combo-matches check, so nothing noticed." Export must encode the port (a
neograph-flavored marker, the way `neograph/oracle_spec` already does) and import
must restore it. Neither is in the acceptance criteria.

### F7 lint's `_framework_field_reads` skips silently on a str boundary. MEDIUM.

`_lint_consumers.py:138` gates the whole terminal-producer block on
`isinstance(construct.output, type)`. A str boundary falls through it, so no node
is registered as a boundary reader and the author's declared port gets a
false-positive `output_field_unconsumed` WARN. CLAUDE.md's "teach that ONE
function" rule applies; the design names the file but not the narrowing.

Also an OPPORTUNITY: with a declared port this block can name ONE terminal
producer instead of every type-compatible one -- which its own docstring says
`members[-1]` gets wrong.

### F8 The YAML/spec surface cannot express the new boundary. MEDIUM.

`ConstructSpec.output: str` is REQUIRED and means a type name. Spec-loaded and
Agent-Spec-imported pipelines therefore keep the heuristic -- and 5suot (native
subgraphs, P0) needs the explicit boundary on exactly those paths. A new
`output_from:` key is needed, or the gap must be stated.

### F9 By-name is not a total replacement: the multi-exit branch has no single port. MEDIUM.

`ArmScopedProducers.output_reachable_on_every_arm` (_validation_arms.py:119-133,
ftnxl.2) DELIBERATELY supports a boundary satisfied by a DIFFERENT node per arm.
One name cannot express that, and at runtime the un-taken arm's field is None, so
a by-name read would hit `_build_update`'s fail-loud. Consequences:

- the type form must SURVIVE. "either goes away or refuses" resolves to "stays".
- any ambiguity refusal must be RUNTIME, over POPULATED values -- an
  assembly-time refusal over declared producer types rejects every branch
  construct. The tests encode runtime; the AC wording ("fails at assembly") does
  not. Say which, explicitly.

### F10 The PARENT's state field type is derived from `sub.output`. MEDIUM.

`state.py:120-182` builds `dict[str, sub.output]` (Each), `list[sub.output]`
(Loop/Oracle), `sub.output | None` (bare). A name-only boundary must already be a
type before `compile_state_model` runs. Third independent argument for eager
resolution at assembly.

### F11 The disease scan's method has a blind spot; a fifth resolver was missed. MEDIUM.

The scan declares the disease SEMANTIC but all three of its commands are
SYNTACTIC (`reversed(`, `isinstance(check_val|val`, `single_type`). A POSITIONAL
resolver matches none of them:

    _agent_spec_boundary.resolve_end_node_sources -> `construct.nodes[-1]`

Same question ("which node's output IS the boundary"), a different answer, not in
the table. `_lint_consumers._framework_field_reads` is a sixth answer (ALL
type-compatible producers) -- correctly allowlisted as "does not pick one", but it
belongs in the design as a CONSUMER of the new authority, not merely as exempt.
Treat "fully enumerable, single-executor sufficient, no fan-out" as unproven.

### F12 The shared-helper scope call is RIGHT, but under-specified in a way that changes what the helper is. MEDIUM.

Right, and not over-engineering: a local edit to `_scan_subgraph_output` leaves
one heuristic with two rules and four-to-six implementations, which is the
condition that produced the bug.

Under-specified: the scan names the helper as "by-name resolution + ambiguity
refusal", and the INPUT side cannot adopt that. `_scan_subgraph_input` reads the
PARENT's state for a value to FEED the child; there is no producing child node to
name. What both halves CAN share is the eligibility + precedence RULE from F3
("only fields the construct's own declared items write; last declared item
wins"), plus a declared-port override on the output half. Specify it as that.

### Test-coverage findings (tests/test_subconstruct_output_boundary.py)

All 5 confirmed RED on develop. Mapping to acceptance criteria:

    AC "name resolves exactly"            -> test 3           OK
    AC "name that does not exist refuses" -> test 4           OK
    AC "AMBIGUOUS name refuses"           -> NO TEST          GAP
    AC "type-scan refuses on >1 match"    -> test 5           see T5
    AC "regression test for context shape"-> tests 1, 2       see T1/T2

T1 MEDIUM -- test 1 can pass for the WRONG reason. It asserts only the boundary
VALUE. A fix that stops forwarding context into the child, or drops context
fields from the child's `output_schema`, turns it green while BREAKING `context=`.
Given the tempting minimal fix is "make context fields ineligible", this is a live
risk, not hypothetical. Add an assertion that the child node actually SAW the
forwarded context.

T2 MEDIUM -- test 2 is vacuous-capable ALONE: `with == without` passes if both are
wrong the same way (both returning the `read` Case). Only test 1 makes the pair
sound. Fine as a pair; the docstring should say it is not a standalone oracle.

T3 LOW -- test 4 wraps BOTH `Construct(...)` and `compile(...)` in one
`pytest.raises`, so it does not pin WHICH gate refuses. Construct-time vs
compile-time is a real difference to a user, and the AC says "at assembly".

T4 MEDIUM -- no test for the AMBIGUOUS-name half of the AC (a name matching no
item but matching a context field; a name shadowed between a top-level item and
an arm node).

T5 HIGH -- test 5 pins the criterion F2 measures as breaking 24 green scans, and
it asserts a RUNTIME raise while its AC says "at assembly". It is a correct test
of a criterion that needs re-deciding, not a bad test.

T6 HIGH -- three-surface parity is ENTIRELY unpinned. All 5 tests use the
declarative `Construct(...)` surface. Missing: the @node route
(`construct_from_functions`, _construct_builder.py:94-101, whose signature is
`output: type[BaseModel] | None` and would have to widen), the programmatic route,
and a STATED exemption for `ForwardConstruct` (forward.py:406/563/777 synthesize
`Construct(output=<inferred type>)` and cannot express a port name -- a defensible
exemption, but CLAUDE.md requires it be argued, not assumed).

T7 MEDIUM -- no test for Agent Spec round-trip (F6), lint (F7), the YAML loader
(F8), the checkpoint fingerprint (F5), or an Each/Loop-modified sub-construct with
a port (F10). And no `tests/check_fixtures/should_fail/` + `should_pass/` pair,
which CLAUDE.md requires for EVERY new validation rule.

### VERDICT: NEEDS_USER_INPUT

Not because the ticket is wrong -- the root cause is right and the bug is real and
P0. Because two of its acceptance criteria are maintainer decisions that change
what gets built and which tests stand, and neither can be settled by refinement:

DECISION A -- is `a -> Case; b -> Case; output=Case` AMBIGUOUS or ORDERED?
  Measured: 24 of 26 ambiguous resolutions in the suite are that shape, and the
  reverse scan gets all 24 right today. Refusing breaks them; the F3 item-order
  rule keeps them and still kills the bug (2/270 delta). Choosing "refuse" is
  defensible at 0.x but it is a breaking change to the canonical refine
  sub-construct, and it must be chosen knowingly. Test 5 and the AC ride on this.

DECISION B -- overload `output=<str>` as a NODE NAME, or add `output_from=`?
  `Portal.output` and `ConstructSpec.output` already use str to mean a TYPE NAME.
  Overloading gives one spelling two meanings (F4), forces `_declared_output` to
  resolve a name it cannot see the construct for (F5), makes the YAML surface
  inexpressible (F8), and silently dies on Agent Spec round-trip (F6). A separate
  eagerly-resolved field avoids all four. The already-written tests 3 and 4 pin
  the overloaded form, so this decision rewrites them.

Recommended shape, if the maintainer wants one: F3's item-eligibility +
last-declared-item rule as the SHARED authority (fixes the bug alone, 2/270
delta), plus `output_from=` as the explicit override resolved to a type at
assembly, plus export/import encoding (F6) and the lint narrowing (F7). Keep the
type form for the branch-arm shape (F9). Refuse only when the port is absent AND
the last-item rule is genuinely undecidable -- a refusal with no false positives.
## Fix (atom neograph-ogk5i.7, 2026-08-25) -- GREEN

### The reported symptom, before and after, in the shape a user writes it

  BEFORE   the LLM computed : Case(docket=D-1, readings=5, claims=3)
           boundary returned: Case(docket=D-1, readings=5, claims=0)   <- opening case
  AFTER    the LLM computed : Case(docket=D-1, readings=5, claims=3)
           boundary returned: Case(docket=D-1, readings=5, claims=3)   <- its own value

  And the action at a distance is gone:
           context=None      -> SETTLED
           context=[read]    -> SETTLED     (was OPENING)

                          _scan_subgraph_output gains eligible=; eligible=None keeps

  construct.py            output_from: str | None

  _agent_spec.py          stamps it on EVERY exported Flow
  _agent_spec_group_import.py  restores it (F6)

### Decisions worth re-reading before touching this again

1. **The bug is fixed by ELIGIBILITY, not by the new field.** `output_from` is an
   override for when position is wrong. Both context tests pass with NO API change --
   verified before the field existed. Measured delta stands at 2 of 270.
2. **`attach_boundary_marker` is called from the EXPORTER, not from

3. **The type form SURVIVES** (review F9): `output_reachable_on_every_arm` supports a

### Regressions the narrowing caused and how they were found -- both real

  • DICT-FORM OUTPUTS. `item_field_names` first returned only `field_name_for(name)`,
    but a dict-form node writes `{node}_{key}` and has NO bare `{node}` field, so every
    dict-form sub-construct boundary became unresolvable. Caught by
    TestGatherProduceSubConstruct, NOT by the boundary tests. Fixed via
    `_declared_output` + `output_field_name`.
  • FOUR STRUCTURAL GUARDS fired, every one a correct signal, none weakened:
      validation-cluster 400-line cap  -> moved the check to _validation_outputs.py,

                                          into the existing output-check block
      iter_with_arms ban in the orchestrator -> went with the move
