title: Field flattening stringifies BaseModel children — breaks {var.attr} dotted template access
description:
## What

In `renderers.py:_render_with_flattening` (line 258), when
`render_for_prompt()` returns a view model with BaseModel child fields,
each field is passed through `_render_single()` which calls
`describe_value()` — stringifying the child.

The template then uses Python `str.format(**template_vars)` which supports
dotted attribute access like `{rep_a.statement}`. If `rep_a` is a string
(stringified by describe_value), the format call crashes:

    AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'statement'

## Repro

Template `rw/resolve-duplicate.txt`:
```
## Candidate A
- Statement: {rep_a.statement}
- Context: {rep_a.context_quote}
```

Model setup:
```python
class ClaimRef(BaseModel):
    statement: str
    context_quote: str
    gen_id: str

class DuplicateCandidateView(BaseModel):
    rep_a: ClaimRef
    rep_b: ClaimRef
    similarity: float

class DuplicateCandidate(BaseModel):
    rep_a: ClaimRef
    rep_b: ClaimRef
    similarity: float

    def render_for_prompt(self) -> DuplicateCandidateView:
        return DuplicateCandidateView(
            rep_a=self.rep_a,
            rep_b=self.rep_b,
            similarity=self.similarity,
        )
```

Runtime: neograph flattens view fields into template_vars, calls
`describe_value(rep_a)` → "{ statement: \"...\", context_quote: \"...\" }"
(a string). Template `{rep_a.statement}` calls `.statement` on the string
→ AttributeError.

## Why this matters

`{var.attr}` dotted access is the natural way to reference nested fields
in Python str.format templates. Consumers write view models that expose
structured sub-objects for composition. Stringifying those sub-objects
breaks the template pattern.

piarch's consumer-side bridge already handles this correctly for CONTEXT
flattening (preserves BaseModel children as objects). Input flattening in
neograph's core renderer should match.

## Fix

In `_render_with_flattening`, when iterating view fields, preserve
BaseModel values as objects (don't call `_render_single`). Primitives
and lists render normally.

```python
for fname, finfo in result.__class__.model_fields.items():
    if finfo.exclude:
        continue
    fval = getattr(result, fname)
    if isinstance(fval, BaseModel):
        # Preserve for {var.attr} template access
        fields[fname] = fval
    else:
        fields[fname] = _render_single(fval, renderer)
return whole, fields
```

Same treatment applies for lists containing BaseModel — but templates
typically iterate via neograph's own rendering there; the common case
is single BaseModel children.

## Verification — integration & E2E only

**Integration**: `tests/renderers/test_field_flattening_preserves_models.py`
— create a view model whose field is a BaseModel with string fields. Run
through `_render_with_flattening`. Assert the flattened field value IS
the BaseModel instance, not a string.

**Integration**: test `str.format("{var.attr}")` against the flattened
output. Assert it renders the child's attribute value.

**E2E**: piarch RW pipeline running BR-RW-034 through resolve-duplicate
completes the LLM call without AttributeError. (This is the crash that
motivated the ticket — 184 duplicate pairs, many LLM calls, all failing.)

## Acceptance

- BaseModel children in view models preserved as objects in flattened
  template_vars
- `str.format("{var.attr}")` against a preserved BaseModel child resolves
  to the attribute value
- Primitives (str/int/float/bool) and non-BaseModel lists unchanged
- Full piarch RW rehearsal passes resolve-duplicate node without crash
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing tests: TestFieldFlatteningPreservesBaseModelChildren::test_basemodel_child_preserved_as_object, ::test_dotted_template_access_works
- Root cause: _render_with_flattening line 258 calls _render_single(fval, renderer) on BaseModel children, which stringifies them. Template {rep.statement} then crashes: AttributeError 'str' has no attribute 'statement'
- Fix: preserve BaseModel children as objects, only render primitives
close_reason: BaseModel children preserved as objects in flattened template vars. Dotted access {rep.statement} works.

title: render_for_prompt() field flattening: returned model fields become individual template vars
description:
## What

When render_for_prompt() returns a BaseModel, neograph currently
BAML-renders it into one string and stores it under the parameter key:

    {"load_uc_composite": "<one BAML blob>"}

Templates that reference individual fields ({existing_si}, {title}) can't
access them — the field names don't exist as separate template vars.

Desired behavior: when render_for_prompt() returns a BaseModel inside a
dict-form (fan-in) input, FLATTEN the returned model's fields into the
parent input dict alongside the whole-model rendering:

    {
        "load_uc_composite": "<full BAML of returned model>",
        "existing_si": "<BAML of existing_si field>",
        "title": "Produce Specification Stack",
        ...
    }

Each field is individually addressable as a template placeholder. The model
controls which fields are surfaced (only the fields on the RETURNED model
appear — not the original model's internal fields).

## Why

UCComposite has ~10 fields. write-si needs {existing_si} (the full raw
stakeholder interests markdown for incremental improvement). explore-internal
needs only {title} + {overview_snippet} (identity context). Without field
flattening, every consumer gets one opaque BAML blob and templates can't
reference individual fields. The alternatives are:
- Push the whole model everywhere (noisy, token-expensive, degrades quality)
- Add bridge-side field extraction (re-invents the flattening the BAML
  refactor just deleted)
- Add extractor @nodes per field (construct bloat)

Field flattening via render_for_prompt() is the clean answer: the model
decides what to expose, neograph makes each field a template var.

## Design

In render_input for dict-form inputs:

    for k, v in input_data.items():
        rendered = _render_single(v, renderer)
        if isinstance(rendered_before_collapse, BaseModel):
            # Flatten fields as BAML-rendered strings
            for fname, fval in rendered_model:
                result[fname] = _render_single(fval)
            result[k] = describe_value(rendered_model)  # whole model too
        else:
            result[k] = rendered

render_for_prompt() return semantics:
- Returns str → used verbatim (unchanged)
- Returns BaseModel → flatten fields + keep whole (NEW)
- Returns None / not defined → BAML render original (unchanged)

For single-input nodes (not dict-form), flattening doesn't apply — the
single input is one template var. Templates for single-input nodes use
{neo_subgraph_input} or similar.

## Verification — integration & E2E only

**Integration**: model with render_for_prompt() returning a BaseModel with
fields a, b. Fan-in node with that model as one input. Assert template_vars
contains {a}, {b}, AND {param_name} (the whole thing).

**Integration**: model WITHOUT render_for_prompt(). Assert no flattening
occurs — only {param_name} is set.

**Integration**: render_for_prompt() returns str. Assert no flattening —
str used verbatim under {param_name}.

**E2E**: piarch write-si node with UCComposite.render_for_prompt() returning
a model with existing_si field. Template uses {existing_si}. Assert
the prompt contains the actual SI markdown, not a KeyError.

## Acceptance

- render_for_prompt() returning BaseModel flattens fields into template vars
- Each field individually addressable as {field_name}
- Whole model also available as {param_name}
- Single-input nodes unaffected (no dict to flatten into)
- str return path unchanged
- No render_for_prompt() / default BAML path unchanged
notes:
## Research

Core invariant: render_for_prompt() returning a BaseModel in a dict-form (fan-in) input flattens its fields into the parent dict as individually addressable template vars, alongside the whole-model rendering under the original parameter key.

### Where to change
renderers.py:render_input, line 224-225. The dict comprehension currently does:
  {k: _render_single(v, renderer) for k, v in input_data.items()}

Change to: iterate dict items, for each value check render_for_prompt(). If it returns a BaseModel, flatten fields AND keep whole model under original key.

### What flattening produces
Input: {"load_uc_composite": UCComposite(existing_si="...", title="...")}
With render_for_prompt() returning Presentation(existing_si="...", title="..."):

Output: {
  "load_uc_composite": describe_value(Presentation(...)),  # whole model
  "existing_si": describe_value(field_val) or str(field_val),  # individual field
  "title": "Produce Specification Stack",  # individual field
}

### Field rendering rules
- BaseModel field values: describe_value()
- Primitive field values: str()
- Field(exclude=True): skip
- Collision with existing keys: original key wins (dont overwrite upstream data)

### Single-input nodes
No flattening — single input is one template var. Only dict-form (fan-in) gets flattening.

### What NOT to change
- _render_single stays unchanged
- str return from render_for_prompt() stays verbatim
- No render_for_prompt() / default BAML path unchanged
- Tool result rendering unchanged (separate path)
close_reason: render_for_prompt() returning BaseModel now flattens fields into individual template vars in fan-in dicts.

title: lint: inspect actual template text for {placeholder} names and validate against rendered input keys
description:
## What

neograph check validates DI bindings (FromInput/FromConfig parameter
resolution) but never reads the actual template .txt files to extract
{placeholder} names and verify they match the keys that will exist in
template_vars at runtime. Result: templates referencing field-level names
like {existing_si} (a field INSIDE UCComposite, not a parameter name) pass
check but crash at runtime with KeyError.

This is the THIRD placeholder/data mismatch caught by runtime crash rather
than by neograph check in a single day:
1. {load_uc_composite} vs neo_subgraph_input (sub-construct remapping)
2. {research_packet} vs explore_internal_tool_log (bridge alias)
3. {existing_si} — field inside a rendered BAML blob, not a top-level key

All three passed neograph check. All three crashed after minutes of LLM
spend.

## Why

The lint operates on the construct graph (nodes, edges, DI bindings) but
never touches the template files that prompt_compiler will call
get_prompt() with. Template text is opaque to the linter. The
--known-vars mechanism is a consumer-side allowlist, not a verification.

With BAML rendering (neograph-qybn), models arrive as opaque strings keyed
by parameter name. Field-level placeholders ({existing_si}, {title},
{uc_id}) that worked when the bridge hand-flattened models are now
unresolvable. The lint must know about this.

## Direction

Extend lint to:

1. For each LLM-calling node, resolve the template file (node.prompt →
   prompt registry path). Read the template text. Extract all {placeholder}
   names via regex.
2. Compute the set of keys that will be available at runtime:
   - Fan-in parameter names (from node inputs)
   - Sub-construct remapped keys (neo_subgraph_input)
   - Standard vars (node_id, project_root, json_schema)
   - Context keys
   - known-vars from CLI
3. Diff: placeholders - available_keys = unresolvable. Report each as
   a lint ERROR.

This requires the linter to have access to the template registry (or
the template files on disk). The prompt_compiler is consumer-provided,
but template files are referenced by node.prompt and the consumer's
registry is loaded at check time via --setup.

## Verification — integration & E2E only

**Integration**: construct with a node whose template references
{field_inside_model}. Lint returns ERROR for that placeholder.

**Integration**: construct with a node whose template references only
valid parameter names. Lint returns no errors.

**E2E**: run neograph check on piarch's uc_derivation.py. Currently
write-si.txt has {existing_si} which is NOT a parameter name.
Lint must flag it.

## Acceptance

- Lint reads template text for every LLM-calling node
- Extracts {placeholder} names from template
- Compares against computed available keys
- Reports unresolvable placeholders as ERROR
- Catches all three classes of mismatch found today
design:
## Architecture

### lint() API change
```python
def lint(
    construct: Construct,
    *,
    config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    known_template_vars: set[str] | None = None,
    template_resolver: Callable[[str], str | None] | None = None,
) -> list[LintIssue]:
```

### _check_template_placeholders changes
Currently handles inline prompts only. Extended:
- If prompt is inline: existing ${var} validation (unchanged)
- If prompt is template-ref AND template_resolver provided:
  1. text = template_resolver(node.prompt)
  2. If text is None: skip (resolver cant find template)
  3. Extract {placeholder} via string.Formatter().parse()
  4. Validate first segment of each against predicted_keys + known_vars
  5. Same issue kinds: template_placeholder_unresolvable (ERROR), template_placeholder_known_vars_only (WARN)

### __main__.py changes
In _load_config or new _load_template_resolver:
- If --setup module exports get_template_resolver(), use it
- Pass to lint(template_resolver=...)

### New issue kind
template_placeholder_unresolvable already exists. Reuse it for template-ref placeholders too.

Risk: LOW. Existing behavior unchanged when no resolver provided.
notes:
## Research

Core invariant: lint must validate template-ref prompt placeholders against runtime input keys when a template_resolver is provided.

### Design
1. lint() gains template_resolver: Callable[[str], str | None] parameter
2. For template-ref prompts (not inline), if resolver provided:
   a. Call resolver(node.prompt) to get template text
   b. Extract {placeholder} names via string.Formatter().parse()
   c. Validate each against predicted input keys + known extras + known_vars
3. __main__.py --setup module can export get_template_resolver() -> Callable
4. Template-ref uses Python str.format {placeholder} syntax, NOT ${var}

### Placeholder extraction
Use string.Formatter().parse(template) which yields (literal, field_name, format_spec, conversion) tuples. field_name is the placeholder name (may be dotted like "claim.text"). Take first segment.

### What counts as available keys for template-ref prompts
Same as inline prompts:
- Predicted input keys (from node.inputs dict)
- Framework extras (node_id, project_root, human_feedback)
- known_template_vars
- PLUS: config keys if config provided (prompt_compiler can access config)
- PLUS: node_name, output_model, etc. (prompt_compiler kwargs)

Actually, we should focus on input_data keys + known_vars. The prompt_compiler can access config separately — thats not part of template_vars. The consumer patterns show template.format(**data) where data = input_data dict.
close_reason: lint reads template text via template_resolver, extracts {placeholder} names, validates against input keys. Catches field-inside-model, sub-construct remapping, and bridge alias bugs.

title: Null coercion for string fields with defaults: null should become default value, not fail validation
description:
## Problem
StepCompleteness.justification is defined as:
```python
justification: str = Field(default='', description='Why this step has zero ECs')
```

R1 returns `"justification": null` in its JSON. Pydantic rejects null for str fields even when a default exists. NeoGraph's JSON repair/coercion should convert null → default value (empty string) before Pydantic validation.

## Evidence
5 consecutive production runs crash at brainstorm-extensions with:
`completeness_check.0.justification: Input should be a valid string`

The field has default=''. R1 returns null. Simple coercion: if field has a default and value is null, use the default.

## Affected fields
- StepCompleteness.justification (str, default='')
- Any str field with a default where R1 returns null

## Fix
In _parse_json_response, before Pydantic validation:
```python
# Coerce null to default for fields that have defaults
for field_name, field_info in output_model.model_fields.items():
    if field_info.default is not None and json_data.get(field_name) is None:
        json_data[field_name] = field_info.default
```
Or handle recursively for nested models.
close_reason: Fixed: _apply_null_defaults coerces null → default before Pydantic validation. Recursive for nested models. 3 new tests.

title: describe_type includes fields with exclude=True in BAML schema
description:
## Problem
describe_type() iterates model_fields and renders ALL fields, including those with exclude=True. These are pipeline-internal fields that the LLM should never produce.

Example: ExtensionCondition.assigned_letter has exclude=True (set by pipeline, not LLM). But describe_type includes it in the output schema. R1 sees it, tries to produce it, returns null, validation fails.

## Fix
In describe_type.py line ~193, check field_info.exclude:
```python
for field_name, field_info in model.model_fields.items():
    if field_info.exclude:
        continue  # skip pipeline-internal fields
```

Same for describe_value (line ~375).
notes:
## Research
5 sites iterate model_fields without checking exclude:
1. describe_type.py:125 _count_classes
2. describe_type.py:193 _render_model_body (PRIMARY)
3. describe_type.py:375 _render_instance
4. renderers.py:77 XmlRenderer._render_model
5. renderers.py:160 DelimitedRenderer._render_model (needs refactor to access field_info)
JsonRenderer NOT affected (uses model_dump_json which respects exclude).
Zero existing tests for exclude=True fields.
close_reason: Fixed: 5 sites now check field_info.exclude. 3 new tests. 1328 pass.

title: construct.py/node.py swallows TypeError/ValueError on llm_config merge
description: construct.py:108-113 and node.py:108-113 — try: item.llm_config = merged; except (TypeError, ValueError): pass. Silently ignores mutation failures on frozen models. Should use model_copy. If sub-construct node is frozen, llm_config merge silently does nothing — child runs without inherited config.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test 1: tests/test_composition.py::TestConstructLlmConfigImmutability::test_llm_config_propagation_does_not_mutate_original_node
- Failing test 2: tests/test_composition.py::TestConstructLlmConfigImmutability::test_renderer_propagation_does_not_mutate_original_node
- Root cause: construct.py:109 does item.llm_config = merged directly (and :119 does item.renderer = self.renderer). Both mutate shared Node instances. The try/except (TypeError, ValueError) never fires because Node isn't frozen — the mutation silently succeeds, corrupting the original.
## Trace Similar
Same pattern as gy9r. See trace analysis on gy9r for full codebase scan.
The construct.py bug has 2 mutation sites (llm_config and renderer), both fixed together.
## Architect Review
Fix is mechanical: replace direct assignment with model_copy + list replacement. Combine llm_config and renderer propagation into a single loop pass.
Core invariant: Node instances are immutable after construction.
Routing: ALL_LOW
close_reason: Fixed: model_copy in construct.py, single-pass propagation

title: loader.py mutates Node.inputs directly — violates immutable IR
description: loader.py:208-215 does node.inputs = input_type and node.inputs = inputs_dict. Comment says 'preserve immutability' but code directly assigns. Contradicts model_copy pattern in _construct_builder.py. If spec-driven pipeline reuses a Node across constructs, second sees mutated inputs. Fix: use model_copy.
design:
## Root Cause
_build_sub_construct(loader.py:204-216) does `node = all_nodes[field_ref]` then `node.inputs = input_type` — direct field mutation on the shared instance. Node is not frozen (model_config only has arbitrary_types_allowed), so the assignment succeeds and corrupts the shared object.

## Fix Approach
Replace lines 208 and 216 with model_copy:
- Line 208: `node = node.model_copy(update={'inputs': input_type})`
- Line 216: `node = node.model_copy(update={'inputs': inputs_dict})`
The local variable `node` is appended to `nodes` list on line 217, so the copy replaces the mutated original correctly.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_spec_loader.py::TestLoaderImmutability::test_sub_construct_does_not_mutate_shared_node
- Root cause: loader.py:208 and :216 directly assign node.inputs = ... on shared Node instances from all_nodes dict. If a Node is reused across constructs, second construct sees mutated inputs.
## Trace Similar
Pattern: direct field mutation on shared Node instances.

Found 6 sites total:
1. loader.py:208 — node.inputs = input_type [BUG, this ticket]
2. loader.py:216 — node.inputs = inputs_dict [BUG, this ticket]
3. construct.py:109 — item.llm_config = merged [BUG, neograph-bchn]
4. construct.py:119 — item.renderer = self.renderer [BUG, neograph-bchn]
5. decorators.py:503 — n.oracle_gen_type = gen_type [SAFE: fresh local Node]
6. decorators.py:586 — n.oracle_gen_type = gen_type [SAFE: fresh local Node]

Sites 1-4 mutate shared instances; sites 5-6 are safe (freshly constructed, pre-return). All 4 bugs are covered by gy9r and bchn tickets.
## Architect Review
Fix is mechanical: replace direct assignment with model_copy. No design decisions.
Core invariant: Node instances are immutable after construction.
Routing: ALL_LOW

title: CRITICAL: Fix Construct(outputs=) → output= in 5 website pages
description: 5 pages use Construct(outputs=ScoredClaims) but the field is output= (singular). Pydantic extra=ignore silently drops it → compile fails. Pages: organizing.mdx, why-neograph.mdx, full-pipeline.mdx (x2), programmatic.mdx, overview.mdx.

title: CRITICAL: Fix construct_from_functions(outputs=) → output= in subgraphs.mdx
description: subgraphs.mdx line 14 uses outputs= but the actual kwarg is output= (singular).

title: Duplicate modifiers silently dropped (Oracle|Oracle, Each|Each, Loop|Loop)
description:
node | Oracle(...) | Oracle(...) silently drops the second Oracle. get_modifier() returns only the first instance. Second modifier is permanently invisible to compiler, state builder, factory, and validator.

Root cause: modifiers.py Modifiable.__or__ (line 64-109) has mutual exclusion for Each+Loop and Oracle+Loop but no same-type duplicate guard.

Fix two locations (belt-and-suspenders):
1. Modifiable.__or__: add `if self.has_modifier(type(modifier)): raise ConstructError` before existing guards
2. _validate_node_chain: add duplicate-type check in the modifier validation block (lines 169-187)

Covers all modifier types including Operator. No valid use case for duplicate modifiers exists.

Fixtures: tests/check_fixtures/known_gaps/mod_double_oracle.py, mod_double_each.py, mod_double_loop.py — move to should_fail/ when fixed.

title: Sub-construct output boundary check bypassed by input-port-as-producer
description:
When a sub-construct has input=TypeA and output=TypeA, the output boundary check passes because the input port is registered as a producer of TypeA. No internal node needs to actually produce TypeA — the check is satisfied by the input port alone. At runtime, make_subgraph_fn silently returns None.

Root cause: _construct_validation.py lines 194-212 — the boundary check iterates ALL producers including neo_subgraph_input (registered at lines 122-127).

Fix (assembly time): Exclude producers with field_name='neo_subgraph_input' from the output boundary check. Only internal nodes should satisfy the output contract.

Fix (runtime defense): factory.py line 800 — if output_val is None and sub.output is not None, raise RuntimeError instead of silently returning None.

Fixtures: tests/check_fixtures/known_gaps/subconstruct_output_mismatch.py, sub_output_none_runtime.py — move to should_fail/ when fixed.
close_reason: Fixed: boundary check excludes input port + runtime defense

title: CRITICAL: FromInput shadows upstream node — silent dependency drop
description:
When a @node param name matches both an upstream node AND has Annotated[T, FromInput], the DI classifier wins and the dependency edge is silently dropped. The pipeline executes in wrong order or skips type validation entirely.

Root cause: decorators.py line 639 — `if p.name in param_res: continue` unconditionally skips DI-classified params from the inputs dict. The adjacency builder at line 1249 does the same.

Fix: In _build_construct_from_decorated, after building the decorated dict (line 1149) and before adjacency wiring (line 1232), check if any DI param name collides with a node in the decorated dict or sub_by_field. Raise ConstructError on collision.

Fixture: tests/check_fixtures/known_gaps/di_from_input_shadows_upstream.py — move to should_fail/ when fixed.
close_reason: Fixed: DI param name collision with upstream node now raises ConstructError

title: C4: _LoopCall mutates class-level Node.inputs — leaks across instances
description: forward.py _LoopCall.__call__ line 569: bn.inputs = input_type directly mutates the Node object from the class __dict__. Second instantiation of the same ForwardConstruct subclass sees already-mutated inputs. Fix: use bn = bn.model_copy(update={'inputs': input_type}) and use copies in the Construct.
close_reason: Fixed in 6a6ac47 with comprehensive regression tests

title: C3: Loop + skip_when — skip bypasses counter increment, infinite hang
description: factory.py: _apply_skip_when returns early (line 120-121) without calling _build_state_update, so neo_loop_count is never incremented. The loop_router sees count < max_iterations, routes back, skip fires again — infinite loop. Fix: _apply_skip_when must increment the loop counter when it fires on a Loop node, or the loop_router must handle the skip case.
close_reason: Fixed in 6a6ac47 with comprehensive regression tests

title: C1: Oracle models= silently ignored on LLM-mode nodes (think/agent/act)
description: factory.py: _make_scripted_wrapper transfers neo_oracle_model from state to config as _oracle_model (lines 279-286). But _make_produce_fn and _make_tool_fn read _oracle_model from config WITHOUT transferring it from state first. All TestOracleModels tests use scripted nodes — the LLM path is completely untested. Fix: add the same state-to-config transfer in produce and tool wrappers.
close_reason: Fixed in 6a6ac47 with comprehensive regression tests

title: C2: Loop + dict-form outputs — _extract_input reads non-existent field on re-entry
description: factory.py _extract_input Loop path reads own_field=node.name but with dict-form outputs (outputs={'result':X,'log':Y}) the state fields are {name}_result and {name}_log — no field named {name} exists. Loop re-entry falls through to normal extraction, re-reading stale upstream. Loop never converges, hits max_iterations. Fix: read from {field_name}_{primary_key} instead of {field_name} for dict-form outputs.
notes: ## Decision: Option A — loop feeds back primary key only. Secondary keys (tool_log) are per-iteration metadata, not loop state.
close_reason: Fixed in 6a6ac47 with comprehensive regression tests

title: TQ-01: mn_revise closure echo in TestLoadSpecMultiNodeConstruct
description: Critical. test_spec_loader.py:423-425. mn_revise ignores input_data, computes score from closure counter review_count[0]. Test passes even if sub-construct wiring is completely broken. Fix: mn_revise must read input_data and derive output from it. The correct pattern already exists in TestLoadSpecWiringHonesty::test_multi_node_construct_revise_actually_reads_review.
close_reason: Fixed in e165b70. All tests honest, 532 passed.

title: TQ-03: ForwardConstruct loop test trivially-true assertion
description: Critical. test_loop.py:410. Assertion 'result["draft"] is not None or result.get("revise") is not None' is always true because draft node always produces output. Tells nothing about whether loop cycled. fc_revise is a lambda ignoring input. Fix: assert _review_count[0] >= 2 (proves loop ran), assert result reflects iterative refinement.
close_reason: Fixed in e165b70. All tests honest, 532 passed.

title: Website full review: every page verified against 0.2.0 API
description:
Every MDX page needs content review — not just sed fixes but reading each page, verifying every code example compiles against 0.2.0, and rewriting stale content.

The prior pass (neograph-femw) fixed output=→outputs= and rewrote the API reference. But 24 remaining pages still have:
- 0.1.0 code examples that don't reflect the current API
- Missing 0.2.0 features (context=, skip_when=, typed tools, describe_value, @merge_fn, retry_policy)
- Stale prose describing old behavior
- Code examples that would fail at runtime
- References to 12 examples when there are now 16
- Version references to 0.1.0

## Approach
Read each page, verify every code example against the source, rewrite what's wrong. Commit per-batch (5-6 pages per commit) so progress is incremental.

## Batches
1. Landing + Getting Started (index, what-is, quick-start, why-neograph) — first impression pages
2. Concepts (node-modes, llm-config, observability, subgraphs, testing) — reference pages
3. Node API (functions-as-nodes, parameters, modifier-kwargs, organizing) — @node docs

5. Runtime + Forward (programmatic, llm-driven, control-flow, branching) — advanced
6. Comparison + Reference (overview, api) — already done in prior pass, verify only
