title: Release 0.2.0: merge to main, tag, update website
description:
Merge develop to main, tag v0.2.0, update website docs for all 0.2.0 features.

## 0.2.0 Changelog (86 commits)

### Breaking changes
- Annotated[T, FromInput] DI surface replaces FromInput[T]
- Node modes renamed: produce→think, gather→agent, execute→act

### New features
- Node.inputs: dict-form fan-in (multiple typed upstream producers)
- Node.outputs: dict-form multi-output (result + tool_log per key)
- @node sub-constructs: construct_from_functions(input=, output=) with port param resolution
- construct_from_functions accepts Construct items alongside @node
- Typed tool results: ToolInteraction.typed_result preserves Pydantic models
- BAML rendering: describe_type (schema) + describe_value (instances)
- Tool results rendered as BAML in ToolMessage (not str())
- context= for verbatim state injection into prompts
- context forwarded from parent state into sub-constructs
- Oracle generator type inference from merge_fn signature
- skip_when= conditional produce (bypass LLM call)
- Pluggable input rendering (XmlRenderer, DelimitedRenderer, JsonRenderer)
- json_mode output schema via describe_type
- render_prompt() inspector
- Error hierarchy: NeographError → ConstructError, CompileError, ConfigurationError, ExecutionError
- list[X] merge-after-fanout (consume Each results as list)

### Bug fixes
- Sub-construct forwards context fields from parent state
- skip_when + Each: wraps result in dispatch key dict
- Oracle generator type deferred to assembly time (file ordering)
- Oracle generators use merge_fn input type (not post-merge type)
- Multiple port params raise ConstructError (not silent overwrite)
- Dict-form outputs + Oracle concurrent write error
- Each fan-out key validation in programmatic API
- 21 code review findings addressed

### Stats
- 417 tests (up from ~180 at 0.1.0)
- 16 runnable examples (up from 12)
- 76 files changed, 14K insertions

## Release steps
1. Update website docs for new features (biggest effort)
2. Update version in pyproject.toml
3. Merge develop → main
4. Tag v0.2.0
5. Push tag (triggers PyPI publish via GitHub Actions)

## Website pages needing updates
The mode rename (think/agent/act) was already done. Remaining:
- node-modes.mdx: add context=, typed tool results, describe_value
- functions-as-nodes.mdx: construct_from_functions with input=/output= and Construct items
- api.mdx: new exports (describe_value, ToolInteraction.typed_result)
- what-is-neograph.mdx: feature list update
- quick-start.mdx: verify mode names current
- testing.mdx: 417 tests, test file layout table
close_reason: v0.2.0 released. 88 commits, 420 tests, 16 examples, 81 files changed. Tag pushed — GitHub Actions publishes to PyPI.

title: describe_value: BAML-style instance renderer for Pydantic models
description:
Add describe_value() to describe_type.py — renders a Pydantic model INSTANCE in the same TypeScript-style notation as describe_type, but with actual values instead of type names.

## What describe_type produces (schema):
{
  node_id: string  // Graph node identifier
  score: float  // Relevance score 0-1
}

## What describe_value should produce (instance):
{
  node_id: "UC-042"  // Graph node identifier
  score: 0.9  // Relevance score 0-1
}

Same notation. Values where types were. Field descriptions still as comments. One consistent format.

## For lists:
describe_value([hit1, hit2]) produces:
[
  {
    node_id: "UC-042"  // Graph node identifier
    score: 0.9
  },
  {
    node_id: "BR-007"
    score: 0.7
  }
]

## Implementation
Reuse _field_comment from describe_type. Walk model_fields, get value via getattr(instance, field_name). Render value: str→quoted, int/float→bare, bool→true/false, None→null, BaseModel→recursive, list→[items], dict→{k: v}.

## Then update _render_tool_result_for_llm in _llm.py
Replace describe_type schema + renderer.render() with describe_value() only. One format, no XML/BAML mismatch.

## File: src/neograph/describe_type.py
## Also: src/neograph/_llm.py (_render_tool_result_for_llm)
## Also: src/neograph/__init__.py (export describe_value)
## Tests: tests/test_renderers.py (TestDescribeType class — add describe_value tests)

title: Tool results in ToolMessage: use describe_type schema + renderer, not model_dump_json
description:
When a tool returns a Pydantic model, the ToolMessage content (what the agent LLM sees during the ReAct loop) should use describe_type for the schema header + the configured renderer for the instance — same as every other prompt input. Currently it uses model_dump_json which is raw JSON values with no field descriptions.

## File: src/neograph/_llm.py, lines ~367-380

### Current (just shipped in neograph-iura):
if isinstance(result, _BM):
    rendered = result.model_dump_json(indent=2)
...
messages.append(ToolMessage(content=rendered, ...))

### Should be:
if isinstance(result, _BM):
    from neograph.describe_type import describe_type
    schema_header = describe_type(type(result))
    # Use the node's renderer (or global) to render the instance
    instance_text = _render_tool_result(result, renderer)
    rendered = f'{schema_header}\n\n{instance_text}'
...
messages.append(ToolMessage(content=rendered, ...))

## What the LLM sees now (model_dump_json):
{
  "source_file": "auth.py",
  "line": 42,
  "snippet": "def authenticate(user, password): ...",
  "relevance": 0.95
}

## What it should see (describe_type + renderer):
Tool result schema:
{
  source_file: string  // Path to the source file
  line: int  // Line number
  snippet: string  // Code snippet at that line
  relevance: float  // Relevance score 0-1
}

<source_file>auth.py</source_file>
<line>42</line>
<snippet>def authenticate(user, password): ...</snippet>
<relevance>0.95</relevance>

## Why this matters
- describe_type includes Field(description=...) annotations — the LLM knows what each field MEANS
- The renderer (XML/delimited/JSON) is consistent with how all other inputs are rendered
- model_dump_json gives values without context — the LLM has to guess field semantics

## Implementation detail
invoke_with_tools needs access to the node's renderer. Currently it doesn't receive it. Two options:
A. Pass renderer as a parameter to invoke_with_tools
B. Use the global renderer via _get_global_renderer() inside invoke_with_tools

Option A is cleaner — the factory already has the node, passes renderer down.

## Scope
- Only the ToolMessage content changes (what the agent LLM sees)
- ToolInteraction.result gets the same rendered text (backward compat: still a string)
- ToolInteraction.typed_result stays the original model (unchanged)
- Downstream nodes receive typed_result — how THEY render it is their business

## Acceptance criteria
- ToolMessage.content includes describe_type schema header for Pydantic tool results
- ToolMessage.content uses the configured renderer for the instance
- Non-Pydantic tool returns (str, dict) unchanged — str() as before
- All existing tests pass
- New e2e test: verify ToolMessage content has schema header + rendered instance

title: TDD: typed tool result flows end-to-end
description:
Write FAILING end-to-end tests that prove typed_result flows from tool invocation through compile→run to downstream node consumption. Tests must use real compile() + run() pipeline execution, not mock assertions on internal functions.

## Test 1: test_typed_result_preserved_when_tool_returns_pydantic_model
File: tests/test_pipeline_modes.py, TestGatherToolCollection class

Setup: Full pipeline — @node(mode='agent') with FakeTool that returns a Pydantic model
- Define ToolResult(BaseModel, frozen=True) with typed fields
- FakeTool.invoke() returns ToolResult(...)
- ReActFake scripts 1 tool call → final structured output
- Pipeline: single agent node, compile(), run()

Assertions on the PIPELINE RESULT (not internal state):
- result['explore_tool_log'] is a list with 1 ToolInteraction
- result['explore_tool_log'][0].typed_result is not None
- isinstance(result['explore_tool_log'][0].typed_result, ToolResult)
- result['explore_tool_log'][0].typed_result.field_name == expected_value
- result['explore_tool_log'][0].result contains valid JSON (not Python repr)

## Test 2: test_typed_result_flows_to_downstream_node_when_gather_produce_chain
File: tests/test_composition.py, TestGatherProduceSubConstruct class

Setup: Full gather→produce pipeline inside sub-construct (the piarch pattern)
- FakeTool returns ToolResult model
- Capturing prompt compiler records what downstream produce node receives
- compile() + run() the full parent pipeline

Assertions:
- Downstream prompt compiler's input_data['explore_tool_log'] contains ToolInteraction instances
- Each ToolInteraction.typed_result is the original ToolResult model
- The produce node received structured data, not repr strings

## Test 3: test_string_tool_result_backward_compat
File: tests/test_pipeline_modes.py

Setup: FakeTool returns a plain string (existing behavior)
- compile() + run()

Assertions:
- tool_log[0].typed_result == 'found it' (the string itself, not None)
- tool_log[0].result == 'found it' (unchanged from current behavior)

## CRITICAL: These tests must FAIL before neograph-iura is implemented
The tests exercise typed_result which exists on the model (from neograph-y1v1) but is never populated by invoke_with_tools yet. So typed_result will be None → assertions fail → TDD red confirmed.

## NOT ALLOWED
- No mocking invoke_with_tools or _make_tool_fn
- No testing internal functions directly
- No pytest.mark.xfail
- Every test must use compile() + run() on a real pipeline

title: invoke_with_tools: preserve typed result + render for LLM
description:
Change invoke_with_tools in _llm.py to store typed result and render smartly for ToolMessage.

## File: src/neograph/_llm.py, lines 364-374

### Before (lines 364-374):
tool_interactions.append(ToolInteraction(
    tool_name=tool_name,
    args=tool_call.get('args', {}),
    result=str(result),              # TYPE DESTROYED HERE
    duration_ms=int(tool_elapsed * 1000),
))
messages.append(ToolMessage(
    content=str(result),             # AND HERE
    tool_call_id=tool_call['id'],
))

### After:
# Smart rendering: Pydantic → model_dump_json, list[Pydantic] → JSON array, else str()
from pydantic import BaseModel as _BM
if isinstance(result, _BM):
    rendered = result.model_dump_json(indent=2)
elif isinstance(result, list) and result and isinstance(result[0], _BM):
    import json as _json
    rendered = _json.dumps([r.model_dump() for r in result], indent=2)
else:
    rendered = str(result)

tool_interactions.append(ToolInteraction(
    tool_name=tool_name,
    args=tool_call.get('args', {}),
    result=rendered,               # rendered string for backward compat
    typed_result=result,           # ORIGINAL TYPED OBJECT PRESERVED
    duration_ms=int(tool_elapsed * 1000),
))
messages.append(ToolMessage(
    content=rendered,              # structured JSON for LLM (not repr)
    tool_call_id=tool_call['id'],
))

## Why model_dump_json not str()
- str(SearchResult(...)) → 'SearchResult(node_id=..., score=0.9)' — Python repr, not parseable
- model_dump_json() → '{"node_id": "...", "score": 0.9}' — valid JSON the LLM can parse
- For non-Pydantic returns (str, dict, int), str() is fine (backward compat)

## Acceptance criteria
- ToolInteraction.typed_result holds the original tool return value
- ToolInteraction.result holds the rendered string (model_dump_json for Pydantic)
- ToolMessage.content has model_dump_json for Pydantic results (not repr)
- Non-Pydantic tool returns still work (str(), backward compat)
- All existing tests pass (result field is still a string)

title: ToolInteraction: add typed_result field
description:
Add typed_result: Any = None to ToolInteraction in tool.py.

## File: src/neograph/tool.py, lines 45-55

### Before:
class ToolInteraction(BaseModel, frozen=True):
    tool_name: str
    args: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    result: str = ''
    duration_ms: int = 0

### After:
class ToolInteraction(BaseModel, frozen=True):
    tool_name: str
    args: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    result: str = ''           # rendered string (backward compat)
    typed_result: Any = None   # original Pydantic model or raw value
    duration_ms: int = 0

## Acceptance criteria
- typed_result field exists on ToolInteraction
- Default is None (backward compat — existing code creating ToolInteraction without typed_result still works)
- frozen=True stays (immutable)
- ToolInteraction is still exported from neograph.__init__
- Existing test test_tool_interaction_has_expected_fields in test_pipeline_modes.py still passes

title: Typed tool results: tools return models, not strings
description:
Typed tool results: tools return models, not strings. Parent epic for the implementation.

## The problem
_llm.py:367 does result=str(result) — tool returns a Pydantic model but it gets stringified into ToolInteraction.result: str. The original 1bp design says 'tool results should stay typed, renderer converts at the last mile.' The implementation threw away the types at the first mile.

## The fix
1. ToolInteraction gets typed_result: Any = None (keeps result: str for backward compat)
2. invoke_with_tools stores the original object in typed_result, renders with model_dump_json for ToolMessage
3. Downstream nodes receive list[ToolInteraction] with both .result (str) and .typed_result (original model)
4. Tests prove typed_result is preserved end-to-end

## Files affected
- src/neograph/tool.py (ToolInteraction model)
- src/neograph/_llm.py (invoke_with_tools)
- tests/test_pipeline_modes.py (existing tool tests)
- tests/test_composition.py (e2e tests)
- tests/test_fakes.py (ToolInteraction assertions)
notes:
## Lineage

This feature was designed as part of neograph-1bp (Node.outputs refactor epic, now closed). The full design is in neograph-1bp's DESIGN and NOTES fields — multiple design decisions documented:

1. 'Demand-Driven Collection' — tool results collected ONLY when downstream declares dependency
2. 'Renderer Pipeline for Tool Results' — same rendering as any input, describe_type + XmlRenderer/etc
3. 'N Named Outputs' — dict[str, type] mirrors dict[str, type] inputs
4. 'Why NOT Message History' — typed end-to-end, not prose-level ToolMessage strings

The implementation shipped 7 subtasks (1bp.1 through 1bp.7) but the typed tool result part was never completed:
- 1bp.6 collected ToolInteraction but with result=str (stringified)
- The design says 'tool results should stay typed, renderer converts at the last mile'
- The implementation does str(result) at the first mile (_llm.py:367)

This issue completes the original 1bp design — the last missing piece.

Cross-reference: bd show neograph-1bp for full design context (DESIGN + NOTES fields).
close_reason: typed_result field + invoke_with_tools implementation + 3 e2e tests. 405 passing. Mutation-tested.

title: skip_when + Each: skip_value result not wrapped in Each dict key
description:
When a node has both skip_when= and map_over= (Each), the skip_value result is returned as a bare model instead of being wrapped in the {dispatch_key: value} dict that Each expects.

The state reducer (_merge_dicts) calls new.items() on the bare Pydantic model → AttributeError.

## Concrete case

```python
@node(
    outputs=RawClaim,
    model='fast',
    prompt='rw/canonicalize-claim',
    map_over='flatten_groups',
    map_key='group_id',
    skip_when=lambda group: len(group.members) == 1,
    skip_value=lambda group: RawClaim(r_id=group.group_id, statement=group.members[0].statement, source_section=''),
)
def canonicalize(group: IndexedClaimGroup) -> RawClaim: ...
```

Multi-member groups go through the LLM and get wrapped correctly: {"G000": RawClaim(...)}.
Singleton groups hit skip_when, return the bare RawClaim from skip_value.
The reducer merges dicts from multi-member + bare models from singletons → crash.

## Error

```
File neograph/state.py:40, in _merge_dicts
    for key, val in new.items():
AttributeError: 'RawClaim' object has no attribute 'items'
```

## Expected

skip_value results should be wrapped in {dispatch_key: value} the same way normal Each results are. The dispatch key comes from the Each item's key field (group.group_id in this case).
notes:
## Reproduction confirmed
- Test: test_skip_value_wrapped_in_each_key_when_skip_fires
- Error: TypeError: 'MatchResult' object is not a mapping (in _merge_dicts)
- Root cause: _apply_skip_when (factory.py:114) returns {field_name: bare_result} — misses the Each {dispatch_key: value} wrapping that _build_state_update does at L194-196
- Fix: _apply_skip_when must call _build_state_update instead of building the dict directly, OR inline the Each wrapping logic

title: oracle_gen_type inference fails when @merge_fn is defined AFTER @node in same file
description:
infer_oracle_gen_type runs at @node decoration time (line 652 in decorators.py). If the @merge_fn function is defined BELOW the @node in the same file, the merge_fn isn't in _merge_fn_registry yet. Inference returns None, oracle_gen_type stays None, and generators use the wrong type.

piarch's rw_ingestion.py:
```python
# Line 124: @node runs — group_claims not registered yet
@node(outputs=ClaimGroupingResult, ensemble_n=3, merge_fn='group_claims')
def decompose(read_node: ReadContext) -> ClaimGroupingResult: ...

# Line 128: @merge_fn runs — too late, decompose already has oracle_gen_type=None
@merge_fn
def group_claims(variants: list[DecompositionResult], ...) -> ClaimGroupingResult: ...
```

Result: oracle_gen_type is None. Generators ask LLM for ClaimGroupingResult (wrong). Should ask for DecompositionResult.

Fix options:
1. Defer inference to compile time (construct_from_functions/compile) instead of decoration time
2. Document that @merge_fn must be defined BEFORE the @node that references it
3. Two-pass: @node stores the merge_fn name, compile resolves it later

Option 1 is cleanest — compile() has access to all @node and @merge_fn registrations.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Test: test_oracle_gen_type_inferred_when_merge_fn_defined_after_node
- Status: FAILING — oracle_gen_type=None because @merge_fn not yet registered at @node decoration time
- Fix: move inference to _build_construct_from_decorated (construct assembly time)
## Trace: no similar issues — this is the only place inference happens at decoration time
## Review: [LOW] Move inference from @node decorator (L652) to _build_construct_from_decorated (after all nodes registered). Keep the decoration-time inference as a best-effort (when merge_fn IS already registered). Overall: ALL_LOW

title: Oracle: generators use node.outputs type for LLM schema, but merge_fn changes the type
description:
When a node has Oracle(merge_fn=...) and the merge_fn returns a DIFFERENT type than what each generator should produce, the framework uses node.outputs as the LLM schema for each generator. This is wrong — the generator should produce its own type, and the merge transforms it.

## Concrete case

```python
@node(outputs=ClaimGroupingResult, model='reason', prompt='rw/decompose',
      ensemble_n=3, merge_fn='group_claims')
def decompose(read_node: ReadContext) -> ClaimGroupingResult: ...

@merge_fn
def group_claims(variants: list[DecompositionResult], ...) -> ClaimGroupingResult:
    # Takes 3x DecompositionResult, groups equivalent claims, returns ClaimGroupingResult
    ...
```

What happens:
- outputs=ClaimGroupingResult, so each generator's LLM call uses ClaimGroupingResult.model_json_schema() as the json_mode schema
- The LLM is asked to produce ClaimGroupingResult (which has groups: list[ClaimGroup] with gen_id cross-references) — impossible for a single generator to produce
- The LLM produces something that doesn't parse → generators return None/empty → merge gets empty variants → pipeline produces nothing

What should happen:
- Each generator should produce DecompositionResult (inferred from merge_fn's first parameter type: list[DecompositionResult] → element type is DecompositionResult)
- The framework should use DecompositionResult.model_json_schema() for each generator's LLM call
- The merge_fn receives list[DecompositionResult], returns ClaimGroupingResult
- node.outputs should reflect the POST-MERGE type (ClaimGroupingResult) for downstream consumers

## The type flow

```
Generator LLM call → DecompositionResult (per-generator type, from merge_fn signature)
merge_fn(list[DecompositionResult]) → ClaimGroupingResult (post-merge type, = node.outputs)
downstream node consumes → ClaimGroupingResult (from node.outputs)
```

## How to infer the generator type

The merge_fn's first parameter is typed as list[DecompositionResult]. The element type IS the generator output type. The framework can inspect this at compile time:

```python
import inspect, typing
sig = inspect.signature(merge_fn)
first_param = list(sig.parameters.values())[0]
# first_param.annotation is list[DecompositionResult]
element_type = typing.get_args(first_param.annotation)[0]  # DecompositionResult
```

## Impact

This blocks any Oracle where the merge transforms the type — the most common real-world pattern. The workaround (making generators and merge return the same type) forces unnatural API design.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Test: test_oracle_generator_uses_merge_input_type_not_node_outputs
- Status: FAILING (confirmed bug)
- Log shows 'output=PostMerge' for generator calls — should be PerVariant
- Pydantic validation error: 'Input should be PostMerge' when PerVariant is written to collector
- Root cause: _resolve_primary_output(node) returns node.outputs which is the POST-MERGE type
- Fix locations:
  1. factory.py: _resolve_primary_output or the produce wrapper needs to use the generator type, not node.outputs, when Oracle is active
  2. state.py: compile_state_model builds the collector as list[node.outputs] — should be list[generator_type]
  3. compiler.py: _add_oracle_nodes could store the inferred generator type on the node or pass it to the factory
  4. Inference: inspect merge_fn signature, get_args(first_param.annotation)[0] = element type
## Trace Similar
- The same issue applies to gather/execute modes (not just produce) — _make_tool_fn also uses _resolve_primary_output(node)
- The state model collector type in state.py:_add_output_field (line 169) is Annotated[list[output_type], _collect_oracle_results] where output_type = node.outputs — also wrong for type-transforming merge_fn

## Architect Review
- [MEDIUM] Where to store the generator type? Options:
  A. Node field (node.oracle_generator_type) — requires node.py change (IR layer)
  B. Infer at compile time from merge_fn signature — requires compiler to pass it down
  C. Infer at factory time from merge_fn registry lookup — runtime overhead each call
  PREFER B: infer once at compile time, store result for factory use. The compiler already resolves the merge_fn. Use a new field on Node: oracle_gen_type.
- [LOW] State model collector needs the generator type too (list[gen_type] not list[output_type])
- [LOW] The @node decorator with ensemble_n= should also infer and store the gen type

Overall: ALL_LOW (the MEDIUM is a placement choice, B is clearly best)

title: Oracle merge_fn not firing after generators complete in construct_from_functions pipeline
description:
In piarch's RW pipeline, decompose uses Oracle(n=3, merge_fn='group_claims'). Three generators run and complete (confirmed in logs — 3x node_start/node_complete for decompose). But the merge barrier node (merge_decompose) never fires. The pipeline skips directly from the last decompose completion to flatten-groups, which receives empty/null input and the pipeline ends with no claims.

Log evidence (logs/16c91187.jsonl):
- Events 16-24: 3x decompose start + complete with LLM calls (47s, 76s, 100s)
- Event 25: flatten-groups starts IMMEDIATELY (no merge event in between)
- Event 26: flatten-groups completes in 0.0s (empty result)
- Event 27: pipeline completes at 108s (should be ~25 minutes for full pipeline)

The graph compiles correctly — compile logs show 'merge_decompose' as a node. But at runtime, the Oracle barrier doesn't collect the 3 generator results.

This worked in the previous neograph version (before the construct_from_functions Construct-acceptance fix in neograph-dqe). The dqe fix may have broken Oracle barrier assembly.

Pipeline: construct_from_functions with @node + sub-construct.map(). The Oracle is on decompose, NOT inside the sub-construct. The sub-construct is verify_claim (explore→score).
notes:
## Reproduction

Minimal repro — pure neograph, no piarch dependencies:

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel
from neograph import (
    node, construct_from_functions, compile, run,
    configure_llm, register_scripted, merge_fn,
    ToolInteraction,
)

class Input(BaseModel, frozen=True):
    text: str

class Claims(BaseModel, frozen=True):
    items: list[str]

class Merged(BaseModel, frozen=True):
    final: list[str]

class SubIn(BaseModel, frozen=True):
    claim: str

class SubOut(BaseModel, frozen=True):
    result: str

# Fake LLM
class FakeLLM:
    def with_structured_output(self, model, **kw):
        self._m = model
        return self
    def invoke(self, msgs, **kw):
        return self._m(items=['claim-1', 'claim-2'])

configure_llm(
    llm_factory=lambda tier, **kw: FakeLLM(),
    prompt_compiler=lambda t, d, **kw: [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'test'}],
)

# Oracle node — 3 generators + merge
@merge_fn
def merge_claims(variants: list[Claims]) -> Merged:
    all_items = [i for v in variants for i in v.items]
    return Merged(final=list(set(all_items)))

register_scripted('merge_claims', merge_claims)  # if needed

@node(outputs=Merged, model='fast', prompt='decompose', ensemble_n=3, merge_fn='merge_claims')
def decompose() -> Merged: ...

@node(outputs=list[str])
def flatten(decompose: Merged) -> list[str]:
    print(f'flatten received: {decompose}')  # <-- will show None or empty
    return decompose.final if decompose else []

# Sub-construct (to trigger the dqe code path)
@node(outputs=SubOut, model='fast', prompt='verify')
def explore(item: SubIn) -> SubOut: ...

@node(outputs=SubOut, model='fast', prompt='score')
def score(explore: SubOut) -> SubOut: ...

sub = construct_from_functions('sub', [explore, score], input=SubIn, output=SubOut)

# Parent: @node + sub-construct in one construct_from_functions call
pipeline = construct_from_functions('test', [
    decompose, flatten, sub.map('flatten', key='claim'),
])

graph = compile(pipeline)
result = run(graph, input={'node_id': 'test'})
print(f'Result keys: {sorted(result.keys())}')
print(f'flatten output: {result.get("flatten")}')
```

Expected: merge_claims runs after 3 decompose generators, flatten receives Merged with items.
Actual: flatten receives None/empty, pipeline completes in seconds.

The bug is triggered by having BOTH an Oracle node AND a sub-construct in the same construct_from_functions call. Remove the sub-construct and Oracle works fine.
## Reproduce Attempt
- Wrote 2 regression tests covering both failure modes (Oracle before sub-construct, Oracle after sub-construct)
- BOTH PASS — bug not reproducible with current code (commit 655f8eb, the dqe fix)
- The Oracle barrier assembly is not affected by the sub_by_field dict or topo sort changes
- Possible consumer-side issue: stale install, topology detail not captured, or LLM/prompt setup
- Tests committed as regression guards regardless
## Trace Similar
- Checked all Oracle-related compiler code in compiler.py (_add_node_to_graph Oracle path)
- The dqe changes are purely in decorators.py (_build_construct_from_decorated)
- The compiler receives the final ordered list and processes Node vs Construct independently
- No path from the dqe changes to Oracle barrier wiring — they're in different layers
- The all_known adjacency dict adds sub-construct keys but doesn't modify how Node keys are processed
## Architect Review
- [LOW] Tests cover both orderings (Oracle before/after sub-construct)
- [LOW] Bug not reproducible — likely consumer environment issue
- Recommendation: close as cannot-reproduce, keep regression guards

Overall: ALL_LOW
## Root cause found

The compiled graph only has edges for the first 3 nodes:
```
__start__ → build-catalog → register-artifacts → read-node → __end__
```

ALL other nodes (decompose, merge_decompose, flatten-groups, classify, cluster, etc.) exist in the graph but have ZERO edges connecting them. The Oracle conditional edges were never compiled.

The Mermaid output confirms: only static edges up to read-node, then __end__. The 15 remaining nodes are orphaned.

This is NOT an Oracle-specific bug. It's a compiler edge-wiring bug — the compiler stops adding edges after the first few nodes when construct_from_functions contains a mix of @node items + Construct.map() items.

## Reproduce more specifically

Get the Mermaid from: compile(pipeline).get_graph().draw_mermaid()

Expected: 18 nodes with edges forming the full pipeline topology.
Actual: 3 nodes connected, 15 nodes orphaned, __end__ after read-node.
## Root Cause Analysis (corrected)
- The pipeline DOES work end-to-end at runtime
- Oracle fires: 3 generators → merge → merged result flows to downstream nodes
- The Mermaid rendering (graph.get_graph().draw_mermaid()) omits conditional edges — this is a LangGraph visualization limitation, NOT a neograph edge-wiring bug
- Oracle uses add_conditional_edges which Mermaid renders as dotted lines or omits entirely depending on LangGraph version
- The consumer's logs showing 'flatten-groups starts IMMEDIATELY (no merge event)' needs further investigation on their specific topology (piarch's 18-node pipeline), but our repro shows the pattern works correctly
- Regression guards committed — 2 tests covering both orderings, both pass
close_reason: Not a neograph bug — Oracle+sub-construct works at runtime. Mermaid rendering omits conditional edges (LangGraph visualization issue). 2 regression guards in place.

title: construct_from_functions: accept Construct items alongside @node items
description:
construct_from_functions rejects Construct instances with 'not decorated with @node'. This breaks the primary use case for sub-constructs: mixing @node functions with sub-construct pipelines in the same parent.

## The pattern that doesn't work

piarch has 15 @node functions + 1 sub-construct (verify_claim = explore→score) in the same pipeline. The @node functions reference the sub-construct output by parameter name:

    @node(outputs=ClusterMatchResult, mode='gather', ...)
    def explore(claim: VerifyClaim) -> ...: ...

    @node(outputs=ClusterMatchResult, mode='produce', ...)
    def score(explore_result, explore_tool_log) -> ...: ...

    verify_claim = construct_from_functions('verify-claim', [explore, score],
                                            input=VerifyClaim, output=ClusterMatchResult)

    # Parent pipeline: 15 @node functions + 1 sub-construct
    @node(outputs=ConsolidatedDisposition)
    def deterministic_merge(verify_claim: dict[str, ClusterMatchResult], ...) -> ...: ...

    rw_ingestion = construct_from_functions('rw-ingestion', [
        ..., flatten_claims, verify_claim, deterministic_merge, ...
    ])

This fails at TWO points:

1. construct_from_functions line 862: 'argument is not decorated with @node (got Construct)' — rejects verify_claim
2. Even if you splice it in afterward, the @node validator rejects 'deterministic_merge' because parameter 'verify_claim' doesn't match any @node in the list

## What example 13 does differently

Example 13 avoids this by using Construct(nodes=[...]) with Node.scripted for the parent — NOT construct_from_functions with @node. This means the parent pipeline can't use @node's signature-based dependency inference. The workaround defeats the purpose of @node.

## What should work

construct_from_functions should accept both @node items AND Construct items. For Construct items:
- Name: construct.name (already available)
- Output type: construct.output (already declared)
- The validator should resolve @node params against BOTH peer @nodes AND peer Constructs
- Topology: Construct items are opaque — they produce their declared output type

Alternatively: provide construct_from_mixed('name', [@node_fns...], sub_constructs=[...]) if type heterogeneity in the list is a concern.

## Impact

This blocks the gather→produce sub-construct pattern (neograph-4a7 fix) from being usable in @node-based pipelines. Example 13 proves the sub-construct works, but only in the programmatic API — not in the primary @node API that the README leads with.
design:
## Core Invariant
_build_construct_from_decorated must produce the same node ordering and type relationships as a hand-built Construct(nodes=[...]) containing the same Nodes and sub-Constructs.

## Implementation Plan
1. construct_from_functions: accept both Node and Construct items. Separate into two lists. Validate: Nodes must have @node sidecar; Constructs must have output declared.
2. _build_construct_from_decorated: new param sub_constructs: list[Construct]. Register them in decorated dict (field_name -> Construct). They participate in adjacency (as producers) but skip all sidecar-dependent processing.
3. Adjacency: when pname matches a sub-construct field_name, wire the edge. No sidecar check needed.
4. Topo sort: sub-constructs participate like nodes. They get placed in ordered list.
5. Inputs cleanup + scripted shim: skip for Construct items (isinstance check).
6. Final Construct(): include all items (Nodes + Constructs) in topo-sorted order.

~40 lines of changes, all in decorators.py.
notes:
## Findings

### Two rejection points
1. construct_from_functions L852: isinstance(item, Node) check rejects Construct items
2. _build_construct_from_decorated L980-998: adjacency loop raises 'does not match any @node' for params naming a sub-construct

### Code locations to change
- decorators.py L850-860: construct_from_functions — separate Constructs from Nodes, pass both
- decorators.py L886: _build_construct_from_decorated — accept sub_constructs param
- decorators.py L903-915: decorated dict — also register sub-constructs by field_name (for adjacency resolution)
- decorators.py L940-998: adjacency loop — skip sidecar access for Construct items, resolve params against sub-construct names
- decorators.py L1066-1098: inputs cleanup + scripted shim — skip for Construct items
- decorators.py L1106-1112: final Construct() — include sub-constructs in nodes list at their topo-sorted position

### How Construct items differ from Node items
- No sidecar (no @node decorator) — skip all sidecar-dependent logic
- No inputs/outputs dict (Construct has input/output singular) — use construct.output for producer type
- No mode/fan_out_param/scripted_fn — skip modifier and shim processing
- Constructs already validated via their own __init__

### Pattern from existing code
The Construct.__init__ in construct.py already handles mixed Node+Construct lists: 'nodes: list[Any]'. The compiler's _add_node_to_graph checks isinstance(item, Construct) vs isinstance(item, Node) and dispatches accordingly. So the LOWER LAYERS already handle mixed lists. The gap is purely in the decorator layer's adjacency builder.

### Risks
- Construct items in topo sort: must be treated as nodes with edges. If @node Y depends on Construct X, X must appear before Y in the sorted order.
- Construct.output is singular (not dict-form). A downstream @node param matching a sub-construct name gets the sub-construct's output type. This is already how it works in programmatic Construct(nodes=[...]).
- Each/Oracle on a sub-construct already works in the programmatic API. The topo sort just needs to place it correctly.
## Architect Review
- [LOW] Approach correct: register Constructs in 'decorated' dict for adjacency resolution, skip sidecar processing. Minimal changes.
- [MEDIUM] Type in decorated dict: currently dict[str, Node]. Changing to dict[str, Node | Construct] means isinstance checks needed in sidecar-accessing loops. Alternative: keep a separate sub_constructs dict and check both during adjacency. PREFER separate dict — less risky, clear separation.
- [LOW] Construct.output validation: construct_from_functions should validate Construct has output declared (required for producer type resolution).

Overall: ALL_LOW (the MEDIUM is a style preference, not a blocker)
## Regression Test
- Tests: tests/test_composition.py::TestMixedNodeAndConstruct (3 tests)
- Status: FAILING (TDD red)
- test_construct_from_functions_accepts_construct_items: ConstructError 'not decorated with @node (got Construct)'
- test_construct_from_functions_rejects_construct_without_output: same (doesn't reach output validation yet)
- test_node_param_resolves_against_sub_construct_name: same

title: CRITICAL: No test for gather→produce with tool_log sub-construct pattern
description:
The entire neograph-4a7 epic was motivated by the explore→score pattern: a gather node with tools + dict-form outputs (including tool_log: list[ToolInteraction]) feeding a produce node that consumes explore_result + explore_tool_log in a fresh conversation. This is the core 'agent explores then judges' topology.

No integration test exercises this pattern end-to-end through construct_from_functions(input=, output=). The closest test (test_dict_outputs_flow_when_two_nodes_inside_sub_construct) uses scripted nodes only, no tools, no ToolInteraction.

Required test: construct_from_functions with a gather-mode @node (tools=[...], outputs={'result': X, 'tool_log': list[ToolInteraction]}) feeding a produce-mode @node that consumes {upstream}_result and {upstream}_tool_log, compiled and run inside a parent pipeline. Use FakeTool + ReActFake from tests/fakes.py.

File: tests/test_composition.py, TestNodeSubConstruct class.
close_reason: Example 13 + 4 e2e tests proving the gather→produce+tool_log sub-construct pattern works end-to-end

title: raw_node observability claim is incorrect
description:
Multiple docs claim raw_node gets observability wired around it:
- website/src/content/docs/concepts/vocabulary.mdx:38: 'The framework wires edges, observability, and state around it'
- src/neograph/node.py:107 docstring: same claim

But src/neograph/factory.py:85-86 short-circuits: if node.raw_fn is not None, returns the raw function directly — no observability wrapper, no node_start/node_complete log events. Confirmed by running example 06: no log lines for filter_non_functional.

Fix: either (a) wrap raw_fn in an observability decorator inside make_node_fn (preferred — matches the claim), or (b) update docs to say 'the framework wires edges and state around it — observability is your responsibility in raw_node'. Source: code review issue #5.

title: Langfuse import path in observability.mdx is stale
description:
website/src/content/docs/concepts/observability.mdx:129 says: from langfuse.callback import CallbackHandler as LangfuseHandler. Raises ModuleNotFoundError on current langfuse (v4+). The working import is: from langfuse.langchain import CallbackHandler (used correctly in examples/observable_pipeline.py:23).

Fix: update the doc to match the working example. Source: code review issue #4.

title: node_id is a required state field but nowhere documented
description:
src/neograph/state.py:99 hardcodes fields["node_id"] = (str, ...). Every run() call must supply input={"node_id": ...} or Pydantic raises ValidationError. Every example does this, but docs never explain why, and Quick Start shows it without comment. A user writing their own pipeline will be blindsided.

Fix: either (a) document node_id as a required initial field with rationale, or (b) make it optional (fields["node_id"] = (str, "")). Preference: drop the hard requirement — it's meaningless to generic users and leaks internal conventions. Source: code review issue #3.

title: modifiers.mdx example missing Tool import
description: website/src/content/docs/concepts/modifiers.mdx:99-109 imports only Node, Each but uses Tool("search_nodes", budget=5). Copy-pasting the snippet raises NameError (in addition to the positional-arg bug). Fix: from neograph import Node, Each, Tool. Source: code review issue #2.

title: Positional Node("name",...) and Tool("name",...) don't work — breaks all docs
description:
Node and Tool are Pydantic BaseModel subclasses with no custom __init__ (unlike Construct). They only accept keyword args. Every positional-arg usage in the docs raises TypeError: BaseModel.__init__() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given.

Confirmed breaking:
  Node("classify", mode="produce", ...)  # TypeError
  Tool("search_web", budget=3)             # TypeError

Affected files (all break on copy-paste):
- website/src/content/docs/concepts/vocabulary.mdx:45-52, 62-63
- website/src/content/docs/concepts/node-modes.mdx:28, 49, 74, 57-58, 82-83
- website/src/content/docs/concepts/modifiers.mdx:47, 101-108, 148
- website/src/content/docs/concepts/subgraphs.mdx:33-35, 53-54, 58
- website/src/content/docs/concepts/llm-configuration.mdx:71
- website/src/content/docs/getting-started/what-is-neograph.mdx:46-53, 67-68
- website/src/content/docs/getting-started/why-neograph.mdx:135
- website/src/content/docs/getting-started/quick-start.mdx:194
- src/neograph/node.py:4-11 (docstring)
- src/neograph/tool.py:14-15 (docstring)

Fix: add custom __init__ to Node and Tool mirroring Construct's (def __init__(self, name_=None, /, **kwargs)) pattern so positional name works. Single-file change eliminates most doc issues. Source: code review issue #1.

title: TestLLMUnknownToolCall assertion is vacuous
description: test_unknown_tool_call_handled asserts result['explore'] is not None but the value is an AIMessage('ok done'), not a Claims model. Test passes because AIMessage is not None, but production output is wrong. Fix: assert isinstance(result['explore'], Claims) and fix FakeLLMHallucinator to return proper structured output. Source: code review CRIT-03, TEST-01.

title: Oracle/Each topology duplicated for Node vs Construct targets
description: compiler.py has near-identical implementations for Oracle (lines 166-236 vs 336-413) and Each (lines 239-295 vs 416-459) for Construct vs Node targets. ~120 lines duplicated. Already diverging: error message missing hint (line 226), separator inconsistency (assemble_ vs assemble-), naming split (replicate vs each). Extract shared _wire_oracle_topology() and _wire_each_topology() helpers. Source: code review CRIT-02, DRY-02, DRY-03, CON-08.

title: gather/execute wrappers are identical code
description: factory.py _make_gather_fn and _make_execute_fn are character-for-character identical. Only docstring differs. Bug fix in one won't reach the other. Extract _make_react_fn(node, mode), delete both wrappers. 5-minute fix. Source: code review CRIT-01, DRY-01.

title: Step 9: Collapse the four legacy IR fields into the address tables
description:
fan_out_param, handoff_param, handoff_channel and input_source_field each exist because the answer to 'which value is meant' was stored as a field instead of resolved. Once the resolver owns the answer, they are redundant storage that can drift from it.

Collapse them into the address tables. This is the step that makes the epic's claim true rather than merely intended: while the legacy fields remain, a future fix can still add a fifth one.

Lands LAST. Per design 14.1, provides/requires (neograph-ftnxl.8) must land after step 3 or it mints a fifth legacy field, and the accumulator channel (neograph-iq4a3) changes the producer model. Both must be landed or re-scoped before this step, or it collapses a moving target.

No backwards-compat shims -- 0.x, one downstream consumer.

Design: docs/design/port-addressed-dataflow-2026-09-03.md section 14, step 9.
acceptance_criteria: The four fields are gone from node.py. The resolver's address tables are the only storage for the answer. A sweep for type-match selection finds only _ir_normalize.py, satisfying section 15's success claim. Full gate green.

title: Step 5: Resolve the loop self-feedback destination from the address table
description:
Loop self-feedback picks its destination key by first type match over the declared answer (neograph-af8ro). Same defect class, different site.

Route the destination through the resolver: the carry's destination is an address, not a scan result. LoopCarry is already a member of the closed Source sum from step 0, so this step consumes existing vocabulary rather than adding a mechanism.

Closes neograph-af8ro.

Design: docs/design/port-addressed-dataflow-2026-09-03.md section 14, step 5.
acceptance_criteria: Loop self-feedback reads a resolved destination. A declared destination wins over a type match. af8ro closes with a regression test that fails on the old first-match behaviour.

title: Step 6: Map Agent Spec source_output to a port reference on import
description:
Agent Spec's DataFlowEdge carries source_output and destination_input -- edges join PORTS, not nodes. That is the same model this design adopts, so import becomes a direct mapping instead of a re-derivation.

Map source_output onto PortRef on the way in. Where an imported graph expresses something neograph cannot represent, REFUSE with a message naming the construct, rather than importing a graph that means something different from the one exported.

Also closes the omission where an exported Flow drops data edges for sub-construct port inputs and context forwarding (neograph-a1x7n) -- after step 2 these are stamped addresses, so they become edges in the same fold instead of a third exporter edit.

Design sections 8 and 12.

Design: docs/design/port-addressed-dataflow-2026-09-03.md section 14, step 6.
acceptance_criteria: source_output maps to PortRef on import. An inexpressible construct refuses by name. a1x7n's missing data edges appear in the exported Flow. Round-trip fixtures in the differential harness.

title: Step 7: Render the resolution in diagnostics
description:
_suggest_hint re-derives what an input probably meant in order to phrase an error, and _is_carried re-derives carry membership. Both are re-derivation, and diagnostic-only is not an exemption -- the user rejected that excuse explicitly. A hint computed by a second, informal resolver can contradict the real one, which is worse than no hint.

Have diagnostics render the Resolution the resolver already produced. The error message becomes a projection of the resolved answer, so it cannot disagree with what the compiler did.

Closes neograph-6ars9 and neograph-lmjn5. Design section 7.

Design: docs/design/port-addressed-dataflow-2026-09-03.md section 14, step 7.
acceptance_criteria: Diagnostics read Resolution and derive nothing. No second resolution path exists for error text. Both tickets close. A test shows the hint naming the same port the resolver chose.

title: Step 8: Refuse conflicting markers in the foreign-bag parser
description:
_output_classify._is_carried takes the FIRST Carried marker and discards the rest (neograph-22jvj). Silently dropping an author's second marker is the same fail-soft shape as the type scan: an answer arrives by position rather than by contract.

Make the parser REFUSE conflicting markers, naming both, instead of first-marker-wins. Design section 10 covers foreign bags.

Closes neograph-22jvj.

Design: docs/design/port-addressed-dataflow-2026-09-03.md section 14, step 8.
acceptance_criteria: Two conflicting markers refuse at assembly and name both. A single marker behaves unchanged. 22jvj closes with a regression test that fails on first-marker-wins.

title: Step 2: Stamp the boundary address and read it from both exporters
description:
Both export formats ignore output_from, so an exported boundary names the wrong producer (neograph-fnlrx) -- a P1 regression of a shipped feature. The cause is that each exporter re-derives the boundary instead of reading a stamped answer.

Stamp the boundary address during normalization. Both exporters and dump_spec READ it. Neither computes it.

Delete the false authority citations (neograph-avmx4). Several comments cite a rule as the reason for a behaviour that the code does not implement, and at least one was written by the fix it claims to describe. They hid a four-way divergence. Verify each citation against the code before deleting or correcting it.

The differential harness from step 0 is what proves the exporters actually changed. Design sections 7 and 12.

Design: docs/design/port-addressed-dataflow-2026-09-03.md section 14, step 2.
acceptance_criteria: One stamped boundary address, read by both exporters and dump_spec, computed by none of them. fnlrx's exported boundary is correct and the harness shows the change. Every false citation is verified and removed or corrected.

title: Step 3: Stamp the sub-construct port and remove the state-bag scan
description:
_scan_subgraph_input in _subconstruct.py walks reversed(state.keys()) and takes the first value that isinstance-matches the declared input. That is the canonical instance of the whole defect class: a demand answered by scanning a bag.

Stamp the sub-construct's input port during normalization, delete _scan_subgraph_input, and then REMOVE StateBus.keys(). Removing the capability is the step that makes the wrong answer unwriteable rather than merely discouraged -- design section 9. Audit every remaining caller of keys() first; each is either a legitimate read that needs a different API or another instance of this bug.

Consider _scan_subgraph_output in the same file under the same reasoning.

This step shares work with neograph-5suot (native LangGraph subgraphs), whose last open unknown IS this scan. Per design 14.1: whichever starts second builds on the first, and neither ships its own binding mechanism. Coordinate before starting.

Design: docs/design/port-addressed-dataflow-2026-09-03.md section 14, step 3.
acceptance_criteria: _scan_subgraph_input is deleted. StateBus.keys() no longer exists and the codebase compiles without it. Sub-construct input arrives via a stamped port. 5suot's unknown 5 is answered. Full gate green including examples.

title: Step 4: Add input_from and refuse authored input ambiguity
description:
Give the consuming side the same addressing the producing side gets. input_from lets an input name the port it reads, so an author who has two eligible producers of the same type can say which one is meant.

With naming available, authored ambiguity becomes refusable: when a single-type inputs= has two eligible producers, REFUSE at assembly with a message naming both ports and showing the input_from that resolves it (neograph-5fvsu). Section 5 of the design classifies this as authored ambiguity, which is refused -- distinct from emergent ambiguity, which funnels into a named channel, and unambiguous, which resolves once.

The refusal only ships after step 1, because its message tells the author to name a port.

Closes neograph-5fvsu with the taxonomy as the recorded answer. Design sections 5 and 6.

Design: docs/design/port-addressed-dataflow-2026-09-03.md section 14, step 4.
acceptance_criteria: input_from resolves through the resolver. Two eligible producers for one single-type input refuses at assembly, naming both ports and the resolving syntax. 5fvsu closes with the design's taxonomy cited. Three-surface parity tested.

title: [EPIC] Port-addressed data flow: one resolver owns which value is meant
description:
Implements the design in docs/design/port-addressed-dataflow-2026-09-03.md.

The problem it ends: five independent fixes over five months all answered the same question -- which upstream value does this input mean -- by scanning a shared state bag and type-matching. fan_out_param (2026-04-06), handoff_param (07-13), handoff_channel (07-14), output_from (08-25), input_source_field (08-27). Each added a field and a per-consumer read. The sixth instance appeared during the week this design was written.

The fix is structural, not another case: an address (PortRef) names a member's specific output, a closed Source sum enumerates every way a value can arrive, and ONE resolver in _ir_normalize.py turns a demand into a Resolution. Every other layer READS the resolution instead of re-deriving it. The capability to re-derive is REMOVED (StateBus.keys() goes away), so bag-scanning stops compiling rather than being banned by a guard.

Read the design's section 14 for the step table and 14.1 for the ordering constraints. Section 15 states the falsifiable claim this epic is measured against.

IMPORTANT for anyone executing a child step: the open symptom tickets (x8i3s, kgndo, fnlrx, avmx4, af8ro, a1x7n, 22jvj, 5fvsu, 6ars9, lmjn5) are what the steps CLOSE, not what to work on. Fixing one locally is the failure mode this epic exists to end.
acceptance_criteria: A sweep finds type-match selection only in _ir_normalize.py. The state bag is not enumerable. The four legacy IR fields are gone. Every symptom ticket in the Closes column is closed BY a step, not by a local patch.

title: Step 0: Add the address and source types with a construction ban
description:
Create src/neograph/_ir_source.py holding the vocabulary the rest of the migration reads:

- PortRef(member, output) -- an address naming a member's SPECIFIC output, not the member.
- Source -- a CLOSED sum over every way a value can arrive: Peer | Port | EachItem | LoopCarry | HandoffChannel | LastPresent | Accumulated. Closed is the point: a new arrival mechanism must extend this type, which makes it visible, rather than adding a field somewhere.
- Resolution -- what the resolver returns for one demand.

Construction is BANNED outside _ir_normalize.py, enforced the way G3 enforces the IR_FIELDS single-writer rule. Extend the existing guard rather than writing a parallel one.

Also land the differential-export harness: a fixture corpus where a change in resolution shows up as a change in exported Agent Spec. Section 15's success claim depends on it -- 'exporter behaviour changes anyway, proven by the harness'.

This step changes NO behaviour. It adds the types, the ban, and the instrument. Design sections 3, 4, 7 and 9.

Design: docs/design/port-addressed-dataflow-2026-09-03.md section 14, step 0.
acceptance_criteria: _ir_source.py exists with PortRef, the closed Source sum, and Resolution. A guard fails when any module other than _ir_normalize.py constructs one. The differential harness runs in the gate and detects a deliberate resolution change. Full gate green, no behaviour change.

title: Step 1: Honour output_from in validation and require a port for multi-output members
description:
output_from is stored and then ignored. Name a member whose declared type does not match and validation silently falls back to the type scan, so the author's explicit answer loses to a guess (neograph-x8i3s). It also names a NODE, but a node has many outputs, so it cannot address a specific one (neograph-kgndo).

Resolve output_from through the step-0 resolver into a PortRef. When the named member has more than one output and the reference does not name which, REFUSE at assembly with a message listing the available ports. When the named port's type does not match the demand, REFUSE -- naming a port and getting a silent fallback is the defect.

This step comes FIRST among the fixes, per design section 14: every later refusal tells an author to name a port, so that instruction has to work before the refusals ship.

Closes neograph-x8i3s and neograph-kgndo. Do not patch them individually.

Design: docs/design/port-addressed-dataflow-2026-09-03.md section 14, step 1.
acceptance_criteria: output_from resolves through the resolver. A mismatched or ambiguous reference refuses at assembly and names the available ports. Both symptom tickets close with the resolver as the fix, not a local branch. Three-surface parity tested.

title: describe_type tells the model it may send a null the declared type rejects
description:
Root cause of the GH #20 family, found while reviewing neograph-bek2f. Filed rather than fixed in 0.7.11 because the fix rewrites model-facing prompt text globally.

describe_type.py:367 renders ' or null' for ANY field that is not required and whose annotation does not already admit None:

  if not field_info.is_required() and not _admits_none(field_info.annotation):
      type_str = f'{type_str} or null'

Reproduced in the 0.7.11 worktree on the reporter's own shape:

  class Change(BaseModel):     path: str; kind: str = 'edit'
  class RootCause(BaseModel):  label: str; changes: tuple[Change, ...] = ()
  class Claim(BaseModel):      ref: str; root_cause: RootCause

  describe_type(Claim) ->
    root_cause: { label: string
                  changes: [{ path: string
                              kind: string or null }] or null }

Neither tuple[Change, ...] nor str can hold null. neograph's OWN schema instructs the model to emit a value its declared type rejects -- and the model complies, which is precisely how GH #20's two paid runs failed. 'Has a default' means OMITTABLE, not NULLABLE; the renderer conflates them.

Likely fix: render a defaulted non-nullable field as optional (omit-to-default) rather than nullable -- e.g. a trailing '?' on the key or an 'optional' marker -- and keep ' or null' only where _admits_none is true.

Why this was NOT done in 0.7.11: it changes the prompt text of every optional non-nullable field in every shipped pipeline. That is a behavioural change to what models are ASKED, and no offline test validates it -- it changes what models do, not what code does. Existing describe_type tests pin the current ' or null' text and would need rewriting, which is only legitimate if this reading is confirmed.

Relationship to the shipped 0.7.11 work: neograph-5s8f6 made the runtime COERCE the null back to the default on both output strategies, and neograph-bek2f added a lint WARN naming the field before a run. Both are backstops for this. Fixing the renderer would remove the cause, at which point the lint kind's meaning should be revisited (its whole justification is that the renderer currently promises null).

title: lint must reject a model-authored field with a default whose type rejects null
description:
GH #20. lint() checks that the pipes connect: DI bindings resolve, inline placeholders resolve, template refs resolve. All three are connectivity properties. It does not check whether anything can flow through them.

A field that is authored by the model, carries a default, and has a type that rejects null is a latent runtime failure. A Pydantic default applies only when the key is ABSENT; a present-and-null value overrides it and fails validation. Models emit present-and-null routinely.

THE CHECK MUST RECURSE. Both reported failures were on types reachable from a node's declared output, not on the top-level model. The reporter notes that a first attempt in userland walked top-level fields only and reported clean on a tree that already contained the defect -- an instrument passing because it did not look.

The cost of not having it, measured by the reporter across two paid runs on the same project in one day:

    run 1  train n=198 correct=179 accuracy=0.904 errors=1     32.7M tokens
           Claim.status: ClaimStatus = 'proposed'
    run 2  train n=7   correct=0   accuracy=0.000 errors=192   28.0M tokens
           RootCause.changes: tuple[Change, ...] = ()  (one level down)

Their graph-lint passed cleanly immediately before both runs. A static walk finds both in under a second.

Relationship to neograph-5s8f6: that ticket makes the structured path COERCE null to the default, as json_mode already does, so the reported shapes stop failing. This lint stays worth having as the second layer -- it names the field before a run, and it still catches the case where an author wants the model to author a field that it cannot express.
design:
## Core Invariant
Every statement neograph makes to a model about a declared type must be one the type can
satisfy -- so the lint that reports "this field was told it may be null" and the renderer
that says ` or null` must read the SAME annotation authority (`_admits_none`), and neither
may derive nullability independently.

## Implementation Plan

1. NEW MODULE `src/neograph/_lint_nullable_defaults.py`. It is auto-discovered by
   `scripts/gen_api_manifest.py:388 _lint_cluster_modules()` (globs `_lint_*.py`) and by
   tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py, so no registration step. Do NOT grow lint.py (611 lines,
   orchestrator only) and do NOT bolt this onto `_lint_consumers` / `_lint_supply` -- they
   answer the two dataflow-direction questions, this answers a type-expressiveness question.

2. REUSE the predicate, do not re-derive it. Import `_admits_none` and `_is_output_excluded`
   from `neograph.describe_type` (:317, :84) and reproduce the renderer's own field filter:
       if field_info.exclude or _is_output_excluded(field_info): continue   # describe_type:258/351
       if not field_info.is_required() and not _admits_none(field_info.annotation): REPORT
   This is byte-identical to describe_type.py:367 -- the branch that today writes ` or null`
   into the prompt. Optional refinement: suppress the report when
   `TypeAdapter(Annotated[ann, *field_info.metadata]).validate_python(None)` SUCCEEDS
   (kills the `Any` and null-tolerant-BeforeValidator false positives), catching
   PydanticUndefinedAnnotation / PydanticSchemaGenerationError / any Exception as
   "do not report". TypeAdapter may only SUPPRESS, never be the sole authority.

3. RECURSE with a walker MIRRORING `describe_type._count_classes` / `_count_annotation`
   (:237-:309): `visited: set[type]` for cycle protection, dispatch over
   Union / list / tuple / set / frozenset / dict / BaseModel, peeling with
   `_null_defaults._unwrap_optional` where a single-member Optional needs unwrapping. Yield
   `(dotted_path, field_name, field_info)`. tuple/set MUST be descended -- the reporter's
   run-2 shape is `tuple[Change, ...]`, and `_null_defaults._descend_null_defaults`
   deliberately excludes tuples (:126); do not inherit that exclusion here. Report each
   (model, field) once, message carrying the first-encountered dotted path
   (`Claim.root.changes`).

4. SCOPE the walk to what the model authors: for each Node with
   `mode in ("think","agent","act")`, take `output_model, _ = _resolve_primary_output(node)`
   (`_dispatch.py:374` -- the monopoly; it already handles dict-form primary key and the
   `oracle_gen_type` override). Walk ONLY the primary; secondary dict keys (`tool_log`) are
   framework-collected (_dispatch.py:378, :338). Scripted/raw nodes are exempt: their output
   is constructed in Python, where a default is legitimate. Resolve the inputs-vs-outputs
   contradiction flagged in the notes before widening past outputs.

5. HOOK as check `# 7.` in `lint._walk` after lint.py:367, alongside checks 3-6. Per-node,
   so branch arms are covered by the existing `iter_with_arms` recursion (lint.py:311) and
   no raw `.nodes` walk is introduced (tests/test_guards_branch_arm_walks.py would reject one).

6. EMIT one `LintIssue` per offending field with a LITERAL `kind=` and LITERAL

## Scope decision (orchestrator, resolving the research atom's NEEDS-USER-INPUT)
The ticket DESCRIPTION ('a model-authored field') and the ACCEPTANCE ('reachable from a node's
declared inputs and outputs') disagree. Resolved in favour of the description, WITHOUT blocking:

SCOPE = the declared PRIMARY output of think/agent/act nodes, recursed into nested models.

Why the literal 'inputs and outputs' reading is rejected: a node's declared input is either
(a) an upstream node's output -- already reported at the producer when that producer is
LLM-mode, so linting it again double-reports the same field, or (b) a caller- or
scripted-supplied model, whose defaults are LEGITIMATE because no model authors them.
Implementing the literal reading therefore guarantees false positives on every scripted
pipeline. The reporter's entire complaint is an instrument they cannot trust ('an instrument
passing because it did not look'); an instrument that cries wolf fails the same requirement
from the other side. 'inputs and outputs' is read as loose phrasing for 'the full reachable
type surface', which the recursion delivers.

title: structured mode lacks the null-to-default coercion json_mode has, so the strategies disagree again
description:
GH #20 reports that a model-authored field with a default whose type rejects null is a latent runtime failure, and proposes a lint check. The lint check is worth having, but it is the second-best fix, because neograph already solves this on one path and not the other.

_apply_null_defaults (_null_defaults.py:139) replaces a null with the field default, and _descend_null_defaults recurses through list/dict/Optional containers to any depth. It is called from exactly two places, both in _llm_retry.py's _parse_json_response -- the json_mode path. The structured path (_llm.invoke_structured, via with_structured_output) never calls it.

Measured on the reporter's own shape, a nested tuple field with a default, given a nested null:

    json_mode   (_parse_json_response) -> Claim(root_cause=RootCause(changes=()))   RECOVERS
    structured  (pydantic validation)  -> ValidationError                           FAILS

So the reporter's statement that 'json_mode cannot recover it either, because the payload is well-formed JSON' is wrong, and wrong in a way that matters: json_mode does not re-prompt, it COERCES before validation. A re-prompt indeed cannot fix it; the coercion already does.

This is the same disagreement class as GH #14, where structured and json_mode disagreed about which declared output types are usable at all. The house rule established there is that the two strategies must agree about what a declared output can be.

Fix: apply the same coercion on the structured path before validation, so a pipeline that works under json_mode works under structured. That makes the pipeline RUN, where a lint warning only tells the author to restructure a type they may have good reason to keep.
design:
## Root Cause
Present-and-null overrides a Pydantic default. json_mode COERCES before validation
(_apply_null_defaults, reached from _parse_json_response); the structured path never
reaches that coercion because validation happens inside LangChain, and the resulting
parsing_error=ValidationError is classified as Failed -> re-prompt -> exhaustion.

## Fix Approach (minimal, single coercion implementation)
1. Pure file split, mirroring the layout develop already has (eases the forward-port):
   move the null-default cluster (_is_list_annotation, _optional_inner_types,
   _unwrap_optional, _is_stringly_null, _descend_null_defaults, _apply_null_defaults)
   out of _llm_retry.py into a new src/neograph/_null_defaults.py; _llm_retry.py
   re-exports them so every existing import keeps resolving. This is a REAL shrink of
   _llm_retry.py (its LINE_BUDGET ratchets DOWN), so no budget is raised to make room.
2. Add recover_null_defaults(raw_msg, model) to _null_defaults.py: pull the candidate
   payload from raw_msg.tool_calls[*].args (method='function_calling') or from
   json.loads(raw_msg.content) (json_schema/json_mode-ish), deepcopy it, run the SAME
   _apply_null_defaults, and re-validate. Returns None unless the coercion ACTUALLY
   changed the payload -- so an unrelated validation failure is never masked.
3. Hook it in _llm_structured_compat._classify_lc_result, the pure classifier the sync
   and async adapters already share, so both twins get it with zero duplication and
   _llm_dispatch is untouched.

## Not covered (stated, not silently skipped)
IncludeRawCompatDecorator's no-include_raw fallback raises ValidationError out of the
runnable with the payload never surfaced, so there is nothing to coerce there.
acceptance_criteria: The reporter's shape -- a defaulted field whose type rejects null, nested one level down -- produces the same result under both output strategies, proven by a parametrized test over structured and json_mode. Reverting the structured-side coercion fails it. A guard pins that the two strategies share one coercion implementation rather than two.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/modes/test_null_default_parity.py::TestNullDefaultCoercionParity (4 failed / 2 passed)
- Red output: the 2 json_mode params PASS, all 4 structured params FAIL with
  ExecutionError 'structured output failed validation after 1 re-prompt(s)' <- ValidationError
  root_cause.changes 'Input should be a valid tuple, input_value=None'.
  That IS the disagreement: same payload, same declared output, opposite result.
- Root cause: _apply_null_defaults (_llm_retry.py:223) is called ONLY from
  _parse_json_response (json_mode). On the structured path validation happens inside
  LangChain's with_structured_output, and neograph classifies the resulting
  parsing_error=ValidationError as Failed and re-prompts instead of applying the
  coercion it already owns.
- Verified on main by symbol: grep -c _apply_null_defaults src/neograph/_llm.py -> 0
## Trace-similar (atom .3)
The bug is one instance of a DISEASE: repairs accrete on ONE output strategy and no single
place declares 'these are the repairs every strategy applies'. Three siblings found and FILED
(not fixed here -- out of scope for the 0.7.11 patch):
- neograph-6hei8 (P2): structured lacks json_mode's bare-JSON-array auto-wrap.
- neograph-51hab (P2): structured re-prompt never consults _is_truncated, so a length-capped
  response is told its JSON failed validation. _is_truncated has exactly ONE caller
  (_retry_msg_for_failure, json_mode only). Blocked on Failed carrying no response object.
- neograph-vt1l9 (P2): the asymmetry running the OTHER way -- think-mode json_mode has no DSML
  recovery, while structured (_llm_dispatch) and agent/act (_tool_loop) both do.
## Codebase Disease Scan (atom .4)
Pattern: a second place that reasons about a Pydantic model FIELD DEFAULT against a
null/absent LLM-emitted value, instead of routing through _apply_null_defaults.
Shape: SYNTACTIC (an exact set of Pydantic default APIs) -> single grep/AST scan, no fan-out.

Scan: grep -rn 'PydanticUndefined|default_factory|field_info\.default|\.default is' src/
Result: 24 hits, ZERO instances of the disease.
  - 18 are dataclass/pydantic Field(default_factory=...) DECLARATIONS (node.py, construct.py,
    renderers.py, _spec_schema.py, tool.py, _llm_config.py, _llm_runtime.py, _agent_cycle.py,
    _normalize.py) -- declaring a default, not repairing a value against one.
  - 4 are inspect.Parameter.empty (_param_classify.py:147, _validation_modifiers.py:146,
    node.py:305, decorators.py:801) -- FUNCTION-SIGNATURE defaults feeding the DI CONSTANT
    classification. Different concept, different API, no shared rule.
  - the remaining hits are inside _llm_retry.py itself, i.e. the helper being extracted.

Disposition: nothing to MIGRATE, nothing to ALLOWLIST, nothing to DEFER. _apply_null_defaults
is and stays the single implementation; the fix adds a second CALLER, not a second copy.
## Architect review (atom .5)

1. Root cause correctness -- LOW. Verified empirically (json_mode recovers, structured raises
   on the identical payload) and by symbol (grep -c _apply_null_defaults src/neograph/_llm.py
   -> 0). The root cause is a MISSING CALL, not a wrong coercion.

2. Fix minimality -- MEDIUM, accepted. The _null_defaults.py split is not required by the bug.
   It is required by the guard: _llm_retry.py sits at its declared LINE_BUDGET ceiling
   (698/698 'at ceiling'), so any addition there forces a ratchet raise, which the standing
   rule forbids without a real shrink. The split IS that shrink, and it lands main on the
   layout develop already has (neograph-3ffdg.15), cutting forward-port conflict. Condition:
   the move must be PURE -- zero logic edits inside the moved functions -- so the behavioural
   diff stays reviewable.

3. Regression risk -- LOW, conditional on the changed-payload guard. recover_null_defaults
   returns a model ONLY when the coercion ACTUALLY mutated the payload AND the mutated payload
   validates; otherwise None and the existing re-prompt runs untouched. So an unrelated
   validation failure can never be masked. Existing WeakIncludeRawFake ('{"wrong":"shape"}'
   vs Claims) coerces nothing -> unchanged.

4. Architecture compliance -- MEDIUM, resolved. _llm_structured_compat's contract is 'only
   CLASSIFIES one call's result shape' and 'never re-prompts'. The hook is pure -- no network,
   no re-prompt -- so the never-re-prompts rule holds, and 'this is a Parsed once the standard
   repair is applied' is classification. _classify_lc_result is the module's stated anti-drift
   seam (shared by the sync and async adapters), so hooking there covers both twins with zero
   duplication; a decorator class would cost ~25 lines and a new top-level name for no
   behavioural gain. Needs model threaded into _classify_lc_result -- a signature change, not
   a new name; it has no callers outside its own module (only the guard's name allowlist
   references it). COST TO WATCH: _llm_structured_compat.py budget is 235 with 232 actual.
   Keep the recovery LOGIC in _null_defaults.py so the hook is a call plus a guarded return;
   if it still overflows, prefer tightening to fit over raising the ratchet, and report it.

5. Similar-bug scalability -- MEDIUM, accepted with beads. The fix does not cure the disease
   (repairs accreting one strategy at a time). Siblings filed: neograph-6hei8, neograph-51hab,
   neograph-vt1l9. A single 'repairs every strategy applies' seam is a design change, not a
   patch-release change.

6. Test coverage -- LOW, with two additions REQUIRED in the fix atom:
