title: Validation ignores output_from when another member type-matches
description:
output_from is stored on the IR and then not honoured by the boundary check. When the NAMED member's output type does not match Construct.output, and a DIFFERENT member produces a matching type, assembly accepts the construct and silently falls back to the type scan.

Reproduced on develop:

    Construct('c', input=Good, output=Good, output_from='settle', nodes=[
        Node.scripted('other',  fn='f', outputs=Good),    # matches by type
        Node.scripted('settle', fn='f', outputs=Wrong),   # NAMED, does not match
    ])
    -> ACCEPTED. The name was ignored; the scan picked 'other'.

With no other producer the construct is refused, but the message reads 'declares output=Good but no internal node produces a compatible value' -- which is not the defect. The defect is that the member you NAMED produces something else.

So the disambiguator is ignored in exactly the situation it exists for: more than one candidate. Naming is the sanctioned escape from an ambiguity refusal, and an escape that silently does nothing is worse than none.

Distinct from neograph-fnlrx, which covers the EXPORTERS ignoring output_from. This is the assembly-time validator ignoring it.
acceptance_criteria: A named member whose output type does not match Construct.output fails at Construct(...), and the message names the member, its type, and the declared boundary type. The presence of another type-compatible member does not change that. A regression test uses the two-producer shape, since a single-producer test passes for the wrong reason.

title: output_from names a node, but a node has many outputs
description:
Construct.output_from names a MEMBER. A member declaring dict-form outputs writes one state field per key, so the name does not say which output crosses the boundary.

Reproduced on develop:

    Construct('c', input=Claims, output=Claims, output_from='settle',
              nodes=[Node.scripted('settle', fn='f',
                                   outputs={'result': Claims, 'tool_log': Log})])
    -> ACCEPTED. output_from = 'settle'
    -> settle writes settle_result AND settle_tool_log

Assembly accepts the declaration and nothing states which output is meant.

The format neograph exports to already solves this. An Agent Spec DataFlowEdge carries source_output and destination_input, so its edges address PORTS, not nodes (_agent_spec_boundary.py:158-160). neograph addresses nodes, which makes its own naming less expressive than the format it serialises to -- and a node-addressed name cannot round-trip a port-addressed edge.

Fix: address a port. 'settle.result', or an explicit pair. The same applies to any input-side naming field, so decide the spelling once for both directions.
acceptance_criteria: output_from addresses a port. A member with dict-form outputs requires the output key, and omitting it fails at Construct(...) naming the available ports. A single-output member keeps the bare form. Round-trip through Agent Spec preserves which port fed the boundary.

title: Delete the false authority citations that hid the four-way divergence
description:
A comment asserting parity with a named module is load-bearing misinformation. Three verified instances hid a four-way divergence through at least one prior review, and a fourth was written BY the fix that was supposed to end it.

Still present and measurably false:

1. _subconstruct.py:58-62 -- claims the eligibility rule 'agrees with _agent_spec_boundary.resolve_end_node_sources, which already answers which node is the boundary positionally. One rule, not a fifth answer.' Written by the neograph-35mur fix itself. neograph-fnlrx is the proof it is false: both exporters ignore output_from=, so they do NOT agree.

2. _agent_spec_dispatch.py -- the eligible=None scan's docstring calling it the 'only resolution available'. Falsified: the dispatched flow passes the same Construct(...) gate before invoke, so its boundary IS resolved.

3. _agent_spec.py:387 (fixed in neograph-t1nbp) -- cited 'the assembly-time validator's single-type resolution' as its authority. The validator performs no resolution; _validation_inputs.py:110 is an existence check that returns on the first compatible producer and discards which. The export did not drift from a rule -- it invented one and cited a non-existent authority.

DELETE them, do not reword. A weaker claim in the same position is still an assertion a reviewer will trust instead of checking. Where a genuine shared rule exists, the code should SHARE THE FUNCTION, not describe the agreement in prose.
acceptance_criteria: The three citations are gone. Any surviving cross-module agreement claim is backed by a shared call or a test that fails when the agreement breaks -- not by prose. A grep for comments asserting parity with a named module returns only claims with such backing.

title: [BUG] Both export formats ignore output_from=, so the exported boundary is the positional rule
description:
neograph-35mur shipped output_from= as the explicit, validated answer to 'which member supplies the construct's boundary output'. The runtime honours it (_subconstruct.py:260) and lint honours it (_lint_consumers.py:143). NEITHER exporter does.

## Measured, not read

    Construct('branch', input=Seed, output=Case, output_from='verify',
              nodes=[verify -> Case, trailing -> Case])

    runtime : branch boundary = Case(label='VERIFY')          output_from HONOURED
    export  : trailing.label -> branch__end.label             output_from IGNORED
    dump    : 'output_from' in dump_spec(...)  ->  False
              two constructs differing ONLY in output_from dump IDENTICALLY

## Two sites

1. _agent_spec_boundary.py:237  resolve_end_node_sources
   Takes construct.nodes[-1] positionally. Does not read output_from (verified: output_from
   has readers at _subconstruct.py:260, _lint_consumers.py:143, _validation_outputs.py:203,
   _agent_spec_markers.py:138 -- this module is not one of them). Also takes the EndNode's
   Properties from _item_outputs(last) rather than construct.output, and walks raw .nodes
   rather than iter_with_arms. Three axes of divergence, not one.

2. _spec_dump.py:366  _dump_sub_construct
   Drops output_from entirely. _spec_loader.py:271 DOES read it and _spec_schema.py:157 DOES
   carry it, so a dump->load round trip silently reverts to the positional rule. This also
   breaks _spec_dump's own stated rule that 'a differ comparing two pipelines whose only
   difference is X must not report identical'.

The Agent Spec side defends the round trip with attach_boundary_marker (_agent_spec_markers.py:123);
the sibling format has no such defence. One export path defends against exactly this, the other does not.

## Why the existing test does not catch it

tests/test_subconstruct_output_boundary.py::test_output_from_is_restored_by_from_agent_spec
uses a sub-construct with ONE node, so nodes[-1] IS the named node and the positional rule
agrees by coincidence. It asserts the MARKER survives; it never asserts the exported Flow's
data edges honour it. Two nodes is all it takes.

## A false docstring is part of the defect

_subconstruct.py:60-63 (written by the 35mur fix) says item_field_names 'agrees with
_agent_spec_boundary.resolve_end_node_sources, which already answers which node is the boundary
positionally. One rule, not a fifth answer.' That is FALSE, measured above. Delete the claim
rather than rewording it -- a comment asserting parity with a named module is the mechanism by
which this stayed invisible through the 35mur review.
acceptance_criteria: A construct declaring output_from= exports an artifact whose boundary data edge names that member, at BOTH export formats. dump_spec round-trips output_from. Two constructs differing only in output_from do not dump identically. Regression test uses a MULTI-node sub-construct so the positional rule cannot agree by coincidence.
notes:
Found by neograph-t1nbp's codebase disease scan (atom neograph-gfhje.4), 2026-08-26, and VERIFIED BY EXECUTION twice -- once by the orchestrator, once independently by the consistency lens, with matching results. Probe scripts under the session scratchpad.

Filed as P1 and SEPARATE from neograph-t1nbp: t1nbp is the single-type inputs= port, this is the output boundary. Same disease (export re-derives a rule the runtime owns), different channel, and this one regresses a fix that already shipped.

title: [BUG] Loop self-feedback dest_key picked by first type match over declared inputs (export)
description:
Sixth site of the neograph-35mur / neograph-t1nbp disease: resolve WHICH declared binding satisfies a type by taking the first positional isinstance/issubclass match over a bag, where the author expected resolution by NAME.

## Site

src/neograph/_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:405-415 -- choosing the destination input key for a Loop node's self-feedback edge during Agent Spec export:

    if ni.is_dict_form and not no_self.is_dict_form:
        self_field = field_name_for(node.name)
        if self_field in ni.by_name:
            dest_key = self_field          # named self-reference: correct, exact
        else:
            for key, typ in ni.by_name.items():
                if isinstance(typ, type) and (issubclass(no_self.primary, typ) or issubclass(typ, no_self.primary)):
                    dest_key = key
                    break                  # FIRST type match wins, silently

The named branch above it is exact and right. The fallback is the disease: forward iteration, break on first hit, no refusal when TWO input keys share a type compatible with the node's own output. A Loop whose dict-form inputs are e.g. {'seed': Draft, 'hint': Draft} has no declared answer to which key the fed-back output lands on, and the export picks whichever pydantic ordered first.

## Why it is filed apart from neograph-t1nbp rather than folded in

Same family, different code path and different repro (a Loop node with two same-typed dict-form input keys, not two same-typed producers). It is EXPORT-only, so its failure mode is t1nbp's portability half: the exported artifact wires a loop-back edge to a key the runtime does not feed. t1nbp's fix may or may not reach this call site; if the shared resolver it lands covers this too, close this as absorbed and say so.

## Precedent for the resolution

_param_classify.py:63-71 already refuses exactly this ambiguity for port params, raising ConstructError naming the candidates. Refuse-on-ambiguity is the house posture; this site silently picks.
acceptance_criteria: A Loop's self-feedback destination key either resolves to a NAMED binding or refuses when more than one declared input key matches the fed-back output type. Export and runtime agree on which key is fed. A regression test pins a two-same-typed-key Loop at the export surface.
notes:
Found by neograph-t1nbp's trace-similar atom (neograph-gfhje.3), 2026-08-26, sweeping src/neograph for positional type-match resolution. Not yet reproduced -- filed on code reading. The repro to write first is a Loop node with dict-form inputs carrying two keys of the same type, exported via to_agent_spec, asserting the self-feedback data_flow_connection lands on the key the runtime actually feeds.

Full six-site inventory with precedence directions is in neograph-t1nbp's notes.
## Scope extended 2026-08-26 (neograph-t1nbp disease scan, atom neograph-gfhje.4)

This was filed as an EXPORT-only defect. Two lenses independently found the RUNTIME half, and
it looks worse than the export half:

  _input_shape.py:70-88  _extract_loop_reentry, multi-key branch

The destination key for the fed-back loop value is decided PER ITERATION from LIVE STATE, by
testing whether each sibling's read_upstream(...) comes back None. It is type-BLIND, and it can
place 'latest' into SEVERAL keys at once -- every key whose upstream happens to be unbound on
this iteration. Only if none took it does the placed_latest fallback (:85-87) put it in the
first key.

  inputs={'seed': Draft, 'notes': Notes} on a Loop producing Draft, with notes' producer in an
  untaken branch arm:
     runtime writes latest into 'notes' (TYPE-MISMATCHED) and leaves the original seed in 'seed'
     export  wires the self-edge to 'seed'

So export and runtime disagree AND the runtime side is independently wrong. Nothing validates
it and the author gets no error, because the decision sits in a layer that cannot refuse.

Both halves should land together -- fixing either alone leaves the artifact and the run
disagreeing. The suggested shape (layering lens): stamp Node.loop_reentry_key in
_ir_normalize.py as a single-writer IR field beside fan_out_param -- it is the same KIND of
fact ('which dict-form input key receives a framework-supplied value') -- and have both the
runtime and the exporter READ it rather than each deriving it.

title: Hand-built ToolInteraction renders as empty body -- renderer drops typed_result, result defaults to ''
description:
GitHub issue #19 (github.com/KonstantinMirin/neograph/issues/19), filed 2026-08-26 against develop (post-0.7.9).

Root cause confirmed: ToolInteraction.result: str = '' defaults empty. The framework's own agent-loop path (_agent_tool_calls.py:_build_tool_interaction) always populates BOTH result= (pre-rendered) and typed_result=, so framework-driven tool calls render fine. A caller hand-building a ToolInteraction (e.g. a scripted node calling a tool directly, feeding the result into a template) typically sets only typed_result -- the validated object it already has -- and leaves result at its silent empty default. renderers.py:299's _render_tool_interactions joins f'{ti.tool_name}:\n{ti.result}', so the rendered packet is the tool name and a blank line. No exception, no warning -- lint() cannot catch it (channel is correctly typed/consumed, only the RENDERING is empty) and a ${...}-placeholder-survival guard cannot catch it either (the placeholder IS substituted, with an empty string).

Reporter's real-world cost: a scripted node makes deterministic opening tool calls so the next agent starts grounded; the agent received tool names and blank bodies on every run including every paid evaluation run, and continued/completed green by silently re-fetching everything itself -- wasted budget, and a grounding premise never delivered, indistinguishable from a tool that legitimately returned nothing.

FIX APPLIED (2026-08-26, TDD): _render_tool_interactions's body is now ti.result when non-empty, falling back to describe_value(ti.typed_result) when typed_result is set and result is empty; empty string only when NEITHER is set (a tool that legitimately returned nothing, correctly indistinguishable from itself). This is the reporter's own preferred fix (non-breaking, makes the good case automatic, reuses describe_value which already exists for exactly this). args/duration_ms stay omitted (true bookkeeping, never payload).

Related: GH #18 (same root: typed_result exists, validated, and wasn't reachable where needed) -- distinct ticket, do not conflate (that one is about DECLARING typed results as node output; this one is about RENDERING an already-declared list[ToolInteraction]).
acceptance_criteria: renderers.to_rendered([ti]) renders typed_result via describe_value when result is empty and typed_result is set. Framework-populated result keeps winning (never overridden by typed_result). Neither-set case still renders an empty body (legitimately indistinguishable from a no-op tool). TDD: 3 tests added to tests/test_renderers.py, mutation-verified.
close_reason: Fixed and released: 0.7.10 (v0.7.10). renderers.py's _render_tool_interactions now falls back to describe_value(.typed_result) when .result is empty. Cherry-picked cleanly onto a fresh release/0.7.10 worktree off main (0.7.9); GH #17's fix was NOT extractable (depends on develop-only file-split architecture not present in main) so this patch is scoped to #19 alone, per explicit user decision.

title: [BUG] Single-type inputs= resolves by isinstance scan, and runtime picks FIRST while export picks LAST
description:
Same disease as neograph-35mur (silent wrong answer from an isinstance scan over a bag of state), on a third and fourth site, found by 35mur's trace-similar atom.

## Site 3 -- runtime, _input_shape.py:135 _extract_single_type

'Scan state fields for first value matching the node's input type.' Forward iteration over state.keys(), first isinstance match wins. The single-type inputs=X form is the DOCUMENTED convenience shorthand (CLAUDE.md: 'the single-type form skips fan-in validation and defers to runtime isinstance scan'), so this is the path a reader is most likely to take.

MEASURED, not theoretical:

    a    -> Case(label='FIRST')
    b    -> Case(label='SECOND')     # consumes a
    sink -> inputs=Case              # declared AFTER b

    runtime: sink consumed 'FIRST'

sink's immediate upstream is b. It got a. No error, run green.

## Site 4 -- export, _agent_spec.py:387

The Agent Spec export mirrors the same heuristic with 'for upstream in reversed(ordered_items[:idx])' -- LAST preceding producer wins. Its own comment says it is 'mirroring the assembly-time validator's single-type resolution'.

MEASURED on the identical construct above:

    runtime: sink consumes a  (FIRST)
    export : wires sink <- b  (LAST)

**The exported artifact wires a different edge than neograph executes.** A consumer running the exported Flow gets a different answer than the pipeline it was exported from. This is worse than either scan alone: it is a portability defect on top of a correctness one.

## The precedence rules do not agree anywhere

    _scan_subgraph_input   (_subconstruct.py:38)  reversed -> LATER wins
    _scan_subgraph_output  (_subconstruct.py:54)  reversed -> LATER wins
    _extract_single_type   (_input_shape.py:135)  forward  -> EARLIER wins
    _agent_spec.py:387                            reversed -> LATER wins

Three implementations of one heuristic, two contradictory rules, no shared authority. Whatever neograph-35mur decides for the output boundary must become that authority, or this multiplies again.
design:
## Root Cause

One question -- 'which producer satisfies this single-type inputs= binding?' -- is answered by
two independent implementations that never consult each other, and they disagree:

  _extract_single_type   (_input_shape.py:139)   forward over state.keys()         EARLIEST wins
  _agent_spec.py:388     (export)                reversed(ordered_items[:idx])     LATEST   wins

Neither resolves to a producer the AUTHOR NAMED; both infer one from an isinstance match over a
bag whose contents depend on unrelated declarations. Measured across the suite: 918 resolutions,
184 multi-candidate, and the runtime and the export disagree by construction.

The exporter's comment cites 'the assembly-time validator's single-type resolution' as its
authority. No such resolution exists -- _validation_inputs.py:110-114 is an EXISTENCE check that
returns on the first compatible producer and discards which. The export did not drift from an
authority; it invented one and cited it, which is how the divergence stayed invisible.

## Fix Approach (REVISED after architect review neograph-gfhje.5; supersedes the prior draft)

The prior draft said 'adopt 35mur's eligibility rule and pick a direction'. Both halves of that
are wrong, and the review measured why. What follows is the corrected design.

### 1. The candidate set, not the direction, is the primary fix

Restrict candidates to DECLARED PRODUCERS. The scan currently admits the whole state bag, so
framework bookkeeping competes as input: measured, a 'neo_node_fingerprints' entry (a dict of
SHA prefixes) matched as a legitimate candidate in 25 sites. Excluding neo_* removes 25 of 149
ambiguities outright and removes a class of absurd matches entirely.

### 2. The input side's eligible set is NOT the output side's -- do not transplant it

Both scan lenses recommended _extract_single_type adopt item_field_names' eligibility rule.
VERIFIED WRONG: a sub-construct's first node reads its PORT through this scan (traced:
'[inner] single-type scan MATCHED state key neo_subgraph_input'), and 195 of 918 resolutions
are exactly that. item_field_names EXCLUDES the port by design -- on the OUTPUT side it is the
paradigm 'value the child was merely HANDED', which is the whole of GH #17. On the INPUT side
that same value IS the legitimate source.

  output side:  declared item fields                        (a handed value must not compete)
  input  side:  declared producer fields  U  the own port   (the handed value is the source)

Two different sets, one shared SHAPE (an explicit eligibility list, never a whole-bag scan).

### 3. Precedence within the set: peer producers outrank the port

Measured: '[step_a, neo_subgraph_input]' and '[probe, neo_subgraph_input]' -- a peer and the
port both match, and the correct answer is the peer. This is not a new rule; _param_classify.py:57
already states it for port params ('peer @node takes priority'). Reuse the wording, do not invent
a second one.

### 4. Resolution, and what it stamps

At assembly, for a node whose inputs is single-type X:
  - compatible declared producers == 1  ->  stamp that field name
  - compatible declared producers == 0  ->  stamp the port, when the construct's input= is
                                            compatible with X
  - compatible declared producers  > 1  ->  RAISE ConstructError naming every candidate, and
                                            point at the existing escape hatch

The escape hatch already exists and needs no new field: dict-form inputs={'b': Case} IS the
named form on the input side, exactly as output_from= is on the output side. The error message
must name it.

### 5. Do NOT flip the runtime to match the export

The obvious reading of this bug is 'two directions, pick one'. Measured, forward is LOAD-BEARING
and reversing silently breaks correct code -- reverse selects a FRAMEWORK KEY over a real
producer in three shapes: [step_a, neo_subgraph_input], [probe, neo_subgraph_input], and
[triage, billing, neo_handoff_triage]. Convergence goes the other way: both surfaces read the
stamped name. With (1)-(4) in place the direction question DISSOLVES -- a set with one element
has no precedence.

### 6. Scope: ONE IR field

  Node.input_source_field: str | None      single writer _ir_normalize.normalize_ir, per the
                                           fan_out_param / handoff_param precedent, pinned by
                                           extending guard G3's IR_FIELDS frozenset

The layering lens proposed three fields. The other two belong to other tickets and must not ride
this one: Construct.input_source_field is neograph-5suot unknown #5; Node.loop_reentry_key is
neograph-af8ro. Rows 1 and 2 (runtime + export) DO land together -- either alone leaves the run
and the artifact disagreeing, which is the defect itself.

Implementation seam left to the fix atom, with one hard constraint: the field has exactly ONE
writer. The normalizer is the sanctioned site but the producer information is built during
validation, so the fix must either have the normalizer build it via the shared
effective_producer_type helpers or move the stamp -- it may NOT be written in two places.

### 7. DECISION (F7): what None means -- it must never fall back to a scan

None means 'this node has no single-type source to resolve' (no inputs, dict-form inputs, or
first-of-chain with no compatible producer and no port). None NEVER means 'ambiguous' -- ambiguity
raised at assembly, so it cannot reach runtime. At runtime, SINGLE_TYPE shape reads the stamped
field and nothing else; when it is None the node receives None, which is today's behaviour when
the scan finds nothing.

A fallback to the old scan would leave every fixed site a silent bypass and make the structural
guard prove nothing. Fail-loud over fail-soft, per the North star: a band-aid that leaves a silent
seam is an existential defect, not deferrable polish.

### 8. DECISION (F4): the blast radius, and the five sites that need judgement

Refusal raises at 124 sites, but only SEVEN are hand-written and TWO of those are this bug's own
repro. The genuine population is FIVE, all one shape: a Portal mesh consumer whose peers (triage,
billing) both produce the type. Each of the five is examined INDIVIDUALLY in the fix atom -- they
are not to be silenced in bulk. If a Portal consumer legitimately wants 'whichever peer ran', that
is a signal it should read the handoff channel (handoff_param / handoff_channel already exist and
are the deterministic answer), not a type scan; factory.py:381 already documents choosing the
channel over a scan 'to avoid feeding a same-typed decoy'.

The remaining 117 sites are hypothesis GENERATOR output (linear chains of same-typed nodes) --
a strategy change, not 117 test edits. Recorded honestly: in 130 of 149 sites the forward and
reverse picks hold the SAME VALUE, so refusal will raise on cases nobody is currently getting
wrong. That is the cost, and it is the same cost 35mur paid deliberately.

### 9. Delete the three false citations, do not reword them

_agent_spec.py:385, _subconstruct.py:60 (written by the 35mur fix, and measurably false), and
_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:399. A comment asserting parity with a named module is the
mechanism that kept five divergent answers invisible; a reworded comment is the same mechanism
with better grammar.

### 10. Guard

Extend G3's IR_FIELDS with the new field (single-writer), and add a structural guard banning a
second derivation of 'which producer satisfies a single-type input' outside the resolver -- the
shape TestSubConstructBoundaryEligibilityMonopoly has for the output side. Per AGENTS.md's
modifier-combo lesson, the consumer list must be re-verified by sweep at fix time, not copied
from the disease scan's table.
acceptance_criteria: A single-type inputs= binding either resolves to a NAMED producer, or refuses when more than one value in state matches. Runtime and export agree by construction -- ideally by reading one shared resolver rather than two implementations that happen to match. A regression test pins the a/b/sink shape above at BOTH surfaces.
notes:
Filed from neograph-35mur atom neograph-ogk5i.3 (trace-similar), 2026-08-24. The input-port twin _scan_subgraph_input is already tracked as neograph-5suot's unknown #5. Repro script shape is in 35mur's reproduction notes; tests/test_subconstruct_output_boundary.py is the output-side equivalent.
## Reproduction (2026-08-26, atom neograph-gfhje.2)

- Failing test: tests/test_single_type_input_resolution.py::TestSingleTypeInputResolvesToADeclaredProducer
  - ::test_the_run_does_not_silently_consume_a_producer_it_never_declared   FAILED  assert 'a' == 'b'
  - ::test_the_exported_artifact_wires_the_edge_the_runtime_takes           FAILED  assert 'b' == 'a'
- Root cause: a single-type inputs=X binding is resolved by TWO independent unnamed
  isinstance scans with OPPOSITE precedence -- _extract_single_type walks state.keys()
  forward (earliest match wins) while the Agent Spec exporter walks reversed(ordered_items[:idx])
  (latest match wins) -- so with two same-typed values in scope each surface silently picks
  a different producer and neither resolves to a producer the author named.

Both halves confirmed on the filed a/b/sink shape, no contrivance beyond two nodes sharing
one domain type:
  runtime:  sink consumed a  -> Case(label='FIRST'),  run green, no error
  export :  data_flow_connections wires  b.label -> sink.label

Test design note: BOTH assertions are deliberately disjunctive on outcome, matching the
acceptance's own 'either resolves to a NAMED producer, or refuses'. The correctness test
returns clean if the run raises NeographError; the portability test asserts runtime/export
AGREEMENT (and symmetric refusal) rather than either particular winner. So the fix may
choose named-resolution or refusal without the test needing an edit -- and neither choice
can make it pass by accident, since today it is the third outcome (silent disagreement).
## Trace-similar sweep (atom neograph-gfhje.3, 2026-08-26)

Pattern searched: 'resolve WHICH value/producer satisfies a declared type by scanning a bag
and taking a positional isinstance/issubclass match', i.e. resolution by TYPE where the
author expected resolution by NAME. Swept src/neograph for reversed( scans, _isinstance_safe,
and issubclass-driven selection loops.

SIX sites, not the four the ticket filed. Precedence still splits two ways, and one site is new:

  1. _subconstruct.py:39   _scan_subgraph_input    reverse whole-state scan   LATER wins   OPEN (5suot #5)
  2. _subconstruct.py:105  _scan_subgraph_output   reverse over ELIGIBLE set  LATER wins   FIXED (35mur)

Probe: a pytest plugin wrapping the resolver, recording candidate lists per (test, node).

### The measurement that drives everything

  resolutions                                          918
  multi-candidate (>1 value in state matches)          184   (149 distinct test/node sites)
  single-candidate where that candidate is a neo_* key  195

  of those 7 hand-written: the bug's own repro           2

### F1 (HIGH) -- 'converge by reversing the runtime to match the export' is NOT viable

The obvious reading of this bug is 'two directions, pick one'. Measured, the forward direction
is LOAD-BEARING and reversing silently breaks correct code:

  ['step_a', 'neo_subgraph_input']   sub-construct node: forward picks the peer, reverse picks the PORT
  ['probe',  'neo_subgraph_input']   same shape, branch-arm operator sub-construct
  ['triage','billing','neo_handoff_triage']  Portal mesh: reverse picks the HANDOFF CHANNEL

In each, reverse selects a framework key over a real producer. So convergence must go the other
direction (export adopts the runtime's rule) or -- better -- both adopt NAMED resolution.
Anyone implementing 'just make them agree' by flipping _extract_single_type will get a green
diff and three broken shapes.

### F2 (HIGH) -- the CANDIDATE SET is the primary defect; direction is secondary

The scan admits the entire state bag, framework bookkeeping included. Measured: a
'neo_node_fingerprints' entry (a dict[str,str] of SHA prefixes) matched as a legitimate input
candidate in 25 sites. Excluding neo_* keys removes 25 of 149 ambiguities outright and removes
a class of absurd matches entirely. Restricting the set is worth more than settling the order,
and it must land FIRST -- settling the order over a bag that still contains bookkeeping fields
fixes the symptom this ticket names and leaves the mechanism.

### F3 (HIGH) -- 35mur's eligibility rule CANNOT be transplanted to the input side

Both scan lenses recommended that _scan_subgraph_input / _extract_single_type 'adopt the same
eligibility set item_field_names defines'. VERIFIED WRONG, and it would break the codebase:

  a sub-construct's first node reads its PORT through this scan --
  traced: [inner] single-type scan MATCHED state key 'neo_subgraph_input'
  195 of 918 resolutions are exactly this.

item_field_names EXCLUDES neo_subgraph_input by design -- it is the paradigm case of 'a value
the child was merely HANDED', which is precisely what GH #17 made ineligible on the OUTPUT
side. On the INPUT side that same value IS the legitimate source. The two sides need
DIFFERENT eligible sets:

  output side:  declared item fields                          (a handed value must not compete)
  input  side:  declared producer fields  U  the own port     (the handed value is the source)

Stating this explicitly is the single most important correction in this review -- the
recommendation as written is a plausible-sounding transplant that fails on 195 sites.

### F4 (MEDIUM) -- refusal is affordable, and the Portal shape needs a decision

Refuse-on-ambiguity would raise at 124 sites, but only 7 are hand-written, and 2 of those are
the bug's own repro. The real population is FIVE sites, all one shape: a Portal mesh consumer
whose peers (triage, billing) both produce the type. Compare 35mur, which measured 270/26/2 --

The 117 hypothesis sites are generator output (linear chains of same-typed nodes); they need a

I expected branch arms to sink the 'stamp one IR field' design: a post-branch consumer whose

So single-type inputs are ALREADY forbidden from crossing arms, and one stamped field is

The layering lens proposed Node.input_source_field + Construct.input_source_field +

## Fix applied (atom neograph-gfhje.7, 2026-08-27)

Resolution chosen: RESOLVE to a named producer, not REFUSE. The acceptance allowed either;
refusal was implemented and measured FIRST, then rejected on evidence and split to
neograph-5fvsu. The deciding finding: a consumer placed AFTER a Portal mesh has no name it
could correctly give -- which member ran last is a runtime fact -- so refusal would make a
CORRECT program unwritable, the inverse of the restriction this ticket adds. Under refusal the
suite showed 33 failures (14 hypothesis-invariant, 5 Portal, rest guards); the Portal special
case needed to rescue it had already started growing a second unnamed rule, which is the
disease this ticket exists to remove.

### What landed

  node.py                    + Node.input_source_field: str | None   (IR field)
  _ir_normalize.py           + resolve_single_type_source()          THE resolver
                             + _producer_pairs() / _stamp_single_type_sources()
  _input_shape.py            _extract_single_type reads the stamped NAME
  _agent_spec.py             the export reads the SAME name; reverse scan deleted

Rule: candidates are the DECLARED producers preceding the node, last one wins (the immediate
upstream -- what an author reading top to bottom means, and what the export already answered;
the runtime's forward whole-bag scan was the wrong side). Branch arms are SCOPED so a false-arm
node can never be stamped with a true-arm field. Zero declared matches falls to the construct's
own port.

### The framework-port channels, and why they are not a bag scan returning

Isolation boundaries re-home a node's input under a framework key, so the named read alone
broke 4 real shapes (oracle isolated cycle, loop-over-agent, run_isolated x2). Traced:
inside an Oracle cycle the state has NO 'seed' key -- the upstream arrives as
neo_subgraph_input. The fallback is an EXPLICIT 2-element ordered tuple
(_FRAMEWORK_PORT_KEYS: SUBGRAPH_INPUT, ISOLATED_INPUT), each a single-purpose key written by
one mechanism. Two USER producers can never compete there, which is the actual defect.

close_reason: Fixed in 1adaad0: single-type inputs= resolves to one named producer at assembly (Node.input_source_field), read by both the runtime and the Agent Spec export. Verified at the acceptance's locus (runtime and export now agree; measured before/after), full gate green, guard added.

title: Accumulator channel: many nodes append, one downstream node reads the union
description:
GH #16. A value can enter state only as a NODE'S OUTPUT. So accumulating across an Each fan costs three artifacts, none of them domain logic: a wrapper type carrying two things through one port, a scripted node inside the branch that exists only to push the tool log out, and a hand-written merge at the parent including de-dup by ref and a load-bearing ordering constraint.

The reporter's own rule is that a node earns its existence by making an LLM or tool call. Two of their six nodes do neither; the module header has to apologise for them in prose.

The failure it already caused was SILENT: a branch returning a bare Claim drops every reading it took BY CONSTRUCTION, so the terminal judge re-decided over only the opening reads while each claim asserted a status whose evidence was gone. An anti-fabrication design defeated by a data-flow limitation.

Wanted shape:
    readings = Accumulate(Reading)
    @node(outputs=Claim, mode='agent', appends={readings: stamp_tool_log})
    def verify(claim_in: Claim): ...
    @node(outputs=Decision)
    def decide(case: Case, readings: Accumulated[Reading]) -> Decision: ...

The fan stays isolated -- that is correct and explicitly not to be changed. Only the DECLARATION of what escapes it moves.
acceptance_criteria: A channel declared once is appended to by every branch of an Each and read as the union downstream, proven by a RUN not an assembly. Ordering across branches is defined and documented. The existing isolation guarantee is unchanged, pinned by a test that would fail if branch state leaked generally.

title: Nothing binds a run value into a tool call argument, so the model can invent one
description:
GH #15's actual production failure, and the part context= does NOT fully close.

Reported trace: 49 tool calls where dealId read 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 1001. Only the two calls issued by their own code carried the real id; every call the MODEL composed queried a deal that does not exist. Each returned ACCESS_DENIED with empty data, which the pipeline read as 'this deal has no data' and concluded 'blocked' from evidence about nothing. Every gate green.

context= makes the model SEE the right value, which is a large improvement over it seeing nothing and guessing -- and would likely have prevented this specific trace. It is not a GUARANTEE. The value reaches the prompt; the tool call is still composed by the model, so an invented argument stays representable.

A guarantee means the framework supplies the argument, not the model. Tool.config is static, so it cannot carry a run value. But the seam already exists: tool factories are invoked per run with the live config (_tool_loop: 'factory(config, _factory_tool_config(tool_spec))'), and neograph already stashes state-derived values into config['configurable'] before dispatch for exactly this kind of plumbing -- _inject_di_inputs and _inject_oracle_config are the precedent.

This is the north-star framing: an invented tool argument is currently REPRESENTABLE. Making it unrepresentable for a declared, framework-supplied argument is the kind of subtraction the project exists to do -- and the failure is silent, which is the class the README claims to be about.
design:
## Core Invariant
A value the FRAMEWORK owns is never sourced from model output. Every change checks against it.

## Design
1. IR: Tool.bound_args: dict[str, str] | None -- argument name -> dotted state path ('ctx.deal_id'). Declarative, so it is visible on the node and checkable.
2. Assembly: the root of each path must be produced by some upstream, reusing the shape of the context= check. Failure is a ConstructError naming bound_args, so a missing binding fails before a run rather than resolving to None at call time.
3. Runtime: resolve the paths ONCE per turn from the state bus into {tool_name: {arg: value}}, and apply in _tool_call_precheck -- already the single pure pre-invoke authority both twins consult. Applying there, rather than at the two invoke sites, is what stops sync/async drift, the same reasoning that made _trace.add_traced_node the right home for GH #6.
4. Order: apply the binding BEFORE _idempotent_repeat_key reads tc['args'], or two calls differing only in an overridden argument collapse in the repeat cache.

## Rejected
- Tool.config: static per compile, cannot carry a run value. That is exactly why the reporter's config workaround only holds while the value is immutable for the run.
- Stripping the bound argument from the schema shown to the model: a smaller prompt, but the model then cannot reason about which deal it is working on, and GH #15's whole point is that the branch needs to KNOW. Show it, and own it.
acceptance_criteria: A node can declare that a tool argument is supplied by the framework from a named run value, and the model cannot override it. Proven by a test where a fake model DELIBERATELY emits a wrong value for that argument and the tool still receives the right one. The declaration is lint-visible, so a missing binding fails before the run.
notes:
## Reproduction
tests/test_bound_tool_args.py::TestBoundToolArguments -- 3 red, 1 green.
The GREEN one is the CONTROL (test_without_the_binding_the_model_wins): it asserts the model's invented deal_id=1 DOES reach the tool today. That is the defect reproducing; if it ever stops passing, the guarded test proves nothing.

Root cause: _agent_cycle invokes 'payload.invoke(tc["args"], config=config)' (sync, :673) and 'await tool_fn.ainvoke(tc["args"], config=config)' (async, :489). tc['args'] is the model's composition verbatim. Nothing between the model and the tool asserts any part of it.

Tool has name/budget/config/idempotent. Tool.config is STATIC per-compile, so it cannot carry a run value -- which is why the reporter's config workaround only works while deal_id is immutable for the run.
## Trace-similar
The framework ALREADY asserts parts of a model-composed tool call, in _tool_call_precheck -- the single pure pre-invoke check shared by the sync and async twins. It rejects an unknown tool name, an exhausted budget, and unparseable args.

So the asymmetry is precise: neograph validates WHICH tool the model picked and whether its args PARSE, and never what the args SAY. A model naming a tool that was not bound is caught; a model inventing the deal id passed to a tool that was bound is not.

That also names the fix's home. _tool_call_precheck is already the one place both twins consult before invoking, so binding applied there cannot drift between sync and async -- the same reason _trace.add_traced_node was the right home for the GH #6 fix.

Portal's entry-port routing is the project's existing example of making a model-chosen value unrepresentable rather than merely checked, but Portal is a 0.8 capability and does not exist on this release line, so it is a precedent to cite rather than code to reuse here.
## Disease scan
Exactly two sinks hand model-composed args to a tool:
  _agent_cycle.py:489  await tool_fn.ainvoke(tc['args'], config=config)   (async)
  _agent_cycle.py:673  payload.invoke(tc['args'], config=config)          (sync)
Both are preceded by _tool_call_precheck, so one seam covers both.

INTERACTION the scan caught, which a fix applied only at the invoke sites would have broken: _idempotent_repeat_key (:430) builds its key as f"{tc['name']}::{args_canon}" from tc['args']. If binding is applied AFTER the key is computed, two calls differing only in an overridden argument collapse to one cached result -- turning a correctness fix into a caching bug. The binding must be applied BEFORE the repeat key is taken.
## Sweep verification
- M1 never apply the binding (today's behaviour): 2 fail.
- M2 binding REPLACES all args: 1 fail -- the model's own unbound arg must survive, so the fix does not over-reach.
- M3 resolver yields nothing: 2 fail.
The CONTROL passes throughout, which is what makes the guarded assertions mean anything.

## Two guards caught real defects in the first draft
- TestOneUpstreamReader: the resolver used bus.get, a SECOND reader of a peer's output field. read_upstream is the one reader because reading an upstream is a rule -- it unwraps a Loop append-list and an Each result dict against the consumer's declared type. A bound argument off a Loop-modified producer would have resolved to the whole history instead of the latest value. Exactly the half-rule failure that guard exists to stop.
- mypy: node.tools is Tool | BaseTool, and a raw LangChain BaseTool has no bound_args. Both sites now read it defensively.

title: context= is the run-state back-reference, but is documented as a rendering concern
description:
GH #15 asks for a way for a step to reference a value produced earlier in the run without threading it through every intervening shape, and states that the only routes today are threading or config. That premise is wrong: context= already does it.

Measured on a fan-out, which is the shape the issue says is hardest:

    verify = Node(name='verify', mode='think', inputs=Claim, outputs=Verdict,
                  model='fast', prompt='check', context=['ctx']) | Each(over='claims.items', key='text')

    branch 0: port item = Claim(text='a')   raw_context = {'ctx': RunCtx(deal_id=4822)}
    branch 1: port item = Claim(text='b')   raw_context = {'ctx': RunCtx(deal_id=4822)}

It meets both properties the issue names. DECLARED, not ambient: context=['ctx'] sits in the node declaration and _construct_validation checks that some upstream produces the field, so a missing binding is a compile-time error. WORKS FOR FAN-OUT: the port carries the mapped item while context carries the run value, verified above.

So the defect is not the capability. It is that a careful reporter, who files issues with traces and measurements, could not find it -- and the reason is the framing.

    node.py:  'Verbatim state fields injected into the prompt alongside typed
               input. Values are passed as-is (not BAML-rendered). Use for
               pre-formatted context like graph catalogs or domain briefings.'

    examples/14_context_injection.py: 'verbatim state in sub-constructs ...
               context= keeps a configured renderer off the value'

Every word frames it as a RENDERING concern -- how to stop a renderer wrapping a pre-formatted string. Someone whose problem is 'reach a value from earlier in the run' reads that and correctly concludes it is about presentation. The general capability is hidden behind its narrowest use case.

This is the same disease as the lint family this release fixed, one level up: the information is present, and the shape it is presented in makes it unusable.
acceptance_criteria: node.context's docstring leads with the capability (reference a value produced earlier in the run, declared and validated) and mentions verbatim rendering as a property, not as the purpose. Example 14 or a sibling shows the fan-out case, since that is the shape people cannot solve. AGENTS.md names context= where a reader looking for run-scoped state would search. The GH #15 reporter can find it from the docs alone.
close_reason: Reframed node.context, AGENTS.md 'Run-scoped state', a new concepts/run-scoped-state.mdx page, and example 14's title. The docs-snippet guard executes the page's code, so the example is runnable rather than illustrative.

title: 0.8 output projection assumed every declared output type is a BaseModel
description:
Found by the GH #14 end-to-end test during the 0.7.9 forward-port. develop's ExcludeFromOutput/Carried projection (neograph-ftnxl.4) has the SAME assumption the parse tail had -- that a declared output type is always a BaseModel SUBCLASS -- at two more sites:

    _output_classify.project_output_model   -> model.model_fields
    _output_classify.splice_carried         -> type(projected_result).model_fields

A node declaring outputs=list[Claim] therefore died with 'type object list has no attribute model_fields' on develop, even after the parse path was fixed, so the 0.7.9 fix alone would not have made develop work.

splice_carried also carried the identity trap in a second guise: 'if type(projected_result) is declared' can never hold for a container, since type([...]) is list while declared is list[Claim].

Both now return the value unchanged when the declared type is not a BaseModel subclass -- a container has no fields to project out and therefore nothing to splice back in.

Recording it as a bug rather than folding it silently into the merge: it is a THIRD independent site of one assumption, which is the argument for a guard that finds the next one rather than waiting for a report.
acceptance_criteria: A guard enumerates every site that reaches for .model_fields on a DECLARED output type and requires each to handle a container, so the fourth site fails a test instead of a run. The GH #14 E2E passes on develop.

title: Decide and document whether bare outputs=list[X] is a supported declaration
description:
GH #14 raises a question the code does not currently answer either way, and the reporter is explicit that either answer would be useful as long as it is stated.

Evidence that it is NOT the intended road:
- Across all 36 examples, outputs=list[X] appears ZERO times. Every many-valued producer uses a container model with one list field: Clusters{groups}, Batch{documents}, Claims.
- _llm_retry auto-wraps a bare JSON array into a BaseModel that has exactly one list field. That is the framework catering to the container idiom, not compensating for a gap.
- Each fans over a dotted path into a field, which presumes a container.

Evidence that it IS meant to work:
- The decorator accepts and stores list[X] whenever the identity comparison does not fire, and binds it downstream.
- describe_type(list[X]) renders a correct array schema since GH #8.
- Dict-form outputs={'result': list[X]} is accepted at assembly.

So today it is a road with three potholes and no signposts, which is the reporter's phrase and a fair one.

The cost of leaving it ambiguous is concrete and measured on their codebase: seven wrapper models minted to give nodes a declarable output type, four of them introduced during bug fixes rather than by design, taking an agreed ten-class domain model to eighteen. A reviewer asking 'when did RoundDelta become part of the ontology?' got the answer 'it did not, it was minted to satisfy an output declaration.'

Note the counter-evidence the reporter volunteered against their own case: examples/02 ships a model called Claims with the same shape as the ClaimsDelta they cite as a wrapper they were pushed into. Both things are true at once -- per-node wrappers minted during bug fixes are real damage, AND a container model is the only exercised road for a producer feeding Each.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded in AGENTS.md. If supported: an example exercises outputs=list[X] end to end through json_mode, and the parse path handles it. If not supported: the decorator fails loud at declaration with a message that says so and names the container idiom, instead of an identity-comparison accident that only fires when a return annotation is present.

title: outputs= vs return annotation is compared by identity, so every generic is rejected
description:
GH #14. decorators.py compares the declared outputs= against the resolved return annotation with 'if outputs is not ret_hint' -- IDENTITY, not equality.

Every evaluation of a subscripted generic builds a fresh types.GenericAlias, so:

    list[Reading] is list[Reading]  -> False
    list[Reading] == list[Reading]  -> True
    Reading       is Reading        -> True     <- why only generics break

That single operator is the whole declaration bug. Confirmed by measurement:

    @node(outputs=list[Reading])
    def emits(x: int) -> list[Reading]: ...   -> ConstructError
    def emits(x: int): ...                    -> ACCEPTED, outputs = list[Reading]
    @node
    def emits(x: int) -> list[Reading]: ...   -> ACCEPTED, outputs = list[Reading]

So nothing about the bare form is unsupported: declaration, storage and downstream binding all handle list[X] already. Only the equality check mishandles it, and it does so precisely when the author does the MORE correct thing and annotates the return type -- which the type checker wants.

The reporter narrowed this themselves and it contradicts their own issue title's framing; their narrowing is right.
acceptance_criteria: outputs=list[X] with a matching list[X] return annotation is accepted. A genuinely mismatched pair still raises. Parametrized over list[X], dict[str, X], tuple[X, ...], X | None and a plain BaseModel, so the fix is not proven on one shape and generalised.
notes:
## Reproduction
tests/decorator/test_edge_cases.py::TestGenericOutputsMatchTheirAnnotation, parametrized over list/dict/tuple/optional/nested/plain. Red: 4 of the 6 shapes plus the message test. The optional and plain shapes PASS before the fix and are guards, not repros -- Claims|None and a bare class already compared equal by identity.

## Root cause
'if outputs is not ret_hint' -- identity. list[X] builds a fresh types.GenericAlias per evaluation.

## Sweep verification
- M1 restore 'is not': 4 fail.
- M2 replace with 'if False' (never compare): 5 fail -- the check is not merely relaxed, it still does its job.
- M3 drop the generic parameter from type_display_name: 2 fail, one of them the check-fixture regex.

title: type_display_name drops the parameter of every subscripted generic
description:
GH #14. The error message that reports an outputs=/annotation mismatch prints 'expected: list, found: list' -- it tells the author that list differs from list, which is unactionable.

type_display_name renders the ORIGIN and discards the parameter:

    list[Reading]         -> 'list'
    dict[str, Reading]    -> 'dict'
    tuple[Reading, ...]   -> 'tuple'
    Reading               -> 'Reading'
    list[Reading] | None  -> 'list | None'

The last row matters: neograph-oq2jk fixed this function for UNIONS in 0.7.9, and that fix recurses into members -- so each member is now rendered, and each member still loses its own parameter. The union fix was half a fix in exactly the way the rest of this issue family is about.

Distinct from the identity-comparison bug filed alongside it: fixing the comparison makes the message stop APPEARING for a matching pair, but a genuinely mismatched pair would still print 'list' vs 'list' when the element types are what differ -- which is the case the message exists to explain.
acceptance_criteria: type_display_name renders list[Reading], dict[str, Reading], tuple[Reading, ...] and nested combinations with their parameters. A genuine element-type mismatch produces a message naming both element types. The existing union and NoneType behaviour is unchanged, pinned by the tests neograph-oq2jk added.
notes:
## Fix
type_display_name recurses through get_origin/get_args, so list[dict[str, Reading]] renders in full and tuple[Reading, ...] keeps its Ellipsis as '...'. Reuses the existing union branch for a member like Claims | None.

Verified across 8 shapes including nested and mixed.

## The fixture suite caught the improvement
tests/check_fixtures/should_fail/type_element_to_list.py asserted 'inputs=list'; the message now reads 'inputs=list[Claims]'. Its CHECK_ERROR regex now asserts the ELEMENT type, so a regression back to bare 'list' fails rather than passing on a looser pattern.

title: The 0.7.8 forward-port dropped release documentation from develop
description:
The forward-port merge (34d5418) carried every code change but silently dropped documentation, because conflicts were resolved in favour of develop's side without checking what main's side said. The merge was reported as verified on the strength of '4966 passed, ruff + mypy clean' -- a signal that cannot distinguish 'the docs merged' from 'the docs were discarded', which is the same failure shape as the release gate this project already fixed once.

Measured with 'git diff origin/develop origin/main -- *.md'. Three real losses:

1. CHANGELOG.md -- the ENTIRE [0.7.7] and [0.7.8] sections are absent from develop. Two shipped releases have no changelog on the branch all future work builds from.
2. AGENTS.md -- the lint section lost the 'Two directions' paragraph (the supply-side kinds from GH #10/#11) and the 'lint() requires no config' paragraph (GH #13), and line 336 reverted to the pre-0.7.8 wording 'DI binding checks (original) -- FromInput/FromConfig params vs config dict'. So develop carries the 0.7.8 lint CODE with the pre-0.7.8 lint DOCS.
3. docs/upstream/langgraph-find-subgraph-pregel-runnablebinding.md -- the drafted upstream LangGraph report is missing entirely.

Verified NOT losses (develop legitimately superseded main): README.md counts, docs/design/agent-spec-api/02-flows-nodes.md, docs/design/agent-spec-ratification-2026-07-13.md.
acceptance_criteria: develop's CHANGELOG contains the [0.7.7] and [0.7.8] sections. develop's AGENTS.md lint section matches the shipped behaviour. The upstream draft exists on develop. A repeatable check exists so the next forward-port cannot drop documentation unnoticed.

title: output_field_unconsumed misses framework consumers and reports live fields as dead
description:
Found by scanning lint() across the whole should_pass check-fixture corpus, not by a report. The GH #11 check reports a field as dead when the thing reading it is the FRAMEWORK rather than a downstream node -- including cases where the reader is declared, by name, in the IR the check is already walking.

Measured on the fixture corpus: 18 output_field_unconsumed reports across graphs the fixture suite calls correct. Four distinct blind spots, each conclusive from the fixture source:

1. A modifier argument that names the field. portal_dispatch_route_to_error.py declares Portal(spec_field='spec', input_field='dispatch_input') and both 'spec' and 'dispatch_input' are reported dead. list_consumer_of_each.py declares Each(over='clusters.groups') and 'groups' is reported dead. The consumer is a string in the modifier, one attribute away from the walk.
2. The Portal mesh handoff field. portal_mesh_minimal.py and portal_operator_combo.py report 'goto', which the mesh runtime routes on.
3. Branch-condition and sub-construct boundary reads. branch_output_boundary_every_arm.py reports 'text', read by the branch condition's attr_chain, and 'value', which is the sub-construct's declared output= surfacing to the parent.
4. An Optional-wrapped single-type input. type_optional_consumer.py declares inputs=Claims | None and 'text' is reported dead, so the union is not unwrapped before the whole-model consumption rule applies.

Why this was missed: the GH #11 close comment measured the check against this repo's EXAMPLES and reported zero. The examples contain no Portal mesh, no dispatch Portal, no branch condition and no Optional single-type input, so the measurement could not have found any of these. This is the same shape as GH #6 -- prove one placement, generalise to the rest -- and it was stated to the reporter as evidence.
acceptance_criteria: lint() reports zero output_field_unconsumed across the whole should_pass fixture corpus. Each of the four blind spots has a regression test naming its shape. A new modifier that reads a named field cannot reintroduce the blind spot silently -- the field-reader derivation is single-sited, and a structural guard pins that it is the only site.

title: Reject lint config keys that no caller could supply, instead of honouring them
description:
GH #12 follow-up, reported against the shipped 0.7.8. The 0.7.8 fix shipped check 1 (`from_input_unsatisfiable`, structure-derived and unpaddable) and deferred check 2 on the stated condition that it earn its place on evidence. The reporter supplied the evidence.

Their account: the linter WAS working and correctly reported that `claim_in` and `claims` were FromInput parameters that could not resolve. Someone chasing a green gate added `claims: []` and `claim_in: {}` to the lint config until the message stopped. The graph then compiled, linted clean, and could not execute a single call -- every run died in `_preflight_di_check`. It stayed that way for days behind a green gate, and an offline stub harness found it only because every row came back empty.

Check 1 makes that error detectable. Check 2 makes it unsuppressable. The hatch is still open, measured on 0.7.8:

    correct   {'question': 'q'}                                  -> 0 issues
    padded    {'question': 'q', 'nonexistent_key': 'PAD',
               'claim_in': {}}                                   -> 0 issues
    only-pad  {'nonexistent_key': 'PAD'}                         -> 1 issue

`nonexistent_key` and `claim_in` correspond to nothing in the graph and `lint()` never mentions them. A config key is accepted purely because it is present.

This is the same principle already written into AGENTS.md for GH #13: a graph checker that has to be told what the world looks like turns its own agreement with that description into non-evidence. Honouring an unmatched key is that failure in its most direct form.

Fix: when config= is passed, validate its keys against the bindings the construct actually declares and report a key that matches none of them. A key that matches a binding which `from_input_unsatisfiable` already flags must not count as satisfying it.
acceptance_criteria: lint(construct, config={...'unmatched_key': X}) reports the unmatched key. A padded key cannot reduce the issue count of a defective graph. Mutation-verified: making the check honour an unmatched key fails a test. Regression test uses the reporter's exact shape -- a config padded until the message stops, over a graph that cannot run.

title: Separate the graph input contract from lint issues so a correct graph lints to zero
description:
GH #13 follow-up, reported against the shipped 0.7.8.

The 0.7.8 fix lowered the severity of caller-suppliable DI bindings to `required=False`. The issue asked for something else: SEPARATE 'unsatisfiable by construction' from 'supplied by the caller at run time'. Changing a boolean on both did not separate them.

Measured on 0.7.8, a correct three-parameter graph with no config:

    total=4
      required=False kind=from_input        param=question
      required=False kind=from_input_model  param=deal_id
      required=False kind=from_input_model  param=user_ref
      required=False kind=from_config       param=auth

Nothing is wrong with that graph, and `lint()` returns four `LintIssue` objects describing it. The reporter sees 18 of 20 on their own graph.

The consequence is not cosmetic. It makes an all-output-fails gate impossible to satisfy, so a consumer who wants the strictest gate must weaken the policy to 'fails on required only' -- which is the same trust-the-classification posture that the padded config in GH #12 exploited. The strict gate is the one this defect class punishes, and the linter's own output shape is what forbids it.

Fix: emit the caller-supplied set through a distinct, positively framed channel -- an input contract -- so an empty issue list is achievable by a correct graph. A `graph_input` kind that still rides in the issue list does NOT satisfy this, because the count stays non-zero.

Note also that `LintIssue.node_name` carries a repr ("Node 'start'"), not a name.
design:
## Root Cause
GH #13 asked to separate two unlike things. The 0.7.8 fix changed a boolean on both. _lint_di.py::_check_binding has four emission points; the two no-config branches build a LintIssue with required=False and an 'input contract' message, which keeps the caller-supplied set inside lint()'s return list. A correct graph therefore cannot lint to zero, and the strictest gate policy is unreachable.

## Fix Approach
Move the channel, not the flag.

1. New public 'input_contract(construct) -> list[InputBinding]' answering 'what must a caller supply?'. InputBinding is a positively-framed record (node_name, param, kind, source, type_name), NOT a LintIssue subclass -- a shim that is still an issue defeats the point.
2. _check_binding stops emitting for the two no-config branches. The config-supplied branches are unchanged: they answer the different question 'does THIS payload satisfy the graph', and an unsatisfied key stays an ERROR.
3. 'neograph check' prints the contract as its own section, outside the blocking/advisory lists that decide the exit code.
4. Rewire the existing tests that assert the contract rides in lint()'s list. The assertion 'the information is not lost' is preserved; only the channel it is read from moves.

## Out of scope, file separately
LintIssue.node_name carries a repr ("Node 'start'") rather than a name. Real, but a different defect.
acceptance_criteria: lint(correct_construct) returns an empty list, with no config and with a satisfying config. The caller-suppliable bindings remain discoverable through a separate public surface. Passing config= still reports a payload that fails to satisfy the graph. Regression test asserts the empty list for a correct graph, and asserts the contract is still reported elsewhere.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing tests: tests/test_lint.py::TestCorrectGraphLintsToZero::test_no_issues_without_a_config and ::test_the_input_contract_is_reported_on_its_own_surface
- Two sibling tests in the same class PASS and are guards, not repros: a satisfying config is already clean, and an unsatisfying config already errors. Those must stay true.
- Root cause: _lint_di.py::_check_binding appends a LintIssue for the no-config caller-suppliable case; the 0.7.8 change edited only the 'required' flag and the message text, so both classes of thing still travel in the same list.

## Confirmed red
2 failed, 2 passed. The first failure shows 4 extra LintIssue objects on a correct graph; the second is ImportError on 'input_contract', which does not exist yet.
## Architect review (atom nfuxu.5)

CORE INVARIANT: lint() returns defects. Anything that is not a defect must not travel in that list. Check every edit against it.

Constraints verified before designing, not assumed:
- File-size ratchet: lint.py is pinned at EXACTLY 615 in tests/test_guards_file_size.py, and an entry must equal the real count. New code therefore goes in _lint_di.py (103 lines, limit 500), which already owns 'what a caller must supply, and what no caller can'. Cohesion agrees with the ratchet here.
- LINT_KIND_META severity guard: the four DI kinds are marked 'varies' because they are emitted with kind=binding.kind.value and required=binding.required. The config branch keeps both variables, so 'varies' stays correct and the manifest generator's re-derivation guard keeps holding. No manifest or website churn.
- from_input_unsatisfiable is structure-derived and unaffected: an unsatisfiable binding stays an ERROR with no config.

## Rated risks
- MEDIUM, mitigated -- a second construct traversal for the contract would drift from _walk's. Mitigation: extract iter_di_bindings(item) as the single enumeration both read. A new binding site then reaches both surfaces or neither.
- MEDIUM, accepted -- lint() stops returning output some consumer may read. That IS the ticket. The information moves to a documented public surface; the sole downstream is the reporter who asked for the move; CHANGELOG and docs carry it.
- LOW -- additive public API, wired through __init__.__all__ per the naming policy.

## Rejected alternatives
- A graph_input LintIssue kind: fails the acceptance outright, since the count stays non-zero.
- Returning a LintReport object from lint(): changes the return type for every consumer to solve a problem only the DI kinds have, and reads as the backwards-compat shim shape the project bans at 0.x.
- Reusing di.DI_TEMPLATE_KINDS for the caller-supplied set: the two sets are equal today and for the same underlying reason (the value comes from config['configurable']), but they answer different questions. Coupling them by coincidence means one changing silently moves the other.

title: Convert the seven develop skips to xfail(strict=True) or make them run
description:
The skip allowlist is gone (deleted 2026-08-24), so these seven now fail the gate with no way to silence them. That is the point; this is the work that clears them.

They are not one problem:

TWO are a GATE BLIND SPOT, not missing coverage.
  tests/test_agent_spec_export.py:1664 and :1689 -- 'got empty parameter set for (combo)'.
  FALLTHROUGH_COMBOS is derived as UNSUPPORTED_COMBOS - PORTAL, and it is empty BECAUSE all five fusion combos got real lowerings. The tests exist so a combo silently LEAVING SUPPORTED_COMBOS re-populates the set and fails there. Nothing is unverified -- but pytest reports an empty parametrize as a skip, and the gate cannot tell that from a test that failed to run.
  Fix: assert the set IS empty directly instead of parametrizing over it. Same invariant, zero skips, and the emptiness becomes an assertion rather than an absence.

FIVE are real export gaps where the test is being HONEST.
  to_agent_spec produces artifacts a third-party pyagentspec loader cannot run: qtfof.6 (Loop/Operator branch predicate has no real DataFlowEdge), qtfof.7 (Each fan-out source, same), qtfof.8 (LlmConfig.api_provider=None), qtfof.9 (outermost EndNode's outputs have no DataFlowEdge). The test declines to claim a green it has not earned.
  Fix: xfail(strict=True), not skip. Reported distinctly from a pass, and it turns RED the moment the gap closes -- so the exemption cannot outlive its reason.

Note what is ALREADY right and must not be lost: EXEC_EXEMPT and COMPARE_EXEMPT are COMPUTED at collection time, not hand-typed. Every cell is attempted, the failure is classified, and an UNCLASSIFIED failure is a hard collection error -- nobody can add a line to excuse a test. It self-heals: COMPARE_EXEMPT has already shrunk from every cell to two (scripted-loop-dict, scripted-loop-single) because qtfof.9 landed, and those two are exactly the Loop-wrapped terminals that fix scoped out. Keep the computation; change only how the result is REPORTED.
acceptance_criteria: make skipcheck passes on develop. Every allowlist entry names the ticket that will remove it. The two empty parameter sets are either fixed so the parametrization produces cases, or the tests are removed with a note saying why.
close_reason: Superseded by the Phase 1 portability work. Five of the seven skips ARE the Agent Spec export gaps (qtfof.6/.7/.8) and disappear when those close -- converting them to xfail would be work thrown away. The remaining two are the empty-parametrize gate blind spot, refiled as its own item.

title: Fix the four failing tests on develop before 0.8
description:
`develop` (a08b1cc) runs a red suite, independent of the 0.7.8 forward-port. Observed in the `port/0.7.8-to-develop` worktree, whose only additions are untracked test and script files that none of these tests read.

## Two distinct failures

**1. The API manifest is stale (3 tests).**

    tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py::TestApiManifestFreshness::test_core_manifest_is_in_sync_with_committed_file
    tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py::TestApiManifestFreshness::test_core_manifest_was_generated_with_sort_keys_for_byte_stability
    tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py::TestReferenceSectionRendering::test_generated_reference_region_matches_render_reference_sections

    AssertionError: api-manifest.json drifted from build_manifest().
    Regenerate with: python scripts/gen_api_manifest.py

Someone changed the public API surface without regenerating the manifest and the api.mdx reference region. The guard exists to catch exactly that, and it is catching it.

**2. A check fixture no longer matches its validator message.**

    tests/test_check_fixtures.py::test_should_fail[type_union_output]
    AssertionError: Import raised ConstructError: [Node 'second' in construct 'broken']
    declares inputs=Scores but no upstream produces a compatible value
      found: upstream producers:

The fixture's `# CHECK_ERROR:` regex does not match the error the validator now raises. Either the validator's message changed and the fixture went stale, or the fixture describes a defect the validator now reports differently. Read the fixture before changing either side: the fixture suite exists to test the validator, so a mismatch is a real signal rather than noise.

## Why this blocks 0.8
