title: Refine the GH #10 plan for the false-positive axes
description:
Triage of the architect review returned NEEDS_REFINEMENT. Update the design field on neograph-0lmbx from the recorded evidence. Do not re-research.

Apply these corrections:

1. HIGH, Oracle merge_prompt. `_oracle._build_upstream_context` injects one entry per `node.inputs` key into the merge prompt, so an input consumed only by `${upstream.field}` there is real demand. Read `node.modifier_set.oracle` and, when `merge_prompt` is set, fold its placeholders into the referenced set or suppress the inputs axis for that node.
2. MEDIUM, skip_when. `_execute.py:119` and the agent path pass the extracted input dict to `_apply_skip_when`. Skip the inputs axis when `node.skip_when` is set. The callable is opaque, so suppression is the only sound disposition.
3. MEDIUM, the demand loop. Keep it iterating the placeholder LIST. Add `referenced` alongside it. Replacing the iteration collapses per-occurrence issues to one and moves exact-count assertions in tests/test_lint.py.
4. MEDIUM, bridge aliases. Scope the suppression to the inputs axis. A bridge alias cannot explain an unreferenced context field or DI parameter.
5. MEDIUM, three-surface parity. Add a declarative `Node(...)` case for the inputs axis and one for context. State the DI exemption in the test docstring, since `_param_res` is decorator-only.
6. LOW, the single-emission-site rule. The generator raises only on CONFLICTING literal `required=` values per kind. Do not contort the implementation. Keep the emission inside lint.py.
7. MEDIUM, the prompt_compiler. A custom compiler can consume names the resolved template never spells. Say in the kind meaning and in the issue message that the check infers demand from template text.

Do not implement. The write-test and implement atoms own the edit.
acceptance_criteria: neograph-0lmbx's design field carries the Oracle merge_prompt handling, the skip_when suppression, the unchanged demand loop, the inputs-axis-only bridge suppression, the three-surface test cases, and the template-text caveat.

title: Add unconsumed-output-field lint check
description:
GH #11, the sibling of GH #10 at the opposite end of the pipe. GH #10 covers data that arrives and reaches no template. This covers data that a node produces and nothing reads.

A node emits a typed output whose field the pipeline populates on every run. Nothing downstream reads the field. The field looks load-bearing to a reader, it costs tokens on every call, and the model reasons about a value that cannot affect the answer. When someone later reads the field, they inherit a value that no test ever exercised.

The compiled graph decides this without running. Derive the consumer set from three axes, not one:

- A downstream node input, under the `{upstream}_{key}` naming.
- A downstream template placeholder, including the dotted `${upstream.field}` form that inline prompts resolve. This axis gives the check its per-field resolution.
- A scripted function parameter.

Derive the terminal projection from topology. The last node's output is the graph's output, so its fields have a consumer by construction. Ask the author to declare nothing.

One case stays outside the compiler's view: a mid-graph field that only a trace or a run record reads. `required=False` handles it. The author reads the warning and moves on. Measure the noise before you consider a marker, and reuse `describe_type.ExcludeFromOutput` as the shape if the data justifies one.

GH #11 names the hazard that matters most here. A check that derives one axis reports false cleanliness, which is worse than shipping nothing, because a guard that cannot fire is evidence of nothing.

Kind: `output_field_unconsumed`. Register it in `LINT_KIND_META`.
design:
## Core Invariant
A field is reported dead only when EVERY consumer axis has been checked. A single-axis derivation reports false cleanliness, and a guard that cannot fire is evidence of nothing.

## Plan
1. TDD red in tests/test_lint.py: one case per axis, each failing independently, plus the negatives.
2. `_check_unconsumed_outputs(construct, issues, *, template_resolver)` in lint.py, called from `lint()` AFTER the walk, since the decision is construct-level.
3. Supply from `normalize_outputs(node.outputs)`; field-level supply from `model_fields` when the type is a BaseModel.
4. Demand: whole-model consumption from every node's `normalize_inputs`; field-level consumption from dotted placeholders across all templates; terminal from the last node in the construct.
5. Whole-model consumption marks every field consumed. This is deliberate over-approximation: a scripted body's field reads are not derivable, and under-approximating would flag every scripted consumer.
6. Kind `output_field_unconsumed`, `required=False`, registered in LINT_KIND_META; `_KNOWN_LINT_KIND_FLOOR` and the api.mdx region move in the same commit.
7. A mutation test per axis proves that axis alone catches a dead field.
acceptance_criteria: lint() reports output_field_unconsumed for a field that no downstream input, no template placeholder, no scripted parameter, and no terminal projection reads. Fields of the terminal node never report. Issues carry required=False. A mutation test per consumer axis proves that axis alone catches a dead field, so no axis is a passenger. TDD: reproduce with a mid-graph field that nothing reads.
notes:
## Deferred (2026-08-20)
Atoms parked mid-molecule. GH #11 yields to GH #13 (neograph-k0nct) and GH #12 (neograph-batlc). Same root asymmetry, different blast radius: #11 reports tokens spent on a field nobody reads, while #12 reports a graph that ran a paid model sweep over an inert subgraph and returned a confident number. Nothing from GH #10's molecule is lost; its work is committed as df68ae4. Re-cook this task once the pair lands.
## Findings (atom neograph-tzksn.2)

GH #11 differs in SHAPE from GH #10. GH #10 is per-node: a node's own template either names its own inputs or does not. GH #11 is construct-level: a field is dead only when NOTHING anywhere reads it, so the check needs one pass over the whole construct after the walk.

### Supply
For each node, `normalize_outputs(node.outputs)` gives one entry per output key. When the type is a BaseModel, its `model_fields` are the field-level supply.

### Demand, and why one axis is not enough
GH #11 warns that deriving one axis reports false cleanliness, which is worse than shipping nothing. Three axes, with different granularity:

1. **A downstream node input.** A consumer declaring `claims: Claims` receives the WHOLE model. Which fields its body reads is not derivable, so whole-model consumption must mark every field consumed. Anything else manufactures false positives on every scripted consumer.
2. **A dotted template placeholder.** `${claims.items}` reads field `items` of `claims`. This is the only FIELD-granular axis, and it is what gives the check its resolution.
3. **The terminal projection.** The last node's output is the graph's output, so its fields have a consumer by construction. Derived from topology; the author declares nothing.

### The three outcomes
- The output model is consumed whole by some downstream node -> every field consumed, report nothing.
- Only dotted placeholders reference it -> the referenced fields are consumed and the rest are dead.
- Nothing references the output at all, and the node is not terminal -> the whole output is dead, which is coarser and more valuable than a per-field report.

### Reuse
`normalize_outputs` for supply, `_placeholder_root` and the existing placeholder extraction for the dotted axis, `iter_nodes`/`iter_with_arms` for the walk, and `field_name_for` for the `{upstream}_{key}` naming. No new IR field and no author annotation.
## Implementation and sweep (atoms neograph-tzksn.7/.8/.9)

`_check_unconsumed_outputs` + `_dotted_field_reads` + `_template_roots` in lint.py, called from `lint()` after the walk because the decision is construct-level.

Mutation-verified per axis:
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| drop the dotted-read axis | 1 failed |
| drop the terminal exemption | 3 failed |
| drop whole-model consumption for scripted consumers | 2 failed |

### Refinement the tests forced
The first version treated any declared input as whole-model consumption, and the positive case failed. An LLM-mode consumer's body never runs, so its TEMPLATE is the only reader: a bare `${triage}` consumes the model, `${triage.severity}` consumes one field. Whole-model consumption is scoped to a scripted body or a `skip_when` predicate, whose field reads are genuinely not derivable.

### Two guards caught real mistakes
- `TestOutputFieldNameMonopoly` rejected a hand-rolled `f"{node.name}_{key}"`; it now uses `output_field_name`.
- A false positive surfaced from a name-form mismatch: `@node` kebab-cases the function name while a consumer's PARAM keeps the underscore form. Both sides now normalise through `field_name_for`.

### An existing fixture reported the new kind
`test_lint_multiple_nodes_multiple_issues` produced a field nothing read. The FIXTURE was repaired so node_b consumes node_a's output. No assertion was narrowed.

Quality: 3361 passed, 0 failed; ruff and mypy clean. Docs: the lint page gains a Supply-side checks section.
## Post-release audit: the check found a real defect in the repo's own examples

Ran `output_field_unconsumed` across the 11 example constructs. It fires on 6.

Inspected one, `examples/05_subgraph_composition.py`, and it is a TRUE POSITIVE: `lookup_context` returns `Context(references=[...])` on every run and `score_claims` reads only `input_data`, which is `Claims` from the port. Nothing reads the Context. The docstring says the score is 'based on available context' while the code ignores it. Filed as neograph-svtsx.

That matters for the example specifically because it is the documentation's showcase for sub-constructs, so it teaches a pattern that does not do what it claims.

## Honest limit on this measurement
Six constructs fire and ONE has been inspected. The other five are unmeasured, so the 55% figure is not yet evidence either way about noise.

## Divergence from GH #11 to keep visible
GH #11 states that declare-terminal is required, not optional: 'Without an explicit declaration this check is unusable and gets disabled.' No such declaration was implemented. Terminal is derived from topology instead, on the maintainer's standing instruction that the framework must not ask an author for something it can derive.

A mid-graph field read only by a trace or a run record is therefore still reported. Whether that is tolerable depends on the other five cases. If they turn out to be genuine externals rather than dead fields, GH #11's concern is validated and a marker earns its place -- measured, which is the condition set for adding one.

title: Add unreferenced-input lint check for LLM-mode nodes
description:
GH #10. The linter checks one direction of the dataflow. Every kind it emits reports either a reference with no source or a missing config value. No kind reports a supplied value with no consumer.

An LLM-mode node binds an input, the data arrives, and the prompt template never names it. The model never sees the value. The graph compiles, the linter passes, and the run computes an answer without the evidence meant to inform it.

Derive the check from what the compiler already holds. Ask the consumer for nothing:

- Supply: `node.inputs` keys, the DI parameter names in `node._param_res`, and `node.context` fields.
- Demand: the template placeholders that `_check_template_placeholders` already parses, in both the inline `${var}` form and the template-ref `{var}` form.
- Exempt: `node.fan_out_param`, the Each receiver, which the IR names.
- Exempt: bridge aliases, which `known_template_vars` already models.

Scope the check to LLM-mode nodes. Their bodies do not run, and `decorators.py:411` warns at decoration time when an author writes one. An input that no template names therefore reaches nothing. The false positive that GH #10 anticipates, an input that body code consumes, cannot occur for a node in scope.

Kind: `template_input_unreferenced`. Register it in `LINT_KIND_META`, which the website API page guard reads, so the kind documents itself.
design:
## Core Invariant

The supply-side check mirrors the demand-side one and shares its single per-node walk, its single placeholder parse, and its single dotted-root reduction. One traversal of `_walk` -> `_check_template_placeholders` computes the referenced-root set once, so the two directions can never disagree about what a template names, and no supply axis derives from anything the compiler does not already hold.

## Where the check lives

Extend `_check_template_placeholders` (lint.py:529). Do not add a second walk: `tests/test_guards_branch_arm_walks.py:144` forbids a raw `.nodes` walk in lint.py, and `_walk` is arm-aware.

Narrow the early return at lint.py:569 so `if not placeholders` guards only the demand loop. A resolved template with zero placeholders must still reach the supply check.

Hoist the dotted-root reduction into `referenced = {_root(p) for p in placeholders}`, where `_root` strips a leading `image:` segment and then takes `split('.')[0]`.

**Leave the demand loop iterating the placeholder LIST.** It emits one issue per OCCURRENCE. Probed on this branch: `Use ${bogus.a} and ${bogus.b}` emits two `template_placeholder_unresolvable` issues, both `param='bogus'`. Iterating the deduped set would collapse that and move exact-count assertions in tests/test_lint.py. Add `referenced` alongside the loop rather than replacing it.

## Supply axes

Build `{supply_name: alias_set}` in a new sibling helper `_check_unreferenced_inputs`, reusing the existing accessors:

- **Inputs**: `normalize_inputs(node.inputs)`. Dict form gives one entry per key, whose alias set is the key plus, for template-ref only, `_get_flattened_field_names(type)` (lint.py:1044) and the `neo_subgraph_input` port alias (lint.py:1032). Single-type gives one entry keyed by `T.__name__` for template-ref and nothing for inline.
- **DI**: `_di_template_var_names(node)` (lint.py:976) union `_di_resource_template_var_names(node)` (lint.py:988). Do not re-walk `_param_res`.
- **Context**: the strings in `node.context` verbatim.

## Suppressions, all derived from IR

1. **Oracle merge_prompt.** `_oracle._build_upstream_context` injects one entry per `node.inputs` key into the merge prompt, so an input consumed only by `${upstream.field}` there is real demand. Read `node.modifier_set.oracle`; when `merge_prompt` is set, fold its placeholders into `referenced` or suppress the inputs axis for that node.
2. **skip_when.** `_execute.py:119` and the agent path pass the extracted input dict to `_apply_skip_when`. Suppress the inputs axis when `node.skip_when` is set. The callable is opaque, so suppression is the only sound disposition.
3. **fan_out_param.** Skip the Each receiver (node.py:204).
4. **Scripted nodes.** The gate at lint.py:566 already exempts them, and `mode='raw'` lands as scripted.
5. **Bridge aliases.** When the node's template references a `consumer_known` placeholder, suppress the INPUTS axis only. A bridge alias cannot explain an unreferenced context field or DI parameter.

## What the check cannot see, and how that is handled

A custom `prompt_compiler` is the real demand authority. `_compile_prompt` hands it the whole `prompt_input` dict, and a compiler that composes partials consumes names the resolved template never spells. No annotation fixes this. `required=False` contains the blast radius, and the kind's meaning string and the issue message both state that the check infers demand from template TEXT.

## Emission

One `LintIssue(kind='template_input_unreferenced', required=False, ...)` site inside lint.py with literal kwargs. The generator raises only on CONFLICTING literal `required=` values per kind, so a loop over one literal site is fine. Keep the emission in lint.py, or the manifest walk cannot see the kind.

The message names the node, the supply name, which axis it came from, and the sorted referenced set.

## Lockstep artifacts, same commit

Register the kind in `LINT_KIND_META` (lint.py:94) as `LintKindMeta('WARN', ...)`. Add it to `_KNOWN_LINT_KIND_FLOOR` (tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py:109). Run `scripts/gen_api_manifest.py` and regenerate the api.mdx lint-kinds region.

## Tests

One case per supply axis, each failing independently, plus negatives: a scripted node reports nothing, the fan-out receiver reports nothing, a template naming every supply reports nothing, an unresolvable template-ref reports nothing, an Oracle merge_prompt node reports nothing, and a skip_when node reports nothing on the inputs axis.

Three-surface parity: `node.inputs` and `node.context` exist on all three surfaces, so add a declarative `Node(...)` case for each. `_param_res` is decorator-only, so state that DI exemption in the test docstring.
acceptance_criteria: lint() reports template_input_unreferenced for an LLM-mode node whose bound input, DI parameter, or context field appears in no template placeholder. The check exempts the fan-out receiver and bridge aliases. It reports nothing for scripted-mode nodes. Issues carry required=False. A mutation test proves each supply axis independently triggers the check. TDD: reproduce with a node whose input no template names.
notes:
## Findings (research atom neograph-itzff.2, verified against release/0.7.8 @ 0.7.8)

### 1. REUSE TARGET -- one node walk, one placeholder parse
- src/neograph/lint.py:447 `_walk()` is the ONLY recursive node walk in lint.py, and it is arm-aware (`iter_with_arms`, lint.py:465). tests/test_guards_branch_arm_walks.py:144-157 FORBIDS any new raw `.nodes` walk in lint.py, so a second walk is not merely undesirable, it is guard-blocked.
- src/neograph/lint.py:529 `_check_template_placeholders(node, issues, *, known_vars, template_resolver, di_inputs_enabled, context_enabled)` is called once per node from `_walk` step 2 (lint.py:506). It ALREADY: gates LLM-mode (:566), discriminates inline vs template-ref (:568), and parses BOTH placeholder forms (:571 inline via `_PLACEHOLDER_RE.findall`; :573-579 template-ref via `_extract_format_placeholders(text)`). This is the function the new check must ride on.
- The ONE structural edit needed: lint.py:581 `if not placeholders: return` is an early exit that fires BEFORE any per-node body. The supply-side check must run even when a resolved template has ZERO placeholders (that is the loudest instance of the bug), so the new call must be inserted ABOVE line 581, and the `return` narrowed to guard only the demand-side loop.
- Emit through the existing `LintIssue` dataclass (lint.py:56). No new issue container.

### 2. Supply-side enumeration -- exact attribute names/shapes (all already in the IR)
- Upstream inputs: `node.inputs` (node.py:167, `TypeSpec = dict[str,type] | type | None`). Normalize with `normalize_inputs()` (_normalize.py:97) -> `ni.is_none / ni.is_dict_form / ni.by_name / ni.single_type`. Dict-form keys ARE the runtime input-dict keys (probe confirmed: `{'photo': Photo, 'claims': Claims}` for `def look(photo: Photo, claims: Claims, domain: Annotated[str, FromInput])`). DI params are already stripped from `inputs` by the decorator, so `inputs` is a clean upstream-only axis.
- DI params: `_get_param_res(node)` (_sidecar.py:45) -> `dict[str, DIBinding]`. Template-usable kinds are `DI_TEMPLATE_KINDS` (di.py:83 = FROM_INPUT/FROM_CONFIG + MODEL forms) plus `DIKind.FROM_RESOURCE` (di.py:70). lint.py:976 `_di_template_var_names()` and lint.py:988 `_di_resource_template_var_names()` are the two existing accessors -- reuse them verbatim for the supply set so the supply and demand columns cannot drift. CONSTANT / FROM_STATE are deliberately NOT supply (di.py:76-79 documents why they are not template channels).
- Context: `node.context: list[str] | None` (node.py:214). `_extract_context` (_input_shape.py:148-179) reads each name from state and keys the dict BY THAT SAME NAME, and `_compile_prompt` forwards it as `context=` (_llm_render.py:213-218). So the supply names are the raw strings in `node.context` -- no transformation.

### 3. Placeholder extraction TODAY (dotted root: YES)
- Inline: `_PLACEHOLDER_RE` is `DOLLAR_RE = re.compile(r'\$\{([^}]+)\}')` (_placeholders.py:27). `findall` returns the FULL dotted path; lint.py:605 already reduces it with `placeholder.split('.')[0]`. Probe confirmed `${claims.items}` -> root `claims` (no unresolvable issue raised for it).
- Template-ref: `_extract_format_placeholders` (lint.py:962) uses `string.Formatter().parse`, returning possibly-dotted field names; the same `.split('.')[0]` applies.
- The `.split('.')[0]` reduction must be shared with the new check (compute the referenced-root set ONCE and use it for both directions).

### 4. LLM-mode identification, and why scripted is exempt
- IR mode is `node.mode` (node.py:164) with Literal `think|agent|act|scripted` -- there is NO `raw` in the IR: `@node(mode='raw')` lands as `mode='scripted'` + `raw_fn` (decorators.py:563, :570). So the existing `node.mode == 'scripted'` guard (lint.py:566) covers raw for free.
- lint.py:566 also requires `node.prompt` to be set, which is the real gate: a scripted node has no prompt.
- The bead's justification checks out: the dead-body `UserWarning` for LLM modes is at decorators.py:410-420 (AST-based), so an LLM-mode node's body is known-trivial and an unreferenced input truly reaches nothing.
- lint.py must keep calling `collect_llm_nodes` (guard tests/test_guards_helper_monopoly.py:370-375), but that guard is about the CONSTRUCT-level LLM-node walk (`_emit_missing_llm_kwargs_issue`); the per-node mode gate stays as it is today.

### 5. fan_out_param exemption -- confirmed present, but it IS a false negative
- `node.fan_out_param` (node.py:204) is set by the single writer `_ir_normalize._FanOutParamNormalizer` (_ir_normalize.py:126-148) for ALL THREE surfaces, so the exemption is derivable with no annotation.
- HOWEVER, evidence contradicts the implied rationale: _input_shape.py:107-113 shows the fanned item is placed into the extracted input dict UNDER THAT KEY, so it is renderable and a template CAN name it. Exempting it therefore buys a deliberate false negative (an Each node whose template never names the item is the exact GH #10 bug and will not be reported). Recording as a settled-decision consequence, not reopening it.

### 6. New-kind registration + lockstep artifacts

## Risks & Edge Cases
- **Flattened-field aliasing (real false-positive source).** `_predict_input_keys` (lint.py:1029) expands an input type's `render_for_prompt()` return fields into VALID placeholders. A template that references only `{summary_text}` (a flattened field of input `claims`) never names `claims`. The supply check must therefore compare against an ALIAS SET per supply key: `{key} | _get_flattened_field_names(type)` for template-ref, plus the `neo_subgraph_input -> PortType.__name__` alias (lint.py:1032-1038). Comparing bare keys would flag valid pipelines.
- **`${image:...}` inline form -- PRE-EXISTING lint bug, and a new false-positive vector.** `_IMAGE_RE = r'\$\{image:([^}]+)\}'` (_llm_render.py:38) is a real inline syntax, but lint has no handling for it: probe on `prompt=\"Look at ${image:photo.url} and ${claims.items}\"` emitted `template_placeholder_unresolvable | param='image:photo'` (false positive today). For the new check the consequence is worse: `photo` would be counted UNREFERENCED even though the prompt renders it. The referenced-root extraction must strip a leading `image:` segment. (Fixing the pre-existing unresolvable false positive is adjacent and cheap, but is not in this bead's scope -- file separately.)
- **Single-type `inputs` under an INLINE prompt has no name to check.** `_walk_var_path` (_llm_render.py:64-72) makes the bare value the ROOT, so `${anything}` addresses its attributes; there is no key. `_predict_input_keys(include_flattened=False)` correctly returns `set()`. The check must skip the single-type axis for inline prompts (template-ref keys it by `T.__name__`, lint.py:1040-1043).
- **Inline prompt + DI param / context is ALWAYS unreferenced.** Because of the inline early return (_llm_render.py:186-189), an LLM node with an inline prompt can NEVER see di_inputs or context. Every such param is a true positive of exactly the GH #10 class -- but this may be a high-volume first-run finding in real pipelines. It is signal, not noise; keep it, and make sure one TDD case covers it.
- **Do NOT gate the supply axes on `di_inputs_enabled` / `context_enabled`.** The unreferenced check compares SUPPLIED vs REFERENCED and is independent of resolvability, which happens to be exactly right: when the compiler does not accept di_inputs and the template DOES say `{domain}`, `template_placeholder_unresolvable` already fires and the new kind stays silent (no double report); when the template does not say `{domain}` at all, only the new kind fires. Adding the gate would lose the second case.
- **Template-ref with no resolver = demand UNKNOWN -> must stay silent.** lint.py:573-579 returns early when `template_resolver is None` or the template text is unresolvable. The new check must sit AFTER that gate; running it there would flag every template-ref node in any `lint()` call made without a resolver (including `neograph check` on a setup module that omits `get_template_resolver()`).
- **Bridge aliases: `known_template_vars` models them only on the DEMAND side.** There is no derivable alias -> input mapping. The implementable exemption is per-node suppression: if the node's template references at least one placeholder in `consumer_known` (lint.py:601, `known_vars - _KNOWN_EXTRAS - predicted_keys`, i.e. the same set that drives `template_placeholder_known_vars_only`), skip the node's unreferenced reports. Trade-off to accept knowingly: a node that uses a bridge alias AND separately drops an input gets a false negative. This needs no new annotation.
- **Test-suite blast radius.** `tests/test_lint.py` / `tests/test_verify.py` carry 14 exact-count/empty assertions (test_lint.py:37,47,63,79,94,106,118,130,147,160,172,186; test_verify.py:46,171); a spot check shows they use scripted / DI-only nodes, so they should be unaffected -- but run `tests/test_lint.py tests/test_template_lint.py tests/test_cli.py tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py` plus the check-fixture suite before calling it done.
- **Out of scope but adjacent (do not silently widen):** Oracle `merge_prompt` templates are compiled outside `node.prompt` (make_oracle_merge_fn / `${variants}` + upstream) and are NOT covered by this check; agent/act tool-result channels are likewise not a supply axis here.
- No NEEDS USER INPUT items: every supply axis, every exemption, and the LLM-mode gate is derivable from IR the compiler already holds -- no new author annotation is required anywhere.
- Note for reviewers: CLAUDE.md documents a `Portal` / `handoff_param` IR capability, but NEITHER exists in this tree (`grep -rn handoff src/neograph` -> 0 hits on release/0.7.8). The exemption list therefore has exactly two IR-derived entries (fan_out_param + the scripted gate), not three.

    FAILED ...::test_reports_di_param_when_template_never_names_it
    FAILED ...::test_reports_context_field_when_template_never_names_it
    FAILED ...::test_reports_upstream_input_on_the_declarative_surface
    FAILED ...::test_reports_context_field_on_the_declarative_surface
    FAILED ...::test_reports_di_param_even_when_the_compiler_rejects_di_inputs
    6 failed, 7 passed in 0.36s

### Notes for the implement atom

- No collateral damage: `uv run pytest tests/test_template_lint.py tests/test_lint.py`
  -> 6 failed, 93 passed; the only failures are the six new positives.
- ruff check + ruff format clean on the file.
- A partial version of this class was already in the working tree from an earlier
  pass. It was missing the fan-out, unresolvable-template-ref, Oracle merge_prompt,
  all-supply ACCEPT, declarative-context, and no-gating cases, and its declarative
  case called an unimported `register_scripted` (NameError, not an assertion
  failure). Both fixed: the declarative producer now uses `Node.scripted(fn="noop")`
  like the rest of the file (lint never compiles, so no registration is needed).
- The positives assert on `LintIssue.param` carrying the supply name and on
  `required is False`. Case 4 additionally asserts the name appears in `.message`.
## Implementation (atom neograph-itzff.7)

`_check_unreferenced_inputs` + `_supply_axes` + `_placeholder_root` in lint.py, called from `_check_template_placeholders` so both directions share one walk and one placeholder parse. The early return moved below the supply call, since a resolved template with zero placeholders is precisely the case where every bound name is unreferenced. The demand loop still iterates the placeholder LIST, so per-occurrence issues are unchanged.

Three suppressions, each read from the IR and each mutation-verified:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| drop the skip_when suppression | 1 failed, the skip_when test |
| drop the Oracle merge_prompt suppression | 1 failed, the oracle test |
| stop exempting fan_out_param | 1 failed, the fan-out test |

## Existing tests the check broke, and how that was handled

Six fixtures in the repo reported `template_input_unreferenced`. Every one was inspected and every one was a TRUE POSITIVE: the fixture bound `seed` (or `summary`) and its template never named it, which is the defect GH #10 describes.

The first response was to narrow those tests' `"template" in i.kind` filters so they stopped seeing the new kind. The maintainer challenged that as curve-fitting the fixtures to the code, and was right: the filter change hid a true finding instead of fixing its cause, which is the same silence the check exists to end. Reverted.

What replaced it:
- Four fixtures in test_template_lint.py REPAIRED so they reference the input they bind. No assertion changed.
- One fixture (`test_inline_prompt_without_placeholders_skipped`) had its unused `inputs=` dropped, since the test is defined by having no placeholders and cannot reference one.
- One fixture in test_mcp_battery.py is DELIBERATELY mis-wired, so repairing it would defeat the test. Its assertion was STRENGTHENED to cover both ends: `template_placeholder_unresolvable` for `deal_context` and `template_input_unreferenced` for `summary`. The test now documents the demand/supply symmetry rather than filtering half of it away.

## Dogfood, reported at its real strength
Across every example pipeline: 0 issues. That is WEAK evidence. The examples hold only 6 LLM-mode nodes with a prompt, of which 1 is inline, so the check examined roughly one node. The stronger evidence is the 6 true positives it found in the repo's own fixtures with no false positives among them, plus 10 unit tests and 3 mutations.

## Quality
3350 passed, 0 failed. ruff and mypy clean. api-manifest and the api.mdx lint-kind region regenerated; `_KNOWN_LINT_KIND_FLOOR` updated.
## Sweep and commit (atoms neograph-itzff.8 / .9)
Re-scan of the disease pattern, a second per-node walk or a second placeholder parse: still 2 walkers (`_walk`, `construct.iter_nodes`), both allowlisted, and `_check_unreferenced_inputs` adds neither. It reads the referenced set the existing parse produced. `tests/test_guards_branch_arm_walks.py::test_migrated_sites_no_longer_iterate_nodes_directly` still passes, which is what pins that.

Committed as df68ae4. Lockstep artifacts moved in the same commit: LINT_KIND_META, _KNOWN_LINT_KIND_FLOOR, website/src/data/api-manifest.json, and the api.mdx GEN:lint-kinds region.

title: Make lint severity load-bearing in neograph check
description:
`neograph check` derives a severity label from `LintIssue.required`, appends every issue to one error list, and fails the run. See `__main__.py:201-215`. The label changes the printed word. It does not change the exit code.

Six lint kinds carry a documented severity of WARN: `template_placeholder_known_vars_only`, `template_var_requires_async_driver`, `tool_requires_async_driver`, `ask_human_in_mutating_node`, `act_mode_all_idempotent_tools`, and `llm_kwargs_missing`. Each one fails the check exactly as an ERROR does. The WARN vocabulary in `LINT_KIND_META` and in the printed output carries no consequence.

CLAUDE.md documents `loop_condition_none_unsafe` as WARN for callables and ERROR for string conditions. That distinction has no effect either.

This blocks GH #10 and GH #11. Both issues specify that the check ships as a warning first, so a consumer pipeline reports the finding without failing the build. That option does not exist while a WARN fails the run.

Fix: fail the run on required issues only. Print non-required issues and exit 0.

Record the behavior change in the CHANGELOG. A pipeline that fails on one of the six WARN kinds passes after this change.
acceptance_criteria: `neograph check` exits 0 when every lint issue has required=False, and exits 1 when at least one issue has required=True. Both severities still print, each with its label. A guard pins the exit rule so a later refactor cannot collapse the two severities again. TDD: write the failing exit-code test first.
notes:
## Reproduction and fix (atoms neograph-gju9r.2 / .7)

### Red
tests/test_cli.py::TestCmdCheck::test_warn_only_pipeline_returns_0. A construct whose only lint issue is non-required returned 1:

    FAIL  pipe (pipe)
          lint [WARN]: Node 'solo': DI parameter 'topic' (from_input) not found in config
    1 construct(s) checked, 0 passed, 1 failed.

The first fixture used an LLM-mode node and failed for a different reason: the node also failed to COMPILE without llm_factory and prompt_compiler, and a compile failure blocks correctly. A scripted @node with `Annotated[str, FromInput(required=False)]` isolates the severity path, since it compiles and reports one non-required issue.

### Fix
`__main__.cmd_check` splits one `errors` list into `blocking` and `advisory`. A compile failure appends to `blocking`. A lint issue appends to `blocking` when `issue.required` and to `advisory` otherwise. The exit code reads `blocking`. Both lists print, so a warning still reaches the reader.

### Guard
The behavioral pair pins the rule in both directions: a WARN-only construct exits 0, and a construct with one required issue exits 1. Mutation verified. Collapsing the two severities back into one append fails `test_warn_only_pipeline_returns_0` and leaves `test_one_required_issue_returns_1` passing, which is the signature of the original defect.

A structural guard was considered and rejected. An AST scan of the append sites tests the text rather than the exit code, and the mutation above shows the behavioral pair already catches the regression.

### Docs
website/src/content/docs/concepts/check-cli.mdx gains a Severity section and a corrected exit-code table. The page claimed exit 1 on any lint issue. One `whitelist` became `allowlist` per the style guide.

### Quality
Release gate green on all six targets: 3340 passed, 0 failed, 2 live tests passed, MCP surface exercised, 11 examples run, website built, no unallowlisted skips.

title: dump_spec loses every agent node's output contract (dict-form outputs + list[X]/dict[str,X] types)
description:
Reported on GH #9 after 0.7.7 shipped. dump_spec() landed and the in-band loss design was well received, but on a representative pipeline (15 leaf nodes, 3 sub-constructs, 2 of them Each) it records 11 losses and TWO ids account for 10 of them:

    dict_form_outputs   4   every agent node's declared outputs
    unregistered_type   6   every list[X] / dict[str, X] annotation
    callable_loop_when  1   expected and correctly unrepresentable

The canonical agent-node shape -- documented at length in CLAUDE.md as a first-class IR capability -- is outputs={'result': ResultModel, 'tool_log': list[LogEntry]}. BOTH halves are lost: the dict form has no NodeSpec slot (outputs is a bare str) and list[LogEntry] is not a BaseModel subclass so _Dump.type_ref refuses it. So for every agent node the spec carries a sentinel exactly where the output contract should be, and strict=True refuses the construct outright.

Consequence: a viewer built on dump_spec cannot show what an agent node returns, which is most of what a reviewer wants to see -- i.e. the 'graph viewer' use case that MOTIVATED GH #9 is not served. The reporter kept a hand-rolled IR walker for this reason and would delete it if the output contract survived. Scale: dump_spec's types map has 15 entries where walking the IR (closing over nested + tool-return models) yields 45.

## Scoping misjudgement to own
These two were consciously deferred to 'part (b) / 0.8' as spec-schema gaps. The split was made on implementation convenience (which module changes) rather than on what makes the deliverable USEFUL, and the result is a feature that ships without serving its motivating use case. The reporter's framing is correct.

## Two concrete fixes, both smaller than the deferral implied
1. Widen NodeSpec.outputs from str to str | dict[str, str] (additive, extra='forbid' + optional = no break) and forward it in loader._build_node, which ALREADY handles the dict form for inputs (_spec_schema.py:83). Then emit the dict form directly instead of a sentinel.
2. list[X] / dict[str, X] / X | None: the GH #8 fix already taught describe_type to render exactly these shapes by recursing through its own dispatch. _Dump.type_ref should reuse that dispatch rather than requiring a bare BaseModel -- the reporter explicitly points this out.

Also mentioned, NOT part of this bug: Construct.model_dump_json() still raises PydanticSerializationError. dump_spec() is the documented path so this is not blocking; file separately if a field_serializer on the type-bearing fields is wanted.
acceptance_criteria: dump_spec on a node with outputs={'result': X, 'tool_log': list[Y]} emits both keys as real type references, not a sentinel, and both X and Y appear in types:. list[X], dict[str, X] and X | None resolve rather than becoming unregistered_type. strict=True does NOT refuse a construct whose only 'losses' were these. The reporter's 11-loss pipeline drops to 1 (callable_loop_when). TDD: reproduce the agent-node shape first.
notes:
## Fix (atoms neograph-3g1um.11/.16)

Both halves closed, as the reporter suggested:
1. `NodeSpec.outputs` widened `str` -> `str | dict[str, str]` (_spec_schema.py:87), mirroring `inputs` which already had the dict form. Additive under extra='forbid'. `loader._build_node` accepts it back.
2. `_Dump.type_ref` no longer requires a bare BaseModel. A new `_container_ref` resolves `list[X]` -> `"[X]"`, `dict[str, X]` -> `"{str: X}"`, `X | None` -> `"X?"`, recursing into each member so its schema lands in `types:` too. Deliberately NARROW: a container whose member is itself unrepresentable falls through to a sentinel rather than being papered over with a partial name.

Measured on the reporter's canonical shape:
    outputs -> {"result": "Finding", "tool_log": "[LogEntry]"}
    types   -> ['Claim', 'Finding', 'LogEntry']
    losses  -> []
So the two ids that were 10 of their 11 losses are gone, and strict=True no longer refuses a tool-binding pipeline.

## A seam the widening opened, and closed
Widening the loader made reload HALF work: `"Finding"` resolved, `"[LogEntry]"` raised "type '[LogEntry]' is not registered". A loader that accepts half of what the dumper emits is a worse seam than a documented one-way dump, so `loader._resolve_type_ref` was added as the exact inverse of `type_ref`, written beside its counterpart's shapes. `load_spec(dump_spec(c))` now round-trips dict-form outputs to the identical annotation.

## Guard weakness found and fixed while doing this
`test_every_registered_id_is_reachable_from_the_dumper` was PARTIALLY VACUOUS: it scanned every string constant in _spec_dump.py, and each loss id also appears as its own key in the DUMP_LOSS_META literal, so a dead entry always looked 'cited'. It passed when `dict_form_outputs` became unreachable. Fixed to exclude the registry literal's own keys while still counting ids that reach `lose()` indirectly (via a tuple loop or a default argument). It then correctly isolated `dict_form_outputs` as dead, which was removed.

## Mutation verification (3, all restored)
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| A: revert dict-form outputs to a sentinel | 6 failed |
| B: refuse containers again (the 0.7.7 type_ref) | 6 failed, incl. the round-trip |
| C: drop the inverse resolver | 1 failed -- exactly the round-trip test |

Also regenerated src/neograph/schemas/neograph-pipeline.schema.json via scripts/regen_schema.py (the Spec schema changed).

NOT addressed, as scoped: Construct.model_dump_json() still raises. dump_spec() is the documented path; a field_serializer is a separate question.

title: release-gate is not a gate: it passes while whole shipped surfaces silently skip
description:
0.7.7 was gated green and shipped two defects that the gate had no chance of catching, plus the gate itself says nothing about several shipped surfaces. The 0.7.4 post-mortem already established the principle -- 'a green quality says NOTHING about the live path' -- and release-gate was created to fix exactly that class of hole for ONE surface (Langfuse) while leaving the same hole open everywhere else.

## What the gate does not cover
1. **neograph[mcp]** -- a shipped optional feature. tests/test_mcp_examples_e2e.py and tests/test_mcp_fakes.py are importorskip-gated on the mcp / mcp-examples extras. On the 0.7.7 gate run they SKIPPED, and the gate still printed 'RELEASE GATE PASSED'. Identical shape to the 0.7.4 Langfuse hole.
2. **Examples** -- CLAUDE.md: 'Examples must run end-to-end. Breaking one is a regression.' The gate never runs them. They were run manually during this session; nothing enforces that.
3. **Website build** -- the api-manifest guard couples website content to the public API, and two of this session's changes required regenerating api.mdx. A stale/broken website is only caught by running npm run build, which the gate does not.
4. **Skips are invisible.** '3211 passed, 86 skipped' reads as success. Nothing asserts WHICH tests skipped or that the set is the expected one, so a newly-skipping test (a broken import, a missing extra, a mis-set marker) silently subtracts coverage while the count still climbs.

Point 4 is the general defect; 1-3 are its instances. A release gate whose success signal is compatible with an arbitrary subset of the suite not running is not a gate.

## Direction
- release-gate runs quality + live + mcp (with the extra) + examples + website build.
- Add an explicit skip ALLOWLIST: the gate fails if any test skips for a reason not on it. This is the ratchet -- it converts every future silently-skipping surface into a hard failure, rather than requiring someone to notice.
- Keep the fast dev loop (make quality) unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: make release-gate fails when: an MCP test skips for a missing extra, an example breaks, the website build fails, or any test skips for a reason not in the documented allowlist. The allowlist is a checked-in file with a reason per entry, and may only shrink. make quality remains fast and unchanged for the dev loop. Verified by mutation: introduce each failure mode and confirm the gate goes red.
notes:
## Fix (atoms neograph-3g1um.20/.25)

### What the old gate missed, measured not guessed
Running the suite WITH the extras installed: 3338 passed, 0 skipped. Without them the gate saw 3224 passed / 86 skipped. So **114 tests -- including 74 covering `neograph[mcp]`, a SECOND shipped top-level package (src/neograph_mcp) -- contributed nothing to the 0.7.7 gate.** My earlier report of 'about 2 skips' was itself wrong; I read the tail of the live run instead of the full skip census.

### The general fix: skips become failures
`scripts/check_skips.py` runs the suite with every extra installed and fails on any skip whose reason is not in `tests/skip_allowlist.txt`. That file is **EMPTY by design** -- with the extras there is nothing that legitimately needs to skip -- and documented as a ratchet that may only shrink. Every future surface that silently stops being exercised now turns the gate red instead of quietly subtracting from a pass count.

### The instances
| target | covers |
|---|---|
| `mcp` | the suite with --extra mcp --extra mcp-examples, so nothing importorskips |
| `examples` | all 11 keyless examples run end-to-end + the MCP e2e harness. CLAUDE.md says breaking one is a regression; the gate never ran them |
| `website` | npm ci + npm run build. The api-manifest guard couples page content to the public API, so a signature change can break the build -- twice this session it did |
| `skipcheck` | the ratchet above |

`release-gate: quality live mcp examples website skipcheck`. `make quality` is untouched, so the dev loop stays fast.

### Mutation verification -- each failure mode introduced and confirmed red
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| a test starts skipping for an unlisted reason | skipcheck FAILS, names the reason and the file |
| an example regresses | examples FAILS on that example |
| the neograph_mcp package regresses | mcp FAILS: 105 failed |
All restored; full gate then run end-to-end and PASSED on every target.

### Honest remaining holes, recorded rather than papered over
- Examples 07 and observable_pipeline.py still are not gated: they need real OpenRouter credentials. Same shape as the Langfuse hole, unresolved -- but now it is written down here rather than invisible.
- The gate does not run the hypothesis suite with a raised example count, so property-test flakes can still hide.
- npm ci makes the gate slower (~1-2 min). That is the cost of the website actually being covered.

title: Each-modified sub-constructs still invisible to LangGraph introspection (_wiring.py:264)
description:
Reported on GH #6 after 0.7.7 shipped. The 0.7.7 fix (neograph-xunot) covered the two make_subgraph_fn call sites -- compiler.py (top level) and _wiring.py (branch arm) -- but MISSED the Each fan-out wiring at _wiring.py:264:

    graph.add_node(fan_name, cast(Any, named(cast(Runnable, fan_fn), fan_name, mode='each')))

Same mechanism: named() -> .with_config() -> RunnableBinding -> find_subgraph_pregel has no branch for it -> get_subgraphs() returns []. That site's comment still cites the original trace-hygiene ticket, so it was simply missed.

Reporter's measurement on a pipeline with a Loop sub-construct containing an Each sub-construct, plus a second Each at top level:
    loop_sub    bound=RunnableLambda    subgraphs=['CompiledStateGraph']   FIXED in 0.7.7
    fan_outer   bound=RunnableBinding   subgraphs=[]                        STILL HIDDEN
    get_subgraphs(recurse=True) -> ['loop_sub'] only; fan_inner (Each nested inside the fixed Loop) also missed.
    xray reaches loop_sub's children but neither fan-out's interior.

## How this escaped the 0.7.7 sweep -- read before fixing
neograph-xunot's own disease scan LISTED this site (row 3: '_wiring.py:215/244/267/335/445 ... MIGRATE by root fix, PREDICTION to be proved') and explicitly said the sweep atom must PROVE the modifier'd paths rather than assume them. The sweep then tested a LOOP-modified sub-construct, saw it recover, and generalised to the whole modifier family. Loop recovers because _add_subgraph_loop passes subgraph_fn through unwrapped; Each does NOT, because it re-wraps at its own named() site. One member of a family was proved and the family was reported.

The fix must therefore be accompanied by a guard parametrized over EVERY modifier placement (plain / Loop / Each / Oracle / Operator / Each-inside-Loop / branch arm), not one representative.

Note _wiring.py:264 is shared between the Node and Construct paths ('Shared Each wiring used by both Node and Construct paths'), so either gate the add_node(metadata=) treatment on fan_fn wrapping a sub-construct, or apply it unconditionally if losing the tags there is acceptable as it was at the other two sites.
acceptance_criteria: get_subgraphs() enumerates an Each-modified sub-construct at top level AND one nested inside a Loop sub-construct; get_subgraphs(recurse=True) finds both; xray expands both interiors. A guard parametrized over every modifier placement (plain/Loop/Each/Oracle/Operator/Each-in-Loop/branch-arm) fails if any placement regresses. TDD: reproduce the reporter's exact shape first.
notes:
## Reproduction + fix (atoms neograph-3g1um.2/.7)

Parametrized the repro over every modifier placement BEFORE fixing -- the discipline 0.7.7 skipped. Result:
    plain   PASS (fixed in 0.7.7)
    loop    PASS (fixed in 0.7.7)
    each    FAIL  <- reporter's finding
    oracle  FAIL  <- NOT in the report; found only because the repro was parametrized
So the 0.7.7 miss was TWO sites, not one. Had this been fixed from the report alone, Oracle would have shipped broken again.

## Fix -- one decision point, not a third patch
The previous two fixes each re-made the same decision at their own call site, which is why the next two were missed. Added `_trace.add_traced_node(graph, name, runnable, *, mode, subgraph_meta=None)`: ONE place that decides whether a graph node may be config-bound, because that is a property of WHAT IS INSIDE the runnable, not of the wiring path.
- `subgraph_meta` given -> the runnable holds a compiled Pregel; add it UNBOUND and let the metadata ride `add_node(metadata=...)`.
- omitted -> ordinary wrapper; bind via `named()` with full run_name + tags + metadata.

Threaded `subgraph_meta=` through `_wire_oracle` and `_wire_each` (both shared between the Node and Construct paths) and supplied it ONLY from the Construct branch in compiler.py, which knows statically that it is wiring a sub-construct. No detection magic and no private langgraph import -- `tests/test_guards_sidecar_imports.py::test_no_private_langgraph_imports` forbids importing `find_subgraph_pregel` from `langgraph.pregel._utils`, and that guard is right.

The oracle MERGE barrier keeps its full binding: it consumes the generators' results and holds no Pregel.

## Tests
tests/test_subgraph_introspection.py: TestEveryModifierPlacementStaysVisible parametrized over plain/loop/each/oracle, plus TestNestedAndRecursiveDiscovery covering the reporter's exact shape -- an Each nested inside a Loop, a second Each at top level, get_subgraphs(recurse=True), and xray reaching the fan-out interior.

## Mutation verification
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| drop subgraph_meta from the Each caller (the 0.7.7 state) | 4 failed -- the each placement AND all three nested/recursive tests |
| drop subgraph_meta from the Oracle caller | 1 failed -- exactly the oracle placement |
Each placement is independently pinned; neither is a passenger.

title: Sub-constructs invisible to LangGraph introspection (get_subgraphs/xray/to_json/Studio/Langfuse)
description:
GitHub issue #6 (github.com/KonstantinMirin/neograph/issues/6), filed 2026-08-18 against 0.7.6.

Root cause (confirmed by reporter's own diagnostics, re-verified against installed langgraph 1.2.7): _trace.py's named() wraps every graph-node runnable -- including the sub-construct's subgraph_fn (compiler.py:437, via make_subgraph_fn) -- in .with_config(run_name=..., tags=..., metadata=...), producing a RunnableBinding. LangGraph's subgraph-detection (find_subgraph_pregel) walks RunnableLambda/.deps but does not unwrap .bound on a RunnableBinding, so get_subgraphs()/xray/Graph.to_json()/Studio/Langfuse's agent-graph view all miss the nested structure -- sub-construct internals render as one opaque box.

Verified against current code: StateGraph.add_node() (langgraph>=1.1,<2.0 pin) accepts metadata= directly but NOT tags= or run_name= -- DeprecatedKwargs (the only **kwargs catch-all) is an empty TypedDict in this version. So a neograph-side-only fix (pass metadata via add_node instead of named()'s with_config for the subgraph case) would preserve metadata but regress the subgraph node's span run_name back to the leaking inner-function name (subgraph_node) -- trading away the exact trace hygiene neograph-3fm1 deliberately added.

DECISION NEEDED before implementation: (a) accept the span-name regression scoped ONLY to the subgraph-wrapping case (add_node(sub.name, subgraph_fn, metadata=...) instead of named(...) for that one call site in compiler.py:437/493), or (b) lead with an upstream LangGraph fix (find_subgraph_pregel needs an isinstance(c, RunnableBinding): candidates.append(c.bound) branch) and treat this as blocked/secondary until that lands, or (c) both -- ship (a) now (real user impact today) and additionally file/PR the upstream fix as offered by the reporter.

Reporter offered to contribute a PR for a fallback IR-level topology API (describe_graph(compiled, declared=True) or a documented CompiledNeograph.construct walk) as an alternative if (a)/(b) prove infeasible, plus offered to file the upstream LangGraph issue themselves.
acceptance_criteria: get_subgraphs()/xray/to_json() correctly enumerate sub-construct internals for a nested cascade (reproduction case from the GH issue: cascade -> investigate -> verify). Decision on the run_name tradeoff documented explicitly, not silently dropped. TDD: reproduce first against a real nested-Construct graph.
notes:
## Reproduction (atom neograph-z7xgk.20)
- Failing tests: tests/test_subgraph_introspection.py::TestSubgraphIntrospection -- get_subgraphs / xray / to_json, all three RED against a real nested Construct (cascade -> verify -> explore, the GH issue's shape).
- Observed: `get_subgraphs()` -> `[]`; `get_graph(xray=True).nodes` -> `['__start__','seed','verify','report','__end__']` (verify still an opaque box, no `verify:explore`).
- Root cause CONFIRMED, not merely restated: `_trace.named()` returns `runnable.with_config(...)` (a RunnableBinding); `langgraph/pregel/_utils.py:47 find_subgraph_pregel` walks RunnableSequence.steps / RunnableLambda.deps / RunnableCallable nonlocals and has NO RunnableBinding branch, so the nested Pregel is unreachable from the parent. Read directly from the installed langgraph 1.2.7.

## The ticket's cost estimate for option (a) is WRONG -- corrected by experiment
The bead says option (a) 'would regress the subgraph node's span run_name back to the leaking inner-function name (subgraph_node), trading away the exact trace hygiene neograph-3fm1 deliberately added.' That is FALSE. Two experiments, run and reverted:

1. Dropping `named()` at compiler.py:460 restores detection immediately -- `get_subgraphs() -> ['verify']`, `xray -> [..., 'verify:explore']`.
2. `make_subgraph_fn` (_subconstruct.py:207) ALREADY returns a `RunnableLambda`, and `RunnableLambda` takes `name=`. Passing `name=sub.name` there keeps the span run_name at `verify` -- verified with a live BaseCallbackHandler over an actual run, which recorded the subgraph node's on_chain_start name as `'verify'`, not `subgraph_node` -- WHILE detection works.

So the real cost of the neograph-side fix is much smaller than the bead assumed:
| Trace attribute | Under `named()` today | Under the corrected option (a) |
|---|---|---|
| run_name | verify | verify (RunnableLambda name=) -- PRESERVED |
| metadata (neograph_node / neograph_mode / neograph_output_type) | present | restorable via `graph.add_node(..., metadata=...)`, which the installed StateGraph.add_node DOES accept (verified by signature inspection) -- PRESERVED |
| tags (`neograph:node`, `neograph:mode:subgraph`) | present | LOST for this one node kind -- `add_node` accepts no `tags=`, and any `.with_config(tags=...)` re-creates the binding that breaks detection |

The whole trade is therefore TWO TAGS on the sub-construct node, not the run_name.

## Scope note for the disease scan
`named()` is applied to the subgraph runnable at compiler.py:460, and the oracle-redirect / each-redirect / loop branches wrap THAT value further (_wiring.py:170, 215, 244, 267, 335, 445). A modifier'd sub-construct therefore hits the same binding barrier one level deeper. The scan atom must check whether those branches are equally invisible, not assume the plain case is the only one.

## DECISION still owed before the fix atom
(a) neograph-side now / (b) upstream-first / (c) both -- to be surfaced at triage with the corrected cost above.
## Similar-pattern trace (atom neograph-z7xgk.21)

## Mechanism, isolated at the object level (asked during atom .25)
Not inferred from code -- measured:

    neograph's RunnableLambda .deps        -> ['CompiledStateGraph']   # the nested Pregel IS reachable
    find_subgraph_pregel(rl)               -> True
    find_subgraph_pregel(rl.with_config()) -> False                    # the ONLY delta is the wrapper

Why 'we create the subgraph, so why can't we tag it' does not resolve it: neograph never hands LangGraph the Pregel directly. A sub-construct needs input/output boundary shaping, so `add_node` receives a RunnableLambda that CLOSES OVER the compiled Pregel. LangGraph therefore discovers nesting by WALKING INTO the node runnable (`find_subgraph_pregel`), not by being told. That walker unwraps RunnableSequence.steps, RunnableLambda.deps and RunnableCallable nonlocals -- and has no RunnableBinding.bound branch. `.with_config()`, LangChain's only way to attach tags/run_name, returns exactly a RunnableBinding.

So tagging is not the problem; tagging is implemented as WRAPPING, and the wrapper is the one shape the walker cannot see through. Three attachments, one with no non-wrapping route:

| attachment | non-wrapping route |
|---|---|
| run_name | YES -- RunnableLambda(name=...) |
| metadata | YES -- add_node(..., metadata=...) |
| tags | NO -- add_node has no tags=, and DeprecatedKwargs is an EMPTY TypedDict in the pinned version (both verified by signature inspection) |

That asymmetry is why the blind spot is upstream's: the walker already unwraps three composition wrappers and omits the most common one, so ANY library binding config onto a subgraph node goes invisible.

description:
Today to_agent_spec() either raises for cases it KNOWS it can't represent (_agent_spec.py:26-35), or silently succeeds -- and 'didn't raise' is being used as a stand-in for 'is portable to a third-party runtime', which is provably false in three known, currently-open, ticketed ways: neograph-qtfof.7 (Each->MapNode's iterated_item has no real DataFlowEdge, metadata-only fan-out source, confirmed live e.g. cell scripted-each-single exports with data_flow_connections=None -- a foreign runtime literally cannot execute it), neograph-qtfof.6 (same pattern for Loop/Operator->BranchingNode's branching_mapping_key), neograph-qtfof.9 (outermost Construct's EndNode declares no outputs by design, so a third-party invoke() silently returns {} even though the graph computed a real result -- verified via an actual EXECUTE+COMPARE harness, neograph-jn555.31/dgbqv.2, not just static shape inspection).

Build a new module (e.g. src/neograph/_agent_spec_conformance.py) exposing export_conformance(construct) -> ConformanceReport with a three-tier verdict: PORTABLE / NEOGRAPH_ROUND_TRIP_ONLY / NOT_EXPORTABLE.   only attach point (both `Flow` and `Swarm` are `extra="forbid"`; `flow.conformance = x` raises
  `ValueError: "Flow" object has no field "conformance"` -- verified live). But
  `tests/test_agent_spec_refactor_snapshot.py` + `tests/fixtures/agent_spec_refactor_snapshot.json`
  pin the EXACT serialized Flow *including metadata* (its docstring calls out `metadata == {}` vs
  `None` as the trap it exists to catch). Stamping a `neograph/conformance` marker by default changes
  the wire output for every export and requires regenerating that fixture. Three options:
  (a) attach the report to the WARNING object (`AgentSpecConformanceWarning(...).report`) and expose
  `export_conformance(construct)` as the programmatic accessor -- zero wire change, snapshot stays
  green; (b) stamp `flow.metadata[_MARK_CONFORMANCE]` by default and regenerate the snapshot;
  (c) stamp only under an explicit opt-in kwarg. Recommendation: **(a)**. Needs the maintainer to
  confirm, because it is a wire-format decision.
- **`_agent_spec.py` is at its EXACT file-size ceiling (650/650) and the ratchet is shrink-only** --
  "raise the number is not a remedy, splitting the file is" (test_guards_file_size.py docstring).

  (docstring lines 25-35) into the new `_agent_spec_conformance.py` docstring, where it now belongs,
  and lower the ceiling in the SAME commit. Do not defer.
- **`check_fixtures` reuse is a poor literal fit.** `test_check_fixtures.py` only imports+compiles and

  nothing, so it cannot live in `should_fail/`, and putting it in `should_pass/` proves nothing about
  conformance. CLAUDE.md records the exact precedent trap: a `known_gaps/` tier was DOCUMENTED but
  never created because nobody taught the scanner about it. If a new fixture tier is wanted, the
  scanner must be extended in the same commit. Recommendation: derive the per-tier fixtures from
  `test_agent_spec_matrix.CELLS` instead, and reserve check_fixtures for the `strict=True` raise case.

- **Ticket-id guard**: `src/neograph/*.py` may not contain `(neograph-xxxx)` with a 3-5 char body in
  parentheses. Put the bead in a registry data field / string literal, never a parenthesized comment.
- **PROC-2**: if the new guard test uses `re`, it needs a NAMED module-level constant plus a

title: [EPIC] Hybrid Data Flow: Reasoned/Carried/Selected output fields, tool ledger, scoped addressing, provides/requires, Agent Spec export fidelity
description:
Umbrella for a design proposal (docs/design/hybrid-dataflow-2026-08-14.md) addressing a real, recurring pain point across neograph consumer projects: node output today welds two things together -- what the model reasons about, and data that must arrive verbatim from a tool/upstream result (a source URL, an exact excerpt, a record ID). Forcing the model to re-transcribe carried data is unreliable (silent corruption: URL normalization, paraphrased excerpts, reformatted timestamps), destroys provenance, costs tokens twice, and degrades reasoning quality on the SAME call as schema pressure grows.

Proposal (full text + prior-art survey in the design doc): three output-field kinds -- Reasoned (model-authored, unchanged), Carried (runtime-copied from a typed path, absent from the LLM schema entirely), Selected (model picks a key from a closed set, runtime materializes the value) -- plus a tool call ledger (ordinal-addressable ReAct tool calls) and provides/requires named-contract dataflow (decouple a consumer from a specific upstream node's identity).

Grounded against the actual codebase (not just the proposal) via a 12-agent workflow: 6 sonnet passes mapped every relevant subsystem with file:line citations, 5 fable passes independently assessed feasibility per primitive against neograph's own layer-discipline/North-star rules, 1 fable synthesis pass produced the sequenced child-epic breakdown below. Full grounding + reasoning: docs/design/hybrid-dataflow-workflow-findings-2026-08-14.md.

VERDICT (from the grounding pass, load-bearing for scoping every child): this bundle is mostly expressiveness/observability, NOT an extension of neograph's 'unrepresentable' compile-time-safety claim -- do not market it as more than that. The one real (small) safety extension is Carried, and only when restricted to a node's OWN input/context (never another node's output, which would add a validator-invisible dataflow edge and escalate DX sugar into IR work). title: main's `make quality` is red on a fresh checkout: pytest-asyncio stranded in the `dev` extra (x75es never reached main)
description:
Found while establishing the baseline for the neograph-l2a7w bug-triage molecule
(epic neograph-ysff2) in a worktree cut from main @ 105b165 (the 0.7.4 tag).

SYMPTOM
A fresh checkout of main + `make quality` fails 49 tests:

  49 failed, 3057 passed, 86 skipped, 2 deselected in 30.56s
  make: *** [test] Error 1

Every failure is async (test_async_concurrency, test_checkpoint_sqlite_async,
test_streaming's async verbs, test_async_harness, the async halves of
test_structured_retry / test_oracle / test_agent_cycle_run_cache, ...).

ROOT CAUSE
On main, pytest-asyncio is declared in [project.optional-dependencies].dev --
the `dev` EXTRA -- which `uv run` does NOT install. But main's Makefile `test:`
target is the bare `uv run pytest -q --tb=short -m "not live"`. So the gate runs
in an environment without pytest_asyncio (confirmed directly:
`uv run python -c "import pytest_asyncio"` -> ModuleNotFoundError), and every
`async def test_*` errors out instead of running.

Re-running the same suite as `uv run --extra dev pytest -q --tb=short -m "not live"`
gives 3106 passed, 86 skipped, 2 deselected, 0 failed. ruff and mypy are clean
either way (they do not need the extra).

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE
An existing worktree whose .venv had once been created with `--extra dev` keeps
pytest-asyncio installed, so `make quality` passes there. Only a FRESH venv
exposes it. That is presumably how 0.7.4 was gated and tagged green.

ALREADY FIXED ON DEVELOP, NOT ON MAIN
neograph-x75es did exactly this: commit e66c7b2 "fix(gate): run the Agent Spec
suite under the project's own gate" moved pytest-asyncio into
[dependency-groups].dev and deleted the `dev` extra. develop's pyproject even
carries the post-mortem comment: "both a `dev` extra and a `dev` group is what
stranded pytest-asyncio". main predates it.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND COSMETICS
`make release-gate` is documented as MANDATORY on merged main before a tag, and
the whole point of that rule (AGENTS.md, after the 0.7.4 flaky-live-test
incident) is that the gate must be mechanically trustworthy rather than
remembered. A gate that cannot be run from a clean clone of the branch it gates
is the same class of hole. Any 0.7.x hotfix branch cut from main hits this on
its first baseline.

FIX
Port the x75es dependency-layout change to main (one namespace:
[dependency-groups].dev; delete the `dev` extra), either as its own hotfix or as
part of the next develop -> main merge. Verify by running the gate in a FRESH
worktree with no pre-existing .venv -- that is the only environment that
reproduces it.

WORKAROUND until then: gate main-based branches with
`uv run --extra dev pytest ...` rather than `make quality`.
design:
## Root Cause

main's pyproject.toml carries TWO dev namespaces:
  [project.optional-dependencies].dev = pytest, pytest-asyncio, ruff, mypy   <- the gate's own toolchain
  [dependency-groups].dev             = hypothesis, langchain*, langfuse, langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite,
                                        pytest-examples, pytest-cov, python-dotenv

uv installs the GROUP by default and the EXTRA only on explicit --extra dev. main's Makefile
`test:` target is the bare `uv run pytest -q --tb=short -m "not live"`, so the gate runs in an
environment with no pytest-asyncio. With asyncio_mode='auto' set in [tool.pytest.ini_options],
every `async def test_*` needs that plugin; without it all 49 async tests error out.

pytest/ruff/mypy survive only by accident (transitive from pytest-cov / pytest-examples, plus a
PATH mypy), which is why the hole presented as 'async tests are broken' rather than 'the gate
cannot start'. An existing worktree whose .venv was once built with --extra dev keeps
pytest-asyncio resident, so the failure is invisible except on a FRESH venv -- presumably how
0.7.4 was gated green.

This is neograph-x75es, already fixed on develop (commit e66c7b2) and never merged to main.
main @ 105b165 predates it.

## Fix Approach

Port the x75es dependency layout to main. Minimal change, two files:

1. pyproject.toml
   - DELETE the `dev` key from [project.optional-dependencies] (one namespace, no second home).
   - ADD pytest, pytest-asyncio, ruff, mypy to [dependency-groups].dev, keeping the post-mortem
     comment develop carries ('both a dev extra and a dev group is what stranded pytest-asyncio').
   - Leave the consumer-facing extras (langfuse, mcp, mcp-examples) untouched.

2. tests/test_guards_test_gate_deps.py
   - Port develop's guard verbatim. It is the regression test: its
     test_default_gate_owns_its_own_toolchain and test_there_is_no_second_dev_namespace are
     RED on main today and green after step 1, so the layout cannot silently regress again.
   - Carry AGENTS.md's gate-command section across in the same change so the documented command
     ('uv run --extra dev pytest') stops naming a deleted extra.

Explicitly NOT in scope: no source change under src/neograph, no Makefile change (the bare
`uv run pytest` target becomes correct once the group owns the toolchain).

Open decision for the review atom: land as a dedicated hotfix branch off main (AGENTS.md allows
'critical hotfix PRs' on main, and a gate that cannot run from a clean clone of the branch it
gates is that class of defect), versus waiting for the next develop -> main release merge.
Recommendation: hotfix -- any 0.7.x branch cut from main hits this on its first baseline, and the
change is packaging-only with zero runtime surface.

## Architect Review (neograph-w0sfh.5, 2026-08-12)

### NEW EVIDENCE — the bug is worse than the ticket states: TWO of the three gate legs are down

`make quality` = test + lint + typecheck. On a fresh clone of main:

* **test** — 49 failures (already established).
* **typecheck** — **does not run at all.** mypy is absent from the fresh venv
  (`ls .venv/bin/mypy` -> absent; only ruff and pytest are there, pulled transitively by
  pytest-examples / pytest-cov). With a sanitized PATH:

      cd <fresh main worktree>
      env PATH="/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:$(dirname $(command -v uv))" \
        uv run --no-sync mypy src/neograph/ --ignore-missing-imports
      -> error: Failed to spawn: `mypy` / Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)

  My earlier probe reported "mypy 1.20.0" only because `uv run` fell back to a PATH binary that
  turned out to be `/Users/konst/projects/neograph/.venv/bin/mypy` — the DEVELOP worktrees venv
  leaking through PATH. On any machine without a pre-existing neograph venv (CI, a new clone, a
  new contributor) main cannot type-check at all.
* **lint** — survives, but only by accident (ruff is a transitive dep of pytest-examples). Nothing
  declares it where the gate can see it.

So the accurate statement of the defect is not "async tests fail on main" but **"main cannot run
its own quality gate from a clean checkout"**. That strengthens, not changes, the fix.

### Findings

**F1 — Root-cause correctness: CONFIRMED, no finding.** Chain verified end to end: `dev` extra ->
`uv run` skips it -> no pytest_asyncio -> `asyncio_mode = "auto"` has no plugin -> 49 async errors.
Corroborated independently by pytests own `Unknown config option: asyncio_mode` warning and by an
exact match to the tickets 49/3057/86/2 counts.

**F2 (MEDIUM) — uv.lock must move with pyproject.** main/uv.lock records the `dev` extra. Editing
`[project.optional-dependencies]` / `[dependency-groups]` without re-locking leaves the lockfile
stale and `uv run` either re-resolves silently or errors. develops own x75es change carries a
40-line uv.lock delta. ACTION: run `uv lock` and commit the lockfile in the same commit.

**F3 (MEDIUM) — the fix changes which mypy/ruff the gate uses; the gate must be re-run, not
assumed.** Today main type-checks with an arbitrary PATH mypy (or not at all) and lints with a
transitively-pinned ruff. Declaring `mypy>=1.8` / `ruff>=0.3` installs real, resolved versions into
the venv for the first time, which can surface type or lint errors that were never actually
evaluated on main. This is a *feature* of the fix, but it means the acceptance evidence must be a
full `make quality` on a fresh worktree — never "packaging-only, cannot regress".

**F4 (MEDIUM) — port the guard file VERBATIM from develop, do not adapt it.** develops
tests/test_guards_test_gate_deps.py already runs 12-passed/2-failed against mains tree, so it is
compatible as-is; its GATED_IMPORT_EXEMPTIONS (mcp, langchain_mcp_adapters) are both real and both
still gated on main. Its docstring narrates the pyagentspec incident, which main has no code for —
tempting to trim, but DO NOT: an adapted copy diverges from develops and turns the next
develop -> main merge into a conflict on the very file that guards the invariant. Byte-identical
is the correct port.

**F5 (MEDIUM) — the change must be forward-ported to develop, and develop has two live defects of
its own.** Two obligations, both concrete:
  (a) After landing on main, merge main back into develop (the repos own precedent: 55edaff
      "merge: forward-port 0.7.4 into develop"). Otherwise mains hotfix commit is main-only and
      the branches drift again on exactly this file.
  (b) The disease scan found AGENTS.md:674 and tests/test_observe_trace_live.py:13 still spelling
      `uv run --extra dev --extra langfuse pytest tests/test_observe_trace_live.py` ON DEVELOP.
      Verified 2026-08-12: `uv run --extra dev ...` now exits non-zero
      (`error: Extra `dev` is not defined ...`). That is the documented command for the live
      Langfuse check that `make release-gate` exists to protect — the one command whose
      trustworthiness the 0.7.4 post-mortem was about. x75es deleted the extra and missed these two
      call sites. Fix them on develop in this wave; do not defer.

**F6 (LOW) — no version bump, no tag.** `[dependency-groups]` is not published in wheel metadata,
so nothing that reached PyPI as 0.7.4 changes meaning. Deleting the `dev` extra does drop a
`Provides-Extra: dev` from future builds, but 0.7.4 is already published and immutable, and the
sole downstream (piarch) pulls from develop. Leave `__version__` and `pyproject.version` at 0.7.4
so TestVersionSync stays green; no republish, no new tag.

**F7 (LOW) — fix minimality is good, but split the commit.** Commit 1: pyproject + uv.lock + the
ported guard (the fix and its regression test). Commit 2: the 26-site `--extra dev` documentation
sweep (mechanical, reviewable separately). Both on the same hotfix branch. Keeps the load-bearing
change readable.

**F8 (HIGH — procedural, not technical) — the acceptance locus is a FRESH clone, and the
already-used repro worktree no longer qualifies.** scratchpad/main-repro now has a populated .venv.
Verification must happen in a NEWLY created worktree with no .venv, or the evidence proves nothing
about the condition that hid this bug for a whole release. The verify atom must also assert the
typecheck leg under a sanitized PATH, per the new evidence above — a green `make quality` in this
shell would otherwise still be borrowing develops mypy.

**F9 (HIGH — needs the maintainers call) — delivery path onto main is not mine to choose.**
The ticket leaves it open ("its own hotfix or as part of the next develop -> main merge"), and
AGENTS.md reserves main for "tagged releases and critical hotfix PRs". Landing on main is an
outward-facing, hard-to-reverse action on the release branch. Routed to the triage atom as
NEEDS_USER_INPUT: hotfix branch + PR to main now, versus develop-only cleanup and let the next
release merge carry it. Everything else in this review is decided and ready either way.

### Verdict: NEEDS_USER_INPUT

Technical plan is sound and unchanged in substance (F1 confirms the root cause; F2/F3/F4 are
execution requirements, not redesigns; F5-F7 extend scope in ways the ticket already anticipates).
The single open item is F9 — where the fix lands — which is the maintainers decision, not the
implementers.

title: prompt_compiler receives input_data['<param>'] as either a rendered str or the Pydantic model — callers must hand-roll a both-ways renderer
description:
THE INCONSISTENCY: for an agent-mode node whose parameter is a Pydantic model, the prompt_compiler is handed input_data as a dict keyed by the param name, but the VALUE is sometimes the model and sometimes an already-BAML-rendered str. The compiler cannot tell which without checking, and the two need opposite handling.

WHY THIS IS A BUG AND NOT A DETAIL: the failure is SILENT and produces a plausible wrong answer. A compiler written the obvious way —

    prose = input_data.get('intake')
    text = str(getattr(prose, 'text', '') or '')

— returns an EMPTY string when the value is a str, because every getattr misses. The prompt then renders with an empty payload, the model reads a blank input, and answers coherently about nothing. Nothing raises, the graph completes, the output is well-typed and confidently wrong.

REAL INCIDENT (ox-troubleshooting-demo, qvoq.3, 2026-08-11): an extraction node reads a prose diagnosis onto a typed taxonomy. Written as above, it scored 0/6 on its accuracy golden, every row answering 'insufficient_data — the arm emitted no diagnosis'. The prose was 5,334 chars and had been passed in correctly. Had that golden not existed, the downstream A/B benchmark would have published 'the third-party prompt never reaches a conclusion' — a claim about someone else's system caused entirely by this rendering seam.

EVIDENCE IT IS A GENERAL TAX, not one team's mistake: the same repo carries a helper, context.render_intake, whose entire body is this workaround —

    if isinstance(input_data, dict): value = input_data.get('intake', input_data)
    else: value = input_data
    if isinstance(value, str): return value
    if hasattr(value, 'model_dump'): return describe_value(value)

It existed as THREE byte-identical private copies across three arms before being extracted. Every single-agent arm in that codebase independently rediscovered the need for it.

SUGGESTED FIX (in preference order):
1. Render consistently. Hand the compiler ONE shape — always the model, or always the BAML-rendered str — and document which. Callers then write one line with no isinstance dance.
2. If both shapes must reach the compiler for real reasons, ship the both-ways renderer IN neograph (a public render_input/describe_input) so it is written and tested once, not rediscovered per project.
3. At minimum, make the shape discoverable: type the compiler signature so a caller cannot silently treat a str as a model.

ACCEPTANCE: a compiler that does the obvious getattr on a model-typed param either works, or fails LOUDLY. It must not render an empty payload and let a confident answer about nothing reach the caller.

and third being two copies of the same split) and the fourth, the Oracle
