rule itself is implemented twice and differently: inline _resolve_var is total
but IGNORES render_for_prompt(); template-ref _render_single honors the
presenter but passes primitives through unrendered. di_inputs skip rendering
entirely.

THE RULE (one rule, one implementation, four call sites): every value handed
to a prompt_compiler is prompt-ready text — BAML-rendered unless already a
string, primitives coerced, None -> "", and render_for_prompt() is the one
presenter hook that overrides the default. No per-channel variation:
input_data, di_inputs and context are one namespace under one rule.

DECISIONS LOCKED:
- Normalize inside _compile_prompt (the one choke point). If _oracle.py needs
  an edit, the decision still lives in the call sites and the fix is wrong.
- Rendering AND typing are both required and do different jobs: Rendered(str)
  with a loud non-AttributeError __getattr__ makes a wrong assumption fail at
  runtime (getattr-with-default and hasattr both propagate it, verified);
  PromptInput = Mapping[str, Rendered] on the PromptCompiler Protocol makes
  the shape discoverable. The annotation alone changes nothing — the Protocol
  is structural and consumers annotate Any.
- PromptInput is TOTAL: primitives and non-renderable objects coerce too. A
  union would be Any wearing a hat and would re-admit the branching this
  ticket removes. A FROM_CONFIG live handle renders ugly but must NOT fail
  loud (di_inputs are injected for every template-usable binding, referenced
  or not).
- Single-type inputs key by producer name (_extract_single_type already knows
  it and discards it), so the dict-vs-bare-value branch dies with the
  str-vs-model branch.
- di_inputs render through the same path; a DI model's own render_for_prompt()
  finally applies. Collision rule unchanged (upstream output shadows).
- raw_inputs escape hatch CONSIDERED AND WITHDRAWN: structured work belongs
  upstream in render_for_prompt()/merge_pre_process. Keeping it reintroduces
  the second shape by the front door.

BLAST RADIUS: merge templates' {variants} repr -> BAML (4 examples);
primitives become text in compilers; inline ${var} now honors presenters;
prompt.py build_vars must stop double-rendering; the iu05 AST guard in
test_guards_examples.py is RETIRED, not carried alongside — it band-aided the
ambiguity this removes. Follow-up: lint has never covered merge_prompt
templates.

GUARD-FIRST: the red test is one compiler + a think node + an Oracle merge
asserting both invocations receive Rendered under the same key; it must fail
on main before anything is written.

title: Agent Spec export: MapNode's iterated_item has no DataFlowEdge -- Each's 'over' source lives only in metadata
description:
Found during dgbqv.2's research/design-decision pass (2026-08-06). neograph's Each export lowering encodes the 'over' collection source ONLY in metadata['neograph/each_spec']['over'] -- the MapNode's iterated_item input has no DataFlowEdge (confirmed live: 'scripted-each-single' cell exports with data_flow_connections is None -- zero data edges). A strictly metadata-blind Agent Spec runtime (per the project's stated full-interop design goal) cannot determine what to iterate over. This blocks true interop with 3rd-party Agent Spec tooling.

Fix direction (not yet designed): the exported Flow should carry a REAL DataFlowEdge from the producing node's output into the MapNode's iterated_item, not just a metadata mirror. Needs its own design pass.
design:
## Core Invariant
The exported Flow must carry every fact a METADATA-BLIND Agent Spec runtime needs to execute
it, as real topology (`DataFlowEdge` + Property SHAPE) -- `neograph/*` metadata is the
round-trip channel only, never the sole carrier of a runtime-load-bearing value; and an edge
that exists but would be interpreted differently by that runtime (broadcast instead of
iterated) is a WORSE outcome than no edge, so the Property shape must make the edge mean
exactly one thing.

## Design decision (evidence-backed)
The bug is not "a missing edge", it is "a receiver Property shape no edge can legally land
on". `_lower_each` flattens the fan-out receiver into per-FIELD Properties (`item:v`), so the
MapNode infers `iterated_item:v` while the collection producer offers `array[Elem]`. Fix the
SHAPE, then the edge follows.

Empirically validated against the real third-party runtime
(`pyagentspec.adapters.langgraph.AgentSpecLoader`, notes section 3): declaring the receiver as
ONE ObjectProperty titled with the `fan_out_param` key makes the MapNode infer
`iterated_item: anyOf[Elem, array[Elem]]`, and a single `DataFlowEdge(producer, 'groups' ->
map_node, 'iterated_item')` drives REAL iteration -- 3 collection elements produced 3 inner
invocations, each receiving one `Elem`, with zero metadata reads.

REJECTED alternative (name it in review): keeping the flattened receiver and wiring
`groups -> iterated_item:v`. It validates and even passes `property_is_castable_to`, but the
loader's own type test (`json_schemas_have_same_type(source, List[inner_input])`) fails, so it
is BROADCAST -- the whole list bound where one item belongs. Silent wrong answers; forbidden.

## Anti-band-aid clause
Do not "make the edge exist" by pointing it at the flattened `iterated_item:v` input, do not
suppress the conformance predicate while the gap remains, and do not add an unfed extra
`iterated_*` Property alongside the old ones -- the loader hard-errors on ANY declared MapNode
input it cannot fill, so an additive shape is not merely untidy, it is broken. If the
translation-eligible or fused path cannot be made truthful in this bead, leave it reporting
NEOGRAPH_ROUND_TRIP_ONLY and file it -- an honest tier beats a green one.

### 1. Where the gap actually is (confirmed live, not read-only)
`_lower_each` builds the Each sub-Flow's StartNode from `_properties_for(_item_inputs(node))`,
which FLATTENS every dict-form input key into one Property per MODEL FIELD titled `key:field`.
So for `inputs={'item': Elem}` + `fan_out_param='item'` the StartNode declares `item:v` (str),
and pyagentspec's `MapNode._get_inferred_inputs` therefore infers `iterated_item:v`
(`anyOf[str, array[str]]`). The collection producer's Property is `groups` (`array[Elem]`).
The two shapes cannot be joined by any DataFlowEdge -- which is WHY the exporter skips the
edge (`_agent_spec.py:497-505`, the `fan_out_param` `continue`) and mirrors `over` into
`metadata['neograph/each_spec']`. The metadata mirror is the SYMPTOM; the flattened receiver
Property is the CAUSE.

### 2. What the third-party runtime actually requires (measured, pyagentspec 26.1.x)
Ran the exported cells through `pyagentspec.adapters.langgraph.AgentSpecLoader` (the same
metadata-blind runtime `tests/test_agent_spec_execute.py` uses):
  * `scripted-each-single`  -> ValueError: "Expected node `target` to have a value for property `iterated_item:v`, but none was found."
  * `scripted-each-context` -> same
  * `scripted-loop-single`  -> "...`branching_mapping_key`..." (the qtfof.6 sibling)
  * `scripted-bare-single`  -> OK
Two decisive loader facts (adapters/langgraph/_langgraphconverter.py:347-371, :385-405):
  a. A MapNode input is treated as ITERATED only when
     `json_schemas_have_same_type(source_prop, ListProperty(item_type=inner_flow_input_prop))`.
     Titles are IGNORED by that comparison (verified: `groups` vs `item` still matched True).
     Any other incoming edge is BROADCAST, not iterated -- so a "real but wrongly-shaped"
     edge would silently pass the whole list as one item. A lying edge is WORSE than none.
  b. When `flow.data_flow_connections is None` the loader AUTO-WIRES same-titled
     output->input pairs ("the conversion recommended in the Agent Spec language
     specification"). The Each sub-Flow currently exports `data_flow_connections=None`, so
     its StartNode->inner wiring works TODAY by name-matching. TRAP: adding even ONE explicit
     sub-flow DataFlowEdge disables auto-wiring for that whole sub-Flow and forces every
     internal edge to be declared. Keep the sub-Flow's `data_flow_connections=None`.

### 3. Proof of concept -- the fix runs end-to-end on the real loader
Patched the exported `scripted-each-single` Flow by hand: declared the fan-out receiver as
ONE ObjectProperty titled `item` (the whole `Elem`) on BOTH the sub-Flow StartNode and the
inner ToolNode/ServerTool, exposed the inner's outputs on the sub-Flow EndNode, and added
`DataFlowEdge(prod, 'groups' -> map, 'iterated_item')`.
Result: MapNode infers `iterated_item: anyOf[Elem, array[Elem]]` and `collected_ok:
array[str]`; the loader RAN it and the inner tool was invoked **3 times for a 3-element
collection, each call receiving one `Elem`** -- real iteration, driven ONLY by the
DataFlowEdge, zero metadata reads. This is the design's empirical proof.

  * `_lower_loop`'s data-edge block (`_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:425-450`) is the

  WILL need updating, deliberately, and the update must be reviewed as a real shape change.

title: Agent Spec export: BranchingNode's branching_mapping_key has no DataFlowEdge -- decision lives only in metadata
description:
Found during dgbqv.2's research/design-decision pass (2026-08-06). neograph's Loop/Operator export lowering (_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:376-385 for loop, :634-641 for operator) encodes the branch predicate ONLY in metadata['neograph/loop_spec']['when'] / metadata['neograph/operator_spec']['when'] -- the BranchingNode's inferred branching_mapping_key input has no DataFlowEdge feeding it. A strictly metadata-blind Agent Spec runtime (per the project's stated full-interop design goal: exported Flows must be correctly wired and executable using only ControlFlowEdge/DataFlowEdge, even if it loses neograph's Oracle/Each/Loop abstractions) cannot determine which branch to take. This blocks true interop with 3rd-party Agent Spec tooling that doesn't understand neograph/* metadata extensions.

Fix direction (not yet designed): the exported Flow should carry a REAL DataFlowEdge feeding the BranchingNode's condition input (e.g. from whatever upstream node's output the predicate reads), not just a metadata mirror. Needs its own design pass on how to represent the reduction from a Python condition to a wire-able DataFlowEdge source.
design:
## Core Invariant

An exported Agent Spec Flow must be correctly wired and executable by a metadata-blind runtime using ONLY ControlFlowEdge/DataFlowEdge: every BranchingNode's branching_mapping_key input must arrive over a REAL declared data path from a real node output, and every branch value plus DEFAULT_BRANCH must have an outgoing ControlFlowEdge. Where neograph cannot honestly produce that data path (an Operator/Loop predicate that is an opaque registry name, not an expression over a determinable upstream field), the export must fail LOUD (modifier_metadata_only_branch conformance finding) rather than emit a Flow that looks wired and silently takes the default branch.

## FINAL DECISION (2026-08-14, reconciling a churned ticket history)

This ticket's NOTES/DESIGN history contains two INCOMPATIBLE plans that were never reconciled (Option B: new opt-in IR field Loop(when_key=)/Operator(when_key=) with @node satellites; vs ToolNode-synthesis: no new API, synthesize a predicate ToolNode between source and BranchingNode). The architect review (fe1d6.12) flagged this as HIGH and required a single choice before write-test.

**DECISION: ToolNode-synthesis. Do NOT add Loop.when_key/Operator.when_key or any new public API/IR field.**

Rationale: ToolNode-synthesis reuses an existing, review-verified in-tree precedent (the Oracle merge_fn ToolNode pattern, _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:196-215, confirmed by the review to synthesize a node AND wire real fan-in DataFlowEdges) and adds ZERO new public API surface, no assembly-time validation rule, no MODIFIER_KWARGS row, nothing that must survive round-trip as a first-class field. Option B is strictly more invasive for a P3 interop-fidelity ticket with uncertain downstream value. Consistent with this project's "no back-compat shims, minimal footprint" default at 0.x.

**SCOPE: v1 covers Loop only. Operator is explicitly OUT of scope for this ticket, and continues firing modifier_metadata_only_branch (still honest fail-loud, not silent -- this is not a regression, it is today's already-correct behavior for Operator).**

Rationale (review HIGH finding #3, verified): Operator's reuse path is dead code as designed -- `_wiring._resolve_condition` has no `parse_condition` expression fallback (confirmed: post-s2 "no fallback registry"), and lint's `loop_condition_unregistered` is an ERROR, so `Operator(when="status == 'retry'")` is a `ConfigurationError` today. Every Operator construct that actually compiles has `when` as an opaque registry NAME whose `condition_fn(state)` reads the WHOLE state bus -- the predicate's source node is genuinely undeterminable, so no DataFlowEdge can be honestly synthesized for it. Extending Operator support requires first deciding whether `_resolve_condition` should gain an expression fallback (a separate, deeper design question -- NOT decided here, filed as a follow-up). Shipping Operator support on top of dead code would be exactly the "ships an assertion nobody verified" defect this review process exists to catch.

## Implementation Plan

### Step 0: RED first, through the outer surface (test-side, before any src change)
Promote the 4-tuple projection into `tests/agent_spec_flow_walk.py` (repoint `test_agent_spec_phase5_reuse.py:57`), go green first so the new RED test is not contaminated by a broken shared fixture. Then add a failing test: export a Loop-modified construct and assert (a) the BranchingNode has >=1 incoming DataFlowEdge in `flow.data_flow_connections`, (b) every mapping value plus `DEFAULT_BRANCH` has an outgoing ControlFlowEdge, (c) the SYNTHESIZED predicate node's OWN inputs are also fed by a real DataFlowEdge (review MEDIUM finding -- do not let the synthesized node itself become a new unfed-node seam one hop upstream). Assert it FAILS on today's tree for reasons (a)/(c).

### Step 0b: File-size ratchet extraction, MUST land before the feature, in its own commit
All three governed files this plan touches sit at their EXACT ceilings today (tests/test_guards_file_size.py:73,74,83): `_agent_spec.py` 650/650, `_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py` 646/646, `modifiers.py` 806/806 (modifiers.py ceiling only matters if any Option-B-shaped code remains anywhere -- verify it does not, since this decision drops Option B entirely). A pure, behavior-preserving extraction (per this project's file-split procedure, docs/file-split-procedure.md) must land BEFORE this feature, with ceilings lowered in the SAME commit as the split -- never raised. Per the ratchet's refusal #2: the extraction may not become a behavior change; if a clean split requires threading callables across many functions, take the smaller extraction and say so rather than force it. Candidate split: the Loop/Operator export-lowering functions in `_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py` are a natural peer-module extraction (mirrors this project's existing `_validation_portal.py`-style split-by-concern precedent).

### Step 1-4: ToolNode synthesis for Loop
Wire a synthesized `ToolNode(tool=ServerTool(...))` between the Loop body's predicate-source output and the BranchingNode, with real `DataFlowEdge`s on both sides, using the exact pattern at `_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:196-215`. The branch input TITLE is a CHOICE, not a constraint (review correction: `_get_inferred_inputs` honours `inputs[0].title`; pyagentspec's own docstring example uses a different title) -- record `branching_mapping_key` as the chosen title explicitly, not as a hard pyagentspec requirement.

### Step 5: Regression gate (review MEDIUM finding -- this is NOT a re-classification exercise)

## Findings (research atom neograph-fe1d6.10, 2026-08-14)

### 1. The gap, verified live (not inferred)
Probe: `Construct(nodes=[seed, refine])`, `refine | Loop(when="keep_going", max_iterations=3)`, `to_agent_spec()`:
- `BranchingNode refine__loop_check` -> `inputs=['branching_mapping_key']` (json_schema `{"type":"string"}`), and **zero incoming DataFlowEdges**. All 4 data edges in the Flow are body<->body / seed->refine; none targets the branch.
- Control edges: `refine -> refine__loop_check`, `refine__loop_check --continue--> refine`, `refine__loop_check --done--> p__end`.
- `mapping={'continue':'continue','done':'done'}` (`_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:375`), so the ONLY inputs that route are the literal strings "continue"/"done" -- which **no node in the exported Flow produces**.

**Two distinct metadata-blind failure modes (worth separating; the ticket text says only "cannot determine which branch"):**
- **Loop = HARD FAIL.** Unmatched key -> `BranchingNode.DEFAULT_BRANCH` ("default"), and there is **no ControlFlowEdge from `default`** -> the foreign runtime dead-ends. Not a wrong-branch, a stuck flow.
- **Operator = SILENT WRONG BEHAVIOUR.** `mapping={'true':'pause','false':'default'}` (`:636`) and the `default` arm IS wired (`_agent_spec.py:337`), so a metadata-blind runtime always falls to `default` and the HITL gate **never pauses**. Silent seam, the exact class the North star forbids.

### 2. pyagentspec 26.1.2 semantics (read from installed source)
- `flows/nodes/branchingnode.py:120-137`: `DEFAULT_INPUT="branching_mapping_key"`; `_get_inferred_inputs` takes only the **title** from a supplied `inputs[0]` and **always re-wraps it as `StringProperty`**. So the branch key is always string-typed; `mapping` is pure **equality on the stringified input**. There is no expression/comparison capability in a BranchingNode.
- `property.py:446-460` `json_schema_is_castable_to`: *"Every value of any type can be cast to a string"* -> `schema_b.type == "string"` returns True unconditionally. **Verified live**: a `DataFlowEdge(source_node=refine, source_output='score' (number), destination_node=refine__loop_check, destination_input='branching_mapping_key')` **constructs and validates**. So the wiring is mechanically available today; nothing in pyagentspec blocks it.
- `flows/edges/dataflowedge.py`: validates source_output in `source_node.outputs`, destination_input in `destination_node.inputs`, castable.
- **No portable expression/transform node exists**: `pyagentspec/transforms/` is message transforms only (`MessageTransform`); `tools/` is `BuiltinTool`/`ServerTool`/`ClientTool`/`RemoteTool` -- all opaque orchestrator-resolved names. There is NO way to compute a derived branch key declaratively in-Flow. **Therefore the reduction must be done either by the mapping itself (equality) or by a real neograph node upstream.** This is the load-bearing constraint on the whole design.

### 3. How neograph represents the condition today
- `Loop.when: str | Callable[[Any], bool]` (`modifiers.py:608`); `Operator.when: str` (`:578`).
- Export **already rejects a callable Loop.when** with a good ConfigurationError (`_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:365-371`) -- so at export time `when` is always a `str`.
- But at COMPILE time `_wiring._resolve_condition` (`_wiring.py:96-112`) resolves a string **only** through the per-compile `conditions={}` dict -- *"post-s2: no fallback registry"*, and **no `parse_condition` fallback**. So the canonical string `when` is a **registry NAME pointing at an opaque Python callable** -> nothing declarative to lower.
- `conditions.parse_condition` (`conditions.py:95`) IS a real declarative grammar: `dotted.field <op> literal`, ops `< > <= >= == !=`, literals num/bool/quoted-str, no eval. It is currently used only by `_spec_loader.py:258` (YAML), `_agent_spec_group_import.py:294` (import side, which already *discriminates* expression-vs-registry-name by try/except), and `lint.py`.
- **=> The reuse target is `conditions.parse_condition`'s grammar**, not a new mini-language in the exporter.

### 4. Predicate DOMAIN asymmetry (design-critical, easy to miss)
- **Loop**: `when` receives the node's LATEST OUTPUT (`modifiers.py:588`, `di._unwrap_loop_value`, `_wiring.py:145` loop_router). The DataFlowEdge source is therefore **always the body node already passed into `_lower_loop`** -- statically known, no upstream lookup needed.
- **Operator**: `when` receives the **WHOLE STATE object** (`_wiring.py:762-763` `condition_fn(state)`; `factory.py:334-340` same). There is no single node output it reads. A wire-able Operator export therefore needs the predicate's dotted root resolved to a *producer node + field*, which `_lower_operator` (which reads only `item.name` + `operator.when`, `:615-646`) has no access to. **Operator is strictly harder than Loop; do not assume one fix covers both.**

- `_agent_spec.py:429-483` `_emit_input_edges` -- the general node-to-node fan-in emitter (dict-form key qualification via `compose_property_title`, placeholder flat-map translation, `iterated_` MapNode prefix). - **Branch LABEL drift is a documented SILENT failure.** `_agent_spec_markers.py:44-76` warns explicitly. Import side matches `from_branch="continue"` for the loop back-edge (`loader.py:196`) and `"pause"` for Operator (`loader.py:117`); the loop's exit label `Branch.DONE` is emitted at `_agent_spec.py:264`. - **Ordering predicates are unrepresentable** in a BranchingNode mapping (`<`,`>`,`<=`,`>=`) and pyagentspec has no node that can evaluate them (see 2). Any fix covers a strict SUBSET unless the reduction is moved into a neograph node.

title: Dict-form fan-in exports dotted Property titles, which pyagentspec rejects on read-back: the Flow cannot be deserialized
description:
Found during the neograph-s7zt3.16 fix (2026-07-30), while extending the erasure repro to dict/object producers. Reproduced on develop @ 82b8836. UNRELATED to s7zt3.16's root cause -- that one is Property-SUBCLASS erasure; this one is an invalid Property TITLE and fails before any neograph import code runs.

SYMPTOM: to_agent_spec() on any pipeline with a dict-form fan-in consumer produces a Flow that Flow.from_dict() CANNOT read back.

  Node.scripted('consumer', fn='y', inputs={'seed': DictBag}, outputs=Result)
  Flow.from_dict(to_agent_spec(c).to_dict())
  -> TypeError: ValueError: 'error' required in context

That TypeError is pyagentspec's own error-reporting path breaking while it tries to RAISE the real error (pydanticdeserializationplugin.py:66 builds a ValidationError from a value_error without the required ctx['error']). The real, masked message is:

  Value error, Titles of properties should not contain special characters or blank space. Found: 'seed.entries'

ROOT CAUSE: _agent_spec_placeholders.py:161 (_properties_for) builds the dict-form input properties by MUTATING the title after construction:

    for p in props:
        p.title = f'{key}.{p.title}'

pyagentspec's Property validates its title at construction and REJECTS dots, but the model does not use validate_assignment, so post-construction mutation slips straight past the validator. The invalid title serializes happily; from_dict re-validates and refuses it.

BLAST RADIUS -- large. Dict-form is the shape the @node decorator ALWAYS produces for a typed upstream param (see tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py::TestDictFormFanInRoundTrip, whose own docstring says so). So essentially every @node pipeline with a typed upstream param exports Agent Spec that no conforming reader -- including pyagentspec itself -- can load. For an interchange format that is the whole point of the feature.

WHY IT HID: TestDictFormFanInRoundTrip asserts the IN-MEMORY path only (from_agent_spec(flow)), never Flow.from_dict(flow.to_dict()). The JSON path for dict-form fan-in has never been exercised.

FIX DIRECTION (needs design, do not guess): the dotted '{upstream}.{field}' convention is load-bearing on the import side (loader un-flattens it, and Option F's flat map is keyed by it). Options: (a) pick a separator pyagentspec accepts and change both sides in lockstep, (b) keep the bare field title and carry the upstream key in a neograph/* metadata marker like the other structural facts, (c) upstream a validate_assignment/allowed-characters change. title: Agent Spec export overrides a field's title with the nested model's title, silently collapsing two fields into one
description:
Found during the neograph-s7zt3.16 architect review (2026-07-30) while probing whether Property.json_schema can carry a $ref. Reproduced on develop @ 82b8836. UNRELATED to s7zt3.16's root cause (that one is Flow.from_dict Property-subclass erasure on the IMPORT side; this one is on the EXPORT side and needs no serialization at all).

REPRO -- no from_dict involved, fails in memory:

  class Leaf(BaseModel):
      x: int
  class Shared(BaseModel):
      a: Leaf
      b: Leaf

  props = model_to_agent_spec_properties(Shared)
  # exported titles: ['Leaf', 'Leaf']      <- field names 'a' and 'b' are GONE
  agent_spec_properties_to_types(props, name='SharedRebuilt')
  lookup_type('SharedRebuilt').model_fields
  # rebuilt fields: ['Leaf']               <- TWO fields collapsed into ONE

ROOT CAUSE: spec_types._annotation_to_property (spec_types.py:446-449). When a field's schema is a JSON pointer (which Pydantic emits whenever a nested model is referenced MORE THAN ONCE, hoisting it into $defs), the ref branch recurses with title=defs[def_name].get('title', title) -- it prefers the DEFINITION's title over the FIELD's name. So the property is titled after the model ('Leaf'), not after the field ('a'). The import side then uses Property.title as the field name (agent_spec_properties_to_types), so both fields rebuild under the same name and the second overwrites the first.

WHY IT HID: Pydantic only emits $ref/$defs when a nested model appears more than once. A model with a single nested model of each type inlines, keeps the field title, and round-trips correctly -- which is every existing fixture.

SEVERITY: this is a SILENT downgrade -- no error, no warning, just a model with fewer fields than it started with. That is worse than s7zt3.16, which at least fails loud. It violates the fail-loud-over-fail-soft North Star directly.

LIKELY FIX: the ref branch must keep the FIELD's title and use the definition only for the SHAPE -- i.e. pass title=title through, not defs[def_name].get('title', title). Verify against the ObjectProperty branch, which does keep the field name (title=field_name at :474). Check whether any existing export fixture depends on the model-title behavior before changing it.

TDD: the repro above is the red test. Extend to list[Leaf] alongside a bare Leaf (the 'c' field in the probe kept its own title, so the two branches disagree today).
close_reason: $ref export branch now keeps the FIELD's title instead of the referenced definition's, so same-typed nested fields no longer collapse into one on import (_agent_spec_types.py:_annotation_to_property). TDD: 2 red-first tests in tests/test_agent_spec_types.py::TestRefFieldKeepsItsOwnTitle. Golden snapshot had pinned the bug (24 list-item titles Elem->groups), patched surgically + documented.

title: Forward-port 0.7.4 to develop — both shipped fixes are ABSENT from develop and would regress in 0.8.0
description:
## The gap
The 0.7.4 release branch was cut from `main`, and its 7 commits were never merged back to `develop`. `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main develop` -> NO.

Verified absent on develop:
- **neograph-yqrsz** — `_llm_dispatch.py` on develop still has the unguarded arm:
  `case Raw(raw_text=raw_text, usage=_usage): _raise_decoded_none(...)`. The empty-response bug is LIVE on develop.
- **neograph-s65y2** — no `StateKeys.TRACE_ID`, no `trace_id_of`, no `_identity_binds`, no trace-id derivation.
- Also absent: the `langfuse>=3.11` floor, `TestConfigCarrierIsTheOnlySite`, `TestStructuredRetryBudgetParityAcrossTwins`, the config-carrier migrations, and the `make release-gate` / `live` marker process change.

## Why it is P1
If 0.8.0 ships from develop as-is, BOTH fixes regress — shipped, then unshipped. Worse, **their beads are already closed** (develop commit b3e40d2, 'both shipped in 0.7.4 and verified downstream'), so nothing in the tracker would catch it. A closed ticket plus absent code is a silent regression by construction.

Forward-porting IS the established convention, not an open question: develop already carries the 0.7.2 hotfix (ffb756e) and the 0.7.3 hotfix (06ed6d4). 0.7.4 is the one that was missed.

## Blocks the follow-ups
Two of the three 0.7.4 follow-ups are UNACTIONABLE on develop until this lands, because they extend code that only exists on main:
- **neograph-lwssj** (caller correlation_id) — its implementation sketch binds into `_execute._identity_binds`, which does not exist on develop (it is still `_run_id_binds`, run-id only).
- **neograph-syhr2** (setdefault copy-not-mutate) — its remedy is to extend `TestConfigCarrierIsTheOnlySite`, which does not exist on develop.
- **neograph-kc7ci** (Langfuse monoculture) — design-level, but its stated interaction is with the trace-id derivation, also absent.

## Scope — it is a REAL merge, not a fast-forward
`git merge-tree` reports conflicts in 5 files, because both lines moved the same code:
`pyproject.toml` (version + langfuse pin), `src/neograph/__init__.py` (`__version__`),
`src/neograph/_state_keys.py`, `src/neograph/runner.py`, `tests/test_guards_llm_runtime.py`
(develop has its own guard/allowlist churn; the 0.7.4 side adds LINE_BUDGETS raises,
the `_llm_retry` name allowlist entry, and two new guard classes).

Version resolution needs a decision: develop is on the 0.8.0 track, so take develop's `__version__`/`version` and 0.7.4's langfuse pin + CHANGELOG entry.

## Suggested approach
`/dev-practices:semantic-merge` — the conflict surface is exactly its use case (union-of-intent per file, then a behaviour-level coherence gate). Afterwards run `make release-gate` on develop, and confirm the two guard classes and both regression suites are present and green.

## Acceptance
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main develop` -> YES
- `tests/modes/test_structured_retry.py` EmptyResponse suite present and green on develop
- `tests/test_observe_trace_correlation.py` + `tests/test_observe_trace_live.py` present; live gate green
- `make release-gate` green on develop
notes:
MERGE SURFACE SIZED (2026-07-30, before any resolution)

develop is 20ff849; origin/main is 105b165; merge-base ef6bed5. 7 commits to forward-port.

Textual dry-run: 6 conflicts (CHANGELOG.md, pyproject.toml, __init__.py, runner.py, tests/test_guards_llm_runtime.py, uv.lock).

THE CONFLICTS ARE NOT THE RISK. The risk is the files that auto-merged CLEANLY into code that no longer lives there. The neograph-3ffdg wave (19 splits, landed today) relocated large parts of exactly the modules 0.7.4 touches:
  _llm_retry.py   -> null-default + json-extract clusters moved to _null_defaults.py / _json_extract.py
  runner.py       -> recursion-budget, checkpoint-rewind/driver and OBSERVE clusters moved out
  _execute.py     -> unchanged, but its _identity_binds neighbourhood is adjacent to moved code
Verified concretely: the 0.7.4 trace-correlation change edits _merge_observe_callbacks (Langfuse CallbackHandler construction + trace_context). That function is NO LONGER IN runner.py -- neograph-3ffdg.9 moved it to _observe.py. A textual merge would either conflict there or, worse, apply the change to a file where the target no longer exists.

CONCLUSION: this is a semantic merge, not a textual one. Resolving per-file by "union of intent" against the CURRENT module layout, then verifying at the behaviour level (both 0.7.4 fixes must be provably live on develop, not merely present in a diff). Using /dev-practices:semantic-merge.

Acceptance is behavioural, not textual:
  1. the empty-structured-response retry actually re-prompts (neograph-yqrsz)
  2. the Langfuse trace id is actually derived from run_id and lands in config (neograph-s65y2)
  3. full gate at the post-merge baseline with no test skipped
DONE — merged in 906a762 (amended), develop now at 55edaff and pushed. git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main develop = YES.

THE FIND (the reason this needed a semantic merge, not a textual one):
0.7.4 edits _merge_observe_callbacks to derive the Langfuse trace id. neograph-3ffdg.9 had moved that function from runner.py into _observe.py hours earlier -- and _observe.py does not exist on main, so no merge machinery could route the change there. Git resolved runner.py without complaint. The scaffolding all auto-merged cleanly (StateKeys.TRACE_ID, _config_carrier.trace_id_of, the docstrings referencing it), and the ONE line that computes Langfuse.create_trace_id(seed=run_id) existed nowhere in src/. Every conflict resolved, every test green, feature absent. Found by auditing each 0.7.4 symbol against the merged tree instead of trusting the conflict list; applied to _observe.py by hand.

Gate (behavioural, per the acceptance recorded before starting):
  full suite 4071 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed (develop was 4043/2; +28 from 0.7.4 tests, +2 skips = the live-Langfuse pair). No drop.
  acceptance 1 neograph-yqrsz: tests/modes/test_structured_retry.py 28 passed
  acceptance 2 neograph-s65y2: tests/test_observe_trace_correlation.py 6 passed
  ruff + mypy clean, 122 source files.
  runner.py ceiling 685 -> 679 (shrank in the merge).

TWO PROCESS NOTES worth keeping:
1. The ff-only merge into the main checkout printed "Updating 1749ec9..906a762" AND "Aborting" -- it did NOT advance, blocked by .hypothesis/ cache files. I initially truncated that output with tail -2 and nearly missed it; the assertion on merge-base is what caught it. Never truncate state-changing git output.
2. I ran git add -A in the merge worktree, which swept 65 .hypothesis/ test-cache artifacts into the merge commit. Stripped by amend, then had to restore .hypothesis to develop-exact state because git rm -r --cached had also untracked 802 files develop legitimately tracks. .hypothesis/ is NOT in .gitignore -- that is the underlying hazard and is worth a separate ticket.
close_reason: 0.7.4 forward-ported in 906a762. Both fixes proven live behaviourally; the trace-derivation hunk the merge silently dropped was found and applied to _observe.py. 4071 passed.

title: Add repo-wide 500-line file-size guard with a shrink-only, per-file ceiling allowlist
description:
Maintainer directive (2026-07-29): files expand indefinitely under this codebase's own development pattern -- 9 files are already over 1000 lines, 19 are over 500. The only existing enforcement is test_guards_ir_compiler.py's compiler.py-specific ratchet (< 775, already raised twice this epic). Generalize it.

RULE: every src/neograph/*.py file must be under 500 lines UNLESS explicitly allowlisted. The allowlist is a per-file CEILING dict (file -> current line count), not a blanket exemption -- mirrors this project's own established ratchet-allowlist discipline (may only SHRINK, growth blocked and fixed in-PR, never deferred). A file already in the allowlist can shrink freely (lowers its own ceiling when it does, via a companion 'ceiling must equal or exceed the file's real current count, and must be exactly right, not merely sufficient' assertion so the ceiling can't drift stale-loose), but can never grow past its current ceiling, and a file NOT in the allowlist must stay under 500 outright.

INITIAL ALLOWLIST (current real line counts, 2026-07-29 -- verify exact numbers via wc -l before writing, do not trust this list once time passes):
di.py=506, spec_types.py=521, node.py=522, describe_type.py=552, _oracle.py=650,
_llm_retry.py=658, state.py=659, _tool_loop.py=727, compiler.py=761, decorators.py=975,
factory.py=1007, _agent_cycle.py=1054, lint.py=1068, modifiers.py=1116, runner.py=1225,
loader.py=1393, _wiring.py=1461, _agent_spec.py=1561, forward.py=1578.

compiler.py ALREADY has its own dedicated guard (test_guards_ir_compiler.py, < 775) -- do not leave two overlapping guards making near-identical claims about the same file. Retire the old compiler.py-specific assertion and fold compiler.py into the new general allowlist mechanism (ceiling should be its current real count per the list above, tightening its existing 775 cap, not loosening it). Verify no other file has a similar file-specific hand-rolled guard before writing the general one (grep test_guards_*.py for other per-file line-count asserts).

NOT in scope for this ticket: refactoring any of the 19 files down. This ticket ONLY adds the guard + allowlist (stops future growth on allowlisted files, and forbids any NEW file or currently-under-500 file from crossing 500 without an explicit, reviewed allowlist addition). The refactor-down work is separate, tracked by a parallel research/design effort (see neograph-s7zt3's epic notes for the swarm dispatched 2026-07-29) and will land as its own follow-up tickets per file/cluster.

Write the guard failing-first (per this project's own guard-first discipline): assert every src/neograph/*.py file is either under 500 lines or has an exact-match entry in the allowlist dict, plus the allowlist-can-only-shrink test (compare against a git-historical snapshot or a committed baseline the same way the duplication-baseline/obligation-allowlist ratchets already do it elsewhere in this codebase -- reuse that existing mechanism's shape, don't invent a new one).
design:
## Core Invariant
Every Python module shipped under `src/neograph/` is either under 500 lines or carries
an explicit, committed per-file ceiling that EXACTLY equals its real current line count
-- so growth past that number is impossible without a reviewable diff to a literal, and
no ceiling can ever sit stale-loose above the file it governs.

## Open questions: ALL RESOLVED (was "NEEDS USER INPUT (three)")
Do not read the three flags as open. #1 (exactness semantics) and #2 (glob scope) are
settled in the MAINTAINER DECISIONS block in the notes; #3 (which number list to trust)
is settled by the FACT CORRECTION block -- re-derive, never transcribe. Settled values:
strict equality (`ceiling == real count`, no tolerance band); recursive `rglob` including
`src/neograph/testing/`, 21 seed entries; drop ONLY the `_llm_retry.py` entry from
LINE_BUDGETS.

## Implementation Plan (refined per architect review, atom neograph-bfjto.12)

1. **Create `tests/test_guards_file_size.py`** (new file; justified in Findings Q4).
   Import ONLY `pathlib` (+ `pytest` for the tmp_path meta-tests). **No `re` anywhere**
   -- exempt-by-construction from `test_guards_meta.py` Discipline 1 (reviewer verified
   this in code at test_guards_meta.py:39-195: `_analyze`'s pass-0 builds re_aliases
   from imports, so a module with no `re` import yields zero violations). Module
   docstring carries the ratchet contract in the style of
   `test_guards_assertion_strength.py:1-19`: the 500 rule, the shrink-only ceiling
   discipline, "growth blocked and fixed in-PR, never deferred", the anti-dead-entry
   rule, the note that a ruff-format pass legitimately requires a number update, and a
   pointer to `docs/design/file-size-refactor-master-proposal-2026-07-29.md`.
   The docstring must ALSO record two scope facts honestly (review LOW-3a):
   - the two surviving `test_guards_assembly.py` caps (330 / 400) are kept because
     their file sets are DISJOINT from this allowlist (all 10 governed files are under
     500; max 289 under the 330 cap, max 373 under the 400 cap) and because extending
     strict equality to 10 more files was never scoped -- NOT because they are
     "complementary" or clean. Both in fact carry the same stale-loose headroom this
     ticket exists to eliminate (330 vs 289 real; 400 vs 373 real); loose semantics
     there are explicitly out of scope, not endorsed.
   - one line rejecting the alternative of consolidating all four mechanisms into a
     single ceiling table: purer per CLAUDE.md's Portal-rollout single-source lesson,
     but it taxes 10 files the maintainer never scoped. Rejected deliberately.

2. **REUSE the counting method, and split the checker in TWO** (review MEDIUM-4).
   Copy `len(path.read_text().splitlines())` from `tests/test_guards_assembly.py:415`
   (verified == `wc -l` for all 93 src files -- Findings Q7). Factor into TWO pure
   module-level checkers, each taking the root as a PARAMETER so both are meta-testable
   against tmp_path without touching real `src/`:
   - `_size_violations(root: Path, allowlist: dict[str, int], limit: int) -> list[str]`
     -- covers over-limit-not-allowlisted AND ceiling-mismatch
   - `_dead_allowlist_entries(root: Path, allowlist: dict[str, int], limit: int) -> list[str]`
     -- covers missing-file AND now-under-limit
   Two functions, not one: step 4 needs three independent live assertions and step 7
   must mutation-target the strict-equality case and the dead-entry case SEPARATELY;
   one function would force fragile substring-filtering of returned strings. Mirrors
   the `_line_cap_violations` / `_symbol_location_violations` pairing at
   `tests/test_guards_assembly.py:407-435`.

3. **Seed `ALLOWLIST: dict[str, int]`** (posix-relative path -> exact line count), keyed
   like `test_guards_assertion_strength.ALLOWLIST`. Re-derive EVERY number with `wc -l`
   in the same session as the write -- both number lists in the ticket are known-wrong;
   the scan's 21 are correct as of HEAD b18cc19 and were independently confirmed by the
   reviewer, but MUST be re-verified at write time. No per-entry reason strings (all 21
   would say the same thing); one docstring pointer instead.
   **Formatting is load-bearing** (review MEDIUM-2): one entry per line, sorted by posix
   path. That is the cheap structural mitigation that keeps ~19 parallel refactor
   branches editing disjoint lines and holds the merge-conflict surface near zero.

4. **Write the guard failing-first, three live assertions** (guard-first discipline:
   write, watch it fail, then make it pass):
   - `test_no_unallowlisted_file_over_limit` -- every `rglob('*.py')` under
     `src/neograph` (skip `__pycache__`): if not in ALLOWLIST, `n < 500`. Message names
     the file, its count, and both remedies (split it, or add a reviewed entry).
   - `test_allowlisted_files_are_at_their_exact_ceiling` -- `n == ALLOWLIST[f]`. The
     ticket's "exactly right, not merely sufficient" companion; blocks growth AND
     forbids stale-loose numbers in one assertion.
   - `test_no_dead_allowlist_entries` -- an entry whose file is MISSING, or is now
     `< 500`, is DEAD and must be DELETED (never lowered to a sub-500 number, which
     would grant a private ceiling to a file the plain 500 rule should govern). This is
     what drives the allowlist toward empty as the refactor wave lands.
   **Failure-message specificity is a requirement, not polish** (review MEDIUM-2):
   under strict equality assertions 2 and 3 are the guard's NORMAL-OPERATION surface --
   they will fire on nearly every PR touching the 21 largest files, not just on abuse.
   - assertion 2 must print: file, declared ceiling, real count, and the EXACT
     replacement literal to paste, e.g. `"forward.py": 1571,  # was 1578`
   - assertion 3 must distinguish its two dead causes (file missing vs now under 500)
     and say DELETE, not lower.
   **Anti-vacuity tripwire** (review LOW-3b): assert the rglob saw a plausible file
   count (84 today, or a documented floor), with a message saying the SRC root path is
   wrong. Precedent: `tests/test_guards_agent_spec_llm_construction_sites.py:189-294`.
   Without it the whole guard passes green against an empty/wrong directory.

5. **Retire the overlapping compiler.py guard**: delete `tests/test_guards_ir_compiler.py`
   lines 522-551 -- the whole method `TestCompilerWiringSplit.test_compiler_under_600_lines`
   (stale name; it asserts `< 775`) including its 24-line cap-raise-history docstring.
   KEEP the class and its two symbol-home siblings (`test_wiring_module_exists`,
   `test_wiring_functions_in_correct_module`). compiler.py enters the ALLOWLIST at its
   exact real count (761), TIGHTENING the retired 775 cap. Reviewer re-confirmed 522-551
   is exactly the method and that 553 starts the sibling to keep; grep for `775` /
   `test_compiler_under_600_lines` hits only that method -- no doc edit needed.

6. **Resolve the one other overlap**: delete the `"_llm_retry.py": 665` entry (and its
   comment history) from `LINE_BUDGETS` in `tests/test_guards_llm_runtime.py:329-392`,
   leaving a one-line comment that the general file-size guard now owns that file at an
   exact ceiling of 658 -- strictly tighter than the 665 budget, which had itself
   drifted stale-loose by 7 lines. Leave the other five budgets and both
   `test_guards_assembly.py` caps alone, for the disjoint-file-sets reason recorded in
   step 1's docstring mandate.

7. **Mutation meta-tests** (non-optional; this repo proves its guards). Copy the tmp_path
   pattern at `tests/test_guards_assembly.py:505-522` and the synthetic-source trio at
   `tests/test_guards_assertion_strength.py:113-131`:
   (a) a 600-line tmp_path file not in the allowlist IS flagged by `_size_violations`;
   (b) a 400-line tmp_path file is NOT flagged;
   (c) an allowlisted tmp_path file whose real count differs from its ceiling by +1 AND
       by -1 is flagged BOTH ways -- proves strict equality, not `>=`;
   (d) an allowlist entry for a 400-line tmp_path file is reported by
       `_dead_allowlist_entries`; and an entry for a missing file likewise.
   (c) is load-bearing: without it a `>=` implementation passes every other test.

8. **Gate**: `uv run pytest tests/test_guards_file_size.py tests/test_guards_ir_compiler.py
   tests/test_guards_llm_runtime.py -q`, then the full `uv run pytest` (bare -- there is
   no `dev` extra), then `make quality`. Re-derive counts one final time immediately
   before commit; if a number moved because another ticket landed, LOWER/CORRECT the
   dict -- never widen it.

9. **Coordinate with the in-flight refactor wave** (review MEDIUM-1 -- the finding that
   most affects other people's work). 19 OPEN `neograph-3ffdg` children (3 P1, ready
   NOW) plus `neograph-s7zt3.11` each change a governed file's line count, so each will
   turn this gate RED by design -- while 3ffdg's own epic text sets its acceptance bar
   at "existing test suite passing unchanged". That contradiction would otherwise land
   on 19 separate implementers with no instruction anywhere. The guard STILL LANDS
   FIRST (it is P1 stop-the-bleeding, and 3ffdg is precisely the wave it must govern;
   deferring it runs the largest refactor wave in the repo ungoverned). So:
   append a note to BOTH `neograph-3ffdg` and `neograph-s7zt3.11` stating that any
   commit changing a governed file MUST lower -- or DELETE, if the file drops under
   500 -- its ALLOWLIST entry in the SAME commit, and that a red
   `test_guards_file_size` is the EXPECTED, CORRECT signal of a successful shrink, not
   a regression to be worked around.

10. **Document the invariant where agents will look** (review MEDIUM-3). The guard binds

title: structured output path: an empty/undecodable response RAISES without retry, while a ValidationError gets max_retries
description:
The structured output path retries a ValidationError but RAISES on an undecodable/empty response, so the single most likely transient provider failure has zero retries while a less likely one has three.

## Where
`neograph/_llm_dispatch.py`, `_acall_structured` / `_call_structured` (async twin at ~:239):

    case Parsed(model=parsed, usage=usage):
        return parsed, usage
    case Raw(dsml=True, raw_text=..., ...):
        ...arecover_dsml() attempt...
    case Raw(raw_text=raw_text, usage=_usage):
        _raise_decoded_none(output_model, raw_text)          # <-- RAISES. never retries.
    case Failed(error=err, ...) if isinstance(err, ValidationError):
        if attempts >= max_retries: _raise_structured_retry_exhausted(...)
        attempts += 1
        current_messages = structured_retry_messages(...)     # <-- retries

An EMPTY provider response (`content == ''`) has nothing to validate, so it never becomes
`Failed(ValidationError)`. It becomes `Raw`, and `_raise_decoded_none` fires on the FIRST
occurrence. `max_retries` is not consulted on that arm at all.

By contrast the json_mode path handles it: `_parse_json_response` raises `ExecutionError` on empty
("Detect non-JSON content: empty result"), and `_ainvoke_json_with_retry` catches `ExecutionError`
and re-prompts up to `max_retries`.

## Why it matters (a real incident, not a hypothetical)
Downstream (ox-troubleshooting-demo) ran a two-arm A/B over 64 held-out scenarios x 3 repeats. One
arm lost **70 of 192 runs**; the other lost **5**. 68 of the 70 were identical:

    ExecutionError: structured output decoded to None
      expected: valid TriageReport
      found: unparseable response (first 200 chars): ''

69 of the 70 fell inside a single UTC hour — a provider empty-response incident that happened to
land on whichever arm was running. The eval's majority gate counts an errored run as a failing vote,
so the outage was published as "the knowledge base under test makes the agent reason worse". With
the errored runs excluded the comparison REVERSES (0.943 vs 0.824). A conclusion about model
behaviour was drawn from a retry gap.

## The fail-loud intent is right; the missing retry is the bug
`_raise_decoded_none`'s docstring is explicit and correct: "Fail loud on the structured path's
parsed=None silent variant (undecodable response), not surface None which the write boundary
swallows." Nothing here argues for returning None quietly. The ask is that it fail loud only AFTER
the same bounded re-prompt budget the ValidationError arm already gets.

## Suggested fix
Treat `Raw` (non-DSML, undecodable/empty) as retryable on the same `attempts`/`max_retries` counter
as `Failed(ValidationError)`, re-prompting via `structured_retry_messages` (or a variant whose
feedback says "your previous response was empty" rather than quoting a validation error), and raise
`_raise_decoded_none` only once the budget is exhausted. That keeps fail-loud semantics, keeps the
single retry counter, and closes the asymmetry.

Two smaller notes:
- An empty response and a non-JSON response are different failure modes; the retry FEEDBACK message
  probably wants to distinguish them, since "your JSON was malformed" is confusing advice for a
  model that returned nothing.
- Consider whether the ceiling should be shared with, or separate from, the transport-level retry —
  an empty 200 is arguably a transport symptom rather than a modelling one.

## Reproduction (no network)
A fake whose `with_structured_output(include_raw=True).ainvoke` returns
`{"parsed": None, "raw": AIMessage(content="")}` on its first call and a valid parse afterwards.
Current behaviour: raises on the first call. Expected: re-prompts, gets the valid parse, returns it.
A working version of this fake lives downstream in
`ox-troubleshooting-demo/tests/test_triage_survives_an_empty_response.py`.

## Downstream mitigation already applied (context, not a fix for this)
ox-troubleshooting-demo moved its `triage` agent node from `output_strategy='structured'` to
`'json_mode'` (commit fcac8a6), because for an AGENT node the strategy selects only the parse-failure
FALLBACK and json_mode's fallback is the retrying one. That works around the asymmetry for that
project; it does not remove it for anyone using `structured` deliberately.
design:
## Root Cause
An empty/undecodable provider response has nothing to validate, so it never becomes Failed(ValidationError). `_llm_structured_compat` classifies {parsed: None, raw: <empty>, parsing_error: None} as Raw(dsml=False). The dispatch arm `case Raw(raw_text=..., usage=_usage)` in _llm_dispatch.py (:160-161 sync, :238-239 async) then calls `_raise_decoded_none` unconditionally — the attempts/max_retries counter driving the adjacent Failed(ValidationError) arm is never consulted on this branch. So the MOST likely transient provider failure gets zero retries while a less likely one gets max_retries.

## Core Invariant
Fail-loud is preserved: an undecodable structured response still raises ExecutionError, with the same message. What changes is only WHEN — the raise happens after the same bounded re-prompt budget the ValidationError arm already spends, on the same single `attempts`/`max_retries` counter. No new counter, no silent None, no unbounded loop, and the sync/async twins stay behaviourally identical.

## Fix Approach (REFINED — atom neograph-y06pq.13, absorbs review findings #2/#4/#6a)

### In _llm_dispatch.py, both twins — make the non-DSML Raw arm retryable
Replace the unconditional raise with the same guard shape the ValidationError arm uses, on the SAME counter:

    case Raw(raw_text=raw_text, usage=_usage):
        if attempts >= max_retries:
            _raise_decoded_none(output_model, raw_text)
        attempts += 1
        current_messages = empty_response_retry_messages(current_messages, raw_text, output_model)
        continue

REUSE `_raise_decoded_none` UNCHANGED as the exhaustion raiser. Do NOT add a new exhaustion helper:
- its message already says the right thing; only the timing was wrong,
- tests/modes/test_llm_internals.py:4897 asserts the literal 'decoded to None' and must keep passing unmodified,
- TestLlmResponsibilityDiscipline (test_guards_llm_runtime.py:201-218) pins the exact function set of _llm_dispatch.py, so a new helper would cost an allowlist entry for no gain.
NET NEW FUNCTIONS IN _llm_dispatch.py: ZERO.

### In _llm_retry.py — one new shared pure helper
`empty_response_retry_messages(messages, raw_text, output_model) -> list`, sited directly beside `structured_retry_messages` (its sibling). Required by TestTwinThinness: a value-builder / message-assembly block may not appear word-for-word in both twins, so the assembly lives in ONE pure helper both twins call. The twins duplicate only the awaiting control skeleton, which is irreducible.

Its feedback must distinguish EMPTY from MALFORMED — telling a model that returned nothing that 'your JSON was malformed' is confusing, actively-wrong advice. It has no ValidationError to quote (that is precisely why this arm exists), so it cannot reuse `build_structured_repair_message`.

### Tests
Keep the 5 red tests from atom .2. ADD one asserting the re-prompt feedback names the empty/no-content condition and does NOT claim a validation/malformed failure (review finding #6a) — without it the wording silently regresses to the ValidationError phrasing.

### Docstring drift (fix in the same commit)
`_call_structured`'s docstring :124-125 still says this arm 'preserve[s] the legacy passthrough: return (None, usage) without re-prompting'. Already false (it raises) and doubly false after this change. Update it and the async twin's contract text.

## Out of scope — do not fold in
- Transport-level retry unification (the ticket's second smaller note): separate concern, separate ticket if wanted.
- Usage/token accounting across the empty-retry (the discarded `usage=_usage`): LOW, and identical to the ValidationError arm's existing behavior. Changing it here would be scope creep.

title: 269 Agent Spec tests silently skip under the project's own gate (pyagentspec not in any dev group)
description:
Found during neograph-tjpn4's architect review (atom neograph-dw76v.4, 2026-07-28) and then
verified decisively against a clean environment.

## The seam

269 tests -- the ENTIRE Agent Spec surface -- are `pytest.importorskip("pyagentspec")`-gated
across 14 files, but `pyagentspec` is declared ONLY in `[project.optional-dependencies].agent-spec`.
It is in neither `[project.optional-dependencies].dev` nor `[dependency-groups].dev`.

Therefore the project's own gate does not run them:
- `make quality` runs bare `uv run pytest -q` -> `[dependency-groups].dev` only -> no pyagentspec.
- The AGENTS.md-documented `uv run --extra dev pytest` -> no pyagentspec either.

Proof (not inference):
```
$ uv run --isolated --extra dev python -c "import importlib.util as u; print(u.find_spec('pyagentspec') is not None)"
Installed 86 packages in 196ms
False
```
The suite passes 3751/3751 on THIS machine only because the local `.venv` retains pyagentspec
from an earlier `--extra agent-spec` run. On a clean checkout the same command reports a green
run with ~269 fewer tests collected -- and nothing announces the difference, because a skipped
importorskip module is not a failure and the collected count is not compared against anything.

## Why it matters beyond bookkeeping

There is NO CI test workflow. `.github/workflows/` contains only `publish.yml`. So the local
gate is the ONLY gate, and the local gate is blind to 269 tests on any environment that has not
happened to install the extra.

Concretely, this bit during neograph-tjpn4: every artifact proving that task's
zero-behaviour-change claim (`test_agent_spec_refactor_snapshot.py` byte-snapshot,
`test_agent_spec_export.py`, `test_agent_spec_matrix.py`, `test_agent_spec_construct_member.py`)
is importorskip-gated. A clean-env run would have landed that migration with its proof never
executed and the gate still green. That is precisely the "single silent seam" the project's
north star names as an existential defect rather than deferrable polish.

The same shape exists for the MCP extras (`importorskip("mcp")` x3,
`importorskip("langchain_mcp_adapters")` x2) -- but that one is DOCUMENTED and deliberate:
AGENTS.md explicitly states "no-key != no extra" and gives the
`uv run --extra dev --extra mcp-examples pytest` command, and the guard that keeps `src/neograph`
MCP-free depends on the extra staying optional. The Agent Spec case has no such documentation and
no such structural reason -- `_agent_spec.py` ships in `src/neograph` and its tests are the
primary proof surface for an actively-developed epic (neograph-s7zt3).

## Options (pick one; they are not equivalent)

1. **Move `pyagentspec` into `[dependency-groups].dev`** (auto-installed by `uv run pytest`),
   mirroring what was already done for `langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite` and `pytest-examples` --
   both of which have an in-file comment explaining they live there specifically "so the file
   collects under the bare test command". This is the established precedent and the smallest
   change. Keep the `agent-spec` extra as the consumer-facing optional dependency.
2. **Make the skip loud**: a session-scoped conftest check that FAILS (not skips) when a
   pyagentspec-gated module is deselected unless an explicit opt-out env var is set. Preserves
   the optional install but converts silence into noise.
3. **Assert a collected-count floor** in a guard test. Cheapest, but brittle and it does not
   actually run the tests.

Recommendation: (1), with (2) as a follow-up if the optionality must be preserved for packaging
reasons. (1) alone closes the hole for the default gate.

## Acceptance

- `uv run --isolated --extra dev pytest --collect-only -q` collects the SAME number of tests as a
  run with `--extra agent-spec` (i.e. 269 no longer vanish).
- `make quality` on a clean checkout runs the Agent Spec suite.
- AGENTS.md's test-conventions section states the resulting gate command, and says plainly which
  extras are still required for which suites (the MCP note is the model to copy).
- A note in the file(s) explaining WHY the dep sits where it does, matching the
  `langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite` / `pytest-examples` comment precedent.
design:
## Root Cause

Proximate: `pyagentspec` sits ONLY in `[project.optional-dependencies].agent-spec`, which no
default-gate command installs, so 271 `importorskip`-gated tests silently collect as zero and
32 more hard-fail.

Structural: **the project has TWO `dev` namespaces** -- `[project.optional-dependencies].dev`
(an extra) and `[dependency-groups].dev` (uv's default group) -- the toolchain lives in the
former while the gate reads the latter, and nothing says which one a new dev dep belongs in.
That ambiguity is what put `pyagentspec` in the wrong place, and it also stranded
`pytest-asyncio`, `pytest`, `ruff` and `mypy`. Clean-checkout `make quality` is therefore not
'silently green' as filed -- it is RED (83 failures), for two independent reasons.

## Invariant

Every dependency the quality gate needs is declared in the ONE place the default gate installs
from, and every dependency-conditional test gate (`importorskip`, `find_spec`->`skipif`) is
either backed by that place or exempted in writing with a structural reason.

## Fix Approach (REFINED -- atom neograph-7iflp, after review verdict NEEDS_REFINEMENT)

Ordering matters: **step 1 lands BEFORE or WITH step 2, never after.** Once `pyagentspec` is
always installed, the environmental proof that core is Agent-Spec-free is gone; the guard must
already be standing when that happens.

### 1. [F2, HIGH -- precondition] Subprocess core-purity guard for agent-spec
Add the MCP-shaped guard: a subprocess runs `import neograph` and asserts `pyagentspec` never
enters `sys.modules`. Model verbatim on
`tests/test_mcp_battery.py::test_neograph_core_imports_with_zero_mcp_deps`. Verified by grep:
no such guard exists today for agent-spec -- the claim in `_agent_spec.py` /
`spec_types.py` ('core stays Agent-Spec-free by default') is currently proven only ACCIDENTALLY,
by the dep being absent. Making the dep present without this guard trades a documented safety
claim for ergonomics and re-admits a silent failure -- the exact trade the north star forbids.

### 2. [F1 row 1, HIGH] Move `pyagentspec>=26.1.0,<27` into `[dependency-groups].dev`
With a comment matching the `langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite` / `pytest-examples` precedent ('in
the default dependency-group so the file collects under the bare test command') plus the
neograph-x75es reference. Keep `[project.optional-dependencies].agent-spec` -- that is the
CONSUMER-facing optional dep and it stays. `src/neograph`'s function-local/guarded imports are
untouched: this is a test-gate change, not a packaging change.

### 3. [F1 rows 2-5, HIGH] Single-source the dev toolchain into `[dependency-groups].dev`
`pytest-asyncio` (51 async failures under the bare gate -- `asyncio_mode = "auto"` at
pyproject.toml:146 has no plugin to drive), `pytest`, `ruff`, `mypy`. Measured: `mypy` is
absent from the default-gate env entirely (it only resolved locally via `uv run` falling back
to the PATH binary); `pytest` and `ruff` are present only TRANSITIVELY via pytest-cov /
pytest-examples. Without this, acceptance criterion 2 ('`make quality` on a clean checkout runs
the Agent Spec suite') is unreachable no matter what happens to `pyagentspec`.

### 4. [F5, MEDIUM] Delete `[project.optional-dependencies].dev`; update the ~30 `--extra dev` refs
Do NOT duplicate the dev list across both namespaces -- that is the duplicated-source-of-truth
disease the modifier-combo retrospective names, and it re-opens the very ambiguity that caused
this bug. Delete the extra; update the ~30 `--extra dev` references (test docstrings,
pyproject comments, `scripts/gen_api_manifest.py`, `examples/29_portal_dynamic_flow.py`,
AGENTS.md). Consistent with the documented preference 'No backwards-compat shims at 0.x'.
FLAGGED FOR VETO: this is the one judgment call in the plan; if the extra must survive for
packaging reasons, substitute a guard asserting the toolchain lives in `[dependency-groups].dev`.

### 5. [F4, MEDIUM] Widen the guard to both spellings of the disease
`tests/test_guards_test_gate_deps.py` (already written RED in the reproduce atom) currently
detects `importorskip` only. Extend the AST detector to the `find_spec("x")` ->
`skipif(not _HAS_X)` form (7 live sites / 5 files, all MCP today, so green by luck) and route
BOTH forms through the single `GATED_IMPORT_EXEMPTIONS` table with its existing mandatory-reason,
non-vacuity and staleness checks. Add meta-tests for the new form.

### 6. [Acceptance] AGENTS.md test-conventions
State the resulting gate command plainly, and say which extras remain required for which suites
-- the existing MCP note is the shape to copy. Must reflect steps 3-4 (the command loses
`--extra dev`).

### 7. [F3, MEDIUM] DO NOTHING, deliberately -- and write down why
The 32 tests that hard-FAIL without `pyagentspec` (they lack the `importorskip` line their 13
sibling files carry) stay unguarded. Loud failure is strictly better than silent skip; adding
`importorskip` to them would EXTEND the disease this ticket exists to remove. Record the
asymmetry in the AGENTS.md note so a later cleanup pass does not 'fix' it.

### 8. [F6/F7, LOW] No action -- recorded
- F6: the `ConfigurationError('pyagentspec is not installed')` branch at `_agent_spec.py:113`
  has no test today and gains none. Pre-existing, unchanged by this fix, not a regression.
- F7: acceptance criterion 1 (collect-count parity) is verified by MEASUREMENT in the e2e-verify
  atom. No count-floor guard -- the ticket already rejected that (option 3) as brittle and it
  runs nothing. Agreed; do not add one.

### Explicitly NOT doing
Ticket options 2 (conftest loud-skip) and 3 (collected-count floor). (2) is redundant once the
dep is default-installed AND the widened guard blocks regrowth; revisit only if packaging
pressure ever forces `pyagentspec` back out of the default group. (3) is brittle and never
actually runs the tests.
notes:
## Reproduction (atom neograph-9odbk.2, 2026-07-28)

- Failing test: `tests/test_guards_test_gate_deps.py::TestImportOrSkipGatesRunUnderDefaultGate::test_every_importorskip_dep_is_in_the_default_dev_group`
- Result: 1 failed, 8 passed. Offender reported: `pyagentspec <- 13 test files`.

available on THIS machine, because the local .venv already retains pyagentspec -- an

### Measured, not inferred
```
uv run --isolated pytest --collect-only -q                    -> 3512 tests collected
uv run --isolated --extra agent-spec pytest --collect-only -q -> 3783 tests collected
```

## Trace-similar: other instances of the same bug (atom neograph-9odbk.3, 2026-07-28)

Bug category: **a test-gate blindness -- a dependency-conditional skip whose backing dep the
project's default gate does not install, so the tests are absent from the only gate that runs.**
Swept the whole suite for every mechanism that can produce that shape.

### 1. `pytest.importorskip` -- the reported instance, plus one exempt family
Exhaustive AST scan (see reproduce notes). Two families only:
- `pyagentspec` x13 files, 271 tests -> **THE BUG**. Undeclared, undocumented.
- `mcp` / `langchain_mcp_adapters` x2 files (test_mcp_fakes.py, test_mcp_examples_e2e.py),
  16 tests -> deliberate, documented in AGENTS.md, structurally required (the
  no-session-ownership guard depends on the MCP stack staying out of src/neograph). NOT a bug.

### 2. `pytest.mark.skipif(not _HAS_MCP, ...)` -- SAME disease, different spelling (2nd instance)
5 files carry a `requires_mcp = pytest.mark.skipif(not _HAS_MCP, ...)` gate:
test_mcp_battery.py, test_mcp_transport_resilience.py, test_mcp_oauth.py, test_mcp_fakes.py,
and -- notably -- **test_guards_api_manifest.py, a STRUCTURAL GUARD**.

Measured:
```
uv run --isolated pytest <those 5 files>  -> 58 passed, 66 skipped   (124 collected)
uv run pytest <those 5 files>             -> 140 passed              (140 collected)
```
So **66 more tests + the 16 importorskip'd = 82 MCP tests** do not run under the default gate.

Two reasons this is NOT filed as a second bug:
- It is the documented, structurally-required MCP optionality (AGENTS.md 'no-key != no extra').
- Crucially, `skipif` is the LOUD form: 66 skips appear in the pytest summary line. The
  `importorskip` form is the SILENT one -- the module yields zero tests and the summary shows
  nothing. That asymmetry is exactly why the pyagentspec case went unnoticed for an entire epic.

DETECTOR GAP NOTED: the guard written in the reproduce atom scans `importorskip` only. A future
`skipif(not _HAS_X)` on a non-MCP dep would evade it. Carried into the disease-scan atom
(neograph-9odbk.4) as the primary question rather than fixed blind here.

### 3. Ruled out -- checked, clean
- `pytest.skip(allow_module_level=True)`: **zero** occurrences suite-wide.
- `try/except ImportError` -> skip in tests: zero (all hits are guard-test PROSE about the
  src-side function-local-import rule, plus one string literal in test_mcp_battery.py).
- `xfail`: all occurrences are `strict=True` in the Agent Spec matrix -- a strict xfail FAILS
  when it unexpectedly passes, so it is a gate, not a hole. (Ironically these live in
  importorskip-gated files, so instance 1 was disabling them too.)
- API-key gating: no test is skipped on a missing key; the key-referencing files
  (test_validation.py, test_docs_snippets.py, test_guards_examples.py,
  test_example_map_reduce.py) set dummy keys instead. Correct pattern.
- `tests/conftest.py:154` `run_driver` async cell: `pytest.skip` guarded on
  `hasattr(neograph, 'arun')`. Phase-0 scaffolding that self-activated when Phase 1 landed
  arun(); inert today. Baseline run reports **0 skipped**, confirming it no longer fires.

### 4. Amplifier (context, not a separate instance)
`.github/workflows/` contains `publish.yml` ONLY -- no test workflow. The local gate is the
sole gate, which is what turns a silent skip from a nuisance into an existential seam. Out of
scope for this fix; worth a separate ticket if CI is ever wanted.

No separate beads tasks filed: instance 1 is this ticket, instance 2 is a documented exemption,
and the detector gap it exposes is handled in-scope by the guard's design.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-x75es) -- atom neograph-9odbk.4, 2026-07-28

Pattern: **a dependency the test gate needs, declared in a location the DEFAULT gate command
does not install (`[project.optional-dependencies].*` instead of `[dependency-groups].dev`),
so the project's only gate is blind to -- or outright broken by -- its absence.**

Shape: SYNTACTIC (two AST-able call forms + a pyproject declaration-location lookup), so a
single deterministic scan is sufficient per the atom's instructions -- NO multi-agent fan-out,
and therefore no `.claude/code-review/neograph-x75es/` artifact (that gate applies to SEMANTIC
diseases only).

Scan commands (exactly reproducible):

### THE TICKET'S PREMISE IS UNDERSTATED -- measured, clean env
The ticket says a clean run is 'green with ~269 fewer tests'. It is not green. Both default
commands are RED on a clean checkout:

### Consequence for the fix (carried to architect review)
Rows 2-5 mean the ticket's own acceptance criterion -- '`make quality` on a clean checkout runs
the Agent Spec suite' -- is UNREACHABLE by moving `pyagentspec` alone: `make quality` does not
currently survive a clean checkout at all. The root confusion is that this project has BOTH a
`[project.optional-dependencies].dev` extra AND a `[dependency-groups].dev` group, and the
toolchain sits in the former while the gate reads the latter. The architect atom must decide
whether to consolidate into the group (and what happens to the ~dozen AGENTS.md commands that
say `--extra dev`).
## Architect Review (atom neograph-9odbk.5, 2026-07-28)

Reviewed the design-field Fix Approach against the scan evidence. Six criteria, 7 rated findings.

### 1. Root cause correctness -- CORRECT but SHALLOW (finding F1, HIGH)
'pyagentspec is declared where the default gate does not install it' is accurate and measured.
But it is an INSTANCE, not the root. The root is: **this project has two `dev` namespaces --
`[project.optional-dependencies].dev` (extra) and `[dependency-groups].dev` (group) -- the
toolchain lives in the former while the gate reads the latter, and nothing says which one a new
dev dep belongs in.** That ambiguity is how pyagentspec landed wrong, and it is unfixed by
moving one dep.

**F1 (HIGH): the fix as designed does not satisfy its own acceptance.** Acceptance says
'`make quality` on a clean checkout runs the Agent Spec suite'. `make quality` does not survive
a clean checkout at all today: `uv run --isolated pytest` = 83 failed, of which 51 are async
tests failing because `pytest-asyncio` is in the dev EXTRA and `asyncio_mode = "auto"`
(pyproject.toml:146) has no plugin to drive it. Moving `pyagentspec` alone leaves the stated
acceptance unreachable. Scan rows 2-5 are IN SCOPE, not scope creep.

### 2. Fix minimality -- ADEQUATE, with one deliberate expansion (F5, MEDIUM)
Rows 1-2 are forced by acceptance. Rows 3-5 (mypy / pytest / ruff) are forced by the same
acceptance clause, since `make quality` = test + lint + typecheck: verified `mypy` is NOT in
the default-gate env (it resolved here only by `uv run` falling back to the PATH binary at
`.venv/bin/mypy`), and `pytest`/`ruff` are present ONLY transitively (pytest-cov /
pytest-examples pull them). A gate whose own runner and linter are accidents of a transitive
dep is not a gate.

**F5 (MEDIUM): do not fix this by duplicating the dev list into both namespaces.** That leaves
exactly the duplicated-source-of-truth the modifier-combo retrospective names as the recurring
architectural disease here, and re-opens 'which one do I add a new dev dep to?' -- the ambiguity
that caused this bug. Recommend DELETING `[project.optional-dependencies].dev` and updating the
~30 `--extra dev` references (docstrings, pyproject comments, scripts/gen_api_manifest.py,
examples/29, AGENTS.md). Mechanical, and consistent with the documented project preference
'No backwards-compat shims at 0.x'. Not a NEEDS_USER_INPUT call: it follows from stated
preferences, and it is flagged here so it can be vetoed on sight.

### 3. Regression risk -- ONE REAL RISK, and it is the north-star kind (F2, HIGH)
**F2 (HIGH): moving `pyagentspec` into the default group DESTROYS the only proof that
`src/neograph` stays Agent-Spec-free.** Today that claim
(`_agent_spec.py` / `spec_types.py` import guards, 'core stays Agent-Spec-free by default') is
proven ACCIDENTALLY -- by the dep being absent from the default env. Make it always-present and
the proof evaporates while the claim stays in the docstrings. A module-scope
`import pyagentspec` regression in `src/neograph` would then pass every gate silently.

That is precisely the trade the north star forbids: buying ergonomics by re-admitting a silent
failure. The MCP family already solved this -- `test_mcp_battery.py::test_neograph_core_imports_
with_zero_mcp_deps` runs a SUBPROCESS and asserts the module never enters `sys.modules`.
Verified by grep: **no such guard exists for agent-spec** (no subprocess test among the 13
pyagentspec files). Adding the MCP-shaped purity guard is a HARD PRECONDITION of the migration,
not a follow-up.

Other risk checked and cleared: no test asserts the `ConfigurationError('pyagentspec is not
installed')` branch at `_agent_spec.py:113`, so always-installing the dep breaks nothing (F6).

### 4. Architecture compliance -- COMPLIANT
Row 1 mirrors the two in-repo precedents exactly (`langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite`,
`pytest-examples`, both with an in-file comment saying they sit in the group specifically 'so
the file collects under the bare test command'). Acceptance's 'a note explaining WHY the dep
sits where it does' is satisfied by copying that comment shape. Guard-first TDD honored: the
guard was written RED before any fix. Keeping `[project.optional-dependencies].agent-spec` for
consumers is correct -- this is a test-gate change, not a packaging change.

### 5. Similar-bug scalability -- INSUFFICIENT AS DESIGNED (F3, F4)
**F4 (MEDIUM): the guard detects `importorskip` only, so it pins half the disease.** The scan
found a second spelling in live use: `find_spec("x")` feeding `skipif(not _HAS_X)`, 7 sites
across 5 files. Today all 7 are MCP (exempt), so the guard is green on them by luck; the next
non-MCP `skipif` gate would evade it entirely. Extend the detector to BOTH forms and route both
through the same `GATED_IMPORT_EXEMPTIONS` table.

Also uncovered by any guard: rows 2-5. A dev dep can still be added to the wrong namespace
tomorrow. If the `dev` extra is deleted per F5, that hole closes structurally (one namespace
left). If it is kept, a guard asserting the toolchain sits in `[dependency-groups].dev` is
mandatory instead.

**F3 (MEDIUM, informational -- resolves to DO NOTHING): 32 tests hard-FAIL without pyagentspec**
rather than skipping, because they lack the `importorskip` line their 13 sibling files carry.
Do NOT 'fix' the inconsistency by adding guards to them -- loud failure is strictly better than
silent skip, and adding importorskip would EXTEND the disease. Leave them; document the
asymmetry so nobody 'tidies' it later.

### 6. Test coverage sufficiency -- SUFFICIENT once F2/F4 are folded in (F7, LOW)
**F7 (LOW):** acceptance #1 (collect-count parity) should be verified by MEASUREMENT in the
e2e-verify atom, not encoded as a count-floor guard. The ticket already rejected the count floor
(option 3) as brittle and it does not run anything -- agreed; do not add one.

### Rated summary
| # | Finding | Rating |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | Fix as designed cannot meet its own acceptance; rows 2-5 required | HIGH |
| F2 | Migration destroys the only proof core is Agent-Spec-free; MCP-shaped subprocess purity guard is a precondition | HIGH |
| F3 | 32 unguarded hard-failures -- deliberate, document, do NOT add importorskip | MEDIUM |
| F4 | Guard detector covers importorskip only; extend to find_spec/skipif form | MEDIUM |
| F5 | Do not duplicate the dev list; delete the `dev` extra for a single source of truth | MEDIUM |
| F6 | `ConfigurationError` missing-dep branch untested (pre-existing, unchanged) | LOW |
| F7 | Verify collect-count parity by measurement, not a count-floor guard | LOW |

### Verdict: **NEEDS_REFINEMENT**
Two HIGH findings. The fix approach must be revised to cover scan rows 2-5, to add the
subprocess core-purity guard BEFORE the dep becomes always-present, and to widen the guard
detector. No NEEDS_USER_INPUT: every open choice resolves against the ticket's own acceptance
text or a documented project preference. F5 is the one judgment call and is flagged for veto.
