title: Implement Portal tool-triggered handoff (trigger='tool'), genuine Swarm parity
description:
Design: docs/design/portal-tool-triggered-handoff-2026-07-27.md, twice adversarially reviewed (docs/design/portal-tool-triggered-handoff-2026-07-27-review.md, -review-2.md, both rounds resolved in place). Grounded in empirical evidence: docs/design/foreign-swarm-import-faithfulness-2026-07-27.md (static analysis) + docs/design/swarm-langgraph-compilation-spike-2026-07-27.md (live-run spike against pyagentspec's real langgraph-swarm-backed adapter, in an isolated worktree). Round 2's own verdict: 'ready for implementation, no further design-level rework needed' -- all 3 of its nits already applied to the design doc.

SCOPE: Portal gains trigger: Literal['output','tool']='output' field (peer mode only). trigger='tool' makes an agent/act mesh member's {node}__tools node a Command-emitting exit (destinations=(peers, {node}__agent)) detecting a synthesized transfer_to_<peer> tool call (built via tool.py's StructuredTool pattern, mirroring resource_reader/_build_read_blob -- never persisted into Node.tools, never touching register_tool_factory), routing via a new factory.py sibling _tool_handoff_to_command (guard G1 untouched -- Command( stays in factory.py) reusing all existing hop-budget/HANDOFF_END/entry-label machinery unchanged. Real plumbing required (do NOT skip this thinking 'no new IR field' means 'no new code'): thread a new handoff_portal: Portal | None parameter through exactly 2 functions -- make_agent_cycle_bodies (closed over by agent_body/aagent_body) and _agent_caller (extends the active tool list passed to bind_tools) -- per the design's corrected §3.1 call chain. Handoff tools are exempt from ToolBudgetTracker/Tool.budget and the idempotent-repeat-call cache, both as free structural consequences of never appearing in node.tools (verified, zero new code for either exemption).

New structural guards required (write failing-first, per AGENTS.md's PORTAL-exception discipline): (1) assert {node}__tools has NO static outgoing edge when is_tool_triggered (LangGraph does NOT enforce this itself -- verified live: it silently double-executes both a static edge and a destinations=-registered Command target in one superstep, a silent data-corruption bug if this guard is skipped); (2) _check_one_mesh_group rejects trigger='tool' on any non-agent/act member (new should_fail/should_pass fixture pair); (3) piggyback on G3's IR_FIELDS frozenset test to assert Node's field set stays exactly {fan_out_param, oracle_gen_type, handoff_param, handoff_channel} -- unchanged by this feature.

Recommended (per design §7) as a first-class native authoring feature (Portal(trigger='tool')), not import-only -- gets three-surface-parity testing for free and closes a real DX gap independent of Agent Spec import.

Import-side integration (HandoffMode mapping, design §5): OPTIONAL/ALWAYS both map to trigger='tool' on import (byte-identical in the real reference backend per the spike); NEVER keeps mapping to trigger='output'. This ticket is the CAPABILITY; wiring it into from_agent_spec's Swarm reconstruction is neograph-s7zt3.12's own scope (C1), sequence after this lands.
close_reason: Portal trigger='tool' tool-triggered handoff: added Portal.trigger field + is_tool_triggered property (modifiers.py), _check_one_mesh_group agent/act-required rule (_validation_portal.py), synthesized transfer_to_<peer> tools + detection threaded through make_agent_cycle_bodies+_agent_caller (_agent_cycle.py), _tool_handoff_to_command + make_portal_agent_cycle_tool_handoff_fn (factory.py), is_tool_triggered wiring branch with destinations= and no static tools->agent edge (_wiring.py), StateKeys.handoff_tool_target (_state_keys.py). Guards a/b/c + 3-surface parity + fixtures added; 673 gate + 435 regression tests green, ruff+mypy clean.

description:
Master doc: docs/design/agent-spec-portal-master-architecture-2026-07-27.md §2/§5 (PORTAL peer, Construct-as-entry row) + Build Plan Phase 1. CORRECTED 2026-07-27 by docs/design/architecture-audit-phase1-design-gap-probe-2026-07-27.md -- the original 2-site fix was incomplete AND partly wrong as worded. Three sites, must land TOGETHER:

(1) compiler.py:254's isinstance(item, Node) gate misroutes a Portal-modified Construct entry to _add_subgraph, which unconditionally raises CompileError with a false 'already rejected at assembly' comment -- relax to isinstance(item, (Node, Construct)) (dispatch-mode line stays Node-only, unaffected).

(2) state.py's Portal state-field builder sources portal_members from nodes_only only. WARNING: the originally-filed fix (concatenate nodes_only + sub_constructs) is WRONG -- verified by repro, string concatenation reorders relative to construct.nodes and reintroduces a wrong-entry bug. The correct fix filters construct.nodes directly, in order, preserving position.

(3) NEW, found by this probe: _ir_normalize.py's normalize_ir has ITS OWN separate portal_members collector (the sole writer of Node.handoff_channel per the single-writer discipline) with the IDENTICAL isinstance(item, Node) gate. Left unfixed, it stamps the WRONG handoff_channel on Node peers even after sites 1+2 are patched -- reproduced as a live runtime failure (handoff resolves to None). Must be fixed in the same PR as sites 1+2, verified with a runtime-invoking (not compile-only) test.

Acceptance test per the earlier correction: assert the state model's declared Portal field names match _wiring.py's actual entry_field for a Construct entry -- NOT 'does not raise' (the real failure mode of a partial fix is silent state-key divergence, not a crash).
notes:
FIXED (three sites, landed together) — neograph-s7zt3.5.

REPRODUCTION (tests/test_portal_construct_entry.py, all 6 red first):
Topology: parent mesh nodes=[origin, entry_sub | Portal(to=["closer"]), closer]
where entry_sub is a sub-Construct as the mesh ENTRY (members[0]), closer a Node peer.
- compile() raised CompileError "Portal on a sub-construct is not supported" (compiler.py _add_subgraph PORTAL arm) — the Construct entry was misrouted.
- compile_state_model declared neo_handoff_closer (peer) instead of neo_handoff_entry_sub — silent state-key divergence.
- closer.handoff_channel stamped neo_handoff_closer (wrong); at runtime closer.handoff resolved to None.

ROOT CAUSE PER SITE (all confirmed live):
1. compiler.py mesh-detection gate `isinstance(item, Node)` excluded the Portal-Construct entry, so it fell through to `elif isinstance(item, Construct)` -> _add_subgraph -> unconditional CompileError. Relaxed to `isinstance(item, (Node, Construct))`. Dispatch arm kept Node-only via `assert isinstance(item, Node)` (a Construct is never is_dispatch). _contiguous_portal_mesh call uses `cast("Node", item)` (its `entry: Node` annotation lives in out-of-scope _wiring.py; already runtime-Construct-agnostic).
2. state.py Portal state-field builder sourced portal_members from `nodes_only` (excludes Construct entry). NOT fixed by concatenating nodes_only+sub_constructs (verified WRONG — reorders, picks Node peer as entry). Fixed by filtering `construct.nodes` DIRECTLY, preserving order, so _group_portal_members[0] is the real entry. _is_dispatch widened to ConstructItem.
3. _ir_normalize.py normalize_ir has its OWN portal_members collector (sole writer of Node.handoff_channel) with the identical `isinstance(item, Node)` gate. Relaxed to `not isinstance(item, _BranchNode)` (runtime-safe equivalent of (Node,Construct) over construct.nodes; Construct cannot be imported here without growing the never-grow function-local-import allowlist). Write-back loop stays Node-only.

- src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py (site 3 + _BranchNode import)

- tests/test_guards_branch_arm_walks.py (allowlist entry for the new top-level construct.nodes Portal-member walk in state.py — D-MESH-LEVEL, deliberately not arm-descending)

title: Phase 3: migrate the remaining 7 ModifierCombo consumers onto COMBO_DECOMPOSITION + land the anti-regrowth guard
description:
Master doc: docs/design/agent-spec-portal-master-architecture-2026-07-27.md, Build Plan Phase 3, and docs/design/modifier-combo-single-source-of-truth-2026-07-27.md for the full consumer inventory. Migrate state.py (three match blocks), _state_write.py, _subconstruct.py, _input_shape.py, runner.py, _wiring.py onto COMBO_DECOMPOSITION -- each is a mechanical 'shared classification, different per-arm body' swap, but VERIFY EACH INDIVIDUALLY against real code rather than assuming the pattern transfers cleanly (state.py's three blocks group combos identically but build different per-producer-category bodies; at least one arm -- the sub-construct block's EACH_ORACLE case -- is a documented, currently-unreachable defensive fallback, not live logic).

Land the structural anti-regrowth guard NOW (not before -- would fail immediately against these files' pre-migration state), enumerating all consumers migrated so far (compiler.py from Phase 2, these 6, eventually _agent_spec.py/loader.py once those migrate too) -- an AST-based check forbidding a second hand-written ModifierCombo enumeration for dispatch purposes outside modifiers.py.
design:
## Core Invariant

"What does this ModifierCombo decompose into" is answered in exactly ONE place --
`COMBO_DECOMPOSITION`/`PrimaryShape`/`SUB_CONSTRUCT_UNSUPPORTED_COMBOS` in `modifiers.py` -- and
every build-time consumer READS that table rather than re-deriving the grouping, while questions
that are genuinely about modifier PRESENCE (not decomposition) stay presence-reads and are never
laundered through the table; the migration itself is zero-behavior-change.

## Implementation Plan

Reuse-first: the table exists (`modifiers.py:107-170`) and `compiler.py:521-590` / `:606-709`
already consume it correctly. Every step below is "make site X read the existing table the way
compiler.py already does" -- no new abstraction is invented except one optional shared predicate
(step 1) and the guard (step 2).

1. **(Optional but recommended, decide first) Add ONE shared shape predicate to `modifiers.py`**,
   next to `classify_modifiers`:
   `def primary_shape(item: ConstructItem) -> PrimaryShape: return COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[classify_modifiers(item)[0]].primary`
   Nine of the thirteen sites are pure membership tests (`is PrimaryShape.PORTAL` x6,
   `is PrimaryShape.LOOP` x3). This collapses them to one call and makes the guard's "reads the
   table" assertion trivially checkable. It EXTENDS the existing table module (single definition
   site preserved); it does not create a second authority. If rejected, sites just inline
   `COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[combo].primary` -- functionally identical.

2. **Write the anti-regrowth guard FIRST, failing** (guard-first discipline; it must be red against
   the pre-migration tree and go green only as the six files land). New file
   `tests/test_guards_combo_decomposition_consumers.py`, PURE `ast` (no `re`) so it is exempt from
   `tests/test_guards_meta.py`'s named-regex/slip-test discipline -- copy the structure of
   `TestComboMapMonopoly` (`tests/test_guards_helper_monopoly.py:631-692`).
   Three assertions:
   - **(a) No second enumeration.** For every file in an independent literal
     `MIGRATED = frozenset({"compiler.py", "state.py", "_state_write.py", "_subconstruct.py",
     "_input_shape.py", "runner.py", "_wiring.py"})`: AST-walk for `ModifierCombo.<MEMBER>`
     attribute accesses occurring in a DISPATCH context -- inside a `match`/`case` pattern
     (`ast.MatchValue`/`MatchOr`), inside an `ast.Compare` with `In`/`NotIn`/`Eq`, or as a
     dict/set/tuple literal element used in such a comparison. Assert zero.
   - **(b) Reads the table.** Each MIGRATED file imports at least one of `COMBO_DECOMPOSITION` /
     `PrimaryShape` / `SUB_CONSTRUCT_UNSUPPORTED_COMBOS` (or the step-1 `primary_shape` helper)
     from `neograph.modifiers`.
   - **(c) Completeness / anti-tautology.** Derive from the FILESYSTEM the set of `src/neograph/*.py`
     files that reference `ModifierCombo` at all; assert it equals
     `MIGRATED | PENDING | PRESENCE_ONLY | {"modifiers.py"}`, where `PENDING = frozenset({"_agent_spec.py"})`
     (documented: Phase 6/7; `loader.py` joins when the s6 recognize->classify design lands -- it
     has ZERO combo references today) and `PRESENCE_ONLY = frozenset({"_fan_agent.py", "__main__.py"})`
     (they read `mods` presence only). MIGRATED/PENDING are independent literals, the actual set is
     filesystem-derived -- the two sides come from different sources, per the
     `tests/test_guards_parity_ratchet.py` anti-tautology lesson. A new file growing combo dispatch
     fails loud.
   - Positive + negative meta-tests per scanner (diseased snippet flagged; the healthy
     `match COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[combo].primary:` form and `_fan_agent`'s `mods` presence read not
     flagged).

3. **Migrate the clean 1:1 sites (no fusion subtlety).** `_input_shape.py:32-33`,
   `_subconstruct.py:90` (LOOP half), `runner.py:116,123,143,154`, `_wiring.py:719`,
   `state.py:143-144`, `state.py:241-242`, `state.py:272`. Each becomes
   `primary_shape(item) is PrimaryShape.{LOOP,PORTAL}`. Leave the neighbouring
   `.modifier_set.portal` / `km.is_dispatch` / `_group_portal_members` reads untouched -- those are
   presence/grouping, already single-sourced.

4. **Fix `state.py:218-232` as a PRESENCE read, not a shape dispatch** (risk R1). Replace the two
   four-member `ModifierCombo` membership tuples with `"oracle" in mods` / `"each" in mods` from
   `classify_modifiers(item)[1]`. This is the semantically correct question AND it removes the
   literals the guard bans. Regression to keep green: a fused `Each x Oracle` node must still get
   `StateKeys.ORACLE_GEN_ID`/`ORACLE_MODEL` in the state model.

5. **`_subconstruct.py:91` `has_each`** -- migrate to `PrimaryShape.EACH` **while preserving the
   `EACH_ORACLE` exclusion** via the sanctioned co-presence idiom
   (`shape is PrimaryShape.EACH and "oracle" not in mods`). Reason in risk R3: `make_subgraph_fn`
   runs before `_add_subgraph`'s unsupported-combo gate, so the line executes for that combo.

6. **`_state_write.py:79-98`** -- replace `match combo:` with
   `match COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[combo].primary:` + `assert_never`; inside `case PrimaryShape.EACH:`
   split the fusion with `if "oracle" in mods: each_mod = None else: each_mod = mods["each"]`
   (the idiom `docs/design/agent-spec-rewrite-2026-07-27.md:115` prescribes and `compiler.py:622`
   already uses). All other shapes -> `each_mod = None`. Do NOT move or duplicate the
   `# MODIFIER_RULE_TOUCHPOINT` sentinels (guard at `tests/test_guards_assembly.py:1041`).

7. **`state.py:165-211` (sub-construct fields)** -- mirror `_add_subgraph`'s gate ORDER: check
   `combo in SUB_CONSTRUCT_UNSUPPORTED_COMBOS` first, but keep the existing NON-raising defensive
   fallback body (`fields[field_name] = (sub.output | None, None)`) -- risk R4: state building
   precedes `_add_subgraph`, so raising here would pre-empt and change the user-visible error.
   Then `match COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[combo].primary:` with ORACLE / EACH / LOOP / BARE / PORTAL arms
   (PORTAL keeps its documented defensive fallback) + `assert_never`.

8. **`state.py:603-650` (single-type output)** -- `match ... .primary:` with the fusion handled
   INSIDE `case PrimaryShape.EACH:`: `if "oracle" in mods:` add
   `StateKeys.eachoracle_collector(field_name)`, then build the shared
   `dict[str, output] | None` + `_merge_dicts` field for both paths (the fused body is literally
   the EACH body plus the collector -- verify byte-equivalence of the resulting field dict).
   BARE/PORTAL share one arm as today; ORACLE and LOOP unchanged in body.

9. **`state.py:544-590` (dict-form outputs)** -- `match ... .primary:` with
   `case PrimaryShape.ORACLE:` (existing body), `case PrimaryShape.EACH:` containing the fusion
   split where the FUSED branch keeps its inline node-level-keyed collector + per-key dict fields
   and the non-fused branch keeps the per-key `_add_single_output_field` delegation (risk R2 --
   these two bodies must NOT be merged; delegation would emit a per-key collector name), and
   `case PrimaryShape.BARE | PrimaryShape.LOOP | PrimaryShape.PORTAL:` -> the existing per-key
   delegation. `assert_never` closes it.

10. **Turn the guard green, then run the gates.** Full `uv run --extra dev pytest` (baseline was
    zero-failure per neograph-g330l.1), `ruff check`/`ruff format --check`, `mypy`. Fast loop
    while iterating: `tests/test_combo_decomposition.py tests/test_composition.py
    tests/test_check_fixtures.py tests/test_guards_*.py tests/test_portal_*.py tests/modifiers/`.
    If `state.py` crosses a line-count cap, bump it with an in-docstring justification following
    `tests/test_guards_ir_compiler.py:522-551`'s precedent (that file's cap is compiler-only today;
    check for a state.py cap before assuming none).

11. **Correct the docs that this research falsified** (small, in-scope, per the docs-are-truth
    rule): update `docs/design/modifier-combo-single-source-of-truth-2026-07-27.md` s1's state.py
    row (SEVEN sites, not three; groupings are NOT identical across the three match blocks) and
    note that `loader.py` has no combo references yet. Leave the mandate itself unchanged.

## Plan amendments (from the codebase disease scan, atom neograph-g330l.3, 2026-07-28)

The scan found three things the plan above assumes wrongly. These amendments OVERRIDE the
corresponding text in the plan; steps 1-11 are otherwise unchanged.

**A1. compiler.py is NOT finished — Phase 3 touches SEVEN files, not six.**
`compiler.py:263-265` holds a third combo-dispatch site (`classify_modifiers(item)[0] in
(ModifierCombo.PORTAL, ModifierCombo.PORTAL_OPERATOR)`, the mesh-ENTRY detection in
`_add_nodes_to_graph`). Phase 2 migrated compiler.py's two `match` statements and left this
compare-shaped one behind; neither the design doc nor the research inventory lists it.
Because `compiler.py` is in the guard's MIGRATED set, the guard stays RED until this site
lands. Add it to step 3's clean-1:1 batch: `primary_shape(item) is PrimaryShape.PORTAL`.
Leave the following `item.modifier_set.portal` / `portal.is_dispatch` reads untouched
(presence/mode, not decomposition).

**A2. The guard's completeness assertion has NO `PRESENCE_ONLY` set — it must be dropped.**
Step 2(c) proposed `PRESENCE_ONLY = frozenset({"_fan_agent.py", "__main__.py"})`. Those two
files reference `classify_modifiers` only and never name `ModifierCombo`, so including them
makes the assertion fail. Filesystem truth (`grep -rl "ModifierCombo" src/neograph/`) is
exactly nine files. The correct identity is:

    MIGRATED | PENDING | {"modifiers.py"} == {files under src/neograph that reference ModifierCombo}

with
    MIGRATED = {"compiler.py", "state.py", "_state_write.py", "_subconstruct.py",
                "_input_shape.py", "runner.py", "_wiring.py"}     # independent literal
    PENDING  = {"_agent_spec.py"}                                  # independent literal

`_fan_agent.py` / `__main__.py` remain useful as NEGATIVE-CONTROL meta-test fixtures (a
`mods` presence read must not be flagged), which is what step 2's meta-tests should use them
for — they just do not belong in the completeness identity.

**A3. The DEFER row is filed: `neograph-tjpn4`.**
`_agent_spec.py:956-995` (flat `if combo == ModifierCombo.X:` chain + a PORTAL membership
test) is deferred to **neograph-tjpn4**, which depends on this task and on
neograph-s7zt3.10. The guard's `PENDING` literal must carry a comment naming that ticket, and
closing tjpn4 must SHRINK `PENDING` to empty — the guard is a ratchet, PENDING never grows.
Note `_agent_spec.py:945` already reads `SUB_CONSTRUCT_UNSUPPORTED_COMBOS` correctly; that
line is the healthy exemplar and must stay unflagged (guard negative control).

**A4. One benign form is invisible to the AST scanner — allowlisted knowingly.**
`compiler.py:174-176` asks a combo question as a STRING compare (`combo.name != "BARE"`) while
building the `compile_start` log dict. It is observability, not decomposition, so it is
ALLOWLIST — but it proves the AST scanner is not total. Do not document the guard as catching
every possible combo question; document it as catching every *member-constant* dispatch.


## Refinements (post-review, atom neograph-g330l.12, 2026-07-28)

Resolves the five MEDIUM and three LOW findings from the architect review (atom
neograph-g330l.4). These OVERRIDE the corresponding text in the plan and in amendments A1-A4.

**R-M1. Guard assertion (c) is rewritten; assertion (a) gains a scope carve-out.**
The review is right that (c) as specified can never be green: the seven MIGRATED files' only
`ModifierCombo` references ARE the dispatch sites being deleted (sole imports at
`_wiring.py:50`, `runner.py:32`, `_state_write.py:15`, `compiler.py:55`, `_input_shape.py:12`,
`_subconstruct.py:18`, `state.py:27`), and ruff F401 forbids keeping a dead import. Adopt
option (ii) -- the STRONGER one -- because it is stable across the migration and keeps an
equality:

    consumers = {f for f in src/neograph/*.py
                 if f references ModifierCombo
                 OR f imports any of COMBO_DECOMPOSITION / PrimaryShape /
                    SUB_CONSTRUCT_UNSUPPORTED_COMBOS / primary_shape from neograph.modifiers}

    assert consumers == MIGRATED | PENDING | {"modifiers.py"}

Pre-migration this holds (all seven reference `ModifierCombo`); post-migration it still holds
(all seven now import table symbols). Both sides stay independently sourced -- `MIGRATED` /
`PENDING` are hand-written literals, `consumers` is filesystem-derived -- so the parity-ratchet
anti-tautology lesson is respected. Accepted tradeoff: any FUTURE file that legitimately reads
the table must be added to `MIGRATED`. That is the intended ratchet (the guard IS the consumer
inventory), not friction to work around; say so in the docstring.

Plan delta: add an explicit step to DELETE the now-unused `ModifierCombo` imports from all seven
files (ruff will flag them otherwise), and keep the import only where a member is still named.

**R-M2. `state.py:203-209`'s PORTAL arm is LIVE -- correct the plan, the notes and the comment.**
Verified independently during refinement: `tests/test_portal_construct_entry.py:117` builds
`Construct("parent_entry_mesh", nodes=[origin, entry_sub | Portal(to=["closer"], max_hops=8),
closer])` and compiles it, so a Portal-modified Construct genuinely reaches this arm. The
existing comment ("rejected at assembly (D-MESH-LEVEL) ... so this arm is
defensively-unreachable") is FALSE and predates neograph-s7zt3.5.

  - Plan step 7 and disposition-table row 4 are amended: only the `EACH_ORACLE` arm is a
    defensive fallback. The PORTAL arm is live Portal-mesh logic.
  - Keep a dedicated `case PrimaryShape.PORTAL:` arm. Do NOT merge it with `EACH_ORACLE`.
  - REWRITE the comment: it is the live Construct-mesh-member output field -- a mesh member
    writes its own output plainly, mirroring `_add_single_output_field`'s BARE/PORTAL arm.
    Carrying the stale comment forward would invite a future "delete the dead arm"
    simplification on a Portal hot path.

**R-M3. Land the missing R4 pin FIRST, as part of the write-test red.**
R4's contract -- `state.py` must not pre-empt `_add_subgraph`'s `CompileError` ("Each x Oracle
fusion is not supported on sub-constructs", `compiler.py:528-534`) -- has zero coverage on the
compile path (the only matches in `tests/` are `test_agent_spec_export.py:986,1002`, a different
raise site: `_agent_spec.py:945`, `ConfigurationError`). Without a pin, a pre-gate raise in
`state.py` changes the error's site, type and text with the suite still green.

Add to the write-test atom: a `tests/check_fixtures/should_fail/` fixture that compiles an
Each x Oracle-modified sub-construct, carrying

    # CHECK_ERROR: Each x Oracle fusion is not supported on sub-constructs

per the repo's "every new validation rule gets a fixture" convention. It must pass BEFORE the
migration (it pins today's behavior) -- unlike the anti-regrowth guard, which must fail first.
Note the two have OPPOSITE red/green polarity at write-test time; state that explicitly so the
implementer does not "fix" a fixture that is supposed to be green.

**R-M4. The guard scanner must be alias-tolerant.**
Before scanning, collect the module's local binding names for `ModifierCombo` from its
`ast.ImportFrom` nodes (`alias.asname or alias.name`) and match attribute accesses against that
SET, not the literal string `"ModifierCombo"`. Otherwise
`from neograph.modifiers import ModifierCombo as MC` + `MC.EACH` walks straight through a guard
whose entire job is anti-regrowth. Add a POSITIVE meta-test using the aliased form.
Also correct `TestComboMapMonopoly`'s docstring (`tests/test_guards_helper_monopoly.py:631-692`),
which claims "alias-tolerant" while the code matches only `v.value.id == "ModifierCombo"` -- fix
the claim or the code; do not leave the false claim standing next to the new guard that copies it.

**R-M5. Extend the docs correction to the MASTER doc.**
Step 11 also updates `docs/design/agent-spec-portal-master-architecture-2026-07-27.md:358`, which
still reads "Phase 3 -- migrate the remaining six non-Agent-Spec consumers" and lists
`state.py (three blocks), _state_write.py, _subconstruct.py, _input_shape.py, runner.py,
_wiring.py` -- treating Phase 2 as having finished compiler.py, the exact claim amendment A1
falsified. Correct it to SEVEN consumers including `compiler.py` (its compare-shaped mesh-entry
site at `:263-265` survived Phase 2) and `state.py`'s seven sites. Leaving the master doc
uncorrected reseeds the hand-picked-list disease this epic exists to kill, for Phase 6/7.

**R-L1. ADOPTED.** At the three sites that already hold a `classify_modifiers` result --
`state.py:143-144` (`arm_combo`), `state.py:241-242` (`n_combo`/`n_mods`), `_subconstruct.py:89-91`
(`sub_combo`, and step 5 needs `mods` there anyway) -- use
`COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[<existing combo>].primary` rather than re-classifying via
`primary_shape(item)`. Reserve the helper for the genuinely inline sites: `compiler.py:263`,
`state.py:272`, `runner.py` x4, `_wiring.py:719`, `_input_shape.py:33`.

**R-L2. ADOPTED -- bead filed: `neograph-c265k`** ("Single-source the Each x Oracle fusion test
(is_each_oracle_fused) -- 5 open-coded copies after Phase 3"), depends on this task. This task
still uses the open-coded `"oracle" in mods` co-presence idiom, per R5 and the authoritative docs;
c265k consolidates it afterwards. Do NOT drive-by that consolidation here.

**R-L3. ADOPTED.** Guard assertion (b) must verify the imported binding is USED (an `ast.Name` /
`ast.Attribute` reference to it elsewhere in the module), not merely imported -- otherwise a dead
import satisfies it. Where it remains cheap rather than load-bearing, say so in the docstring.

### Net scope after refinement

7 source files migrated (`compiler.py`, `state.py`, `_state_write.py`, `_subconstruct.py`,
`_input_shape.py`, `runner.py`, `_wiring.py`) + 7 dead imports removed + 1 new anti-regrowth guard
file (alias-tolerant, 3 assertions, positive/negative meta-tests) + 1 new should_fail check
fixture pinning R4 + 1 stale comment rewritten (`state.py` PORTAL arm) + 1 stale docstring
corrected (`TestComboMapMonopoly`) + 2 docs corrected (master doc Phase 3 line, combo doc s1 row).
Deferred with beads filed: `neograph-tjpn4` (_agent_spec.py chain), `neograph-c265k` (fusion
predicate).

title: Phase 4: fix _lower_construct_item's Construct-item-modifier-silent-drop bug
description:
Master doc: docs/design/agent-spec-portal-master-architecture-2026-07-27.md §5 (EACH/ORACLE/LOOP/OPERATOR Construct-export rows, all currently 'BROKEN -- silent drop') + Build Plan Phase 4. Confirmed by repro: _agent_spec.py's isinstance(item, Construct) branch in _lower_construct_item wraps a FlowNode and returns immediately -- classify_modifiers(item) is never called on a Construct-as-item, so Construct(...) | Each()/Oracle()/Loop()/Operator() used as an item inside another Construct has its modifiers silently vanish on export today: no error, no marker, no diagnostic.

Fix: add the same classify_modifiers + SUB_CONSTRUCT_UNSUPPORTED_COMBOS check _add_subgraph already performs (Phase 2), before wrapping the FlowNode. For EACH_ORACLE/EACH_ORACLE_OPERATOR specifically, the target is FAIL LOUD mirroring compiler.py's own permanent rejection (that fusion has no Construct-level meaning -- not a bug to fix, a restriction to mirror accurately). For EACH/ORACLE/LOOP/OPERATOR, reuse _lower_each/_lower_oracle/_lower_loop/_lower_operator on the Construct item the same way the Node-level path already does. title: Portal mesh->Swarm export ships RAW ${var} in Agent system_prompt (untranslated _make_agent at _lower_portal_mesh_to_swarm)
description:
SURFACED BY neograph-tjupj's exhaustive-guard research (2026-07-27, req-4 mutual-blind-spot escalation). CORE-INVARIANT / NORTH-STAR SILENT SEAM confirmed empirically.

_lower_portal_mesh_to_swarm (src/neograph/_agent_spec.py ~:945) lowers a Portal mode-(a) peer mesh to a pyagentspec Swarm, calling _make_agent(member, tools_mod, [], [], member.prompt or '') for each member — passing member.prompt UNTRANSLATED (no _translate_placeholders in that function) as Agent(system_prompt=...). The in-code comment assumes 'mesh Agents carry NO I/O Properties (inputs=[]), so there is nothing to placeholder-translate' — but that assumption is FALSE: a Portal mesh member can be mode='agent'/'think' with inputs={'handoff': Payload} (the reserved handoff input, validated by _check_portal_mesh:291-306) and a ${handoff.field} prompt.

REPRO (confirmed 2026-07-27): build a 2-member Portal mesh, each Node(mode='agent', prompt='Handle ${handoff.note}', inputs={'handoff': Handoff}, outputs=Handoff) | Portal(...). Construct builds OK, to_agent_spec succeeds, and flow.first_agent.system_prompt == 'Handle the case: ${handoff.note}' — a RAW neograph ${...} shipped to a foreign Swarm runtime that uses pyagentspec {{ }} placeholders and will NEVER fill it. pyagentspec does not flag it (${...} is not its {{jinja}} grammar), so it silently ships.

This is the EXACT class of seam the epic's exhaustive-matrix + guard work exists to eliminate. It escaped BOTH the matrix (classifies Portal as per-node UNSUPPORTED, so it never exercises the successful Swarm lowering) AND the pre-tjupj guards (walk LlmNode/AgentNode, not the _make_agent->Agent Swarm path) — a mutual blind spot.

FIX DIRECTION (design, TDD): in _lower_portal_mesh_to_swarm, route each member's prompt through the SAME Option-F _translate_placeholders/_node_translation the AgentNode branch uses (translate ${handoff.note}->{{ handoff_note }} and declare the corresponding Agent inputs Property), OR — if mesh-member prompts with real placeholder inputs are genuinely out of scope for Swarm export — FAIL LOUD (ConfigurationError) rather than ship raw ${var}. Decide via TDD; the North Star forbids the silent raw-${ ship. Must round-trip if translated.

TRACKED BY tjupj's guard: neograph-tjupj adds the exhaustive guard covering _make_agent/Agent construction sites; the :945 site is on tjupj's SHRINKING allowlist tagged with THIS ticket id until fixed here.
design:
## Root Cause
_lower_portal_mesh_to_swarm builds each mesh member's Agent via _make_agent(member, tools_mod, [], [], member.prompt or '') — the ONLY _make_agent call site that does not first route the prompt through _translate_placeholders. The :912 comment's 'mesh Agents carry NO I/O Properties, so there is nothing to placeholder-translate' assumption is false: _check_portal_mesh validates the reserved 'handoff' input on mesh members, and an agent/think-mode member may reference ${handoff.field} in its prompt. pyagentspec cannot flag ${...} (not its {{jinja}} grammar), so the raw placeholder ships silently — North-Star silent-seam class.

## Fix Design (reviewed ALL_LOW, rugo8.5)
DECISION: TRANSLATE (Option F), not fail-loud — mesh members with placeholder prompts are a validated legitimate shape; the machinery exists and every sibling site uses it.

1. EXPORT (_agent_spec.py, _lower_portal_mesh_to_swarm member loop): per member —
   rewritten, ref_props, flat_to_original = _translate_placeholders(member.prompt or '', _properties_for(member.inputs), member.name)
   agent = _make_agent(member, tools_mod, ref_props, [], rewritten)
   Stamp the round-trip marker on the Agent itself (Agent is a pyagentspec Component; metadata survival proven by the step-1 gate test): agent.metadata = {**(agent.metadata or {}), _MARK_PROMPT_SPEC: _prompt_spec_marker(member, flat_to_original)}. Keep outputs=[] (payload/routing still rides neograph/portal_spec). Update the now-false :903-:915 comments.
2. IMPORT (loader.py, _reconstruct_swarm_mesh): read pm = (getattr(agent, 'metadata', None) or {}).get(_MARK_PROMPT_SPEC); when present use pm['original_text'] (untranslated ${var}) as the member's prompt instead of the translated system_prompt — minimal marker-preferred read mirroring the LlmNode Option-F import; foreign Swarms (no marker) keep the current path unchanged. Best-effort/warning status of the Swarm import is NOT upgraded (payload synthesis stays route-centric).
3. GUARDS (tests/test_guards_agent_spec_llm_construction_sites.py): remove the MAKE_AGENT_UNPAIRED_ALLOWLIST entry per its own exactly-1 meta-check instructions (allowlist + its two allowlist-specific tests removed; unpaired offenders check keeps running with empty allowlist semantics), EXPECTED_PAIRED_MAKE_AGENT_SITES 1→2.
4. TESTS: keep the fix-agnostic repro (goes green); add (i) translated system_prompt == 'Handle the case: {{ handoff_note }}' + Agent declares StringProperty 'handoff_note', (ii) to_agent_spec→from_agent_spec round-trip recovers prompt 'Handle the case: ${handoff.note}', (iii) existing scripted-mesh tests stay green (no-placeholder members: ref_props=[] → shape identical to today).
notes:
## Reproduction (rugo8.2, 2026-07-27)
- Failing test: tests/test_agent_spec_export.py::TestPortalMeshMemberPromptNeverShipsRawPlaceholder::test_mesh_member_prompt_placeholders_never_ship_raw (FAILED confirmed; fix-shape-agnostic: passes on either Option-F translation or fail-loud, forbids only the silent raw-${ ship)
- Empirically confirmed: 2-member agent-mode Portal mesh with inputs={'handoff': Handoff} and prompt 'Handle the case: ${handoff.note}' exports Swarm with first_agent.system_prompt == 'Handle the case: ${handoff.note}' and first_agent.inputs == [].
- Root cause: _lower_portal_mesh_to_swarm (_agent_spec.py:916) calls _make_agent(member, tools_mod, [], [], member.prompt or '') — bypassing _translate_placeholders that every other _make_agent caller (_lower_generation_step agent/act branch, :345-347) routes through; the :912 comment's 'nothing to placeholder-translate' assumption is false for members with the reserved 'handoff' input.
## Trace-similar (rugo8.3, 2026-07-27)
Pattern category: prompt-carrying pyagentspec construction site that bypasses the Option-F _translate_placeholders seam.

Census (from tjupj's exhaustive AST guard, tests/test_guards_agent_spec_llm_construction_sites.py): exactly 4 prompt-shipping sites in _agent_spec.py — LlmNode:322 (paired/translated), LlmNode merge:560 (paired), _make_agent@_lower_generation_step:347 (paired), _make_agent@_lower_portal_mesh_to_swarm:916 (UNPAIRED — this bug, the sole MAKE_AGENT_UNPAIRED_ALLOWLIST entry). No other instances of the bug exist; the guard ratchets new sites. No separate beads needed.

ADJACENT FINDING (in-scope for THIS fix, round-trip requirement): the import mirror _reconstruct_swarm_mesh (loader.py:715) calls _node_from_spec_agent(agent.name, agent, None, ...) with marker=None unconditionally and takes prompt straight from agent.system_prompt. Today the raw ${var} round-trips only BY ACCIDENT (raw text out, raw text back). A translating fix must stamp the neograph/agent_spec (or prompt_spec) marker on each mesh Agent's metadata at export AND read it (validated) in _reconstruct_swarm_mesh — else the imported prompt becomes '{{ handoff_note }}' and round-trip breaks. Native YAML spec surface keeps ${} grammar — not affected.
## Codebase Disease Scan (s7zt3.1) — rugo8.4

Pattern: prompt text shipped into a pyagentspec component (LlmNode.prompt_template / Agent.system_prompt via _make_agent) without routing through the single Option-F _translate_placeholders seam.
Shape: SYNTACTIC (exact constructor forms; tjupj's AST guard test_guards_agent_spec_llm_construction_sites.py is already an exhaustive census of _agent_spec.py).
Scan command: grep -rn 'prompt_template=\|system_prompt=\|LlmNode(\|_make_agent(' src/ --include='*.py' (plus pyagentspec-importer module list: _agent_spec.py, loader.py, _hot_swap.py, factory.py, spec_types.py — only _agent_spec.py constructs prompt-carrying pyagentspec components).
Total instances found: 4 pyagentspec sites (+6 native-runtime prompt_template= sites, not the disease).

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | _agent_spec.py:322 | LlmNode(prompt_template=rewritten) think branch | ALLOWLIST | paired with _translate_placeholders:321 |
| 2 | _agent_spec.py:347 | _make_agent(...rewritten) agent/act branch | ALLOWLIST | paired with _translate_placeholders:345 |
| 3 | _agent_spec.py:560 | LlmNode merge (Oracle) | ALLOWLIST | paired with _translate_placeholders:556 |
| 4 | _agent_spec.py:916 | _make_agent(member,...,member.prompt or '') in _lower_portal_mesh_to_swarm | MIGRATE | THE bug — sole unpaired site (tjupj MAKE_AGENT_UNPAIRED_ALLOWLIST entry to be emptied by the fix) |
| 5-10 | _dispatch.py:273,304 / _oracle.py:281,369 / _tool_loop.py:473,519 | invoke_structured/loop prompt_template= | ALLOWLIST | neograph's own runtime, native ${} grammar — not a foreign-format ship |
## Architect Review (rugo8.5, 2026-07-27)

1. Root cause correctness — LOW (confirmed): sole unpaired _make_agent site (tjupj guard census exact); empirical repro in bead notes.
2. Fix minimality — LOW (with the refined design below): translate-in-member-loop mirrors _lower_generation_step's agent branch exactly; the only scope beyond :916 is the round-trip pair (export marker stamp + _reconstruct_swarm_mesh marker read), which the ticket itself mandates ('Must round-trip if translated').
3. Regression risk — LOW: (a) members without placeholders get ref_props=[] → identical Agent shape to today, existing scripted-mesh tests unaffected; (b) ref_props exactly match the rewritten {{ flat }} names, so pyagentspec ComponentWithIO._validate_no_extra_property passes by construction (the very reason inputs=[] was originally passed evaporates once the prompt is translated); (c) foreign-Swarm import (no marker) keeps the current best-effort path byte-for-byte.
4. Architecture compliance — LOW: reuses the ONE translator (_translate_placeholders), the established neograph/prompt_spec marker convention, and the proven Component.metadata round-trip (step-1 gate test). No new grammar, no layer violation.
5. Similar-bug scalability — LOW: tjupj guard ratchets all current+future sites; fix empties MAKE_AGENT_UNPAIRED_ALLOWLIST making the guard strictly tighter.
6. Test coverage sufficiency — LOW given fix-atom additions: repro test (in tree, failing) + REQUIRED new tests: (i) translated system_prompt + declared flat Property on the mesh Agent, (ii) export→import round-trip recovers the original ${handoff.note} prompt, (iii) guard file updated (allowlist emptied/removed, EXPECTED_PAIRED_MAKE_AGENT_SITES 1→2).

DECISION translate-vs-fail-loud: TRANSLATE. Mesh members with ${handoff.*} prompts are a legitimate, validated shape (_check_portal_mesh admits them); fail-loud would regress a valid pipeline export when the Option-F machinery already exists and every sibling site uses it. Fail-loud reserved only if translation proved unsound — it does not (see 3b).

VERDICT: ALL_LOW — proceed to fix with the refined design (see design field).
## Fix landed (rugo8.7, 2026-07-27)
- _agent_spec.py _lower_portal_mesh_to_swarm: member prompts now routed through _translate_placeholders; Agent declares referenced flat Properties; per-member neograph/prompt_spec marker stamped on the Agent for round-trip. Stale :903-:915 comments rewritten.
- loader.py _reconstruct_swarm_mesh: prefers the prompt_spec marker's original_text (untranslated ${var}) over the translated system_prompt; foreign Swarms unchanged.
- Guard tightened: MAKE_AGENT_UNPAIRED_ALLOWLIST removed per its own meta-check; EXPECTED_PAIRED_MAKE_AGENT_SITES 1->2; req-4 discrepancy test flipped to closed-and-pinned.
- Tests: repro (fix-agnostic) green; + translated-wire-form test; + round-trip test (imports under the pre-existing '-agent' best-effort rename, prompt grammar recovered exactly).
- Mutation verified: reverting :916 to the raw form fails 2 tests (never-ships-raw + wire-form); restored.
- Gates: pytest 3659 passed / 0 failed (baseline 3658 + 3 new - 2 removed allowlist meta-tests); mypy clean (84 files); ruff clean.
## Sweep Verification (s7zt3.1) — rugo8.8

Re-scan command: grep -rn 'prompt_template=\|system_prompt=\|LlmNode(\|_make_agent(' src/ --include='*.py' | grep -v test
Pre-fix instances: 4 pyagentspec sites (1 MIGRATE, 3 ALLOWLIST) + 6 native-runtime ALLOWLIST
Post-fix instances: 4 pyagentspec sites (0 unpaired) + 6 native-runtime — count unchanged, the MIGRATE row re-localized by content

Structural guard: tests/test_guards_agent_spec_llm_construction_sites.py (pre-existing tjupj guard, TIGHTENED by this fix: allowlist emptied/removed, all _make_agent sites must be paired). Positive meta-tests (test_positive_paired_llmnode_is_not_flagged, test_node_translation_wrapper_also_satisfies_pairing) AND negative meta-tests (test_negative_unpaired_llmnode_is_flagged, test_negative_unpaired_make_agent_is_flagged) present. title: Implement Option F: translate neograph ${var} prompts to pyagentspec {{ var }} placeholders (amends m57mn's fail-loud guard, commit a109a7e)
description:
AMENDS an already-shipped decision. neograph-m57mn (commit a109a7e) added _check_placeholder_inputs, which makes any think/agent/act-mode node with real inputs raise ConfigurationError when its prompt text doesn't contain matching pyagentspec {{ jinja }} placeholders -- because neograph's own prompts use ${var} (dollar-brace), never jinja. This was reviewed and shipped as 'Option B: fail loud', on the reasoning that no faithful translation was possible.

That reasoning was WRONG, not just costly (maintainer correction, 2026-07-26): neograph's ${var} and pyagentspec's {{ var }} are two syntaxes for the IDENTICAL operation -- both are flat, non-recursive regex-based text substitution. pyagentspec's own placeholder regex is r'{{\\s*(\\w+)\\s*}}' (\\w+-only, no dots); neograph's shared scanner in src/neograph/_placeholders.py is DOLLAR_RE = r'\\$\\{([^}]+)\\}'. The fix is a real syntax-level TRANSLATION (rewrite ${prod.a} -> {{ prod_a }} in the literal prompt text, reusing neograph's EXISTING apply_scanner/DOLLAR_RE -- do not write a second scanner), not the previously-shipped fail-loud rejection.

Full design, verified against real source in two review cycles: docs/design/agent-spec-placeholder-translation-2026-07-26.md -- READ THE WHOLE FILE INCLUDING THE '§8.5 Addendum (post-review...)' SECTION, which corrects and REPLACES parts of the earlier sections. The addendum exists because the first adversarial review (docs/design/agent-spec-placeholder-translation-2026-07-26-review.md) found the doc as originally written was NOT implementable: _translate_placeholders emits Properties only for scanned names, but to_agent_spec's _emit_input_edges (_agent_spec.py:843-914 as of the m57mn commit) independently builds DataFlowEdge.destination_input from the FULL untranslated Property set, and pyagentspec's DataFlowEdge validator hard-rejects the mismatch (reproduced empirically in the review). Read both docs before starting -- do not re-derive the design, implement the addendum's corrected version.

Required implementation (5 sites, not 4 -- the review's headline finding was that the original 4-site plan missed a required consumer-side fix):
1. _agent_spec.py: replace _check_placeholder_inputs with _translate_placeholders(prompt_text, input_props, node_name) -> (rewritten_text, referenced_properties, flat_to_original_map). Called at the same 4 sites the old guard occupied: _lower_node's think branch, _make_agent (agent/act), _lower_oracle's think-mode variant loop, _lower_oracle's merge_prompt branch.
2. _emit_input_edges (the 5th, review-mandated site): route DataFlowEdge.destination_input through the same flat_to_original_map; DROP the edge entirely for any declared input NOT in that map (unreferenced in the prompt, or depth>=3 paths with no corresponding _properties_for Property at all) -- a real, acknowledged topology change (the exported primitive genuinely has no data path to that value), not a silent bug.
3. tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py: update cell-builder prompt strings to reference REAL declared input names (e.g. 'process ${prod.a}', not the current generic 'process ${x}') -- Option F cannot turn a cell green whose prompt never references its own input.
4. loader.py: add _MARK_PROMPT_SPEC ONLY at the 2 sites genuinely lacking a pre-existing marker (_reconstruct_primitive_node's LlmNode/think branch, _reconstruct_oracle_group's base_prompt) -- do NOT touch _reconstruct_agent_node or the oracle.merge_prompt reconstruction branch, both already read the untranslated original text from a pre-existing marker (_MARK_AGENT_SPEC['prompt'] / _MARK_ORACLE_SPEC['merge_prompt']); adding a second marker there is a redundant, driftable source of truth (verify this yourself before coding, don't take it on faith).
5. Re-scope the xfail reason for the 8 cells this task does NOT touch ({agent,act}-oracle-{merge_fn,merge_prompt}-{single,dict} -- see sibling task neograph-i7k7j) so the matrix's bookkeeping correctly says 'blocked on missing Oracle+agent/act lowering', not 'placeholder coupling'.

Collision rule (design doc §2.1 rule 6): two distinct ${path} references flattening to the same name -> ConfigurationError naming both. Unreferenced-input test required: declare inputs={'prod': T, 'unused': U}, prompt references only prod, assert exported LlmNode.inputs has ONLY the prod-derived Property and NO DataFlowEdge targets unused, but the round-trip marker still lets from_agent_spec reconstruct unused in the original Node.inputs.

TDD mandatory: confirm each of the 27 target cells (see design doc §8 for the exact list) currently fails for the placeholder-coupling reason, implement, confirm all 27 flip green, confirm the 8 out-of-scope cells (neograph-i7k7j) still fail but for the correctly re-scoped reason.

Gates: full matrix (uv run --extra dev --extra agent-spec pytest tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py -v), full agent-spec suite, full pytest suite, mypy, ruff.

Scope discipline: only src/neograph/_agent_spec.py, src/neograph/loader.py, test files. Do NOT implement template-ref prompt support (design doc explicitly defers -- to_agent_spec() has no prompt_compiler= param, none of the 27 cells need it). Do NOT touch the 8 Oracle+agent/act cells (neograph-i7k7j, separate task, separate root cause).

This must go through dev-practices:execute properly (research/plan/review/write-test/implement/verify/commit atoms, dp-reviewer gate) -- NOT ad hoc agent orchestration. A prior attempt at this exact task was done via unauthorized ad-hoc Agent spawning outside /execute discipline and was killed mid-flight per maintainer instruction (2026-07-26); the WIP diff is stashed (git stash, message 'WIP: unauthorized Option F implementation attempt') in case any of it is salvageable during the research/plan atoms, but it should NOT be trusted or reapplied without going through proper review.
design:
## Core Invariant
to_agent_spec produces a Flow that is BOTH a portable, foreign-consumable Agent Spec (every literal prompt string a foreign runtime sends to an LLM contains real, functioning `{{ flat_name }}` placeholders that pyagentspec OWN flat-substitution templating fills correctly) AND a lossless neograph round-trip source (untranslated `${path}` text + full original input TypeSpec ride ignorable, JSON-native `neograph/*` markers) -- with the SINGLE non-negotiable structural constraint that every Property declared on, and every input-name targeting (DataFlowEdge.destination_input AND sub-flow StartNode.inputs), a translated LlmNode/Agent uses the SAME flat name the ONE translator computed, so pyagentspec exact-set-match / edge validators pass by construction.

## Implementation Plan (reuse-first; TDD each of the 27 cells red->green) -- REFINED per review (j8bch.12)

## Core Invariant
The matrix's completeness must be MECHANICALLY DERIVED from two closed enumerations — pyagentspec's concrete flows.nodes.Node subclass set AND neograph's own introspected axes (Node.mode Literal, ModifierCombo, Oracle merge_fn XOR merge_prompt) — with a LOUD partition/completeness assertion on EACH axis, so any new pyagentspec primitive OR new neograph combo fails a loud test instead of silently going uncovered (the failure that let the Oracle merge_prompt cell escape).

## Implementation Plan (refined post-review)

1. **Shared capability module tests/agent_spec_capabilities.py — two-tier, importorskip NOT at top (M2).**
   - Tier A (always importable, NO pyagentspec dependency): the hand-authored name-string -> family classification dict, e.g. NODE_FAMILIES: dict[str,str] mapping 'LlmNode'->'text_scan', 'AgentNode'->'structural', 'ToolNode'->'echo', ... for all 14 concrete flows.nodes classes. Pure str->str data, no import of pyagentspec. Downstream neograph-tjupj imports THIS name-only and stays always-on (pure-AST guard must not become extra-gated/skipped — north-star: a structural guard silently not running is the forbidden silent seam).
   - Tier B (lazy, pyagentspec-dependent): a function all_concrete_flow_node_classes() that imports pyagentspec inside the function body, walks recursive Node.__subclasses__() filtered by inspect.isabstract, and a assert_registry_complete() that asserts set(NODE_FAMILIES) == {c.__name__ for c in walk}. Callers (the matrix) invoke these under their OWN pytest.importorskip('pyagentspec'). Module top does NOT importorskip.

2. **Enumerate neograph axes by introspection + LOUD partition on the modifier axis (M1).**
   - modes = typing.get_args(Node.model_fields['mode'].annotation) -> ('think','agent','act','scripted') ('raw' correctly excluded — it is raw_fn-set, not a mode Literal).
   - Modifier axis: derive from ModifierCombo (12 members). Define TWO explicit sets: SUPPORTED = {BARE,EACH,ORACLE,LOOP,OPERATOR} (what _lower_construct_item lowers) and UNSUPPORTED = {PORTAL + the 6 fusion combos that RAISE}. Add a LOUD partition assertion: set(ModifierCombo) == SUPPORTED | UNSUPPORTED AND SUPPORTED & UNSUPPORTED == empty — so a future combo added to the enum forces classification (mirrors step 1's registry-completeness assertion). Do NOT hand-type a single 'exclude PORTAL/composed' expression with no completeness check.
   - Oracle config discriminator: read field names off Oracle.model_fields ({merge_fn, merge_prompt}); fails loud (KeyError) on rename. Add a code comment noting the residual drift risk (won't auto-pick a future 3rd mutually-exclusive merge_* variant added to the XOR validator — modifiers.py:445-457) (LOW).

3. **Generate the cross product with a pinned builder contract (LOW).**
   - Axes: mode x modifier x oracle-config x input-shape. SUPPORTED modifier x 4 modes; ORACLE x 4 modes x {merge_fn,merge_prompt} x {single,dict}; input-shape {single,dict,+context(Each only)}. Also emit expected-RAISE cells for each UNSUPPORTED combo (pins 'restricted to what dispatch claims').
   - Pin the generic cell-builder contract explicitly: for each (mode,shape) document the @node kwargs it emits and the prompt CONTENT each LLM mode injects to trigger/avoid _check_placeholder_inputs (think: prompt=+model= referencing an input; agent/act: tools= + input-referencing system_prompt; oracle merge_prompt: gen_outputs-referencing prompt; scripted: no prompt). Reuse register_scripted / tests/schemas.py / conftest reset; extend schemas.py only if a model is missing.

4. **Make BOTH completeness diffs loud, key-spaces reconciled (M3).**
   - Express the 8 prior GREEN CELLS as their explicit NEW-scheme cell-ids (a hand-written PRIOR_GREEN: set[str] of new-scheme ids) and assert PRIOR_GREEN <= generated-key-set (true coverage check, not an old-vs-new string coincidence that fails or passes vacuously). Confirm input-shape (single AND dict) is crossed for ORACLE too (old had oracle-single AND oracle-dict), not just mode x config.
   - Keep the per-family GREEN baseline passing; mark surfaced RED cells with xfail(strict=True) carrying the neograph-i7k7j blocker id (mirrors existing _XFAIL_EXPORT/_XFAIL_ROUND_TRIP at lines 201-203) so the suite stays green-when-run yet records every red cell. strict=True makes a later fix XPASS->fail, a correct ratchet for i7k7j. Do NOT fix red cells (that is neograph-i7k7j). Record the final red-cell list (Findings families 1-5) as the handoff.

5. **Run** uv run --extra dev --extra agent-spec pytest tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py and confirm: registry completeness passes, ModifierCombo partition passes, PRIOR_GREEN-coverage diff passes, baseline green, red cells xfail-recorded. Also run the core suite subset for test_guards_agent_spec_lowering.py WITHOUT the agent-spec extra to confirm importing the shared module (Tier A) does NOT skip the always-on AST guard.

## Findings

### Reuse targets (do NOT re-derive)
- **pyagentspec closed enumeration**: walk `pyagentspec.flows.nodes` concrete `Node` subclasses. The module's own `__all__` == the 14 concrete classes (verified): AgentNode, ApiNode, BranchingNode, CatchExceptionNode, EndNode, FlowNode, InputMessageNode, LlmNode, MapNode, OutputMessageNode, ParallelFlowNode, ParallelMapNode, StartNode, ToolNode. The completeness assertion should compare the registry keyset against the reachable-concrete-subclass walk of `pyagentspec.flows.node.Node` (recursive `__subclasses__()`, filter `inspect.isabstract`), which yields exactly these 14 — matching `flows.nodes.__all__`.
- **neograph mode axis**: `typing.get_args(Node.model_fields['mode'].annotation)` -> `('think','agent','act','scripted')` (node.py:164). NOTE: 'raw' is NOT a mode Literal value — raw is expressed via `raw_fn` being set (rejected by `_reject_unrepresentable_fields`), so the closed mode axis is exactly these 4.
- **neograph modifier axis**: `Modifier.__subclasses__()` -> `[Oracle, Each, Operator, Loop, Portal]` (modifiers.py). BUT the per-node lowering dispatch (`_lower_construct_item`, _agent_spec.py:641) only handles `ModifierCombo` values {BARE, ORACLE, EACH, LOOP, OPERATOR} and raises for PORTAL/composed combos. Portal is exported at the *construct* level to a Swarm (`_lower_portal_mesh_to_swarm`), not via a per-node combo — so Portal is OUT of the per-node cross product. Use `ModifierCombo` (modifiers.py:65) + `classify_modifiers` (modifiers.py:107) to define the supported modifier axis; do not hand-type {BARE,ORACLE,EACH,LOOP,OPERATOR}.
- **Oracle config discriminator (the §4.3 missing axis)**: `Oracle.merge_fn` (modifiers.py:430) XOR `Oracle.merge_prompt` (modifiers.py:428), both `str | None`. The XOR is enforced by Oracle's model_validator (modifiers.py:445-457: "not both", "exactly one required"). Pull the two config-variant values FROM these field names / validator, not copy-typed into the test.

### pyagentspec `_get_inferred_inputs` family classification (verified from source)
- **text-scan / placeholder-coupled** (scans text/config for `{{ }}` via `get_placeholder(_properties)_from_json_object`; real inputs MUST appear as jinja placeholders): **LlmNode** (prompt_template), **ApiNode** (url/data/params/headers), **InputMessageNode** (message), **OutputMessageNode** (message).
- **structural / subflow-based** (inputs read from a nested flow's StartNode / subflow / agent — structural, not text): **AgentNode** (agent.inputs), **FlowNode** (subflow.inputs), **CatchExceptionNode** (subflow.inputs), **MapNode** (module-level `_get_inferred_inputs` -> `iterated_`-prefixed sub-flow StartNode inputs), **ParallelMapNode** (same), **ParallelFlowNode** (union of subflows' inputs).
- **unconstrained-echo** (inputs just echo self.inputs/tool.inputs/outputs; no coupling): **ToolNode** (tool.inputs), **BranchingNode** (single StringProperty branch-name), **StartNode** (self.inputs or outputs), **EndNode** (self.inputs or outputs).

### Which primitives the exporter actually constructs (dispatch claims)
- `_lower_node` (_agent_spec.py:214): mode think->LlmNode(placeholder-coupled), agent/act->AgentNode+Agent composite (placeholder-coupled via `_make_agent`->`_check_placeholder_inputs` on system_prompt), scripted->ToolNode(echo, safe).
- `_lower_oracle` (:355): variant per node.mode — think->LlmNode, scripted->ToolNode, **agent/act->raises ConfigurationError "no lowering yet" (:405)**; merge per config — merge_prompt->LlmNode(placeholder check on gen_outputs, :440), merge_fn->ToolNode(:459).
- `_lower_each`(:500)->MapNode wrapping single-node sub-Flow; `_lower_loop`(:540)->BranchingNode+back-edge over `_lower_node(body)`; `_lower_operator`(:613)->BranchingNode+InputMessageNode over `_lower_node(primary)`. EACH/LOOP/OPERATOR all delegate their inner node to `_lower_node`, so they inherit its full 4-mode dispatch.
- Exporter NEVER constructs: ApiNode, CatchExceptionNode, OutputMessageNode, ParallelFlowNode, ParallelMapNode (registry still must classify them for completeness; they are simply "not a lowering target").

### Currently-RED cells (surfaced by prototype cross-product; for neograph-i7k7j to fix — do NOT fix here)
Baseline GREEN (all scripted-mode / merge_fn, the existing 8 CELLS): none-single, none-dict, each-single, each-context, oracle-single, oracle-dict, loop-single, operator-single (16 passing = 8 x {export, round-trip}).
NEW RED families surfaced by adding the mode + oracle-config axes:
1. **think-mode + any real input -> RED**. Root cause: @node dict-form inputs give a Property title `{upstream}.{field}` (e.g. `prod.a`, _agent_spec.py:208); pyagentspec's placeholder scan can't match a DOTTED title to a jinja `{{ }}` (dots illegal in placeholders), so even a prompt literally containing `{{ a }}` still fails `_check_placeholder_inputs`. Verified.
2. **agent/act-mode + any real input -> RED**. Same coupling via `_make_agent`'s `_check_placeholder_inputs` on the system_prompt.
3. **Oracle scripted-mode + merge_prompt (with real gen_outputs) -> RED**. `_lower_oracle` merge branch builds an LlmNode and runs `_check_placeholder_inputs(oracle.merge_prompt, gen_outputs)` (:440); dotted/unreferenced output titles fail. This is the exact §4.3 / 4th-site gap.
4. **Oracle think-mode (variant) + real inputs -> RED** (variant LlmNode placeholder check, :391).
5. **Oracle agent/act-mode -> RED** (explicit ConfigurationError "Oracle+agent/act export has no Agent Spec lowering yet", :405).
Leaf LLM nodes with NO inputs stay GREEN (nothing to placeholder-couple).
