title: to_agent_spec: Oracle-modified node with ANY external input fails export — pyagentspec LlmNode rejects non-placeholder input Properties
description:
Discovered by the neograph-sdfgz coverage matrix (tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py, cells oracle-single / oracle-dict).

An Oracle(ensemble)-modified node that consumes ANY upstream input (dict-form fan-in like gen(prod: Alpha), OR single-type) fails to_agent_spec export:

    pydantic ValidationError: The LlmNode component received a property titled 'prod.a', but did not expect any properties

Root cause (DISTINCT from the neograph-hf505/3lk2l fan-out family): _lower_oracle builds each variant as an LlmNode with inputs=_properties_for(node.inputs). pyagentspec's LlmNode couples inputs to {{placeholder}} names in its prompt_template (ComponentWithIO._validate_no_extra_property) — an input Property not referenced as a prompt placeholder is rejected. neograph's variant prompt is a template-ref (e.g. 'rw/ensemble') or empty, so the dict-form-prefixed 'prod.a' is never a placeholder. Confirmed for BOTH scripted and think mode.

This is why the existing Oracle export test only ever used a node with NO inputs (outputs=Claims only). Oracle+inputs export has no coverage and no working representation yet.

FIX DIRECTION (needs design): either (a) map the node's input Properties to prompt placeholders the LlmNode accepts, or (b) represent Oracle variant inputs via a StartNode+DataFlowEdge sub-flow shape instead of LlmNode.inputs, or (c) document Oracle-with-inputs as a NO-REPR export and fail loud with a clear ConfigurationError (not a raw pydantic error).

The sdfgz matrix marks oracle-single/oracle-dict xfail(strict) referencing THIS id; removing the xfail is the acceptance test.
design: Root cause bifurcates: (1) _lower_oracle unconditionally builds LlmNode variants regardless of node.mode (unlike _lower_node's scripted/think/agent dispatch) -- this alone fully explains and fixes both xfail'd matrix cells (oracle-single/oracle-dict are merge_fn-only i.e. mode=scripted, so dispatching to ToolNode+ServerTool sidesteps the placeholder coupling entirely, verified against real pyagentspec source: ToolNode._get_inferred_inputs just echoes tool.inputs). (2) A broader, currently-UNTESTED latent bug: LlmNode/Agent's _get_inferred_inputs is a hardcoded {{ }} text-scan over prompt_template/system_prompt (component.py's ComponentWithIO validator runs on the primitive itself, not influenced by any wrapping Flow/StartNode -- confirmed the _lower_each StartNode-wrapping precedent does NOT transfer to LlmNode/Agent), so ANY think/agent/act node with real Node.inputs and a non-jinja prompt (i.e. every realistic neograph ${var}/template-ref prompt) fails the same way -- not Oracle-specific. Recommendation: ship the mode-dispatch fix now (resolves both failing cells), and for the residual think-mode-with-inputs case prefer fail-loud ConfigurationError (matches existing raw_fn/skip_when/callable-condition NO-REPR gaps) over synthesizing {{ }} placeholder text into the exported prompt, since the latter corrupts the literal prompt a foreign Agent-Spec consumer would send to an LLM -- undermining the exporter's stated cross-ecosystem-portability purpose. Full design + options B/C/D tradeoffs: docs/design/agent-spec-oracle-inputs-2026-07-25.md
notes:
Implemented Option A + 4-site Option B guard exactly per the reviewed design (docs/design/agent-spec-oracle-inputs-2026-07-25.md + review). 

Option A: _lower_oracle now dispatches variant construction per node.mode (mirrors _lower_node): think->LlmNode(guarded), scripted/raw->ToolNode+ServerTool (zero placeholder coupling), agent/act->ConfigurationError (out of scope, no test exercises it).

Option B: new _check_placeholder_inputs(prompt_text, input_props, node_name) helper (reuses pyagentspec's own get_placeholders_from_json_object, no second scanner), called from all 4 sites: (1) _lower_node think branch, (2) _make_agent (covers _lower_node's agent/act branch), (3) _lower_oracle's think-mode variant construction, (4) _lower_oracle's merge_prompt branch (gated on oracle.merge_prompt truthiness, not node.mode, per the review's 4th-site finding).

Also fixed loader.py's _reconstruct_oracle_group, which assumed variants are always LlmNode (used prompt_template/mode='think' unconditionally) -- this broke the matrix's oracle round-trip cells once Option A introduced ToolNode variants. Now dispatches per variant SpecNode type (LlmNode->think, ToolNode->scripted+scripted_fn), mirroring _reconstruct_primitive_node.

TDD: wrote failing tests first for all 4 sites (confirmed raw pydantic ValidationError pre-fix), then implemented, then confirmed ConfigurationError post-fix. Removed xfail(strict=True) markers from oracle-single/oracle-dict in test_agent_spec_matrix.py -- all 16 matrix cells (export + round-trip) pass for real.

Gates: full pytest suite 3497 passed (0 failed) including tests/test_agent_spec_export.py (32), tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py (16), tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py, tests/test_agent_spec_import.py, tests/test_agent_spec_types.py, tests/test_agent_spec_operator_export_doc.py (104 total agent-spec tests). mypy src/neograph: clean. ruff check on all touched files: clean (one pre-existing unrelated ruff hit on tests/test_agent_spec_export.py's original import block, confirmed present on develop before this change, not introduced by this task).

Files touched: src/neograph/_agent_spec.py, src/neograph/loader.py, tests/test_agent_spec_export.py, tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py.

title: BUG: from_agent_spec — @node map_over Each round-trip fails (reconstructed element type mismatch, synthesized AgentSpecType_ classes)
description:
Reproduced 2026-07-24 (independent verification of the qtfof.1-4 batch). A primary @node(map_over=...) Each pipeline EXPORTS fine (qtfof.1 fixed the export) but FAILS to round-trip:

    @node(outputs=Items) def prod()->Items: ...
    @node(outputs=B, map_over='prod.groups', map_key='v') def ver(item:Item)->B: ...
    flow = to_agent_spec(c)            # OK
    from_agent_spec(flow)              # ConstructError: Each(over='prod.groups') element type mismatch
                                       #   expected AgentSpecType_01b0c1e5..., found list[AgentSpecType_...]

The reconstructed types are synthesized AgentSpecType_<hash> classes that do NOT match the producer's element type, so Each's assembly-time element-type check rejects the round-tripped Construct. Type-IDENTITY loss on round-trip — same family as qtfof.4 (structural naming) and wqb5t (register_type compares names not types); those fixes did not close this path. v1-gating: 'round-trip-faithful' is false for the primary Each shape.
notes: FIXED by neograph-sdfgz consolidated family-B pass. Repro (@node map_over Each round-trip) now passes; pinned by tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py cell each-single. loader._dict_form_inputs_from_props un-groups the dotted fan-out-receiver Properties so the element reconstructs to the SAME structural class as the producer's list element.

title: Systematic Agent Spec export/round-trip COVERAGE MATRIX: parametrize modifier x input-shape x round-trip (converge the surface, end the whack-a-mole)
description:
The Agent Spec export/round-trip surface has produced a sibling bug on every fix: ozxqw -> qtfof.1/.2/.3 -> hf505 -> neograph-3lk2l. All cluster in two root-cause families: (a) dict-form title/property mapping in DataFlowEdge wiring, (b) type-identity loss on round-trip (synthesized AgentSpecType_ classes). The green suite misses them because export/round-trip tests use single-type-input WORKAROUND shapes, not the primary @node shapes (map_over=, dict-form, +context).

DELIVERABLE: a PARAMETRIZED export+round-trip test matrix over {no modifier, Each(map_over), Oracle(ensemble), Loop, Operator} x {single-type inputs, dict-form fan-in, +non-fan-out context input} x {export, round-trip}, all using the PRIMARY @node shapes. Run it to enumerate EVERY hole at once (do not fix one at a time). Then consolidate the fixes around the two root-cause families rather than per-symbol patches. This test becomes the permanent guard that the surface stays converged. ACCEPTANCE: the full matrix is green (or each red cell has a filed, wired blocker); 2ev48 does not close until this matrix passes.
design:
## Core Invariant
The Each fan-out receiver key is NOT a dict-form fan-in upstream — it is the iterated ELEMENT. Its Agent-Spec representation must round-trip to the SAME structural type as the producer's list element, and context (non-fan-out) inputs must lower to VALID MapNode 'iterated_'-prefixed inputs. One rule (the fan_out_param skip already in _check_fan_in_inputs) governs the split on BOTH export and import; never re-derive it per-symptom.

## Implementation Plan (consolidated, two families)

### Family A — export: context inputs -> valid MapNode iterated_ inputs (fixes hf505)
1. _agent_spec._lower_each: populate the inner sub-flow's StartNode.inputs with the inner node's input Properties (the context-input props), so MapNode._get_inferred_inputs yields iterated_{title}. (Fan-out-receiver-only case still exports — inputs may be unconnected.)
2. to_agent_spec dict-form DataFlowEdge loop (line ~774): when the destination item is Each-modified (MapNode), prefix destination_input with 'iterated_'. Detect via modifier_set.each is not None (the same node object is in scope).

### Family B — round-trip: fan-out receiver type identity (fixes 3lk2l)
3. _agent_spec._lower_each / EachSpec marker: record fan_out_param in _MARK_EACH_SPEC so import knows which dotted-prefix group is the element.
4. loader._reconstruct_each_node: un-prefix the fan-out receiver's dotted group ('item.v' -> 'v') before reconstructing, so the element type synthesizes to the SAME AgentSpecType_ hash as the producer's list element. Context groups stay dict-form fan-in.

### wqb5t (P2, do in same pass — cheap, prevents future sibling)
5. spec_types._fields_match: compare (name, _property/field type-signature) pairs, not names only.

## Verify
- Parametrized matrix test (write FIRST, RED): {no-mod, Each(map_over), Oracle(ensemble), Loop, Operator} x {single-type, dict-form fan-in, +context} x {export, round-trip}, PRIMARY @node shapes. Reproduce hf505/3lk2l as red cells first.
- Gate: uv run --extra dev --extra agent-spec pytest ; baseline 3476, zero regressions.
- Close hf505/3lk2l/wqb5t each only after its own repro passes under the consolidated fix.
notes:
## Findings (research neograph-56d7f.2)

The whack-a-mole cluster (ozxqw -> qtfof.1/.2/.3/.4 -> hf505 -> 3lk2l -> wqb5t) reduces to ONE disease with two faces: neograph encodes fan-in/fan-out STRUCTURE in pyagentspec Property TITLES via three prefix conventions, and those conventions are applied INCONSISTENTLY between the export (title -> DataFlowEdge) side and the import (title -> reconstructed type) side. The green suite misses it because export/round-trip tests use single-type-input WORKAROUND shapes (Node.scripted(inputs=Tagged)) instead of the primary @node shapes (map_over=/dict-form/+context).

The three prefix conventions in play:
- dict-form: _properties_for() prefixes a dict-form inputs/outputs Property title with '{key}.' (src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:167).
- Each fan-out receiver skip: the fan_out_param key is NOT an upstream edge; it is fed per-item by the MapNode sub-flow, so it is skipped (export loop already mirrors this).
- MapNode 'iterated_' prefix: pyagentspec MapNode INFERS its external input Properties from the inner sub-flow StartNode and PREFIXES every one with 'iterated_' (confirmed against installed pyagentspec MapNode docstring: 'complemented with the iterated_ prefix', type Union[inner, List[inner]]).

### Root-cause family A -- export title/property mapping in DataFlowEdge wiring
- hf505: an Each node with BOTH a fan-out key AND a non-fan-out context key (inputs={'source':RawText,'cluster':ClusterGroup}, fan_out_param='cluster'). The dict-form fan-in loop skips 'cluster' and emits a DataFlowEdge to the MapNode with destination_input='source.text' -- but the MapNode's real inner property is 'iterated_source.text', so pydantic raises ValidationError ('does not have any property with that name'). The dest_node for an Each item IS the MapNode (_lower_construct_item:586 returns map_node as both primary and data_node). The fix locus is the destination_input line (currently f'{upstream_name}.{prop.title}') at _agent_spec.py:781, which must become 'iterated_{upstream_name}.{prop.title}' when the destination is a MapNode.

### Root-cause family B -- type-identity loss on round-trip (synthesized AgentSpecType_ classes)
- 3lk2l: a primary @node(map_over=) Each EXPORTS fine but FAILS round-trip with 'Each(over=...) element type mismatch: expected AgentSpecType_X, found list[AgentSpecType_Y]'. The Each element-type check (_validation_inputs.py:252 _check_each_path) compares the fanned-out RECEIVER input_type against the element_type of the producer's over-path list field via _types_compatible. On round-trip these must be the SAME synthesized class. They are NOT, because the inner Each node's fan-out receiver Property titles carry the dict-form '{key}.' prefix (from _properties_for), so on import _agent_spec_props_to_type(spec_node.inputs) synthesizes a model whose FIELDS differ structurally from the producer's element model -> different _structural_type_name hash -> different class -> mismatch. Same disease as qtfof.4 (structural naming) and wqb5t (register_type).
- wqb5t: register_type's idempotency check _fields_match (spec_types.py:45-47) compares field NAMES only, never TYPES. Two structurally-different models with the same field-name set registered under the same explicit name silently collapse to the first (wrong) one. Must compare (field_name, field_type) pairs.

## Relevant Code (file:line)
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:731-811 -- to_agent_spec's per-item DataFlowEdge loop; dict-form branch 739-784, fan_out_param skip 745-752 (already mirrors _validation_inputs). Family-A fix locus: destination_input at :781.
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:410-437 -- _lower_each: MapNode wrapping single-node sub-flow; inner = _lower_node(node) so inner inputs = _properties_for(node.inputs) = dict-form '{key}.field' titles. This is where the 'iterated_' contract originates on the pyagentspec side.
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:154-170 -- _properties_for: the '{key}.' dict-form title prefix (the shared convention).
- src/neograph/_validation_inputs.py:157-159 -- the REUSE target: 'if upstream_name == fan_out_key: continue' skip pattern the export loop already copies. fan_out_candidates() (imported from _ir_normalize) is the single shared fan-out-key rule.
- src/neograph/_validation_inputs.py:197-260 -- _check_each_path; the element-type check at :252 that rejects the round-tripped Each (family B symptom site).
- src/neograph/loader.py:339-367 -- _reconstruct_each_node (inverse of _lower_each); inner reconstructed via _reconstruct_primitive_node then renamed; KEEPS inner inputs.
- src/neograph/loader.py:255-268 -- _reconstruct_primitive_node: inputs = _inputs_from_data_edges(...) or _agent_spec_props_to_type(spec_node.inputs); the fallback path that synthesizes the divergent receiver type from prefixed titles.
- src/neograph/loader.py:80-97 -- _agent_spec_props_to_type: name = _structural_type_name(props); agent_spec_properties_to_types(props,name); the reuse mechanism intended to unify identical structures into ONE class.
- src/neograph/spec_types.py:45-47 -- _fields_match (wqb5t fix locus: compare (name,type) pairs).
- src/neograph/spec_types.py:244-301 -- _property_type_signature + _structural_type_name (structural hash; qtfof.4 recursion already lands here).
- src/neograph/spec_types.py:398-418 -- agent_spec_properties_to_types (explicit-name register path wqb5t warns can still collapse).

## Test infra / gap
- Extra gating: [agent-spec] optional extra (pyproject.toml:70, pyagentspec>=26.1.0,<27). All agent-spec test files module-gate with pytest.importorskip('pyagentspec') at top; run with 'uv run --extra dev --extra agent-spec pytest ...'. This is the correct import-guard pattern to copy.
- Existing tests use WORKAROUND single-type shapes: tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py:103 Each via Node.scripted('each_step', inputs=Tagged, ...) | Each(...) -- NOT @node(map_over=). Loop via inputs=Draft (single type). The primary @node shapes (map_over=, dict-form fan-in from construct_from_functions, +context) are exactly what is untested.
- Helpers: tests/schemas.py:54-58 _producer/_consumer (Node.scripted single-type -- these are the workaround generators). Schemas RawText/Claims/ClusterGroup/Clusters/MatchResult available. build_test_compile_kwargs / register_scripted used for run-level round-trip.
- Existing structural guards live in tests/test_guards_agent_spec_lowering.py (TestDictFormFanInResolvesRealPropertyTitles, TestDictFormFanInSkipsFanOutReceiver) -- the permanent-guard home once the matrix is green.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- MapNode 'iterated_' prefix applies to ALL inferred inputs; when an Each node has ONLY the fan-out key (qtfof.1, already fixed) there are no context DataFlowEdges so the bug is invisible -- it only surfaces with a SECOND context input (hf505). The matrix's '+context' column is what forces this cell.
- Family B fix must keep the _structural_type_name + register_type reuse mechanism (do NOT add a parallel type synthesizer). The fix is to NORMALIZE the receiver's Property titles (strip the dict-form '{key}.'/'iterated_' prefix) BEFORE structural hashing on import, so the receiver hashes identically to the producer's element type. Alternatively resolve the receiver type from the over-path producer element. Prefer the prefix-normalization since it keeps ONE walker.
- wqb5t _fields_match change (names+types) could newly WARN/overwrite on legitimately-distinct same-name models -- ensure existing register_type idempotent callers (load_project_types) still no-op for genuinely identical schemas.
- Three-surface parity: agent-spec is IR-level free-function testing (to_agent_spec/from_agent_spec), exempt from the @node/declarative/programmatic triple per the roundtrip file's own stated exemption -- but the matrix SHOULD still drive the primary @node shape (map_over=/construct_from_functions) since that is the shape whose gap caused every bug.
- Do NOT fix cells one at a time: build the full matrix, run it, enumerate ALL red cells at once, then consolidate around the two families (per task acceptance).
## Findings (research neograph-56d7f.2)

The whack-a-mole cluster (ozxqw -> qtfof.1/.2/.3/.4 -> hf505 -> 3lk2l/wqb5t) reduces to ONE disease with two faces: the fan-in/fan-out prefix conventions that encode DAG structure in Agent-Spec Property TITLES are applied ASYMMETRICALLY between the export (title -> DataFlowEdge) and import (title -> reconstructed type) sides. Three title conventions are in play and each side must honor all three:
  1. dict-form fan-in prefix `{upstream_name}.{field}` (from `_properties_for`, _agent_spec.py:167)
  2. Each fan-out receiver SKIP (the `fan_out_param` key names no upstream node)
  3. MapNode `iterated_{...}` prefix -- pyagentspec MapNode INFERS its external inputs from the inner sub-flow StartNode and PREFIXES every one with `iterated_` (confirmed live against installed pyagentspec MapNode docstring: "The names of the inputs will be the ones of the inner flow, complemented with the `iterated_` prefix").

### Family A (export -- hf505, dict-form title/property mapping in DataFlowEdge wiring)
For an Each node with BOTH a fan-out key AND a non-fan-out context key (`inputs={'source':RawText,'cluster':ClusterGroup}`, fan_out_param='cluster'), the export loop skips 'cluster' correctly but emits the context edge with `destination_input='source.text'` -- while the dest MapNode only exposes `iterated_source.text`. pyagentspec DataFlowEdge validation rejects it. The existing fan_out skip (already mirrors _check_fan_in_inputs) is CORRECT; the missing piece is the `iterated_` prefix when the destination data_node is a MapNode (Each combo).

### Family B (round-trip -- 3lk2l/qtfof.4/wqb5t, type-identity loss)
The primary `@node(map_over=...)` shape EXPORTS fine (qtfof.1) but FAILS `from_agent_spec` with "Each(over=...) element type mismatch: expected AgentSpecType_X, found list[AgentSpecType_Y]". Root: the Each inner node's fan-out receiver input Properties are titled with the dict-form prefix `item.<field>` (via `_properties_for`), so on import `_agent_spec_props_to_type(spec_node.inputs)` synthesizes a model whose FIELD NAMES / structural signature include the `item.` prefix -- structurally DIFFERENT from the producer's element type (the same `Item` nested inside `prod.groups` reconstructs WITHOUT the prefix). Two different `_structural_type_name` hashes -> two different synthesized classes -> `_check_each_path`'s `_types_compatible(element_type, input_type)` (_validation_inputs.py:252) rejects. The intended dedup mechanism (`_structural_type_name` + `register_type` idempotency) never fires because the prefixed titles make the shapes genuinely diverge. wqb5t compounds this: `_fields_match` (spec_types.py:45-47) compares field NAMES only, so a same-named-different-typed collision under a reused explicit name silently keeps the WRONG class.

### Existing reuse targets (do NOT reinvent)
- Export fan_out skip: _agent_spec.py:745-752 already replicates `_validation_inputs.py:158` (`if upstream_name == fan_out_key: continue`). The new context-key branch must ROUTE (not skip) with the `iterated_` prefix -- reuse `classify_modifiers(item)` / ModifierCombo.EACH (already imported) to detect a MapNode destination.
- Structural type dedup: `_structural_type_name` (spec_types.py:273) + `register_type`/`_fields_match` (spec_types.py:45-67) is the ONE canonical reuse-a-class mechanism. Family B fix = make the fan-out receiver reconstruct WITHOUT the dict-form prefix so its structural signature matches the producer element (then dedup fires for free), PLUS strengthen `_fields_match` to compare (name, type) pairs.
- Single JSON-Schema walker invariant: `_resolve_field_type` / `_property_to_field_type` are twins; keep any type change inside them, never a 3rd walker.

### Current-vs-workaround coverage gap (why green suite missed it)
The round-trip suite pins Each with a SINGLE-TYPE-input workaround: `Node.scripted("each_step", inputs=Tagged, ...) | Each(...)` (test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py:103) -- NOT the primary `@node(map_over=..., map_key=...)` dict-form shape. `_producer`/`_consumer` (tests/schemas.py:54-59) are single-type too. So the dominant @node shape was never exercised for Each/Oracle/Loop/Operator x dict-form x round-trip.
## Findings (ground-truthed via repro + pyagentspec source)

### Reproduced holes (primary @node shapes)

title: to_agent_spec: Each-modified node's non-fan-out context inputs don't route to MapNode's iterated_-prefixed inner properties
description:
Discovered while fixing neograph-qtfof.1 (dict-form Each fan-out receiver export bug).

When an Each-modified node has BOTH a fan-out receiver key AND a non-fan-out upstream context key in its dict-form inputs (e.g. inputs={'source': RawText, 'cluster': ClusterGroup} with fan_out_param='cluster'), to_agent_spec's dict-form fan-in loop emits a DataFlowEdge targeting the MapNode with destination_input='source.text' -- but pyagentspec's MapNode infers its own input Properties from the inner sub-flow's StartNode, each PREFIXED with 'iterated_' (e.g. 'iterated_source.text'), per MapNode's own docstring. So any Each-modified node with additional context inputs beyond the fan-out item fails export with a pydantic ValidationError: 'DataFlowEdge ... does not have any property with that name'.

Repro (raises pydantic.ValidationError, not caught by qtfof.1's fix which only handles the fan-out-receiver-only case):

    @node(outputs=RawText)
    def source() -> RawText: ...

    @node(outputs=Clusters)
    def clusters() -> Clusters: ...

    @node(outputs=MatchResult, map_over='clusters.groups', map_key='label')
    def verify(source: RawText, cluster: ClusterGroup) -> MatchResult: ...

    pipeline = construct_from_functions('mixed', [source, clusters, verify])
    to_agent_spec(pipeline)  # raises pydantic ValidationError

FIX: to_agent_spec's dict-form fan-in loop (and/or _lower_each) needs to route non-fan-out context-key DataFlowEdges with destination_input prefixed 'iterated_' when the destination is a MapNode (Each-modified), instead of the bare dict-form-prefixed title used for non-Each destinations.
notes: FIXED by neograph-sdfgz consolidated family-A pass. Repro (Each map_over + non-fan-out context input) now exports AND round-trips; pinned by tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py cell each-context. _lower_each declares StartNode inputs so MapNode infers iterated_ inputs; to_agent_spec routes context-input edges to iterated_{title} via input_targets.

title: to_agent_spec: dict-form Each fan-out receiver breaks export (sibling of ozxqw)
description:
Discovered while implementing neograph-e3b4j's docs example (examples/31_agent_spec_each_oracle_loop.py).

When an @node uses map_over= sugar (or any dict-form inputs where one key is the Each fan-out receiver, e.g. inputs={'item': Tagged} with fan_out_param='item'), to_agent_spec's dict-form fan-in branch (the branch fixed for neograph-ozxqw) raises ConfigurationError: 'node's dict-form inputs references upstream X, which has no exportable Agent Spec node' -- because 'item' (or whatever the fan-out receiver param is named) is not an upstream NODE name, it's the fan-out item slot.

ROOT CAUSE: _agent_spec.py's to_agent_spec dict-form fan-in loop (the code fixed by ozxqw) does not check item.fan_out_param and skip it, unlike _validation_inputs.py's _check_fan_in_inputs which correctly does 'if upstream_name == fan_out_key: continue'.

BEFORE ozxqw's fix, this case was accidentally silent (source_node lookup failed -> None -> continue, no edge, no error) -- ozxqw's fix correctly converted that silent skip to a fail-loud ConfigurationError for the general case, but this specific sub-case (Each fan-out receiver) is a LEGITIMATE shape that should export successfully (presumably by NOT emitting a DataFlowEdge for the fan-out slot at all, since MapNode's own sub-flow wiring handles the per-item dataflow internally -- see _lower_each).

WORKAROUND used in e3b4j's example: build the Each-fanned node with explicit single-type inputs= (not map_over= dict-form), then pipe | Each(...) afterward -- this is the already-proven export shape (test_agent_spec_export.py's own Each test uses this shape too, not map_over=).

FIX: to_agent_spec's dict-form fan-in loop should check item.fan_out_param (mirroring _validation_inputs.py's skip) and skip that key when building DataFlowEdges, for both @node's map_over= sugar and the programmatic Node(inputs={...}) | Each(...) equivalent.
design:
## Root Cause
_agent_spec.py's dict-form fan-in DataFlowEdge-emission loop (to_agent_spec) does not check item.fan_out_param before treating an inputs-dict key as an upstream node name, unlike _validation_inputs.py's _check_fan_in_inputs which correctly skips it.

## Fix Approach
Added a fan_out_key = getattr(item, 'fan_out_param', None) check inside the dict-form fan-in loop; skip the key equal to fan_out_key before doing the upstream node/property lookup. Applies uniformly to both @node's map_over= sugar and the programmatic Node(inputs={...}) | Each(...) surface, since fan_out_param is set by the single IR normalizer (_ir_normalize.py) for both.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_agent_spec_export.py::TestToAgentSpecLowersModifiers::test_map_over_dict_form_fan_out_receiver_exports_without_error
- Also added: test_programmatic_each_with_dict_form_fan_out_receiver_exports_without_error (three-surface parity)
- Root cause: to_agent_spec's dict-form fan-in loop (_agent_spec.py ~line 720) iterated ni.by_name without skipping item.fan_out_param, so the Each fan-out receiver key (e.g. 'cluster') was treated as an upstream node name and raised ConfigurationError since no such node exists.
- NOTE: during repro I found a DEEPER, SEPARATE bug: when an Each-modified node ALSO has a non-fan-out context upstream key (e.g. inputs={'source': RawText, 'cluster': ClusterGroup}), the emitted DataFlowEdge targets the MapNode with destination_input='source.text', but pyagentspec's MapNode expects inner-flow inputs prefixed 'iterated_<name>' (per MapNode's own docstring: inputs inferred from StartNode, prefixed 'iterated_'). This is OUT OF SCOPE for qtfof.1 (which is specifically the fan-out-receiver-only case) -- filing a follow-up bug for it separately.
## Trace Similar Patterns
Searched all ni.by_name / dict-form inputs iteration sites in src/neograph/ (_construct_builder.py, _construct_graph.py, _fan_agent.py, _fan_agent_wrap.py, _ir_normalize.py, _input_shape.py, _param_classify.py, lint.py).

Only _agent_spec.py's dict-form fan-in loop had the specific disease: 'raise if dict key not found as a real producer node', without first excluding item.fan_out_param. _construct_graph.py's adjacency builder iterates the same by_name dict but uses a membership check ('if dep_field in decorated') rather than a raise-on-miss, so it is naturally immune to this disease (a fan-out key simply produces no adjacency edge, which is correct).

Two RELATED-but-DISTINCT bugs surfaced during this trace, already filed as separate beads issues (different root cause, different fix):
- neograph-hf505: Each-modified node's non-fan-out context inputs need 'iterated_' prefix routing to MapNode -- NOT a missing fan_out_param skip, but a destination-node property-naming convention gap.
- neograph-qtfof.2 (sibling in this same epic): Loop self-edge assumes bare (unprefixed) destination property titles -- a different resolution-shape bug, not a missing-skip bug.

No further instances of this exact pattern (missing fan_out_param skip causing false 'unknown upstream' errors) found elsewhere in the codebase.
## Codebase Disease Scan (qtfof.1)
Disease pattern (SYNTACTIC): a loop over dict-form inputs (ni.by_name) that RAISES when a key is not found among real producer nodes, without first excluding item.fan_out_param.

| Site | Verdict | Notes |
|------|---------|-------|

| runner.py:491 | ALLOWLIST (already correct) | add_edge is tolerant, no raise-on-miss |
| _input_shape.py:118, _param_classify.py:54, lint.py:989 | N/A | DI/param classification, not upstream-producer lookup -- different concern |

No other instance of the disease found. Scan method: grep for by_name iteration sites + manual read of each (SYNTACTIC, single exact pattern, no fan-out needed).
## Architect Review (qtfof.1)

1. Root cause correctness: CONFIRMED. The dict-form fan-in loop in to_agent_spec treated every ni.by_name key as an upstream node name; the Each fan-out receiver key is not one. Matches _validation_inputs.py's precedent exactly.
2. Fix minimality: LOW risk. 6-line addition (fan_out_key lookup + one skip-continue), no change to any other branch. Mirrors the exact pattern the validator already uses (getattr(item, 'fan_out_param', None), skip on match).
3. Regression risk: LOW. The skip only fires when upstream_name == item.fan_out_param, which by construction (single IR-normalizer writer, _ir_normalize.py) is never a real upstream node name — so no legitimate edge is dropped.
4. Architecture compliance: PASS. Change confined to src/neograph/_agent_spec.py (the Agent Spec interop layer, off the node.py/construct.py/_construct_validation.py/factory.py/modifiers.py off-limits list). Does not touch fan_out_param's single-writer invariant (only reads it).
5. Similar bug scalability: covered by trace-similar (neograph-03k9k.3) -- no sibling sites found; the two adjacent-but-distinct bugs (hf505, qtfof.2) are already filed separately with their own fix scope.
6. Test coverage sufficiency: PASS. Covers both @node map_over= sugar surface AND programmatic Node(inputs=...) | Each(...) surface (three-surface parity rule). Full suite run clean (3462 passed, 0 failed, baseline 3460 + 2 new tests).

VERDICT: ALL_LOW -- fix proceeds to commit.
## Sweep Verification (qtfof.1)

- File: tests/test_guards_agent_spec_lowering.py

title: to_agent_spec/from_agent_spec: Loop self-edge requires single-type inputs, breaks on dict-form
description:
Discovered while implementing neograph-e3b4j's docs example (examples/31_agent_spec_each_oracle_loop.py).

A Loop-modified node with DICT-FORM inputs (e.g. @node's primary shape, inputs={'upstream': T}) breaks _lower_loop's self-edge construction: 'for prop in _properties_for(node.outputs): DataFlowEdge(source_node=body, source_output=prop.title, destination_node=body, destination_input=prop.title)' assumes destination_input (a bare field title like 'content') is a real Property on the destination node -- but dict-form inputs prefix titles as 'upstream.content' (per _properties_for's dict-form convention), so pydantic's DataFlowEdge validator rejects it: 'destination node does not have any property with that name'.

WORKAROUND used in e3b4j's example: pass inputs=<SingleType> explicitly to @node (overriding the dict-form inference) for any Loop-wrapped node, matching the single-type convention the existing proven test (test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py::test_loop_round_trips_and_runs) already uses.

FIX: _lower_loop's self-edge construction needs to handle dict-form inputs the same way the general fan-in fix (ozxqw) does -- resolve per-field Property titles that match BOTH the destination's actual (possibly prefixed) input properties AND the source's (its own) output properties, rather than assuming both are bare/unprefixed.
design:
## Root Cause
_lower_loop's self-edge DataFlowEdge always used the bare output Property title as destination_input, assuming node.inputs is single-type (bare titles). Dict-form inputs prefix titles as '{key}.{field}'.

## Fix Approach
Resolve the correct dict-form key to prefix destination_input with: (1) the Loop self-reference key (field_name_for(node.name)) if present in ni.by_name, else (2) the dict-form key whose declared type is compatible (issubclass either direction) with the node's own output type -- covers the realistic 'inputs={upstream_name: T}' shape. No prefix when inputs is single-type or None (existing bare-title behavior preserved).
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing tests written:
  - tests/test_agent_spec_export.py::TestToAgentSpecLowersModifiers::test_loop_dict_form_inputs_self_edge_exports_without_error (self-referencing dict-form key)
  - tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py::TestEachOracleLoopRoundTripPreservesBehavior::test_loop_dict_form_inputs_round_trips_and_runs (realistic @node primary shape: inputs={'seed': Draft}, full export->import->compile->run)
- Root cause: _lower_loop's self-edge construction (_agent_spec.py ~line 475) unconditionally used the BARE output Property title as destination_input, but dict-form inputs prefix input Property titles as '{upstream}.{field}' per _properties_for's dict-form convention. For inputs=SingleType (the only previously-tested case) titles are bare so no bug manifested; for dict-form inputs (@node's PRIMARY shape) the self-edge crashed pyagentspec's own DataFlowEdge validator.

title: BUG: to_agent_spec fails on dict-form fan-in (@node's primary shape) — DataFlowEdge source_output uses node name not property
description:
to_agent_spec() cannot export the PRIMARY @node fan-in shape. A downstream node with a typed upstream param (`def summ(seed: A)`) compiles to `inputs={'seed': A}` (dict-form keyed by upstream node name) — the dominant shape @node produces. Exporting it raises a raw pydantic ValidationError, not a clean neograph error.

REPRO (fails):
    import neograph as n
    from pydantic import BaseModel
    class A(BaseModel): x: int
    class B(BaseModel): y: int
    seed = n.Node.scripted('seed', fn='f', outputs=A)
    summ = n.Node.scripted('summ', fn='g', inputs={'seed': A}, outputs=B)
    n.to_agent_spec(n.Construct('rt', nodes=[seed, summ]))
    # -> ValidationError: DataFlowEdge 'seed_to_summ' source_output 'seed' is not a property of source node 'seed'
The pipeline COMPILES in neograph (valid). A real @node two-node pipeline reproduces it identically.

ROOT CAUSE: src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:647 — the general fan-in DataFlowEdge sets `source_output=upstream_name` (the inputs-dict KEY = the upstream NODE name) instead of the source node's real exported output PROPERTY title. Contrast the correct paths: Oracle (line ~398) and Loop (line ~478) use `source_output=prop.title`. Single-type inputs (inputs=Model, not dict) go through a different path and export fine.

TEST COVERAGE GAP: the export/round-trip suites (test_agent_spec_export.py, csdcl round-trip) used `_producer`/`_consumer` helpers with SINGLE-TYPE inputs — never the dict-form (@node) shape — so they were green while the primary shape was broken.

FIX: wire the fan-in DataFlowEdge(s) to the source node's actual output property/properties (match how outputs are exported, per-field like the Oracle/Loop paths). If any dict-form case is genuinely unrepresentable, fail loud via ConfigurationError, never a raw pydantic error. ACCEPTANCE: add a dict-form-fan-in EXPORT test AND a dict-form round-trip test; a real @node two-node pipeline must export + round-trip.
design:
## Root Cause
_agent_spec.py's general fan-in DataFlowEdge builder (dict-form branch, ~line 636-647) confuses the inputs-dict KEY (upstream node name, e.g. 'seed') with the upstream node's exported output Property TITLE (e.g. field name 'x' for a single-type output, or 'seed.x' were dict-form outputs involved). It sets both source_output and destination_input to the bare upstream_name, which pyagentspec's DataFlowEdge validator rejects because no node exports a property literally named after another node.

## Fix Approach
Mirror the single-type-inputs path (lines ~658-673) and the Oracle/Loop precedent (prop.title): for each dict-form inputs entry (upstream_name -> expected_type), resolve the upstream node's real output properties via _properties_for(upstream.outputs) (or normalize_outputs), and emit one DataFlowEdge per shared field: source_output=<upstream's real output Property title>, destination_input=<this node's own input Property title for that key — 'key.field' per _properties_for's dict-form prefixing convention>. If the upstream node cannot be resolved to a real property (fail-loud), raise ConfigurationError instead of letting pydantic's raw ValidationError leak through.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_agent_spec_export.py::TestToAgentSpecExportsDictFormFanIn::test_two_node_dict_form_fan_in_chain_exports_without_raising
- Confirmed red: pydantic.ValidationError raised at src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:644 (DataFlowEdge construction) — 'source_output' seed does not exist as a property of node 'seed'.
- Root cause: the dict-form fan-in branch in _agent_spec.py (~line 630-647) sets source_output=upstream_name (the inputs-dict KEY, which is the upstream NODE'S NAME), instead of the upstream node's actual output Property title(s). Contrast Oracle (line ~399) and Loop (line ~479), which correctly iterate _properties_for(...) and use prop.title.
## Similar Pattern Analysis (trace-similar)
Bug pattern category: constructing a pyagentspec DataFlowEdge with a raw dict/name KEY instead of a resolved output-Property TITLE.

Grepped all 4 DataFlowEdge construction sites in _agent_spec.py (source_output=/destination_input=):
- line 399/401 (Oracle fan-out/fan-in): uses prop.title -- CORRECT
- line 479/481 (Loop): uses prop.title -- CORRECT
- line 647/649 (general dict-form fan-in, the bug): uses upstream_name (the dict KEY / upstream node NAME) -- INCORRECT
- line 674/676 (single-type inputs fallback): uses shared_title (resolved from _properties_for) -- CORRECT

Conclusion: this is an ISOLATED instance, not a repeated pattern. The other 3 call sites already follow the correct convention (resolve real output/input Property titles via _properties_for before building the edge); only the dict-form fan-in branch skipped that resolution and used the raw dict key. No other beads tasks filed -- no other instances found.
## Codebase Disease Scan (ozxqw)

Pattern: pyagentspec DataFlowEdge constructed with an unresolved dict-key/node-name string instead of a resolved output-Property title (SYNTACTIC -- all call sites confined to one file, one construct name).
Scan command (reproducible): `grep -rn "DataFlowEdge(" src/neograph/`
Total DataFlowEdge construction sites found: 4 (all in src/neograph/_agent_spec.py; grep -rln confirms no other file constructs a DataFlowEdge)

| 4 | _agent_spec.py:671 (single-type inputs fallback) | source_output=shared_title | ALLOWLIST | already correct — shared_title is resolved via _properties_for |

No DEFERs. Fix scope is exactly the one MIGRATE row (lines 644-649).
## Architect Review (ozxqw)

1. **Root cause correctness**: CONFIRMED LOW risk of being wrong. Verified live (`python -c ...` repro) that pydantic.ValidationError is raised exactly where the design says (_agent_spec.py:644, dict-form fan-in branch), and confirmed by grep that the OTHER 3 DataFlowEdge sites in the same file already use resolved `prop.title`/`shared_title` — this branch is the only one using the raw dict key.

2. **Fix minimality — LOW risk, with one refinement**: the design's fix approach (resolve per-field Property titles instead of the bare upstream_name) is minimal and localized to lines ~636-650. Refinement for the fix atom: destination_input must use the ALREADY-established dict-form prefixing convention `_properties_for` applies to the destination node's own declared inputs (`f'{key}.{p.title}'`, e.g. 'seed.x') — not a bare field title — because that is what the destination SpecNode's own `inputs=` property list actually contains (verified at _agent_spec.py:176-177, _properties_for lines 152-166). source_output should use the upstream node's real output Property titles, resolved via `_properties_for(upstream_item.outputs)` (mirroring the single-type fallback path at lines 658-679), for symmetry with how the producer side is already computed everywhere else in this file.

3. **Regression risk — LOW**: change is additive/corrective inside one existing loop body; does not touch node.py/construct.py/_construct_validation.py/factory.py/modifiers.py (layer discipline respected — this is agent-spec-interop-only, per CLAUDE.md's off-limits list for those modules). Existing single-type-inputs and Oracle/Loop DataFlowEdge tests are unaffected (different code branch).

4. **Architecture compliance — LOW**: stays within _agent_spec.py, matches the file's existing prop-title-resolution convention exactly (no new pattern introduced) — in fact it REMOVES the one place that deviated from that convention.

5. **Similar-bug scalability — MEDIUM finding (adjacent, in-scope per the bug's own acceptance)**: the sibling line `if source_node is None: continue` (line 640-642) silently DROPS a DataFlowEdge whenever `upstream_name` doesn't match any node's bare `.name` — which is exactly what happens for a dict-form-OUTPUT producer referenced downstream via the '{upstream}_{key}' naming convention (documented in CLAUDE.md's Node.outputs section). ozxqw's own acceptance text says: 'If any dict-form case is genuinely unrepresentable, fail loud via ConfigurationError, never a raw pydantic error' — a silent `continue` is the fail-SOFT failure mode that invariant exists to prevent. The fix atom's acceptance additionally requires a round-trip test per ozxqw's own text — not yet written, tracked for the implement atom.

Proceed to fix. title: 0.7.3: stringly-null coercion misses interiors of Optional-wrapped nested models/lists
description:
Follow-up to stark-h46 (shipped 0.7.2). The spec addendum framed the gap as '_is_stringly_null coerces scalar Optional inner types but not list/BaseModel inner types'. Empirically that framing is WRONG on main@0.7.2: _is_stringly_null already returns True for list[str]|None, list[Model]|None, and Model|None, so the DIRECT top-level cases ({"langs":"null"} where langs: list[str]|None) already coerce to None and pass.

The ACTUAL incompleteness is in the RECURSION DESCENT of _apply_null_defaults (src/neograph/_llm_retry.py:161). It only recurses into a nested model when isinstance(annotation, type) and issubclass(annotation, BaseModel), and into list items only when get_origin(annotation) is list. When the field is Optional-wrapped -- parent: Company|None or products: list[Product]|None -- the annotation is a Union, so BOTH recursion branches are skipped and stringly-null sentinels on the INTERIOR fields never get normalized.

Empirically confirmed failing on main@0.7.2:
- {"parent": {"langs": "null"}} where parent: Company|None -> ValidationError list_type (interior never reached)
- {"products": [{"price": "null"}]} where products: list[Product]|None -> ValidationError int_parsing (interior never reached)

Passing already (regression-guard, must stay green): direct top-level list[X]|None / list[Model]|None / Model|None = 'null'; nested inside NON-optional list[Model]; legit list/model values preserved; non-Optional 'null' still fails loud.

Fix: teach the two recursion branches to see through the Optional wrapper -- unwrap Union-with-None to the single inner type before the BaseModel / list-origin checks. Centralize the 'inner model type of this annotation' derivation so scalar/optional-scalar/model/optional-model/list-of-model/optional-list-of-model are all driven by one annotation walker rather than the current inline hand-rolled introspection (the reason the Optional cases were missed).

Also: chaos/Hypothesis property test across random Optional/list/nested topologies asserting no bare pydantic crash on stringly-null and no destruction of legit values. Review for wrong-layer plumbing (inline type introspection in _llm_retry that duplicates the type-structure walking centralized elsewhere).

Worktree: ../neograph-073 on branch fix/stringly-null-containers off main. Target release 0.7.3.
notes:
FIXED in worktree ../neograph-073 (branch fix/stringly-null-containers).

Root cause (empirically pinned, spec framing corrected): _is_stringly_null ALREADY returned True for direct list[X]|None / list[Model]|None / Model|None on main@0.7.2, so the direct top-level cases the spec named already worked. The real defect was the RECURSION DESCENT in _apply_null_defaults, which hand-enumerated only two container shapes (bare BaseModel field, bare list[BaseModel]) and silently skipped every other shape. Confirmed-failing shapes on main: Optional-wrapped model (Company|None), Optional-wrapped list-of-models (list[Product]|None), dict-of-models (dict[str,Product]), list-of-optional-models (list[Product|None]).

Fix: replaced the per-shape branch list with ONE recursive shape classifier -- _unwrap_optional (peels a single X|None) + _descend_null_defaults (dispatches on runtime value: model dict -> recurse; list[...] -> recurse each element; dict[K,V] -> recurse each value; re-peels Optional at every level). Kills the whole missing-shape bug family, not just the 2 spec cases. tuple[...] intentionally out of scope (LLM structured output doesn't emit heterogeneous tuples).

Layer verdict: NOT wrong-module -- _apply_null_defaults correctly lives on the LLM-JSON-repair axis in _llm_retry.py; reusing the IR-layer _validation_types walker would be a layer violation. The defect was wrong-SHAPE plumbing (hand-enumeration) not wrong-layer. Single-caller (only _parse_json_response), no parallel normalizer, so no three-surface/DRY duplication.

Tests: 5 deterministic regressions in TestParseJsonResponseLenientParsing (optional-model, optional-list-of-models, dict-of-models, list-of-optional-models, legit-preservation) + Hypothesis TestStringlyNullChaosAcrossTopologies (200 examples x 2 props over randomized Optional/list/dict/optional-element topologies). Mutation-verified all 6 descent tests fail without the fix. Guards updated: allowed-names (+_unwrap_optional,+_descend_null_defaults), line budget 615->665, version sync. Full suite 3078 passed. Bumped to 0.7.3 + CHANGELOG.
close_reason: Fixed via shape-driven descent (_unwrap_optional + _descend_null_defaults). Merged to main (ef6bed5), tagged v0.7.3, publish workflow triggered. Full suite 3078 passed.

title: [EPIC] Portal x Agent Spec: safe dynamic routing + round-trip-faithful interop
description:
Umbrella coordinating the Portal primitive (epic neograph-07inf) and Agent Spec interop (epic neograph-2ev48). Two tracks, sequenced so the round-trip fidelity contract is defined once.

INVARIANT (Portal): dynamic routing targets a region's declared ENTRY PORT, never its interior — a class of LangGraph deadlocks/runaway loops stays unrepresentable. Grounded in the port-taxonomy design doc.

INVARIANT (Agent Spec): added BESIDE the native neograph Spec, not replacing it. Portal mode (b) dispatches the NATIVE neograph Spec (modifier-aware, already round-trips) and does NOT depend on Agent Spec.

EXPORT-FIRST (decided 2026-07-15): the Agent Spec track does EXPORT before IMPORT. Export owns the round-trip fidelity contract — you cannot write a faithful reader before deciding what the writer emits. to_agent_spec emits x-neograph reconstruction metadata so a neograph-produced spec re-imports losslessly (same Oracle/Each/Loop/Portal primitives that compile to LangGraph); from_agent_spec READS that metadata (primitive-level fallback for external specs); the round-trip test is the proof. Tradeoff: export is the harder direction (Oracle->ParallelFlow lowering is the flagship gap), so this front-loads difficulty — accepted for contract cleanliness.

PHASES
0 Ratify: Command(goto) lowering CONFIRMED (Plan A); airpr spike done -> 7t7tf CLOSED.
1 Foundations (parallel): [Portal] port-taxonomy design doc; [A-Spec] nkjv9 (type layer).
2 Build (parallel): [Portal] nnds9, do0d9 (against the design doc); [A-Spec] EXPORT 03djs -> i3zsh (with x-neograph metadata).
3 Import + harden + DX: [A-Spec] 01i0g (round-trip import, reads metadata) -> csdcl (round-trip proof), l7gvy; [Portal] mode-b hardening 2aw5c/4pr04/5x43u, kdr1u (Portal+Operator), a37vk/fefar; optional: Portal dispatches an EXTERNAL Agent Spec.

CRITICAL PATH: nkjv9 -> i3zsh -> 01i0g -> csdcl. Export before import; ratify before extending the mesh.
notes:
ONE-MACHINE-FORMAT (2026-07-15): the neograph-flavored Agent Spec (Agent Spec envelope + x-neograph reconstruction metadata, inert to external consumers) is the SINGLE machine/runtime spec format with THREE uses: (1) export IR->spec (i3zsh, defines it); (2) import spec->IR (01i0g, reads it; primitive fallback for external); (3) Portal mode (b) emits+dispatches it (0la8v, re-points off the v1 bespoke load_spec dict). The human-authoring neograph Spec (_spec_schema.py) stays as AUTHORING DX only. Export-first is thus doubly justified: the format Portal emits is defined by the export side.
STATUS (2026-07-23): Portal v1 CLOSED (07inf). Agent Spec interop is one P1 bug from v1-complete: neograph-ozxqw (to_agent_spec fails on @node's primary dict-form fan-in shape). The round-trip-faithful goal is NOT met until that lands. Deferred P3 tail (both sides) consolidated under v2 epic neograph-qtfof. This umbrella closes when 2ev48 closes (i.e., when the export bug is fixed).

title: json_mode: a repair_json failure is fatal instead of retryable; truncated (finish_reason=length) responses are fed to the repairer
description:
OBSERVED (ox-troubleshooting-demo, live cascade run 2026-07-14, Langfuse trace 2e08bafb527849ccf2c9645af2fc81a9, deal 4869):
one cascade run died with ValueError: 'Input nesting exceeds the supported parser recursion depth.' The run counted as a FAIL vote in the eval gate, indistinguishable from a wrong diagnosis.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED (from the trace, not theory):
- GLM-5.1 reasoned in prose inside the json_mode completion and hit max_tokens EXACTLY (output=65536, 285,810 chars), truncated mid-sentence while writing hypothesis 1 of 3. It never emitted a single character of the JSON payload.
- The truncated text (an unterminated JSON string) went to repair_json(), whose recursive-descent parser blew Python's stack. json_repair converts the RecursionError into ValueError.
- The payload was NOT deeply nested: max bracket nesting was 2. The recursion came from LENGTH + truncation, not nesting. The error message is misleading.

TWO DEFECTS:

1. FATAL INSTEAD OF RETRYABLE (_llm_retry.py:191).
   repair_json() is called OUTSIDE the try block that starts at :194 — the block whose except (ValueError, TypeError) converts parse failures into ExecutionError, which _invoke_json_with_retry (:339) catches and turns into a re-prompt. Because the repair call sits one line above the guard, the single malformation json_repair itself chokes on escapes uncaught and kills the run, bypassing the retry machinery designed for exactly this.
   FIX: move repair_json() inside the guarded block so a repair failure becomes an ExecutionError like every other malformation.

2. TRUNCATION IS NOT DETECTED, AND A NAIVE RETRY WOULD NOT HELP.
   A finish_reason=='length' response is KNOWN incomplete; feeding 290KB of unterminated JSON to a repairer is pointless work. Worse, the retry that fix (1) unlocks would re-issue the same prompt at temperature=0 -> very likely the same runaway -> another 65k tokens burned, same truncation.
   The reasoning was already essentially COMPLETE (correct funnel arithmetic, correct break stage identified) — it just never got to the JSON. So the correct recovery is CONTINUATION, not retry: on finish_reason==length with no parseable payload, re-prompt with the truncated reasoning fed back plus 'your analysis was cut off; do not analyze further; emit ONLY the JSON payload for <Model> now'. That converts 65k of otherwise-wasted tokens into a result in one cheap call.

CALIBRATION (why this matters but is not merely a cap problem): across passing runs of the same graph the LARGEST single generation is 4.5k-12k tokens. This run's 65k is 5-14x the norm — so raising max_tokens is the wrong lever (it was on hypothesis 1 of 3 at 65k and would need 100k+), and the consumer's prompt-side over-deliberation is a separate concern owned by the consumer, not by neograph. neograph's job is to make the failure RECOVERABLE and OBSERVABLE rather than fatal.

ACCEPTANCE:
- a repair_json ValueError is surfaced as ExecutionError and retried (regression test with a payload that makes json_repair raise)
- finish_reason==length with no parseable payload triggers the continuation re-prompt, not a blind re-issue (test asserts the follow-up message instructs emit-only and carries the prior text)
- neither path can raise an uncaught exception out of _invoke_json_with_retry
design:
## Root Cause
_parse_json_response calls repair_json OUTSIDE its guarded try; ValueError/TypeError/RecursionError from the repairer escape as raw exceptions past _invoke_json_with_retry (which only catches ExecutionError). Separately, _invoke_json_with_retry/_ainvoke_json_with_retry ignore response_metadata['finish_reason'], so a length-truncated response is retried with the generic repair message — a blind re-issue that likely reproduces the same runaway at temperature=0.

## Fix Approach
1. In _parse_json_response, wrap repair_json in try/except (ValueError, TypeError, RecursionError) -> raise ExecutionError.build('json repair failed...', hint carries underlying error). Retry machinery then handles it like any malformation.
2. Add _is_truncated(response) helper reading response_metadata finish_reason=='length' (and Anthropic stop_reason=='max_tokens'). In both retry twins, when parse fails AND the response was truncated, build a CONTINUATION message instead of _build_retry_msg: carry raw_text as the assistant turn (already done) + user message 'your analysis was cut off... do not analyze further; emit ONLY the JSON object for <Model> now'. Non-truncated failures keep the existing repair message. Parse is still attempted first so a truncated-but-complete payload returns normally.
3. Async twin mirrors sync verbatim (twin-parity).
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing tests: tests/modes/test_json_mode_repair_retry.py (7 failing, 3 guard existing behavior)
  - TestRepairFailureIsRetryable: '['*4000 payload makes json_repair raise RecursionError (locally; ValueError in the consumer's json_repair build) which escapes _parse_json_response and _invoke_json_with_retry uncaught
  - TestTruncationContinuation: finish_reason=length + unparseable prose gets the generic 'response failed validation' repair message, not a continuation re-prompt

design:
## Core Invariant
The hop budget is enforced (counter read-modify-write + max_hops check) INSIDE the keymaker wrapper BEFORE the Command(goto) is emitted, using the ENTRY member's max_hops/on_exhaust and a single shared entry-keyed counter, so every hop remains exactly one checkpointed superstep and the counter persists verbatim across resume — never a new exception class, never a router, never a state-schema change.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Thread the entry's budget into every member's wrapper.** In _wiring.py:_add_keymaker_mesh (:735 entry=members[0]), extract entry.modifier_set.keymaker.max_hops / .on_exhaust / entry.name and pass them into make_keymaker_fn for EVERY member (:748). Do NOT read the per-member keymaker for the budget — non-entry members carry defaults. (Reuse the existing loop over members; add 3 params to the call.)

- **'exit' writes counter too**: the on_exhaust='exit' branch returns Command(goto=exit_name, update={**update, count_field:n, channel_key:payload}) — no raise, last payload stays on the bus (design §3.4 deliberate rename vs Loop's 'last').
- **Shared counter across members**: because all members key the counter by entry_field, the RMW must read incoming `state` (not the local update dict) so hops accumulate across DIFFERENT members' wrappers, not per-member.
- **Recursion floor interaction**: a mesh with agent/act members is already illegal (D-MEMBER-MODES), so the mesh term and the agent term never overlap on the same node — but a construct can have BOTH a mesh and separate agent nodes; sum both terms.

description:
INVARIANT: a Keymaker construct violating any assembly rule in design section 5 — unknown peer, non-Keymaker peer, non-contiguous mesh, two meshes at one level, max_hops on non-entry, Construct/agent/act member, dict-form outputs, producer named 'handoff', non-uniform payload, bad route field, and Keymaker+Operator (D-NO-OPERATOR-COMBO) — fails at Construct(...) with a ConstructError naming the offender, on BOTH the pipe path (_SLOT_RULES excludes incl. operator) and the direct-ModifierSet path (explicit model_post_init arms at modifiers.py:646-658 — review M2); effective_producer_type is untouched (pinned by test); Node.handoff_param is written ONLY by _ir_normalize.py, keyed off the reserved 'handoff' inputs key (review H2, the fan_out_param/neograph-k7bg ownership rule). ANTI-BAND-AID: mesh checks live in the _construct_validation.py walk (new _check_keymaker_mesh helper), not inline in decorators or compiler; no surface special-casing. SCOPE per design sections 2.1/3/4.1/5: modifiers.py (class, keymaker slot, ONE ModifierCombo.KEYMAKER, _COMBO_MAP row, combo property, post_init arms), node.py, _ir_normalize.py, _state_keys.py (handoff_hops/handoff_payload), state.py (fields + combo arms at :202,:512,:569 + membership checks :142,:211-233), _construct_validation.py + helpers, __init__.py (Keymaker, HANDOFF_END), check_fixtures (should_fail x6 incl. keymaker_operator_combo.py, should_pass x1), tests (test_keymaker_validation.py + legality half of tests/modifiers/test_keymaker.py). design:
## Core Invariant
A Keymaker construct that violates any design-§5 assembly rule fails at `Construct(...)` with a `ConstructError` naming the offender on BOTH the pipe path (`_SLOT_RULES` excludes) and the direct-`ModifierSet` path (explicit `model_post_init` arms); `Node.handoff_param` is written ONLY by `_ir_normalize.py` (keyed off the reserved 'handoff' inputs key), mesh checks live ONLY in the `_construct_validation.py` walk, and `effective_producer_type` is untouched — the KEYMAKER modifier plugs into every existing single-source-of-truth table (ModifierCombo/_COMBO_MAP/_SLOT_RULES/_NORMALIZERS/StateKeys) rather than adding a parallel mechanism, and all lowering is fail-loud-staged as `CompileError` until T2.

## Implementation Plan
(Reuse-first; every step extends an existing exemplar. TDD: failing test first for each behavior.)

1. modifiers.py — add `Keymaker(Modifier, frozen=True)` copying `Loop` (mode-discrimination + `max_hops>=1` in `model_post_init`, per design 2.1); add module-level `HANDOFF_END = "__end__"`. Register the slot in all six tables in lockstep: `ModifierCombo.KEYMAKER` (one enum member), one `_COMBO_MAP` row, one `_SLOT_RULES` row with `excludes=` each/oracle/loop/operator (D-NO-OPERATOR-COMBO), `ModifierSet.keymaker` slot field, `ModifierSet.combo` property arm, and both `classify_modifiers` branches + `has_modifier`/`get_modifier`/`to_list`. Add the FOUR explicit keymaker exclusion arms to `ModifierSet.model_post_init` (review M2 — the hard-coded pairwise arms don't read `_SLOT_RULES`).

2. node.py — add `handoff_param: str | None = None` directly below `fan_out_param` (:204), same doc-comment style; sole-writer is the normalizer.

3. _ir_normalize.py — add `_HandoffParamNormalizer` mirroring `_FanOutParamNormalizer`: `applies_to` = keymaker slot set + dict-form inputs + reserved `"handoff"` key present + field unset; `apply` returns `{"handoff_param": "handoff"}`. Append to `_NORMALIZERS`.

4. _state_keys.py — add `handoff_hops(field)` → `neo_handoff_hops_{field}` and `handoff_payload(field)` → `neo_handoff_{field}` static methods beside `loop_count`.

5. state.py — add `case ModifierCombo.KEYMAKER:` to the three assert_never matches (:202 sub-construct arm and :512 dict-form arm are validation-unreachable → fail-loud CompileError or fold into the defensive fallback consistently; :569 single-output arm folds KEYMAKER into `BARE | OPERATOR` so a member's own output field is a plain `(output_type|None, None)`). Add a mesh-entry membership pass (modeled on the loop-counter loop :231-235) that adds `handoff_hops` (int,0) + `handoff_payload` (PayloadModel|None) neo_ fields for each mesh entry. Grep-confirm the non-exhaustive `in (...)` tuples at :142/:211-233 need no KEYMAKER addition.

6. _construct_validation.py (+ _validation_modifiers.py) — add `_check_keymaker_mesh(construct, producers)` called ONCE from `_validate_node_chain`, enforcing every design-§5 rule (unknown peer via the fan-in "no upstream node named X" message shape; peer-not-Keymaker; non-contiguous; two-meshes; max_hops-on-non-entry; Construct/agent-act member; dict-form-outputs member; producer-named-'handoff'; non-uniform payload; route-field str/Literal + Literal-membership via `_resolve_field_annotation`; handoff-key on non-mesh / wrong-typed). Register mesh members as producers of their declared output (frontier union per design §5). Leave `effective_producer_type`/`effective_producer_type_for` untouched.

7. __init__.py — import `Keymaker` + `HANDOFF_END`; add both to `__all__` beside Loop/Operator.

8. compiler.py — add `case ModifierCombo.KEYMAKER:` staging arms to both assert_never dispatch matches (:516, :620) raising `CompileError.build("Keymaker lowering lands in T2")`; add a pinning test asserting this, which T2 replaces.

9. Guards — add `"handoff_param"` to `TestNormalizeIrIsSoleIrFieldWriter.IR_FIELDS` (tests/test_guards_llm_runtime.py) so the single-writer invariant PINS the new field.

10. Fixtures — should_fail ×6: keymaker_unknown_peer, keymaker_literal_stray_target, keymaker_loop_combo, keymaker_operator_combo, keymaker_nonuniform_payload, keymaker_dispatch_missing_output (each minimal, one defect, `# CHECK_ERROR: <regex>`). should_pass ×1: keymaker_mesh_minimal. Auto-discovered by test_check_fixtures.py.

11. Tests — new tests/test_keymaker_validation.py (every §5 assembly error, message asserted) + modifier-legality half of tests/modifiers/test_keymaker.py (slot conflicts, duplicate, Keymaker+Operator rejected on BOTH pipe and direct-ModifierSet paths — the M2 pin — mode discrimination). Test legality via declarative + programmatic surfaces (three-surface parity; @node sugar deferred to T4, ForwardConstruct exempt).

Gates before commit: `uv run --extra dev pytest` on touched suites (tests/modifiers/, tests/test_keymaker_validation.py, tests/test_check_fixtures.py, tests/test_guards_llm_runtime.py) + full mypy (all FIVE assert_never sites handled: compiler.py ×2, state.py:202/512/569) + ruff. No existing test broken.
notes:
## Findings

REUSE-OVER-REINVENTION: T1 is almost entirely "add one more row/arm/normalizer beside the existing Loop/Each/Oracle/Operator exemplars." The IR machinery is table-driven; the KEYMAKER modifier plugs into the same tables. Minimal net-new: the `Keymaker` class, the `_HandoffParamNormalizer`, and the `_check_keymaker_mesh` walk helper. Everything else is one-line additions to existing single-source-of-truth tables.

- Modifier class + slot exemplar = `Loop` (mode discrimination in model_post_init) and `Operator` (slot with empty excludes). New `Keymaker(Modifier, frozen=True)` copies `Loop.model_post_init` (modifiers.py:566-577) for mode-discrimination + `max_hops>=1` validation. Surface pinned in design 2.1.
- Slot registration is fully table-driven: (1) add `keymaker: Keymaker | None = None` field to `ModifierSet` (modifiers.py:627-630); (2) add ONE `_SlotRule(Keymaker, "keymaker", "Keymaker", excludes=(...each,oracle,loop,operator...))` row to `_SLOT_RULES` (modifiers.py:604-614) — this is the PIPE-PATH exclusion; (3) add ONE `ModifierCombo.KEYMAKER = auto()` to the enum (modifiers.py:65-83, add after OPERATOR); (4) add ONE `_COMBO_MAP` row `frozenset({"keymaker"}): ModifierCombo.KEYMAKER` (modifiers.py:89-100); (5) extend `ModifierSet.combo` property (modifiers.py:632-644) with `if self.keymaker is not None: has.add("keymaker")`; (6) extend `classify_modifiers` fast-path (modifiers.py:116-123) AND fallback (:131-144) + `has_modifier`/`get_modifier` (:269-291) + `to_list` (:694-705). NOTE: D-NO-OPERATOR-COMBO means NO `KEYMAKER_OPERATOR` combo — Keymaker excludes operator, so a lone `ModifierCombo.KEYMAKER` is the only new enum value.
- DIRECT-ModifierSet path (review M2, design 4.1): `ModifierSet.model_post_init` (modifiers.py:646-658) has HARD-CODED pairwise arms (each/loop, oracle/loop) that do NOT read `_SLOT_RULES`. Without new arms, `ModifierSet(keymaker=..., loop=...)` silently passes while the pipe path rejects — the exact parity hazard. MUST add explicit keymaker×each/oracle/loop/operator arms here (or refactor post_init to read `_SLOT_RULES`; simpler + lower-risk to add the four arms mirroring the two existing).
- `Node.handoff_param: str | None = None` is the EXACT `fan_out_param` parallel (node.py:204). Add it right below fan_out_param with the same doc-comment style. It is written ONLY by the normalizer.
- `_ir_normalize.py` is the SOLE writer (review H2 / D5, the neograph-k7bg rule). Add a `_HandoffParamNormalizer` (mirror `_FanOutParamNormalizer` at :126-148) + append to `_NORMALIZERS` (:206-209). `applies_to`: `node.handoff_param is None and node.modifier_set.keymaker is not None and normalize_inputs(node.inputs).is_dict_form and "handoff" in <keys>`. `apply`: `return {"handoff_param": "handoff"}` (the reserved key is a literal, not inferred by candidate-elimination like fan_out — simpler). Keyed off the reserved 'handoff' inputs key per design 3.3.
- Runtime read site: `_input_shape.py:_extract_fan_in_dict` (:96-118) reads `node.fan_out_param` → EACH_ITEM. T2 will teach it to read `handoff_param` → the mesh channel. NOT a T1 change (T1 is IR + validation only), but note the field must exist for T2.
- `_state_keys.py`: add two static methods beside `loop_count` (:124-127): `handoff_hops(field_name) -> f"neo_handoff_hops_{field_name}"` and `handoff_payload(field_name) -> f"neo_handoff_{field_name}"`. Design 3.3/3.4/4.1. TestNeoStateKeysCentralized guard requires these be the ONLY producers of those literals.
- `state.py` THREE combo-match arms need a KEYMAKER arm each (mypy assert_never forces it): (a) sub-construct arm at :164-202 (assert_never :202) — Keymaker on a Construct is ILLEGAL (D-MESH-LEVEL, member cannot be a Construct), but the match still needs an arm; simplest is to fold KEYMAKER into a defensive arm or raise. Since validation rejects Keymaker-on-Construct upstream, this arm is defensively-unreachable — mirror the EACH_ORACLE defensive-fallback comment (:197-200). (b) `_add_output_field` dict-form arm at :472-513 (assert_never :512) — dict-form outputs on a Keymaker node are ILLEGAL (D-DICT-OUTPUTS), so again defensively add KEYMAKER to a rejecting/fallback arm. (c) `_add_single_output_field` at :527-569 (assert_never :569) — this IS reached: a mesh member's single-type output. For T1 (no lowering), the member's own output field is written as BARE (`fields[field_name] = (output_type | None, None)`) — add `ModifierCombo.KEYMAKER` to the `case ModifierCombo.BARE | ModifierCombo.OPERATOR` arm at :566. Also add the mesh-entry `neo_handoff_hops_*` (int,0) + `neo_handoff_<entry>` (PayloadModel|None) channel fields — but design 4.1 marks the channel/counter as an entry-only concern; T1 may add the plain state fields OR defer to T2. title: MCP resilience layer re-raises the ExceptionGroup wrapper, not the unwrapped leaf — consumer exceptions surface grouped (qslrx regression)
description:
## Invariant
Every neograph_mcp boundary surfaces a single-leaf transport ExceptionGroup as its BARE leaf (fails loud and PRECISE). A consumer catching a specific exception type (RuntimeError/ValueError/their own guard) around an MCP tool call gets that type, never an ExceptionGroup wrapper.

## The regression (found downstream: ox-troubleshooting-demo, blocker ox-troubleshooting-demo-8ym P0)
Two demo tests went red after bumping to neograph f491db4 (qslrx):
- tests/test_mcp_factory.py::test_factory_raises_a_clear_error_when_no_token_provider_is_wired
- tests/test_mcp_factory_typed_roundtrip.py::test_missing_provider_fails_loud_before_any_wire_traffic
Both: a consumer token_provider that raises RuntimeError('no token provider…') now surfaces as ExceptionGroup[RuntimeError], so pytest.raises(RuntimeError) no longer matches. The SECOND half of the contract still holds (the auth flow raises BEFORE the request is sent — nothing reaches the wire); only the exception SURFACE regressed. Demo working tree clean; not demo code.

## Verified mechanism (against neograph source)
1. qslrx (f491db4) moved token_provider invocation from connect-time (synchronous, OUTSIDE anyio) into the per-request httpx.Auth: _TokenProviderAuth.async_auth_flow (_client.py:373) awaits _resolve_token -> invokes the consumer's token_provider. That now runs INSIDE the streamable-http transport's anyio TaskGroup, which wraps any raise in an ExceptionGroup. Pre-qslrx the same provider raised bare.
2. neograph does NOT raise on a missing provider (_resolve_token: token_provider is None -> return None -> anonymous). The RuntimeError is the CONSUMER's own guard, now invoked per-request and thus grouped.

## ROOT CAUSE (more specific than 'add an unwrap' — the machinery already exists)
_unwrap_single (_client.py:92) recursively descends a single-leaf BaseExceptionGroup to the bare error. EVERY OTHER boundary already uses it correctly on the way out:
- _session.py:230/239, _prompt.py:105, _run_context.py:102/117 -> raise _unwrap_single(exc) from None.
The transport-resilience wrapper _resilient (_client.py:188-206) is the ONE boundary OUT OF STEP: it computes leaf = _unwrap_single(exc) for CLASSIFICATION (retry decision) but the terminal raise statements re-raise the ORIGINAL exc (the ExceptionGroup), discarding the unwrapped leaf:

    except BaseException as exc:
        leaf = _unwrap_single(exc)
        if isinstance(leaf, (ToolException, asyncio.CancelledError)): raise   # raises the GROUP
        if not _is_transport_error(leaf): raise                              # <- consumer's case: raises the GROUP
        if attempt >= max_attempts: raise                                    # raises the GROUP
        if not idempotent and not _is_pre_send_safe(leaf): raise             # raises the GROUP

So a non-transport error is correctly classified 'don't retry, propagate' but propagates GROUPED. qslrx did not create this — it EXPOSED it: before qslrx a config-time provider error did not flow through the per-request auth_flow inside anyio, so it never hit this path as a group.

## Fix
In _resilient, the terminal raises become 'raise leaf from None' (the exact pattern _session/_prompt/_run_context already use). The load-bearing one is 'if not _is_transport_error(leaf): raise leaf from None' (the consumer's case). This restores precise surfacing for ANY consumer exception through a tool call, not just token_provider.

REVIEW NUANCE (flag for the review atom): the CancelledError branch needs care — re-raising an unwrapped CancelledError 'from None' must preserve cooperative-cancellation semantics; confirm, or EXEMPT CancelledError from the unwrap (keep bare raise for it). The RuntimeError / transport-exhausted / non-idempotent-ambiguous cases are unambiguous — use 'raise leaf from None'.

## ANTI-BAND-AID (the invariant, not the one site)
Do NOT fix only the consumer's exact RuntimeError case. The defect is that _resilient is INCONSISTENT with every other neograph_mcp boundary: they unwrap on exit, it doesn't. Converge them — the resilience layer's terminal raises must surface the unwrapped leaf like the rest. Consider a small guard/meta-test asserting no neograph_mcp exit-boundary re-raises a BaseExceptionGroup wrapper when a single-leaf unwrap is available (so this boundary can't drift back out of step).

## Guard-first / TDD
1. ## Scope

## Provenance
Downstream regression filed by ox-troubleshooting-demo (blocker ox-troubleshooting-demo-8ym P0; the demo's bug-triage molecule ox-troubleshooting-demo-xom is stopped at its baseline gate on this).
