design:
## Core Invariant
Every neograph_mcp exit-boundary surfaces a single-leaf transport ExceptionGroup as its BARE leaf (fails loud and PRECISE). A consumer catching a specific exception type around an MCP tool call OR factory build gets that type, never an ExceptionGroup wrapper.

## Refine (atom 6 — addresses dp-reviewer NEEDS_REFINEMENT, MEDIUM finding)
REVIEWER VERDICT: NEEDS_REFINEMENT (1 MEDIUM, 7 LOW, 0 HIGH). Root cause soundness CONFIRMED ('could not refute'). The MEDIUM: the CancelledError exemption is untested AND structurally untestable with the existing ExceptionGroup-based double (CancelledError is a BaseException since 3.8, so it can only nest in a BaseExceptionGroup, not ExceptionGroup -> TypeError).

REFINED DECISION — split the inner CancelledError/ToolException branch:
- ToolException (grouped): 'raise leaf from None' (a RESULT — surface bare; unambiguous).
- CancelledError (grouped): EXEMPT — keep bare 'raise' (re-raise original exc, grouped-or-bare). Preserves asyncio/anyio cooperative-cancellation propagation through BaseExceptionGroup; unwrapping to a bare CancelledError 'from None' risks disturbing the group's cancellation tracking.
- Bare ToolException/CancelledError: caught by the FIRST except (ToolException, CancelledError): raise — unchanged.

NEW TEST (pins the exemption so a future 'consistency' refactor can't silently remove it):
- A BaseExceptionGroup wrapping asyncio.CancelledError, through _with_transport_resilience -> asserts it surfaces as a BaseExceptionGroup (NOT unwrapped to bare CancelledError). Uses a BaseExceptionGroup-based double (ExceptionGroup cannot hold CancelledError). This is the testable pin the reviewer asked for.

LOW findings addressed:
- Guard scope: the optional boundary-consistency guard is DEFERRED to neograph-lcrwd (which already references it — 'if neograph-2itlh ships that guard, this task makes the 4 boundaries pass it'). This fix stays focused on the 4 MIGRATE boundaries; the 8 RED repros + 1 GREEN multi-leaf pin + 1 NEW CancelledError-exemption pin lock the contract behaviorally.
- Stale DESCRIPTION 'Fix' section: corrected below (the DESCRIPTION still says 'Fix: In _resilient...' — the actual fix is broader).

## Fix Approach (converge BOTH out-of-step boundaries with _session/_prompt/_run_context)
_unwrap_single (_client.py:92) already descends a single-leaf group to the bare error and preserves a genuine multi-leaf group. Reuse it — no second helper.

### Boundary 1 — get_tools() (the demo-breaker, qslrx regression)
Wrap the get_tools()/load_mcp_tools() call sites so a grouped failure unwraps on exit (try/except BaseException as exc: raise _unwrap_single(exc) from None):
- _discover_tool_names (_client.py:487)
- _factory (_client.py:571 held-session load_mcp_tools AND :575 client.get_tools)
Inline try/except matching the _session/_prompt/_run_context idiom (3 sites — not worth a helper).

### Boundary 2 — _resilient (_client.py:188-206, latent)
except (ToolException, asyncio.CancelledError): raise  # BARE — unchanged (first except)
except BaseException as exc:
    leaf = _unwrap_single(exc)
    if isinstance(leaf, ToolException): raise leaf from None      # RESULT — bare (was: raise the group)
    if isinstance(leaf, asyncio.CancelledError): raise            # EXEMPT — preserve cancellation (was: raise the group)
    if not _is_transport_error(leaf): raise leaf from None        # consumer's case (was: raise the group)
    if attempt >= max_attempts: raise leaf from None              # transport exhausted (was: raise the group)
    if not idempotent and not _is_pre_send_safe(leaf): raise leaf from None  # ambiguous non-idempotent (was: raise the group)
    await asyncio.sleep(...)

## Anti-band-aid
Converge EVERY out-of-step MIGRATE boundary (get_tools x3 + _resilient terminals). The 4 DEFER boundaries are neograph-lcrwd. Reuse _unwrap_single.

## Regression pins (GREEN before and after)
- transport error retries then surfaces bare after exhaustion.
- isError ToolException surfaces bare (not grouped), no retry.
- genuine MULTI-leaf group NOT flattened.
- CancelledError exemption: grouped CancelledError stays grouped (NEW pin).
- static-string provider still works (existing test_mcp_identity_refresh).
notes:
## Reproduction (RED, verified on HEAD 2026-07-13)
- Failing tests (8 RED, 1 GREEN multi-leaf pin):
  - tests/test_mcp_transport_resilience.py::TestGroupedExceptionUnwrappedToBareLeaf (4 RED: non-transport RuntimeError/ValueError, transport-exhausted ConnectionRefusedError, grouped isError ToolException; 1 GREEN: genuine multi-leaf group NOT flattened)
  - tests/test_mcp_exception_surface.py::TestTokenProviderErrorSurfacesBareAtFactory (4 RED: singular factory invocation + plural build-time, each x RuntimeError/ValueError twin)
- Run: uv run --extra dev --extra mcp-examples pytest tests/test_mcp_transport_resilience.py::TestGroupedExceptionUnwrappedToBareLeaf tests/test_mcp_exception_surface.py
- Each failure shows: leaf 'single exception in ExceptionGroup' — the bare type is wrapped by the transport's anyio TaskGroup and re-raised grouped at the boundary.

## Root cause (CORRECTED — richer than the original analysis)
The original analysis identified the _resilient wrapper (_client.py:188-206) as the ONE boundary out of step. Empirical probing (real demo http server + a grouped-exception double) shows TWO boundaries re-raise the grouped exc instead of the unwrapped leaf:

1. get_tools() boundaries (THE ACTUAL DEMO-BREAKER — NOT in the original analysis):
   - _discover_tool_names (_client.py:487) — build-time plural enumerate.
   - _factory (_client.py:571 held-session load_mcp_tools, :575 per-call client.get_tools) — per-call.
   A consumer token_provider that raises (RuntimeError guard) now invokes INSIDE the streamable-http transport's anyio TaskGroup (qslrx moved it into _TokenProviderAuth.async_auth_flow, _client.py:373). The raise is wrapped in an ExceptionGroup. get_tools() propagates the GROUP raw — no unwrap. This is what broke the ox-troubleshooting-demo test_mcp_factory / test_mcp_factory_typed_roundtrip tests (pytest.raises(RuntimeError) no longer matches ExceptionGroup[RuntimeError]). Pre-qslrx the provider raised at connect-time OUTSIDE anyio (bare), so this is a true qslrx REGRESSION at these boundaries.

2. _resilient tool-call wrapper (_client.py:188-206 — the original analysis's target, LATENT):
   Computes leaf = _unwrap_single(exc) for CLASSIFICATION but every terminal raise re-raises the original grouped exc. Affects ALL terminal paths (non-transport, transport-exhausted, grouped-isError), not just the consumer's RuntimeError case. Latent since a1def8f/uixi1 (shipped grouped); qslrx EXPOSED it by routing per-request identity raises through anyio, but the demo's tests fail at get_tools() (boundary #1) BEFORE any tool call reaches _resilient, so _resilient alone is NOT the demo-breaker.

Confirmed via probes: token_provider RuntimeError surfaces as ExceptionGroup at BOTH _discover_tool_names (build-time, sync) and _factory invocation (per-call, async) — never reaches _resilient (tool never built). A grouped-exception double through _with_transport_resilience surfaces grouped at _resilient's terminal raises.

## Why fixing _resilient ALONE would NOT fix the demo
The demo's failing tests exercise the factory build/invocation (get_tools), which fails before any tool call. Fixing _resilient leaves boundary #1 grouped → demo tests stay red. The invariant ('every neograph_mcp boundary surfaces the bare leaf') requires converging BOTH boundaries with _session/_prompt/_run_context.

Searched every transport-touching call site in src/neograph_mcp/ against the unwrap invariant. Pattern: a call into the MCP/anyio transport whose raise is caught (or uncaught-but-propagated) at a boundary that does NOT apply _unwrap_single on exit.

Catches bare McpError inside the async-with and re-raises after; a GROUPED McpError would miss the except and re-wrap via anyio teardown -> nested group. ### IN STEP (correct — unwrap on exit)
- _session.__aenter__ (_session.py:229-230) and __aexit__ (:238-239) — unwrap. VERIFIED: mcp_session with a raising provider surfaces bare RuntimeError at __aenter__ (streamable-http sends initialize at enter -> auth_flow raises -> __aenter__ unwraps).

- _run_context.py:102, :117 — unwrap.

### Scope discrepancy (flag for architect review, atom 5)
The task's stated Scope says IN: _resilient only. But the demo-breaker is boundary 1 (get_tools), which is OUTSIDE that stated scope, and there are 4 MORE latent similar instances (4-7). Fixing _resilient alone leaves the demo red and the invariant violated at 6 boundaries. The invariant ('every neograph_mcp boundary surfaces the bare leaf') requires converging ALL out-of-step boundaries. Recommend: fix 1+2+3 in THIS task (1+2 are the demo-breaker, 3 is the original target); file a follow-up for 4-7 (latent held-session/resource-path twins).

## Architect Review (atom 5)

### Adversarial attempt to REFUTE the corrected root cause

I tried to refute "get_tools is the demo-breaker, not _resilient." The bug report's original analysis says the fix is in _resilient ONLY. For the original analysis to be right, the demo's tests would have to fail at tool.ainvoke (reaching _resilient), not at get_tools. I checked:

- The factory path (_discover_tool_names:487, _factory:571/575) calls MultiServerMCPClient.get_tools() DIRECTLY — it does NOT go through neograph's McpSession.__aenter__ (which unwraps at _session.py:229-230). The adapter's internal session lifecycle has NO neograph unwrap.
- get_tools() drives an HTTP request (tools/list) through _TokenProviderAuth.async_auth_flow (qslrx, f491db4), which calls _resolve_token -> token_provider(configurable). If the provider raises, the raise is INSIDE the transport's anyio TaskGroup -> wrapped in ExceptionGroup -> propagated raw by get_tools() (no unwrap).
- The tool never gets BUILT (get_tools fails first), so tool.ainvoke / _resilient is never reached. The bead's empirical claim is correct.

VERDICT on root cause: SOUND. The empirical departure from the bug report is justified. I could not refute it.

### Rated findings

- [LOW] Root cause correctness — SOUND. The corrected root cause (get_tools is the demo-breaker, _resilient is latent) is consistent with the code, the qslrx commit, and the reproduction evidence. The 8 RED repros use a REAL demo HTTP server (tests/test_mcp_battery.py:_demo_http_server — a real FastMCP subprocess on an ephemeral port, not a mock) for the factory boundary, and a precise grouped-exception double for the _resilient boundary. The mechanism (provider raises inside anyio TaskGroup -> ExceptionGroup -> factory propagates raw) is verified against _client.py:372-379 (_TokenProviderAuth.async_auth_flow) and _client.py:487/571/575 (get_tools/load_mcp_tools with no unwrap).

- [MEDIUM] CancelledError exemption is untested AND the existing test double cannot produce the right exception type. The design exempts grouped CancelledError from the unwrap (keeps bare 'raise') — a conservative, defensible choice. However: (a) NO test pins this behavior; (b) asyncio.CancelledError is a BaseException subclass (since Python 3.8), so it can only be nested in a BaseExceptionGroup, NOT an ExceptionGroup; (c) the existing _grouped_tool double (test_mcp_transport_resilience.py:332) uses ExceptionGroup("taskgroup", [leaf_factory()]) which would raise TypeError: "Cannot nest BaseExceptions in an ExceptionGroup" if leaf_factory() returned a CancelledError. So the exemption path is structurally untestable with the current double. The implementer must either: (1) add a modified double using BaseExceptionGroup for the CancelledError case and assert the group is preserved (not unwrapped), OR (2) document in a code comment that a grouped CancelledError is a BaseExceptionGroup (not ExceptionGroup) handled specially by asyncio, making the exemption a defensive no-op. Without this, a future "consistency" refactor could remove the exemption and break cancellation propagation with no test catching it.

- [LOW] Boundary-consistency guard scope is underspecified. The optional anti-band-aid guard ("no neograph_mcp exit-boundary re-raises a BaseExceptionGroup wrapper when a single-leaf unwrap is available") would FAIL for the 4 deferred boundaries (neograph-lcrwd) AND for the CancelledError exemption. The bead doesn't specify the guard's scope. Recommendation: if added, scope to all boundaries with the 4 deferred ones marked xfail (referencing neograph-lcrwd), and explicitly allow the CancelledError exemption (a BaseExceptionGroup path, not an ExceptionGroup path).

- [LOW] Deferral of 4 latent twins is acceptable. The deferred boundaries (_session._ensure_listing:253, _session.call:325, fetcher grouped-McpError:814, replayer:828) are reachable by mcp_session/mcp_resource_fetcher consumers (not purely theoretical), but are lower-traffic than the factory path and the follow-up neograph-lcrwd (P2) is filed. The implementer should add a brief inline comment at each deferred site referencing neograph-lcrwd for code-level discoverability.

- [LOW] Fix minimality and architecture compliance — GOOD. The proposed fix converges on the exact _unwrap_single idiom used by _session/__aenter__/__aexit__ (229-230, 237-239), _prompt/_fetch (104-105), _run_context/__aenter__/_aclose (100-102, 116-117). No new helpers (correct for 3 get_tools sites — the bead considers and rejects a single-sited helper). raise leaf from None for _resilient terminals reuses the already-computed leaf (no recompute). The inline try/except for get_tools matches the existing pattern exactly.

- [LOW] Test coverage sufficiency — GOOD for main paths. 8 RED + 1 GREEN cover: factory boundary (REAL transport, RuntimeError/ValueError, singular mcp_tool_factory + plural mcp_tool_factories); _resilient boundary (non-transport RuntimeError/ValueError, transport-exhausted ConnectionRefusedError, grouped isError ToolException); multi-leaf preservation (genuine double-failure group NOT flattened). Existing tests (TestTransportRetryWithinBound, TestIsErrorNeverRetried, TestAmbiguousFailureIdempotencyGate, TestBudgetCountsLogicalCallOnce, TestPerCallTimeout) serve as regression pins for retry/classification behavior. The one gap is the CancelledError exemption (see MEDIUM above).

- [LOW] DESCRIPTION "Fix" section is stale. It focuses on _resilient only ("In _resilient, the terminal raises become 'raise leaf from None'"). The DESIGN supersedes it by proposing BOTH boundaries (get_tools + _resilient). The implementer should follow the DESIGN, not the DESCRIPTION's "Fix" section. No action needed beyond awareness.

- [LOW] raise leaf from None on transport-exhausted / non-idempotent-ambiguous paths — NO regression. Currently 'raise' re-raises the grouped exc; the fix changes to 'raise leaf from None' (unwrapped). For bare exceptions (existing tests), leaf == exc, so behavior is identical (from None only suppresses chaining context, which is empty for a freshly-caught exception). For grouped exceptions, the consumer's except ConnectionError / except TimeoutError now actually catches the bare type — an IMPROVEMENT over the current grouped surface. The from None pattern matches _session/_prompt/_run_context. No information loss (the ExceptionGroup wrapper adds no debugging value; the bare leaf is more informative).

### Scan completeness verification

I re-ran the bead's scan command (grep for await sites + except blocks in src/neograph_mcp/). Found 11 await sites + 1 _resilient except-block + 1 fetcher except-McpError = 13 candidates. The bead's disposition table covers all 13 (4 MIGRATE, 4 DEFER, 5 ALLOWLIST). No missed boundaries.

Overall: NEEDS_REFINEMENT

title: P1: parity test matrix + ratchet — declarative/forward() twin corpus asserted IR-identical
description:
Epic neograph-e9zse Phase 1 deliverable/guard. Design doc: docs/design/forwardconstruct-expressiveness-parity-2026-07-10.md

## What (test-only task — the anti-band-aid guard)
Build the PARITY TEST MATRIX: a corpus of declarative topologies, each paired with a forward() twin, asserted to trace to IDENTICAL IR. Include, at minimum, one entry per row of the design doc's capability table that is in scope for Phase 1:
- straight-line pipeline
- fan-in (multi-upstream)
- per-node fan-out (bare-for sugar, key="label")
- self.each() fan-out with custom key over a sub-construct
- loop over nodes
- loop over a sub-construct body containing an Each fan-out
- nested sub-construct composition
- multi-output dict node
- the REFERENCE integration test: the cascade shape (intake -> triage -> Loop(investigate{ verify | Each(over, key='id') }) -> explain) — forward() twin traces to the SAME IR as the declarative form.

## The ratchet
A property/parametrized test comparing traced IR to declarative IR across the corpus, structured so a NEW declarative capability lacking a forward() path FAILS LOUD when its corpus row is added. Do NOT special-case the cascade — it is one row, not the mechanism. Decide file placement (suggest tests/test_forward_parity.py) and define ONE IR-equality helper (normalize + compare nodes/modifiers/boundary types) reused by every row.

## Depends on
neograph-e9zse.1 and neograph-e9zse.2 (the twins need self.each() and relaxed loop bodies).

## Acceptance
Corpus + ratchet committed and green; cascade reference row present; review-atom-style check that every in-scope declarative capability has a row. Full suite green.

title: P1: relax self.loop() body validation — accept sub-construct-producing body items
description:
Epic neograph-e9zse Phase 1, fix #2. Design doc: docs/design/forwardconstruct-expressiveness-parity-2026-07-10.md

## What
Relax self.loop() body validation in src/neograph/forward.py (:491-498) to accept sub-construct-producing items (_LoopCall / _EachCall results from neograph-e9zse.1) alongside _NodeCall. Construct(nodes=...) already accepts list[Node | Construct], so the tracer is artificially stricter than the IR it targets.

- Reuse _declared_output port inference (forward.py:519) for input/output boundary types on MIXED bodies (nodes + modified sub-constructs). This is the only fiddly part: type inference when a body member is a modified sub-construct (e.g. an Each'd construct whose effective producer type is dict[str, X] — use effective_producer_type from _construct_validation, do NOT re-inline modifier rules).
- Enables free nesting: loop containing an Each fan-out (the cascade shape), each inside loop, loop inside loop.

## Core Invariant
Same as the epic: traced IR == declarative IR; emit only existing IR; zero IR/compiler changes. effective_producer_type is the single source of truth for modifier-aware type effects.

## Acceptance
A forward() twin of declarative `Loop(over=...)` applied to a Construct whose nodes include an Each'd sub-construct traces to IDENTICAL IR as the declarative form. The cascade shape (intake -> triage -> Loop(investigate{ verify | Each(over, key='id') }) -> explain) becomes expressible. TDD: failing IR-equality test first.

## Depends on
neograph-e9zse.1 (shares the DSL composition design confirmed by its review gate; _EachCall must exist).
design:
## Core Invariant
Traced IR == declarative IR: self.loop() with a mixed body must emit EXACTLY the Construct(input=, output=, nodes=[Node..., Construct|Each, ...]) | Loop(...) the declarative form produces (verified working end-to-end 2026-07-11), with effective_producer_type as the single source of truth for modifier-aware types and zero changes outside src/neograph/forward.py.

## Implementation Plan (TDD: failing IR-equality test first)
1. TEST FIRST (tests/test_forward.py, new class TestLoopOverSubConstructBody): forward() cascade twin — intake -> self.loop(body=[self.get_claims, self.each(body=[self.verify], over='get_claims.claims', key='cid'), self.collect], when=lambda d: d is None or d.score < 0.5)(intake_out) — asserted IR-identical (extend TestSelfEachTracing._assert_ir_identical to recurse into nested Construct members) to the declarative twin: Construct('loop-...', input=ClaimBatch, output=Diagnosis, nodes=[get_claims, Construct('each-verify', input=Claim, output=MatchResult, nodes=[verify-copy])|Each(over='get_claims.claims', key='cid'), collect])|Loop(...). Verify it FAILS (current :509-516 rejects _EachCall body items).
2. _EachCall refactor (build vs record): extract _materialize(root_resolver, port_input_type) -> Construct returning the Construct|Each WITHOUT tracer.record_construct; __call__ becomes resolve-over (existing proxy/raw paths) + _materialize + record + proxy — zero behavior change, existing 13 e9zse.1 tests stay green.
3. self.each(over=) construction-time binding: add over: str | None = None to _ForwardSelf.each() and _EachCall.__init__. Raw string only for nested use; ConstructError on double-binding (construction over + __call__ over) and on a proxy-over reaching materialization inside a loop body.
4. Relax _LoopCall.__call__ body validation (:509-516) to _NodeCall | _EachCall | _LoopCall; materialize members IN ORDER: _NodeCall -> node copy (inputs=input_type fill only when inputs is None, model_copy, unchanged); _EachCall -> _materialize with root resolution against (a) preceding materialized peers via field_name_for(name) and (b) StateKeys.SUBGRAPH_INPUT -> walk the loop's input_type; root type for peers = effective_producer_type(peer) imported via the _construct_validation facade (mirrors _check_each_path's matched.effective_type). Fail loud on unmatched root / missing over.
5. _LoopCall nesting (loop-in-loop): symmetric _materialize on _LoopCall — input_type = previous member's normalize_outputs(_declared_output(prev)).primary (or outer input_type when first); when/max_iterations/on_exhaust pass through; no record. Same deterministic naming via next_occurrence('loop', slug).
6. Mixed-body port inference: output_type = normalize_outputs(_declared_output(last_member)).primary (monopoly selector — never getattr); trace-time fail-loud when effective_producer_type(last_member) shows an Each'd terminal member (dict[str,X] can never satisfy the output-boundary contract, _construct_validation.py:320-342) with hint to add a collector node. body_slug built from materialized member names.
7. More tests: neo_subgraph_input-root over (fan over the loop's input field); loop-in-loop IR twin; Each'd-member-last fail-loud; unmatched nested root fail-loud; double-binding fail-loud; re-trace determinism (loop body inside an if-branch); class-level Node non-mutation; deferred each used in body AND standalone. End-to-end compile+run of the traced cascade (mirrors the verified declarative run). Refresh tests/test_guards_any_audit.py forward.py raise-allowlist line numbers.
8. Do NOT widen _EachCall's own body validation (each-containing-loop/each) in this ticket unless the shared _materialize makes it a one-liner — note the decision either way for e9zse.4's parity matrix.
9. Gates: uv run --extra dev pytest tests/test_forward.py tests/test_loop.py tests/test_composition.py, then full suite + ruff + mypy.
notes:
## Findings (research, 2026-07-11)

REUSE TARGET: the change is CONFINED to src/neograph/forward.py — extend _LoopCall.__call__ (forward.py:507-585) and _EachCall (forward.py:588-735, shipped in a2834d6 by e9zse.1). Zero IR/compiler edits: Construct(nodes=...) already accepts list[Node | Construct], and the declarative cascade shape ALREADY assembles, compiles, AND runs end-to-end (verified by scratch script 2026-07-11: parent[intake, Construct('investigate', input=ClaimBatch, output=Diagnosis, nodes=[get_claims, Construct('verify',input=Claim,output=MatchResult,nodes=[check])|Each(over='get_claims.items',key='cid'), collect])|Loop(when=...)] — compile_complete + RAN OK). The declarative parity oracle exists; the tracer is the only blocker.

- CONFIRMED API (e9zse.1 triage + parent directive): loop body items are the DEFERRED _EachCall objects (step-1 result of self.each(...), NEVER called), placed directly in self.loop(body=[...]). NOTE a wording contradiction in this ticket's own description ('_LoopCall / _EachCall results') — the RESULT of calling either is a _Proxy, which cannot nest (calling records at top level via tracer.record_construct, forward.py:657/:577). The review-gate decision resolves it: deferred objects nest; call-results do not. Do not implement proxy-in-body.
- THE ONE OPEN API POINT (nested over binding): a deferred _EachCall in a loop body is never __call__'d, so its over path must be supplied at construction. Recommendation: add optional over: str | None = None to _ForwardSelf.each()/_EachCall.__init__ (additive; e9zse.1 surface unbroken). Nested over is a RAW DOTTED STRING whose root is either (a) a loop-body PEER's field name (field_name_for(peer.name), e.g. 'get_claims.items') or (b) StateKeys.SUBGRAPH_INPUT ('neo_subgraph_input.<field>') to fan over the loop's own input port — exactly the two root forms _check_each_path accepts inside a sub-construct (src/neograph/_validation_inputs.py:188-245; SUBGRAPH_INPUT early-return at :202-204, peer-producer lookup otherwise). A _Proxy over at construction references TOP-LEVEL traced state, which the loop's isolated sub-state cannot see — reject at materialization with a clear ConstructError. Double-binding (construction over AND __call__ over) → fail loud.
- record_construct suppression: refactor _EachCall.__call__ into build-vs-record: _materialize(...) returns the Construct|Each WITHOUT recording; __call__ keeps existing behavior (resolve over via proxy/tracer, _materialize, tracer.record_construct, return _Proxy). _LoopCall.__call__ calls _materialize for nested items; the nested construct lands INSIDE the loop Construct's nodes list and is never recorded top-level (record_construct is the only top-level channel; an uncalled _EachCall records nothing — correct by construction).
- Nested item-type inference must mirror _check_each_path: root type = effective_producer_type(peer) (NOT _declared_output) — _check_each_path uses matched.effective_type (_validation_inputs.py:198). effective_producer_type/_for live in src/neograph/_validation_types.py:78/:104 (Each → dict[str, X]; duck-typed .modifier_set.each) and are re-exported through _construct_validation.__all__ (:54-55, :81-82 — the import-seam guard requires facade imports; e9zse.1 already extended this seam for _MISSING/_extract_list_element/_resolve_field_annotation). Root == SUBGRAPH_INPUT → walk the loop's input_type instead. Then _resolve_field_annotation per segment + _extract_list_element, fail-loud errors as in _EachCall._infer_item_type (forward.py:710-735).
- Mixed-body output boundary: replace normalize_outputs(body_nodes[-1].outputs).primary (forward.py:535) with normalize_outputs(_declared_output(last_member)).primary — the monopoly selector (TestDeclaredOutputSelectorMonopoly bans inline getattr forms). If the LAST member is Each'd, its bus type is dict[str, X] which can NEVER satisfy the output-boundary contract (_construct_validation.py:320-342 requires an internal producer whose effective_type is _types_compatible with construct.output; dict[str,X] vs X is not) — so the cascade REQUIRES a collector node after the each inside the loop body (the verified declarative shape has one: collect(inputs={'verify': dict}) -> Diagnosis). Detect via effective_producer_type(materialized_last) and fail loud at trace time with hint 'add a collector node consuming dict[str, X] after self.each(...)'; never inline .modifier_set.each checks.
- Loop body validation to relax: forward.py:509-516 (isinstance _NodeCall check; line refs shifted from the ticket's :491-498 by e9zse.1). Widen to _NodeCall | _EachCall | _LoopCall (loop-in-loop is in this ticket's 'free nesting' bullet); keep the fail-loud else-branch. _LoopCall nesting needs the symmetric refactor: a _LoopCall._materialize(input_type) (input inferred from the previous member's declared primary, or the outer loop's input_type when first) — its when/max_iterations/on_exhaust pass through, no record.
- Naming/determinism: materialized members contribute their generated names to body_slug ('loop-get_claims-each-verify-collect'); per-(kind,slug) tracer.next_occurrence (forward.py:378, generalized in e9zse.1) keeps re-trace passes deterministic (fresh _Tracer per pass resets counters). Materialization happens inside _LoopCall.__call__ during the trace, so counters stay per-pass-deterministic.
- inputs default-fill (forward.py:559-563): fill inputs=input_type only on Node members with inputs=None (copy-not-mutate via model_copy, neograph-2o9n); materialized Constructs carry their own input= port — never fill them.
- Collector DX note: inside the loop, the each construct's state field is field_name_for('each-verify') = 'each_verify' (src/neograph/naming.py:7-9), so a @node collector's param must be named each_verify (or declare explicit inputs). Workable; an optional name= kwarg on self.each() would fix the DX and let forward twins match arbitrarily-named declarative subs — additive follow-up, NOT this ticket.
- Current vs deprecated: none in play; forward.py is the actively-maintained current way (e9zse.1 landed a2834d6, 2026-07-11). Bare-for sugar (_apply_loop_modifiers, key='label') stays untouched.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/forward.py:507-585 — _LoopCall.__call__: THE site to change (body validation :509-516; type inference :531-546; naming :555-557; copies :559-563; build+record :565-577)
- src/neograph/forward.py:588-735 — _EachCall (e9zse.1): refactor __call__ into _materialize + record; _resolve_over :665-708 (raw-string root reverse-resolution pattern to adapt for peers); _infer_item_type :710-735
- src/neograph/forward.py:768-814 — _ForwardSelf.loop()/.each(): add over= kwarg to each()
- src/neograph/_validation_inputs.py:188-245 — _check_each_path: the assembly-time semantics nested resolution must mirror (effective_type root, SUBGRAPH_INPUT escape)
- src/neograph/_validation_types.py:78-126 — effective_producer_type(_for): single source of truth for Each -> dict[str,X]; import via _construct_validation facade (:54-55)
- src/neograph/_construct_validation.py:320-342 — output-boundary contract that forbids an Each'd member as the loop's terminal producer
- tests/test_forward.py:980-1109 — TestSelfEachTracing._assert_ir_identical: the IR-equality assertion pattern to extend for the cascade twin
- tests/test_composition.py:3190-3229 + :329-346 — declarative Each'd-sub twins (peer-root and neo_subgraph_input-root forms)
- tests/test_loop.py:166-315 — declarative Loop-on-sub-construct + Each-over-looping-sub patterns
- tests/test_guards_any_audit.py — forward.py raise-allowlist line numbers WILL shift again; refresh (e9zse.1 did the same)

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Wording contradiction ('_EachCall results' vs deferred objects) — resolved by the e9zse.1 review-gate decision (deferred two-step nests); documented above, no user input needed.
- The construction-time over= kwarg is an API-surface addition not explicitly enumerated in the confirmed two-step decision ('zero rework' understated it: nested each cannot receive over any other way). Route this to the execute molecule's independent-review atom (the epic routes DSL-surface decisions there), not to the user.
- Each'd member as LAST loop-body item: impossible declaratively (output-boundary contract) — fail loud at trace time, and add a should_fail-style test; do NOT try to make Construct.output carry dict[str,X].
- A deferred _EachCall placed in a body AND also called standalone builds two distinct constructs (distinct occurrence-suffixed names) — coexistence is safe; pin with a test or leave as documented behavior.
- Loop-in-loop declarative legality not runtime-verified in this research (only the cascade was); verify with a declarative fixture before/alongside the forward twin (e9zse.3 owns runtime verification; the .2 acceptance is trace-IR equality).
- Collector param naming ('each_verify') is the sharpest DX edge for real users; document in the test docstring; name= kwarg is the follow-up fix.

## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-e9zse.2)

Pattern: tracer sub-construct builders that (a) fuse build+record into one step (record_construct inside construction — blocks nesting) and (b) select the member output type via inline .outputs instead of the _declared_output monopoly selector (breaks on Construct members).
Scan command: grep -n "record_construct\|body_nodes\[-1\]\|_declared_output\|isinstance(nc, _NodeCall)" src/neograph/forward.py

No DEFER rows. Scope matches the design (all MIGRATE rows are in the plan).
## Architect Review (independent, neograph-bhsdk.12)

Gate hard-check PASSED: research:complete + codebase-scan:complete both present.

### Routed API decision (construction-time `over: str | None` on self.each()/_EachCall) — APPROVED

It is additive (e9zse.1 surface unbroken), string-only by type (so a proxy-over cannot enter at construction), and its two accepted root forms (peer field_name via field_name_for + neo_subgraph_input) are byte-for-byte the two forms _check_each_path accepts inside a sub-construct (_validation_inputs.py:203 SUBGRAPH_INPUT early-return + peer-producer lookup). effective_producer_type/_for are genuinely re-exported through the _construct_validation facade (:54-55, :81-82), so the 'import via facade' instruction is correct. No HIGH here.

### Findings
- [MEDIUM] Mixed-body per-member input fill is under-specified. Step 4 keeps the current blanket rule 'fill inputs=input_type when inputs is None' (forward.py:559-563) applied to ALL body members. In a MIXED body the post-each collector consumes the each's dict field (each_verify), NOT the loop port type — so blanket-filling the loop input_type onto a None-inputs post-each member produces WRONG IR (silent misfill or a confusing downstream type error), diverging from the declarative twin whose collector carries its own inputs. Realistic collectors (@node param-named each_verify, or explicit inputs=) are non-None so the guard skips them and the acceptance cascade is safe — but the plan should scope the fill to port-consuming members (first member / members reading neo_subgraph_input) OR fail loud when a non-first mixed-body member has inputs=None. - [MEDIUM] Loop-in-loop (step 5) is built toward an UNVERIFIED declarative reference. Research itself flags 'Loop-in-loop declarative legality not runtime-verified' and there is NO declarative loop-in-loop fixture in the suite (grep of tests/test_loop.py confirms). The .2 acceptance is 'traced IR == declarative IR' — asserting equality to a reference that may not compile is unsound. Make a declarative loop-in-loop compile+assemble sanity fixture a FIRM precondition to the loop-in-loop twin test, not a soft risk note.
- [MEDIUM] Existing TestLoopBodyValidation (tests/test_forward.py:1527, neograph-ndm1) is not reconciled in the plan's test list (step 7). Its docstring (:1528-1530) currently codifies 'Passing proxies, nested loops, or non-node objects should raise' — after this ticket, nested _LoopCall/_EachCall body items become LEGAL, so that docstring/scope becomes FALSE while test_proxy_in_body_raises and test_non_node_object_in_body_raises MUST keep raising (a _Proxy/str is still not _NodeCall|_EachCall|_LoopCall). It is still worth doing for the 'add a collector node' hint AND it correctly routes through effective_producer_type (no inline .modifier_set.each), so no double-siting — keep it, just note it as DX polish over an existing guard, not a new safety net.
- [LOW] Collector param-name DX ('each_verify') is the sharpest real-user edge; the optional name= kwarg is correctly deferred as follow-up. Document the field-name coupling in the twin test docstring as planned.

### Verdict
Overall: NEEDS_REFINEMENT
(3 MEDIUM, 2 LOW, 0 HIGH. The routed over= API decision is APPROVED. Refine: scope the mixed-body input fill, gate loop-in-loop on a compiled declarative reference, reconcile the neograph-ndm1 test contract.)
## Refinement (resolves review MEDIUMs, 2026-07-11)
1. Mixed-body inputs fill SCOPED: node-only bodies keep the existing blanket fill (zero behavior change for shipped loop IR). In a MIXED body, fill inputs=input_type only for _NodeCall members that PRECEDE the first construct member; a None-inputs _NodeCall member AFTER a construct member fails loud at trace time (ConstructError; hint: declare inputs= or name the @node param after the construct's state field, e.g. each_verify). title: P1: self.each() tracing surface — fan-out over sub-construct with custom key
description:
Epic neograph-e9zse Phase 1, fix #1. Design doc: docs/design/forwardconstruct-expressiveness-parity-2026-07-10.md

## What
Add self.each(body=[...], over=..., key=..., on_error=...) to ForwardConstruct's _ForwardSelf in src/neograph/forward.py, mirroring the existing self.loop()/_LoopCall machinery (forward.py:462-621) as the blueprint:
- Build Construct(input=, output=, nodes=body) | Each(over=over, key=key, on_error=on_error)
- record_construct into the tracer, return an output proxy
- Reuse _declared_output port inference for input/output boundary types
- Keep the existing bare `for x in proxy` form as sugar for the trivial single-node / key="label" case (today forward.py:652 hardcodes key="label" and applies Each PER-NODE — that path stays as sugar; self.each() is the general form)

## Fixes
(a) custom Each key (not just "label"); (b) fan-out over a SUB-CONSTRUCT (multi-node body wrapped as one Each'd sub-construct); (c) on_error pass-through (e.g. 'collect').

## Core Invariant
New tracer surfaces must emit ONLY existing IR (Construct | Each) — identical to what the equivalent declarative form produces. Never ForwardConstruct-only IR. Zero changes to IR/compiler modules (node.py, construct.py, _construct_validation.py, compiler.py, factory.py, state.py, modifiers.py).

## Independent-review gate (from the epic — review atom must cover)
DSL-surface API decisions: bare-for sugar vs explicit self.each() builder; how self.loop()/self.each() compose and nest; whether key="label" default stays. The review atom is the fresh-context reviewer the epic requires BEFORE Phase 1 implementation.

## Acceptance
A forward() twin of declarative `Construct(input=X, output=Y, nodes=[a, b]) | Each(over=..., key="id")` traces to IDENTICAL IR (same nodes list, same modifier params, graph-diff clean). Tested via TDD: failing IR-equality test first.

## Confirmed API shape (review gate resolved 2026-07-11)

4. Add _ForwardSelf.each(body, key, on_error='raise') next to .loop() (forward.py:600-621) returning _EachCall.

- Each modifier: src/neograph/modifiers.py:484-510 — fields `over: str` (dotted path), `key: str`, `on_error: Literal['raise','collect']='raise'`. Pass all three through verbatim.
- over-path from a proxy: the bare-for sugar already computes it — `_Tracer.record_iteration` forward.py:377-385 (`field_name_for(source.name)` + `_attr_chain_after_prefix`). Extract/reuse that computation (module-level helper) rather than duplicating it in _EachCall.

Assembly validation then re-checks it via `_check_each_path` (src/neograph/_validation_inputs.py:188-240), so a wrong inference fails loud at Construct.__init__.
- Output type: `normalize_outputs(body_nodes[-1].outputs).primary` — identical to _LoopCall forward.py:517.
- Copy-not-mutate: _LoopCall model_copy's body nodes to set `inputs` without mutating class-level Nodes (forward.py:541-545, pinned by TestLoopCallDoesNotMutateClassNodes, neograph-2o9n). self.each() body copies must do the same with `inputs=item_type`.

NOTE: the existing counter dict is keyed by body_slug only; either key it by `(kind, slug)` or include the 'each'/'loop' prefix in the slug so a loop and an each over the same body don't share a counter.
- Bare `for x in proxy` sugar STAYS: `_apply_loop_modifiers` forward.py:638-654 applies Each PER-NODE with hardcoded key='label' (line 652). Do not change it; self.each() is the general form (custom key, multi-node body, on_error).
- Current vs old: no deprecated pattern in play — forward.py is actively maintained (recent monopoly refactors b7dd223/d9e9731 moved `_declared_output`/`normalize_outputs` into _normalize; USE those, not `getattr(item,'output',None)` — TestDeclaredOutputSelectorMonopoly bans the inline form).

- src/neograph/forward.py:600-621 — _ForwardSelf.loop(): where the sibling `each()` method goes

## Data-flow trace (one concrete example)
forward(): `items_out = self.seed(x); results = self.each(body=[self.verify], over=items_out.items, key='item_id')` -> _EachCall computes over_path 'seed.items' (field_name_for + attr chain), infers item_type=FanItem (seed.outputs=FanCollection -> .items -> list[FanItem]), copies verify with inputs=FanItem, builds Construct('each-verify', input=FanItem, output=MatchResult, nodes=[copy]) | Each(over='seed.items', key='item_item_id'... key='item_id', on_error='raise'), record_construct, returns proxy(source=sub). ## Risks & Edge Cases
- API-shape decision (flagged for the epic's independent-review gate, NOT resolved here): _LoopCall is two-step (`self.loop(...)(proxy)`); for each, `over=` already carries the input binding, so a one-step `self.each(body, over=proxy.attr, key=...)` returning the output proxy directly is more natural and is what the bead text implies ('return an output proxy'). - [HIGH] Finding (mandated item (a)+(b) — one-step vs two-step AND compose/nest): The plan's recommended ONE-STEP self.each(body, over, key) returning an output proxy is in direct contradiction with sibling ticket neograph-e9zse.2. e9zse.2's design and its 'Depends on' both state '_EachCall must exist' and relax self.loop() body validation (:491-498) to 'accept sub-construct-producing items (_LoopCall / _EachCall) alongside _NodeCall'. That mechanism requires _EachCall to be a DEFERRED, placeable-in-a-body-list object exactly like _LoopCall — i.e. self.each(...) must return an _EachCall instance you can drop into self.loop(body=[ self.each(...) ], ...), where the loop's __call__ lowers it into the loop's per-iteration sub-construct. A one-step each instead EAGERLY calls record_construct at top level and returns a _Proxy: there is no persistent _EachCall to nest, and eager top-level recording double-records the sub-construct when it should live INSIDE the loop body. Since the epic's ENTIRE justification is the cascade topology 'Loop(investigate{ verify | Each(over, key="id") })' (each nested inside a loop), the each API shape is load-bearing for e9zse.2 and cannot be chosen in isolation. The leaf-only acceptance test for e9zse.1 would pass with one-step and mask the defect — the break only surfaces in e9zse.2. Suggestion: adopt the TWO-STEP _EachCall shape, mirroring _LoopCall — self.each(body=[...], key=..., on_error=...) returns _EachCall; its __call__(over_proxy) computes over_path + item_type and builds Construct(input=item_type, output=..., nodes=copies) | Each(over, key, on_error), record_construct, returns the output proxy. 'Fail loud' would make the raw-string escape unusable. Suggestion: either (i) require an explicit item/port type argument when over is a raw string, or (ii) resolve the producer by matching split_each_path(over)'s root field back to a traced node (field_name_for inverse) and infer from there, or (iii) drop raw-string over from this ticket's scope. Pick one and specify it before implementing.

- [LOW] Finding (mandated item (c) — key='label' bare-for default): Keeping the bare 'for x in proxy' sugar with hardcoded key='label' as-is is fine and correctly ALLOWLISTed. Note for the parity matrix (e9zse.4): bare-for emits PER-NODE (node | Each) whereas self.each emits a wrapped (Construct | Each) sub-construct — so for a single-node body the two forms are NOT IR-identical by design. Add an explicit re-trace-determinism test for the loop+each-same-slug case so the generalization is pinned, not just asserted.

- HIGH (API shape): TWO-STEP _EachCall confirmed. self.each(body=[...], key=..., on_error=...) returns a deferred _EachCall; calling it with the over argument builds Construct|Each, record_construct, returns output proxy. title: ForwardConstruct expressiveness parity: forward() must express every topology the declarative form can (identical IR)
description:
## Invariant (the whole point)
Every topology the declarative Construct form can express, ForwardConstruct.forward() must ALSO express — tracing to IDENTICAL IR. The forward.py docstring already promises this for straight-line pipelines (:15); this epic extends it to the full modifier/composition surface. Parity is BOUNDED BY declarative capability (ForwardConstruct need not exceed it — e.g. Each x Oracle fusion on sub-constructs is a documented declarative non-support and stays out of scope for both).

## Why we absolutely need to ship this
The imperative 'write the graph as Python control flow' DX is compelling but appears in ZERO apps (only demo example 15) — NOT because it's unwanted, but because its expressible topology set is a tiny subset (straight-line + per-node fan-out keyed 'label' + node-only loops + constant-comparison branches). Real agent pipelines need fan-out-inside-loop over sub-constructs, ensembles, HITL — none expressible today. The fix is PARITY, not new IR: the tracer is artificially stricter than the IR it already targets.

## Authoritative analysis
docs/design/forwardconstruct-expressiveness-parity-2026-07-10.md — tracer mechanism (torch.fx symbolic proxy), the full capability x coverage x difficulty table, per-gap fix shapes with code sites, acceptance principle, anti-band-aid parity-matrix guard, phasing, effort, independent-review gate.

## The load-bearing fixes (PHASE 1 — ship first, ~2-3 days, zero IR/compiler changes, all in forward.py)
Both blockers are 'teach the tracer to emit what the IR already accepts', with self.loop() as the working blueprint:
1. self.each(body=[...], over=..., key=...) mirroring _LoopCall/self.loop() (:462-621): build Construct(input=,output=,nodes=body) | Each(over,key,on_error=), record_construct, return proxy. ~40 lines. Keep bare 'for x in proxy' as sugar for the trivial single-node/key='label' case. FIXES: custom key + fan-out over a SUB-CONSTRUCT (today :652 hardcodes key='label' and applies Each PER-NODE).
2. Relax self.loop() body validation (:491-498) to accept sub-construct-producing items (_LoopCall/_EachCall results) alongside _NodeCall. Construct(nodes=...) already takes list[Node|Construct]; reuse _declared_output port inference (:519). FIXES: Loop over a sub-construct body (loop containing an Each fan-out) — the exact cascade shape.
3. Verify (mark with tests): fan-in multi-input node calls; multi-output dict nodes ({node}_{key} wiring through tracing).

## PHASE 2 (medium)
Oracle (ensemble_n+merge) is ENTIRELY ABSENT from forward() today (Oracle not even imported; no self.ensemble()). Operator/interrupt_when (HITL) not exposed. Add self.ensemble()/HITL tracing surfaces that build the EXISTING modifiers. Verify skip_when/skip_value survive tracing.

## PHASE 3 (hard — CLOSE or CAP)
Branch richness (re-trace is 2^N, constant-comparisons only, max 8 — :33-36) and try/except fallback (dead-code under symbolic tracing, :38-47). These do NOT block the unused-making topologies (the cascade 'branch' is an LLM output field, not graph control flow). Recommendation: keep as documented v1 limits with a LOUD escape to the declarative form rather than a fragile 2^N expansion. Decide during the epic.

## Acceptance — one verifiable principle
Traced IR == declarative IR, per topology class (graph-lint diff clean). Reference integration test = the cascade shape (intake -> triage -> Loop(investigate{ verify | Each(over, key='id') }) -> explain): a ForwardConstruct expressing it must trace to the SAME IR the declarative ox cascade compiles.

## Anti-band-aid
Do NOT special-case the cascade. Deliverable is PARITY enforced by a PARITY TEST MATRIX: a corpus of declarative topologies, each with a forward() twin, asserted IR-identical. Permanent guard = a property test comparing traced IR to declarative IR across the corpus, so a new declarative capability lacking a forward() path FAILS LOUD (the parity ratchet). New tracer surfaces must build EXISTING IR, never ForwardConstruct-only IR.

## Independent-review gate
The DSL-surface design (bare-for sugar vs explicit self.each(); how loop/each compose+nest; keep the key='label' default?) is an API decision — fresh-context reviewer confirms BEFORE Phase 1. Review the parity matrix for coverage.

## Not 0.6.0-gating (0.6 shipped). Post-0.6, HIGH priority (maintainer: 'we absolutely need to ship this').

title: Expose a public LAZY single-tool MCP factory with explicit tool_name + rename (no build-time discovery)
description:
## What
Add a public neograph_mcp helper — e.g. a singular `mcp_tool_factory(server_key, spec, *, tool_name, rename_to=None, token_provider=None) -> ToolFactory`, or a `lazy=True` + explicit `tools={server: [names]}` / `rename={key: name}` option on `mcp_tool_factories` — that returns a single async ToolFactory which (a) DEFERS the MCP connect into the async factory body (NO build-time `_run_sync(_discover_tool_names)`), and (b) renames the discovered (possibly gateway-namespaced) tool to an explicit `rename_to` name. The internal `_make_tool_factory` (src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:198) ALREADY implements BOTH behaviours (a lazy `_factory` body that connects on await + a `rename_to` param); this is purely a public-API-exposure gap.

## Why
A consumer binding a gateway-federated tool into a neograph node with a fixed `Tool('<bare-name>')` binding needs BOTH the factory-dict key AND the bound `tool.name` to be the BARE name. IBM ContextForge re-exposes federated tools NAMESPACED as `<peer>-<tool>`, but `mcp_tool_factories` only offers `namespace=True` ('server::tool') or `namespace=False` (the discovered namespaced name) — NEITHER yields the bare name. Separately, `mcp_tool_factories` connects EAGERLY at build time via `_run_sync(_discover_tool_names)`, which fires a live gateway connect inside a consumer's OFFLINE factory-build path (agent-stark's `build_tool_factories` runs at compile for every run + directly in offline fast tests) and breaks the deterministic suite. Today consumers must reach into the private `_make_tool_factory` or hand-roll the MultiServerMCPClient plumbing — both duplicate what neograph owns (nmb2). Surfaced by agent-stark's stark-63q.54.4 MCP-gateway GATE, which is BLOCKED on this.

## Expectations after delivery
- A consumer can bind ONE gateway-federated MCP tool into a node whose `Tool(name)` binding is a fixed bare name, with the factory built offline (no network until run/superstep time).
- agent-stark stark-63q.54.4 unblocks: build_tool_factories swaps the perplexity_research entry to this public lazy+rename factory with zero build-time connect.

## Verification — integration & E2E only
- Integration: constructing the factory performs ZERO network I/O (assert no connection attempted at build); the connect happens only on first `await factory(config, tool_config)`. Against a live/fake MCP server exposing `<peer>-perplexity_research`, the awaited tool has `.name == 'perplexity_research'` (the rename) and invokes correctly. nmb2: the client is owned inside the factory (existing session-ownership guard stays green).

## Acceptance
- Public API in `neograph_mcp.__all__` builds a single async ToolFactory for a known (server, tool_name) with NO build-time network I/O.
- Returned tool `.name == rename_to` when provided (renames a gateway-namespaced `<peer>-<tool>` back to bare).
- nmb2 session-ownership invariant preserved; covered by a test.
- (Reuses the already-implemented internal _make_tool_factory — should be a thin public wrapper.)
design:
## Core Invariant
The MultiServerMCPClient is created and OWNED strictly inside the returned async factory body (nmb2) AND no MCP network I/O happens until the first await -- the singular helper adds a public name over _make_tool_factory without moving one line of connect logic out of the deferred _factory body.

## Implementation Plan
1. Add `mcp_tool_factory(server_key, spec, *, tool_name, rename_to=None, token_provider=None, stdio_token_arg='token') -> ToolFactory` in src/neograph_mcp/_client.py, immediately after `mcp_tool_factories` (near :259). Body is a THIN delegation: `return _make_tool_factory(server_key, spec, tool_name, rename_to, token_provider, stdio_token_arg)`. Do NOT call _run_sync / _discover_tool_names / get_tools -- the whole feature is that build-time is connect-free. Docstring: state the single-tool / gateway-federated use case, the zero-build-network guarantee, and that `rename_to` maps a discovered (possibly namespaced <peer>-<tool>) name back to the bare Tool(name) binding. Mirror the plural's docstring voice.
2. Export it: add `mcp_tool_factory` to the import block (src/neograph_mcp/__init__.py:35-41) and to `__all__` (:43-49). __all__ is the public contract (AGENTS.md naming policy).
3. Add a demo tool to exercise the namespaced->bare rename faithfully: `@mcp.tool(name='crm-perplexity_research')` in examples/_mcp_demo_server.py (a bare read-only echo tool, ~5 lines, token-echoing like crm_search). Safe: E2E/battery tool-set assertions are subset/membership.
4. Tests in tests/test_mcp_battery.py, new methods under (or beside) `TestOneConsumerSmoke`, all `@requires_mcp`, run via `uv run --extra dev --extra mcp pytest tests/test_mcp_battery.py`:
   (a) construction is zero-network: `f = mcp_tool_factory('crm', _demo_stdio_server(), tool_name='crm-perplexity_research', rename_to='perplexity_research')`; assert `asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(f)` with NO subprocess spawned (no get_tools at build). Optionally construct against an unreachable spec and assert it still returns without raising.
   (b) awaited tool renames + invokes: `tool = await f(config, None)`; assert `tool.name == 'perplexity_research'`; assert it invokes correctly against the real demo server (echoes acting_as / returns payload).
   (c) token injection BEFORE rename: pin the order -- a stdio token_provider still injects `stdio_token_arg` even though the tool is renamed (proves inject introspects the real pre-rename schema). Assert the echoed token arrives AND `tool.name == rename_to`.
   (d) nmb2 preserved: rely on the existing tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py guard (scans all of src/neograph_mcp) -- confirm it stays green; the client is born inside the delegated _factory, so preservation is by construction. No new guard needed.
5. Run gates: `uv run --extra dev --extra mcp pytest tests/test_mcp_battery.py tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py` + mypy on the two touched src files. Full suite per landing-the-plane.
6. Follow-up (separate, not this atom): website single-tool/gateway subsection; unblock agent-stark stark-63q.54.4 (swap perplexity_research entry to this lazy+rename factory).
notes:
2026-07-09 SEAM ANALYSIS (session leader, claim verified against src/neograph_mcp/_client.py): confirmed pure exposure gap — _make_tool_factory:183 is already fully lazy (all I/O incl. get_tools + rename inside the async _factory body, lines 198-212) and already takes rename_to. The ONLY build-time connect is the plural builder's _run_sync(_discover_tool_names) at :243. DECIDED SHAPE: the singular public helper mcp_tool_factory(server_key, spec, *, tool_name, rename_to=None, token_provider=None, stdio_token_arg='token') -> ToolFactory — a thin delegation to _make_tool_factory + __all__ export. NOT the lazy= flag on the plural: discovery is inherently a connect, so lazy=True would contradict mcp_tool_factories' own contract and require a parallel tools={} argument (a second function wearing a flag). Tests: (1) zero network at construction (count connect attempts; first await connects), (2) awaited tool .name == rename_to against the demo server's namespaced name + invokes correctly, (3) nmb2 session-ownership guard green (preserved by construction — client born inside the factory body), (4) stdio token injection applies through the singular path, (5) PIN the order: token injection BEFORE rename (:208 -> :210) so stdio_token_arg introspects the server's real declared args. Effort: small (wrapper + docstring + integration tests via the FastMCP demo server, --extra mcp-examples harness). Gates y5ux (wired). Website: add a short 'single-tool / gateway-federated' subsection to walkthrough/mcp-client.mdx + concepts/mcp-integration.mdx when it lands.
## Findings (research grounded 2026-07-09, dp-researcher against current source)

- CONFIRMED pure exposure gap. `_make_tool_factory` (src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:183-214) is ALREADY fully lazy and ALREADY takes `rename_to`. Its returned inner `_factory` (198-212) performs ALL I/O on await: `_resolve_token`(199) -> `_client_for`(200) -> `get_tools`(201) -> tool lookup by name(202) -> stdio token inject(208-209) -> rename(210-211). Zero I/O runs at `_make_tool_factory` call time. Signature is positional: `(server_key, spec, tool_name, rename_to, token_provider, stdio_token_arg) -> ToolFactory`.

- REUSE TARGET: `_make_tool_factory`. The public helper is a thin keyword-wrapper that delegates to it + an `__all__` export. NOT a reimplementation. Verified NO singular `mcp_tool_factory` exists yet (grep across src/tests/examples/website = 0 hits).

- The ONLY build-time connect is the PLURAL builder's `_run_sync(_discover_tool_names(server_key, spec))` at _client.py:243 (inside `mcp_tool_factories`, 217-259). `_discover_tool_names` (176-180) is the eager connect. The singular helper MUST NOT call `_run_sync`/`_discover_tool_names` — the whole point is deferring the connect.

- DECIDED SHAPE (matches prior SEAM ANALYSIS, re-verified): `mcp_tool_factory(server_key, spec, *, tool_name, rename_to=None, token_provider=None, stdio_token_arg='token') -> ToolFactory`. Keyword-only after spec (mirrors `mcp_tool_factories`'s kw-only tail). NOT a `lazy=` flag on the plural: discovery IS a connect, so `lazy=True` would contradict `mcp_tool_factories`' own docstring contract (connects once per server to enumerate) and force a parallel `tools={}` arg — a second function wearing a flag. Singular helper wins.

- Public surface today: src/neograph_mcp/__init__.py:35-49 imports {HttpServer, StdioServer, ToolFactory, mcp_resource_fetcher, mcp_tool_factories} and lists them in `__all__`. Add `mcp_tool_factory` to BOTH the import block (35-41) and `__all__` (43-49). Per AGENTS.md naming policy, `__all__` IS the public contract.

- Order pin (208-210): stdio token injection happens BEFORE rename. `_inject_stdio_token` (153-173) introspects `tool.args` to decide whether to inject `stdio_token_arg`; must run against the server's real declared schema. Rename (model_copy of `name`) does not touch `args`, but the ordering is a real invariant the wrapper inherits for free by delegating (it does NOT re-implement the body). Pin it in a test so a future refactor can't reorder.

- Demo server tool set (examples/_mcp_demo_server.py): crm_search(191-202), kb_lookup(204), get_deal(215), update_deal(242), arm_email_expiry — all BARE names, NONE namespaced. FastMCP derives tool name from the fn name, so a literal `<peer>-<tool>` hyphenated name needs `@mcp.tool(name='crm-perplexity_research')`. E2E harness (tests/test_mcp_examples_e2e.py:77,254) asserts the tool set with SUBSET (`<=`) — adding a namespaced demo tool is SAFE, won't break it; test_mcp_battery.py:217-219 uses membership `in`, also safe.
## Relevant Code
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:183-214 -- `_make_tool_factory`: the REUSE target. Already lazy + already renames. Wrapper delegates here.
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:198-212 -- the inner async `_factory` body: proves all I/O is deferred to await (token, client, get_tools, inject, rename).
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:243 -- `_run_sync(_discover_tool_names(...))`: the eager build-time connect the singular helper must AVOID.
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:217-259 -- `mcp_tool_factories` (plural): the sibling to sit beside; copy its docstring style + kw-only tail.
- src/neograph_mcp/__init__.py:35-49 -- public facade: add `mcp_tool_factory` to the import block AND `__all__`.
- tests/test_mcp_battery.py:207-262 (`TestOneConsumerSmoke`) -- the exemplar integration-test class to mirror: `@requires_mcp` skipif, `_demo_stdio_server()`, real arun against demo server. New tests go HERE (same file), not a new one.
- tests/test_mcp_battery.py:43-44 -- `_HAS_MCP` / `requires_mcp` skipif gate; the extra is `--extra mcp` (pyproject.toml:43-47), NOT mcp-examples, for battery tests.
- tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py:107-124 (`TestMcpBatteryImportsNoEngineSurfaces`) -- nmb2 guard; already scans all of src/neograph_mcp, so it covers the new wrapper automatically. NO new guard code needed; the invariant is preserved BY CONSTRUCTION (client born inside the delegated `_factory`).
- examples/_mcp_demo_server.py:191-202 -- `crm_search`; the real tool the integration test drives (rename target).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Namespaced-name test data gap: NO demo tool is hyphen-namespaced, so the faithful `<peer>-<tool>` -> bare rename can't be shown against an existing tool. Two options: (A) rename an existing bare tool (crm_search -> 'search') -- proves rename mechanics but is bare->bare, not namespaced->bare; (B) add `@mcp.tool(name='crm-perplexity_research')` to the demo server and rename it to 'perplexity_research' -- faithful to ContextForge, and SAFE (E2E + battery assertions are subset/membership, not equality). RECOMMEND (B): it makes the acceptance criterion ('renames a gateway-namespaced <peer>-<tool> back to bare') literally true, and a fake-double factory CANNOT test rename (rename lives inside _make_tool_factory, which a fake bypasses) -- so a real-server integration test is mandatory anyway.
- Zero-network-at-construction assertion: to prove NO connect at build, the strongest signal is that `mcp_tool_factory(...)` returns a coroutine-function WITHOUT the demo subprocess ever being spawned. Constructing with a bogus/unreachable spec must still return a factory without raising (connect deferred). Assert `asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(factory)` on a spec that would fail if connected, then assert first `await` connects. Mirror the plural's `iscoroutinefunction` check at test_mcp_battery.py:220.
- Three-surface parity does NOT apply here: this is a neograph_mcp battery helper (a factory builder), not an IR-level change to node.py/factory.py/state.py. The produced ToolFactory is consumed through the SAME existing tool-factory seam the plural already uses; no @node/declarative/programmatic split to cover.
- Website follow-up (out of scope for this atom, note for impl): add a single-tool/gateway-federated subsection to website/src/content/docs/walkthrough/mcp-client.mdx + concepts/mcp-integration.mdx when it lands (AGENTS.md: update website on API-surface change).
## Codebase Disease Scan (g2jg)

Pattern: single-tool MCP factory construction that bypasses a public helper — a direct reach-in to the private `_make_tool_factory` OR hand-rolled `MultiServerMCPClient` tool-binding plumbing standing in for a shipped public single-tool lazy+rename factory.
Scan command: `grep -rn '_make_tool_factory\|MultiServerMCPClient\|_discover_tool_names\|_client_for' src/ tests/ examples/`
Shape: SYNTACTIC (bounded, greppable) — single-executor scan sufficient; no multi-agent targeted scan.
Total instances found: all hits enumerated below; ZERO in-repo MIGRATE sites (pure additive exposure gap — the sole real consumer, agent-stark, is external, tracked by stark-63q.54.4).

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:251 | plural builder calls `_make_tool_factory(...)` | ALLOWLIST | sanctioned internal delegation; the new singular helper will delegate to the SAME private builder — not a bypass to eliminate |
| 2 | src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:97-104,176-180,200,333,350 | `_client_for`/`_discover_tool_names` internals | ALLOWLIST | the module-internal plumbing being wrapped; owning the client inside the module IS the design (nmb2) |
| 3 | tests/test_mcp_examples_e2e.py (all MultiServerMCPClient uses) | raw-client E2E harness | ALLOWLIST | drives the raw MCP protocol directly to PROVE the demo server end-to-end; a test harness, not a consumer binding a tool into a node |
| 4 | tests/test_mcp_async_factory.py:73, tests/test_mcp_battery.py:4, tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py | doc/guard mentions | ALLOWLIST | docstring text + the nmb2 guard regex that BANS the pattern in src — not a bypass site |
| 5 | examples/23_mcp_client_selective_binding.py:427-468 | commented-out illustration | ALLOWLIST | all lines `#`-prefixed; illustrative comment, not executed code |
| 6 | examples/24_mcp_resources_from_resource.py:178-401 | raw `client.session()` for resource-fetch + one-shot expiry-arming demos | ALLOWLIST | demonstrates the RESOURCE protocol + self-heal, not the single-tool tool-factory seam the helper wraps |
| 7 | examples/_mcp_demo_server.py:57 | docstring | ALLOWLIST | prose describing how the demo server is reached |

Conclusion: no MIGRATE and no DEFER rows. The design (add `mcp_tool_factory` singular public wrapper + `__all__` export) stands unchanged — the scan confirms it is purely additive, with no in-repo bypass sites to also migrate.
## Architect Review (neograph-bajq.4, independent, fresh context)

Gate hard-check PASSED: both research:complete and codebase-scan:complete present on g2jg.

Verified against source (not taken on trust):
- _make_tool_factory (_client.py:183-214) is fully lazy: all I/O (resolve_token->_client_for->get_tools->lookup->inject->rename) is inside the async _factory closure (198-212); zero I/O at call time. CONFIRMED.
- Order token-inject (208-209) BEFORE rename (210-211). CONFIRMED. Signature is positional (server_key, spec, tool_name, rename_to, token_provider, stdio_token_arg) -> ToolFactory; the plan's delegation arg order matches exactly. CONFIRMED.
- The sole build-time connect is the PLURAL builder's _run_sync(_discover_tool_names) at :243; the singular wrapper correctly avoids it. CONFIRMED.
- __init__.py:35-49 needs the name added to BOTH import block and __all__. CONFIRMED (currently absent; grep = 0 hits for a singular helper).
- Demo tools all bare @mcp.tool(); adding @mcp.tool(name='crm-perplexity_research') is feasible and SAFE: E2E harness asserts tool set with subset '<=' (test_mcp_examples_e2e.py:77,254) and battery uses membership 'in' (test_mcp_battery.py:217). CONFIRMED by reading both.
- Reuse target correct; alternative (lazy= flag on plural) soundly rejected (discovery IS a connect). Plan is faithful and complete.

title: hydrate_resource_ref re-derivation ignores ref.kind — multi-link producer heals to WRONG resource_link
description:
INVARIANT: on the hydration replay path, re-deriving an expired ResourceRef MUST resolve to the resource_link whose KIND matches ref.kind. Healing must never silently substitute a different-kind blob.

DEFECT (verified by seat-3m6g via two live-server probes, root cause confirmed by maintainer in src): di.py:222 re-derives the fresh uri via _first_resource_link_uri(replay_result), which returns the FIRST resource_link regardless of kind. When the producing_call is a multi-link tool (the real demo server's get_deal returns [text, activity-history link, email-history link] — activity FIRST), healing an email-history ref reads the ACTIVITY blob and silently parses it as EmailHistory -> emails=[] (wrong data, no error). Exposed by the real FastMCP demo server via example 24 (neograph-3m6g); the shipped mcp_resource_fetcher replayer returns get_deal's whole content, so first-link != ref.kind.

FIX (anti-band-aid, kind-aware re-derivation): extract a single shared _resource_link_kind(block) derivation (currently inlined at _agent_cycle.py:456 as ) so lift-side and replay-side use ONE derivation and cannot drift. Add _content_blocks helper resolving the resource_link uri whose derived-kind == ref.kind. di.py replay becomes: kind-matched link -> first link (back-compat) -> ref.uri. NO band-aid in the example/battery.

TDD: failing regression test FIRST (multi-link replay result + email-history ref must heal to the EMAIL uri, not activity), verify red, then fix, verify green. Test in tests/modes/test_resource_manifest.py (NOT test_di.py — reserved for the concurrent prompt-surface seat). Parity note in docstring: hydration is surface-agnostic (FromResource DI runs the same for all three surfaces) so one hydration-level regression suffices.

DISCOVERED-BY: neograph-3m6g example-24 verification. BLOCKS: 0.6.0 (y5ux) — a featured example must not showcase a path that silently returns wrong data.

title: structured output strategy: no re-prompt retry on Pydantic ValidationError (parity with json_mode)
description:
_llm_dispatch._call_structured (and _acall_structured): the 'structured' strategy handles Parsed|Raw|Failed with DSML recovery, but has NO re-prompt retry when the provider returns structurally-valid JSON that fails Pydantic model validation (a schema/constraint violation). json_mode routes through _invoke_json_with_retry(max_retries=...) and re-prompts; structured surfaces the ValidationError and kills the node/round.

This bites on providers whose constrained-decode does NOT truly enforce the schema (e.g. z-ai/glm-5.1 via OpenRouter): ~13% of structured agent-node calls emit an output that fails validation. Observed in ox-troubleshooting-demo GLM full-corpus run: 5 round-fatal ValidationErrors across HypothesisSet, Evidence, RoundState, Diagnosis (all output_strategy=structured), each failing a cascade scenario that would otherwise pass. Errors seen: 'ExecutionError: Validation failed for RoundState', 'ValidationError: 1 validation error for {HypothesisSet,Evidence,Diagnosis}'.

Ask: give the structured path the same bounded re-prompt-on-ValidationError retry json_mode has (honor max_retries; feed the validation error back as a repair hint), so a single weakly-enforced structured decode doesn't fail the whole node. Consumers currently work around it by switching hot nodes to json_mode, losing constrained-decode's guarantees on well-behaved providers.
notes:
2026-07-08 MAINTAINER-SIDE ANALYSIS (claims verified against develop HEAD). CONFIRMED: ValidationError from a weakly-enforced constrained decode surfaces as Failed(error=ValidationError) from the compat adapter chain (_llm_structured_compat.py:153,164 — the decorators catch validation exc and wrap); the structured strategy's Failed arm raises immediately with NO retry, while json_mode routes through _invoke_json_with_retry's bounded re-prompt loop (_llm_retry.py:292, honoring max_retries; LlmConfig.max_retries exists at _llm_config.py:44). The machinery for parity EXISTS — the structured path just never engages it for validation failures.

TWO SITES to cover (both bitten by the consumer): (1) the think-mode primary structured path (invoke_structured/ainvoke_structured -> adapter chain -> Failed handling in _llm.py) and (2) the agent-mode structured fallback (_call_structured/_acall_structured Failed arms, _llm_dispatch.py:129 + async twin). Fix at the SHARED seam so both inherit — post-ykun the error builders are already module-level; the retry loop must follow the same extract-then-thin discipline (a structured-flavored bounded retry pair sharing a pure repair-hint-message builder with the existing DSML/json retry builders in _llm_retry — do NOT re-inline the loop per twin; TWIN_TABLE + thinness guard apply).

FIX SHAPE: on Failed(error=ValidationError) (discriminate: retry ONLY validation failures — TypeError/provider-rejection Failed arms keep their current handling), re-invoke the SAME structured adapter with the validation error appended as a repair-hint message (the model sees what constraint it violated), bounded by cfg.max_retries; after exhaustion raise the existing ExecutionError with attempts count in the message. Constrained decode stays engaged on retries (that is the point — keep structured guarantees on well-behaved providers, repair on weak ones). Zero behavior change for Parsed-on-first-try and for json_mode/text.

TESTS: fake emitting invalid-then-valid structured results (StructuredFakeWithRaw sequence or a Failed-then-Parsed adapter fake) — assert exactly one re-prompt, repair hint present in the retry messages, max_retries honored (exhaustion -> ExecutionError), sync+async cells for BOTH sites (think primary + agent fallback), first-try-Parsed makes zero extra calls. Consumer scenario pin: an agent node with output_strategy=structured surviving a single weak decode.

WAVE PLACEMENT: Wave 9 FOURTH SEAT — region (_llm.py/_llm_dispatch.py/_llm_retry.py/compat + tests/modes) is disjoint from 12dc (errors.py/di.py), hhlr (_run_cache/runner), fdyy (_dispatch.py carrier/guards). Gated on y5ux and blocks m0tv (reformat stays last).
close_reason: Already shipped as 'structured retry parity' (commit 8722666) — _call_structured now re-prompts on Failed(ValidationError) bounded by max_retries. Verified in the installed editable neograph; the ox-demo agent nodes reverted to structured to use it. Duplicate of shipped work.

title: (EPIC) neograph-owned MCP session + mcp_servers= typed config (two-lifetime factory)
description:
Prerequisite foundation for w74k.3.1 (per-run MCP token-provider auth). Discovered 2026-07-04: the token-provider hook config['configurable']['mcp_auth'][server] has nothing to attach to because neograph does NOT own the MCP session lifecycle. Current MCP support (Phase 3 re-scoped) only accepts user-created BaseTools in tools=, with the session captured inside the tool closure. To stamp/re-mint per-call bearer tokens neograph must OWN session creation.

Scope: mcp_servers= typed config (transport: HTTP->bearer, stdio->env); a session factory obeying the TWO-LIFETIME rule (provider/factory across checkpoints; live session CACHED per (process,loop) within a run, invalidated/re-created on resume, disposed at run-end and on cancellation). Discovery decoupled from live session; static headers= as the simple default. See design docs/design/async-streaming-mcp-hitl-2026-07-02.md 6.3 (epic w74k.3) and 6.3.1 (the auth FR that depends on this).

This is the piece explicitly re-scoped OUT of Phase 3 (see neograph-w74k.3 NOTES: 'Re-scoped barrier-removal + ergonomics deliverables COMPLETE'). Filing so w74k.3.1 has a real blocker instead of silently assuming a non-existent foundation.
notes:
2026-07-05 ADVERSARIAL ARCHITECT REVIEW — VERDICT (c): KILL THIS EPIC. Full primary-sourced writeup: docs/design/mcp-session-ownership-review-2026-07-05.md (pinned to langchain-mcp-adapters 0.3.0 wheel source + mcp SDK 1.28.1).

The premise is false on two independent counts: (1) there is NO long-lived MCP session for neograph to own — adapter get_tools() without an explicit client.session() opens a FRESH session per tool call (stateless mode; client.py L170 docstring verbatim: a new session will be created for each tool call); the adapter owns open+dispose per call, so nmb2's disposal-on-cancellation solves a problem the adapter does not create. (2) The typed mcp_servers= config already exists as the adapter's Connection TypedDict union, and the per-run auth hook attaches NATIVELY via Connection.auth: httpx.Auth whose auth_flow runs PER REQUEST — the exact mint-fresh-audience-bound-token-per-call cadence of w74k.3.1; the SDK ships OAuthClientProvider / ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider / PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider for on-behalf-of. Version trap recorded: in mcp 1.28.x transport-level headers=/auth= are DEPRECATED AND IGNORED — auth belongs on the httpx.AsyncClient; adapter 0.3.0 already uses the non-deprecated path.

THE SYNC-FACTORY WALL IS ONE UN-TWINNED LINE, not a missing foundation: _tool_loop.py ~L275 factory(config, tool_spec.config) in shared prep is the only sync-only site; the agent-cycle bodies are already dual-path. An async factory awaited on the arun() path (fail-loud on run(), khff pattern) dissolves the nothing-to-attach-to claim with zero new config surface. BONUS finding: the across-checkpoint half of the two-lifetime rule is ALREADY satisfied — factories are re-invoked every superstep reading config fresh (no caching), so resume-in-fresh-process re-mints automatically; owned-session's only real win is within-run latency, which is the adapter's opt-in persistent mode, reachable by consumers, not neograph's to build.

What the author got right: the blocker was real (sync factory cannot await an async broker); two-lifetime was the right lens; static headers as default. What was missed: the foundation lives in the ecosystem; the blocker is a 1-line H2 twin gap; per-superstep re-instantiation already gives resume re-mint.

CONSEQUENCE: epic closed as wontfix-superseded; w74k.3.1 re-scoped to async-factory twinning + ecosystem-native auth (see its notes).
2026-07-05 addendum (research corroboration, versions pinned to adapter 0.3.0 / mcp 1.28.1): all findings confirmed against actual wheel/SDK source. STRENGTHENING nuance: mcp 1.28.x DEPRECATED transport-level auth=/headers= mid-1.x (moved to httpx.AsyncClient; transport runtime-warns and IGNORES them) — the auth plumbing is actively churning between SDK versions, which is exactly the layer an owned-session nmb2 would have inherited maintenance for. Adapter 0.3.0 absorbs the churn; Connection.auth works end-to-end for consumers. Minor correction: machine-to-machine providers live in mcp/client/auth/extensions/client_credentials.py (top-level export is OAuthClientProvider only); all are httpx.Auth — on-behalf-of claim holds. Verdict and w74k.3.1 re-scope unchanged. Review doc updated in place.
close_reason: Killed by adversarial architect review (docs/design/mcp-session-ownership-review-2026-07-05.md): reinvents langchain-mcp-adapters. No long-lived session exists to own (stateless per-call mode); typed config + per-request httpx.Auth hook already ship in the ecosystem. w74k.3.1 re-scoped to the 1-line-class fix: async tool factories on arun().

title: arun() over a sub-construct runs the child graph synchronously (no async twin in _subconstruct.py)
description:
Phase-1 twinning gap found by the three-layer audit (docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md section 2.5.1). _subconstruct.py has exactly one sync subgraph_node calling sub_graph.invoke() at _subconstruct.py:117; no ainvoke/afunc twin exists anywhere in the module. Consequence: arun() over any pipeline containing a sub-construct executes the child synchronously inside the async driver — blocks the event loop, and any async-only leaf inside the child (MCP tool, LLM ainvoke) is silently downgraded to the sync path.
