title: Phase 1f: observability-across-await E2E + perf gate + M1 concurrency/watchdog/cancellation
description: Research plan step 6 (a+c) + the M1 non-parity trio. (6a) Observability survives await: the async twins MUST pass the SAME config into every .ainvoke(messages, config=config); assert a Langfuse-style span/callback propagates across the await boundary (contextvar tracers propagate across await natively). (6c) Perf gate: async path adds no per-call overhead beyond threshold vs sync; note the within-run MCP session-reuse dimension (§5/H1) is a forward-reference to Phase 3, only partially testable here. M1 trio (Phase-0 primitives): real-concurrency (N runs, one loop, GatedAsyncFake), event-loop-lag watchdog (catches a silent blocking twin — the ONLY guard for the H2 silent-failure mode), cancellation E2E. Depends on Phase 1d.
design:
## Core Invariant
The async driver (arun/graph.ainvoke) must preserve BEHAVIORAL and OBSERVABILITY parity with the sync driver over one shared pure core — every awaited network hop threads the SAME RunnableConfig (so callbacks/tracers survive the await), runs cooperatively on the event loop (never blocking it), and tears down cleanly on cancellation — WITHOUT the async path adding per-call overhead beyond a generous bound.

## Implementation Plan
(Mostly TESTS. One conditional SOURCE FIX only if an E2E finds a dropped-config hop — code review says the LLM/think/agent vertical is already threaded, so expect zero LLM source fixes.)

1. [TEST] Observability-survives-await E2E (M6a): new tests/test_async_observability.py. Hand-rolled BaseCallbackHandler (langchain_core.callbacks.base, NO langfuse) recording on_chain_start (fake-independent, LangGraph-emitted per node). Run a scripted+think pipeline via run() and via asyncio.run(arun()) with config={"callbacks":[h],"configurable":{...}}; assert the same node-level events fired on both. Reuse tests/test_async_llm_tool.py:272 _ConfigCapturingFake as the low-level LLM-hop assertion (config marker reaches .ainvoke) if an LLM-level span is wanted. If any hop drops config -> that hop is the SOURCE FIX (thread config through); none expected.

2. [TEST] Perf gate: build a K-node (K~=20) chained scripted pipeline; warm up; median-of-M (M>=5) of run() vs single asyncio.run(arun()); assert per-node delta (arun_median-run_median)/K < generous absolute bound AND arun_median < max(run_median*5, run_median+0.100s). Comment the rationale + the flag: within-run MCP session reuse (H1/§5) is Phase 3, NOT covered here.

3. [TEST] M1-a real-concurrency: N graphs, each its own GatedAsyncFake think node; tasks=[create_task(arun(graph_i,...))]; poll until all enter_count==1 (interleave, all parked, none done); release all; gather; assert each returns its OWN result (isolation). Copy tests/test_async_llm_tool.py:146 + tests/test_async_harness.py:66.

4. [TEST] M1-b event-loop-lag watchdog: async with event_loop_lag_watchdog(interval_s=0.01) around arun of a blocking node (time.sleep inside an ASYNC-def body so it stays on the loop thread, avoiding LangGraphs threadpool-masking of truly-sync nodes) -> assert handle.max_lag > threshold; cooperative twin (await asyncio.sleep) -> assert max_lag < 0.5. This is the ONLY guard for the H2 silently-blocking-twin failure mode.

5. [TEST] M1-c cancellation E2E: task=create_task(arun(graph, input=..., config=file_backed_AsyncSqliteSaver thread)); poll until fake.enter_count==1 (parked); task.cancel(); with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError): await asyncio.wait_for(task, timeout=2); then assert clean teardown — re-arun the same thread_id resumes/completes cleanly (proves saver connection released + checkpoint consistent). Use AsyncSqliteSaver per the bead DECISION (not InMemorySaver).

6. [DOC] In each test module docstring, mark TEST vs (contingent) SOURCE-FIX and flag the two partial-coverage boundaries: MCP session-reuse (Phase 3) and tool-invocation config (symmetric pre-existing gap, out of 1f scope — file a follow-up bead rather than band-aid).

Three-surface note: these are DRIVER/runtime E2Es (not IR-level shape changes), so the 6-cell three-surface matrix does not apply; @node think/scripted nodes suffice. State this explicitly in the docstrings.
notes:
## DECISION (user): checkpoint/persistence assertions here also use real file-backed Sqlite savers (not InMemorySaver). See w74k.2.5.
## Findings

### config/callbacks flow end-to-end (M6a) — ALREADY THREADED, no LLM source fix
- LangChain/LangGraph callbacks propagate via RunnableConfig: caller passes config={"callbacks":[handler]} (or config["configurable"]) to arun; LangGraph ainvoke fans that config into each node run; neograph must re-thread the SAME config into every llm.ainvoke(messages, config=config). Contextvar tracers (Langfuse @observe / langchain run tree) propagate across await natively — asyncio copies the contextvars.Context into each Task, so the parent span is visible after the await WITHOUT explicit passing. The load-bearing requirement is only that neograph does not DROP config on the hop (explicit callbacks path).
- Verified threaded end-to-end on the async LLM vertical:
  - runner.arun -> graph.ainvoke(input, config=config) (runner.py:478/489/495)
  - factory ThinkDispatch.aexecute -> _llm.ainvoke_structured(..., config=config)
  - _llm.ainvoke_structured -> _acall_structured(llm, messages, ..., config, ...) (_llm.py:261)
  - _acall_structured threads config into EVERY awaited hop (_llm_dispatch.py:139/145/161/163/184): adapter.ainvoke(...,config), arecover_dsml(...,config), llm.ainvoke(messages,config=config), _ainvoke_json_with_retry(...,config)
  - compat adapter ainvoke hops all pass config=config (_llm_structured_compat.py:126/156/161/202)
  - _llm_retry async hops all pass config=config (_llm_retry.py:388/407/453/462)
  - agent/tool path: ainvoke_with_tools threads config into llm_with_tools.ainvoke(messages,config=config) (_tool_loop.py:637) and into _acall_structured finalize (_tool_loop.py:759/773/779)
- Cell 5 of the 1c harness ALREADY proves think-hop config threading: tests/test_async_llm_tool.py:272 TestAsyncThinkConfigThreading with _ConfigCapturingFake (captures k.get("config") in ainvoke) asserts config["configurable"]["_async_marker"] survives to the .ainvoke hop. The 1f E2E is the higher-level twin: attach a real BaseCallbackHandler via config["callbacks"] and assert on_llm_start/on_chain_start fired under arun the same as under run.

### Observability wiring that exists
- examples/observable_pipeline.py is the ONLY integration exemplar: from langfuse.langchain import CallbackHandler; passes config={"callbacks":[langfuse_handler]} into run() (lines 110/117-120). Docs: website/src/content/docs/concepts/observability.mdx.
- There is NO in-code Langfuse coupling to test — it is generic LangChain callbacks via config. The 1f E2E should use a hand-rolled BaseCallbackHandler (langchain_core.callbacks) that records on_llm_start / on_chain_start, NOT langfuse (langfuse is not a hard dep; test_guards_examples.py:596 treats it as optional). This keeps the E2E dependency-free.

### How to attach + observe a callback in a test
- Subclass langchain_core.callbacks.base.BaseCallbackHandler, record event names into a list in on_llm_start/on_chat_model_start/on_chain_start. Pass config={"callbacks":[h], "configurable":{...}}. Run once via run() and once via asyncio.run(arun(...)); assert the same events fired on both. Use a real ChatModel fake that routes through with_structured_output — StructuredFake already provides sync invoke + async ainvoke, but callbacks only fire if the fake is a real BaseChatModel OR if we assert at the on_chain level (LangGraph fires on_chain_start per node regardless of the LLM fake). SIMPLEST robust assertion: on_chain_start / node-level events fire under arun == under run (LangGraph-level, independent of LLM fake internals). For on_llm_start specifically we would need a langchain BaseChatModel-derived fake; the shared fakes are duck types, so prefer the chain-level callback assertion for non-flakiness (flag this).

### Concurrency / GatedAsyncFake wiring (M1 trio)
- GatedAsyncFake (tests/fakes.py:624): async-native, ainvoke increments enter_count, sets _entered, awaits _gate; with_structured_output returns self and stores _model; release() sets gate; wait_entered() awaits first entry. bind_tools/abind_tools return self (agent path works too).
- Drive it through a think node exactly as tests/test_async_llm_tool.py:146 TestThinkSeamAwaitFiresOnLoop does: compile(construct_from_functions("p",[gen]), **build_test_compile_kwargs(), **build_fake_llm_kwargs(lambda tier: fake)) with @node(mode="think", model=, prompt=).
- N concurrent arun on ONE loop: async def test; build N graphs (or N threads on one graph with distinct thread_ids); fakes each a GatedAsyncFake; tasks=[asyncio.create_task(neograph.arun(graph_i, input={...})) for i]; poll until all enter_count==1 (all parked => interleave), assert none done; release all; await asyncio.gather(*tasks); assert each result is its OWN value (isolation). Exemplar for the gather+park+release loop: tests/test_async_harness.py:66. NOTE: build_fake_llm_kwargs takes a per-tier factory closure — give each graph its own GatedAsyncFake instance so enter_count/results are isolated.
- event-loop-lag watchdog E2E: event_loop_lag_watchdog (tests/fakes.py:686, .max_lag). Blocking node = @node scripted body doing time.sleep(0.15); wrap arun in async with event_loop_lag_watchdog(interval_s=0.01) as h; assert h.max_lag > threshold. Cooperative twin = async @node body await asyncio.sleep; assert h.max_lag < 0.5. Exemplar: tests/test_async_harness.py:88-108 already proves the watchdog primitive itself; 1f wires it around a REAL arun. CAVEAT: a truly-sync scripted body is threadpooled by LangGraph under ainvoke (masks the block) — to trip the watchdog the blocking body must run INLINE on the loop. Phase 1a wired scripted afunc to run inline (test_async_dual_path.py thread-identity assertion). Confirm the block lands on the loop thread; if LangGraph threadpools it, the watchdog E2E needs an async-def body that blocks (time.sleep inside async def) so it stays on the loop.
- cancellation E2E: task=asyncio.create_task(neograph.arun(graph, input=...)); await park (poll fake.enter_count==1); task.cancel(); assert with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError): await task; assert no hang (wrap await in asyncio.wait_for). Confirm resources released (checkpointer connection closed) — use a file-backed AsyncSqliteSaver per user DECISION and assert the run can be re-arun-ed / the saver still usable after cancellation.

### Perf gate — non-flaky formulation
- asyncio.run creates+tears a loop PER call: that is fixed per-RUN, not per-NODE. To isolate PER-CALL (per-node) overhead, amortize loop setup across many nodes: build a K-node chained scripted pipeline (e.g. K=20), measure median run() time and median single asyncio.run(arun()) time over M repeats (warm up first). Gate on per-node delta: (arun_median - run_median)/K < generous absolute bound (e.g. 20ms/node) OR arun_median < max(run_median*5, run_median+0.100s). Absolute floor prevents ratio flakiness when sync is trivially fast; the ratio catches pathological regressions (accidental per-node loop creation). Use time.perf_counter, median-of-M (M>=5), no wall-clock in CI-parallel asserts beyond the generous bound.
- PARTIAL COVERAGE (flag): within-run MCP session reuse (H1/§5) is Phase 3 — the 1f gate can only assert the async node/LLM vertical adds no per-call overhead. Document that the gate does NOT cover MCP session-reuse amortization.

### Recency / current-way
- The 1c/1d harnesses (test_async_llm_tool.py, test_async_runner.py) are the NEWEST exemplars (commits 877f196, 946da8e). Copy their compile/drive patterns. Drive at neograph.arun now (exists post-1d) rather than graph.graph.ainvoke (that was only because arun did not exist in 1a-1c).
## Risks & Edge Cases
- PERF-GATE FLAKINESS (highest): ratio-only gates flake when sync run is sub-ms; MUST include an absolute floor and use median-of-M with a warmup. Keep bounds generous (documented rationale). Prefer per-node-amortized delta over per-run comparison (asyncio.run loop setup is a fixed per-run cost that would otherwise dominate and falsely inflate "async overhead").
- WATCHDOG vs THREADPOOL: LangGraph threadpools a TRULY-SYNC node under ainvoke, which MASKS a blocking body (the watchdog would NOT trip). To trip it deterministically, the blocking body must run inline on the loop thread — use an async-def scripted body that calls time.sleep (stays on the loop) OR confirm via thread-identity (test_async_dual_path.py pattern) that the sync scripted afunc runs inline post-1a. Pick whichever is deterministic; a sync body that gets threadpooled is a false-green.
- CALLBACK FIRING DEPTH: on_llm_start only fires if the LLM is a real langchain BaseChatModel; the shared duck-typed fakes (StructuredFake) do NOT emit LLM callbacks. Assert at the CHAIN level (on_chain_start per node, emitted by LangGraph itself) for a fake-independent, non-flaky observability-survives-await E2E; reserve on_llm_start for a real-model manual/opt-in check. Do NOT couple the E2E to langfuse (optional dep).
- GatedAsyncFake think-path depth: with_structured_output returns self and stores _model; ainvoke returns _respond(_model) as a BARE model (not include_raw tuple). Confirm the think seam accepts a bare-model return from with_structured_output().ainvoke (StructuredFake mirrors this — cell 1/3 of 1c already pass, so the path is proven). For AGENT mode the gate parks on llm_with_tools.ainvoke; bind_tools returns self so it works, but the ReAct finalize turn also calls the gate — a single-gate fake parks on the FIRST hop, which is enough for concurrency/cancellation.
- CANCELLATION LEAVING A SAVER OPEN: a mid-flight cancel of a task holding an AsyncSqliteSaver connection may leave the connection/file lock open. Assert post-cancel the saver is reusable (re-arun the same thread_id resumes cleanly) — that both proves clean teardown AND checkpoint consistency. Use file-backed AsyncSqliteSaver (user DECISION on this bead: not InMemorySaver for persistence assertions).
- CONFIG-CARRIES-CALLBACKS-THROUGH-ARUN: confirmed at code level (runner.arun passes config straight to graph.ainvoke; LangGraph owns callback fan-out). The only neograph responsibility is not dropping config on the LLM hop — verified threaded. No source fix expected on the LLM/think/agent vertical.
- TOOL-INVOCATION CONFIG GAP (parity-consistent, NOT a 1f fix): both sync (_tool_loop.py:462) and async (_tool_loop.py:691) call tool_fn.[a]invoke(tool_call["args"]) WITHOUT config, so on_tool_start callbacks fire on NEITHER path. Because it is symmetric, it is NOT an async regression and NOT in 1f scope — flag as a pre-existing observability gap (file a follow-up bead if tool spans are wanted), do not band-aid it into 1f.
- N-concurrent isolation: give each concurrent arun its OWN GatedAsyncFake + its own compiled graph (or distinct thread_ids) so enter_count and results do not cross-contaminate; a single shared fake would conflate enter_count across runs (though shared-fake enter_count==N is a valid interleave proof, per-run isolation needs distinct result payloads).

## Relevant Code (exemplars to copy)
- tests/test_async_llm_tool.py:146 TestThinkSeamAwaitFiresOnLoop — GatedAsyncFake + think node + park-before-release. COPY for concurrency/cancellation.
- tests/test_async_llm_tool.py:272 TestAsyncThinkConfigThreading + _ConfigCapturingFake — config-threading proof; the low-level twin of the 1f observability E2E.
- tests/test_async_harness.py:66 (gather+park+release) and :88 (watchdog around a block) — the primitive-level patterns 1f lifts to real arun.
- tests/test_async_runner.py:114 TestArunCheckpointResume — arun + checkpointer resume shape (extend to AsyncSqliteSaver + cancel).
- examples/observable_pipeline.py:110-120 — the config={"callbacks":[handler]} attach pattern.
- src/neograph/runner.py:461 arun — config passed straight to graph.ainvoke (no drop).
- src/neograph/_llm_dispatch.py:121 _acall_structured — config threaded into every awaited hop.
- src/neograph/factory.py ThinkDispatch.aexecute / ToolDispatch.aexecute — where async LLM/tool twins are dispatched (already await the config-threaded twins post-1c).
## Codebase Disease Scan (mybm.3)
Pattern: async .ainvoke hops that DROP config the sync path threads (would break observability across await — M6a).
Scan: grep async .ainvoke in the LLM/tool vertical; compare config threading vs sync.

Result: NO async-only config drop. All LLM async hops thread config:
- _llm_structured_compat.py:156/:202, _llm_dispatch.py:139 -> config passed positionally (adapter sig (llm,model,messages,config)).
- _tool_loop.py:112 _CoercingToolWrapper.ainvoke -> config rides in **kwargs (forwarded).
- runner.arun -> graph.ainvoke(config=config); _llm.ainvoke_structured/_acall_structured thread config end-to-end.
=> M6a observability parity holds in SOURCE; 1f needs no LLM source fix (confirms research).

ALLOWLIST/DEFER: tool_fn invocation omits config SYMMETRICALLY (sync :462 + async :691 both) -> pre-existing, NOT an async regression -> filed neograph-ddb3 (thread config into tool invocations, both surfaces). Out of 1f scope (1f requires async==sync observability parity, which holds).
1f is tests-only (no source MIGRATE). Structural dual-path guard is 1g.
## Architect Review (mybm.4 — dp-reviewer, independent)

Gate hard-check PASS: research:complete + codebase-scan:complete both present. Source claims spot-verified against actual code (runner.arun runner.py:466-495, ScriptedDispatch.aexecute _dispatch.py:127-142 calls self.fn inline + awaits, factory.py:84 RunnableLambda(node_wrapper, afunc=anode_wrapper), GatedAsyncFake fakes.py:673-687, test_async_dual_path.py inline-on-loop assertion, test_async_llm_tool.py:272 _ConfigCapturingFake, test_checkpoint_sqlite_async.py:112 AsyncSqliteSaver pattern).

- [MEDIUM] PERF GATE (the #1 risk) — the plan is internally inconsistent and the arun side is under-sampled. DESIGN step 2 says '...AND arun_median < max(run_median*5, run_median+0.100s)'; RESEARCH says the same clause with 'OR'. AND is the FLAKIER choice (test reds if EITHER sub-condition trips); the ratio*5 term flakes when a trivial scripted pipeline runs sub-ms, and the +0.1s is a per-RUN loop-setup floor that conflates exactly the overhead you claim to have amortized away. Worse, 'single asyncio.run(arun())' takes ONE unmedianed arun sample vs median-of-M for run() — a single sample has no outlier rejection on a loaded box. CONCRETE VERDICT on the assertion: measure BOTH sides as median-of-M (M>=7, after warmup) INSIDE ONE asyncio.run() that awaits arun M times in a loop (this amortizes loop-setup to ~0 AND gives outlier rejection), use NO checkpointer (or InMemory) so per-node sqlite I/O does not inflate variance, and assert a SINGLE generous absolute per-node ceiling: (async_med-sync_med)/K < ~0.020 (20ms/node). Drop the ratio/max() term entirely; if a gross-regression catch is wanted add it as an OR escape, never AND. Strongly consider marking it @pytest.mark.perf (non-blocking / xfail-soft) — a flaky perf gate that randomly reds CI is worse than none. Suggestion: adopt the median-both-sides-in-one-loop + single-absolute-ceiling formulation.

- [MEDIUM] OBSERVABILITY-SURVIVES-AWAIT TEST VALIDITY — on_chain_start parity does NOT prove the claim the test is named for. LangGraph emits on_chain_start per node from its OWN config fan-out under both invoke and ainvoke; that is a LangGraph guarantee, independent of whether neograph re-threads config into llm.ainvoke. The actual await-boundary claim (neograph does not drop config across ITS LLM await hop) is ALREADY proven at the config-dict level by _ConfigCapturingFake (test_async_llm_tool.py:272, cell 5). So the new on_chain_start test is largely redundant/mis-named — it re-proves LangGraph's behavior, not neograph's. To be genuinely additive it should assert an LLM-LEVEL callback (on_llm_start/on_chat_model_start) firing under arun == under run, which requires a callback-emitting structured fake (a BaseChatModel-derived fake that implements with_structured_output; langchain_core is already a hard dep, so no new dependency — but real friction wiring it through the structured think seam). Acceptable alternative: keep the chain-level E2E but explicitly SCOPE its docstring claim to 'config[callbacks] is not dropped through arun's node fan-out' and cite cell 5 as the LLM-hop proof, documenting that a true on_llm_start span check needs a real model and is a deferred manual/opt-in check. Either is fine; do NOT ship a test whose name ('observability survives await') overpromises what on_chain_start actually demonstrates. Suggestion: pick LLM-level assertion OR re-scope the claim — implementer-resolvable.

- [LOW] WATCHDOG RATIONALE contradicts the cited dual-path guarantee. The plan/research says 'time.sleep inside an ASYNC-def body ... avoiding LangGraph's threadpool-masking of truly-sync nodes'. But test_async_dual_path.py (same research's exemplar) asserts post-1a @node scripted bodies run INLINE on the loop thread (node_tid==loop_tid) via factory.py:84 afunc=anode_wrapper -> _aexecute_node -> ScriptedDispatch.aexecute calls self.fn INLINE. So a PLAIN SYNC time.sleep(0.15) body also blocks the loop and trips the watchdog — the 'threadpool-masking' concern is moot for @node scripted post-1a. The async-def choice still works (also runs on the loop), so the TEST is sound; only the stated rationale is wrong and could mislead a future reader into 'fixing' it back to a threadpool assumption. Suggestion: correct the docstring rationale (both sync-inline and async-def bodies block the loop post-1a; async-def is chosen for explicitness, not to dodge threadpooling).

- [LOW] CANCELLATION RESUME LEG has an unstated hang trap. The 're-arun same thread_id completes cleanly' assertion requires the gate be RELEASED (or the resume leg use a fresh non-gated fake) — re-running with the still-gated GatedAsyncFake would re-park and hang the resume (only masked by the wait_for timeout as a FAILURE). Also make explicit that the AsyncSqliteSaver's async-with is owned by the TEST scope (not the cancelled task) so cancel does not tear down the connection (matches test_checkpoint_sqlite_async.py:112). Saver-consistency reasoning is otherwise SOUND: parked at the LLM gate = between superstep checkpoints, so no partial write / no held write-lock, and re-arun resumes from the last consistent checkpoint. Suggestion: state the gate-release step and saver-ownership in the plan.

- [LOW / AFFIRM] Deferring the tool-invocation config gap (neograph-ddb3) is CORRECT and 1f's observability claim does NOT require tool spans. The omission is SYMMETRIC (sync _tool_loop.py:462 + async :691 both drop config), so the parity invariant holds — it is not an async regression. 1f correctly scopes to scripted+think, and its chain-level assertion fires for tool nodes too, so tool-span coverage is genuinely orthogonal. No change.

VALIDATED (no finding): concurrency test is sound — GatedAsyncFake.ainvoke (fakes.py:673) parks on 'await self._gate.wait()' BEFORE computing/returning the structured response, so no run can complete before release; cell 3 (test_async_llm_tool.py:146) already proves the think seam parks; per-graph fake isolation is correctly flagged in research (each concurrent arun needs its OWN GatedAsyncFake). No deadlock as long as the poll loop yields (await wait_entered/sleep(0), per test_async_harness.py:66).

Overall: NEEDS_REFINEMENT
## Triage (mybm.5): NEEDS_REFINEMENT -> refine neograph-mybm.12 (perf-gate median-both-sides-in-one-loop + single absolute ceiling + non-blocking; observability test re-scoped/LLM-level; watchdog rationale corrected; cancellation gate-release + saver ownership). write-test mybm.6 depends on it.
## Refinement applied (mybm.12) — amends design plan
STEP 2 (perf) REPLACED: median-of-M (M>=7, post-warmup) for BOTH run() and arun() measured INSIDE ONE asyncio.run() looping M arun awaits (amortizes loop-setup, outlier rejection); no checkpointer/InMemory; assert single absolute per-node ceiling (async_med-sync_med)/K < 0.020 s; drop ratio/max (OR-escape only if wanted, never AND); mark @pytest.mark.perf / non-blocking.
STEP 1 (observability) RE-SCOPED: keep chain-level on_chain_start run==arun E2E but docstring-scope the claim to 'config[callbacks] not dropped through arun node fan-out' and CITE _ConfigCapturingFake (test_async_llm_tool.py:272 cell 5) as the LLM-hop proof; note true on_llm_start span check needs a real model (deferred). [Optionally do the LLM-level assertion instead.]
STEP 4 (watchdog) RATIONALE CORRECTED: post-1a both sync-inline and async-def bodies run on the loop; async-def chosen for explicitness not to dodge threadpool.
STEP 5 (cancellation) RESUME leg: release the gate OR use a fresh non-gated fake for the resume (else it re-parks/hangs); AsyncSqliteSaver async-with owned by TEST scope so cancel doesn't tear the connection.
Core Invariant unchanged.
## Regression Tests (mybm.6 — dp-test-author, Phase 1f CHARACTERIZATION)
Three test files added; all 6 tests PASS (characterization locks working async behavior). Stable across 3 back-to-back runs (~0.65s). Refinement corrections (mybm.12) applied verbatim.

### Files + behavior pinned
- tests/test_async_observability.py::test_node_level_callbacks_fire_the_same_under_run_and_arun — PASS. Hand-rolled BaseCallbackHandler (langchain_core.callbacks.base) recording on_chain_start; scripted(fetch)+think(gen, StructuredFake) pipeline run via run() and asyncio.run(arun()) with config={callbacks:[h],configurable:{}}. Asserts {fetch,gen} node-level events fired on BOTH. Docstring SCOPES the claim to 'config[callbacks] not dropped through arun node fan-out' and CITES _ConfigCapturingFake (test_async_llm_tool.py:272 cell 5) as the LLM-hop proof (on_chain_start alone does NOT prove LLM-await observability — LangGraph emits it per node regardless).

title: Phase 1g: structural guards locking the dual-path invariant
description: Research plan step 7. Guard: 'every LLM mode exposes BOTH a sync AND an async dispatch path' (no sync-only mode) — the structural counter to the H2 silent-failure hazard. Guard: async twins live in the SAME module as their sync counterpart (no async-only module importing decorators.py — respects layer-discipline guards test_guards_sidecar_imports / assembly import DAG). AST-based, positive+negative meta-tests. Depends on Phase 1a, 1c, 1d.
design:
## Core Invariant
Every LLM-mode dispatch class exposes BOTH a sync `execute` AND an async `aexecute` (with `aexecute` being `async def`), and every async twin is defined in the SAME module as its sync counterpart — so no PR can silently reintroduce a sync-only execution path (the H2 silent-failure mode).

## Implementation Plan
1. NEW FILE `tests/test_guards_async_dispatch.py`, pure-AST (zero `re` → auto-exempt from the regex-slip meta-guard), mirroring tests/test_guards_async_fakes.py structure (module-level `ast.parse` of the target source, a small collector, per-class asserts, a not-vacuous slip meta-test).

2. GUARD A — dual-path dispatch completeness.
   - Detector: parse src/neograph/_dispatch.py; a "dispatch class" = any top-level ClassDef whose body defines a method named `execute`. This enrolls ModeDispatch (Protocol) + ScriptedDispatch + ThinkDispatch + ToolDispatch and excludes NodeInput/NodeOutput. Do NOT key on the `*Dispatch` suffix.
   - Assertion: every dispatch class also defines `aexecute`, AND its `aexecute` node is `ast.AsyncFunctionDef` (blocks a sync stub), AND `execute` is a plain `def` (`ast.FunctionDef`).
   - Sanity assert: the detected dispatch-class set on today's source == {ModeDispatch, ScriptedDispatch, ThinkDispatch, ToolDispatch} (catches detector drift / a future non-dispatch class sprouting an execute).
   - Meta-tests (mandatory, mirror test_delegation_detector_is_not_vacuous):
       * POSITIVE: synthetic `class X: def execute(...); async def aexecute(...)` → detector treats X as a dispatch and passes.
       * NEGATIVE 1: synthetic `class X: def execute(...)` (no aexecute) → flagged.
       * NEGATIVE 2: synthetic `class X: def execute(...); def aexecute(...)` (sync aexecute) → flagged.
       * EXCLUSION: synthetic class with only a `value` property → NOT a dispatch (not flagged).

3. GUARD B — async-twin co-location, scoped to the gap ONLY.
   - Delegate the 4 LLM-vertical twins to test_guards_llm_runtime.py ALLOWED_NAMES (document this in the docstring; do NOT re-assert them).
   - Assert same-module co-location for the twins NOT covered by ALLOWED_NAMES, as a `{module: [(sync, async), ...]}` table:
       _execute.py: (_execute_node, _aexecute_node)
       _tool_loop.py: (invoke_with_tools, ainvoke_with_tools)
       runner.py: (run, arun), (_has_existing_checkpoint, _ahas_existing_checkpoint), (_verify_checkpoint_schema, _averify_checkpoint_schema), (_auto_resume_from_divergence, _aauto_resume_from_divergence)
       factory.py: (_make_raw_wrapper, _make_araw_wrapper)
     For each pair: both names are top-level defs in that module's AST (async one is AsyncFunctionDef). A twin migrating to an async-only module fails this.
   - Meta-tests: POSITIVE (both defs present in one synthetic module → passes); NEGATIVE (async twin missing / moved to a second synthetic module → flagged).
   - Do NOT add a new decorators-import-DAG guard: no async-only module exists (Phase 1a-1f co-located every twin), so there is nothing to police; the existing sidecar/import guards remain sufficient. Note this decision in the file docstring.

4. Run `pytest tests/test_guards_async_dispatch.py -q` (expect all green — this is a lock over already-correct 1a-1f code, not a red TDD test). Also run tests/test_guards_meta.py to confirm the new file trips no regex-slip / near-duplicate discipline.
notes:
## Findings (Phase 1g research — neograph-46vu.2)

### State after 1a-1f (verified)
- src/neograph/_dispatch.py: ModeDispatch Protocol (lines 80-102) declares BOTH `execute` (sync, l.88) and `aexecute` (`async def`, l.96). All 3 concrete dispatch classes define both:
  - ScriptedDispatch: execute l.116, aexecute l.127 (isawaitable-at-call-boundary async)
  - ThinkDispatch: execute l.156, aexecute l.186 (awaits _llm.ainvoke_structured)
  - ToolDispatch: execute l.265, aexecute l.276 (awaits _tool_loop.ainvoke_with_tools)
  Dual-path invariant currently HOLDS; guard should be TDD-green on write (this is a lock, not a red test — unlike Phase 0's test_guards_async_fakes which shipped red).

### GUARD A detection rule (robust, NOT name-based)
A "dispatch class" = any top-level ClassDef in _dispatch.py whose body defines a method named `execute`. This catches the ModeDispatch Protocol AND the 3 concrete classes, and EXCLUDES NodeInput/NodeOutput (they only have a `value` @property, no execute). Do NOT key on the `*Dispatch` suffix — a rename would silently disable the guard, and the Protocol is named `ModeDispatch` (also ends in Dispatch but is the Protocol, not a concrete class). Keying on presence-of-`execute` is the invariant of BEING a dispatch: a future 4th mode class must define execute, so it is auto-enrolled; if it adds execute but forgets aexecute → guard FAILS (exactly the H2 sync-only reintroduction). Strengthen: assert aexecute is `ast.AsyncFunctionDef` (blocks a sync `def aexecute` stub) and execute is a plain `def`.

### GUARD B — redundancy analysis (scope precisely, do NOT duplicate)
Async twins and their modules (all co-located with sync counterpart already):
- _execute.py: _execute_node (l.55) / _aexecute_node (l.99)
- _llm.py: invoke_structured (l.128) / ainvoke_structured (l.231)
- _llm_dispatch.py: _call_structured (l.38) / _acall_structured (l.121)
- _llm_retry.py: _invoke_json_with_retry (l.272)/_ainvoke_json_with_retry (l.375); recover_dsml (l.318)/arecover_dsml (l.421)
- _tool_loop.py: invoke_with_tools (l.346) / ainvoke_with_tools (l.583)
- runner.py: run (l.305) / arun (l.461) + 3 checkpoint-helper twins (_ahas_existing_checkpoint/_averify_checkpoint_schema/_aauto_resume_from_divergence)
- factory.py: _make_raw_wrapper / _make_araw_wrapper

ALREADY covered by test_guards_llm_runtime.py `TestLlmResponsibilityDiscipline.ALLOWED_NAMES` (l.173-236): this pins BOTH the sync name AND its async twin into the SAME module's frozenset for the 4 LLM-vertical modules — _llm.py, _llm_dispatch.py, _llm_retry.py (and _llm_structured_compat.py's _classify_lc_result/_reclassify_dsml). For those 4 modules, "async twin lives in the same module as sync counterpart" is FULLY REDUNDANT — the name-set guard already fails if the twin moves. => GUARD B must NOT re-assert these.

NOT covered by ALLOWED_NAMES (the real gap GUARD B fills): _tool_loop.py (ainvoke_with_tools), _execute.py (_aexecute_node), runner.py (arun + 3 checkpoint twins), factory.py (_make_araw_wrapper). Partially related: test_guards_meta.py `TestNoNearDuplicateHelperNames.ALLOWLIST` (l.333-384) already enumerates every sync/async twin PAIR (aexecute pattern) — but it only enforces the near-duplicate NAMING convention + allowlist reason; it does NOT assert same-module co-location. So it does not subsume GUARD B either.

"no async-only module importing decorators.py" (task's layer-discipline concern): MOOT — Phase 1a-1f created ZERO async-only modules; every twin sits in its sync module. None of those modules import decorators.py. The existing `TestSidecarModule.test_construct_builder_does_not_import_from_decorators` (tests/test_guards_sidecar_imports.py l.36) is scoped to _construct_builder.py only; the assembly import-DAG guard (test_guards_assembly.py `TestAssemblyClusterImportDAG` l.305) does NOT track decorators edges at all. Recommendation: GUARD B = same-module co-location assertion for the twins NOT already pinned by ALLOWED_NAMES; skip a new decorators-import-DAG guard (no async-only module exists to police, and building a broad one is out of 1g scope).

### Convention to mirror
- tests/test_guards_async_fakes.py (Phase 0) is the exemplar: pure-AST, module-level `ast.parse` of a target source file, a `_..._methods()` collector, per-class assertion, and a `test_delegation_detector_is_not_vacuous` slip meta-test with good+bad synthetic sources.
- tests/test_guards_meta.py `TestNoNearDuplicateHelperNames.test_meta_positive_*/test_meta_negative_*` is the positive+negative meta-test naming pattern.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/_dispatch.py:80-308 — ModeDispatch Protocol + ScriptedDispatch/ThinkDispatch/ToolDispatch, each with execute + aexecute (GUARD A target).
- tests/test_guards_async_fakes.py — AST-guard + slip-meta-test convention to copy.
- tests/test_guards_llm_runtime.py:173-236 — ALLOWED_NAMES that already pins the 4 LLM-vertical twins' module membership (GUARD B redundancy source).
- tests/test_guards_meta.py:333-384 — twin-pair ALLOWLIST (naming convention, not co-location).
- tests/test_guards_sidecar_imports.py:36-51 + tests/test_guards_assembly.py:305-367 — existing import-DAG guards (do NOT cover a general decorators-import ban).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Brittle detection: keying GUARD A on `*Dispatch` suffix would break on a rename and would wrongly include the Protocol by name. MITIGATION: key on presence of an `execute` method (structural invariant).
- Over-broad flagging: NodeInput/NodeOutput are top-level classes in _dispatch.py but are NOT dispatches — the execute-presence rule excludes them (they have only `value`). Verify the guard yields exactly 4 dispatch classes {ModeDispatch, ScriptedDispatch, ThinkDispatch, ToolDispatch} on today's source, else the detector drifted.
- Vacuous pass: without the negative meta-test, an empty detector (finds 0 dispatch classes) passes silently. The slip meta-test (synthetic execute-only class must be flagged; synthetic both-methods class must pass) is mandatory — mirror test_delegation_detector_is_not_vacuous.
- GUARD B redundancy: re-asserting the 4 LLM-vertical twins duplicates ALLOWED_NAMES and creates two places to update on a rename. Scope GUARD B to the 4 non-allowlisted modules only (_tool_loop, _execute, runner, factory) and note the ALLOWED_NAMES delegation in the docstring.
- async-not-sync stub: someone could add `def aexecute` (sync) to satisfy a naive presence check while reintroducing a blocking path. GUARD A must assert aexecute is AsyncFunctionDef.

Pattern this guard LOCKS: a sync-only dispatch path (dispatch class with execute but no aexecute) — the H2 silent-failure mode.

## Architect Review (neograph-46vu.4)

Gate: research:complete + codebase-scan:complete both present — PASS. Pressure-tested against actual src/neograph/_dispatch.py, factory.py, runner.py, _execute.py, _tool_loop.py and the meta-guards.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: GUARD B's blanket assertion 'async one is AsyncFunctionDef' is FALSE for the factory.py pair. `_make_araw_wrapper` (factory.py:112) is a plain `def` wrapper-FACTORY that returns an inner `async def araw_node_wrapper` closure — its top-level AST node is ast.FunctionDef, not ast.AsyncFunctionDef. 7 of 8 GUARD-B twins are genuinely `async def` (_aexecute_node, ainvoke_with_tools, arun, the 3 runner checkpoint twins), but _make_araw_wrapper is not. Implementing the plan literally makes GUARD B RED on correct 1a-1f code (contradicts step 4 'expect all green'), and worse invites a wrong 'fix' converting _make_araw_wrapper to async (it must stay a sync factory). If any async-ness check is kept, special-case factory.py so the wrapper-factory is exempt.

- [LOW] Finding: GUARD A on the ModeDispatch Protocol is meaningful and correct. The Protocol is an ast.ClassDef; its `def execute(...): ...` is FunctionDef and `async def aexecute(...): ...` is AsyncFunctionDef (stub bodies do not change the node kind). Requiring aexecute on the Protocol itself is the right contract lock — dropping it from the Protocol would let concrete classes omit aexecute without a type error. title: Phase 1d: arun() runner + async checkpoint helpers + CompiledNeograph async delegations + export
description: Research plan step 4. Add arun() (runner.py:270) mirroring run(), reusing _inject_input_to_config/_preflight_di_check/_strip_internals verbatim; await graph.ainvoke (:314/:344/:346/:360). Async twins of _has_existing_checkpoint (:253), _verify_checkpoint_schema (:78), _auto_resume_from_divergence (:133) using aget_tuple/aget_state_history (AsyncSqliteSaver has no sync get_tuple). Add ainvoke/aget_state/aget_state_history/astream delegations to CompiledNeograph (_compiled.py:28). Export arun from neograph.__init__ (:69/:82) — this LIGHTS UP the Phase-0 conftest async run_driver cell automatically (its 1 skip flips to running). Depends on Phase 1a, 1c.
design:
## Core Invariant
arun() is a driver-parallel twin of run() over ONE shared pure core: the no-await input-prep/resume-inject logic is EXTRACTED into shared helpers both drivers call, and arun mirrors run()'s exact three-mode branch structure (resume / input+nested-checkpoint / crash-recovery), diverging ONLY where the sync API touches the graph/checkpointer — graph.invoke -> await graph.ainvoke, checkpointer.get_tuple -> await aget_tuple, graph.get_state_history -> async-for aget_state_history — so the two drivers cannot behaviorally fork.

## Implementation Plan (reuse-first; twins beside sync counterparts, same modules)

STEP 0 — extract the no-await prep into shared helpers (refactor SYNC run() first, behavior unchanged, run quality):
- Extract runner.py ~321-333 (CONFIG_INPUT stash + defensive input copy + SCHEMA/NODE fingerprint injection) into a pure helper, e.g. _prepare_new_input(graph, input, config) -> (input, config). run()'s input branch calls it.
- Extract the resume re-inject (~310-313) if it is likewise await-free into a small helper both call. Keep the extraction minimal and pure (no I/O).
- Rerun make quality after the sync refactor — no behavior change expected.

STEP 1 — arun() (runner.py, directly below run() ~:270):
- async def arun(graph, input=None, resume=None, config=None, auto_resume=True). Mirror run()'s exact three-mode branch structure, calling the STEP-0 shared helpers for prep. Diverge ONLY at: the 4 graph.invoke sites (:314/:344/:346/:360) -> await graph.ainvoke; the two _has_existing_checkpoint calls -> await _ahas_existing_checkpoint; the two _verify_checkpoint_schema calls -> await _averify_checkpoint_schema.
- LOW-2: preserve run()'s branch asymmetry EXACTLY — bare 'config' at the input-branch _has_existing_checkpoint (:342) vs 'config or {}' at crash-recovery (:358/:359). Do not normalize.

STEP 2 — async checkpoint twins (runner.py, beside sync originals):

## Core Invariant
Each sync LLM/tool orchestrator gets a THIN async twin in the SAME module: the pure preamble/render/parse/classify/budget/usage/logging bookends are EXTRACTED into shared helpers that BOTH sync and async call, so the twin adds only the awaited network seam (.invoke -> await .ainvoke, _generate -> await _agenerate) and the interleaving-await control flow — sync and async cannot drift, and config threads into every .ainvoke hop so observability survives the await.

## Implementation Plan (EXTRACT-then-THIN, bottom-up; pure refactors first, sync behavior unchanged)

STEP 0 — pure extractions (refactor SYNC path, no behavior change, run quality after each):
- _llm_structured_compat.py: extract the pure result-classification (lines ~97-108 and ~150-159) into a shared classify helper; sync invoke() calls it. Async ainvoke() will call the same.
- _llm.py invoke_structured (~151-192): extract the pure preamble (log.bind + usage_info assembly) and postamble (llm_log.info + _notify_cost) into shared helper(s) that invoke_structured calls; the awaited seam is _call_structured (~179).

design:
## Core Invariant
A scripted/raw async body is awaited by DETECTING the awaitable at the call boundary (`inspect.isawaitable(result)` AFTER invoking self.fn / raw_fn), NOT by inspecting the function object — because for @node the user body is hidden behind a synchronous shim (`scripted_shim` returns an un-awaited coroutine), so `iscoroutinefunction(self.fn)` is blind to it; one call-then-isawaitable check works identically across @node, declarative, and programmatic surfaces, so sync and async scripted paths share the exact same shim/registry/compiler machinery and cannot drift.

## Implementation Plan (reuse-first; touch ONLY _dispatch.py + factory.py)
1. ScriptedDispatch.aexecute (_dispatch.py:126-137): add `import inspect` to the module; change the body to
   `result = self.fn(input_data.value, config)` -> `if inspect.isawaitable(result): result = await result` -> `return NodeOutput(single=result)`. DELETE the `# noqa: RUF029` on line 126 (the conditional await now satisfies RUF029). Reuse the EXISTING `scripted_shim` unchanged — it already returns `fn(*args)` which is a coroutine when the sidecar body is `async def`, and returns the raw value otherwise. Do NOT add per-surface branches, do NOT thread the sidecar into ScriptedDispatch, do NOT touch _scripted_registry.py / decorators.py / compiler.py / node.py.
2. Raw async twin (factory.py): add an async raw wrapper mirroring `_make_raw_wrapper` (:86-108) — same node_start/node_complete logging + timing, but `result = raw_fn(state, config); if inspect.isawaitable(result): result = await result` (conditional await; no noqa needed). Wire it in make_node_fn raw branch (:53-54): `return RunnableLambda(_make_raw_wrapper(node), afunc=<async_twin>(node))`. `raw_fn = node.raw_fn` is the user fn directly (no shim), so isawaitable-on-result also handles the async-raw case; keep detection identical to scripted to avoid drift. 3. Tests — extend tests/test_async_dual_path.py (reuse `_sync_async_node_thread` harness, register_scripted, Claims/RawText). Add async-body cells for THREE surfaces driven under graph.ainvoke only (sync driver + async body is out of scope):

## Findings (dp-researcher — Phase 1b: async scripted shim + async raw twin)

### THE CRUX — the shim HIDES the async body (iscoroutinefunction(self.fn) is WRONG for @node)
ScriptedDispatch.fn (_dispatch.py:123/136) is `self.fn(input_data.value, config)`. What `self.fn` IS differs by surface, and this is the whole ballgame:
- @node surface: `self.fn` = the `scripted_shim` closure built by `_register_node_scripted` (_scripted_registry.py:47-68). That shim is ALWAYS a plain `def` (sync) — it ends `return fn(*args)` (line 68) where `fn` is the user`s ORIGINAL function pulled from the sidecar (`fn, param_names = _get_sidecar(n)`). If the user wrote `async def`, `fn(*args)` returns an UN-AWAITED coroutine and the sync shim returns it. So `inspect.iscoroutinefunction(self.fn)` == False for EVERY @node scripted node, async body or not. The async-ness is hidden one layer down in the sidecar.
- declarative `Node.scripted(name, fn="x")` (node.py:267) + programmatic `Node()|Modifier`: `scripted_fn` is a STRING; the actual callable is registered via `register_scripted(name, actual_fn)` (_runtime_registry.py:32) and looked up into the per-compile scripted dict. Here `self.fn` IS the user`s registered `(input_data, config)` fn directly — so `iscoroutinefunction(self.fn)` WOULD be correct for these two surfaces, but NOT for @node.

### THE UNIFORM DETECTOR (reuse-first — zero shim/registry/compiler changes)
Do NOT branch per-surface and do NOT thread the sidecar into ScriptedDispatch. CALL first, then `inspect.isawaitable(result)`:
- @node: `self.fn(...)` (sync shim) returns `fn(*args)` = coroutine when body is async -> isawaitable True.
- declarative/programmatic async fn: `self.fn(...)` (async fn) returns coroutine -> isawaitable True.
- any sync body (all three surfaces): returns a BaseModel/dict -> isawaitable False -> no await.
Creating a coroutine does NOT run it (no loop needed), so `result = self.fn(...)` never blocks/errors even for async bodies. ONE check covers all three surfaces. This is strictly better than iscoroutinefunction (which needs the sidecar for @node) and matches the epic Core Invariant "one shared core".

### @node ALLOWS async def scripted bodies TODAY (nothing rejects/mishandles them at decoration)
- Mode inference (decorators.py:344-350) ignores async-ness: `async def` with no prompt/model infers `scripted`.
- The dead-body AST walk (decorators.py:373-402) already handles `ast.AsyncFunctionDef` (line 377) but is gated to LLM modes only (line 355) — scripted bodies are never inspected. So an async scripted body gets NO warning, NO rejection.
- Sidecar stores `f` verbatim (`_register_sidecar` _sidecar.py:34 `n._sidecar = (fn, param_names)`), async preserved.
Net: async @node scripted bodies are constructible today but currently BROKEN on both drivers (shim returns an un-awaited coroutine). 1b fixes the ASYNC driver; the sync-driver case is out of scope (see Risks).

### RAW path — no shim, so raw_fn IS the user fn (async twin deferred from 1a)
factory.make_node_fn raw branch (factory.py:53-54) returns `RunnableLambda(_make_raw_wrapper(node))` with NO afunc. `_make_raw_wrapper` (factory.py:86-108) -> `raw_node_wrapper` calls `raw_fn(state, config)` (line 101) where `raw_fn = node.raw_fn` is the user fn DIRECTLY (no shim hiding it). 1b: add an async twin wrapper + `afunc=`. Same isawaitable-on-result pattern (or equivalently `iscoroutinefunction(node.raw_fn)` since there is no shim — both correct for raw; prefer isawaitable to keep raw+scripted detection identical).

### Async spine already wired (1a) — 1b only fills the terminal await
`_aexecute_node` (_execute.py:99-140) awaits `dispatch.aexecute(...)` at line 135 and reuses every pure helper. Once ScriptedDispatch.aexecute awaits the awaitable, an async body flows through end-to-end. make_node_fn normal path already returns `RunnableLambda(node_wrapper, afunc=anode_wrapper)` (factory.py:83). ONLY the raw path lacks an afunc.

## Relevant Code

Change to: `result = self.fn(input_data.value, config); if inspect.isawaitable(result): result = await result; return NodeOutput(single=result)`. The conditional `await` satisfies RUF029 -> DELETE the `# noqa: RUF029`. Add `import inspect` (module has none today).
- src/neograph/_scripted_registry.py:47-68 scripted_shim — the sync `def` that returns `fn(*args)`; UNCHANGED (it already produces a coroutine when the sidecar fn is async). This is why no shim/registry/compiler plumbing is needed.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- SHIM-HIDES-ASYNC TRAP (headline): using `inspect.iscoroutinefunction(self.fn)` detects nothing for @node (shim is sync) — async @node bodies would silently NOT be awaited (coroutine written to state, tests may pass on `is not None`). MITIGATION: detect via `inspect.isawaitable(result)` AFTER calling, not on the function object.
- SYNC-DRIVER + ASYNC-BODY = OUT OF 1b SCOPE (but real): under `run()` (graph.invoke -> ScriptedDispatch.execute :123) an async scripted body returns an un-awaited coroutine -> silently wrong output. Task scopes 1b to `aexecute` + raw async twin ONLY. Nothing in mode inference rejects async scripted bodies, so this latent footgun remains after 1b. Recommend a follow-up: either a decoration-time guard (async scripted body requires arun) or await-in-sync via a loop — do NOT do it in 1b. Flagging so it is not mistaken for done.
- SYNC BODY UNDER ainvoke IS CORRECT AS-IS: `result = self.fn(...)` returns a BaseModel, `isawaitable` False, no await — LangGraph`s ainvoke already threadpools nothing extra here (the node runs inline on the loop via the afunc; the sync body just executes). No regression, matches task ("call it sync").
- RUF029: the current 1a `# noqa: RUF029` on ScriptedDispatch.aexecute (:126) MUST be removed once the conditional `await` lands (the function now has an await). Leaving it is a dead-noqa lint failure under repo ruff. Same for the new async raw twin — it has a conditional await, so no noqa needed.
- THREE-SURFACE PARITY (neograph-ts7 class): async body must be exercised via @node (`async def f(x)->Y`), declarative Node.scripted(fn registered as `async def g(input_data,config)`), AND programmatic Node()|Modifier. The async-body cell can only be driven under graph.ainvoke (sync driver + async body is the out-of-scope footgun above), so assert the ainvoke result is the real Out (NOT a coroutine object) on all three; a body doing `await asyncio.sleep(0)` + flag proves it ran to completion, not left pending.
- isawaitable false-positive: a sync scripted body returning a Future/awaitable is theoretically mis-awaited. Not a real neograph case (scripted nodes return Pydantic models/dicts). Acceptable; note in a comment.
- LAYER DISCIPLINE: the fix stays in _dispatch.py (ScriptedDispatch) + factory.py (raw twin) — NO change to _scripted_registry.py / decorators.py / node.py / compiler.py. The shim is reused as-is; this respects "no @node-layer logic in low-level modules" and the sidecar-import guards.

title: FR — per-run MCP identity via token-provider hook (on-behalf-of, no passthrough)
description:
config['configurable']['mcp_auth'][server] = provider(run_ctx) -> bearer JWT; static headers= stays the default, provider is the per-run escape hatch. On-behalf-of: neograph CARRIES identity, never DECIDES (ADR-0009; enforcement is the tool server's Permify check).

Cadence (review M2): provider invoked once per run, cached for the run, RE-MINTED on resume (fresh process -> cache miss). Cache lives OUTSIDE checkpoint state (live secret, never persisted). Provider may be async (blocking broker must not stall the loop); sync provider via threadpool.

Audience binding (review H4): DECLARED client-side, ENFORCED server-side. The audience URI is what the provider is expected to bind (RFC 8707); the tool server validates aud on receipt. neograph does NOT parse the token (carries-not-decides). No verbatim upstream-token forwarding. HTTP->bearer; stdio->env (no OAuth).

Guards: token never enters checkpoint state, schema fingerprint, OR any log / ToolInteraction (review L2); a structural guard that neograph never parses token contents.

Verification: integration — two run-context identities, assert each tools/call carried the correct per-identity token at a stub server, no-auth default path unaffected. E2E — one tool call resolves different server-side authz under two operators.

Depends on Phase 3 (neograph-w74k.3). Design: docs/design/async-streaming-mcp-hitl-2026-07-02.md §6.3.1.
design:
## Core Invariant
neograph CARRIES per-run identity and never DECIDES it: an async tool factory on the arun() path reads config['configurable'] and returns per-run tools whose per-request auth is minted by the ecosystem's httpx.Auth — neograph owns NO MCP session, parses NO token, and never lets a token reach checkpoint state, schema fingerprint, log, or ToolInteraction.

## Implementation Plan (refined 2026-07-06 per architect review)

1. **Twin the ONE sync factory line, don't rebuild the loop.** In src/neograph/_tool_loop.py factor the tool-instantiation loop (L266-275) out of _prepare_tool_loop into a shared helper, then add an async twin (_aprepare_tool_loop) co-located in the SAME module. Sync path fail-loud ORDER MATTERS (LOW-4): first `if asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(factory): raise ...` BEFORE calling (avoids creating an un-awaited coroutine and re-emitting the 'coroutine never awaited' RuntimeWarning); only if not a coroutine function, call `result = factory(config, tc)` then `if inspect.isawaitable(result): raise ...`. Both raises use ConfigurationError.build (LOW-3: NOT ExecutionError — driver/config mismatch, convergent design-doc §3 + exemplar _agent_cycle.py:352 + research) with the 4-field shape: expected='an async driver (arun())', found='sync run() driving an async tool factory', hint=..., node=node.name. Async path: `inst = factory(config, tc); inst = await inst if inspect.isawaitable(inst) else inst`.

2. **Route the 3 async bodies through an async prep.** Add _abuild_turn_prep in _agent_cycle.py (async twin of _build_turn_prep, L96) that awaits _aprepare_tool_loop; wire aagent_body/atools_body/aparse_body (L272/375/444) to it. Leave the 3 sync bodies on the sync prep unchanged. Node-level RunnableLambda(sync, afunc=async) twin at _wiring.py:755-757 already selects by driver — no wiring change.

3. **Fix lint introspection (item 2), reuse existing kind.** In src/neograph/lint.py _resolve_tool_object (L556) / _check_async_only_tools (L443): if asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(factory) BEFORE calling factory({}, spec.config), emit the EXISTING LintIssue kind 'tool_requires_async_driver' (L470) without invoking. Silences the current 'coroutine never awaited' RuntimeWarning. Extend tests/test_lint_mcp.py with an async-factory fixture (assert no RuntimeWarning).

4. **Extend GUARD B TWIN_TABLE — co-location alone does NOT lock the new twins (MEDIUM-1).** GUARD B (tests/test_guards_async_dispatch.py:293-308) is TABLE-DRIVEN and checks only what TWIN_TABLE names. Add: _tool_loop.py list += ('_prepare_tool_loop','_aprepare_tool_loop'); NEW key '_agent_cycle.py': [('_build_turn_prep','_abuild_turn_prep')]. Without these rows the anti-band-aid 'no async-only module' clause is UNENFORCEABLE for exactly these twins.

5. **Three NEW guards (item 3) — a+b as ONE runtime-sentinel test, not vacuous AST (MEDIUM-2).**
   - Guards (a) token-never-in-checkpoint/fingerprint/log/ToolInteraction AND (b) never-passthrough: ONE runtime-sentinel test. Inject a known token sentinel via a stub httpx.Auth; run() AND arun() a tool-bearing agent with a real (file-backed) checkpointer; assert the sentinel string appears in NONE of: the checkpoint state dump, the _neo schema fingerprint, captured structlog output, ToolInteraction.args/result. The ToolInteraction/outbound-args assertion doubles as never-passthrough (sentinel must not reappear verbatim in outbound tool args). This avoids the codebase's vacuous-guard hazard (a NEGATIVE-about-runtime-values assertion has no AST signature).
   - Guard (c) neograph contains NO MCP session-lifecycle code: structural grep — assert no 'client.session('/persistent-session ownership / ClientSession under src/neograph/ (locks the kill-nmb2 verdict). Include a non-vacuity meta-assertion (the grep matches a planted positive control).

6. **6-cell tests (item 4), copy tests/test_async_dual_path.py:79 shape.** 3 API surfaces (@node(tools=) / declarative Node(tools=) / programmatic Node()|Modifier) × run/arun via conftest.py:66 run_driver fixture. Explicitly (LOW-5): fail-loud-under-run() asserted on ALL 3 SYNC surface cells (not once) with the 3 async cells succeeding — shared async-factory fixture. Plus integration: two run-context identities each carry the correct per-identity token at a stub httpx.Auth/stub server; no-auth default path unaffected.

7. **Zero new config surface, zero new publics.** Async factory reads config['configurable']['mcp_auth'][server] (or any consumer-chosen key) and returns MultiServerMCPClient tools carrying auth: httpx.Auth. The optional mcp_tool_factory() convenience + docs/website MCP recipe are a SEPARATE optional ticket, not this atom. mcp>=1.28 deprecates transport-level headers=/auth= — auth belongs on httpx.AsyncClient; adapter 0.3.0 already does this.

## Anti-band-aid clause
Do NOT resurrect the deleted invoke_with_tools monolith, do NOT add an async-only module (GUARD B rows in Step 4 enforce this), do NOT add @node-layer logic to _tool_loop.py/lint.py beyond the factory-await twin, do NOT cache the live tool/session across supersteps (re-mint per superstep from fresh config IS the resume-correct behavior). Guards (a)+(b) must be a runtime-sentinel test, never a signature-free AST assertion.

title: Phase 1 — async foundation (arun, driver-selected async, async checkpointer)
description:
The keystone. Add async execution as a DIMENSION (dual sync/async, never a flip).

Core (review H2 — the load-bearing correction): async-ness is chosen by the DRIVER (run vs arun), NOT by the node body. think/agent/act have EMPTY bodies — there is no async def to detect. Under arun() the LLM/tool/MCP vertical (_execute_node->_dispatch->_tool_loop) awaits llm.ainvoke()/tool.ainvoke(); under run() it stays sync. The body's async-ness governs ONLY how a scripted body is invoked (await vs threadpool). Getting this wrong is SILENT (tests pass; prod still blocks the loop).

Scope: dual-path factory emitting an async node_wrapper twin; async scripted-shim (await async body); async twins for the custom seams (_CoercingToolWrapper/abind_tools _tool_loop.py:251; think-mode structured-output/coercion path — review L3/L4); async checkpointer (AsyncSqliteSaver/AsyncPostgresSaver). DI resolution is pure dict lookup — no await (review L3).

Phase-1 acceptance MUST include (review M6): (a) observability survives await (trace/contextvars across await — Langfuse example); (b) mixed-driver checkpoint resume (sync SqliteSaver thread resumes under AsyncSqliteSaver, same thread_id) — resolve, don't leave open; (c) a performance gate (async adds no per-call overhead beyond threshold; exercises within-run MCP session reuse per §5/H1).

Depends on Phase 0. Design: docs/design/async-streaming-mcp-hitl-2026-07-02.md §6.1, §4, §9.
design:
## Core Invariant
One compiled Construct, two drivers over ONE shared execution core: async is a DRIVER-selected
dimension (run->func / arun->afunc on a single RunnableLambda node), never a body-detected flip — the
sync and async paths share every pure preamble/postamble/rendering/parse helper and diverge ONLY at the
terminal `await llm.ainvoke()/tool.ainvoke()`, so they cannot silently drift and the sync surface is
never rewritten.

## Implementation Plan (reuse-first; extend existing seams, do not rebuild)

1. **Dual-path node registration via RunnableLambda (the spine).** Change `factory.make_node_fn`
   (factory.py:22) to return `RunnableLambda(node_wrapper, afunc=anode_wrapper)`. `node_wrapper` stays
   the current sync shell; `anode_wrapper` is a new async shell calling `_aexecute_node`. All add_node
   sites in _wiring.py stay unchanged. Raw wrapper (_make_raw_wrapper): await raw_fn only if it is a
   coroutine function, else call sync.

2. **Async twin of the execution core, reusing every pure helper.** Add `_aexecute_node` in _execute.py
   that reuses adapt_state / _inject_oracle_config / _extract_input / _apply_skip_when /
   _extract_context / NodeInput shaping / _build_state_update verbatim and only `await
   dispatch.aexecute(...)`. Add `async def aexecute` to the ModeDispatch Protocol (_dispatch.py) and the
   three classes: ScriptedDispatch (await async body via inspect.iscoroutinefunction, else sync call —
   this is the ONLY place body async-ness matters, review H2); ThinkDispatch -> `_llm.ainvoke_structured`;
   ToolDispatch -> `_tool_loop.ainvoke_with_tools`. Reuse _render_input / _resolve_primary_output /
   budget-tracker / oracle-override setup unchanged.

3. **Async twins for the custom LLM/tool seams (review L3/L4).** In _tool_loop.py add
   `ainvoke_with_tools` (keep bind_tools sync; await `_CoercingToolWrapper.ainvoke` and
   `tool_fn.ainvoke(args)`); give `_CoercingToolWrapper` an `ainvoke` + async `_agenerate` recovery
   mirror of the sync string-args coercion. In _llm.py add `ainvoke_structured`; in _llm_dispatch.py add
   `_acall_structured` (await the structured adapter + async json-retry); in _llm_structured_compat.py add
   an async adapter method awaiting `structured.ainvoke` through the same Parsed/Raw/Failed
   classification; in _llm_retry.py add async twins only where the LLM is invoked (_parse_json_response
   stays shared). _get_llm and _compile_prompt stay sync (no I/O). DI resolve stays sync (L3).

4. **arun() runner + async checkpoint helpers.** Add `arun` in runner.py mirroring run() and reusing
   _inject_input_to_config / _preflight_di_check / _strip_internals verbatim; `await graph.ainvoke(...)`.
   Add async twins of _has_existing_checkpoint / _verify_checkpoint_schema / _auto_resume_from_divergence
   using `aget_tuple` / `aget_state_history`. Add ainvoke/aget_state/aget_state_history/astream explicit
   delegations to CompiledNeograph (_compiled.py). Export `arun` from neograph.__init__ — this lights up
   the Phase-0 conftest async cell automatically.

5. **Async checkpointer wiring.** compile() already passes checkpointer through to graph.compile()
   unchanged — no compiler change needed; an async saver just works. For tests use InMemorySaver (has
   both sync + async surfaces) for parity/unit; decide on langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite (AsyncSqliteSaver)
   for the true cross-driver mixed-resume E2E (see NEEDS USER INPUT in notes).

6. **Three mandatory acceptance areas (review M6), each an E2E/guard:**
   (a) Observability survives await — pass `config` into every `.ainvoke(messages, config=config)`;
       assert a Langfuse-style callback/trace span propagates across the await boundary.
   (b) Mixed-driver checkpoint resume — a thread started under a sync saver resumes under the async
       saver on the same thread_id (arun's async checkpoint helpers).
   (c) Performance gate — benchmark asserting the async path adds no per-call overhead beyond a
       threshold; forward-references §5/H1 within-run session reuse (fully realized in Phase 3).
   Plus the M1 non-parity trio using Phase-0 primitives: real-concurrency (N runs, one loop,
   GatedAsyncFake), event-loop-lag watchdog (catches a silent blocking twin), cancellation E2E.

7. **Lock the invariants with structural guards.** "Every LLM mode exposes BOTH a sync and an async
   dispatch path" (no sync-only mode); async twins live in the SAME module as their sync counterpart
   (no async-only module importing decorators.py — respects the layer-discipline guards). Land each
   step green through the dual-surface harness; 6-cell coverage is MANDATORY for the IR-level changes
   in steps 1-2 (@node / declarative / programmatic x sync / async).

## Scope judgment — DECOMPOSE (do NOT run as one implement atom)
This epic spans 8 source files, 6 distinct async-twin seams, an async checkpointer path, and 3
mandatory acceptance E2Es plus 3 non-parity concurrency tests. It is far past a single implement atom
and the review flagged the silent-failure mode as the central hazard. Recommended child atoms, ordered:
  1. Dual-path factory + _aexecute_node + ModeDispatch.aexecute (steps 1-2) — the IR spine, 6-cell tested.
  2. Async scripted shim (await async body vs threadpool) — three-surface parity.
  3. Async LLM+tool seams (_llm / _tool_loop / _llm_dispatch / _llm_structured_compat / _llm_retry) (step 3).
  4. arun() + async checkpoint helpers + CompiledNeograph async delegations + __init__ export (step 4).
  5. Async checkpointer wiring + mixed-driver resume E2E (steps 5, 6b).
  6. Observability-across-await E2E (6a) + performance gate (6c) + M1 concurrency/watchdog/cancellation.
  7. Structural guards locking the dual-path invariant (step 7).
See notes "NEEDS USER INPUT" on the sqlite-async test dependency before atom 5.
notes:
## Findings (dp-researcher, l7js.2)

### The keystone reuse target — RunnableLambda(func, afunc=...) for dual-path node registration
LangGraph accepts any LangChain Runnable as a graph node and dispatches by driver:
`graph.invoke()` calls the node's `.invoke` (func); `graph.ainvoke()` calls `.ainvoke` (afunc).
`RunnableLambda(sync_func, afunc=async_func)` is the ONE primitive that gives "one Construct, many
drivers" with ZERO duplication at the registration seam (verified: RunnableLambda.__init__ takes
`afunc=`; instance has both invoke+ainvoke). So `factory.make_node_fn` should return
`RunnableLambda(node_wrapper, afunc=anode_wrapper)` instead of a bare function — every add_node call
site (_wiring.py:209/454/458/577/578) stays UNCHANGED (they pass one object to add_node). This is the
reuse-first spine of the whole phase: do NOT register two nodes or branch the wiring.

### The shared-core / thin-shell split (reuse-over-reinvention)
`_execute_node` (_execute.py:55) is preamble -> `dispatch.execute()` -> postamble. EVERYTHING except
the single `dispatch.execute()` middle call is pure, sync, I/O-free and REUSED VERBATIM by an async
twin: adapt_state, _inject_oracle_config, _extract_input, _apply_skip_when, _extract_context,
NodeInput shaping, _build_state_update, the two structlog lines, timing. So `_aexecute_node` is a
~10-line async twin that reuses the same helpers and only `await dispatch.aexecute(...)`. The
ModeDispatch Protocol (_dispatch.py:79) gains an `aexecute` method; the three dispatch classes get
async twins that reuse ALL their sync setup (rendering, output-model resolution, budget tracker,
oracle override) and differ ONLY in the terminal LLM/tool call. Same pattern one layer down: the
LLM/tool orchestrators (`invoke_structured`, `invoke_with_tools`) are long but only a handful of lines
touch the network — those get awaited; prompt compile / parse / usage-summing / logging are pure and
reused.

### DI resolution is pure dict lookup — NO await needed (review L3 CONFIRMED)
`DIBinding.resolve` (di.py:132) and `scripted_shim` (_scripted_registry.py:47) only read
`config['configurable'][...]` and construct Pydantic models. Zero I/O. The scripted shim body needs an
async twin ONLY to `await fn(*args)` when the user body is `async def` (detect via
`inspect.iscoroutinefunction`), else call sync (LangGraph threadpools a sync body under ainvoke). This
is the ONLY place body async-ness matters — review H2's load-bearing point.

### Driver chooses async, not the body (review H2)
think/agent/act have empty bodies (`...`) — there is no `async def` to detect. Async-ness of the
LLM/tool/MCP vertical is selected by which driver (run vs arun) invoked the graph, which selects
func vs afunc on the RunnableLambda automatically. Getting this wrong is SILENT: if the async node
just threadpools the sync vertical, tests pass but the loop still blocks and MCP (async-only) can't
bind. The afunc MUST route to the awaiting vertical.

### Async infra already present in installed deps
- CompiledStateGraph exposes ainvoke/astream/astream_events/aget_state/aget_state_history (verified).
- InMemorySaver supports BOTH sync (get_tuple/put) and async (aget_tuple/aput) — the test reuse target
  for mixed-driver resume without needing a new package.
- `langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite` is NOT installed (AsyncSqliteSaver import fails). Real AsyncSqliteSaver/
  AsyncPostgresSaver live in separate packages and expose ONLY the async API (sync get_tuple raises).
- Zero async in src/neograph today (grep count = 0). No async-body detection exists yet.

### Phase-0 harness to build on (w74k.1, landed)
- tests/conftest.py `run_driver` fixture params=['sync','async']; the async cell skip-guards on
  `hasattr(neograph,'arun')` and auto-activates the moment arun is exported from neograph.__init__.
- tests/fakes.py: all 8 shared fakes have bare-delegation `ainvoke`/`abind_tools`/`_agenerate`;
  GatedAsyncFake (awaitable-gated, for real-concurrency + cancellation) + event_loop_lag_watchdog
  (blocking detector) primitives exist.
- pyproject asyncio_mode='auto' set. Structural drift-guard tests/test_guards_async_fakes.py locks it.

## Relevant Code (file:line -> exact seam that needs an async twin)
- src/neograph/factory.py:22 make_node_fn -> return RunnableLambda(node_wrapper, afunc=anode_wrapper). :70 node_wrapper is the sync shell; add async anode_wrapper calling _aexecute_node. :79 _make_raw_wrapper -> async twin only if raw_fn is a coroutine (raw nodes take (state,config); await if async).
- src/neograph/_execute.py:55 _execute_node -> add _aexecute_node twin; REUSE every helper (preamble/postamble pure). Only line :91 `dispatch.execute(...)` becomes `await dispatch.aexecute(...)`.
- src/neograph/_dispatch.py:79 ModeDispatch Protocol -> add `async def aexecute`. :96 ScriptedDispatch (await async body vs sync). :119 ThinkDispatch.execute:143 -> aexecute calls _llm.ainvoke_structured. :160 ToolDispatch.execute:200 -> aexecute calls _tool_loop.ainvoke_with_tools. _render_input/_resolve_primary_output (:231/:254) are pure — reused.
- src/neograph/_tool_loop.py:65 _CoercingToolWrapper.invoke:84 -> add async `ainvoke` awaiting self._bound.ainvoke (and _agenerate on the coercion recovery path :121). :149 invoke_with_tools -> ainvoke_with_tools twin: :252 llm.bind_tools stays sync (not I/O); :266 llm_with_tools.invoke -> await ainvoke; :324 tool_fn.invoke(args) -> await tool_fn.ainvoke(args). Budget/preamble/parse/usage logic reused verbatim.
- src/neograph/_llm.py:128 invoke_structured -> ainvoke_structured twin. _get_llm:93 stays sync (factory call, not I/O). :179 _call_structured -> await _acall_structured. _compile_prompt pure.
- src/neograph/_llm_dispatch.py:33 _call_structured -> _acall_structured twin: :59 build_default_adapter().invoke -> await ainvoke; :106 _invoke_json_with_retry -> await async twin. match arms pure.
- src/neograph/_llm_structured_compat.py:83 LangChainStructuredAdapter.invoke:90 (structured.invoke) + decorators (IncludeRawCompat:123, DsmlClassifier:148) -> add async adapter method awaiting structured.ainvoke; classification pure.
- src/neograph/_llm_retry.py -> _invoke_json_with_retry / recover_dsml / _call_structured callers need async twins where they invoke the LLM; _parse_json_response is pure (reuse).
- src/neograph/runner.py:270 run() -> arun() twin. REUSE _inject_input_to_config/_preflight_di_check/_strip_internals verbatim (all pure). :314/:344/:346/:360 graph.invoke -> await graph.ainvoke. :253 _has_existing_checkpoint (get_tuple), :78 _verify_checkpoint_schema (get_tuple), :133 _auto_resume_from_divergence (graph.get_state_history) -> async twins using aget_tuple/aget_state_history (AsyncSqliteSaver has no sync get_tuple).
- src/neograph/_compiled.py:28 CompiledNeograph -> add ainvoke/aget_state/aget_state_history/astream explicit delegations mirroring the sync ones (:51-66).
- src/neograph/__init__.py:69/82 add `arun` import+export (the conftest async cell lights up on this).
- src/neograph/_wiring.py:209/454/458/577/578 add_node sites -> UNCHANGED if make_node_fn returns a dual RunnableLambda. Modifier nodes (gen/merge/fan/barrier/loop_exit/empty_bypass) are pure state-shuffle — threadpooled fine under ainvoke; only make_node_fn's LLM/tool output needs the async twin.
- src/neograph/di.py:132 DIBinding.resolve -> pure, NO async change (review L3).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- SILENT-FAILURE risk (H2): an async node twin that just calls the sync vertical passes every parity test but never awaits — loop still blocks, MCP can't bind. The event-loop-lag watchdog + a GatedAsyncFake concurrency test (Phase-0 primitives) are the ONLY guards that catch this; parity cannot. A structural guard "every LLM mode has both a sync AND async dispatch path" (design §7) must be added.
- Observability across await (M6a): neograph threads `config` (carrying LangChain callbacks) into every llm.invoke(messages, config=config). The async twins MUST pass the SAME config into every `.ainvoke(messages, config=config)` — callbacks propagate via config, and contextvar-based tracers (Langfuse @observe) propagate across `await` natively (unlike threadpooled sync nodes). Dropping config on any async hop silently breaks the trace. Acceptance = a Langfuse observable_pipeline span survives the await boundary.
- Mixed-driver resume (M6b): sync SqliteSaver thread resumed under AsyncSqliteSaver same thread_id. Data is compatible (same DB). The real work is that arun()'s checkpoint helpers must call aget_tuple/aget_state_history (AsyncSqliteSaver's sync methods raise). InMemorySaver (both surfaces, same process) is the cheap unit-test vehicle; a TRUE cross-process/cross-saver E2E needs langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite which is NOT currently a dependency. NEEDS USER INPUT below.
- Perf gate (M6c): async adds no per-call overhead beyond threshold; must exercise within-run MCP session reuse (§5/H1) — but MCP is Phase 3. In Phase 1 the perf gate can only assert the async node/LLM vertical adds no per-call overhead vs sync; the session-reuse dimension is a forward-reference to Phase 3, not fully testable here. Flag the partial coverage.
- NEEDS USER INPUT: add `langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite` (AsyncSqliteSaver) as a (dev/test) dependency for the mixed-driver + perf E2Es? Without it, mixed-driver resume can only be exercised via InMemorySaver (single-process, cannot prove the sync-file -> async-file resume the review names).
- Import-graph discipline: async twins must live in the SAME modules as their sync counterparts (no new async-only module that re-imports decorators.py) to respect the layer-discipline guards (test_guards_sidecar_imports / assembly import DAG).
