title: PROC-3: multi-agent codebase scan as in-loop ticket gate
description:
## Architectural invariant

Architecturally-significant tickets gain a fast multi-agent codebase-wide review as a phase-gate INSIDE the ticket, not just as a periodic full audit. The seven-reviewer scan that was previously a `/dev-practices:code-review` session now has a callable form scoped to a single disease pattern, runnable in 2-3 minutes from inside a ticket's review atom.

## Phase 1 — Code archaeology

Read:
- `/Users/konst/projects/pi-agentic-coding/plugins/dev-practices/skills/code-review/` — the existing skill
- `.claude/code-review/020626_2218/` — the report shape from the Jun-2026 review
- The current `feature-dev:code-reviewer` agent definition — what it can do today

The current code-review skill spawns 5 review agents in parallel (testing, dry, consistency, layering, python-practices) plus 2 optional (architecture, security). Each writes a separate Markdown report. The synthesis is post-hoc.

## Phase 1b — Codebase-wide disease scan

Disease pattern: "architectural tickets that close without a codebase-wide elegance review." Scan:
- Recently-closed P1 architectural tickets (last 30 days): `bd list --status=closed --priority=1`
- For each, did the close note reference a multi-agent scan?
- Most probably did NOT. Count them.

Disposition table per ticket (this is a process-correctness scan, not a code-pattern scan).

## Phase 2 — Target design

Define a `codebase-elegance-scan` callable form:

1. **Scope** — takes a one-line "disease pattern spec" (the same spec produced by the molecule's `codebase-scan` atom). Example: "raw `getattr(state, ...)` instead of `bus.get/get_required` in routing modules."

2. **Agents to spawn (in parallel, single message)**:
   - `review-dry` — does this disease appear elsewhere (DRY violations)?
   - `review-consistency` — is this the only naming/regex form?
   - `review-layering` — does the fix cross layer boundaries it shouldn't?
   - Optional: `feature-dev:code-reviewer` (opus model) for the elegance question.

3. **Output** — each writes to `.claude/code-review/<ticket-id>/`. The synthesizer (the ticket's executor) reads all, produces a one-page verdict for the bead notes.

4. **Time budget** — ≤ 5 minutes per scan. (The Jun-2026 review was 7 agents over the whole codebase and took ~3 minutes per agent. A single-disease scan is faster.)

5. **Integration with the molecule** — the `review` atom in `task-execute.yaml` / `bug-triage.yaml` SHOULD invoke this scan. Phase 6 of the per-ticket discipline ("independent codebase-wide elegance review") becomes mechanical.

## Phase 3 — Iterative elegant solution

Apply SOLID + GRASP. Iterate until:
- The callable form is documented in the dev-practices skill (probably as a new sub-skill `code-review-targeted` or as an option in the existing one)
- The molecule formulas reference it from the `review` atom
- A probe ticket exercises the in-loop scan end-to-end
- The scan produces actionable output (a disposition table for the disease pattern, NOT a 41-finding catalog)

## Phase 4 — Anti-band-aid clauses

- NO defining the discipline without making it callable. "Reviewers should run a scan" is aspirational; "the molecule spawns the scan as part of the review atom" is structural.
- NO collapsing the targeted scan with the full audit — they serve different purposes (the targeted scan is fast and disease-specific; the full audit is periodic and exhaustive).

## Phase 5 — Sweep verification

Re-scan the recently-closed P1 ticket list. The discipline for NEW tickets includes the in-loop scan. (Old tickets are not retroactively fixed — that's what ARCH-1..4 do.)

## Phase 6 — Independent review

Opus reviewer:
1. Is the callable scan actually faster than a full multi-agent run? Time it.
2. Does the disposition table format integrate cleanly with the molecule's existing bead-notes conventions?

design:
## Core Invariant
Architecturally-significant tickets gain a fast, single-disease multi-agent codebase scan as a STRUCTURAL phase-gate inside the ticket -- delivered as a --targeted MODE of the existing code-review skill (NOT a duplicate skill) -- that fans out disease-scoped lenses, writes to .claude/code-review/<ticket-id>/, and produces a one-page disposition table the codebase-scan:complete gate REQUIRES to exist; the full periodic audit stays a separate mode.

## Implementation Plan (deliverable in agentic-toolkit; commit + PUSH)

### Step 1 -- review-disease-scan agent (the missing primitive)
New agents/review-disease-scan.md (dev-practices plugin). Read-only. Input contract (via spawn prompt): a one-line DISEASE-PATTERN SPEC + a LENS in {dedup, consistency, layering}. Behavior:
- WHOLE-TREE scope (explicitly NO git-diff/Changed-Function anchor -- unlike the dimensional review-* agents).
- Find every instance of THE ONE pattern through its lens (dedup=semantic duplicate logic; consistency=naming/form drift, dominant-usage; layering=does the pattern cross a layer boundary).
- Output ONLY disposition rows: | # | file:line | Form | Disposition (MIGRATE/ALLOWLIST/DEFER) | Reason |. NO Critical/High/Med/Low severity catalog.
- Write to the assigned output file.

### Step 2 -- code-review --targeted MODE (no new skill)
Edit skills/code-review/SKILL.md: keep args '[scope]'; add a Targeted Mode section. Invocation: /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<disease-spec>" [ticket-id].
- Output dir .claude/code-review/<ticket-id>/ (ticket-id arg; fallback DDMMYY_HHMM).
- Spawn IN ONE MESSAGE: review-disease-scan x3 (lens=dedup/consistency/layering) -> <dir>/disease-<lens>.md; + optional opus feature-dev:code-reviewer (elegance question) for architectural tickets -> <dir>/elegance.md.
- Executor synthesizes a ONE-PAGE disposition table (merge the 3 lens rows, dedup by file:line+Form) appended to bead notes -- NOT a multi-section synthesis.md.
- Time budget <=5 min (3+1 agents, single disease) -- contrast documented vs the full mode (5-7 agents, whole-codebase, periodic).
- SEMANTIC-vs-SYNTACTIC boundary documented: targeted fan-out is the prescribed method for SEMANTIC diseases (logic duplicated under different names); for purely syntactic patterns (getattr(state), magic-string keys, dual-name alias) a single executor grep in the codebase-scan atom suffices -- don't fan out for those.

### Step 3 -- Wire into molecule formulas (REPLACE manual, don't augment)
task-execute.yaml + bug-triage.yaml codebase-scan atom: replace the 'executor greps by hand' narrative with 'produce the disposition table by invoking /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<spec>" <ticket-id> (semantic diseases) or a single grep (syntactic)'. Gate label/acceptance otherwise unchanged. sweep-verify re-scan step (step 1 'Re-run the scan') re-invokes the same mode.

### Step 4 -- Structural un-skippability
Amend the codebase-scan atom acceptance: codebase-scan:complete REQUIRES .claude/code-review/<ticket-id>/ to exist AND contain the disposition table. Reuses the existing label-gate hard-check (downstream review atom greps the label). Now the gate can't be earned without the scan having run + written output.

### Step 5 -- Static wiring guard (toolkit repo)
A check (test or the plugin's validation) asserting: (a) skills/code-review/SKILL.md documents the --targeted mode + arg contract; (b) agents/review-disease-scan.md exists; (c) both formula codebase-scan atoms contain the literal 'code-review --targeted'. Proves wired, not just markdown.

### Step 6 -- Probe ticket end-to-end
File a probe bead; run code-review --targeted on a real SEMANTIC disease spec (e.g. 'merge/redirect logic re-derived inline instead of via the single oracle merge helper' OR reuse a PROC-2 semantic pattern); confirm .claude/code-review/<probe-id>/ output + 1-page table; time it (<5 min, faster than the full run).

### Step 7 -- gates
make quality (neograph side unaffected); independent Opus review (faster-than-full? disposition integrates with bead-notes? can a ticket SKIP it? -> artifact gate must make NO). ELEGANT>=85. Then commit + push BOTH repos.

## Acceptance mapping
- callable exists -> Steps 1-2 (--targeted mode + review-disease-scan agent)
- task-execute + bug-triage review/scan atoms invoke it -> Step 3
- probe exercises in-loop scan; output in .claude/code-review/<ticket-id>/ -> Step 6
- independent ELEGANT>=85 -> Step 7

## Verification (non-code deliverable)
RED artifact = the Step-5 wiring guard failing before the skill/agent/formula edits exist; GREEN after. Probe run = behavioral proof.

A new skill skills/code-review-targeted/SKILL.md that: takes a one-line disease-pattern spec (arg); spawns review-dry + review-consistency + review-layering in ONE message (parallel), each scoped to the SINGLE disease (not whole-codebase dimensions); optional opus elegance reviewer (feature-dev:code-reviewer or reviewer); each writes .claude/code-review/<ticket-id>/<agent>.md; the invoking executor synthesizes a one-page disposition verdict into bead notes; time budget <=5 min. - Scope creep: targeted scan must NOT collapse into the full audit (different purpose). Keep agent count small (3 + optional 1) and disease-scoped.

title: Make y20i routing!=label invariant universal: remove dead __name__ overrides (_subconstruct.py:147, _construct_builder.py:705)
description: Phase-5 opus review of neograph-y20i flagged two __name__ overrides outside the epic's scope: _subconstruct.py:147 (subgraph_node.__name__ = field_name) and _construct_builder.py:705 (scripted_shim.__name__ = field_name_for(n.name)). But the 'routing identity != display label' principle established by y20i is not yet universal. design:
## Core Invariant
The 'LangGraph routing identity (add_node arg) != user-facing label' separation established by neograph-y20i is UNIVERSAL across the IR/factory layer: no wrapper/shim closure overrides __name__ to a mangled field_name to satisfy routing, because routing never reads closure __name__.

- _subconstruct.py:147 `subgraph_node.__name__ = field_name`: DEAD WEIGHT. subgraph_fn is always added via explicit sub.name/item.name (_wiring.py:554,623,632; compiler.py:446). field_name still used at _subconstruct.py:~157/159 (update dict + loop_count) so removing only the override line orphans nothing.

The shim is registered under item.scripted_fn (compiler.py:274 lookup[item.scripted_fn]=shim), NEVER under shim.__name__. field_name_for stays used (lines 190,227,239,414,596,626) so the import is not orphaned.

Watch it FAIL against current code. Pair with a behavioral check that a sub-construct graph + a scripted @node graph still compile() and route (reuse existing compile()+invoke coverage).

3. make quality green; net negative LOC.

title: fan_out_param divergence when an Each node consumes a multi-output upstream's per-key field
description:
## Architectural invariant (must hold after this fix)

The set of "known field names" used by `_FanOutParamNormalizer.apply` (and any future normalizer that needs to recognize what counts as an upstream producer) is IDENTICAL to the set the validator's `_check_fan_in_inputs` computes from `producers`. Multi-output nodes contribute one field per output key (`{node}_result`, `{node}_tool_log`); single-output nodes contribute one field (`{node}`). One source of truth, applied in two places (normalizer + validator), via a shared helper that lives in the IR layer — not duplicated logic.

## Phase 1 — Code archaeology (MANDATORY, BEFORE design)

Read and document in the bead notes:

1. `src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py::normalize_ir` (lines ~180-205) — how `peer_field_names` is built today (one entry per node name only).
2. `src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py::fan_out_candidates` — how it uses `known_field_names` to identify the unique unknown key.
3. `src/neograph/_construct_validation.py::_validate_node_chain` — how the validator builds the FULL producer set, including per-output-key fields for multi-output nodes. Trace the code path that registers producers for dict-form `Node.outputs`.
4. `src/neograph/_construct_validation.py::_check_fan_in_inputs` — confirms it sees `gen_result` as a real producer field (not just `gen`).
5. `src/neograph/state.py` / `src/neograph/_normalize.py` — how `normalize_outputs` exposes `all_keys` / `primary_key` for dict-form outputs.
6. Existing test fixtures: search `tests/` for any case combining multi-output upstream (`outputs={"key1": T1, "key2": T2}`) AND a downstream `Each` consumer that takes one specific output key as a fan-in input. If none exists, that gap is itself a finding.

Output in bead notes: a side-by-side table of "what `peer_field_names` contains today" vs "what the validator's producer set contains" for a sample multi-output construct. The divergence row IS the bug.

## Phase 2 — Target design

READ the `design` field on this bead before proposing implementation.

## Phase 3 — Iterative elegant solution (keep iterating until elegant)

Apply SOLID + GRASP + DRY rigorously. Iterate until ALL of the following are true:

- A SHARED helper computes "field names contributed by a Node IR" — handles both single-type outputs (returns `{field_name_for(node.name)}`) and dict-form outputs (returns `{f"{field_name_for(node.name)}_{key}" for key in output_keys}`). Single source of truth.
- The normalizer's `peer_field_names` is computed via this helper, NOT inlined.
- The validator's per-producer registration is ALSO via this helper (or otherwise verifiably consistent — a structural guard pins agreement).
- A behavioral test that EXERCISES the bug: build a Construct with a multi-output node `gen` (`outputs={"result": T1, "log": T2}`), a downstream Each node consuming `inputs={"gen_result": T1, "cluster": ClusterGroup}` over `gen.result`. Pre-fix: `fan_out_param` is None and runtime `_extract_fan_in_dict` raises. Post-fix: `fan_out_param = "cluster"` and the pipeline runs.
- A structural guard that pins agreement between normalizer's known-field computation and validator's producer-field computation (so a future change to multi-output semantics in one place breaks the other test loudly).

If the proposed diff special-cases the dict-form output path inside the normalizer (rather than via the shared helper that BOTH sides consume), STOP. That's a band-aid.

## Phase 4 — Anti-band-aid clauses

- NO branching-over-polymorphism (if a future output form is added, the shared helper grows ONE branch in ONE place, not three).
- NO inline `field_name_for(...)` enumeration that duplicates dict-form handling.
- NO patching just the normalizer to "see" the missing fields — fix the underlying duplication. The validator and normalizer must agree by sharing a function, not by parallel inline computation.
- Net acceptance is STRUCTURAL: the new shared helper lives in `_ir_normalize.py` (or a sibling module like `_ir_fields.py`) and BOTH the normalizer and the validator import it. Duplication is mechanically impossible.

## Phase 5 — Independent review (correctness AND elegance)

After implementation, spawn a feature-dev:code-reviewer agent with model: opus. Demand evaluation of:

1. CORRECTNESS — the multi-output + Each consumer pipeline COMPILES and RUNS. Existing single-output + Each cases unchanged. All 1925 existing tests pass.
2. ELEGANCE — is there ONE function/method that owns "what field names does this Node contribute?" Or is the rule still spread across normalizer + validator?
3. INVARIANT — try to construct a Node IR form where the normalizer's view of "known fields" and the validator's view would still diverge. If you can, the fix is incomplete.
4. NO NEW HYDRA — when a hypothetical THIRD output form is added (e.g., tagged-union outputs), how many places must change? Must be ONE.
5. PINNING — is there a structural test that fails loudly if a future change drifts the two views apart?

Reviewer must verdict ELEGANT or NOT, confidence ≥85. If NOT ELEGANT, reopen.

## Why this is P1 not P3

Filed initially as P3 because no real user has hit it (no fixture covers the case). Re-evaluated: the bug is a SILENT MISCOMPILE — the construct passes validation but fails at runtime with a confusing error. Multi-output Each consumers are a legitimate use case (the audit doc itself includes `tool_log` as a typical secondary output key). Shipping with this latent miscompile is the kind of debt a real user would file as P0 the moment they hit it. Fix now, before any user encounters it.

## Acceptance

- Shared helper exists: one function computes the field-name contribution of a Node IR
- Normalizer and validator both consume it (verified by structural guard)
- Behavioral test: multi-output upstream + Each consumer compiles AND runs end-to-end
- All existing tests pass (1925 baseline)
- Independent reviewer (opus) verdicts ELEGANT with confidence ≥85, written to bead notes
- bd close after reviewer ELEGANT verdict
design:
## Root Cause
normalize_ir's peer_field_names = {field_name_for(name)} (peer NODE names) is NARROWER than the validator's producer field-name set (per-output-key fields for dict-output nodes). An Each consumer fanning over a multi-output upstream's suffixed field (gen_result) sees it as an extra unknown candidate -> 2 candidates -> fan_out_param=None; validator (full producer set) sees 1 and tolerates -> construct validates with a wrong (None) IR -> runtime _extract_fan_in_dict cannot route the fanned item.

## Fix Approach (refined per architect — exact-parity shared helper)
1. _ir_normalize.py: add output_field_name(base, key) -> f'{base}_{key}' (the suffix convention) and declared_output_fields(item) -> set[str]:
   - dict-output Node: {output_field_name(base, k) for k in normalize_outputs(item.outputs).all_keys}
   - single-type Node: {base}
   - outputs=None Node: set()  (validator registers no producer)
   - non-Node (sub-construct): {base}
   built on normalize_outputs (NOT isinstance(dict)). base = field_name_for(item.name).
2. normalize_ir: peer_field_names = union of declared_output_fields(item) over construct.nodes. Exact parity with validator producer NAMES (no bare base for dict-output nodes).
3. _construct_validation.py producer loop (~357): key_field = output_field_name(field_name, output_key) — single source for the naming convention (anti-drift). Function-local import if needed (cycle already broken via the existing fan_out_candidates deferred import).
4. Tests: keep IR unit test; add (a) compile+run integration test for a multi-output Each pipeline (runtime routing), (b) agreement test declared_output_fields(node) == validator producer field_names for a multi-output node.

## Core Invariant
The set of field names the normalizer treats as 'known producers' is IDENTICAL to the validator's producer field-name set, derived from one shared output-field-naming helper.
notes:
## Reproduction (atom fsth.2)
- Failing test: tests/test_ir_normalize.py::TestNormalizeIrOwnsFanOutParam::test_fan_out_param_set_when_each_consumes_multi_output_upstream
- FAILED: assert None == 'item' (Construct ACCEPTED — validator tolerates — but consumer.fan_out_param is None).
- Root cause: _FanOutParamNormalizer derives candidates via fan_out_candidates(node, peer_field_names) where peer_field_names = {field_name_for(n.name)} — peer NODE names only. A multi-output upstream 'gen' (outputs {result, log}) produces FIELDS 'gen_result'/'gen_log', which are NOT in peer_field_names, so an Each consumer with inputs={'gen_result', 'item'} sees TWO candidates -> declines -> fan_out_param=None. The validator uses the full producer field set (incl. per-output-key names) so it sees ONE candidate and passes.
## Trace similar (atom fsth.3)
Searched for the same 'peer field set from node NAMES, blind to per-output-key fields' pattern. Result: ISOLATED to ONE site — normalize_ir's peer_field_names (_ir_normalize.py:192-193). 
- construct.py:137 is the llm_config/renderer propagation loop (no field-set logic).
- The CORRECT multi-output expansion already exists in _construct_validation.py:348-373 (producer loop): single-output -> field_name_for(name); dict-output -> f'{field_name}_{output_key}' per key. state.py builds matching per-key state fields. Both the validator and state model already handle multi-output; only the normalizer lagged.
- No systemic spread. Fix mirrors the validator's f'{field_name}_{output_key}' naming when expanding peer output fields. No other call site needs changing.
## Architect Review (pragmatic, 2026-06-02)

DECISION: exact-parity via SHARED helper. NOT additive. Shared helper = YES (mandatory, not optional).

- [LOW] Q1 additive-safety: additive (keep bare base + suffixed) is SAFE in isolation — adding names can only REMOVE candidates, never miss a legit receiver. The only 'missed receiver' counter-case requires the user to name the fan-out receiver identically to a real producer field (e.g. receiver param 'gen_result' while node 'gen' has output key 'result'), which is a pre-existing name collision the construct was already broken by. Not introduced by the fix.

- [NEEDS_REFINEMENT] Q3 additive vs exact-parity: choose EXACT PARITY (drop the bare 'gen' for dict-output nodes). RATIONALE: the validator does NOT register a bare-base producer for dict-output nodes (validation:354-364 takes the dict branch, skips the else at 365). The bead invariant demands the two sets be IDENTICAL. Additive leaves the normalizer's set a strict SUPERSET of the validator's -> technically violates the invariant and could let the structural guard pass while the views differ. Parity is correct.

- [NEEDS_REFINEMENT] Q2 edge cases — the prompt's additive snippet has TWO real defects vs the validator:
  1. outputs=None Node: validator registers NO producer (gated 'output_type is not None' at val:349). Additive snippet keeps the base -> INVERSE divergence (normalizer sees a field the validator doesn't). Exact-parity helper must return EMPTY set for None-output nodes.
  2. Sub-construct (not Node): validator registers ONE producer at field_name_for(name) via .output (singular). Helper must return {field_name_for(name)} for sub-constructs (base only). The 'isinstance(item, Node)' guard handles this only if the None-output gate is also respected.
  3. Each-wrapped multi-output upstream: validator wraps per-key TYPES in dict[str,X] but field NAMES unchanged. Helper is name-only/type-independent -> no impact. Correct.

- [LOW] Q4 site + shared helper: CORRECT site, but hand-mirroring f'{base}_{key}' is the band-aid the bead forbids. MANDATORY shared helper. Place it in _ir_normalize.py (or sibling _ir_fields.py). PRECEDENT: _construct_validation already deferred-imports fan_out_candidates FROM _ir_normalize (val:622-624) specifically to break the _construct_validation->_ir_normalize->_sidecar cycle. The new helper rides the SAME deferred-import pattern — proven, low-risk. Helper MUST be built on normalize_outputs(node.outputs) (.all_keys / .is_dict_form), the existing leaf primitive in _normalize.py — do NOT re-roll isinstance(outputs, dict). The validator's producer loop (val:346-376) should then derive its field NAMES from the same helper so name-convention drift is mechanically impossible.

- [NEEDS_REFINEMENT] Q5 TDD: IR-level assertion (fan_out_param=='item') is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT. The bug's severity claim is a SILENT MISCOMPILE failing at runtime in _extract_fan_in_dict. Need BOTH: (a) IR unit test pinning the inference, (b) compile+run integration test proving the runtime fan-in path consumes fan_out_param for the multi-output case, (c) structural guard pinning normalizer<->validator field-name agreement (bead already requires this).

Decision: EXACT-PARITY (not additive); SHARED HELPER = YES, built on normalize_outputs, deferred-imported by validator per existing fan_out_candidates precedent; helper must reproduce validator's None-output and sub-construct gating exactly.
Overall: NEEDS_REFINEMENT (fix approach is right in spirit but the prompt's literal additive snippet diverges from the validator on None-output + sub-construct + bare-base; tighten to exact-parity shared helper).
## Triage (atom fsth.5)
NEEDS_REFINEMENT — autonomously resolvable. Architect gave precise direction (exact-parity shared helper + None/sub-construct gating + integration & agreement tests). Refine atom neograph-b994 created; fix proceeds after.
## Fix (atom fsth.6)
- naming.py: added output_field_name(base, key) -> f'{base}_{key}' — single source of the per-output-key naming convention.
- _ir_normalize.py: added declared_output_fields(item: ConstructItem) -> set[str] (built on normalize_outputs; dict->per-key fields, single->base, None->empty, sub-construct->base). normalize_ir's peer_field_names is now the union of declared_output_fields over all nodes — EXACT parity with the validator's producer field-name set.
- _construct_validation.py: producer loop uses output_field_name(field_name, output_key) (shared convention, anti-drift).
- declared_output_fields typed ConstructItem (not Any) to satisfy the IR Any-audit.
- Tests: IR repro (test_fan_out_param_set_when_each_consumes_multi_output_upstream) now PASSES; added TestDeclaredOutputFields (dict/single/None/hyphen parity) + TestFanOutMultiOutputRuntime (compile+run proving _extract_fan_in_dict routes the fanned item end-to-end).
- Quality: PASS (1931 passed, lint + mypy clean). No regressions.
## E2E verify (atom fsth.7)
- TestFanOutMultiOutputRuntime: compile+run multi-output Each pipeline routes both fanned items (PASS).
- example 04 (each fanout) runs clean end-to-end.
- 295 fan-out/each/modifier/composition/loop tests green. No behavioral regression.
close_reason: Fixed via exact-parity shared output-field-naming (output_field_name + declared_output_fields); normalize_ir peer set now identical to validator producer set. IR repro + parity units + compile+run integration green. 1931 tests pass.

title: EPIC 3: Split LangGraph routing key from user-facing label
description:
## Architectural invariant (must hold after this epic)

LangGraph node routing identity and user-facing display labels are two structurally distinct fields on the IR. Neither leaks into the other's domain. Wrapper closures may be assigned synthesized routing keys for LangGraph's add_node(name, fn) requirement, but they do NOT override their __name__ to a mangled form. User-facing error messages, log breadcrumbs, and observability events source labels from node.name (the user's original declaration), accessed through the captured Node instance — never through __name__ or threaded string parameters.

## Phase 1 — Code archaeology (MANDATORY, BEFORE design)

Read and document in the bead notes:

1. src/neograph/factory.py:121 (and similar lines) — every `<wrapper>.__name__ = field_name` assignment. Trace what uses each.
2. src/neograph/_oracle.py — three closure factories (make_oracle_redirect_fn, make_eachoracle_redirect_fn, make_each_redirect_fn). Document the node_name kwarg threading + the _ = node_name placeholder at line 68 + every site that propagates raw_fn.__name__.
3. src/neograph/compiler.py — every graph.add_node(name, fn) call. Document where `name` comes from (it's the routing key) and where `fn.__name__` is used independently (if anywhere — checking for the double-duty conflation).
4. src/neograph/_wiring.py — closure-construction sites. Where do node identities flow?
5. The recent commit (6cfab66 7nan + 5e4560c kg8l) — the entire history of node_name threading. Each call site is symptomatic of the underlying conflation.

Output: a table in bead notes:
- Each closure factory: does it need __name__ for LangGraph routing? If yes, what routing key would work? If no, can we stop overriding __name__?
- Each error-message site: what does it currently use (raw_fn.__name__ vs threaded node_name vs node.name)?
- Identify the single point where the conflation originates (factory.py:121 is the suspect).

## Phase 2 — Target design

READ docs/design/architecture-review-synthesis-2026-06-02.md AND the design field on this bead before proposing implementation.

## Phase 3 — Iterative elegant solution (keep iterating until elegant)

Apply SOLID + GRASP rigorously. Iterate until ALL of the following are true:

- Factory.py no longer overrides closure __name__ to a mangled form. Wrapper closures retain their natural __name__ (e.g., "node_wrapper", "oracle_redirect_fn") which is informational, not load-bearing.
- LangGraph routing keys are passed EXPLICITLY as the first argument to graph.add_node(name, fn), as they already are. Wrapper closures don't need to satisfy LangGraph identity through their __name__ at all — the routing key is the add_node argument.
- Where a closure needs a routing key for its OWN identity (e.g., LangGraph node references in conditional edges), it gets a synthesized name via a helper (`_make_routing_key(node, suffix)`) that is documentedly internal.
- Error messages and observability events source labels from node.name (or sub.name for Constructs), accessed via the Node instance captured in the closure — NOT through raw_fn.__name__, NOT through a threaded node_name kwarg.
- The node_name kwarg DISAPPEARS from make_oracle_redirect_fn, make_eachoracle_redirect_fn, make_each_redirect_fn. The `_ = node_name` placeholder DISAPPEARS. The closures take the Node instance (or a NodeIdentity dataclass extracted from it) instead.

If the proposed diff KEEPS node_name as a kwarg threaded through factories, STOP. The conflation has not been resolved at its root.

## Phase 4 — Anti-band-aid clauses

- NO collapsing the three closure factories into one branching function (the user and all three reviewers were explicit: three distinct topologies, polymorphism is real).
- NO removing __name__ entirely if LangGraph relies on it anywhere — verify the routing-key flow first.
- The acceptance test is that adding a hypothetical FOURTH redirect factory (e.g., make_eachloop_redirect_fn) requires ZERO new threading: it captures the Node, uses node.name, done. If a fourth factory would re-introduce node_name kwarg, the design is wrong.

# TARGET DESIGN (preserved from epic)

## Target design (from architecture-review-synthesis-2026-06-02.md, Epic 3)

### Pattern

Separate concern, separate field. LangGraph identity is one thing (used by graph wiring); user-facing label is another (used by error messages, logs, observability). Both already exist; the bug is that one (label) was sourced from the other (identity) via the closure's __name__.

The Information Expert principle says: the data should be queried at the source. node.name is the source of truth for the user label. Closures should ASK the Node, not receive a string parameter.

### Structural change

Currently:
```python
# factory.py:121
node_wrapper.__name__ = field_name  # MANGLED form, e.g. "score_claim"

# _oracle.py:75-100 (and 322-345, and 49-72)
def make_eachoracle_redirect_fn(
    raw_fn, field_name, collector_field, each_key, *, node_name: str,
):
    label = node_name  # string threaded through

    def eachoracle_redirect_fn(state, config):
        # ...
        item = adapt_state(state).get_required(
            StateKeys.EACH_ITEM, node_label=label,
        )
        # ...
```

Target:
```python
# factory.py
# DO NOT override __name__ to mangled form. Let it stay as the function name
# the closure was defined with ("node_wrapper", "oracle_redirect_fn", etc).

# _oracle.py
def make_eachoracle_redirect_fn(
    raw_fn, node: Node, collector_field, each_key,
):
    """Closure captures the Node IR directly. node.name is the user label."""

    def eachoracle_redirect_fn(state, config):
        # ...
        item = adapt_state(state).get_required(
            StateKeys.EACH_ITEM, node_label=node.name,
        )
        # ...
```

The factory signature now takes a Node, not a bare string. The closure has access to node.name (un-mangled), node.outputs (for dict-form detection), and anything else the IR carries. The factory becomes Information Expert — it ASKS the Node for what it needs.

### Routing-key flow

LangGraph: `graph.add_node(name, fn)`. The `name` argument is the routing key. compiler.py and _wiring.py already pass explicit strings here (e.g., `field_name`, `sub.name`, synthesized barrier/empty names like `f"merge_{node.name}"`). These DON'T depend on the closure's __name__.

So: stop overriding __name__ on closures. LangGraph never reads __name__ for routing; it reads the add_node argument. The override at factory.py:121 was either historical or for a different concern (probably traceback readability). Verify in archaeology.

If __name__ override IS load-bearing somewhere (e.g., LangGraph's debug tracing), preserve it but in a non-conflated way: synthesize a unique routing key independently (e.g., `f"{field_name}__{id(closure)}"`) that has nothing to do with user-facing labels.

### Why pass the Node instance (not a NodeIdentity dataclass)

The closure may need MORE than just .name in the future (e.g., access to .modifier_set for dispatch decisions, or .llm_config for runtime overrides). Passing the Node gives the closure the full IR. The Node is already frozen-ish (Pydantic immutable-style); the closure can safely retain a reference.

The alternative — a NodeIdentity dataclass with (name, field_name, ...) — adds an indirection without earning it. Rule-of-three: do we have ≥3 closures that need EXACTLY name+field_name and nothing else? If yes, extract. If not, pass the Node.

Recommend: pass the Node. Re-evaluate if a real need for a narrower identity object appears.

### The three closure factories remain three

make_oracle_redirect_fn: wraps a generator function, redirects output from field_name to collector_field. Does NOT call get_required today.

make_eachoracle_redirect_fn: wraps a generator function for Each×Oracle fusion. Tags each result with the each_key. CALLS get_required(EACH_ITEM).

make_each_redirect_fn: wraps a function for plain Each fan-out. Keys result by each.key. CALLS get_required(EACH_ITEM).

These are three structurally distinct topologies. The user and all three architectural reviewers explicitly rejected collapsing them. The win here is that each factory becomes SMALLER (no node_name kwarg, no _ = node_name placeholder), not that there are fewer factories.

### Why this is Information Expert

GRASP Information Expert: assign a responsibility to the class that has the data. The data here is "what is the user-declared name of this node?" — that's stored on Node. The closure currently RECEIVES this data via a kwarg, which is the anti-pattern. Closure should ASK Node directly.

### Why NOT make this Modifiable.__or__ work

An earlier design option (rejected for aqau) was to push inference into Modifiable.__or__ at pipe time. Doesn't apply here — there's no inference, just a reference. The Node already has its name from the moment Node(name="X") is called. The fix is purely about WHO reads it (closure via captured reference) vs HOW it's transported (string kwarg, the band-aid).

### Net complexity expected

Delete:
- node_name kwarg from 3 factories in _oracle.py (-15 LOC)
- _ = node_name placeholder at _oracle.py:68 (-1 LOC)
- Threading at _wiring.py:204, compiler.py:429, compiler.py:437, compiler.py:524 (-4 LOC)
- node_name="..." in tests/test_state_bus.py and tests/test_coverage_gaps.py (-10 LOC)
- Possibly factory.py:121 __name__ assignment if confirmed unnecessary (-2 LOC)

Add:
- Node instance flowing through factory signatures (no LOC change; replaces field_name + node_name with node)
- Possibly minor adjustments to internal helper signatures (~5 LOC)

Net: -20 to -25 LOC.

The win is again structural, not line count. The conflation that caused 7nan and kg8l is structurally resolved. A fourth redirect factory added in the future does NOT need to add a node_name parameter — it captures the Node directly.

### What stays the same

- All three closure factories still exist as separate functions
- Error messages still surface node.name (hyphenated form preserved)
- LangGraph routing still works (graph.add_node passes explicit names)
- Tests still verify the user's hyphenated name surfaces in errors

### Rejected alternatives

- "Collapse the three factories into one make_redirect(node, transform)" — three reviewers + user rejected. Different topologies.
- "Use a NodeIdentity dataclass with (name, field_name)" — primitive obsession in reverse; rule-of-three not met; pass Node.
- "Stop overriding __name__ entirely" — verify load-bearing first. If LangGraph or LangChain debug uses __name__, leave it but synthesize uniquely and stop conflating with field_name.

title: EPIC 2: Provider-quirk compat shim — neograph._llm_structured_compat
description:
## Architectural invariant (must hold after this epic)

Every LangChain BaseChatModel structured-output call site in neograph passes through a SINGLE compat shim that normalizes the underlying `with_structured_output(model, include_raw=True)` polymorphism into one typed result variant: Parsed | Raw | Failed. Provider-quirk fixes (DSML recovery, TypeError-on-include_raw, parsed=None+raw) are decorators on adapters at construction time, never try/except arms at dispatch time. Adding support for a new provider quirk is a new file, not a new branch.

## Phase 1 — Code archaeology (MANDATORY, BEFORE design)

Read and document in the bead notes:

1. src/neograph/_llm_dispatch.py::_call_structured — every branch of the 4-arm try/except ladder. For each branch: which provider failure does it absorb? Cite the original ticket (neograph-0tid is one).
2. src/neograph/_llm_retry.py::_DSML_PATTERN + _attempt_dsml_recovery — the central DSML detection helper.
3. src/neograph/_llm_retry.py::_invoke_json_with_retry — the json_mode/text retry concern.
4. src/neograph/_tool_loop.py — any DSML recovery call sites here.
5. Every other call site of llm.with_structured_output() across src/neograph/.

Output: a classification table in bead notes:
- Each branch in _call_structured: what error case does it handle? Is the recovery local or escalates to retry?
- Each DSML-detection call site: is detection the same regex (yes/no), what differs in the surrounding recovery flow?
- Are there OTHER provider-quirk patches scattered across the codebase that aren't in _call_structured (e.g., model-specific error handling in _tool_loop)?

## Phase 2 — Target design

READ docs/design/architecture-review-synthesis-2026-06-02.md AND the design field on this bead before proposing implementation.

## Phase 3 — Iterative elegant solution (keep iterating until elegant)

Apply SOLID + GRASP + DRY rigorously. Iterate until ALL of the following are true:

- New neograph._llm_structured_compat module defines a StructuredResult sum-type (Parsed | Raw | Failed) with a single typed factory function call_structured(llm, model, messages, config) -> StructuredResult.
- The 4-branch try/except in _llm_dispatch.py::_call_structured is REPLACED by a switch on the StructuredResult variant. No try/except for include_raw=True remains.

title: EPIC 1: Unify IR finalization via neograph._ir_normalize
description:
## Architectural invariant (must hold after this epic)

For every Node in a constructed Construct, the value of every IR field (fan_out_param, oracle_gen_type, scripted_fn, and any future inferred field) is identical regardless of which API surface built it. This invariant is enforced STRUCTURALLY by a single normalization site, not by parallel inference in two assembly paths plus structural guards policing drift.

## Phase 1 — Code archaeology (MANDATORY, BEFORE design)

Read and document in the bead notes:

1. _construct_builder.py::_cleanup_inputs_and_register — every updates[field] = ... write, the condition under which it fires, and the inferences it performs.
2. construct.py::Construct._normalize_fan_out_params + _normalize_oracle_gen_type — the retroactive-replay logic added by vgc1 + aqau.
3. loader.py::_apply_modifiers + _build_construct — what the YAML loader does NOT do.
4. _construct_validation.py::_check_fan_in_inputs — the parallel fan-out detection logic at validator time.
5. tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestConstructNormalizesEveryAtNodeOnlyIRField — the guard policing the drift.
6. tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestNoRuntimeFanOutDetection — the guard policing runtime band-aid recurrence.

Output: a classification table in bead notes:
- Which inferences are TRULY @node-specific (requires Python function with annotations)?
- Which inferences are IR-level (must produce identical IR regardless of surface)?
- Which inferences appear in BOTH _cleanup_inputs_and_register AND Construct._normalize_*?

## Phase 2 — Target design

READ docs/design/architecture-review-synthesis-2026-06-02.md AND the design field on this bead before proposing implementation.

## Phase 3 — Iterative elegant solution (keep iterating until elegant)

Apply SOLID + GRASP + DRY rigorously. Iterate until ALL of the following are true:

- New neograph._ir_normalize module exposes ONE entry point normalize_ir(construct) that all three assembly paths call exactly once.
- Each IR-level inference is a separate IrNormalizer Protocol implementation with applies_to + apply methods. Normalizers are REGISTERED, not enumerated.
- _construct_builder.py::_cleanup_inputs_and_register no longer writes updates[<IR-level-field>]. The @node-specific work stays.
- Construct._normalize_fan_out_params and _normalize_oracle_gen_type are DELETED. Construct.__init__ calls normalize_ir(self) once.
- The structural guard TestConstructNormalizesEveryAtNodeOnlyIRField is REPLACED by a stronger invariant: a test that checks normalize_ir is the ONLY writer of IR-level fields post-construction.
- The validator no longer needs parallel fan-out detection — fan_out_param is set by the time validation runs.

If the proposed diff adds another _normalize_<field> method to Construct, STOP. The iteration is incomplete.

## Phase 4 — Anti-band-aid clauses

- NO branching-over-polymorphism (N normalizers must be N Protocol implementations, not one function with N if/elif branches).
- NO dict-over-types (Protocol registry stays typed; use list[IrNormalizer] not dict[str, Callable]).
- NO new structural guards to police things that should be impossible by construction. If a new guard is proposed, ask: what abstraction would make this guard structurally redundant?
- Acceptance is NET-NEGATIVE complexity: lines deleted (from _construct_builder, construct.py, structural guards) must exceed lines added (in _ir_normalize).

## Phase 5 — Independent review (correctness AND elegance)

After implementation, spawn a feature-dev:code-reviewer agent with model: opus. The prompt must demand evaluation of:

1. CORRECTNESS — does the unification preserve every behavior of the three pre-fix paths?
2. ELEGANCE — does the solution apply the codebase's exemplary pattern (Protocol + registered implementations + boundary normalization, same as StateBus/normalize_outputs/fakes)?
3. NET COMPLEXITY — count lines added vs deleted across all touched files. Must be negative.
4. INVARIANT — is there a code path where IR can be inconsistent across surfaces? Try to construct one.
5. NO NEW HYDRA — can the next normalizer be added in 10 LOC in one file, or does it touch three places?

Reviewer must explicitly verdict ELEGANT or NOT, confidence ≥85. If NOT ELEGANT, reopen the ticket.

## Tickets subsumed by this epic

- aqau (already shipped — refactor into the new structure)
- vgc1 fan_out_param normalization (already shipped — refactor)
- fbk5 (aqau hardening: normalizer dispatch list) — fully subsumed
- gup9 (ghost state-model fields) — subsumed
- 3zai (split _construct_builder.py) — partially subsumed

## Acceptance

- src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py: Protocol + ≥2 registered normalizers + normalize_ir entry point
- Construct.__init__ delegates to normalize_ir; two _normalize_* methods deleted
- _construct_builder.py stops writing IR-level updates
- One structural guard deleted/replaced
- All existing tests pass
- Net diff: lines deleted > lines added across touched files
- Independent reviewer (opus) verdicts ELEGANT with confidence ≥85, written to bead notes
- bd close after reviewer ELEGANT verdict, not after make quality green
design:
## Target design (from architecture-review-synthesis-2026-06-02.md, Epic 1)

### Pattern

Protocol + registered implementations + boundary normalization. This is the SAME pattern the codebase has already perfected for StateBus + _DictStateBus/_ModelStateBus, for normalize_outputs/normalize_inputs, and for the test fakes layer. We are applying that pattern to IR-level field inference.

### Module shape

```python
# src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py

from typing import Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable

@runtime_checkable
class IrNormalizer(Protocol):
    """Infers a single IR field on a Node post-construction.

    Stateless. Idempotent. Called exactly once per Construct.__init__
    regardless of which API surface built the Construct.
    """
    def applies_to(self, node: Node) -> bool: ...
    def apply(self, node: Node, peer_field_names: set[str]) -> dict[str, Any]: ...


# Registered implementations (one per IR-level field):

class _FanOutParamNormalizer:
    def applies_to(self, node): ...   # has Each, dict-form inputs, fan_out_param is None
    def apply(self, node, peers): ...  # returns {"fan_out_param": <inferred>} or {}


class _OracleGenTypeNormalizer:
    def applies_to(self, node): ...   # has Oracle.merge_fn, oracle_gen_type is None
    def apply(self, node, peers): ...  # returns {"oracle_gen_type": <inferred>} or {}


_NORMALIZERS: list[IrNormalizer] = [
    _FanOutParamNormalizer(),
    _OracleGenTypeNormalizer(),
]


def normalize_ir(construct: Construct) -> None:
    """The single IR-level normalization entry point.

    Walks construct.nodes once, applies every registered normalizer, writes
    updates via model_copy. Idempotent: normalizers that find a field already
    set return {} and are no-ops.
    """
    peer_field_names = {field_name_for(it.name) for it in construct.nodes if ...}
    for i, item in enumerate(construct.nodes):
        if not isinstance(item, Node):
            continue
        updates: dict[str, Any] = {}
        for normalizer in _NORMALIZERS:
            if normalizer.applies_to(item):
                updates.update(normalizer.apply(item, peer_field_names))
        if updates:
            construct.nodes[i] = item.model_copy(update=updates)
```

### Call-site changes

1. `src/neograph/construct.py::Construct.__init__` — replace the two `self._normalize_*` calls with one `normalize_ir(self)` call. Delete both methods. Remove the `infer_oracle_gen_type` import.

2. `src/neograph/_construct_builder.py::_cleanup_inputs_and_register` — Phase 3 (deferred oracle_gen_type inference at line 577-583) DELETED. The fan_out_param assignment at line 565 can either stay (defensive, idempotent with the normalizer) or delete (cleaner). Recommend delete for elegance — normalize_ir owns IR-level fields exclusively.

3. `src/neograph/loader.py` — no change needed. YAML loader builds a Construct, Construct.__init__ now calls normalize_ir automatically.

4. `tests/test_structural_guards.py::TestConstructNormalizesEveryAtNodeOnlyIRField` — REPLACE with a stronger guard: AST-scan _construct_builder.py for any `updates[<IR-LEVEL-FIELD>] = ...` write, fail if any present. The IR-level field list is `{"fan_out_param", "oracle_gen_type"}` today. The new guard enforces: IR-level writes happen ONLY in _ir_normalize.

### Why Protocol not ABC

Protocol enables structural typing and runtime checking. New normalizers can be defined in any module (including downstream consumer code) without inheriting from a base class. Aligns with the StateBus Protocol pattern already in the codebase.

### Why list[IrNormalizer] not dict[str, Callable]

The list preserves the typed Protocol contract (`IrNormalizer` is a type, `Callable` is not). Future maintainers cannot accidentally insert a bare function and lose the `applies_to`/`apply` contract.

### Why one applies_to + one apply method (not just apply returning Optional)

Separating predicate from mutation is the GRASP Pure Fabrication principle — each method does one thing, both can be tested independently, the call site reads naturally.

### Rejected alternatives

- "Inline all inferences in normalize_ir as if/elif branches" — branching-over-polymorphism, the explicit anti-pattern.
- "Pydantic model_validator(mode='after') on Node" — would need to access peer producer set, which isn't available to Node in isolation; creates a circular import with merge_fn registry. Construct.__init__ is the natural place because peers are known there.
- "Push inference to Modifiable.__or__ at pipe time" — registry not always populated at pipe time for programmatic code. Rejected for the same reason as in aqau analysis.

### Net complexity expected

Add: ~80 LOC for _ir_normalize.py (Protocol + 2 normalizers + entry point).
Delete:
- ~30 LOC across two _normalize_* methods in construct.py
- ~10 LOC oracle_gen_type inference in _construct_builder.py Phase 3
- ~50 LOC TestConstructNormalizesEveryAtNodeOnlyIRField (replaced by ~25 LOC stronger guard)
- Net: -10 to -20 LOC

The win is structural (single source of truth), not line count. The structural-guard delta is what matters.
notes:
## Phase 1 — Code Archaeology (research atom neograph-i2rc.2, 2026-06-02)

### 1. _construct_builder.py::_cleanup_inputs_and_register (lines 518-593)
Single-pass loop over decorated @node dict. Three phases accumulate `updates`:
- **Phase 1 (inputs + fan_out_param), lines 543-565**: strips DI params, rewrites port/loop keys → `updates['inputs']`. Line 564-565: `if skip: updates['fan_out_param'] = next(iter(skip))` where `skip = fan_out_params.get(field)` (precomputed by _detect_fan_out_params at line 627).
- **Phase 2 (scripted_fn), lines 567-575**: `_register_node_scripted` → `updates['scripted_fn']`. TRULY @node-specific (needs the function sidecar).
- **Phase 3 (oracle_gen_type), lines 577-583**: `infer_oracle_gen_type(merge_fn)` → `updates['oracle_gen_type']` when gen_type differs from outputs. DUPLICATES construct.py logic exactly.

### 2. construct.py::Construct.__init__ + _normalize_* (lines 156-218)
`__init__` calls `_normalize_fan_out_params()` then `_normalize_oracle_gen_type()` BEFORE `_validate_node_chain(self)`.
- **_normalize_fan_out_params (163-195)**: for each Node with Each + dict-form inputs + fan_out_param unset, computes peer_field_names, finds the single `unknown` input key (not a peer, not self) → `model_copy(update={'fan_out_param': unknown[0]})`. Only fires when len(unknown)==1.
- **_normalize_oracle_gen_type (197-218)**: for each Node with oracle.merge_fn + oracle_gen_type unset, `infer_oracle_gen_type(merge_fn)` → model_copy. IDENTICAL inference to _construct_builder Phase 3.

### 3. loader.py::_apply_modifiers (244-275) + _build_construct (121-151)
Loader builds `Node | Oracle/Each/Loop/Operator` then wraps in `Construct(...)`. Sets NEITHER fan_out_param NOR oracle_gen_type — relies entirely on Construct.__init__ normalization. This is the proof the normalization MUST live in Construct.__init__ to serve the YAML surface.

### 4. _construct_validation.py::_check_fan_in_inputs (587-655)
Lines 611-629: PARALLEL fan-out detection. `fan_out_key = item.fan_out_param`; `_each_skip_used = (fan_out_key is not None)`. If fan_out_param unset BUT `has_each`, the FIRST unmatched input key is skipped as the fan-out receiver (band-aid for programmatic Each before normalization ran). After normalize_ir sets fan_out_param pre-validation, the `has_each and not _each_skip_used` fallback becomes dead for the single-receiver case.

### 5/6. Structural guards (test_structural_guards.py)
- **TestNoRuntimeFanOutDetection (4129)**: AST-asserts _extract_fan_in_dict has no state.keys() scan. Polices runtime band-aid recurrence. KEEP (orthogonal — runtime layer).
- **TestConstructNormalizesEveryAtNodeOnlyIRField (4168)**: AST-scans _construct_builder for `updates[<field>]` writes; requires each to be in PASSTHROUGH_FIELDS={inputs,scripted_fn} or NORMALIZED_FIELDS={fan_out_param,oracle_gen_type}. This is the drift-policing guard to REPLACE with the stronger 'normalize_ir is sole writer' invariant.

### Classification table
| Inference | TRULY @node-specific? | IR-level (surface-invariant)? | In BOTH builder + construct? |
|---|---|---|---|
| inputs (strip DI / rewrite ports) | YES (needs fn signature + DI bindings) | no | no (builder only) |
| scripted_fn | YES (needs the sidecar fn) | no | no (builder only) |
| **fan_out_param** | no | **YES** | builder Phase1(565) + construct._normalize_fan_out_params |
| **oracle_gen_type** | no | **YES** | builder Phase3(581) + construct._normalize_oracle_gen_type (IDENTICAL code) |

→ The two IR-level inferences (fan_out_param, oracle_gen_type) are EXACTLY the targets for _ir_normalize. inputs+scripted_fn stay in _construct_builder (@node-specific).

### Note on builder vs construct fan_out_param sourcing
Builder derives fan_out_param from `_detect_fan_out_params` (signature analysis: param with no producer + Each). Construct derives it from the 'single unknown input key' heuristic. Both must yield the SAME value. Normalizer must reproduce the construct.py heuristic (it's surface-agnostic; works on the assembled Construct). The @node path will ALSO converge because by the time Construct.__init__ runs, the @node builder has already set fan_out_param — normalizer is idempotent (skips when already set). RISK to verify in implementation: builder currently sets fan_out_param via model_copy at line 565; if we DELETE that (recommended in design), the normalizer must reproduce it for @node Each nodes too. Must test all three surfaces (parity rule).
## Architect Review (fresh-context architect, 2026-06-02)

Reviewed against Core Invariant, source files (construct.py 114-218, _construct_builder.py 293-319/518-593, _construct_validation.py 587-655, loader.py 244-275, _sidecar.py 79, test_obligation_r1r2.py 240-314, structural guards 4129-4269).

- [LOW] Invariant alignment: The decomposition is correct. Phase-1 classification (fan_out_param + oracle_gen_type are the only IR-level surface-invariant inferences; inputs/scripted_fn are @node-specific) matches the source exactly. Moving the two to a single normalize_ir(construct) called from Construct.__init__ is the right structural fix. loader.py confirms the YAML surface sets NEITHER field and relies on Construct.__init__, so the single site genuinely serves all three surfaces. Pattern (Protocol + registered list[IrNormalizer] + boundary normalization) matches the codebase's StateBus/normalize_outputs exemplar. Granularity (one applies_to + one apply per field) is right.

- [HIGH] Approach soundness / derivation divergence: The design proposes DELETING the fan_out_param write at builder:565 and letting _FanOutParamNormalizer reproduce it. THE TWO DERIVATIONS ARE NOT EQUIVALENT.
  - @node (_detect_fan_out_params, builder:318): derives from FUNCTION SIGNATURE param names — {p for p in pnames if p not in decorated and p not in di_params and p not in _ports}. Returns a SET; builder:565 does next(iter(skip)) — picks ARBITRARILY if 2+.
  - construct.py heuristic (_normalize_fan_out_params:187): derives from the INPUTS DICT keys (ni.by_name), excludes peers+self, fires ONLY when len(unknown)==1.
  These differ on the multi-unknown case. test_obligation_r1r2.py:271 (two_unmatched_is_error) proves the construct heuristic intentionally does NOT pick when 2+ unmatched (validator errors). The @node path with next(iter(skip)) would have PICKED one and succeeded. So for an @node Each node with 2+ non-peer/non-DI/non-port params, deleting :565 changes behavior: today @node picks arbitrarily; post-delete the normalizer no-ops (len!=1) and the validator path decides. This is a real behavioral delta, not idempotent.
  Suggestion: Either (a) KEEP builder:565 (the design lists this as an allowed option — 'stay, defensive, idempotent'); the normalizer's applies_to no-ops because @node already set the field, so there is no double-write and no drift — OR (b) before deleting :565, prove via a three-surface test that no @node Each fixture produces a 2+ -element skip set (the DI/port stripping likely reduces it to 1 in practice, but that must be ASSERTED, not assumed). Recommend (a) for safety + (b) as the test that justifies eventually doing (a)-with-delete. Do NOT delete :565 on the bare claim of idempotency — the derivations are not the same function, only coincidentally equal in the single-key case.

- [MEDIUM] Validator parallel detection (611-629) removal: The design says 'validator no longer needs parallel fan-out detection.' After normalize_ir runs pre-validation, the single-receiver programmatic case gets fan_out_param set, so the has_each and not _each_skip_used fallback IS dead FOR len(unknown)==1. BUT it is NOT dead for: (1) 2+ unknown keys (normalizer no-ops, fan_out_param stays None, has_each fallback still skips exactly one then errors on the second — this is the behavior test:271 and test:287 lock in); (2) 0 unknown keys; (3) the fan_out_param-set + extra-key double-fire BUG that test:287 documents (match='mystery'). If you remove 611-629 in THIS epic you will change/break those three tested behaviors. Suggestion: DO NOT remove the validator fallback in this epic. Scope this epic to unifying the WRITE site (normalize_ir as sole writer). The validator's defensive skip is a separate concern (the 287 double-fire is a known bug with its own ticket surface). Leave 611-629 as-is; note in the epic that it becomes partially-dead-but-defensive. Removing it is a follow-up that must first resolve the test:287 double-fire semantics.

- [LOW] Pattern compliance / circular import: construct.py already imports infer_oracle_gen_type from _sidecar and field_name_for/normalize_inputs. _ir_normalize.py will need Node (node.py), normalize_inputs (_normalize), field_name_for (naming), infer_oracle_gen_type (_sidecar). construct.py imports node.py already (line 34), so construct.py -> _ir_normalize -> node.py is fine (node.py must not import _ir_normalize or construct — verify it doesn't). _sidecar import should MOVE from construct.py into _ir_normalize.py (construct.py no longer calls it directly). No cycle: _ir_normalize -> {node, _normalize, naming, _sidecar}; none of those import _ir_normalize. construct.py -> _ir_normalize is the only new edge. Confirm node.py has no import-time dependency on construct.py (it defines fan_out_param at node.py:169 as a plain field, so it should be clean).

- [LOW] oracle_gen_type coverage after deletion: Tracing — @node oracle node: builder Phase-3 (578-583) sets it today; if deleted, normalize_ir's _OracleGenTypeNormalizer must catch it. Its applies_to (oracle.merge_fn present AND oracle_gen_type is None) fires for the @node case identically because builder Phase-3 and construct._normalize_oracle_gen_type are BYTE-IDENTICAL inference (infer_oracle_gen_type(merge_fn), gen_type is not None and is not outputs). Unlike fan_out_param, there is NO derivation divergence here — both call the same _sidecar function. SAFE to delete builder Phase-3 AND construct._normalize_oracle_gen_type and let the normalizer own it. This is the clean half of the epic.

- [MEDIUM] Net-negative complexity claim (-10 to -20 LOC): Optimistic. Protocol + 2 normalizer classes (each with applies_to + apply + docstrings) + registry + normalize_ir walker is realistically ~90-110 LOC, not 80. Deletions: ~30 (two construct methods) + ~7 (builder Phase-3) + guard replacement (~50 deleted, ~25-40 added). If builder:565 STAYS (recommended), you delete ~7 fewer lines. Net could be slightly POSITIVE. Recommend: drop the hard 'net diff must be negative' acceptance gate OR scope it to 'net structural-guard + duplicated-inference LOC negative' rather than total LOC. The win is single-source-of-truth, which the epic itself acknowledges ('the win is structural, not line count'). The acceptance criterion contradicts the design's own caveat — fix the criterion.

- [MEDIUM] Replacement guard 'normalize_ir is the ONLY writer of IR-level fields post-construction': AST-checkable but the proposed framing (scan _construct_builder for updates[<IR-field>]) is too narrow — it only polices ONE file. A node.fan_out_param = / object.__setattr__(n, 'fan_out_param', ...) anywhere else evades it (test:307 already uses object.__setattr__). Concrete suggestion: guard scans ALL of src/neograph/*.py (excluding _ir_normalize.py) for (a) Assign/AnnAssign targets of form <x>.fan_out_param / <x>.oracle_gen_type, (b) model_copy(update={...}) calls whose dict literal contains those keys, (c) object.__setattr__(_, 'fan_out_param'|'oracle_gen_type', _). Allowlist only _ir_normalize.py and node.py field declarations. This is AST-checkable and not brittle if you match attribute NAME on the IR-level field set, not exact call shape. Keep the existing TestNoRuntimeFanOutDetection guard (orthogonal — runtime layer, not write-site).

- [LOW] Idempotency: Confirmed correct. @node path sets fan_out_param/oracle_gen_type BEFORE Construct.__init__ runs (in _cleanup_inputs_and_register, before the Construct(...) call at builder:639). Both normalizers' applies_to gate on 'field is None', so they no-op on already-set @node IR. Idempotency holds REGARDLESS of whether :565 is kept — that is exactly why keeping :565 is safe.

- [LOW] Alternative not fully weighed: The design rejects model_validator(mode='after') on Node (needs peers — correct rejection). But it does not consider making normalize_ir a model_validator(mode='after') on CONSTRUCT, where peers ARE available. That would make normalization automatic for EVERY Construct construction path including any future bypass of __init__. Minor — current __init__ call is fine and more explicit. Note it as considered-and-deferred rather than unconsidered.

Overall: NEEDS_REFINEMENT.
Two changes before implementation: (1) Do NOT delete builder:565 fan_out_param write on the idempotency claim alone — the @node signature derivation and the construct inputs-dict heuristic diverge on the 2+ unknown-key case (proven by test_obligation_r1r2.py:271). Keep :565 (design-sanctioned option) or gate deletion behind a three-surface test proving no @node Each fixture yields a 2+ skip set. (2) Do NOT remove validator 611-629 in this epic — it remains live for 0/2+ unknown keys and the documented double-fire bug (test:287); removing it changes tested behavior. Scope this epic to the WRITE-site unification only. Also: relax the net-negative-LOC acceptance gate (contradicts the design's own 'win is structural' note) and broaden the replacement guard to scan all src files for IR-field writes, not just _construct_builder. The oracle_gen_type half is clean and safe to fully unify.
## Triage verdict (atom neograph-i2rc.4)
NEEDS_REFINEMENT — two substantive findings, both autonomously resolvable. Refine atom neograph-edps created with the adjusted approach (keep builder:565, keep validator 611-629, relax net-LOC gate, broaden sole-writer guard, relocate infer_oracle_gen_type import). Proceeding via refine, not blocking for user.
## Refined plan AGREED (atom neograph-edps)
The architect refinements (1-5) are accepted as the implementation contract. Authoritative scope:
- ADD src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py: IrNormalizer Protocol (applies_to/apply) + _FanOutParamNormalizer + _OracleGenTypeNormalizer + _NORMALIZERS list + normalize_ir(construct). infer_oracle_gen_type imported HERE.
- construct.py: __init__ calls normalize_ir(self) once before _validate_node_chain; DELETE _normalize_fan_out_params + _normalize_oracle_gen_type + the _sidecar import.
- _construct_builder.py: DELETE Phase 3 (577-583 oracle_gen_type). KEEP Phase 1 line 565 fan_out_param write (additive @node parity — normalizer is idempotent and only fills YAML/programmatic).
- VALIDATOR _check_fan_in_inputs 611-629: UNCHANGED this epic (defensive, still live for 0/2+/double-fire cases).
- GUARD: replace TestConstructNormalizesEveryAtNodeOnlyIRField with a sole-writer guard scanning ALL src/neograph/*.py for fan_out_param/oracle_gen_type writes, allowlisting _ir_normalize.py + Node constructor passthrough + the sanctioned builder:565 fan_out_param write (which is parity-additive, not drift).
- ACCEPTANCE: structural single-source-of-truth is the goal; net LOC may be ~neutral (criterion relaxed). Three-surface parity tests mandatory.
Note: builder:565 stays, so the guard must allowlist that ONE builder write of fan_out_param (it is the @node signature-derived value, computed before Construct.__init__; the normalizer does not overwrite it). The sole-writer invariant applies to oracle_gen_type strictly (normalize_ir only) and to fan_out_param with the documented builder:565 exception.
## Regression Test (atom neograph-i2rc.5)

title: Audit + normalize ALL IR fields with @node-path-only assignment (class fix, not instance)
description:
## Architectural property (the invariant)

The CLAUDE.md claim — 'all three API surfaces (declarative, @node, programmatic/YAML) produce the same internal IR' — must hold for EVERY field on Node and Construct. Any IR field whose value depends on which API surface built the node violates this invariant and is a latent surface-divergence bug of the same class as fan_out_param (vgc1).

vgc1 fixed ONE instance (fan_out_param). aqau closes the class.

## Anti-band-aid clause

IF YOUR FIX TARGETS A SINGLE FIELD (e.g., 'add oracle_gen_type normalization'), STOP. The task is to AUDIT every IR field set during @node assembly, classify each, and produce a complete fix that handles the class — not a second one-field special case sitting next to _normalize_fan_out_params.

If the diff adds another '_normalize_<field>' method per field, that is a band-aid pattern. The right shape is either:
(a) a single normalization pass that infers every applicable field, OR
(b) move each field's inference into Node.__init__ / Modifiable.__or__ so the field is set at the moment the modifier is applied (regardless of construct assembly path)

Decide which shape is correct and document the choice in the design field BEFORE writing code.

## Required audit (mandatory, BEFORE implementation)

Grep _construct_builder.py for every `updates[<field>] = ...` write in _cleanup_inputs_and_register and related @node-assembly helpers. For each discovered field, produce a classification table:

| Field | Set by @node | Set by Node() ctor | Set by Modifiable.__or__ | Set by YAML loader | Divergence? |

Paste the table into the bead's notes field. Every row marked 'Divergence: yes' is a sibling bug to vgc1.

Known starting points (per reviewer aa14ccfd):
- fan_out_param — fixed by vgc1 (Construct._normalize_fan_out_params)
- oracle_gen_type — set only by _cleanup_inputs_and_register; programmatic Oracle(merge_fn=type_transforming_fn) gets None
- scripted_fn — possibly OK (set by programmatic Node(scripted_fn=...) constructor too)
- inputs — possibly OK (set everywhere)

The audit must enumerate every field that appears in 'updates' dict in _construct_builder.py and verify whether the programmatic path also sets it.

## Required architectural shape (after audit)

Based on the classification table, either:

**Option A** — Generic Construct normalization pass:
`Construct._normalize_post_init_ir_fields()` runs once after the existing model_copy loop. Internally calls _normalize_fan_out_params, _normalize_oracle_gen_type, and any other divergent fields. _normalize_fan_out_params is RENAMED to fit the new structure.

**Option B** — Push inference earlier:
Modifiable.__or__ for Each computes fan_out_param at pipe time. Modifiable.__or__ for Oracle computes oracle_gen_type. By the time any Construct is built, all fields are already set. _normalize_fan_out_params becomes dead code and is removed.

Option B is architecturally cleaner (the reviewer flagged this as the deeper fix). Document the trade-off in design field. If Option A is chosen, justify why.

## Breadth tests that MUST break a one-field implementation

1. **oracle_gen_type via Modifiable.__or__**: `Node(...) | Oracle(merge_fn=fn_that_changes_type)` — assert node.oracle_gen_type is set on the IR Node after construction.
2. **oracle_gen_type via YAML**: equivalent YAML spec — assert node.oracle_gen_type is set after load_spec.
3. **Three-surface parity**: build the same logical Oracle node via @node, programmatic, and YAML; assert all three produce identical IR (every field equal).
4. **Structural guard extension**: TestNoRuntimeFanOutDetection becomes TestNoRuntimeIRFieldRecovery — forbid runtime band-aids that recompute ANY '@node-only' IR field from state.

## Independent-review gate (acceptance criterion)

After implementation, spawn a fresh feature-dev:code-reviewer agent with this exact prompt: 'Review the fix for neograph-aqau. Confirm with high confidence (>=90) whether the implementation handles the CLASS of bug (IR-field surface drift) rather than just enumerating known instances. Specifically: (a) is there a structural guard that catches future @node-only assignments without a matching normalizer? (b) was the audit table complete (every `updates[...]` write classified)? (c) for any field claimed as fixed, can you build a programmatic equivalent that arrives at Construct.__init__ with the field set?' Paste the verdict.

## Acceptance

- Audit table in notes covering every field assigned in _cleanup_inputs_and_register
- Design field documents Option A vs B trade-off and choice
- Three-surface parity tests for every divergent field discovered (currently known: oracle_gen_type)
- Structural guard rejects future @node-only field writes that lack normalization OR pipe-time inference
- Independent reviewer verdict 'class-level fix', high confidence

notes:
## Reproduction
Test test_oracle_gen_type_set_on_programmatic_oracle_with_merge_fn confirms programmatic Node()|Oracle(merge_fn='X') with X: list[T] -> U arrives at Construct.__init__ with oracle_gen_type=None. The @node path runs _construct_builder.py:583 which infers and sets it; other surfaces don't.

## Audit table — every IR field assigned in _cleanup_inputs_and_register

| Field | Site | Set by Node()? | Set by Modifiable.__or__? | Set by YAML loader? | Drift vs @node? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| inputs | line 563 | YES (constructor) | YES (passthrough) | YES (loader) | NO — passthrough |
| fan_out_param | line 565 | NO | NO (band-aid before vgc1) | NO | FIXED by vgc1 + ta43 (Construct._normalize_fan_out_params) |
| scripted_fn | line 575 | YES via Node(scripted_fn=...) | YES (modifier passthrough) | YES (loader) | NO — set at constructor |
| oracle_gen_type | line 583 | NO | NO | NO | YES — DRIFT, scope of aqau |

Only oracle_gen_type drifts. Three other 'updates[...]' writes are passthroughs of fields already set by other surfaces.

## Architectural decision — Option A vs B
Option A (generic Construct normalization pass): extend _normalize_fan_out_params or add a sibling _normalize_oracle_gen_type. Pro: consistent with vgc1 fix shape. Con: each new divergent field adds a new method.

Option B (push inference earlier into Modifiable.__or__): when Oracle is applied via pipe, run infer_oracle_gen_type and set the field at that moment. Pro: by Construct construction, all fields already set; both _normalize and _construct_builder Phase 3 become redundant.

Decision: Option B is architecturally cleaner per reviewer. BUT — Modifiable.__or__ runs at pipe time, before the merge_fn is necessarily registered. The infer requires the merge_fn to be reachable via _merge_fn_registry, which only happens after @merge_fn decoration runs. For programmatic code that pipes Oracle BEFORE the @merge_fn decoration fires, Option B is unsafe.

Final: Option A. Add inference inside Construct._normalize_fan_out_params (rename to _normalize_post_init_ir_fields). At Construct.__init__ time the registry is populated, the inference is safe. The Phase 3 inference in _construct_builder also stays (defensive layering: @node path can still set it).

Idempotency: like fan_out_param normalization, only fires when oracle_gen_type is None — both paths converge on the inferred value.

- Option A (Construct.__init__) vs B (pipe time) — Option A correctly chosen (Q3: confidence 90)
- YAML test exercises load_spec() properly (Q4: confidence 95)
- No hidden drift in other IR fields today (Q5: confidence 85)

Net: the structural guard IS present and functional; the verdict's load-bearing premise is incorrect. Updated reading: STRUCTURAL CLASS-LEVEL FIX.

Added mutation test (test_mutation_unannotated_updates_write_is_detected) that synthesizes an unannotated updates[<str>] = ... pattern and verifies the scanner logic catches it. Makes the guard's behavior self-evident rather than relying on review interpretation.

IF YOUR FIX ADDS YET ANOTHER 'node_name: str | None = None' KWARG TO YET ANOTHER CLOSURE FACTORY, STOP. If the diff just adds kwargs with default=None, it is a band-aid. The default=None silently preserves the broken fallback for any caller — internal or external — that omits the kwarg.

title: 51m7 band-aid: recursive validator with ambient_producers; depth>=2 sub-constructs uncovered
description:
## Architectural property (the invariant)

Context-field producer validation must hold at compile time for inner Node.context references at ANY depth of sub-construct nesting (parent -> sub -> sub-sub -> sub-sub-sub ...). The validator must be recursive over construct topology, not a special case for depth-1.

The 'if it compiles, it runs' positioning depends on this invariant. Today (post commit 0330cea), the validator catches typos at depth 1 only and silently passes them at depth >= 2 — independent reviewer aa14ccfd confirmed.

## Anti-band-aid clause

IF YOUR FIX ADDS ANOTHER 'elif' BRANCH OR ANOTHER ENUMERATED CASE, STOP AND REDERIVE. The existing 'elif' branch at _construct_validation.py:312 MUST be REMOVED, not extended. The acceptance test is whether the new diff is NET NEGATIVE in special-case branches.

## Required architectural shape

Refactor _validate_node_chain to:

```python
def _validate_node_chain(
    construct: Construct,
    *,
    ambient_producers: list[Producer] | None = None,
) -> None:
```

Inner sub-constructs are validated by a recursive call:
```python
_validate_node_chain(item, ambient_producers=producers + [...])
```

The context-field check uses `known_fields = {p.field_name for p in (ambient_producers or []) + producers}` so inner nodes see both the sub-construct's own port AND the parent's producers. One code path. Arbitrary depth.

## Breadth/depth tests that MUST break a special-case implementation

1. **Depth-3 typo**: parent -> sub -> sub-sub where the sub-sub's inner Node.context=['typo'] — must raise ConstructError at Construct(parent, ...) time.
2. **Depth-2 happy path**: parent -> sub -> sub-sub where the deepest context is produced by the parent — compiles cleanly.
3. **Depth-2 forward reference**: parent has producer X AFTER the sub-construct in node order; sub-sub's context=['X'] — current architecture rejects forward refs at top level; the recursive validator must apply the same rule consistently.
4. **Mixed nesting**: parent contains [seed, sub_A, sub_B] where sub_B contains a sub-sub referencing a context produced by sub_A's output — verify the producer aggregation.

## Audit step (mandatory)

Before implementing: grep the codebase for OTHER 'construct.input is None' gates in validation logic. Each one is a potential band-aid sibling. Report findings in the bead notes.

## Independent-review gate (acceptance criterion)

After implementation, spawn a fresh feature-dev:code-reviewer agent with this exact prompt: 'Review the fix for neograph-ta43. Confirm with high confidence (>=90) whether this is a structural recursive solution or a band-aid that handles depth 1-2 only. Specifically test: does the validator catch a typo at depth 3? Does the implementation REMOVE the prior elif branch rather than extend it?' Paste the reviewer's verdict into the bead notes. If the reviewer reports band-aid, REOPEN the ticket.

title: Sub-construct context-field validation (close compile-time gap)
description: P1. Validator at _construct_validation.py:296 skips context-field producer check when construct.input is not None (i.e., sub-constructs). Implication: typoed context inside a sub-construct compiles cleanly; the StateMissingError from izo1-B fires only at runtime on first dispatch. Breaks the 'if it compiles, it runs' positioning for sub-constructs. Per audit doc Q3, two valid resolutions: (a) tighten — sub-construct parent must populate every declared context field, validator walks both layers; (b) document explicit exemption with runtime fail-loud as the contract. Pick one; today's behavior is neither. Acceptance: documented rule in CLAUDE.md + matching validator behavior + 2 should_fail fixtures.
design:
## Root Cause
The validator's per-node context check skips when construct.input is not None (i.e. for every sub-construct). Reason: at the sub-construct's own validation pass, producers contain only the sub-construct's port (neo_subgraph_input), not the parent's producers. The validator never crossed the boundary.

## Fix Approach
When _validate_node_chain processes a Construct that contains a sub-Construct (item with .input != None), recursively walk that sub-construct's nodes and validate each context field against the PARENT's producers (already collected).

Concrete: in _validate_node_chain, after building parent producers, iterate top-level items; for each sub-Construct found, walk its .nodes and check every Node.context entry against parent producer field_names. Use field_name_for() consistently.

Core Invariant: 'context typos are caught at compile time regardless of whether the consuming node lives at the top level or inside a sub-construct.'
