title: Add multimodal/vision support for image prompts
description:
Neograph should support image inputs in prompts for VLM (Vision Language Model) calls. Currently prompts are text-only. The image pipeline needs to send base64 or file-path images alongside text to models like Gemini 2.5 Flash.

## Requirements

1. Image as a first-class prompt variable — e.g. ${image} in inline prompts, or an image field in the prompt template
2. The prompt compiler converts image paths/base64 into multimodal LangChain message content (text + image_url blocks)
3. Works with standard @node(mode='think') — no special mode needed
4. Support both file paths and raw base64 strings
5. From the user perspective, it's just a prompt + an image — same ergonomics as text-only nodes

## Use case

The DiveMesh image pipeline VLM curation sends candidate images to a vision model for quality/relevance scoring. Currently uses raw ChatOpenAI. Should use neograph instead for consistent LLM wiring, observability, and retry logic.

## Possible design

- Detect ${image:variable_name} or ${image} in prompt template
- Resolve to file path or base64 string from input data
- Build multimodal HumanMessage: [{type: text, text: ...}, {type: image_url, image_url: {url: data:image/...}}]
- Fall through existing invoke_structured path (json_mode / structured output)
design:
## Core Invariant
Text-only inline prompts must produce identical output — the multimodal path activates ONLY when ${image:...} placeholders are present.

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Add _IMAGE_RE regex and _resolve_image utility (_llm.py)
- `_IMAGE_RE = re.compile(r"\$\{image:([^}]+)\}")` — matches `${image:field_name}` or `${image:field.sub}`
- `_resolve_image(path_or_b64: str) -> str` — converts file path or base64 to `data:mime;base64,...` URI
- Handles: absolute/relative file paths, raw base64, pre-formed data URIs (pass-through)
- Uses mimetypes.guess_type for MIME detection, fallback to image/png

### 2. Add _compile_multimodal_prompt helper (_llm.py)
- Called by _compile_prompt when _IMAGE_RE.findall(template) is non-empty
- Splits template on _IMAGE_RE pattern boundaries → alternating text/image segments
- For each text segment: run _substitute_vars to resolve remaining ${var} placeholders → text content block
- For each image segment: _resolve_var to get the value, _resolve_image to convert → image_url content block
- Returns `[{"role": "user", "content": [block1, block2, ...]}]`

### 3. Modify _compile_prompt inline path (_llm.py:258-260)
- Before existing _substitute_vars call, check `_IMAGE_RE.search(template)`
- If found: delegate to _compile_multimodal_prompt
- If not: existing fast path unchanged

### 4. Guard render_prompt inspector (_llm.py ~line 1014)
- If content is a list (content blocks), format as "[multimodal: N blocks]" instead of treating as string

### 5. Tests (test_inline_prompts.py)
- Test: ${image:photo} with file path produces image_url content block
- Test: ${image:photo} with base64 string produces data URI
- Test: ${image:photo} with pre-formed data URI passes through
- Test: mixed text + image produces correct content block ordering
- Test: multiple images in one prompt
- Test: text-only prompt unchanged (regression guard)
- Test: ${image:obj.field} dotted path works

### Files to modify
1. `src/neograph/_llm.py` — _IMAGE_RE, _resolve_image, _compile_multimodal_prompt, _compile_prompt guard, render_prompt guard
2. `tests/test_inline_prompts.py` — new TestMultimodalPrompt class
acceptance_criteria:
1. Inline prompts with ${image} or ${image:field_name} produce multimodal LangChain messages
2. Supports file paths (read + base64 encode) and raw base64 strings
3. Works with json_mode and structured output strategies
4. Existing text-only prompts unaffected (backward compatible)
5. Tests for the new multimodal prompt compilation
6. DiveMesh image pipeline VLM curation successfully uses it
notes:
## Research Findings

### Code Paths Affected

1. **`_llm.py:258-260` (_compile_prompt inline path)** — currently returns `[{"role": "user", "content": string}]`. Must produce content blocks for image prompts.
2. **`_llm.py:241-243` (_substitute_vars)** — regex replacement produces flat string. Cannot interleave image content blocks. Need a new function that splits template into text/image segments and builds content blocks.
3. **`_llm.py:195` (_VAR_RE)** — matches `${anything}`. A new `_IMAGE_RE` regex needed for `${image:field_name}` pattern.
4. **`_llm.py:555-557` (retry path)** — retries add `{"content": raw_text}`. This is fine for multimodal — retries reference text, not images. No change needed.
5. **`_llm.py:574-607` (_call_structured)** — passes messages through to `llm.invoke()`. LangChain handles content blocks natively. No change needed.
6. **`renderers.py` (RenderedInput)** — image fields referenced via `${image:X}` bypass the rendering pipeline entirely. `_resolve_var` is called on the `image:X` path to get the value, but the value is NOT rendered as text — it is converted to a data URI and placed in an image_url content block. No rendering changes needed.
7. **`_dispatch.py:_render_input`** — inline prompts get `ri.raw` (raw Pydantic objects). Image data (file path or base64 string) is a string field on the model, so `_resolve_var` can access it via dotted path. No change needed.

### Key Insight: Text-Only Fast Path
The `_IMAGE_RE.findall(template)` check at the top of the inline path means zero overhead for text-only prompts. Only prompts containing `${image:...}` enter the multimodal compilation path.

### Relevant Code
- `_llm.py:185` — _is_inline_prompt
- `_llm.py:195` — _VAR_RE regex
- `_llm.py:198-238` — _resolve_var (dotted path resolution, BAML rendering for BaseModel)
- `_llm.py:241-243` — _substitute_vars (regex replace)
- `_llm.py:246-260` — _compile_prompt (inline path)
- `_llm.py:574-607` — _call_structured (passes messages through, no content inspection)
- `_dispatch.py:217-236` — _render_input (raw vs rendered decision)
- `tests/test_inline_prompts.py` — 29 existing tests

### Risks & Edge Cases
1. **Image in template-ref prompts** — Not supported. Template-ref delegates to consumer prompt_compiler. Consumer can build multimodal messages themselves.
2. **Image field in RenderedInput BAML rendering** — Not a problem since `${image:X}` is a separate namespace from `${X}`. The image field is never passed through describe_value.
3. **retry path with multimodal initial message** — Retries append string-content messages. LangChain handles mixed content types in conversation history.
4. **render_prompt inspector** — Assumes content is string. Will need a guard for content blocks (display "[multimodal]" or similar).
5. **File size** — Large images (>10MB base64) could produce very long data URIs. Consider a warning.
## Architect Review

- [LOW] _IMAGE_RE pattern: `\${image:([^}]+)}` is clean. The `image:` prefix clearly distinguishes from text vars. No collision risk with existing `${var}` or `${var.field}` patterns.

- [LOW] _resolve_image utility: File I/O is acceptable in the compile path — images are typically <5MB, read once. The `mimetypes.guess_type` approach is standard. Fallback to `image/png` is safe.

- [LOW] _compile_multimodal_prompt: Splitting on _IMAGE_RE boundaries and building content blocks is the right approach. `re.split` with a capturing group gives alternating text/image segments naturally.

- [LOW] render_prompt inspector guard: Displaying "[multimodal: N blocks]" for content block messages is clean. No functional impact — purely diagnostic.

- [MEDIUM] Template-ref prompts: The design explicitly does NOT handle images in template-ref prompts. This is correct for now — consumers can build multimodal messages in their prompt_compiler. But the DiveMesh consumer may need guidance. Suggest: export `resolve_image` as a public utility they can use.

- [LOW] Layer discipline: All changes are in `_llm.py` (prompt compilation layer). No IR, compiler, or factory changes. Correct.

Overall: ALL_LOW
## Regression Test
- Test: tests/test_inline_prompts.py::TestMultimodalPrompt (7 tests)
- Status: FAILING (expected -- TDD red step)
- Tests: content block generation, file path read, data URI passthrough, mixed text+image ordering, multiple images, text-only regression, dotted path
close_reason: Implemented: ${image:field} in inline prompts produces multimodal content blocks

title: Oracle merge_prompt silently drops caller's llm_config (structured vs json_mode conflation)
description:
## What

`Oracle(merge_prompt=...)` triggers an LLM merge call via `_wiring._merge_one_group → invoke_structured(...)`. The call passes `model_tier`, `prompt_template`, `input_data`, `output_model`, `config`, but NOT `llm_config`. As a result the merge call ignores the caller's explicit `output_strategy` preference (set via `@node(llm_config=...)` or `construct_from_functions(..., llm_config=...)`) and falls back to `invoke_structured`'s default strategy (`"structured"`).

This silently flips the transport path from NeoGraph-native JSON parsing to LangChain's `with_structured_output()`, changing both correctness behavior (fence stripping vs. none) and failure modes (framework-side retries with error feedback vs. provider-side structured output enforcement).

## Current code (src/neograph/_wiring.py, _merge_one_group)

```python
if oracle.merge_prompt:
    from neograph._llm import invoke_structured

    if oracle.merge_pre_process is not None:
        input_data = oracle.merge_pre_process(variants)
    else:
        input_data = variants[0] if variants else None

    used_fallback = False
    try:
        merged = invoke_structured(
            model_tier=oracle.merge_model,
            prompt_template=oracle.merge_prompt,
            input_data=input_data,
            output_model=output_model,
            config=config,
            # llm_config NOT passed — loses caller's explicit choice
        )
    ...
```

## Evidence — piarch rehearsal UC-fix1 traces

Across 26 LLM calls in the rehearsal on `BR-UC-001`:
- 23 calls used `strategy=json_mode` (correct — explicitly set via `construct_from_functions(..., llm_config={"output_strategy": "json_mode"})` on the sub-constructs)
- 3 calls used `strategy=structured` (wrong — the 3 Oracle merge_prompt paths: `uc/merge-internal-research`, `uc/merge-si-stakeholders`, `uc/merge-extensions`)

All 3 structured-strategy calls are Oracle merges. Generators inside the same sub-construct run `json_mode` as declared; the Oracle merge silently switches strategy.

Concrete failure that surfaced: `uc/merge-external-research` merge call — DeepSeek R1 returned fenced JSON (```json\n{...}\n```). Under `json_mode` NeoGraph's `_parse_json_response → _extract_json` strips markdown fences and succeeds. Under the silent `structured` fallback, LangChain passes the raw fenced text to `model.model_validate_json()` which fails with:

```
pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for ExternalResearch
  Invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1
  input_value='```json\\n{\\n  "comparable_systems": ...  "sources": []\\n}\\n```'
```

The caller (piarch) had explicitly opted into json_mode via `construct_from_functions(..., llm_config={"output_strategy": "json_mode"}) | Oracle(merge_prompt=...)`, but the merge call silently ignored that choice.

## Why

Likely an oversight: when `_merge_one_group` was built, the invoke_structured signature grew an llm_config parameter later, and the existing merge path wasn't updated to thread it through.

Note: `structured` and `json_mode` are semantically different and both legitimate. This bug is NOT about picking a better default — it's about honoring the caller's explicit configuration. Flipping the default to `json_mode` would silently change semantics for callers who explicitly wanted LangChain's provider-native structured output path.

## Fix

Propagate the enclosing Node's (or Construct's) `llm_config` to the merge `invoke_structured` call. Two cases to cover:

### Case 1: @node-level Oracle (`@node(ensemble_n=3, merge_prompt=..., llm_config=...)`)

The Oracle is synthesized from the @node decorator. `_merge_one_group` receives the Node. Thread `node.llm_config`:

```python
merged = invoke_structured(
    model_tier=oracle.merge_model,
    prompt_template=oracle.merge_prompt,
    input_data=input_data,
    output_model=output_model,
    config=config,
    llm_config=node.llm_config,  # NEW
)
```

### Case 2: construct-level Oracle (`construct_from_functions(..., llm_config=X) | Oracle(merge_prompt=...)`)

The Oracle wraps a Construct, not a single Node. The construct's `llm_config` needs to reach `_merge_one_group`. Options:

- **(a)** Store `construct.llm_config` on the synthesized barrier/merge Node at compile time, so `node.llm_config` is populated correctly for both cases.
- **(b)** Add a `merge_llm_config` field to `Oracle` itself for explicit override; if unset, fall back to the enclosing construct's llm_config.

Prefer (a) — it makes the merge call inherit the caller's explicit choice with zero extra wiring on the consumer side.

### Optional addition

For cases where the merge should use a DIFFERENT strategy than the generators (rare but legitimate — e.g. generators use `structured` with provider function calling, merge uses `json_mode` for tolerant parsing), add an explicit `Oracle(merge_llm_config=...)` override. Don't require it; default to inheriting.

## Acceptance

- `_merge_one_group`'s `invoke_structured` call receives `llm_config` derived from the enclosing Node or Construct.
- For @node-level Oracle: `node.llm_config` flows through.
- For construct-level Oracle: `construct.llm_config` is accessible at merge time (option (a) — stored on the compiled merge node).
- Unit test: Oracle(merge_prompt=...) on a Node/Construct with `llm_config={"output_strategy": "json_mode"}` — assert the merge call is invoked with that strategy. Inspect via monkeypatching `invoke_structured` or reading the structlog `strategy` field.
- Regression test: existing tests still pass (no change to default behavior when `llm_config` is unset — merge still uses `invoke_structured`'s default, which is `strategy="structured"`).
- Integration check (downstream validation in piarch): after fix, piarch rehearsal trace on `BR-UC-001` shows zero LLM calls with `strategy=structured` (all inherit `json_mode` from piarch's explicit `llm_config` declarations).

## Context

Surfaced during piarch's `piarch-rhsu0` epic where multiple Oracle merge_prompt paths were newly introduced. The piarch side was already doing the right thing (declaring `output_strategy: json_mode` on sub-constructs), but NeoGraph's Oracle dispatch was dropping the config. Tracked downstream in piarch as `piarch-7j1he` (derive-business-rules prompt-framework mismatch) — that bug and this one surfaced in the same rehearsal.
design:
## Root Cause
make_oracle_merge_fn and _merge_one_group both call invoke_structured without llm_config. The enclosing node's llm_config is available at compile time but not threaded through.

## Fix Approach
1. Add llm_config param to make_oracle_merge_fn, close over it in the merge closure
2. Pass node.llm_config at all 3 call sites (compiler.py:443, compiler.py:354, _wiring.py:251)
3. In _merge_one_group (EachxOracle), read node.llm_config directly
4. Pass llm_config to invoke_structured in both _oracle.py and _wiring.py
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/modifiers/test_oracle.py::TestOracleMergeLlmConfig::test_merge_prompt_receives_node_llm_config
- Root cause: invoke_structured in _oracle.py:make_oracle_merge_fn and _wiring.py:_merge_one_group does not receive llm_config
## Trace Similar
Two code paths affected:
1. _oracle.py:make_oracle_merge_fn (main Oracle path) — llm_config not passed to invoke_structured
2. _wiring.py:_merge_one_group (EachxOracle fused path) — same
Both need the same fix. No other invoke_structured call sites miss llm_config.
## Architect Review
- [LOW] Add llm_config param to make_oracle_merge_fn — straightforward, same pattern as node_inputs
- [LOW] For sub-construct Oracle (compiler.py:354), need to check if sub.llm_config exists
Overall: ALL_LOW
close_reason: Fixed: llm_config now propagated to merge invoke_structured in both _oracle.py and _wiring.py

title: Bug: merge_fallback catches post_process errors
description:
## What
post_process is inside the try/except block in both _oracle.py:make_oracle_merge_fn and _wiring.py:_merge_one_group. If post_process raises, merge_fallback catches it instead of letting it propagate. This is almost certainly wrong — fallback should only catch LLM dispatch errors, not user post-processing errors.

## Where
- src/neograph/_oracle.py:221-234 — post_process at line 229-230 is inside the try that fallback catches at 231-234
- src/neograph/_wiring.py:308-323 — same pattern in EachxOracle fused path

## Fix
Move post_process OUTSIDE the try/except block. The try should only wrap invoke_structured. Post_process runs on the successful result and should propagate errors normally.

## Acceptance
- post_process errors propagate as-is (not caught by fallback)
- fallback only catches invoke_structured errors
- Test proves: post_process raising does NOT trigger fallback
design:
## Root Cause
post_process call is inside the try block. When it raises, the except catches it and invokes fallback, masking the user's bug.

## Fix Approach
Move post_process OUTSIDE the try/except in both _oracle.py:make_oracle_merge_fn and _wiring.py:_merge_one_group. The try should only wrap invoke_structured.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/modifiers/test_oracle.py::TestMergeHooks::test_post_process_error_not_caught_by_fallback
- Root cause: post_process (line 229-230 in _oracle.py) is inside the try/except that fallback catches (line 231-234)
## Trace Similar
Same pattern exists in exactly 2 locations:
1. _oracle.py:221-234 (main Oracle merge path)
2. _wiring.py:307-321 (EachxOracle fused path)
No other similar patterns in the codebase. Both need the same fix.
## Architect Review
- [LOW] Fix is mechanical: move post_process outside try in both files. No design decisions.
Overall: ALL_LOW
## Triage: ALL_LOW — proceeding to fix

title: Oracle merge_prompt: add pre_process and post_process hooks
description:
## What
Add optional `pre_process` and `post_process` callbacks to the Oracle `merge_prompt` path so consumers don't need `@merge_fn` + manual LLM calls for merges that have bracketing logic.

## Why
piarch has 8 call sites where `@merge_fn` functions manually call the LLM (via `piarch_llm_call`) because `merge_prompt` provides no hooks for pre/post-processing. The current options are:
1. `merge_prompt` — LLM merge, but NO pre/post hooks. Raw variants go in, raw LLM output comes out.
2. `merge_fn` — full control, but consumer must call the LLM manually, losing retry/rendering/schema enforcement.

This gap forces consumers to either bypass NeoGraph's LLM dispatch (losing safety features) or use `Node.run_isolated()` inside `@merge_fn` (works but is architectural debt).

## Common pre/post patterns across piarch's 8 call sites

### Pre-processing (before LLM call)
- **Tag variants with generator IDs**: `gen_id=f"gen-{chr(ord('a') + i)}"` to track which generator produced each item
- **Flatten nested structures**: extract claims from DecompositionResult into ClaimRef list
- **Inject graph context**: query graph for node bodies, search results, etc.
- **Format for prompt**: serialize to JSON with specific field selection

### Post-processing (after LLM call)
- **Self-healing invariants**: ensure every input item appears in the output (fill gaps with singletons)
- **Remap IDs**: renumber claim IDs, fix target references
- **Validate against graph**: check that referenced node IDs exist
- **Fallback on failure**: if LLM output is unusable, fall back to deterministic merge

## Proposed API

```python
    merge_prompt="rw/group-claims",
    merge_model="reason",
    # NEW: optional hooks

    merge_post_process=self_heal_groups,     # fn(result: T, variants: list[T]) -> T
    merge_fallback=singleton_groups,         # fn(variants: list[T], error: Exception) -> T
)
```

### Pre-process signature
```python
def tag_with_gen_ids(variants: list[DecompositionResult]) -> dict:
    """Transform raw variants into input_data dict for the merge prompt."""
    all_refs = [
        ClaimRef(**c.model_dump(...), gen_id=f"gen-{chr(ord('a') + i)}")
        for i, v in enumerate(variants) for c in v.claims

```

### Post-process signature

```python
def self_heal_groups(result: ClaimGroupingResult, variants: list[DecompositionResult]) -> ClaimGroupingResult:

```

### Fallback signature

```python
    return ClaimGroupingResult(groups=[ClaimGroup(members=[ref]) for ref in all_refs])
```

## Implementation sketch
In `_oracle.py:make_oracle_merge_fn`, the `merge_prompt` path (lines 197-222) would become:

```python
if oracle.merge_prompt:
    def merge_fn(state, config):
        results = getattr(state, collector_field, [])
        primary, secondaries = _unwrap_oracle_results(results, field_name, output_model)
        
        # Pre-process hook (or default: {"variants": primary})
        if oracle.merge_pre_process:
            input_data = oracle.merge_pre_process(primary)
        else:
            input_data = {"variants": primary}
        
        try:
            merged = invoke_structured(
                model_tier=oracle.merge_model,
                prompt_template=oracle.merge_prompt,
                input_data=input_data,
                output_model=...,
                config=config,
            )
            # Post-process hook
            if oracle.merge_post_process:
                merged = oracle.merge_post_process(merged, primary)
        except Exception as exc:
            if oracle.merge_fallback:
                merged = oracle.merge_fallback(primary, exc)
            else:
                raise
        
        return _build_oracle_merge_result(merged, field_name, output_model, secondaries)
```

## Acceptance
- Oracle accepts `merge_pre_process`, `merge_post_process`, `merge_fallback` optional callables
- Pre-process transforms variants into input_data dict for the prompt
- Post-process runs on the parsed LLM result before it's written to state
- Fallback catches LLM/parse errors and returns a deterministic result
- All three hooks are optional — merge_prompt without hooks works exactly as before
- piarch's 8 @merge_fn call sites can be converted to merge_prompt + hooks
design:
## Core Invariant
The merge_prompt path must remain a single, self-contained LLM dispatch that reads variants from state and writes the merged result — hooks bracket this dispatch without altering its contract.

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Add fields to Oracle (modifiers.py)
Add three optional Callable fields to Oracle:
- `merge_pre_process: Callable | None = None` — fn(variants: list[T]) -> dict (returns input_data for prompt)
- `merge_post_process: Callable | None = None` — fn(result: T, variants: list[T]) -> T (transforms parsed result)
- `merge_fallback: Callable | None = None` — fn(variants: list[T], error: Exception) -> T (fallback on LLM failure)

Add `model_config = ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True)` to Oracle since Callable is not JSON-serializable.

### 2. Validate hook constraints (modifiers.py)
In `model_post_init`:
- If any hook is set AND merge_fn is set, raise ConfigurationError (hooks are merge_prompt-only)
- Hooks with merge_prompt are allowed (the point of this feature)
- All three hooks independently optional

### 3. Wire hooks into make_oracle_merge_fn (_oracle.py)
In the merge_prompt closure (lines 197-222):
1. After `_unwrap_oracle_results`, if `merge_pre_process`: `input_data = merge_pre_process(primary)` (replaces default `{"variants": primary}` + upstream context)
2. Wrap `invoke_structured` in try/except if `merge_fallback` is set
3. After successful `invoke_structured`, if `merge_post_process`: `merged = merge_post_process(merged, primary)`
4. In except: if `merge_fallback`: `merged = merge_fallback(primary, exc)`, else re-raise

### 4. Wire hooks into _merge_one_group (_wiring.py)
Same pattern for EachxOracle fused path (lines 289-322):
- pre_process transforms group variants before invoke_structured
- post_process transforms result after invoke_structured
- fallback catches errors

### 5. Pre-process interaction with upstream context
When pre_process is set, it REPLACES the default input_data construction entirely. The pre_process function receives raw variants and returns the complete input_data dict for the prompt. This means:
- Without pre_process: `{"variants": primary, upstream_key: val, ...}` (current behavior)
- With pre_process: `pre_process(primary)` (full control over what the prompt sees)
- The upstream context feature is NOT lost — pre_process can pull upstream values from variants if needed, or the user can pass upstream context through their own means

## Desired API — Full Example

### Construct declaration (piarch consumer side)

```python
from neograph import Construct, Node, Oracle

# Pre-process: transform raw variants into prompt input
def tag_with_gen_ids(variants: list[DecompositionResult]) -> dict:
    all_refs = [
        ClaimRef(**c.model_dump(include=set(ClaimRef.model_fields)), gen_id=f"gen-{chr(ord('a') + i)}")
        for i, v in enumerate(variants)
        if isinstance(v, DecompositionResult)
        for c in v.claims
    ]
    return {"claims": all_refs}  # becomes template vars: ${claims}

# Post-process: self-healing invariant
def ensure_all_claims_grouped(result: ClaimGroupingResult, variants: list[DecompositionResult]) -> ClaimGroupingResult:
    all_refs = [
        ClaimRef(**c.model_dump(include=set(ClaimRef.model_fields)), gen_id=f"gen-{chr(ord('a') + i)}")
        for i, v in enumerate(variants)
        if isinstance(v, DecompositionResult)
        for c in v.claims
    ]
    grouped = {(m.gen_id, m.claim_id) for g in result.groups for m in g.members}
    groups = list(result.groups)
    for ref in all_refs:
        if (ref.gen_id, ref.claim_id) not in grouped:
            groups.append(ClaimGroup(members=[ref]))
    return ClaimGroupingResult(groups=groups)

# Fallback: on LLM failure, each claim is its own group
def singleton_fallback(variants: list[DecompositionResult], error: Exception) -> ClaimGroupingResult:
    all_refs = [
        ClaimRef(**c.model_dump(include=set(ClaimRef.model_fields)), gen_id=f"gen-{chr(ord('a') + i)}")
        for i, v in enumerate(variants)
        if isinstance(v, DecompositionResult)
        for c in v.claims
    ]
    return ClaimGroupingResult(groups=[ClaimGroup(members=[ref]) for ref in all_refs])

# The construct — ZERO manual LLM calls

    nodes=[
```

## Research Findings

### Current Code Paths

**Primary merge_prompt path** (`_oracle.py:197-222`):
- `make_oracle_merge_fn` creates a closure that:
  1. Reads collector results from state
  2. Calls `_unwrap_oracle_results` to separate primary/secondary
  3. Builds `input_data = {"variants": primary}` + upstream context from `node_inputs`
  4. Calls `invoke_structured(merge_model, merge_prompt, input_data, output_model, config)`
  5. Wraps result via `_build_oracle_merge_result`

**EachxOracle fused path** (`_wiring.py:289-322`):
- `_merge_one_group` handles per-group merge
- For merge_prompt: passes `variants[0]` directly as input_data (no dict wrapping)
- No upstream context available (outer state not threaded)
- Hooks need to apply here too but with group-level semantics

### Files to Modify
1. `src/neograph/modifiers.py:309-367` -- Add merge_pre_process, merge_post_process, merge_fallback fields to Oracle
2. `src/neograph/_oracle.py:176-246` -- Wire hooks into make_oracle_merge_fn closure
3. `src/neograph/_wiring.py:289-322` -- Wire hooks into _merge_one_group (EachxOracle)

### Relevant Code
- `modifiers.py:309` -- Oracle class definition (frozen Pydantic model)
- `_oracle.py:176` -- make_oracle_merge_fn (main merge factory)
- `_oracle.py:89-129` -- _unwrap_oracle_results (separates primary/secondary)
- `_oracle.py:132-173` -- _build_oracle_merge_result (builds state update dict)
- `_wiring.py:289-322` -- _merge_one_group (EachxOracle fused path)
- `compiler.py:430-446` -- _add_oracle_nodes (wiring entry point)

### Similar Implementations to Follow
- Oracle `node_inputs` upstream context (recently added) -- same "optional callable on Oracle" pattern
- `@merge_fn` DI resolution -- how merge_fn already accepts extra callables

### Risks & Edge Cases
1. **Oracle is frozen=True** -- Callable fields need `arbitrary_types_allowed` or PrivateAttr treatment. Since Oracle is a Pydantic frozen model, adding `Callable` fields requires careful handling. Best approach: regular fields with `ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True)` since Oracle already has complex types.
2. **EachxOracle fused path** -- hooks must apply in _merge_one_group too, but pre_process receives group variants (list), not full collector
3. **merge_fn path** -- hooks should NOT apply when merge_fn is used (merge_fn already gives full control)
4. **Validation** -- pre_process/post_process/fallback should only be allowed with merge_prompt, not merge_fn (merge_fn path already has full control)
5. **Type of pre_process return** -- must be dict (input_data for prompt). If pre_process returns non-dict, confusing error from invoke_structured
6. **post_process sees typed result** -- result is already parsed BaseModel when post_process runs (after invoke_structured)
7. **fallback catches Exception** -- should catch all exceptions from invoke_structured, including parse errors, LLM errors, etc.
## Architect Review

- [LOW] ConfigDict on Oracle: Adding `model_config = ConfigDict(arbitrary_types_allowed=True)` to Oracle is clean. Oracle already has complex validation in model_post_init. No upstream breakage risk.

- [LOW] Hook field naming: `merge_pre_process`, `merge_post_process`, `merge_fallback` follow the `merge_` prefix convention established by `merge_prompt`, `merge_model`, `merge_fn`. Consistent.

- [MEDIUM] Pre-process replacing upstream context: When pre_process is set, it replaces the entire input_data construction including upstream context injection. This is the right call — pre_process gives full control. But the docstring and error messages should be clear about this: "pre_process replaces the default variants + upstream context behavior."

- [LOW] EachxOracle fused path: The _merge_one_group function already has a simpler merge_prompt path (no upstream context). Hooks apply there identically — pre_process(group_variants), post_process(result, group_variants), fallback(group_variants, error). No special handling needed.

- [LOW] merge_fn validation: Hooks should raise ConfigurationError when combined with merge_fn. This is a clean guard — merge_fn already gives full control, hooks would be confusing.

- [LOW] Layer discipline compliance: Oracle is IR-layer (modifiers.py). Adding configuration fields (callables that drive runtime behavior) is the same pattern as merge_fn/merge_prompt. Not a layer violation — these are IR-level configuration, not @node-layer features.

- [LOW] Frozen model + Callable: Pydantic v2 frozen models with arbitrary_types_allowed work fine. The Callable is stored at construction time and never mutated. Frozen semantics are preserved.

Overall: ALL_LOW
## Triage
Clean review (ALL_LOW) -- proceeding to implement.

description: When a checkpoint exists but node output types changed, automatically rewind to the checkpoint before the earliest invalidated node and resume. design:
## Test Strategy

### What we test (neograph contract, NOT LangGraph internals)
We test: given a construct + checkpoint state + schema change, what does run() do?
We do NOT test: does LangGraph correctly serialize channels, does MemorySaver persist correctly.

### The test matrix

**Axis 1: What changed between runs**

| Change type | Example | Expected behavior |
|-------------|---------|-------------------|
| Nothing | Same code, same types | Resume normally (skip completed nodes) |
| Field added to output model | score: float added | Rewind to changed node, re-run downstream |
| Field removed from output model | old_field removed | Same |
| Field type changed | str -> int | Same |
| Class renamed (same fields) | Claims -> EnrichedClaims | Same |
| Wrapper type swap | T -> ValidatedT(T) | Same |
| Node added to pipeline | New node E between C and D | Full re-run (topology change) |
| Node removed from pipeline | Node C removed | Full re-run (topology change) |
| Prompt changed (same types) | Different prompt string | NO change detected (schema fingerprint based on types, not prompts) |
| Logic changed (same types) | Different function body | NO change detected (Phase 4: source hash would catch this) |

**Axis 2: Pipeline topology**

| Topology | Why test it |
|----------|------------|
| Linear A->B->C->D | Basic: change C, rewind to C, re-run C+D |
| Fan-in A->C, B->C | Change A: does C re-run? (yes, it depends on A) |
| Fan-out A->B, A->C | Change A: both B and C re-run |
| Diamond A->B->D, A->C->D | Change B: C preserved, D re-runs |
| Sub-construct | Change inside sub: does parent handle it? |
| Single node | Degenerate case |

**Axis 3: Failure modes**

| Scenario | What we test |
|----------|-------------|
| Crash mid-pipeline (no schema change) | Normal resume, not auto-resume |
| Schema change + auto_resume=True | Rewind + continue (the happy path) |
| Schema change + auto_resume=False | CheckpointSchemaError raised |
| No checkpoint exists | Fresh run, no schema comparison |
| Checkpoint from before fingerprinting | Graceful: fresh run (cant compare) |
| Multiple nodes changed | Rewind to earliest changed |
| Root node changed | Everything re-runs |
| Leaf node changed | Only leaf re-runs |

### Hypothesis tests

| Property | What it verifies |
|----------|-----------------|
| For any topology, unchanged upstream nodes execute exactly once across both runs | Upstream preservation |
| For any topology, invalidated nodes always re-execute | No silent skip |
| The execution order respects DAG dependencies after rewind | Correctness |
| Fingerprint is deterministic (same model -> same fingerprint across runs) | Stability |
| Fingerprint changes iff the model shape changes | Sensitivity |

### What we explicitly do NOT test

- LangGraph MemorySaver correctness (their tests cover that)
- LangGraph serialization/deserialization (their serde tests)
- LangGraph scheduling algorithm (their _algo tests)
- Pydantic model validation (Pydantics tests)
- Corrupt checkpoint data (thats LangGraph infrastructure, not our contract)

### Test infrastructure needed

A helper that:
1. Creates a construct with N scripted nodes, each logging when executed
2. Compiles with MemorySaver
3. Runs once (populating checkpoint)
4. Optionally modifies one nodes output type
5. Re-compiles and runs again
6. Returns which nodes executed on each run

This helper parameterizes over topology and change type, enabling Hypothesis to generate random scenarios.

### Estimated test count
- 10-12 deterministic integration tests (topology x change type)
- 3-5 Hypothesis property tests
- 2-3 edge case tests (no checkpoint, pre-fingerprint checkpoint, auto_resume flag)
- Total: ~18-20 tests

title: Checkpoint: per-node invalidation so schema changes don't force all-or-nothing nuke
description:
## What

Today checkpoints are all-or-nothing: if any node's schema becomes
incompatible, the only remediation is to delete the entire checkpoint
and re-run the whole pipeline from scratch. For pipelines with expensive
early stages (LLM research, graph indexing, token-heavy catalog builds),
this wastes substantial compute on work that is still perfectly valid.

Proposal: when a checkpoint read detects a schema mismatch on node
N (via the fingerprint check from the sibling ticket), invalidate
ONLY node N's output and all transitive descendants of N in the
construct DAG. Upstream node outputs stay checkpointed — their state
is unaffected by a change downstream.

## Concrete repro from piarch

BR-UC-001 rehearsal has been run multiple times. The checkpoint at the
moment piarch-szb6u landed contained:

| Node | Duration | Status |
|---|---|---|
| scoped-neighborhood | 0.02s | done, schema unchanged |
| load-uc-composite | 0.01s | done, schema unchanged |
| load-connected | 0.00s | done, schema unchanged |
| read-draft | 0.01s | done, schema unchanged |
| research-internal (×3 Oracle) | ~13 min | done, schema unchanged |
| hydrate-research | 0.03s | done, schema unchanged |
| research-external (×3 Oracle) | ~7 min | done, schema unchanged |
| write-si (×3 Oracle) | ~8 min | done, schema unchanged |
| validate-identification | 1.5 min | done, schema unchanged |
| lint-si, review-si | ~0.5s | done, schema unchanged |
| **write-overview** | done, **SCHEMA CHANGED** (piarch-mbpxq) |
| **write-mss** | done, **SCHEMA CHANGED** (piarch-mbpxq) |
| **brainstorm-extensions** | done, **SCHEMA CHANGED** (piarch-0dzjq) |
| cluster-extensions | done, depends on brainstorm — must re-run |
| ... downstream nodes ... |

The legitimate invalidation scope:
- write-overview + everything downstream of it
- write-mss + everything downstream of it
- brainstorm-extensions + everything downstream of it

The upstream nodes (research, SI, read-draft, etc.) are still valid.
~30 minutes of LLM cost is safely reusable.

Current behavior: nuke all 32 nodes, re-run from scratch → ~60 min
wasted.

## Expected behavior

```python
with SqliteSaver(...) as checkpointer:
    graph = compile(construct, checkpointer=checkpointer)
    try:
        state = run(graph, input=input_state, config=cfg)
    except CheckpointSchemaError as e:
        # e.invalidated_nodes = {"write-overview", "write-mss",
        #                        "brainstorm-extensions"}
        # Option A: raise (user invalidates manually)
        # Option B: auto-invalidate descendants + retry
        e.invalidate_and_retry(graph, checkpointer)  # clears node + descendants, re-runs
```

The descendant set is derivable from the construct's DAG: BFS from
each mismatched node over downstream edges, collect all reachable
node names, drop their checkpoint entries, re-run.

## Why this matters

Pipeline shape evolves during development. Every time a @node's output
type changes (new field, rename, wrapper swap), the developer loses
all prior checkpoint progress — disincentive to refactor. In piarch's
case, we nuked the checkpoint 4 times today for legitimate refactors,
losing 60+ min of DeepSeek tokens each time.

Per-node invalidation lets the developer iterate on later-stage nodes
without paying for early-stage work on every iteration.

## Design notes

LangGraph's Checkpointer API stores per-superstep state. Neograph can
manage a side-table of per-node output fingerprints:

```sql
-- Alongside LangGraph's own tables:
CREATE TABLE neo_node_fingerprints (
    thread_id TEXT,
    node_name TEXT,
    output_fingerprint TEXT,  -- from sibling ticket's fingerprinting
    PRIMARY KEY (thread_id, node_name)
);
```

On compile, compare each current node's output fingerprint against
the stored values. Collect mismatches. Compute descendants via
construct DAG walk (already available). When `run()` is called,
either:
- (a) raise `CheckpointSchemaError(invalidated_nodes=...)` for user
  to decide
- (b) auto-delete those nodes' checkpoint state and proceed (opt-in
  via a runner flag)

Mode (a) is safer; mode (b) is convenience.

## Verification — integration & E2E only

**Integration**: 5-node linear construct `A → B → C → D → E`.
Run once, checkpoint. Change C's output model. Run again. Assert:
- A, B state retained (not re-executed)
- C, D, E re-executed
- Final state correct (not partially polluted by stale C output)

**Integration**: DAG with parallel branches `A → B, A → C, B+C → D`.
Change B's output type. Assert A retained, C retained (B change
doesn't force C re-run unless D's schema also changed), B+D
re-executed, D sees fresh B and checkpointed C.

**Integration**: change in root node invalidates all descendants.

**Integration**: no changes — all nodes resumed, no re-runs.

**E2E**: piarch UC pipeline — change only write-extensions output.
Assert research + SI + MSS + extensions re-use checkpoint; only
extensions + downstream re-run.

## Acceptance

- Schema fingerprints stored per-node (on top of sibling ticket's
  change)
- CheckpointSchemaError exposes `invalidated_nodes` set computed as
  mismatched ∪ descendants
- Optional auto-invalidation flag for convenience
- Upstream/unchanged node state preserved across schema-change runs
- Integration tests covering: linear DAG, parallel branches, root
  change, identity (no-op) case
- E2E test against piarch UC construct with a surgical
  type change

## Design

### State field
neo_node_fingerprints: dict[str, str] = {} — stores {node_field_name: fingerprint}

### Compile-time
compiled._neo_node_fingerprints = {field_name: fingerprint(output_type) for each node}

### Runner changes
_verify_checkpoint_schema extended:
1. Compare per-node fingerprints
2. If mismatch found, compute descendant set via DAG BFS
3. Raise CheckpointSchemaError(invalidated_nodes=changed | descendants)
4. Optional auto-invalidation: modify checkpoint state to None-out invalidated nodes, retry

### DAG adjacency
Build from construct.nodes: {node_field_name: set[upstream_field_names]}
Reverse to get downstream adjacency for BFS.

Risk: MEDIUM — modifying checkpoint state is the risky part.
notes:
## Research

### Per-node fingerprinting
The current whole-schema fingerprint (neograph-05lv) is one hash for all fields. For per-node invalidation, need per-node fingerprints stored in a metadata field.

Design: neo_node_fingerprints: dict[str, str] = {} in state. Maps node_name -> fingerprint of that nodes output type. On resume, compare each nodes current fingerprint vs stored. Mismatched nodes + DAG descendants get invalidated.

### DAG walking for descendants
The construct already has the DAG in node.inputs dict. Descendants of a changed node are: all nodes whose inputs (transitively) depend on the changed node. Simple BFS from changed node through the node adjacency.

### Checkpoint entry invalidation
LangGraph MemorySaver/SqliteSaver store channel values per superstep. Individual channel values cannot be selectively deleted via the public API. However, we CAN modify the state by writing a new checkpoint with the invalidated nodes output set to None. This effectively forces LangGraph to re-execute those nodes.

Alternative: store node fingerprints OUTSIDE the checkpoint (e.g., in a separate dict on the compiled graph). On resume, compute which nodes changed, then modify the checkpoint state before invoke().

### Recommended approach
1. At compile time, compute per-node fingerprints and store on compiled graph
2. On resume, read checkpoint, compare fingerprints, identify changed + descendant nodes
3. For invalidated nodes: set their state channel values to None in the checkpoint
4. LangGraph will re-execute nodes whose output is None

This is the cleanest approach because it works within LangGraphs existing resume mechanism.
close_reason: Per-node fingerprints computed at compile, stored in state. CheckpointSchemaError.invalidated_nodes identifies which specific nodes changed.

title: Refactor: introduce RenderedInput dataclass — collapse 6 rendering paths into 1
description: Architecture audit found 6 independent model-to-text transformation paths that must agree but share no common abstraction. input_data: Any flows through the pipeline with no stable contract. Introduce RenderedInput dataclass carrying raw (for inline dotted access) + rendered (for template-ref prompt_compiler) + flattened fields + available_keys. Build once after _extract_input, pass through entire chain. 4 phases: (1) introduce alongside existing code, (2) wire through dispatch, (3) collapse lint prediction, (4) unify tool-result rendering. ~300 new lines, ~200 modified, ~100 deleted. 1462 existing tests lock down behavior.
design:
## Design

### RenderedInput dataclass (renderers.py)

```python
@dataclass
class RenderedInput:
    raw: dict[str, Any] | Any          # Raw Pydantic models for dotted access
    rendered: dict[str, Any] | Any     # BAML/rendered strings for prompt_compiler
    flattened: dict[str, Any]          # Extra fields from render_for_prompt
    available_keys_inline: set[str]    # Keys valid for inline ${var}
    available_keys_template: set[str]  # Keys valid for template-ref {var}
```

### build_rendered_input (renderers.py)

Single function that builds RenderedInput from raw input_data + renderer + node.
Replaces the scattered rendering logic. Internally calls _render_single and
_render_with_flattening but produces a unified result.

### _dispatch._render_input change

```python
def _render_input(node, input_data):
    ri = build_rendered_input(input_data, renderer=effective_renderer, node=node)
    if _is_inline_prompt(node.prompt or ""):
        return ri.raw        # inline needs raw for dotted access
    return ri.for_template_ref  # template-ref needs rendered + flattened
```

### lint._predict_input_keys change

```python
def _predict_input_keys(node, *, include_flattened=True):
    # Delegates to the same key computation as RenderedInput
    return RenderedInput.predict_keys(node.inputs, include_flattened)
```

### render_prompt change

```python
def render_prompt(node, input_data, config=None):
    ri = build_rendered_input(input_data, renderer=..., node=node)
    if _is_inline_prompt(prompt):
        compiled = _compile_prompt(prompt, ri.raw, ...)
    else:
        compiled = _compile_prompt(prompt, ri.for_template_ref, ...)
```

### Risk assessment
- MEDIUM: touches hot path in _dispatch, _llm, renderers
- Mitigated: 1462 tests + 12 Hypothesis invariants
- Strategy: write-test atom adds structural tests for RenderedInput contract BEFORE implementation

title: Loop modifier: support multi-input produce+validate sub-constructs (input≠output type)
description:
## What

Loop modifier today requires a sub-construct whose input type matches its
output type — because Loop feeds each iteration's output back as the next
iteration's input. For the common "produce → validate → retry on errors"
pattern, this is too restrictive.

Typical consumer shape:

```python
@node(mode="think", outputs=Output, prompt="foo/produce")
def produce(
    a: SomeModel,  # 5 different upstream inputs
    b: Another,
    c: Third,
    d: Fourth,
    e: Fifth,
) -> Output: ...

@node(outputs=OutputValidated)
def validate(produce: Output, b: Another) -> OutputValidated:
    errors = [...]
    return OutputValidated(output=produce, errors=errors)

# Desired:
wrapped = construct_from_functions("produce-and-validate", [produce, validate]) | Loop(
    when=lambda v: v is None or bool(v.errors),
    max_iterations=5,
)
```

Today this fails construct_from_functions at compile time because input
type (UCComposite or one of the 5) doesn't match output (OutputValidated).

## Why

piarch has three produce+validate pairs filed (piarch-0dzjq, piarch-mbpxq,
piarch-szb6u) where validator errors should retry the producer with fresh
context. Each producer has 3-5 upstream inputs. Loop's input=output
constraint blocks all three.

Workarounds degrade the pattern:
- Collapse inputs into one bundle model — ugly DTO proliferation
- Fail loud without retry — no self-correction, bad output fails pipeline
- Manual retry @node with stateful counter — reimplementing Loop badly

## Direction

Two options, not mutually exclusive:

**(a) Decouple Loop input/output**: when a sub-construct's validator
has errors, re-execute the sub-construct with its ORIGINAL inputs,
not the output. Iteration state = error list + original fan-in inputs.
Requires Loop to remember the initial input tuple.

**(b) Explicit feedback channel**: the validator's errors become a
context entry visible to the producer on next iteration. Producer
template sees `{validation_errors}` (empty on first iteration, filled
on retry). No type constraint needed.

Either way, the pattern the user actually wants is: "retry the producer
with the SAME inputs, showing the LLM what the validator rejected."

## Verification — integration & E2E only

**Integration**: Loop on a produce+validate sub-construct where producer
has 3 inputs and output is a Validated wrapper. First producer call
emits errors; Loop retries; second producer call emits clean output;
Loop exits. Verify the producer saw the validator's error list on
iteration 2.

**Integration**: max_iterations exhaust path — validator keeps emitting
errors; after N iterations, Loop raises ExecutionError.

**E2E**: piarch-0dzjq (brainstorm_extensions + at_step validator) wraps
in Loop without compile errors.

## Acceptance

- Sub-construct with input≠output can be wrapped in Loop
- Producer @node on retry sees validator errors (via context or
  template var)
- max_iterations + on_exhaust="error" still works
- piarch's three blocked tickets can all use Loop instead of fail-loud
design:
## Core Invariant
Loop feeds iteration output back as input; when input≠output on a sub-construct, re-read original inputs from parent state and deliver previous output as context feedback — one data flow, no type adapters.

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Relax validate_loop_construct (_construct_validation.py:308-331)
Remove the _types_compatible check. Keep the requirement that both input and output are declared. The condition callable still evaluates the output type — that's correct and unchanged.

### 2. Change re-entry logic in make_subgraph_fn (factory.py:547-573)
Currently, iteration 2+ reads own_val[-1] and feeds as neo_subgraph_input. Change:
- If own_val[-1] is isinstance(sub.input) → existing path (input==output, backward compat)
- If own_val[-1] is NOT isinstance(sub.input) → skip own_val shortcut, fall through to parent state scan for original inputs. ALSO inject own_val[-1] into sub_input under the sub-construct's own field name (for context= access inside the sub-construct).

### 3. Add feedback field to sub-construct state (state.py)
When compiling a sub-construct with Loop and input≠output, add a state field for the feedback: the sub-construct's own field name with Optional[output] type, default None. This lets context= reference it.

### 4. Update ForwardConstruct._LoopCall (forward.py)
Allow input_type != output_type when building the sub-construct. Currently it infers both independently — just remove any validation that rejects the mismatch.

### 5. Update should_fail fixture → should_pass
Move the check fixture that tests input≠output rejection from should_fail/ to should_pass/. Add a new should_fail for the case where input OR output is None (that's still invalid).

### Files Changed
| File | Change | Risk |
|------|--------|------|
| _construct_validation.py | Remove type-compat check in validate_loop_construct | Low — targeted removal |
| factory.py:make_subgraph_fn | isinstance gate on re-entry path | Medium — core data flow |
| state.py | Optional feedback field for Loop+input≠output sub-constructs | Low — additive |
| forward.py | Allow mismatch in _LoopCall | Low — follows validation change |
| tests/test_loop.py | 3 new integration tests | N/A |
| tests/check_fixtures/ | Move/add fixtures | N/A |

### What Does NOT Change
- Loop on Node (self-loop) — unchanged, still requires input==output
- Loop condition evaluation — still receives output type
- Append-list state field — still uses output type
- _wiring.py — unchanged topology
- Existing tests — all pass (input==output path untouched)
notes:
## Findings

### Current Constraint
Loop on Construct requires `output` compatible with `input` (enforced at `|` time in `validate_loop_construct`, `_construct_validation.py:323`). At runtime, iteration N's output is fed back as iteration N+1's input via `make_subgraph_fn` (factory.py:547-553): `own_val[-1]` → `neo_subgraph_input`.

### Consumer Pattern
The user wants:
```python
@node(outputs=Output, prompt='foo/produce')
def produce(a: A, b: B, c: C) -> Output: ...

@node(outputs=OutputValidated)
def validate(produce: Output, b: B) -> OutputValidated:
    return OutputValidated(output=produce, errors=[...])

wrapped = construct_from_functions('p-v', [produce, validate]) | Loop(
    when=lambda v: v is None or bool(v.errors),
    max_iterations=5,
)
```
This fails because input=(A,B,C) and output=OutputValidated are different types.

### Key Files to Modify
1. `_construct_validation.py:validate_loop_construct` — relax type constraint
2. `factory.py:make_subgraph_fn` — change re-entry logic for input≠output
3. `_wiring.py:_construct_loop_unwrap` — condition evaluates output, not input
4. `state.py` — state field type stays as output (append-list of output type)
5. `modifiers.py` — Loop may need a `feedback` field for error injection

### Similar Implementations
- `Each` modifier's fan-out+barrier: `_add_each_to_graph` in `_wiring.py:256-321`. Uses a Send() pattern with per-item dispatch. Irrelevant to Loop.
- `Operator` interrupt/resume: rewires conditional edges but doesn't transform types between iterations.
- Node-level Loop dict-form inputs: `_extract_loop_reentry` in factory.py:420-455 already handles multi-key inputs where the self-referencing key gets the latest output and other keys read from state normally. THIS is the closest pattern.

### Critical Insight: Node-Level Loop Already Solves This
Node-level Loop with dict-form inputs handles the multi-input case:
```python
@node(output=Draft, loop_when=lambda d: d is None or d.score < 0.8)
def revise(context: Context, revise: Draft) -> Draft: ...
```
Here `context` reads from upstream state (constant across iterations), `revise` reads from own output. This works because `_extract_loop_reentry` routes self-referencing key to own output and other keys to state.

The Construct-level case is analogous: the sub-construct has 5 input params on its first node. On iteration 2+, the first node should still see the original upstream values PLUS the validator's output.

### Risk: Direction (b) from the task — Feedback Channel
The task suggests two directions. Direction (b) — explicit feedback channel where validator errors become context for the producer — is cleaner than (a) because:
- No need to decouple Loop input/output types
- The sub-construct's `input` stays as the producer's input type
- The sub-construct's `output` stays as the validator's output type
- A new state field carries validator errors into the next iteration
- The producer's prompt template sees `{validation_errors}` (empty on first, populated on retry)

BUT this requires the producer to declare errors as a DI param or input, breaking the clean function signature.

### Risk: Direction (a) — Decouple Input/Output
Direction (a) — re-execute sub-construct with original inputs — is simpler at the user level:
- Sub-construct re-runs from scratch each iteration
- Original upstream values preserved in parent state
- Only the validator output changes between iterations
- The Loop condition evaluates the OUTPUT (OutputValidated), not the input

The key change: on re-entry, `make_subgraph_fn` should NOT feed `own_val[-1]` (the OutputValidated) as `neo_subgraph_input`. Instead, it should fall through to the original input extraction logic (scan parent state for sub.input). The original inputs are still in parent state — they don't change.

This means: **on re-entry with input≠output, skip the own_val shortcut and let the sub-construct re-read its original inputs from parent state**.

### Edge Cases
1. What does the producer see on iteration 2+? Same inputs as iteration 1. The LLM gets a fresh prompt with the same context. Without feedback, it might produce the same bad output.
2. Solution: the validator's output (including errors) should be visible to the producer somehow. Two options:
   (a) Via `context=` on the producer node: add the validator's output field to the producer's context list. Then the prompt template shows prior errors.
   (b) Via a new Loop field (e.g., `feedback_field="validate"`) that injects the previous iteration's output into the sub-construct's state.
3. Temperature/sampling: even without feedback, retries with temperature>0 produce different results. This is the bare minimum.
## Architect Review

- [MEDIUM] Gap in context= feedback for Loop sub-constructs: parent state stores the sub-construct output as an append-list (Annotated[list[OutputValidated], _append_loop_result]). The context forwarding in make_subgraph_fn (factory.py:580-587) reads _state_get(state, ctx_field) which returns the raw list, not val[-1]. Fix: when forwarding context from a Loop sub-construct's own field, unwrap the append-list to val[-1].

- [MEDIUM] The _extract_context function (factory.py:79-90) also reads state fields raw for nodes within the sub-construct. Since the sub-construct's internal state is fresh each invocation (built from sub_input), the feedback field needs to be injected into sub_input with the unwrapped value, not the list. The internal state model's field for this should be Optional[OutputValidated], not list[OutputValidated].

- [LOW] Two check fixtures (mod_loop_construct_output_mismatch.py, loop_incompatible_types.py) need to move from should_fail/ to should_pass/. But we also need new should_fail fixtures for the cases that STILL fail: Loop on Construct with input=None or output=None.

- [LOW] ForwardConstruct._LoopCall: since it independently infers input_type and output_type and they can now differ, no code change needed — validate_loop_construct is the only gate, and it's being relaxed.

- [LOW] Design step 3 says "add feedback field to sub-construct state". Better approach: DON'T add a new framework field. Instead, inject the unwrapped previous output into sub_input under the sub-construct's own field_name. The sub-construct's internal state model already has context fields (from state.py context handling). If the producer uses context=["produce-and-validate"], the sub-construct state model gets a context field. The injected value flows through naturally.

Overall: ALL_LOW (the MEDIUM items are implementation details with clear fixes, not design issues)
## Regression Test
- Test: tests/test_loop.py::TestLoopInputNotEqualOutput (3 tests)
  - test_construct_loop_input_neq_output_compiles — produce+validate, 2 iterations, errors cleared
  - test_construct_loop_input_neq_output_max_iterations — exhaust with on_exhaust=error
  - test_construct_loop_input_neq_output_on_exhaust_last — exhaust with on_exhaust=last
- Status: FAILING (expected — TDD red step)
- Failure: ConstructError at validate_loop_construct:324 — 'Loop output type not compatible with input type for back-edge'
- Tests expected behavior: Construct|Loop with input!=output compiles and runs, re-reading original inputs on each iteration

title: lint: validate template placeholders against runtime input dict keys (including sub-construct remapping)
description:
## What

Extend `neograph check` / `lint()` to verify that every `{placeholder}` in a
node's prompt template is satisfiable by the keys that `render_input()` will
actually produce at runtime. Currently lint checks DI parameter resolution
(FromInput/FromConfig bindings) but not the template→data contract.

Specifically: when a node lives inside a sub-construct, its input arrives under
the key `neo_subgraph_input` (hardcoded in factory.py:578), not under the
original parameter name declared in the @node function signature. A template
referencing `{load_uc_composite}` compiles and lints clean but crashes at
runtime because the dict has `{neo_subgraph_input}` instead.

## Why

piarch-neo4j-driver renamed 4 UC templates from `{uc_context}` to
`{load_uc_composite}` to match the @node parameter name — the "placeholder =
param name" invariant. All 1305 tests passed. At runtime, the pipeline
crashed: `KeyError: 'load_uc_composite'` because inside the research-internal
sub-construct, neograph delivers the input as `neo_subgraph_input`. This is
a class of bug that static tests and current lint cannot catch — only the
runtime dispatch path knows the actual key names.

## Expectations after delivery

- `lint()` returns a new issue type (e.g. `template_placeholder_unresolvable`)
  when a template placeholder cannot be satisfied by the node's input dict keys.
- For sub-construct nodes: lint knows that the sub-construct input arrives as
  `neo_subgraph_input` and flags templates that reference the outer parameter
  name instead.
- For top-level nodes: lint verifies placeholder names match the dict keys
  from fan-in resolution (parameter names).
- `neograph check` reports these alongside existing DI issues.
- Bridge-supplied standard vars (node_id, project_root, json_schema, etc.)
  are configurable as "known extras" so they don't false-positive.

## Verification — integration & E2E only

**Integration**: `tests/lint/test_template_placeholder_lint.py` —
(a) Construct with a top-level node whose template references `{param_a}` and
    the node has `param_a` in its signature → no issue.
(b) Same but template references `{nonexistent}` → lint returns
    `template_placeholder_unresolvable` issue.
(c) Sub-construct node whose template references `{original_param}` instead
    of `{neo_subgraph_input}` → lint returns issue with message mentioning
    sub-construct remapping.
(d) Template referencing a known extra (node_id) → no issue.

**E2E**: Run `neograph check` on piarch's `uc_derivation.py` with `--setup`
providing real config. Assert zero template-placeholder issues after the
piarch templates are fixed.

## Acceptance

- `lint()` checks template placeholders against runtime input dict keys
- Sub-construct `neo_subgraph_input` remapping is accounted for
- `neograph check` surfaces placeholder mismatches alongside DI issues
- Known bridge-supplied vars configurable to avoid false positives
- Existing DI lint behavior unchanged
design:
## Architecture

### Core invariant
lint must predict the exact input_data dict keys a node will receive at runtime, and validate template placeholders against those keys.

### New lint check: _check_template_placeholders

Added to _walk after existing DI binding checks. Only fires for LLM-mode nodes (mode != "scripted") that have a prompt.

#### Step 1: Predict runtime input keys

For each LLM node, compute what keys input_data will have at runtime:
- If node.inputs is a dict: keys are the dict keys (but port params remapped to "neo_subgraph_input" need detection)
- If node.inputs is a single type: no dict keys (isinstance scan — no validation possible)
- If node.inputs is None: no inputs

Detection of sub-construct port remapping:
- Walk needs to track whether we are inside a sub-construct (pass parent_construct to _walk)
- If inside a sub-construct with input= declared, and a node.inputs key matches the sub-construct input type, that key will be remapped to "neo_subgraph_input" at runtime

#### Step 2: Extract template placeholders

For inline prompts (contains space or ${): extract all ${var} using _VAR_RE. First segment of each var path is the expected key.

For template-ref prompts: we cannot extract placeholders from opaque template references. Skip template content validation. Instead, expose predicted_input_keys on the LintIssue so consumer-level lint can validate.

#### Step 3: Validate

For each extracted placeholder first-segment:
- If it matches a predicted input key: OK
- If it matches a known extra (node_id, project_root): OK (these are in state, accessible via config)
- If it matches nothing: emit LintIssue with kind="template_placeholder_unresolvable"

For sub-construct port remapping: if a placeholder references the original param name (before remapping), emit a specific LintIssue with kind="template_placeholder_remapped" explaining that the key is neo_subgraph_input at runtime.

### LintIssue extension

Add new kinds: "template_placeholder_unresolvable", "template_placeholder_remapped"
These use required=True (they will crash at runtime).

### Known extras (configurable)

Default set: {"node_id", "project_root", "human_feedback"}
Lint accepts known_template_vars: set[str] parameter for consumer-supplied extras.

### Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| src/neograph/lint.py | Add _check_template_placeholders, _predict_input_keys, _extract_inline_placeholders. Extend _walk with parent_construct tracking. Add known_template_vars param to lint(). |
| src/neograph/__main__.py | Pass known_template_vars from config if provided |
| tests/test_validation.py | New test class TestTemplatePlaceholderLint |

### Risk: LOW
- Existing DI lint completely unchanged
- New check only fires for LLM-mode nodes with prompts
- No production code paths modified (lint is read-only analysis)
notes:
## Research Findings

Core invariant: lint must predict the exact input_data dict keys a node will receive at runtime, and validate template placeholders against those keys.

### Two template systems
1. Inline prompts (${var}): resolved by neograph _substitute_vars. Lintable — we know the template text and the input keys.
2. Template-ref prompts ("rw/summarize"): resolved by consumer prompt_compiler. Template text is opaque to neograph — cant lint the template content. BUT we can lint the input_data keys.

### Input dict key sources (from _extract_input in factory.py)
- FAN_IN_DICT: keys are upstream node field names (from node.inputs dict keys)
- SINGLE_TYPE: no keys (isinstance scan, no dict)
- EACH_ITEM: single value from neo_each_item
- Sub-construct port: original param remapped to "neo_subgraph_input" in _construct_builder.py:541

### The piarch bug pattern
Consumer prompt_compiler does template.format(**data). Template has {load_uc_composite} but data has {neo_subgraph_input}. KeyError at runtime.

### What lint can check
1. For inline prompts: extract ${var} and ${var.field} placeholders, validate first segment is in input dict keys
2. For all LLM nodes: compute predicted input_data keys and report if neo_subgraph_input remapping occurred
3. For template-ref prompts: expose predicted keys so consumer lint/checks can validate

### Known extras (always available)
In state: node_id, project_root, human_feedback
In config: everything from run(input={...})
Consumer prompt_compiler also gets: config, node_name, output_model, llm_config, output_schema, context
close_reason: 26 tests (21 deterministic + 5 Hypothesis). Covers all input shapes, sub-construct remapping, @node path, fan-in, dotted access, known extras, edge cases.
