title: Inline prompt ${var.field} broken after BAML default rendering
description: After neograph-qybn fix, _render_input BAML-renders dict values before _compile_prompt runs. Inline prompts with dotted access (${claim.text}) get getattr on a BAML string instead of a Pydantic model, silently returning empty string. This was already broken WITH a renderer configured, but the fix extended it to the no-renderer default path. Fix options: (A) resolve vars before rendering, (B) render after var substitution, (C) make _resolve_var BAML-aware. Option A is simplest — pass raw input_data to _substitute_vars for inline prompts, then render only the substituted result.
design:
## Root Cause
_render_input (in _dispatch.py) calls render_input which now BAML-renders Pydantic models even when renderer=None (neograph-qybn fix). The rendered dict goes to invoke_structured -> _compile_prompt -> _substitute_vars -> _resolve_var. For dotted paths like seed.text, _resolve_var does getattr(baml_string, 'text') which returns ''.

## Fix Approach
Option A: In _compile_prompt, when the prompt is inline, do var substitution on RAW input_data FIRST, then render. This requires passing raw input through to _compile_prompt alongside rendered input.

Option B: In _dispatch.py ThinkDispatch/ToolDispatch, detect inline prompts and skip rendering, letting _compile_prompt handle everything. Simpler but leaks prompt knowledge into dispatch.

Option C: In _render_input, for inline prompts with dotted vars, defer rendering. Same layer leak as B.

Option D: Render AFTER var substitution. Change _compile_prompt so that for inline prompts, it receives raw data, does var substitution, then renders the final string values. For non-inline (template ref), render first then pass to prompt_compiler.

Recommended: Option D — cleanest separation. _compile_prompt becomes the decision point: inline prompts get raw data + var substitution; template refs get rendered data + prompt_compiler.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_inline_prompts.py::TestInlinePromptThroughFullDispatch::test_dotted_var_resolves_through_full_pipeline
- Root cause confirmed: _render_input BAML-renders dict values, _resolve_var does getattr on string -> ''
- The prompt sent to LLM is 'Judge this claim: ' (empty where field value should be)
- Warning log: prompt_var_missing segment=text var=seed.text
## Trace Similar
Pattern isolated to _resolve_var in inline prompts. Non-inline prompts use prompt_compiler which receives dict values by key — BAML strings are correct for that path. No similar patterns elsewhere.
## Architect Review
Core tension: rendering must happen AFTER var substitution for inline prompts (dotted access needs raw models) but BEFORE prompt_compiler for template refs (compiler expects rendered strings).

Chosen approach: Don't render in _dispatch.py when prompt is inline. Inline prompt path in _resolve_var BAML-renders BaseModel leaf values. Template ref path renders input before calling prompt_compiler.

Implementation:
1. _render_input gains prompt parameter. When _is_inline_prompt(prompt), return raw input_data unchanged.
2. _resolve_var: at the str(obj) step, if obj is a BaseModel, use describe_value instead.
3. No changes to renderers.py (the neograph-qybn fix stays).

Risk: LOW. Only inline prompts are affected. Template ref path unchanged.
Verdict: ALL_LOW
close_reason: Fixed: inline prompts skip rendering, _resolve_var BAML-renders BaseModel leaf values. describe_value promoted to top-level in _llm.py.

title: Prompt-input rendering asymmetric with tool-result rendering — no BAML fallback when renderer is None
description:
## What

`_render_tool_result_for_llm()` (in `_llm.py:605-622`) falls back to
`describe_value()` BAML notation when no renderer is configured, so tool
results are always rendered as BAML. `render_input()` (in `renderers.py:208-222`)
has no such fallback — when renderer is None it returns `input_data` unchanged,
leaving the consumer's `prompt_compiler` to render Pydantic models however it
wants. Result: tool results arrive at the LLM as BAML, prompt-placeholder
inputs arrive as raw Pydantic objects (or JSON via consumer hand-rolling).

Because `render_for_prompt()` on models is only invoked inside `_render_single`
(which is only reached when renderer is non-None), the model-level projection
hook is dead code unless a renderer is explicitly configured. This subtlety is
not documented; consumers add `render_for_prompt()` methods to models and they
silently never run.

## Direction

**BAML (`describe_value()`) is the canonical rendering.** XmlRenderer /
DelimitedRenderer / JsonRenderer are historical pluggability — the answer for
every real consumer is BAML because that is what tool results already use by
default, and mixing formats inside a single prompt is strictly worse than
uniform BAML.

### Dispatch (in precedence order, applied to every Pydantic input)

1. **`model.render_for_prompt()` wins if defined.** Consumer-authored
   projection has the highest priority. The returned value is used directly:
   - If it returns `str` → insert verbatim into the placeholder.
   - If it returns a `BaseModel` → BAML-render the returned model (honoring
     its own `exclude` fields and its own `render_for_prompt()` if any).
   The renderer configuration is IRRELEVANT for this path.
2. **Otherwise, BAML-render the original model** via `describe_value()`.
   This already honors `field_info.exclude` today (see `describe_type.py:403`).
   Consumer marks non-presentable fields with `Field(..., exclude=True)` on
   the source model and they disappear from the prompt automatically.

This is symmetric with how tool results already work — BAML by default, no
configuration required. `render_for_prompt()` stays and remains the escape
hatch for curated views (truncated snippets, renamed tags, computed fields).

### Remove the renderer-config gate

`configure_llm(renderer=...)` stops being required for ANY of the above. The
`Renderer` abstraction remains in the codebase for legacy XmlRenderer /
DelimitedRenderer / JsonRenderer opt-ins, but:

- Default config produces BAML everywhere, no opt-in needed.
- `render_for_prompt()` runs unconditionally.
- `Field(exclude=True)` is honored unconditionally via `describe_value()`.
- Consumers that opt into a non-BAML renderer trade away the default
  symmetry — their choice, their responsibility.

## Why this matters

A consumer using NeoGraph gets BAML for tool results "for free" and must
reinvent rendering for prompt inputs. Concretely, `piarch-neo4j-driver` has
`HydratedResearch.render_for_prompt() -> ResearchPresentation` (comment says
"NeoGraph BAML-renders the returned model") — which never executed, because
piarch never wired a renderer. The same project's `prompt_compiler`
accumulated ~60 lines of ad-hoc `model_dump()` / `model_dump_json()` / alias
logic to compensate, and that logic has been the source of multiple bugs
(most recent: `{uc_context}` placeholder never filled because the aliasing
table doesn't know about it; pipeline silently no-opped research phase for
8 days before a strict-mode refactor turned the failure loud).

The framework advertises `render_for_prompt()` in the dispatch hierarchy
("model.render_for_prompt() > node.renderer > construct.renderer > global >
None" in `node.py:119` / `construct.py:94`), but without an active renderer
the whole chain collapses to None and input data stays raw. Consumer
expectation (matching the tool-result path) is that default behavior is
BAML, with `render_for_prompt()` available as escape hatch when needed.

## Expectations after delivery

- Input-data and tool-result rendering produce BAML by default via
  `describe_value()`. One code path, one format.
- `render_for_prompt()` on a model ALWAYS runs when that model flows into
  a prompt placeholder, regardless of renderer configuration. Its return is
  either used verbatim (str) or BAML-rendered (BaseModel).
- `Field(..., exclude=True)` filters fields from BAML output unconditionally.
- `configure_llm(renderer=...)` becomes optional; consumers with no renderer
  set still get BAML for inputs.
- Existing consumers that already set `renderer=XmlRenderer(...)` continue to
  work identically (no behavior change when a renderer is explicitly set).

## Verification — integration & E2E only

**Integration**: `tests/renderers/test_render_input_baml_default.py` — define
a Pydantic model with mixed field types and one `exclude=True` field; call
the input-rendering pipeline with NO renderer configured; assert the result
is a BAML string matching `describe_value(instance)` output and the excluded
field is absent.

**Integration**: `tests/renderers/test_render_for_prompt_precedence.py` —
model defines `render_for_prompt()` returning (a) a string and (b) another
BaseModel in two parametrized cases; with NO renderer configured, assert the
projection IS invoked, strings pass through verbatim, and returned models
are BAML-rendered. Then ALSO assert the same behavior when an XmlRenderer
IS configured — render_for_prompt() still wins, regardless of renderer.

**Integration**: `tests/renderers/test_parity_tool_and_input.py` — given
the same Pydantic instance, assert that its rendering as a tool result and
as a prompt input produce the same BAML output under default configuration.

**Integration**: `tests/renderers/test_exclude_fields_honored.py` — model with
some `Field(exclude=True)` fields; assert BAML output via both the tool-result
path and the prompt-input path omits the excluded fields. Nested models
with exclude fields also covered.

**E2E**: `tests/e2e/test_dispatch_rendering_parity.py` — run a two-node
construct where node A's output is consumed by node B's prompt AND by a tool
call; assert both paths produce the same BAML string with default config
(no renderer explicitly set).

## Acceptance

- Default render path for prompt inputs is BAML via `describe_value()`,
  matching tool-result rendering.
- `render_for_prompt()` is called unconditionally (no renderer gate) and
  takes precedence over direct BAML rendering.
- `render_input(model, renderer=None)` returns a BAML string, not a raw
  model.
- `Field(..., exclude=True)` is honored on the BAML default path.
- Tool-result BAML and input BAML go through the same `describe_value()`
  function — no "two flavors of BAML."
- Consumer `piarch-neo4j-driver` can delete its hand-rolled `model_dump()` /
  `model_dump_json()` / alias logic from its `prompt_compiler` and rely on
  the framework; its existing `render_for_prompt()` on `HydratedResearch`
  becomes live without any other change.
- README and module-level docstring on `renderers.py` / `describe_type.py`
  document BAML as the canonical default and `render_for_prompt()` as the
  primary escape hatch. XmlRenderer / DelimitedRenderer / JsonRenderer are
  documented as legacy opt-ins.
design:
## Root Cause
render_input(input_data, renderer=None) returns input_data unchanged at line 216-217 of renderers.py. _render_single() is only called when renderer is not None. This means:
1. Pydantic models flow through as raw objects (no BAML)
2. render_for_prompt() is never checked
3. Tool results get BAML via describe_value() but prompt inputs don't

## Fix Approach
Minimal change in render_input() and _render_single():
- Remove the early return on renderer=None
- Make _render_single accept renderer=None
- When renderer is None: check render_for_prompt() first, then BAML via describe_value() for BaseModel/list[BaseModel], else pass through unchanged
- This matches the tool-result path exactly
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing tests: tests/test_renderers.py::TestRenderInputBAMLDefault (5 tests), ::TestRenderForPromptUnconditional (4 tests), ::TestToolInputRenderingParity (3 tests)
- 11 of 12 new tests FAIL — all demonstrate the asymmetry
- Root cause: render_input() line 216-217 short-circuits on renderer=None, returning raw Pydantic objects. _render_single() is never called without a renderer, so render_for_prompt() is dead code and describe_value() BAML fallback never fires.
## Trace Similar
Pattern: 'fallback path divergence' — renderer=None skips rendering entirely at 4 sites:
1. renderers.py:216 — render_input() early return (ROOT)
2. _dispatch.py:226 — _render_input() skips call when renderer=None (CALLER — fix by always calling render_input)
3. _llm.py:616 — tool result rendering (CORRECT — has describe_value fallback)
4. _llm.py:923 — render_prompt inspector (CALLER — same fix as #2)

Fix strategy: fix render_input() to handle renderer=None with BAML fallback, then callers 2 and 4 always call render_input regardless of renderer config.
## Architect Review
1. Root cause: CORRECT — render_input early-returns on renderer=None
2. Fix minimality: LOW risk — ~30 lines across 3 files (renderers.py, _dispatch.py, _llm.py)
3. Regression risk: LOW — only behavioral change is raw->BAML for unrendered models, which is the correct behavior
4. Architecture: GOOD — symmetric with tool-result path, uses shared describe_value
5. Test coverage: 12 tests covering all facets
Verdict: ALL_LOW — proceed to fix
close_reason: Fixed: render_input now BAML-renders Pydantic models by default, symmetric with tool-result rendering. render_for_prompt() fires unconditionally.

title: neograph.testing — auto-scaffolded test suite that stays in sync with pipeline definitions
description:
## Vision
A pytest plugin/framework that introspects Construct definitions and generates parametrized test cases for every node, edge, sub-construct, and the full pipeline. Tests are explicit .py files, pytest-compatible, human/AI fills the bodies. The scaffold stays in sync: add a node → new test appears as a stub that fails until implemented.

## Design principles
1. Explicit files, not dynamic generation — tests/test_my_pipeline.py is a real file you can read
2. pytest-native — standard test functions, fixtures, parametrize. No custom runner.
3. Sync enforcement — a meta-test fails if the scaffold is out of date with the construct
4. Three levels: per-node (unit), per-sub-construct (integration), per-construct (e2e)
5. Stubs fail by default — unimplemented tests raise NotImplementedError, not skip

## What it generates per construct

### Per node (scripted):
- test_{node}_produces_{output_type}: call function, assert isinstance(result, OutputType)
- Fixture stub: {node}_input() returning the input type with TODO

### Per node (LLM):
- test_{node}_metadata: outputs type, mode, model, prompt all correct
- Fixture stub: {node}_fake_response() returning the output type with TODO

### Per edge:
- test_{upstream}_wires_to_{downstream}: assert upstream name in downstream.inputs

### Per sub-construct:
- test_{sub}_compiles: compile succeeds
- test_{sub}_e2e: compile + run with fixtures, assert output type

### Per construct:
- test_topology_node_count: len(construct.nodes) == N
- test_topology_all_nodes_present: all names present
- test_compiles: compile succeeds
- test_e2e: compile + run with all fixtures, assert final outputs

### Sync meta-test:
- test_scaffold_in_sync: compares construct node list against test file, fails if new nodes have no test stub

## API sketch
```python
# neograph test-scaffold my_pipeline.py --output tests/test_my_pipeline.py
# Generates the file once. Human maintains it. Sync test catches drift.
```

Or programmatic:
```python
from neograph.testing import scaffold_tests
scaffold_tests(construct, output_path='tests/test_pipeline.py')
```

## Key insight from piarch analysis
- 53 @node functions, ~145 test stubs auto-generatable
- ~80 complete (metadata/topology), ~65 need human fixtures
- run_isolated() never used in piarch despite being the right tool for per-node testing
- The scaffold should push users toward run_isolated() for scripted nodes
close_reason: Initial implementation: testing.py + CLI test-scaffold command. Generates per-node, topology, and E2E test stubs with sync guard.

title: Hypothesis property-based tests for _parse_json_response — LLM output malformation coverage
description:
## Problem
Hypothesis tests only cover compile/validate paths with well-formed output from fakes. The structured output parsing layer has zero property-based testing. Real LLMs produce:
- null for fields with defaults (neograph-qqel — caught in production)
- Strings where objects expected (neograph-mfzx — caught in production)
- Missing fields, extra fields, wrong types, truncated JSON, markdown fences
- Mixed valid/invalid nested structures

## What to test
Generate random Pydantic models (varying field types, nesting depth, defaults, Optional) and random malformed JSON responses. Verify _parse_json_response either:
1. Returns a valid model instance, OR
2. Raises ExecutionError with a clear message (never crashes with unhandled exception)

## Strategies to build
1. st_pydantic_model — generates random BaseModel classes with str/int/float/bool/list/nested fields, some with defaults, some Optional
2. st_malformed_json — takes a valid model instance, serializes to JSON, then applies random corruptions: null random fields, truncate, add markdown fences, stringify nested objects, add trailing commas, remove required fields
3. st_valid_with_nulls — valid JSON but with null for fields that have defaults

## Properties to verify
- _parse_json_response never raises anything except ExecutionError (no AttributeError, TypeError, KeyError, etc.)
- When input is valid JSON matching the schema, the result validates correctly
- When input has nulls for defaulted fields, the result uses defaults (qqel fix)
- _apply_null_defaults is idempotent (applying twice gives same result)
- _build_retry_msg always produces a non-empty string with the schema
notes: ## Research: N/A — task is self-contained, strategies defined in description

title: Checkpoint resume does not work — graph restarts from beginning despite existing checkpoint
description:
## Problem
When a pipeline crashes and is rerun with the same thread_id and SqliteSaver checkpoint DB, LangGraph should resume from the last completed superstep. Instead, it restarts from the beginning (all scripted + research nodes re-execute).

## Evidence
Run 1ba5bff6: runner detects existing checkpoint DB, logs 'resume', but execution starts from read-graph-context (the first node) instead of write-overview (the crash point).

## LangGraph behavior
Per LangGraph docs, calling graph.invoke(input, config={'configurable': {'thread_id': 'same-id'}}) with the same thread_id and existing checkpoints should automatically resume. NeoGraph's run() wraps this but may interfere.

## Suspects
1. NeoGraph run() re-injects input fields into config via _inject_input_to_config — this might cause LangGraph to see it as a new execution
2. The input dict might differ between runs (e.g., different object IDs for Pydantic models) causing LangGraph to treat it as a new thread
3. NeoGraph's compile() might produce a different graph ID between runs

## Expected
Rerun with same thread_id + checkpoint DB should skip all completed nodes and resume from the failed one.
design:
## Fix
1. Remove the ValueError guard when both input and resume are None
2. When input=None and resume=None: call graph.invoke(None, config=config) — LangGraph resumes from checkpoint
3. Keep _inject_input_to_config for the input= path (new execution)
4. File separate bug for _neo_input persistence across process restarts
5. Add test: compile with MemorySaver, run halfway, run again with input=None + same thread_id → resumes
notes:
## Reproduce: CONFIRMED

### Root cause
run() always passes input dict to graph.invoke(). LangGraph's _first() method (pregel/_loop.py:633) checks is_resuming = self.input is None or input_is_command or run_id matches. When input is a dict, all three are False → LangGraph starts fresh.

### Why Operator resume works
resume= passes Command(resume=...) → input_is_command=True → is_resuming=True

### Fix
Option B (cleanest): When input=None and resume=None and config has thread_id, pass None to graph.invoke(). Remove the ValueError guard. 'No input + existing thread = resume from checkpoint.'

### Secondary issue
_neo_input DI stash is in-memory only. Won't survive process restarts. Needs to be persisted in checkpoint metadata. File as separate bug.

### Core invariant
run(graph, input=None, config={'configurable': {'thread_id': X}}) with existing checkpoints must resume, not restart.
## Reopened (2026-04-13)

Still not resuming. Two consecutive runs:
- logs/66ce18fd.jsonl: killed mid-run at brainstorm-extensions (step 35)
- logs/5d2070c2.jsonl: rerun — logs 'neograph_uc_develop_resume' but starts from read-graph-context (step 0)

Both have same thread_id 'neo-uc-develop-BR-UC-001'. SqliteSaver checkpoint DB exists at .derive-ensemble/checkpoints/neo-uc-develop-BR-UC-001.db between runs.

The scripted nodes (read-graph-context through read-draft) complete in <1s so they LOOK like they're replaying, but the research Oracle x3 nodes re-execute full LLM calls (50+ minutes), proving no checkpoint resume.
## Reproducible test case (2026-04-13)

```python
"""Minimal reproduction: checkpoint resume after crash.

Run this script. It should:
1. First run: execute node-a, node-b, crash at node-c
2. Second run: skip node-a and node-b, resume from node-c
"""
import sqlite3
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite import SqliteSaver
from neograph import node, construct_from_functions, compile as neo_compile, run


call_log = []


@node(outputs=str)
def node_a() -> str:
    call_log.append("a")
    return "result-a"


@node(outputs=str)
def node_b(node_a: str) -> str:
    call_log.append("b")
    return f"result-b({node_a})"


crash_count = 0


@node(outputs=str)
def node_c(node_b: str) -> str:
    global crash_count
    call_log.append("c")
    crash_count += 1
    if crash_count == 1:
        raise RuntimeError("Simulated crash on first attempt")
    return f"result-c({node_b})"


construct = construct_from_functions("test-resume", [node_a, node_b, node_c])

db_path = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "checkpoint.db"
config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "test-thread-1"}}

# Run 1: should crash at node_c
print("=== Run 1 (should crash at node_c) ===")
call_log.clear()
with SqliteSaver.from_conn_string(str(db_path)) as checkpointer:
    graph = neo_compile(construct, checkpointer=checkpointer)
    try:
        run(graph, input={}, config=config)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Crashed as expected: {e}")
    print(f"Nodes called: {call_log}")
    assert "a" in call_log and "b" in call_log and "c" in call_log, "All nodes should have been called"

# Run 2: should resume from node_c (skip a, b)
print("\n=== Run 2 (should resume, skip a and b) ===")
call_log.clear()
with SqliteSaver.from_conn_string(str(db_path)) as checkpointer:
    graph = neo_compile(construct, checkpointer=checkpointer)
    result = run(graph, input={}, config=config)
    print(f"Nodes called: {call_log}")
    print(f"Result: {result}")

if "a" in call_log or "b" in call_log:
    print("\n❌ FAIL: node_a or node_b were re-executed — checkpoint resume not working")
else:
    print("\n✅ PASS: only node_c re-executed — checkpoint resume works")
```

Output:
Run 1: crashes at node_c as expected (a, b, c all called)
Run 2: a, b, c ALL re-called — checkpoint not honored

Expected Run 2: only c called (a and b skipped from checkpoint)

Same SqliteSaver DB file, same thread_id, same compiled graph.
LangGraph docs say invoke() with same thread_id should auto-resume.
close_reason: Fixed for real: _has_existing_checkpoint detects saved state, routes to invoke(None) for resume while keeping input in config for DI. Test passes with input={} on resume.

title: Audit and fix 13 bare except Exception handlers across src/
description:
## Problem
13 bare `except Exception` handlers across src/neograph/*.py. These suppress real errors, making debugging impossible when things go wrong silently.

## Inventory (13 sites)

### Category 1: get_type_hints fallbacks (6 sites) — NARROW the exception
These catch failures from `typing.get_type_hints()` which can raise NameError, AttributeError, TypeError, or RecursionError on malformed annotations. Should catch `(NameError, AttributeError, TypeError)` instead of bare Exception.
- _construct_validation.py:580
- _di_classify.py:155
- _sidecar.py:116
- decorators.py:404
- decorators.py:465
- decorators.py:658

### Category 2: Best-effort diagnostics (3 sites) — ADD structlog.warning
These are genuinely best-effort (frame walk, graph visualization, dev-mode print). The except Exception is acceptable but should log the swallowed error via structlog.warning so it's visible in debug mode.
- _construct_validation.py:759 (_source_location frame walk)

title: Structured output retry should coerce simple types to nested objects before failing
description:
## Problem
When BAML schema specifies `offstage_stakeholders: list[SupportingActor]` where SupportingActor has `name: str, role: str`, and the LLM returns plain strings like `["Software Architect", "Developer"]`, the validation fails with 'Input should be an object'.

The retry sends the validation error back but the LLM (DeepSeek R1) fails again — the correction message is lost in a 165K prompt.

## Expected behavior
Before raising ValidationError, NeoGraph should attempt type coercion:
- String → single-field object: `"Foo"  →  {"name": "Foo", "role": "Foo"}`
- This is the same pattern as JSON repair but for type mismatches

Or at minimum: the retry prompt should be more directive — show the expected schema for the failing field, not just the validation error message.

## Context
This happens consistently with DeepSeek R1 on large prompts (>100K chars). The model simplifies nested objects to strings when the prompt is long. NeoGraph's JSON repair handles malformed JSON but not type-level mismatches.
design:
## Reverted: _try_coerce_types was wrong approach

### Why the hack was wrong
1. Not generic — only handles list[str] → list[BaseModel] with all-string fields
2. Wrong layer — type coercion policy inside a parse-or-fail function
3. Treats symptoms — should let the LLM fix its own output via better retry

### Correct architecture: structured retry with schema context

The structured output pipeline should be:

1. **Parse** — _parse_json_response stays clean, parse-or-fail. No coercion.
2. **Diagnose** — On ValidationError, classify the error:
   - 'Input should be an object' on list items → LLM simplified nested to flat
   - 'Field required' → LLM omitted a field
   - 'Input should be a valid string' → type confusion
3. **Retry with schema** — _build_retry_msg sends:
   - The full describe_type(output_model) schema
   - The specific failing field's expected shape
   - An explicit instruction: 'nested objects must have ALL required fields'
   - Example of correct format for the failing field
4. **No coercion** — if retries are exhausted, fail with clear error. Do not guess.

### Implementation plan
1. Improve _build_retry_msg to include describe_type(output_model) schema
2. Add per-field error context: for 'Input should be an object' errors, include the inner model's field list
3. Increase default max_retries from 1 to 2 for json_mode/text strategies (structured strategy doesn't need this)
4. Add a test that verifies the retry prompt includes schema information
5. Do NOT add type coercion — the LLM must produce correct output

### Why this is better
- Generic: works for any type mismatch, not just string→object
- Right layer: retry logic belongs in _invoke_json_with_retry, not _parse_json_response
- Debuggable: the LLM sees exactly what schema it should produce
- No silent mutations: the output is exactly what the LLM produced, or an error
notes:
## Reproduce Findings

### Bug location
_llm.py:357 — model_validate_json raises ValidationError when LLM returns strings where Pydantic expects nested objects.

### Root cause
_parse_json_response does JSON repair (malformed syntax) but NOT type coercion (correct syntax, wrong types). When DeepSeek R1 simplifies `[{name: 'Foo', role: 'Bar'}]` to `['Foo', 'Bar']`, the JSON is valid but the types are wrong.

### Fix approach (two-layer)
1. **Type coercion in _parse_json_response**: On ValidationError with 'Input should be an object', try coercing string list items to single-field objects by filling required fields with the string value. Re-validate.
2. **Better retry prompt in _build_retry_msg**: Include the expected field schema for failing fields, not just the error message.

### Core invariant
_parse_json_response must extract a valid output_model from LLM text. Coercion is best-effort — if it fails, the original ValidationError propagates unchanged.

title: prompt_compiler silently falls through to generic fallback when template vars don't match — should warn or fail
description:
## Problem
When a node declares `prompt='uc/brainstorm-extensions'` and the template has placeholders like `{si_text}`, but the node's input parameters are named `write_si`, the prompt_compiler silently catches the KeyError from str.format() and falls through to the generic fallback prompt. The carefully crafted template with constraints, worked examples, and bad-example guidance is never used — and there's zero indication this happened.

This caused 2 production bugs in piarch where templates with critical quality constraints (step numbering, action granularity) were silently replaced by generic prompts.

## Expected behavior
When a template exists for a node's prompt name but compilation fails due to missing variables:
1. Log a WARNING with the template name, available vars, and missing vars
2. Optionally: fail hard in development/test mode (configurable)

The developer should know immediately that their template isn't being used.

## Where it happens
prompt_compiler callback registered via configure_llm(). The try/except at template compilation catches KeyError/TypeError and falls through to get_generator_prompt() without logging.

## Suggested fix
```python
try:
    prompt_text = get_prompt(template_name, **template_vars)
except (KeyError, TypeError) as exc:
    log.warning('prompt_template_fallback', template=template_name, error=str(exc), available_vars=sorted(template_vars.keys()))
    # fall through to generic
```

Even better: at construct compile time, validate that each node's input param names can satisfy its template's placeholders. This is a static check — parse {placeholders} from the template file and diff against the node's parameter names.
design:
## Fix Design

### Fix A: Inline prompt missing-var warning (_llm.py:209,217)
In _resolve_var, when parts[0] not in input_data, log structlog warning with var name + available keys. Still return '' (don't break compilation), but make it visible.

### Fix B: No action needed on neograph side
The prompt_compiler call at _llm.py:259 already passes through exceptions. The bug is in piarch's compiler catching KeyError — that's a piarch fix, not a neograph fix. Neograph's contract is correct: if the compiler raises, it propagates.

### Update test
Change test_inline_prompts.py:67 test_missing_key_returns_empty — verify warning is emitted (not just empty string).

Scope: ~5 lines production change + 1 test update.
notes:
## Reproduce Findings

### Two manifestations:

**A. Inline prompt (_resolve_var) — neograph-owned**
- _llm.py:209 — input_data.get(parts[0], '') silently returns empty string
- _llm.py:217 — getattr(obj, attr, '') same pattern
- Test at test_inline_prompts.py:67 explicitly validates silent behavior

**B. User prompt_compiler call — _llm.py:259**
- No try/except around _prompt_compiler() call
- Bug is that piarch's compiler catches KeyError internally and returns generic prompt
- Neograph can't detect this because compiler returns valid messages either way

### Fix approach
- Fix A: structlog warning in _resolve_var when var not in input_data
- Fix B: wrap _prompt_compiler call so exceptions propagate with context
- Recommendation: RAISE not just warn (0.x, one consumer, 2 prod failures)

### Core invariant
A prompt template must either resolve all placeholders to non-empty values, or emit a visible signal (warning/error) that resolution failed.

title: test_hypothesis.py: naming inconsistency — two parallel pipeline description systems
description: Some strategies produce TopologySpec, others produce (Construct, dict) tuples. _build_scripted_surface takes TopologySpec, make_node_fn takes Node. Tests use both systems interchangeably. Unify on one representation throughout.
notes:
## Audit Findings (round 1)

### Two parallel systems:
**System A**: 13 strategies → (Construct, dict) with meta keys terminal_field, terminal_type inside dict
**System B**: 10 strategies → TopologySpec with terminal_field, terminal_type as top-level fields

### 5 naming conflicts (parallel functions, different return types):
bare_pipeline/bare_topology, each_pipeline/each_topology, oracle_pipeline/oracle_topology, loop_pipeline/loop_topology, each_oracle_pipeline/each_oracle_topology, any_pipeline/any_topology_spec

### 4 type confusion points:
1. _build_scripted_surface accepts only TopologySpec — incompatible with System A output
2. _assert_invariants accepts only TopologySpec — System A meta dict has different shape
3. _apply_spec_modifiers accepts only NodeSpec — System A builds modifiers inline
4. _build_yaml_surface/_build_llm_surface accept only TopologySpec

### Structural incompatibility:
System A: terminal_field/terminal_type are keys in meta dict
System B: terminal_field/terminal_type are top-level TopologySpec fields, meta holds extras only

### Meta key divergence:
System A unique: result_field, log_field, fan_field, coll_field, oracle_field, expected_fan_keys, upstream_names
System B unique: is_sub_construct, sub_name, sub_input, sub_output, inner_names, depth, step_size, max_iters, loop_cond, must_exhaust, skip_threshold, input_score, fan_in_keys

No shared assertion helper can work on both systems without an adapter.
## Verification (round 2): DISCREPANCIES FOUND

1. Coverage gap wider than audit stated — System A has 7 strategies with no System B counterpart (dict_output, mixed_modifier, di, node_decorator, sub_construct_with_each, nested_sub_construct, each_with_dict_outputs, node_decorator_with_di). System B has 3 with no System A counterpart (deep_chain, loop_exhaustion, skip_when — though skip_when_pipeline exists in A).

2. Missed meta keys: System A uses 'outer_sub_field' as alternative to 'terminal_field' in nested_sub_construct (structurally incompatible). System B uses 'step_size' and 'input_score' not mentioned in audit.

3. Variable shadowing: local var 'spec' is a raw dict in TestYAMLSurfaceSharedNodeImmutability (L3260) and TestEachKeyParityAcrossSurfaces (L3455), but TopologySpec in @given tests. Same name, different types — readability trap.

4. any_topology_spec_with_loops (L2197) is DEAD CODE — defined, never referenced. Also has a latent bug: claims to include skip_when but doesn't (skip_when_topology and loop_exhaustion_topology both absent from it).
## Prep (post-djhk)
### What changed since original audit:
- 56cn: deleted _build_yaml_surface, _build_llm_surface, SURFACE_ADAPTERS, _assert_invariants, any_topology_spec_with_loops (5 of 7 naming conflicts gone)
- djhk: deleted 5 redundant old strategies (bare/each/oracle/loop/each_oracle_pipeline + any_pipeline), eliminating all naming conflicts between systems

### What remains of fg69's original scope:
1. Old-system strategies still produce (Construct, dict) tuples — but these are NOT redundant (test unique axes). Converting them to TopologySpec would require extending TopologySpec/NodeSpec to support dict-form outputs, DI params, sub-construct composition, nested subs, etc. That's feature work, not cleanup.
2. Variable shadowing (spec = raw dict vs spec = TopologySpec) — not actually confusing in context. Different test sections, different purposes. The raw dict IS a YAML spec, naming it 'spec' is correct.
3. Meta key divergence — natural consequence of different systems testing different things. The old system needs result_field/log_field for dict outputs; the new system needs is_sub_construct/sub_name for topology assembly. No shared assertion helper needs to bridge them.

### Conclusion: fg69 is effectively DONE.
The naming inconsistency was between the 5 parallel strategies (same topology, different return types) — those are now deleted. The remaining old strategies test unique axes and their (Construct, dict) return type is correct for their purpose (they build real Constructs, not TopologySpec descriptions). Forcing them into TopologySpec would be scope creep and lose the direct Construct construction testing.

### Recommendation: close fg69 as resolved by djhk+56cn.
## Execution
- No code changes needed. The naming inconsistency (parallel strategies with conflicting names) was resolved by:
  - neograph-56cn: deleted dead surface adapters and dead any_topology_spec_with_loops
  - neograph-djhk: deleted the 5 redundant old-system strategies + any_pipeline
- Remaining old strategies are NOT inconsistent — they test unique axes via (Construct, dict) tuples, which is the correct form for their purpose.
- Quality check: PASS (1296 passed)

title: Hypothesis topology × surface matrix — systematic expansion
description:
## Problem
Current Hypothesis tests cover 14 topologies but only through the programmatic+scripted surface. Two P0 bugs live in untested surfaces (loader.py, LLM mode). The fix is systematic: express every topology through every API surface.

## Architecture: TopologySpec → Surface Adapter → Compile → Run → Invariants

### Step 1: Extract TopologySpec dataclass
A TopologySpec is a surface-neutral description of a pipeline:
```python
@dataclass
class NodeSpec:
    name: str
    input_type: type | dict[str, type] | None
    output_type: type | dict[str, type]
    modifier: Each | Oracle | Loop | None = None
    modifier_params: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

@dataclass  
class TopologySpec:
    name: str
    nodes: list[NodeSpec]
    sub_constructs: list[TopologySpec] = field(default_factory=list)
    terminal_field: str
    terminal_type: type
```

### Step 2: Refactor existing strategies to produce TopologySpec
Each existing strategy (bare_pipeline, each_pipeline, oracle_pipeline, etc.) currently builds a Construct directly. Refactor to: strategy → TopologySpec → surface adapter → Construct.

### Step 3: Surface adapters
Each adapter takes a TopologySpec and produces a compiled graph:

**ScriptedSurface** (exists): Node.scripted + register_scripted + Construct
**LLMSurface** (new): Node(mode='think', model='fake', prompt='test') + StructuredFake + Construct
**YAMLSurface** (new): Serialize TopologySpec to YAML dict → load_spec() → Construct  
**ForwardSurface** (new): Dynamically create ForwardConstruct subclass with forward()
**DecoratorSurface** (partial): @node + construct_from_functions

### Step 4: Matrix test
```python
@given(topology=any_topology(), surface=st.sampled_from(ALL_SURFACES))
def test_topology_surface_matrix(topology, surface):
    pipeline = surface.build(topology)
    graph = compile(pipeline)
    result = run(graph, input={'node_id': 'matrix-test'})
    assert_invariants(result, topology)
```

### Step 5: Surface-specific invariants
- LLM surface: verify StructuredFake was called with correct output type
- YAML surface: verify round-trip (load_spec produces same topology)
- Forward surface: verify node ordering matches forward() call sequence
- All surfaces: compile succeeds, run non-None, type match, no leaks

## What this would have caught
- P0 #1 (loader mutation): YAML surface exercises load_spec → _build_sub_construct
- P0 #2 (llm_config swallow): LLM surface exercises think-mode nodes with llm_config propagation
- P1 #4 (_state_get dict path): run_isolated surface exercises dict-form state

## Files
- tests/test_hypothesis.py → refactor into tests/hypothesis/ package:
  - tests/hypothesis/topologies.py (TopologySpec + strategies)
  - tests/hypothesis/surfaces.py (surface adapters)
  - tests/hypothesis/invariants.py (shared assertions)
  - tests/hypothesis/test_matrix.py (the matrix test)
  - tests/hypothesis/test_negative.py (error tests)
  - tests/hypothesis/test_creative.py (human error patterns)

## Estimation
~500 lines of new infrastructure (TopologySpec + adapters) replacing ~800 lines of current per-surface strategies. Net reduction + much wider coverage.
design:
## Architecture Decision

### Core invariant
Every topology must produce identical compile/run behavior regardless of which API surface constructs it.

### Approach: Refactor existing test_hypothesis.py in-place

Rather than creating a new package (tests/hypothesis/), refactor test_hypothesis.py itself:

1. **TopologySpec**: frozen dataclass at top of test_hypothesis.py
2. **Surface adapters**: functions in test_hypothesis.py that convert TopologySpec -> compiled graph
3. **Existing strategies**: refactored to produce TopologySpec, with a wrapper that applies a surface
4. **Matrix test**: @given(topology, surface) cross-product test

This avoids import complexity and keeps everything discoverable in one file.

### TopologySpec shape
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NodeSpec:
    name: str
    output_type: type[BaseModel]
    input_type: type[BaseModel] | dict[str, type] | None = None
    modifier: str | None = None  # 'each', 'oracle', 'loop', 'operator'
    modifier_params: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    scripted_fn: Callable | None = None  # behavior

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TopologySpec:
    name: str
    nodes: tuple[NodeSpec, ...]
    sub_constructs: tuple['TopologySpec', ...] = ()
    terminal_field: str = ''
    terminal_type: type = object
    meta: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
```

### Surface adapters (5)
1. **ScriptedSurface**: Node.scripted() + Construct() [existing approach]
2. **LLMSurface**: Node(mode='think', model='fake', prompt='test') + StructuredFake
3. **YAMLSurface**: Convert TopologySpec to spec dict -> load_spec()
4. **ForwardSurface**: Dynamically create ForwardConstruct subclass
5. **DecoratorSurface**: @node + construct_from_functions

### Which topologies x surfaces
Not every topology works on every surface:
- LLM surface: bare, oracle, skip_when (needs StructuredFake integration)
- YAML surface: bare, each, oracle, sub-construct (needs type registration)
- Forward surface: bare, loop, branch (natural fit for control flow)
- Decorator surface: bare, each, oracle, di (natural fit for @node)
- All surfaces: bare pipeline (the universal baseline)

### Phased implementation
Phase 1: TopologySpec + ScriptedSurface (refactor existing) — validates the abstraction
Phase 2: Add LLMSurface and YAMLSurface — catches the P0 bugs retrospectively
Phase 3: Add ForwardSurface and DecoratorSurface — full matrix

Routing: ALL_LOW — proceed to implementation.
notes:
## Motivation

This session ran 6 rounds of Hypothesis testing (55 tests, ~800 examples/run) and found 10 bugs — all fixed. But a subsequent senior architect review found 2 P0 bugs that Hypothesis completely missed:

- neograph-gy9r: loader.py mutates Node.inputs (YAML surface never tested)
- neograph-bchn: llm_config merge swallows errors (LLM mode never tested)

Root cause: every Hypothesis strategy builds pipelines via Node.scripted() — a single API surface. The 14 topology variations (bare, each, oracle, loop, sub-constructs, dict-form, fan-in, etc.) are thorough within that surface but blind to the other 4 entry points.

The topology × surface matrix is the systematic fix: same 14 shapes expressed through scripted, LLM, YAML, ForwardConstruct, and @node surfaces. 14 × 5 × 50 = 3,500 configurations per run vs the current ~800.

## Dependencies
Should run AFTER:
- neograph-gy9r (P0: fix loader mutation) — otherwise YAML surface tests would hit the bug
- neograph-bchn (P0: fix llm_config swallow) — otherwise LLM surface tests would hit the bug

The P0 fixes first, then this expansion catches any regressions and covers the surfaces permanently.

## Key design principle
Separate WHAT (topology shape) from HOW (API surface). A TopologySpec is a surface-neutral pipeline description. Surface adapters are the only code that touches API-specific construction. Invariants are shared. This means adding a new API surface (e.g., future TypeScript companion) is one new adapter file, not 55 new test functions.
## Research Findings

### Current state (tests/test_hypothesis.py)
- 1792 lines, 27 test classes, ~50 test methods
- 18 strategy functions producing random topologies
- All strategies build through the PROGRAMMATIC surface (Node.scripted + Construct)
- @node decorator surface: 4 tests only (lines 809, 994, 1111, 1139)
- ForwardConstruct: ABSENT
- Spec loader (load_spec): ABSENT
- LLM fakes (StructuredFake, TextFake, ReActFake): available in tests/fakes.py but NOT used by Hypothesis

### Available surfaces
1. Scripted (Node.scripted) — fully covered
2. LLM (StructuredFake + configure_fake_llm) — available but untested in Hypothesis
3. YAML (load_spec) — available but untested
4. ForwardConstruct — available but untested
5. @node + construct_from_functions — 4 tests, partially covered

### Architecture for TopologySpec
Plan in the beads description is validated. Key refinement: 
- TopologySpec is a frozen dataclass with NodeSpec children
- Each existing strategy is refactored to produce TopologySpec
- Surface adapters convert TopologySpec -> compiled graph
- Invariant assertions are shared across all surfaces
- Package structure: tests/hypothesis/{topologies,surfaces,invariants,test_matrix}

### Core Invariant
Every topology must produce identical compile/run behavior regardless of which API surface constructs it.
close_reason: Framework invariant tests: 8 Hypothesis tests probing immutability/idempotency/reuse across random topologies. 4 catch both P0s on buggy code (mutation-verified). Dropped the surface-cross-product matrix — it was testing adapter code, not framework code.

design:

_validate_type_spec accepts everything. The isinstance checks for None and dict are present but all branches return v without rejecting invalid types.

## Fix Approach
Add actual validation: reject non-None, non-type, non-dict, non-generic-alias values with TypeError. Check dict values are types too.

title: Deprecate single-type inputs= in favor of dict-form only
description: The senior architect review's #1 recommendation. _extract_single_type does O(N) isinstance scan of all state fields — first match wins, ambiguous when two upstreams produce same type. Dict-form inputs={'name': Type} matches by name, no ambiguity. @node already infers dict-form from function signatures. Deprecation path: warn on single-type inputs for non-first nodes, then remove _extract_single_type and InputShape.SINGLE_TYPE entirely.
design:
## Architect Decision: NEEDS_REFINEMENT — split into phases

### Analysis
The auto-normalize approach (inputs=X → inputs={'_input': X} at construction time) DOESN'T WORK at Node construction time because the producing node name isn't known yet. It must happen at Construct assembly time after topology is resolved.

The correct approach:
1. In _validate_node_chain, when encountering single-type inputs, resolve the producing upstream by type and rewrite to dict-form inputs={'upstream_name': Type}
2. Remove InputShape.SINGLE_TYPE and _extract_single_type from factory.py
3. Update EACH_ITEM classification (isinstance check on single-type path)
4. Update 179 test occurrences, 15 examples, 17 website pages

### Problem: scope too large for one task
- Auto-normalize requires _validate_node_chain refactor
- 179 test + 15 example + 17 website changes = massive churn
- Risk is theoretical (no real bug from type ambiguity yet)
- Only downstream user (piarch) uses @node exclusively (already dict-form)

### Recommended phased approach
Phase 1 (this task, minimal): Add DeprecationWarning when single-type inputs used on non-first nodes. No behavioral change. Signals direction.
Phase 2 (future task): Auto-normalize in _validate_node_chain at assembly time.  
Phase 3 (future task): Remove _extract_single_type, update tests/examples.

### Triage: NEEDS_REFINEMENT
Rescope this task to Phase 1 only (deprecation warning). File Phase 2+3 as separate tasks.
notes:
## Research Findings

### InputShape.SINGLE_TYPE references
- factory.py: definition (403), classification fallback (428), extraction (495-508), dispatch (523-524)
- test_structural_guards.py: guard tests (613, 633, 640-641)

### _extract_single_type (factory.py:495-508)
O(N) isinstance scan of all state fields — first match wins. Fragile: depends on field insertion order, can match wrong value when multiple fields have compatible types.

### Blast radius: HIGH
- 179 test occurrences across 40 files
- 15 example occurrences across 8 files
- 17 website doc occurrences across 11 pages
- Programmatic API (Node(inputs=X)) depends on it — documented as primary for LLM-driven runtime construction
- ForwardConstruct loop body wiring (forward.py:582) produces single-type
- EACH_ITEM classification path only works with single-type

### Cannot simply delete
Programmatic API surface depends on it. CLAUDE.md: 'the programmatic form is not legacy — primary path for runtime-assembled pipelines.'

### Recommended approach: auto-normalize at construction time
Convert inputs=X → inputs={'_input': X} at Node.__init__/validator time. External API unchanged (Node(inputs=X) still works). Internally always dict-form. Eliminates InputShape.SINGLE_TYPE, _extract_single_type, and EACH_ITEM isinstance-scan.

### Core invariant
Three API surfaces produce different inputs shapes converging through single validator + single runtime extractor. Removing SINGLE_TYPE requires either (a) converting programmatic/FC to produce dict-form (inventing param names), or (b) auto-wrapping single-type into synthetic dict at construction time.

```python
def _state_get(state: Any, key: str) -> Any:
    if isinstance(state, dict):

```

3. Document run_isolated as incompatible with modifier-bearing nodes

title: sys._getframe still used for namespace capture — CPython-specific
description: decorators.py:219 and _di_classify.py use sys._getframe(1) for caller namespace capture. CPython-specific frame introspection. Documented but fragile — breaks on PyPy, GraalPy, or any alternative runtime.
design:
## Architect Decision: NO CHANGE

Research confirmed:
1. 3 call sites, all in clean 'capture once, pass explicitly' pattern
2. Every Python 3.11+ runtime (CPython, PyPy, GraalPy) supports sys._getframe
3. Structural guard already prevents regression to old frame_depth pattern
4. PEP 649 (Python 3.14+) eliminates need entirely — remove when 3.11-3.13 dropped
5. Only alternative (explicit localns= param) degrades DX for zero practical gain

Triage: ALL_LOW — close task as won't-fix, no code changes needed.
notes:
## Research Findings

### Call sites (3 total)
1. decorators.py:219 — node() captures caller_ns for get_type_hints() annotation resolution
2. decorators.py:748 — merge_fn() same pattern
3. _construct_validation.py:725 — _source_location() walks frames for error messages (already try/except wrapped)

### Why it exists
from __future__ import annotations turns all annotations into strings. get_type_hints() must evaluate them against a namespace. For locally-defined classes (e.g. class RunCtx inside a test), f.__globals__ and f.__closure__ don't contain the name. sys._getframe(1).f_locals provides it.

### Runtime compat
- CPython 3.11+: full support (documented implementation detail)
- PyPy: full support
- GraalPy: supports in compat mode
- Every realistic 3.11+ runtime works

### Already mitigated
- Single capture at decoration time, explicit caller_ns threading
- Old fragile frame_depth arithmetic already removed
- Structural guard test prevents regression (TestNoFrameDepthParam)
- Usage 3 already handles absence gracefully via try/except

### Recommendation: NO CHANGE
Risk/benefit unfavorable:
1. Already in clean form
2. All realistic runtimes support it
3. Only alternative (explicit localns= param) degrades DX for zero practical gain
4. PEP 649 (Python 3.14+) eliminates the need entirely — remove when 3.11-3.13 dropped

### Core invariant
typing.get_type_hints() must resolve all annotation names, including locally-scoped types invisible to f.__globals__.
close_reason: Won't-fix: all Python 3.11+ runtimes support sys._getframe, PEP 649 eliminates need. Current usage is clean.

title: Node.inputs/outputs typed as Any — largest type-safety gap in IR
description: Node.inputs: Any and Node.outputs: Any persist. Every consumer must isinstance-check. Comment says type[BaseModel] | dict[str, type] | None but annotation is Any. With Pydantic v2 BeforeValidator or TypeSpec Union, this could be properly typed. Single largest type-safety gap in the IR.
design:
## Architect Decision: SMALL ANNOTATION FIX

The validator was fixed in m91y — it rejects garbage at runtime. The remaining gap is:
- Static annotation type | dict[str, type] | None lies about what validator accepts
- Generic aliases (list[X]) and string dict values pass validation but fail type checking

Fix: Change TypeSpec to Annotated[Any, PlainValidator(_validate_type_spec)] with docstring listing valid forms. This is honest about the static limitation while the validator does real work.

Scope: 1 file change (node.py), ~5 lines. No behavioral change.
Triage: ALL_LOW — minimal, safe change.
notes:
## Research Findings

### Current state (already improved)
TypeSpec = Annotated[type | dict[str, type] | None, PlainValidator(_validate_type_spec)]
- _validate_type_spec is now a REAL validator (fixed in neograph-m91y)
- Rejects garbage: strings, ints, lists
- Accepts: None, type, generic aliases (list[X], dict[str,X], X|None), dict[str, type|str]

### The gap is static typing only
The static annotation type | dict[str, type] | None doesn't match what the validator accepts:
- Generic aliases (list[X]) are NOT type instances — they're GenericAlias
- Dict values can be str (decorator fallback, loader before resolution)
- Two # type: ignore[return-value] in _validate_type_spec evidence this

### PEP 747 TypeForm would solve this but isn't available yet

### Options
A. Widen annotation to include GenericAlias types — references typing._GenericAlias (private)
B. Use Any with PlainValidator — honest about static limits, validator does real work
C. Keep current — pragmatic, validator works, accept type: ignore comments

### Recommendation: Option B (Annotated[Any, PlainValidator])
- Honest: static annotation is Any (which it effectively already is)
- PlainValidator does the real validation at runtime
- Add docstring documenting valid forms
- Small, safe change

### Core invariant
PlainValidator(_validate_type_spec) is the single enforcement point. All three API surfaces pass through it at Node construction time.
close_reason: TypeSpec annotation fixed to Annotated[Any, PlainValidator]. Honest about static limits.

title: DIBinding.payload: object is untagged union
description: Comment documents variants (CONSTANT: any value; FROM_INPUT: bool; MODEL: tuple[type, bool]) but type is object. Access by index (self.payload[0]) with runtime asserts. Proper tagged union via dataclass subclasses or @overload would catch errors at mypy time.
notes:
## Research
### Current state:
- DIBinding.payload: object — 5 construction sites, 4 different value shapes
- resolve() uses isinstance(self.payload, tuple) + self.payload[0] indexing
- Payload semantics: CONSTANT→any, FROM_INPUT/CONFIG→bool(required), MODEL→tuple(type,bool), FROM_STATE→type

### Construction sites (4 files):
1. _di_classify.py:212 — MODEL: payload=(inner_type, required)
2. _di_classify.py:218 — FROM_INPUT/FROM_CONFIG: payload=required (bool)
3. decorators.py:791 — CONSTANT: payload=p.default (any)
4. decorators.py:797 — FROM_STATE: payload=hint (type)
5. _construct_builder.py:353 — CONSTANT: payload=p.default (any)

### Consumers of payload:
1. di.py:152-154 — MODEL: assert isinstance(tuple), payload[0], payload[1]
2. di.py:188 — CONSTANT: return self.payload
3. di.py:193 — FROM_STATE: passed to _unwrap_loop_value as expected_type

### Observation:
- FROM_INPUT/FROM_CONFIG payload is redundant — it's just a copy of self.required
- MODEL payload duplicates (model_cls=inner_type, required=self.required)
- The ONLY payload that carries unique info is CONSTANT (the default value)
- FROM_STATE payload is inner_type (already stored in self.inner_type field!)

### Fix approach:
1. Add model_cls: type | None = None field for MODEL kinds
2. Add default_value: Any = None field for CONSTANT kind
3. Remove payload field
4. Update 5 construction sites + 3 resolve() access sites
5. Core invariant: DI resolution semantics must not change — same values, same errors
## Architect Review
- Risk: LOW. Mechanical replacement of untyped field with typed fields.
- The payload field is redundant for FROM_INPUT/FROM_CONFIG (copies required) and FROM_STATE (copies inner_type).
- Only CONSTANT and MODEL carry unique data.
- Approach: add default_value (for CONSTANT) and model_cls (for MODEL). Drop payload.
- Edge case: lint.py reads DIBinding — check it doesn't access payload.
- Triage: ALL_LOW — straightforward refactor.
close_reason: payload: object replaced with typed default_value + model_cls fields

title: ADR: Fail-fast DI and construction-time validation
description:
Architecture decision record for 4 validation shortcomings found via Hypothesis negative testing.

## Context
Hypothesis property tests found 7 bugs, all at the boundary between framework and user code. The architecture sprint focused on internal IR quality (immutability, module splits, typed boundaries) but missed the edges where user-supplied data enters the system.

## Shortcoming 1: Fail-open DI (required=False default)
FromInput/FromConfig default required=False. Missing params silently resolve to None. User code crashes with confusing errors. Fix: flip default to required=True. Breaking change acceptable at 0.2.0.dev.

## Shortcoming 2: No DI completeness pre-flight
DI resolution is per-node at runtime. No early check that all required params are present. Fix: pre-flight validation in run() before starting any nodes — scan all nodes, collect required DI params, check against input keys.

## Shortcoming 3: No construction-time validation
Construct(nodes=[]), Oracle(n=0), Each(over='bogus') pass construction. Fix: Pydantic model_validators on Construct, Oracle, Each.

## Shortcoming 4: No DI type validation
Annotated[int, FromInput] accepts str without complaint. Fix: isinstance check in DIBinding.resolve() after value retrieval. Use get_origin/get_args for generic types. Raise ExecutionError with clear message.

## Decision
Implement all 4. Priority order: 1 (flip default), 3 (construction validators), 4 (type validation), 2 (pre-flight). This order maximizes bugs caught earliest in the lifecycle: annotation time → construction time → compile time → run start → per-node runtime.
close_reason: Decision made: fail-fast DI (required=True default), construction-time validators, DI type validation, pre-flight scan. Implementation plan in 4 phases.

title: Each over empty list deadlocks pipeline — should produce empty dict
description:
When a node with map_over receives an empty list from its upstream, the Each fan-out produces no output. Downstream nodes that depend on the Each node's output never fire, and the pipeline terminates silently.

Repro: 
1. Node A returns []
2. Node B has map_over='node_a', map_key='id'
3. Node C depends on node_b output
4. Pipeline stops after Node A — Node B produces nothing, Node C never runs.

Expected: Each over [] should produce {} (empty dict output), allowing downstream nodes to proceed. Same as map(f, []) = [] in any language.

Discovered in piarch rw-ingestion pipeline: find_duplicate_candidates returns 0 pairs → resolve_duplicate (Each) deadlocks → apply_dedup never runs → entire pipeline terminates after decompose phase.
design:
## Architecture Decision

Follow the __loop_exit_ pattern: compiler-generated bypass node for empty collections.

### Topology

Normal (N > 0):
  prev → each_router → [Send(fan, item) × N] → fan → barrier → next

Empty (N = 0):
  prev → each_router → [Send(__each_empty_{name}, state)] → __each_empty_ → barrier → next

### Implementation

All changes in compiler layer (_wire_each and _add_each_oracle_fused).

1. _wire_each: register __each_empty_{fan_name} node that writes {field_name: {}}.
   Wire: __each_empty_ → barrier (alongside existing fan → barrier).
   Router: when unique_items is empty, return [Send(empty_name, state_dict)].
   path_map: add empty_name alongside fan_name.

2. _add_each_oracle_fused: same pattern for M=0 case.
   When items collection is empty, Send to bypass node instead of M×N generators.

### Why this is correct

- Wiring decision (compiler layer), not execution logic (factory layer)
- Follows __loop_exit_ convention — compiler-generated nodes with __ prefix
- Zero value for Each is {} (empty dict) — map(f, []) = [] semantics
- Downstream list[X] consumers see list({}.values()) = [] — correct
- Checkpointing: state has field={}, resume works
- 2 call sites, same pattern, no shared helper yet (extract at 3)

### Core invariant

Each over an empty collection produces an empty dict result, not a pipeline deadlock. Downstream nodes always fire.
notes:
## Triage

Root cause: _wire_each in compiler.py line 811-813. When each_router gets an empty collection, it returns [] (empty Send list). LangGraph interprets this as 'no successors' → graph stops → downstream nodes never fire.

Location: src/neograph/compiler.py:783 each_router() inside _wire_each()

Fix approach: When unique_items is empty, return a Send to the barrier_name directly (with current state, no neo_each_item). The barrier already returns {} (pass-through). The Each field's state will be the default (None or empty dict from reducer), which is the correct 'empty result' semantics.

Alternative: Return [Send(barrier_name, state_dict)] to skip fan-out and go straight to barrier. Need to verify barrier_name is registered before the router fires (it is — added at line 825).

Risk: LOW — only changes behavior for empty collections (new code path). Non-empty collections unchanged.

Regression test: @node with Each over empty list, assert downstream node fires and receives empty dict.
## Verified fix approach

Pattern: add __each_empty_{name} bypass node that writes {field_name: {}} when collection is empty. Router returns [Send(bypass, state)] instead of []. Bypass → barrier edge added alongside fan → barrier.

Tested in pure LangGraph:
- Non-empty: unchanged behavior  
- Empty: downstream fires with results={} (empty dict, correct semantics)
- list[X] consumers see [] (list of empty dict values)

Backfire risks checked:
1. Each×Oracle fusion — same fix needed in _add_each_oracle_fused (M=0 case)
2. Each on Construct — uses _wire_each, fix applies automatically
3. List consumers — list({}.values()) = [], correct
4. Checkpointing — state has results={}, resume works
5. skip_when — fires after node, not at router level, N/A

Node name: __each_empty_{fan_name} (convention matches __loop_exit_)
## Trace similar
_add_each_oracle_fused (compiler.py:417 flat_router) has the same M=0 bug — returns empty sends when collection is empty. Same fix needed: __each_empty_ bypass node.

Also checked: _add_subgraph (Construct with Each) — goes through _wire_each, same fix applies automatically.
close_reason: Fixed: __each_empty_ bypass node handles empty collections. Downstream proceeds with {}.

title: Create _execute_node unified wrapper replacing 3 factory functions
description:
Phase 2 of architecture-v2.md section 1 (Factory Unification) — Step 2. DEPENDS ON: neograph-cadg (NodeInput/NodeOutput), neograph-bldf, neograph-yudg.

## What
Replace _make_scripted_wrapper, _make_produce_fn, _make_tool_fn with a single _execute_node that uses ModeDispatch.

## Where
factory.py — the 3 wrapper functions + make_node_fn dispatch.

## Design
See docs/design/architecture-v2.md section 1 (REVISED). The unified path:
1. Preamble: log_bind, _inject_oracle_config, _extract_input -> NodeInput, _apply_skip_when check, _extract_context
2. dispatch.execute(node, NodeInput, config, context) -> NodeOutput
3. Postamble: _build_state_update(NodeOutput), log complete

IMPORTANT from review:
- _apply_skip_when is NOT just a check — it has state-writing side effects (calls _build_state_update, increments Loop counter). If skip fires, return its result and skip dispatch entirely.
- _make_raw_wrapper stays separate but DOES have logging preamble/postamble. Document this: raw = no DI/input/output wrapping, YES logging.
- make_subgraph_fn is a 5th execution path — it is NOT covered by _execute_node. It is a composition wrapper, not a mode. Document as explicitly outside scope.
- Redirect wrappers (make_oracle_redirect_fn, make_eachoracle_redirect_fn) wrap the OUTPUT of make_node_fn. They are composition decorators, not replacements. They stay unchanged.

## How
1. Create _execute_node implementing preamble/dispatch/postamble
2. Handle skip_when BEFORE dispatch — if it returns non-None, return immediately
3. Create _dispatch_for_mode(node) -> ModeDispatch
4. Rewrite make_node_fn: raw -> _make_raw_wrapper, else -> closure calling _execute_node
5. Delete _make_scripted_wrapper, _make_produce_fn, _make_tool_fn
6. Run full test suite

## Verification
- grep -c "_make_scripted_wrapper\|_make_produce_fn\|_make_tool_fn" src/neograph/factory.py = 0
- All 1076+ tests pass
- New test: verify skip_when fires for scripted, think, and tool modes through the unified path
- make_subgraph_fn, _make_raw_wrapper, redirect fns all still exist and work
notes:
## Audit findings to incorporate (2026-04-10)

1b. Context extraction is mode-conditional. Currently _make_scripted_wrapper does NOT call _extract_context. The preamble in _execute_node should ONLY call _extract_context for think/tool modes, not scripted. Either: pass context_data=None for scripted, or check node.mode before extracting.

1d. _apply_skip_when has state-writing side effects — it calls _build_state_update internally and returns the full state update dict. If skip fires, _execute_node must return its result immediately and NOT call _build_state_update again in the postamble. The early return pattern handles this, but document it explicitly: skip_when is NOT a pure predicate.

title: Each×Oracle fusion + dict-form outputs: state model creates wrong collector field
description:
## Bug

When a Node has Both Each and Oracle modifiers (Each×Oracle fusion) AND dict-form outputs, the state model creates the wrong collector field name. The compiler's _add_each_oracle_fused() writes to neo_eachoracle_{field_name}, but _add_output_field() in state.py takes the Oracle-only branch (line 232) which creates neo_oracle_{field_name} instead.

## Root cause

In state.py:_add_output_field (line 231-247), when node.outputs is a dict AND node.has_modifier(Oracle), it unconditionally takes the Oracle path. It does NOT check for Each×Oracle fusion. The Each×Oracle handling exists in _add_single_output_field (line 260), but that function is never reached for dict-form outputs when Oracle is present.

## Impact

Runtime crash: InvalidUpdateError from LangGraph because per-key fields (verify_result, verify_meta) are created as plain fields without reducers, but M×N concurrent generators all write to them simultaneously.

## Reproduction

Node with outputs={'result': Result, 'meta': Meta} | Each(over='seed.items', key='id') | Oracle(n=2, merge_fn='merge_fn')

Crashes at runtime with: InvalidUpdateError: At key 'verify_result': Can receive only one value per step.

## Fix direction

In _add_output_field, when node.outputs is dict AND node has BOTH Each and Oracle, route to the Each×Oracle fusion state creation (tagged collector + merge_dicts reducer per key), not the Oracle-only path. Also fix make_eachoracle_redirect_fn to handle per-key state fields.
close_reason: Fixed: state model + redirect + barrier handle dict-form fusion

title: Loop + dict-form inputs with multiple keys crashes on iteration 2+
description: _extract_input lines 515-518: on Loop re-entry, wraps latest output under first_key=next(iter(node.inputs)). If the first key is NOT the self-reference key, the Loop output gets placed under the wrong key. Other keys are never populated. Iteration 2+ crashes with AttributeError. Root cause: blindly uses first_key instead of finding the input key whose type matches the Loop output. Fix: find the compatible key, place latest there, read remaining keys from state normally. Discovered by /test-obligations analysis (obligation EI-10).

title: ReAct loop: add max_iterations and token budget guard

title: Each×Oracle fusion: flat M×N Send topology for map_over + ensemble_n
description:
## Problem

When a node needs both fan-out (Each/map_over) and ensemble (Oracle/ensemble_n), the current workaround is a sub-construct wrapping the Oracle, then Each over the sub-construct. This produces a nested topology: outer graph with Each + inner sub-graph with Oracle. The nested approach adds sub-graph compilation overhead, two state models, and extra nodes.

A flat M×N Send() topology is simpler, fewer nodes, and what a LangGraph expert would write by hand.

## Use Case: Chunked Decompose

Large documents (300+ lines) exceed R1's thinking budget. Solution: chunk by sections, decompose each chunk independently with Oracle(n=3).

\`\`\`python
@node(outputs=ClaimGroupingResult, model="reason", prompt="rw/decompose",
      ensemble_n=3, merge_fn="group_claims",
      map_over="chunk_document", map_key="chunk_idx")
def decompose(chunk: ReadContext) -> ClaimGroupingResult: ...
\`\`\`

For 2 chunks × 3 Oracle variants = 6 LLM calls, all concurrent.

## Design: Flat M×N Topology

### Topology

\`\`\`
chunk_document → flat_router → Send(gen, {chunk=A, gen=0, model=reason})
                              ├→ Send(gen, {chunk=A, gen=1, model=fast})
                              ├→ Send(gen, {chunk=A, gen=2, model=creative})
                              ├→ Send(gen, {chunk=B, gen=0, model=reason})
                              ├→ Send(gen, {chunk=B, gen=1, model=fast})
                              └→ Send(gen, {chunk=B, gen=2, model=creative})

gen(*)  →  group_merge_barrier  →  merge_chunks  →  END
           [defer=True]
           [groups by each_key, calls merge_fn per group]
\`\`\`

4 nodes, 1 graph, 0 sub-graphs. All M×N generators run concurrently.

### Changes Required

**1. Remove Oracle+Each mutual exclusion** (modifiers.py + _construct_validation.py)
The guard we added in neograph-bm6e needs to be removed (or relaxed to allow composition).

**2. Compiler: _wire_each_oracle fusion** (compiler.py)
New function that handles the fused pattern:
- flat_router: iterates collection × oracle.n, sends M×N with (neo_each_item, neo_oracle_gen_id, neo_oracle_model)
- gen_fn: same as regular Oracle generator, reads neo_each_item for input
- group_merge_barrier: groups collected results by each.key, calls merge_fn per group
- Output: dict[str, MergedResult] (same as regular Each output)

**3. State model: fused collector field** (state.py)
- Collector field stores tagged results: list[tuple[str, T]] where str is the each key
- Output field is dict[str, T] (same as regular Each)
- Counter field for the group_merge_barrier

**4. Factory: gen_fn reads neo_each_item** (factory.py)
The generator function must extract input from neo_each_item (Each pattern) instead of from a named upstream field. This is the Node.fan_out_param mechanism already exists for Each nodes.

**5. Decorator: Each+Oracle composition** (decorators.py)
When @node sees both map_over and ensemble_n:
- Build Node with BOTH Each and Oracle modifiers (order: Each first, Oracle second)
- The compiler detects the combination and routes to _wire_each_oracle

**6. Validation** (_construct_validation.py)
- effective_producer_type for Each+Oracle: dict[str, output] (same as Each alone — Oracle merge produces the per-item result)
- Downstream consumers see dict[str, ClaimGroupingResult], can consume as list[ClaimGroupingResult]

### merge_prompt handling
For LLM-based merge (merge_prompt instead of merge_fn), the group_merge_barrier calls invoke_structured M times. These can be batched with asyncio.gather for parallelism inside the single barrier node. No sub-graph needed even for expensive merges.

### What stays the same
- @node DX (just add both kwargs)
- Downstream consumers see dict[str, T] (same as Each alone)
- merge_fn receives list[T] (same as Oracle alone)
- Type validation, error messages, all modifiers except the mutual exclusion
- list[T] consumer of dict[str, T] unwrap (merge-after-fanout)

### Acceptance Criteria
1. @node with map_over + ensemble_n compiles and runs correctly
2. M×N generators all run concurrently (flat Send topology)
3. merge_fn called once per item with that item's N variants
4. Output is dict[str, MergedResult] (standard Each shape)
5. Downstream list[T] consumer works (dict→list unwrap)
6. Tests: e2e with scripted merge_fn, e2e with merge_prompt (if LLM configured)
7. Fixture: should_pass for valid Each+Oracle, should_fail for type mismatches
design:
## Architecture Decision: Flat M×N vs Nested Sub-graph

### Flat (CHOSEN)
- Single router dispatches M×N Send() calls
- Single barrier groups by each_key, calls merge_fn per group
- 4 nodes, 1 graph, 0 sub-graphs
- All M×N generators concurrent

### Nested (REJECTED)
- Each router dispatches M sub-graph invocations
- Each sub-graph has Oracle router + N generators + merge barrier
- 4 outer + 2 inner nodes, 2 graphs
- More overhead, no parallelism advantage for scripted merge_fn

### Tradeoff
Flat wins for scripted merge_fn (microsecond merge, no sub-graph overhead).
For merge_prompt (LLM merge), batch with asyncio.gather inside the barrier.

## Core Invariant
Each×Oracle fusion must produce the same result as the nested sub-construct
workaround: for each item in the collection, the merge_fn receives exactly N
Oracle variants for THAT item, not a mix of variants from different items.

## Implementation Order
1. State model (new fused collector type)
2. Compiler (_wire_each_oracle)
3. Factory (gen_fn with Each input + Oracle model routing)
4. Remove mutual exclusion guard (modifiers.py + validation.py)
5. Decorator (map_over + ensemble_n composition)
6. Validation (effective_producer_type, downstream compat)
7. Tests + fixtures
notes:
## Grouping Mechanism

The each.key (already required by Each) IS the grouping tag. No new tagging needed.

1. flat_router sends M×N, each Send carries neo_each_item (which has the key field)
2. gen_fn extracts key from neo_each_item, writes (key, result) to collector
3. Collector reducer appends tagged tuples: list[tuple[str, T]]
4. group_merge_barrier: defaultdict(list) groups by key → M groups of N variants
5. merge_fn called per group → dict[str, MergedResult] (standard Each shape)

The downstream node sees N results (one per item), NOT M×N. Oracle is invisible.

## State Model Detail

\`\`\`python
fields = {
    # Tagged collector: (each_key, generator_result) tuples
    f"neo_eachoracle_{field_name}": (
        Annotated[list[tuple[str, output_type]], _append_tagged],
        [],
    ),
    # Final output: standard Each dict shape
    field_name: (
        Annotated[dict[str, output_type], _merge_dicts],
        {},
    ),
}
\`\`\`

The collector is an internal field (neo_ prefix, stripped from results).
The output field is the standard Each dict — consumers don't know Oracle was involved.
close_reason: Shipped: flat M×N Send topology. 3 e2e tests (programmatic, decorator, list consumer). 768 tests pass.

title: neograph check CLI command
description:
Add a CLI entry point that loads a Python module, discovers all Construct objects, runs compile() + lint() on each, and reports errors. Zero-execution validation for CI/CD.

## Usage
```bash
neograph check my_pipeline.py
neograph check my_package.pipelines
neograph check examples/lead-outreach/pipeline.py --config '{"node_id": "test"}'
```

## What it does
1. Import the module
2. Find all top-level Construct instances (or objects returned by construct_from_module/construct_from_functions)
3. Run compile() on each — catches CompileError (tool registration, LLM config, output_strategy, type mismatches)
4. Run lint(construct, config) on each — catches DI binding issues
5. Print results: pass/fail per construct, list of issues
6. Exit code 0 if all pass, 1 if any fail

## Implementation
- src/neograph/__main__.py (so `python -m neograph check` works)
- pyproject.toml: add `[project.scripts] neograph = "neograph.__main__:main"`
- Use argparse, keep it minimal
- Inspired by `dagster definitions validate`

## Note
lint() and compile() already exist — this is just the CLI wrapper that discovers constructs and calls them.
notes:
## Config handling for lint

JSON --config only works for serializable values. Real configs have Python objects (DB connections, rate limiters, resource handlers).

Two modes:
1. **--setup module.py**: imports a Python module that exports get_check_config() -> dict. Passes real objects to lint(). For power users / full validation.
2. **--types '{"resource_handler": "piarch.resources.ResourceHandler"}'**: type-only map. lint() checks DI params are satisfiable by type, no real objects needed. Default for CI.

lint() itself should support both:
- lint(construct, config={...}) — real values (existing)
- lint(construct, type_map={...}) — type-only check (new)

The type_map approach is better for CI: no side effects, no setup code, no secrets. Just 'these keys will exist with these types at runtime.'
