title: The api manifest is interpreter-coupled, and the guard encodes which Python built it
description:
website/src/data/api-manifest.json is generated by introspection and guarded for BYTE-EXACT freshness. Some values are annotation reprs that differ by interpreter:

    3.12: "Optional[Literal['output', 'tool']]"
    3.14: "Literal['output', 'tool'] | None"

So the guard does not check 'the manifest matches the code'. It checks 'the manifest matches the code AS SEEN BY THE INTERPRETER THAT GENERATED IT'. On any other supported Python it fails, and the obvious fix -- regenerate and commit -- moves the failure to everyone else.

Observed twice in one session. The main worktree ran 3.12.9 with no pin and showed three red manifest guards on a clean develop; earlier, a stray .python-version pinning 3.12 in the release worktree made the release gate run on the wrong interpreter entirely.

Mitigated for now by committing .python-version = 3.14, which makes the artifact reproduce. That pins the DEV interpreter; pyproject still declares requires-python >=3.11 for the package, so the mitigation hides a real coupling rather than removing it: the repo now cannot regenerate its own docs on a Python it claims to support.
acceptance_criteria: Either the manifest generator normalises interpreter-dependent reprs so the artifact is identical on every supported Python, or the freshness guard states the interpreter requirement and fails with that as its message instead of a byte diff. A contributor on 3.11 or 3.12 can run the suite green without regenerating anything.

title: Let an agent's typed tool results be declared as node output via a projection
description:
GH #18. neograph already knows the type of every tool result: tools declare an output model, the battery hydrates it, and it arrives on ToolInteraction.typed_result -- typed, validated, done. So when an agent node finishes, the framework is holding a typed record of everything the agent read, and the consumer still has to write a NODE to get it out.

Wanted shape:
    @node(mode='agent', outputs=Claim, tools=[...], emits=stamp_readings)
    def verify(claim_in: Claim): ...

The projection is deliberately a PLAIN FUNCTION the caller passes, not something the framework guesses -- turning a tool result into a domain Reading means assigning a locus and banding against norms. The ask is that the projection be a function, not a node to add to the graph and explain in a module docstring.

Distinct from neograph-iq4a3 (GH #16, the general accumulator) which would also make this expressible: here neograph is ALREADY doing the hard part -- typing, hydration and accumulation of tool_log all exist. Only the declaration of a projection is missing. Filed separately so it is not blocked behind the general mechanism, and so the narrower one can ship first if the general design takes longer.
acceptance_criteria: An agent node declares a projection over its tool interactions and the projected value is available as node output, surviving a fan boundary. Proven by a RUN. The projection receives the typed results, not re-parsed text. Declaring no projection changes nothing about today's tool_log behaviour.

title: A scripted node cannot reference run state via context=
description:
context= resolves only for LLM-mode nodes. _execute.py gates it twice:

    context_data = _extract_context(bus, node) if node.mode != 'scripted' else None

So the back-reference GH #15 asks for is available to think/agent/act nodes and NOT to a scripted node, though the issue's title says 'a step' and a scripted step has the same need -- it is the mode most likely to be making the call that needs run identity.

The exclusion looks like a consequence of where context= grew up rather than a decision: it was built as a PROMPT-injection channel ('verbatim state fields injected into the prompt'), and a scripted node has no prompt, so the branch reads as 'nothing to inject into'. But the capability is not about prompts; the value is in state either way, and a scripted body could receive it the same way it receives its DI params.

Confirm the reasoning before widening: read whether anything downstream assumes context implies an LLM path, as the runtime was read before widening Each to tuples in neograph-wojl8.
acceptance_criteria: A scripted node declaring context=['ctx'] receives the value, proven by a test that RUNS rather than assembles. The three-surface parity rule applies -- @node, declarative and programmatic. If the exclusion turns out to be load-bearing, that reason is written at the gate instead of the current silent branch.
notes:
## Investigated, and the fix is NOT to build it

The bead assumed a scripted node needs context= and cannot have it. Measured on both surfaces, a scripted node ALREADY reads run state while its port carries a fanned item:

  programmatic: inputs={'item': Claim, 'ctx': RunCtx}, fan_out_param='item'
  @node:        def branch(item: Claim, ctx: RunCtx) -> Out  with map_over=
  both:         {'a': 'a@4822', 'b': 'b@4822'}

For a scripted node an upstream read IS a normal declared input. There was never a special mechanism to find.

## Why widening context= would be worse, not neutral
A fan-in input is TYPE-CHECKED by the validator and creates a real dataflow edge. A context field is typed Any in state.py and declares no edge. Adding context= support for scripted nodes would trade a checked mechanism for an unchecked one and leave two ways to do one thing -- against the north star, which is about removing ways to be wrong.

The ScriptedDispatch comment said 'scripted nodes have no LLM context needs', which read as an oversight. It was right, for a reason it did not state. Now it states it.

## Closed as won't-fix, with the capability PINNED
tests/test_scripted_run_state.py covers both surfaces, because 'it already works' only justifies not building something for as long as it keeps working. Documented in AGENTS.md and at the dispatch site.
close_reason: Won't fix: a scripted node already reads run state as a typed fan-in input, on both surfaces, including under Each. That route is type-checked where context= is Any, so widening context= would add a weaker second way. Capability pinned by tests/test_scripted_run_state.py.

title: Bug triage: GH #14 container output types
description: Triage and fix bugs through a reproduction-first workflow: reproduce -> trace similar -> architect review -> triage -> fix -> e2e verify -> commit. Each atom is self-contained -- findings stored in the beads task itself.

title: Each rejects a tuple terminal field, forcing a mutable list into a frozen domain model
description:
GH #14, section 5. Each requires the fanned terminal field to be annotated list; a tuple[X, ...] field is rejected at assembly:

    Each(over='seed.claims') terminal field is not a list
      expected: list[...]
      found: tuple

Reproduced: an identical construct with claims: list[Claim] is accepted and with claims: tuple[Claim, ...] is not.

For a domain model built on frozen pydantic with tuple fields throughout -- which is what a frozen model naturally uses, since list is mutable and defeats the freeze -- this forces a mutable list field purely to satisfy the fan-out. The framework is dictating a mutability choice inside the consumer's domain model to serve its own iteration.

Runtime almost certainly does not care: Each navigates the dotted path and iterates the resulting value, and a tuple iterates. The check is a validation-time narrowing, not a runtime requirement -- to be confirmed rather than assumed before widening it.

Filed separately from the list[X] defects at the reporter's own suggestion, since it is the same container-type family but a different code path (_validation_inputs, not the decorator or the parser).
acceptance_criteria: Each accepts a tuple[X, ...] terminal field and fans over it, proven by a construct that RUNS rather than only assembles. A non-collection terminal field still fails loud. Whether Sequence[X] and other collection annotations are in scope is decided explicitly and stated, not left to whatever the implementation happens to accept.
notes:
## Runtime confirmed, not assumed
_collect_each_items iterates 'list(obj)', which takes any iterable, and each_router only builds a Send per item. The narrowing was validation-only, verified by reading the runtime before widening the validator -- and then by a test that RUNS the fan rather than only assembling it.

## Scope decided explicitly
- list[X]                   accepted (unchanged)
- tuple[X, ...]             accepted
- tuple[X, X] fixed-length  accepted (homogeneous in effect)
- tuple[X, Y] heterogeneous REFUSED -- no single element type, so which one a branch receives is undefined
- str / any scalar          REFUSED (unchanged)
- set / frozenset           NOT included: unordered, and Each's dedup logs kept/dropped INDICES, which are meaningless without an order. Revisit on evidence, not by symmetry.

## Sweep verification
- M1 revert to list-only: 2 fail (assemble + the run).
- M2 accept any tuple: 1 fail -- the heterogeneous guard. Widening did not collapse into 'accept any tuple'.

## Message
'terminal field is not a list' -> 'not a collection of one type', since more than one collection kind now qualifies. Three assertions in test_validation.py and one check-fixture regex track the wording; the behaviour they grade (a scalar is refused) is unchanged.

title: main's AGENTS.md documents Portal and examples that do not exist on main
description:
AGENTS.md on main describes the Portal dynamic-handoff surface as a shipped, sanctioned IR capability, names examples 28 and 29 as its showcases, and names tests/test_example_portal.py and tests/test_example_portal_dynamic_flow.py as pinning them. None of it exists on main:

    grep 'class Portal' src/neograph/*.py   -> no match
    ls examples/ | grep -i portal           -> no match
    from neograph import Portal             -> ImportError

Portal is a develop-only (0.8) capability. main has 86 modules; develop has 147.

AGENTS.md is symlinked as CLAUDE.md and is the agent-facing source of truth, so an agent working on main reads it and plans against capabilities the branch does not have -- the North-star section, the layer-discipline rules, and the examples inventory all describe develop.

The question this raises is a policy one, which is why it is filed rather than fixed: is main's AGENTS.md meant to describe main, or is it a single shared document that necessarily runs ahead of the release line? Both are defensible; today it is neither by decision, only by merge order.

Found while porting the lint fixes to release/0.7.9. Not a shipping defect, and deliberately not fixed inside a patch release.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded on whether AGENTS.md tracks the branch it sits on. If it does, main's copy describes only what main has, and the forward-port check grows a rule for it. If it does not, the document says so near the top so a reader is not misled.

title: Example 05 computes a context that nothing reads
description:
Found by running the new `output_field_unconsumed` check (GH #11) against the repo's own examples.

`examples/05_subgraph_composition.py` builds the `enrich` sub-construct from two nodes:

    def lookup_context(input_data, config):
        """Look up implementation references for each claim."""
        return Context(references=["auth.py:42", "logger.py:18", "crypto.py:7"])

    def score_claims(input_data, config):
        """Score claims based on available context."""
        # input_data is Claims (from neo_subgraph_input)
        ...

`score_claims` reads `input_data`, which is `Claims` from the port, and never touches the `Context`. So `lookup` runs on every invocation, produces `references`, and nothing anywhere reads it. Its own docstring says the scoring is "based on available context" while the implementation ignores that context entirely.

This is the exact defect GH #11 describes: a field that looks load-bearing to a reader, costs work on every call, and cannot affect the answer. It is more consequential here than in ordinary code because this example is the documentation's showcase for sub-constructs, so it teaches a pattern that does not do what it says.

## Decide which the example means
- If the context SHOULD inform scoring, wire it: `score` takes the `lookup` output and uses it.
- If `lookup` exists only to show a two-node sub-construct, say so in the comment and stop claiming the score depends on it.

The second is cheaper and may be the honest reading, but the docstring has to change either way.

## Audit note
Across the repo's 11 example constructs the check fires on 6. Only this one has been inspected. Whether the other five are true positives or noise is unmeasured, and that question decides whether GH #11's requested declare-terminal escape hatch is needed.
acceptance_criteria: examples/05_subgraph_composition.py either wires the Context into scoring or states plainly that lookup exists to demonstrate a two-node sub-construct. The docstring no longer claims the score depends on context it never reads. Running lint() on the example reports no output_field_unconsumed for lookup, or the remaining report is explained in a comment.
notes:
## Fixed
`score` now takes dict-form inputs, reading the port under `neo_subgraph_input` and the peer under `lookup`, which is the shape the loader already builds for a spec-defined sub-construct. Both the plain and the Oracle-ensembled variant were wired; only the first was fixed initially and the check caught the second.

The example's isolation lesson is unchanged: lookup and score still stay out of the parent's result.

lint() reports no output_field_unconsumed anywhere in examples/, down from five when the check first ran.

title: Render a union's members in error messages on Python 3.14
description:
Python 3.14 gave `types.UnionType` a `__name__` of "Union". `describe_type.type_display_name` trusts `__name__`, so on 3.14 every error message naming a union loses the one detail the reader needs:

    (Claims | str).__name__   ->  'Union'          on 3.14
                              ->  AttributeError   on 3.12, so the str(t)
                                  fallback happened to be right

A fan-in mismatch therefore reports the producer as "Union" instead of "Claims | str".

Found on develop, which runs 3.14. On main, which runs 3.12, the message still names the members, so the defect is LATENT there and surfaces on the next interpreter bump.

The check-fixture suite caught it: `tests/test_check_fixtures.py::test_should_fail[type_union_output]` asserts the message names `Claims | str`, and its CHECK_ERROR regex stopped matching. The fixture was right and the validator had regressed, which is what that suite exists for.

Fixed on port/0.7.8-to-develop; this bead tracks the same fix on main. The fix also drops the module prefix that 3.12's `str(t)` fallback leaks: main renders `__main__.Claims | str` today and `Claims | str` after.
acceptance_criteria: type_display_name renders a union as its members joined by ' | ' on both 3.12 and 3.14. NoneType renders as 'None'. The dict-form branch recurses through type_display_name rather than re-deriving __name__, so all three paths share one rule. tests/test_check_fixtures.py::test_should_fail[type_union_output] passes on both interpreters.
notes:
## Fixed on both branches
- develop: commit on port/0.7.8-to-develop; suite went 1 failed -> **4960 passed, 0 failed**. This was the last failure there.
- main: commit 02d7a28, under a new [Unreleased] CHANGELOG section since v0.7.8 was already tagged. The tag still points at the commit that was gated.

Verified on both interpreters:

    3.14 (develop):  Claims | str, Claims | None, {result: Claims}
    3.12 (main):     Claims | str   (was __main__.Claims | str)

The 3.12 fallback leaked the module prefix, so the fix improves the message there too rather than only preventing a 3.14 regression.

the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified

canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and

     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:

       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.

       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

   ```
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>
   ```

   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-o5z7j
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-o5z7j` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-o5z7j/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-o5z7j
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-o5z7j)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-o5z7j --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-o5z7j --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-o5z7j/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-o5z7j codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-o5z7j/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

     structural tools over text grep when available:

       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.

executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted

     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-0lmbx/`:


     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance

title: Sweep verification for neograph-gjhpu
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-gjhpu
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-gjhpu`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-gjhpu)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-gjhpu --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-gjhpu sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-gjhpu
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-gjhpu` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-gjhpu/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-gjhpu
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-gjhpu)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-gjhpu --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-gjhpu --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-gjhpu/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-gjhpu codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-gjhpu/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: dump_spec part (a): Construct -> spec dict with in-band unrepresentable markers
description:

- C11: in-band sentinels at the site, manifest as index.
- Layer discipline: free function, new module, none of node.py/construct.py/_construct_validation.py/factory.py/modifiers.py touched.

ONE LOWERING SEMANTICS: dump_spec mirrors loader.py function-for-function and emits, for every IR value it cannot represent, an IN-BAND sentinel at that value's own site -- so no consumer can mistake an unrepresentable value for an absent one, and no second traversal of the IR grows next to the loader's.

4. TIER E -> _unrepresentable(id, ref, source) helper returning the in-band sentinel dict (C11); every emitted id registered in DUMP_LOSS_META.
5. neograph/losses index, sorted by path (C7); repo-relative source paths.

title: Prerequisite for qtfof.12: make a Portal mesh cell EXECUTABLE under the real pyagentspec AgentSpecLoader
description:
Filed by neograph-qtfof.12's fix atom (neograph-zvjhn.16), 2026-08-18. qtfof.12's data-plane half is BLOCKED on this and cannot be closed until it lands.

Measured against installed pyagentspec 26.1.2 (see tests/test_agent_spec_portal_gated_boundary.py::TestTheDataPlaneHalfIsBlockedByTheSdk, which pins all of this and FAILS LOUD the day any of it stops being true):

1. UNGATED peer mesh -> Swarm(handoff=NEVER). AgentSpecLoader raises ValueError 'Handoff mode NEVER is not supported for conversion in LangGraph adapter' (_langgraphconverter._swarm_convert_to_langgraph). neograph exports NEVER deliberately -- it is the faithful encoding of a Portal mesh's non-conversation-sharing semantics -- so this is a real semantic collision, not a typo.
2. GATED mesh -> a Flow that LOADS but cannot RUN: TypeError 'AgentNodeExecutor can only be used with AgentSpecAgent agents' (_node_execution.py:506). pyagentspec accepts AgentNode(agent=Swarm) at the SCHEMA level (SerializeAsAny[AgenticComponent]) while its own reference runtime refuses it. So the mesh-exit pause composite is schema-legal and runtime-dead.
3. Swarm members are Agents with llm_config.api_provider=None (neograph-qtfof.8). Even with 1 and 2 solved, execution needs a resolvable provider.

## Work
- Decide whether an executable cell is reachable AT ALL without changing the export shape (blocker 2 in particular is a property of neograph's chosen composite, not of Agent Spec).
- If a shape change is required, that is a design decision about how a Portal mesh's HITL gate is represented -- weigh it against the round-trip fidelity the current shape buys (tests/test_agent_spec_portal_operator.py).
- Consider whether the blockers should be reported upstream to pyagentspec (1 and 2 are arguably SDK gaps: a schema-legal composite its own adapter cannot execute).

## Downstream
Unblocks neograph-qtfof.12 half B (declare + wire the gated Flow's two exit EndNodes, reusing _agent_spec_boundary.close_sub_flow -- note it assumes ONE terminal producer, while this shape has TWO exits and none, so that gap needs an answer, not an override).
acceptance_criteria: Either a Portal mesh cell that a third-party AgentSpecLoader loads AND runs (which unblocks qtfof.12), or a written, measured verdict that no such cell is reachable without a shape change, with the shape decision made explicitly.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-mtwy7
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-mtwy7
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-mtwy7`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-mtwy7)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-mtwy7 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-mtwy7 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-mtwy7
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-mtwy7` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-mtwy7/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-mtwy7
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-mtwy7)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-mtwy7 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-mtwy7 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-mtwy7/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-mtwy7 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-mtwy7/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: describe_type: optional fields render a duplicated null ('or null or null')
description:
GitHub issue #7 (github.com/KonstantinMirin/neograph/issues/7), filed 2026-08-18 against 0.7.6.

Confirmed exact mechanism: describe_type.py's _render_type already renders T | None as 'T or null' from the union itself (the None member of the type annotation). _render_model_body (describe_type.py:283) then UNCONDITIONALLY appends a second ' or null' whenever field_info.is_required() is False (true for any field with a default, which every Optional field has) -- producing 'T or null or null' for every single Optional field in every rendered schema. Affects Literal unions AND plain Optional[str]-style fields identically.

This text is injected verbatim into every LLM prompt using structured output, so the defect ships in the actual model-facing contract, repeated for every optional field in every schema.

Fix: only append ' or null' at line 283 when the already-rendered type_str does not already end in the null marker (i.e. dedupe rather than blindly append) -- the None-ness signal from the annotation's own Union and from is_required() should collapse to ONE null token, not stack.
design:
## Root Cause
An `X | None` field expresses its nullability TWICE in Pydantic's model:
1. in the annotation itself (`Union[X, NoneType]`), which `_render_type` already lowers to a `null` union member via `_PRIMITIVE_MAP[type(None)]` (describe_type.py:319-330);
2. in `field_info.is_required() is False` -- true for any field with a default, and every Optional field has one.

`_render_model_body` (describe_type.py:283-284) treats (2) as an independent signal and appends a second ` or null`, so every Optional field in every schema renders `T or null or null`. describe_type output is injected verbatim into structured-output prompts, so the defect ships in the model-facing contract.

## Fix Approach (REFINED -- atom neograph-z7xgk.31, supersedes the endswith sketch)

Predicate on the ANNOTATION, never on the rendered string.

Add a module-local helper in describe_type.py:

    def _admits_none(annotation: Any) -> bool:
        """True when *annotation* is a union that admits None (or is None itself)."""
        if annotation is None or annotation is type(None):
            return True
        origin = get_origin(annotation)
        if origin is Union or origin is types.UnionType:
            return any(a is type(None) for a in get_args(annotation))
        return False

and gate line 283-284 with it:

    if not field_info.is_required() and not _admits_none(field_info.annotation):
        type_str = f"{type_str} or null"

### Why annotation-shape, not string-shape (`type_str.endswith('null')`)
PEP-604 unions preserve author order, verified on the installed interpreter:
`get_args(None | str)` -> `(NoneType, str)`, so `None | str` renders `null or string` -- which does NOT end in `null`. An `endswith` guard leaves that field at `null or string or null`: the bug survives for the one shape nobody tests. The annotation predicate asks the SAME question `_render_type` answered when it emitted the first token, so emitter and guard cannot drift.

### Implementation constraints
- Reuse the module's existing union spelling verbatim: `origin is Union or origin is types.UnionType`. `types`, `Union`, `get_args`, `get_origin` are ALREADY imported at module scope in describe_type.py -- no new imports.
- Do NOT import `_optional_inner_types` from `_llm_retry.py`: private helper of the retry layer; reaching into it from the renderer inverts the dependency direction for a 4-line predicate.
- Single site. No signature change, no public-API change, `__init__.__all__` untouched.

### Explicitly PRESERVED (do not 'fix')
A NON-nullable field with a default (`name: str = 'x'`) is `is_required() is False` with a non-nullable annotation and today renders `string or null`. That is pre-existing 'optional field may be absent' semantics, out of this bug's scope. The annotation predicate keeps it by construction.

## Required test cases (from review finding #6 -- fix atom MUST NOT close without them)
1. NoneType-LAST nullable field (`str | None = None`, `Optional[Literal[...]]`) -> exactly one ` or null`. [already in the RED test]
2. NoneType-FIRST nullable field (`None | str`) -> exactly one null. **This is the case that discriminates the two candidate fixes; the endswith variant fails it.**
3. Non-nullable field WITH a default (`name: str = 'x'`) -> still renders ` or null` (preservation).
4. REQUIRED nullable field (`x: str | None` with no default) -> exactly one null.
acceptance_criteria: neograph.describe_type() on a model with Optional[Literal[...]] and plain Optional[str] fields renders exactly one 'or null' per field, never two. TDD: reproduce with the exact repro from the GH issue first.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_renderers.py::TestDescribeType::test_optional_field_renders_exactly_one_null_when_annotation_is_nullable
- Observed (RED): band: "a" or "b" or null or null // d / plain: string or null or null / nested: [string] or null or null
- Root cause: _render_model_body (describe_type.py:283) appends ' or null' unconditionally whenever field_info.is_required() is False, on top of the 'or null' _render_type already emitted from the annotation's own X | None union -- the same None-ness fact counted twice.
## Similar-pattern trace (atom neograph-z7xgk.3)
Pattern category: a single semantic fact (field nullability) derived from TWO independent sources and combined ADDITIVELY (string append) instead of idempotently.

Searched: `is_required()`, the literal `or null`, `type(None)`/`NoneType` handling, and every string-append-onto-already-rendered-type site in src/.

Findings -- NO other instance:
- `is_required()` appears exactly once in src/ (describe_type.py:283) -- the buggy site itself.
- The literal ` or null` append appears exactly once (describe_type.py:284).
- Other `type(None)` sites (_validation_types.py, di.py, _llm_retry.py, decorators.py) all STRIP NoneType from union args for type comparison; none render text, so none can double-count.
- `describe_value`/`_render_instance` render concrete values and never emit an optionality suffix -- not affected.
- `renderers.py` (Xml/Delimited/Json) has no type-level nullability rendering.

No follow-up beads tasks filed -- the pattern is genuinely single-site.

Cross-reference for neograph-vduhp (GH #8): `describe_value` (describe_type.py:474-478) ALREADY dispatches at its top level on BaseModel / list / primitive. `describe_type` -- its sibling in the same module -- does not, and that asymmetry IS bug #8. Worth citing when choosing #8's fix shape.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-g21jc)

Pattern: a nullability/optionality marker string-appended UNCONDITIONALLY onto a type string that the type-renderer may already have emitted the same marker into (fact counted twice, combined additively).

Shape: SYNTACTIC (one exact literal form) -- grep/AST is sufficient per the atom's own rule; multi-agent targeted scan deliberately NOT fanned out.

Scan commands (reproducible):
    grep -rn 'is_required()' src/
    grep -rn 'or null' src/
    grep -rnE '(type_str|rendered|schema_str|out_str)\s*=\s*f?"' src/neograph/
    grep -n 'type_str' src/neograph/describe_type.py
    grep -rn 'type(None)\|NoneType' src/

Total instances found: 1

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | src/neograph/describe_type.py:284 | `type_str = f"{type_str} or null"` guarded only by `not field_info.is_required()` | MIGRATE | The motivating site; fixed by atom neograph-z7xgk.7 |

No ALLOWLIST and no DEFER rows: the scan surfaced no second instance, so nothing is being knowingly left behind and no follow-up ticket is owed. The three near-miss families examined and cleared:
- `type(None)` sites in _validation_types.py / di.py / _llm_retry.py / decorators.py -- all STRIP NoneType for type comparison, emit no text.
- `describe_value`/`_render_instance` -- renders concrete values, no optionality suffix.
- renderers.py (Xml/Delimited/Json) -- no type-level nullability rendering at all.
## Architect Review (atom neograph-z7xgk.5)

### 1. Root cause correctness -- LOW
Confirmed empirically, not just by reading. The RED output shows all three nullable-field shapes (Literal union, plain str, list) rendering `... or null or null`, and the only site that can produce the second token is describe_type.py:284. `_render_type`'s Union arm (describe_type.py:319-330) maps NoneType through `_PRIMITIVE_MAP` to `null` and joins with `or_splitter`, so the first token is annotation-derived and the second is is_required()-derived. No competing explanation.

### 2. Fix minimality -- LOW
One conditional at one site. No signature change, no new module, no public-API change. `__init__.__all__` untouched.

### 3. Regression risk -- **HIGH** (this is the finding that changes the fix)
The obvious dedupe -- `and not type_str.endswith("null")` -- is UNSOUND. Verified with the installed interpreter:

    get_args(None | str)       -> (NoneType, str)     # NoneType FIRST
    get_args(Union[None, str]) -> (NoneType, str)     # NoneType FIRST
    get_args(str | None)       -> (str, NoneType)     # NoneType last
    get_args(Optional[str])    -> (str, NoneType)     # NoneType last

PEP-604 unions preserve author order, so `None | str` renders `null or string` -- which does NOT end in `null`. An `endswith` guard leaves that field rendering `null or string or null`: the bug survives, silently, for exactly the shape nobody writes a test for. (`endswith` is also coupled to `or_splitter`/hoisting incidentals rather than to the fact it is trying to test.)

REQUIRED instead: predicate on the ANNOTATION, not on the rendered string -- "does this annotation admit None?" That is the same fact `_render_type` used to emit the first token, so the two can no longer disagree.

Second regression axis, must be PRESERVED not broken: a NON-nullable field with a default (`name: str = 'x'`) is `is_required() is False` with a non-nullable annotation, and today renders `string or null`. That is pre-existing semantics ("optional field may be absent"), out of scope for this bug, and the annotation-based predicate keeps it -- the `endswith` variant happens to keep it too, but only by accident.

### 4. Architecture compliance -- LOW
Fix stays inside describe_type.py, the module that owns schema-notation rendering. Do NOT import `_optional_inner_types` from _llm_retry.py: that is a private helper of the retry layer, and reaching from the renderer into it inverts the dependency direction for a 4-line predicate. describe_type.py ALREADY imports `types`, `Union`, `get_args`, `get_origin` at module scope and already spells the union test as `origin is Union or origin is types.UnionType` at line 319 -- the new helper must reuse that exact spelling so the emitter and the guard cannot drift.

### 5. Similar-bug scalability -- LOW
Disease scan (atom .4) found exactly one instance. No ratchet/allowlist and no structural guard is warranted; a behavioral test at the render surface is the right and sufficient pin.

### 6. Test coverage sufficiency -- **MEDIUM**
The current RED test covers only NoneType-last shapes, so it would pass against the unsound `endswith` fix. Before the fix atom closes, the regression test MUST also cover:
- a NoneType-FIRST union (`None | str`) -- the case that discriminates the two candidate fixes;
- a non-nullable-with-default field still rendering ` or null` (preservation);
