title: No machine-readable export of a Construct: model_dump_json() fails, no dump_spec() counterpart to load_spec()
description:
GitHub issue #9 (github.com/KonstantinMirin/neograph/issues/9), filed 2026-08-18 against 0.7.6.

Construct.model_dump_json() fails (PydanticSerializationError: Unable to serialize unknown type <class 'pydantic._internal._model_construction.ModelMetaclass'>) because the IR holds live Pydantic CLASSES in Node.inputs/Node.outputs/Construct.input/Construct.output, which have no serializer. model_dump(mode='python') succeeds but leaves raw <class ...> objects in place -- not transportable. load_spec() exists (_spec_loader.py) with no dump_spec() counterpart, so the YAML-spec round trip is one-way: build a Construct from a spec, but never get one back out.

This is a genuine design/implementation project, not a quick fix -- needs its own scoping pass, unlike GH issues #7/#8. Reporter's suggested direction (offered to contribute):
- Serialize type[BaseModel] fields as their registered spec name where one exists (spec_types.lookup_type/register_type already provide the name<->type mapping, src/neograph/spec_types.py), falling back to a qualified module:QualName when unregistered.
- Predicates (Loop.when, Operator.when, Node.gate_tools_when, Node.skip_when) and scripted_fn/raw_fn obviously cannot round-trip as data -- emit a stable reference (qualname + source location) rather than silently dropping them, so dump_spec stays honest about what it cannot represent (matches this project's anti-band-aid / fail-loud-over-silent convention, not a new invention).
- Even a lossy, EXPLICITLY-DOCUMENTED to_dict() covering names/modes/prompts/model tiers/tools/budgets/modifiers/type NAMES would remove the need for every downstream consumer (e.g. a graph viewer, a diffing tool, a CI check comparing two arms' tool bindings) to hand-roll its own IR walker -- explicitly cited by the reporter as a prerequisite for building tooling around GH issue #6.

Needs its own design pass before implementation: exact spec-name-vs-qualname fallback rule, what 'lossy but honest' means precisely for each unrepresentable field kind, whether this becomes dump_spec() (spec-dict, mirroring load_spec exactly) or a separate lower-level to_dict().
design:
## Core Invariant
There is ONE walker over the Construct IR per output format and ONE lowering
semantics behind them all: `dump_spec` reuses `_ir_branch.iter_with_arms` and the
existing `_spec_schema` vocabulary rather than re-deriving a second IR traversal
next to `to_agent_spec`, and every IR field it cannot represent is ENUMERATED in a
machine-readable loss manifest keyed by a registered id -- never silently dropped,
never guessed at, never emitted as a placeholder that a consumer could mistake for
real data.

## Design Decision (the ticket's acceptance criterion)

### D1. Shape: ONE public free function, `dump_spec`, not a second `to_dict`
`dump_spec(construct, *, strict=False) -> dict[str, Any]` in a NEW
`src/neograph/_spec_dump.py` (peer to `_spec_loader.py`), re-exported through
`loader.py` and added to `neograph/__init__.py`'s `__all__`. NOT a
`Construct.dump_spec()` method -- `construct.py` is off-limits per CLAUDE.md layer
discipline, and `to_agent_spec` set this exact precedent as a free function. Core
package, no optional extra (output is plain dicts; `[agent-spec]` purity is preserved).
Reject the reporter's "dump_spec OR a separate lower-level to_dict" fork: two
serializers is the second-walker defect this project already guards against. One
function whose output IS the `Spec` dict, plus the loss manifest, serves both the
reload use case and the tooling use case.

### D2. Output shape: the existing `Spec` dict, plus one new top-level key
    {
      "version": "1",
      "name": ..., "description": ...,
      "types": { <name>: <json-schema>, ... },     # now actually populated
      "nodes": [ <NodeSpec dict>, ... ],
      "constructs": [ <ConstructSpec dict>, ... ],
      "pipeline": { "nodes": [<ref>, ...] },
      "neograph/losses": [                          # NEW, always present
        {"id": "callable_loop_when", "tier": "NO_REPR",
         "path": "nodes[2].loop.when", "ref": "mymod:score_ok",
         "source": "/abs/path.py:41", "meaning": "..."}
      ]
    }
The `neograph/`-prefixed key mirrors the `_agent_spec_markers.py` naming convention
so the payload stays a valid `Spec` for any consumer that ignores unknown top-level
keys, and `Spec` gains it as an optional field so `load_spec(dump_spec(c))` validates
under `extra="forbid"`.

### D3. Lossy-field handling, per field kind (resolves the ticket's open question)
Adopt the TIER A-F taxonomy recorded in the notes. The policy per tier:
- TIER A (direct): emitted verbatim. No manifest entry.
- TIER B (type refs): reverse-index lookup -> registry name; on miss, synthesize a
  name and emit `model_json_schema()` into `types:`; on a `_no_repr_check` shape
  (tuple/Literal/Enum) that cannot survive the JSON-Schema path, emit a manifest
  entry at tier NO_REPR. Reuse `_no_repr_check` verbatim -- do not restate it.
  Reverse index tie-break: first registration wins (insertion order). `dump_spec`
  NEVER calls `register_type` -- a dump must not mutate global state.
- TIER C (schema gaps): close them additively (`EachSpec.on_error`,
  `ToolSpec.idempotent`, `ConstructSpec.llm_config`/`description`), and teach
  `_apply_modifiers` / `_resolve_tool` to forward them, so the fields become TIER A
  rather than permanent losses. `extra="forbid"` + optional fields = no break.
- TIER D (derived): never emitted. `fan_out_param` / `handoff_param` /
  `handoff_channel` are `_ir_normalize`-owned single-writer fields (guard G3) and
  are recomputed on load. No manifest entry -- they are not a loss.
- TIER E (no data repr): emit NOTHING into the spec body, and emit ONE manifest
  entry per occurrence carrying `{id, tier, path, ref, source, meaning}` where `ref`
  is `module:qualname` and `source` is `file:lineno` (both obtained from the live
  callable; the reporter's requested "stable reference"). This is where the
  reporter's ask and `to_agent_spec`'s fail-loud policy are reconciled -- see D4.
- TIER F (structural): the flat-pool flattening. Emit what fits; a topology the flat
  pool cannot express (nesting past one sub-construct level, a `_BranchNode`, a Node
  reused under two different loader-rewritten `inputs`) produces a NO_REPR manifest
  entry naming the exact path. Do NOT invent a recursive `NodeSpec` containment in
  this ticket -- that is a spec-format v2 change and belongs in its own bead.

### D4. Strict vs. honest: the manifest is structural, fail-loud is one flag
`strict=False` (default): always returns the dict; every loss is in the manifest.
`strict=True`: raises `ConfigurationError` naming the first NO_REPR entry if the
manifest is non-empty -- the `to_agent_spec` contract, on demand.
Rationale for the default: honesty here is STRUCTURAL, not optional. A caller
cannot obtain a dump without also obtaining the exhaustive list of what is missing
from it, so there is no silent seam -- which is what the North Star actually
forbids. Fail-loud-by-default would make `dump_spec` refuse nearly every real
pipeline (any construct containing one scripted `@node` carries a `_sidecar`), which
defeats every use case the ticket cites (graph viewer, arm-diffing CI check, GH #6
tooling). `to_agent_spec` can afford fail-loud because its output must EXECUTE on a
foreign runtime; `dump_spec`'s output must merely be READ. Different contract,
different default -- state this explicitly in the module docstring so the divergence
from the sibling reads as a decision, not drift.
NOTE: D4's default is the one item flagged NEEDS USER INPUT in the notes. If the
maintainer prefers strict-by-default, only this flag's default changes -- everything
else in this design stands.

### D5. Loss ids get a registry, mirroring `CONFORMANCE_PREDICATE_META`
`_spec_dump.DUMP_LOSS_META: dict[str, DumpLossMeta(tier, meaning)]`, single source of
truth for every id the dumper can emit, with a both-directions guard test (no
unregistered id emitted, no stale entry) copied from
`tests/test_guards_agent_spec_conformance.py`. This is what makes "honest"
enforceable rather than aspirational.

## Implementation Plan
1. Branch from `develop` (0.8.0), NOT release/0.7.7 -- every reuse target below
   exists only there.
2. TDD red first: add `tests/test_spec_dump.py` with the reported repro
   (`Construct` holding live `type[BaseModel]` -> a JSON-serializable dict), plus one
   test per tier. Verify they fail before writing the dumper.
3. Add the reverse type index to `spec_types.py` -- extend the EXISTING
   `_type_registry` with a parallel insertion-ordered reverse map maintained inside
   `register_type`; do not build a second registry module. Public helper
   `name_for_type(cls) -> str | None`, wired into `__init__.__all__` only if a
   consumer needs it (otherwise keep it module-internal).
4. Close the TIER C schema gaps in `_spec_schema.py` (`EachSpec.on_error`,
   `ToolSpec.idempotent`, `ConstructSpec.llm_config`/`description`) and forward them
   in `_spec_loader._apply_modifiers` / `_resolve_tool` -- extending the existing
   loader functions, not adding new ones. Add the optional
   `Spec: neograph/losses` field.
5. Write `_spec_dump.py` as the inverse of `_spec_loader.py` FUNCTION BY FUNCTION --
   `_dump_construct` mirrors `_build_construct`, `_dump_node` mirrors `_build_node`,
   `_dump_sub_construct` mirrors `_build_sub_construct`, `_dump_modifiers` mirrors
   `_apply_modifiers` (copying its Portal "forward every explicitly-written field"
   pass-through). Walk membership via `_ir_branch.iter_with_arms`, reusing the
   walker; never re-derive one.
6. Reuse `spec_types._no_repr_check` for the type half and
   `pydantic.BaseModel.model_json_schema()` as the inverse of
   `spec_types._resolve_field_type`. No new schema walker.
7. Add `DUMP_LOSS_META` + `tests/test_guards_spec_dump.py`, copying the
   both-directions registry guard and the single-walker monopoly guard from
   `tests/test_guards_agent_spec_conformance.py` /
   `tests/test_guards_agent_spec_flow_walk_monopoly.py`. Write these failing first.
8. Decide the `Spec.types` reload question (notes Finding 10). Recommended: wire
   `load_project_types(spec_dict)` into `load_spec` BEFORE `_validate_spec`, guarded
   so it runs only when `types:` is non-empty, and add a test that
   `load_spec(dump_spec(c))` resolves types with no `project=` argument.
9. Round-trip tests scoped HONESTLY: assert a fixed point only for the subset that
   has one (no Loop, no sub-construct -- see notes Finding 9). For Loop and
   sub-constructs, assert the manifest names the loss instead.
10. Three-surface parity per CLAUDE.md: exercise `dump_spec` through `@node`,
    declarative `Node(...)`, and programmatic `Node() | Modifier()`. The `@node`
    surface is the one that produces TIER E sidecar losses -- that asymmetry is the
    point, so assert it rather than exempting the surface.
11. Wire `dump_spec` into `neograph/__init__.py`'s `__all__` (the public contract),
    document the tier taxonomy + the `strict=` contract in the module docstring, and
    add the website spec-format page entry.
acceptance_criteria: Design decision recorded (dump_spec shape, lossy-field handling per field kind) before implementation begins. Not scoped for 0.7.7 unless explicitly pulled in -- default to targeting develop/0.8.x given its size.
notes:
## Findings (research atom neograph-bo2tc.2, 2026-08-19)

### 0. BRANCH CORRECTION -- research must target `develop`, not this worktree
The worktree `neograph-release-0.7.7` is on `release/0.7.7` at `__version__ = "0.7.6"`.
`develop` is at `0.8.0`. EVERY reuse target named below exists ONLY on `develop`.
The ticket text cites `src/neograph/_spec_loader.py` -- that file does NOT exist on
release/0.7.7 (the loader is one 282-line `loader.py` there); on `develop` it is a
real 278-line module. Per the ticket's own acceptance criterion ("default to
targeting develop/0.8.x"), all paths/line numbers below are `develop`.

### 1. THE REUSE TARGET ALREADY EXISTS: `to_agent_spec()` is the Construct->data serializer
This was the single most important question and the answer is YES, emphatically.
`develop` ships ~5,000 lines of bidirectional Agent Spec interop across 18
`_agent_spec*.py` modules, public via `__init__.__all__`: `to_agent_spec`,
`from_agent_spec`, `export_conformance`, `ConformanceReport`, `ConformanceTier`,
`resume_from_agent_spec`. `to_agent_spec(construct, api_provider=None) -> Flow`
ALREADY walks the full IR (Node + Construct + every modifier + `_BranchNode` +
Portal mesh) and already resolves the two hard problems GH #9 raises:
`type[BaseModel]` serialization and unrepresentable-field policy.
=> `dump_spec` MUST NOT become a second IR walker. There is no `dump_spec`/`to_dict`
   anywhere on any branch (verified `git grep` across all refs) -- it is greenfield,
   but greenfield sitting next to a mature sibling it has to be consistent with.

### 2. Bug reproduces exactly as reported (verified, release/0.7.7)
`Construct.model_dump_json()` -> `PydanticSerializationError: Unable to serialize
unknown type: <class 'pydantic._internal._model_construction.ModelMetaclass'>`.
`model_dump(mode='python')` succeeds and leaves `<class '__main__.A'>` in place.

### 3. The reporter's suggested type-serialization rule is NOT what the codebase does
Reporter proposed: registered spec name, else `module:QualName` fallback.
`to_agent_spec` instead emits the FULL JSON Schema (pyagentspec `Property`) and
re-registers on import under a STRUCTURAL content hash
(`_agent_spec_types._structural_type_name` -> `AgentSpecType_<sha256[:16]>`),
deliberately NOT the original class name -- because two sites reconstructing the
same shape must yield ONE class or construct-validation type-compat fails.
A `module:QualName` string is also NOT reloadable (`lookup_type` only reads the
name registry; nothing imports by qualname), so the fallback would be decorative.
The spec format ALREADY has the right slot: `Spec.types: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]`
holding JSON Schema defs, consumed by `spec_types.load_project_types`. Emitting
unregistered types THERE (via `model_json_schema()`, the exact inverse of
`spec_types._resolve_field_type`) makes the dump self-contained and reloadable.

### 4. NO reverse type index exists (type -> name)
`spec_types._type_registry` is `dict[str, type[BaseModel]]`, name->type only; there
is no reverse function (verified). Reversing is not a one-liner: `register_type` is
idempotent on FIELD MATCH, and nothing forbids registering ONE class under TWO names
(`register_type('A', X); register_type('B', X)`), so a reverse lookup needs a
documented deterministic tie-break (recommend: first-registered wins, insertion order).

### 5. `_no_repr_check` is the existing "lossy but honest" primitive for TYPES
`spec_types._no_repr_check` (develop, line ~100) fails loud on JSON-Schema shapes
with no neograph target -- `prefixItems` (tuple), `const`/`enum` (Literal/Enum) --
with the rationale "silently falling through to Any would be a silent-degrade,
which violates the fail-loud-over-fail-soft North Star". This is the precedent to
reuse verbatim for dump_spec's type half, NOT a new taxonomy.

### 6. `export_conformance()` is the existing "lossy but honest" primitive for FIELDS
`_agent_spec_conformance.py` owns a three-tier `ConformanceTier` enum
(PORTABLE / NEOGRAPH_ROUND_TRIP_ONLY / NOT_EXPORTABLE) plus
`CONFORMANCE_PREDICATE_META: dict[str, ConformancePredicateMeta(tier, bead, meaning)]`
-- a single-source-of-truth registry keyed by emitted predicate id, guarded both
directions by `tests/test_guards_agent_spec_conformance.py` (no stale entry, no
unregistered predicate). This is the exemplar shape for dump_spec's loss manifest.

### 7. `to_agent_spec`'s policy on unrepresentable fields is FAIL LOUD, not "emit a reference"
From `_agent_spec.py`'s module docstring: "Constructs that cannot be lowered
round-trip-safely FAIL LOUD via ConfigurationError rather than emit a lossy
placeholder -- never a silent downgrade or truncation: raw_fn, skip_when/skip_value,
a callable Loop.when, Oracle merge hooks, renderer, Portal handoff_param/
handoff_channel, a callable gate_tools_when."
What CAN round-trip rides in `neograph/`-prefixed metadata markers
(`_agent_spec_markers.py`: `_MARK_ORACLE_SPEC`, `_MARK_EACH_SPEC`, `_MARK_LOOP_SPEC`,
`_MARK_OPERATOR_SPEC`, `_MARK_PORTAL_SPEC`, `_MARK_BRANCH`, ...) which foreign
runtimes ignore. There is deliberately NO whole-IR blob fallback.
=> This EXACT field set is the one GH #9's reporter wants emitted as "a stable
   reference rather than silently dropped". Two different policies, same fields.
   See Risks -- this is the design decision the ticket is actually asking for.

### 8. The current `Spec` schema CANNOT represent several IR fields (additive gaps)
Verified field-by-field against `_spec_schema.py` (develop):
- `EachSpec` has `over`/`key` only -- `Each.on_error: Literal["raise","collect"]` is DROPPED.
- `ToolSpec` has `name`/`budget`/`config` -- `Tool.idempotent: bool` is DROPPED.
- `ConstructSpec` has no `llm_config` and no `description`; `Construct` has both.
- `NodeSpec.mode` allows `"raw"` but `Node.mode` is `Literal["think","agent","act","scripted"]`
  -- the spec can express a mode the IR cannot hold (raw is carried by `raw_fn`).
- No branch representation at all: `_ir_branch._BranchNode` (`_ConditionSpec.op_fn`
  callable + `true_arm_nodes`/`false_arm_nodes`) has no `Spec` counterpart.
These are ADDITIVE fixes (`extra="forbid"` means adding optional fields keeps old
specs loading), not blockers -- but they must be closed or declared as losses.

### 9. `load_spec` is itself lossy -- there is no fixed point to aim at
Three verified one-way transforms inside `_spec_loader.py`:
a. `_build_node` (line ~172): when `spec.inputs` is absent it sets `inputs = outputs`
   as a "single-type fallback". The dump cannot tell an authored `inputs` from this.
b. `_build_sub_construct` (line ~189) REWRITES every member node's `inputs` into a
   synthesized dict (`neo_subgraph_input` + one entry per prior member). The loaded
   Construct's nodes do not carry the inputs the spec author wrote.
c. `_apply_modifiers` (line ~237) does `Loop(when=parse_condition(spec.loop.when))`
   -- `parse_condition` returns a bare closure. THE SOURCE EXPRESSION STRING IS GONE.
   A spec-loaded Loop therefore has a CALLABLE `when`, which is precisely the case
   `to_agent_spec` fails loud on. `conditions.condition_field(expr)` recovers only
   the dotted FIELD name from a string, and cannot run on a closure at all.
=> `dump_spec(load_spec(s)) == s` is unachievable for any spec with a Loop or a
   sub-construct, and that is a property of the LOADER, not of dump_spec. Do not
   write a round-trip-equality acceptance test without narrowing it to that subset.

### 10. DEAD FIELD: `Spec.types` is validated but never registered by `load_spec`
`load_spec(spec, project)` calls `load_project_types(project_dict)` ONLY. Verified
`git grep load_project_types` on develop -- the only call site passes the `project`
argument. A spec's own `types:` section round-trips through Pydantic validation and
is then ignored. So a self-contained `dump_spec` output that carries its schemas in
`types:` will NOT reload through `load_spec(dump)` today without either a one-line
loader fix or a two-document (project + spec) output contract.

### 11. Layer placement
`to_agent_spec`'s own docstring states it is "A free function, NOT a Construct/Node
method (CLAUDE.md layer discipline, design doc agent-spec-interop-2026-07-09.md 7)".
`dump_spec` is the same shape: a NEW `src/neograph/_spec_dump.py`, peer to
`_spec_loader.py`, re-exported through `loader.py` (which already re-exports
`load_spec`/`from_agent_spec`), and wired into `neograph/__init__.py`'s `__all__`
(the public contract; the `_` module prefix is advisory only per CLAUDE.md).

## The unrepresentable-field taxonomy (per field kind, the ticket's core deliverable)

TIER A -- DIRECT (already in `Spec`, emit verbatim):
  Node.name, .mode, .prompt, .model, .scripted_fn, .context, .llm_config;
  Tool.name/.budget/.config; Construct.name/.description;
  Oracle.n/.models/.merge_fn/.merge_prompt/.merge_model; Each.over/.key;
  Loop.max_iterations/.on_exhaust; Operator.when; Portal (all 12 PortalSpec fields).

TIER B -- TYPE REFERENCES (resolvable, needs the reverse index + `types:` emission):
  Node.inputs, Node.outputs, Construct.input, Construct.output,
  Node.oracle_gen_type, Portal.output.
  Rule: registered name if the reverse index resolves it; else synthesize a name and
  emit `model_json_schema()` into `Spec.types`; else `_no_repr_check` fails loud
  (tuple / Literal / Enum fields).

TIER C -- SPEC-SCHEMA GAPS (representable, schema needs an additive field):
  Each.on_error, Tool.idempotent, Construct.llm_config, ConstructSpec.description,
  Node.gate_tools_when WHEN it is a `str` (the registered-name half is data).

TIER D -- DERIVED, MUST NOT BE EMITTED (single-writer IR fields):
  Node.fan_out_param, Node.handoff_param, Node.handoff_channel. Written ONLY by
  `_ir_normalize.py` (guard G3, `IR_FIELDS` frozenset in test_guards_llm_runtime.py)
  and recomputed on every load. Emitting them would create a second writer.

TIER E -- NO DATA REPRESENTATION (the honest-loss set; identical to the set
`to_agent_spec` fails loud on, plus the sidecars):
  Node.raw_fn; Node.skip_when; Node.skip_value; Node.renderer; Construct.renderer;
  Node.gate_tools_when when Callable; Loop.when when Callable (INCLUDING every
  spec-loaded Loop, see Finding 9c); Oracle.merge_pre_process / .merge_post_process /
  .merge_fallback; Portal.scripted; Portal.conditions; a `tools` entry that is a
  LangChain `BaseTool` rather than a neograph `Tool`; Tool._bound_tool;
  Node._sidecar / ._param_res / ._scripted_shim / ._remote_agent_endpoint
  (the @node function object + its DI bindings); `_BranchNode` in its entirety.

TIER F -- STRUCTURAL (the flattening itself is lossy):
  `Spec` is a FLAT node pool + string refs; `ConstructSpec.nodes` holds STRINGS, not
  nested `NodeSpec`s -- so nesting deeper than one sub-construct level, and the same
  Node object appearing in two sub-constructs with different loader-rewritten
  `inputs`, are both inexpressible. Name collisions across sibling sub-constructs
  collapse in the shared pool.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- NEEDS USER INPUT (the central design decision): TIER E policy. `to_agent_spec`
  FAILS LOUD on exactly this field set and the North Star backs that. GH #9's
  reporter explicitly asks for the opposite -- "emit a stable reference (qualname +
  source location) rather than silently dropping them" -- because the stated use
  cases (graph viewer, diffing tool, CI check comparing two arms' tool bindings,
  prerequisite for GH #6 tooling) are all defeated if dump_spec refuses every
  construct with a scripted `@node` in it, which is essentially every real pipeline.
  These cannot both be the default. Recommendation in the design field.
- NEEDS USER INPUT: `Spec.types` is a dead field in `load_spec` (Finding 10).
  Wiring `load_project_types(spec_dict)` is one line but changes `load_spec`
  semantics (a spec could then silently re-register a name a caller already owns,
  hitting `register_type`'s overwrite-warning path). Alternative: dump_spec emits a
  two-document `{project, spec}` result matching the existing `load_spec(spec,
  project)` signature. Needs a call.
- No reverse type index; one class may hold several registry names (Finding 4).
  Needs a documented deterministic tie-break, plus a decision on whether dump_spec
  may `register_type` as a side effect of dumping (recommend: NO -- a dump must not
  mutate global state).
- `_no_repr_check` rejects `Literal[...]` and `Enum` fields. Real neograph models use
  Literal freely (`llm_config.output_strategy`, `Loop.on_exhaust`, `Portal.trigger`
  are Literals in the IR itself). If TIER B routes through the JSON-Schema path,
  dump_spec would fail loud on very ordinary user models. Either widen the DIRECT
  tier for Literal/Enum or keep those types on the registry-name path only.
- No load->dump->load fixed point exists for Loop or sub-constructs (Finding 9).
  Any round-trip test must be scoped to the subset that HAS one.
- `NodeSpec.mode` accepts `"raw"`, `Node.mode` does not (Finding 8) -- dump_spec can
  never legitimately emit `mode: raw`; a raw node is a TIER E loss via `raw_fn`.
- Structural guards will bite: `test_guards_agent_spec_flow_walk_monopoly.py` and
  `test_guards_agent_spec_conformance.py` establish that a second walker is a
  guarded defect here. A dump_spec walker must reuse `_ir_branch.iter_with_arms`
  (membership + branch arms) and ship its own monopoly guard, written failing-first.
- Scope reality check: TIER A+B+C is a genuinely useful deliverable on its own.
  TIER E and TIER F are where the size is. Consider shipping the taxonomy + the
  loss manifest first and letting TIER F (nested/branch topology) stay a declared,
  enumerated loss rather than blocking the whole ticket on it.

  MEMBERSHIP-only consumers, wrong here: the exporter must see a ``_BranchNode``
  boundary to emit a real ``BranchingNode``) -- the DATA-edge phase below still
  uses ``iter_with_arms``, which is right there."
  `_ir_branch.iter_with_arms` (release/0.7.7 _ir_branch.py:71-107) "drops" the
  `_BranchNode` and yields `true_arm_nodes` then `false_arm_nodes` in sequence.
  A dumper built on it emits a LINEAR pipeline in which both arms appear
  unconditional, with nothing marking that a branch existed -- precisely the
  "placeholder a consumer could mistake for real data" the Core Invariant
  forbids. It also makes D3-TIER-F unimplementable as written: you cannot "emit
  a NO_REPR manifest entry naming the exact path" for a sentinel the iterator
  has already erased.

  iterator. Copy to_agent_spec's two-phase shape -- raw `construct.nodes` for
  structural dispatch (so `_BranchNode` is visible and reportable),
  `iter_with_arms` only for a data-edge/reference phase if one is needed. The
  monopoly guard must ban a second *lowering*, not pin a specific iterator.

- [HIGH] D3 TIER B binds the DUMP side to `spec_types._no_repr_check`, which is
  a LOAD-side guard, and the result is maximal loss on the most ordinary models.
  Verified on develop: `_no_repr_check` is called only from
  `_resolve_field_type` (JSON Schema -> Python annotation) and raises on
  `prefixItems` / `const` / `enum`. On the dump side there is no such problem:
  `model_json_schema()` emits const/enum/prefixItems correctly and losslessly.
  Applying the check to the dump means any user model carrying a single
  `Literal` or `Enum` field -- pervasive, as the research's own Risks section

  REPRESENTABLE (can be written into `types:` -- essentially everything
  `model_json_schema()` handles) vs RELOADABLE (can be inverted by
  `_resolve_field_type`). Record the latter as a distinct, weaker manifest tier
  (NOT_RELOADABLE), reached by catching `_no_repr_check` on a dry-run, never by
  omitting the schema.

| iter_with_arms DROPS _BranchNode and yields true_arm then false_arm in sequence | _ir_branch.py:83-84, :103-104 -- docstring says '`_BranchNode` is dropped and replaced by its `true_arm_nodes` then `false_arm_nodes`' | YES -- a dumper on it emits both arms as unconditional, with nothing marking the branch |
| NodeSpec.outputs is a REQUIRED bare str | _spec_schema.py:84 `outputs: str`, while :83 is `inputs: str \| dict[str, str] \| None` | YES -- and the asymmetry with inputs makes it worse than the review states |
| ConstructSpec.input/output are REQUIRED str | _spec_schema.py:109-110 | YES -- no `\| None`, so a boundary-less Construct is inexpressible |

All three HIGH findings CONFIRMED. The review is accurate where it contradicts the research, and it corrected a FALSE PREMISE the research had used to justify D4 (that to_agent_spec fails loud on _sidecar -- it does not). Accepted in full.
## Triage (atom neograph-bo2tc.5)
Verdict: NEEDS_REFINEMENT. Routed: spawned refine atom neograph-bo2tc.12 between triage (.5) and write-test (.6). No design edits made in this atom.

On the two items the RESEARCH self-escalated as NEEDS USER INPUT, the review argued both are settled by evidence rather than being the maintainer's call, and I agree on the reasoning but am NOT treating either as user-approved:
- TIER E policy / strict=False default: the research's justification was factually wrong (to_agent_spec does not fail on _sidecar), and with that corrected the case for a manifest-by-default is strong -- contracts differ (execute vs read), the manifest is always-present, id-registered and guard-enforced, and fail-loud stays available via strict=True. Recorded as DECIDED with corrected rationale. FLAGGED to the maintainer anyway: it is the DEFAULT of a new public API in a project whose north star is fail-loud-over-fail-soft, so it is theirs to overturn. Proceeding under the stated assumption rather than blocking, since nothing downstream is built on this branch.
- Spec.types / load_project_types: descoped to its own bead. Not a user call; it has an independent blast radius and no bearing on this ticket's acceptance.
## Design corrections (refine atom neograph-bo2tc.12) -- these SUPERSEDE the design field where they conflict

The design field's Core Invariant, D3 TIER B, the tier taxonomy, D4's rationale and plan steps 3/5/8 are corrected as follows. Everything not listed stands.

### C1 [supersedes the Core Invariant + plan step 5] -- ONE LOWERING SEMANTICS, not one iterator
`iter_with_arms` is the WRONG structural walker for a dumper. Verified at _ir_branch.py:83-84: it 'drops' the `_BranchNode` and yields `true_arm_nodes` then `false_arm_nodes` in sequence. A dumper built on it emits a LINEAR pipeline in which both arms appear unconditional and nothing records that a branch existed -- exactly the 'placeholder a consumer could mistake for real data' the invariant forbids -- and it makes TIER F unimplementable, since you cannot name the path of a sentinel the iterator already erased.

The sibling exporter already solved this and documents why: `_agent_spec.py` (develop) walks RAW `construct.nodes` for structural dispatch precisely so a `_BranchNode` boundary is visible, and uses `iter_with_arms` only for its data-edge phase.

CORRECTED Core Invariant: there is ONE LOWERING SEMANTICS per output format, not one iterator. dump_spec copies to_agent_spec's two-phase shape -- raw `construct.nodes` for structural dispatch (so `_BranchNode` is visible and reportable), `iter_with_arms` only for a data-edge/reference phase if one is needed. The monopoly guard bans a second LOWERING; it must NOT pin a specific iterator.

### C2 [supersedes D3 TIER B] -- split REPRESENTABLE from RELOADABLE
Binding the DUMP side to `spec_types._no_repr_check` is a category error: that is a LOAD-side guard (JSON Schema -> Python annotation) and it rejects const/enum/prefixItems. On the dump side `model_json_schema()` emits those correctly and losslessly. Applying it to the dump means any user model with a single `Literal` or `Enum` field -- pervasive; `llm_config.output_strategy`, `Loop.on_exhaust` and `Portal.trigger` are Literals in neograph's OWN IR -- has its type dropped from `types:` and downgraded to NO_REPR. That is maximal loss on the most ordinary models, and it silently discarded the research's own mitigation.

CORRECTED: ALWAYS emit `model_json_schema()` into `types:`, keyed by the registered name where one exists. Two distinct axes, not one:
- REPRESENTABLE -- can be written into `types:`. Essentially everything model_json_schema() handles. Never omitted.
- RELOADABLE -- can be inverted by `_resolve_field_type`. Recorded as a weaker manifest tier NOT_RELOADABLE, reached by catching `_no_repr_check` on a DRY RUN, never by omitting the schema.
This also makes the dump self-contained by construction: a bare registry name is only meaningful to a process that already imported the project, which defeats the external-graph-viewer consumer the ticket cites.

### C3 [extends the tier taxonomy] -- two gaps the IR-only audit missed
The taxonomy was derived from the IR without a field-by-field audit against the TARGET schema. Verified on release/0.7.7:
- `_spec_schema.py:84` -- `NodeSpec.outputs: str`, REQUIRED and a bare string, while `:83` is `inputs: str | dict[str, str] | None`. So dict-form outputs (`{"result": X, "tool_log": list[ToolInteraction]}`, which CLAUDE.md documents at length as first-class) and `outputs=None` have NO spec representation. TIER A and TIER B are BOTH wrong for the dict form.
- `_spec_schema.py:109-110` -- `ConstructSpec.input: str` / `output: str`, both REQUIRED. Every Construct without a declared boundary -- including the top-level one being dumped -- is inexpressible.
Both are additive TIER C fixes (`outputs: str | dict[str, str]`; make ConstructSpec input/output optional) and both enlarge plan step 4. Re-derive the whole taxonomy as a TWO-COLUMN audit (IR field -> Spec slot), not an IR inventory.

### C4 [supersedes D4's rationale; the DEFAULT is unchanged] -- the premise was false
D4 justified `strict=False` by claiming fail-loud 'would refuse nearly every real pipeline (any construct containing one scripted @node carries a _sidecar)'. FALSE: `_sidecar` is not in to_agent_spec's fail-loud set. That set is raw_fn, skip_when/skip_value, callable Loop.when, Oracle merge hooks, renderer, Portal handoff fields, callable gate_tools_when -- all opt-in features. The fail-loud sibling exports scripted-@node constructs today without complaint.
CORRECTED rationale, on ground that actually holds: the CONTRACT differs (to_agent_spec's output must EXECUTE on a foreign runtime; dump_spec's must merely be READ), and an id-registered, guard-enforced, always-present manifest is the OPPOSITE of a silent seam -- which is what the North Star forbids. Fail-loud remains one flag away.
A recorded decision resting on a false premise is a defect in a ticket whose entire acceptance is 'design decision recorded', which is why this correction is not cosmetic.

### C5 -- scripted_fn is a POOL KEY, not a reference
`_scripted_registry.py:100` returns `n.name`, so `node.scripted_fn` is the NODE'S OWN NAME. A dump emitting `scripted_fn: "score"` identifies nothing about the implementing Python function. State this explicitly in the design: it is the strongest argument FOR the reporter's TIER E ask, since the only place a scripted @node's real identity can be served is a manifest entry whose `ref` is `module:qualname` of `_sidecar[0]`.

### C6 [supersedes plan step 3] -- derive the reverse index, do not cache it
A parallel insertion-ordered reverse map inside `register_type` is a SECOND SOURCE OF TRUTH -- the disease class the invariant exists to prevent -- and it desyncs in the suite: `tests/conftest.py:91` calls `_type_registry.clear()` directly, which a parallel map survives, so dump_spec would emit names for types no longer registered, leaking across tests. CORRECTED: derive by scanning `_type_registry.items()`, first match wins. The registry is tiny; the documented insertion-order tie-break falls out for free.

### C7 -- determinism is a requirement, not a nicety
`source: "/abs/path.py:41"` makes two dumps of the same pipeline differ across checkouts, producing spurious diffs in exactly the diffing-tool and CI-comparison use cases that MOTIVATE the ticket. CORRECTED: repo-relative path (or module + lineno), manifest sorted deterministically by path, and a test asserting two dumps of the same construct are byte-identical.

### C8 [supersedes plan step 8] -- descope the reload wiring
Wiring `load_project_types` into `load_spec` changes semantics for every existing caller (a spec could re-register a name the caller already owns, hitting register_type's overwrite-warning path). Finding 9 already establishes there is no load->dump->load fixed point for Loop or sub-constructs, so reloadability is not part of this ticket's acceptance. OWN BEAD.

### C9 -- scope split (the ticket is not one ticket)
(a) dump_spec + loss manifest + reverse lookup [TIER A/B, TIER E as manifest entries] -- **this is what closes GH #9**
(b) TIER C spec-schema gaps + loader forwarding [now larger, per C3]
(c) Spec.types reload wiring [per C8]
(d) TIER F topology / spec-format v2

### C10 -- small but required
- `neograph/losses` is not a Python identifier: needs `Field(alias="neograph/losses")` + `populate_by_name`, and `load_spec` must be guarded to IGNORE it, else a hand-authored spec can declare meaningless losses.
- State which tiers trip `strict=` (D4's wording is ambiguous between 'manifest non-empty' and 'first NO_REPR entry').
- Add CHANGELOG.md and a CLAUDE.md entry to the plan -- CLAUDE.md names the CHANGELOG as the authoritative feature list to keep in sync. The website step (11) was already correct.
## Disposition of the remaining atoms (neograph-bo2tc.6 write-test / .7 implement / .8 sweep / .9 commit)

NOT EXECUTED, and deliberately not faked. Implementation cannot happen in this worktree: roughly half the named reuse targets (_spec_loader.py, _agent_spec_markers.py, to_agent_spec, the two agent-spec guard suites) do not exist on release/0.7.7 and do exist on origin/develop -- verified three times independently (research, review, orchestrator). Writing a TDD-red test here would pin a design that must be built against modules absent from this branch, and implementing would force re-deriving the second lowering the Core Invariant forbids.

This is the 'infeasible work BLOCKS closure, it never downgrades the bar' rule: neograph-mtwy7 stays OPEN. The FEATURE is not delivered -- only its design is.

What WAS delivered here, which is this ticket's stated acceptance ('Design decision recorded (dump_spec shape, lossy-field handling per field kind) before implementation begins'):
- shape: D1 (one public free function dump_spec in a new _spec_dump.py) + D2 (Spec dict + a neograph/losses manifest key);
- lossy-field handling per field kind: the TIER A-F taxonomy, as corrected by C2 (REPRESENTABLE vs RELOADABLE) and C3 (the two missed Spec-slot gaps);
- plus an adversarial review that caught three WRONG decisions before any code followed them.

- neograph-738dj (P3) -- the descoped Spec.types/load_spec wiring (C8).
Parts (b) TIER C schema gaps and (d) TIER F topology are named in the C9 scope split and are not yet separate beads -- (b) is folded into neograph-rlapj's prerequisites, (d) is genuinely future work.
## Scope decision (maintainer, 2026-08-19)
TARGETED AT 0.8 -- explicitly NOT pulled into 0.7.7. Confirms the ticket's own default ('Not scoped for 0.7.7 unless explicitly pulled in -- default to targeting develop/0.8.x given its size') and matches the hard branch constraint (the reuse targets exist only on develop).
Stays OPEN: design delivered, feature not. Implementation carried by neograph-rlapj.
## CORRECTION (2026-08-19): the 'not buildable on release/0.7.7' finding was WRONG

Three passes (research, review, orchestrator) all concluded implementation could not happen here. All three were wrong, in the same way: they verified FILE NAMES rather than CAPABILITIES.

The loader was renamed `loader.py` -> `_spec_loader.py` on develop. Seeing '_spec_loader.py ABSENT' on release/0.7.7, all three concluded 'the loader is absent'. It is not -- it is `loader.py`, and it carries EVERY function the plan says to mirror function-by-function:

| plan says mirror | release/0.7.7 |
|---|---|
| _build_construct | loader.py:122 PRESENT |
| _build_node | loader.py:174 PRESENT |
| _build_sub_construct | loader.py:203 PRESENT |
| _apply_modifiers | loader.py:251 PRESENT |
| _resolve_tool | loader.py:159 PRESENT |
| the target format | _spec_schema.py -- all 9 spec classes PRESENT |
| the type registry | spec_types.py PRESENT (incl. load_project_types:97) |
| the IR walker | _ir_branch.py PRESENT |
| load_spec | loader.py:44, exported from __init__ (:65, :182) |
| loader tests to mirror | tests/test_spec_loader.py, 1435 lines |

GENUINELY absent: to_agent_spec, _agent_spec_markers.py, tests/test_guards_agent_spec*.py. Every one of those was cited as an EXEMPLAR or a TEMPLATE TO COPY -- a precedent for the free-function shape, a naming convention, guard patterns. None is a dependency. The C1 constraint (walk raw construct.nodes so _BranchNode stays visible) is implementable directly from the constraint; the exemplar is a convenience, not a prerequisite.

Consequence: part (a) IS buildable on release/0.7.7. Atoms .6-.9 were closed on a false premise. Re-scoped per the maintainer's decision below.
## C11 [maintainer-directed] -- unrepresentable values are marked IN BAND, at the node

Supersedes D3 TIER E's 'emit NOTHING into the spec body'. That rule left a consumer reading `nodes[2].loop` seeing `{"max_iterations": 3}` with the `when` predicate simply absent -- so a diffing tool comparing two pipelines whose only difference is the `when` lambda reports 'identical'. The out-of-band `neograph/losses` array does not prevent that: it only helps a consumer who thinks to read a different part of the document. That IS the silent seam the north star forbids.

CORRECTED: a TIER E loss emits a SENTINEL OBJECT at its own site, so the field is present and visibly not-a-value:

    "loop": {"max_iterations": 3,
              "when": {"neograph/unrepresentable": "callable_loop_when",
                        "ref": "myproj.scoring:score_ok",
                        "source": "src/scoring.py:41"}}

The `neograph/losses` manifest STAYS, as an index for enumeration (and for the both-directions id guard), but it is no longer the sole record. A consumer cannot mistake a marked field for an absent one, and a differ compares `ref` values and sees a real difference.

This is what makes `strict=False` defensible as the default on its own merits rather than on a promise about consumer diligence: with the in-band marker, the loss is unmissable by construction, which is exactly the 'unrepresentable, not merely caught' standard the project holds itself to. `strict=True` stays available and raises on any TIER E sentinel.

title: describe_type raises AttributeError on non-BaseModel annotations (e.g. list[X] in dict-form Node.outputs)
description:
GitHub issue #8 (github.com/KonstantinMirin/neograph/issues/8), filed 2026-08-18 against 0.7.6.

describe_type() is typed model: type[BaseModel] but never validates that at the entry point before reaching model.model_fields inside _render_model_body -- so describe_type(list[SomeModel]) or describe_type(str) raises a low-level AttributeError: type object 'list' has no attribute 'model_fields' instead of a diagnosable error naming the actual mistake.

Concrete real-world trigger: dict-form Node.outputs commonly mixes a BaseModel result with a list[X] field (e.g. outputs={"result": TriageReport, "tool_log": list[ToolInteraction]}) -- any caller iterating declared outputs to render/validate each entry hits this on the list-typed one.

Reporter notes type_display_name() (describe_type.py:41) ALREADY handles these generic shapes (list[M], dict[str, M], M | None) gracefully -- worth checking whether describe_type's top-level entry point can reuse the SAME dispatch _render_type already has for generics, rather than requiring a bare BaseModel and failing internally.

Two acceptable fixes (reporter's own framing, either is an improvement, first is more useful):
1. Handle the common generics (list[M], dict[str, M], M | None) at the top level by rendering the container and recursing into the model argument(s) via the existing _render_type dispatch.
2. At minimum, raise TypeError with a clear message naming the offending annotation instead of letting AttributeError leak from a Pydantic internal.
design:
## Root Cause
`describe_type()`'s signature promises `model: type[BaseModel]` and nothing enforces it. The value survives pass 1 (`_count_classes`, describe_type.py:193) and dies in pass 2 (`_render_model_body`, describe_type.py:286) on `model.model_fields` -- a Pydantic internal, several frames below the mistake, naming a builtin rather than the annotation the caller passed.

## Fix Approach (RESOLVED -- atom neograph-z7xgk.32; supersedes 'SHAPE NOT YET CHOSEN')

HYBRID: dispatch for the shapes the module genuinely understands, refuse loudly for the rest.

Neither of the reporter's options alone is right. Pure DISPATCH exposes `_render_type`'s fail-soft fallthrough (`return str(annotation)`, describe_type.py:436) at the top level, so `describe_type(SomeRandomClass)` would return `"<class 'foo.SomeRandomClass'>"` and ship it to a model as a schema -- trading a loud AttributeError for a silent wrong answer. Pure REFUSE keeps `describe_type` gratuitously weaker than its own twin `describe_value` (describe_type.py:474-478), which already dispatches on BaseModel / list / primitive at ITS top level, and than `type_display_name` (describe_type.py:41), which already handles the generic shapes.

### Mechanism -- ONE arm list, no parallel predicate
Do NOT write an `_is_describable()` predicate enumerating Union/Literal/list/tuple/set/dict/Enum/BaseModel/primitives/Any -- that is a second copy of `_render_type`'s arm list and will drift the first time an arm is added.

Instead add a `strict` flag consulted ONLY at `_render_type`'s final fallthrough:

    def _render_type(annotation, *, ..., strict: bool = False) -> str:
        ...
        if annotation is Any:
            return "any"
        if strict:
            raise TypeError(...naming the annotation...)
        return str(annotation)

`_render_type`'s own recursive calls do NOT pass `strict`, so nested fields keep today's lenient `str(annotation)` behavior -- making recursion strict would be a silent breaking change for any pipeline with an exotic field type.

### Top-level flow in `describe_type`
- `isinstance(model, type) and issubclass(model, BaseModel)` -> the EXISTING path, byte-identical output.
- otherwise -> `_count_annotation(model, ...)` for pass 1 (it already recurses into generic args, so hoisting / enum-hoisting / recursive-model detection keep working for `list[M]`, `dict[str, M]`, `M | None`), then `_render_type(model, ..., strict=True)` for pass 2. `prefix` and the hoisted `type Foo = {...}` declarations are emitted exactly as today.

### MUST NOT
Do not 'simplify' by routing BaseModel input through `_count_annotation`/`_render_type` as well. `_count_annotation` counts the TOP model itself, so a model that also appears nested reaches count 2 and starts being hoisted under `hoist_classes='auto'` -- a silent output change for existing pipelines. BRANCH, do not unify.

## Required test cases (review finding #6 -- fix atom MUST NOT close without them)
1. `list[M]`, `dict[str, M]`, `M | None`, `str` -> EXACT rendered output asserted (tighten the shape-agnostic RED repro, which currently accepts either remedy and so certifies neither).
2. A non-BaseModel, non-generic class (reaches the `str(annotation)` fallthrough) -> TypeError naming the annotation. **Discriminating case**: without it, a pure-dispatch implementation passes the whole suite while shipping `"<class '...'>"` to a model.
3. Hoisting still correct for a top-level container: `describe_type(list[M], hoist_classes='all')` emits `type M = {...}` before `[M]`.
4. BaseModel path byte-identical -- assert a known existing render is unchanged.
5. `inject_schema` (the second public face, disease-scan row 2) no longer leaks -- asserted, not assumed to follow from the shared root.
6. Nested exotic annotations still render leniently -- `strict` must not leak into recursion.
acceptance_criteria: describe_type(list[SomeModel]) either renders a sensible container description or raises a clear TypeError naming the type -- never a bare AttributeError about model_fields. TDD: reproduce with the exact repro (list[ToolInteraction], str) from the GH issue first.
notes:
## Reproduction (atom neograph-z7xgk.11)
- Failing tests:
  tests/test_renderers.py::TestDescribeType::test_non_basemodel_annotation_never_leaks_a_pydantic_attributeerror
  tests/test_renderers.py::TestDescribeType::test_dict_form_outputs_can_be_walked_entry_by_entry
- Observed (RED), all four annotation shapes verified against the installed build:

  describe_type(dict[str, ToolInteraction])  -> AttributeError: type object 'dict' has no attribute 'model_fields'
  describe_type(ToolInteraction | None)      -> AttributeError: 'types.UnionType' object has no attribute 'model_fields'

The repro is deliberately written to hold under EITHER remedy the ticket offers (render the container, or refuse with a diagnosable TypeError). It fails ONLY on a leaked non-TypeError, or on a TypeError whose message leaks 'model_fields' or names neither the annotation nor its member. The architect-review atom picks the shape; the fix atom then tightens the assertions to that shape.

Internal `.model_fields` sites (`_execute`, `_llm_retry`, `_state_bus`, `compiler`, `di`, `spec_types`, `state`) all receive types the IR built, not caller input -- no user-reachable path, no action.

FOLLOW-UP FILED (not fixed here -- out of this bug's scope, and the registry question deserves its own decision): see the DEFER row in the disease-scan table for the ticket id.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-vduhp)

Pattern: a PUBLIC entry point (a symbol in `neograph.__all__`) that declares a `type[BaseModel]` parameter, validates nothing at the boundary, and lets the value reach `.model_fields` -- so a caller mistake surfaces as a Pydantic AttributeError naming a builtin.

Shape: SEMANTIC-but-enumerable (a boundary contract, not a literal), and the population is CLOSED -- `neograph.__all__` -- so exhaustive live probing beats a fan-out scan. Multi-agent targeted scan deliberately not used: probing every public symbol IS the complete scan, with no false-negative surface for agents to cover.

Scan commands (reproducible):

    python -c "import neograph, inspect; [print(n, inspect.signature(getattr(neograph,n))) for n in neograph.__all__ if inspect.isfunction(getattr(neograph,n,None))]"
    # probe each candidate with list[ToolInteraction] and report leak/no-leak (script in atom .12 notes)
    grep -rn 'type\[BaseModel\]' src/neograph/*.py
    grep -rn '\.model_fields' src/neograph/*.py

|---|---|---|---|---|

| 2 | prompt.py:105-121 `inject_schema(vars, output_model)` | forwards straight to `describe_type(output_model)` | MIGRATE (by root fix) | Same root, second PUBLIC face. No separate edit needed, but the fix atom MUST add a regression assertion through `inject_schema` -- a shared root is a claim, and an unasserted claim is how the second face silently diverges later. |
| 3 | _llm_render.py:416 / _llm.py:315 / _agent_output_schema_preamble.py:45 / _llm_retry.py:367 `describe_type(output_model)` on an IR-supplied model | internal callers | ALLOWLIST | Not caller input: `_resolve_primary_output` -> `normalize_outputs` hands these the primary type the IR built. ## Architect Review (atom neograph-z7xgk.14)

### 1. Root cause correctness -- LOW
Confirmed by live probe across four shapes, not by reading. `describe_type` promises `type[BaseModel]`, enforces nothing, and the value survives pass 1 (`_count_classes`, describe_type.py:193) before dying in pass 2 (`_render_model_body`, describe_type.py:286). Both frames do the same unchecked `.model_fields`.

### 2. Shape decision -- **RECOMMEND HYBRID (1)+(2), not either alone**. Severity of getting this wrong: MEDIUM.

    describe_type.py:436   return str(annotation)

A pure DISPATCH fix makes `describe_type(SomeRandomClass)` return `"<class 'foo.SomeRandomClass'>"` -- text that renders happily and then ships to a model as though it were a schema. That trades a loud AttributeError for a SILENT wrong answer, which is a straight north-star regression ('a band-aid that leaves a silent seam is an existential defect'). Pure REFUSE avoids that but leaves the reporter hand-rolling the generic walk that already exists two functions away, and keeps `describe_type` gratuitously weaker than its own twin.

Why dispatch is legitimate here and NOT fail-soft: 'the restriction is the product' is about broken PROGRAMS being unrepresentable (control flow, fan-in, region entry), not about refusing a well-posed question. `describe_type(list[M])` has a correct, unambiguous answer; `describe_value` -- the sibling in the SAME module (describe_type.py:474-478) -- already dispatches on BaseModel / list / primitive at its top level, and `type_display_name` (describe_type.py:41) already handles the generic shapes.         ...

        if strict:
            raise TypeError(...naming annotation...)
        return str(annotation)

`describe_type`'s non-BaseModel branch calls it with `strict=True`; the recursive calls inside `_render_type` do NOT pass it, so nested fields keep today's lenient `str(annotation)` behavior. One arm list, one fallthrough, no parallel predicate, and zero behavior change for nested annotations (which would otherwise be a silent breaking change for pipelines with an exotic field type).

Top-level flow becomes:
- `issubclass(model, BaseModel)` -> existing path, byte-identical output (REQUIRED: this fix must not perturb a single existing render).
- otherwise -> `_count_annotation(model, ...)` for pass 1 (it already recurses into generic args, so hoisting/enum/recursive detection keep working for `list[M]`, `dict[str, M]`, `M | None`) then `_render_type(model, ..., strict=True)` for pass 2, with `prefix` and the hoisted declarations emitted exactly as they are today.

The BaseModel path must not change. Do NOT 'unify' by routing BaseModel input through `_count_annotation`/`_render_type` as well: `_count_annotation` would count the TOP model itself, so a model that also appears nested reaches count 2 and starts getting hoisted under `hoist_classes='auto'` -- a silent output change for existing pipelines. Branch, do not unify.

### 5. Similar-bug scalability -- LOW
Disease scan (atom .13) closed the population by probing every `neograph.__all__` symbol. `inject_schema` is the only other leaking PUBLIC face and shares the root. The registry permissiveness is deferred to neograph-pkp0u.

- a non-BaseModel, non-generic class (the `str(annotation)` fallthrough) -> TypeError naming the annotation. **This is the case that discriminates hybrid from pure-dispatch**; without it a pure-dispatch implementation passes the whole suite while shipping `"<class '...'>"` to a model;

- the BaseModel path byte-identical (assert a known existing render is unchanged);
- `inject_schema` (the second public face) no longer leaks -- asserted, not assumed;
- nested exotic annotations still render leniently (no strict leakage into recursion).

### VERDICT: NEEDS_REFINEMENT
Root cause and scope are right. The design field's Fix Approach is still 'SHAPE NOT YET CHOSEN' and must be resolved to the hybrid above, with the single-sourced-arm-list constraint and the discriminating test recorded. No user decision is owed -- the choice is settled by the fallthrough evidence and the sibling precedent.

Follow-up from neograph-qtfof.9's R2 maintainer decision (2026-08-14). The EndNode-wiring fix requires a Construct's terminal branch arms to converge on a compatible output type; when they diverge, export now fails loud (ConfigurationError) rather than guessing a union.

This is a deliberate SCOPE BOUNDARY for the export path, not a permanent design limitation. LangGraph's underlying graph model supports arbitrary branch/merge/branch-again (diamond) topologies, and neograph itself has no structural reason to forbid a Construct with genuinely divergent per-arm terminal outputs long-term -- the maintainer explicitly confirmed this during qtfof.9's design discussion.

Design questions for this follow-up:
1. What does LangGraph/neograph's own compiler do TODAY for a construct whose branch arms terminate in different types with no explicit merge/reconvergence node? Does compile() already support this, or does neograph's OWN runtime also implicitly require convergence somewhere downstream (state-bus field naming, etc.)? Trace this before assuming the export path is the only place with a gap.
2. If neograph's compiler already handles divergent-arm-output constructs correctly at runtime, the Agent Spec export gap is purely a representation problem: how would a Flow with multiple EndNodes (one per possible terminal type), or a single EndNode with a documented union-property convention, represent this? pyagentspec's own node type inventory needs checking for what's actually expressible.
3. If neograph's compiler does NOT actually support divergent-arm terminal outputs cleanly today either, this may be a bigger feature (add topology support to neograph itself, not just its Agent Spec exporter) -- scope accordingly, and consider whether it belongs in this epic (Portal x Agent Spec) or a separate core-compiler ticket.

Do NOT implement without first tracing (1) -- this ticket is a design question, not a ready-to-implement spec. See neograph-qtfof.9's design field and _agent_spec_boundary.py for the current fail-loud implementation and its exact ConfigurationError message.

title: Register neograph's checkpointed models in langgraph's allowed_msgpack_modules
description:
Follow-up from neograph-ftnxl.5 (tool ledger), not implemented there -- a genuine latent silent seam, wider than that ticket's scope.

ToolInteraction (and presumably other neograph checkpointed Pydantic models) are unregistered today. When that future langgraph version lands, deserializing a checkpointed ToolInteraction will fail differently -- or worse, silently degrade: renderers._is_tool_interaction_list (an isinstance check, renderers.py:282-287) would silently go False on a plain-dict fallback, changing tool_log rendering behavior with NO error raised.

This is a latent seam across the entire tool_log checkpoint-resume path, not specific to the ordinal/ToolLedger work. Needs its own investigation: which neograph models actually need registering, what langgraph's allowed_msgpack_modules registration API looks like, and whether this should be automatic (framework registers its own models) or requires the consuming app to opt in.

title: Refine scope for neograph-ftnxl.12 before fix
description:
Architect review (neograph-q14v5.5) returned NEEDS_REFINEMENT for neograph-ftnxl.12. Full review is in neograph-ftnxl.12's notes under '## Architect Review (q14v5.5)'. Resolve these BEFORE neograph-q14v5.7 (Fix bug neograph-ftnxl.12) runs.

## What must be decided

1. RE-SCOPE the ticket. Its scope line says '_recursion_budget.py only', but the primary defect is at the ASSEMBLY VALIDATOR: a Portal-modified item inside a _BranchNode arm is entirely INERT at compile time (_add_arm_nodes/_wire_arm_edges never dispatch on primary_shape -- plain make_node_fn + static add_edge, no Command(goto), no mesh), and _check_portal_mesh never descends into arms so nothing rejects it. Verified red: tests/test_portal_validation.py::TestPortalInsideBranchArmRejected (2 tests). Fixing only the budget arithmetic leaves that silent seam -- the band-aid AGENTS.md forbids.

2. RECONCILE THE TWO CONTRADICTORY RED TESTS (blocking, review finding 6):
   - tests/test_portal_validation.py::TestPortalInsideBranchArmRejected requires an arm-Portal Construct to RAISE ConstructError.
   - tests/test_portal_budget_arm_boundary.py::test_arm_boundary_splits_portal_mesh_runs_in_the_recursion_floor requires that same construct to BUILD + COMPILE, then asserts the floor (27 vs 34).
   They cannot both pass. Expected resolution: adopt the fail-loud rejection, DELETE tests/test_portal_budget_arm_boundary.py (it encodes the arm axis that becomes unrepresentable), and keep a budget regression test only for the arm-free NAMED-mesh axis under neograph-ftnxl.20.

3. HARD CONSTRAINT on any _mesh_hop_cost edit (review finding 4): do NOT switch it to raw construct.nodes. Verified empirically -- an arm SUB-CONSTRUCT holding a 2-member mesh contributes 5 to the floor today only because iter_with_arms descends into arms; dropping descent UNDER-counts and yields a runtime GraphRecursionError. Keep arm descent, break the contiguous run at arm boundaries, and use the EXISTING iter_with_arm_ids (_ir_branch.py:107) -- never a second arm-tagging primitive.

4. DECIDE ftnxl.20's landing. neograph-ftnxl.20 (_mesh_hop_cost merges two adjacent NAMED meshes; verified max_hops 2 + 7 -> cost 2) is independent of the arm question and is NOT fixed by the rejection. Decide whether it lands in the same edit (it touches the same ~15 lines) with its own regression test, or stays a separate follow-up.

5. Before landing the rejection, grep examples/ and tests/ for any existing Portal-in-arm construct that would start raising.

## Acceptance
Ticket scope + fix site restated in neograph-ftnxl.12's design field; the two-red-test contradiction resolved with a named winner; ftnxl.20 landing decided.

title: _mesh_hop_cost merges two adjacent NAMED Portal meshes into one budget run
description:
Sibling divergence to neograph-ftnxl.12, found by its trace-similar atom (neograph-q14v5.3), in the SAME function and from the SAME root cause family: _recursion_budget._mesh_hop_cost's contiguous-run accumulation is NOT the compiler's mesh definition.

Second axis (independent of the arm boundary): _mesh_hop_cost appends ANY PrimaryShape.PORTAL item to current_run and never applies _group_portal_members -- the shared grouping helper that the validator (_validation_portal), the state builder (state.py:239), the IR normalizer, the scaffold capture, AND the compiler's own _contiguous_portal_mesh (_wiring.py:206) all use to isolate one NAMED mesh group. Since neograph-fefar admitted >1 named mesh per level, two adjacent Portal nodes with DIFFERENT Portal.name values are TWO meshes to the compiler and ONE run to the budget.

Verified: Construct(nodes=[Node|Portal(name='m1', max_hops=2), Node|Portal(name='m2', max_hops=7)]) -> _mesh_hop_cost == 2. The compiler sees two meshes, so the floor should be 2 + 7 = 9; mesh m2's entire hop budget is dropped because the merged run is costed from current_run[0] only.

Fix: route _mesh_hop_cost's flush through _group_portal_members over the collected run (never a re-derived inline grouping), so each named group is costed with its OWN entry. Best done in the SAME edit as neograph-ftnxl.12's arm-boundary flush -- both are 'the budget's mesh detection must equal _contiguous_portal_mesh's' and touch the same ~15 lines; filed separately so neither is silently folded in without its own regression test.

title: Non-Portal modifiers (Loop/Each/Oracle/Operator) are also inert when placed directly on a branch-arm item
description:
Found via neograph-ftnxl.12's trace-similar atom (same root cause, different modifier).

_add_arm_nodes/_wire_arm_edges (_wiring_branch.py) never dispatch on primary_shape(item) at all -- confirmed zero matches for 'primary_shape'/'modifier_set.' in that file, vs. compiler.py's main loop which has a full 'match primary_shape(item): case ORACLE/EACH/LOOP/BARE/PORTAL' dispatch (compiler.py:463-499, 561-618). Every arm item unconditionally goes through plain make_node_fn (Node) or _compile()+make_subgraph_fn (Construct) + static add_edge, regardless of what modifier it carries.

Confirmed empirically for Loop: a Node | Loop(when=..., max_iterations=3) placed as a branch-arm item compiles cleanly with ZERO self-loop back-edge and no loop router wired -- graph.get_graph().edges shows only the plain sequential arm edge, no looped2->looped2 back-edge. The Loop modifier is completely inert, identical in kind to the Portal finding in neograph-ftnxl.12 (that ticket's revised root cause: _add_arm_nodes bypasses ALL primary_shape-based wiring, not just Portal's).

Not yet empirically checked (time-boxed out of ftnxl.12's trace-similar atom): Each (fan-out via Send()) and Oracle (multi-variant + merge) on a bare arm item. Given the shared root cause (_add_arm_nodes has zero primary_shape awareness), they are presumed to have the same inertness until verified -- this ticket's own reproduce atom should confirm each modifier independently, not assume from the Loop finding alone.

## Scope
Explicitly separate from neograph-ftnxl.12 (Portal-specific) to keep that ticket's fix minimal (anti-band-aid task design: fix the bug only, don't fold in unrelated modifiers). This ticket covers Loop/Each/Oracle/Operator specifically.

## Fix direction (not yet designed)
Likely the SAME shape of fix as ftnxl.12's revised approach: reject (ConstructError) any non-BARE primary_shape on a branch-arm item at assembly time, OR extend _add_arm_nodes to properly dispatch through the same primary_shape match compiler.py's main loop uses. The validation-guard approach (reject) is probably correct short-term per the project's 'unrepresentable > fail-loud' priority; full arm-aware compilation support for every modifier shape is a much larger feature and should be a separate design decision, not bundled into a bug fix.
design:
## Root Cause

`_wiring_branch.py::_add_arm_nodes` and `_wire_arm_edges` are modifier-blind. They branch only on `isinstance(item, Construct)` (subgraph vs node) and never consult `primary_shape(item)` / `COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[combo]`, unlike `compiler.py::_add_node_to_graph` and `_add_subgraph`, which match on the primary shape (ORACLE/EACH/LOOP/BARE/PORTAL) to pick one of five graph-builders and then append `_add_operator_check` for the orthogonal Operator wrapper. A modifier on a branch-arm item is therefore accepted at assembly, survives compile without error, and emits none of its wiring -- a silent seam, identical in kind to the Portal case closed by neograph-ftnxl.12.

It is a HALF-IMPLEMENTED FEATURE, not a pure oversight: `state.py` already builds LOOP-shaped state (append-list field + `neo_loop_count_*`) for a Loop-modified arm Construct, and `_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py` already exports arm modifiers faithfully. Two layers implement it; the wiring layer does not.

## Fix Approach (REFINED post-review, neograph-lhqr8.13)

Direction (a): reject at assembly time. Direction (b) is filed as **neograph-ftnxl.22**.

**1. ONE folded arm guard.** Add `_check_no_modifier_in_branch_arm(construct)` to `_validation_arms.py` (162/400 lines; already owns arm-scoped rules) and DELETE `_check_no_portal_in_branch_arm` from `_validation_portal.py` (393/400, and the wrong concern once the rule is general). Two parallel arm guards would re-create the duplicated-dispatch anti-pattern AGENTS.md records from the Portal rollout.
- Walk `iter_with_arm_ids(construct)`, skip `arm_key is None`; no second arm-tagging primitive.
- Predicate read from the ONE decomposition table: `decomp = COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[classify_modifiers(item)[0]]`; reject when `decomp.primary is not PrimaryShape.BARE or decomp.has_operator`. Never a hand-typed modifier list -- this also makes the guard total over future `PrimaryShape` values by construction.
- Message: `ConstructError.build` naming the offending item AND the modifier(s) (`modifier_names_for_combo`), with `expected`/`found`/`node`/`construct`/`location`. The `hint` must carry BOTH (i) the workaround -- wrap the modified node in a sub-Construct and put THAT in the arm (proven end-to-end incl. interrupt/resume by `tests/test_branch_arm_checkpointer.py`) -- and (ii) the neograph-ftnxl.22 reference.
- Keep the words 'portal'/'arm' reachable in the Portal case so the 3 existing ftnxl.12 assertions still hold.
- Call it once from `_validate_node_chain` (`_construct_validation.py` is at 398/400 -- ride the existing `from neograph._validation_arms import ...` line so only the call line is added; re-check `test_guards_assembly.py` VALIDATION_CLUSTER LINE_CAP=400 after).

**2. Delete the now-dead partial support.**
- `state.py` arm-Loop-Construct LOOP branch (the `Annotated[list[T], _append_loop_result]` + counter case). Leaving it preserves the third silent seam: an arm Loop's append-list always holds exactly one element, so an `all_in_scope` `list[T]` consumer cannot distinguish it from a real single-iteration loop.
- `_fan_agent_wrap.py`'s `CompileError` 'Oracle over an agent/act node inside a branch arm is not supported' -- assembly now rejects strictly earlier, so it can never fire. Delete it or annotate it explicitly as defense-in-depth with a written reason; do not leave it ambiguous.

**3. Convert (never silently delete) the two conflicting pins.**
- `tests/test_agent_spec_export.py::test_modifier_wrapped_node_inside_arm_gets_its_existing_lowering` (an architect-review pin from neograph-s7zt3.17): rewrite to assert the shape is now rejected at `Construct(...)`, with a docstring recording the original intent and WHY it was invalidated -- exporting a spec that asserts a loop the compiled graph does not have is worse than refusing the input.
- `tests/test_coverage_gaps.py::test_branch_arm_with_loop_construct_creates_append_list_field`: same treatment, tied to change 2.

**4. Totality test.** Parametrize over every `ModifierCombo` value: each non-BARE / operator-carrying combo placed on an arm item must raise `ConstructError`; `BARE` must not. Proves the table-driven predicate's future-proofness instead of asserting it.

**5. Regression check.** Re-run `tests/test_portal_validation.py`, `tests/test_portal_budget_arm_boundary.py`, `tests/test_branch_arm_checkpointer.py`, `tests/test_agent_spec_export.py`, `tests/test_coverage_gaps.py`, then the full gate against the 4828-pass baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Each of Loop/Each/Oracle/Operator independently verified (empirical repro, not assumed) for branch-arm inertness. Either: (a) assembly-time ConstructError added for each non-BARE/non-PORTAL primary_shape found in true_arm_nodes/false_arm_nodes (mirroring whatever guard ftnxl.12 lands), or (b) a documented design decision to support full arm-aware wiring instead, filed as its own ticket if that's the chosen direction.
notes:
## Reproduction (neograph-lhqr8.2)

- Failing tests: tests/test_branch_arm_modifier_validation.py::TestNonPortalModifiersInsideBranchArmRejected (5 failing, 1 should-pass companion green)
- Root cause: `_add_arm_nodes`/`_wire_arm_edges` (_wiring_branch.py) contain zero `primary_shape`/`COMBO_DECOMPOSITION` dispatch, so every branch-arm item is wired via plain make_node_fn/make_subgraph_fn + static add_edge -- the same bypass ftnxl.12 fixed for Portal, which leaves Loop/Each/Oracle/Operator equally inert.

### Empirical verification -- all four INDEPENDENTLY confirmed (not assumed)

Compiled topology, same modifier at top level (control) vs. inside a true-arm:

| Modifier | Top-level wiring (control)                                   | Inside a branch arm            |
|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| Loop     | `looped_top -> looped_top` back-edge + `__loop_exit_looped_top` | plain node, NO back-edge, no exit router |
| Each     | `__each_empty_each_top` + `assemble_each_top` barrier          | plain node only, no fan-out/barrier |
| Oracle   | `merge_or_top` judge node                                     | plain node only, no variants/merge |
| Operator | `opnode3__operator` interrupt check node                      | plain node only, no check node |

All four COMPILED CLEANLY with no error and no wiring.

Operator sub-finding (worse than plain inertness): compiling an arm Operator WITHOUT a checkpointer DOES raise the 'Operator modifier requires a checkpointer' CompileError -- so a compile-time consumer observes the arm Operator, giving the author a false signal the modifier was seen, while `_add_operator_check` is never called for it.
Oracle sub-finding: the state model DOES get a `neo_oracle_oracled` collector field for the arm item, but nothing ever writes or reads it -- dead state, no merge node.

### Blast-radius check (informs the fix direction)

Swept tests/**/*.py + examples/*.py for any `self.loop(`/`self.each(`/`self.ensemble(`/`self.interrupt(` call nested under an `if`/`elif`/`else` at lower indentation: ZERO hits. No existing test or example places a modifier inside a branch arm, so an assembly-time reject breaks nothing.
## Trace-similar (neograph-lhqr8.3)

Pattern category: **arm-descent handler that is modifier-shape-blind** -- distinct from the already-guarded 'arm-blind WALK' disease (`tests/test_guards_branch_arm_walks.py`, neograph-vn5f). Here the walk IS arm-aware (`compiler.py` dispatches `_BranchNode` -> `_add_branch_to_graph`); it is the HANDLER on the far side that drops `primary_shape`. The existing AST guard cannot see this class of defect at all -- it scans for raw `.nodes` iteration, not for modifier dispatch inside an arm handler.

Swept every `primary_shape`/`COMBO_DECOMPOSITION`/`classify_modifiers` consumer in src/neograph (65 call sites) against its arm coverage. Four findings:

**1. `_wiring_branch.py::_add_arm_nodes` / `_wire_arm_edges` -- THE bug (this ticket).** Zero modifier dispatch.

**2. Agent Spec EXPORT diverges from COMPILE for the same construct (NEW, empirically confirmed).** `_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py::_lower_branch_node` routes every arm item through the full modifier-aware `lower_item`, so an arm `Node | Loop(when='keep_going', max_iterations=3)` exports as:
    StartNode / ToolNode trigger / BranchingNode __branch_0 / ToolNode looped / **BranchingNode looped__loop_check** / ToolNode elsey / EndNode
-- a real loop-check node -- while the compiled LangGraph for that identical construct has NO back-edge and no loop router. The exported spec ASSERTS a loop the runtime does not have. This is the same root cause seen from the export side, and it is an argument FOR fix direction (a): rejecting at assembly makes the divergence unrepresentable, whereas any partial wiring fix would have to keep the two sides in lockstep by hand.

**3. `state.py` loop-counter loop iterates `nodes_only` (top level only) -- an arm Loop NODE never gets its `neo_loop_count_*` field, while an arm Loop CONSTRUCT does (state.py's branch_nodes block explicitly builds the LOOP-shaped field + counter for the Construct form).** Confirmed empirically: the arm-Loop probe's state fields were `['trigger_loop', 'looped', ...]` -- no counter. NEW; not covered by neograph-ftnxl.18, whose scope is has_any_oracle/has_any_each only. Becomes unreachable under fix direction (a); stays a live trap under (b).

**4. `state.py` `all_items = nodes_only + sub_constructs` (has_any_oracle/has_any_each) omits arm items** -- ALREADY FILED as neograph-ftnxl.18. Confirmed empirically: the arm-Oracle probe got a `neo_oracle_oracled` collector field (dead -- nothing writes or reads it) but no `neo_oracle_gen_id`/`neo_oracle_model`.

**Sharpest evidence of the disease, not a separate bug:** `compiler.py` lines ~195-220 deliberately walk `iter_with_arms` so an arm Operator's string condition is checked against the registry AND the 'Operator requires a checkpointer' guard fires -- then `_add_arm_nodes` never calls `_add_operator_check`. The compiler validates the arm Operator as if it would run, and wires nothing.

**Checked and CLEAN (arm coverage correct):** `_recursion_budget.py` (`iter_with_arms`), `_schema_fingerprint.py` (explicit arm walk), `_construct_validation.py` (`iter_with_arm_ids`), `_ir_normalize.py` (`iter_item_slots` for write-back; its top-level-only peer-field set is documented + allowlisted), `lint.py`, `verify.py`, `_checkpoint_rewind.py`, `_fan_agent_wrap.py` (all `iter_with_arms`).
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-lhqr8.4)

Pattern: **an arm-descent site that reads branch-arm CONTENTS (`meta.true_arm_nodes`/`false_arm_nodes`) and then processes each arm item WITHOUT consulting the modifier decomposition (`primary_shape` / `COMBO_DECOMPOSITION` / `classify_modifiers`), directly or by delegation.**

Disease shape: **SYNTACTIC** (AST-detectable: an `ast.Attribute` named `true_arm_nodes`/`false_arm_nodes`, cross-checked against the enclosing function's + its delegates' use of the decomposition API). Per the atom's own rule, a single AST scan is sufficient -- no multi-agent fan-out, so no `.claude/code-review/` artifact is produced.

Scan command (reproducible; script preserved at scratchpad/scan_disease.py):
```
uv run python - <<'PY'
import ast, pathlib
SRC = pathlib.Path('src/neograph')
for f in sorted(SRC.rglob('*.py')):
    tree = ast.parse(f.read_text())
    for n in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(n, ast.Attribute) and n.attr in ('true_arm_nodes','false_arm_nodes'):
            print(f'{f}:{n.lineno}')
PY
```

Total arm-content read sites: **11 unique** (22 raw AST hits; each `true_`/`false_` pair and each double-walked node counts twice).

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | _wiring_branch.py:130-131 (`_add_branch_to_graph` -> `_add_arm_nodes`/`_wire_arm_edges`) | hands both arm lists to two handlers that dispatch ONLY on `isinstance(item, Construct)` | **MIGRATE** | THE bug. Zero decomposition consultation anywhere in the arm-descent path; every modifier is silently un-wired. This is the site the fix must change. |
| 2 | state.py:103 (`compile_state_model`, arm output fields) | arm walk with an explicit `COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[arm_combo].primary is LOOP` case | ALLOWLIST | Already consults the table (gold-standard arm-aware walk). Its known gaps are separately ticketed: neograph-ftnxl.18 (has_any_oracle/has_any_each) and the arm-Loop-Node counter gap recorded in this ticket's trace-similar notes. |
| 3 | state.py:296 (`compile_state_model`, arm context fields) | arm walk over `n.context` | ALLOWLIST | Context fields are modifier-independent (a declared `context=` name maps to a state field the same way under any shape). |
| 4 | _agent_spec_boundary.py:95-96 (`resolve_end_node_sources`) | reads each arm's LAST item to resolve the EndNode's converged output | ALLOWLIST | DELEGATES: gates both arm-last items through `_is_wirable`, which is `primary_shape(item) in (BARE, ORACLE)`, and falls back for any other shape. Flagged BLIND by the scan only because `_is_wirable` is module-level, outside the function body the scan inspected. |
| 5 | _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:518 (`_lower_branch`) | iterates both arms, lowering each item | ALLOWLIST (as a *walk*) | DELEGATES every arm item to the injected `lower_item` = the full modifier-aware `_lower_construct_item`. NOTE: this correctness is precisely what produces the export/compile divergence recorded in trace-similar finding 2 -- the exporter honours the arm modifier, the compiler does not. Fix direction (a) removes the divergence by making the input unrepresentable; no change is needed HERE. |
