title: Carried + Reasoned output-field markers (schema projection + assembly, think mode)
description:
Mirrors the existing FromInput/FromConfig Annotated-marker idiom (di.py DIKind enum, decorators.py:70-71) -- but that idiom classifies function PARAMETERS via inspect.signature/get_type_hints in _di_classify.py; there is currently ZERO code that inspects Annotated metadata on an output model's FIELDS (describe_type.py's two-pass renderer, _count_classes then _render_model_body/_render_type, walks model_fields but only reads FieldInfo/type/description/constraints/default -- never get_type_hints(model, include_extras=True) per field).

Hook points (both already exist, no restructuring needed): (1) projection -- describe_type needs a marker-aware skip so Carried fields are omitted from the schema shown to the LLM, mirroring the include_extras=True pattern _di_classify.py already uses for params; the projected schema must also drive the actual with_structured_output(model=...) call in _llm.py:239/371, not just the rendered TS-notation text -- string surgery on the prompt alone is insufficient. (2) assembly -- ThinkDispatch.execute/aexecute (_dispatch.py:280-284 sync, 301-315 async) has an exact post-parse/pre-state-write seam: result is already the fully-parsed, validated model instance and nothing downstream (_build_state_update) inspects how it got there. Insert one _assemble_output(node, result, input_data, config) call before the NodeOutput(...) wrap, splicing Carried values from the node's OWN input_data + config paths only. The agent/act ReAct cycle has the equivalent seam in _shape_tool_output (_dispatch.py:318-338) -- phase 2, not this ticket's think-mode-only scope.

SCOPE FENCE (unanimous recommendation from the feasibility pass): Carried may reference ONLY the node's own input_data/config, never another node's output by path -- referencing another node's output would add a validator-invisible dataflow edge and escalate this from DX-layer sugar into genuinely new IR work (Node field + single-writer normalizer + guard test, the Portal precedent). This ticket is scoped to stay sugar.

FAIL-LOUD REQUIREMENT (the highest silent-seam risk identified): an unresolvable Carried path is an ExecutionError at runtime PLUS a lint rule + should_fail fixture at assembly time -- never None-fill. A Pydantic default on a Carried field must NOT mask a missed splice (a Carried field with a default that gets stripped from the schema but never spliced is a silently-defaulted value the model 'never lied about' -- exactly the di_inputs lint/runtime-divergence failure mode this codebase already lived through once). Add a structural guard pinning describe_type-strip <-> dispatch-splice lockstep, and audit describe_value so few-shot examples never show an unprojected instance.

Reasoned rides along as the zero-cost default (model-authored fields, unchanged, optionally rendered with their FieldInfo description as the rationale prompt). Three-surface parity: since markers live on the output MODEL (not the node), they should work surface-neutrally across @node/declarative/programmatic -- test this explicitly rather than assuming it.

Coordinate with neograph-jtawq (file-size/architecture DEFER epic): this touches describe_type.py (already 552 lines) and _dispatch.py -- if jtawq schedules either file's split first, land that before or scope this epic to the post-split layout to avoid double churn.

Full grounding: docs/design/hybrid-dataflow-workflow-findings-2026-08-14.md, section 'ir_outputs' + 'raw_channels' (raw_inputs/raw_di_inputs/raw_context are a related-but-distinct INPUT-side mechanism -- do not conflate; Carried is OUTPUT-side).
design:
## Core Invariant (unchanged, now with a fix target)
Exactly one function decides which fields of a node's output model the LLM is asked to produce, and exactly one function fills the fields it removed -- so the schema the model is constrained by, the schema text it is shown, the schema compile_prompt() reports, and the instance written to the state bus can never disagree; and any field removed-but-unfillable is a loud failure, never a default.

TODAY THIS INVARIANT IS ALREADY FALSE for the existing ExcludeFromOutput marker under the default output_strategy -- see disease-scan notes. Fixing that is IN SCOPE for this ticket, not a pre-existing wart to route around.

## REVISED Implementation Plan (supersedes the original DESIGN section; scope reduced per elegance review -- Reasoned dropped, context= deferred, lint.py check deferred)

**Scope for this ticket: Carried only** (Reasoned dropped -- delivers zero behavior beyond existing Field(description=...) rendering; ship it later if/when Selected lands and a real three-member contrast exists).

1. **New module `src/neograph/_output_classify.py`** (NOT describe_type.py -- closes the plan's original fork; describe_type.py has only 49 lines of headroom and this would eat it). Contains:
   - `ExcludeFromOutput` MOVES here from describe_type.py (re-exported from describe_type.py for back-compat import path, or updated at its 2 call sites -- decide during implementation; public contract is neograph/__init__.__all__ either way).
   - `Carried(path: str)` marker class -- Annotated metadata, fail-loud __init__ parsing (mirrors FromResource.__init__), parses into `.segments` ONCE (shared by both the assembly checker and the runtime splicer -- never re-split the path string in two places).
   - `output_markers(field_info) -> set[Literal["excluded","carried"]]` -- the ONE generalized predicate both `describe_type` and `describe_value` and the projector consume. Replaces `_is_output_excluded`.
   - `project_output_model(model: type[BaseModel]) -> type[BaseModel]` -- builds a STRUCTURAL SIBLING via `create_model(f"{model.__name__}_Projected", __base__=BaseModel, **remaining_fields)` -- NEVER a subclass (pydantic cannot remove an inherited field in a subclass; a subclass projection is a silent no-op). Depth-0 only: a Carried/Excluded marker on a NESTED model's field is an assembly-time ConstructError (not silently ignored) -- the recursive-strip-vs-flat-splice mismatch elegance review flagged. `functools.lru_cache`-wrapped (pure function of the model class), never a module-level mutable dict.
   - `splice_carried(node, declared: type[BaseModel], projected_result: BaseModel, input_data, config) -> BaseModel` -- resolves each Carried field's path against `input_data.fan_in` (upstream-rooted) or `config[...][StateKeys.DI_INPUTS]` (DI-rooted), shallow-copies `{k: getattr(projected_result, k) for k in type(projected_result).model_fields}`, merges in the resolved carried values, constructs `declared(**merged)`. A `pydantic.ValidationError` from that final construction (type mismatch, cross-field validator) is caught and re-raised as `ExecutionError.build(...)` naming node + field + path -- never let a raw pydantic error escape. MISSING (unresolvable root/attribute) always raises; a PRESENT-but-None value splices as None if the declared field is Optional, raises if not (the missing-vs-None distinction elegance flagged).

2. **Assembly-time validator**: `_check_carried_paths(construct)` in new `src/neograph/_validation_outputs.py` (joins the validation cluster -- add to `VALIDATION_CLUSTER`, `private_modules` in `_seam_violations`, AND `EXPECTED_LOCATIONS` in `tests/test_guards_assembly.py`, all three, in the same commit -- three independently-maintained lists, confirmed by the layering scan). Rejects: (a) a Carried path whose root is not a key of `node.inputs` or a `_param_res` DI param name -- the corrected SCOPE FENCE wording (a `fan_in[root]` IS an upstream node's output, but it's a DECLARED, validator-visible one, so this is fine -- the fence bans an UNDECLARED root, not any upstream reference at all); (b) a Carried/Excluded marker on a nested (depth>0) model field. Where the path is not statically resolvable (single-form `inputs=`, opaque `FromConfig` type), defer to the runtime check -- state this honestly in the error message, don't overclaim compile-time coverage. Wired into `_validate_node_chain` via ONE delegating call + import, the exact `_check_portal_mesh` shape (`_construct_validation.py` has 23 lines of headroom against its 400 cap -- fine).

3. **Dispatch integration**: project + splice at the SINGLE choke point both invoke_structured/ainvoke_structured share (`_llm.py`'s `_prepare_structured_call`/`_resolve_primary_output`-adjacent call site) -- confirmed by the layering scan's call-graph trace as the one place that reaches the constrained-decode schema (`_call_structured`), the rendered TS text (`describe_type` at json_mode), AND the prompt-compiler kwarg (`_compile_prompt`) simultaneously. Mirror at `_tool_loop.py`'s `_parse_final_turn`/`_aparse_final_turn` (agent/act's structured fallback) -- separate seam, same fix, same function reused. Do NOT apply in `_dispatch.py` (would skip the two `_oracle.py` merge call sites that share `_llm.py`'s function and must inherit the fix automatically). Also project at `_llm_render.py:429` (the `output_model` ASSIGNMENT, not the `describe_type` call at :431) for `compile_prompt()` out-of-graph parity -- fixes the file-cite the plan originally had wrong.

4. **`_agent_output_schema_preamble.py` (agent/act preamble)**: explicitly OUT of scope (think-mode-only per the original ticket's own scope fence) -- but per the consistency scan, this must be a FAIL-LOUD assembly-time rejection (`_check_carried_paths` raises `ConstructError`: "Carried is not supported on agent/act nodes yet") — NOT a passive written exemption, since the preamble already strips text with no splice mechanism and a silent pass would ship the exact silent seam this ticket exists to prevent, on an agent/act node, on day one.

5. **Fix `ExcludeFromOutput` in the same change** (per dedup scan's explicit recommendation -- not deferred): route it through step 1's shared `output_markers`/`project_output_model`, so it gets the SAME projection fix as `Carried` for free. Also fix `_describe_value.py:76` to honor the shared predicate (few-shot examples currently teach the model to produce excluded fields -- the third divergent consumer). BEHAVIOR CHANGE NOTE (elegance flagged this explicitly, must be stated not silently shipped): under the default `structured` strategy, `ExcludeFromOutput` currently does NOTHING (describe_type never runs, with_structured_output gets the field intact) -- after this fix it will actually strip+require-a-default. At 0.x with one downstream consumer (piarch) this is an accepted, deliberate behavior change, not a side effect to discover later.
   - No-default enforcement: assembly-time check that any `Excluded`/`Carried` field has a Pydantic default (the existing marker's documented-but-unenforced promise) -- one shared validator in `_validation_outputs.py`, written failing-first.

6. **Structural guard** (`tests/test_guards_*.py`, new file e.g. `test_guards_output_projection.py`): anchored on OUTPUT_MODEL FLOW into the dispatch/structured-call seam, NOT on `describe_type(` call sites (the latter is blind to the default `structured` strategy where no `describe_type` call happens at all -- the consistency scan's critical correction). Derives the splice set as `set(declared.model_fields) - set(projected.model_fields)` (computed from the projection's own output, so it cannot disagree with the strip set by construction -- never a second independent marker scan) and asserts it equals the actually-spliced field set. Non-vacuity pin: a Carried field WITH a Pydantic default, stripped but unspliced, must FAIL the suite (mirrors `test_guards_prompt_channels.py`'s `test_detector_flags_a_synthetic_channel_...` pattern). Also pins: `splice_carried`'s signature takes no `state`/state-bus parameter ever (the SCOPE FENCE's real enforcement is structural -- this guard prevents a future edit from silently re-opening it).

7. **Deferred, filed as follow-ups (not silently dropped from this ticket's scope, just sequenced after)**:
   - `lint.py`'s 7th check (Carried path lint diagnostics) -- lint.py sits at its EXACT 662-line file-size ceiling; adding a check without extraction violates the ratchet, and per CLAUDE.md's 2nd refusal a pure split must never ride inside a behavior-change commit. File as its own follow-up once `jtawq`'s lint.py split lands (or as a standalone split-first-then-add commit).
   - `context=` support for Carried -- mechanically blocked today (`_extract_context` hands the splice seam `dict[str,str]` rendered strings, not typed objects; needs a `raw_context`-shaped fix at that seam first, the exact gap CLAUDE.md already documents for the input side).
   - Agent Spec export's `model_json_schema()` path is a third marker-blind schema consumer -- separate ticket once Carried ships and Agent Spec export of Carried-carrying models becomes a real question.
   - `_llm_render.py` vs `_dispatch.py._resolve_primary_output`'s pre-existing output-model-resolution divergence for dict-form/Oracle nodes -- pre-existing bug, unrelated to Carried, file separately.

## Test coverage required
- Guard-first (TDD red): the strip<->splice lockstep guard, non-vacuity pin, no-default enforcement, depth-0-only rejection, agent/act rejection -- all written failing before the implementation lands.
- Regression proving the ExcludeFromOutput fix: a field with default, no default (should_fail), under structured/json_mode/text strategies, sync+async, verifying the model handed to with_structured_output no longer contains the field (or contains it with the enforced default only where unavoidable).
- Carried happy path: node consuming its own input_data (fan_in root) and DI param, spliced correctly into the final output; missing root raises ExecutionError; present-but-None on an Optional field splices as None; present-but-None on a non-Optional field raises.
- Three-surface note: markers live on the output MODEL (not the node), so they are surface-neutral by construction across @node/declarative/programmatic -- verify this explicitly with one test per surface, per CLAUDE.md's three-surface parity rule.
- Checkpoint/fingerprint non-interference: a Carried field does not change compute_node_fingerprints' hash and does not reach the state bus as a projected instance (explicit assertion, not assumed).

Full grounding: docs/design/hybrid-dataflow-workflow-findings-2026-08-14.md 'ir_outputs' + 'raw_channels'; .claude/code-review/neograph-ftnxl.4/{disease-dedup,disease-consistency,disease-layering,elegance}.md for the complete reasoning behind each revision above.
notes:
## Findings

**REUSE TARGET #1 (the ticket's premise is wrong, and this is good news): an output-field
Annotated-marker mechanism ALREADY EXISTS and is public.** `ExcludeFromOutput`
(`src/neograph/describe_type.py:53-71`, exported from `neograph/__init__.py:45,171`,
documented at `website/src/content/docs/reference/api.mdx:218`, demonstrated in
`examples/18_typed_projections.py`, tested at `tests/test_renderers.py:302`) is exactly
"strip this field from the LLM-facing output schema, keep it visible in input rendering".
The ticket description's claim -- "there is currently ZERO code that inspects Annotated
metadata on an output model's FIELDS" -- is FALSE, and so is the design doc's prescription
to add `get_type_hints(model, include_extras=True)`. Pydantic v2 already parks unrecognised
`Annotated` extras on `FieldInfo.metadata`, so `_is_output_excluded(field_info)` is a
one-line `any(...)` over `model_fields[name].metadata` -- no `get_type_hints` needed
anywhere. **Carried is `ExcludeFromOutput` + a mandatory splice + fail-loud; Reasoned is
`ExcludeFromOutput`'s inverse (a no-op that documents intent).** Copy `_is_output_excluded`,
do not invent a second detection idiom.

**REUSE TARGET #2 (marker class shape): `FromInput`/`FromConfig`/`FromResource`**
(`_di_classify.py:21,55,86`). Bare-class-or-instance markers (`Annotated[str, FromInput]`
AND `Annotated[str, FromInput(required=False)]`), detected by
`m is X or isinstance(m, X)` -- the identical predicate `_is_output_excluded` uses.
`Reasoned` should be bare-or-instance (`Reasoned` / `Reasoned("why you picked it")`);
`Carried("path")` is instance-only, exactly like `FromResource(uri)`, whose `__init__`
raises `ConstructError.build(...)` on a bad marker-arg contract
(`_di_classify.py:125-132`) -- copy that fail-loud-in-`__init__` pattern for a malformed
Carried path.

**REUSE TARGET #3 (the Carried VALUE source is already resolved and sitting in config).**
`ThinkDispatch.execute` line 262 / `aexecute` line 296 already call
`_inject_di_inputs` / `_ainject_di_inputs` (`_dispatch.py:40-112`), which resolve the node's
`FromInput`/`FromConfig` bindings through the canonical `DIBinding.resolve` and stash the
RAW `{param_name: value}` map into `config['configurable'][StateKeys.DI_INPUTS]`. A Carried
path rooted at a DI param name therefore needs **zero new resolution code** -- read
`StateKeys.DI_INPUTS` back out, four lines below where it was written. Do NOT add a second
resolver (the codebase's stated rule for `di_inputs`).

**CURRENT vs OLD -- the projection must NOT go into `describe_type`.** The design doc says
"add a marker-aware pass to describe_type". That is the wrong site now, for three reasons:
(1) there are **six** `describe_type(output_model)` call sites, five outside the module
(`_llm.py:315`, `_llm_render.py:431`, `prompt.py:121`, `_llm_retry.py:143`,
`_agent_output_schema_preamble.py:45`) -- teaching describe_type about Carried fixes the
rendered TEXT at all six but fixes `with_structured_output` at none of them;
(2) `describe_type.py` is at 451/500 lines with no allowlist entry -- 49 lines of headroom;
(3) the model handed to `with_structured_output` comes from a *different* argument
(`output_model` threaded `_llm.invoke_structured:289 -> _llm_dispatch._call_structured ->
_llm_structured_compat:134 llm.with_structured_output(model)`).
**The correct site is one projection function producing a synthesized Pydantic subclass,
applied where `output_model` is chosen -- then every one of the six describe_type sites AND
`with_structured_output` receive the projected model for free, with zero edits to
`describe_type.py`.** This is strictly better than the ticket's plan and removes its
file-size collision with neograph-jtawq.

**PRE-EXISTING LATENT BUG this uncovers (worth its own ticket, do not silently fix inside
this one).** Because `ExcludeFromOutput` strips only inside `describe_type`, an
`ExcludeFromOutput` field is still present in the schema `with_structured_output` hands the
provider under the DEFAULT `output_strategy="structured"`. The rendered text says "don't
produce this"; the constrained-decode schema says "produce this". The field's mandatory
default then masks it. That is precisely the strip/splice-divergence disease this ticket
exists to prevent -- already shipped, in the public API. The projection built here fixes it
as a side effect if `ExcludeFromOutput` is routed through the same projector.

**SECOND STRIP SITE the dispatch-only plan would miss.** `_llm_render.py:429-431`
(`render_prompt`, behind the public `compile_prompt()`) reads `node.outputs` DIRECTLY and
calls `describe_type` on it -- it never goes through `ThinkDispatch`. CLAUDE.md advertises
`compile_prompt()` as giving "in-/out-of-graph parity". If the dispatch projects and
`render_prompt` does not, `compile_prompt()` shows the user a schema the model never saw.
**The lockstep guard must cover this site, not just dispatch.**

**The splice must RECONSTRUCT the declared model, not return the projected instance.**
`_state_write._build_state_update` (`_state_write.py:52`) does not itself type-check, but
the compiled LangGraph state field is typed with the DECLARED model
(`state.py` / `compute_node_fingerprints`), and downstream consumers read via
`read_upstream(expected_type=...)` isinstance checks. So `_assemble_output` must do
`declared(**projected_result.model_dump(), **carried)` -- returning the projected instance
would put a structurally-different class on the state bus and silently break fan-in
validation and checkpoint fingerprints.

**Fail-loud furniture is all in place.** `ExecutionError.build(msg, node=, expected=,
found=, hint=)` is the runtime form (`_llm_dispatch.py:40-95` is the canonical multi-site
example); `ConstructError.build(...)` is the assembly form. Assembly-time validation hangs
off `_construct_validation._validate_node_chain` (line 111) with the exemplar being
`_check_portal_mesh`, which lives in its OWN module `_validation_portal.py` and is invoked
from a single line, `_construct_validation.py:349`. Lint extension point is
`lint._walk` (`lint.py:353-433`) which already has a numbered list of six checks;
lint kinds are registered in `_lint_kind_registry.LINT_KIND_META` (which
`scripts/gen_api_manifest.py` reads, so the website reference table updates itself).
Check-fixture convention: one defect per file, `# CHECK_ERROR: <regex>` first line --
see `tests/check_fixtures/should_fail/di_double_marker.py` for the exact shape.

**Lockstep-guard exemplar is exact, not approximate.**
`tests/test_guards_prompt_channels.py` derives BOTH sides of a two-site invariant by AST
(what `_compile_prompt` offers vs what `DefaultPromptCompiler.__call__` answers) and uses a
`KNOWN_IGNORED: dict[str, str]` mapping each exemption to a WRITTEN REASON rather than a
bare set. Its docstring states the lesson verbatim: "the offered set and the answered set
were related only by someone remembering." Copy this file's shape for the
strip<->splice guard.

**Three-surface parity -- the honest split (test it, do not assume it).** Markers live on
the output MODEL, so **Carried-from-input_data is surface-neutral by construction** (works
identically for `@node`, declarative `Node(...)`, and programmatic `Node() | Modifier()`).
But **Carried-from-DI is `@node`-ONLY by construction**: it reads `StateKeys.DI_INPUTS`,
which `_inject_di_inputs` populates from `node._param_res`, which only the `@node`
decorator's `_classify_di_params` ever writes (`_dispatch.py:53-55` returns config

## Risks & Edge Cases

- **NEEDS USER INPUT: the ticket description and the grounding doc both assert
  `describe_type` is marker-blind and prescribe `get_type_hints(model, include_extras=True)`
  in a new `_output_classify.py`. Both are contradicted by shipped code**
  (`ExcludeFromOutput` / `_is_output_excluded`, public since example 18). Confirm the
  intended resolution: (a) Carried/Reasoned join `ExcludeFromOutput` as siblings of one
  marker family sharing one detector, and (b) `ExcludeFromOutput` is routed through the new
  projector so its `with_structured_output` divergence is closed. Both are recommended;
  (b) is arguably a separate bug ticket, but leaving it unrouted ships two contradictory
  strip mechanisms.
- **NEEDS USER INPUT: `lint.py` is at 662, its EXACT allowlist ceiling
  (`tests/test_guards_file_size.py:82`), and that ratchet states "raise the number is not a
  remedy, splitting the file is."** Adding lint check 7 grows the file. Either the Carried
  lint check is paid for by extracting an existing cluster out of `lint.py` in the same
  commit (net-negative), or the ceiling policy needs an explicit exception here. Same
  pressure, milder, on `_construct_validation.py` (374 against the validation cluster's
  `LINE_CAP = 400` in `tests/test_guards_assembly.py` -- 26 lines of headroom, so the new
  check MUST live in its own module with a one-line call).
- **File-size headroom is the reason to prefer the projection design**: `describe_type.py`
  451/500 and `_dispatch.py` 434/500, neither allowlisted. The recommended design adds
  ~0 lines to describe_type.py and ~6-10 to `_dispatch.py`. The ticket's coordination note
  with neograph-jtawq becomes moot rather than blocking.
- **Path-root ambiguity for single-type `inputs`.** `NodeInput.value` returns `fan_in` (a
  `{upstream_name: value}` dict, clean path roots) when dict-form, else the bare `single`
  value (no name to root a path at). Phase 1 should either require dict-form `inputs` for a
  path rooted at an upstream, or define a reserved root for the single-value case -- and
  fail loud on the ambiguous case rather than guessing.
- **Loop/Each-modified upstreams.** A Carried path into an upstream whose producer carries
  `Each` sees `dict[str, X]`, and a `Loop`-modified upstream is an append-list whose
  "latest" reading is what `_extract_context`'s `read_upstream(expected_type=...)` already
  does. Whatever is chosen, word the guarantee the way CLAUDE.md words `raw_context` --
  "the object the value was read FROM" -- not "the raw state value".
- **A Carried field with a Pydantic default is the marquee silent seam** (ticket is right):
  stripped from the schema, never spliced, silently defaulted, model "never lied". The
  guard must be structural (AST, both sites), not a behavioral test that could be deleted.
- **Assembly-time reach of the path check is real but partial.** `node.inputs`
  (`dict[str, type]`) makes an upstream-rooted path statically resolvable -- same footing as
  `_check_fan_in_inputs`. A DI-rooted path resolves against `_param_res[...].inner_type`,
  also static. But `FromConfig` of a non-BaseModel type is opaque, and a `single`-form
  `inputs=` gives no name. Do not overclaim "compile-time checked" for those cases; make
  them runtime-fail-loud and say so.
- **Oracle interaction**: `_resolve_primary_output` returns `node.oracle_gen_type` when set
  (`_dispatch.py:377-379`) -- the per-variant type, not the post-merge type. Projection must
  apply to whichever model is actually returned, and the splice must reconstruct THAT model.
  An Oracle node whose generator type carries Carried fields is a real edge case to test.
- **Dict-form outputs**: the primary key is wrapped AFTER the seam (`NodeOutput(multi={pk:
  result})`). Splice before the wrap; `tool_log` and other framework-collected secondary
  keys must not be projected or spliced.
- **agent/act is explicitly out of scope** but `_agent_output_schema_preamble.py:45` calls
  `describe_type(output_model)` on that path. If phase 1 leaves agent/act unprojected, the
  lockstep guard must record that as a WRITTEN exemption (the `KNOWN_IGNORED` reason-map
  pattern), not an omission -- otherwise phase 2 has no tripwire.
- **Checkpoint fingerprints**: `compute_node_fingerprints` hashes the DECLARED type, and
  markers do not change field types, so adding a Carried marker to an existing field will
  NOT invalidate a checkpoint even though the value's provenance changed. Acceptable
  (fingerprints are type-based, not content-based) but should be stated, since a resumed run
  will carry a model-authored value in a now-Carried field.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-ftnxl.4)

Pattern: an Annotated output-field marker whose effect on the schema shown to the LLM and the schema that actually validates the parsed response are computed by two different code paths that could drift.

Scan: 3 lenses (dedup/consistency/layering) + opus elegance review. Full reports: .claude/code-review/neograph-ftnxl.4/{disease-dedup,disease-consistency,disease-layering,elegance}.md

## HEADLINE FINDING: ExcludeFromOutput (the EXISTING marker this ticket extends) has a REAL, CURRENTLY-SHIPPING production bug

Empirically proven (dedup scan): under the DEFAULT output_strategy="structured", describe_type() prunes the excluded field from the rendered prompt text, but with_structured_output(output_model) receives the model UNPROJECTED -- the excluded field is still in the schema handed to the provider's constrained decoder, and if it has no default it is listed as REQUIRED. The model is asked (via constrained decoding) to produce a value for a field the prompt text never mentions -- forcing hallucination. The marker's own documented promise ("LLM won't try to produce it", describe_type.py:62) is FALSE in the default strategy. json_mode/text/agent/act "accidentally work" only via an undocumented, unenforced "must have a default" convention -- a no-default excluded field raises ValidationError on every call in those strategies.

Per project standard (fix production defects immediately, not deferred polish): this bug is fixed IN THE SAME CHANGE as ftnxl.4, not routed around -- shipping Carried on the same one-sided seam would triple the defect.

## Merged disposition (all MIGRATE rows folded into the revised design below; ALLOWLIST/DEFER summarized)

MIGRATE (all incorporated into revised design):
- ExcludeFromOutput's single reader (_is_output_excluded, describe_type.py) must be lifted into a shared projection function BOTH the shown-schema side (describe_type) and the validating-schema side (with_structured_output) consume.
- Single fix point: _llm.py's _prepare_structured_call / _resolve_primary_output call site (both invoke_structured/ainvoke_structured share it) -- NOT _dispatch.py (would skip the two _oracle.py merge call sites), NOT per-call-site patching (would recreate the exact duplication being fixed).
- _tool_loop.py's _parse_final_turn/_aparse_final_turn (agent/act structured fallback) also needs the projection -- separate seam, same fix.
- render_prompt (_llm_render.py:429, the ASSIGNMENT not the describe_type call at :431) needs projecting too, for compile_prompt() out-of-graph parity.
- No enforcement exists today that an ExcludeFromOutput field has a default (grep confirmed zero hits outside describe_type.py) -- Carried needs the identical assembly-time check, build it once, shared.
- No structural guard pins shown-schema == validated-schema (the di_inputs lint-vs-runtime lesson, unapplied here) -- must build one, AST-derived, field-set based (not call-site based -- call-site guards are blind to the default 'structured' strategy where NO describe_type call happens at all).
- describe_value (_describe_value.py:76) already ignores ExcludeFromOutput -- a third, separately-divergent consumer (few-shot examples teach the model to produce excluded fields). Fold into the same shared predicate.

BLOCKING DESIGN CORRECTIONS from consistency+layering+elegance (resolved in revised design below):
1. Guard must anchor on OUTPUT_MODEL FLOW into the dispatch/structured-call seam, not on describe_type( call sites -- the latter is structurally blind to the default strategy.
2. Projected model must be a STRUCTURAL SIBLING (create_model(name, __base__=BaseModel, **fields)), NOT a subclass -- pydantic cannot remove an inherited field in a subclass, so a subclass-based projection is a no-op bug on day one.
3. Reconstruction must be a SHALLOW field-wise copy ({k: getattr(projected,k) for k in projected.model_fields} | carried, then declared(**merged)) -- NOT declared(**projected.model_dump(), **carried), which deep-dumps nested models to plain dicts, re-runs non-idempotent validators, and destroys non-serializable field values.
4. Nesting is UNSUPPORTED (depth-0 only) -- stated explicitly, enforced at assembly time with a should_fail fixture -- not silently broken one level down (describe_type's strip IS recursive; a flat splice is not, so a nested Carried field would strip from text, stay in the validating schema, and be unreachable by the splice -- the exact bug being fixed, reproduced one level down).
5. DROP Reasoned entirely (elegance's strongest simplification recommendation) -- it delivers literally zero new behavior beyond what Field(description=...) already does via existing describe_type rendering. Ship Carried only.
6. Splice failure must raise ExecutionError.build(...) naming node+field+path -- never let a raw pydantic ValidationError escape. Must distinguish MISSING (raise always) from present-but-None (splice as None if Optional, raise if not) -- 'None at a required step raises' is ambiguous between these.
7. Scope fence reworded: Carried may root ONLY at a name the node itself declares (a node.inputs key or a _param_res DI param name) -- NOT 'never another node's output' verbatim, since a fan_in root literally IS an upstream node's output, just a declared (hence validator-visible) one. context= is explicitly OUT of scope for this ticket (mechanical blocker: _extract_context hands the seam dict[str,str] rendered strings, not typed objects -- needs a raw_context-shaped fix first, same gap CLAUDE.md already documents) -- named, not silently dropped.
8. CLAUDE.md's file-size claim is WRONG: describe_type.py is 451 lines (not 552) -- correct it. The REAL ratchet collision is lint.py at its EXACT 662-line ceiling (ticket never mentioned this) -- if lint.py needs a 7th check for Carried, sequence a separate, PURE split commit first (per CLAUDE.md's 2nd refusal: never let a pure split ride inside a behavior change) -- OR skip the lint check for this ticket and file it as a follow-up once lint.py is split under the separate jtawq epic. RESOLVED: skip lint check for this ticket, file follow-up.
9. Guard must also pin assemble_output's signature (no `state` parameter ever) -- the SCOPE FENCE's real enforcement mechanism is structural (the splice seam cannot see the state bus), and a future edit threading state in would silently re-open the validator-invisible-edge risk with everything else green.
10. project_output_model must be cached via functools.lru_cache (pure (model)->type), never a module-level mutable dict (no-module-level-registration guard).

DEFERRED (real, filed as follow-ups, not silently dropped):
- _agent_spec_types.py's model_json_schema() export path is a THIRD marker-blind schema consumer (Agent Spec export) -- separate ticket, becomes relevant once Carried ships.
- _llm_render.py's output-model resolution (raw node.outputs) vs _dispatch.py's _resolve_primary_output (normalize_outputs + oracle_gen_type) already diverge for dict-form/Oracle nodes, independent of this ticket -- pre-existing bug, file separately.
- context= support for Carried -- future phase-1.5 once a raw_context-shaped typed channel exists at the splice seam.

## Architect Review (neograph-p6ssl.12, adversarial pass on the REVISED design)

Verified against shipped code, not against the plan's own citations. Confirmed correct
in the revision: the ExcludeFromOutput production bug is real (`_llm.py:289` hands the
UNPROJECTED `output_model` to `_call_structured`; `describe_type` runs only under
`json_mode` at `:314-315`); the structural-sibling-not-subclass correction is right;
the shallow-copy-not-model_dump correction is right; dropping `Reasoned` is right;
`_llm_render.py:429` is indeed the `output_model = getattr(node, "outputs", None)`
assignment; the three-list validation-cluster claim checks out (VALIDATION_CLUSTER
`tests/test_guards_assembly.py:17`, `private_modules` `:1768`, EXPECTED_LOCATIONS `:1834`).
The findings below are what the revision introduced or still leaves open.

  available is the RENDERED one — so Carried resolution silently becomes prompt-type
  dependent.** `_dispatch.py:263/297` calls `_render_input(node, input_data.value)` and
  passes its RESULT as `invoke_structured(input_data=rendered, ...)`. `_render_input`
  (`_dispatch.py:341-361`) returns `ri.raw` (typed Pydantic objects) for an INLINE
  prompt but `ri.for_template_ref` (BAML-rendered STRINGS + flattened extras) for a
  template-ref prompt. So the identical `Carried("claims.title")` declaration resolves
  to a typed value on an inline-prompt node and to a rendered string (or an unresolvable
  root, since `for_template_ref` is a flat merged dict, not the fan_in dict) on a
  template-ref node — same model, same marker, two behaviours. This is exactly the
  mechanical blocker the plan itself cites for deferring `context=` (`_extract_context`
  hands the seam `dict[str,str]`), reproduced on the input_data channel, and it was
  introduced by the revision moving the splice off the site the research had correctly
  chosen. Suggestion: split step 3 in two. PROJECTION belongs at `_llm.py` (the shared
  choke point — that argument is sound). The SPLICE belongs where the research put it,
  `_dispatch.py` `ThinkDispatch.execute/aexecute` immediately before the `NodeOutput(...)`
  wrap (`:282`/`:313`), resolving against the RAW `input_data.value` (the `NodeInput`),
  never against `rendered`. Restate step 3 as "project at one site, splice at a
  different, raw-typed site", and say so explicitly so a later edit does not
  "consolidate" them back together.

- [HIGH] Finding: **Splitting projection and splice leaves the Oracle merge path
  projected-but-unspliced — the marquee silent seam, on day one.** Step 3's stated
  reason for choosing `_llm.py` is that the two `_oracle.py` merge call sites (`:213`,
  `:301`) "must inherit the fix automatically". They will inherit the PROJECTION. They
  cannot inherit the splice: `_merge_prompt_input` builds `input_data` as

  disposition in the design — either (a) `_check_carried_paths` rejects a Carried marker
  on any model reachable as an Oracle merge output (`oracle.merge_prompt`'s primary
  output) with the same fail-loud ConstructError shape step 4 uses for agent/act, or

  in-scope answer. Either way it must be a rejection or a splice, never a pass.

title: Branch-arm cross-arm reachability leakage in the fan-in validator
description:
_construct_validation.py:141-150's own comment documents this exactly: 'iter_with_arms expands _BranchNode sentinels into their arm items so a bare arm Node is producer-registered... Registering a conditional arm output as a parent-scope producer is intentional... Cross-arm leakage (a false-arm node reading a true-arm output) is NOT caught here -- arms are flattened without recording which arm each producer belongs to; this is a documented limitation, not a regression... See neograph-vn5f (site 1).' neograph-vn5f itself is CLOSED (it fixed branch-arm nodes being validation-blind entirely, a different and larger bug) but explicitly left this narrower soundness gap as future work.

Concretely: _validate_node_chain (_construct_validation.py:111-374) walks nodes in declaration order accumulating one flat OrderedDict[field_name, Producer] (e.g. :236-240) with no per-arm membership tracking. A consumer node placed after a Branch can currently validate successfully against a producer that only exists on a DIFFERENT (non-taken) arm -- the validator answers 'was this declared upstream in source order', not 'is this guaranteed present on every path that reaches this node'.

Why this blocks provides/requires (this epic's own later child): a contract-satisfaction guarantee ('requires is satisfied on every path') sitting on top of this leaky reachability check would be FALSE by construction -- an existential defect per the North star (advertising compile-time safety the validator can't actually provide), not deferrable polish.

Fix: per-path producer accumulation for Branch arms in _validate_node_chain/iter_with_arms -- a producer registered inside one arm is visible downstream of the join only if ALL arms produce it; otherwise it's arm-local and a cross-arm consumer must fail loud with a specific ConstructError naming the arm mismatch. Should-fail fixture: cross-arm consumption. Should-pass fixture: all-arms-produce. No new IR fields -- this is validator-internal bookkeeping in _construct_validation.py/_ir_branch.py.

Full grounding: docs/design/hybrid-dataflow-workflow-findings-2026-08-14.md, section 'fan_in_contracts' finding #2.

## Root Cause
(unchanged from reproduce atom — see prior design section)

## Fix Approach (finalized post-disease-scan)

**New primitive** — `_ir_branch.py`: `iter_with_arm_ids(construct) -> Iterator[tuple[ConstructItem, tuple[int, bool] | None]]`. Yields `(item, arm_key)`: `arm_key=None` for a top-level item, `arm_key=(branch_id, is_true_arm)` for an arm item. Implemented over `enumerate(construct.nodes)` (a Call — invisible to `test_guards_branch_arm_walks.py`'s AST detector, per the layering scan's explicit recommendation; avoids an allowlist-count bump). `iter_with_arms` itself is UNCHANGED (kept as a thin wrapper: `(item for item, _ in iter_with_arm_ids(construct))`), preserving its flat contract for the 12 membership-only consumers.

**`_validate_node_chain` restructuring** (`_construct_validation.py`), replacing the single flat `producers` accumulator:
- `producers: ProducerMap` — now holds ONLY top-level producers + promoted all-arms-produce producers (see below). This is what gets handed to `_check_item_input` for a top-level consumer, and is also what the end-of-walk `construct.output` boundary check (line 356-374) reads — so MIGRATE site #4 (output boundary) is fixed for free by this restructuring, no separate logic needed.
- `current_branch: dict[bool, ProducerMap]` — transient, reset whenever `arm_key[0]` (branch_id) changes. Accumulates each arm's OWN producers as its items are walked (true arm fully walked before false arm, matching `iter_with_arm_ids`'s yield order == today's `iter_with_arms` order, so zero reordering risk).
- `all_producers: ProducerMap` — full unfiltered union (today's buggy flat map), kept ONLY for error-message diagnostics (see below), never for actual availability decisions.
- For an item with `arm_key=(bid, is_true)`: the VISIBLE producer map handed to `_check_item_input`/`_check_fan_in_inputs` = `{**producers, **current_branch[is_true]}` (top-level-so-far union same-arm-so-far). For `arm_key=None`: visible = `producers` alone (today's semantics, unchanged).
- **Branch-exit promotion**: when the walk moves off a branch_id (next item's `arm_key[0]` differs, or is `None`, or the walk ends), for every `field_name` present in BOTH `current_branch[True]` and `current_branch[False]` with `_types_compatible` types, copy it into `producers` (this is the ticket's own 'all-arms-produce' rule — the should_pass fixture). Field names present in only one arm are dropped, NOT promoted — this is the actual leak fix. Then reset `current_branch = {True: {}, False: {}}`.
- The `context=` check (line 190-201) and the `ambient_for_recursion` build for arm sub-constructs (line 207-212) both switch from reading flat `producers` to reading the same per-item VISIBLE map — fixes MIGRATE sites #2 and #3 with the identical mechanism, no divergent logic.
- `all_producers` is updated unconditionally on every producer registration (top-level AND arm), independent of the promotion logic — it is a pure diagnostic index, never consulted for a pass/fail decision.

**New error path** — `_validation_inputs.py`: `_check_item_input`/`_check_fan_in_inputs`/`_check_each_path` gain one new parameter, `all_producers: ProducerMap` (diagnostics-only; the existing `producers` param stays the VISIBLE set and its semantics are unchanged — this is the 'zero signature churn on the availability logic' the layering scan asked for; the churn is additive-only, for error quality). When a name is missing from `producers` (visible) but present in `all_producers` (known somewhere), raise a NEW, distinct `ConstructError` (per the consistency scan's drafted shape): `what="declares inputs['{name}']=... but '{name}' is produced only on a branch arm this node cannot reach"`, `expected="a producer reachable on every path to '{item.name}'"`, `found="'{name}' is produced on the {arm} arm; available upstreams: {sorted(visible)}"`, `hint="move the producer above the branch, or have both arms produce a compatible value"`. When absent from BOTH, the existing 'no upstream node named X exists' error is unchanged (still correct — genuinely unknown).

**Test changes**:
- `tests/test_branch_arm_noniter_walks.py:416-445` currently PINS the buggy behavior (asserts cross-arm construction does NOT raise) — must be corrected in the SAME commit as the fix, with a comment explaining why (sacred-rule-compliant: documenting the correction, not silently adjusting a test to fit new code — the test was asserting a documented bug, now fixed).
- New `tests/check_fixtures/should_fail/branch_cross_arm_consumption.py` + `tests/check_fixtures/should_pass/branch_all_arms_produce.py`.
- `tests/test_branch_arm_cross_arm_leakage.py` (reproduce atom) becomes the primary regression pin; extend with an all-arms-produce positive case if not already covered by the check_fixtures pass.

**Explicitly OUT of scope** (per disease scan): Portal mesh producer registration (line 214-259) stays flat — deliberate, documented, separate (docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md). `_recursion_budget.py`, `state.py` seen_fields, `testing/scaffold.py` are filed separately (neograph-ftnxl.12/.13/.14).

## Reproduction

## Trace-Similar Pattern Analysis

Bug category: flat producer-availability accumulation across mutually-exclusive
IR paths (branch arms) with no per-path membership tracking, letting a
validator answer 'declared upstream in source order' instead of 'guaranteed
present on every path that reaches this node'.

Searched every iter_with_arms(construct) call site (grep across src/neograph/):
__main__.py, _agent_spec.py, _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py,
_checkpoint_rewind.py, _construct_validation.py, _fan_agent_wrap.py,
_recursion_budget.py, _subconstruct.py, compiler.py, lint.py, verify.py,
tool.py.

  fix scope):** _construct_validation.py's context= check (lines 190-201)
  reads from the SAME flat 'producers' OrderedDict the inputs check uses —
  a false-arm node's context='some_true_arm_field' reference has the
  identical leak. The fix for the inputs-check accumulator must cover this
  read too, or the same defect survives under a different code path.

- **Structurally similar walk, but NOT a soundness defect (existence-only,
  not per-name availability):** lint.py's _has_resource_link_producer
  (line 231) and _check_resource_hydration answer 'does ANY agent/act
  producer of resource_links exist anywhere' -- a boolean OR across the
  whole construct including all arms. This is already documented as a
  static approximation (per-kind matching is 'not statically knowable' —
  see the docstring), so over-approximating across arms is consistent with
  its existing best-effort contract, not a regression to fix here.

  affected):** lint.py's DI/template-placeholder _walk (line 353) predicts

## Fix Applied (neograph-as3qd.7)

Implementation notes (deviations from the pre-implementation design, discovered during actual coding):

1. **iter_with_arm_ids** (_ir_branch.py): new sibling primitive to iter_with_arms, yields (item, arm_key) where arm_key is None (top-level) or (id(branch_meta), is_true_arm) for an arm item. iter_with_arms is now a thin wrapper delegating to it. Uses enumerate(construct.nodes) so it's invisible to test_guards_branch_arm_walks.py's raw-.nodes-walk AST detector -- the now-stale _ir_branch.py allowlist entry was removed (allowlist shrink, not growth).

2. **ArmScopedProducers** (NEW module src/neograph/_validation_arms.py, added as a 6th peer to VALIDATION_CLUSTER): encapsulates the arm-scoped producer bookkeeping. Required because the inline version pushed _construct_validation.py to 471 lines (over its 400-line TestValidationModuleBoundary cap) -- extracted as a proper module split (docs/file-split-procedure.md), not a workaround. tests/test_guards_assembly.py's VALIDATION_CLUSTER, private_modules (seam check), EXPECTED_LOCATIONS, and class docstring were all updated to register the new module -- the guard-first discipline applied to the split itself, not just the original fix.

3. **DESIGN CORRECTION during implementation -- the 'all-arms-produce, same field name' promotion is UNREACHABLE and was removed.** The original design (and architect review) assumed a should_pass fixture could exercise 'both arms register a producer under the SAME field_name, promoted for a post-join consumer'. Building that fixture failed at compile() with LangGraph's own 'Node  already present' -- two arm nodes can NEVER share a literal .name (add_node requires graph-wide unique names, verified directly, not inferred). Since field_name is a pure function of node name (field_name_for), 'same field_name in both arms' is only reachable via 'same node name in both arms', which is independently illegal. So the name-based promotion the ticket asked for is dead code in any construct that would also compile -- REMOVED from the design. Fan-in/context/Each/merge_fn consumers now see an arm-registered producer ONLY within that same arm, NEVER after the join, full stop -- simpler and still completely correct for the reported bug.

4. **The output-boundary check (MIGRATE site #4) needed separate, TYPE-based logic, not the name-based promotion.** Unlike the fan-in checks, sub-construct output= satisfaction is inherently type-only (no name matching), and TWO DIFFERENTLY-NAMED arm producers of a compatible type IS reachable/compilable (no name collision). Implemented as : true when some branch's every arm has >=1 producer type-compatible with construct.output. This is the correctly-scoped fix for site #4 (previously it silently accepted a construct where only ONE arm produced the declared output -- see test coverage below).

5. **New ConstructError variant** (_build_cross_arm_error, now in _validation_arms.py) for the specific 'known here, not reachable' case -- distinct wording from 'no upstream node named X exists' (which would be factually wrong), per the disease-scan's consistency-lens recommendation. Wired into both _check_fan_in_inputs (named inputs) and _check_each_path (Each.over root resolution) via an additive, diagnostics-only all_producers parameter -- zero change to existing pass/fail signatures.

## M1 -- justify the _llm_render.py budget bump in-plan (step 5)

_extract_context reads each field via read_upstream(..., expected_type=str, required=True), so the

the seam comment (step 3), the prompt.py docstring rewrite (step 6), and the mdx prose (step 7).

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-ebxdg`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).

     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.

       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   ```bash

   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

exists:

```bash

```

  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-ebxdg
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-ebxdg` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-ebxdg/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-ebxdg
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-ebxdg)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-ebxdg --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-ebxdg --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-ebxdg/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-ebxdg codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

Pattern category: 'a compiler-facing channel in _compile_prompt's all_kwargs that is unconditionally rendered with no raw/typed passthrough.'

Agent/act mode's ReAct cycle (_agent_cycle.py) reuses the same _inject_di_inputs + _compile_prompt (no second mechanism, per AGENTS.md), so the fix at the one seam covers think/agent/act uniformly -- no second instance to patch there.

- context: already has an analogous opt-out via each model's render_for_prompt() override -- a different mechanism (per-model, not per-seam), but functionally closes the same gap -- NOT an instance of the bug.
- di_inputs: the ONLY channel with no raw path -- this is the sole instance.

Conclusion: no other occurrence of this pattern exists in the codebase. This is a single, isolated gap, not a systemic disease -- confirmed by exhaustive enumeration of the 3-channel set, not sampling.

title: No raw/typed escape hatch for di_inputs (FromInput/FromConfig scalars unconditionally stringified)
description:
Since 0.7.5's rendering unification, every FromInput/FromConfig-resolved scalar
reaching a prompt compiler via di_inputs is rendered to text unconditionally:

    all_kwargs["di_inputs"] = to_prompt_input(di_inputs, renderer=runtime.renderer)

(src/neograph/_llm_render.py:227). There is no opt-out for this channel.

Confirmed via both compile_prompt() and a from-scratch minimal @node(mode="think")
run() dispatch (not just the test helper): a param declared
Annotated[int, FromInput] arrives at the compiler as the STRING "4822", not the
int 4822.

Contrast with input_data (peer/port dataflow values), which DOES have an escape
hatch: raw_inputs= gives a compiler the original unrendered objects when it needs
structure/type rather than ready-to-substitute text. context= has an analogous
opt-out via render_for_prompt(). di_inputs has no equivalent.

Impact (downstream, in ox-troubleshooting-demo): a compiler that uses a DI value
as a LOOKUP KEY for computed logic — not as a literal template value — silently
broke. Specifically, cascade.py's _window_note(deal_id) does
`isinstance(deal_id, int)` to decide whether to look up a seeded date window;
once deal_id arrived as "4822" the check failed silently, and the deal-window +
current-time banners vanished from every cascade prompt with no error. Fixed
downstream with an isdigit()-and-cast patch, but that doesn't generalize — a
future bool DI param stringifies to "True"/"False", a float to "4.2", a date to
something else again, each needing its own bespoke un-stringification.

Proposal: a raw_di_inputs= (or equivalent) compiler-declared channel, mirroring
raw_inputs='s existing shape, that hands back the real typed DI values alongside
(or instead of) the rendered di_inputs text — so a compiler that needs the typed
value for logic isn't forced to reverse-engineer it out of rendered text.

Filed from ox-troubleshooting-demo (sibling repo) after the 0.7.5 upgrade
surfaced this while removing hand-rolled hasattr/describe_value rendering
crutches in favor of render_inputs() — this is the one seam that upgrade
couldn't clean up without a framework-side primitive.
design:
## Root Cause
_llm_render.py's _compile_prompt has three input channels reaching a prompt_compiler: input_data, context, di_inputs. Two of the three (input_data via raw_inputs=, context via render_for_prompt()) can hand a compiler the real typed object when it needs structure/logic rather than literal template text. di_inputs cannot -- it is unconditionally rendered with to_prompt_input() and there is no raw_inputs=-shaped escape hatch for it, so a compiler that needs a DI scalar for a branch (isinstance(deal_id, int)) has no way to recover the type once it crosses the seam.

## Fix Approach
Mirror raw_inputs= exactly: add a raw_di_inputs channel to all_kwargs in _compile_prompt, built via to_raw_inputs(di_inputs) -- the SAME function raw_inputs itself already uses (it is generic over any Mapping, so di_inputs, being config[configurable][StateKeys.DI_INPUTS], needs no new renderer-layer code). Opt-in via the existing _accepted_params introspection gate (same mechanism raw_inputs/context/di_inputs already ride) -- no lint changes needed since raw_inputs never got a lint placeholder column (it is read directly by compiler logic, not resolved into {var} template slots). tests/test_guards_prompt_channels.py'\''s AST-derived offered/answered guard will pick up the new channel automatically and require either DefaultPromptCompiler to declare it or a KNOWN_IGNORED entry with reason (DefaultPromptCompiler renders everything itself, same reason raw_inputs has).
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_prompt_compiler.py::TestRawDiInputsEscapeHatch::test_raw_di_inputs_carries_the_typed_value_behind_the_rendered_text (plus a passing sibling test_compiler_that_does_not_declare_raw_di_inputs_does_not_receive_it, pinning the opt-in contract for when the fix lands)
- Root cause: _compile_prompt (src/neograph/_llm_render.py:225-227) reads di_inputs off config and unconditionally calls to_prompt_input(di_inputs, renderer=...) into all_kwargs['di_inputs'] with no companion raw channel -- unlike input_data, which gets both a rendered all_kwargs['input_data'\''] AND an opt-in all_kwargs['\''raw_inputs'\''] via to_raw_inputs(input_data) two lines above it.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-fqcm6)

Pattern: SYNTACTIC — an entry written into _compile_prompt's all_kwargs via to_prompt_input(...) with no companion raw_<channel> sibling in the same dict, denying a compiler the typed value behind the rendered text.
Scan command: grep -n 'all_kwargs\[' src/neograph/_llm_render.py (cross-checked against the dict-literal keys in the same function)
Total instances found: 2 (one is the bug being fixed; one is a genuine second instance, disposed separately)

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | src/neograph/_llm_render.py:227 | all_kwargs["di_inputs"] = to_prompt_input(di_inputs, ...) with no raw_di_inputs sibling | MIGRATE | This IS neograph-fqcm6 -- fixed in this molecule's implement atom |
| 2 | src/neograph/_llm_render.py:218 | all_kwargs["context"] = to_prompt_input(context, renderer=None) with no raw_context sibling | DEFER | neograph-ebxdg. context's claimed escape hatch (render_for_prompt() model override) only customizes rendered TEXT, never hands back the live object -- same disease under a different excuse. Out of fqcm6's reported scope (di_inputs specifically, from a real consumer); no reported consumer pain for context yet. Filed as its own P3 ticket rather than scope-creeping a third untested channel into this release. |

input_data's raw_inputs= (line 197/211) is the THIRD channel and already has its raw sibling -- not an instance, it's the pattern's origin/model to copy.
## Architect Review (neograph-mle81.5)

1. Root cause correctness — LOW. Confirmed by a failing test that reproduces the exact reported symptom (int DI param arrives stringified) and traced to one line (_llm_render.py:227) with no companion raw channel, unlike its two siblings.

2. Fix minimality — LOW. One new all_kwargs entry, reusing the existing to_raw_inputs() (already generic over any Mapping, zero new renderer code). No IR change, no new public type.

3. Regression risk — LOW. Purely additive and opt-in: gated by the same _accepted_params introspection raw_inputs/context/di_inputs already ride, so a compiler that does not declare raw_di_inputs never receives it (pinned by this molecule's second repro test). DefaultPromptCompiler does not declare it -> zero behavior change for every existing pipeline.

4. Architecture compliance — LOW. Matches the documented pattern exactly (AGENTS.md's di_inputs section already describes raw_inputs= as the sibling shape this channel lacks). The seam stays singular -- _llm_render.py's _compile_prompt -- no parallel implementation.

5. Similar-bug scalability — LOW, with one filed follow-up. trace-similar + codebase-scan exhaustively enumerated all 3 compiler-facing channels: di_inputs is the only unfixed instance; context has the same underlying gap under a different excuse (render_for_prompt() only customizes TEXT, never returns the live object) but is out of THIS bug's reported scope -- filed separately as neograph-ebxdg (P3), not blocking this fix.

6. Test coverage sufficiency — LOW, with 3 required additions the fix atom MUST include (not open design questions, just completing the shape already established for di_inputs itself):
   a. An agent/act-mode test mirroring TestDiInputReachesAgentModelEndToEnd (test_prompt_compiler.py:510) -- di_inputs itself has both a think-mode AND an agent-mode test since _agent_cycle.py's _turn_prep_kwargs is a separate call site into the same _compile_prompt seam; raw_di_inputs needs the same pairing for the same reason, not just the think-mode test written in reproduce.
   b. tests/test_guards_prompt_channels.py's AST-derived guard (TestSeamChannelsAreAnswered) will fail the moment raw_di_inputs is added to all_kwargs unless DefaultPromptCompiler declares it or KNOWN_IGNORED gets a new entry -- add the KNOWN_IGNORED entry (same reason raw_inputs has: DefaultPromptCompiler renders everything itself) rather than silence the guard by omission.
   c. Update the two doc claims that are now stale: AGENTS.md's di_inputs section ("unconditionally rendered with no raw escape hatch") and any website concept page making the same claim (website/src/content/docs/concepts/prompt-compiler.mdx per the earlier prompt-compiler-input-shape doc pass) -- a docs claim that is now false is worse than silence.

## Verdict: ALL_LOW -> proceed to fix. No open design questions; (6a)-(6c) are scope items for the fix atom to complete, not blockers requiring refinement or user input.
## Fix implemented (neograph-mle81.7)
- src/neograph/_llm_render.py: added all_kwargs['raw_di_inputs'] = to_raw_inputs(di_inputs) next to the existing raw_inputs line in _compile_prompt. Opt-in via the same _accepted_params introspection gate.
- tests/test_prompt_compiler.py::TestRawDiInputsEscapeHatch: 3 tests -- typed value reaches an opted-in compiler (think mode), opt-out compiler never receives it (closed signature), and the agent-cycle compiler receives it too (three-surface-across-modes parity, mirroring TestDiInputReachesAgentModelEndToEnd).
- tests/test_guards_prompt_channels.py: KNOWN_IGNORED entry for raw_di_inputs + added to the non-vacuity pin list. This AST-derived guard would otherwise fail the moment the channel was added, per its own design.
- tests/test_guards_llm_runtime.py: _llm_render.py line budget 445 -> 452, cited.
- AGENTS.md + website/src/content/docs/concepts/prompt-compiler.mdx: documented the new channel; removed the now-false 'di_inputs has no raw escape hatch' framing.
- Pre-req fix (separate commit, neograph-rod1j, already closed): examples/24_mcp_resources_from_resource.py was broken on main since 0.7.5, ported the same fix already proven on develop.

Gate: 3251 passed (baseline 3248 + 3 new), 0 failed, 2 skipped. ruff/mypy clean. Website builds (45 pages).
## Sweep Verification (neograph-mle81.8)

title: lint has no column for the context channel, so a resolvable {ctx} is reported unresolvable
