title: DefaultPromptCompiler swallows the context kwarg in **_kw, so a {context_var} stays literal in the compiled prompt
description:
Found by the consistency lens of the neograph-l2a7w disease scan (D15/I2).

_compile_prompt passes context= to the prompt compiler (introspection-gated like
di_inputs), but DefaultPromptCompiler.__call__ accepts it into **_kw and never
threads it into build_vars. Verified by the lens: a {ctx_ch} placeholder stays
LITERAL in the compiled output.

That is the exact failure mode neograph-hjwv existed to prevent — hjwv shipped
substitute(strict=True) so an unfilled placeholder fails loud instead of shipping
'{domain}' to a model. Here the var never enters the namespace at all, so with
strict=True it raises PromptVarMissing naming a var the user DID declare, and
with strict=False the literal ships. Either way the node's declared context
channel is dead in the framework's own 90%-case compiler.

Fix: thread context into build_vars as a layer (decide precedence vs di_inputs
and upstream outputs explicitly). Artifacts:
.claude/code-review/neograph-l2a7w/disease-consistency.md (D15, I2).
design:
## Root Cause
The seam OFFERS four channels; the framework's own compiler CONSUMES three.

_llm_render._compile_prompt builds all_kwargs with node_name, config, output_model,
llm_config, output_schema, raw_inputs, plus context (when the node declares it) and
di_inputs (when resolved), then filters by the compiler's declared parameters.
DefaultPromptCompiler.__call__ declares output_model, output_schema, di_inputs,
node_name — and **_kw. The introspection gate therefore PASSES context (a **kwargs
compiler accepts everything), and __call__ swallows it.

The gate cannot catch this: **_kw makes the compiler claim it accepts every channel.
Declaring a parameter is how a compiler opts IN, and **_kw opts in to everything
while implementing nothing.

## Fix Approach
1. DefaultPromptCompiler.__call__ declares context: dict[str, Any] | None = None and
   forwards it to build_vars; build_vars takes it as a LAYER.
2. Precedence, decided explicitly rather than discovered:
       di_inputs (base)  ->  context  ->  rendered input_data (top)
   Same rationale already written down for di_inputs vs outputs: the narrower,
   dataflow-derived binding wins. di_inputs is run-wide ambient; context is a
   node-declared supplement; input_data is the node's own dataflow. A collision can
   only happen when one node is named as BOTH an input and a context field, in which
   case the two carry the same value and only the rendering differs.
3. Do NOT touch what context IS (verbatim raw model vs rendered text). That is
   neograph-ufqr7 and it is a separate decision — see the note below.

## Scope boundary discovered during reproduction
tests/modes/test_llm_internals.py already PINS the current semantics: 'Verbatim — the
raw RawText, not BAML-rendered', asserting hasattr(ctx_val, 'text'). So the context
channel today carries RAW MODELS while _extract_context's signature says dict[str,str]
and casts to str. That contradiction is exactly ufqr7. This ticket only makes the
channel reach the template; ufqr7 decides what the channel carries.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing tests: tests/test_prompt_compiler.py::TestDefaultCompilerThreadsContext
    ::test_context_var_resolves_when_default_compiler_is_strict
    ::test_context_var_is_not_left_literal_when_default_compiler_is_lenient
- Root cause: DefaultPromptCompiler.__call__ accepts context= into **_kw and never
  forwards it to build_vars, so a declared context field never enters the template
  namespace at all.

Observed:
  strict=True  -> neograph.errors.PromptVarMissing: prompt variable 'brief' has no value
  strict=False -> the literal '{brief}' ships to the model
Both halves are tested, because they fail differently and only one of them is loud.

Test-design note: the first draft used the consumer's OWN upstream as the context
field and proved nothing — that name is already in the namespace via render_inputs,
so the template resolved through the input channel and the context channel was never
exercised. The context node is now deliberately NOT a parameter of the consumer.
## Trace-similar (atom irryo.12)

Pattern category: the compiler seam OFFERS a channel and a shipped consumer SWALLOWS it
in **kwargs, so the introspection gate — whose whole job is to pass only what a compiler
declares — cannot tell the difference. **_kw opts IN to every channel while implementing
none of them.

Population, enumerated from the seam itself (_llm_render.py:198-223 is the only site that
builds compiler kwargs; _llm_render.py:234 is the only call):

| Channel | DefaultPromptCompiler | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| node_name, output_model, output_schema, di_inputs | declared + used | fine |
| config, llm_config | swallowed | NOT the disease — not template-relevant; no user declaration is being ignored |
| raw_inputs | swallowed | NOT the disease — opt-IN by design (a compiler declares it to get the objects); the default compiler renders everything itself, so not declaring IS the correct opt-out |
| context | swallowed | **THE BUG** — the only swallowed channel the USER DECLARES on the node |

That is the discriminator worth keeping: ignoring a channel the COMPILER may opt into is
a choice; ignoring a channel the NODE AUTHOR declared is a defect. Population = 1.

Second sweep — other user-declared channels that must reach the template:
  - node inputs        -> reach via render_inputs                    OK
  - DI params          -> reach via di_inputs (neograph-l2a7w)       OK
  - context            -> THIS BUG
No others exist; Node declares no fourth template-bound channel.

Third sweep — does the fix cover every MODE? think/raw reach the compiler through
ThinkDispatch and agent/act through _agent_cycle.py:154, and BOTH hand context to the same
_compile_prompt. The fix is in the compiler, below that fork, so it covers all modes.

Blast radius — every build_vars OVERRIDER (adding a parameter to a public override hook):
  - examples/_shared.py::_ExamplePromptCompiler.build_vars — signature is
    (self, input_data, **kw) and it forwards **kw to super(). SURVIVES untouched.
  - website concepts/prompt-compiler.mdx:170 documents the override signature verbatim
    and MUST be updated in the same commit.
  - AGENTS.md:363 documents the build_vars precedence rule and MUST gain the context layer.
No new tickets filed: population 1, and the two doc sites are part of this fix.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-cbfd9)

Pattern: a SHIPPED implementation of a framework callback protocol that accepts **kwargs
and silently drops a channel the framework passes it — so the introspection gate, whose
job is to pass only what a compiler declares, is defeated by a signature that claims to
declare everything.

Shape: SYNTACTIC (a **kwargs catch-all in a shipped callback implementation). Single grep;
no fan-out, per the skill's own rule. No .claude/code-review/neograph-cbfd9/ — deliberate.

Scan commands (run in src/neograph):
  grep -rn 'class.*Protocol)' *.py                                    # the protocols
  grep -rn '^\s*\*\*[a-z_]*: Any|\(\*\*[a-z_]*\)' --include='*.py' .   # every catch-all
  grep -rn 'prompt_compiler(' *.py                                    # every seam call site
Total catch-alls found: 14. Real instances of the disease: 1.

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | prompt.py:257 DefaultPromptCompiler.__call__ | **_kw: Any | **MIGRATE** | THE BUG — declares 4 of the seam's channels, swallows context |
| 2 | _llm_protocols.py:31/62/83 (LlmFactory, PromptCompiler, CostCallback) | *args/**kwargs in a Protocol | ALLOWLIST | PROTOCOL DECLARATIONS, not implementations. The catch-all is load-bearing: it is what lets the Simple callback shape (tier) -> model satisfy the Protocol structurally. Removing it would break the documented two-shape contract |
| 3 | _compiled.py (12 sites) | *args/**kwargs | NOT INSTANCES | transparent pass-throughs to the wrapped LangGraph object — they forward everything and drop nothing |
| 4 | di.py:449, _fan_agent_wrap.py:220, _llm_config.py:113, loader.py:266, forward.py:1279, construct.py:153, node.py:269 | **kwargs at a CALL site | NOT INSTANCES | argument expansion, not a signature catch-all |
| 5 | _agent_cycle.py:177/199, _llm.py:197 | **kwargs at a call site | NOT INSTANCES | same; _llm.py:197 is in fact the OPPOSITE pattern — it filters by introspection before calling, which is the discipline this bug violates |

No DEFER rows, so no follow-up tickets are owed.

## Guard the fix must add (≥1 MIGRATE row, so it is required)
Assert that EVERY channel _compile_prompt puts into all_kwargs is either declared as a
parameter of DefaultPromptCompiler.__call__ or listed in a KNOWN_IGNORED map with a
written reason. Derived by AST from the seam itself, NOT from a hand-copied channel list —
so adding a channel to the seam and forgetting the shipped compiler fails CI, which is
exactly how context slipped through.
## Architect review (atom irryo.14) — verdict NEEDS_REFINEMENT

**R1 root cause — LOW.** Reproduced both halves (strict crash, lenient literal). The
introspection gate is not at fault: **_kw makes the compiler claim every channel.

**R2 minimality — LOW.** One parameter on __call__, one layer in build_vars, one guard.
No seam change: _compile_prompt already offers context correctly.

**R3 regression risk — LOW.** A template naming a context field previously CRASHED
(strict) or shipped a literal (lenient); both are strictly improved. Overriders survive:
the repo's own _ExamplePromptCompiler.build_vars forwards **kw to super().

**R4 architecture — LOW, one decision to record.** Precedence
di_inputs -> context -> rendered input_data reuses the rationale already written in
AGENTS.md for di_inputs: the narrower, dataflow-derived binding wins. NOTE for a future
ticket, not this one: when one node is named BOTH as an input and as a context field the
two channels carry the same value under one name, and neograph's fail-loud instinct would
say reject that at assembly rather than silently pick. Out of scope here.

**R5 similar-bug scalability — LOW.** Guard derives the channel list by AST from
_compile_prompt itself, so it scales to channels that do not exist yet.

**R6 test coverage — MEDIUM. The fix ships a channel that renders as a Pydantic repr.**
Context values are raw MODELS today (pinned by test_llm_internals: 'Verbatim — the raw
RawText, not BAML-rendered'), and substitute() does str(vars[name]). So after this fix
'{brief}' resolves to "items=['ship it']" — the Pydantic repr — not to clean text. That is
still strictly better than a crash or a literal placeholder, and making it TEXT is exactly
neograph-ufqr7, the next ticket on this branch. But it must not be left implicit:
  REFINEMENT (a) the reproduction must assert the ACTUAL observable, not a substring that
    happens to survive inside a repr — otherwise the test passes for the wrong reason and
    will not notice when ufqr7 changes the shape.
  REFINEMENT (b) say so in the docstring, naming ufqr7, so the interim shape is a recorded
    decision rather than an accident someone else has to rediscover.
  REFINEMENT (c) add an agent-mode case. The trace-similar ARGUES all modes are covered
    because the fix sits below the think/agent fork; a test PROVES it, and the cost is one
    node declaration.

Verdict: NEEDS_REFINEMENT (no HIGH; no user input needed).
## Fix applied (atom irryo.16)

DefaultPromptCompiler.__call__ declares context= and forwards it; build_vars lays it as
a layer between di_inputs (base) and rendered input_data (top). Guard:
tests/test_guards_prompt_channels.py.

All three review refinements applied:
(a) the lenient test now pins the SHAPE, not just a substring: it asserts "text='ship it'",
    the Pydantic repr that actually reaches the model. A bare 'ship it' assertion passes
    under both the current raw-model contract and the rendered one ufqr7 will introduce,
    so it would not have noticed the change. That assertion is SUPPOSED to break when
    ufqr7 lands, and says so in-place.
(b) build_vars' docstring records the interim raw-model shape and names ufqr7.
(c) agent-mode test added — and it EARNED its place: it was red before the fix, so the
    'the fix sits below the mode fork' reasoning is now evidence rather than argument.

### The guard
tests/test_guards_prompt_channels.py derives BOTH sides by AST: the offered channels from
_compile_prompt's own all_kwargs (dict literal + subscript assignments), the answered ones
from DefaultPromptCompiler.__call__'s parameters. KNOWN_IGNORED is a map to a REASON, not
a set — 'the default compiler does not need this' is a claim someone has to type out.
Mutation-verified: undeclaring context makes it fail. Plus three meta-tests — the seam scan
finds the real channels (non-vacuity), no KNOWN_IGNORED entry names a channel the seam no
longer offers (staleness), and every entry carries a reason.

### Two test-harness defects found while writing the reproduction
1. First draft used the consumer's OWN upstream as the context field. That name is already
   in the namespace via render_inputs, so the template resolved through the input channel
   and the context channel was never exercised at all.
2. The think-mode recorder subclassed StructuredFake — whose with_structured_output returns
   a NEW StructuredFake, not self, so the override was discarded before invoke and the
   recorder captured nothing. The test failed on an empty transcript, i.e. red for the
   wrong reason. Replaced with the self-returning idiom the suite's other capture fakes use.
Both are recorded in-test so the next author does not repeat them.

### Docs updated in the same commit (blast radius from trace-similar)
- website concepts/prompt-compiler.mdx: override signature + the layering rule + the advice
  to write overrides as (self, input_data, **kw) and forward. Website builds, 45 pages.
- AGENTS.md: build_vars precedence now names the context layer and the new guard.

Gate: 3129 passed / 0 failed (baseline 3114), mypy clean 82 files, ruff clean.
## Sweep Verification (atom irryo.17)

Re-scan command: identical to the codebase-scan atom.
Pre-fix real instances: 1.  Post-fix real instances: 0.

| # | Phase 1b site | Disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | prompt.py DefaultPromptCompiler.__call__ | MIGRATE | context now DECLARED and forwarded; **_kw REMAINS at prompt.py:275 | yes |
| 2 | _llm_protocols.py Protocol declarations | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | yes |
| 3 | _compiled.py pass-throughs | NOT INSTANCES | unchanged | yes |
| 4-5 | call-site **kwargs expansions | NOT INSTANCES | unchanged | yes |

Note on row 1: **_kw stays, and that is deliberate rather than a half-migration. It is what
keeps the compiler forward-compatible with a seam that grows a channel it does not consume.
What made **_kw dangerous was that it was the ONLY thing standing between an offered channel
and silence — nothing related the two sets. The guard now does, so the catch-all is back to
being a compatibility affordance instead of a silent drop.

## Structural guard: tests/test_guards_prompt_channels.py
- In tests/test_guards_*.py                                          yes
- AST on both sides; neither list is hand-copied from the other      yes
- Mutation-verified: undeclaring context fails it                    yes

  KNOWN_IGNORED entry for a channel the seam no longer offers), and every exemption

title: Oracle merge upstream context skips the Each/Loop unwrapping that the fan-in reader applies to the same keys
description:
Found by the consistency lens of the neograph-l2a7w disease scan (D10).

_oracle._build_upstream_context reads the SAME node.inputs keys from the SAME
state bus as _input_shape._extract_fan_in_dict, but without _unwrap_loop_value /
_unwrap_each_dict (di.py). So an Each-produced upstream declared as list[X]
arrives correctly unwrapped on the think path and RAW (dict-shaped) in the merge
prompt's upstream context.

This is a second divergence on the merge path, independent of the rendering one
neograph-l2a7w fixes: rendering makes the value TEXT, but the value being
rendered is already the wrong shape. Fixing l2a7w alone will render the wrong
thing consistently.

Scope: read both readers side by side and make the merge path reuse the fan-in
reader's unwrapping rather than re-deriving a second read. Artifacts:
.claude/code-review/neograph-l2a7w/disease-consistency.md (D10).
design:
## Root Cause
TWO readers of the same state keys, only one of which knows the unwrapping rule.

_input_shape._extract_fan_in_dict walks node.inputs and per key does
    value = state.get_required(field_name_for(input_name))
    value = _unwrap_loop_value(value, expected_type)
    value = _unwrap_each_dict(value, expected_type)
_oracle._build_upstream_context walks the SAME node.inputs and does
    val = bus.get(field_name_for(key))            # no unwrapping
Its docstring calls itself 'the SINGLE source of the upstream-context rule' — true of
its SIBLING (the Each x Oracle fused merge) and beside the point: two paths agreeing
with each other is not one rule. It also has no fan_out_param arm.

Third recorded instance of the pattern AGENTS.md already names (effective_producer_type;
the ModifierCombo retrospective): a rule re-derived per consumer instead of read once.

## Fix Approach  (REFINED by atom irryo.31 after the review's NEEDS_REFINEMENT)

The first draft said 'extract the read+unwrap and have both call it'. That does not
survive contact: the two readers differ in required-ness (get_required, fail loud, vs
get, best-effort skip). Refined per review option (b):

1. ONE reader in _input_shape.py — the module that already declares itself the home of
   read-side shaping for both node-body executors:
       read_upstream(bus, key, expected_type, *, required, node_label) -> Any
   Body = field_name_for -> get/get_required -> _unwrap_loop_value -> _unwrap_each_dict.
   required= is the ONE honest difference between the call sites; parameterising it is
   not a fake unification, it is the actual variation.
2. _extract_fan_in_dict calls it with required=True. Its fan_out_param arm STAYS in the
   caller: EACH_ITEM is not a peer field at all, so pushing it down would widen the
   helper to serve exactly one caller.
3. _build_upstream_context calls it with required=False and keeps its own None-skip.
4. STRUCTURAL GUARD, written failing-first (AGENTS.md makes this mandatory for a new
   single-source-of-truth, not optional): no field_name_for(...) composed into a bus
   read outside _input_shape.py. Allowlist exactly one site — _subconstruct.py:145 —
   with its reason recorded (it FORWARDS parent state into a sub-graph under the same
   field name; the sub-node's own read consumes it, so unwrapping there would pre-empt
   and double-apply the inner reader).
5. TESTS: the Each case is the existing repro. Add the LOOP case — the fix restores both
   unwraps and the loop arm would otherwise ship unproven.

REJECTED: copying the two _unwrap_* calls into _oracle.py. Three sites agreeing today
is the same disease with a wider blast radius.

## Known, intended behaviour change
A Loop-modified upstream feeding a merge prompt currently renders its whole append-list;
after the fix it renders the latest value. That is the point, but it is an output change
— the sweep atom runs the FULL suite, not just the oracle file.
notes:

- Failing test: tests/modifiers/test_oracle.py::TestMergePromptUpstreamContext::test_merge_context_matches_the_node_prompt_for_an_each_upstream
- Root cause: _oracle._build_upstream_context re-derives the upstream read (bus.get(field_name_for(key))) instead of reusing the fan-in reader, so it skips the _unwrap_loop_value/_unwrap_each_dict pair _input_shape._extract_fan_in_dict applies to the same key on the same bus.

  merge prompt (_build_upstream_context): { alpha: { ... } }             <- raw Each dict
Each's internal map_key leaks into an LLM prompt as if it were data the author asked for.

rendering literal. The invariant is that the two agree; an equality cannot be
satisfied by teaching one channel a second private shape, which is the failure
mode a literal-match test would have allowed.

there instead of opening a duplicate. This makes 13k4i and ufqr7 ONE design question —
who reads an upstream field, and does every reader get the same rule — so the helper
that fixes 13k4i should be the one ufqr7 adopts.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-13k4i)

Pattern: a consumer that reads a PEER node's output field off the state bus by
re-deriving field_name_for(...) + get/get_required, instead of calling the one
read-side reader — and so silently drops the unwrapping rule that reader applies.

Shape: SYNTACTIC (one regex-able form: field_name_for composed into a bus read).
Per the skill's own rule a single grep is sufficient and fanning out is wrong, so
NO multi-agent scan was run and no .claude/code-review/neograph-13k4i/ exists —
deliberate, not skipped. (Contrast neograph-l2a7w, which WAS semantic — 'the render
rule re-implemented under three different names' — and did earn the 4-lens fan-out.)

Scan command (run in src/neograph, both forms — the inline one and the
assign-then-read one the inline regex cannot see):
  grep -rn '\(get\|get_required\)(.*field_name_for(' *.py
  grep -rn -B1 '\(state\|bus\)\.\(get\|get_required\)(\(state_key\|field_name\|field\|own_field\|ctx_field\|dep_field\|node_own_field\)' *.py

Total instances found: 9 candidate reads (1 regex false positive, 8 real).

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | _input_shape.py:114 (_extract_fan_in_dict) | read + loop-unwrap + each-unwrap | KEEP — THE reader | the rule everything else must match |
| 2 | _input_shape.py:125 (_extract_single_type) | read + both unwraps | KEEP | already correct |
| 3 | _input_shape.py:78 (_extract_loop_reentry) | read + loop-unwrap | KEEP | each-dict cannot reach this shape |
| 4 | _oracle.py:239 (_build_upstream_context) | read, NO unwrap | **MIGRATE** | THE BUG. Also missing a fan_out_param arm |
| 5 | _input_shape.py:167 (_extract_context) | read, NO unwrap, cast(str) | **MIGRATE (neograph-ufqr7)** | same disease, same file as #1, 50 lines apart |
| 6 | _subconstruct.py:100 + :105 | self-field read + _unwrap_loop_value(object) | NOT AN INSTANCE | loop-routing self-read that DOES unwrap |
| 7 | _wiring.py:602 + :603 | self-field read + _unwrap_loop_value(object) | NOT AN INSTANCE | same; twin of #6 |
| 8 | _subconstruct.py:145 | ctx_field read, raw, copied into sub_input | ALLOWLIST | FORWARDING, not consumption — copies parent state into the sub-graph under the same field name; the sub-node's own _extract_context does the consuming read. Unwrapping here would pre-empt the inner reader and double-apply |
| 9 | _construct_builder.py:223 | decorated.get(field_name_for(...)) | NOT AN INSTANCE | plain lookup in a local dict at assembly time; no state bus |

No DEFER rows, so no follow-up tickets are owed by this scan.

Consequence for the fix: exactly TWO sites migrate (#4, #5), they are the two open
bugs 13k4i and ufqr7, and they must migrate onto the SAME extracted helper. #8 is the
one place raw is right, and the reason is stated so a future sweep does not 'fix' it.
## Architect review (atom irryo.5) — verdict NEEDS_REFINEMENT

Reviewed adversarially against the six criteria. One MEDIUM finding invalidates the
Fix Approach as written; the root cause itself survives.

**R1 root-cause correctness — LOW.** Reproduced and diffed the two readers directly;
the equality test fails on shape, not on rendering, so it cannot be a mis-diagnosis of
the l2a7w rendering bug. Confirmed.

**R2 fix minimality — MEDIUM. The stated approach does not survive contact.**
'Extract the per-key read+unwrap from _extract_fan_in_dict and have both call it'
assumes the two readers want the same read. They do not:
  _extract_fan_in_dict  -> state.get_required(...)  fail loud; a missing fan-in
                           upstream is a wiring bug the validator promised cannot happen
  _build_upstream_context -> bus.get(...)           best-effort; absent/None is SKIPPED,
                           because merge context is decoration, not the payload
Forcing one function makes required-ness a parameter. Two options, and the choice must
be explicit rather than discovered during implementation:
  (a) share the UNWRAP PAIR only — helper takes (value, expected_type), lives beside the
      two unwraps in di.py. Smallest, but leaves TWO sites each remembering to call it,
      which is a weaker ratchet than one reader.
  (b) share the READ — read_upstream(bus, key, expected_type, *, required, node_label).
      required= is honest: it is the ONE real difference between the two call sites.
REFINEMENT: take (b), because the disease is 'a second reader exists', not 'an unwrap was
forgotten' — (a) fixes today's symptom and leaves the shape that regrows it. The
fan_out_param arm stays in _extract_fan_in_dict: it is genuinely the fan-in reader's own
concern (EACH_ITEM is not a peer field at all), and pushing it down would widen the helper
to serve one caller.

**R3 regression risk — MEDIUM, bounded and intended.** For a LOOP-modified upstream feeding
a merge prompt, today's whole append-list becomes the latest value. That is the fix, but it
IS an output change for any existing pipeline in that shape. Existing merge-context tests
use single-type upstreams and are unaffected. The sweep atom must run the full suite, not
just the oracle file.

**R4 architecture compliance — LOW, with a required addition.** _input_shape.py already
declares itself the home of read-side input shaping for BOTH node-body executors
(_extract_context's docstring says so), and _oracle -> _input_shape introduces no cycle
(_input_shape imports only _normalize/_state_bus/_state_keys/di/modifiers/naming/node).
MISSING from the approach: nothing stops a FOURTH reader. Per AGENTS.md's own rule for a
new single-source-of-truth ('a structural guard enumerating every real consumer is
mandatory before the change is considered done'), the fix owes an AST guard — no
field_name_for(...) composed into a bus read outside _input_shape.py, with the ONE
forwarding site (_subconstruct:145) allowlisted with its reason. Written failing-first.

**R5 similar-bug scalability — LOW.** Same helper serves neograph-ufqr7's context read
(expected_type str: loop-unwrap fires, each-unwrap no-ops). The scan proved the population
is exactly two migrations, so the helper is not speculative generality.

**R6 test coverage — MEDIUM.** The repro covers the EACH unwrap only. The fix restores
BOTH, so the LOOP arm would ship unproven. Add a Loop-upstream-into-merge-prompt case.

Verdict: NEEDS_REFINEMENT (no HIGH, no user input needed) — refine the Fix Approach to
option (b), add the structural guard, add the Loop test.
## Fix applied (atom irryo.7)

di.read_upstream(state, key, expected_type, *, required, node_label) — the one reader.
Migrated onto it: _extract_fan_in_dict (required=True), _extract_loop_reentry
(required=False), _oracle._build_upstream_context (required=False, keeps its own
None-skip). Guard: tests/test_guards_upstream_read.py, written failing-first (it named
5 offenders before the fix; 0 after).

### THREE things the process caught that the plan did not

1. **The helper could not live where the plan said.** _input_shape was the obvious home
   and both repo ratchets refused it: the assembly-cluster import DAG declares _oracle
   and _input_shape LEAVES (no upward edges), and a cohesion guard reserves

3. **The first version of the reproduction was NOT proof.** Asserted purely as an

   wrong TOGETHER once they share one reader. Mutation run: deleting both unwraps inside
   read_upstream left all 6 tests GREEN. Both tests now carry a positive anchor on the

title: Tool results are rendered by a THIRD parallel implementation of the rendering rule: render_for_prompt() ignored, dict[str,BaseModel] ships Python repr to the model
description:
Found by the trace-similar atom (neograph-ysff2.3) while triaging neograph-l2a7w.
Same disease, different channel: a rendering rule re-implemented at a call site
instead of being read from one place, silently diverging from the others.

WHERE
src/neograph/_tool_loop.py:50 `_render_tool_result_for_llm`, the only renderer of
a typed tool result into the ToolMessage content the model reads (called from
_agent_cycle.py:459).

TWO CONFIRMED DEVIATIONS (measured, not inferred)

1. `render_for_prompt()` is IGNORED.
   A tool returning a model that defines a presenter:
     _render_tool_result_for_llm(T(label='a'))
     -> 'Tool result:\n{\n  label: "a"\n}'      (BAML)
   The SAME model as a node input renders to 'PRESENTER'. So a user's presenter
   governs the model's input but not the model's tool results — the identical
   asymmetry neograph-l2a7w documents between the inline and template-ref
   channels (_llm_render._resolve_var also skips the presenter check).

2. `dict[str, BaseModel]` falls through to `str(result)` — Python repr.
     _render_tool_result_for_llm({'k': T(label='a')})
     -> "{'k': T(label='a')}"
   The input path folds exactly this shape via renderers._render_model_dict into
   describe_value blocks (it is the shape an Each fan-out produces). A tool
   returning a keyed bag of models therefore ships Pydantic repr to the LLM.

WHY IT IS THE SAME BUG
neograph-l2a7w's root cause is "the render decision is made per call site rather
than once". `_render_tool_result_for_llm` is the THIRD such site (after
renderers._render_single and _llm_render._resolve_var), and it differs from both
in a different way each time:
  - _render_single:  honors presenter, does NOT coerce primitives
  - _resolve_var:    coerces primitives, does NOT honor presenter
  - _render_tool_result_for_llm: honors an explicit renderer=, does NOT honor the
    presenter, does NOT fold dict[str,BaseModel], DOES coerce via str()
Three implementations of one rule, pairwise inconsistent.

RELATION TO neograph-l2a7w
l2a7w's agreed design (docs/design/prompt-compiler-input-shape-2026-08-11.md,
section 4.2) collapses _render_single and _resolve_var into ONE rendering
function. This channel was not in that design's scope. The fix for l2a7w MUST
write that shared function so this path can adopt it (not a private helper buried
in the compiler seam) — then this ticket is a small follow-on rather than a
fourth re-implementation.

DECISION NEEDED: fold into l2a7w's fix (one rule really means all four channels)
or land separately after it. Behaviour change either way: tool results begin
honoring presenters and folding model dicts.
close_reason: Fixed by neograph-l2a7w: _render_tool_result_for_llm now delegates to the one ladder (renderers.to_rendered) with prefix='Tool result:'. Presenter honored, None -> '', dict[str,BaseModel] folded. Verified before/after.

fix is designed, so the fix addresses every instance — not just the
motivating site.

introduces (or codifies) a helper for.

   Write a one-line spec — see task-execute.yaml::codebase-scan for

   manifests). Choose the method by disease shape:

     disease-scoped lenses + optional opus), which writes per-lens

title: Portal: a dispatch-mode Portal at mesh level hijacks the peer mesh's handoff channel key
description:
Found by neograph-wvp7j's architect review (2026-08-11) as an OUT-OF-SCOPE observation it explicitly declined to trace ('I read only these two sites and did not trace it to a failing case'). The orchestrator REPRODUCED it -- it is real, and the effect is larger than the review suspected.

THE ASYMMETRY (both sites verified in-tree):
  src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py:277   collects members with  item.modifier_set.portal is not None
  src/neograph/_validation_portal.py:65 filters members with portal_member_class(item) not in (None, DISPATCH)
A dispatch-mode Portal (route='decide') is NOT a mesh member -- it is a standalone linear node -- and the validator correctly excludes it. _ir_normalize does not, so it can land in the collected list and, being first in node order, become members[0]. The mesh channel is keyed off members[0].name.

REPRODUCTION (run, not reasoned):
  disp = Node.scripted('planner', ...) | Portal(route='decide', spec_field='spec',
                                                input_field='dispatch_input', output=Handoff, max_depth=2)
  m1   = Node.scripted('triage',  ...) | Portal(to=['billing'], max_hops=5)
  m2   = Node.scripted('billing', ...) | Portal(to=['triage'])
  normalize_ir(Construct('asym', nodes=[disp, m1, m2]))
    planner: handoff_channel=neo_handoff_planner
    triage:  handoff_channel=neo_handoff_planner     <-- WRONG
    billing: handoff_channel=neo_handoff_planner     <-- WRONG
CONTROL, same mesh without the dispatch node:
  normalize_ir(Construct('control', nodes=[m1, m2]))
    triage:  handoff_channel=neo_handoff_triage
    billing: handoff_channel=neo_handoff_triage
So the dispatch node does not merely shift the entry -- it takes over the channel key for the entire peer mesh, and is itself given a mesh channel it has no use for.

WHY IT IS SILENT: the validator ran its checks against a DIFFERENT member list (the correct one), so assembly validation passes. The mesh then wires against a channel keyed off a non-member. Nothing raises.

SEVERITY: unproven at runtime. The reproduction is at the IR-normalization layer; whether a compiled+run mesh actually misroutes (or whether the shared key happens to still work because every member agrees on the same wrong key) was NOT traced. Do that first -- it decides whether this is a latent naming defect or a live routing bug.

FIX DIRECTION: _ir_normalize's collection must use the same authority as the validator -- portal_member_class(item) not in (None, DISPATCH) -- so 'what is a mesh member' has ONE definition. That is the same single-source discipline neograph-dgbqv.3 established for PortalMemberClass, and this site is a consumer that was missed: tests/test_guards_portal_member_class_consumers.py declares _ir_normalize.py, so the guard already believes this file routes through the classifier for member-class questions. It does for some, not for this one.
acceptance_criteria: _ir_normalize collects mesh members through portal_member_class, matching _validation_portal exactly. A dispatch Portal at mesh level leaves the peer mesh's handoff channel keyed off the real entry. Regression test uses the reproduction above, asserting the control and the with-dispatch cases produce the SAME channel key for triage/billing.
notes:
## Reproduce (bug-triage) -- ESCALATED: this is a LIVE bug, not latent

The ticket left severity open ('whether a compiled+run mesh actually misroutes was NOT traced
-- do that first'). Traced. It misroutes.

THE WRITE AND THE READ USE DIFFERENT KEYS:
  _wiring.py:198 SKIPS dispatch members explicitly
      (if portal_member_class(item) is PortalMemberClass.DISPATCH: ...)
    -> _group_portal_members -> MeshContext.build(members)[0] == 'triage'
    -> ctx.channel_key = neo_handoff_triage          <- what the runtime WRITES
  _ir_normalize.py:277 does NOT skip dispatch (portal is not None)
    -> members[0] == 'planner' -> node.handoff_channel = neo_handoff_planner
    -> _input_shape.py:123 does state.get(node.handoff_channel)   <- what members READ

Measured on the ticket's repro construct:
  IR stamped (read key)   : planner/triage/billing ALL -> neo_handoff_planner
  MeshContext (write key) : neo_handoff_triage
  MISMATCH: True

So every mesh member reads a state key the runtime never writes. The handoff payload is
delivered to neo_handoff_triage and read from neo_handoff_planner -> the member sees None.
Nothing raises: _input_shape's read is a state.get, and the validator already passed because
it computed the CORRECT member list independently.

SEVERITY: raise from 'unproven' to LIVE. The exact user-visible symptom (does the member get
None and fail its input shape, or silently proceed on a default?) still needs one run to pin
down, and that is what the failing regression test should assert.

FIX CONFIRMED as the ticket's direction, and now with a third witness: _wiring ALREADY uses
portal_member_class to skip DISPATCH, and _validation_portal already does. _ir_normalize is
the ONLY one of the three that does not. It is a one-line change to the same authority, not a
design question -- which also means the guard inventory
(tests/test_guards_portal_member_class_consumers.py) lists _ir_normalize.py as a declared
consumer while this particular site bypasses the classifier.
## Fix + trace-similar + sweep (2izkd.3, .4, .7, .8)

FIX: _ir_normalize now asks portal_member_class at BOTH sites, matching _wiring and
_validation_portal. TWO sites, not one -- the ticket named only the collection:
  :277  member COLLECTION   (decides members[0], hence the channel KEY)
  :319  channel STAMPING    (decides WHO carries a channel)
Fixing only the first left the dispatch node still stamped with the mesh channel, which
_input_shape would have read -- feeding a standalone dispatch node a payload addressed to the
mesh. Found because the third regression test failed after the 'one-line fix' was applied;
had the test only checked the two real members, this would have shipped.

TRACE-SIMILAR (2izkd.3): swept 'modifier_set.portal is not None' across src. After the fix
exactly ONE hit remains and it is PROSE -- _validation_portal's _member_portal docstring
claimed 'members are collected by node.modifier_set.portal is not None', which is not what
that module does (it uses the classifier at :65). Corrected: a docstring describing the loose
rule is how this bug gets reintroduced. Zero live loose member tests remain.

A CLAIM I MADE IN THIS TICKET WAS WRONG, corrected here: the description says the consumer
guard 'lists _ir_normalize.py as a declared consumer while this particular site bypasses the
classifier'. It did NOT list it -- before this fix _ir_normalize never called the classifier
at all, so it was not a consumer and correctly absent. The guard caught the file as UNDECLARED
the moment the fix made it one, and it is now declared with the reason. The guard was right and
my read of it was wrong.

MYPY: the classifier check cannot narrow Portal | None, so the stamping site binds
member_portal first. The redundant 'is not None' is documented in-line as a NARROWING aid, not
a second membership test -- otherwise the next reader sees two member tests and 'simplifies'
one away.

REGRESSION TEST tests/test_portal_dispatch_mesh_channel.py, 3 tests, all RED before / GREEN
after:
  * control vs with-dispatch produce the SAME channel for triage/billing
  * the stamped READ key equals the runtime WRITE key (the bug's actual bite)
  * a dispatch Portal carries NO mesh channel at all
The second is the one that pins the defect class rather than the symptom: it compares what
_ir_normalize stamps against what MeshContext/_wiring would write, so any future divergence
between the two member filters fails here regardless of how it arises.

   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-wvp7j`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-wvp7j)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-wvp7j --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):

     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

description:

a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:

   ```

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:

     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched

   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff

   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).

     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   ```bash

   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-dgbqv.10 sweep:complete
```

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.

  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-dgbqv.9
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-dgbqv.9
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-dgbqv.9`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-dgbqv.9)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-dgbqv.9 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-dgbqv.9 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-dgbqv.9
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-dgbqv.9` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-dgbqv.9/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-dgbqv.9
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-dgbqv.9)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-dgbqv.9 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-dgbqv.9 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-dgbqv.9/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-dgbqv.9 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-dgbqv.9/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Agent Spec export: outermost Construct's EndNode has no DataFlowEdge feeding its outputs -- standalone exported Flows never surface a result
description:
Found during dgbqv.2's implementation (neograph-jn555.31, 2026-08-06) while building the COMPARE tier. src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:604-622's own comment explains the design: 'an unconsumed StartNode input / unfed EndNode output is legal -- the payload flows through the item's own peer edges' -- this is TRUE when the Construct is used as a sub-flow item (a FlowNode wrapping it infers input/output from the boundary nodes, and the PARENT wires the actual value flow via peer edges), but FALSE when the Construct is exported and run STANDALONE (not as anyone's sub-flow item): there is no parent to wire a peer edge, so the EndNode's declared outputs (even when construct.output IS set) have zero DataFlowEdge feeding them, and pyagentspec's AgentSpecLoader either (a) returns an empty outputs dict when construct.output is None (end_props never computed), or (b) raises 'Expected node <end> to have a value for property <X>' when construct.output IS set but no DataFlowEdge feeds it.

CONSEQUENCE: a third-party Agent Spec runtime invoking a standalone exported Flow directly (the exact scenario the differential-execution grid's COMPARE tier needs) can NEVER surface neograph's own computed result, for ANY cell shape -- this is not scoped to think/agent/act mode or Each/Loop/Operator combos like qtfof.6/.7/.8; it is a universal property of every outermost Construct export. Confirmed empirically: scripted-bare-single (the simplest possible cell -- two ToolNodes, no modifiers) exhibits it.

FIX DIRECTION (not yet designed): the outermost Construct's export needs a DataFlowEdge from the terminal producer node(s) into the EndNode when construct.output is declared -- i.e. an outermost Construct should be treated as implicitly having output=<terminal node's type> if not otherwise declared, and that boundary should get the SAME peer-edge wiring a sub-flow item's parent would provide, applied to the EndNode itself. Needs its own design pass; touches the same _lower_node / edge-wiring machinery qtfof.6/.7 touch, so coordinate line-number citations against current HEAD, not this ticket's.

Relevant to the project's stated full-interop design goal (see neograph-dgbqv.2's Design Decision note): 'the agentspec should be 100% the same in execution as in neograph itself' cannot hold if the third party can never read the result at all.
close_reason: Duplicate of neograph-qtfof.9 (same root cause: outermost Construct's EndNode has no declared/wired outputs for a third-party runtime to read). qtfof.9 was filed first (during dgbqv.2's implementation, before the orchestrator took over from a stalled agent) and has the more rigorous root-cause analysis (cites the exact pyagentspec SDK source). Complementary detail merged into qtfof.9's notes.

title: Refine dgbqv.2 per review (pivot to AgentSpecLoader)
description:
Architect review (neograph-jn555.28) returned NEEDS_USER_INPUT: the plan was hand-rolling a mini-executor when the pinned pyagentspec dependency already ships pyagentspec.adapters.langgraph.AgentSpecLoader with the same injection seams. User decision (2026-08-06): PIVOT to AgentSpecLoader as the EXECUTE tier. Full review text and the user-clarification note (how tool_registry substitutes for a neograph import) are in neograph-dgbqv.2's notes.

Rewrite dgbqv.2's Core Invariant + Implementation Plan around this pivot:

## Core Invariant (must be rewritten)
The current Core Invariant ("the mini-executor is a second, independent implementation... derived from the exported Flow alone") now CONTRADICTS the metadata-aware Design Decision AND the AgentSpecLoader pivot. New invariant should state something like: the EXECUTE tier runs the exported Flow through a genuinely third-party, independently-authored runtime (pyagentspec.adapters.langgraph.AgentSpecLoader) rather than code neograph's own team writes and could get wrong in the same way twice -- independence comes from authorship, not from hand-rolling.

## Implementation Plan (must be rewritten to use AgentSpecLoader)
1. EXECUTE tier: for each GREEN cell, export the Construct (already exists via WIRE tier dgbqv.1), then `AgentSpecLoader(tool_registry=<per-cell registry>, checkpointer=<matching neograph's checkpointer usage>).load_dict(flow.to_dict())` to build a LangGraph graph independently, then `.invoke(...)`.
2. tool_registry construction: map each exported node/tool name to a callable. For scripted cells, reuse the SAME scripted-fn dict `build_cell` already provides (test_agent_spec_matrix.py). For LLM-mode cells, reuse the SAME `configure_fake_llm`/`StructuredFake`/`ReActFake` fakes already wired via `_llm_kwargs`. Do NOT invent a second fake-wiring mechanism.
3. FIX the Oracle node-name mismatch (review finding): "keyed by node name == compile()'s scripted key" is FALSE for every Oracle-bearing cell (compile uses gen__variant_0/gen__variant_1/gen vs scripted={'gen':...}+m_combine) -- ~60 of 100 GREEN cells. The tool_registry keys must match whatever names AgentSpecLoader/the exported Flow actually use for these nodes, not neograph's internal compile-time keys. Verify by reading the actual exported Flow's node names for an Oracle cell before writing the registry-building code.
4. RESOLVE the two-DataFlowEdges-into-one-destination_input ambiguity: state explicitly whether Oracle fan-in means "collect" or the Loop self-edge means "latest-wins" -- undefined today, a wrong pick yields false GREENs in the comparison.
5. Reference existing filed tickets instead of re-filing: step 0's "file two tickets for the metadata gaps" must reference neograph-qtfof.6 and neograph-qtfof.7 (already filed) -- do not create duplicates. Also reference the newly-filed neograph-qtfof.8 (third export gap: LlmConfig api_provider=None for think-mode cells, found by review) as a third EXEC_EXEMPT-relevant gap alongside .6/.7.
6. STRENGTHEN EXEC_EXEMPT: "non_empty" is far too weak (66/100 cells would trivially satisfy it). Use a projection-coverage test over (combo, config, shape) instead -- verified in review to make the exemption provably mode-only rather than accidentally passing today.
7. Each subflow export gap (Each's subflow exports zero data edges) is the SAME underlying issue as neograph-qtfof.7 -- do not treat as a fourth separate gap, just note it's covered by .7's scope.
8. The disease-scan atom's "0 instances" finding (neograph-jn555.27) was independently re-verified by the review's 3-lens targeted scan and found to be too narrowly scoped -- it correctly found 0 instances of "the NEW mini-executor duplicating logic" (which is now moot since AgentSpecLoader eliminates the need for a hand-rolled walker), but the review found ~20-25 duplicate-graph-walk-primitive instances in EXISTING test files, now filed as neograph-dgbqv.9 (consolidation, likely out of scope for dgbqv.2 itself post-pivot) and neograph-dgbqv.10 (branch-label coverage gap, proven by mutation testing, independently valuable). Reference both in the design field so the discrepancy is documented, not silently dropped.

Update dgbqv.2's design field with the corrected Core Invariant + Implementation Plan before write-test starts. This is a substantial rewrite, not an incremental patch -- the EXECUTE tier's entire mechanism changed.

title: Agent Spec tests: None-guard every data_flow_connections read (exporter emits 'or None'; 3 test sites deref unguarded)
description:
Found by dgbqv.2's codebase disease scan (2026-08-06), consistency lens (.claude/code-review/dgbqv.2/consistency.md, 'Latent bugs found').

The exporter writes data_flow_connections=data_edges or None at src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:649 and again at src/neograph/_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:340, so the attribute is genuinely None-able. Confirmed live by dgbqv.2's own research: the 'scripted-each-single' cell exports with data_flow_connections is None (zero data edges).

UNGUARDED reads (would raise TypeError: 'NoneType' is not iterable, NOT an assertion failure):
  - tests/test_agent_spec_placeholder_translation.py:89
  - tests/test_agent_spec_export.py:185
  - tests/test_agent_spec_export.py:240
  - tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py:447 (serialized twin: dict-key access on exported['data_flow_connections'])

CORRECTLY guarded siblings (the reference form, '(flow.data_flow_connections or [])'):
  test_agent_spec_export.py:1144, :1177; test_agent_spec_phase5_reuse.py:174, :185; src/neograph/_agent_spec_node_import.py:74

Today the three unguarded sites are protected only by their fixtures happening to wire at least one data edge; a control-only shape breaks them.
acceptance_criteria: All four sites use the guarded form. Optionally a guard pins that no test dereferences .data_flow_connections without an 'or []' (or equivalent None handling).
notes:
## Prep (fwait.2)

Files to modify:
- tests/test_agent_spec_placeholder_translation.py:89
- tests/test_agent_spec_export.py:185, :240
- tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py:447 (serialized twin, dict-key form)
- NEW guard: tests/test_guards_agent_spec_data_flow_reads.py

Verified live (read-only sweep):
- Writers confirmed None-able: _agent_spec.py:649 and _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:340 both emit 'X or None'.
- Fixture proof: tests/fixtures/agent_spec_refactor_snapshot.json carries literal
  "data_flow_connections": null at ~15 sites, so the None shape is exported today.
- Reference guarded form confirmed at test_agent_spec_export.py:1144/:1177,
  test_agent_spec_phase5_reuse.py:174/:185, src/_agent_spec_node_import.py:74 -> '(flow.data_flow_connections or [])'.
- Sweep is complete: grep over src/ + tests/ (excluding fixtures) returns exactly
  3 src lines and 9 test lines; the 4 named sites are the only unguarded reads.

Approach:
1. Rewrite the 4 sites to the reference form. Attribute sites get
   '(flow.data_flow_connections or [])'; the serialized site gets
   '(exported.get("data_flow_connections") or [])'.
2. Add the optional guard from the acceptance criteria, modelled on
   test_guards_branch_arm_walks.py: AST-scan src/neograph + tests for every LOAD of
   .data_flow_connections (ast.Attribute) and every subscript read of the
   'data_flow_connections' key, requiring each to be the left operand of a
   BoolOp(Or). Keyword-arg WRITES (ast.keyword) are structurally not Attributes, so
   the two exporter sites are not false positives.

Non-weakening check (why guarding is safe per site):
- export.py:185 -> followed by 'assert any(...)': empty list still fails loudly.
- export.py:240 -> followed by 'next(...)': empty list raises StopIteration, fails loudly.
- placeholder:89 -> 'assert not any(...)': vacuous on empty, but was already vacuous
  for any edge-free shape; guarding changes TypeError into the test's pre-existing
  negative semantics. Not weakened relative to intent.
- roundtrip:447 -> 'dest_inputs <= titles': vacuous on empty; the real pin is the
  preceding 'titles == {seed:items}' assert. Noted, not expanded (out of scope).
## Execution (fwait.3)
Changes made:
- tests/test_agent_spec_placeholder_translation.py:89 -> (flow.data_flow_connections or [])
- tests/test_agent_spec_export.py:185, :240 -> same guarded form
- tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py:447 -> (exported.get('data_flow_connections') or [])
- NEW tests/test_guards_agent_spec_data_flow_reads.py: AST guard over src/neograph AND
  tests/, flagging every Load-context read (attribute / string-subscript / one-arg .get)
  not wrapping in a BoolOp(Or). Scans tests/ deliberately -- the disease lived test-side.

Non-vacuity PROVEN by controlled mutation (Edit-based revert, never git checkout):
reverting placeholder_translation.py:89 to the raw form made the guard FAIL and it named
the exact offending file:line. Reverted; guard green again.
Guard also carries two self-tests: one asserting the disease shape is detected, one
asserting all four sanctioned spellings (attribute-or, subscript-or, get-or, get-default)
are accepted -- so the guard cannot rot into a vacuous pass.

Quality check: PASS (4511 passed, 106 skipped, 0 failed; baseline 4508 -> +3 new guard
tests). ruff clean, mypy clean (131 files).

title: Agent Spec export tests: the four Operator-combo 'pairs' assertions are invariant under a branch relabelling
description:
Found by dgbqv.2's codebase disease scan (2026-08-06), elegance lens, PROVEN by controlled source mutation (artifact: .claude/code-review/dgbqv.2/elegance.md).

Four test modules assert control-graph shape via
  pairs = {(e.from_node.name, e.to_node.name) for e in flow.control_flow_connections}
at test_agent_spec_each_operator.py:136, test_agent_spec_oracle_operator.py:138, test_agent_spec_loop_operator.py:146, test_agent_spec_each_oracle_operator.py:148 (+ the subflow variant at test_agent_spec_each_oracle.py:168).

The idiom DISCARDS edge.from_branch, so the assertions hold under any relabelling of the branch arms.

EVIDENCE (mutation, reverted): changing _agent_spec.py:265's loop-arm exit label from 'done' to 'continue' produces a BranchingNode with TWO 'continue' successors and NO 'done' successor -- an unrunnable program for any spec-conformant literal executor. title: Sweep verification for 2j208
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on 2j208
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" 2j208`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (2j208)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update 2j208 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add 2j208 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Sweep verification for dgbqv.5
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on dgbqv.5
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" dgbqv.5`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (dgbqv.5)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update dgbqv.5 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add dgbqv.5 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
