title: Codebase-wide disease scan for dgbqv.2
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show dgbqv.2` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/dgbqv.2/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" dgbqv.2
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (dgbqv.2)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update dgbqv.2 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update dgbqv.2 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/dgbqv.2/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add dgbqv.2 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show dgbqv.4` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/dgbqv.4/`:

     ```

     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (dgbqv.4)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update dgbqv.4 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash

   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/dgbqv.4/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add dgbqv.4 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for jtawq.10
description:

executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show jtawq.10` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/jtawq.10/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" jtawq.10
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (jtawq.10)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash

   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash

   ```

ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/jtawq.10/` MUST exist (it is

title: Sweep verification for dgbqv.3
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on dgbqv.3
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" dgbqv.3`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (dgbqv.3)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update dgbqv.3 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add dgbqv.3 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.

  regressed.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for dgbqv.3
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show dgbqv.3` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/dgbqv.3/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" dgbqv.3
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (dgbqv.3)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update dgbqv.3 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update dgbqv.3 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/dgbqv.3/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add dgbqv.3 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/dgbqv.3/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for jtawq.3

the motivating site.

canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/jtawq.3/`:

   Total instances found: <N>

   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |

  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Sweep verification for jtawq.2
description:

a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on jtawq.2
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" jtawq.2`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (jtawq.2)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update jtawq.2 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add jtawq.2 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Sweep verification for 5nvb0
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" 5nvb0`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (5nvb0)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update 5nvb0 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add 5nvb0 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.

  regressed.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for 5nvb0
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show 5nvb0` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/5nvb0/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" 5nvb0
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (5nvb0)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update 5nvb0 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update 5nvb0 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/5nvb0/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash

```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must

- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep

     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:

       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

title: Agent Spec export flattens ForwardConstruct branches: both arms run unconditionally
description:
Found while fixing neograph-s7zt3.15 (control-edge topology), probed at that fix's HEAD. PRE-EXISTING and distinct from the three gaps s7zt3.15 closed.

to_agent_spec() walks the IR via iter_with_arms(), which DROPS the _BranchNode sentinel and yields the true-arm nodes then the false-arm nodes in place. The exporter therefore never sees a branch: _lower_construct_item's _BranchNode arm (which builds the BranchingNode + neograph/branch marker) is DEAD CODE on the to_agent_spec path.

Observed on a Construct(nodes=[seed, _BranchNode(meta, 0)]) with one node per arm:
  branchy__start -> seed
  seed -> arm_a
  arm_a -> arm_b
  arm_b -> branchy__end
No BranchingNode, no neograph/branch marker, no conditional edges. Both arms are wired to run UNCONDITIONALLY and in sequence.

Under the maintainer's 2026-08-03 policy for this epic ('a faithful, independently executable program'), that is a semantic corruption, not just a lost marker: a foreign Agent Spec runtime executes BOTH arms of an if/else. It is also not round-trip-recoverable -- the reimported Construct is a straight line.

Note the topology is REACHABLE and LIVE, so tests/test_agent_spec_reachability.py (added by s7zt3.15) passes on it -- reachability is necessary, not sufficient. A fix needs the _BranchNode sentinel preserved through the export walk (either a branch-aware iteration in to_agent_spec instead of iter_with_arms, or an arm-carrying variant), then the existing _BranchNode arm wired with real per-branch ControlFlowEdges (true/false) that reconverge on the next item -- the same entry/exits shape s7zt3.15 introduced.

Also worth deciding: whether ForwardConstruct branch export was ever exercised. There is no test asserting a BranchingNode with the neograph/branch marker appears in an exported Flow, which is why this went unseen.
design:
## Root Cause
iter_with_arms() is the wrong walk primitive for to_agent_spec(). It exists for callers (lint, verify, runner, schema-fingerprinting) that need to see arm-NESTED nodes but don't care about branch structure. to_agent_spec needs the opposite: it must see the _BranchNode boundary itself to emit a real BranchingNode with divergent true/false ControlFlowEdges into each arm, reconverging on the successor -- exactly parallel to how compiler.py's LangGraph path does NOT use iter_with_arms and instead handles isinstance(item, _BranchNode) directly (compiler.py:312-322 -> _wiring_branch.py:_add_branch_to_graph), and to test_guards_branch_arm_walks.py's own allowlist, which documents compiler.py as deliberately exempt for exactly this reason.

## Fix Approach (post-architect-review)
1. Add a new branch-lowering function to _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py (NOT inline in _agent_spec.py, which sits at its exact 652/652 file-size-ratchet ceiling) -- co-located with the existing _lower_loop/_lower_operator, matching that module's established precedent for modifier-specific Agent Spec lowering. Update the file-size allowlist entry to the exact new line count in the same commit.
2. The new function takes a _BranchNode and returns the SAME _LoweredItem shape _lower_construct_item already returns: (all_spec_nodes, extra_control_edges, extra_data_edges, entry_node, exits, data_node, input_targets). It:
   a. Emits a real BranchingNode (mapping={'true':'true','false':'false'}, metadata={_MARK_BRANCH: True}) -- reusing the existing dead stub's shape (_agent_spec.py:172-178, to be removed since it becomes genuinely reachable via the new dispatch and should live in the new function instead).
   b. Lowers each arm's own item list by recursively calling _lower_construct_item per item, chaining each arm's own items sequentially via the SAME adjacent-pair reconvergence pattern already in to_agent_spec's outer loop (zip(exits, entries[1:])) -- this is what gives arm items (Construct sub-pipelines, Oracle/Each/Loop/Operator-wrapped nodes) their existing modifier-dispatch support for free.
   c. Wires the BranchingNode's true/false edges into each arm's first entry (from_branch='true'/'false'), mirroring Loop's back-edge / Operator's pause-edge convention already in _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py. An empty arm's edge targets the branch's own successor directly (mirrors _wiring_branch.py's true_target/false_target = END fallback).
   d. Returns exits = the concatenation of both arms' final item exits (each retaining its own from_branch tag), so the EXISTING adjacent-pair reconvergence loop in to_agent_spec (lines 410-419) fans both arm tails into the next top-level item's entry -- the same 'multiple exits reconverge on one entry' shape the Operator postlude already established for s7zt3.15.
3. Change to_agent_spec's iteration (lines 362, 393, 428) from iter_with_arms(construct) to a raw walk of construct.nodes with explicit isinstance(item, _BranchNode) dispatch to the new function (else: existing _lower_construct_item) -- mirroring compiler.py's graph-wiring loop shape. Behavior-identical for every non-branch construct since iter_with_arms is a strict pass-through for non-_BranchNode items.
4. Remove the dead isinstance(item, _BranchNode) arm from _lower_construct_item (_agent_spec.py:172-178) -- superseded by the new function, and its old shape (single flat exit, no true/false divergence) was incomplete anyway.
5. Test additions beyond the hytk0.2 repro: (a) multi-node-per-arm case (arm-internal sequential wiring + last-node exit reconvergence), (b) a modifier-wrapped node inside one arm (proves recursive _lower_construct_item reuse generalizes).
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_agent_spec_export.py::TestToAgentSpecLowersModifiers::test_forward_construct_if_else_lowers_to_branching_node_not_unconditional_sequence

## Trace-similar (atom 3)

title: Agent Spec import parses a Loop 'when' as an expression, so a registered condition NAME fails to reimport
description:
Found while implementing neograph-s7zt3.11 (Phase 8), 2026-07-31, on develop. PRE-EXISTING and NODE-level -- reproduced with no Construct item and no Phase 8 code involved. Out of Phase 8's scope; filed rather than bundled.

REPRO -- Node-level, in memory, no serialization:

  register_condition('ln_never', lambda s: None)
  p = Construct('p', nodes=[
      Node.scripted('seed', fn=..., outputs=A),
      Node.scripted('body', fn=..., inputs=A, outputs=A) | Loop(when='ln_never', max_iterations=3),
  ])
  from_agent_spec(to_agent_spec(p))
  -> ValueError: Invalid condition expression: 'ln_never'. Expected: field op literal
     (e.g. 'score < 0.8', 'passed == true', 'name != "draft"')

  The same pipeline with an EXPRESSION (Loop(when='v < 5')) reimports fine.

ROOT CAUSE: _reconstruct_loop_item does
    condition = parse_condition(loop_spec['when']) if isinstance(loop_spec['when'], str) else loop_spec['when']
It assumes any string 'when' is an EXPRESSION. But a Loop 'when' string is a REGISTERED CONDITION NAME by design -- lint has a dedicated rule for exactly that (loop_condition_unregistered, ERROR: string condition not in registry, documented in AGENTS.md). So the importer rejects the form the rest of the system treats as canonical.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT GIVES AWAY THE FIX: Operator handles this correctly and does nothing clever -- loader.py:1263 passes the marker string straight through as Operator(when=<string>) and lets the modifier resolve it. Loop is the only reconstructor that eagerly parses.

WHY IT HID: every existing Loop round-trip fixture uses an expression form. The registry-name form has never been round-tripped in a test.

FIX DIRECTION (small, but NOT a blind one-liner): Loop 'when' legitimately accepts BOTH a registry name and an expression, and the expression path currently works and is covered. So the fix must accept both -- resolve against the condition registry first and fall back to parse_condition -- rather than simply deleting the parse call and mirroring Operator. Check whether the compile path expects a callable or tolerates a string before choosing, and pin BOTH forms with tests.

IMPACT ON neograph-s7zt3.11: its required matching-boundary LOOP-on-Construct row was originally written with a registered condition name and was blocked by THIS bug, not by anything Construct-related. The fixture was switched to an expression so the row tests the seam it exists to test; a comment there cites this ticket.
close_reason: Fixed in neograph-s7zt3.11 (commit 110e8d6). _reconstruct_loop_item now discriminates instead of assuming: parse_condition is tried, and a string that does not parse is a REGISTERED CONDITION NAME passed through for compile() to resolve — the same thing the Operator postlude does. Both forms round-trip. title: Loop-on-Construct with differing boundary types fails Agent Spec export: self-loop DataFlowEdge names the output field on an input port
description:
Found while verifying the neograph-s7zt3.11 (Phase 8) research re-scope, 2026-07-30, on develop @ 51b7b6e. Scoped OUT of Phase 8 by maintainer decision (2026-07-31) so the import seam stays a single reviewable change; filed here instead of being silently inherited as 'already done'.

REPRO -- fails at EXPORT, no import or serialization involved:

  class A(BaseModel): v: str
  class B(BaseModel): w: str
  sub = Construct('sub', input=A, output=B, nodes=[Node.scripted('inner', fn=..., inputs=A, outputs=B)])
  parent = Construct('p', nodes=[Node.scripted('seed', fn=..., outputs=A), sub | Loop(when=...)])
  to_agent_spec(parent)

  pydantic ValidationError: 1 validation error for DataFlowEdge
    Value error, Flow data connection named sub__loop_self_w is connected to a property
    named w of the destination node sub, but the node does not have any property with
    that name.

BOUNDARY CONDITION -- this is why it hid: it fails ONLY when the sub-Construct's input and output types DIFFER. With input == output the self-loop edge happens to name a field that exists on both ports and export succeeds. Every existing Loop-on-Construct fixture uses the matching-boundary shape.

ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed, not guessed): the Loop lowering builds the self-loop DataFlowEdge from the loop body's OUTPUT field name and points it at the node's own input port. For a Construct whose boundary types differ, the input port declares the INPUT type's fields, so the named property does not exist there and pyagentspec rejects the edge at construction.

NOT AN INVALID PIPELINE: this shape is legal and supported at the compiler level -- tests/test_loop.py::TestLoopInputNotEqualOutput::test_construct_loop_input_neq_output_compiles pins that it compiles and runs. So this is an Agent Spec EXPORT gap, not a validation catching a bad pipeline.

BLAST RADIUS: LOOP and LOOP_OPERATOR on a Construct item, differing-boundary only. Node-level Loop is unaffected (a Node's inputs/outputs are separate declarations and the existing lowering already handles it).

FIX DIRECTION (needs design, do not guess): decide what the self-loop edge should carry when the boundary types differ. The loop feeds the body's output back as the next iteration's input, so an output field named w cannot address an input port declaring v -- either the edge must target the input port's own field names (requiring a declared mapping between the two boundary types), or the differing-boundary case must fail loud at export with a neograph error explaining the limitation rather than surfacing a raw pydantic ValidationError from pyagentspec. The second is cheap and is strictly better than today; the first is the real fix.

TDD: the repro above is the red test. Add the matching-boundary case alongside as the green control, so the boundary condition is pinned and cannot silently widen.
notes:
DECISION (2026-08-03, maintainer): real fix, not the cheap fail-loud stopgap. "If it can be described in neograph and it works in LangGraph, ship it."

Verified against the actual runtime (src/neograph/_wiring.py:508 _add_subgraph_loop, _wiring_loop.py router) why LangGraph runs this fine with zero field-aliasing: the loop-back is a pure CONTROL edge (graph.add_conditional_edges re-entering the same node). LangGraph state is a shared, accumulating dict keyed by field name, not a strict single-slot pipe -- the input field (e.g. 'v') persists unchanged in state across iterations since nothing overwrites it, the output field (e.g. 'w') lives in its own separate slot, and the loop router reads the exit condition straight off 'w' without ever feeding it back as 'v'.

So the Agent Spec exporter's mistake is trying to build a literal field-aliasing DataFlowEdge for the self-loop at all -- that requirement doesn't exist in the thing being exported. FIX DIRECTION: emit the loop-back as a control-only edge carrying NO field mapping when the boundary types differ (mapping only structurally-identical fields, which is zero when the types fully differ). No new mapping DSL, no user-declared boundary mapping needed -- this mirrors actual LangGraph semantics exactly, it is not a workaround.
close_reason: Loop self-edge now decides per field against the lowered body's own declared Properties (castable pair via pyagentspec's property_is_castable_to); differing-boundary Construct loops export as control-only, mirroring LangGraph's pure-control loop-back. Red/green pair + structural guard added; _agent_spec.py held at its 981 ceiling by moving _item_inputs/_item_outputs next to _properties_for.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-s7zt3.11
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-s7zt3.11
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-s7zt3.11`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-s7zt3.11)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-s7zt3.11 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-s7zt3.11 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-s7zt3.11
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-s7zt3.11` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-s7zt3.11/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-s7zt3.11
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-s7zt3.11)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-s7zt3.11 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-s7zt3.11 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-s7zt3.11/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-s7zt3.11 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: .hypothesis/ is tracked in git and not gitignored — test-cache artifacts leak into commits
description:
Surfaced during the 0.7.4 forward-port (neograph-5w8a6), where a routine `git add -A` in a merge worktree swept 65 .hypothesis/constants/ files into the merge commit, and the subsequent cleanup revealed that ~802 .hypothesis/ files are ALREADY tracked on develop.

THE HAZARD, twice over:
1. .hypothesis/ is a Hypothesis test-run cache (constants/, unicode_data/, examples database). It is regenerated by every test run, so it shows up as modified/untracked noise in every git status and is a standing trap for `git add -A` / `git add .`.
2. It also BLOCKED a fast-forward: `git merge --ff-only` refused with 'local changes would be overwritten' + 56 untracked files, printed 'Aborting' AFTER printing 'Updating x..y', and left HEAD at the stale base. That near-miss was caught only by an explicit merge-base assertion.

WHAT TO DECIDE (not obvious, hence a ticket rather than a fix):
 (a) Add .hypothesis/ to .gitignore and `git rm -r --cached .hypothesis` -- the usual answer. But check first whether anything depends on the committed database: a checked-in Hypothesis example DB is sometimes deliberate, so failing examples replay in CI. If so, that intent is undocumented and should be written down rather than deleted.
 (b) If the example DB IS wanted, narrow the tracking to just that path and gitignore constants/ + unicode_data/, which are pure caches.

Acceptance: git status is clean after a full test run, `git add -A` cannot capture test-cache artifacts, and if any part of .hypothesis/ stays tracked there is a comment saying why.
notes:
## Recurrence evidence (2026-07-31) -- hit twice more in one session

1. During the neograph-s7zt3.16 work, .hypothesis/unicode_data/15.0.0/codec-utf-8.json.gz showed as modified after every full pytest run, and BLOCKED git pull --rebase with 'cannot pull with rebase: You have unstaged changes'. It had to be discarded with git restore before the push could proceed.
2. Repeated at the start of the Phase 8 work.

This is the third distinct incident: the original one swept 65 cache files into a merge commit, and the over-correction (git rm -r --cached .hypothesis) untracked 802 legitimately-tracked files.

WHAT MAKES THIS NON-TRIVIAL -- do not just add a gitignore line. The directory holds TWO different kinds of thing:
  - .hypothesis/examples/ and .hypothesis/unicode_data/ -- regenerable machine caches. Pure noise; safe to ignore and untrack.
  - .hypothesis/constants/ -- currently ~35 untracked entries in git status. Whether the DB of discovered failing examples is meant to be shared (so a found counterexample re-runs on every machine and in CI) is a deliberate choice, not an oversight. Hypothesis's own guidance is that the example database is usually local, but some projects commit it on purpose.

DECIDE, then implement, in this order:
  a. Confirm whether any tracked .hypothesis path is load-bearing for CI reproducibility (check .github/workflows and whether HYPOTHESIS_DATABASE_FILE or a profile is configured anywhere).
  b. If nothing is load-bearing: gitignore the whole directory and untrack it in ONE commit that states the file count, so the diff is auditable rather than looking like mass deletion.
  c. If the constants DB is deliberate: gitignore only examples/ and unicode_data/, and add a one-line comment in .gitignore saying why constants/ is exempt -- otherwise the next person removes the exemption.

Until this lands, the operational workaround is: git restore the modified cache file before any pull/rebase. Never git add -A in this repo.
close_reason: Landed 2026-08-03: .hypothesis/ added to .gitignore, 803 tracked cache files untracked via git rm --cached (commit 137aba0).

title: loader.py: mechanical move of the swarm-import cluster (the injection design it needed already exists)
description:
RESCOPED 2026-08-05 per docs/design/agent-spec-target-architecture-2026-08-03.md (Pillar B2,
ticket-ground-truth table). The ORIGINAL ticket's "needs injection design" clause is CLOSED-AS-STALE:
the injection seam it was asking for already exists elsewhere in the codebase, built for a different
but structurally identical need. Verified: `_construct_from_subflow(subflow, name, from_spec)` at
_agent_spec_group_import.py:48 is exactly this pattern (a single injected `from_spec: Callable`
avoiding a back-import of loader.py). No new design work remains -- this is now a MECHANICAL move.

REMAINING SCOPE: move loader.py:237-491 (six functions, ~255 lines -- re-verify current line numbers
with `wc -l` and a fresh read before starting, this file has moved before) to a new
`_agent_spec_swarm_import.py`, injecting the single `from_spec` callable at the two dispatch points
(loader.py:525, :533) via the SAME `_construct_from_subflow` pattern already proven at
_agent_spec_group_import.py:48 -- do not invent a second injection mechanism. Keep loader.py's F401
re-export idiom (:617-667) so nothing importing from `neograph.loader` breaks.

SEQUENCING: land AFTER neograph-jtawq.2 (the ComboDecomposition.fused fix), because the moved swarm-
import code should read `decomp.fused` from day one rather than being migrated twice.

FILE-SIZE BOOKKEEPING: loader.py drops under 500 lines after this move -- DELETE its ALLOWLIST entry
in tests/test_guards_file_size.py entirely (never lower it to a new sub-500 number; the exact-ceiling
rule means a file under the general cap gets no private entry at all).

Full detail in the design doc.
design:
## Core Invariant

The Agent Spec import path stays a strictly one-way import chain with exactly ONE owner per
seam: a module may only be reached by injecting its parent's entry point as a callable, never by
importing back up -- and every structural guard that scans this path must scan the moved code at
its NEW home, so the guard surface follows the code instead of silently narrowing.

## Implementation Plan

Mechanical move only. No behaviour change, no new design. Re-derive every line number with a
fresh read before editing -- the numbers below were re-measured against source on 2026-08-06
(refine atom neograph-jn555.55) and this file moves often. Note the earlier research atom's
loader.py import line numbers drift by about +1 against current source (e.g. `warnings` is at
:18 not :19, `from typing import Any, Literal` at :20 not :21, `BaseModel` at :25 not :26) --
another reason to re-grep rather than trust any number here.

1. **Create src/neograph/_agent_spec_swarm_import.py** by MOVING loader.py:226-482 verbatim
(the six functions: _swarm_agents_ordered, _synthesize_swarm_payload, _swarm_trigger,
_flow_member_to_construct, _reconstruct_swarm_mesh, _reconstruct_swarm_mesh_with_operator_gates).
Bodies and docstrings unchanged except the threading in step 2. Write the module docstring by
COPYING the shape of _agent_spec_group_import.py:1-16 -- what the module owns, why from_spec is
injected rather than imported, and the AST-verified layer order
(_agent_spec_node_import <- _agent_spec_group_import <- this module <- loader; no back-edges).
Cite neograph-jtawq.10 as the extraction ticket, matching the s7zt3.11 precedent.

2. **Extend, do not invent, the existing injection.** Reuse the SAME signature convention as
_construct_from_subflow(subflow, name, from_spec) at _agent_spec_group_import.py:48 --
from_spec: Callable[[Any], Construct] as the LAST positional parameter, from collections.abc
import Callable. Add it to exactly three functions and thread it through:
_reconstruct_swarm_mesh_with_operator_gates(flow, from_spec) -> _reconstruct_swarm_mesh(swarm, from_spec)
_reconstruct_swarm_mesh(swarm, from_spec) -> _flow_member_to_construct(agent, payload, from_spec)
_flow_member_to_construct(agent, payload, from_spec) -> _construct_from_subflow(agent, agent.name, from_spec)
The other three functions are pure and take no new parameter. Do NOT introduce a second
injection mechanism, a module-global, or a late import of loader.

3. **Import the cluster's own dependencies directly** in the new module (they all resolve one
layer down, so no cycle): _MARK_MODIFIER/_MARK_PORTAL_OPERATOR_SPEC/_MARK_PORTAL_SPEC/
_MARK_PROMPT_SPEC from _agent_spec_markers; _agent_spec_props_to_type/_node_from_spec_agent
from _agent_spec_node_import; _construct_from_subflow from _agent_spec_group_import;
_with_declared_io from _normalize; Construct, Node, Operator, Portal; BaseModel/create_model;
warnings; Any/Literal.

3b. **Correct the layer-order docstring the move invalidates** (review LOW finding 4, folded in).
_agent_spec_group_import.py:14-15 currently pins "Layer order, verified from the AST:
``_agent_spec_node_import`` <- this module <- ``loader``. No back-edges." After this move the
real chain is node_import <- group_import <- swarm_import <- loader, and the new module becomes
a SECOND importer of _construct_from_subflow. Update that line in the SAME commit so the two
module docstrings do not contradict each other on day one. Step 1 copies the docstring SHAPE;
this step keeps its SOURCE true.

4. **Update loader.py's two dispatch points** (currently :514 and :522 inside from_agent_spec,
NOT the stale :525/:533) to pass from_agent_spec as the injected callable:
_reconstruct_swarm_mesh(flow, from_agent_spec) and
_reconstruct_swarm_mesh_with_operator_gates(flow, from_agent_spec). Passing the name as an
ARGUMENT is the sanctioned pattern and is explicitly NOT a recursion call site under
test_guards_agent_spec_import_seam.py's detector (pinned by its own slip test at :156-161).

5. **Preserve the re-export surface** with a new F401 block in loader.py, a sibling of the
s7zt3.11 block at :603-618 -- same comment style, same # noqa: E402,F401, naming
neograph-jtawq.10. Re-export the six moved names, and ADD # noqa: F401 to the ten loader.py
imports that become re-export-only after the move: warnings, Literal, BaseModel, create_model,
_MARK_PORTAL_SPEC, _MARK_PORTAL_OPERATOR_SPEC, _MARK_PROMPT_SPEC, _with_declared_io, Node,
Portal. Without the noqa, ruff --fix strips them and the surface silently shrinks -- the
exact failure mode the :620-623 comment documents.

   **Placement mechanics differ by import shape** (review LOW finding 5, folded in -- do not
   guess, the two shapes need different noqa forms):
   - `Literal` shares its line with the STILL-USED `Any` (`from typing import Any, Literal`,
     currently :20). A per-name noqa is impossible there; use a LINE-level noqa on that line.
     Same for `import warnings` (currently :18) and `from neograph.node import Node`, which are
     already single-name lines.
   - `BaseModel` and `create_model` sit inside the parenthesized pydantic block (currently
     :24-28) whose sibling `ValidationError` ALREADY carries a PER-NAME `# noqa: E402,F401`.
     The three `_MARK_*` names sit inside the parenthesized `_agent_spec_markers` block
     (currently :30-38), and `_with_declared_io` inside the `_normalize` block (:39-42) whose
     sibling `primary_output_field` also already carries a per-name noqa. Copy that PER-NAME
     form inside parenthesized blocks.
   - PROVE it before committing with `uv run ruff check --fix --diff src/neograph/loader.py` --
     an empty diff on those lines is the evidence; a diff that deletes any of the ten means the

design:
## Core Invariant

A machine-emitted runtime spec reaches execution ONLY through the one canonical modifier-aware
gate (AgentSpecDeserializer.from_dict -> from_agent_spec -> compile, the SAME Construct(...)
validation a hand-written pipeline passes), and LangGraph Command construction stays confined to
exactly {factory.py, runner.py}; relocating the gate to its own module must pin BOTH ends of the
new seam -- the gate still calls only the canonical path, AND factory's wrapper still calls the
gate -- so the extraction strengthens the invariant rather than opening a hole behind a green test.

title: Render a tool EXPLANATION preamble, the same way the budget preamble is rendered (announce_tool_docs)
description:
THE OBSERVATION (from a consumer, ox-troubleshooting-demo, 2026-07-30).

neograph already synthesizes ONE system message about the tools: _tool_budget_preamble turns
(tools, max_iterations) into prose and puts it in the message body as the first system message.
That preamble is a CONSTRAINT ("You have a limited tool-call budget... you need not use every
call. Stop and answer once you have enough."). There is no counterpart that EXPLAINS the tools.

WHY THAT ASYMMETRY MATTERS. A tool's description exists, but it travels in a DIFFERENT CHANNEL:
the provider's tools array (bind_tools -> the OpenAI tool schema), not the message body. Two
consequences a consumer measured:

  1. It is INVISIBLE IN THE TRACE. Langfuse's LangChain integration records the generation input
     as the message list, so a trace shows the budget preamble verbatim but shows NOTHING of what
     the model was told each tool is for. Verifying that a description reaches the model needed an
     ad-hoc probe against a live server (bind the tool, convert_to_openai_tool, read the string).
     Everything neograph itself puts in the prompt IS auditable from the trace; the tool docs are
     the one gap.
  2. It is the WEAKER position. The budget CONSTRAINT sits first in the message body; the tool's
     PURPOSE sits in a side-channel array. The measured behaviour is consistent with that
     asymmetry: a capability-gated knowledge tool was called 0/503 times at one node while bound,
     budgeted and announced -- the model was told it had 1 call, and was not told in the body what
     the tool was for.

THE REQUEST. An announce_tool_docs llm_config flag (sibling to announce_tool_budget) that renders
a second synthesized system message from the BOUND tools' own descriptions -- same source of
truth, no hand-written duplicate, and the same "the numbers the model is TOLD are the numbers
ENFORCED" invariant that makes the budget preamble trustworthy. Roughly:

    Tools available to you:
      - NAME: DESCRIPTION (read from the bound tool)

WHY IT BELONGS UPSTREAM RATHER THAN IN EVERY CONSUMER'S TEMPLATE. Hand-copying descriptions into a
prompt template is exactly the drift the budget preamble was built to prevent: the docstring
changes, the template does not, and the model is then told something false. Rendering from the
bound tools keeps ONE source of truth. It also makes the whole tool-facing prompt surface auditable
from a trace, which is currently only half true.

SECONDARY REQUEST. Tool carries only [budget, config, idempotent, name] -- there is no way to
override or enrich a bound tool's description at the neograph layer (per-node when-to-use text, or
MCP tool annotations such as readOnlyHint / openWorldHint). A per-node override is precisely what a
consumer wants when the same tool means different things at different steps: the same playbook tool
is "what can go wrong" at hypothesis generation and "how to rule" at verdict time.

EVIDENCE THIS IS TESTABLE, NOT SPECULATIVE: the consumer is running an ablation that isolates
delivery CHANNEL with content held constant (description-in-schema vs description-in-preamble),
pull-rate as the metric, across four agent nodes. Results can be fed back here.

title: Execute: 3ffdg wave 2 (16 remaining splits, Phase-8 files first)
description:
Lightweight formula for executing well-defined beads tasks. Three atoms per task: prep (read and plan), execute (implement and verify), commit. Use instead of task-execute when the task description already contains sufficient context and doesn't need architect review or triage routing.
Total atoms: 1 (baseline) + 3N (per task) + 1 (verify-final) = 3N + 2. Compare task-execute at 7N + 2.
notes:
## Baseline (atom .1) -- develop 48672b9
make quality: 4043 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed | ruff clean | mypy clean (93 files).
Order: Phase-8-file children FIRST (.2 _wiring, .11 decorators, .12 forward, .6 factory, .7 _agent_cycle, .8 compiler), then the ten that touch files Phase 8 never names. Rationale in neograph-3ffdg's notes.
Strictly sequential, enforced by deps: each task's Prep is blocked by the previous task's Commit.
PROCESS RULES (from the .3 incident): explicit file lists on every ruff invocation, never a directory; never an unquoted shell variable for a file list; commit as soon as the gate is green.
