title: Correlate structlog run_id with the Langfuse trace id (or expose both) — today the two identities for one run cannot be joined
description:
When `observe=` is on, neograph produces TWO independent identities for the same execution and never relates them:

- the structlog `run_id` on every `node_start` / `node_complete` line — `uuid4().hex`, minted by `_mint_run_id` (runner.py:595)
- the Langfuse trace id, minted separately by the observability layer

Both are 32-hex, which makes them look interchangeable; they are not. Verified downstream: a `run_id` taken from a real eval log returns 404 against `GET /api/public/traces/{id}`.

## Why that costs the caller
The logs and the traces answer different questions and cannot be joined:

- structlog has the mechanics — `loops`, `tool_calls`, `tools`, `prompt`, `tier`, token counts, durations, and crucially the ERRORS.
- Langfuse has the content — the rendered prompt, the model's reasoning, the tool payloads.

To debug "why did this run fail", or to compute an error rate per experiment arm, you need both, joined per run. Today the only join key is `config['run_name']` (which becomes the trace NAME) — and a name is not an id: it is caller-supplied, not enforced unique, and degrades silently. A downstream 503-row eval produced the run name `node-assess-NODE-assess-?` for many rows because a scenario field was absent, collapsing distinct runs into one unusable label.

This is not hypothetical. A downstream two-arm A/B lost 70 of one arm's 192 runs to an empty-response incident (see neograph-yqrsz). Establishing that the failures were an infrastructure artifact rather than a property of the arm required correlating structlog errors against trace content by hand, via timestamps and log-file archaeology, because there was no id to join on. The wrong conclusion had already been published.

## The request
When observability is enabled, make the two the same id, or make each discoverable from the other. In rough order of preference:

1. **Derive `run_id` from the Langfuse trace id when `observe=` is active.** A trace id is also fresh-per-attempt, so this preserves the property `_mint_run_id`'s docstring is protecting. `Langfuse.create_trace_id()` exists precisely for minting one ahead of use.
2. **Emit the trace id as an additional structlog field** (`trace_id=...`) alongside `run_id`. Non-breaking, keeps the two identity spaces separate, and makes the join exact.
3. **Accept an optional caller `correlation_id`** that is logged on every line and attached to the trace, WITHOUT replacing `run_id`. This also lets a caller stamp its own unit of work (an Inspect sample id, an eval arm) into the framework's own log lines — something the caller cannot do today because it does not control neograph's logger.

Explicitly NOT asking for `run_id` to be caller-settable: the docstring's reasoning for framework-minting (fresh per attempt, re-minted on resume, never in state or the checkpoint fingerprint) is sound and should stay.

## Note for whoever picks this up
Option 3 is the most general: even with 1 or 2, callers still need to attach THEIR unit of work (sample id, arm, epoch) to the framework's log lines. Downstream that is being worked around with `structlog.contextvars`, which functions but depends on the host application configuring the processor chain — a caller who does not know to add `merge_contextvars` gets nothing, silently.
design:
## Core Invariant
The framework stays the SOLE minter of `run_id` — fresh per attempt, config-only, never in state and never in the checkpoint fingerprint — and every observability identity is DERIVED from it rather than replacing it, so toggling `observe=` can never change `run_id` or anything keyed on it (`_run_cache` entries, latches, `evict_run`). Every config-side-channel read/write goes through `_config_carrier`, whose docstring already declares that one-site rule.

## Scope (REFINED — atom neograph-ehuks.12)
IN: ticket options 1+2, delivered as one thing — derive the trace id from run_id, and emit it on every node log line.
OUT: ticket option 3 (caller `correlation_id`) -> split to **neograph-lwssj** (filed, dep-wired to land after this). It is new PUBLIC config surface with its own docs/website obligation; bundling it with a dependency bump and three carrier migrations made one unreviewable commit.

## Implementation Plan

**Step 1 — pay the carrier debt FIRST (prerequisite, not cleanup).**
The naive implementation would add a 4th inline carrier write and a 2nd inline identity read to a module already violating `_config_carrier`'s documented one-site invariant. Import `_with_configurable` + `run_id_of` into runner.py (it imports neither today) and migrate:
- runner.py:591 `_mark_stream_custom` -> `_with_configurable(config, **{StateKeys.STREAM_CUSTOM: True})`
- runner.py:608 `_mint_run_id` -> same idiom (this is the function step 2 extends; `_mint_run_id`'s docstring claims it 'Mirrors `_mark_stream_custom` EXACTLY', so both move together or the stated mirror breaks)
- runner.py:704 `_evict_run_cache` -> `run_id_of(config)`

**Step 2 — derive, don't mint a second identity.**
Add `StateKeys.TRACE_ID` ('_neo_trace_id') beside RUN_ID in _state_keys.py:99-108 with the same config-only comment. In `_merge_observe_callbacks` (runner.py:656), on the ATTACH path only: read run_id via `run_id_of`, derive `Langfuse.create_trace_id(seed=run_id)`, construct `CallbackHandler(trace_context={'trace_id': tid})`, and carry the tid in configurable via `_with_configurable`. Keep the langfuse import function-local (TestNoModuleLevelLangfuseImports). The two early-outs (observe off / keys absent, and the dedupe branch where the user wired their own handler) must stash and emit NOTHING — in the dedupe case our derived id would not match their handler's trace, so emitting it would be a silent lie.

**Step 3 — emit it.**
Extend `_execute._run_id_binds` (_execute.py:41) — the SINGLE site building the structlog bind dict, consumed by both node-lifecycle twins at :97 and :151 — to also bind `trace_id` when present. Rename to an identity-shaped name since it no longer binds only run_id; update both call sites.

**Step 4 — guard the non-twin blind spot.**
`TestTwinThinness` catches a re-inlined carrier only in TABLED TWIN PAIRS; all three step-1 sites are single functions and are structurally invisible to it. Add a guard banning the inline `{**config, 'configurable': {...}}` write idiom and the inline `configurable.get(StateKeys.RUN_ID)` read outside `_config_carrier.py`. Write it failing-first.

**Step 5 — pin.** `langfuse>=3.0` -> `>=3.11` at pyproject.toml:35 (extra) and :153 (dev group). Measured: `CallbackHandler(trace_context=)` first exists at 3.11.0. Maintainer confirmed 2026-07-29.

## Closure constraint (review finding #3, HIGH — do not skip)
The acceptance decomposes into three sub-claims:
 (a) trace_id == create_trace_id(seed=run_id), deterministic — in-process, testable.
 (b) every node_start/node_complete line carries it — in-process, testable.
 (c) Langfuse records the trace UNDER that id — **EXTERNAL. Not provable without live LANGFUSE_* keys.**
The implement atom may close on (a)+(b)+an assertion that the handler was constructed with our trace_context. **neograph-s65y2 itself must NOT be closed as done** until (c) is verified live; it stays open with the unproven path stated plainly. Green on (a)+(b) is proof of the sub-claims, never of the acceptance.
notes:
## Findings (atom neograph-ehuks.2)

### The decisive finding: Langfuse can be TOLD the trace id, and it can be DERIVED from run_id
Probed the installed SDK (langfuse 4.0.6):
- `Langfuse.create_trace_id(*, seed: str | None = None) -> str` is a **staticmethod** and is **deterministic on the seed** — verified: same seed -> same id, different seed -> different id, and the output is the first 32 hex of sha256(seed) (seed='abc' -> ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223).
- `CallbackHandler(*, public_key=None, trace_context: TraceContext | None = None)` — the handler ACCEPTS a caller-supplied trace id. `TraceContext = {trace_id: str, parent_span_id: NotRequired[str]}`.

This makes the ticket's option 1 achievable WITHOUT its stated cost. The ticket proposed deriving run_id FROM a Langfuse trace id; the reverse is strictly better — derive the TRACE id from the existing run_id via `create_trace_id(seed=run_id)`. Then:
- `_mint_run_id`'s fresh-per-attempt property is untouched (run_id is still framework-minted uuid4; the trace id inherits freshness).
- run_id itself never changes, so NOTHING keyed on it changes (see blast radius below).
- the join key is COMPUTABLE OFFLINE: given only a structlog line's run_id, anyone can compute the trace id. Even a log predating the feature can be joined retroactively.
Options 1 and 2 stop being alternatives — 2 becomes a convenience field over a relationship that already holds.

### Blast radius of touching run_id (why the derivation direction matters)
`run_id` is NOT log-only. It keys the per-run cache:
- _run_cache.py:67 `_run_id(config)`, :115-145 cache/latch keys are `(run_id, subkey)`, :158 `evict_run(run_id)` — this is the MCP run-scoped connection reuse (reconnect-safe across resume).
- runner.py:704 `_evict_run_cache` reads RUN_ID back from config in every verb's finally.
Replacing run_id with a Langfuse-sourced id (ticket option 1 as written) would make the cache key's provenance depend on whether observe= is on. Deriving the other direction has zero blast radius.

## Relevant Code (reuse targets — extend these, do not build parallels)
- src/neograph/runner.py:595 `_mint_run_id` — the exemplar for config-only identity: fresh dict, never mutates caller's config, `StateKeys.RUN_ID` in `configurable` so it never enters state or the schema fingerprint. Any new id follows this shape.
- src/neograph/runner.py:656 `_merge_observe_callbacks` — where `CallbackHandler()` is constructed. THE site to pass trace_context. Keep the langfuse import function-local (TestNoModuleLevelLangfuseImports pins it).
- src/neograph/runner.py:786-787 — ordering is already correct: `_mint_run_id` runs BEFORE `_finalize_prepare_config` (which calls the observe merge), so run_id is available when the handler is built. Preserve this order.
- src/neograph/_execute.py:41 `_run_id_binds(config)` — **the single site** that builds the structlog bind dict, consumed at :97 (`node_start`) and :151 (its twin). Adding a key here lights up every node log line in ONE edit. This is the reuse target for the trace_id field.
- src/neograph/_config_carrier.py:38 `run_id_of(config)` — canonical reader; use it, do not re-read configurable inline.
- src/neograph/_state_keys.py:101-108 — the RUN_ID declaration + its 'config-only, never in state' comment; a TRACE_ID key mirrors it verbatim.

### For option 3 (caller correlation_id)
The LangChain handler honors these keys off `config['metadata']`: `langfuse_session_id`, `langfuse_user_id`, `langfuse_tags`, `langfuse_trace_attributes`. So a caller-supplied correlation id can reach the TRACE without any new langfuse surface — and reach the LOGS through the same `_run_id_binds` dict. Both halves of option 3 land on primitives that already exist.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- **NEEDS USER INPUT: the langfuse pin is `>=3.0` but the API was probed on 4.0.6.** `create_trace_id(seed=)` and `CallbackHandler(trace_context=)` must be confirmed present in 3.x, or the pin tightened to `>=4` / a version guard added. Shipping against an unverified floor would fail loud at runtime for a 3.x user. Cheapest resolution: tighten the extra to the version actually tested.
- **Dedupe branch**: `_merge_observe_callbacks` returns early when the user already wired their own CallbackHandler. That handler carries ITS own trace id, which our derived one would not match. Emitting a derived trace_id into logs there would be a silent lie. Correct behavior: in the dedupe branch do NOT stash/emit a trace id (or emit only if we attached). Must be decided explicitly, not by omission.
- **Env gate**: no LANGFUSE keys -> observe is a documented clean no-op -> no trace exists -> no trace_id field. Logs keep run_id alone. Correct, but the field is then absent rather than null — consumers must tolerate absence.
- **Determinism cuts both ways**: seeding from run_id means anyone who learns a run_id can compute the trace id. That is the feature, but worth stating; run_id is not a secret today either.
- Direct `graph.invoke()` (bypassing the runner verbs) mints no run_id at all — already true for the cache; the trace id inherits the same 'absent' behavior.
## RESOLVED: the 'NEEDS USER INPUT' pin risk (measured, not inferred)

Bisected the real langfuse API floor in a scratch venv (uv pip install per version + inspect.signature — the source-regex probe was unreliable, multiple __init__ in that file):

| langfuse | `create_trace_id(seed=)` | `CallbackHandler(trace_context=)` |
|---|---|---|
| 3.0.0  | YES | **NO** (only `public_key`) |
| 3.8.0  | YES | NO |
| 3.9.0  | YES | NO |
| 3.10.0 | YES | NO |
| **3.11.0** | YES | **YES** <- first version |
| 3.15.0 | YES | YES |
| 4.0.6  | YES | YES |

`create_trace_id(seed='abc')` returns the IDENTICAL id (ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223) at 3.0.0, 3.15.0 and 4.0.6 — the derivation is stable across the whole supported range, so a trace id computed today stays joinable.

**The declared pin `langfuse>=3.0` is therefore WRONG for this feature** — it would break at 3.0-3.10.

Decision: raise the floor to `langfuse>=3.11` in BOTH sites (pyproject.toml:35 the `langfuse` extra, and :153 the dev dependency-group). Rejected alternatives, each of which introduces a silent seam the north star forbids:
- Feature-detect and skip trace_context on old versions -> observe= silently produces the old unjoinable behavior with no signal.
- Emit trace_id in logs but skip binding it to the handler on old versions -> the logged id would not match the real trace: a silent LIE, strictly worse than today's honest disconnect.
Bumping a floor is safe here per AGENTS.md: 0.x, no back-compat shims, sole maintainer, sole downstream consumer (piarch).

No user input required after all — the measurement decides it.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-s65y2) — atom neograph-ehuks.3

Pattern: **the `config['configurable']` carrier idiom hand-rolled inline where `_config_carrier` already provides it** — an inline `{**config, 'configurable': {**...}}` write instead of `_with_configurable`, or an inline read of the framework-minted run id instead of `run_id_of`.

This is the ticket's disease because the fix's two reuse targets ARE those carriers, and `_config_carrier.py`'s module docstring states the invariant outright: *"Every framework layer that stashes a value onto the config side-channel ... or reads the framework-minted run id routes through here, so the copy-not-mutate carrier idiom and the run-id read each live at ONE site."* Implementing s65y2 naively would add a 4th inline write (TRACE_ID) and a 2nd inline identity read, compounding it.

Scan commands (whole codebase, reproducible):
- writes: `grep -rn '"configurable": {\*\*\|configurable = {\*\*' src/neograph/*.py`
- reads:  `grep -rn 'get("configurable"\|\["configurable"\]' src/neograph/*.py`
Total instances of THIS pattern found: 3 (+1 adjacent violation).

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | runner.py:591 `_mark_stream_custom` | inline configurable WRITE | MIGRATE | `_with_configurable(config, **{StateKeys.STREAM_CUSTOM: True})`. `_mint_run_id`'s docstring says it 'Mirrors `_mark_stream_custom` EXACTLY' — so leaving one and fixing the other breaks the stated mirror. |
| 2 | runner.py:608 `_mint_run_id` | inline configurable WRITE | MIGRATE | Same idiom; this is the function the ticket extends, so it must be clean before TRACE_ID joins it. |
| 3 | runner.py:704 `_evict_run_cache` | inline READ of StateKeys.RUN_ID | MIGRATE | `run_id_of(config)` is the canonical reader and is named in the carrier docstring's invariant. This site bypasses it verbatim. |
| 4 | node.py:478-480 `run_isolated` | MUTATES caller's configurable | DEFER -> **neograph-syhr2** | Real copy-not-mutate violation but a different concern (testing helper, not identity, not the carrier idiom this ticket reuses). Filed P3. |

ALLOWLIST (scanned, deliberately not migrated): reads of `ORACLE_MODEL_OVERRIDE` (_agent_cycle.py:141, _dispatch.py:265/:299), `DI_INPUTS` (_llm_render.py:203), `CONFIG_INPUT` (runner.py:549), LangGraph's own `checkpoint_id` (runner.py:248/:989), the DI resolver's generic lookups (di.py:91/:167 — these ARE the canonical resolver), progress.py:73, and runner.py:101/:128 input-merge. The docstring's invariant names the run-id read specifically; these other keys have no canonical reader, and inventing one per key is a separate refactor, not this ticket's disease.

### Guard gap discovered
`runner.py` does not import `_config_carrier` AT ALL — all three sites hand-roll. The existing protection (TestTwinThinness, test_guards_llm_runtime.py:1804/:1833) only flags the re-inlined carrier when it appears in BOTH twins of a TABLED pair; these three are single, non-twin functions and sit in its blind spot. The sweep atom must add a guard covering non-twin sites, or the pattern returns.
## Architect Review (atom neograph-ehuks.4) — inline, adversarial

### 1. Problem statement correctness — LOW
Verified in source: `_mint_run_id` (runner.py:595) mints `uuid4().hex`; `_merge_observe_callbacks` (runner.py:656) constructs a bare `CallbackHandler()` which mints its own trace id. Two independent 32-hex identities, no relation. The ticket's downstream 404 evidence is consistent with this.

### 2. Derivation direction — LOW (plan is strictly better than the ticket asked for)
Deriving trace_id FROM run_id (not the reverse) leaves `_mint_run_id` and therefore `_run_cache`/`evict_run` untouched. Determinism is a bonus the ticket did not anticipate: the join is computable from a bare log line, retroactively. Predictability is not a security concern — run_id is not a secret today and trace ids are not credentials.

### 3. HIGH — the external half of the acceptance is NOT provable offline
The acceptance is 'a structlog run_id can be joined to the Langfuse trace for the same run'. That decomposes into three sub-claims:
 (a) trace_id == create_trace_id(seed=run_id), deterministic — IN-PROCESS, fully testable.
 (b) every node_start/node_complete line carries that trace_id — IN-PROCESS, fully testable.
 (c) Langfuse actually records the trace UNDER that id — **EXTERNAL side effect. Not testable without real LANGFUSE_* keys and a live instance.**
Per the locus rule, (a)+(b) green is proof of the sub-claims, NOT of the acceptance. Reporting them as 'run_id now joins to the trace' would be the category error the rule names.
Mitigating evidence (strong but not proof): the langfuse SDK's own `CallbackHandler` docstring gives `CallbackHandler(trace_context={'trace_id': 'my-trace-id'})` as the documented usage for exactly this, and the implementation stores it (`self.trace_context = trace_context`) and forwards it (`trace_context=self.trace_context`) into span creation.
CONSEQUENCE FOR CLOSURE: the implement atom may close on (a)+(b)+a handler-construction assertion. **neograph-s65y2 itself must NOT be closed as done** until (c) is verified against a live Langfuse; it stays open/blocked with the live path explicitly recorded as unproven. Infeasible integration blocks closure; it does not lower the bar.

### 4. MEDIUM — scope: option 3 does not belong in this ticket
The ticket lists three options; 'The request' ('make the two the same id, or make each discoverable from the other') is FULLY satisfied by 1+2, which are one coherent change. Option 3 (caller `correlation_id`) is a different thing: new PUBLIC config surface, which per AGENTS.md drags in website/docs updates ('don't forget to update website content when API surfaces change'). Bundling it with a dependency-floor bump and 3 carrier migrations makes one unreviewable commit.
DECISION: implement 1+2 here; split option 3 into its own bead NOW (not 'later'). This is scoping a distinct feature the ticket itself frames as an alternative, not deferring a fix.

### 5. MEDIUM — the scan's 3 MIGRATE rows must land in THIS change, plus a guard
runner.py:591/:608/:704 violate `_config_carrier`'s documented one-site invariant, and the naive implementation adds a 4th. They are prerequisites, not adjacent cleanup. The existing protection (TestTwinThinness) is TWIN-TABLED only and structurally cannot see these single functions — so a new guard covering non-twin carrier re-inlines is required, or the pattern returns the moment this ticket looks away.

### 6. LOW — absent-trace branches must stay honest
`_merge_observe_callbacks` has two early-outs: observe off / keys missing, and the dedupe branch (user wired their own handler). Neither may stash or emit a trace_id — in the dedupe case OUR derived id would not match THEIR handler's trace, and logging it would be a silent lie. Emit the field only on the path where we attached.

### 7. LOW — pin
Measured, not inferred: floor must move `langfuse>=3.0` -> `>=3.11` in both pyproject sites. Safe at 0.x with a single downstream consumer.

### Verdict: NEEDS_REFINEMENT
No unknowns requiring the user. Two structural corrections: split option 3 out (#4), and write the closure constraint from #3 into the plan so the ticket is not falsely marked done.

## Implemented (atom neograph-ehuks.7)

**Step 1 — carrier debt paid first (the scan's 3 MIGRATE rows).** runner.py now imports `_with_configurable` + `run_id_of` (it imported neither):
- `_mark_stream_custom` and `_mint_run_id`: 3-line inline carrier -> a single `_with_configurable(...)` call each. The two move together because `_mint_run_id`'s docstring claims it mirrors `_mark_stream_custom` exactly.

## STATUS: implementation landed (a1ed56b), task deliberately NOT closed

Per the architect review's closure constraint (finding #3, HIGH), the acceptance has three sub-claims:
 (a) trace_id == create_trace_id(seed=run_id) — PROVEN in-process.
 (b) every node_start/node_complete line carries it — PROVEN in-process.
 (c) **Langfuse actually records the trace UNDER that id — UNPROVEN.**

(c) is an external side effect requiring live LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY/PUBLIC_KEY and a reachable instance. Nothing in the offline suite can establish it; the strongest in-process evidence is that the handler is constructed with `trace_context={'trace_id': <derived>}`, which the langfuse SDK documents for exactly this purpose and stores/forwards into span creation.

Infeasible integration BLOCKS closure — it does not lower the bar. So this bead stays OPEN. Do not close it on the green suite.

### To close it
Run any pipeline with real Langfuse keys and `observe=True`, take a `trace_id` off a node_start line, and confirm `GET /api/public/traces/{trace_id}` returns 200 with that run's spans (the same call that 404s on a run_id today). Record the result here, then close.

- neograph-lwssj — caller `correlation_id` (ticket option 3), dep-wired to land after this.
- neograph-syhr2 — the `setdefault('configurable', ...)` copy-not-mutate sites this ticket's guard does not cover.
## Sub-claim (c) PROVEN LIVE — 2026-07-29

Ran a real scripted pipeline with `observe=True` against the production Langfuse instance using the repo's .env credentials:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| run_id on node lifecycle lines | 29f7ef4260034ea8bf1bc13e704139d3 (stable across all 4 lines) |
| trace_id on the same lines | 95b5e754c31d3b4ba2881269ce33c3ad (stable) |

The control is the important row: it reproduces exactly the symptom this ticket was filed on ('a run_id taken from a real eval log returns 404 against GET /api/public/traces/{id}'), and shows the derived id resolving where the run_id does not.

### Made repeatable, not a one-off
`tests/test_observe_trace_live.py` — 2 tests, live-keyed, committed at 5956e39. Skips without LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY + LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY. AGENTS.md documents the run command AND states that the skip is a known hole rather than coverage, so a green `make quality` is never mistaken for evidence about the live path (the neograph-x75es lesson).
Live: 2 passed in 25.5s. Default gate: 3106 passed, 88 skipped (was 86), 0 failed.

title: Refine neograph-c265k per review
description:
Adjust the implementation plan in neograph-c265k's design field to resolve the THREE MEDIUM
findings from the architect review (atom neograph-dw76v.12). Use the EXISTING research -- do NOT
re-research. Output is an updated design field (append a "Refinements (post-review)" section;

**RC1 -- Step 3 turns an UNRELATED guard RED ON SUCCESS, and the polarity contract omits it.**
`tests/test_guards_any_audit.py` keys `NEOGRAPH_ERROR_ALLOWLIST` by LINE NUMBER (the scanner
computes `key = f"{py_file.name}:{node.lineno}"` and tests membership, :687-688). Three entries

insertion point (after `primary_shape`, ~line 246). Proven empirically: even a 5-line stub moves

`TestPublicFunctionsRaiseNeographError::test_no_bare_stdlib_raises` fails with 3 offenders the
moment Step 3 lands. Blast radius is exactly those 3 (a grep for `"<file>.py:<n>"`-shaped keys
finds nothing for the other five touched files).

allowlist keys in the SAME commit, DERIVED from the post-insertion file (read the real line
numbers; do not guess or arithmetic them), and adding `tests/test_guards_any_audit.py` to the
MUST-be-GREEN list in the polarity contract. Explicitly FORBID the two wrong fixes: relocating
the predicate to the end of `modifiers.py` (it would abandon the "beside the table" placement
the plan correctly argues for) and deleting or loosening any allowlist entry. There is no
insertion point above line 281 that avoids the shift, so re-pinning is mandatory.

hit it when `primary_shape` was added. Same file, same three keys, same cause.

positives, so closing the hole is free.

lexically inside a `match_case` whose pattern names `PrimaryShape.EACH` (scan pattern, guard and
body)", and adding a synthetic POSITIVE meta-test for the `.get` form inside an EACH arm.

`ms.each is not None and ms.oracle is not None`. That spelling is in LIVE use for adjacent

project's modifier-combo lesson names as binding.
Resolve by: adding rule R3 -- a `BoolOp` whose set of `<attr> is not None` slot reads, restricted
to the modifier vocabulary {each, oracle, loop, operator, portal}, equals exactly {each, oracle}.
The reviewer RAN it: ZERO hits on the current tree, so it needs no allowlist, and it spares
`modifiers.py:962/968/978/980` (each+loop, oracle+loop, portal+each, portal+oracle) and
`_validation_inputs.py:140` by construction. Add positive and negative meta-tests for it.

## LOW findings -- adopt if cheap, record the decision either way

(a) but FALSE for assertion (c), which is an EQUALITY over `FUSION_READERS`: if Phase 7
(neograph-s7zt3.10) deletes `_agent_spec.py`'s fusion check, that file leaves the derived set and

implementer the opposite. Correct the note, and put the "when a consumer legitimately disappears,
SHRINK the literal" instruction in the new guard's docstring, mirroring the PENDING ratchet
wording in tests/test_guards_combo_decomposition_consumers.py.

RL2 -- Predicate spelling could be strictly more robust at zero cost:
`mods.get("each") is not None and mods.get("oracle") is not None` is exactly equivalent to
`"each" in mods and "oracle" in mods` under `classify_modifiers`'s documented key-only-when-set
contract, but is also correct for any dict carrying None values, and it makes site 1 a literal
collapse rather than a re-spelling. Still one `BoolOp`, so assertion (b)'s "exactly one R1 hit"

acceptance signal.** Step 4 introduces `_raise_no_agent_spec_lowering(item, combo) -> NoReturn`,

restating step 11's acceptance signal as **zero DISPATCH-CONTEXT `ModifierCombo` occurrences**

title: Sweep verification for neograph-c265k
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-c265k
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-c265k`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-c265k)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-c265k --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-c265k sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-c265k
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-c265k` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-c265k/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-c265k
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-c265k)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-c265k --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-c265k --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-c265k/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-c265k codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). description:

executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-tjpn4/`:

     ```

     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>

   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |

   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope

title: Single-source the Each x Oracle fusion test (is_each_oracle_fused) -- 5 open-coded copies after Phase 3
description:
Filed from the architect review of neograph-s7zt3.7 (finding L2, atom neograph-g330l.4, 2026-07-28).

## Problem

`(primary, has_operator)` deliberately does NOT distinguish `EACH` from `EACH_ORACLE`
(`docs/design/agent-spec-rewrite-2026-07-27.md:253` states this as a design decision), so every
consumer that must tell a fused Each x Oracle node from a plain Each one uses the co-presence
idiom `"oracle" in mods` inside its `case PrimaryShape.EACH:` arm
(`agent-spec-rewrite-2026-07-27.md:115` prescribes it; `compiler.py:622` already does it).

After neograph-s7zt3.7 lands there will be FIVE hand-written instances of that test:
`compiler.py:622`, `_state_write.py`, `state.py` (x2 -- the dict-form and single-type output
blocks), and `_subconstruct.py` (negated, as the `has_each` exclusion). That is the same
duplicated-source-of-truth shape that grew into the neograph-s7zt3 epic in the first place --
just at a smaller scale and one level down (fusion detection rather than combo decomposition).

## Why it was deferred, not fixed in s7zt3.7

s7zt3.7 is a zero-behavior-change migration and the docs are authoritative on the idiom, so
adopting it there was correct. Research risk R5 explicitly said a table-shape change "needs its
own bead + doc update, not a drive-by" -- this is that bead.

## Proposed fix (cheapest option; needs NO ComboDecomposition shape change)

Add a named predicate beside `primary_shape` / `COMBO_DECOMPOSITION` in `modifiers.py`:

    def is_each_oracle_fused(mods: Mapping[str, object]) -> bool: ...

and have the five sites call it. It stays a modifier-PRESENCE read (which the Core Invariant
explicitly carves out of the decomposition table), keeps the single definition site in
`modifiers.py`, and gives the concept one name instead of five open-coded spellings.

Rejected alternative: adding a `fused: bool` field to `ComboDecomposition`. That contradicts
`agent-spec-rewrite-2026-07-27.md:253`'s explicit decision that the decomposition tuple does not
distinguish the fusion; changing it needs a doc amendment first.

## Sequencing

Do this AFTER neograph-s7zt3.7 (which creates the fifth instance) and consider it alongside
neograph-s7zt3.10 (Phase 7), which changes what the five fusion combos mean.

## Acceptance

- One definition of the fusion test in `modifiers.py`; all five call sites read it.
- A structural guard (or an extension of s7zt3.7's anti-regrowth guard) pinning that no sixth
  open-coded spelling appears.
- Zero behavior change; full gates green.
design:
## Core Invariant

"Is this item the fused Each x Oracle node?" is answered by exactly ONE named predicate in
`modifiers.py` -- a modifier-PRESENCE read over the `classify_modifiers` dict, never a second
`ModifierCombo` enumeration and never a change to `COMBO_DECOMPOSITION`'s
`(primary, has_operator)` shape -- and every consumer that must split a fused node from a plain
Each one CALLS it, in either polarity, with zero behavior change.

## The settled design question (predicate name, signature, location, argument)

```python
# src/neograph/modifiers.py, immediately AFTER primary_shape (currently line 246)

def is_each_oracle_fused(mods: Mapping[str, object]) -> bool:
    """True when this item carries BOTH Each and Oracle -- the fused M x N Send
    topology `compiler.py`'s `_add_each_oracle_fused` lowers.

    A modifier-PRESENCE read, deliberately NOT a decomposition question:
    COMBO_DECOMPOSITION folds EACH_ORACLE/EACH_ORACLE_OPERATOR to primary=EACH
    (the fusion is a Node concern), so a consumer standing in a PrimaryShape.EACH
    arm needs this second, orthogonal test to tell a fused node from a plain Each
    one. `mods` is the dict `classify_modifiers` returns; it holds a key only when
    that modifier slot is set, so membership IS non-None-ness.

    Inside a PrimaryShape.EACH arm the `"each"` half is redundant-but-true (every
    EACH-primary combo contains `each`) -- it is kept so the ONE definition also
    reads correctly at `compiler.py`'s pre-`match` call site, and so the concept
    has one spelling rather than two. Do not "optimize" a call site back to a bare
    `"oracle" in mods` (neograph-c265k).
    """
    return "each" in mods and "oracle" in mods
```

- **Name**: `is_each_oracle_fused` (as the ticket proposes; also already referenced by the
  in-code comment at `_agent_spec.py:994-999`).
- **Argument**: `mods`, not `item` and not `combo`. All six sites already hold `mods` from
  `classify_modifiers` (so no re-classification cost, mirroring `primary_shape`'s own
  "call this only where the caller does NOT already hold a classify result" guidance); a
  `combo`-based form would be a combo-member enumeration and would violate the Phase-3 Core
  Invariant; an `item`-based form would force a redundant `classify_modifiers` at all six.
- **Location**: `modifiers.py`, directly after `primary_shape` -- the same "named helper beside
  the table" neighborhood, so the whole vocabulary is readable in one screen.
- **Visibility**: INTERNAL. `primary_shape`/`COMBO_DECOMPOSITION` are not in
  `neograph/__init__.__all__`; neither is this. No `__init__` wiring.
- **Both polarities are pure substitutions** because inside a `PrimaryShape.EACH` arm
  `"each" in mods` is guaranteed True, so `is_each_oracle_fused(mods) == ("oracle" in mods)`
  there, and `not is_each_oracle_fused(sub_mods)` == `"oracle" not in sub_mods` there.
  Only `compiler.py:619` (pre-`match`) needs the both-halves form -- and it already writes it.

## Implementation Plan

### Step 0 -- baseline
`uv run --extra dev --extra agent-spec pytest` green (dw76v.1 already established it).
Re-run the census before editing: the six sites and their line numbers move.

### Step 1 -- RED FIRST: the anti-regrowth guard
New file `tests/test_guards_each_oracle_fusion_predicate.py`, pure `ast`, no `re`
(exempt by construction from `tests/test_guards_meta.py` discipline -- copy the header note
from `tests/test_guards_combo_decomposition_consumers.py:50-53`). Two scan rules, both
required, both already SIMULATED by the researcher against the real tree:

- **R1 (expression-level co-presence)**: an `ast.BoolOp` in which the set of modifier names
  membership-tested / `.get()`-ed is a subset of `{"each","oracle"}`, contains `"oracle"`, and
  which also contains either the `"each"` test or a `PrimaryShape.EACH` attribute reference.
  -> catches `compiler.py:619` and the NEGATED `_subconstruct.py:98`.
  The `<= {"each","oracle"}` subset condition is load-bearing: it is what spares
  `testing/scaffold.py:520` (`n.get("oracle") or n.get("each") or n.get("loop") or
  n.get("operator")` -- a serialized-node "has any modifier" filter, a false positive under a
  naive scanner).
- **R2 (context-level)**: an `"oracle"` membership test lexically inside an `ast.match_case`
  whose PATTERN names `PrimaryShape.EACH` (scan the pattern, the `guard`, and the body).
  -> catches `state.py:559` (the guard itself), `state.py:621`, `_state_write.py:84`,
  `_agent_spec.py:1000`.

Assertions:
1. **(a) no open-coded fusion test** anywhere under `src/neograph` EXCEPT the owner

## Core Invariant

"What does this ModifierCombo decompose into" is answered ONLY by
`COMBO_DECOMPOSITION`/`PrimaryShape`/`SUB_CONSTRUCT_UNSUPPORTED_COMBOS` in `modifiers.py`, so
`_agent_spec.py`'s export dispatch READS that table instead of re-enumerating combo members —
while every user-visible export outcome (which combos lower, which raise, and the exact error
type/site/text) stays byte-identical, because deciding what the five fusion combos MEAN belongs
to Phase 7 (neograph-s7zt3.10), not to this migration.

## Implementation Plan

Reuse-first. Nothing new is invented: the table exists (`modifiers.py:107-245`), the dispatch
shape exists (`compiler.py:516-587` / `:601-706`), the zero-change snapshot harness exists
(`tests/test_agent_spec_refactor_snapshot.py`), the Construct-side behavioural net exists
(`test_agent_spec_export.py:850-1005`), and the anti-regrowth guard exists
(`tests/test_guards_combo_decomposition_consumers.py`). This task moves ONE function onto the
table and shrinks ONE allowlist.

### Phase A — write-tests FIRST (both must be GREEN before and after; note the polarity)

Unlike Phase 3 (whose guard had to be RED first), the anti-regrowth guard is ALREADY green and
must STAY green. Both new artifacts here pin TODAY's behaviour.

1. **Pin the uncovered fallthrough raise (risk T4 — zero coverage today).** New test class in
   `tests/test_agent_spec_export.py` (where the Construct-item export contract already lives),
   parametrized over the five fallthrough combos — EACH_ORACLE, EACH_OPERATOR, ORACLE_OPERATOR,
   LOOP_OPERATOR, EACH_ORACLE_OPERATOR — asserting `ConfigurationError` with the exact message
   `"has modifier combination {COMBO} — no Agent Spec lowering yet"` plus `expected=`
   `"BARE, ORACLE, EACH, LOOP, or OPERATOR"`. Derive the combo list from
   `test_agent_spec_matrix.UNSUPPORTED_COMBOS - {PORTAL, PORTAL_OPERATOR}` so it cannot drift
   from the partition. Build the nodes with `Node.scripted(...) | Modifier()` (LOOP_OPERATOR
   needs same-type in/out, empirically confirmed). Also assert the SEPARATE dispatch-mode-Portal
   message is NOT what fires for these.
2. **Close the byte-snapshot's arm gap (risk T5).** Extend
   `test_agent_spec_refactor_snapshot.py`'s `REPRESENTATIVE_CELLS` with GREEN each/loop/operator
   cells (e.g. `scripted-each-single`, `scripted-each-dict`, `scripted-each-context`,
   `think-each-single`, `scripted-loop-single`, `scripted-loop-dict`, `think-loop-single`,

title: Sweep verification for neograph-s7zt3.7
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-s7zt3.7
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-s7zt3.7`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-s7zt3.7)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-s7zt3.7 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-s7zt3.7 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-s7zt3.7
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-s7zt3.7` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-s7zt3.7/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-s7zt3.7
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-s7zt3.7)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-s7zt3.7 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-s7zt3.7 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-s7zt3.7/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-s7zt3.7 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Phase 7: implement the 5 non-Portal fusion ModifierCombo values at the Node level (EACH_OPERATOR, ORACLE_OPERATOR, LOOP_OPERATOR, EACH_ORACLE, EACH_ORACLE_OPERATOR)
description:
Master doc: docs/design/agent-spec-portal-master-architecture-2026-07-27.md §5 (each combo's row) + Build Plan Phase 7. These 5 combos currently hit _lower_construct_item's generic 'no lowering yet' ConfigurationError on export, and have zero round-trip fixtures. All 5 are confirmed glue-only (no new pyagentspec primitive needed) -- compose existing lowering functions:
EACH_OPERATOR/LOOP_OPERATOR (single wrap, do these FIRST): _lower_each/_lower_loop + _lower_operator's pause composite chained after.
ORACLE_OPERATOR (single wrap, alongside the above pair): _lower_oracle + _lower_operator.
EACH_ORACLE (two proven wraps composed, do THIRD): MapNode whose inner subflow IS what _lower_oracle already produces un-fused -- nest Oracle's variant-fan-out+merge Flow inside the Each MapNode's subflow.
EACH_ORACLE_OPERATOR (three-way, do LAST): same fusion as EACH_ORACLE plus the Operator pause composite chained after.
Each combo needs its own new round-trip fixture and its own matching loader.py recognition-walk extension (see the separate loader.py task) landed in lockstep -- an export-only combo with no import support fails the matrix's round-trip axis. Depends on Phase 3 (all consumers migrated) and Phase 4 (Construct-item fix, for consistency).
design:
## Core Invariant
Every one of the five fusion combos must be lowered AND recognized by COMPOSING the
existing per-modifier functions under a decomposition read from the single
`COMBO_DECOMPOSITION` / `_COMBO_MAP` tables in `modifiers.py` — never by a second,
locally re-derived enumeration of what a combo means, and never with an export arm
whose import counterpart does not land in the same change.

## Implementation Plan (REFINED per architect review, atom neograph-nmyw7.12)

Gate command everywhere: **`uv run pytest` (bare)**. There is no `dev` extra.
Every step is guard-first / TDD: write the failing test, WATCH IT FAIL, then fix.
Scope is the NODE level only (Construct level = neograph-s7zt3.11).

### Evidence rules that bind every fixture in this ticket (review M1 + M2)
- **R1 — full serialization is REQUIRED, not avoided.** The earlier claim that
  `Flow.from_dict(flow.to_dict())` is broken for all exports is REFUTED (probed twice,
  independently: BARE/OPERATOR/LOOP/ORACLE/EACH all round-trip cleanly). Every new fixture
  MUST assert `Flow.from_dict(flow.to_dict())` survival, copying
  `tests/test_agent_spec_portal_operator.py::test_flow_from_dict_to_dict_round_trip_then_reimport`.
  Do NOT settle for the in-memory-Flow-only path.
- **R2 — the four `*_OPERATOR` combos need a checkpointer to run.** `build_test_compile_kwargs()`
  supplies none, and an Operator node raises `CompileError: Operator modifier requires a
  checkpointer`. Use `compile(imported, **build_test_compile_kwargs(checkpointer=MemorySaver()))`
  (the helper merges `**extra`) plus a deliberately-FALSE `when` condition so the run completes.
  State in each fixture's docstring that **pause/resume semantics under a fan-out barrier is NOT
  claimed** by these fixtures — only that the modifier survives export -> import -> compile -> run.
- **R3 — combo preservation must be asserted explicitly.** Every per-combo fixture asserts
  `classify_modifiers(<reimported item>)[0] is ModifierCombo.<X>`. Structure-shape asserts alone
  cannot distinguish a correct import from a silent downgrade.

### Step 0 — fix the `@node` map_over/Operator silent drop (decorators.py only)
`decorators.py:661` and `:672` early-return from the two `map_over` branches BEFORE the
`interrupt_when` tail at `:701`, so `@node(map_over=..., interrupt_when=...)` silently
classifies as EACH (and the fused form as EACH_ORACLE). Operator is the ONLY modifier
dropped — `map_over`+`loop_when` (`:403`) and `portal`+`map_over` (`:416`) already raise
ConstructError. Confirmed in scope by the review (decorators.py-only = layer-compliant; a
silent seam, which the North Star forbids deferring).

- Write the two failing assertions FIRST:
  `classify_modifiers(...)[0] is ModifierCombo.EACH_OPERATOR` and `... is EACH_ORACLE_OPERATOR`.
- Let both `map_over` branches FALL THROUGH to the shared Operator tail instead of returning,
  re-registering sidecar/param_res on each new instance exactly as the tail already does.
- **The fused branch's `return _apply_eager_oracle_gen_type(n)` must become
  `n = _apply_eager_oracle_gen_type(n)`** (review M6). A discarded rebind is the same
  silent-drop class this step exists to remove.
- **NAME AND ASSERT the second effect** (review M6): both early-returns also sit BEFORE the
  eager `_register_node_scripted` block at `:776`, so falling through newly sets `scripted_fn`
  on EVERY `map_over` `@node`. Probed at HEAD: `@node(map_over=...)` yields `scripted_fn=None`
  while `@node(interrupt_when=...)` yields a registered name. This is almost certainly a latent
  FIX — a bare `@node(map_over=)` dropped into a declarative `Construct(nodes=[...])` currently
  dies with "Scripted function 'None' not registered". Add that declarative-Construct Each case
  as an explicit test so the change lands NAMED, not as an unnamed side effect.
- Three-surface parity: assert the programmatic `| Each | Operator` and declarative surfaces
  still classify identically (they already do — this step brings `@node` up to them).

### Step 1 — EACH_OPERATOR + LOOP_OPERATOR + ORACLE_OPERATOR: ONE change, THREE fixture sets
Bundling is CONFIRMED compatible with the maintainer's lockstep directive: that directive binds
import<->export PER COMBO, not one-combo-per-landing, and bundling satisfies it by construction
(one hoisted postlude + one shared lookahead covers all three on both sides simultaneously).
Land three SEPARATE fixture sets failing-first so one green run cannot mask one combo.

**Export** (`_agent_spec.py::_lower_construct_item`), mirroring `compiler.py:584-585`/`:703-704`:
1. Delete the `if decomp.has_operator: _raise_no_agent_spec_lowering(item, combo)` guards from
   the ORACLE (`:987`), EACH (`:1001`) and LOOP (`:1006`) arms. Keep EACH's
   `is_each_oracle_fused(mods)` half until Step 2. Leave the PORTAL arm untouched.
2. Hoist the BARE arm's Operator composite (`:1019-1026`) OUT of the match into ONE
   unconditional postlude after it: each arm BINDS its 6-tuple instead of returning, then
   `if decomp.has_operator:` builds `check, extra_nodes, extra_control = _lower_operator(item,
   mods["operator"])`, prepends `ControlFlowEdge(f"{item.name}__to_operator_check",
   from_node=<arm primary>, to_node=check)`, returns `[*arm_nodes, check, *extra_nodes]` with
   `primary=check`, and keeps the arm's `data_node` + `input_targets` unchanged.
   **Both hazards named in the arm's own comment are cleared** (review Q4, verified): the postlude
   goes AFTER the match so no `case ... if ...` guard is introduced (`case _`/`assert_never` stays
   unreachable — no ConfigurationError->AssertionError swap), and it hoists the LOWERING, not a
   raise, so the PORTAL arm still raises its own dispatch-mode message from inside the arm.
3. Delete the now-stale `:980-984` and `:1014-1018` comments; re-check
   `_raise_no_agent_spec_lowering`'s docstring ("four arms") and its `expected=` string, which
   no longer describe reachable state.

**Import** (`loader.py::_group_flow_items`) — the review-2 §6 variable-length lookahead:
4. Add ONE shared `_trailing_operator(nodes, j, primary_spec, flow)` helper: `nodes[j]` must carry
   `_MARK_MODIFIER == "operator"`, a real `ControlFlowEdge primary_spec -> nodes[j]` must exist,
   and `nodes[j] --from_branch="pause"--> nodes[j+1]` must exist; on match it consumes 2 nodes and
   contributes `"operator"` to the group's recognized name set. Structural confirmation only —
   never marker trust. Call it from the each / oracle / loop branches AND **rewrite the existing
   bare+operator branch (`:631-641`) onto it** — consolidation, not a sixth bespoke pattern.
5. Convert the walk from ad-hoc `kind` strings to recognize->classify: emit the recognized
   `frozenset[str]` of modifier names and classify via a new `combo_for_modifier_names(names)` in
   `modifiers.py`, then dispatch in `from_agent_spec` on `COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[combo].primary` +
   `.has_operator` — the exact mirror of the export dispatch. Reconstruction reuses
   `_reconstruct_each_node` / `_reconstruct_oracle_group` / `_reconstruct_loop_item` unchanged,
   with `| Operator(when=spec["when"])` as the trailing compose (copy `_reconstruct_operator_item:558`;
   `Operator.when` is always a str, no `parse_condition`).
   - `combo_for_modifier_names` MUST be **fail-loud on a miss** (review LOW): mirror
     `classify_modifiers`' `.get()` + `ConstructError.build` shape — a foreign/hand-edited Flow can
     yield an unmapped set like `{"each","loop"}` and must not produce a bare `KeyError`. Add a
     should-fail import test for that. `TestComboMapMonopoly` counts DICT LITERALS, not readers, so
     a third reader is guard-legal (`ModifierSet.combo` is already a second one).
   - `loader.py` must import AND USE `COMBO_DECOMPOSITION`/`PrimaryShape`, not merely the accessor:
     the anti-regrowth guard's assertion (b) requires an imported-and-used TABLE_SYMBOL and (c)'s
     census keys on it.
6. Add `"loader.py"` to `MIGRATED` in `tests/test_guards_combo_decomposition_consumers.py:68`. Its
   docstring at `:90-92` already pre-declares this move; assertion (c) is an EQUALITY census and
   WILL fail loud otherwise.

**Fixtures + matrix**:
7. One new test module per combo (or one class each in a shared module) copying
   `tests/test_agent_spec_portal_operator.py`'s structure: export-shape asserts + an
   "unchanged when ungated" zero-behavior-change assert + a `TestRoundTrip` class built on
   `tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py:87`'s programmatic `Node.scripted(...) | Modifier(...)`
   pattern — subject to **R1, R2, R3** above.
8. Move the three combos from `UNSUPPORTED_COMBOS` to `SUPPORTED_COMBOS`
   (`tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py:108-127`) and extend `build_cell` with their branches.
9. **`_generate_cells` (`:350`) MUST be extended too** (review M4). Its if-chain crosses
   `ORACLE_CONFIGS` only for `combo is ModifierCombo.ORACLE` and adds the `"context"` shape only
   for `combo is ModifierCombo.EACH`; everything else falls to the `else` branch (single/dict
   only). Extending only `build_cell` silently yields ZERO merge_prompt cells for
   ORACLE_OPERATOR / EACH_ORACLE / EACH_ORACLE_OPERATOR and no context cell for EACH_OPERATOR —
   under-crossing the very axis that file's docstring names as "the sdfgz disease".
   **DERIVE membership from the table, never a second hand-typed combo list**: add a
   `modifier_names_for_combo(combo) -> frozenset[str]` inverse accessor in `modifiers.py`
   (a `_COMBO_MAP` reader, guard-legal like the one above), then cross `ORACLE_CONFIGS` iff
   `"oracle" in names` and add `"context"` iff `"each" in names`.
10. **Cell classification is a DECISION PROCEDURE, not an outcome mandate** (review M5). For each
    newly generated cell:
      - GREEN iff `to_agent_spec` AND `from_agent_spec` both succeed;
      - UNREPRESENTABLE iff `build_cell` raises `ConstructError`;
      - otherwise **STOP AND ESCALATE** — a cell that builds but fails export belongs in neither
        bucket, and a non-empty `RED_EXPORT` is a FINDING, not a bucket to route around.
    Probe **EACH_ORACLE in agent/act mode first** (Design-B AgentNode variants nested inside a
    MapNode subflow) — flagged as the most likely third-state cell; nobody has probed it.
11. **Strengthen the matrix round-trip axis** (review M3): `TestAgentSpecRoundTripMatrix::test_round_trip`
    (`:582-597`) asserts only `isinstance(imported, Construct)` and `imported.nodes`, so moving
    EACH_OPERATOR into SUPPORTED goes GREEN even if loader.py reimports it as plain EACH — the
    vacuously-green hazard, import side. Add a combo-preservation assertion to that test. Without
    it, the matrix cannot discharge the lockstep rule this plan leans on it for.
12. Fix the file's stale `--extra agent-spec` docstring command to bare `uv run pytest`.

### Step 2 — EACH_ORACLE (Node level)
**Export**: extend `_lower_each` with an OPTIONAL caller-lowered body group — copy the seam
`_lower_loop(node, loop, body)` already uses — so the fused arm passes what
`_lower_oracle(item, mods["oracle"])` returns and `_lower_each` builds the subflow around it.
Probe-verified subflow shape: `StartNode(inputs=inner_inputs) -> merge` as the single start edge
(pyagentspec requires exactly one), plus `_lower_oracle`'s own variant->merge control edges, its
fan-in edges passed as `data_flow_connections=`, plus `merge -> EndNode`. The inner merge may keep
the MapNode's name (verified). In `_lower_construct_item`, split the fusion out BEFORE the match
with `is_each_oracle_fused(mods)` exactly as `compiler.py:703` does, returning the EACH arm's tuple
shape. Keep the fused path INSIDE `_lower_each` and keep the spellings
`_is_translation_eligible(node)`, `_node_translation(node)`, `inputs=inner_inputs` (pinned by
`tests/test_guards_agent_spec_lowering.py:384`); composing existing lowerings also keeps
`EXPECTED_NODE_SITES = 6` intact.

**Import**: teach the walk's `each` branch to inspect `map_node.subflow`'s non-Start/End nodes for
the `oracle` marker + shared `_MARK_GROUP_ID`; on match contribute `{"each","oracle"}` and
reconstruct via the EXISTING `_reconstruct_oracle_group(inner_nodes, map_node.subflow, {})` piped
`| Each(over=..., key=...)`.
**Element-type decision made UP FRONT** (review LOW, do not discover this mid-implementation):
`_reconstruct_each_node` recovers the fan-out receiver's element type by un-grouping dotted
Properties off the INNER spec (`loader.py:509-512`), while `_reconstruct_oracle_group` derives
inputs from the merge node's data edges + prompt marker — the two do not compose. **Decision: the
fused import applies `_dict_form_inputs_from_props` to the FIRST VARIANT node's inputs** (the fused
analogue of "the inner spec"). Pin it failing-first with an explicit assertion that the producer's
`list[X]` element type equals the reimported receiver's type, or neograph-3lk2l regresses silently
inside the fusion.
Then move EACH_ORACLE to `SUPPORTED_COMBOS` and classify its cells per step 10.

### Step 3 — EACH_ORACLE_OPERATOR (Node level)
No new code path: Step 1's unconditional postlude composes with Step 2's fused arm, and Step 1's
`_trailing_operator` helper already folds the pause triple onto the fused MapNode. Deliverable is
the failing-first round-trip fixture (under R1/R2/R3), the matrix move + cell classification, and an
explicit assertion that ALL THREE modifiers survive export -> import.

### Step 4 — consolidation gate
Full `uv run pytest` + `uv run ruff check src tests` + `uv run mypy src` on the MERGED tree (not
per-step scoped runs), against the recorded baseline of 3831 passed / 0 failed. Plus
`uv run --extra mcp-examples pytest tests/test_mcp_examples_e2e.py` untouched.

### Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE (do not fix here, do not assert against)
- **Construct-level** EACH_OPERATOR / ORACLE_OPERATOR / LOOP_OPERATOR: these START EXPORTING as a
  side effect of the unconditional postlude (Phase 4 routes Construct items through the same
  dispatch). Do NOT add an artificial `isinstance(item, Node)` gate to withhold it — that would
  re-introduce the asymmetry this epic removes. Smoke-check it does not crash; fixtures + matrix
  cells belong to **neograph-s7zt3.11**. EACH_ORACLE / EACH_ORACLE_OPERATOR on a Construct stay
  rejected by the `SUB_CONSTRUCT_UNSUPPORTED_COMBOS` gate that runs BEFORE the dispatch
  (`_agent_spec.py:965`) — unchanged.
- **Export topology** (Operator/Loop check node bypasses the body; pause node has no outgoing edge;
  fused Each variants have no inbound control edge): PRE-EXISTING, filed as **neograph-s7zt3.15**.
  No new fixture may assert foreign-executable semantics the export does not have.
- **Dispatch-mode Portal**: permanent scope boundary, PORTAL arm keeps raising.
