title: Phase 8: extend the 5 fusion combos to the Construct level
description:
Master doc: docs/design/agent-spec-portal-master-architecture-2026-07-27.md, Build Plan Phase 8. CORRECTED 2026-07-27 -- the probe (docs/design/architecture-audit-phase8-design-gap-probe-2026-07-27.md) initially claimed ORACLE_OPERATOR-on-Construct needs a genuinely new variant-generation architecture because 'Construct-level Oracle has no .model concept to swap, unlike Node-level's per-variant model swap.' This is FALSE, caught by maintainer pushback and verified against real code: _wire_oracle (_wiring.py:216) is explicitly 'Shared Oracle wiring used by both Node and Construct paths' -- its oracle_router already sets a per-variant StateKeys.ORACLE_MODEL override for ANY fanned-out target, and _subconstruct.py:176 already calls _inject_oracle_config to forward that override into the compiled sub-graph's config, which every LLM-mode node's dispatch (_dispatch.py/_agent_cycle.py) already reads generically via config.get('configurable', {}).get(StateKeys.ORACLE_MODEL_OVERRIDE, node.model). Construct-level Oracle ALREADY supports per-variant model swapping at the compile-to-LangGraph level, with zero new runtime design needed.

CORRECTED remaining scope: the real gap (if any) is narrower and Agent-Spec-representation-specific, not a runtime architecture gap -- does the Agent Spec EXPORT of a Construct-level Oracle need to record which of oracle.models each of the N sub-flow copies uses (mirroring how Node-level Oracle's models list is already recorded in _MARK_ORACLE_SPEC)? This needs its own small, scoped verification pass before implementation -- do NOT implement the probe's original 'N FlowNodes ignoring Oracle.models' framing, it was wrong.

Remaining confirmed-real items from the probe (verify these still hold independently, they weren't part of the models-swap error): _lower_each/_lower_loop/_lower_oracle hard-crash (AttributeError) on a Construct today at the AGENT SPEC EXPORT layer specifically (this is about _agent_spec.py's lowering functions, NOT the compiler.py runtime path just corrected above -- these are two different codepaths, don't conflate them). LOOP_OPERATOR/EACH_OPERATOR-on-Construct export are closeable with bounded, mechanical isinstance-dispatch fixes. _lower_operator is already Construct-safe (touches only .name). Depends on Phase 4 and Phase 7.
design:
## Core Invariant

A Construct used as ONE ITEM inside a parent Construct must survive the Agent Spec round
trip with EXACTLY the modifier combo it was written with AND its declared boundary port
(input/output) intact, such that the reimported parent STILL COMPILES -- and the
Node-vs-Construct difference must be absorbed in ONE seam per direction, never re-inlined
per modifier, per reconstructor, or per combo.

The boundary/compile half is not decoration. Without it the acceptance passes on a
Construct that has been gutted of its ports (verified: a BARE sub-Construct declared
input=A/output=B round-trips to input=None/output=None and the reimported parent then
fails to compile with "sub-construct has no output type"). An item that keeps its combo
but stops being a usable sub-construct is not what this ticket is for.

NOTE on the mirror: it is often asserted in this repo that EXPORT absorbs the difference
in exactly one seam (_lower_item_body). That is FALSE -- there are two FlowNode
construction sites, _agent_spec.py:141 and _agent_spec.py:199 (the Construct-variant arm
of _lower_oracle, which needs a distinct per-variant name). Filed separately. Do not
repeat the one-seam claim in code or guard docstrings.

## Scope (binding, set 2026-07-31)

IN  -- Agent Spec IMPORT of a modified sub-Construct: the FlowNode reconstruction seam and
       every row that needs it.
OUT -- LOOP / LOOP_OPERATOR on a Construct with DIFFERING boundary types. They fail at
       EXPORT (neograph-rh5fb) and cannot reach the seam. The MATCHING-boundary LOOP row
       is IN and REQUIRED -- it exports fine and then dies on import with the seam's own
       error, so it is a genuine red row.
OUT -- any export-side lowering change, including _lower_oracle's second FlowNode site.
IN, by explicit decision -- restoring the sub-Construct boundary inside the seam. This is
       NOT adjacent-defect creep (contrast rh5fb / p7dyq / 8zvd1, all correctly filed
       rather than bundled): it is a defect in the seam being built, it would be
       replicated at five call sites the instant the seam is hoisted, and the plan's own
       acceptance could not see it.

## Implementation Plan

1. RED FIRST. Add a Construct-level ROUND-TRIP suite (a sibling
   tests/test_agent_spec_construct_item_roundtrip.py, or extend
   tests/test_agent_spec_export.py::TestConstructItemModifierExport). For each row assert,
   in this order: (a) the reimported item is a Construct, (b) classify_modifiers(item)[0]
   equals the original combo, (c) its input/output boundary equals what was declared, and
   (d) THE REIMPORTED PARENT COMPILES. (d) is the outermost acceptance and the only one
   that catches a seam reconstructing shape but not port.

   Rows: BARE, OPERATOR, EACH, ORACLE, EACH_OPERATOR, ORACLE_OPERATOR, and
   matching-boundary LOOP. BARE and OPERATOR are NOT merely controls any more -- under (c)
   and (d) they start RED, because the boundary drop is live today. Expect
   red-then-green for them; a plan that leaves them green is testing the wrong thing.

   Round trip is OBJECT-LEVEL only -- to_agent_spec then from_agent_spec, with NO
   Flow.from_dict hop. Dict-form fan-in cannot survive JSON until neograph-8zvd1 lands;
   adding a JSON hop here would surface 8zvd1 and invite misdiagnosing it as a Phase 8 bug.
   Each requires key= (Each(over=...) alone raises a pydantic missing-field error).
   The matching-boundary LOOP row's docstring MUST state the boundary condition, so a
   passing matching-boundary test is never read as coverage of the differing-boundary case.

2. BUILD THE SEAM IN TWO LAYERS. One layer is not enough, because the two callers need
   different things (this is what makes disposition row 2 satisfiable):

     INNER  (subflow, name, from_spec) -> Construct
            recurse via the injected from_agent_spec, rename to name, and RESTORE the
            boundary: read the exported FlowNode/subflow Properties back through the same
            _agent_spec_props_to_type that _reconstruct_primitive_node already uses, and
            set input=/output= on the Construct. This is the single site that calls
            from_agent_spec on a sub-flow.
     OUTER  (spec_node, flow, output_types, from_spec) -> Construct
            unwrap the FlowNode, call INNER, and register the REAL boundary type into
            output_types under the item name. Today the BARE arm registers None there, so
            a downstream consumer's fan-in reconstruction is typeless too -- fix that here.

   The BARE arm then CALLS OUTER instead of holding the special case.
   _flow_member_to_construct (loader.py:877) calls INNER: it receives a Flow, not a
   FlowNode, has no flow/output_types to pass, renames from agent.name, and must NOT
   register into any output_types map. It keeps ONLY its payload-forcing delta, and its
   docstring stops claiming a reuse it does not perform.
   The seam's internal rename is redundant at three of four call sites (each/oracle rename
   to the group name afterwards) -- harmless; consider leaving the rename to the caller.

3. ROUTE THE FAILING RECONSTRUCTORS THROUGH OUTER:
   _reconstruct_each_node (loader.py:517), _reconstruct_loop_item (:561),
   _reconstruct_oracle_group (:424, base variant; its FlowNode raise disappears),
   _reconstruct_operator_primary (:578). Per-variant model tier needs NO new work:
   spec['models'] is already read positionally at :484/:487 and the merge marker already
   carries the full list for Construct variants. Oracle reconstructing only the base
   variant is CORRECT for a Construct (every variant is an identical copy of the same
   sub-flow per _lower_oracle).

4. FIELD SURGERY -- fix the WRITE side, which is where the silent failure is. Reading is
   already monopolized by _normalize._declared_output and that monopoly is CLEAN (scan
   confirmed one inline form, in its sanctioned home) -- so step 4 must ADD no new inline
   form. The write side has no monopoly: _reconstruct_loop_item:572 and
   _reconstruct_each_node:550 do model_copy(update={'inputs'/'outputs': ...}), and on a
   Construct that does NOT raise -- pydantic v2 silently attaches a phantom attribute. Add
   the WRITE counterpart beside _declared_output in _normalize.py (one writer routing to
   the plural fields for a Node and to input/output for a Construct, refusing unknown
   keys) and have all three sites call it. Do NOT re-inline isinstance at three sites.

5. Correct the false diagnostic at loader.py:409 -- it names FlowNode as accepted by the
   primitive path, which is exactly the path that rejects it. The sibling at :489 is
   already accurate; leave it.

6. LINE BUDGET -- REDRAWN. loader.py sits at its EXACT ceiling 1181. The originally
   proposed boundary (366-675) does NOT work: it strands five loader-local helpers the
   moved cluster calls, so it needs FIVE injected callables -- worse than the
   three-callables-across-six-functions shape AGENTS.md already refused, and a
   module-level import back is a hard cycle while a deferred import would grow
   FUNCTION_LOCAL_IMPORT_ALLOWLIST (refusal 1).

   Draw the boundary at the REAL transitive closure, 117-674, and split it in TWO:
     module A: 117-234  (_agent_spec_props_to_type, _inputs_from_data_edges,
                         _dict_form_inputs_from_props, _augment_inputs_from_prompt_marker)
                         ~130L, no from_agent_spec dependency
     module B: 237-674  (the reconstructors) ~390L, takes the ONE injected callable
   Nothing in the closure calls back into a stayer, so the direction is one-way; loader
   imports back only _agent_spec_props_to_type, _node_from_spec_agent and
   _subflow_oracle_group. Two modules rather than one ~540L module specifically so NEITHER
   needs a fresh 500-plus allowlist entry. Lower loader.py's 1181 entry to its new exact
   count in the SAME commit; a red test_guards_file_size after the split is the expected
   signal. Re-derive every count with wc -l -- the numbers above were measured 2026-07-31.
   R2 is genuinely avoided: the census predicate _touches_combo_vocabulary fires only on
   ModifierCombo or on importing a TABLE_SYMBOL, and the closure imports only the modifier
   CLASSES (Each/Loop/Oracle). Keep COMBO_DECOMPOSITION dispatch in loader.py.
   Coordinate with neograph-jtawq.10, which targets a different cluster in this same file.

   HARD PLACEMENT CONSTRAINT (derived 2026-07-31, was not stated before). Nothing in the
   closure calls from_agent_spec TODAY -- the only callers are _flow_member_to_construct
   (loader.py:877) and from_agent_spec itself, both stayers. The injected callable is
   required ONLY because of this ticket's own change. Therefore: the INNER seam MUST live
   in module B. If it stayed in loader.py, the reconstructors in B would call a stayer and
   the one-way property breaks. This is a constraint, not a preference.

   ORDER OF WORK: seam FIRST (steps 2-4), split SECOND. Splitting first would relocate code
   whose call graph is about to change, forcing the one-way proof to be redone.

   The back-import list is NINE names, not three: the six reconstructors (called by the
   COMBO_DECOMPOSITION dispatch, which stays) plus _agent_spec_props_to_type,
   _node_from_spec_agent and _subflow_oracle_group. Plain imports, not injections -- the
   split stays legal, the import block is just larger than the review stated.

7. LEAVE ALONE (verified correct; changing them is the failure mode):
   - compiler.py / _wiring.py / _subconstruct.py -- runtime is green for every row.
   - modifiers.py COMBO_DECOMPOSITION -- total over ModifierCombo, no new combo value.
   - _lower_each / _lower_oracle / _lower_operator / _lower_construct_item -- export
     verified working and item-kind-agnostic.
   - _lower_loop -- left alone by SCOPE DECISION, NOT because it is correct
     (neograph-rh5fb). Do not record LOOP export as done.
   - SUB_CONSTRUCT_UNSUPPORTED_COMBOS at _agent_spec.py:580 and its two pins --
     EACH_ORACLE(_OPERATOR) on a Construct stays permanently rejected.
   - _group_flow_items -- recognition already handles every Construct shape.

8. GATES. Guard-first, then uv run pytest (whole suite, bare), ruff, mypy. Prove green:
   test_agent_spec_export.py, test_agent_spec_matrix.py,
   test_guards_combo_decomposition_consumers.py, test_guards_file_size.py,
   test_guards_modifier_composition_completeness.py. Compare the PASS COUNT against the
   4085 / 4 skipped baseline and explain every delta; skips must not move.

9. STRUCTURAL GUARD (required -- the disease scan has MIGRATE rows). Assert the
   FlowNode-to-Construct recursion has exactly ONE site on the import path: exactly one
   function calls from_agent_spec on a sub-flow, namely INNER. This is satisfiable ONLY
   once _flow_member_to_construct is rebased (step 2) -- today there are two such sites,
   loader.py:896 and :1150. Include positive AND negative detector meta-tests and an
   anti-vacuity check that fails if a new recursion site appears unregistered. State the
   export-side TWO-site fact honestly in the docstring; do not phrase the guard as
   mirroring a single export seam that does not exist.

title: Phase 9: Construct-as-Portal-mesh-member export/import (entry + non-entry) and dispatch-mode Portal Flow-node lowering -- own tracked epic
description:
Master doc: docs/design/agent-spec-portal-master-architecture-2026-07-27.md §2/§5 (PORTAL Construct-member rows, C1/C2) + Build Plan Phase 9. Largest remaining item, deliberately its own scope:
C1: full Construct-as-Portal-mesh-member export (non-entry: WORKS at the IR/compile level via do0d9, per verified fixture tests/check_fixtures/should_pass/portal_construct_member.py + test_portal_cross_subconstruct.py, but Agent Spec export is BROKEN -- the mesh-detection filter misclassifies it (see Phase 5/A1) and even once detected, _lower_portal_mesh_to_swarm would AttributeError on member.prompt for a Construct member, since Constructs have no .prompt). New _make_agent-equivalent Construct lowering needed, reusing the existing recursive-Flow-production pattern already in _agent_spec.py. Entry case additionally depends on Phase 1 landing first.
C1 import: _reconstruct_swarm_mesh has no Construct-member branch at all -- new reconstruction branch needed, reusing the FlowNode-to-Construct recursion pattern used elsewhere in loader.py.
C2: Swarm-in-Flow feasibility for dispatch-mode Portal's Flow-node lowering -- currently NO lowering exists at all for dispatch-mode Portal export.
GATE (do not skip): before committing to any implementation approach for either C1 or C2, check tests/agent_spec_capabilities.py's pyagentspec primitive registry against the INSTALLED pyagentspec package for a conditional/dynamic-routing node type or Swarm-composability capability -- do not assume infeasibility without that check, per this whole investigation's core lesson (repeated false 'not supported' claims were failures to check for existing capability, not genuine gaps).
notes:
DECIDED (2026-07-27, maintainer): C2's scripted/conditions marker convention resolved -- use {"scripted": [...], "conditions": [...]} (mirrors the Portal field names directly, least indirection). Both are name-only registry-key lists, exported/imported via the SAME established pattern Loop.when/merge_fn/scripted_fn already use (register_condition/register_scripted, conditions.py/_runtime_registry.py) -- confirmed via code read, not a new mechanism, just applied to a dict of names instead of one.
RESOLVED (2026-07-27): dispatched focused research (docs/design/foreign-swarm-import-faithfulness-2026-07-27.md) into whether _reconstruct_swarm_mesh's Portal-typed-goto target is even correct for a genuinely foreign (non-neograph) Swarm, given real pyagentspec Swarms route via mid-conversation tool calls (send_message/handoff_conversation), not typed output. FINDING: Portal's typed-goto model IS the best available representation -- verified directly from wiring code that neograph's agent/act tool loop is structurally incapable of transferring control flow to a peer node (only the node's single reconverging exit port {node}__parse ever emits Command(goto=...), even in neograph's own Portal mesh implementation; the tools superstep always loops back to the same node). Building a tool-triggered-handoff mechanism would mean reinventing Portal itself with weaker guarantees, not a more faithful capture of the foreign semantics. NO CHANGE to the import target -- keep _reconstruct_swarm_mesh's existing design.

ACTION ITEM: sharpen the existing 'best-effort/structural downgrade' warning in loader.py (lines ~726-733) to name the SPECIFIC mismatch precisely (tool-call-vs-typed-output; HandoffMode.OPTIONAL collapsing into a must-always-emit-goto contract) -- exact suggested wording is in the research doc. Documentation precision fix, not an architecture change.

This also informs the original fail-loud-vs-coerce question (C1 import, foreign-Swarm Construct-member case): given a foreign Swarm's members were never designed to produce a goto value, and a Construct member's interior nodes are already-fixed/compiled (unlike an agent-mode Node, which can simply be told to produce the payload schema going forward), FAIL LOUD is the more defensible default for that specific case -- coercion would just defer a real failure to a worse, silent place. Maintainer leaning coerce-with-warning initially, reconsidered coerce->fail-loud given this finding -- confirm before implementation.
MAJOR UPDATE (2026-07-27): empirical spike (docs/design/swarm-langgraph-compilation-spike-2026-07-27.md), built in an isolated worktree, actually installed pyagentspec[langgraph] and ran real Swarm objects through pyagentspec's OWN official LangGraph adapter (langgraph-swarm), including a live compiled.invoke() with a stubbed LLM tool-call -- not static analysis this time.

REVERSES the prior research doc's (foreign-swarm-import-faithfulness-2026-07-27.md) 'would mean reinventing Portal, weaker' framing. Ground truth: pyagentspec's real handoff mechanism is ONE MORE TOOL whose handler returns Command(goto=agent_name, graph=Command.PARENT), invoked from inside the SAME ReAct tool loop -- LangGraph's own tool-node machinery recognizes the Command return and jumps control to a peer node's top-level subgraph, mid-turn, within one invoke() call. Live-verified.

This means genuine Swarm parity for neograph is a BOUNDED, ADDITIVE capability, not a new control-flow paradigm: add one handoff-tool-kind to _agent_cycle.py's existing tool-dispatch path, whose handler returns Command(goto, graph=PARENT), gated so it can ONLY target declared peer entry ports (reusing Portal's existing handoff_channel/entry-port machinery for the gate). neograph can additionally validate topology at COMPILE time (something the real pyagentspec/langgraph-swarm reference does NOT do at all -- it only 'enforces' topology via which tools got bound, no structural check) -- a place neograph is strictly better than the reference implementation.

Also found: HandoffMode.OPTIONAL vs ALWAYS compile to byte-identical graphs in the real adapter (only NEVER is special-cased/rejected) -- don't try to faithfully split OPTIONAL/ALWAYS on import, that distinction doesn't materially exist in the reference LangGraph backend. Map NEVER to neograph's existing static/typed routing; map OPTIONAL/ALWAYS both to 'bind a handoff tool per relationship.'

NEXT STEP: this needs its own proper design pass (architect + adversarial review, same rigor as the rest of this epic) for the concrete 'handoff tool' IR/runtime capability -- a new, sanctioned new-IR-capability on the same footing as Portal itself (per AGENTS.md's PORTAL-exception precedent), NOT yet designed in implementation detail. Not started.
DESIGN SPEC WRITTEN (2026-07-27): docs/design/portal-tool-triggered-handoff-2026-07-27.md -- the 'own proper design pass' this thread's NEXT STEP called for. Verified: no graph=Command.PARENT needed (neograph's flat, non-nested StateGraph compilation makes plain Command(goto=...) sufficient); extends Portal with a new trigger:Literal['output','tool'] field (NOT a new ModifierCombo value, mirrors is_dispatch precedent); zero new Node-level IR fields (Portal.to already sufficient, handoff_channel/handoff_param reused unchanged); Command( construction stays in factory.py via one new sibling next to _portal_route_to_command (guard G1 unchanged, no allowlist edit); _check_portal_mesh reused unchanged plus one narrow new rule (trigger='tool' requires agent/act member); recommends first-class authoring feature, not import-only. Not started -- status/children untouched. Three implementation-detail gaps flagged for adversarial review before coding: synthesized-tool shape/budget interaction, static-edge-XOR-Command LangGraph invariant re-verification, repeat-call-idempotency interaction.
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (2026-07-27): docs/design/portal-tool-triggered-handoff-2026-07-27-review.md -- verdict NEEDS-REVISION. Blocking gap: the design's tool-binding seam (§3.1) never actually threads Portal into _agent_cycle.py's _agent_caller/active-tool-list construction (hard-wired to node.tools), so as specified the synthesized transfer_to_<peer> tool would never reach llm.bind_tools() and could never be called. Also corrected: the 'LangGraph forbids static-edge+destinations=Command' claim is empirically false (live-tested: LangGraph silently double-executes both targets instead of erroring) -- still the right engineering call to avoid it, but not for the stated reason. graph=Command.PARENT resolution (§2) and G1/peer-resolution (§3.3) both independently CONFIRMED sound.
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW ROUND 2 (2026-07-27): docs/design/portal-tool-triggered-handoff-2026-07-27-review-2.md -- verdict NEEDS-REVISION (minor). All four round-1 findings substantively resolved (tool genuinely reaches bind_tools; static-edge framing now accurate + concretely testable guard; budget/idempotency exemptions confirmed zero-new-code); but re-verifying the tool-binding call chain against real _agent_cycle.py source found the design's own §3.1 threading diagram is factually wrong -- _agent_caller is called directly from agent_body/aagent_body closures (siblings of _build_turn_prep), not downstream of _build_turn_prep/_abuild_turn_prep/_turn_prep_kwargs, so only make_agent_cycle_bodies + _agent_caller need new params, not all four functions. Fix is simpler than described, not blocked. Ready for implementation once §3.1's chain is corrected (non-blocking doc fix).
DESIGN COMPLETE (2026-07-27): docs/design/portal-tool-triggered-handoff-2026-07-27.md, through 2 rounds of adversarial review (both filed alongside it), both verdicts NEEDS-REVISION-minor -> corrected in place each round -> round 2 explicitly states 'ready for implementation, no further design-level rework needed' once the round-2 nits were fixed (all 3 applied: corrected call-chain diagram to the real 2-function change (make_agent_cycle_bodies + _agent_caller, not 4 functions), cited tool.py's StructuredTool precedent for the synthesized handoff tool, corrected the IR_FIELDS frozenset citation to its real 4-element set).

Design: Portal gains trigger: Literal['output','tool'] field (peer mode only). trigger='tool' makes an agent/act mesh member's {node}__tools node a Command-emitting exit (destinations=(peers, {node}__agent)) detecting a synthesized transfer_to_<peer> tool call, routing via a new factory.py sibling _tool_handoff_to_command reusing all existing hop-budget/HANDOFF_END/entry-label machinery. Zero new Node-level IR fields (Portal.to is sufficient); Command( stays in factory.py (guard G1 untouched); graph=Command.PARENT is never needed (neograph's Portal mesh members are always siblings in one StateGraph per Construct level, verified not an overbroad 'everything is flat' claim). Recommended as first-class native authoring feature (Portal(trigger='tool')), not import-only. Resolves the Swarm-parity gap for HandoffMode.OPTIONAL/ALWAYS (map both to trigger='tool'; NEVER keeps mapping to existing trigger='output').

Grounded in real empirical evidence, not assumption: docs/design/foreign-swarm-import-faithfulness-2026-07-27.md (static analysis) + docs/design/swarm-langgraph-compilation-spike-2026-07-27.md (live-run spike against pyagentspec's real langgraph-swarm-backed adapter, in an isolated worktree).

STATUS: design-complete, twice-reviewed, NOT implemented. This is a genuinely new sanctioned IR capability (same footing as Portal's own original introduction) -- should be filed as its own tracked implementation task (with TDD, structural guards written failing-first per the design's §6) when the maintainer decides to proceed, separate from C1/C2's still-open Construct-as-mesh-member work.
CORRECTION (2026-07-27): the previously-flagged 'foreign-Swarm coerce-vs-fail-loud' open question (C1, typed-payload mismatch on a reconstructed Construct member) is MOOT for the realistic case, superseded by this ticket's own later tool-triggered-handoff design work. Under the NEW design (docs/design/portal-tool-triggered-handoff-2026-07-27.md), HandoffMode.OPTIONAL/ALWAYS -- which the empirical spike confirmed is what real pyagentspec Swarms actually are -- map to Portal(trigger='tool'), which has NO synthesized uniform payload type at all (routing is a tool call, not a typed-output read). The coerce/fail-loud dilemma only existed under the old trigger='output' typed-goto import path, which this design supersedes for OPTIONAL/ALWAYS. Remaining residual: HandoffMode.NEVER (first_agent never transfers; other agents may still be invoked via send_message as a sub-task call, not a graph transfer) may not even need Portal/goto representation at all -- possibly better modeled as ordinary tool-calling sub-invocation. NOT yet verified -- flag as a small follow-up check when C1/NEVER-mode import is actually implemented, not a blocking design gap. DO NOT re-ask the coerce-vs-fail-loud question again; it no longer applies to the primary import path.
SCOPE NARROWED (2026-07-27): the tool-triggered-handoff CAPABILITY (Portal trigger='tool', the design work done in this thread) is split out to its own task, neograph-s7zt3.14 -- implement that first. This ticket (s7zt3.12) is back to its original scope: C1 (Construct-as-Portal-mesh-member export/import, entry + non-entry) and C2 (dispatch-mode Portal Flow-node lowering). C1's HandoffMode-mapping detail (OPTIONAL/ALWAYS -> trigger='tool' on import) is cleaner to wire once s7zt3.14 exists, but C1's core 'can a Construct be a mesh member at all' work is not hard-blocked by it -- soft sequencing preference, not a dependency.

title: Phase 5: five pure reuse-and-delete Agent Spec fixes (A1, A5, B3, B2, B4) -- no open design questions
description:

comments.text:
Phase 5 complete (5 rows). All in src/neograph/_agent_spec.py + loader.py + new tests/test_agent_spec_phase5_reuse.py (11 tests, 9 red pre-fix).

A1 (mesh-detection filter): replaced isinstance(Node)-gated filter in to_agent_spec with new module-level _is_peer_mesh_member() reusing classify_modifiers (reads .modifier_set on Node AND Construct) + is_dispatch check. A Construct non-entry mesh member is now DETECTED (no longer false-rejected as 'mixed mesh/non-mesh'). Actual Construct-member lowering remains C1 (out of scope) -- call site casts to list[Node] with a comment marking the interim AttributeError boundary.

A5 (loader re-validation): NO production change needed. Verified via a _check_portal_mesh spy that from_agent_spec(Swarm) already routes the reconstructed mesh through _check_portal_mesh -- because _reconstruct_swarm_mesh returns Construct(...), whose __init__ runs the assembly gate (the audit's preferred option a). Adding an explicit second call would be redundant double-validation. Pinned with a monkeypatch spy test so a future model_construct-style bypass fails loud.

B3 (_MARK_PORTAL_SPEC read-back): _reconstruct_swarm_mesh now reads swarm.metadata[neograph/portal_spec] and applies max_hops/on_exhaust/route to the ENTRY member's Portal only (entry-only per _check_portal_mesh); non-entry members stay plain Portal(to=peers). Copies the sibling _MARK_*_SPEC read-back pattern. Round-trips: export max_hops=6/on_exhaust=exit -> re-import -> entry Portal carries them.

B2 (Oracle guard-skip): added _reject_unrepresentable_fields(node) at the top of _lower_oracle (the per-variant loop previously skipped the guard _lower_node runs). An Oracle-modified node with skip_when/renderer/raw_fn etc. now fails loud instead of exporting silently.

B4 (dict-form outputs): NOT pure reuse as the audit framed it. Root cause discovered: the consumer references a dict-form producer via {producer}_{key} state-field naming (validator requirement), so the reachable failures are (i) the 'no exportable Agent Spec node' raise for a dict-form INPUT consumer and (ii) a SILENT edge drop for a single-type consumer -- and the producer's output Property is already {key}.{field} while the consumer's input is bare {field}, so source_output != destination_input. Fixed by adding an optional dest_title param to _emit_input_edges (defaults to source_title, zero change for existing callers) and resolving {producer}_{key} via the canonical naming.split_output_field. title: Rebuild _lower_construct_item as compositional (mirroring compiler.py's Operator-orthogonal pattern) so all 12 ModifierCombo values get REAL lowerings, not fail-loud rejections
description:
Discovered 2026-07-27 while investigating neograph-s7zt3.2: tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py's UNSUPPORTED_COMBOS bucket (EACH_ORACLE, EACH_OPERATOR, ORACLE_OPERATOR, LOOP_OPERATOR, EACH_ORACLE_OPERATOR, PORTAL, PORTAL_OPERATOR -- 7 of 12 total ModifierCombo values) currently means 'the matrix generates zero cells for these combos', not 'verified to behave correctly'. This is exactly the same masking pattern that let neograph-s7zt3.1 and neograph-s7zt3.2 hide undetected: Portal was classified UNSUPPORTED and turned out to have TWO real bugs, found only by manually testing it, not by the matrix.

Manual spot-check (2026-07-27) of the other 5 (non-Portal, composed) combos: EACH_ORACLE verified empirically to raise a clean ConfigurationError via _lower_construct_item's fallback; EACH_OPERATOR/ORACLE_OPERATOR/LOOP_OPERATOR/EACH_ORACLE_OPERATOR share the IDENTICAL, provably-reached code path (not independently reproduced each one). This is probably correct behavior but has ZERO regression coverage -- nothing pins it, so a future refactor of _lower_construct_item's dispatch could silently change this and no test would catch it.

Scope: extend the matrix generator (built in neograph-00447) to enumerate ALL 12 ModifierCombo values from the SAME introspection source it already uses (src/neograph/modifiers.py's ModifierCombo enum + _COMBO_MAP), not just the 5 currently hand-picked as 'supported'. For each of the 7 currently-UNSUPPORTED combos, generate a cell that asserts the CORRECT outcome:
- EACH_ORACLE, EACH_OPERATOR, ORACLE_OPERATOR, LOOP_OPERATOR, EACH_ORACLE_OPERATOR: assert a clean ConfigurationError naming the combo (matching _lower_construct_item's existing fallback message shape) -- these become a new GREEN-via-expected-error category, not a gap.
- PORTAL, PORTAL_OPERATOR: depends on how neograph-s7zt3.1 and neograph-s7zt3.2 are resolved -- these cells should assert whatever the FIXED behavior is (translated placeholder + represented/rejected approval gate), and should be written so they FAIL until those two tickets land (i.e. do this task AFTER s7zt3.1/s7zt3.2, or write it as red/xfail referencing both, same convention as the rest of this epic's lineage).

This closes the actual root cause the epic's own retrospective diagnosed (matrix decomposition should be derived from closed type enumerations, not narrowed to what's convenient) -- the ORIGINAL neograph-00447 task partitioned SUPPORTED vs UNSUPPORTED as a coverage-scoping decision, which was reasonable at the time (m57mn's scope was narrower), but the epic's own north star ('any neograph structure compiling to LangGraph is representable in Agent Spec, anything less is poor design') means UNSUPPORTED should not be a permanent, untested category for constructs the compiler happily runs.
notes:
CORRECTED SCOPE (2026-07-27, maintainer): the original framing of this ticket ('assert a clean ConfigurationError for the 5 composed non-Portal combos, that's a GREEN outcome') is WRONG. Verified against compiler.py: EACH_ORACLE, EACH_OPERATOR, ORACLE_OPERATOR, LOOP_OPERATOR, EACH_ORACLE_OPERATOR all compile to real, running LangGraph pipelines (compiler.py's match statement handles Operator as an orthogonal wrapper composed onto EACH/ORACLE/LOOP/BARE/PORTAL bodies -- 5 explicit 'X | X_OPERATOR' arms). Per the maintainer's north star ('any neograph structure that compiles to LangGraph must be representable in Agent Spec -- anything less is poor design'), a permanent ConfigurationError for these is NOT an acceptable target state, the same way Option B's fail-loud-for-placeholder-mismatch was rejected earlier in this epic's history.

REAL SCOPE: this ticket (or a renamed/split successor) is now 'rebuild _lower_construct_item compositionally, mirroring compiler.py's case-arm structure, so Operator's existing pause-check composite (BARE|OPERATOR case, already implemented) can wrap the output of ANY other body lowering (_lower_each's MapNode, _lower_oracle's variant+merge structure, _lower_loop's branch, and the Portal-mesh Swarm export)'. This subsumes s7zt3.2's PORTAL_OPERATOR case as one instance of the general pattern, not a special case.

This is a genuine architecture change on the same footing as Option F -- needs its own design pass (architect -> adversarial review) verifying pyagentspec actually HAS a composable way to represent 'run body X, then pause for approval' generically (the existing BARE|OPERATOR lowering -- primary node + BranchingNode + InputMessageNode -- may or may not generalize cleanly to a MapNode/ParallelFlow/Swarm body; verify per-case, don't assume). Do not implement without that design pass. The matrix-extension work (covering all 12 combos with real assertions) should follow the design, not precede it -- the matrix can only assert what the corrected lowering actually produces.
REFINEMENT (2026-07-27, maintainer): this is confirmed to be the SAME duplicated-source-of-truth anti-pattern the retrospective flagged for 2s2o6 (_lower_node/_lower_oracle), one level higher -- _agent_spec.py as a whole independently re-derived 'what does this ModifierCombo mean' instead of sharing that decision logic with compiler.py, which already encodes it correctly and is the proven-correct reference (it's literally what makes these pipelines run). The OUTPUT-construction code legitimately differs per target (LangGraph primitives vs pyagentspec primitives, like separate compiler backends) -- but the COMPOSITION logic (which combos exist, which pair with _OPERATOR, in what structure) should have ONE source of truth, not two independently-authored, independently-drifting copies.

Rebuilding _lower_construct_item to merely 'mirror' compiler.py's pattern by hand-copying its shape once is insufficient -- that's how it drifted the first time (compiler.py handles 12/12 combos compositionally; _agent_spec.py was hand-written to cover 5/12 plus a bolted-on Portal special case that never learned the Operator-orthogonality lesson). The design pass for this ticket MUST include a structural guard (same discipline as 2s2o6/tjupj) that keeps the two dispatches from re-diverging -- e.g. a test asserting _agent_spec.py's handled ModifierCombo set (and Operator-pairing grouping) matches compiler.py's, so a future modifier addition that updates one without the other fails loud immediately, not after another matrix-driven discovery cycle. Whether that's literally a shared lookup table both modules import, or two independent implementations pinned equal by a guard test, is a design-pass decision -- but 'mirror it once by hand' is explicitly not an acceptable resolution given this is the second time this exact class of drift has been found in this epic.
SUPERSEDED (2026-07-27): the master architecture doc (docs/design/agent-spec-portal-master-architecture-2026-07-27.md) replaced this task's monolithic 'rebuild _lower_construct_item compositionally' scope with a properly-sequenced 10-phase build plan (Phase 0-10), each phase filed as its own task under neograph-s7zt3. Closing as superseded, not as done -- none of the underlying work landed under this task ID. See the new Phase 0/2/3/4/7/8 tasks for what this scope became.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-2s2o6
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-2s2o6` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-2s2o6/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-2s2o6
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-2s2o6)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-2s2o6 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-2s2o6 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-2s2o6/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-2s2o6 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-2s2o6/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). title: Sweep verification for neograph-tjupj
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-tjupj
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-tjupj`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-tjupj)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-tjupj --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-tjupj sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the

     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a

description:

a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:

   ```

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>

   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).

   ```bash
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py

   ```

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The

title: Sweep verification for neograph-cbpyx
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-cbpyx
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-cbpyx`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-cbpyx)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-cbpyx --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-cbpyx sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-cbpyx
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-cbpyx` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-cbpyx/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-cbpyx
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-cbpyx)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-cbpyx --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-cbpyx --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-cbpyx/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-cbpyx codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

M1 (ModifierCombo completeness): step 2/3 must apply the SAME loud-completeness discipline to the neograph modifier axis as step 1 applies to the pyagentspec node axis. title: Sweep verification for neograph-00447
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-00447
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-00447`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-00447)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-00447 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-00447 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-00447
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-00447` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-00447/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-00447
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-00447)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-00447 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-00447 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-00447/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-00447 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Refactor: unify _lower_node/_lower_oracle's duplicated per-node.mode dispatch into one shared function
description:
The actual core architectural fix the retrospective names in section 2.1 and 4.2. m57mn's fix (commit a109a7e) corrected _lower_oracle's dispatch CONTENT (it now mirrors _lower_node's think/scripted/agent-act branching) but did NOT eliminate the STRUCTURAL duplication -- there are still two independently hand-written copies of the three-way mode dispatch, one in _lower_node, one inline in _lower_oracle's variant loop. This is the exact 'one validator, not two' / 'single source of truth, do not re-inline modifier checks elsewhere' pattern CLAUDE.md already prohibits for effective_producer_type and _check_fan_in_inputs -- it was just never applied here.

Do this LAST, not first -- it must be verified safe by BOTH:
1. neograph-i7k7j's fully green, exhaustive matrix (proves no behavioral regression across every real mode x modifier x input-shape x config-variant combination)
2. neograph-tjupj's AST guard (proves every LlmNode/Agent construction site post-refactor still has its placeholder guard paired correctly)

Implementation sketch (from the retrospective, adjust as the actual code demands): extract a single function, e.g. _lower_generation_step(node, *, name, outputs, metadata) -> SpecNode, containing exactly one copy of the think/agent-act/scripted-or-raw three-way dispatch (ToolNode+ServerTool / LlmNode-guarded / AgentNode+Agent-guarded), parameterized by caller-supplied name (Oracle passes f'{node.name}__variant_{i}', _lower_node passes node.name) and metadata (Oracle attaches its group/variant markers). _lower_node becomes a thin wrapper around it. _lower_oracle's variant loop calls the same shared function per variant tier.

This structurally removes the possibility of the two dispatches drifting again -- e.g. if agent/act-mode Oracle variants are ever implemented, they get _make_agent's exact lowering for free instead of a third hand-written copy.

Reference: docs/design/agent-spec-oracle-inputs-2026-07-25-architecture-retrospective.md section 4.2, and its parent epic neograph-2ev48/neograph-154vl (layer-discipline: this stays entirely within src/neograph/_agent_spec.py, no IR/compiler-layer changes).

One dispatch, not two: the per-node.mode three-way lowering (think->LlmNode / agent,act->AgentNode+_make_agent / scripted,raw->ToolNode) lives in EXACTLY ONE function; both callers reuse it with ZERO behavior change, and both safety nets (i7k7j matrix + tjupj AST guard, plus the lowering source-guard) stay green.

## Implementation Plan
1. Add `description: str | None = None` to `_make_server_tool` (:450); default -> current f"neograph node {node.name!r} (mode={node.mode})". No other caller changes.
2. Extract `_lower_generation_step(node: Node, *, name: str, outputs: list[Property], metadata: dict[str, Any], model_tier: str | None = None, tool_description: str | None = None) -> SpecNode` containing ONE copy of the three-way dispatch:
   - import flow classes; inputs = _properties_for(node.inputs).
   - think: rewritten,ref_props,flat = _translate_placeholders(node.prompt or "", inputs, name); return LlmNode(name=name, inputs=ref_props or None, outputs=outputs or None, llm_config=_make_llm_config(Node(name=node.name, model=model_tier or node.model)), prompt_template=rewritten, metadata={**metadata, _MARK_PROMPT_SPEC:_prompt_spec_marker(node,flat)}).
   - agent/act: rewritten,ref_props,flat = _translate_placeholders(...); agent_source = node.model_copy(update={"name":name,"model":model_tier or node.model}); agent = _make_agent(agent_source, tools_mod, ref_props, outputs, rewritten); return AgentNode(name=name, inputs=ref_props or None, outputs=outputs or None, agent=agent, metadata={**metadata, _MARK_MODE:node.mode, _MARK_AGENT_SPEC:_agent_spec_marker(node), _MARK_PROMPT_SPEC:_prompt_spec_marker(node,flat)}).  (markers use ORIGINAL node, not agent_source.)
   - scripted/raw: return ToolNode(name=name, inputs=inputs or None, outputs=outputs or None, tool=_make_server_tool(node, tools_mod, inputs, outputs, description=tool_description), metadata=metadata).  MUST pass metadata=metadata directly (base {} for the node path) -- NEVER `metadata or None` (verified {}!=None on pyagentspec wire).

### Provable zero-behavior-change unifications

So _make_llm_config(node) == _make_llm_config(Node(name=node.name, model=model_tier or node.model)) when model_tier is None. One expression serves both. NOTE the current asymmetry to PRESERVE: think oracle variants all share llm name f"{node.name}-llm"; agent/act oracle variants get UNIQUE f"{variant_name}-llm" (because model_copy sets name=variant_name). Since a single Oracle has ONE node.mode, all its variants take the SAME branch -- the asymmetry is BETWEEN oracle nodes, never within one, so it survives so long as think uses gen-node-name=node.name and agent/act uses gen-node-name=name.
- agent/act source: node.model_copy(update={'name':name,'model':model_tier or node.model}) with name=node.name, model_tier=None reduces to a value-identical copy of node; _make_agent reads only fields -> identical Agent. So one expression (model_copy) serves both.

## Core Invariant
Every construction site in src/neograph/_agent_spec.py that emits a pyagentspec primitive carrying neograph-authored ${var} prompt text — LlmNode.prompt_template, AgentNode via nested Agent.system_prompt, AND every _make_agent(...) call (which builds Agent(system_prompt=...)) — MUST be preceded, in the same enclosing function body, by a _translate_placeholders(/_node_translation( call, so no untranslated ${var} ever reaches the Agent Spec wire. The guard proves this PAIRING exhaustively (positive shape-guard), reusing the neograph-00447 registry as the single classification source (DERIVED, never hand-copied), and any KNOWN unpaired site rides a SHRINKING allowlist tagged with the tracking bug — never a silent skip.

## Implementation Plan (REFINED per review kgbo0.12 — 2 MEDIUM resolved)
1. MEDIUM-1 FIX (derive, do not hardcode): in tests/agent_spec_capabilities.py add
   `PLACEHOLDER_PROMPT_EMITTING_CONSTRUCTORS = frozenset({n for n, f in NODE_FAMILIES.items() if f == "text_scan"}) | {"AgentNode"}`
   — DERIVED from NODE_FAMILIES text_scan members (NOT a hardcoded {LlmNode}; a future text_scan prompt-bearing primitive is then a LOUD add, not a silent miss) PLUS the AgentNode augmentation (AgentNode is `structural` to pyagentspec — NODE_FAMILIES faithfully mirrors _get_inferred_inputs, do NOT reclassify it — but placeholder-coupled in neograph EXPORT via nested Agent.system_prompt). Docstring names why: LlmNode = flow-node fed prompt_template; AgentNode = export-coupled; the OTHER text_scan members it collects (currently InputMessageNode) are narrowed by the req-3 exemption list, not hidden.
2. Create tests/test_guards_agent_spec_llm_construction_sites.py. Always-on (pure `ast` + Tier-A dict import; NO importorskip). Parse _agent_spec.py once.
3. Collect TWO site families by AST walk:
   (a) NODE-construction sites: every ast.Call whose callee trailing name is in the derived set -> LlmNode :309/:504/:589, AgentNode :330/:544, InputMessageNode :812 (6 collected).
   (b) _make_agent CALL sites: every ast.Call to `_make_agent` -> :329, :539 (paired), :945 (Portal->Swarm, UNPAIRED). This family is what catches the mutual blind spot the AgentNode-only walk misses.
4. Req 2 pairing (post-cbpyx target = _translate_placeholders, the retired _check_placeholder_inputs is GONE per cbpyx 72fa5a1): for each collected site assert a _translate_placeholders(/_node_translation( Call exists in the SAME enclosing FunctionDef with lineno < site lineno. EXEMPTIONS (named, req-3):
   - InputMessageNode :812 — Portal routing-CHECK node, not prompt-bearing (no neograph ${var} text).
   - Agent() :370 inside _make_agent — receives an already-(or not)-translated system_prompt PARAM; pairing is enforced at its _make_agent CALL sites (family b), not here.
   ALLOWLIST (SHRINKING, req-4 escalation — do NOT paper over):
   - _make_agent :945 (_lower_portal_mesh_to_swarm) is a CONFIRMED unpaired site: it ships raw ${var} to a foreign Swarm agent (empirically reproduced 2026-07-27). Tracked by BUG neograph-s7zt3.1. The guard asserts this ONE site is the sole allowlist entry, keyed to s7zt3.1, and a meta-assert that the allowlist has exactly 1 entry (so when s7zt3.1 is fixed, the entry is removed and the guard tightens). NOT a silent exemption — a documented, ticketed, shrinking allowlist.
5. Req 3 counts: assert collected node-sites == 6 AND _make_agent sites == 3; paired == 5 node-sites (InputMessageNode:812 exempt) + 2 _make_agent sites (:945 allowlisted). Drift comment: "if any count changes, a new placeholder-emitting/_make_agent site was added — verify paired _translate_placeholders OR named exemption OR ticketed shrinking-allowlist entry; never silent drift."
6. Req 4 reconciliation: assert the guards paired-site enumeration equals the matrixs 5 dispatch branches (_lower_node think+agent/act, _lower_oracle think-variant+agent/act-variant+merge_prompt), AND record that the Portal->Swarm path (:945) is the discrepancy req-4 surfaced — the matrix classifies Portal as per-node UNSUPPORTED so it never exercises the successful Swarm lowering; guard family (b) is what closes that mutual blind spot. Escalated as neograph-s7zt3.1, not papered over.
7. Meta-guard (positive+negative, plain-substring, mirrors tests/test_guards_agent_spec_lowering.py): feed a synthetic FunctionDef constructing an LlmNode (and one calling _make_agent) with NO preceding _translate_placeholders and assert the pairing check flags it — not vacuously green.
8. Do NOT touch src/ (the s7zt3.1 FIX is a SEPARATE bug/task — tjupj only ADDS the guard + allowlists the known site). Guard + registry-set only.
