title: Implement Oracle+agent/act export lowering (8 red cells, missing-feature gap)
description:
Re-scoped 2026-07-26 (was: 'fix every red cell', which conflated two unrelated root causes -- split per neograph-<placeholder-translation-task> handling the placeholder-coupling family).

This task's remaining scope, after the placeholder-translation task resolves the other 27: the 8 cells `{agent,act}-oracle-{merge_fn,merge_prompt}-{single,dict}` in tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py. These fail not because of pyagentspec's placeholder coupling but because _lower_oracle has NO lowering implemented at all for Oracle-modified nodes in agent/act mode -- it raises 'Oracle+agent/act export has no Agent Spec lowering yet' (_agent_spec.py, see the ConfigurationError message for the exact line).

This is real, undesigned feature work, not a bugfix: what SHOULD an Oracle-modified agent/act-mode node lower to? Each variant is presumably an Agent Spec AgentNode+Agent (mirroring _make_agent), N of them in parallel, merged the same way _lower_oracle's think-mode variants already merge (ParallelFlowNode + merge node). Needs its own design pass (does an ensemble of AGENTS -- each potentially running a multi-turn ReAct tool loop -- even make sense as a pyagentspec composite? verify against pyagentspec's actual Agent/AgentNode capabilities before assuming a mechanical mirror of the think-mode case works) before implementation. Do not assume this is a small mechanical extension of _make_agent -- verify.

Run this through dev-practices:execute properly (research atom should include: does ANY existing neograph pipeline actually use Oracle+agent/act? is this combination even meaningful, or should it be a permanent, documented NO-REPR ConfigurationError rather than a feature gap? -- that's a real open design question, not a given).
design:
## Core Invariant
to_agent_spec expresses the SAME SEMANTIC modifier lowering neograph uses when compiling (N Oracle variants + one merge), never a second divergent one — so Oracle+agent/act must lower through the SAME per-node.mode primitive builder _lower_node's agent/act branch uses (_make_agent -> AgentNode+Agent), reusing the type-agnostic variant->merge edge loop, and MUST round-trip (loader reconstructs the exact Node|Oracle IR, which re-auto-wraps for isolation on re-compile). The export path is ALSO the sole guard for combinations qzrv declared unrepresentable — to_agent_spec never runs the compile pre-pass, so every unrepresentable sub-case (dict-form agent OUTPUTS) must fail loud IN the exporter, not rely on a compile-only fixture.

## Verdict: FEATURE, not NO-REPR (Oracle+agent is a supported compiling combination — should_pass/oracle_over_agent_node.py). Design B (direct AgentNode variants mirroring _lower_node), CONFIRMED sound by architect review (not a maintainer escalation): retrospective §4.2 anticipates bare AgentNode variants via _make_agent; the semantic lowering is "N variants + one merge" (isolation excluded — a LangGraph-runtime detail); matches shipped think-mode Oracle export; round-trip re-wraps on recompile => no isolation seam.

## Implementation Plan (REFINED per review 4j5gm.12)
1. EXPORT (src/neograph/_agent_spec.py, _lower_oracle variant loop ~:513): replace the agent/act raise with a branch MIRRORING _lower_node's agent/act branch (:318-346) per variant: _translate_placeholders(node.prompt, inputs, variant_name) (Option F, same as think branch), agent=_make_agent(node.model_copy(update={"model": model_tier or node.model}), tools_mod, ref_props, gen_outputs, rewritten) to honor Oracle.models per-variant tiers, append AgentNode(name=variant_name, inputs=ref_props or None, outputs=gen_outputs or None, agent=agent, metadata=variant_metadata | {_MARK_MODE: node.mode, _MARK_AGENT_SPEC: _agent_spec_marker(node), _MARK_PROMPT_SPEC: _prompt_spec_marker(node, flat_to_original)}). Do NOT touch the merge node or the variant->merge edge loop (both already mode/type-agnostic).
   1b. **MEDIUM FIX (export-path silent-seam guard): BEFORE building variants, if the agent/act node has dict-form (multi-key) OUTPUTS, raise ConfigurationError mirroring the qzrv message (dict-form OUTPUTS across fanned agents is undefined / unrepresentable).** This is the SOLE export-path guard for this combo — to_agent_spec (:941) walks the raw construct via iter_with_arms and NEVER runs wrap_fan_over_agents, so the compile-only qzrv rejection in _fan_agent_wrap.py is unreachable here; the old unconditional raise at :516 was previously catching it. Single-type outputs proceed. (Preserves the North Star: no silent seam replaces the removed raise.)
2. IMPORT/ROUND-TRIP (src/neograph/loader.py, _reconstruct_oracle_group ~:419-437): add `elif base_cls == "AgentNode"` recovering base_mode/base_prompt/base_model/tools/gate_tools_when/context by reusing _reconstruct_agent_node (:283), so reconstructed base_node | Oracle(...) matches the original. Mandatory — the 8 round-trip cells xfail(strict) XPASS-fail otherwise.
3. GUARD-FIRST verification: run tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py — the 8 RED_EXPORT export cells + their 8 round-trip cells flip green; move the 8 ids into GREEN (RED_EXPORT = CELLS-GREEN-UNREPRESENTABLE empties; strict xfails are the ratchet). The compile-only should_fail/oracle_over_agent_multi_output.py stays fail-loud but is NOT sufficient export coverage — see 5.
4. Three-surface parity: fixtures build via @node (construct_from_functions); verify programmatic Node(mode="agent",...) | Oracle(...) + declarative reach the same lowering (should_pass fixture already uses the programmatic surface — cite it).
5. **MEDIUM FIX (export negative test): add a should_fail-AT-EXPORT test** — a should_fail check-fixture that exercises to_agent_spec (NOT compile), OR a focused pytest — calling to_agent_spec on Oracle+agent+dict-form OUTPUTS and asserting the step-1b ConfigurationError. The matrix varies INPUT shape only (single/dict/context = fan-in), never OUTPUT arity, so it gives ZERO coverage of this seam; this test is the ratchet for it. Also add the positive should_pass export fixture (Oracle+agent single-output -> Agent Spec) noted before.
notes:
SUPERSEDED SCOPE (2026-07-26): Option B (fail-loud) rejected by maintainer as poor design -- corrected to Option F (syntax-level ->{{ var }} translation, docs/design/agent-spec-placeholder-translation-2026-07-26.md + its review addendum). Reviewed and revised: _emit_input_edges is a required 5th site (routes DataFlowEdge.destination_input through the same flat-name map, drops edges for unreferenced inputs), matrix fixture prompts need updating to reference real input names, loader.py marker plan narrowed to 2 sites (not 4). Expected outcome: 27 of the 35 red cells go GREEN via Option F; 8 agent/act-Oracle cells (root family 3) remain red for a re-scoped reason -- missing lowering, not placeholder coupling -- and may be split into a separate follow-up task rather than bundled into this implementation.
## Research (neograph-4j5gm.2, dp-researcher)

### VERDICT: FEATURE (build the lowering) — NOT a permanent NO-REPR ConfigurationError

Strongest single evidence: Oracle-over-agent is a FIRST-CLASS, SUPPORTED, COMPILING combination in neograph today. tests/check_fixtures/should_pass/oracle_over_agent_node.py builds `Node(mode='agent') | Oracle(n=2, merge_fn=...)` and compiles cleanly (it was a should_fail fixture, MOVED to should_pass by neograph-m6d3.6). The combination is meaningful, constructible, and documented (docs/design/fan-over-agent-node-2026-07-07.md), not merely reachable via the exhaustive test matrix. So the missing agent/act Oracle *export* is a real feature gap to fill, symmetric with the think/scripted Oracle export that already works. NO-REPR would contradict neograph's own should_pass fixture.

Q1 (does anything use Oracle+agent/act?): YES. should_pass fixture above; should_fail/oracle_over_agent_multi_output.py pins the ONE rejected sub-case (dict-form OUTPUTS across fanned agents is undefined — stays fail-loud). Examples 03/05/10/31 use Oracle broadly. So single-output Oracle+agent is a real supported shape.

### How neograph LOWERS Oracle+agent AT COMPILE (the Core-Invariant reference)
compiler.compile() runs the pre-pass wrap_fan_over_agents() (src/neograph/_fan_agent_wrap.py) BEFORE state-model build: it rewrites `Node(mode=agent)|Oracle` into an ISOLATED single-node sub-Construct(input=port, output=..., nodes=[bare_agent], modifier_set=Oracle), because an inline fan Sends into the ReAct cycle's SHARED reducer channels and collapses N>1 branches (LangGraph isolation limit). NOTE: this auto-wrap is a LangGraph-RUNTIME isolation detail, not the SEMANTIC modifier lowering. to_agent_spec() does NOT run this pre-pass — it walks the raw construct via iter_with_arms, so _lower_oracle sees node.mode='agent' and hits the raise (_agent_spec.py:513-523).

Q2 (pyagentspec capability — is a mechanical mirror valid?): YES, structurally. pyagentspec 26.1.2: flows.nodes.AgentNode is a concrete flows Node subclass (MRO: AgentNode->Node->ComponentWithIO); Agent(llm_config, system_prompt, tools, inputs, outputs, human_in_the_loop) exists. N AgentNode variants each with their own Agent, fanned to a merge node by explicit ControlFlowEdge/DataFlowEdge, is the SAME shape the think path uses with LlmNode. The export does NOT use ParallelFlowNode (docstring mentions it but the code fans via explicit edges); the existing variant->merge edge loop (_agent_spec.py:600-625) is variant-type-AGNOSTIC and already works for AgentNode variants. So no new pyagentspec primitive is needed. pyagentspec's placeholder coupling (Agent/AgentNode couple inputs= to {{ }} prompt vars) is satisfied the SAME way _lower_node's agent branch already does it: Option-F _translate_placeholders.

### Reuse targets (Q3 — minimal correct lowering, all already at HEAD post-cbpyx)
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:318-346 — _lower_node's agent/act branch: the EXACT AgentNode+Agent+markers recipe to copy into _lower_oracle's agent/act variant slot.
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:357-378 _make_agent(node, tools_mod, ref_props, outputs, system_prompt) — reuse verbatim for each variant (pass node.model_copy(update={'model': model_tier}) to honor Oracle.models per-variant tiers, mirroring the think branch's per-variant _make_llm_config at :508).
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:156-220 _translate_placeholders (Option F) — reuse per variant, same as think branch (:499).
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:418-440 _agent_spec_marker + :253-272 _prompt_spec_marker — the markers _lower_node's agent branch stamps; the variant must carry _MARK_MODE + _MARK_AGENT_SPEC + _MARK_PROMPT_SPEC.
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:494-544 — the think/agent-act/else dispatch in _lower_oracle's variant loop is the insertion point; the agent/act elif currently raises.

### Round-trip is IN SCOPE (critical): both matrices xfail(strict) the 8 cells
tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py: RED_EXPORT is exactly the 8 cells; BOTH TestAgentSpecExportMatrix AND TestAgentSpecRoundTripMatrix parametrize sorted(CELLS) and apply xfail(strict=True) to RED_EXPORT. Fixing export alone makes the 8 ROUND-TRIP tests XPASS->strict-fail. The loader MUST also learn AgentNode variants: src/neograph/loader.py:419-437 _reconstruct_oracle_group dispatches base_cls LlmNode/ToolNode and RAISES 'unsupported type' for AgentNode. Add an AgentNode branch reusing the existing loader.py:283 _reconstruct_agent_node (which reads mode/prompt/model/tools back from the neograph/agent_spec marker).

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:513-523 -- the raise to replace (the whole gap).
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:318-346 -- _lower_node agent/act branch = the exemplar to mirror.
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:357-378 -- _make_agent = the reuse target.
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:600-625 -- variant->merge edge loop, already type-agnostic (no change needed).
- src/neograph/loader.py:419-437 -- _reconstruct_oracle_group dispatch that must gain an AgentNode branch.
- src/neograph/loader.py:283 -- _reconstruct_agent_node, reuse it for that branch.
- src/neograph/_fan_agent_wrap.py:34 -- wrap_fan_over_agents (the compile-time auto-wrap; the alternative Design A would run this in export — NOT recommended, see design).
- docs/design/agent-spec-oracle-inputs-2026-07-25-architecture-retrospective.md:45-67 -- names 'agent/act-mode Oracle lowering' as the next case of the SAME per-mode dispatch _lower_node/_lower_oracle should share (neograph-2s2o6).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- ROUND-TRIP loader extension is mandatory, not optional (see above) — the single most likely thing to be missed. Guard-first: the 8 round-trip xfails ratchet it.
- Oracle.models per-variant model tiers: _make_agent builds llm_config from node.model, so pass a model_copy with the variant tier or the tier axis is silently ignored. Mirror the think branch's :508 per-variant _make_llm_config.
- merge_prompt cells: the merge node is already handled (_agent_spec.py:553-577, gated on oracle.merge_prompt truthiness, mode-agnostic) — no change needed there; only the VARIANT slot changes.
- dict-form OUTPUTS on the agent stays fail-loud (should_fail/oracle_over_agent_multi_output.py) — do NOT accidentally admit it. Single-type outputs only (Oracle merge contract).
- DESIGN TENSION (named, not blocking): Core Invariant says 'the SAME lowering neograph performs when compiling'. Compile auto-wraps agent+Oracle into a sub-Construct (Design A: variants as FlowNode-wrapped sub-flows); the retrospective instead anticipates direct AgentNode variants (Design B). Recommending Design B — see design field. Not NEEDS-USER-INPUT because the authoritative retrospective already points at Design B and Design B introduces no silent seam (round-trip IR reconstructs to Node|Oracle, which re-auto-wraps on re-compile, preserving isolation).
## Findings (research neograph-4j5gm.2)

### VERDICT: FEATURE (build the lowering), NOT a permanent NO-REPR ConfigurationError.
Strongest single piece of evidence: Oracle-over-agent is already a FIRST-CLASS, COMPILING neograph combination -- tests/check_fixtures/should_pass/oracle_over_agent_node.py (Node(mode='agent') | Oracle(n=2, merge_fn=...)) compiles cleanly via the fan-over-agent AUTO-WRAP (src/neograph/_fan_agent_wrap.py:wrap_fan_over_agents, design docs/design/fan-over-agent-node-2026-07-07.md, neograph-m6d3.6). It is meaningful, constructible, and runnable today -- NOT merely reachable via the exhaustive matrix. The ONLY thing missing is the Agent Spec EXPORT lowering. So this is a real export-feature gap, symmetric with the already-shipped agent/act _lower_node branch, not an unrepresentable combination. (The single-type/self-contained + single-key-dict shapes are supported at compile; multi-output dict-form OUTPUTS over an agent is the ONE fail-loud case -- should_fail/oracle_over_agent_multi_output.py -- and the 8 matrix cells all use single-type Out outputs, so none hit that guard.)

### Q1 (does anything use Oracle+agent/act?) -- YES, it compiles today
- should_pass fixture above; examples use Oracle heavily (03/05/10/31) and agent mode heavily (13/14/23). The combination is a documented supported shape, gated only by output-arity.

### Q2 (is agent/act a mechanical mirror of the think-variant path, or does pyagentspec not support it?) -- pyagentspec SUPPORTS it structurally.
- pyagentspec 26.1.2: flows.nodes.AgentNode is a concrete flows Node subclass (MRO: AgentNode->Node->ComponentWithIO), fields {inputs,outputs,agent,branches}. agent.Agent(llm_config, system_prompt, tools, inputs, outputs, human_in_the_loop). N AgentNode variants + explicit ControlFlowEdge fan-out to a merge node is structurally identical to the existing think-mode N-LlmNode fan-out. pyagentspec places NO constraint against an ensemble of multi-turn ReAct AgentNodes wired by plain control/data edges.
- NOTE: the module + _lower_oracle docstrings SAY 'ParallelFlowNode', but the ACTUAL code (src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:600-625) uses explicit ControlFlowEdge/DataFlowEdge fan-out, NOT ParallelFlowNode. title: Agent Spec round-trip: scripted_fn re-derived from exported node's hyphenated .name, breaks @node self-registration
description:
Discovered while implementing neograph-e3b4j's docs example (examples/31_agent_spec_each_oracle_loop.py).

@node's decoration-time hyphenation convention (node_label = (name or f.__name__).replace('_', '-'), decorators.py:452) means a Python function named e.g. each_seed gets node.name='each-seed'. For a @node-decorated SCRIPTED node, node.scripted_fn is set per-compile from the node's own _scripted_shim PrivateAttr sidecar (n.name is the lookup key, _scripted_registry.py's _register_node_scripted) -- this sidecar is LOST across an Agent Spec round-trip (from_agent_spec reconstructs a brand-new Node with just a string scripted_fn = the exported node's .name, no callable, no sidecar).

This means: ANY @node-decorated scripted function, once round-tripped through to_agent_spec -> from_agent_spec, requires an explicit scripted={'each-seed': fn, ...} kwarg at compile() time keyed by the HYPHENATED node name -- @node's own self-registration mechanism (sidecar-based, per-compile) provides no help post-round-trip, unlike the decoration-time GLOBAL registry (neograph._runtime_registry.register_scripted) that plain register_scripted()-registered functions use (and which DOES survive round-trips, since compile() unconditionally merges it in regardless of any particular Node's sidecar state).

WORKAROUND used in e3b4j's example: use the declarative Node.scripted(name=X, fn=X, ...) + a matching module-level register_scripted(X, fn) call (mirroring test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py's own proven pattern) instead of @node's sugar, for any scripted node that needs to survive a round-trip without an explicit scripted= kwarg at every call site.

This is arguably WORKING AS DESIGNED (from_agent_spec explicitly documents 'no modifier/sidecar recovery, primitive-level import') but the DX gap (a scripted @node pipeline silently requires a DIFFERENT, hyphenation-aware scripted= dict after round-tripping, with no error/warning pointing this out) is worth a documented fail-loud check or a docs callout at minimum.
design:
## Root Cause
No code defect -- from_agent_spec's primitive-level reconstruction (documented, intentional) combined with @node's hyphenation convention already produces a fail-loud ConfigurationError with an accurate hint at compile() time (factory.py's scripted-registration check, pre-existing).

## Fix Approach
DOCS ONLY: added a 'Known gap: @node hyphenation after round-trip' section to website/src/content/docs/runtime/agent-spec.mdx explaining the pitfall, the fail-loud hint, and the Node.scripted()+register_scripted() workaround for round-trip-durable scripted nodes. Added 3 regression tests pinning the existing fail-loud contract (missing kwarg, wrong underscore key, correct hyphenated key) since no such coverage existed before.
notes:
## Reproduction / Investigation
Manually reproduced the round-trip scenario: @node-decorated scripted function 'each_seed' hyphenates to node.name='each-seed'; after to_agent_spec -> from_agent_spec, compile() WITHOUT scripted= raises ConfigurationError('Scripted function 'each-seed' not registered', hint="Pass scripted={'each-seed': fn} to compile().") -- this hint ALREADY names the correct hyphenated key. Also verified the natural-but-wrong guess (scripted={'each_seed': fn}, underscore form matching the user's Python function name) ALSO fails loud with the same accurate hint, never silently misresolves.

CONCLUSION: the fail-loud check the ticket asks for ('worth a documented fail-loud check ... at minimum') ALREADY EXISTS and is already correct/accurate (factory.py:77-82, pre-existing). This bug's remaining scope, per its own text, is DOCS-ONLY.
- Root cause: N/A (working as designed, already fail-loud)
- Failing test: N/A -- wrote 3 REGRESSION tests (not TDD-red, since no code bug exists) pinning the existing fail-loud contract: tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py::TestScriptedNodeHyphenatedNameAfterRoundTrip (missing-kwarg case, wrong-underscore-key case, correct-hyphenated-key-resolves case). All 3 passed immediately on first run -- confirms no regression, not a TDD-red/green cycle.
## Trace Similar Patterns
Checked all per-compile sidecar-based lookups keyed by node.name (the hyphenated form) in factory.py: only scripted_fn (node._scripted_shim) fits this pattern. tool_factory_lookup is keyed by tool name (not node name); Loop/Operator condition strings are registered independently by an explicit @condition name (never derived from node.name); merge_fn is registered globally by function qualname (per the CLAUDE.md 'Known open DX items' note), not per-node-name. No sibling instance of 'hyphenated node.name used as a per-compile lookup key that a round-trip loses' found.
## Codebase Disease Scan (qtfof.3)
No code fix was made for this bug (working-as-designed, already fail-loud with an accurate hint) -- the deliverable is a docs callout + regression tests pinning the existing contract. There is no disease pattern to scan for since no source code changed.

## Architect Review (qtfof.3)

2. Fix minimality: PASS -- docs-only change (one new mdx section) + 3 regression tests. No source code touched.
3. Regression risk: NONE -- zero source changes.
4. Architecture compliance: PASS -- docs content only; website builds cleanly (npm run build, 47 pages).

title: Refine kdr1u per review
description:

MEDIUM 1 (missing combo-classification plumbing): Lifting the reciprocal Operator<->Portal excludes in modifiers.py alone is insufficient. There is NO frozenset({'portal','operator'}) entry in _COMBO_MAP (modifiers.py:90-101), and ModifierSet.combo does a direct [] subscript (line 793) -- so .combo raises KeyError the moment a portal+operator ModifierSet is constructed. Fix: add a PORTAL_OPERATOR ModifierCombo + _COMBO_MAP entry, and teach BOTH == ModifierCombo.PORTAL predicates (compiler.py:254, _wiring.py:714) to also treat portal+operator as a mesh member. Write the guard-first test constructing a portal+operator node across all three surfaces FIRST -- it must KeyError immediately pre-fix, proving the gap.

If an Operator lands on an agent/act or sub-construct Portal member before that branch has the approval splice wired, it compiles WITHOUT an approval node -- Operator.when never interrupts, silent no-fire, D4 reintroduced for those classes. Fix: track ban-lift scope EXACTLY to implementation coverage. Safe default: implement atomic first, and KEEP a narrowed fail-loud rejection (ConfigurationError, with a should_fail fixture each) of Operator on agent/act + sub-construct Portal members until those classes get the approval splice too. Never lift the ban wider than the splice actually reaches. Resolve the DESCRIPTION-step-4-vs-DESIGN-step-7 contradiction (one says 'accept Operator on any member', the other says atomic-vs-all is undecided) toward this narrowed-scope resolution.

Also fold in while refining (LOW, non-blocking): the ban removal has 3 edit sites, not 2 -- modifiers.py:748 (Operator row), modifiers.py:757 (the reciprocal Portal row), and model_post_init's pairwise arm (~:819, not '_validate' as the design misnames it) -- test BOTH pipe orders (node|Operator()|Portal() and node|Portal()|Operator()).

title: Refine 2aw5c per review
description:

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for pt85t
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show pt85t` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/pt85t/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" pt85t
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (pt85t)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update pt85t --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update pt85t --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/pt85t/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add pt85t codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/pt85t/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for 5x43u
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show 5x43u` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/5x43u/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" 5x43u
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update 5x43u --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash

   ```

ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/5x43u/` MUST exist (it is

hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add 5x43u codebase-scan:complete
```

  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-do0d9
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-do0d9` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-do0d9/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-do0d9
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-do0d9)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-do0d9 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-do0d9 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-do0d9/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-do0d9 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: from_agent_spec: AgentNode reconstruction + Swarm-onto-Portal-mesh + RemoteAgent best-effort import
description:
01i0g's from_agent_spec() (src/neograph/loader.py) implements primitive import (LlmNode/ToolNode), per-group marker reconstruction (Oracle/Each/Loop/Operator), and FlowNode recursion -- but explicitly does NOT implement:

1. AgentNode -> agent/act Node reconstruction. Currently fails loud (ConfigurationError) when an AgentNode is encountered on import, even though neograph-i3zsh.1 shipped a real AgentNode+Agent+ServerTool export with a neograph/agent_spec marker carrying every field needed (mode/prompt/model/tools/gate_tools_when/context). This atom should read that marker back and reconstruct the exact agent/act Node, with a dedicated export->import round-trip test proving losslessness.

2. Swarm-onto-Portal-mesh import. Per the 2026-07-22 user decision (docs/design/agent-spec-ratification-2026-07-13.md §3a, now superseded), a Swarm-shaped Agent Spec should import onto a native Portal mesh (v1: sibling-node peers at one construct level). This requires understanding pyagentspec's Swarm/Agent-level composite shape (distinct from the Flow/Node primitives from_agent_spec currently walks) and building Portal-modified Node(s) with handoff_param/handoff_channel wiring -- a substantial separate undertaking, not attempted in 01i0g.

3. RemoteAgent/A2AAgent best-effort lowering (ratification doc §3b): map to a name-bound scripted/raw Node + WARNING, per the ratified best-effort behavior. Not yet implemented -- from_agent_spec currently only recognizes LlmNode/ToolNode/AgentNode(fail-loud)/FlowNode.

Cite: src/neograph/loader.py's _reconstruct_primitive_node (the dispatch point for all three).
design:
## Core Invariant
Import is the EXACT inverse of export and NEVER silently downgrades: a neograph/agent_spec (or neograph/tool_spec) marker reconstructs the exact node losslessly; a marker-less/foreign primitive is either reconstructed structurally onto a REAL neograph primitive (Swarm->Portal mesh) or best-effort lowered to a name-bound Node WITH a warning -- and the reconstructed IR is always subjected to the same assembly-time validation (_check_portal_mesh etc.) a hand-written pipeline gets, so no invalid or misreconstructed mesh can compile.

## Implementation Plan
1. Gap 1 (loader.py _reconstruct_primitive_node AgentNode branch, :120-133): REPLACE the fail-loud. Read spec_node.metadata['neograph/agent_spec']; build the agent/act Node by inverting _agent_spec_marker (mode/prompt/model/tools->Tool(...)/gate_tools_when/context), reusing the existing _inputs_from_data_edges + _agent_spec_props_to_type for inputs/outputs. INVERT the fail-loud pin at tests/test_agent_spec_import.py:183 into a losslessness assertion; add the round-trip + tool_spec/agent_spec metadata-survival test to tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py.
2. Gap 3 (same AgentNode branch): when spec_node.agent has NO neograph/agent_spec marker, dispatch on type(spec_node.agent).__name__ -- 'Agent' -> best-effort agent-mode reconstruction (mode='agent', from Agent.system_prompt/llm_config/tools); 'RemoteAgent'/'A2AAgent'/'OciAgent' -> name-bound scripted Node (scripted_fn=agent name) + warnings.warn (reuse the loader.py:173 warnings.warn pattern), stash endpoint shape in metadata['neograph/remote_agent']. ServerTool-as-agent stays fail-loud (orchestrator-side line, ratification §3b).
3. Gap 2 (from_agent_spec entry, loader.py:353): add a top-level `if type(component).__name__ == 'Swarm'` branch -> new _reconstruct_swarm_mesh(swarm) helper (sibling of the existing _reconstruct_* cluster). It: (a) SYNTHESIZES a uniform payload model via create_model with a 'goto: str' route field; (b) for each Swarm agent builds an agent-mode member Node (reusing gap-1 reconstruction) with inputs={'handoff': Payload}, outputs=Payload, then | Portal(to=[b for (a,b) in swarm.relationships if a is agent]); (c) orders members with swarm.first_agent FIRST and sets max_hops/on_exhaust only on the entry Portal; (d) returns Construct(name=swarm.name, nodes=members). Do NOT set handoff_param/handoff_channel -- normalize_ir/_HandoffParamNormalizer are the sole writers and fire automatically in Construct.__init__. Let _check_portal_mesh validate the result (disconnected/non-contiguous Swarm -> clear ConfigurationError). v1 scope: one connected mesh at one construct level (cross-construct handoff deferred to neograph-do0d9). Add a Swarm->mesh reconstruction test (compile with FakeLLM) to tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py.
4. Update from_agent_spec docstring (loader.py:370-372) which currently says AgentNode + Swarm import are 'explicitly NOT implemented / fail loud' -- now they are. Keep ServerTool/BuiltinTool-as-agent fail-loud.
5. Gate: full `uv run --extra dev --extra agent-spec pytest tests/test_agent_spec_*.py` green, plus the general suite; each gap has its own regression test (AgentNode round-trip losslessness incl. tool budget/config/idempotent, Swarm->Portal mesh reconstruction, RemoteAgent best-effort+warning).

## Scope addendum (disease scan, 2026-07-23) — Step 0: centralize marker keys FIRST
Before any reconstruction branch, land the marker-key centralization the disease scan flagged (23 inline "neograph/*" literals across _agent_spec.py + loader.py, no shared constant — the export↔import contract can drift by a typo and silently downgrade). Introduce a module-level named-constant block in _agent_spec.py (_MARK_MODE='neograph/mode', _MARK_AGENT_SPEC='neograph/agent_spec', _MARK_TOOL_SPEC='neograph/tool_spec', _MARK_REMOTE_AGENT='neograph/remote_agent', plus the existing oracle/each/loop/operator/modifier/group_id/variant/branch keys), import them into loader.py, and swap ALL existing literals + aa5gq's new reads/writes to reference them. Guarded by tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py + test_agent_spec_import.py (any typo now fails a test instead of silently downgrading). Steps 1-5 below then reference the constants, never fresh inline literals. Full disposition table is in this bead's notes.

## Refinement addendum (architect review, neograph-hhgnz.29, 2026-07-23)
- SHARED HELPER (supersedes 'reuse gap-1' phrasing in steps 1-3): factor _node_from_spec_agent(spec_agent) that dispatches on marker presence — metadata['neograph/agent_spec'] present -> lossless gap-1 inversion; absent (foreign Swarm agents carry NO marker) -> best-effort gap-3 (mode='agent' from Agent.system_prompt/llm_config/tools). BOTH the AgentNode branch (step 1/2) and the Swarm member builder (step 3) call this helper. A raw metadata['neograph/agent_spec'] read in the Swarm path would KeyError on foreign agents.
- STEP 0 STRUCTURAL GUARD (a shared symbol does NOT catch a VALUE typo — both sides move together): add a guard-first STRUCTURAL test (tests/test_guards_*) banning re-inlined '"neograph/' string literals outside the single constant block, PLUS value-pinning asserts (_MARK_AGENT_SPEC == 'neograph/agent_spec', ...) since the constants ARE the wire format foreign tools/stored YAMLs literally expect. Behavioral round-trip coverage alone is insufficient.
- SWARM DOWNGRADE WARNING (Core Invariant no-silent-downgrade): Swarm import is a best-effort/warning arm, NOT the clean structural arm. Emit warnings.warn documenting (a) route-only payload synthesis and (b) name-bound live-LLM members; AND fold the Swarm's declared Properties (+ agent output schemas where available) into the create_model payload as data fields, so a data-carrying Swarm does not silently lose its data channel.
- SINGLE SHARED PAYLOAD INSTANCE: _check_portal_mesh checks uniform-payload + reserved-handoff-key by IDENTITY ('is', :135/:243). Synthesize EXACTLY ONE payload model object and reuse the SAME instance as every member's outputs AND inputs['handoff']; a create_model-per-member fails assembly.
- HOP KNOBS: do NOT set max_hops/on_exhaust on the synthesized entry Portal (Swarm carries no budget); Portal defaults (10/'error') apply and the entry-only check keys on model_fields_set, so omitting the knobs passes trivially and is the correct minimal move.
acceptance_criteria: All three gaps closed, each with its own regression test proving the specific behavior (AgentNode round-trip losslessness, Swarm->Portal mesh reconstruction, RemoteAgent best-effort+warning). Full quality gate green.
notes:
Also covers l7gvy's deferred import+round-trip slice: once AgentNode import reconstruction lands, add a test proving a Tool's budget/config/idempotent survive via the neograph/tool_spec marker each ServerTool carries (src/neograph/_agent_spec.py::_tool_to_server_tool, shipped by l7gvy 2026-07-22).
## Findings (research neograph-hhgnz.2)

### Core reuse targets (do NOT reinvent)
- The importer already exists and is well-factored: `from_agent_spec()` in src/neograph/loader.py:353 with a per-modifier reconstruction cluster (_reconstruct_oracle_group / _reconstruct_each_node / _reconstruct_loop_item / _reconstruct_operator_item) each declared 'the inverse of _agent_spec._lower_X'. All three gaps EXTEND this existing pattern -- they add branches, not new subsystems.
- The dispatch point for gaps 1 & 3 is _reconstruct_primitive_node (loader.py:111): its `elif cls_name == 'AgentNode'` branch (loader.py:120-133) currently FAILS LOUD. Gap 1 (real Agent) and gap 3 (RemoteAgent/A2AAgent) both dispatch HERE by inspecting spec_node.agent's runtime type. Gap 2 (Swarm) dispatches at the TOP-LEVEL from_agent_spec entry (a Swarm is an AgenticComponent, NOT a Flow, so it never reaches _reconstruct_primitive_node).

### Gap 1 -- AgentNode -> agent/act Node (LOSSLESS, marker-driven)
- The export side (src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:168-183 _lower_node, :249-271 _agent_spec_marker) stamps AgentNode.metadata['neograph/agent_spec'] = {mode, prompt, model, tools:[{name,budget,config,idempotent}], gate_tools_when(str-only), context}. Import is the EXACT inverse: read that blob, build Node(name, mode=marker['mode'], prompt=marker['prompt'], model=marker['model'], tools=[Tool(t['name'],budget=t['budget'],config=t['config'],idempotent=t['idempotent']) for t in marker['tools']], gate_tools_when=marker['gate_tools_when'], context=marker['context'], inputs=..., outputs=...). inputs/outputs reconstruct via the SAME existing helpers _inputs_from_data_edges + _agent_spec_props_to_type already used at loader.py:141-150.
- Tool ctor: Tool(name_, /, budget=0, config={}, idempotent=False) frozen BaseModel (src/neograph/tool.py:38-73) -- reads back directly from the marker dict.
- The redundant tool_spec survival test (l7gvy deferred slice): each ServerTool attached to the Agent ALSO carries metadata['neograph/tool_spec']={name,budget,config,idempotent} (_agent_spec.py:212-246 _tool_to_server_tool). The agent_spec marker's flat tools list is the PRIMARY reconstruction source (single blob, by design per _agent_spec_marker docstring); the tool_spec marker is an independent carrier on the ServerTool. Add a standalone assertion that spec_node.agent.tools[i].metadata['neograph/tool_spec'] survives to_dict->from_dict (the §6.1 metadata-survival concern, ratification doc:131-133).
- Must FLIP the existing fail-loud pin: tests/test_agent_spec_import.py:183 TestFromAgentSpecFailsLoudOnAgentNode currently asserts ConfigurationError on AgentNode import -- that test INVERTS to a round-trip losslessness test.

### Gap 2 -- Swarm -> Portal mesh (structural reconstruction, NOT marker-driven)
- pyagentspec Swarm shape (v26.1.2): Swarm(first_agent: AgenticComponent, relationships: List[Tuple[AgenticComponent,AgenticComponent]] (directed from->to handoff pairs), handoff: bool|HandoffMode, inputs, outputs). Swarm subclasses AgenticComponent -- it is a TOP-LEVEL document, never a Flow node.
- Target IR = a Portal PEER-mode mesh (src/neograph/modifiers.py:600 Portal). Each Swarm agent -> a Node | Portal(to=[peer names from relationships], ...); first_agent -> entry member (must be FIRST in construct.nodes order, gets max_hops/on_exhaust which are entry-only). Exemplar to copy: examples/28_portal_swarm.py (declarative surface: Node.scripted(name, inputs={'handoff': Payload}, outputs=Payload) | Portal(to=[peers], max_hops=6)).
- Reuse the mesh wiring machinery -- do NOT set handoff_param/handoff_channel yourself. _ir_normalize.py::_HandoffParamNormalizer (SOLE writer of handoff_param, fires when portal set + dict-form inputs has reserved 'handoff' key) and normalize_ir (SOLE writer of handoff_channel, entry-keyed, :271-273/:291-292) auto-wire the mesh in Construct.__init__. The importer ONLY needs to produce each member as Node(inputs={'handoff': Payload}, outputs=Payload) | Portal(to=[...]). Validation is enforced by _validation_portal.py::_check_portal_mesh (contiguity, uniform single payload type, peer existence, single connected component, entry-only knobs, route field on payload).
- CRITICAL synthesis requirement (from _check_portal_mesh:207-237): the shared payload model MUST carry a route field (Portal.route default 'goto') annotated str or Literal[member-names]. A foreign Swarm has no such neograph payload model, so the importer must SYNTHESIZE one via pydantic create_model (spec_types uses create_model at :173/:221) -- e.g. a model with a 'goto: str' field -- and use it uniformly as every member's inputs['handoff'] type AND outputs type.
- Each Swarm agent is itself an Agent composite -> reuse gap-1's agent-mode reconstruction to build each member's underlying Node before piping | Portal.

### Gap 3 -- RemoteAgent/A2AAgent/OciAgent -> name-bound scripted Node + WARNING (best-effort)
- These arrive as an AgentNode whose .agent is a RemoteAgent/A2AAgent/OciAgent (all AgenticComponent subclasses; AgentNode.agent is typed AgenticComponent). So the SAME _reconstruct_primitive_node AgentNode branch inspects type(spec_node.agent).__name__: 'Agent' -> gap 1; 'RemoteAgent'/'A2AAgent'/'OciAgent' -> gap 3.
- Best-effort lowering (ratification §3b, doc:95-101): map to a name-bound scripted Node (scripted_fn = agent name; factory supplied at bind time, same contract as any ToolNode import at loader.py:119) + warnings.warn (reuse the existing warnings.warn pattern already in loader.py:173 _reconstruct_oracle_group). Stash endpoint/connection shape in metadata['neograph/remote_agent'] for re-export (A2AAgent carries agent_url/connection_config/session_parameters).
- The principled line (doc:101): client-initiated (RemoteAgent/A2AAgent/OciAgent) -> lowerable; orchestrator-side (ServerTool/BuiltinTool) -> FAIL. ServerTool-as-agent stays fail-loud.
## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/loader.py:111 _reconstruct_primitive_node -- THE dispatch point for gaps 1 & 3; the AgentNode branch (:120-133) is the fail-loud to replace.
- src/neograph/loader.py:353 from_agent_spec -- TOP-LEVEL entry; add a `type(component).__name__ == 'Swarm'` branch here for gap 2 (Swarm is not a Flow). Param is already typed Any.
- src/neograph/loader.py:141-150 -- inputs/outputs reconstruction helpers (_agent_spec_props_to_type + _inputs_from_data_edges) to reuse verbatim for the agent Node.
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:249-271 _agent_spec_marker -- the EXACT blob shape gap 1 must invert (mode/prompt/model/tools/gate_tools_when/context).
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:212-246 _tool_to_server_tool -- the neograph/tool_spec marker (budget/config/idempotent) the l7gvy survival test asserts.
- src/neograph/modifiers.py:600 Portal (peer mode: to=, route='goto', max_hops entry-only, on_exhaust); modifiers.py:591 HANDOFF_END.
- src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py:152 _HandoffParamNormalizer + :239 normalize_ir -- SOLE writers of handoff_param/handoff_channel; the importer must NOT set these fields (single-writer invariant, guard G3). Just emit inputs={'handoff': Payload} + | Portal(to=...).
- src/neograph/_validation_portal.py:40 _check_portal_mesh -- the mesh rules the synthesized IR must satisfy (uniform single payload type, route field str/Literal on payload, contiguity, entry-first, peer existence).
- examples/28_portal_swarm.py -- the exemplar Portal mesh (both @node and declarative Node.scripted|Portal surfaces). Copy the declarative form for programmatic reconstruction.
- src/neograph/spec_types.py:173/:221 -- create_model usage precedent for synthesizing the Swarm payload model with a 'goto: str' route field.
- tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py -- the round-trip test home (module-level pytest.importorskip('pyagentspec')); add AgentNode losslessness + Swarm->mesh + RemoteAgent-warning tests here.
- tests/test_agent_spec_import.py:183 TestFromAgentSpecFailsLoudOnAgentNode -- INVERT this pin (fail-loud -> lossless round trip).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Portal payload route field: _check_portal_mesh REQUIRES a route field (default 'goto') on the payload model annotated str or Literal. A foreign Swarm carries no such model -> the importer MUST synthesize one (create_model, 'goto: str'). If omitted, import produces an invalid mesh that fails assembly validation. This is the substantial part of gap 2, not the marker read.
- Swarm relationships are DIRECTED tuples (from,to); Portal.to= is per-node directed successors. Map each agent A's to= to [b for (a,b) in relationships if a is A]. entry = first_agent (must be nodes[0]).
- Single-mesh + contiguity: _check_portal_mesh rejects two disjoint meshes and non-contiguous members. A Swarm with a disconnected relationship graph will fail assembly -- surface this as a clear ConfigurationError at import (v1 scope: one connected mesh, one construct level; cross-construct handoff is deferred to neograph-do0d9).
- Swarm members are Agent composites -> each reconstructed member is an agent-mode Node needing a live LLM factory at compile; the mesh is structurally lossless but members are name-bound (runtime binding required), same best-effort contract as RemoteAgent. Document this in the test (compile with a FakeLLM).
- Marker-less foreign Agent (AgentNode with a plain Agent but NO neograph/agent_spec marker): cannot distinguish agent vs act -> default mode='agent' (read-only, conservative); reconstruct prompt/model/tools from Agent.system_prompt/llm_config.model_id/tools (each ServerTool.metadata['neograph/tool_spec'] or name-only). Keep this path best-effort + note it; the marker path is the lossless one.
- Oracle scripted-mode round-trip bug is OUT OF SCOPE here (already noted at test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py:153-162) -- do not conflate.
- metadata survival (ratification §6.1, doc:131-133): assert neograph/agent_spec AND neograph/tool_spec survive a full to_dict->from_dict before trusting the marker tier -- this is the one carried caveat that gates lossless reconstruction.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-aa5gq) — 2026-07-23

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for l7gvy
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show l7gvy` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/l7gvy/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" l7gvy
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (l7gvy)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update l7gvy --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update l7gvy --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/l7gvy/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add l7gvy codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>

   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:

   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).

     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.

       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   ```

     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

exists:

```bash

```

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.

   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for i3zsh.1
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show i3zsh.1` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/i3zsh.1/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" i3zsh.1
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (i3zsh.1)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update i3zsh.1 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update i3zsh.1 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/i3zsh.1/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add i3zsh.1 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must

  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Structured-parse aborts on stringly-"null" GLM emissions for Optional fields (no repair/retry)
description:
What

neograph's structured-output parse path (the think/agent node parse in _llm_retry.py, via _apply_null_defaults) raises ExecutionError: Validation failed for <Model> — an un-retried, un-repaired hard abort — when the LLM emits the string literal "null" (also seen: "none", "n/a", "") as the value of an Optional numeric or enum field. The JSON itself is well-formed; the failure is a pydantic ValidationError (int_parsing / enum) on a field that is already declared X | None, because the recovery layer coerces JSON null / missing keys to None but not the string "null".

Why

- This is a general bridge defect, not a per-model or per-consumer issue: any structured node whose output model has Optional int/enum/other-non-str fields can hit it whenever the model stringifies a null.
- It is distinct from the null-default class already handled (the neograph-s1u4 _apply_null_defaults work): that recovers JSON null/absent fields; a value of "null" (a str) slips past it and reaches pydantic as an unparseable string.
- It makes any downstream live-GLM gate non-deterministically red. Observed concretely in agent-stark (stark-h46): a full make ci-test run had 3 live-GLM tests crash on this, all in the research_company -> research-normalize node producing NormalizedResearch:
ExecutionError: Validation failed for NormalizedResearch
  company.freshness_days:                 Input should be a valid integer  [input_value='null', input_type=str]
  company.hiring_signals.0.total_open_roles: Input should be a valid integer  [input_value='null', input_type=str]
  company.funding_rounds.0.round_type:    Input should be 'Series A'|'Series B'|'IPO'|...  [type=enum, input_value='null']
- Earlier runs of the same suite passed — the flake surfaces only when the model happens to stringify a null. A single bad emission aborts the whole run.

Root cause (precise)

- The construct does enable output_strategy="json_mode" (so JSON parses and the null-default recovery runs), and the fields are int | None / Enum | None.
- _apply_null_defaults maps JSON null/missing -> None for Optional fields, but has no rule for the string sentinel "null", so the str reaches pydantic and fails.
- There is no retry on a transient structured ValidationError (only the null-default disposition), so one malformed field aborts the node instead of re-prompting.

Reproduction (deterministic — the right test layer, boundary)

Replay a hand-constructed / recorded-real structured response through _parse_json_response for a model shaped like:
class Company(BaseModel):
    freshness_days: int | None = None
    round_type: SomeEnum | None = None
    hiring_signals: list[HiringSignal] = []   # HiringSignal.total_open_roles: int | None
with {"freshness_days": "null", "round_type": "null", "hiring_signals": [{"total_open_roles": "null"}]}.
Current behavior: raises ExecutionError: Validation failed.
Expected: the Optional fields normalize to None (or the node retries and yields a valid model); a bare pydantic crash mid-run should not happen for this recoverable class.

Proposed direction (for the maintainer to own/design)

Mirror the existing _apply_null_defaults recovery (neograph-s1u4):
1. For Optional fields only (never a field whose declared type is/includes str), recognize the string sentinels "null"/"none"/"nil"/"n/a"/"na" (and "" where the field can't be a plain str) and normalize to None before the null/default disposition — recursing into nested models and list[BaseModel] items. A legitimate str value must never be destroyed.
2. A non-Optional field that receives "null" must still fail loud (retry / re-prompt territory), not be silently coerced.
3. Consider a bounded retry on transient structured ValidationError (the model usually returns valid on re-prompt), so this and truncation-class malformations self-heal before aborting.

Acceptance
- Deterministic tests at the parse boundary: string "null" -> None for Optional int and for Optional enum; "null"/"none" inside list[Model] items -> None; a legit str | None value and a legit "" for a str field are preserved; a non-Optional int receiving "null" still raises.
- Only Optional fields are ever touched (verified via the annotation, not the value).
- Downstream live-GLM structured nodes no longer abort on this class.

Cross-reference

- Downstream tracking issue: agent-stark stark-h46 (the flake as seen in agent-stark's engage/research gate).
- Related prior art in-repo: neograph-s1u4 (_apply_null_defaults null-default recovery), which this extends.
- A candidate/prototype patch exists on a local branch (stark-h46-stringly-null-repair, commit 2f3e1fd) that was produced without maintainer authorization — flagged here only so you're aware; it's yours to review, rework, or discard. Not merged, published, or otherwise acted on as part of filing this bug.
notes:
## Candidate patch verified (2026-07-16, read-only)

Commit 2f3e1fd on the stray branch 'stark-h46-stringly-null-repair' was inspected and independently verified WITHOUT merging, checking out, or otherwise touching develop -- via an isolated 'git worktree add --detach' at the commit, run, and torn down.

### What it does
Adds `_is_stringly_null`/`_optional_inner_types` to `src/neograph/_llm_retry.py`, called from `_apply_null_defaults` before the existing null-disposition branches. Coerces the STRING sentinels "null"/"none"/"nil"/"n/a"/"na" (and "" when the field's non-null type isn't itself `str`) to real `None` -- gated by `_optional_inner_types` so ONLY Optional-typed fields are touched (checked via the annotation, never the value). Applies recursively via the pre-existing nested-BaseModel/list[BaseModel] recursion in `_apply_null_defaults` (unchanged) -- confirmed by reading the full function body, not just the diff hunk.

### Test coverage (tests/modes/test_llm_internals.py, 5 new tests)
- stringly "null" -> None for Optional[int] -- PASS
- stringly "null" -> None for Optional[Enum] -- PASS
- stringly "null"/"none" -> None inside list[BaseModel] items (nested recursion) -- PASS
- a real str value (str | None) and "" for a plain str field are preserved untouched -- PASS
- a REQUIRED (non-Optional) int field receiving "null" still raises ExecutionError (fail-loud preserved, not silently coerced) -- PASS

All 5 match this bug's acceptance criteria exactly.

### Verification run (isolated worktree, commit 2f3e1fd, not merged)
