title: to_agent_spec: proper AgentNode+tools lowering for agent/act mode (currently ToolNode placeholder)
description: i3zsh's implementation (src/neograph/_agent_spec.py, _lower_node) currently lowers agent/act-mode Nodes to a ToolNode placeholder (stamped metadata['neograph/mode']) instead of a proper pyagentspec AgentNode+tools composite, because AgentNode.agent requires an AgenticComponent (pyagentspec.agenticcomponent) whose construction wasn't researched in the i3zsh implement atom (scope was bounded by the write-test atom's pinned tests, which don't exercise agent/act mode). Research AgenticComponent's shape (fields, how tools/instructions attach), then replace the ToolNode placeholder with a real AgentNode lowering that surfaces Node.tools + the ReAct loop identity, with a dedicated regression test (agent-mode node -> AgentNode, not ToolNode). Cite: src/neograph/_agent_spec.py's _lower_node agent/act branch and its inline comment.
design:
## Core Invariant
to_agent_spec() must never silently drop a Node field it cannot represent (the exporter's Core Invariant, already stated in _agent_spec.py's module docstring) -- every irreversible flattening either lowers to a real Agent Spec primitive PLUS a neograph/-prefixed round-trip marker, or fails loud; agent/act mode is no exception, and closing this gap must not re-open a silent seam anywhere else (e.g. must not silently drop budget/idempotent/gate_tools_when just because they don't exist on plain pyagentspec Tool/Agent fields).

## Implementation Plan
1. Replace the fail-loud branch in _lower_node's mode in ('agent','act') case (src/neograph/_agent_spec.py ~145-176) with a real lowering: build `pyagentspec.agent.Agent(name=f'{node.name}-agent', llm_config=_make_llm_config(node), system_prompt=node.prompt or '', tools=[_make_server_tool-equivalent per node.tools[i]], inputs=_properties_for(node.inputs) or None, outputs=_properties_for(node.outputs) or None)`, then wrap in `nodes_mod.AgentNode(name=node.name, agent=agent, metadata={'neograph/mode': node.mode, 'neograph/agent_spec': {...}})`. Reuse _make_llm_config verbatim (already parametrized by node.model).
2. Add a small tool-lowering helper (parallel to _make_server_tool) that builds one ServerTool per node.tools[i] using tool.name; do NOT reinvent -- copy _make_server_tool's ServerTool(name=..., description=..., inputs=None, outputs=None) shape (tool-level typed I/O isn't tracked on neograph's Tool, so leave None like the existing scripted-mode caller does).
3. Populate the neograph/agent_spec marker dict (mirrors neograph/oracle_spec's shape in _lower_oracle) with everything NOT representable in plain Agent/ServerTool fields: {'mode': node.mode, 'prompt': node.prompt, 'model': node.model, 'tools': [{'name', 'budget', 'config', 'idempotent'} per Tool -- reuse ToolSpec's field names from _spec_schema.py:66], 'gate_tools_when': node.gate_tools_when (str form only; still reject callable via existing _reject_unrepresentable_fields), 'context': node.context}. This is the completeness net for a future from_agent_spec().
4. Update tests/test_agent_spec_export.py: replace test_agent_act_node_is_rejected_not_silently_downgraded with a positive test asserting (a) result is an AgentNode (not ToolNode), (b) node.agent.system_prompt/llm_config.model_id/tools names match the source Node's prompt/model/tools, (c) node.metadata['neograph/agent_spec'] contains the full reconstruction fields (mode/prompt/model/tools w/ budget+idempotent/gate_tools_when/context) so no field is silently dropped -- this is the achievable round-trip-fidelity proof at export-only scope (see NEEDS USER INPUT note in Findings about whether a from_agent_spec import path is also in scope here or a sibling task).
5. Update the module docstring's paragraph 3 (currently lists 'agent'/'act' mode among constructs that FAIL LOUD) to remove it from that list now that it lowers.
6. Run the full to_agent_spec test file + guard suite (test_guards_* for import-DAG/no-Any) to confirm nothing regresses; this is an EXPORT-only change (no compiler.py/factory.py/runtime touch), so blast radius is contained to _agent_spec.py + its test file.
acceptance_criteria: EXPORT-SIDE COMPLETENESS ONLY (re-scoped 2026-07-22 per architect review): to_agent_spec() must lower an agent/act mode Node to a real pyagentspec AgentNode+Agent+ServerTool composite (not the ToolNode fail-loud placeholder), AND stamp a neograph/agent_spec marker carrying every field needed for a future importer to reconstruct the node losslessly (mode, prompt, model, tools incl. budget/config/idempotent, gate_tools_when string form, context). Acceptance is proven by a regression test asserting: (a) the lowered SpecNode is an AgentNode, not a ToolNode; (b) the marker dict contains all the above fields; (c) json.dumps(marker) succeeds with no callable/_bound_tool leak. The ACTUAL export->import round-trip test (proving a from_agent_spec() importer reconstructs the exact same node) is EXPLICITLY DEFERRED to neograph-01i0g, which depends on this task and owns the importer. This task does not implement or call from_agent_spec().
notes:
REFRAME (2026-07-22): this is NOT a cosmetic 'nicer AgentNode representation' — it is a ROUND-TRIP-FIDELITY / never-silently-drop fix. The v1 ToolNode placeholder silently dropped the node's prompt/model/tools (only a neograph/mode marker survived) with NO flow-level neograph/source fallback (that fallback was a docstring promise the code never delivered). INTERIM (shipped 03dc849): to_agent_spec now FAILS LOUD on agent/act mode rather than emit the lossy placeholder — the silent seam is closed. THIS task replaces the fail-loud with the real lowering: either (a) a proper pyagentspec AgentNode+tools composite, OR (b) a full neograph/agent_spec reconstruction blob (mode/prompt/model/tools/budgets/context) mirroring neograph/oracle_spec, so from_agent_spec can rebuild the exact agent node. Acceptance MUST include an export->import round-trip test proving an agent node survives losslessly. Until this lands, agent/act is export-rejected.
## Findings
- REUSE TARGET (concrete class): `pyagentspec.agent.Agent` (site-packages/pyagentspec/agent.py) is the ONLY concrete `AgenticComponent` (pyagentspec/agenticcomponent.py is `abstract=True`, no fields of its own — it's a marker base). `Agent` fields: `llm_config: SerializeAsAny[LlmConfig]`, `system_prompt: str`, `tools: list[SerializeAsAny[Tool]]`, `toolboxes`, `human_in_the_loop: bool=True`, `transforms`. `pyagentspec.flows.nodes.agentnode.AgentNode(name=, agent=)` wraps it — `agent: SerializeAsAny[AgenticComponent]`, inputs/outputs are INFERRED from `agent.inputs`/`agent.outputs` (not passed directly to AgentNode).
- Ratified doc row already names the target: `docs/design/agent-spec-ratification-2026-07-13.md:22` — `Node mode agent/act` -> `Agent / AgentNode (+ tools)` | DIRECT | ReAct cycle. This task closes exactly that already-approved gap; no new design decision needed, just implementation.
- Tool mapping: neograph `Tool` (`src/neograph/tool.py:38`) has `name`, `budget`, `config`, `idempotent` (+ private `_bound_tool`) — NONE of these (budget/idempotent/config) exist on pyagentspec's plain `Tool`/`ServerTool` (site-packages/pyagentspec/tools/servertool.py — `ServerTool(Tool): pass`, only `name`/`description`/`inputs`/`outputs`). So a straight `ServerTool` per `node.tools[i]` loses budget/idempotent/config — these must ride in the round-trip marker blob, exactly like Oracle's `models`/`merge_fn` riding in `neograph/oracle_spec` (`_agent_spec.py` `_lower_oracle`).
- Existing per-tool round-trip precedent to copy field names from: `_spec_schema.py:66` `ToolSpec(name, budget, config)` (the YAML-spec tool shape) — reuse this shape (add `idempotent`) for the `neograph/agent_spec` marker's tools list, don't invent new field names.
- `_make_server_tool`/`_make_llm_config` in `_agent_spec.py` are the exact helpers to extend/reuse: `_make_llm_config(node)` already builds `SpecLlmConfig(name=f'{node.name}-llm', model_id=node.model or 'default')` and is called unconditionally for think mode AND Oracle variants — same call for agent/act's `Agent.llm_config`.
- Current deprecated/rejected code path: `_lower_node`'s agent/act branch in `_agent_spec.py` (lines ~145-176) currently raises `ConfigurationError` (interim fail-loud, shipped 03dc849) with hint text pointing at neograph-i3zsh.1 — this whole branch is what gets replaced.
- Pinned test that currently asserts the (to-be-replaced) fail-loud behavior: `tests/test_agent_spec_export.py::TestUnrepresentableFieldsRejected::test_agent_act_node_is_rejected_not_silently_downgraded` (parametrized agent/act) — this test must be REPLACED (not just deleted) with a positive lowering + round-trip-fidelity assertion per the bead's REFRAME acceptance criteria.
- `gate_tools_when` is ALREADY separately rejected by `_reject_unrepresentable_fields` (only the callable form; string/condition-name form is NOT currently checked against agent/act — since agent/act itself currently fail-loud-rejects first, this interaction was never exercised). Once agent/act lowering lands, decide whether string `gate_tools_when` rides in the `neograph/agent_spec` marker (recommended: yes, alongside mode/prompt/model/tools/context) or is separately rejected — must not silently drop it either way.
- No `from_agent_spec()` (import direction) exists yet anywhere in `src/neograph` — this task is EXPORT-side only (to_agent_spec). The bead's acceptance criteria mention 'export->import round-trip test' but there is no importer to round-trip through yet; the achievable round-trip proof at this task's scope is: lower to `AgentNode`, assert `node.agent.system_prompt/llm_config/tools` match the source Node, AND assert the `neograph/agent_spec` metadata blob contains every field needed to reconstruct (mode, prompt, model, tools w/ budget+idempotent+config, gate_tools_when, context) — a full functional from_agent_spec() reconstruction is a SEPARATE task (likely covered by another wave-3 sibling, 01i0g/0la8v/l7gvy — worth checking bd show on those before final acceptance sign-off, flagged as NEEDS USER INPUT below).
- NEEDS USER INPUT: the bead's acceptance text says '...OR (b) a full neograph/agent_spec reconstruction blob... so from_agent_spec can rebuild the exact agent node' and requires 'an export->import round-trip test proving an agent node survives losslessly' — but no `from_agent_spec` importer exists in this codebase at all (grep returns zero hits outside this task's own prose). Confirm whether this task is expected to ALSO stand up a minimal from_agent_spec path for agent/act nodes only, or whether the round-trip test should assert marker-blob completeness (lossless-IN-PRINCIPLE) without an actual importer, deferring the general from_agent_spec() to a sibling task.

- `node.inputs`/`node.outputs` (neograph's typed I/O) must still surface on `AgentNode` for downstream data-flow edges to attach -- but `AgentNode._get_inferred_inputs/_get_inferred_outputs` derive from `agent.inputs`/`agent.outputs`, NOT from a param passed to AgentNode directly.    Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |

   ```
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   ```

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for do0d9
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show do0d9` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/do0d9/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" do0d9
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |

   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update do0d9 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

the motivating site.

findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a

   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"

   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/nnds9/`:

title: Sweep verification for neograph-03djs
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-03djs
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-03djs`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-03djs)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-03djs --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-03djs sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

description:

executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-ozrct` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-ozrct/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-ozrct
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-ozrct)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-ozrct --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-ozrct --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-ozrct/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-ozrct codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Portal addressability: port-taxonomy design doc (route-to-entry-port; entry-map + mesh-transparent-exit) — Core Invariant for mesh extensions
description:
Write docs/design/portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md — the Core Invariant for the Portal mesh extensions (nnds9 / do0d9 / a37vk). They implement AGAINST this one invariant, not as bespoke tasks (anti-band-aid).

CONTENT:
- Three-class addressability taxonomy: ATOMIC (scripted/think = 1 node, goto works) | PORT-BEARING REGION (sub-Construct, agent/act cycle = multi-node but single defined entry+reconverging exit -> addressable WITH machinery) | PORTLESS REGION (bare Each/Oracle/Loop/Operator inline = fork/join or interrupt-on-static-edge, NO single boundary port -> permanently NON-addressable by design; wrap in a sub-Construct to hand off to it).
- The invariant: runtime routing operates on BOUNDARY PORTS; modifiers are internal wiring, not ports. neograph already has the port concept — Construct.input/output (singular).
- The two mechanisms that unlock port-bearing regions: (1) a compile-time entry-label map (DX destination name -> LangGraph entry node), stashed on the graph like schema_fingerprint; (2) mesh-transparent exit (the region's last_name consults the mesh channel instead of falling to its static successor).
- Framing: reducibility-by-construction (structured goto — reach a region's entry, never its interior). Prior art: Harel statecharts / UML entry-point pseudostates + history, behavior-tree uniform tick interface, FBP/HDL/ADL ports, Temporal child workflows, OpenAI Swarm agent-granularity handoffs, LangGraph subgraph + Command.PARENT.
- Bound the claim: ports kill invalid-entry-by-construction; max_hops handles the residual nonterminating-legal-routing class.
design:
## Core Invariant
Runtime routing operates on BOUNDARY PORTS, never region interiors -- a Command(goto=...) target (or, pending D-LOWERING-DISSENT, a router+path_map equivalent) must always resolve to a construct's declared entry (Construct.input's compiled entry node, an entry-label-map destination, or a Portal peer name), so an "addressable region" is defined by having exactly one such entry AND one reconverging exit; modifiers (Each/Oracle/Loop/Operator) are internal wiring that never qualifies as a port, which is why bare fork/join/interrupt regions stay permanently non-addressable unless wrapped in a sub-Construct.

## Implementation Plan
1. Write `docs/design/portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md` as a design doc, NOT new code -- this task (u7gy8.2) only produces the doc; nnds9/a37vk/do0d9 implement against it.
2. Structure the doc around the existing `Construct.input`/`Construct.output` port concept (`src/neograph/construct.py:113-123`) as the anchor -- state explicitly that PORT-BEARING REGION addressability is "give Construct.input's compiled entry node a stable, DX-facing label" and "make the region's exit consult the mesh channel instead of its static successor," not a new port primitive.
3. Present the three-class taxonomy with ONE worked example per class, reusing code already in the repo instead of inventing hypotheticals. Lead with symbol names (`make_portal_fn`, `_add_agent_cycle`, `_add_subgraph`) in doc prose; keep line numbers only as an as-of-2026-07-15 parenthetical, not the primary reference (design docs outlive line numbers):
   - ATOMIC: any scripted/think node under `Portal(to=[...])` -- cite `make_portal_fn` (`src/neograph/factory.py:103`, as of 2026-07-15) as the shipped mechanism.
   - PORT-BEARING REGION: (a) a sub-Construct compiled via `_add_subgraph` (`src/neograph/compiler.py:438`) -- single typed entry (`sub.input`) already enforced fail-loud; (b) the agent/act ReAct cycle (`_add_agent_cycle`, `src/neograph/_wiring.py:989`) -- single entry `{node}__agent`, reconverging exit via its conditional router. Name both as candidates the entry-label map + mesh-transparent-exit mechanisms unlock, motivating nnds9 (agent/act mesh members) and a37vk (self.handoff builder needs a stable name to target).
   - PORTLESS REGION: a bare `Each`/`Oracle`/`Loop`/`Operator` applied inline (not as a sub-Construct) -- no single entry/exit exists structurally (fan-out barrier or static post-edge), so it is permanently non-addressable; the doc's prescribed fix is "wrap it in a sub-Construct" (which then becomes PORT-BEARING via mechanism (a)), not a bespoke routing rule.
4. Specify mechanism 1 (entry-label map) as a compile-time artifact stashed on the compiled graph exactly like `schema_fingerprint`/`node_fingerprints` (`compiler.py` CompiledNeograph construction, near the `result = CompiledNeograph(...)` block) -- `dict[str, str]` DX-name -> LangGraph node name, computed once per compile() level (never crossing a sub-Construct boundary -- that crossing is explicitly do0d9's Command.PARENT mechanism, keep the two mechanisms textually separate so implementers don't conflate them).
5. Specify mechanism 2 (mesh-transparent exit) as extending the existing Portal exit pattern: a region's exit-node's successor-resolution step additionally checks the entry-keyed mesh channel (`StateKeys.handoff_payload(field_name)`, `src/neograph/_state_keys.py:130-139`) before falling through to its static next-node edge -- same channel/state-key convention Portal peer routing already uses, no new state-key scheme. NOTE: for a multi-node PORT-BEARING region (agent/act cycle, sub-Construct), which node is the 'exit node' (the parse node? the router's done-arm? the subgraph's opaque-node boundary?) is a per-region-class detail this taxonomy doc does NOT pin -- it is deferred to nnds9/do0d9, and the doc must say so explicitly rather than imply a single well-defined 'last_name' for all region classes.
6. Any `Command(goto=...)` emission the two mechanisms require must land in `factory.py` or `runner.py` only (guard G1, `TestCommandConstructionMonopoly` in `tests/test_guards_assembly.py`) -- state this explicitly as a constraint on nnds9/do0d9/a37vk implementers, not something this doc's own text needs to satisfy (it writes no code). HOWEVER: D-LOWERING-DISSENT (`docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md`) is explicitly ESCALATED/contested -- v1 kept `Command(goto)+destinations=` per the 07inf bead pin, but the reviewer (H3) preferred router+path_map, and the decision log's own morning action is "DECIDE: ratify Command(goto) or switch to router+path_map" (filed as a bead, unresolved as of this doc's writing). The doc MUST add a paragraph acknowledging D-LOWERING-DISSENT is contested and state that the entry-label-map + mesh-transparent-exit mechanisms are LOWERING-SUBSTRATE-AGNOSTIC: they name a destination; whether that destination is reached via `Command(goto)+destinations=` or a router+path_map is the separate, still-open D-LOWERING-DISSENT decision, not something this taxonomy doc settles. This keeps the taxonomy durable if v1's lowering substrate changes.
7. Any new mesh-assembly validation rule implied by the taxonomy (e.g. rejecting a Portal target that names a PORTLESS node) belongs in `src/neograph/_validation_portal.py`'s `_check_portal_mesh`, per the existing single-sited-validation-cluster discipline -- name this explicitly so a future implementer doesn't inline the check in the compiler or decorators.
8. Cite `docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md`'s D-MESH-LEVEL / D-MEMBER-MODES / D-FORWARD-EXEMPT entries verbatim as the origin and justification for nnds9/do0d9/a37vk -- do not re-derive rationale the decision log already recorded. ALSO cite D-LOWERING-DISSENT verbatim (per step 6 above) as the one contested entry the taxonomy's substrate-agnostic framing insulates against.
9. Include the "bound the claim" framing required by the task brief: ports make invalid-entry unrepresentable BY CONSTRUCTION (same class of guarantee as Portal's existing peer-target validation); `max_hops` (already shipped, `Portal.max_hops`/`on_exhaust`, `src/neograph/factory.py:146-199`) is what handles the residual nonterminating-but-legally-routed class -- these are two different guarantees and the doc must not conflate "addressable" with "terminating."

title: Sweep verification for neograph-q0svc
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-q0svc
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-q0svc`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-q0svc)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-q0svc --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-q0svc sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

description:

a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-f27xo`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-f27xo)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   ```bash

   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):

     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-f27xo sweep:complete
```

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The

description:

a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to

   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-on6jt`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).

     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.

       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   ```bash
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>

   ```

   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

exists:

```bash

```

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard

title: Sweep verification for neograph-rwion
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-rwion
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-rwion`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-rwion)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   ```bash

   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-rwion sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard

- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.

description:

executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-rwion` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-rwion/`:


   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import

   ```
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |

   ```

   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:


description:

INVARIANT: an invalid emitted spec raises BEFORE any sub-flow node executes, via the SAME Construct(...) gate as hand-written pipelines (construct.py:194); the dispatched flow can only reference pre-registered building blocks (Keymaker(scripted=, conditions=) — D-DISPATCH-REGISTRIES capability boundary); the result is typed by required Keymaker.output and lands on {node_field}_dispatch. ANTI-BAND-AID: dispatch goes through load_spec + compile() — no bespoke validator, no schema subset. Per design sections 3.5/4.2: modifiers.py (dispatch-mode discrimination + kwarg completeness), factory.py (make_keymaker_dispatch_fn, sync uses inner invoke, async ainvoke, no checkpointer — durability documented-opaque, Tier-2 belongs to neograph-mrb2y), compiler.py/_wiring.py (linear arm, no Command), state.py (_dispatch field, fingerprinted), tests + 2 fixtures (keymaker_dispatch_missing_output.py, keymaker_dispatch_minimal.py). ACCEPTANCE: happy path, rejection path (wrapped ConstructError before execution), and output-contract mismatch tested, sync + async.

Design doc (decision-complete, cite it): docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md. Decision log: docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md. Research grounding: docs/design/dynamic-handoff-research-2026-07-13.md. Epic: neograph-t1f7z (feature bead neograph-07inf). Execute via /dev-practices:execute discipline: TDD (failing test first), quality gates (uv run --extra dev pytest on touched suites, mypy, ruff) before commit; commit per task, no push until consolidation task.
design:
## Core Invariant
An emitted spec is validated by the SAME `Construct(...)` gate (construct.py:194, reached via `load_spec`) and compiled through the SAME `compile()` as hand-written pipelines — no bespoke validator, no schema subset — so an invalid spec raises (a `ConstructError` wrapped in `ExecutionError`) BEFORE any dispatched node executes, the dispatched flow references ONLY the pre-registered `Keymaker(scripted=,conditions=)` blocks, and the result is typed by the required `Keymaker.output` landing on `{node_field}_dispatch`.

## Implementation Plan
1. **factory.py — `make_keymaker_dispatch_fn(node, keymaker)`**, sibling of `make_keymaker_fn` (factory.py:100). Wrap `make_node_fn` (inner). Sync twin: `inner.invoke` → read `spec_field`/`input_field` off the node's own payload (`primary_output_field(field_name_for(node.name), node.outputs)`), then the shared `_dispatch(spec_dict, input_dict, config)` helper. Async twin: `inner.ainvoke` then the SAME helper but with `await compiled.ainvoke`. Return `RunnableLambda(sync, afunc=async)` via `named(...)` — mirror make_keymaker_fn/make_subgraph_fn EXACTLY. NO Command (reduced v1 linear arm — keep G1 monopoly narrow).
2. **The dispatch helper (steps §3.5)**: (a) `try: sub = load_spec(spec_dict) except ConstructError/ConfigurationError as e: raise ExecutionError.build(... spec name + str(e), node=node.name)` — wrapped rejection BEFORE anything runs. (b) resolve `expected = keymaker.output` (class as-is; str via `spec_types.lookup_type`); if `sub.output != expected` raise `ExecutionError` (output-contract mismatch). (c) `compiled = compile(sub, scripted=keymaker.scripted, conditions=keymaker.conditions)` — no checkpointer. (d) `result = compiled.invoke(input_dict, config=config)` (async: `await compiled.ainvoke`). (e) `out = _scan_subgraph_output(result, expected)` (REUSE `_subconstruct.py:43`); None → `ExecutionError`. ## Findings

REUSE TARGETS (do not reinvent):
- **Dispatch = a runtime `make_subgraph_fn`.** Mode (b) is structurally "compile+invoke a sub-flow, but at RUNTIME from an emitted dict instead of at compile time from a static Construct". The exemplar wrapper is `make_subgraph_fn` (`_subconstruct.py:57`): dual-path `RunnableLambda(sync, afunc=async)`, `sub_graph.invoke` / `await sub_graph.ainvoke`, output extracted by TYPE via `_scan_subgraph_output(sub_result, sub.output)` (`_subconstruct.py:43`). `make_keymaker_dispatch_fn` should mirror this shape (sync=invoke, async=ainvoke) and REUSE `_scan_subgraph_output` for the typed-output extraction.
- **The validation gate is `load_spec` (`loader.py:44`).** `load_spec(spec_dict)` → `_validate_spec` → `_build_construct` → `Construct(...)` (the eager `_validate_node_chain` at construct.py:194). This IS the anti-band-aid path — no bespoke validator. A bad spec raises `ConstructError`/`ConfigurationError` here, before compile/execute.
- **compile() already takes `scripted=`/`conditions=` kwargs** (`compiler.py:65`, sig at :74-75). D-DISPATCH-REGISTRIES: pass `compile(sub, scripted=keymaker.scripted, conditions=keymaker.conditions)` — no checkpointer (durability documented-opaque, Tier-2 = neograph-mrb2y). An unknown scripted_fn fails loud at compile (existing check).
- **Mode discrimination already exists in the modifier** (`modifiers.py:595-672`): `route == "decide"` ⇒ dispatch mode; `model_post_init` already enforces kwarg completeness (`spec_field`/`input_field`/`output` required, peer knobs forbidden). T1 already shipped this + the `keymaker_dispatch_missing_output.py` should_fail fixture. So mode-b CONFIG validation is done; only RUNTIME DISPATCH + the `_dispatch` state field + compiler discrimination remain.
- **Output type resolution**: `Keymaker.output: type[BaseModel] | str`. String form resolves via `spec_types.lookup_type` (`spec_types.py:61`); class form used directly. Same registry the emitted spec's types resolve through.

CURRENT-STATE GAP (the actual work):

A dispatch node has `peers=None` → it would wire as a degenerate 1-member mesh. ## Risks & Edge Cases
- **Feeding the sub-flow input**: `input_field` is a dict; call `compiled.invoke(input_dict, config=...)` directly (the dict maps to the sub-flow's initial state like `run()`'s engine_input). Do NOT thread through `run()` (adds checkpoint/DI prep). Confirm the emitted-flow entry node reads its inputs from these dict keys — document as the mode-b authoring contract.
- **Output-contract mismatch (design §3.5 step 2)**: after `load_spec`, verify the built `Construct.output` equals `Keymaker.output` (resolve string via lookup_type) → `ExecutionError` BEFORE compile. Separately, `_scan_subgraph_output` returning None (no node produced the type) is the runtime-defense `ExecutionError` (`_subconstruct.py:165`) — two distinct mismatch checks.
- **Wrapped rejection (on_invalid="raise", §3.5)**: the `ConstructError` from `load_spec` must be caught and re-raised WRAPPED in `ExecutionError` naming the spec + underlying message (the E2 demo catches at run() level). Don't let the bare ConstructError escape unwrapped.
- **No checkpointer on the inner graph** (§7, D-mrb2y deferral): compile the sub-flow with NO checkpointer; on parent resume the whole dispatch node re-executes. Documented-opaque — assert in a test/docstring, don't add durability machinery.
- **Three-surface parity**: mode (b) is DECORATOR-EXEMPT by design (§2.2: "Mode (b) has no decorator sugar in v1"). Parity applies to declarative `Node.scripted(...) | Keymaker(route="decide",...)` and programmatic pipe — which are the SAME pipe construction — so one parity assertion covers both live surfaces; document the @node exemption in the test docstring (mirrors the mode-a ForwardConstruct exemption note).
- **Guard G1 (Command monopoly)**: reduced mode-b uses NO Command (linear arm) — do not construct Command in the dispatch wrapper, or it needlessly widens the G1 monopoly surface.
- **`_dispatch` field must be fingerprinted** (regular field, not neo_-prefixed) so an output-contract change correctly invalidates checkpoints (§4.2).

title: Portal: first-class dynamic handoff + runtime flow-definition (Command(goto), spec-driven, validated-at-dispatch)
description:
## What
A FIRST-CLASS dynamic-handoff / runtime-routing construct: a node decides at RUNTIME which peer (from a declared set) takes over next, lowering to LangGraph's Command(goto=...) (and Send for dynamic fan-out) rather than a statically-known conditional edge. This is genuine dynamic multi-agent workflow (the OpenAI-Swarm / CrewAI-hierarchical handoff pattern), currently NOT expressible in neograph's IR.

## Why (first-class, not an import hack)
neograph's IR today is STATIC-TOPOLOGY: edges inferred from typed params; if->add_conditional_edges (arms known at compile/re-trace time); Loop->static back-edge; Each->Send over a statically-declared collection. None expresses "a node returns which peer to route to next from a runtime-decided set." LangGraph HAS this (Command(goto)/Send) and neograph targets LangGraph, so there is NO runtime barrier — the gap is purely a missing IR primitive. Maintainer decision 2026-07-13: build it regardless of Agent Spec; dynamic workflows are a real capability neograph wants.

DOWNSTREAM BENEFIT (not the driver): Agent Spec's Swarm (dynamic decentralized handoff; first_agent + relationships) becomes a FAITHFUL import target once this exists. The swcy1 ratification chose reject-on-import for Swarm precisely because the only path today is a static fake (mis-reconstructs peer-to-peer as topological order). This construct changes that from 'reject forever' to 'reject until the combinator lands, then faithful import via Command(goto)'. Re-scope the Agent Spec Swarm decision accordingly once this ships. RemoteAgent/A2A is a SEPARATE (client-initiated call-node) concern, not this.

## The genuinely-new-IR caveat (layer discipline)
AGENTS.md: adding new IR capability is the SANCTIONED exception to 'no new IR primitives' — do it DELIBERATELY and document it (like _BranchNode for ForwardConstruct). This is that case. It touches modifiers.py / compiler.py / state.py / _wiring.py (the compiler must emit Command(goto)-based routing) — a real IR + compiler change, maximum blast radius. NOT a DX-layer sugar.

## Design spike FIRST (this ticket = the spike)
Open questions to settle before any code, with independent architect review:
1. SURFACE: what does the author write? A `Handoff`/`Router` modifier (`node | Handoff(peers=[...], route='cond')`)? A `self.handoff(peers, route)` ForwardConstruct builder? A dynamic-edge construct? Pin against the three-API-surface parity rule (declarative / @node / programmatic).
2. RUNTIME CONTRACT: how does a node signal its next hop? Return a routing value the compiler maps to Command(goto)? A typed HandoffDecision output? How does this interact with the state bus (the chosen peer reads what)?
3. TERMINATION / cycles: dynamic handoff can loop forever — max-hops budget? cycle detection? (parallels Loop.max_iterations / Tool budget).
4. VALIDATION: the whole neograph thesis is compile-time 'if it compiles it runs'. A runtime-routed graph is inherently less statically checkable — what CAN we validate (peers exist, types compatible across every possible hop, route condition registered) and what becomes a runtime guarantee? This is the crux: how much of the static-safety pitch survives dynamic routing.
5. LOWERING: exact Command(goto)/Send emission in compiler.py; how it composes with existing modifiers (can a handoff peer be an Oracle/agent node?); checkpoint/interrupt interaction.
6. Fan-out variant: is Send-based dynamic fan-out (runtime-decided N) part of this or separate?

## Deliverable (spike)
docs/design/dynamic-handoff-<date>.md: the surface decision, runtime contract, validation-vs-runtime boundary, lowering sketch, termination story, three-surface plan, and the Swarm-import re-scope. Independent architect review gate BEFORE implementation is greenlit.

## Priority / sequencing
Post-0.7. Parallel to the Agent Spec interop epic (2ev48) but NOT blocking it — the import/type-layer/export children proceed without this; only the Swarm-import faithfulness depends on it. Maintainer sequencing 2026-07-13: Agent Spec comes earlier than the TS port; this dynamic-workflow capability is first-class regardless.
notes:
SCOPE EXPANSION + NAMING (maintainer, 2026-07-13):

1. NAMING: this gets a NEOGRAPH-NATIVE term, not 'Swarm' borrowed from Agent Spec. Matrix-themed to match the Oracle (merge-judge) / Operator (HITL) precedent. Pending maintainer pick — candidates: Keymaker (creates a path/door to ANY destination incl. runtime-defined ones — best fit for spec-driven mode), Switch (Matrix crew member + routing pun — best for peer-routing mode), Trainman (transit router between realms). 'Swarm' acceptable as fallback.

2. TWO MODES OF ONE CONSTRUCT:
   (a) PEER ROUTING: a node picks its successor at runtime from a KNOWN declared peer set -> Command(goto). The classic Swarm handoff / faithful Swarm-import target.
   (b) DYNAMIC FLOW DEFINITION (the powerful one): a node emits AT RUNTIME the SPEC for the next flow (an Agent Spec Flow OR a neograph Spec), which neograph VALIDATES -> COMPILES -> dispatches. 'I want to dynamically define the next flow -- here we go, here is the spec.' This FUSES: dynamic handoff + runtime graph construction (already a first-class use case) + from_agent_spec/load_spec.

3. COUPLING TO AGENT SPEC (revises the 'largely parallel' note): mode (b) USES from_agent_spec (neograph-01i0g) / load_spec at RUNTIME as the flow-definition seam. So from_agent_spec is not just 'load a saved file' -- it becomes the runtime dynamic-flow mechanism. The peer-routing mode (a) stays independent; the spec-driven mode (b) depends on 01i0g (import). Agent Spec import gains a second, load-bearing consumer.

4. VALIDATION CRUX RESOLVED (supersedes the earlier 'how much static safety survives' worry): a runtime-supplied flow can't be statically checked, but it IS validated at DISPATCH -- the existing validator/lint runs on the emitted spec BEFORE it executes. This is the 'validation as safety rail for MACHINE-authored graphs' thesis realized. The pitch becomes: 'if it dispatches, it was validated' -- machine-authored or hand-written, every flow passes the same gate before running. The spike must pin: what runs at dispatch (full compile+validate vs a fast subset), failure mode on an invalid emitted spec (reject-and-route-to-error vs raise), and the max-hops/recursion budget for self-extending flows.

Spike deliverable updated accordingly: cover BOTH modes, the from_agent_spec runtime coupling, and the dispatch-time validation contract.
NAME PINNED (maintainer, 2026-07-13): the construct is KEYMAKER (Matrix-native, beside Oracle/Operator). Rationale: the Keymaker makes a key to ANY door, including destinations not pre-wired — captures both modes, especially the spec-driven one ('here is the door to the next flow; here is the key'). Surface sketch: node | Keymaker(peers=[...]) for known-peer routing; node | Keymaker(route='decide') for the emit-a-spec-at-runtime mode. The spike settles the exact kwargs, the routing/flow-emission return contract, and the dispatch-time validation gate.
