title: Verify Operator's Agent Spec HITL-pause EXPORT target against pyagentspec before to_agent_spec lowering
description:
## What
Before writing Operator's to_agent_spec() export lowering, VERIFY the real Agent Spec HITL-pause target against pyagentspec 26.1.2 itself (not the neograph repo).

## Why (from swcy1 ratification + independent review, 2026-07-13)
The swcy1 ratification corrected a real design-doc error: Operator(when=) is a conditional HITL interrupt (LOWER), NOT a DIRECT BranchingNode — grounded in _wiring.py:951-961 (single linear check node; interrupt()+HUMAN_FEEDBACK; checkpointer-required; no fork, both paths reconverge). GO on that. BUT the independent reviewer flagged: the ratification's proposed EXPORT target — 'BranchingNode(gate) -> InputMessageNode -> reconverge' — asserts InputMessageNode == interrupt()/pause semantics with ZERO grounding (InputMessageNode is an Agent Spec concept; grep of neograph finds nothing, correctly). It also contradicts master-synthesis line-78's GAP characterization. So the corrected target is itself UNVERIFIED.

## Deliverable
Verify against pyagentspec 26.1.2 (the installed package / its docs / source): what Agent Spec node ACTUALLY expresses 'interrupt the flow, checkpoint, retrieve human input, resume'? Is it InputMessageNode, a BranchingNode+InputMessageNode pair, or is there NO faithful HITL-pause primitive (=> Operator export is a documented GAP, marker-only round-trip)? Pin the real target with pyagentspec evidence, THEN correct docs/design/agent-spec-api/02-flows-nodes.md (:22, :132-137), 00-master-synthesis.md (:38, :78), and agent-spec-interop-2026-07-09.md §5. Do NOT apply the ratification's unverified InputMessageNode correction to the master docs until this is done.

## Scope
Blocks ONLY the to_agent_spec() EXPORT task (Operator lowering). The import path (from_agent_spec), structural mappings, Oracle/Each/Loop LOWER, Swarm-reject/RemoteAgent-best-effort, and the [agent-spec] dep decision are all RATIFIED and unblocked. Not blocking the import/type-layer children.
design:
## Core Invariant
Every Agent-Spec EXPORT lowering must be traceable to a REAL pyagentspec primitive verified against the installed package (source/docstring/reference-adapter), never asserted from the neograph side alone or from a prior design doc's unverified claim — a lowering target is only 'ratified' once grounded in pyagentspec 26.1.2 itself.

## Implementation Plan
1. Do NOT introduce a new IR node/class for 'Operator export'. Reuse the existing to_agent_spec() lowering machinery (task neograph-i3zsh scope) and, for `Operator(when=cond)` specifically, emit a **composite of two existing pyagentspec classes** already imported/available via the `pyagentspec` dependency: `pyagentspec.flows.nodes.BranchingNode` (conditional gate) feeding `pyagentspec.flows.nodes.InputMessageNode` (the actual pause/interrupt/resume node) on the pause branch, with both the post-InputMessageNode path and the bypass branch wired via `ControlFlowEdge` to a single shared reconverge downstream node — mirroring the existing Loop lowering pattern already documented for `BranchingNode` (back-edge/continue/done) in `agent-spec-interop-2026-07-09.md` §5, since that is the closest existing precedent for 'condition -> BranchingNode -> divergent then reconverge' in this codebase's own design docs.
2. **Corrected wiring (per architect review MEDIUM finding — do NOT ship 'zero extra plumbing'-style language)**: `BranchingNode.mapping` is `{INPUT-VALUE-string : BRANCH-NAME-string}` — the mapping VALUE is a branch LABEL, not a node name, and `ControlFlowEdge.from_branch` selects on that label. The precise composite is: `BranchingNode(mapping={<condition-string>: PAUSE_BRANCH})` + `ControlFlowEdge(from_branch=PAUSE_BRANCH) -> InputMessageNode` + `ControlFlowEdge(from_branch=DEFAULT_BRANCH) -> reconverge` (unmapped inputs fall to `DEFAULT_BRANCH`, which is exactly the bypass path — no second explicit mapping entry needed for the false case). **Explicit coercion obligation, must be stated in the doc correction, not hidden**: neograph's `Operator.when` yields a Python truthy `should_pause` (bool or message string) via a `DataFlowEdge` into the BranchingNode's input — but the mapping key is a literal string (e.g. `"true"`). Without an explicit boolean-to-string-key coercion step, a Python `True`/truthy value will NOT match the literal key and the composite would silently ALWAYS take `DEFAULT_BRANCH` (bypass), never pausing — a silent fail-soft degradation this project's North Star forbids. neograph-i3zsh MUST either implement the coercion explicitly (render `should_pause` to the exact mapping-key string before the DataFlowEdge) or the doc must mark this as a documented GAP if left unhandled — it must NOT be presented as automatic/zero-plumbing.
3. Populate InputMessageNode.outputs with a single StringProperty (its ONLY supported shape per `_validate_outputs_have_right_format`) and map neograph's `StateKeys.HUMAN_FEEDBACK` to that output on import/round-trip. Interrupt-payload asymmetry to document explicitly in the doc correction: the pyagentspec reference LangGraph adapter lowers InputMessageNode to `interrupt("")` with the prompt carried by the STATIC `message:` field, whereas neograph's Operator passes `interrupt(should_pause)` — a DYNAMIC runtime value. neograph-i3zsh must treat a dynamic-payload Operator as an explicit, DOCUMENTED lossy-export edge case (flag in metadata, do not silently coerce) rather than extending InputMessageNode past its schema. Additionally: a callable `Operator.when=` is a separate export GAP (14-adapters.md already notes callable-valued fields do not serialize) — the doc correction should add a one-line annotation for this alongside the message-payload GAP, since only the string/registered-condition case is handled by the composite above.
4. Before writing the exporter code for neograph-i3zsh, update the FOUR doc locations identified by research + codebase-scan to remove the now-resolved TBD/unverified language, using the CORRECTED composite wording from step 2 (not 'zero extra plumbing'): `docs/design/agent-spec-api/02-flows-nodes.md` (:22 BranchingNode row phrasing + :132-137 Operator section, replace 'Status: TBD' with the composite target + coercion-obligation note), `docs/design/agent-spec-api/00-master-synthesis.md` (:78, annotate InputMessageNode gap as import-direction-only), `agent-spec-interop-2026-07-09.md` (:174, replace 'exact lowering TBD' with the composite target + point at this bead as the verification record), and `docs/design/agent-spec-api/14-adapters.md` (:142, same 'gated edge (exact lowering TBD)' row in the Export-lowering table -- found by the codebase-wide disease scan, NOT in the ticket's originally-cited file list; must be corrected alongside the other three or the doc set is left internally inconsistent). Do this doc correction as its own preparatory step, separate from and before the neograph-i3zsh exporter implementation, per this task's explicit scope boundary. Do NOT edit `docs/design/agent-spec-ratification-2026-07-13.md:101,103` — it is a historical decision record whose proposal is now confirmed correct, not a live doc that goes stale.
5. When neograph-i3zsh actually implements the exporter, the construction call sites to copy are the pyagentspec-internal reference patterns already inspected in this research (not neograph in-repo code, since neograph has zero existing InputMessageNode/BranchingNode-into-pyagentspec call sites): `InputMessageNode(name=..., message=..., outputs=[StringProperty(title='user_input')])` per the class docstring in `pyagentspec/flows/nodes/inputmessagenode.py`, and `BranchingNode(name=..., mapping={<condition-string>: PAUSE_BRANCH}, inputs=[...])` + separate `ControlFlowEdge(from_branch=...)` wiring per `pyagentspec/flows/nodes/branchingnode.py`'s docstring example (mapping value is a branch label, per the step-2 correction — not a node name).
notes:
## Findings
- VERIFIED against real pyagentspec 26.1.2 (pip-installed in scratchpad venv, not just grepped from the neograph repo). Source: `pyagentspec/flows/nodes/inputmessagenode.py`, `pyagentspec/flows/nodes/branchingnode.py`, `pyagentspec/adapters/langgraph/_node_execution.py`, `pyagentspec/adapters/langgraph/_langgraphconverter.py`.
- **InputMessageNode IS the faithful HITL-pause primitive — now grounded, not asserted.** Its own docstring: "This node interrupts the execution of the flow in order to wait for a user input, and restarts after receiving it." More decisively: pyagentspec's OWN reference LangGraph adapter (`InputMessageNodeExecutor` at `_node_execution.py:568-576`) lowers `InputMessageNode` to `langgraph.types.interrupt("")` — the exact same LangGraph primitive neograph's `Operator` uses (`_wiring.py:1097`, `human_input = interrupt(should_pause)`). `_langgraphconverter.py:419-421` also treats `InputMessageNode` presence as the signal requiring `uses_interrupt=True` / checkpointer, matching Operator's checkpointer-required semantics. This closes the reviewer's ZERO-grounding flag from swcy1.
- **BranchingNode has NO interrupt/pause semantics of any kind** — confirmed by source: it is a pure Dict[str,str]-keyed router (`mapping: Dict[str, str]`), input value → branch name, default branch on miss. No message, no wait, no resume. This CONFIRMS (does not contradict) the swcy1 ratification's core correction that `Operator(when=)` is NOT itself a `BranchingNode` — the pause logic cannot live in BranchingNode; it can only live in InputMessageNode.
- **Corrected export target for `Operator(when=cond)`**: `BranchingNode(gate on cond)` -> true-branch: `InputMessageNode` -> reconverge node; false-branch: reconverge node directly (bypass). This is a COMPOSITE of two real, grounded primitives — BranchingNode supplies the CONDITIONAL gating (Operator's `when=` is conditional; InputMessageNode alone is unconditional/always-pauses), InputMessageNode supplies the actual pause/interrupt/resume semantics. Neither node alone is faithful; the pair is. This differs from the swcy1 ratification's literal wording ('BranchingNode(gate) -> InputMessageNode -> reconverge') only in that the wording is now CORRECT/grounded rather than asserted without evidence — no change to the shape itself is needed.
- Multiple control-flow edges converging on one downstream node (the 'reconverge' node) is a standard, unrestricted pattern in pyagentspec — `Flow`'s pydantic validators (`flow.py`) place no in-degree cap; `BranchingNode`'s own docstring example converges two branches into two separate `EndNode`s (not a shared node, but nothing structurally prevents targeting a shared node instead).
- **neograph's OWN Operator lowering is a single linear node with an in-node conditional interrupt call** (`_wiring.py:1082-1103`, `_add_operator_check`): one node `{node_name}__operator` wired via a single `graph.add_edge` (no fork, no conditional_edges), whose body does `if should_pause: interrupt(should_pause)`. This reconfirms swcy1's LOWER (not DIRECT BranchingNode) classification of Operator on the neograph-IR side; it says nothing about the EXPORT-target shape on the Agent-Spec side, which is the composite BranchingNode+InputMessageNode above.
- Currently `InputMessageNode` is NOT modeled anywhere in neograph — grep of `src/neograph` confirms zero references (matches the existing GAP-AS row in `02-flows-nodes.md`). The export lowering (task neograph-i3zsh) will be the FIRST code to construct an `InputMessageNode`, so there is no existing in-repo call site to copy; the pyagentspec docstring's own `Flow` example (in `inputmessagenode.py`) is the best available template for correct field usage (`outputs=[StringProperty(title=...)]`, `message=` for the prompt appended before pausing).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Operator's `interrupt(should_pause)` payload is the CONDITION VALUE (whatever `should_pause` evaluates to, often a bool or message string), not a fixed prompt string. InputMessageNode's `message:` field is a static/templated string (Optional[str], Jinja-style `{{var}}` placeholders via `get_placeholder_properties_from_json_object`), not an arbitrary runtime payload. If `Operator.when` needs to carry a dynamic message into the interrupt payload, that has no 1:1 InputMessageNode field — likely needs to render `should_pause` into `message` via a DataFlowEdge from the BranchingNode's condition output, or accept lossy flattening (documented GAP, not silent).
- InputMessageNode ALWAYS returns a single string output (`DEFAULT_OUTPUT = 'user_input'`, enforced by `_validate_outputs_have_right_format` — exactly one output, type=string). neograph's `StateKeys.HUMAN_FEEDBACK` is untyped/Any at the interrupt() call site (`_wiring.py:1097-1098`) — if piarch's real usage of `Operator` ever expects structured (non-string) human feedback, the export loses type fidelity to a bare string. Verify against actual `Operator` call sites in piarch before finalizing the lowering's output-type contract.
- Doc contradiction to fix (not a NEEDS USER INPUT — this task's own deliverable): `docs/design/agent-spec-api/02-flows-nodes.md:22` current text 'Operator compiles to check node + conditional edge' for the BranchingNode row is imprecise post-verification — Operator compiles (on the neograph IR side) to a check node with an UNCONDITIONAL edge in, and an IN-NODE conditional interrupt call, not a graph-level conditional edge (confirmed by `_add_operator_check`, which calls `graph.add_edge`, not `add_conditional_edges`). The EXPORT-side BranchingNode+InputMessageNode composite is the Agent-Spec-side reconstruction of that in-node condition, not a mirror of neograph's own wiring shape.
- `docs/design/agent-spec-api/02-flows-nodes.md:132-137` ('Status: exact lowering still TBD in implementation') and `agent-spec-interop-2026-07-09.md:174` ('gated edge vs explicit check node — TBD') are now RESOLVABLE by this research — should be updated to the BranchingNode+InputMessageNode composite, TBD removed.
- `00-master-synthesis.md:78` InputMessageNode/OutputMessageNode row ('interrupt() not first-class in neograph... GAP-AS') describes the neograph-side gap correctly (still true — neograph has no InputMessageNode-equivalent IR node) but should be annotated that the EXPORT path can still SYNTHESIZE a faithful InputMessageNode from Operator, i.e., the GAP is import-direction / native-modeling only, not export-direction.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: Plan step 2's 'only true->pause_branch is needed... zero extra plumbing' misreads BranchingNode's contract. Verified source: mapping is {INPUT-VALUE-string : BRANCH-NAME-string}; routing matches the input value as a literal string key and ControlFlowEdge.from_branch selects on the mapping VALUE (a branch label, not a node). Two consequences the 'zero extra plumbing' claim hides: (a) the condition output must be DELIVERED as the exact string 'true' via DataFlowEdge — neograph's Operator.when yields a Python truthy should_pause (bool/message), which will NOT match key 'true' without an explicit coercion, so the composite would silently always take the DEFAULT/bypass branch and never pause; (b) step 5's example 'mapping={"true": <pause_node_name>}' conflates branch-name with node-name (docstring uses mapping value CORRECT_PASSWORD_BRANCH as a branch label wired separately by from_branch). Suggestion: when the doc-correction lands, do NOT ship 'zero extra plumbing'; state the composite as BranchingNode(mapping={<condition-string>: PAUSE_BRANCH}) + ControlFlowEdge(from_branch=PAUSE_BRANCH)->InputMessageNode + ControlFlowEdge(from_branch=DEFAULT_BRANCH)->reconverge, and note the boolean->string-key coercion obligation as an explicit lowering detail (or documented GAP) for neograph-i3zsh. This keeps the very doc this task exists to make accurate from baking in an imprecise contract.

- [LOW] Finding: Interrupt-payload asymmetry — reference adapter lowers InputMessageNode to interrupt("") with the prompt carried by the static message: field, whereas neograph's Operator passes interrupt(should_pause) (dynamic runtime value). Research Risks section already captures this; just ensure the doc correction carries the note so i3zsh treats dynamic-payload Operators as documented-lossy, not silently coerced.

- [LOW] Finding: Operator.when may be a callable; 14-adapters.md itself notes callable-valued fields do not serialize. The composite handles the string/registered-condition case cleanly; a callable when= is an export GAP worth a one-line doc annotation alongside the message-payload GAP.

description:
## Invariant
The MCP unwrap-boundary ratchet guard (tests/test_guards_mcp_unwrap_boundary.py) must fail CI when a transport-exit handler re-raises the WRAPPER instead of the unwrapped LEAF — including in the real capture-then-reraise code shape, and at EVERY transport-method await.

## Two verified gaps (adversarial verification of neograph-lcrwd, 2026-07-13)
Both found by mutation probes; the fix's MECHANISM is sound (all 4 boundaries surface the bare leaf, behaviorally pinned), but the permanent GUARD is weaker than billed:

### Gap 1 (load-bearing): the guard checks SHAPE, not the LEAF
_has_unwrap_raise walks the except-handler subtree and returns True if ANY `ast.Assign` has value `_unwrap_single(...)` OR any `raise _unwrap_single(...)` exists — it does NOT verify the re-raised variable actually holds the unwrapped leaf. PROBE (RED-worthy, but guard PASSED): in the real fetcher/replayer shape — which retains `leaf = _unwrap_single(exc)` for the CancelledError isinstance check AND captures `error = ...` for post-block re-raise — mutating the capture to `error = exc` (re-raise the WRAPPER) while KEEPING the `leaf = _unwrap_single(exc)` line: the guard PASSED (4 passed). The coexisting unwrap-assign (present for a different purpose) satisfies the shape check while the actual re-raised value is the group. The behavioral surface test (test_fetcher_surfaces_grouped_mcp_error_as_bare) DID catch it — so the code is protected — but the RATCHET (the thing meant to catch FUTURE drift structurally) can be fooled by exactly the real code shape. A pure `error = exc` with NO `_unwrap_single` anywhere IS flagged; the hole only opens when an unwrap-assign coexists — which is the real shape.
FIX DIRECTION: teach the guard to verify the RE-RAISED value traces to `_unwrap_single(exc)` (data-flow, not mere presence) — e.g. for the capture form, the variable in the post-block `raise <var>` must be assigned from `_unwrap_single(...)`; for in-place, the `raise` argument must be `_unwrap_single(...)`. A `leaf = _unwrap_single(exc)` that is only used in an isinstance guard but NOT re-raised must NOT satisfy the check. Add a meta-test: capture-then-reraise-the-wrapper (with a coexisting unwrap-assign) => guard RED.

### Gap 2 (minor, behaviorally safe): list_prompts omitted from the guard method set
_prompt.py:120 `list_prompts` (inside _declared_prompt_args) is NOT in the guard's _TRANSPORT_METHODS set, so the guard does not check that call site directly. Runtime is CORRECT (it is always awaited within _fetch's unwrap try, and recursive _unwrap_single peels the group), but a regression at THIS await would not be caught by the guard. FIX: add list_prompts to _TRANSPORT_METHODS (and confirm the _fetch-enclosed site still passes because the enclosing handler unwraps).

## Secondary finding (test-infra, optional): fake-CM doubles don't emulate anyio teardown
The exception-surface test doubles' _FakeSessionCM.__aexit__ returns None and does NOT wrap an in-body exception the way an anyio task group does. Consequence: those behavioral tests CANNOT regression-test the in-place-vs-capture distinction — mutating the fetcher to raise in-place still passes the fake-CM test. The load-bearing capture-then-reraise property is proven only by the anyio mechanism (verified: anyio.create_task_group __aexit__ wraps an in-body raise into an ExceptionGroup), not by any shipped test. OPTIONAL: an anyio-backed (or real-transport) test that raises in-place and asserts the group, so the capture-then-reraise choice is regression-pinned, not just mechanism-argued.

## Scope
- IN: harden _has_unwrap_raise to a data-flow leaf check + its meta-test (Gap 1, the priority); add list_prompts to _TRANSPORT_METHODS (Gap 2). Optional: an anyio/real-transport in-place-re-wrap pin (secondary).
- OUT: the lcrwd fix itself (mechanism verified sound); no production _client/_session change needed for Gaps 1-2 (guard-test-only), unless the anyio pin motivates a test-double upgrade.

## Provenance
Follow-up to neograph-lcrwd (fix 77d60e7). Both gaps mutation-verified by the lcrwd adversarial re-verification (2026-07-13). Not blocking — the shipped code is behaviorally correct and pinned by surface tests; this hardens the RATCHET so future drift is caught structurally, which is the ratchet's whole purpose.
close_reason: WON'T-DO (not started; deliberate close). The lcrwd invariant is already pinned behaviorally: tests/test_mcp_exception_surface.py reddens on a wrapper-re-raise mutation at every one of the 4 boundaries (verifier-confirmed). Both hardening asks are non-trivial guard complexity for a theoretical hole on an already-protected path: (1) 'verify the leaf not the shape' needs AST data-flow analysis; (2) list_prompts has no LOCAL unwrap handler (covered by the enclosing _fetch), so adding it to _TRANSPORT_METHODS naively would red a behaviorally-correct site — it'd need enclosing-handler awareness. The structural guard being shape-only is a documented limitation, not a live bug; the behavioral surface tests are the actual regression net. Same judgment as neograph-i657 ('do not implement on aesthetic momentum'). If a broken capture ever ships AND its surface test is missing, re-open.

title: Converge remaining neograph_mcp exit boundaries on the bare-leaf unwrap invariant (mcp_session.call/list, fetcher grouped-McpError, replayer)
description:
## Invariant
Every neograph_mcp exit-boundary surfaces a single-leaf transport ExceptionGroup as its BARE leaf (the neograph-2itlh invariant). The factory path (get_tools) and _resilient are fixed in neograph-2itlh; these 4 LATENT twins remain out of step.

## Out-of-step boundaries (from neograph-2itlh trace-similar atom)
1. mcp_session.call — _session.py:325 call_tool — no _unwrap_single. A grouped tools/call failure (server-side error wrapped by anyio) surfaces grouped. Reached when __aenter__ succeeds (provider raised-at-enter is already unwrapped).
2. mcp_session._ensure_listing — _session.py:253 list_tools — no unwrap. tool_names() inherits.
3. fetcher — _client.py:812-821 read_resource — catches bare McpError inside async-with, re-raises after; a GROUPED McpError misses the except and re-wraps via anyio teardown. Verify the grouped case; if real, unwrap.
4. replayer — _client.py:827-828 call_tool — no unwrap.

## Fix
Apply the same 'raise _unwrap_single(exc) from None' idiom _session.__aenter__/__aexit__, _prompt, _run_context already use. Reuse _unwrap_single — no second helper. CancelledError: keep bare raise (exempt) per the neograph-2itlh decision.

## TDD
RED-first: a grouped-exception double (ExceptionGroup wrapping a single leaf) through each boundary, asserting pytest.raises(<leaf type>). Reuse the test_mcp_transport_resilience.TestGroupedExceptionUnwrappedToBareLeaf pattern. The mcp_session boundaries need a real-transport harness (the held-session connect must SUCCEED, so the provider must NOT raise at enter — use a server-side tools/call error or a double that injects a grouped raise post-enter).

## Anti-band-aid
Optional boundary-consistency guard (the one neograph-2itlh may add): assert no neograph_mcp exit-boundary re-raises a BaseExceptionGroup wrapper when a single-leaf unwrap is available. If neograph-2itlh ships that guard, this task just makes the 4 boundaries pass it.

## Provenance
Filed by neograph-2itlh trace-similar atom (atom 3). Latent twins of the _resilient bug; not the demo-breaker (demo fails at get_tools, fixed in neograph-2itlh).
design:
## Root Cause
Four neograph_mcp exit boundaries reached only after a successful connect lack the bare-leaf unwrap: McpSession.call (call_tool), McpSession._ensure_listing (list_tools), mcp_resource_fetcher's fetcher (read_resource; its bare 'except McpError' misses grouped) and replayer (call_tool). A single-leaf transport ExceptionGroup surfaces grouped, breaking consumer except-clauses and the -32002 replay trigger.

## Fix Approach (refined by architect review)
Two idioms by boundary shape, both via the canonical _unwrap_single (no second helper):
1. HELD-SESSION boundaries (_session.py call/call_tool, _ensure_listing/list_tools) — no CM exit between raise and consumer: wrap the await in try/except BaseException; if the unwrapped leaf is asyncio.CancelledError, bare 'raise' (exemption, per neograph-2itlh); else 'raise _unwrap_single(exc) from None'.
2. CONSUMER-OWNED-SESSION boundaries (_client.py fetcher/read_resource, replayer/call_tool) — an in-place raise would be RE-WRAPPED by the anyio teardown of 'async with client.session(...)' (documented _client.py:837): capture leaf = _unwrap_single(exc) inside the block (CancelledError leaf: bare raise), re-raise the leaf AFTER the block closes. Fetcher's existing bare 'except McpError' collapses into this (a bare McpError unwraps to itself).
3. GUARD: extend tests/test_guards_mcp_unwrap_boundary.py::_has_unwrap_raise to also accept an ASSIGNMENT of _unwrap_single(...) in the handler (capture-then-reraise form), add a meta-test pinning it, then REMOVE all 4 rows from _DEFERRED_ALLOWLIST (ratchet shrink; the stale-allowlist assertion enforces removal).
notes:

- Harness: post-enter grouped-raise doubles (_GroupedRaiseSession/_FakeClient) via monkeypatched _client_for (neograph_mcp._session for mcp_session, neograph_mcp._client for fetcher/replayer) — enter succeeds, transport method raises ExceptionGroup([leaf]), exactly the anyio TaskGroup form. Sanctioned by the ticket's TDD note; mirrors _grouped_tool in test_mcp_transport_resilience.py.
- Root cause: the 4 boundaries (_session.py call/call_tool ~:325, _ensure_listing/list_tools ~:253; _client.py fetcher/read_resource ~:835, replayer/call_tool ~:849) await the transport with NO try/except raise _unwrap_single(exc) from None — a single-leaf ExceptionGroup escapes grouped; the fetcher's bare 'except McpError' additionally MISSES a grouped McpError so the -32002 expiry->replay path never engages.

Pattern: awaited MCP transport method (get_tools/load_mcp_tools/call_tool/list_tools/read_resource/get_prompt) not inside a try whose except raises _unwrap_single(exc) — SYNTACTIC, AST-enumerable.

Total instances found: 4 (whole src tree — identical to the guard allowlist; examples/ and tests/ are consumer/harness code, out of invariant scope)

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | src/neograph_mcp/_session.py:325 | call::call_tool | MIGRATE | this fix |

## Architect review (atom neograph-i556h.5)

1. Root cause correctness: LOW risk — confirmed by 7 RED tests; the 4 sites match the guard's AST-enumerated violation set exactly.
2. Fix minimality: LOW — reuses _unwrap_single, no new helper, no behavior change for bare exceptions or multi-leaf groups.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-2itlh

Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored AND a
structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

1. **Re-run the scan** using the EXACT same command from the

   Pre-fix instances: <N>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-hnbsq
description:

executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is

## Precondition

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and

title: Sweep verification for neograph-q4p72
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-q4p72
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-q4p72`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-q4p72)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-q4p72 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-q4p72 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

design:
## Core Invariant

No `test_*` function in tests/ has a lone `assert <x> is not None` as its only assertion (excluding fake-internal guards and crash-only fuzz tests), and no `assert A or B` has an always-true disjunct where the test name claims a property the assertion cannot detect regressing.

## Implementation Plan

1. **Strengthen test_mcp_tools.py:194 (MED-01)** — The worst site. Currently only asserts `result is not None`. Must:
   - Assert the output value: `assert result["scan"] == Claims(items=["done"])`
   - Pin tool invocation via `FakeTool("run_search")` (records `.calls`) or a `StructuredTool` closing over a call-recording list
   - Add: `assert tool.calls == [{"query": "q"}]`

2. **Strengthen test_execution.py:584 (TQ-02)** — Drop the always-true disjunct:
   - Replace: `assert "__interrupt" in str(result) or result.get("a") is not None`
   - With: `assert "__interrupt" in str(result)` (on first run)
   - Alternative: Assert the state snapshot's `.next` is non-empty (captures the interrupt-fired property)

3. **Strengthen test_rendering_invariants.py:98,112 (TQ-03)** — Two Hypothesis crash-only tests:
   - Option A: Add real invariant checks (`isinstance(result, str)` or non-empty for dict results)
   - Option B: Rename to `*_never_raises` and drop the no-op assert (make crash-only intent explicit)
   - Recommendation: Option A — adds value

4. **Strengthen test_public_fakes.py:120-122 (TQ-04)** — Import-smoke checks:
   - Replace importability checks with object-identity assertions against the internal source:
   - `from neograph.testing.fakes import StructuredFake as _S; assert StructuredFake is _S`
   - This guards the "one implementation, two consumers" contract

5. **Verification Protocol** (per site):
   - Temporarily break the production path the assertion now pins
   - Confirm the strengthened assertion fails (RED phase)
   - Restore the production path
   - Confirm the assertion passes (GREEN phase)
   - Example for MED-01: break the tool dispatch or output value, watch `assert result["scan"] == ...` fail

6. **No code changes for benign/meaningful sites**:
   - Benign guards (`self._model is not None` in fake classes) are internal to test doubles
   - Meaningful assertions are all multi-assert conjunctions or have error context

7. **Audit gate**:
   - After strengthening: `grep -rn "is not None" tests/ | grep assert` reviewed to confirm only benign/meaningful hits remain
   - `grep -rnE "assert .* or .*is not None" tests/` returns only the fixed site (or none if disjunct dropped)

title: Unify mcp_session/mcp_run_context stdio .call() onto per-call identity re-resolution — kill the last freeze fork
description:
## Invariant
Identity is per-call fresh on EVERY MCP surface and EVERY transport; a consumer PINS identity by returning a constant from token_provider (never by the framework freezing it). One semantic, no transport-dependent surprise.

## The defect (last freeze fork left by neograph-qslrx)
Within the SAME mcp_session.call() surface, identity handling forks by transport (src/neograph_mcp/_session.py):
- http (:220): auth = _http_identity(...) — per-request httpx.Auth (_TokenProviderAuth re-invokes token_provider every request). FRESH.
- stdio (:225/:227 mint at __aenter__ -> :312-316 .call() reads self._token): the bearer/identity is minted ONCE at session open and the frozen self._token is reused as the tool argument on every .call(). FROZEN.

So mcp_session.call() refreshes on http but freezes on stdio. mcp_run_context has the same stdio mint-once. This is the single remaining mint-once site the qslrx completeness audit found (adversarial verifier, 2026-07-11): 'the direct mcp_session/mcp_run_context stdio .call() path (self._token) mints once at __aenter__ and reuses per .call().' qslrx documented it as a scope-out (design items 8/9: 'stdio: unchanged; sessions rarely stdio'); THIS ticket rejects that scope-out.

## Why it is an inconsistency, not a principled second path (verified against code)
- NO technical barrier: self._token_provider AND self._config are already held on the session (_session.py:203/:206), so .call() can re-resolve per call — await _resolve_token(self._token_provider, self._config) — instead of reading self._token. ~2 lines.
- The FACTORY path ALREADY does exactly this for stdio (_inject_stdio_token re-resolves per call). mcp_session is the ONLY stdio surface still minting once — out of step with its own sibling, not with any transport constraint.
- Not perf (token_provider is a cheap consumer callable); not connection semantics (the stdio token is an ARGUMENT, not a connection property — changing it per call is free).
- The design's stated justification ('sessions rarely stdio; per-call arg injection is the factory concern') is a FREQUENCY argument, not a correctness one — the same 'rare therefore harmless' reasoning that kept Loop.history (neograph-eef83) alive. An inconsistency where a surface refreshes on http but freezes on stdio is a latent footgun regardless of frequency: test on http (see refresh), ship on stdio (silent freeze).
- The only real argument for mint-once — 'pin the whole session to one principal' — is already achievable the consistent way: a token_provider returning a constant pins identity (exactly like the http side). The framework must not FORCE pinning by freezing.

## Fix (Option: unify onto per-call, mirrors the qslrx factory path)
mcp_session.call() and mcp_run_context .call() (stdio branch) re-resolve identity per call via _resolve_token(self._token_provider, self._config) (or _resolve_token_no_config when config is None) instead of self._token minted at __aenter__. http stays on _http_identity (already per-request). Result: ONE semantic — identity per-call fresh on all surfaces/transports; constant provider pins.

## Guard-first / TDD (same shape qslrx used)
1. Write the FAILING stdio-session freshness test FIRST: a rotating/counter token_provider over a stdio mcp_session; make >=2 .call()s; assert the SECOND call carries the FRESH token (demo server echoes it under acting_as). RED on current HEAD (self._token frozen). Mirror mcp_run_context if it exposes a direct .call().
2. Implement per-call re-resolution until green.
3. Static-provider regression: a constant token_provider still sends the same value every .call().
4. Consider extending tests/test_guards_mcp_identity_freeze.py (or a sibling) to ban 'mint identity once at __aenter__ then reuse across .call()' if AST-expressible; otherwise the behavioral tests are the pin.

## Scope
- IN: mcp_session + mcp_run_context stdio direct .call() identity re-resolution; freshness + static-regression tests; docs note that identity is per-call on ALL surfaces now (kill the 'except stdio sessions' caveat in _session.py:218-219 / _run_context.py:88-90 docstrings + design doc items 8/9).
- OUT: http path (already per-request via qslrx); the agent-loop factory/stdio path (already per-call).

## Provenance
Follow-up to neograph-qslrx (fix f491db4). Surfaced by the qslrx adversarial verification (the lone documented scope-out) + maintainer challenge 2026-07-11: 'this means there are two paths instead of one — why keep two?' Design context: docs/design/mcp-identity-refresh-2026-07-11.md (items 8/9 are the scope-out this reverses).

## Fix Approach (minimal)

Drop the __aenter__ mint (self._token) entirely. Gate the injection on self._token_provider is not None instead of self._token is not None. Update the docstrings in _session.py (class + call + module) to say identity is per-call fresh on ALL surfaces/transports; also update design doc items 8/9 caveat (docs/design/mcp-identity-refresh-2026-07-11.md). description:

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-eef83
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-eef83` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-eef83/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-eef83
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-eef83)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-eef83 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-eef83 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-eef83/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-eef83 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: MCP run-cache serves a build-time bearer for the whole run — no mid-run token refresh (stale-token failures on long runs)
description: neograph_mcp/_run_cache deliberately does no mid-run expiry recheck: the tool instance built per (RUN_ID, node_name) bakes in the bearer minted at BUILD time and reuses it for every call across the run's ReAct supersteps. Any run whose tool phase outlives the IdP's access-token lifespan then sends a STALE token and the server denies — surfacing as a spurious ACCESS_DENIED for a fully-authorized principal. Found downstream in the ox-troubleshooting-demo (an Each verify fan-out spanning >5min against Keycloak's 300s lifespan produced a mid-run denial 'storm'; trace: round-1 reads FOUND at 03:54, round-2 all denied at 03:59). Downstream mitigations shipped there (a distinguishable TOKEN_EXPIRED envelope so an expired token isn't conflated with an authz deny, + raising the realm lifespan), but the durable fix is upstream. Proposed: re-resolve token_provider per call, OR make the cache entry expiry-aware (re-mint on/near expiry) — the held session/token is a config-only key that never enters the checkpoint, so refresh is replay-safe. Ref: downstream ox-troubleshooting-demo bead kh3 (root-caused) + zrw (dependency tracker).
design:
OPTION D (decided): collapse the static token_provider bearer onto the SAME httpx.Auth mechanism the OAuth path (27h3s) already uses. Wrap token_provider in an internal _TokenProviderAuth(httpx.Auth) whose async_auth_flow re-invokes token_provider PER REQUEST and stamps Authorization; DELETE _connection's static-bearer header branch (_client.py:262-263) so the choke point has ONE http-identity mechanism. Precedence: explicit HttpServer.auth (real OAuth) WINS over the token_provider wrap (unchanged). stdio sub-fix: re-resolve token per call inside _inject_stdio_token's coroutine wrapper instead of closing over a build-time value (lower urgency). Framework/consumer boundary: unifying makes refresh POSSIBLE; whether the token CHANGES is the consumer's token_provider's job -- a static-string provider still returns the same value. token_provider contract (configurable->str, sync-or-async) UNCHANGED. For turnkey exchange/refresh, HttpServer.auth+client_credentials_auth stays the path (durable answer for ox/Keycloak). Full design: docs/design/mcp-identity-refresh-2026-07-11.md.

CHANGE MANIFEST (12 edit sites; 10 production + 1 docs + 1 tests):
1. _client.py:247-269 _connection -- delete static-bearer branch; sig (spec,token)->(spec,*,auth=None); http sets conn['auth']=auth or spec.auth; token param dropped.
2. _client.py (new, near _connection) -- add _TokenProviderAuth(httpx.Auth) + _http_identity(spec,token_provider,config,*,use_config) builder (httpx imported function-local; explicit-auth-wins precedence).
3. _client.py:272-291 _client_for -- token:str->auth:Any; forward to _connection(auth=).
4. _client.py:452-489 _factory -- drop build-time _resolve_token for http; http: auth=_http_identity(...) -> _client_for(auth=); stdio: no header identity, inject per call (item5).
5. _client.py:355-377 _inject_stdio_token -- take (token_provider,config) not baked token; _with_identity re-resolves PER CALL; call site :476 updated.
6. _client.py:380-384 _discover_tool_names -- pass auth=spec.auth (OAuth discovery); RECOMMENDED also wrap token_provider (close anonymous-discovery gap).
7. _client.py:699-725 mcp_resource_fetcher fetcher+replayer -- http build auth (use_config=False); LOWER urgency (one-shot reads).
8. _session.py:213-218 McpSessionHandle.__aenter__ -- http build auth, pass to _client_for; long-lived session = real freeze case.
9. _run_context.py:86-92 __aenter__ -- http build auth, pass to _client_for; held run-scoped sessions long-lived across supersteps.

(Line 77 already claims 'per request by an httpx.Auth' -- code now matches.)

CONFIRMED by httpx contract + tests/test_mcp_oauth.py:208 (refresh-on-revoke on the SAME mcp_session, no reconnect). acceptance_criteria: A run whose tool phase outlives the IdP access-token lifespan refreshes the bearer mid-run (per-call re-resolution or expiry-aware cache) rather than sending a stale token; a test simulates an expired-then-refreshed token across supersteps without reconnect; documented in the MCP auth/token_provider docs.

CODE VERIFICATION (2026-07-11, orchestrator — confirmed against source, not description):

CONFIRMED for the STATIC token_provider bearer path:
- The built tools are RUN_ID-cached: _tool_loop.py:484 get_or_build / :530 await aget_or_build wrap _ainstantiate_tools, which calls the factory -> _resolve_token (_client.py:455) -> token baked into the client connection headers at CONNECT (_connection: headers['Authorization']=f'Bearer {token}', _client.py:263). Cache key = RUN_ID (stable within a run). So the bearer is minted ONCE at the first superstep and FROZEN for every subsequent ReAct turn of that run. A run whose tool phase outlives the token lifespan sends the stale bearer -> ACCESS_DENIED. Bug reproduces exactly as the ox trace shows.
- Note: file path in the description ('neograph_mcp/_run_cache') is imprecise — the cache is neograph/_run_cache; the token is in neograph_mcp/_client. Mechanism is otherwise exact.

CRUCIAL NUANCE — a durable fix ALREADY EXISTS for the OAuth path (does NOT need building):
- HttpServer.auth (an httpx.Auth, e.g. the battery's client_credentials_auth from neograph-27h3s) is attached to the transport's PERSISTENT httpx client and runs auth_flow() PER REQUEST — 'token exchange, expiry, and 401-triggered refresh WITHOUT a reconnect' (_client.py:227-254 + HttpServer docstring). auth= WINS over the static bearer (no double header). Because the cached tool wraps a client whose httpx.Auth refreshes per tools/call, the RUN_ID cache freeze does NOT affect it — 27h3s verified refresh-without-reconnect against a real RFC-8414 OAuth fixture.
- So: the FREEZE is specific to the static token_provider bearer (connect-time credential). The OAuth auth= path already satisfies the acceptance criterion 'refreshes mid-run without reconnect'. The ox consumer hit this because they used the static token_provider bearer with Keycloak, NOT HttpServer.auth.

RECONCILES with cnxlx verification ('identity re-minted on both paths'): that was about FRESH-RUN / resume-reconnect (new RUN_ID -> re-mint). TRUE. This bug is the WITHIN-run freeze on one long run (same RUN_ID -> cache hit -> no re-mint), which cnxlx did not test.

FIX LANDSCAPE (design decision needed):
- Option A: make the static token_provider path re-resolve per call (refresh mid-run). Complex — the token lives in the client CONNECTION headers baked at connect; per-call refresh means not baking it into a cached client (rebuild-per-call defeats the cache, or wrap token_provider into an httpx.Auth-like per-request shim). token_provider returns a bare str with NO expiry info, so an 'expiry-aware cache' can't know when to refresh without a contract change.
- Option B (leaner, likely correct): DOCUMENT that the static token_provider bearer is a connect-time credential frozen for the run's duration, and steer any run that may outlive the IdP token lifespan to HttpServer.auth + client_credentials_auth (which already refreshes per-request). Add a test proving auth= refreshes an expired token across supersteps under the RUN_ID cache (pins the durable path). This satisfies the acceptance criterion via the existing mechanism.
- Option C: both — B now + A if a static-bearer consumer needs mid-run refresh without OAuth.

Recommendation: B (the durable fix exists; the gap is guidance + a pinning test), with A gated on real demand. This is an API-design call — maintainer decides before /execute.

description:
## What
loop_history= / Loop(history=True) works at runtime but appears REDUNDANT: on its only legal surface (Node self-loop; banned on Constructs), the main output field result[node] ALREADY accumulates every iteration via _append_loop_result. neo_loop_history_{node} duplicates that data, differing only in accessibility (get_state vs output dict).

Survived by passivity: write wired in the pgso factory rewrite (8bb9f80) because the field existed; loop_history= kwarg added in d5pvl (e67fa03, 3 months later) for three-surface parity because the modifier field existed. Sibling on_exhaust earned its keep; reenter/loop_to were pruned; history was neither pruned nor justified.

tests/test_loop.py::TestLoopHistoryRuntimeAndRedundancy (3 tests): history collects at runtime; history field == main append field per-iteration; main field alone preserves all iterations without the flag. The redundancy is now provable, not inferred.

## The decision

title: Sweep verification for d5pvl
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on d5pvl
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" d5pvl`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (d5pvl)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update d5pvl --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add d5pvl sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for d5pvl
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show d5pvl` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/d5pvl/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" d5pvl
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (d5pvl)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update d5pvl --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update d5pvl --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/d5pvl/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add d5pvl codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Sweep verification for gtzkd
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on gtzkd
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" gtzkd`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (gtzkd)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update gtzkd --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add gtzkd sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for gtzkd
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show gtzkd` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/gtzkd/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" gtzkd
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (gtzkd)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update gtzkd --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update gtzkd --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/gtzkd/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add gtzkd codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: ForwardConstruct parity RATCHET is tautological — REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES derives from the corpus it checks (no teeth)
description:
## Invariant the ratchet is supposed to enforce
A declarative capability that ships WITHOUT a forward() parity twin must FAIL LOUD (the 'parity ratchet' — e9zse's permanent anti-drift guard). A silently-deleted parity row must also fail loud.

## The defect (confirmed 2026-07-11, adversarial verify of e9zse + reconfirmed directly)
tests/test_forward_parity.py:766: REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES = frozenset(row.capability for row in PARITY_CORPUS) — the 'required' set is DERIVED FROM THE CORPUS IT CHECKS. test_every_required_capability_has_a_corpus_row (:798) then computes covered = {row.capability for row in PARITY_CORPUS} and asserts REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES - covered == empty. Both sides come from the SAME list, so the difference is ALWAYS empty — tautological. The module docstring claims the opposite contract ('a new declarative capability is added here FIRST; the coverage test fails loud until its forward() twin row lands') but that intent is not realized.

PROOF (verifier, reverted): commenting out the loop_in_loop corpus row dropped the file to 19 passed and TestParityRatchet stayed 3 passed GREEN — a load-bearing parity twin silently deleted with ZERO ratchet response. It is weaker than even a hardcoded assert len(rows) >= N (which would at least catch a deletion).

## Scope / impact
NOT a correctness defect in the shipped feature: the IR-equality helper assert_ir_identical (:169-229) is genuinely DEEP (verified — catches Each key/over/on_error, Loop when-identity/max_iterations/on_exhaust, Oracle params+hook identity, Operator.when, boundary ports, recursive nesting; three valid-IR mutation probes each went RED). The rows that EXIST enforce IR-identity for real. The hole is ONLY in the forward-looking guard: future declarative capabilities can ship without a forward() twin, and existing twins can be deleted, with no failure.

## Fix (anti-band-aid: the ratchet must have an INDEPENDENT source of truth)
REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES must NOT be derived from PARITY_CORPUS. Two options:
  A. Hardcoded independent frozenset of capability names — adding a name without a corpus row fails; deleting a row fails. Minimal.
  B. (Preferred) ENUMERATE the declarative modifier/composition surface from neograph itself — the modifier classes (Each, Loop, Oracle, Operator) + composition capabilities (sub-construct nesting, fan-in, multi-output dict, branch/cap) — and assert each maps to >=1 covered corpus row. This makes a NEW declarative modifier that lacks a forward() twin fail loud automatically (the ratchet's actual stated purpose), and is the real 'parity ratchet' the epic promised.

## Guard-first / TDD
1. Failing test FIRST: delete/comment a corpus row (or add a REQUIRED capability with no row) -> the ratchet must go RED. Verify it currently stays GREEN (the bug).
2. Implement independent enumeration until the deletion/omission is caught.
3. Meta-test: assert the ratchet itself is non-tautological (e.g. REQUIRED source is not ).

## Acceptance
- Deleting any corpus row -> ratchet RED.
- A declarative modifier/capability with no forward() twin -> ratchet RED (mutation-proven).
- The self-referential derivation is gone; independence pinned by a meta-test.

Found in the e9zse post-ship adversarial verification (7/8 claims CONFIRMED; this was the one REFUTED). Design context: docs/design/forwardconstruct-expressiveness-parity-2026-07-10.md ('permanent guard = a property test ... so a new declarative capability lacking a forward() path FAILS LOUD (the parity ratchet)') — that promised guard is the thing this bug says is not yet real.
design:
## Root Cause
REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES = frozenset(row.capability for row in PARITY_CORPUS) — both sides of test_every_required_capability_has_a_corpus_row come from the same list; deletion of a row or shipping a capability without a twin can never fail.

## Fix Approach (post-review, final)
1. Replace derivation with a HARDCODED literal frozenset of the 14 capability names. Change the coverage test to assert set EQUALITY (covered == REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES) so a deleted row AND an unregistered new row both fail loud.
2. Surface-enumeration ratchet: required modifier types = {r.mod_type for r in neograph.modifiers._SLOT_RULES} (the production registration table — NOT Modifier.__subclasses__, which is process-global and pollutable). Exercised types = walk every PARITY_CORPUS row's declarative_nodes() IR recursively (Node/Construct .modifier_set slots, recurse into Construct.nodes), collect type(mod) per occupied slot. Assert required <= exercised.
3. Meta-guard already landed (RED): AST check that REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES assignment does not reference PARITY_CORPUS.
4. Mutation proofs (transient, reverted): (a) comment out loop_in_loop row -> equality test RED; (b) simulate a new modifier in _SLOT_RULES (or drop a row so a modifier loses sole coverage) -> enumeration test RED.

     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"

   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:
