title: Sweep verification for neograph-e9zse.5
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-e9zse.5
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-e9zse.5`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-e9zse.5)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-e9zse.5 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-e9zse.5 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-e9zse.5
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-e9zse.5` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-e9zse.5/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-e9zse.5
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-e9zse.5)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-e9zse.5 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-e9zse.5 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-e9zse.5/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-e9zse.5 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted

     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and

     ```

     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   Pattern: <one-line spec>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |

   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

title: FakeMcpSession: support per-args / sequenced results (a composite calls one tool N times by args)
description:
## What
neograph_mcp.testing.FakeMcpSession.call resolves scripted results by TOOL NAME only (testing.py:94,139: results is dict[str, McpCallResult], .get(tool_name)). A CLIENT-SIDE COMPOSITE that calls the SAME federated tool multiple times differing only by ARGS (e.g. agent-stark hubspot_comms: search_crm_objects(companies,domain) then 4x search_crm_objects(<type>, associatedWith company)) cannot be scripted — every call returns the identical payload, so the fast-tier oracle cannot assert the ASSEMBLED result.

## Why
The 0.6 composite pattern (mcp_session + example 26) is a first-class use case, but FakeMcpSession can only fake 1:1 tools. Consumers must hand-roll an args-aware session double, defeating the 'parity-pinned test double' value. This is the deterministic per-commit oracle the composite assembly logic needs.

## Expectations after delivery
- FakeMcpSession can script results keyed by (tool_name, args) OR as an ordered sequence per tool, so a composite's N same-tool calls return distinct recorded-real envelopes; still parity-pinned to the real output_model rehydration.

## Verification — integration & E2E only
- Integration: a FakeMcpSession scripted with per-args results; a composite issuing 5 same-tool calls receives the 5 distinct scripted envelopes; assembly asserted. Parity with real McpSession.call rehydration preserved.

## Acceptance
- FakeMcpSession supports per-args or sequenced results; documented; agent-stark stark-8ok's composite fast-tier can assert the assembled list without a hand-rolled double.
design:
## Core Invariant
A FakeMcpSession must resolve N same-tool calls the way the REAL server would (as a function of args, or over a scripted sequence) while every resolved envelope STILL rehydrates through the one shared neograph_mcp._typed.rehydrate — and a bare McpCallResult keeps meaning 'constant every call' so every existing name-only user stays green. (Backward-compatible parity, not a new double.)

## Implementation Plan
1. WIDEN the results value type in FakeMcpSession only (src/neograph_mcp/testing.py). Add a type alias, e.g.:
   `ResultResolver = Callable[[dict[str, Any]], McpCallResult]`
   `ScriptedResult = McpCallResult | list[McpCallResult] | ResultResolver`
   and change __init__ signature to `results: dict[str, ScriptedResult] | None`. This covers BOTH ticket options in one tri-modal value:
   - bare McpCallResult  -> constant (UNCHANGED backward-compat path)
   - list[McpCallResult] -> ordered SEQUENCE, consumed FIFO per tool (the 'same tool N times in known order' case)
   - Callable(args)->McpCallResult -> PER-ARGS resolver (the parity-faithful case; directly replaces agent-stark's hand-rolled objectType-dispatch double)
   Recommend the CALLABLE resolver as the primary/blessed mechanism (most parity-faithful — server IS a function of args — and sidesteps the unhashable-args problem entirely), with the list SEQUENCE as convenience sugar for order-only cases. Do NOT implement a (tool, frozenset(args)) keyed dict (unhashable filterGroups).
2. In __init__: keep `self._results` but pre-convert any list value to a per-tool iterator held in a separate map (e.g. self._sequences: dict[str, Iterator[McpCallResult]]) so FIFO cursor state survives across calls; leave callables/bare McpCallResult in self._results.
3. Add a private `_resolve(tool_name, args) -> McpCallResult | None` that: returns None if unscripted; if a list/iterator -> next() (raise a loud 'FakeMcpSession scripted sequence for tool X exhausted after K calls' on StopIteration); if callable -> call it with dict(args or {}); if bare McpCallResult -> return as-is. Call this ONCE at the top of .call(), BEFORE the errors/None/rehydrate branches (keeps testing.py:142-154 logic intact, just fed a resolved McpCallResult).
4. Leave the rehydrate call (testing.py:154) BYTE-FOR-BYTE — resolver/sequence only pick WHICH McpCallResult; .structured still flows through the shared _typed.rehydrate. Anti-echo-chamber invariant untouched.
5. Update the FakeMcpSession + module docstrings (testing.py:75-83, and the class docstring at 8-11) to document the tri-modal results value and the per-args use case; keep the anti-echo-chamber section unchanged.
6. TEST (extend tests/test_mcp_fakes.py, the neograph way — obligation tests, fake-only, zero subprocess, monkeypatch _client_for to _boom for the zero-network proof as at :112-115): add a TestFakeSessionPerArgs class proving (a) a composite issuing 5 SAME-tool calls differing only by args receives 5 DISTINCT scripted envelopes and the assembled list is asserted (the ticket's exact scenario, mirroring the hubspot objectType fan); (b) list-sequence value consumed FIFO returns distinct results in order; (c) parity — a per-args-resolved envelope still rehydrates == the real captured model (reuse the captured-structuredContent idiom at :217-242, or assert the resolved envelope goes through rehydrate by re-using ClientCrmResult); (d) sequence-exhaustion raises loud; (e) a bare-McpCallResult results= dict still behaves exactly as today (regression pin). Assert on .calls[].args sequence (idiom at :184-189). No new fake file — extend this one.
7. After green: agent-stark stark-8ok deletes tests/tools/test_hubspot_composite.py:53 _RecordedRealCrmSession and scripts FakeMcpSession with a per-args resolver instead (acceptance criterion). File/note the follow-up; do NOT edit agent-stark here.
notes:
## Findings (research neograph-82fys.2)

REUSE TARGET — extend the existing FakeMcpSession, do NOT add a new double. Widen the VALUE type of the existing `results=` dict; keep everything else.

- Current resolver is TOOL-NAME-ONLY: `self._results = dict(results)` (testing.py:94) then `scripted = self._results.get(tool_name)` (testing.py:139). One McpCallResult per tool name => N same-tool calls all return the identical envelope. That is the whole limitation.

So the fake's job for N same-tool calls is to return DISTINCT scripted results the way the server would. description:

a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-e9zse.2`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-e9zse.2)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |

   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-e9zse.2 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-e9zse.2 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

title: Unify construct builders: one core builder + module-filter adapter (fixes silent sub-construct drop)
description:
## Core invariant
There is ONE selection contract for what counts as a pipeline member, shared by both build entry points. construct_from_module never silently omits a module-level pipeline component. (neograph's 'if it compiles, it runs' guarantee: a builder that quietly discards a declared sub-construct produces a different-but-valid-looking graph than the author wrote — the worst failure mode for that guarantee.)

## The defect (confirmed, repro in the design doc)
construct_from_module(mod) with a module containing @node functions AND a Construct collects ONLY the Nodes; the Construct is discarded with NO error/warning (verified 2026-07-10: result.nodes==['seed'], sub-construct gone). Root cause = duplicated selection logic that DRIFTED on two axes:

| source member | construct_from_module | construct_from_functions |
| @node Node (sidecar) | collect | collect |
| plain Node(...) (no sidecar) | collect (plain_nodes) | REJECT (:163) |
| Construct | SILENTLY SKIP (bug) | collect (:138) |
| import/helper/constant | silently skip | reject (loud) |

Both already share the wiring engine (_build_construct_from_decorated); only SELECTION is duplicated.

## Target architecture — Option B' (authoritative: docs/design/construct-from-module-silent-drop-2026-07-10.md)
ONE core builder + a thin filter adapter:
- **Core builder** (extract from today's construct_from_functions body): takes an explicit list of pipeline members -> collect/validate/wire; rejects unrecognized members LOUDLY. Sole home of 'collect + wire + reject'.
- **construct_from_module = thin adapter**: filter vars(mod) to pipeline-member types, delegate to the core builder. Sole home of 'skip unrecognized namespace member'.
- **One selection predicate** (e.g. _classify_member) — the single source of truth both paths use.

The ONE legitimate entry-point difference (skip-vs-reject unknowns: a module namespace always carries imports/helpers; an explicit list is a cleanliness promise) is expressed by WHERE the predicate is applied (filter skips, core rejects), NOT by two contracts. This makes the drift structurally impossible.

## Decisions to settle — each PINNED by a test
1. **Member set (resolve the plain-Node inconsistency):** unify what both paths accept. Recommend the UNION — @node Nodes + plain declarative Node(...) + Construct. So a plain Node passed to construct_from_functions is now accepted (today it raises), OR deliberately decide to keep rejecting it and document why. No silent asymmetry.
2. **Imported-Construct behavior:** vars(mod) includes imported names. Decide (a) accept namespace semantics (collect any module-level Construct — consistent with today's imported-Node behavior) + document, or (b) add a provenance guard. Pin either way.
3. **ForwardConstruct exposure:** a module-level MyForwardConstruct() instance — collect / reject / explicitly out-of-scope. Pin.

## Guard-first / TDD (mandatory order)
1. Write the FAILING test first: module with @node + Construct -> assert the sub-construct is present and wired via its output port in the compiled graph. Verify it FAILS on current HEAD.
2. Add should_fail + should_pass fixtures in tests/check_fixtures/ mirroring the repro.
3. Add a STRUCTURAL GUARD asserting a single selection predicate (no duplicated isinstance-collection across the two entry points) — permanent anti-drift protection.
4. Then refactor to B' until green.

## Three-surface parity
Builder-layer change. Cover the @node path end-to-end; declarative Construct(nodes=[...]) and programmatic Node|Modifier build Constructs directly (exempt) — state it explicitly.

## Docs updates (part of the fix, not follow-up)
- examples/10_full_pipeline.py:18-19 — 'construct_from_module cannot inline subgraphs' becomes FALSE; rewrite the comment + the manual-assembly narrative.
- website scripted-pipeline.mdx + runtime/programmatic.mdx — 'walks all @node functions' phrasing must acknowledge sub-constructs.
- Regenerate the API manifest if builder docstrings/signatures change (verifiable-docs freshness guard must stay green).

## Independent-review gate
The member-set + imported-Construct + ForwardConstruct decisions are architectural. Confirm with a fresh-context reviewer BEFORE merge; the review must check the single-predicate guard actually bites.

## Audit
- Confirm no other vars(mod)/module-walk collector drops types (spike found only this one).
- After the refactor, confirm the extracted core builder is the SOLE collection site.

## Acceptance criteria
- construct_from_module over a module with a sub-construct includes it, wired via its output port, and is runtime-equivalent to construct_from_functions over the same members (assert on the compiled graph, not internals).
- Exactly ONE selection predicate exists; the structural guard fails if a second collection site is reintroduced.
- plain-Node, imported-Construct, ForwardConstruct behaviors each pinned by a test with a documented decision.
- example 10 + website docs updated; API manifest fresh; full suite + fixtures green.
- Independent review recorded on the bead.

## Fallback
If the imported-Construct ambiguity cannot be cleanly resolved in the filter, ship Option A (fail-loud: construct_from_module raises naming the dropped Construct, pointing to construct_from_functions/declarative form) as the guaranteed floor — never the silent drop. Prefer B'.

## Non-goals
- ox-troubleshooting-demo cmu.8 AC correction (separate, ox-side).

## Effort
Medium — focused refactor of src/neograph/_construct_builder.py + tests (fixtures, guard) + doc touches. No IR/compiler changes.

construct_from_module and construct_from_functions duplicate member-SELECTION logic (both already share the wiring engine _build_construct_from_decorated). The module walk (src/neograph/_construct_builder.py:78-83) collects only Node instances (sidecar -> nodes, else plain_nodes) and silently skips Construct; the explicit-list path (:137-154) collects Construct + sidecar Nodes but REJECTS plain Nodes. title: Sweep verification for uagu7
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on uagu7
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" uagu7`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (uagu7)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update uagu7 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add uagu7 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for uagu7
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show uagu7` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/uagu7/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" uagu7
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (uagu7)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update uagu7 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update uagu7 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/uagu7/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add uagu7 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for 27h3s
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show 27h3s` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/27h3s/`:

     ```

     ```

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

   found must appear:

   ```
   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update 27h3s --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash

   ```

ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed

- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-x51j3
description:

executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-x51j3` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-x51j3/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-x51j3
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-x51j3)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-x51j3 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash

   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-x51j3/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-x51j3 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

   ```
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   ```

   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances

title: Surface MCP progress notifications for long-running tools into stream()/astream()
description:
CORE INVARIANT: a long-running MCP tool that emits MCP progress notifications surfaces that progress to the caller through neograph streaming verbs (stream()/astream()), instead of the run appearing frozen until the tool returns.

WHY: MCP defines progress notifications (progressToken + notifications/progress) for long-running tools. neograph tool loop is request/response; a 60s tool call is a black box to the caller. Streaming is already first-class (four verbs), so progress is a natural custom-stream channel.

SCOPE: wire the MCP adapter progress callback into a neograph stream channel (LangGraph custom stream_mode / StreamWriter). A tool call carrying a progressToken forwards each notification as a stream event tagged with node + tool + progress fraction/message. No-op when the caller is not streaming or the tool emits no progress.

ANTI-BAND-AID: progress is OBSERVABILITY, never control flow — a missing/last progress notification must not affect the tool result, budgets, or replay. Progress events must NOT enter state or the checkpoint (ephemeral, like log lines), so they never touch the schema fingerprint.

ACCEPTANCE: a demo long-running tool emitting progress surfaces N events through astream() IN ORDER; a non-streaming arun() of the same pipeline is unaffected; progress never enters state/checkpoint; the tool result is byte-identical with and without a progress consumer. NOT 0.6.0-gating.
design:
## Core Invariant
MCP progress notifications are ephemeral OBSERVABILITY surfaced ONLY through the existing custom-stream seam (emit_progress) — they never enter state, checkpoint, schema fingerprint, tool result, or budgets, and are a silent no-op when the caller is not streaming.

## Implementation Plan (REFINED per architect review neograph-5jrd0.53)
1. REUSE emit_progress as the surfacing mechanism (do NOT invent a stream channel). In src/neograph_mcp, define typed event model `McpProgress(BaseModel)` {server: str, tool: str, progress: float, total: float | None, message: str | None}. The callback calls PUBLIC neograph.emit_progress(McpProgress(...)); the src/neograph MCP-free guard stays green (wiring lives in the battery).
2. **[REVISED — constructor path, smaller diff]** Thread a `callbacks: Callbacks | None = None` param (default None) through `_client_for(server_key, spec, token, *, callbacks=None)` (_client.py:104) into `MultiServerMCPClient(connections, callbacks=callbacks)`. In _make_tool_factory's per-run _factory, build `Callbacks(on_progress=_on_progress)` and pass it to _client_for, then KEEP the existing `client.get_tools(server_name=server_key)` call intact — get_tools() forwards self.callbacks into load_mcp_tools verbatim, so the returned tools are byte-identical and the post-steps (stdio token-inject -> rename model_copy -> _wrap_output_model) stay unchanged in order. Do NOT switch to load_mcp_tools(connection=). _discover_tool_names (:203) and mcp_resource_fetcher are unaffected (callbacks defaults None).
3. **[REVISED — no envelope hand-roll]** on_progress closure: `async def _on_progress(progress, total, message, context: CallbackContext)` -> emit_progress(McpProgress(server=context.server_name, tool=context.tool_name, progress=progress, total=total, message=message)). PREFER the bare emit_progress path (per-call session + receive-loop task are created inside the node ainvoke context, so asyncio copies node contextvars at task creation — get_stream_writer() should resolve). If the E2E proves contextvars DO reach the callback task, ship exactly this and DROP any fallback. If a fallback is genuinely required, EXTEND neograph.emit_progress with an optional injected-writer param (emit_progress(event, *, writer=None)) so envelope-construction + warn-once stay single-sited in progress.py — NEVER call writer(payload) / reconstruct the {neograph_event/event_type/data} envelope inside neograph_mcp (that would reopen the Pattern-A single-seam bypass the scan pins at 0).
4. Add an async long-running demo tool to examples/_mcp_demo_server.py (e.g. `slow_export(n, ctx)`) looping `await ctx.report_progress(i, n, f'step {i}')` with small sleeps, then a deterministic result. FastMCP auto-attaches progressToken when the client passes a progress callback.
5. Acceptance test in tests/test_mcp_battery.py (extra-gated): (a) agent node binds slow_export, drive via astream(stream_mode='custom'); assert exactly N McpProgress envelopes surface IN ORDER; (b) arun() (non-streaming) returns a byte-identical tool result, unaffected (warn-once tolerated); (c) assert no progress payload in final state or checkpoint AND assert the McpProgress envelope key is NOT neo_*-prefixed (pins the actual state-isolation mechanism, mirroring test_emit_progress.py).
6. Three-surface note: agent/act (tool-loop) behavior in the neograph_mcp battery, not an IR change — no @node/declarative/programmatic parity obligation; seam is emit_progress (already three-surface-safe). NOT 0.6.0-gating.

## Disease disposition update
:277 remains the single MIGRATE site but the change is now 'thread callbacks= through _client_for so get_tools carries the on_progress callback', NOT 'replace get_tools with load_mcp_tools'. :203 stays ALLOWLIST.
notes:
## Findings (research neograph-5jrd0.26)

REUSE TARGET (surfacing side) — do NOT build a new stream channel. `emit_progress` already IS the sanctioned custom-stream seam:
- `src/neograph/progress.py` — `emit_progress(event: BaseModel)` wraps a typed event in the stable envelope {"neograph_event":"progress","event_type":<cls>,"data":model_dump} and writes to LangGraph `get_stream_writer()`. Public API (neograph/__init__.py:74,115). Handles warn-once when non-streaming; never raises; never enters state (envelope key is deliberately NOT neo_*-prefixed so runner._finalize_chunk passes it through untouched). This is the CURRENT pattern (q8ec); there is NO deprecated alternative.
- `StateKeys.STREAM_CUSTOM` (_state_keys.py:69, config-only key) — set by stream/astream when consuming stream_mode='custom'; lets emit_progress distinguish a live consumer from a non-streaming driver. Never enters state/fingerprint. Matches the ANTI-BAND-AID clause exactly (ephemeral, like log lines).
- runner.py:612 `_wants_custom`, :819 `_finalize_chunk` (custom chunks pass through untouched), astream at :1104.

REUSE TARGET (MCP callback side) — langchain-mcp-adapters already exposes a progress seam:
- mcp SDK `ClientSession.call_tool(name, args, read_timeout_seconds, progress_callback, *, meta)` — progress_callback is native; passing it auto-mints a progressToken. Verified on installed mcp 1.28.x.
- `langchain_mcp_adapters.callbacks.Callbacks(on_logging_message, on_progress, on_elicitation)` with `.to_mcp_format(context=CallbackContext(server_name, tool_name))`. `on_progress` signature: `async def on_progress(progress: float, total: float|None, message: str|None, context: CallbackContext)`. CallbackContext carries server_name + tool_name (the 'tool + progress fraction/message' tagging the scope wants).
- `load_mcp_tools(session=None, *, connection=<dict>, callbacks=Callbacks(...), server_name=..., tool_name_prefix=..., handle_tool_errors=...)` and `convert_mcp_tool_to_langchain_tool(..., callbacks=...)` BOTH accept callbacks and thread progress_callback into call_tool. CONSTRAINT: `MultiServerMCPClient.get_tools(server_name=)` does NOT accept callbacks — the current factory build path bypasses the seam.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:252 `_make_tool_factory` — the exemplar to EXTEND. Its inner `_factory(config, tool_config)` runs per-superstep INSIDE the node's async context; currently builds tools via `client.get_tools(server_name=server_key)` (line ~276) which cannot carry callbacks. This is where progress wiring must land (switch to load_mcp_tools(connection=_connection(...), callbacks=...) or convert per-tool). Identity injection (_inject_stdio_token :175), rename (model_copy), and _wrap_output_model (:207) all operate on the returned BaseTool AFTER — order preserved.
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:88 `_connection` — already builds the connection dict load_mcp_tools needs.
- src/neograph/_agent_cycle.py:459 `_ainvoke_tool_timed` — `await tool_fn.ainvoke(tc['args'], config=config)`: the async tool call site inside the ReAct cycle where progress notifications actually fire. Progress is async-only; the sync loop (_tool_loop.py invoke path / run()) cannot surface it (acceptable — acceptance is astream/arun).
- examples/_mcp_demo_server.py:217+ — plain FastMCP @mcp.tool server; has NO long-running progress tool yet. Add an async tool taking `ctx: Context` that calls `await ctx.report_progress(i, total, msg)` in a loop (e.g. slow_export). FastMCP Context.report_progress is the standard emit.
- tests/modes/test_emit_progress.py + tests/test_streaming.py — the emit/astream-custom test exemplars to copy the acceptance test shape from.
- tests/test_mcp_battery.py:172 `_build_agent_construct`, :193 `_react_fake`, :225 arun-through-battery — the extra-gated harness to add the acceptance test to.
- GUARD: tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py — src/neograph must stay MCP-free; ONLY src/neograph_mcp may import the adapter. So callback wiring lives in neograph_mcp and calls the PUBLIC neograph.emit_progress seam (neograph_mcp already depends on neograph).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- CONTEXTVAR PROPAGATION (primary risk): emit_progress uses get_stream_writer() which reads LangGraph contextvars set during the node superstep. The on_progress callback fires from the mcp ClientSession receive-loop task (anyio task group). asyncio copies contextvars at task-creation; the on-the-fly per-call session is created INSIDE call_tool during the node's ainvoke, so it SHOULD inherit the writer — but this must be proven by the E2E test. FALLBACK if the writer isn't visible from the callback task: capture get_stream_writer() (or a bound emit closure) once inside _factory (which is in node context) and close over it in on_progress, instead of calling get_stream_writer() from within the callback.
- Build-path switch: moving from client.get_tools() to load_mcp_tools(connection=..., callbacks=...) changes the per-call session model — verify token injection/rename/output_model wraps still compose (they act on the returned BaseTool, so composition order is unchanged).
- warn-once: under a non-streaming arun() the demo tool's progress will trip emit_progress's once-per-process UserWarning; benign and required-by-design (must not vanish silently), does not affect result — assert result byte-identical anyway.
- Ordering: emit_progress writes synchronously per notification as it arrives, so N events surface IN ORDER naturally.
- No doc/code contradiction found; progress.py + STREAM_CUSTOM is the documented, current seam (no NEEDS USER INPUT).
## Codebase Disease Scan (fflpt)

Two patterns checked:

### Pattern A: hand-rolled custom-stream channel bypassing emit_progress
Scan command: grep -rn 'emit_progress\|get_stream_writer\|STREAM_CUSTOM\|stream_mode.*custom' src/ | grep -v test
Total instances found: 0 bypasses. emit_progress (src/neograph/progress.py) is the SOLE sanctioned seam over get_stream_writer; STREAM_CUSTOM is a documented KEEP. Design step 1 correctly reuses it. No MIGRATE/DEFER — clean.

### Pattern B: callback-blind client.get_tools() dropping the MCP progress callback
Scan command: grep -rn 'client.get_tools\|\.get_tools()' src/
Total instances found: 2

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:277 | _make_tool_factory per-run _factory: `tools = await client.get_tools(...)` | MIGRATE | tool-EXECUTION path — must build via callback-carrying adapter seam (Callbacks(on_progress=...)) so progress surfaces; this is design step 2 |
| 2 | src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:203 | _discover_tool_names: `tools = await client.get_tools(...)` | ALLOWLIST | discovery/listing ONLY — enumerates tool NAMES, never executes a tool, so there are no progress notifications to surface; wiring a callback here would be dead code |

No DEFER rows. Scope confirmed = 1 MIGRATE site (matches design), 1 ALLOWLIST false positive. SYNTACTIC disease → single-executor grep sufficient; no multi-agent artifact required.
## Architect Review (neograph-5jrd0.28/.29)

Gate: research:complete + codebase-scan:complete both present. PASS.

Verified against installed deps + source: emit_progress seam (progress.py) is the sole sanctioned custom-stream writer and never enters state/fingerprint (docstring + envelope key confirm); Callbacks/CallbackContext/on_progress signature (progress,total,message,context); load_mcp_tools(session,*,connection,callbacks,server_name,...); _make_tool_factory:252, _factory get_tools at :277 (MIGRATE) and _discover_tool_names get_tools at :203 (ALLOWLIST). Disposition table is accurate. Core Invariant is preserved (additive observability, no state/checkpoint/result/budget impact). No HIGH.

- [MEDIUM] Research conclusion is subtly WRONG and drove a more invasive plan than needed. The notes state "MultiServerMCPClient.get_tools does NOT accept callbacks — the current factory build path bypasses the seam", concluding step 2 must REPLACE client.get_tools() with load_mcp_tools(connection=_connection(...), callbacks=...). But MultiServerMCPClient.__init__ accepts callbacks=Callbacks(...) and get_tools() forwards self.callbacks into load_mcp_tools verbatim (confirmed by reading get_tools source in installed langchain-mcp-adapters). The get_tools METHOD lacks a callbacks kwarg; the CLIENT does not. Suggestion: prefer threading callbacks through the existing _client_for -> MultiServerMCPClient(connections, callbacks=Callbacks(on_progress=_on_progress)) and KEEP the client.get_tools(server_name=server_key) call intact. This is a strictly smaller diff, preserves the nmb2 client-ownership/session model verbatim, and ELIMINATES the plans own "build-path switch" risk item (token-injection/rename/output_model composition) because get_tools produces byte-identical tools. Add callbacks param to _client_for with default None so _discover_tool_names/resource fetcher are unaffected. Note: the single-server get_tools(server_name=key) branch awaits load_mcp_tools in the current context (no asyncio.create_task), so it does not disturb node contextvar propagation; the multi-server branch does wrap in create_task, but the battery never uses it.

- [MEDIUM] Contingent-fallback collides with the single-seam invariant the disease scan (Pattern A) protects. Step 3 fallback says "capture get_stream_writer() (or a bound emit) once inside _factory and close over it". If the E2E shows contextvars do not reach the on_progress task and the fallback captures the writer directly, calling writer(payload) hand-rolls the envelope in neograph_mcp — exactly the emit_progress bypass Pattern A reports as 0 instances and must stay 0. emit_progress acquires its writer internally via get_stream_writer(), so binding a writer cannot route back through the public seam as written. Suggestion: if the fallback is needed, EXTEND emit_progress with an optional injected-writer parameter (e.g. emit_progress(event, *, writer=None)) so the envelope construction + warn-once logic stay single-sited, rather than reconstructing the {neograph_event/event_type/data} envelope in the battery. Primary bare-emit_progress path is likely fine (per-call session + receive-loop task are created inside the node ainvoke context, so asyncio copies node contextvars at task creation) — this only bites if the E2E forces the fallback.

- [LOW] Step 2 passes _connection(spec, token) as load_mcp_tools connection= (only under the plans rewrite; moot if the constructor-path MEDIUM is adopted). StdioConnection is a total TypedDict (__required_keys__ = all 8 keys incl cwd/encoding/session_kwargs), while _connection emits a partial dict. Works at runtime (existing code already casts past this for MultiServerMCPClient) but keep the cast(Any, ...) if this path is used. The constructor path avoids the issue since _client_for already casts.

- [LOW] Add a brief assertion in the acceptance test that the McpProgress envelope key is NOT neo_*-prefixed (the mechanism that keeps it out of _finalize_chunk/state), not merely that state lacks a progress payload — pins the actual isolation mechanism, mirroring test_emit_progress.py.

Overall: NEEDS_REFINEMENT
## Triage (neograph-5jrd0.28): NEEDS_REFINEMENT -> injected refine neograph-5jrd0.53 (2 MEDIUM: callbacks-via-constructor, no-envelope-handroll-in-fallback; 2 LOW); write-test (neograph-5jrd0.30) re-pointed to wait on it.
## Refine (neograph-5jrd0.53) applied: design step 2 -> constructor callbacks path (keep get_tools); step 3 -> bare emit_progress primary, optional emit_progress(writer=) if fallback needed (no battery envelope hand-roll); test asserts non-neo_* envelope key. No re-research.
## Regression Test (TDD red, neograph-5jrd0.30)
- Test: tests/test_mcp_battery.py::TestMcpProgressStreaming — 4 tests:
  - test_slow_export_progress_surfaces_in_order_via_astream_custom
  - test_arun_unaffected_and_tool_result_identical_with_and_without_consumer
  - test_progress_never_enters_state_or_checkpoint
  - test_tool_emitting_no_progress_is_a_noop
- Status: FAILING (expected — TDD red). All 4 fail with ImportError: cannot import name 'McpProgress' from 'neograph_mcp' (the missing public surface; body-local imports keep collection green, per the mcp_session/mcp_run_context red precedent in the same file).
- Tests expected behavior: a long-running MCP tool's progress notifications surface as typed McpProgress envelopes (server+tool tagged, exactly N, in order) via astream(stream_mode='custom') through the emit_progress seam, while remaining pure observability — arun unaffected, tool result identical with/without a consumer, nothing in state/checkpoint (envelope key non-neo_*, pinned against a real AsyncSqliteSaver incl. raw DB bytes), and a progress-less tool is a total no-op.
- Test infrastructure added: examples/_mcp_demo_server.py gained the async slow_export(n, ctx, token) demo tool (ctx.report_progress(i, n, 'step i') per step, tiny sleeps, deterministic result) — smoke-verified working via mcp_session against the real stdio server.
- Run with: uv run --extra dev --extra mcp-examples pytest tests/test_mcp_battery.py -k TestMcpProgressStreaming
## Implementation (neograph-5jrd0.31)
- NEW src/neograph_mcp/_progress.py: McpProgress(BaseModel){server,tool,progress,total,message} + _progress_callbacks(server_key) building adapter Callbacks(on_progress=...) that calls PUBLIC neograph.emit_progress — the ONE custom-stream seam, no envelope hand-roll (primary bare path worked; no writer-injection fallback needed).
- _client.py: _client_for gains callbacks=None (constructor path — get_tools forwards verbatim per review MEDIUM-1; discovery/resource paths unchanged); _make_tool_factory._factory builds the progress callbacks and passes them on BOTH branches — held session (load_mcp_tools(held, callbacks=...)) and stateless (_client_for(..., callbacks=...)).
- examples/_mcp_demo_server.py: slow_export(n, ctx) demo tool (test author, ctx.report_progress loop).
- Exported McpProgress via __init__ __all__; api-manifest regenerated.
- Test fixes (documented): the byte-identical result comparison normalized for langchain's run-random lc_<uuid> content-block ids (create_text_block stamps a fresh id per invocation — two separate RUNS can never match on that field; run randomness, not progress drift). Applied to .result and repr(.typed_result).
- Tests: TestMcpProgressStreaming 4/4 — N events IN ORDER w/ server+tool tags; arun unaffected + result identical (normalized); never enters state/checkpoint (sqlite history + raw DB bytes) + envelope key not neo_*-prefixed; no-progress tool = no-op.
- GATES: 91/91 MCP suites; make quality all green; mypy both packages.
## Sweep Verification (neograph-5jrd0.32)
Re-scan A: grep -rn 'get_stream_writer|neograph_event' src/neograph_mcp/ -> 0 hits (no envelope hand-roll, no direct writer use); the battery's ONLY emission is via public neograph.emit_progress (_progress.py). Pattern A stays at 0 bypasses.
Re-scan B: grep get_tools sites -> :360 _discover_tool_names (ALLOWLIST, unchanged — name discovery, no execution, no progress) and :445 _make_tool_factory stateless branch — now CALLBACK-CARRYING via _client_for(..., callbacks=_progress_callbacks(server_key)) (MultiServerMCPClient ctor forwards into load_mcp_tools); the held branch passes the same callbacks to load_mcp_tools directly. MIGRATE row satisfied on BOTH branches.

| # | Phase 1b row | Disposition | Post-fix | Verified |
|---|--------------|-------------|----------|----------|
| A | emit_progress bypasses | 0 expected | 0 found | YES |
| B1 | _client.py:277 (now :445 + held branch) | MIGRATE | callbacks threaded via ctor / load_mcp_tools on both branches | YES |
| B2 | _client.py:203 (now :360) | ALLOWLIST | unchanged, discovery-only | YES |

Class-level pin: behavioral — TestMcpProgressStreaming pins ordered surfacing, result-invariance, state/checkpoint isolation (incl. raw sqlite bytes), and the non-neo_* envelope mechanism. The Pattern-A single-seam rule is additionally covered by the emit_progress design (any future writer hand-roll in the battery would show in re-scan A; the isolation test fails if the envelope shape drifts).

title: MCP test fakes: FakeMcpSession + fake tool factory / resource fetcher (keyless, serverless consumer tests)
description:
CORE INVARIANT: a downstream consumer can unit-test an MCP-composite (a scripted node calling federated primitives via mcp_session, OR an agent/act node bound to mcp_tool_factory tools) with NO subprocess and NO network — scripted structured results in, recorded calls out.

WHY: mcp_session (2plcl) shipped the capability for composites like agent-stark hubspot_comms to issue their own primitive calls, but the ONLY way to exercise one today is against the real stdio demo server or hand-rolled mocks. Mirrors the neograph.testing LLM-fakes precedent (dyp3): fakes are what make a capability testable by the people who use it.

SCOPE:
- FakeMcpSession: an async-CM drop-in for McpSession whose .call(tool, args, output_model=) returns scripted results (honoring output_model rehydration EXACTLY like the real session) and records (tool, args, resolved-identity) for assertions.
- A fake tool factory + fake resource fetcher matching the mcp_tool_factory / mcp_resource_fetcher signatures, returning scripted tools/resources, so agent/act nodes and FromResource hydration run keyless.
- Live in neograph_mcp.testing, exported via __all__.

ANTI-BAND-AID: the fake MUST honor the SAME output_model / typed_result contract and the SAME identity-carrying semantics as the real session/factory — a test green on the fake but red on the real server is an echo chamber. Pin a PARITY test: fake and real demo-server session agree on typed_result shape for the same scripted payload.

ACCEPTANCE: a composite-node test runs green with zero subprocess/network; the fake records identity+args; output_model rehydration matches the real path; parity test pins the contract. NOT 0.6.0-gating.
design:
## Core Invariant
The fake honors the SAME output_model/typed_result rehydration (via the shared _rehydrate helper — identical model_validate/parse, identical missing-structuredContent ValueError, identical McpToolCallError) and the SAME identity-minting semantics (_resolve_token/_resolve_token_no_config) as the real McpSession/factory/fetcher — so any test green on the fake is green on the real demo server (no echo chamber).

## Implementation Plan (REFINED per architect review neograph-5jrd0.52)
1. **Factor the shared rehydration + error out of _session.py/_client.py** so real and fake call ONE helper. Add `_rehydrate(output_model, parse, structured, tool_name) -> BaseModel` (raises the existing ValueError when structured is None) in a neutral spot (src/neograph_mcp/_typed.py) and have McpSession.call (L334-343) and _wrap_output_model._typed (L239-247) call it. Parity becomes structural.
2. **Create src/neograph_mcp/testing.py** (single MODULE — NOT a package; simpler for one file's worth of fakes; diverges intentionally from neograph.testing's package shape). Export via THIS module's own __all__; do NOT add to top-level neograph_mcp __all__. Contents:
   - `FakeMcpSession`: async-CM drop-in for McpSession. Ctor takes scripted results keyed by tool name (structuredContent dict AND/OR content blocks AND/OR isError flag), plus optional token_provider/config so __aenter__ mints identity via the REUSED _resolve_token/_resolve_token_no_config. `.call(tool, args, *, output_model=, parse=)` looks up the scripted payload, records (tool, dict(args), resolved-identity) on a public `.calls` list, then: isError -> raise McpToolCallError; output_model set -> return _rehydrate(...); else -> return McpCallResult(content, structured). `.tool_names()` returns scripted keys. NO subprocess, NO network. **DOCSTRING (per review LOW): transport-level stdio_token_arg injection-into-args is NOT simulated (the fake has no server tools-list); identity is surfaced via .calls[].identity, NEVER via args — consumers must not write args-injection assertions.**
   - `fake_mcp_tool_factory(...)`: returns a ToolFactory = async (config, tool_config) -> a StructuredTool (graduate tests/test_mcp_battery.py L276-281) that records calls and, when output_model is declared, returns the REAL rehydrated model via the shared _rehydrate so ToolInteraction.typed_result parity holds. Reuse _resolve_token for recorded identity.
   - `fake_mcp_resource_fetcher(...)`: returns the (fetcher, replayer) tuple with scripted (content, mime) / replay content-list, matching mcp_resource_fetcher's signature, so FromResource hydration runs keyless.
3. **Export** the three via src/neograph_mcp/testing.py __all__ (import path `from neograph_mcp.testing import FakeMcpSession, fake_mcp_tool_factory, fake_mcp_resource_fetcher`).
4. **Consumer-composite test (acceptance)**: a raw-mode composite node (copy examples/26 shape) driven with FakeMcpSession — assert zero subprocess/network, .calls records identity+args, output_model rehydration produces the client model.
5. **PARITY test (acceptance, gated by requires_mcp) — REWRITTEN per review MEDIUM to avoid the tautology**: because step 1 makes fake AND real call ONE _rehydrate, a shared hand-authored literal proves nothing. Instead: (a) call REAL mcp_session against examples/_mcp_demo_server.py and CAPTURE its raw structuredContent dict + the rehydrated model; (b) script FakeMcpSession from that CAPTURED structuredContent; (c) assert the fake's rehydrated model == the real captured model.
