title: Cross-superstep MCP connection reuse WITH transparent reconnect (ReAct loop reconnects every turn today)
description:
CORE INVARIANT: within a run, an agent/act ReAct loop reuses ONE live MCP connection per server across its N supersteps instead of reconnecting every turn — BUT the cache MUST transparently RECONNECT when the cached connection is absent or dead. 'Reuse' is an optimization layered over a reconnect-capable path, NEVER an assumption a connection survives.

WHY (maintainer, 2026-07-10): a HITL interrupt can pause the ReAct loop mid-flight; on resume the run continues from the same step, possibly in a DIFFERENT PROCESS, where no live connection exists. Today each superstep re-invokes the factory, which rebuilds a MultiServerMCPClient and reconnects every turn (nmb2: client owned inside the factory). An 8-turn agent pays 8 connects; but naive caching would hand a resumed run a dead handle.

SCOPE: extend _run_cache (RUN_ID-keyed, already caches the LLM handle + tool instances + FromResource fetch, evicted at run end) to memoize the CONNECTED client per (run, server). On resume RUN_ID is fresh -> cache miss -> transparent reconnect (verify this holds and that a stale/dead cached handle never surfaces as a hang or use-after-close). Preserve nmb2 (client stays consumer-owned, cached in the config-scoped cache, not neograph core) and per-run identity (reconnect re-mints identity from config via token_provider).

ANTI-BAND-AID: do NOT cache a raw socket/session that can go stale silently — the cache path must lazily rebuild on miss OR failed reuse, so a dead connection triggers reconnect, not a hang.

ACCEPTANCE: an N-turn agent against the demo server does 1 connect not N (assert connect count); an interrupt/resume MID-LOOP reconnects cleanly and completes; a killed/dead cached connection triggers transparent reconnect (no hang); per-run identity preserved across reconnect. NOT 0.6.0-gating.
design:
## Core Invariant (REFRAMED per maintainer decision 2026-07-10 + deep research docs/design/mcp-connection-reuse-2026-07-10.md)
Connection reuse is CONSUMER-HELD and OPT-IN: a battery async CM (mcp_run_context) opened by the consumer AROUND arun()/astream() holds one live session per server for the whole run — opened AND closed in the consumer's single long-lived task (the only disposal the task-affine cancel scopes allow; spike-proven) — while supersteps' tool calls ride it from their own tasks (spike-proven safe). Without the CM, the factory falls back UNCHANGED to the adapter's documented stateless per-call default — reuse is an optimization layered over the reconnect-capable path, never an assumption a connection survives. nmb2 strengthened: the consumer literally owns the client/session lifecycle; neograph core untouched.

## Implementation Plan
1. NEW battery async CM in src/neograph_mcp (e.g. _run_context.py): `mcp_run_context(servers: dict[str, StdioServer|HttpServer], *, token_provider=None, config=None, stdio_token_arg='token', timeout=30.0)`. __aenter__: for each server, mint identity (SAME _resolve_token/_resolve_token_no_config path) and open the adapter persistent session (_client_for(...).session(key)) — all in the caller's task; bounded by timeout (copy McpSession.__aenter__'s asyncio.timeout + _unwrap_single normalization). __aexit__: close every session in reverse (LIFO) order in the same task.
2. Config threading: ctx.config(base_config) (or a documented configurable key, mirroring RESOURCE_FETCHER_KEY) stashes a {server_key: live_session} map under a config-only StateKeys-style key. Never enters state/checkpoint (not serializable — same rule as McpSession).
3. EXTEND _make_tool_factory: at the top of the per-superstep _factory, check config for a held session for this server_key; if present, bind via load_mcp_tools(session=held) (skipping client build + connect) and apply the SAME post-steps in order (stdio token-inject -> rename -> _wrap_output_model). If absent (no CM, resumed run, dead entry) -> existing stateless path unchanged (transparent reconnect for free).
4. Per-run identity: minted at CM entry per server (consumer's config); factory identity injection unchanged (token from _resolve_token at factory time still governs stdio arg injection — document that http bearer rides the held connection minted at entry).
5. mcp_session (composite path) and mcp_resource_fetcher: OUT OF SCOPE (already consumer-owned per-body); note in docstring that mcp_run_context serves the FACTORY (agent/act) path.
6. Acceptance (revised): (a) an N-turn agent against the demo server under mcp_run_context does 1 connect not N (assert connect count via server-side or client_for call count); (b) the same pipeline WITHOUT the CM still passes (stateless fallback unchanged); (c) closing happens in the consumer task — no cancel-scope RuntimeError (the spike repro as a regression test shape); (d) a dead/absent held session falls back to reconnect, not a hang; (e) per-run identity rides both paths.
7. Export mcp_run_context via neograph_mcp __init__ __all__; docs note the opt-in pattern + when it matters (slow-spawn stdio; stateful servers) per docs/design/mcp-connection-reuse-2026-07-10.md.
8. Gates: extra-gated tests (importorskip), guard test_guards_mcp_session_ownership stays green (all in battery), mypy/ruff/full pytest.
notes:
## Findings (dp-researcher, 2026-07-10)

### The REUSE target already exists: McpSession persistent-session mode
- `McpSession` / `mcp_session()` in **src/neograph_mcp/_session.py** IS the 'connect ONCE, call N tools over one connection' primitive. It wraps the adapter's PERSISTENT session mode (`client.session()` -> one live ClientSession, then N `session.call_tool()`), the exact opposite of the bound-tool path. This is the connected-per-server object the task wants memoized. Do NOT build a new persistent-connection type — reuse McpSession (or its underlying `_client_for(...).session(server_key)`).
- The per-run cache seam already exists: **src/neograph/_run_cache.py** `aget_or_build(config, subkey, build)` + `evict_run(run_id)`. It ALREADY memoizes the LLM handle and the consumer tool instances per RUN_ID (`tools:{node_name}`, _tool_loop.py:472/518) and is evicted in every runner verb finally (runner.py `_evict_run_cache`, 4 sites). RUN_ID is re-minted on resume => cache MISS => transparent rebuild is ALREADY the structural contract (docstring §1). The 'fresh RUN_ID on resume' half of the ask is free.

### Why it reconnects every turn today (the current, not-deprecated path)
- The bound-tool ReAct path uses the STATELESS adapter model: neograph_mcp `_make_tool_factory._factory` (_client.py:274) builds a fresh `MultiServerMCPClient` and calls `client.get_tools()`; those adapter tools open+close a NEW session PER `tool.ainvoke()` ('disposed by the adapter's stateless-per-call session model', _client.py:267). The FACTORY result is already per-run cached, so the factory runs once — but each of the N tool CALLS across the N ReAct supersteps still connects. N turns = N connects. To reach '1 connect', the factory must return tools bound to a PERSISTENT session (adapter `load_mcp_tools(session=<live session>)`) whose session is the cached-per-(run,server) object.
- Agent/act supersteps drive through _agent_cycle.py `_abuild_turn_prep` -> _tool_loop.py `_aprepare_tool_loop` -> `aget_or_build('tools:{node}', _ainstantiate_tools)`. That is where a session-bound variant would hook.

### Ownership boundary (nmb2 — LOCKED, do not reopen)
- src/neograph owns NO MCP session lifecycle. Enforced by tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py, which scans ONLY src/neograph (SRC_DIR) and bans `ClientSession`, `MultiServerMCPClient`, `langchain_mcp_adapters`, `.session(`, `import mcp`. **src/neograph_mcp is EXEMPT** — the client/session cache + reconnect + disposal MUST live in neograph_mcp, never in core. Verdict doc: docs/design/mcp-session-ownership-review-2026-07-05.md.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph_mcp/_session.py:193-345 (McpSession) — persistent one-connection-N-calls primitive to REUSE; note the same-task/never-store constraints it documents.
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:252-292 (_make_tool_factory) — the reconnect-per-call factory to CONVERT to session-bound tools.
- src/neograph/_run_cache.py:138-171 (aget_or_build / evict_run) — the per-run cache + eviction seam to memoize the connected session on.
- src/neograph/_tool_loop.py:487-522 (_aprepare_tool_loop) — where tool instances are per-run cached; the integration point.
- src/neograph/_agent_cycle.py:182-201 (_abuild_turn_prep) — per-superstep entry that rebuilds the preamble each turn.
- examples/_mcp_demo_server.py:141-163 — stdio spawns a fresh subprocess per session (connect == subprocess spawn); the acceptance 'count connects' assertion hangs off this.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- **LOAD-BEARING RISK — anyio cancel-scope task-affinity.** A live `client.session()` / McpSession enters an anyio cancel scope + background reader task group at connect; McpSession's own docstring (_session.py:19-23) states it MUST be entered AND exited in the SAME task ('crossing tasks fails loudly with a RuntimeError'). LangGraph runs each superstep's node body as a SEPARATE asyncio task, so a session opened in turn 1's task and reused/closed from turn 3's task risks a RuntimeError or use-after-close. This is the crux the task's 'no hang / no use-after-close' clause is really about, and it is UNVERIFIED. A spike must confirm whether the adapter's ClientSession tolerates cross-task call_tool + deferred close, or whether cross-superstep reuse is fundamentally blocked (forcing option: run the whole ReAct loop in one node body/task, which trades away the per-turn HITL-interrupt checkpoint granularity that is the task's WHY).
- **Disposal gap.** `evict_run` (src/neograph/_run_cache.py:158) is SYNC and only deletes dict entries — it never calls `__aexit__`. The currently-cached values (LLM handle, stateless tool instances, resource data) need no async close. A cached LIVE session would be DROPPED without closing => leaked connection / orphaned stdio subprocess, and closing it here would be (a) from the wrong task and (b) in core, tripping the ownership guard. A new async run-end disposal hook owned by neograph_mcp is required; there is no existing seam.
- NEEDS USER INPUT: the task SCOPE says 'extend _run_cache' (core) but also 'client stays consumer-owned, cached in the config-scoped cache, NOT neograph core'. Those pull opposite ways: the cache MECHANISM is core (src/neograph/_run_cache.py) yet a cached live session + its disposal are session-lifecycle, which the ownership guard forbids in core. Resolution likely = neograph_mcp imports the run-cache seam (new battery->core private-module dependency; today neograph_mcp imports NOTHING from core) OR a public disposal-hook seam is added. Maintainer should confirm the intended coupling before implementation.
- 'Dead cached connection => transparent reconnect' needs an explicit liveness path: a cached session whose transport died must be detected (transport error on call, NOT an isError result) and trigger drop-entry+reopen, distinct from uixi1's retry-on-transport-error. Do not conflate with McpToolCallError (isError), which must NOT reconnect.
- Acceptance instrumentation: no connect-counter exists yet. Prereq bead neograph-32qtx (FakeMcpSession + fake factory) lands first per the epic's maintainer-set order and is the clean vehicle for the 'N-turn agent => 1 connect' assertion without a live subprocess.

title: MCP tool-call resilience: per-call timeout + bounded retry on TRANSPORT errors (never on isError)
description:
CORE INVARIANT: a transient TRANSPORT failure (connection reset, DNS blip, streamable-http 5xx/timeout) on an MCP tool call inside an agent/act ReAct loop is retried with bounded backoff, not fatal to the run — while a tool-level isError result is NEVER retried (it is a real result the model must see).

WHY: mcp_session ships timeout=30 + raises on isError, but the agent/act TOOL-LOOP path (factory-bound tools) has NO transport retry. LLM retry exists (_llm_retry) and does not cover MCP calls. One network blip on a remote tool fails the whole run.

SCOPE: bounded retry-with-backoff on TRANSPORT exceptions only, integrated with the existing retry-policy shape (single-responsibility retry — reuse, do not fork). Add a per-call timeout on the factory/tool-loop path (parity with the session timeout=30). Classify: transport/timeout -> retry; isError / tool-domain error -> surface immediately.

ANTI-BAND-AID: do NOT blanket-retry all exceptions — that would replay a mutating tool call (dangerous for act mode / non-idempotent tools). Retry only PRE-RESULT transport failures; respect the idempotent= flag — a non-idempotent tool that MAY have partially executed must NOT be silently retried. A retry is the same logical call — it does not consume tool budget twice.

ACCEPTANCE: a flaky-transport fake tool retries and succeeds within the bound; an isError result surfaces on first return (no retry); a non-idempotent tool is not replayed after an ambiguous failure; budget counts the logical call once. NOT 0.6.0-gating.
design:
## Core Invariant
A retry re-issues ONLY a pre-result MCP TRANSPORT failure (and, for idempotent
tools, an ambiguous post-send one) as the SAME logical tool call — it never retries
an isError/tool-domain result, never replays a non-idempotent tool that may have
partially executed, and never lives in `src/neograph` (transport-classification
stays in the `neograph_mcp` battery; core stays MCP-free and retry_policy-free).

## Implementation Plan
1. In `src/neograph_mcp/_client.py`, add `_with_transport_resilience(tool, *,
   timeout, max_attempts, idempotent)` that wraps `tool.coroutine` via the existing
   `tool.model_copy(update={"coroutine": ...})` pattern (copy `_inject_stdio_token`
   / `_wrap_output_model`). The wrapped coroutine loops up to `max_attempts`, each
   attempt inside `async with asyncio.timeout(timeout)` (mirror `_session.py:234`),
   with bounded exponential backoff between attempts (`asyncio.sleep`).
2. Classify inside the loop: re-raise `ToolException` (isError/tool-domain) and
   `asyncio.CancelledError` immediately; `_unwrap_single(exc)` (REUSE from
   `_session.py:174`; extract to a shared `neograph_mcp/_transport.py` or import it)
   then test a NARROW transport allowlist (ConnectionError, TimeoutError,
   `mcp.shared.exceptions.McpError`, connect-time errors). Anything not transport
   surfaces immediately. A `ValidationError` from the output-model wrap is NOT in the
   allowlist and surfaces.
3. Idempotency + pre/post-send split: pre-send failures (connect refused/DNS/connect
   timeout) retry regardless of `idempotent`; ambiguous post-send failures (call-time
   `TimeoutError`, mid-flight reset) retry ONLY when `idempotent=True`, else surface.
   Mirror the resource-replay gate posture (`di.py:180`/`NonIdempotentReplayError`);
   conservative default is non-idempotent.
4. Compose the wrap OUTERMOST in `_make_tool_factory` (`_client.py:252`) — after
   identity injection, rename, and `_wrap_output_model` — so a retry re-runs the
   whole transport call while result/domain errors still propagate.
5. Thread new params: `timeout: float = 30.0` (parity with `mcp_session`),
   `max_attempts`/backoff knobs, and `idempotent: bool = False` on `mcp_tool_factory`
   (:352); on `mcp_tool_factories` (:295) add `idempotents: dict[str, bool] | None`
   and a per-tool timeout mirroring the existing `output_models`/`parses` dict shape.
   Consumer sets `idempotent` to match their `Tool(idempotent=)`.
6. NO core change: budget-once and the async-only invoke path are already satisfied
   (`_agent_cycle.py` records one logical call; retry inside the coroutine is
   invisible to `ToolBudgetTracker`). Only ASSERT this in tests.
7. Tests (battery tier, keyless, deterministic fake double — copy `test_mcp_battery.py`
   style; TDD the four acceptance cases FIRST):
   (a) flaky-transport fake (raises transport error N< max then succeeds) -> succeeds
   within the bound; (b) isError/`ToolException` fake -> surfaces on first return, no
   retry; (c) non-idempotent tool + ambiguous (timeout) failure -> not replayed,
   surfaces; idempotent tool + same -> retried; (d) assert `ToolBudgetTracker` counts
   the logical call exactly once across a retried-then-succeeded call.
8. Update `website/src/content/docs/concepts/retry-semantics.mdx`: document MCP-tool
   transport retry as the tool-path arm of Layer 1 (the factory now bounds each call
   and retries transport-only), preserving the "never retry isError / never replay a
   non-idempotent tool" rationale. NOT 0.6.0-gating.
notes:
## Findings

REUSE TARGET — the resilience wrapper lives in the BATTERY, not core. Add a new
`_with_transport_resilience(tool, *, timeout, max_attempts, idempotent)` coroutine
wrapper in `src/neograph_mcp/_client.py`, applied as the OUTERMOST wrap in
`_make_tool_factory` (after identity injection, rename, and `_wrap_output_model`).
This is the SAME wrap-the-`.coroutine`-via-`tool.model_copy(update={"coroutine":...})`
pattern already used TWICE in that file: `_inject_stdio_token` (_client.py:175) and
`_wrap_output_model` (_client.py:207). Do NOT invent a new mechanism — copy that shape.

WHY the battery, not `src/neograph`: `tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py`
scans `src/neograph` ONLY and bans `import mcp` / MCP client lifecycle there; core
must stay MCP-free. Separately, `tests/test_guards_function_local_imports.py`
(neograph-s5yk) enforces ZERO `retry_policy`/`RetryPolicy` references anywhere in
`src/neograph`. Both guards force transport-retry into `neograph_mcp`.

THE "single-responsibility retry" the task says to REUSE-not-fork is the three-layer
retry MODEL (doc `website/src/content/docs/concepts/retry-semantics.mdx`), NOT a
RetryPolicy class — that class was deliberately removed. This task adds the missing
piece of Layer 1 (transport) for the MCP-tool call path, which today has none. Frame
it in the doc's terms; do not resurrect `compile(retry_policy=)`.

CLASSIFICATION IS CLEAN BY CONSTRUCTION (the isError-never-retry guarantee):
- isError on the factory path raises `_MCPToolExecutionError`, a `ToolException`
  subclass (`langchain_mcp_adapters/tools.py:99`). With `handle_tool_errors=True`
  (the adapter default the battery preserves) langchain CATCHES it in `arun` and
  returns a normal error `ToolMessage` — so isError usually is not even an exception
  at our wrapper, and when it is, it is a `ToolException`.
- Transport failures are NOT `ToolException` subclasses — they propagate raw
  (ConnectionError, TimeoutError, `mcp.shared.exceptions.McpError`, anyio
  `ExceptionGroup`).
  => The wrapper catches a NARROW transport allowlist and re-raises `ToolException`
  (and CancelledError) immediately. isError/tool-domain/ValidationError are never
  retried because they are never in the allowlist. This is the anti-band-aid.

REUSE `_unwrap_single` (`src/neograph_mcp/_session.py:174`) to normalise the anyio
`ExceptionGroup` wrapping BEFORE classifying — it already handles the nested-group
cases (refused port -> ExceptionGroup(ConnectError); dead stdio ->
ExceptionGroup(ExceptionGroup(McpError))). It currently lives in `_session.py`;
extract to a shared spot (e.g. a small `neograph_mcp/_transport.py`) or import it
into `_client.py`. Do not re-implement group-unwrapping.

PER-CALL TIMEOUT PARITY: `mcp_session`/`McpSession` already bound each call with
`timeout=30.0` default (`_session.py:32,323-324` via `read_timeout_seconds`, and the
connect via `async with asyncio.timeout(self._timeout)` at `_session.py:234`). The
FACTORY path (`mcp_tool_factory`/`mcp_tool_factories`) passes NO timeout today, so a
bound tool inherits the adapter's 300s read timeout. Add a `timeout: float = 30.0`
factory param and enforce it by wrapping the coroutine in `async with
asyncio.timeout(timeout)` (mirror the session's connect line) — same default as the
session for parity.

BUDGET-ONCE IS FREE if the retry lives in the coroutine wrapper. The ReAct loop
calls the tool exactly once per logical call and records budget once:
`_agent_cycle.py` `_tool_call_precheck` -> `tracker.record_call` (sync path
`_record_tool_result` :450; async path pre-reserves at :668). A retry INSIDE the
wrapped `.coroutine` is invisible to `ToolBudgetTracker`, so the logical call counts
once automatically — no core change needed. Verify with an assertion, do not
re-plumb budgeting.

MCP TOOLS ARE ASYNC-ONLY: the adapter tool has no sync `.func`; the sync tools seam
raises via `_raise_sync_tool_async` (`_agent_cycle.py:365,638-639`). All MCP tool
execution goes through `_ainvoke_tool_timed` -> `tool_fn.ainvoke` -> `.coroutine`
(`_agent_cycle.py:454-461,670`). The wrapper only needs the async coroutine — which
is all `_client.py` ever wraps. No sync path to cover.

IDEMPOTENCY GATE precedent to mirror: the resource-replay path already refuses to
replay a non-idempotent producer — `di.py:180,209` gates on `producer_idempotent`,
raising `NonIdempotentReplayError` (`errors.py:288`); the flag originates on
`Tool.idempotent` (`tool.py:58`, conservative default False) and is read in core as
`idempotent_by_tool` (`_agent_cycle.py:533`). Apply the SAME conservative posture
here: an AMBIGUOUS post-send failure (read timeout / mid-flight reset — the call may
have partially executed) is retried ONLY when idempotent=True; a definitively
pre-send failure (connect refused / DNS / connect timeout) is safe to retry
regardless.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:175 `_inject_stdio_token` and :207 `_wrap_output_model` -- the exact coroutine-wrap pattern (`tool.model_copy(update={"coroutine": ...})`) to copy; :252 `_make_tool_factory` is where the new wrap is composed (outermost, after output_model); :295 `mcp_tool_factories` / :352 `mcp_tool_factory` get the new `timeout`/`idempotent`(+ dict form)/`max_attempts` params.
- src/neograph_mcp/_session.py:174 `_unwrap_single` -- REUSE for ExceptionGroup normalisation; :234 `asyncio.timeout(self._timeout)` and :323 `read_timeout_seconds` -- the timeout=30 parity precedent; :66 `McpToolCallError` -- the raw-session isError type (session path, not factory path).
- langchain_mcp_adapters/tools.py:99 `_MCPToolExecutionError(ToolException)` -- the isError type to EXCLUDE from retry.
- src/neograph/_agent_cycle.py:454 `_ainvoke_tool_timed` (single async invoke site), :450/:668 budget record-once, :533 `idempotent_by_tool`, :365/:638 sync-tool-async guard.
- website/src/content/docs/concepts/retry-semantics.mdx -- the three-layer model to align with (and update: MCP-tool transport retry is Layer 1 for the tool path).
- tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py + tests/test_guards_function_local_imports.py:356 -- the two guards forcing this into neograph_mcp.
- tests/test_mcp_battery.py -- battery test-harness style (fake tool double keeps the fast tier deterministic, keyless).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- WORKTREE COLLISION (from epic neograph-n34iy): this task overlaps sibling
  neograph-cnxlx (connection-reuse+reconnect) and neograph-32qtx (mcp test fakes) on
  `_client.py`/`_session.py`; the epic mandates a SEPARATE WORKTREE per child and
  sets execution order fakes(32qtx) -> reuse(cnxlx) -> resilience(uixi1). Expect to
  rebase onto their `_client.py` edits.
- The acceptance "flaky-transport fake tool" needs an async fake tool whose coroutine
  raises a transport error N times then succeeds. neograph-32qtx (MCP test fakes) is
  slated to land FIRST and may provide it; if not yet available, build a minimal
  langchain `StructuredTool`/`Tool` with a flaky `coroutine` directly in the test.
- Wrap ORDER matters: resilience must be OUTERMOST so a transport blip during the
  output-model call retries the whole transport call, but it must catch ONLY
  transport types so a `ValidationError` from `_wrap_output_model` (a result/domain
  error) surfaces, never retried.
- `asyncio.timeout` raises `TimeoutError` — treat as an AMBIGUOUS post-send failure
  (call may have executed): retry only if idempotent. Do not classify a call-time
  timeout as pre-send.
- Do NOT catch bare `BaseException`/`CancelledError` in the retry loop (the
  ReAct-loop cancellation path must propagate); catch the transport allowlist +
  re-raise `ToolException` first.
- NEEDS USER INPUT: the idempotent flag is ALREADY declared on the neograph

   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-btqzq`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>

   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.

       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-btqzq --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):

     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you

a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:

   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used

     remaining instance

   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).

       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>

   ```

     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash

```

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard

design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,

the structural counter-measure.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted

     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and

     structural tools over text grep when available:

       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.

       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.

     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

   found must appear:

design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-uw54v` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-uw54v/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-uw54v
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-uw54v)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-uw54v --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-uw54v --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-uw54v/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-uw54v codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-2plcl
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-2plcl` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-2plcl/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-2plcl
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-2plcl)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-2plcl --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-2plcl --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-2plcl/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-2plcl codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Cross-linking capstone: reference-anchor coverage guard — every autolinkable symbol has a rendered heading (turn silent-inert into loud-fail)
description:
CORE INVARIANT: for every symbol the remark-api plugin CAN autolink (present in api-manifest.json with an anchor, per the tiered-confidence rule), the rendered reference page MUST contain exactly one heading whose github-slugger slug == that anchor.

WHY (from Stage-C verification, 2026-07-10): today the plugin declines to emit a link when no matching heading exists (remark-api.mjs:161). That prevents dead anchors — but it ALSO means a prose reference to node/Node/tool/Tool (and any symbol whose reference section is not rendered) SILENTLY stays inert instead of linking. The cross-linking invariant is therefore 'satisfiable but not satisfied': nothing fails loud when a symbol's section is missing. This ticket flips silent-inert -> loud, making full prose->symbol cross-linking a permanent, drift-checked property.

SCOPE: once kec0k/cvjfm/uorb4 render the sections, add a guard (pytest over the parsed reference page + manifest, and/or an Astro-build assertion) that FAILS when any autolinkable manifest symbol lacks a rendered heading with slug==anchor.

ANTI-BAND-AID: do NOT satisfy the guard by hand-adding headings. The headings must be the manifest-generated ones from kec0k/cvjfm/uorb4 — the guard asserts GENERATION IS COMPLETE (every public symbol has a home), not that a human patched gaps. Scope the autolinkable set to the manifest symbols the plugin actually links (exclude the intentionally-inert bare lowercase tokens); enumerate any deliberate exclusions IN the guard with a reason (self-documenting, like the self-cleaning ignore file).

ACCEPTANCE:
- Guard fails if any autolinkable symbol lacks a slug==anchor heading; mutation-proven (delete one generated heading -> guard RED).
- node/Node/tool/Tool prose references emit RESOLVING links in website/dist/ (the four Stage-C collision symbols now link, verified in built HTML) — closes the exact gap the Stage-C verifier found.

## Implementation Plan
1. In tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py add a NEW class TestAutolinkCoverageCapstone (distinct from kec0k's TestReferenceSectionRendering, which it formalizes -- keep kec0k's guard, do not delete). REUSE _reference_heading_slugs + _HEADING_RE + gen.build_manifest().
2. Encode the plugin's SOFT predicate as two PROC-2 NAMED regexes mirroring remark-api.mjs:38-39: _RE_BARE_PASCAL = r'^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]+$', _RE_BARE_SNAKE = r'^[a-z][a-z0-9_]+$'. Add test_slip_bare_pascal / test_slip_bare_snake meta-tests (match Node/Oracle/compile/render_prompt; reject dotted, mixed underscore+upper, empty).

## Findings

### The plugin's EXACT autolinkable predicate (website/plugins/remark-api.mjs)
Two tiers, both gate the ACTUAL link emit on `headings.has(anchor)`:
- SOFT tier (remark-api.mjs:159-165): a BARE token whose name matches RE_BARE_PASCAL `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]+$` (:38) OR RE_BARE_SNAKE `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]+$` (:39), is an exact manifest name match, AND has a live heading -> autolinks; else stays inert (the decline-to-emit fall-through after :161, and :149 for HARD).
- HARD tier (:138-154): dotted `Type.member` for the 14 fielded owners -> links to the OWNER's anchor iff `headings.has(anchor)` (:145); :149 is the HARD silent-inert decline (resolved-but-undocumented).
- VERIFIED against committed manifest (74 symbols): EVERY manifest name matches one of the two bare regexes (the SOFT-inert-name set is EMPTY today). So the plugin's link-CAPABLE set = all 74 symbols; whether a link actually emits is gated purely by heading presence. The 4 collision anchors are node->node-function, Node->node-model, tool->tool-function, Tool->tool-model (kind-namespaced, rfl7b).

### The deliberate exclusions wqzel must ENUMERATE
1. exception-kind symbols (10: NeographError, ConstructError, CompileError, ConfigurationError, ExecutionError, NodeOutputError, NonIdempotentReplayError, PromptVarMissing, ResourceExpiredError, CheckpointSchemaError). All PascalCase => SOFT-linkable, BUT they render as uorb4's FENCED error-hierarchy tree with NO per-symbol heading (fence-skipped by the harvester), so prose refs to them intentionally stay inert. Reason to bake into the guard: 'owned by the fenced error tree (uorb4 DECISION 3), not per-symbol headings.'
2. 'intentionally-inert bare lowercase tokens' = manifest names matching NEITHER bare regex. EMPTY set today, but the guard must encode the regex predicate so a future non-matching name is correctly excluded (and ideally surfaced as 'publicly unlinkable').

### Does wqzel duplicate kec0k? -- OVERLAPS, but adds a DISTINCT layer
kec0k's TestReferenceSectionRendering::test_every_non_exception_anchor_has_exactly_one_matching_heading (tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py:768) ALREADY asserts every non-exception manifest anchor has exactly ONE slug==anchor heading.   (b) enumerate the exclusions IN the guard WITH reasons (self-documenting, anti-band-aid);

The Python suite (45) is green.

- website/plugins/remark-api.mjs:145,149,161 -- the heading-gate + the silent-inert decline sites wqzel flips to loud.
- tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py:680 _reference_heading_slugs + :76 _HEADING_RE -- REUSE the fence-aware harvester (already byte-mirrors the plugin); :707 _non_exception_symbols; gen.build_manifest() is the symbol source.

- The node harness is ALREADY RED (case f). Do NOT defer -- repair it in this task (Oracle now links; assert node/Node/tool/Tool resolving). Leaving it breaks website 'npm test'.
- PROC-2: the two mirrored regexes (RE_BARE_PASCAL/RE_BARE_SNAKE) are NEW named constants -> each needs a test_slip_* meta-test.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-wmmhc
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-wmmhc
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-wmmhc`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-wmmhc)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-wmmhc --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-wmmhc sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-wmmhc
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-wmmhc` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-wmmhc/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-wmmhc
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-wmmhc)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-wmmhc --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-wmmhc --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-wmmhc/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-wmmhc codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Typed MCP tool results on the agent path: output_model= on neograph_mcp factories
description:
## What
Add `output_model: type[BaseModel] | None = None` (+ `parse=`) to `mcp_tool_factory` / `mcp_tool_factories` (dict form `output_models=`). When declared, the factory wraps the discovered adapter tool so the TOOL RESULT IS the rehydrated Pydantic model: the adapter coroutine returns `(content, artifact)` under response_format='content_and_artifact'; take `artifact['structured_content']` (MCPToolArtifact is a TypedDict — use .get, not getattr), `output_model.model_validate` it (via `parse` if given), return the model, and reset response_format='content' on the copied tool. Mirrors `resource_reader(output_model=, parse=)` — same layer, same names.

## Why (user direction 2026-07-10 — THE primary deliverable of the MCP typed-results design, not an optional follow-up)
The agent-bound MCP path structurally DROPS structuredContent today: neograph's tool loop invokes with plain args (_agent_cycle.py:459) and langchain attaches the artifact only on the ToolCall->ToolMessage path. So typed_result is a raw content-block list, the next ReAct turn's ToolMessage gets str(list-of-dicts), and demos compensate with shortcuts (example 23's _parse_mcp_json). Per MCP spec 2025-06-18 the text block accompanying structuredContent is a BACKWARDS-COMPAT MIRROR — a structured-aware client must treat structuredContent as the single source of truth, not consume both. The framework mechanism already exists: _render_tool_result_for_llm (_tool_loop.py:50) renders Pydantic-model results via renderer/describe_value (BAML-style) into the ToolMessage — it just never receives a model on the MCP path. PROBED end-to-end 2026-07-10: wrapped crm_search -> ainvoke returns the model -> _render_tool_result_for_llm emits the typed block. ZERO core changes; src/neograph stays MCP-free (nmb2).

Full design: docs/design/mcp-session-api-2plcl-2026-07-10.md §4bis (rejected variants: core Tool spec output=, outputSchema-derived auto-models, raw-dict default — see doc).

## Semantics
- output_model declared + structuredContent present -> model (parse= hook optional); ValidationError propagates untouched.
- output_model declared + NO structuredContent -> typed error naming the tool and the server-annotation fix.
- isError=True -> adapter's existing error path, unchanged.
- No output_model -> behavior unchanged (content blocks); type channel is opt-in by declaration.
- Naming alignment battery-wide: `output_model=` on factory, factories, AND McpSession.call (supersedes the session design's earlier `output=`).

## Demos de-shortcut (same bead)
Example 23 beat 5: declare output_model on reader factories, DELETE _parse_mcp_json, assert model attributes. Example 25: gateway-renamed tool declares output_model. Demo server already emits structuredContent (crm_search returns CrmSearchResult — landed 2026-07-10).

## Verification — integration & E2E only
Integration (tests/test_mcp_battery.py, @requires_mcp): factory with output_model -> awaited tool ainvoke returns the model instance; missing-structuredContent (get_deal + output_model) -> typed error; ValidationError propagates. E2E: agent run via compile()+arun() — assert ToolInteraction.typed_result IS the model AND the ToolMessage content in message history is the describe_value rendering (not a JSON/repr of blocks). Examples harness green after 23/25 de-shortcut.

## Acceptance
- output_model= public on both factories (+ output_models dict form), documented; zero src/neograph changes; session-ownership guard green.
- Example 23 has no _parse_mcp_json; typed_result carries models.
- Website MCP pages updated (typed results section: structuredContent as source of truth, BAML rendering into the next turn).
design:
## Core Invariant
The MCP typed-result channel is opt-in-by-declaration and lives ENTIRELY in the neograph_mcp battery package: declaring output_model= makes the wrapped adapter tool return the rehydrated Pydantic model as the tool result, and every downstream mechanism (ToolInteraction.typed_result, _render_tool_result_for_llm BAML rendering) already handles a model with ZERO changes to src/neograph.

## Implementation Plan (refined per architect review neograph-8w6a9.4/.12)

1. EXTEND src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:_make_tool_factory with output_model: type[BaseModel]|None=None, parse: Callable[[dict],BaseModel]|None=None. At the END of the _factory closure (AFTER _inject_stdio_token :208-209 and rename :210-211, BEFORE return :212), when output_model is set, wrap:
     orig = tool.coroutine
     async def wrapped(**kw):
         content, artifact = await orig(**kw)   # isError RAISES here (see invariant) — propagates, NOT caught
         sc = artifact.get('structured_content') if artifact else None
         if sc is None:
             raise ValueError(\"MCP tool '<tool_name>' declared output_model=<Name> but the server returned no structuredContent — the server tool likely has a bare '-> dict'/'-> list' annotation; use '-> dict[str, Any]' or a Pydantic return type.\")
         return parse(sc) if parse else output_model.model_validate(sc)
     tool = tool.model_copy(update={'coroutine': wrapped, 'response_format': 'content'})
   Let ValidationError propagate untouched (it IS the type-mismatch signal).

   isError MECHANISM (corrected — the plan's earlier tuple-return rationale was WRONG): against langchain_mcp_adapters/tools.py:258-283, a SERVER isError=True does NOT return '(ToolMessage|Command, None)' — it RAISES _MCPToolExecutionError (ToolException subclass, raise :274) from inside orig(). The '(ToolMessage|Command, None)' returns at :260-265 fire ONLY for INTERCEPTOR-returned messages, which the battery NEVER wires. Therefore:
   - NO isError guard is needed: the ONLY None-artifact case the wrapper ever sees is a genuine missing-structuredContent (a bare -> dict/list server annotation). The interceptor ToolMessage/Command path is dead-for-battery (document this caveat in the wrapper; do not add a branch for it).
   - LOAD-BEARING INVARIANT (state it in the code comment): model_copy(update={coroutine, response_format:'content'}) PRESERVES handle_tool_errors (True), and the wrapper MUST let the _MCPToolExecutionError PROPAGATE — do NOT try/except-convert it. langchain's arun catches the ToolException via the preserved handle_tool_errors and surfaces it as a self-correcting error ToolMessage (the adapter-native path). A catch here would break that.

2. THREAD the params through the two public delegators: mcp_tool_factory gains output_model=/parse= (pass straight down). mcp_tool_factories gains output_models: dict[str,type[BaseModel]]|None and parses: dict[str,Callable]|None (keyed like the returned factory dict — namespaced/bare key), looked up per tool inside the build loop and passed to _make_tool_factory. Mirror resource_reader() docstrings (src/neograph/tool.py:336-361) for the new params.

3. NO new public symbol — output_model rides the already-exported mcp_tool_factory/mcp_tool_factories in neograph_mcp/__init__.__all__. No __init__ edit.

4. DE-SHORTCUT example 23: define client output models for BOTH readers.
   - crm_search client model: shape its 'hits' field as list[Deal] (the existing example Deal model) so 'search.typed_result.hits[0]' IS a Deal directly. This DROPS the old line 333 'deal = Deal(**hit)' (which would break — cannot ** a BaseModel once hits[0] is a model).
   - kb_lookup client model: a flat model declaring at least 'acting_as' (kb_lookup emits a FLAT structuredContent {topic,article,acting_as,bearer_identity}; Pydantic extra='ignore' default lets a narrower model validate).
   - Pass output_models={crm_search: ..., kb_lookup: ...} to mcp_tool_factories. DELETE _parse_mcp_json (:279-293). Rewrite :324 who-map to 'i.typed_result.acting_as' and :332 hit to 'search.typed_result.hits[0]' (already a Deal). Beat 5 becomes a true typed-results demo.

5. DE-SHORTCUT example 25: the gateway-renamed tool declares output_model on its mcp_tool_factory call; rewrite :193 'json.loads(call.typed_result[0][\"text\"])' to read 'call.typed_result.<field>' on the model.

6. TESTS in tests/test_mcp_battery.py (@requires_mcp, real _demo_stdio_server, mirror TestLazySingleToolFactory):
   (a) factory+output_model -> awaited tool.ainvoke returns the MODEL instance (isinstance BaseModel + field assert).
   (b) get_deal (-> list, no structuredContent) + output_model -> the typed ValueError (missing-structuredContent, names the tool + annotation fix).
   (c) a wrong-shape output_model -> Pydantic ValidationError propagates (not swallowed).
   (d) isError native path (NEW — named acceptance item, zero coverage today): a call the server errors (missing required arg or unknown tool) on a tool WITH output_model set surfaces the adapter-native ToolException / error ToolMessage — NOT the missing-structuredContent ValueError. Proves the wrapper lets the raise propagate and handle_tool_errors survives model_copy.
   (e) E2E via compile()+arun(): assert ToolInteraction.typed_result IS the model AND the ToolMessage content in message history is the describe_value rendering (not [{'type':'text'...).

7. GUARDS: run tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py (must stay green — zero src/neograph edits) and the battery import guard. Update website MCP pages (typed results section: structuredContent as single source of truth, BAML rendering into the next turn).

8. NOTE the session API (McpSession.call output_model=, design doc §4/§4bis) is a SIBLING bead (neograph-2plcl), NOT this one — do not implement _session.py here.
notes:
## Findings

REUSE TARGET (mirror it exactly): resource_reader() in src/neograph/tool.py:336-386. It is the existing typed-tool precedent — same layer, same param names (output_model=, parse=). It builds a StructuredTool(coroutine=..., func=None, response_format defaults content), and its returned model flows through ToolInteraction.typed_result unchanged. Copy its output_model/parse shape onto the battery factory.

WRAP POINT: src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:198-214 _make_tool_factory._factory — the single private builder BOTH public factories delegate to (mcp_tool_factory:295 and mcp_tool_factories:251 both call _make_tool_factory). Add output_model/parse params to _make_tool_factory and thread them from both public functions. The wrap goes at the END of _factory, AFTER identity injection (_inject_stdio_token, :208-209) and rename (:210-211), so it wraps whatever coroutine is current (injected or not).

ADAPTER CONTRACT (verified against installed langchain_mcp_adapters, tools.py, mcp 1.28.1):
- Discovered tool is a StructuredTool with response_format="content_and_artifact" (tools.py:533) and coroutine call_tool(runtime=None, **arguments) (tools.py:399-508) returning tuple (content, artifact).
- artifact is MCPToolArtifact | None, a TypedDict (tools.py:161-172) with ONE key structured_content. Use .get("structured_content") — NOT getattr (it is a plain dict at runtime).
- PROBED live against demo server: tool.ainvoke({...}) returns CONTENT-ONLY (list of blocks) — structuredContent is STRUCTURALLY DROPPED on the direct/agent path (this is the whole bug). tool.coroutine(**args) returns the 2-tuple; artifact["structured_content"] carries the payload.
- get_deal (annotated -> list) returns artifact=None — the fixture for the missing-structuredContent typed-error path.

WRAP MECHANISM (probed end-to-end, returns the model): capture orig = tool.coroutine; define async wrapped(**kw): content, artifact = await orig(**kw); sc = artifact.get("structured_content") if artifact else None; if sc is None: raise typed error naming tool + server-annotation fix; return (parse(sc) if parse else output_model.model_validate(sc)); then tool = tool.model_copy(update={"coroutine": wrapped, "response_format": "content"}). With response_format="content" a bare-model coroutine return makes ainvoke return the MODEL INSTANCE (verified: isinstance BaseModel).

DOWNSTREAM IS ZERO-CHANGE (already exists):
- _agent_cycle.py:429-436 (_build_tool_interaction) sets typed_result=result (the raw ainvoke return) and renders via _render_tool_result_for_llm.
- _tool_loop.py:50-63 _render_tool_result_for_llm: a BaseModel result renders via renderer or describe_value (BAML) into the ToolMessage; non-model falls back to str(). So a model result emits the typed block; the current MCP path hits the str(list-of-dicts) fallback.

PUBLIC FACADE: src/neograph_mcp/__init__.py:35-49 re-exports mcp_tool_factory/mcp_tool_factories via __all__. No new symbol needed (params added to existing functions); output_model is public by living on already-exported functions.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/tool.py:336-386 — resource_reader(): THE exemplar to mirror (output_model=, parse=, StructuredTool coroutine, typed_result flow).
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:183-214 — _make_tool_factory: the shared wrap point; add output_model/parse here.
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:262-302 — mcp_tool_factory: add output_model=, parse=; thread to _make_tool_factory.
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:217-259 — mcp_tool_factories: add output_models: dict[str,type[BaseModel]]|None (keyed like the returned dict) + parses dict; thread per tool.
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:153-173 — _inject_stdio_token: precedent for model_copy(update={"coroutine": ...}); the output_model wrap composes AFTER this.
- .venv/.../langchain_mcp_adapters/tools.py:161-172 (MCPToolArtifact TypedDict), :399-508 (call_tool coroutine), :528-534 (StructuredTool + response_format).
- src/neograph/_tool_loop.py:50-63 — _render_tool_result_for_llm (the BAML render that receives the model).
- src/neograph/_agent_cycle.py:417-437 — _build_tool_interaction (typed_result=result).
- examples/23_mcp_client_selective_binding.py:279-335 — _parse_mcp_json + its 3 call sites (:324, :332) to DELETE; crm_search bound via mcp_tool_factories namespace=False (:224-231).
- examples/25_mcp_single_tool_gateway.py:144-169 — gateway-renamed tool to grow output_model.
- examples/_mcp_demo_server.py:199-229 — CrmSearchResult{query, hits:list[DealHit], acting_as, bearer_identity}; kb_lookup:241 returns dict[str,Any] (also structured); get_deal:252 -> list (NO structuredContent, the error fixture).
- tests/test_mcp_battery.py:296-368 TestLazySingleToolFactory (@requires_mcp, _demo_stdio_server, real await; :308 zero-network pattern); :225-262 compile+lint+arun E2E asserting on typed_result/result.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- mcp_tool_factories de-shortcut ripple (example 23): the demo iterates ALL tool_log entries for who[tool]=acting_as. crm_search AND kb_lookup both need typed handling. crm_search -> CrmSearchResult (has acting_as). kb_lookup returns dict[str,Any] with acting_as -> needs its own client output_model (with acting_as field) OR the who-assert restructured. Implementer must define a kb_lookup client model, not just crm_search, to fully kill _parse_mcp_json.
- Ordering: output_model wrap MUST come after _inject_stdio_token + rename in _factory, so stdio token still injects (the wrapped coroutine calls the injected one).
- parse signature: resource_reader parse is Callable[[Any, str|None], BaseModel]. Here there is no mime; use Callable[[dict], BaseModel] (design §4bis:347). Do NOT blindly copy resource_readers 2-arg parse signature.
- isError=True must keep the adapters existing error path (handle_tool_errors default True returns a ToolMessage; content_and_artifact -> a ToolMessage, not a (content,artifact) tuple). When response_format is reset to content and isError produced a ToolMessage/list, artifact is None -> our sc-is-None branch would raise the missing-structuredContent error, MASKING the real tool error. GUARD: detect the error/ToolMessage case before treating None-artifact as a schema annotation miss (adapter returns (call_tool_result, None) for ToolMessage/Command per tools.py:258-265). Design says isError follows the adapter path unchanged — the wrapper must not swallow it into the generic ValueError.
- ValidationError from model_validate must propagate untouched (it IS the type-mismatch signal) — do not catch.
- three-surface parity is N/A: this is battery-package (neograph_mcp) config, not a core IR change; the guard tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py scans src/neograph only and must stay green (zero src/neograph edits).

Pattern: hand-parsing MCP structured tool results out of content-block text (`_parse_mcp_json`, `json.loads(...typed_result[0]["text"])`) instead of declaring `output_model=` and letting the typed channel carry the model. ## Architect Review (neograph-8w6a9.4, independent)

Gate: research:complete + codebase-scan:complete both present. Read the adapter source, resource_reader, _tool_loop/_agent_cycle, examples 23/25, demo server; PROBED FastMCP + a StructuredTool model_copy/error harness to verify claims empirically.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: The isError risk analysis is factually wrong about the adapter mechanism, and the stated 'isError path stays adapter-native' acceptance has NO test. Against tools.py:258-283, a SERVER isError=True does NOT yield '(ToolMessage|Command, None)' — it RAISES _MCPToolExecutionError (a ToolException subclass, class def :99, raise :274). The '(ToolMessage|Command, None)' return path (:260-265) fires ONLY for INTERCEPTOR-returned messages, which the battery never wires. Consequence: the planned guard is HARMLESS but guards the wrong case; masking of a real error CANNOT occur for server-isError because 'orig' raises before the sc-None check is reached. I proved end-to-end that the prescribed code is safe: model_copy(update={coroutine, response_format:'content'}) PRESERVES handle_tool_error (True), the success path returns the bare model (Out(x=1)), and a raised ToolException from orig propagates through the wrapper to the preserved handler (-> 'HANDLED:...'), never hitting sc-None. The plan should (a) correct the rationale (isError = raise, not tuple-return), (b) state the load-bearing invariant it currently omits — handle_tool_error must survive the model_copy AND the wrapper must let the raise propagate (do NOT try/except-convert it), and (c) add an explicit isError integration test locking the native path, since it is a named acceptance item. Risk if unrefined: an implementer trusting the wrong mental model writes an isError test asserting a tuple return (never happens) or over-engineers a catch that breaks the native self-correct path. Suggestion: refine steps 1 & 6 with the corrected mechanism + an isError test; specify what the ToolMessage/Command guard returns (or drop it as dead-for-battery, documenting the interceptor caveat).

- [LOW] Finding: example 23 de-shortcut under-specifies the hit rewrite. Line 333 is 'deal = Deal(**hit)' where hit currently comes from _parse_mcp_json(...)['hits'][0] (a dict). After migration 'search.typed_result.hits[0]' is a MODEL, so 'Deal(**hit)' breaks (can't ** a BaseModel). Suggestion: shape the client crm_search model's 'hits' field as list[Deal] so 'search.typed_result.hits[0]' IS a Deal directly (drop line 333), or use hit.model_dump().

- [LOW] Finding: guard action is under-specified — 'guard the isError/ToolMessage case first' does not say what the branch returns. Given it only reaches for the interceptor path, spell out the return (pass the ToolMessage through) or remove it. Cosmetic given the battery doesn't use interceptors.

VERIFIED CORRECT (verdict earned, not rubber-stamped):
- kb_lookup DOES emit structuredContent: probed outputSchema={additionalProperties:true,...} and structured={topic,article,acting_as,bearer_identity} as a FLAT dict (not wrapped). The ripple analysis is right — both readers need client models; a client model declaring acting_as validates (Pydantic extra='ignore' default). get_deal outputSchema=null -> genuine missing-structuredContent fixture (confirmed). crm_search emits the full CrmSearchResult shape.
- parse=Callable[[dict],BaseModel] (no mime) is correct — the structured payload is already a dict; do NOT copy resource_reader's 2-arg (content,mime) form.
- Wrap ordering correct: output_model wrap belongs after _inject_stdio_token(:208-209)+rename(:210-211), before return(:212); wrapped captures orig=tool.coroutine (already the identity-injected _with_identity), so token injection is preserved.
- response_format reset to 'content' is required (content_and_artifact expects a 2-tuple; wrapper returns a bare model) — probed: success ainvoke returns the model instance.
- Downstream zero-change confirmed: _render_tool_result_for_llm(:50-63) renders BaseModel via describe_value/renderer; _build_tool_interaction sets typed_result=result (:434). _ainvoke_tool_timed captures the raw ainvoke return (:459).
- Reuse is right: resource_reader for the output_model=/parse= param SHAPE, _inject_stdio_token for the model_copy WRAP mechanism — both cited, no closer exemplar, no reinvention.
- nmb2/layer discipline: battery-only (neograph_mcp/_client.py + examples + tests + website); zero src/neograph edits; session-ownership guard scope holds.
- Tests a-d are genuine, not echo chambers (E2E goes through compile()+arun() and inspects real message history for the describe_value block). Gap is only the missing isError test noted above.
- Session API (McpSession.call output_model=) correctly scoped OUT to sibling bead neograph-2plcl.

Overall: NEEDS_REFINEMENT
