notes:
## Findings

CRUX SETTLED — RECOMMEND FALLBACK (consistency test), NOT generate-partial.

- The site has ZERO codegen-into-.mdx precedent AND zero MDX partial-import precedent — confirmed. api.mdx is 100% hand-authored; the ONLY manifest machinery is (a) scripts/gen_api_manifest.py which EMITS website/src/data/api-manifest.json, and (b) website/plugins/remark-api.mjs which VALIDATES/AUTOLINKS backticked refs against it. Nothing writes .mdx. remark-api.mjs:14 states outright: 'neograph reference content stays hand-written until Stage C generates it from the manifest' — Part B (this task) is where that could happen, and the recommendation is to NOT introduce a rendering pipeline.

- The fenced-block requirement is already SATISFIED and load-bearing. remark-api.mjs setup() collects reference-page heading slugs but SKIPS fenced content (the `if (fence) continue;` loop, remark-api.mjs:76-79). So the error-hierarchy tree, being a plain ``` fence, emits NO headings/anchors. The 11 exception classes already carry manifest anchors as SYMBOLS (symbols[] entries, anchors = slug(name)); if the tree were re-rendered as headings the anchors would double-emit and github-slugger would append `-1`, breaking the manifest-owns-both-ends invariant that test_stage_c_reference.py pins. Keeping the tree fenced is therefore mandatory, and any 'generate a partial' path must reproduce a fence (Expressive Code), not headings — extra risk for zero anchor benefit.

- The manifest CANNOT reproduce the curated tree. exception_hierarchy[] carries only {name, parent, anchor, doc}. The live tree adds three curated things absent from (or divergent from) the manifest: (1) the '(ValueError)' base-class note on ConstructError; (2) em-dash short descriptions that are NOT the manifest 'doc' first-lines (e.g. tree says 'assembly-time validation failures'; manifest doc = 'Assembly-time validation errors during Construct creation.'); (3) a deliberate NON-alphabetical, lifecycle-phase sibling order (ConstructError, CompileError, ConfigurationError, ExecutionError at top; PromptVarMissing, StateMissingError, NodeOutputError, NonIdempotentReplayError, ResourceExpiredError under ExecutionError) that the prose at api.mdx:690 explicitly references ('while the graph is executing / assembly / compile / configuration'). The manifest ships entries ALPHABETICALLY sorted (gen_api_manifest.py:359 `sorted(..., key=lambda c: c.__name__)`). So a generator would need a hand-authored order+annotation sidecar anyway — reintroducing the very hand-authored content the generation was meant to remove, with no net win.

- Structure is a perfect match TODAY: manifest 11 entries == tree 11 classes, and parent-links agree. So a consistency test passes immediately and only guards against future drift.

## Relevant Code
- website/src/content/docs/reference/api.mdx:688-708 — the '### Error Hierarchy' section: prose (690, references the lifecycle order), the FENCED tree (692-704, the curated content), CheckpointSchemaError bold note (706), importable-list (708). This is the block to preserve verbatim.
- website/src/data/api-manifest.json exception_hierarchy[] — 11 parent-linked {name,parent,anchor,doc}; NeographError has parent=null; alphabetical.
- scripts/gen_api_manifest.py:351-373 _exception_hierarchy() — introspects neograph._errors, sorts by __name__, one entry per NeographError subclass, parent = first NeographError base. slug() at module scope gives anchors.
- website/plugins/remark-api.mjs:76-79 — the fence-skipping heading collector (proves fenced tree emits no anchors). remark-api.mjs:14-20 — 'hand-written until Stage C' + the accepted SOFT seam.
- tests/test_stage_c_reference.py — Stage C RED guard; Core Invariant 'heading slug == manifest anchor'; the reuse EXEMPLAR for reading the committed manifest (_load_committed_manifest) and for how anchors must stay unique/slug-stable.
- tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py:56-74 (_load_gen_api_manifest via importlib), :45-49 path constants, :229 test_every_symbol_anchor_is_slug_of_its_name — the file where a manifest-vs-doc consistency test BELONGS and the load/parse patterns to copy.
- website/ build gate: `cd website && npm run build` (Astro+Starlight, ~2s, remark-api runs in-build so a broken ref FAILS build); `npm test` runs the plugin's node:test suite.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- If ever regenerated: alphabetical manifest order would silently reorder the tree and DESYNC the prose at api.mdx:690 (which narrates the lifecycle order). The consistency test must assert STRUCTURE ONLY (name set + parent map), NOT order and NOT description text, or it will fight the curated content.
- The consistency test must parse the fence by INDENTATION (├──/└──/│ tree-glyphs) to recover parent nesting, then compare the derived parent-map to manifest parent-links. Strip the '(ValueError)' parenthetical and the em-dash tail before extracting each class name.
- Do NOT add headings for the 11 errors to 'fix' SOFT-autolink inertness — that reintroduces the double-emit the fence exists to avoid (test_stage_c_reference invariant). Error autolink inertness is the accepted Stage B/C seam.
- generate-partial risk if pursued anyway: introduces first-ever .mdx codegen + first-ever partial import to a live-deploy (Amplify-on-push) site; Expressive Code fence rendering of an imported partial is unverified; the curated sidecar makes it net-negative. Declined.
## Codebase Disease Scan (atom uqy66.19)
Pattern: hand-authored error-hierarchy STRUCTURE (class set + parent links) that can silently drift from api-manifest.json exception_hierarchy[] with no guard; plus the no-double-emit invariant (an exception class must NOT appear as a markdown heading, else its anchor is emitted twice).

- [LOW] Finding: step 5's no-double-emit check ('no class name appears as a markdown heading') does not specify exact-match vs substring. The invariant is slug(heading)==anchor double-emit, so the correct test is heading-text EQUALS a class name (exact/slug-equality), not 'contains'. This is acceptable — the guard's PURPOSE is to fire on tree edits and force re-verification — but note the fragility so it is a deliberate choice, not a surprise.

Structure-only assertion (name set + parent links, NOT order, NOT descriptions) is correctly targeted: it catches a new/removed/reparented exception while allowing the curated order+annotation divergence. Confirmed sound.

Overall: NEEDS_REFINEMENT

## Implementation Plan (refined)

title: Stage A precursor: enrich manifest lint_issue_kinds with severity/meaning + capture dynamically-constructed DI kinds
description:
Prerequisite for rfl7b's lint-kind reference section (design-doc Open Question #3, resolved: enrich-first). Today scripts/gen_api_manifest.py emits lint_issue_kinds as a bare list of ~10 NAME strings, and its AST-walk MISSES the dynamically-constructed DI kinds (from_input/from_config/from_input_model/from_config_model) that the docs document. The api.mdx lint table has 3 columns (Kind/Severity/Meaning) and its kind-set overlaps the manifest by only 3.

Scope:
1. Extend the manifest lint_issue_kinds entries from bare names to objects carrying {kind, severity, meaning} (or a parallel structure) sourced from the authoritative lint kind definitions in src/neograph/lint.py, so the Severity/Meaning columns are manifest-owned, not hand-authored.
2. Capture the DI kinds the current AST-walk misses (from_input/from_config + their _model forms) so the manifest kind-set is COMPLETE vs the docs.
3. Re-pin the Stage-A snapshot/freshness guard for the new shape.
Once done, rfl7b generates the lint-kind table from the enriched manifest (drift-checked) instead of hand-writing it. Until then, rfl7b keeps the lint section hand-written (excluded from Stage C rendering).
design:
## Core Invariant
The manifest's lint_issue_kinds set stays COMPLETE and zero-drift with what lint() actually emits: every kind emitted by src/neograph/lint.py (literal-emitted AND DI-variable-emitted) appears exactly once, and its severity follows the single canonical required->ERROR/WARN rule (__main__.py:199) -- no hand-authored kind list, severity, or meaning may silently diverge from the code.

## Implementation Plan
1. Add ONE authoritative registry constant to src/neograph/lint.py (e.g. LINT_KIND_META: dict[str, tuple[severity, meaning]] or a small frozen dataclass/list). It carries all 14 kinds with severity in {ERROR, WARN, WARN/ERROR, varies} and a one-line meaning. Source severity from the derivation in Findings (matches __main__.py:199 + the dual/varies cases the bool can't express); source meaning by MOVING the hand-authored strings out of api.mdx:540-548 into this registry (that is what makes Severity/Meaning 'manifest-owned'). This lives in lint.py because lint.py is the authoritative home for lint kinds (task scope 1).
2. In scripts/gen_api_manifest.py, EXTEND (do not replace) extract_lint_issue_kinds(): keep the AST walk to discover literal-emitted kinds, UNION in the 4 DI kinds from neograph.di.DI_TEMPLATE_KINDS (reuse the frozenset -> .value), then look up severity+meaning from the lint.py registry, and emit a list of {kind, severity, meaning} objects sorted by kind. Rename the fn if its list[str] contract changes (e.g. build_lint_issue_kinds()), update the module docstring at scripts line ~17.
3. Add a COMPLETENESS cross-check in the generator (or as a guard): (AST-literal kinds UNION DI kinds) == registry.keys(); raise loud on mismatch so adding a kind without a registry entry breaks regen. This preserves the zero-drift property the AST walk exists for.
4. Regenerate the snapshot: run scripts/gen_api_manifest.py (or its main()) to rewrite website/src/data/api-manifest.json with the 14-object enriched lint_issue_kinds (sort_keys=True/indent=2 already handled by _write_json).
5. Re-pin tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py: extend _KNOWN_LINT_KIND_FLOOR from 10 -> 14 (add the 4 DI kinds), update test_extracted_kinds_are_superset_of_known_floor to read kind from the object shape (item['kind']), and add an assertion that each entry carries non-empty severity+meaning and that severity is in the allowed set. Keep the superset/floor semantics (future kinds auto-picked-up). The TestApiManifestFreshness class already asserts committed==fresh-regen, so step 4 must be run before this passes.
6. Do NOT touch api.mdx in THIS task -- rfl7b (neograph-cvjfm) keeps the lint section hand-written and Stage-C-excluded until it consumes this enriched manifest. Removing the api.mdx table now would strand rfl7b; leave it, this task only makes the manifest the future source of truth.
7. Gates: uv run --extra dev pytest tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py, plus mypy on lint.py + the generator. No website build needed (api.mdx unchanged).
notes:
## Findings

REUSE TARGETS (do not reinvent):
- scripts/gen_api_manifest.py:374 extract_lint_issue_kinds() -- the existing AST walk. EXTEND it, keep it. It walks lint.py for ast.Call keywords kind=<str literal>. It captures the 10 LITERAL kinds but STRUCTURALLY CANNOT see the 4 DI kinds because they are emitted as kind=kind_str where kind_str=binding.kind.value (a variable, lint.py:77). That is exactly the 'AST-walk misses DI kinds' gap in the task.
- src/neograph/di.py:48 DIKind enum + di.py:77 DI_TEMPLATE_KINDS frozenset -- the AUTHORITATIVE source for the 4 missing DI kind strings: from_input/from_config/from_input_model/from_config_model (FROM_STATE and FROM_RESOURCE do NOT emit a from_* lint kind; FROM_RESOURCE surfaces as the literal resource_hydration_kind_unmatched). DI_TEMPLATE_KINDS lists exactly these 4 -- reuse it (or DIKind members) rather than hardcoding strings.
- Canonical severity rule ALREADY EXISTS: src/neograph/__main__.py:199 -- severity = 'ERROR' if issue.required else 'WARN'. This is the single mapping from LintIssue.required(bool) -> ERROR/WARN. Any manifest 'severity' must follow this same rule, not invent a parallel one.

COMPLETE KIND SET = 14 (10 literal + 4 DI). Per-kind severity derived from the required= at each LintIssue site:
- loop_condition_unregistered: required=True -> ERROR (lint.py:559)
- loop_condition_none_unsafe: emitted BOTH True (lint.py:579) and False (lint.py:599) -> WARN/ERROR (dual)
- resource_hydration_kind_unmatched: required=True -> ERROR (lint.py:253)
- template_placeholder_unresolvable: required=True -> ERROR (lint.py:473)
- template_placeholder_known_vars_only: required=False -> WARN (lint.py:512)
- template_var_requires_async_driver: required=False -> WARN (lint.py:492)
- tool_requires_async_driver: required=False -> WARN (lint.py:640,660)
- ask_human_in_mutating_node: required=False -> WARN (lint.py:734)
- act_mode_all_idempotent_tools: required=False -> WARN (lint.py:774)
- llm_kwargs_missing: no required= kwarg -> defaults False -> WARN (lint.py:302)
- from_input/from_config/from_input_model/from_config_model: required=binding.required (variable) -> 'varies'

MEANING has NO structured source in lint.py today -- it is hand-authored in website/src/content/docs/reference/api.mdx:540-548 (a 7-row Kind/Severity/Meaning table that overlaps the manifest's 10 by only 3, and marks DI severity as 'varies', loop_condition_none_unsafe as 'WARN/ERROR' -- matching the derivation above). To make Severity/Meaning 'manifest-owned not hand-authored' (task scope 1), the authoritative meaning must be ADDED to lint.py as a registry constant; there is nothing to merely extract.

## Relevant Code
- scripts/gen_api_manifest.py:374-407 -- extract_lint_issue_kinds() + build_manifest() 'lint_issue_kinds' key. The one place to change the emitted shape.
- src/neograph/lint.py:55 LintIssue dataclass (node_name/param/kind/message/required) -- required is the severity signal; there is no severity or meaning field.
- src/neograph/di.py:48,77 -- DIKind + DI_TEMPLATE_KINDS, the 4-DI-kind authoritative set.
- website/src/data/api-manifest.json:71 -- committed snapshot; lint_issue_kinds is currently a bare sorted list of 10 strings. Only consumer besides the generator is the guard test (grep confirms: no website plugin reads it; remark-api validates symbols only).
- tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py:79 _KNOWN_LINT_KIND_FLOOR (10-kind frozenset) + :369 test_extracted_kinds_are_superset_of_known_floor -- the Stage-A guard to re-pin. Floor is a SUPERSET assertion (kinds may be added). Must extend floor to 14 (add the 4 DI kinds) and assert the new object shape carries severity+meaning.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Dual-severity: loop_condition_none_unsafe is the ONLY kind emitted with both required=True and required=False. A pure AST-derived severity must MERGE both sites into 'WARN/ERROR', not pick one. Simpler to author severity in the registry (matches api.mdx already).
- 'varies' for DI kinds is a legitimate non-{ERROR,WARN} value (required is runtime binding.required). The schema/guard must allow severity in {ERROR, WARN, WARN/ERROR, varies}.
- Zero-drift is the whole point of the AST walk (guard docstring, ryn4h). If severity+meaning move to a static registry, add a completeness cross-check: (AST-literal kinds UNION DI kinds) MUST equal registry.keys(), fail loud on mismatch, so a new kind added without a registry entry (or vice-versa) breaks the build -- do NOT regress to a hand-list that silently drifts.
- Canonical-rule reuse: do not hardcode a second required->severity map in the generator; if deriving severity from code, reuse __main__.py:199's rule. Recommend authoring severity in the lint.py registry so it stays adjacent to meaning and to the dual/varies cases the boolean cannot express.
- JSON determinism: _write_json uses sort_keys=True + indent=2. Objects sort fine; emit the list sorted by 'kind' to keep the snapshot stable.
- rfl7b (neograph-cvjfm, blocked by this) will render the lint table from this enriched manifest. Shape must be self-describing enough to generate the 3-column table verbatim (kind/severity/meaning).
## Codebase Disease Scan (atom uqy66.3)
Pattern (SYNTACTIC/enumeration): hand-authored, parallel enumerations of the lint-kind set + severity + meaning that can DRIFT from lint()'s actual emissions (the fix codifies a single authoritative LINT_KIND_META registry in lint.py).
Scan commands: grep required->ERROR/WARN severity sites; grep lint-kind string enumerations across src/scripts/website/tests; grep 'Kind | Severity | Meaning' tables.
Total instances found: 6 loci (2 doc tables actively divergent).

| # | Locus | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | website/src/data/api-manifest.json lint_issue_kinds | 10 bare names, missing 4 DI kinds, no severity/meaning | MIGRATE | THIS task enriches to 14 {kind,severity,meaning} objects from the registry |
| 2 | src/neograph/lint.py kind-emission sites | 14 kinds emitted (10 literal + 4 DI-variable) | MIGRATE | fix ADDS LINT_KIND_META registry here as the authoritative severity+meaning source |

| 4 | concepts/lint.mdx:67 table | 10-kind hand-authored Kind/Sev/Meaning, DIVERGENT from api.mdx (7) & both incomplete vs 14 | DEFER -> neograph-7mr02 (filed) | 2nd table, not covered by any of the 6 tasks; render from manifest post-cvjfm |
| 5 | src/neograph/__main__.py:199 severity | 'ERROR' if required else 'WARN' | ALLOWLIST | single canonical runtime severity mapping (no parallel copy); the registry severity MUST follow this same rule |
| 6 | src/neograph/di.py:77 DI_TEMPLATE_KINDS | frozenset of the 4 DI kinds | ALLOWLIST | authoritative reuse target for step 2 (union into the walk) |

Test files (test_lint.py/test_template_lint.py/test_resource_hydration.py) reference kinds as behavioral assertions, not enumeration duplication -> ALLOWLIST (not disease).
DRIFT PROOF: api.mdx(7) vs lint.mdx(10) already diverge and BOTH are incomplete vs the true 14 -- exactly the drift this task's manifest-owned registry eliminates.
## Architect Review

Verified against code: lint.py emits exactly 10 literal kind= sites + 4 DI-variable kinds (kind_str=binding.kind.value, lint.py:77) = 14; DI_TEMPLATE_KINDS (di.py:77) holds exactly the 4 from_*; guard floor already contains all 10 literals; __main__.py:199 = 'ERROR' if required else 'WARN'; _write_json uses sort_keys+indent; sole lint_issue_kinds consumer besides the generator is the guard test (no website plugin reads it). Both doc tables (api.mdx:540 -> 'varies'/'WARN/ERROR'; lint.mdx:67 -> DI 'ERROR', none/unsafe 'ERROR/WARN') confirm the divergence the task kills. But the plan authors severity as static strings in LINT_KIND_META and the only cross-check (step 3) is KEY-SET equality (AST-literal UNION DI == registry.keys()). Nothing binds the stored severity to the actual required= at each emission site. For the 9 single-site literal kinds a future required=True->False flip (or vice-versa) changes runtime severity at __main__.py:199 while the registry string silently stays put -- reintroducing exactly the hand-authored-parallel-enumeration disease this task exists to kill, now for the severity column. Suggestion: extend the generator/guard to co-derive severity from each LintIssue(...) ast.Call that carries BOTH a literal kind= and a literal required= (they share the same Call node the walk already visits): assert registry[kind] == ('ERROR' if required else 'WARN'). loop_condition_none_unsafe appears at two sites with conflicting required -> merge to 'WARN/ERROR'; the 4 DI kinds have kind=variable so the literal walk skips them -> 'varies' authored in the registry is the sanctioned exception. This makes the severity clause of the Core Invariant actually enforced rather than merely correct-at-write-time.

- [LOW] Finding: Step 5 keeps the floor-test 'superset (future kinds auto-picked-up)' semantics, but once step 3's generator enforces registry.keys()==extracted, a NEW literal kind added to lint.py WITHOUT a registry entry now breaks regen (and thus TestApiManifestFreshness). Suggestion: update the floor-test docstring/comment at tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py:73-78,375 so it no longer claims kinds are picked up automatically with no other action -- a new kind now ALSO requires a LINT_KIND_META entry. Functional behavior is correct; only the comment misleads.

- [LOW] Finding: The meaning strings moved out of api.mdx:540 become canonical, and the registry adopts api.mdx's DI severity 'varies'. When 7mr02 later renders lint.mdx from this manifest, lint.mdx's DI rows flip ERROR->varies and meaning text changes. That is the correct value (DI severity is binding.required-dependent) and is 7mr02's scope, not this task's -- flagged only so the registry handoff notes the expected downstream content change.

Confirmed NON-issues: api.mdx untouched (step 6) correctly UNBLOCKS cvjfm rather than stranding it (cvjfm is blocked-by this task and renders from the enriched manifest); lint.mdx 2nd table correctly deferred to 7mr02; list-of-objects determinism is handled (explicit sort by 'kind' + sort_keys on dict keys); no reuse target reinvented.

## Triage (atom uqy66.5)
Verdict = NEEDS_REFINEMENT (1 MEDIUM, 2 LOW). Routed: created refine atom neograph-uqy66.52 (bind severity to required= at emission sites via ast.Call co-derivation + assert; sanctioned exceptions loop_condition_none_unsafe='WARN/ERROR' and 4 DI kinds='varies'; plus the floor-test docstring LOW). write-test (uqy66.6) now depends on uqy66.52. Refine adjusts approach using EXISTING research -- no re-research.
## Refinement (atom uqy66.52) -- plan adjustment per review MEDIUM
Amends Implementation Plan steps 3 & 5 (approach change, same research):
- STEP 3 (revised): the completeness cross-check is NOT just key-set equality. In scripts/gen_api_manifest.py's lint-kind extraction, for each LintIssue(...) ast.Call the walk visits that carries BOTH a literal kind= and a literal required=, CO-DERIVE severity = 'ERROR' if required else 'WARN' and ASSERT registry[kind] == that derived value (raise loud on mismatch). title: Fix 5 drifted doc snippets caught by Stage D snippet testing (neograph-3my4x)
description:

design:
## Root Cause
Five doc snippets drifted from the current API and were skip-masked to keep Stage D green. Each is an independent doc-local defect (wrong kwarg name / non-exported import / doc-local fake signature), not a single systemic API break.

## Fix Approach (doc-only, minimal per snippet)
1. lint.mdx: output= -> outputs= (all 3 occurrences for correctness; 2 are in skipped illustrative fragments). In the executable 'full lint workflow' block, build a self-contained 'pipeline' from summarize (e.g. construct_from_functions('lint-demo',[summarize]) or Construct) so the max_len from_config assertions hold; do NOT rely on the page-threaded 'flat' pipeline.
2. modifier-kwargs.mdx (loop_history): ARCHITECT DECISION REQUIRED. Option A (doc-only, in-scope): rewrite the executable snippet to use programmatic 'refine_node | Loop(history=True)' (or construct the Loop modifier), and reframe prose so loop_history is presented as a Loop-modifier feature, not a @node kwarg. Option B (out-of-nominal-scope but parity-correct, ~3 lines): add loop_history param to decorator and pass history= into the Loop(**loop_kwargs) build at decorators.py:629. Prefer whichever the architect blesses; default to A since the bead is scoped doc-only.
3. api.mdx: remove RenderedInput and build_rendered_input from the 'from neograph import (...)' example (internal, not exported); keep ExcludeFromOutput.
4. oracle-ensemble.mdx: drop merge_model="reason" from the @node(...) call (no such kwarg).
5. produce-and-gather.mdx: change FakeSearchTool.invoke(self, args) -> invoke(self, args, config=None) to match framework tool-invocation (_agent_cycle.py:637 payload.invoke(args, config=config)).

Fixes change DOCS (and doc-local fakes) to match the API, never the reverse (unless the architect elects Option B parity-wiring for loop_history).

title: Sweep verification for 3my4x
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on 3my4x
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" 3my4x`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (3my4x)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update 3my4x --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add 3my4x sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Sweep verification for rfl7b
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on rfl7b
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" rfl7b`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (rfl7b)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).

     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update rfl7b --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add rfl7b sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for 3my4x
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show 3my4x` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/3my4x/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" 3my4x
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update 3my4x --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash

   ```

title: Sweep verification for ryn4h
description:

a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" ryn4h`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (ryn4h)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update ryn4h --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):

     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash

```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.

title: Runtime graph hot-swap: emit Agent Spec -> validate -> recompile -> durable resume
description:
Cite docs/design/agent-spec-interop-2026-07-09.md s1a (motivating use case). Demonstrate + provide a thin API for the payoff: a running agent whose graph is re-emitted as Agent Spec at runtime, recompiled, and resumed durably.

TIER 1 (no recompile): known path-set -> one compiled superset graph; LLM/router picks path via Command(goto)/Send/conditional edges. Durable + streaming intact. Agent Spec serializes superset + routing.

TIER 2 (recompile + resume): novel shape -> from_agent_spec -> compile-time VALIDATE (fail before execution -- the safety rail for machine-authored graphs) -> recompile -> resume same thread_id. LEVERAGES EXISTING checkpoint auto-rewind (_auto_resume_from_divergence): changed schema fingerprint re-runs only invalidated nodes, reuses checkpointed state. Do NOT rebuild rewind -- compose it.

DELIVERABLES: thin hot-swap helper (recompile-from-new-Agent-Spec on same thread_id + resume), an example, and a test proving (a) emitted-graph validation rejects a bad spec BEFORE any node runs, (b) resume after topology change re-runs only changed nodes. Depends on from_agent_spec import (neograph-01i0g); pairs with docs/example child (neograph-e3b4j).
design:
## Core Invariant
Tier-2 hot-swap must COMPOSE the existing seam -- route the new topology through from_agent_spec -> Construct.__init__(_validate_node_chain) -> compile(same checkpointer) -> run(same thread_id, auto_resume=True) so that (1) a machine-authored spec is type-channel-validated and fails BEFORE any node executes, and (2) the already-wired _auto_resume_from_divergence re-runs only fingerprint-invalidated nodes -- NEVER re-implement rewind, fingerprinting, or validation inside the hot-swap helper.

## Implementation Plan
1. THIN HELPER (compose, don't build). Add a new advisory-underscore module src/neograph/_hot_swap.py exporting one public free function (e.g. hot_swap or resume_from_agent_spec), wired through neograph/__init__.__all__ (public contract per CLAUDE.md naming policy). Body is ~3 lines: construct = from_agent_spec(flow); graph = compile(construct, checkpointer=checkpointer, **runtime_kwargs); return run(graph, config=config, auto_resume=True). Thread llm_factory/prompt_compiler/renderer kwargs through for LLM-mode nodes; add an arun/astream twin for parity. NO rewind/validation logic inside -- it is pure orchestration over loader+compiler+runner. Chosen module home avoids the loader->compiler->runner import cycle that putting it in loader.py would create (mirrors how _agent_spec.py sits beside loader.py).
2. EXAMPLE. Clone examples/19_checkpoint_auto_resume.py's all-scripted @node + MemorySaver + same-thread_id shape into a new examples/NN_hot_swap_agent_spec.py, but source the v2 pipeline via to_agent_spec(construct_v2) -> Flow -> from_agent_spec(Flow) (the round-trip), then hand it to the helper. The 'topology change' must change a node OUTPUT TYPE (add a field, exactly like AnalysisV1->V2) so the schema fingerprint actually diverges and rewind fires. Docstring must state the scope bound: think/scripted(+modifier) only; agent/act-mesh hot-swap awaits aa5gq (AgentNode import). Register it in tests/test_example_*.py if that harness auto-discovers examples.
3. TEST -- two proofs (new tests/test_hot_swap_agent_spec.py; reuse tests/fakes.py build_test_compile_kwargs/register_scripted). (a) VALIDATION-BEFORE-EXECUTION: build a deliberately type-mismatched emitted Flow (or a Construct whose fan-in types clash), give each node a body that appends to a module-level sentinel list; assert from_agent_spec(...)/compile(...) raises ConstructError/ConfigurationError/CompileError AND the sentinel list is empty (no node ran). (b) SELECTIVE RE-RUN AFTER TOPOLOGY CHANGE: copy tests/test_checkpoint_auto_rewind.py's per-node execution-counter style -- run v1 to checkpoint, hot-swap to a v2 whose changed node has a new output type, resume same thread_id via the helper, assert EXACTLY the changed node + its transitive downstream re-ran while untouched upstream did not, and the final result reflects the v2 schema.
4. THREE-SURFACE / FAIL-LOUD parity (cheap add-ons): assert the helper inherits the existing fail-loud contracts unchanged -- a hot-swap that leaves no rewind point raises CheckpointSchemaError(invalidated_nodes=...) (runner.py:346), and an AgentNode-bearing Flow fails loud on import today (honest bound documenting the aa5gq dependency). Do NOT add band-aids to paper over the AgentNode gap; fail loud is correct until aa5gq lands.
5. DOCS: cite docs/design/agent-spec-interop-2026-07-09.md s1a and docs/design/dynamic-handoff-research-2026-07-13.md (Tier-2 compose note) in the module + example docstrings; update website if a public helper symbol is added (CLAUDE.md website rule).
## Scope addendum (disease scan, 2026-07-23) — cite the in-graph gate exemplar
Disease scan confirmed all four seams (rewind=runner.py, fingerprint=state.py, spec-load=loader.py::from_agent_spec, in-graph reuse=factory.py) are SINGLE-SITED — zero duplication, no migration debt; mrb2y is a pure thin compose. Refinement: deliverable (a) 'validation rejects BEFORE any node runs' has a direct in-graph EXEMPLAR at factory.py:440-490 (make_portal_dispatch_fn._prepare): from_agent_spec(flow) -> Construct(...) validation raises ConstructError/ConfigurationError/ValidationError at factory.py:479-490 BEFORE compiled.invoke. mrb2y's helper is the OUT-of-graph durable sibling of that path — compose the SAME from_agent_spec + Construct gate (do NOT wrap in ExecutionError; raise the gate error straight to the caller), then compile(checkpointer=...) + run(same thread_id, auto_resume=True). Cite factory.py:440-490 in the helper docstring as the in-graph analog so the two stay a single discipline, never a fork. title: Tool/MCP mapping: Tool/MCPTool <-> neograph tool surface (name-only; runtime binding)
description:
Cite docs/design/agent-spec-interop-2026-07-09.md s7, s8. Serialize/deserialize tool references between neograph and Agent Spec. Spec carries tool NAME + budget/config only; the concrete tool binds at compile time via factory (mcp_tool_factory in src/neograph_mcp/_client.py; tool_factories dict passed to compile()). This mirrors Agent Spec's own name-vs-tool_registry split (WayFlow AgentSpecLoader(tool_registry=...)).

MAP: neograph Tool(name,budget,config) <-> Agent Spec Tool/ServerTool/MCPTool (name-only). Keep factory binding a RUNTIME concern out of the wire format. Strategic note (doc s8): this is the MCP typed-binding seam -- the defensible niche; do NOT try to own an MCP gateway as infra. Blocked by import + export tasks.
design:
## Core Invariant
Tool identity crossing the neograph <-> Agent Spec boundary is NAME-ONLY: the wire format may carry a tool's name, budget, config, and idempotent flag, but MUST NEVER embed a concrete callable/factory/bound-tool reference -- factory binding is exclusively a runtime, post-deserialization concern.

## Implementation Plan (REFINED 2026-07-22 per architect review)
1. Build the Tool->ServerTool+metadata mapping as a STANDALONE PURE HELPER, e.g. `_tool_to_server_tool(tool: Tool) -> ServerTool` in src/neograph/_agent_spec.py, with NO dependency on _make_server_tool (that function builds the ServerTool for a scripted/think node's OWN ToolNode.tool= field -- node-as-tool -- not an agent/act node's tools=[...] list). The new helper's output attaches to the AgentNode's tools= list, wired in by i3zsh.1's AgentNode lowering, not by _make_server_tool.
2. Use ServerTool for ALL neograph Tool exports (MCP-bound or not) -- commit explicitly, no further deliberation. pyagentspec==26.1.2 has no MCPTool class (confirmed via _import_agent_spec_flow_classes' own tools_mod); BuiltinTool(tool_type='mcp',...) would violate the name-only invariant by encoding MCP-ness into the wire format. metadata['neograph/tool_spec'] = {'budget':..., 'config':..., 'idempotent':...} carries the rest, mirroring ToolSpec's shape (_spec_schema.py:66). File a small follow-up doc-fix ticket for design-doc s2's landscape table (still says MCPTool) -- not blocking this task.
3. SPLIT delivery into two slices:
   (i) NOW-DOABLE export-only slice: the _tool_to_server_tool pure helper + an EXPORT-ONLY structural regression test asserting (a) no callable/bound-tool object appears in the serialized metadata dict, (b) json.dumps of just the {name, budget, config, idempotent} sub-dict succeeds. This slice is closeable today.
   (ii) DEFERRED import+round-trip slice: gated on neograph-01i0g landing (from_agent_spec import side). Do NOT gate this atom's closure on the full bidirectional round-trip -- only on slice (i).
4. The structural test's JSON-serializability assertion must be scoped NARROWLY to 'no callable/bound-tool key present', not a blanket json.dumps(full_metadata) -- Tool.config is dict[str, Any] and a user could legitimately put a non-JSON-serializable value there for reasons unrelated to the _bound_tool-leak invariant this test guards.
notes:
## Findings
- Blocked in practice: DEPENDS ON neograph-01i0g (from_agent_spec import) which is still OPEN. neograph-i3zsh (export) is closed, but its child neograph-i3zsh.1 (proper AgentNode+tools lowering for agent/act mode) is still OPEN — to_agent_spec currently FAILS LOUD on agent/act nodes (src/neograph/_agent_spec.py, commit 03dc849) rather than emit a lossy placeholder, so there is no agent/act Node.tools export path to map yet. This task (tool/MCP name-only mapping) can only be fully wired for scripted/think nodes today; agent/act tool export is gated on i3zsh.1 landing first.
- REUSE target 1 (the exact pattern to copy): `_resolve_tool` in src/neograph/loader.py:159 — normalizes `str | ToolSpec` -> `Tool` name-only, deferring factory binding entirely to compile()'s `tool_factories=` kwarg (see loader.py:159-170, ToolSpec at src/neograph/_spec_schema.py:66). It does NOT yet carry neograph's `Tool(name, budget, config, idempotent)` fields for agent/act tools=[...] — that's the gap this task fills, following the established `metadata['neograph/*_spec']` marker convention (see neograph/oracle_spec, neograph/each_spec, neograph/loop_spec, neograph/operator_spec at _agent_spec.py:241-401) for round-trip-losslessness of budget/config/idempotent.

So 'MCPTool' in the design doc's landscape table (s2) and MAP line (task description) does not correspond to a real class in the pinned SDK version — the closest fits are `ServerTool` (already used by _make_server_tool) or `BuiltinTool` (has `tool_type`/`configuration` which could carry an MCP marker). ## Risks & Edge Cases

This task's actual near-term scope is: (1) design + implement the Tool<->ServerTool+metadata mapping helper, (2) wire it into `_make_server_tool`/agent-mode lowering once i3zsh.1 unblocks it, (3) the corresponding import-side reader in `from_agent_spec`.

Any exporter helper must explicitly drop it, not rely on Pydantic's default serialization behavior (PrivateAttrs are excluded by default, but confirm rather than assume given `model_copy` preserves it in-process).
- NEEDS USER INPUT: MCPTool class absence in installed pyagentspec 26.1.2 (see Findings) — confirm mapping target (ServerTool+metadata vs BuiltinTool) before implementation.
## Codebase Disease Scan (l7gvy)

Pattern: a tool serialization/wire-format path that embeds a concrete callable/closure/bound-tool reference (e.g. Tool._bound_tool) instead of staying name-only (name/budget/config/idempotent), violating the neograph<->Agent Spec tool boundary this ticket's Core Invariant states.

| 2 | src/neograph/tool.py:95 (object.__setattr__(spec, "_bound_tool", base_tool)) | runtime binder | ALLOWLIST | sets the PrivateAttr at Tool.bind()-time; internal factory registration, never touches the exported wire format |
| 3 | src/neograph/tool.py:124-140 (register_bound_tool_factories) | runtime factory registration | ALLOWLIST | exactly the RUNTIME-side reuse target l7gvy's Core Invariant cites as precedent (loader.py::_resolve_tool's own split) -- consumed AFTER deserialization, not part of it |
| 4 | src/neograph/compiler.py:61,162 (register_bound_tool_factories call site) | compile-time wiring | ALLOWLIST | invoked during compile(), strictly after any Agent Spec import/export boundary; out of l7gvy's scope (wire format only) |
| 5 | src/neograph/lint.py:903,916 (getattr(spec, "_bound_tool", None)) | lint-time introspection | ALLOWLIST | lint() reads the private attr to warn about unregistered bound tools locally -- never serializes it, no Agent Spec involvement |
| 6 | src/neograph/node.py:177 (comment only, no code) | doc comment | ALLOWLIST | describes the same PrivateAttr mechanism, not a code instance |

The actual disease pattern (a callable leaking into a SERIALIZED tool representation) has zero existing instances -- because no neograph<->Agent Spec tool mapping exists yet (l7gvy is greenfield on both the export and import sides); the scan's purpose here is confirming there is no PRE-EXISTING leak this ticket would need to route around, and there is none.
## Architect Review

- [MEDIUM] Finding: Step 2 names the wrong wiring seam. `_make_server_tool` (_agent_spec.py:198-204) builds the SINGLE ServerTool that fills a scripted/think node's `ToolNode.tool=` field — i.e. the node itself lowered as a callable. Framing the Tool->ServerTool+metadata mapping as 'extend _make_server_tool' conflates node-as-tool with agent-tools-list and will send the implementer to the wrong call site. Suggestion: build the mapping as a standalone pure helper (e.g. _tool_to_server_tool(tool) -> ServerTool) with no dependency on _make_server_tool, and defer its attachment point to the AgentNode lowering (i3zsh.1). The 'or add a sibling helper' escape hatch is the correct path — make it the ONLY path and drop the _make_server_tool framing.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: The research tags 'NEEDS USER INPUT' twice over the MCPTool-class absence in pyagentspec 26.1.2, but the decision is already foreclosed by the ratified Core Invariant, not open. Name-only wire format + doc s8 'do not own the MCP gateway' mean MCP-ness must never be a wire-format distinction; option (c) BuiltinTool(tool_type='mcp', configuration=...) would itself VIOLATE the invariant by encoding MCP-ness into the serialized form, and option (b) 'wait for a newer SDK' blocks indefinitely. Only option (a) (ServerTool-for-all + metadata['neograph/tool_spec']) survives the invariant — this is the production pattern _make_server_tool already uses. Suggestion: commit the plan explicitly to (a), strike all 'MCPTool' language from the MAP line and design-doc s2 landscape table (note the doc correction as a follow-up), so the implementer does not stall on a non-decision.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: The atom's own hard dependency 01i0g (from_agent_spec import) is OPEN, so step 3 (import-side reader) and step 4's round-trip assertion (export -> import lossless) are not authorable-to-green now — the acceptance criterion 'bidirectional map' cannot be met in this atom. design:
## Core Invariant
`to_agent_spec()` is a free function that LOWERS the existing neograph IR (walked via `iter_with_arms`, typed via the already-bridged `spec_types.model_to_agent_spec_properties`) into flat Agent Spec primitives -- exactly the same lowering neograph already performs when compiling to LangGraph (Oracle fan-out/barrier, Each router/Send/barrier, Loop back-edge, Operator's single check-node-with-in-node-interrupt) -- and it must NEVER retarget or replace the high-level neograph `Spec`/modifier-aware IR to do so; every irreversible flattening (Oracle's flagship gap, Each's `over`/`on_error`, Loop's `when`/`max_iterations`, Operator's coercion) must be preserved losslessly via `neograph/`-prefixed `metadata` markers so the export remains BOTH a faithful flat Agent Spec (portable, ignorable markers) AND a lossless neograph round-trip source -- and it must fail loud (never silently downgrade or truncate) on any construct it cannot lower (raw_fn, skip_when/skip_value, Loop.when-as-callable, Oracle merge hooks, renderer, unresolvable _BranchNode, Portal handoff_param/handoff_channel, gate_tools_when-as-callable).

## Implementation Plan
1. Step 0 gate (mirrors nkjv9's step-0 pattern): `uv sync --extra dev --extra agent-spec` and write/run the metadata round-trip survival smoke test against real `pyagentspec` FIRST (ratification §6 residual item) -- confirms `Component.metadata` survives `to_dict -> from_dict` including disaggregation before trusting the Layer A/B marker strategy for anything beyond primitive-level export.
2. Add `src/neograph/_agent_spec.py` (free function, NOT a Construct/Node method -- per CLAUDE.md layer discipline and design doc §7). Copy `spec_types._import_agent_spec_property_classes()`'s function-local-import-guard shape for `pyagentspec.flows.nodes.*` / `pyagentspec.flows.flow.Flow` / `pyagentspec.flows.edges.*` / `pyagentspec.property` -- keep `src/neograph` core Agent-Spec-free by default.
3. `to_agent_spec(construct: Construct) -> Flow`: walk `iter_with_arms(construct)` (`_ir_branch.py`) as the top-level traversal (NOT `construct.iter_nodes`, which over-flattens and loses the Construct/_BranchNode boundaries needed to lower into `FlowNode`/`BranchingNode`). For each item: `Construct` -> `FlowNode` (nested Flow, recurse); `_BranchNode` -> `BranchingNode` (genuine sum-type, DIRECT per ratification); `Node` -> dispatch on `mode` (`think`->`LlmNode`, `agent`/`act`->`AgentNode`+tools, `scripted`/`raw`->`ToolNode`/`ApiNode`).
4. For every `Node.inputs`/`Node.outputs` (handle all three `TypeSpec` shapes: `None`, single type, dict/multi-output), call the ALREADY-BUILT `spec_types.model_to_agent_spec_properties(model)` to get `Property` lists -- do not hand-roll a second type walker. Emit `DataFlowEdge`s from the inferred `Node.inputs` dict (source_output -> destination_input) and `ControlFlowEdge`s from `Construct.nodes` order -- both explicit-from-implicit per the ratified structural mapping table.
5. Modifier lowering (read `_wiring.py`'s actual runtime sections for each before implementing, not just the design doc paraphrase):
   - `Oracle` -> `ParallelFlowNode` of N single-`LlmNode` flows (one `LlmConfig` per `Oracle.models` entry, or N copies if `models` is None) + merge `LlmNode` (`merge_prompt`) or `ToolNode` (`merge_fn`, name-only) + fan-out `ControlFlowEdge`s + fan-in `DataFlowEdge`s. Stamp `metadata["neograph/modifier"]="oracle"` + the full `OracleSpec` (incl. `models`, which has no primitive representation) + a `group_id` linking the N variant nodes + the merge node.
   - `Each` -> `MapNode`/`ParallelMapNode` wrapping an extracted sub-`Flow`; stamp `metadata["neograph/modifier"]="each"` + `EachSpec` (over/key/on_error).
   - `Loop` -> `BranchingNode({continue: back-edge, done: next})` + cyclic `ControlFlowEdge` + self `DataFlowEdge`; stamp `metadata["neograph/modifier"]="loop"` + `LoopSpec` (when/max_iterations/on_exhaust/history). Reject a callable `Loop.when` with a clear error (only registered-string conditions serialize) -- `Loop.when` IS typed `str | Callable` (modifiers.py:573), so this rejection branch is real and reachable.
   - `Operator` -> the FULLY PINNED composite (neograph-03djs): `BranchingNode(mapping={<condition-string>: PAUSE_BRANCH})` + `ControlFlowEdge(from_branch=PAUSE_BRANCH) -> InputMessageNode(outputs=[StringProperty(title='user_input')])` + `ControlFlowEdge(from_branch=DEFAULT_BRANCH) -> reconverge`. MUST implement the boolean-to-string-key coercion (render `should_pause` to the literal mapping-key string before the DataFlowEdge) -- this is a required correctness step, not an optional nicety; add a dedicated test asserting the PAUSE_BRANCH edge (not DEFAULT_BRANCH) is taken for a truthy condition. Treat dynamic `interrupt(should_pause)` payload vs static `InputMessageNode.message` as a documented-lossy edge case in metadata, never silently coerced. **CORRECTION (refine, neograph-vihe7.28): `Operator.when` is typed `str`-only (modifiers.py:543 -- 'registered condition function name') -- it CANNOT hold a callable, so a 'reject callable Operator.when' branch is unreachable dead code. Do NOT implement an Operator.when-callable reject; there is nothing to reject at this field. Only `Loop.when` (str | Callable) needs the callable-reject, per the corrected bullet above.**
6. Reject-or-placeholder callable-valued fields (doc s6): `raw_fn`, `skip_when`/`skip_value`, `renderer` -- raise a `ConfigurationError`-style error naming the field and node when encountered (mirrors existing `ConfigurationError.build(...)` usage elsewhere in the codebase, e.g. `modifiers.py`'s Oracle/Loop validators). `scripted_fn`/`merge_fn`/`Operator.when`(string)/`Loop.when`(string) are ALREADY name-only and serialize fine -- only genuinely-callable fields are the gap. **ADDED (refine, neograph-vihe7.28): two more genuinely-unrepresentable fields must be added to this reject set:**
   - **Portal `handoff_param`/`handoff_channel` (node.py:212/221)**: a node with either field set participates in runtime peer-to-peer `Command(goto)` mesh routing, which Agent Spec has NO combinator for (the ratification doc already rules peer-to-peer handoff/Swarm a GAP with import-REJECT, agent-spec-ratification-2026-07-13.md:45). Without an explicit reject, step 3's mode-dispatch would silently emit a plain `LlmNode`/`ToolNode` and DROP the mesh routing entirely -- a silent seam the Core Invariant forbids. Raise the same `ConfigurationError`-style error, naming the field + node, symmetric to the ratified Swarm import-reject.
   - **`gate_tools_when` (node.py:248, typed `Callable | str | None`)**: reject ONLY the `Callable` case (the `str` form name-serializes like `scripted_fn`/`operator.when` and needs no rejection). A callable `gate_tools_when` would otherwise serialize to nothing and silently vanish.
7. Layer B whole-pipeline embed: stash the original neograph `Spec` verbatim (if the construct was built via `load_spec`/has a recoverable Spec) into `Flow.metadata["neograph/source"]` for lossless re-import (per doc §6a). If no Spec is recoverable (e.g. construct built purely programmatically or via `@node`), this layer is best-effort/absent -- Layer A per-group markers remain the primary round-trip mechanism in that case.
8. Wire `to_agent_spec` through `neograph/__init__.py.__all__` (currently has zero Agent-Spec exports -- this is the first).
9. Tests: new `tests/test_agent_spec_export.py` following `tests/test_agent_spec_types.py`'s `pytest.importorskip("pyagentspec")` gating convention. Cover: structural DIRECT mappings, each modifier's LOWER composite (Oracle/Each/Loop/Operator, including the Operator coercion truthy-path test from step 5), reject-with-clear-error for each callable-valued field (raw_fn, skip_when/skip_value, renderer, Loop.when-callable, Oracle merge hooks, Portal handoff_param/handoff_channel, gate_tools_when-as-callable), `_BranchNode` -> `BranchingNode`, and the metadata-marker presence/shape for each modifier group. Round-trip proof itself (export -> import -> compile equivalence) is scoped to neograph-csdcl, downstream -- this task's tests assert export correctness and marker presence, not full round-trip equivalence.

## Refinement applied (neograph-vihe7.28, 2026-07-16)
Per architect review (neograph-vihe7.4, NEEDS_REFINEMENT): added explicit reject-with-error for Portal handoff_param/handoff_channel nodes (step 6) and gate_tools_when-as-callable (step 6); corrected step 5's Operator.when-callable reject as unreachable dead code (Operator.when is str-only) and clarified only Loop.when needs the callable-reject. Step 9's test list updated to cover the two newly-added reject cases.

## Findings
- Everything is ratified. i3zsh's own two blocking deps (swcy1 GATE, 03djs Operator-lowering verification, nkjv9 type-layer bridge) are all CLOSED. No further ratification/verification work remains before writing the exporter -- this is now a pure implementation task against a fully-specified target.
- **REUSE, do not reinvent, the type bridge**: `model_to_agent_spec_properties(model: type[BaseModel]) -> list[Property]` already exists in `src/neograph/spec_types.py:398`. It is the canonical Pydantic-model -> Agent Spec `Property` list converter (uses `model_json_schema()`, walks via `_annotation_to_property`, fails loud via `_no_repr_check` on tuple/Literal/Enum). `to_agent_spec()` MUST call this for every `Node.inputs`/`Node.outputs` type -- do NOT hand-roll a second schema walker.
- **REUSE the import-guard pattern**: `spec_types._import_agent_spec_property_classes()` (spec_types.py:225) is the canonical function-local-import-guard shape for the optional `[agent-spec]` extra (raises `ConfigurationError` with an `expected=`/`found=`/`hint=` triple pointing at `uv sync --extra agent-spec`). `_agent_spec.py` must copy this exact shape for importing `pyagentspec.flows.nodes.*` / `pyagentspec.flows.flow.Flow` / `pyagentspec.flows.edges.*` -- keeps `src/neograph` core Agent-Spec-free by default (mirrors the `mcp-examples` extra pattern, per `[project.optional-dependencies].agent-spec` in pyproject.toml).
- **REUSE the IR walk**: `iter_with_arms(construct)` (`src/neograph/_ir_branch.py:71`) is the single arm-aware top-level walk already used by compiler.py/runner.py/lint.py/tool.py -- expands `_BranchNode` sentinels into `true_arm_nodes`/`false_arm_nodes` in place, one level only (sub-Constructs stay opaque so the exporter's own recursion handles `FlowNode` nesting, exactly like the compiler's own lowering). Use this, NOT `construct.iter_nodes` (which flattens leaves and loses the Construct/_BranchNode boundary the exporter needs to lower into `FlowNode`/`BranchingNode`).
- **REUSE `compiler.py` as the "same lowering neograph already does" reference** (per design doc s5 framing: "same lowering neograph does when compiling to LangGraph"). `compiler.py` + `_wiring.py` are the ground truth for exactly how each modifier's runtime shape works (Oracle fan-out/barrier at `_wiring.py`'s Oracle section, Each router+Send+barrier, Loop back-edge, Operator's single check node + in-node `interrupt()` at `_wiring.py:1082-1103` `_add_operator_check`) -- read these sections when implementing each lowering branch so the Agent Spec shape matches actual runtime semantics, not the design doc's paraphrase.
- **Operator export target is FULLY PINNED (neograph-03djs, verified against real pyagentspec 26.1.2 source)**: `BranchingNode(mapping={<condition-string>: PAUSE_BRANCH})` + `ControlFlowEdge(from_branch=PAUSE_BRANCH) -> InputMessageNode(outputs=[StringProperty(title='user_input')])` + `ControlFlowEdge(from_branch=DEFAULT_BRANCH) -> reconverge`. Construction templates (no in-repo call site exists yet -- this task is the first): `pyagentspec/flows/nodes/inputmessagenode.py` docstring, `pyagentspec/flows/nodes/branchingnode.py` docstring. Mapping VALUE is a branch LABEL not a node name; `ControlFlowEdge.from_branch` selects on that label. EXPLICIT coercion obligation: neograph's `Operator.when` yields a Python truthy `should_pause`, which must be rendered to the exact string mapping-key (e.g. `"true"`) before the DataFlowEdge into BranchingNode, or the composite silently always takes DEFAULT_BRANCH (never pauses) -- this coercion must be implemented, not skipped.
- **Oracle export is THE flagship irreversible gap (by design, not a bug)**: no single Agent Spec node represents Oracle. Lower to `ParallelFlowNode` of N single-`LlmNode` flows (one LlmConfig per model/variant) + a merge `LlmNode` (merge_prompt) or `ToolNode` (merge_fn) + fan-out ControlFlowEdges + fan-in DataFlowEdges. `Oracle.models` (per-variant round-robin) has literally no Agent Spec representation -- must ride in the `neograph/modifier="oracle"` metadata marker (round-trip contract, see below) since there is no primitive-level substitute.
- **Each -> `MapNode`/`ParallelMapNode`** wrapping an extracted sub-`Flow` (router + Send + barrier is the runtime shape; `over` dotted path + `on_error` have no native representation -> ride in `EachSpec` metadata).
- **Loop -> `BranchingNode`(`{continue: back-edge, done: next}`)** + cyclic ControlFlowEdge + self DataFlowEdge. A bare BranchingNode+back-edge is ambiguous (loop vs branch) without the `neograph/modifier="loop"` marker.
- **Round-trip contract is ALREADY RATIFIED and now the DEFINING contract for i3zsh** (per the 2026-07-15 SCOPE ADD / UNIFICATION notes on i3zsh itself): emit `x-neograph`/`neograph/` metadata markers so export output == import input == Portal mode (b) runtime dispatch format. Two layers (doc s6a, `agent-spec-ratification-2026-07-13.md` §6): Layer A -- per-group markers (`metadata["neograph/modifier"]="oracle"/"each"/"loop"` + the modifier's own Spec dict (OracleSpec/EachSpec/LoopSpec) + a `group_id` linking the N variant nodes); Layer B -- whole-pipeline embed of the original neograph `Spec` verbatim in `Flow.metadata["neograph/source"]`. **CAVEAT (ratification §6 residual item, UNVERIFIED)**: the metadata round-trip survival test (does `Component.metadata` survive a full pyagentspec `to_dict -> from_dict` including disaggregation/reaggregation?) has NOT been proven by a test yet. This blocks trusting the LOSSLESS (marker-based) tier -- it does NOT block primitive-level export (export still runs and produces valid Agent Spec). First implementation step for i3zsh should assert this survives, or the marker strategy needs a different carrier (flag to whoever implements if it fails).
- **Callable-valued fields REJECT-OR-PLACEHOLDER (doc s6)**: `raw_fn`, `skip_when`/`skip_value`, `Loop.when`-as-callable, Oracle merge hooks (`merge_pre_process`/`merge_post_process`/`merge_fallback`), `renderer` -- these never serialize. Exporter must raise a clear `ConfigurationError`-style error (mirrors how `scripted_fn`/`merge_fn`/`operator.when` are ALREADY name-only, i.e. string-registered, so those three specifically DO serialize fine -- only genuinely-callable fields are the gap). A callable `Operator.when=` is a documented GAP annotation already added to `02-flows-nodes.md` by neograph-03djs.
- **`_BranchNode` sentinels** (from `ForwardConstruct`) appear in `Construct.nodes` -- `iter_with_arms` already expands these; the exporter's `_BranchNode` handling should lower to `BranchingNode` (genuine sum-type routing, ratified DIRECT mapping) using the SAME composite-construction helpers as the Loop/Operator BranchingNode paths, not a third bespoke branch-node builder.
- **Types must round-trip through `spec_types.py`'s registry**, already fully bridged (nkjv9, closed): `model_to_agent_spec_properties()` for export, `agent_spec_properties_to_types()` for import. i3zsh's ONLY job on the type axis is to CALL the export function per Node.inputs/outputs Pydantic type -- no new type-walking code.
- **Dependency**: `pyagentspec>=26.1.0,<27` behind `[agent-spec]` optional extra (pyproject.toml, already added by nkjv9). Depend on `pyagentspec.serialization`/`pyagentspec.flows.*`/`pyagentspec.property` only -- explicitly do NOT depend on `pyagentspec.adapters.langgraph` (neograph is its own compile target, not a consumer of that adapter).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- The metadata round-trip survival test (ratification §6, residual/unverified) should be written FIRST as a smoke test against the real installed `pyagentspec` package (mirrors nkjv9's step-0 gate) -- if `Component.metadata` does NOT survive a full serialize/deserialize round-trip including disaggregation, the Layer A/B marker strategy needs a different carrier before it's trusted for lossless round-trip (though primitive-level export is unaffected either way).
- Oracle's `models=` per-variant selection and `merge_pre_process`/`merge_post_process`/`merge_fallback` hooks have NO Agent Spec representation at all (not even via a workaround) -- these MUST ride entirely in metadata; a pure-primitive-level Agent Spec consumer loses this information entirely (expected/documented, not a defect).
- Operator's `interrupt(should_pause)` payload is dynamic (the condition's return value) vs `InputMessageNode.message` being a static/Jinja-templated string -- treat a dynamic-payload Operator as an explicit documented-lossy export edge case (flag in metadata), do NOT silently coerce/truncate to fit the static field.
- Boolean-to-string-key coercion for the Operator `BranchingNode.mapping` is REQUIRED, not optional -- omitting it produces a compiling-but-silently-wrong export (always bypasses the pause) which is exactly the class of silent-seam regression the project's North Star forbids. This must have its own explicit test (feed a truthy condition through and assert the PAUSE_BRANCH edge, not DEFAULT_BRANCH, is taken).
- `Node.inputs`/`Node.outputs` `TypeSpec` can be `None`, a single type, or a dict (multi-output). The exporter must handle all three shapes when calling `model_to_agent_spec_properties` -- a single-type node has no dict to iterate, and `None` means no declared boundary type (State-bus-implicit) which may need a fallback/skip.
- No fixture/test scaffolding for `to_agent_spec()` currently exists (greenfield) -- this task should ALSO add the `should_pass`/`should_fail`-style check fixtures per CLAUDE.md test conventions IF export-time validation errors are introduced (e.g. rejecting a `raw_fn` node), though the primary round-trip fixture work is scoped to neograph-csdcl (downstream task), not i3zsh itself.
