## Risks & Edge Cases
- **NEEDS USER INPUT: neograph_mcp import requires the 'mcp' extra.** The light CI suite is 'uv run --extra dev pytest' (no mcp); the mcp-gated tier is 'uv run --extra dev --extra mcp pytest'. Options: (a) manifest omits neograph_mcp section when extra missing + guard skipif's the neograph_mcp subsection -- means a neograph_mcp.__all__ drift ships unguarded on default CI; (b) commit the manifest regenerated WITH the extra always (require devs to run regen with --extra mcp) and guard the full manifest on default CI -- but then default-CI devs cannot regenerate without the extra; (c) split into api-manifest.json (core, always) + api-manifest-mcp.json (gated) with two guards. Recommend (c) -- cleanest separation, each guard is self-contained, default CI stays light. Decision needed before implementation.
- **JSON byte-stability.** MUST use json.dumps(..., indent=2, sort_keys=True) so dict iteration order does not churn the committed file. Verified insertion-order is stable in CPython, but sort_keys=True is the belt-and-braces guarantee; this is what test_pipeline_schema_in_sync effectively relies on via Spec.model_json_schema() (which is internally sorted).
- **Slugging fidelity vs the JS github-slugger.** Python identifier signatures are ASCII so the algorithm is trivial, BUT the contract Stages B/C depend on is "same slug as Starlight produces for the rendered heading" -- a snapshot test with hand-verified values from the actual 'github-slugger' npm package is the canonical reference. If a discrepancy surfaces later, Stage B's RAMP-style slug-the-real-headings is the safety net (mitigation, not excuse to skip the snapshot test).
- **Pydantic v2 model_fields introspection.** Node/Construct/Each/etc. are Pydantic v2 models -- use model.model_fields (the v2 API, returns dict[str, FieldInfo]); FieldInfo.annotation, .is_required(), .default. Do NOT use the deprecated __fields__ (v1). Each/Oracle carry configuration PrivateAttrs that should NOT appear in the manifest (they are runtime mechanics, not API). The manifest should also skip fields with field_info.exclude or the ExcludeFromOutput marker (reuse describe_type._is_output_excluded at line 56-58).
- **ForwardConstruct is a subclass of Construct** -- model_fields introspection will surface Construct's fields too. Decide: emit only fields declared on the class itself (model.model_fields with __fieldnames__ filter), or all inherited fields. Recommend: emit declared-on-this-class only, with a 'bases' list pointing at parent symbols (manifest consumer can resolve the chain). Avoids duplicating Construct's fields under ForwardConstruct's entry.
- **Lint kind extraction assumes kind=string-literal.** If lint.py ever uses kind=variable or kind=f-string, the AST-walk silently misses it. Pin with an assertion: len(extracted) >= 10 and cross-check against a hardcoded floor set in the guard test.
- **Staleness window (documented in the spec).** A direct push that skips CI ships a stale manifest. Mitigation already noted: Stage B remark plugin hard-fails on refs to symbols missing from the manifest, so drift surfaces at the next docs build regardless. No Stage-A action beyond documenting.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: The planned `render_annotation(annotation)` alias passes `hoisted=set()` to `_render_type`, which produces 40+-line INLINE EXPANSIONS of any referenced public model. title: Verifiable docs: compile-time-verified, auto-cross-linked documentation from library code (post-0.6)
description: Eliminate code<->docs drift STRUCTURALLY for the neograph website, porting the RAMP-Protocol mechanism (remark plugin over a machine-readable symbol inventory, fail-loud on high-confidence dangling refs, dead-anchor prevention, self-cleaning ignore file) with the source of truth changed from a proto descriptor to the Python package itself. Authoritative design: docs/design/verifiable-docs-research-2026-07-09.md (deep-research report, adversarially verified claims; sections 1-4 prior art, section 5 the staged plan). Four independently-shippable stages, each catching a drift class the previous cannot: A manifest+guard (any public-surface delta fails pytest), B remark validation (prose refs to dead/renamed symbols, dead anchors, zero page edits), C generated reference sections (signature/field-table drift), D snippet testing (snippets that resolve but no longer run). Key constraints pinned by the research: Amplify build image has no Python -> the bridge is a COMMITTED api-manifest.json with a pytest freshness guard (drift detection lives in the test suite, where the repo's guard culture already is); shape-detected backticked refs are the only incremental-adoption path for 45 existing pages, but REQUIRE tiered confidence (dotted refs may fail the build; bare tokens autolink-only, never fail) + the self-cleaning ignore file; anchor identity is the fragile seam until Stage C makes anchors manifest-owned. NOT 0.6.0-gating.
notes: 2026-07-09 POSITIONING RATIONALE (from the maintainer discussion after the research landed): the research scoreboard shows RAMP and Pydantic each automated only their DOMINANT drift class — RAMP verifies symbol references always-fail (nobody mainstream does) but never executes its examples; Pydantic lints/runs/output-asserts collected snippets (with --update-examples auto-repair) but verifies zero prose symbol mentions. neograph is BOTH things at once: a library people copy-paste from (Pydantic's risk, closed by Stage D) AND prose full of symbol talk (RAMP's risk, closed by Stage B). Stages B+D together with always-fail defaults would cover both drift classes — a combination the research found no existing project shipping. Always-fail is affordable here for the same reason the ~400 structural guards are: a sole maintainer owns 100 percent of the content, so strictness has no legacy-adoption cost (the reason every ecosystem tool defaults to warn).

title: Sweep verification for g2jg
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on g2jg
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" g2jg`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (g2jg)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update g2jg --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add g2jg sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for g2jg
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show g2jg` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/g2jg/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" g2jg
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (g2jg)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update g2jg --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update g2jg --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/g2jg/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add g2jg codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/g2jg/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Auto-rewind on a NON-COERCIBLE field-type change raises raw pydantic ValidationError before rewind (found during TQ-01 E2E)
description:
Surfaced by the neograph-oitm auto-rewind E2E. When a checkpointed pipeline is recompiled with an INCOMPATIBLE (non-coercible) output field-type change (e.g. int->str) and resumed on the same thread_id with auto_resume=True, the resume does NOT produce a clean CheckpointSchemaError. Instead a raw pydantic ValidationError is raised INSIDE the get_state_history() walk in _auto_resume_from_divergence, BEFORE the rewind decision runs: LangGraph materializes every historical snapshot into the CURRENT state schema, and the old tip's score=int fails str validation. Coercible changes (int->float) work correctly and are proven by the landed E2E.

Impact: the durability/auto-rewind pitch implies schema evolution on resume works generally; today only COERCIBLE evolution is clean. The 0.6.0 release notes must NOT claim arbitrary schema evolution on resume until this is handled (relates to neograph-y5ux release-notes framing and the neograph-oitm marketing precondition).

Disposition to design: detect the schema divergence and raise CheckpointSchemaError(invalidated_nodes=...) BEFORE walking get_state_history into the new schema (or wrap the history materialization so a per-snapshot validation failure is translated into the invalidated-node signal rather than bubbling raw). Add an E2E cell (sync+async) mirroring TQ-01 for the non-coercible case asserting the clean error. Discovered-from neograph-oitm.
close_reason: Non-coercible field-type change (int->str) on checkpoint resume now raises a clean CheckpointSchemaError(invalidated_nodes=...) before any node re-executes, instead of a raw pydantic ValidationError bubbling from the get_state_history re-materialization. Added _raise_incompatible_schema translator single-sited between sync/async rewind twins; wrapped both history walks. TDD: added sync+async non-coercible E2E cells (real file-backed Sqlite/AsyncSqlite savers) to tests/test_checkpoint_auto_rewind.py, verified red then green. Coercible int->float path unregressed.

title: PAT-02 fail-soft audit: silent degradation on durability/type-resolution paths under a fail-loud banner — bounded 6-site queue (review 080726_2107)
description:
From .claude/code-review/080726_2107/synthesis.md PAT-02 (fail-soft sub-scan ranked these; the ~15 legitimately-documented degrade paths — Oracle merge_fallback, Each on_error, Loop on_exhaust, progress-drop — are ALREADY separated out; this queue is bounded and every item is where silence hands back a WRONG result):

1. runner.py:451 _has_existing_checkpoint: checkpoint-read errors (AttributeError/TypeError/KeyError) -> return False -> 'no checkpoint' -> a fresh run SILENTLY IGNORING DURABLE STATE. The file's own docstring names the swallow. Durability-critical. Disposition: narrow the catch to the genuinely-expected absent-checkpoint shape; corrupt/unreadable checkpoint RAISES (ConfigurationError with the probe error chained). Keep the yc38 breadcrumb.
2. runner.py:396 _required_checkpointer_driver: source-introspection failure -> None -> the sync/async-mismatch guard's SOLE INPUT goes unknown -> an unrecognized saver silently bypasses the exact protection the guard exists for (also the agent-dev reviewer's sharpest LangGraph-leak: inspect.getsource on a saver to guess its driver). Disposition: on introspection failure, log.warning naming the saver class + the fact the mismatch guard is bypassed (raising is too strict — third-party savers are legitimate); ALSO evaluate replacing source-sniffing with capability probing (does the saver define aget_tuple/get_tuple natively — check method __qualname__ owner) which removes the leak entirely.
3. THE HIGHEST-VALUE SINGLE FIX — six near-identical sites: decorators.py:468/532/773, _di_classify.py:214, _sidecar.py:120, _validation_types.py:154 — except (NameError, AttributeError, TypeError): resolved = {} around typing.get_type_hints(). One unresolvable forward-ref silently discards hint resolution for EVERY parameter of that function, mis-classifying DI bindings/Node.inputs types that surface later as confusing downstream mismatches instead of 'could not resolve annotation X on function Y'. Directly undercuts if-it-compiles-it-runs. Disposition: extract ONE shared _resolve_hints helper (six copies is also a DRY hole) that catches per-annotation where feasible and raises ConstructError naming the function + the unresolvable annotation (fail at decoration/assembly, the right time); genuinely-optional paths (which of the six can legitimately proceed without hints?) get a documented per-site rationale.
4. _llm_render.py:50-94 inline missing var -> log.warning + BLANK TEXT to the model — documented + lint-gated, but this exact class shipped the agent-stark {domain} incident. Disposition: decide strict-by-default-with-optout vs keep (the template-ref path is now strict via PromptVarMissing — the asymmetry is the smell); written rationale either way.
5. _tool_loop.py:183 malformed tool args -> {} and :102-141 inner recovery failure -> AIMessage(content='') ('the model said nothing'). Disposition: the {} arm should surface a ToolMessage error to the LLM (it can retry) not silently empty-arg the tool; the empty-AIMessage arm needs a log.warning naming the recovery failure.

Each site gets: TDD repro of the silent path, the disposition applied, and the per-site rationale recorded in the ticket on close. Gates y5ux.
notes:
PAT-02 fail-soft audit — per-site dispositions (all TDD, repro-first).

SITE 1 — runner._has_existing_checkpoint + async twin _ahas_existing_checkpoint (runner.py)
Disposition: a checkpoint READ that raises (AttributeError/TypeError/KeyError) now RAISES ConfigurationError with the probe error chained, instead of returning False. Fixed BOTH sync and async twins for parity; kept the yc38 breadcrumb in the comment.
Rationale: an absent checkpoint returns None from get_tuple; a raise is genuine corruption/misconfig. Silently returning False started a FRESH run that ignored durable state — the durability pitch's worst false spot.
Tests: test_corrupt_checkpoint_read_raises_not_silent_fresh_run (+async twin); updated the pre-existing modes/test_execution.py::test_checkpoint_check_handles_broken_checkpointer -> ..._raises_on_broken_checkpointer.

SITE 2 — runner._required_checkpointer_driver (runner.py)
Disposition: on inspect.getsource failure, log.warning naming the saver class + that the sync/async mismatch guard is BYPASSED; still return None (do NOT raise — third-party savers are legitimate).
Capability-probing evaluated and REJECTED: LangGraph's sync SqliteSaver/PostgresSaver define their OWN aget_tuple stub (verified: qualname 'SqliteSaver.aget_tuple') that raises NotImplementedError, so a method-owner probe cannot distinguish a sync-only saver from a dual-capable one (InMemorySaver also owns aget_tuple). Reading the method source for the NotImplementedError raise is the only signal that separates the stub from a real async impl — source-sniffing stays.
Test: test_driver_introspection_failure_warns_that_guard_is_bypassed.

SITE 3 — the six get_type_hints copies (decorators.py x3, _di_classify.py, _sidecar.py, _validation_types.py)
Disposition: extracted ONE shared helper resolve_hints() into a NEW leaf module src/neograph/_hints.py (imports only typing + structlog — no neograph imports, so no import cycle; imported by all four caller modules). Behavior: try get_type_hints (fast path); on failure fall back to PER-ANNOTATION resolution so ONE unresolvable annotation no longer discards EVERY parameter's hint (the named defect). Resolvable siblings survive; unresolvable ones are omitted and logged at debug naming them. Six copies collapsed to one (DRY hole closed).
FAIL-LOUD-RAISE evaluated and REJECTED with a documented rationale: a blanket ConstructError on any unresolvable annotation breaks legitimate code. Under `from __future__ import annotations` every annotation is a string, and a non-DI Annotated marker or a locally-scoped type (e.g. Annotated[str, CustomMarker()] with a test-local CustomMarker) is unresolvable from the classifier's namespace yet perfectly valid — the param is simply wired by name as an upstream. Proven by the EXISTING tests decorator/test_di.py::test_non_di_annotated_marker_skipped and ::test_fallback_when_get_type_hints_raises, which a raise regressed. The audit's actual defect is the all-or-nothing DISCARD; per-annotation isolation removes it without penalising valid decorations.
Three-surface parity: unaffected. resolve_hints runs only on the @node/@merge_fn decorator paths; declarative Node(...) and programmatic Node()|Modifier() carry no FromInput/FromConfig bindings and no annotations to resolve here.
Tests: test_resolve_hints_isolates_one_bad_annotation_from_the_rest, test_resolve_hints_logs_the_omitted_annotation, test_resolve_hints_resolves_valid_annotations, test_node_with_non_di_annotated_marker_does_not_raise.

SITE 4 — _llm_render.py inline missing var
Disposition: KEEP AS-IS (log.warning + blank), no code change.
Rationale: this inline soft-fail is a DELIBERATE prior decision (neograph-9pcb chose warn-over-raise after 2 prod failures, pinned by test_inline_prompts.py::test_missing_key_returns_empty_with_warning) and is LINT-GATED at assembly time (the primary defense — catches the class before runtime). The agent-stark incident was specifically the template-ref DI {domain} vector, now closed by PromptVarMissing strictness + di_inputs. The inline/template-ref asymmetry is intentional: inline resolves via raw attribute access where optional nested attrs legitimately resolve to "" (test_nonexistent_dotted_attr_returns_empty), whereas template-ref ships an unresolved {domain} literal to the model. Making inline strict would break optional-nested-attr access AND contradict neograph-9pcb.

SITE 5 — _tool_loop.py
5a) Malformed tool args (the `tc["args"] = {}` fallback in _coerce_string_args_result): now emits log.warning naming the tool + the un-parseable payload before falling back to {} (the tool schema requires a dict). The full disposition (surface a retriable ToolMessage ERROR to the LLM) requires the ToolMessage-building path in _agent_cycle.py, which is OUT of this task's file scope — filed as a follow-up. The warning removes the silence. Test: test_malformed_tool_args_warns_not_silently_blanked.
5b) Empty-AIMessage recovery: unified BOTH the _generate-raised branch AND the coercion-produced-nothing branch through a new _empty_recovery_message(reason) helper that WARNS before returning AIMessage(""). Pre-audit only the raised branch logged; the produced-nothing branch shipped an empty "model said nothing" turn silently. Test: test_empty_recovery_message_warns_when_coercion_yields_nothing.

GATES (scoped — full suite not run per concurrent-edit instruction): mypy clean on all 7 changed src files; ruff clean on changed src + new test file; pytest 936 passed across all affected suites. Two UNRELATED failures in the shared working tree are concurrent edits by other agents to files OUTSIDE my scope (both show ` M` in git status, I did not touch them): modifiers.py function-local imports (test_guards_sidecar_imports) and an inline regex at test_guards_any_audit.py:598 (test_guards_meta).

New file: src/neograph/_hints.py. New test: tests/test_fail_soft_audit_7ymj.py.

Site1 corrupt-checkpoint read now raises ConfigurationError (sync+async twins); Site2 driver-introspection failure warns of guard bypass (capability-probe rejected, evidence recorded); Site3 six get_type_hints copies collapsed to one shared _hints.resolve_hints with per-annotation isolation (fail-loud-raise rejected — breaks legit __future__ non-DI markers); Site4 inline missing-var kept-as-is (neograph-9pcb decision + lint gate); Site5 malformed tool args + empty-AIMessage recovery now warn. New follow-up filed for the retriable-ToolMessage enhancement (out of file scope).

title: Four verified small correctness bugs: merge-hook error names wrong param; GraphBubbleUp swallowed in merge twins; sequential parallel tool calls; _notify_cost double-count (review 080726_2107)
description:
From .claude/code-review/080726_2107/synthesis.md, all four VERIFIED:
1. _validation_modifiers.py:185 — the merge-hook check reads param_names[variants_idx] (index 1 for merge_post_process) but the raised message interpolates param_names[0], pointing the user at the RESULT param where it means the VARIANTS param. One-line fix (bind variants_name once) + a test asserting the message names the right param for merge_post_process.
2. _oracle.py:287/361 — the two merge_prompt twins swallow GraphBubbleUp into merge_fallback where make_each_redirect_fn (:619) correctly re-raises it before the broad except. VERIFIED asymmetry: with a user merge_fallback set, a HITL-interrupt/cancellation bubbling through the merge LLM call is treated as a merge failure. Low blast radius today, latent the moment a merge hook can bubble. Add the same except GraphBubbleUp: raise guard to both twins (shared helper per twin-thinness) + a test with a bubbling fake.
3. _agent_cycle.py:604 — parallel tool calls in ONE ReAct turn are awaited sequentially in atools_body: latency n_tools x RTT where ~max(RTT) is achievable. Fix ASYNC TWIN ONLY (sync body stays sequential — no threads): asyncio.gather the per-call coros, record results in the original tool_call order (ToolMessage/ToolInteraction ordering is part of the message-history contract — pin it), preserve budget-tracker correctness under concurrency (the tracker mutates shared state — guard with the established lock pattern or pre-reserve budget before gathering). Latency, not correctness — but it is the difference between a demo agent and a production one on multi-tool turns.
4. _llm.py:178 _notify_cost — callback-arity detection via except TypeError RE-INVOKES the callback if the user's body raises TypeError for a real reason -> double-counted cost. The codebase already has _accepted_params signature introspection — use it once instead of catching. Test: a callback whose body raises TypeError must not be invoked twice.
Gates y5ux.

title: PAT-01 live guard bypasses: 4 verified holes — hasattr discrimination, from-neograph import form, _oracle_model key, allowlist reason strings (review 080726_2107)

title: TQ-01: auto-rewind END-TO-END proof — real pipeline, real checkpointer, schema mutation, assert exactly the invalidated nodes re-ran (review 080726_2107, the highest-leverage gap)
description:
From .claude/code-review/080726_2107/synthesis.md (TQ-01, Medium, VERIFIED: 0 execution-count assertions in any test_checkpoint*.py/test_resume*.py). THE FINDING, verbatim evidence: the headline auto-rewind feature is tested as three DISJOINT units (fingerprint diff; rewind-point selection via a hand-built _FakeGraph; persistence roundtrip). No test runs a real pipeline against a real checkpointer, mutates an output schema, resumes on the same thread_id, and asserts exactly the invalidated nodes re-ran. If _verify_checkpoint_schema stopped calling _auto_resume_from_divergence, ALL THREE units still pass. The agent-dev reviewer called auto-rewind the genuine novelty no other framework ships — and it is the one feature whose core seam is proven only by a fake.

DELIVERABLE: one E2E (sync + async cells) — build a 3+ node pipeline with per-node EXECUTION COUNTERS (scripted bodies incrementing a shared dict); run to completion on a real file-backed SqliteSaver/AsyncSqliteSaver with a thread_id; recompile with ONE node's output model structurally changed (same qualname, changed field — exercising the v63o _type_signature depth); run() again on the SAME thread_id with auto_resume=True; assert: (a) the changed node AND its transitive downstream re-ran (counters +1), (b) untouched upstream nodes did NOT re-run (counters unchanged), (c) the result reflects the new schema. Add the negative cell: auto_resume=False raises CheckpointSchemaError with the right invalidated_nodes. Also fold TQ-02 (Low): the check_fixtures CHECK_ERROR alternations are broad enough to match the wrong error in the right family — tighten the named fixtures' regexes while in the test area.

This test is also the marketing precondition: the release notes should lead with auto-rewind (agent-dev verdict) and may only do so with this proof landed. Gates y5ux.
notes:
TQ-01 DONE (tests/test_checkpoint_auto_rewind.py, class TestAutoRewindEndToEnd, sync+async+negative cells). Real 3-node scripted chain ingest->enrich->report, per-node execution counters, real file-backed SqliteSaver/AsyncSqliteSaver on tmp_path, fixed thread_id. v1 run to completion; recompile with enrich's output model structurally mutated (same __qualname__ _make_mid_model.<locals>._Enriched, score field int->float — exercises v63o _type_signature depth-fold: differing str(annotation) flips the per-node fingerprint); resume same thread_id. Asserts (a) enrich+report counters==2 (changed node + transitive downstream re-ran), (b) ingest counter==1 (untouched upstream did NOT re-run — catches over-rewind), (c) final report.summary=='score=2.0' (result reflects NEW schema, not stale tip). Seam-broken proof: if _auto_resume_from_divergence were a no-op, invoke(None) resumes from the completed tip, nothing re-runs -> counters stay {1,1,1} and summary stays 'score=1', so (a) and (c) both fail — empirically confirmed during dev (the incompatible int->str probe showed exactly {1,1,1}). Negative cell: auto_resume=False raises CheckpointSchemaError with invalidated_nodes=={'enrich','report'} and no counter ticks twice.

FINDING (latent gap, out of scope): auto-rewind with an INCOMPATIBLE field-type change (e.g. int->str) does NOT surface a clean CheckpointSchemaError — it raises a raw pydantic ValidationError inside _auto_resume_from_divergence's get_state_history walk (LangGraph materializes every historical snapshot into the CURRENT state schema; the pre-change tip's score=int fails str validation) BEFORE the rewind completes. Coercible changes (int->float) are fine. Worth a follow-up ticket if release notes promise arbitrary schema evolution.

TQ-02 DONE: tightened 50 should_fail CHECK_ERROR regexes from broad alternations (e.g. 'type.*compatible|no upstream produces', 'no field', 'not registered') to patterns anchored on each fixture's exact isolated error message (captured with conftest-equivalent registry cleanup to avoid cross-fixture merge_fn-collision pollution). Cross-check script: remaining regex overlaps reduced to only 4 inherent identical-message twin pairs (declarative vs programmatic forms of the same rule: each+loop, oracle+loop, sub_output TypeA, inputs=TypeB->TypeA) which legitimately share their intended error string. No pattern now matches a semantically wrong error.

Scoped gate (uv run --extra dev pytest tests/test_checkpoint_auto_rewind.py tests/test_check_fixtures.py): 90 passed, stress-verified 20/20 green after clearing pycache. NOTE for team lead: my ad-hoc debug scripts had imported fixture modules out-of-band and left stale check_fixtures __pycache__; that caused a transient 13-fail episode. Cleared it (find tests/check_fixtures -name __pycache__ -delete); suite deterministically green since. src/ NOT touched.

title: @merge_fn silently overwrites same-named functions + still on the global-dict registry @node moved off (review 080726 PAT-02)
description: From the 2026-07-08 review (verified Medium; decorators.py:763). Two defects, one root: (1) SILENT OVERWRITE — registering a second @merge_fn with the same function name silently replaces the first in _merge_fn_registry; two modules defining merge helpers with a common name (merge/combine) corrupt each other's Oracles with zero signal. FIX: fail loud on duplicate registration (ConstructError/ConfigurationError naming both definition sites), unless identical function object (idempotent re-import must stay safe — module reloads re-register). (2) REGISTRY PATTERN DEBT: @merge_fn remains on the module-global name-keyed dict while @node moved to the PrivateAttr sidecar and the 2026-05 architecture decisions made PER-COMPILE registries the norm (scripted/conditions/tool_factories all flow per-compile). AGENTS.md currently BLESSES the name-keyed pattern for string-referenced decorators — the review challenges that; the ticket owner evaluates migrating merge_fn resolution to the per-compile registry shape (Oracle references by string name -> resolve via compile-time lookup like conditions) and either migrates or documents WHY name-keyed-global stays (updating AGENTS.md either way so doc and decision agree). TDD the overwrite fail-loud first — that half is unambiguous. Gates y5ux.
notes:
DECISION (neograph-pbya defect #2, registry-pattern debt): DOCUMENT why the name-keyed global registry STAYS for @merge_fn — do NOT migrate to a per-compile / PrivateAttr-sidecar shape.

RATIONALE:
- The reason @node could move to a PrivateAttr sidecar is that @node RETURNS the Node it decorates — decoration site and storage target are the SAME object. @merge_fn is structurally different: it decorates a standalone function, returns the bare function (decorators.py: 'return f'), and that function is referenced from a DIFFERENT object (Oracle) purely by STRING NAME (Oracle(merge_fn='combine')). There is no Node/Oracle instance in scope at decoration time to hang a sidecar on — the two are wired later, by name. A name->metadata mapping is therefore a structurally-required symbol table, not incidental global state.
- Migrating to per-compile would NOT remove the global. Metadata is produced at import/decoration time and consumed at compile time; compile() would still need SOME import-time global to look the name up from (or the Oracle would need to carry resolved metadata, which it cannot because the Oracle does not exist when @merge_fn runs). This mirrors conditions/tool_factories, which the 2026-05 per-compile architecture STILL seeds from the decoration-time _runtime_registry fallback bridge. So @merge_fn's global is consistent with the actual current state of conditions/tool_factories — @node is the outlier precisely because it can self-store.
- The review's real correctness defect was the SILENT OVERWRITE, which is fully closed by the fail-loud collision guard (below). The 'process-global' concern does not by itself cause corruption once collisions fail loud.

RECOMMENDATION for the AGENTS.md-blessing agent (85nb): AGENTS.md's 'Known open DX items' note blessing the name-keyed pattern for string-referenced decorators STANDS and is now stronger — the blessing should cite the structural reason (decoration site decoupled from reference site by a string name = symbol table) plus the new fail-loud guard. No migration recommended.

FIX SHIPPED (defect #1, silent overwrite):
- decorators.py: on @merge_fn registration, a same-name collision between two DIFFERENT definition sites now raises ConstructError.build(...) naming BOTH sites (module.qualname + file:lineno). Idempotency preserved via _same_def_site(): same object, same code object (def re-run in a loop / hypothesis example -> new fn object, shared code object), or same source site+qualname (module reload recompiles code object but keeps file/line/name). Genuine cross-module collisions differ in filename/qualname/lineno -> raise.
- Added _qualname_site() and _same_def_site() module-level helpers in decorators.py.

TESTS (tests/decorator/test_di.py::TestMergeFnDuplicateRegistration):
- test_raises_when_two_different_functions_share_a_name
- test_raises_on_bare_name_collision_via_function_name
- test_reregistering_same_function_object_is_idempotent
- test_reexecuting_same_def_statement_is_idempotent (pins the loop/hypothesis code-object path)
- test_different_names_do_not_collide
TDD: the two raise-tests were confirmed RED before the guard, GREEN after.
close_reason: @merge_fn duplicate registration now fails loud (ConstructError naming both def sites), idempotent for same def-site/module reloads. Registry-debt: decided KEEP name-keyed global (structural symbol-table, unlike @node sidecar) + documented. TDD, 5 new tests.

title: Checkpoint auto-rewind can silently no-op — resume-from-tip skips invalidated nodes with no warning; per-node fingerprints too coarse (review 080726 PAT-03)
description:
From the 2026-07-08 full-tree review (.claude/code-review/080726_2001/synthesis.md, PAT-03 — VERIFIED by the reviewer; the highest-leverage fix: the durable/if-it-compiles-it-runs pitch is actively false on this path). TWO halves, one ticket:

(1) SILENT NO-OP: when schema fingerprints mismatch and _compute_invalidated_nodes returns a non-empty set, _auto_resume_from_divergence walks get_state_history for a snapshot whose .next intersects the invalidated set — and when NONE matches (runner.py:227-235 region), it no-ops WITHOUT WARNING and resumes from the tip, SKIPPING the changed nodes. A user trusting auto_resume gets stale results with no error. FIX (fail-loud house style): when invalidated is non-empty and no rewind point is found, do NOT silently resume — raise CheckpointSchemaError (with invalidated_nodes and a hint explaining why no rewind point exists: e.g. history pruned, nodes already past) OR at minimum log.warning auto_resume_no_rewind_point + document; the ticket owner decides raise-vs-warn WITH a written rationale, but silent is not an option. Both sync and async twins (the extracted _decide_checkpoint_schema/_auto_resume pair — keep extract-then-thin).

(2) FINGERPRINT COARSENESS compounds it: compute_node_fingerprints hashes only type.__qualname__ (state.py:373) — a field-level change to an output model with the same class name does not invalidate the node, so the rewind never even triggers. The richer annotation string is ALREADY COMPUTED for the schema fingerprint at state.py:415 — fold it into the per-node fingerprint. NOTE the migration consequence: existing checkpoints carry old-format node fingerprints; on first resume after upgrade every node looks changed — decide + document the behavior (probably correct-and-desired: one full re-run after upgrading) and pin it with a test.

TDD: failing repro first for the silent no-op (schema change + a history where no snapshot has the invalidated node in .next); regression for the coarse fingerprint (same class name, changed field type -> must invalidate). Cite the review synthesis. Gates y5ux.
notes:
v63o decisions (executor):

RAISE vs WARN -> RAISE. When auto_resume=True, the schema fingerprint mismatched, invalidated is non-empty, and NO checkpoint in get_state_history has an invalidated node pending in .next, we now raise CheckpointSchemaError(invalidated_nodes=...) via a single-sited _raise_no_rewind_point(NoReturn) shared by the sync (_auto_resume_from_divergence) and async (_aauto_resume_from_divergence) twins. Rationale: silently resuming from the tip returns stale results with no signal -- the one spot where the durable/if-it-compiles-it-runs pitch is actively false. A crash at resume-time (BEFORE any stale node body re-executes) with an actionable message (why: history pruned or all invalidated nodes already ran; how to recover: new thread_id or invalidate the checkpoint) is strictly better than silent staleness, and matches the existing auto_resume=False contract that hands the caller invalidated_nodes as a setup signal. Empty invalidated stays a genuine no-op (nothing changed) -- no raise.

FINGERPRINT COARSENESS -> structural signature folded into BOTH fingerprints. New state._type_signature(typ) replaces qualname-only hashing: a Pydantic model now hashes module.Qualname + sorted (field, str(annotation)) pairs (one level, cycle-safe, matching schema-fp depth); generics (list[X]/dict[K,V]/Each's dict[str,X]) are unwrapped so a field change on the wrapped model is visible. CRITICAL: this had to go into compute_schema_fingerprint too, not just compute_node_fingerprints. Verified empirically that str(annotation) on a same-qualname model with a changed field is IDENTICAL, so the schema fingerprint (the GATE: _decide_checkpoint_schema returns None on a match) would never open and the enriched node fingerprint would be dead code. Both now move in lockstep. (Also fixed a latent bug: the dict-form branch hashed type(typ).__name__ = the metaclass name, collapsing all dict-form outputs to the same hash.)

MIGRATION -> correct-and-desired, pinned. Both fingerprint FORMATS change, so existing pre-v63o checkpoints show a schema mismatch on first resume after upgrade -> every node looks changed -> one full re-run. Better than trusting a coarser stale signature. Pinned by test_old_format_node_fingerprint_invalidates_on_upgrade (stores a hand-computed old qualname-only fp and asserts the node is invalidated).

THREE-SURFACE PARITY: fingerprint computation is surface-agnostic -- compute_node_fingerprints/_type_signature walk construct.nodes reading .outputs/.name/.output, identical for @node, declarative, and programmatic. The regression tests use the programmatic Node.scripted surface; the observability contract tests exercise the declarative surface end-to-end through run(). No per-surface branch touched.
close_reason: Fail-loud on no-rewind-point (raises CheckpointSchemaError instead of silent tip-resume); per-node + schema fingerprints now fold structural _type_signature so same-qualname changed-field invalidates; also fixed latent dict-form metaclass-hash bug. TDD, 9 new tests.

title: FR: optional neograph[mcp] DX battery — ship the client-side stitching as a shipped, overridable helper (DefaultPromptCompiler precedent)
description:
## What
Ship an OPTIONAL, consumer-side MCP-client DX battery — a thin `neograph[mcp]` extra (outside the guarded `src/neograph` core) that turns a typed server config into the consumer-owned `tool_factories` + resource-fetcher that `compile()` already accepts. This GRADUATES the client-side stitching demonstrated by the MCP examples (neograph-g4q9/qb7q/3m6g) from copy-me-per-consumer boilerplate into a shipped, overridable helper — following the exact `PromptCompiler` Protocol + `DefaultPromptCompiler` seam-plus-battery precedent already in the codebase.

Sketch (names illustrative — the shape is the proposal, not the identifiers):

```python
# lives in the optional extra (e.g. src/neograph_mcp/ or neograph.contrib.mcp),
# NOT src/neograph — imports langchain-mcp-adapters, so the no-session-ownership
# guard (which scans src/neograph only) stays green, same exemption as mcp-examples.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StdioServer:
    command: str
    args: list[str]
    env: dict[str, str] | None = None

def mcp_tool_factories(
    servers: dict[str, StdioServer | HttpServer],
    *,
    token_provider: Callable[[dict], Awaitable[str] | str] | None = None,  # per-run identity (config["configurable"])
    namespace: bool = True,                                                # ADR §4.5 server::tool namespacing
) -> dict[str, ToolFactory]:
    """Build the {name: async factory} dict for compile(tool_factories=...).
    The MultiServerMCPClient / session is created and OWNED inside the returned
    factories (consumer-held) — never by neograph core. token_provider mints
    per-request auth (httpx.Auth) from config['configurable'] on the arun() path."""

def mcp_resource_fetcher(servers, *, token_provider=None):  # for FromResource(ref=/uri=)
    """Return the mcp_resource_fetcher (+ replayer) callables the consumer drops
    into config['configurable'] so FromResource hydration works out of the box."""
```

The consumer wires MCP in a handful of lines:

```python
factories = mcp_tool_factories({"crm": StdioServer(sys.executable, [".../server.py"])}, token_provider=exchange)
compiled = compile(construct, tool_factories={**graph_factories, **factories})
```

Use the default, or hand-roll your own factory — identical opt-in/override story as `DefaultPromptCompiler`.

## Why
The client-side stitching (MultiServerMCPClient + stdio/http transport config + the token-provider seam → a `tool_factory`) is genuinely consumer-side — g4q9's thesis is correct, it *needs* no framework code. But "needs no framework code" is not the same as "should be re-hand-rolled per consumer." It is IDENTICAL boilerplate across every adopter:
- agent-stark (ADR-0014) is the anticipated **second consumer** and is about to hand-roll exactly this in its `bridge.py::build_tool_factories`; ox-troubleshooting-demo is the first. That is two copies of the same MultiServerMCPClient/token-provider glue, drifting independently.
- The `DefaultPromptCompiler` precedent already settles the philosophy: a prompt compiler also "needs no framework code" (agent-stark in fact overrides it), yet neograph ships a `PromptCompiler` Protocol (seam) + `DefaultPromptCompiler` (battery) so adopters get DX out of the box and override only for house rules. The MCP client wiring is the same shape and deserves the same treatment.
- The examples (g4q9) already build the reference stitching + the `mcp-examples` extra. This FR asks: rather than have every consumer copy the example, expose that stitching as a supported helper the examples themselves consume (dogfood).

Net: a new adopter goes from "read the example, re-derive the MultiServerMCPClient + auth + namespacing glue" to "call `mcp_tool_factories(config)` and pass the result to `compile()`."

## Non-goals / invariant respect (this does NOT reopen nmb2)
- Does NOT move session lifecycle into core. The `MultiServerMCPClient`/`ClientSession` is created and disposed INSIDE the returned factory, which the CONSUMER holds — neograph core never creates/holds/disposes it. The latency + async-cancellation-cleanup surface the nmb2 verdict removed stays removed.
- `src/neograph` stays MCP-free; the battery lives in the optional extra (outside the guard's scan scope), exactly like the `mcp-examples` extra precedent. The no-session-ownership guard stays green.
- The seam is unchanged and already in core: `compile(tool_factories=...)`, the `Tool` spec, `resource_reader`, StructuredTool recognition. This adds only an optional, overridable default on top of that seam.

## Verification
- The g4q9 examples (23/24) are rewritten to CONSUME `mcp_tool_factories` / `mcp_resource_fetcher` instead of inlining the MultiServerMCPClient stitching — proving the helper covers the real selective-binding + FromResource + per-operator-identity + gated-mutation beats end-to-end against the real FastMCP demo server, offline.
- `test_guards_mcp_session_ownership` stays green (helper is in the extra, not `src/neograph`).
- A one-consumer smoke: bind one tool from a stdio server via the helper → compile passes, lint validates the binding, an arun() call succeeds, and swapping the factory for a recorded-real double keeps the fast tier deterministic.
- Extra-gated: `uv run` without the extra imports neograph core with zero MCP deps (skipif in the harness).

## Acceptance
- An optional extra ships `mcp_tool_factories(...)` (+ a resource-fetcher builder) returning consumer-owned factories for `compile(tool_factories=...)`, with a per-run `token_provider` seam and opt-in server::tool namespacing.
- The default is overridable (hand-rolled factory still works) — the `DefaultPromptCompiler` story.
- Examples g4q9/qb7q/3m6g consume the helper (dogfood); `src/neograph` MCP-free; no-session-ownership guard green.
- API shape signed off by the maintainer (this is an FR — the interface is the deliverable to agree first).

## Relationship / provenance
Raised by agent-stark (the ADR-0014 second consumer, task stark-63q.54 — external tool surface → MCP) after mapping the shipped MCP client + FromResource: the "no node rewrite" claim held, doublability held, but each consumer must build the MultiServerMCPClient adapter itself. Builds on / generalizes neograph-g4q9 (shared demo server + mcp-examples extra); would be consumed by the qb7q + 3m6g examples. Maintainer's call given the explicit "client-side stitching needs no framework code" thesis — this FR argues the DX/dedup case for an OPTIONAL battery that honors it.

title: _run_cache hardening: per-key single-flight + run-end eviction + the two concurrency pins (review PAT-03)
description: From the 2026-07-07 pre-release review (PAT-03; python-practices PP-01 re-scoped + PP-02 verified at source). _run_cache is sound for today's two consumers but unhardened as a shared primitive: (1) NO PER-KEY SINGLE-FLIGHT — get_or_build/aget_or_build lock only the map; two concurrent misses on one key (fan-over-agent branches under arun) both build: double LLM-handle build (waste) / double resource fetch (cost; correctness edge for non-idempotent fetchers). Fix: per-key in-flight latch minted under the map lock — sync threading.Lock-per-key, async asyncio.Lock-per-key (loop-affine: key the async latch map per loop or store latches in the same (run_id, subkey) namespace; do NOT share an asyncio.Lock across loops). (2) NO RUN-END EVICTION — bounded LRU only, so loop-bound MCP/LLM handles linger past their run until LRU pressure. Fix: evict the run's keys in the runner verbs' finally (the same finalize seam observe= flush uses — one hook, all four verbs; _prepare knows the run_id it minted). (3) The two Wave-8 unpinned properties land HERE as tests (moved from yc38): parallel-arun cross-run isolation (two concurrent aruns sharing a caller config -> factory call count == 2, no cross-contamination; GatedAsyncFake parking) and expiry-vs-cache (replay -> fresh run_id -> cache miss -> refetch, pinned with a two-run test; document no-mid-run-expiry-recheck by design). Twin-thinness applies to the single-flight twins.
close_reason: _run_cache hardening: per-key single-flight (sync threading.Lock / loop-affine asyncio.Lock minted under the map lock), evict_run() wired into all four runner verbs' finally, latch/eviction/loop-affinity + two Wave-8 arun pins added. Public get_or_build/aget_or_build signatures unchanged.

title: Error-hierarchy rule + re-parent ResourceExpiredError/NonIdempotentReplayError under ExecutionError + di.py raise-style migration + parentage guard (review PAT-01)
description:
From the 2026-07-07 pre-release review (synthesis: .claude/code-review/070726_prerelease_arc/synthesis.md, HIGH-01 live-verified). THE PATTERN: error types are parented ad hoc per ticket — PromptVarMissing subclasses ExecutionError while ResourceExpiredError and NonIdempotentReplayError (equally runtime failures raised during node execution) subclass bare NeographError, so a consumer's except ExecutionError around run() silently misses expiry/replay failures. This ships as public API at 0.6.0 — fix before release.

SCOPE: (1) write THE RULE into errors.py module docstring: failures raised during graph execution subclass ExecutionError; assembly-time -> ConstructError; configuration/setup -> ConfigurationError; compile -> CompileError. (2) Re-parent ResourceExpiredError + NonIdempotentReplayError under ExecutionError (0.x no-compat rule — no shims). (3) Decide-and-document the two PRE-EXISTING direct children: StateMissingError (runtime read miss -> likely re-parent) and CheckpointSchemaError (resume-time schema decision — arguably ConfigurationError-adjacent; the ticket owner decides WITH the rule, then documents the rationale in the class docstring either way). (4) CON-02: migrate di.py's legacy raw _ExecutionError(...) raises to the 4-field .build(hint=) style — one style, whole module. (5) GUARD: a parentage test pinning category->parent for every public error type, so the next new error cannot re-drift (table-driven; new types must be added to the table or the guard fails). title: Framework-minted per-run id: StateKeys.RUN_ID (_neo_run_id) minted in _prepare — fresh per attempt, stable within run, config-only
description:
The missing primitive that blocks neograph-m6d3.8 (within-run LLM handle reuse) and neograph-43do (per-run FROM_RESOURCE fetch cache). Design settled by adversarial architecture review 2026-07-07 (executed repros in session scratchpad; verdicts on the y5ux notes):

WHY NOTHING EXISTS TODAY (all verified): config carries no run identity (_prepare mints nothing in any of its three branches); thread_id fails BOTH soundness halves (absent without a checkpointer; REUSED across resume — keying a live-handle cache on it reuses stale handles across fresh-process resume, the exact two-lifetime violation). ENGINE-NATIVE ALTERNATIVES REFUTED BY REPRO: config['run_id'] (the LangSmith field) is None inside nodes; __pregel_task_id is per-SUPERSTEP (opposite of required); checkpoint_ns is per-node. Must mint our own.

THE DESIGN: StateKeys.RUN_ID = '_neo_run_id' in _state_keys.py following the documented _neo_ config-key convention (CONFIG_INPUT/STREAM_CUSTOM/DI_INPUTS docstrings are the template). Mint in _prepare AND _aprepare (the single pre-engine brains — minting in the verbs would fork the drivers), after config normalization, via a _mint_run_id(config) helper returning a FRESH dict (mirror _mark_stream_custom exactly — no caller-dict mutation, so parallel arun sharing a config dict each get their own). uuid4().hex.

TWO-LIFETIME BY CONSTRUCTION: config-only key -> never enters state -> cannot touch the schema fingerprint and never persists in checkpoints; resume calls _prepare again -> NEW id = invalidate-on-resume for free; _prepare runs once per execution -> stable across all supersteps within the run. Do NOT inject into the input dict (unlike fingerprints) and do NOT accept a user-supplied value (breaks fresh-per-attempt).

EXPOSE READ-ONLY to users via the existing DI-context path (node_id/project_root precedent) — natural structlog/trace correlation key; consider adding to node_start/llm_call log binds (cheap, high observability value).

TESTS (from the review): (1) present in-node; (2) stable across supersteps; (3) differs across two run() calls; (4) RE-MINTED ON RESUME — same thread_id, different run_id (THE two-lifetime assertion); (5) fresh-dict/no-mutation under parallel arun; (6) never in returned state/stream chunks/checkpoints. Twin guard: _prepare/_aprepare mint symmetrically. Size ~0.5-1d. Sub-constructs inherit the parent's id via config flow (correct — same run).
close_reason: Landed on develop (847e7b7): StateKeys.RUN_ID minted in _prepare/_aprepare via _mint_run_id (mirrors _mark_stream_custom), config-only, re-minted on resume, surfaced read-only via _execute node lifecycle log binds. 14 tests incl. two-lifetime resume w/ real Sqlite saver + twin guard.

title: json_mode: send provider-native response_format={"type":"json_object"} (or document provider_kwargs), don't rely on schema-in-prompt + text parse
description:
CONTEXT: output_strategy=\"json_mode\" currently (src/neograph/_llm.py:144, 188-189) injects the describe_type schema into the prompt and parses the model's raw TEXT via _parse_json_response, WITHOUT sending the provider's native JSON mode (response_format={\"type\":\"json_object\"}). Confirmed: `grep -rniE \"response_format\" src/neograph/` returns NOTHING. So json_mode reliability rests entirely on the model emitting clean-enough JSON in free text — a parse-failure surface.

EVIDENCE / IMPACT (from ox-troubleshooting-demo, gemini-2.5-pro via OpenRouter):
- We switched the reasoning verdict nodes (assess/synthesize/explain) to json_mode so the model can reason-then-coerce (vs 'structured' = provider constrained decoding, which skips the free reasoning pass).
- Under 'structured' we saw an intermittent 'structured output decoded to None' ExecutionError (the fail-loud in _llm_dispatch.py). Under json_mode the parse depends on the model's raw text being valid JSON.
- REFERENCE IMPL that works: ~/projects/piarch (deepseek/glm) binds `llm.bind(response_format={\"type\":\"json_object\"})` + max_tokens=16384 (scripts/run_eval.py:206-208; evals/_llm_factory.py). The provider's native JSON mode GUARANTEES valid JSON, removing the parse-failure class. For a THINKING model (gemini-2.5-pro, deepseek-reasoner) response_format=json_object does NOT cost the reasoning (thinking is internal / a separate reasoning field), so you keep BOTH reliable parse AND free reasoning.

PROPOSAL:
1. For providers that support it, json_mode should SEND response_format={\"type\":\"json_object\"} on the model call (OpenAI / Gemini / DeepSeek OpenAI-compat all support it). Note: OpenAI-compat json_object requires the word 'json' to appear in the prompt — the injected describe_type schema likely satisfies this; verify.
2. If not made automatic, DOCUMENT that json_mode users should pass response_format via LlmConfig.provider_kwargs, and note reasoning-inline behaviour for reasoning models.
3. Clarify the docstring (_llm.py:144) — it reads 'inject schema into prompt, LLM returns raw JSON, framework parses', which implies more guarantee than there is (nothing forces the model to return JSON).

EVIDENCE FILES: src/neograph/_llm.py:144,188-189; src/neograph/_llm_dispatch.py (parse + recover_dsml + 'decoded to None' fail-loud); ~/projects/piarch/scripts/run_eval.py:206-208 + evals/_llm_factory.py. Reported from ox-troubleshooting-demo overnight json_mode reasoning work.
notes:
2026-07-07 ANALYSIS + RECOMMENDED SOLUTION (maintainer-reviewed; claims verified: response_format appears 0 times in src; json_mode = describe_type schema string + text parse only).

THE SEAM (verified): _prepare_structured_call in _llm.py is the SHARED pure preamble both invoke_structured and ainvoke_structured consume (post-ykun extraction) — it already branches on strategy == json_mode to build output_schema and returns (llm, messages, strategy, llm_log). Native binding is a few lines THERE: when strategy is json_mode, return llm.bind(response_format={'type':'json_object'}) instead of bare llm. ONE site, both twins inherit, twin-thinness preserved by construction. Also check the OTHER json_mode call paths reached via _llm_retry (_invoke_json_with_retry / recover_dsml receive the llm object — if they receive the already-bound llm from the caller, nothing more needed; verify and pin).

PROVIDER-COMPAT (the real design question — a hard bind breaks providers without response_format support, e.g. ChatAnthropic passes it to an API that rejects it): do NOT provider-sniff by class name (drift) and do NOT switch to with_structured_output(method='json_mode') (it would replace neograph's parse/recovery machinery and lose the reason-then-coerce raw-text path the consumer explicitly wants). One shared helper; the parse machinery stays as the universal safety net either way. Consumers keep the manual llm_factory bind (the piarch pattern) as the documented escape hatch — no new LlmConfig knob needed.

THE JSON-WORD REQUIREMENT (ticket item 1 caveat): OpenAI-compat json_object REQUIRES the literal word json in the messages. VERIFY the injected describe_type instruction block contains it; if not guaranteed, the json_mode preamble appends one instruction line. Pin with a test either way — this is the silent-400 trap.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-jhz4
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-jhz4
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-jhz4`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-jhz4)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-jhz4 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-jhz4 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-jhz4
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-jhz4` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-jhz4/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-jhz4
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-jhz4)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-jhz4 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-jhz4 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-jhz4/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-jhz4 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must

- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: di_inputs config-injection for agent/act modes (_agent_cycle.py) — completes euyh
description:
Completes neograph-euyh. euyh delivered di_inputs (resolved FromInput/FromConfig values reaching prompt templates) for THINK mode only. Closes the SAME agent-stark production incident for tool-using (agent/act) nodes.

MECHANISM — reuse the exact think-mode pattern, NO second mechanism: think uses ThinkDispatch._inject_di_inputs (src/neograph/_dispatch.py), which resolves node._param_res once via the canonical DIBinding.resolve(config) and stashes {param_name: value} into config['configurable'][StateKeys.DI_INPUTS] ('_neo_di_inputs', copy-not-mutate, mirrors _inject_oracle_config). _compile_prompt reads it back and passes an introspection-gated di_inputs= kwarg. Agent/act nodes bypass _execute_node/ThinkDispatch (they compile to the ReAct cycle via _wiring._add_agent_cycle / _agent_cycle.py), so _inject_di_inputs never runs for them. FIX: call the same injection at the agent-cycle entry (before the cycle's _compile_prompt path in _tool_loop). Reuse di.DI_TEMPLATE_KINDS and StateKeys.DI_INPUTS — do NOT introduce a new key or a new resolver.

TESTS: add an E2E parallel to tests/test_prompt_compiler.py::TestDiInputReachesModelEndToEnd but for an agent/act node ({domain} FromInput reaches the model, no seed node).

DOCS: flip the AGENTS.md di_inputs section note from 'think only' to 'think + agent/act', and remove the lint runtime-vs-lint-coverage caveat once runtime matches lint.

BLOCKED until ykun's twin-extraction (neograph-ykun) lands — _agent_cycle.py / _tool_loop.py were mid-refactor when euyh closed; rebase on that first. Gated into 0.6.0 via neograph-y5ux.
design:
## Core Invariant
DI resolution is single-sourced: there is exactly ONE resolver (`DIBinding.resolve`), ONE injection function (`_dispatch._inject_di_inputs`), ONE config key (`StateKeys.DI_INPUTS`), and ONE reader (`_llm_render._compile_prompt`) — agent/act must REUSE all four, never add a parallel mechanism.

## Implementation Plan
1. In `src/neograph/_agent_cycle.py:45`, extend the existing `from neograph._dispatch import ...` line to also import `_inject_di_inputs` (free function, no cycle).
2. In `_turn_prep_kwargs` (`src/neograph/_agent_cycle.py:98`), make the FIRST statement `config = _inject_di_inputs(node, config)` — before line 119 first reads config and before line 129 packs it into `prepare_kwargs["config"]`. This single shared seam feeds both sync/async twins and all three cycle bodies (agent/tools/parse); the resolved DI values then ride config into `_prepare_tool_loop` -> `_build_loop_preamble` -> `_compile_prompt`, which already reads them back via the introspection-gated `di_inputs=` kwarg. Zero changes to `_tool_loop.py`, `_llm_render.py`, `di.py`, `_state_keys.py`.
3.
