title: FromResource DI marker: declarative MCP resource wiring — Annotated[Model, FromResource(uri)] fetches + validates at node entry (async DI twin)
description:
Consumer-requested (2026-07-06, maintainer confirms a real consumer wants declarative resource wiring). MCP resources are untyped at the protocol level (mime + bytes Blobs via langchain-mcp-adapters MultiServerMCPClient.get_resources, adapter 0.3.0, async-only, stateless-session model) — the typed-channel paradigm supplies the missing half: the node boundary is where blob becomes contract.

THE FEATURE: a new DI marker joining the FromInput/FromConfig family — parameter annotated Annotated[ContractDoc, FromResource('mcp://server/uri')] is fetched at node entry per execution, parsed, validated into the declared model, and injected. Downstream nodes consume a validated model; fan-in validation sees the declared type at assembly time.

PURITY-TEST JUSTIFICATION (docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md): a resource READ is side-effect-free I/O, safe to replay on resume — legal inside node-entry resolution (unlike mutating calls). Fetch-per-execution also gives resume-in-fresh-process re-fetch for free (same property as tool factories / token provider — no caching, no invalidation machinery).

HARD CONSTRAINTS (all carry prior-decision weight):
1. NO SESSION OWNERSHIP (nmb2 verdict, docs/design/mcp-session-ownership-review-2026-07-05.md + the structural guard): the client/connections are CONSUMER-OWNED, supplied via config['configurable'] (a client instance or an async resource-fetcher callable), exactly like tool factories. neograph never creates/holds/disposes MCP sessions.
2. THE DI RESOLVER IS SYNC TODAY (_resolve_di_value in decorators/di layer): FromResource needs an ASYNC resolution twin — the same H2 gap-shape as tool factories (neograph-w74k.3.1), solved the same way: async DI path on arun(), FAIL LOUD with ConfigurationError on run() (khff pattern). Do NOT introspect-and-branch inside one path; the driver selects.
3. Three-surface parity + 6-cell coverage (IR-level change).

DESIGN DECISIONS for the research/architect atoms:
- URI shape: static string first; templated URIs (per-run interpolation from FromInput values, e.g. mcp://server/tickets/{ticket_id}) as an explicit scope decision — likely v2.
- Parse strategy by mime: application/json -> model_validate_json (v1 scope); text/* -> require an explicit parser callable in the marker or defer to a think-node recipe (schema-aligned LLM parse is the documented pattern for unstructured content — do NOT silently LLM-parse inside DI resolution, that is hidden cognition + cost).
- Error path: missing resource / fetch failure / validation failure -> typed error at node entry naming the param, uri, and node (fail-loud house style); decide retry semantics (probably none in v1 — the consumer wraps with Loop/skip_when if needed).
- Lint: FromResource param + run()-driven graph -> reuse/extend tool_requires_async_driver-style check; lint knows the marker so template/DI key prediction stays coherent (interacts with neograph-euyh's di_inputs work — coordinate key naming).
- Where resolution lives: the DI classifier (_classify_di_params) gains a binding kind; the shim resolution gains the async twin. Keep ONE resolver/classifier for @node and @merge_fn (existing monopoly rule).

INTERIM (document in the ticket + docs until this lands): the three working patterns today — fetch-ahead into run(input=), async scripted node body fetching + returning its declared type (purity-legal), resource-as-tool for agent-driven pulls.

SEQUENCING: NOT wired into the 0.6.0 gate (y5ux) — it is a new feature, not a known fix; maintainer decides whether it gates the release or lands in 0.6.x. Depends conceptually on nothing open; can run as its own molecule post-wave-3.
notes:
2026-07-06 DEEP-RESEARCH FINDINGS (docs/design/mcp-resources-patterns-2026-07-06.md — 19 claims survived 3-vote adversarial verification, 6 refuted). THE HEADLINE: the field has NO named pattern for reference-in-state + hydrate-later-across-pause (the one focused publication, Frees arXiv 2510.05968, states these patterns remain undocumented; the protocol community itself routed deferred results through task tokens with negotiated TTLs — SEP-1686 — after explicitly REJECTING a resource-based approach). Independent precedents converge on our design regardless: Google ADK mandates references-in-state + artifact store + deliberately-ephemeral always-re-fetch hydration; LangGraph designates checkpointed thread-scoped state (not Store) as the HITL-survival tier. neograph would be NAMING this pattern, not adopting one.

PROTOCOL FACTS THAT SHAPE v2 SCOPE: (1) resource_link is a first-class tool-result content type explicitly designed for deferred client fetch (MAY, not SHOULD — servers are permitted, not encouraged). (2) Tool-emitted links are NOT guaranteed to appear in resources/list — a later step CANNOT validate a link by enumeration; the only check is resources/read + handle error -32002. (3) The spec is SILENT on URI stability/TTL/expiry (only lastModified annotation exists); cross-checkpoint durability is 100 percent server-defined. NOTE: the 2026-07-28 protocol RC adds ttlMs/cacheScope to list/read results — the protocol is catching up to exactly this gap; design v2 so ttlMs slots in when servers ship it.

RESEARCH-BACKED v2 DESIGN (extends the v1 FromResource marker): (a) typed ResourceRef manifest in a CHECKPOINTED state channel — and each ref SHOULD CARRY THE PRODUCING TOOL CALL (tool name + args) so an expired link is re-derivable; (b) hydration default = app-curated DI-injected fetch (FromResource/manifest-driven), read_resource-as-tool as opt-in for model-controlled pulls; (c) re-fetch on every hydration (replay-safe read, matches ADK's deliberate ephemerality) with OPTIONAL under-size-threshold caching into state; (d) LAYERED EXPIRY HANDLING on hydration failure: try resources/read -> on -32002 replay the producing tool call from the ref -> fail loud with a typed error naming ref+node. title: Sweep verification for nva4
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on nva4
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" nva4`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (nva4)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.

       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   ```bash
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>

   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add nva4 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for nva4
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show nva4` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/nva4/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" nva4
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (nva4)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update nva4 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update nva4 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/nva4/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add nva4 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/nva4/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for dyp3
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show dyp3` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/dyp3/`:

     structural tools over text grep when available:

       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.

     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

   found must appear:

   ```

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes


   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash

   ```

ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/dyp3/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):


  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Sweep verification for hjwv
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on hjwv
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" hjwv`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (hjwv)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update hjwv --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add hjwv sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

title: observe= opt-in: auto-attach Langfuse CallbackHandler (merge, no-clobber, no-op without keys) + flush in finalize; wire-or-drop the aspirational extra (GH issue 4, option A)
description:
From GitHub issue 4. VERIFIED: pyproject.toml:35 declares the langfuse extra; grep -rni langfuse src/ returns ZERO hits — the extra installs a package and wires nothing (aspirational-extra false advertising). Consumers must hand-attach langfuse.langchain.CallbackHandler to config.callbacks and remember to flush.

SCOPE (this is prepare()/finalize() territory — thin-verb-compatible per docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md, it merges config BEFORE the engine verb and never wraps the engine): (1) observe='langfuse' (and observe=True auto-detect) accepted by run/arun/stream/astream — decide run-level vs compile-level (run-level is right: the handler is per-run/per-trace; document why); (2) semantics per the issue, all three non-negotiable: gate on env keys present (clean no-op when LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY absent — never crash offline/CI), MERGE into config.callbacks (never clobber user-supplied handlers), flush on completion — which for stream verbs means flush after the generator is exhausted (and on generator close/cancellation — coordinate with the 51tr cancellation semantics), i.e. a finalize concern, not an exit line in each verb; (3) import langfuse lazily inside the observe path only — the extra stays optional, core import graph unchanged (function-local import allowlist entry + guard); (4) EITHER this lands and the extra is real, OR if rejected the extra gets dropped from pyproject — the current state (extra with zero wiring) is the bug; (5) example: observable_pipeline.py loses its hand-rolled handler attachment in favor of observe=True (keep the manual form documented as the escape hatch); website observability page updated.

EXPLICITLY REJECTED from the same GH issue — option B (native OTEL spans for graph lifecycle): EMPIRICALLY REFUTED premise. Probe 2026-07-06 (scratchpad cb_span_probe.py): a plain BaseCallbackHandler in config.callbacks receives on_chain_start for LangGraph AND every node (chain events: LangGraph, step-a, node_wrapper, step-b, node_wrapper) — the engine already broadcasts the whole DAG through its own callback abstraction; Langfuse v4 is OTEL-native so callbacks ARE the OTEL path. Building parallel neograph OTEL spans = the reinventing-runtime disease (same verdict shape as nmb2). Span HYGIENE is the real residue — see companion ticket.
design:
## Core Invariant
observe= is a per-run config merge that happens in the pre-engine brain (_prepare/_aprepare) and a finalize-time flush in the verb's finally — it MERGES into config.callbacks (never clobbers), NO-OPs cleanly when LANGFUSE env keys are absent, and imports langfuse lazily inside the observe path only; it must NEVER wrap the engine verb, add a compile-level hook, or import langfuse at module level (three-layer thin-verb principle preserved).

## Implementation Plan
1. GUARD-FIRST (per repo memory): write the NEW structural guard RED first — "langfuse imported only function-locally inside runner.py observe helpers; never module-level anywhere in src/." Model on tests/test_guards_examples.py `_third_party_import_roots` (AST third-party root extraction) + test_guards_sidecar_imports.py::test_no_private_langgraph_imports (src/ glob AST-walk). This enforces non-negotiable (3) and is currently UNENFORCED (the existing function-local allowlist only scans `from neograph...`). Put it in test_guards_sidecar_imports.py.
2. Add pure helper `_merge_observe_callbacks(config, observe) -> RunnableConfig` in runner.py beside `_mark_stream_custom`: resolve observe (None/False -> return config unchanged; True or 'langfuse' -> langfuse; unknown str -> raise); gate on os.environ (LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY [+PUBLIC_KEY] present, else return config unchanged); function-local `from langfuse.langchain import CallbackHandler`; build a FRESH config dict merging the handler into a FRESH callbacks list (`[*existing, handler]`), handling list/None (and BaseCallbackManager via add_handler or documented-unsupported). Copy `_mark_stream_custom`'s no-mutation discipline.
3. Add `_flush_observe(observe)` helper: same env-gate; if it passes, function-local `from langfuse import get_client; get_client().flush()`; else no-op. Symmetric gate = flush iff attached; keeps _prepare's 2-tuple contract untouched.
4. Add `observe` param to `_prepare` AND `_aprepare` (twin-guarded — both or neither), calling `_merge_observe_callbacks` after `_mark_stream_custom`/before `_ensure_agent_recursion_limit`. Add `observe: bool | str | None = None` to run/arun/stream/astream and thread through.
5. FINALIZE flush: run/arun -> `try: return graph.invoke(...) finally: _flush_observe(observe)`. stream/astream -> wrap the `for/async for chunk ...: yield _finalize_chunk(...)` loop in `try: ... finally: _flush_observe(observe)` so flush fires after exhaustion AND on GeneratorExit/CancelledError (rides the 51tr cancellation finally — 51tr CLOSED).
6. Three-surface parity is N/A (driver/runtime feature, not IR shape — same exemption as test_async_observability.py). FLUSH is a FINALIZE concern, symmetric-gated (non-negotiable 3 + stream caveat):

title: Public neograph.testing fakes with a loop-compat guarantee (FakeLLM / install helper) (GH issue 5 addendum)
description:
From GitHub issue 5 addendum. CONSUMER BREAKAGE EVIDENCE: consumers fake the LLM at the llm_factory seam with hand-rolled AIMessage duck-types; the m6d3 agent-cycle refactor coerces messages through LangChain (_to_lc_messages -> add_messages), so every hand-rolled fake broke at once with NotImplementedError: Unsupported message type / MESSAGE_COERCION_FAILURE — with no version bump (editable path dep), looking like an env flake until traced.

THE FAKES ALREADY EXIST AND ARE BATTLE-HARDENED: tests/fakes.py ships StructuredFake, StructuredFakeWithRaw, ReActFake, StringArgsFake, GuardFake, StubbornFake, FakeTool, _final_json_content, configure_fake_llm — they survived the f7nt/eoi8/m6d3 refactors because WE update them with every loop change. The consumers broke precisely because they cannot import them. SCOPE: promote the fake contract to a public, supported API: (1) namespace decision FIRST — src/neograph/testing.py is already occupied by the scaffold codegen (bd neograph-gfoq touched it); likely resolution: convert to a neograph/testing/ package (codegen + fakes submodules) or a new neograph.fakes module — decide with a one-line ADR note in the ticket; (2) export a canned FakeLLM(outputs: dict[node_name -> BaseModel|str]) guaranteed compatible with the agent cycle: real langchain_core AIMessage types, bind_tools/with_structured_output/bind surface, empty-tool_calls final-turn semantics, per-node routing INCLUDING the Oracle-merge node_name=='' case (all already implemented in tests/fakes.py — this is extraction+export, not new code); (3) install_fake_llm(monkeypatch, outputs) / pytest-fixture helper patching the llm_factory seam; (4) THE GUARANTEE: a compat test in neograph's own suite drives a public FakeLLM through an agent node end-to-end — any future loop refactor that breaks the public double breaks OUR suite first, not every consumer's; (5) docs page under testing.

ANTI-DUPLICATION: neograph's own tests migrate to import from the public location (or a structural guard pins that tests/fakes.py re-exports from it) — one implementation, two consumers. Optional stretch from the issue (recorded-real/VCR variant): file separately if wanted, NOT in scope. Reply-to-GH cross-link once maintainer approves commenting.
design:
## Core Invariant
There is EXACTLY ONE implementation of the fake LLM contract, and neograph's own test suite consumes it through the public location — so any future loop refactor that breaks the public double breaks OUR suite first, before it can silently break a consumer.

## Implementation Plan

## Findings

### The reuse target (this is extraction+export, NOT new code)
- tests/fakes.py already ships the ENTIRE battle-hardened fake contract: StructuredFake, StructuredFakeWithRaw, ReActFake, StringArgsFake, TextFake, FakeTool, GuardFake, StubbornFake, GatedAsyncFake, event_loop_lag_watchdog, _final_json_content, plus the wiring helpers build_fake_llm_kwargs / configure_fake_llm / build_fake_runtime / build_fake_tool_lookup / drive_agent_via_cycle. They survive every loop refactor because we edit them with each change. Consumers broke only because they cannot import them.
- ReActFake (tests/fakes.py:256) is the exemplar double for the loop-compat guarantee: it ALREADY implements the full agent-cycle surface — bind_tools()/abind_tools() (return self so counter persists), with_structured_output() (clone), invoke() that emits real langchain_core AIMessage, empty-tool_calls final-turn semantics (_final_message -> _final_json_content), and history-driven turn indexing (neograph-m6d3: counts prior tool-call turns in message history so it works whether the agent runs as one node body OR a cycle of supersteps). The public canned FakeLLM router should wrap ReActFake per node, not reinvent a double.

### The llm_factory seam (SINGLE resolution point, two import bindings)
- llm_factory is a compile() kwarg (compiler.py:65), captured into the frozen LlmRuntime bundle (_llm_runtime.py:55). It is NOT a module global — there is no default factory to patch.
- Resolution funnels through ONE function: _get_llm(runtime, tier, node_name=..., llm_config=...) in _llm.py:93. It calls runtime.llm_factory(tier, **kwargs) where kwargs are FILTERED to the params the factory declares (_llm.py:120-125 via LlmRuntime.llm_factory_params). So a router factory that declares node_name will receive it; a lambda tier: fake ignores it. This is exactly the per-node routing hook.
- BOTH LLM paths resolve via _get_llm: produce/think at _llm.py:191, and the agent/tool ReAct path at _tool_loop.py:312 (used by _agent_cycle prep). CRITICAL: _tool_loop.py:23 does 'from neograph._llm import _get_llm', binding the function into its own namespace — so monkeypatching neograph._llm._get_llm alone will NOT affect the agent path. install_fake_llm must patch _get_llm at BOTH binding sites (neograph._llm and neograph._tool_loop).

### Oracle-merge node_name=='' case
- _oracle.py:273 calls invoke_structured(runtime, model_tier=oracle.merge_model, ...) WITHOUT passing node_name, so _get_llm defaults node_name='' (_llm.py:96). A per-node routing FakeLLM must accept '' as the merge key (or provide a merge default), else Oracle pipelines KeyError.

### Current wiring pattern (the current way; nothing deprecated here)
- Post-ezqz: configure_llm() (module-state mutation) is GONE. Current way = pass llm_factory=/prompt_compiler= as compile() kwargs. build_fake_llm_kwargs(factory) returns that dict; tests splat compile(c, **build_fake_llm_kwargs(lambda tier: fake)). configure_fake_llm is now a back-compat alias returning the same dict (tests/fakes.py:792). Exemplar call sites: tests/test_agent_subgraph_keystone.py:163-167,324,385,473.

### Anti-duplication surface
- 124 test files import via 'from tests.fakes import ...' (440 import lines), consistent single style. Migrating all 124 is churn; the ticket's own alternative — tests/fakes.py RE-EXPORTS from the public location pinned by a structural guard — is the low-risk one-implementation-two-consumers path.
- tests/test_guards_async_fakes.py already AST-guards the 8 shared fakes for bare-delegation async mirrors, hardcoding FAKES_PATH=tests/fakes.py. If the canonical bodies move, this guard must repoint to the public module (or follow the re-export).

title: Prompt compilation: exported fail-loud primitives + DefaultPromptCompiler (GH issue 5, layers 1-2)
description:
From GitHub issue 5 (consumer evidence: piarch and agent-stark both hand-roll the prompt_compiler seam and DIVERGED on the safety property — piarch fail-loud RuntimeError on unfilled placeholder, agent-stark silent .replace() which shipped the literal string {domain} to a production LLM, caught only by live e2e). The framework currently leaves 'unfilled var -> crash vs silent' to each app to get wrong. This is quintessential Layer-2 node-internal DX per docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md — exactly where neograph value belongs.

SCOPE — Layer 1, exported primitives (composable): (a) render_inputs(input_data) -> dict[str,str] exposing the BAML input-to-var rendering already done internally (renderers.py build_rendered_input — expose, do not duplicate); (b) substitute(template, vars, *, strict=True, syntax='brace'|'dollar'|Callable) -> str — ONE substitution primitive; strict raises typed PromptVarMissing(var, available=[...]); must be BRACE-SAFE so an injected JSON schema's {} does not break substitution (the exact reason agent-stark fell back to .replace); (c) inject_schema(vars, output_model|output_schema, key='json_schema') riding describe_type. Layer 2: DefaultPromptCompiler(loader, *, strict=True, syntax='brace', system=None, schema_var='json_schema') so the 90-percent case is compile(construct, prompt_compiler=DefaultPromptCompiler(Path('prompts'))); override hooks load_template/build_vars/render_messages — override one method, keep the rest.

PRINCIPLES (from the issue, all match house style): fail-loud by default (strict=True — the {domain}-reaches-the-model class becomes impossible without explicit opt-out); composable not monolithic (a custom compiler is ~10 lines of primitive composition); engine-agnostic syntax (brace/dollar/pluggable). ANTI-DUPLICATION: the primitives must be THE internals, re-exported/extracted — not a parallel second rendering path (one substitution rule; _llm_render inline-prompt handling and the new substitute must share the placeholder-parsing core or a guard explains why not).

ACCEPTANCE: from neograph import DefaultPromptCompiler, substitute, render_inputs (names finalizable); DefaultPromptCompiler + a prompts/ dir renders with zero app compiler code; unfilled placeholder raises PromptVarMissing under strict; existing custom prompt_compiler consumers unaffected (opt-in, zero behavior change without it). Companion tickets: di_inputs-to-compiler (layer 3) and public test doubles are filed SEPARATELY — do not fold in. Reply-to-GH cross-link once maintainer approves commenting.
design:
## Core Invariant
There is ONE substitution rule and ONE input-rendering path in neograph: the exported prompt primitives must be the existing internals (renderers.build_rendered_input, the _llm_render placeholder scanner, describe_type) re-exported/extracted — never a second parallel rendering path — and they compose behind the unchanged compile(construct, prompt_compiler=...) seam so consumers with their own compiler see zero behavior change.

## Implementation Plan
1. NEW public module src/neograph/prompt.py (Layer-2 node-runtime helper, sibling to renderers.py/describe_type.py). Holds the four primitives + DefaultPromptCompiler. Keep it engine-free (no langgraph imports).
2. EXTRACT the placeholder scanner (currently _VAR_RE at _llm_render.py:29 + the single-pass re.sub body of _substitute_vars:110) into a shared location both prompt.py and _llm_render.py import. Add the brace regex r'\{([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)\}' alongside the existing dollar _VAR_RE. Refactor _llm_render._substitute_vars to call the shared single-pass apply with its own resolver (fail-soft, dotted+BAML) — proving one scanner, two policies. Do NOT change inline fail-soft behavior.
3. substitute(template, vars, *, strict=True, syntax='brace'|'dollar'|Callable) -> str: single-pass over the chosen scanner; per-match resolver looks up vars; on miss raise PromptVarMissing(var, available=sorted(vars)) when strict else leave token verbatim. Brace-safe by construction (single pass, token-only pattern).
4. render_inputs(input_data, *, renderer=None) -> dict[str,str]: thin wrapper over renderers.build_rendered_input(...).for_template_ref. Reuse, do not reimplement.
5. inject_schema(vars, output_model=None, *, output_schema=None, key='json_schema') -> dict: sets vars[key] = output_schema or describe_type(output_model). Ride describe_type; accept the precomputed output_schema string the seam already threads.
6. PromptVarMissing in errors.py subclassing ExecutionError (runtime substitution failure); structured attrs var:str, available:list[str]; message via NeographError.build with hint listing available keys.
7. DefaultPromptCompiler(loader, *, strict=True, syntax='brace', system=None, schema_var='json_schema') — callable satisfying the PromptCompiler Protocol (_llm_protocols.py:33). __call__(template, input_data, *, output_model=None, output_schema=None, **kw): (a) load_template(template) via loader (Path -> read {name}.md, or a callable), (b) build_vars(input_data) via render_inputs [+ inject_schema when output_model/output_schema present], (c) render_messages(template_text, vars) via substitute -> [{'role':'system',...}?, {'role':'user','content':...}]. Each of load_template/build_vars/render_messages is an override hook — override one, keep the rest (~10-line custom compiler).
8. Export from __init__.py __all__: DefaultPromptCompiler, substitute, render_inputs, inject_schema, PromptVarMissing (coordinate with yc38 which also edits __all__).
9. TESTS (three-surface not required — this is Layer-2, exempt; but cover): unit for substitute brace-safety (injected schema with literal {} renders intact), strict PromptVarMissing(var, available), dollar+brace+Callable syntaxes; render_inputs returns BAML-rendered dict matching build_rendered_input; inject_schema uses describe_type; end-to-end compile(construct, prompt_compiler=DefaultPromptCompiler(Path('prompts'))) renders with zero app compiler code; an existing custom prompt_compiler still works unchanged (opt-in proof). Add a should_pass check_fixtures entry for the DefaultPromptCompiler happy path.
10. GUARD: structural test asserting the placeholder regex(es) are defined once (shared) and that prompt.py has no langgraph import; if the scanner is only partly shared, a guard-comment must state why (resolution-fusion in _llm_render is intentionally not shared).
notes:
## Findings (dp-researcher — atom 938w.2)

REUSE TARGETS (the primitives must BE these internals, re-exported/extracted — not a parallel path):
- render_inputs(input_data) -> dict[str,str]: WRAP renderers.build_rendered_input (renderers.py:278). The BAML input->var rendering already exists there; RenderedInput.for_template_ref (renderers.py:55) is exactly the merged rendered+flattened dict a template-ref compiler consumes. render_inputs = thin wrapper returning that dict view. DO NOT reimplement _render_single/_render_with_flattening.
- substitute(template, vars, *, strict, syntax): share the placeholder-parsing core with _llm_render.py. The dollar-brace regex _VAR_RE = re.compile(r'\$\{([^}]+)\}') at _llm_render.py:29 is the existing single-pass scanner and IS ALREADY BRACE-SAFE (only matches ${...}, leaves literal {} untouched). _substitute_vars (_llm_render.py:110) is the exemplar: re.sub with a per-match resolver fn = single-pass, never re-scans substituted text (this is THE brace-safety mechanism; str.format is not single-pass over a fixed token set, which is why agent-stark fell back to .replace).
- inject_schema(vars, output_model|output_schema, key='json_schema'): RIDE describe_type (describe_type.py:73). Signature already returns the TS-style schema string; inject_schema just sets vars[key]=describe_type(output_model) (or the precomputed output_schema string). The compiler ALREADY computes output_schema and threads it: render_prompt at _llm_render.py:261-262 does 'if strategy==json_mode: output_schema = describe_type(output_model)'.

CURRENT prompt_compiler SEAM (how it is wired today):
- compile(construct, ..., prompt_compiler=...) at compiler.py:60-116. Kwarg folded into LlmRuntime.build (compiler.py:107) -> frozen LlmRuntime (_llm_runtime.py:46). Callable signature is the PromptCompiler Protocol (_llm_protocols.py:33): __call__(template:str, input_data:Any, *args, **kwargs) -> list. Simple shape (template, input_data)->list; advanced accepts kwargs.
- Invocation site: _llm_render.py:_compile_prompt (line 151), branch at :200-213. It builds all_kwargs = {node_name, config, output_model, llm_config, output_schema, (context)} then FILTERS by runtime.prompt_compiler_params (introspected once at build via _accepted_params, _llm_runtime.py:29) — so a compiler that declares output_model=/output_schema= in its signature receives them; one that only takes (template, data, **kw) gets everything. This means DefaultPromptCompiler can pull output_model/output_schema straight from the seam — no new plumbing needed for layer 1-2.
- Inline-prompt fast path: _compile_prompt short-circuits BEFORE the prompt_compiler when _is_inline_prompt (space or ${ present, _llm_render.py:33). File-ref templates (e.g. 'rw/decompose') go to the user prompt_compiler. DefaultPromptCompiler is the file-ref handler.

EXISTING hand-rolled exemplar (the thing being productized): examples/_shared.py make_template_prompt_compiler — loads {dir}/{name}.md and string.Template.safe_substitute. Header explicitly says 'NOT public API, every production consumer writes their own' — hjwv makes that unnecessary. Note it uses ${var} (dollar) precisely to avoid crashing on literal {curly} in code samples — same brace-safety motivation.

OPT-IN / zero-behavior-change: DefaultPromptCompiler is just a callable passed as prompt_compiler=. Consumers who pass their own callable are untouched (the seam is unchanged). No default is wired into compile(); absence still raises ConfigurationError (_llm_render.py:200-204).
## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/renderers.py:278 build_rendered_input + :55 RenderedInput.for_template_ref — REUSE for render_inputs (the internal BAML input->str rendering; do not duplicate _render_single/_render_with_flattening at :320/:357).
- src/neograph/_llm_render.py:29 _VAR_RE (dollar-brace scanner, brace-safe) + :110 _substitute_vars (single-pass re.sub exemplar) — the placeholder-parsing core substitute() must share.
- src/neograph/_llm_render.py:151 _compile_prompt + :200-213 — the seam call site; shows kwargs (output_model/output_schema/config) already delivered to compilers via param-filtering.
- src/neograph/_llm_runtime.py:29 _accepted_params + :84 prompt_compiler_params — signature introspection that routes output_model=/output_schema= to a declaring compiler.
- src/neograph/describe_type.py:73 describe_type — RIDE for inject_schema.
- src/neograph/compiler.py:60-116 compile() prompt_compiler kwarg -> LlmRuntime.build (the wiring; unchanged by this ticket).
- src/neograph/_llm_protocols.py:33 PromptCompiler Protocol — the callable contract DefaultPromptCompiler must satisfy (structurally, __call__).
- examples/_shared.py:26 make_template_prompt_compiler — the hand-rolled pattern being productized (load .md, safe_substitute); dollar syntax chosen for brace-safety.
- src/neograph/errors.py:24 NeographError.build / :96 ExecutionError — PromptVarMissing subclasses here.
- src/neograph/__init__.py:78 __all__ — where the new public names register.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- BRACE-SAFETY (the load-bearing test): for syntax='brace', use a single-pass regex like r'\{([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)\}' with a per-match resolver — NEVER str.format. Empty {} and JSON-schema fragments ({ "foo": ... } with space/quote after brace) must not match the token pattern, and single-pass re.sub never re-scans the injected schema value. Write a should_pass-style test: template with {json_schema} where the injected schema contains literal {} — must render intact. This is the exact agent-stark regression.
- STRICTNESS ASYMMETRY: existing inline ${var} handling is fail-SOFT (log.warning at _llm_render.py:62/76, returns ''). New substitute() default is strict=True (raise PromptVarMissing). Do NOT flip the inline path to strict — that changes documented behavior (would break existing inline-prompt tests/examples). Reuse the parsing core, not the strictness policy. A structural guard can pin 'both use the shared regex' and explain the policy split.
- SHARE-CORE vs SEMANTIC GAP: inline path FUSES resolution (dotted attr access + BAML describe_value via _resolve_var, _llm_render.py:43) with substitution; substitute() takes a pre-built vars: dict[str,str]. The shareable unit is the token SCANNER (the two compiled regexes + single-pass apply), not _resolve_var. Extract the scanner to a shared spot both import; a guard/comment explains why resolution is not shared.
- syntax=Callable third form: allow syntax to be a user regex/tokenizer for engine-agnostic use; keep default 'brace' per the ticket, with 'dollar' matching neograph's own inline syntax.
- PromptVarMissing must carry (var, available=[...]) as structured attrs (the issue is explicit) — mirror the log.warning 'available=sorted(...keys())' shape at _llm_render.py:65.
- SCOPE FENCE: di_inputs->compiler (euyh, layer 3) and public test doubles are SEPARATE tickets — do not fold in. No lint changes here (that is euyh).
- Companion housekeeping yc38 also touches __all__ exports — coordinate to avoid __init__.py merge conflict, but names here (DefaultPromptCompiler/substitute/render_inputs/inject_schema/PromptVarMissing) are this ticket's.

title: Node completing with None against a declared outputs= type is silently swallowed at the write boundary — decide enforce-vs-tolerate and make it explicit
description:
Companion to the Each-navigation crash ticket (consumer-reported, reproduced 2026-07-06). MECHANISM FOUND: _state_write.py:34 — 'if result is None or node.outputs is None: return {}'. A node that RAN and returned None against its declared outputs= type writes NOTHING to the bus: no validation, no warning, node_complete fires normally (probe evidence: scripted node declaring outputs=HypothesisSet returned None; logs show clean node_start/node_complete; downstream saw an absent field). The None then surfaces far from its source (in the reporter's case as a TypeError inside the Each router; in other graphs as fan-in validation confusion or a silent hole in results).

DESIGN DECISION REQUIRED (the reporter framed enforce-vs-tolerate as mutually exclusive — our diagnosis says they are NOT, and the distinction is the resolution): (1) RAN-AND-VIOLATED-CONTRACT: a node that executes and produces None (or a type-mismatched value) against its declared outputs= should FAIL LOUD at the write boundary — a legible NodeOutputError('hypothesize declared HypothesisSet, produced None') naming the node, matching the house fail-loud style (khff sync/async error, PromptVarMissing direction, agent-mode ExecutionError on unparseable finals). (2) NEVER-RAN / LEGITIMATELY ABSENT: untaken branch arms and skip_when nodes leave fields absent by design — that case is handled by the Each empty-bypass fix in the companion ticket and must NOT be affected by (1).

AUDIT STEP (required before implementing): enumerate every path where a mode can complete with None reaching _build_state_update — the reporter's real case was an LLM think-mode structured decode flake (gemini), which suggests a retry-exhaustion or compat-shim path returns None instead of raising; the agent-mode parse tail already raises ExecutionError on silent None (f7nt/eoi8) — check whether think mode has the same guarantee or predates it. Fix at the SOURCE path(s) too if the audit finds a silent-None LLM return: the write-boundary check is the backstop, not the only defense.

SCOPE GUARD: enforcement must be at the single monopolized write boundary (_build_state_update / _state_write), not re-inlined per mode. Dict-form outputs get the per-key equivalent. isinstance check against declared type: decide whether to enforce full type match or None-only first (None-only is the observed footgun; full isinstance may break legitimate duck-typing — the ticket owner decides with a fixture pair). 6-cell/three-surface rules apply. Website: document the committed behavior on the node-api page either way.
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE:
- errors.py: added NodeOutputError(NeographError); re-exported in __init__.py (import + __all__).
- _state_write.py: _build_state_update now distinguishes node.outputs is None (no contract -> {}) from result is None WITH declared outputs (ran+violated -> raise NodeOutputError via new _raise_none_output helper naming node+declared-type+state-field). Dict-form: primary key None raises; secondary framework keys (tool_log) None stay tolerant. None-only, not full isinstance.
- _llm_dispatch.py (SOURCE fix): the structured-strategy Raw(parsed=None) silent arm (sync + async) now raises ExecutionError via shared _raise_decoded_none(NoReturn) helper instead of returning (None, usage). Backstop is the write boundary; this is the complementary source defense for the gemini decode-flake path.
- Enforcement lives ONLY at the monopolized boundary (_build_state_update) + the source raise; not re-inlined per mode.

TESTS (all green):
- tests/modes/test_execution.py::TestNodeOutputContract (7): scripted-None raise, valid-output regression, skip_when-absent tolerant, outputs=None no-contract, dict-form primary-None raise, dict-form secondary-None tolerant, three-surface parity (@node / Node.scripted / Node|Each).
- tests/modes/test_output_strategies.py::TestStructuredSilentNoneSource (1): think-mode source raise.
- tests/modes/test_llm_internals.py::TestCallStructuredParsedNoneFailsLoud (1): rewrote the ex-ble3 R1 test that pinned legacy silent-None -> now asserts ExecutionError.
- tests/test_coverage_gaps.py::TestBuildStateUpdate: split the old test_returns_empty_when_result_none into raise (declared) + tolerant (outputs=None).
- tests/modifiers/test_oracle.py: fixed a misconfigured merge_prompt test whose 'write' node was scripted (...-body -> None) and only passed because of the silent swallow; added prompt=/model= to make it a valid think node (assertion unchanged).

title: Each over-path navigation crashes on None/absent intermediate instead of routing to the existing empty_bypass
description:
Consumer-reported (ox-troubleshooting-demo cascade: hypothesize | Each(over='hypothesize.candidates') — intermittent ~11 percent whole-run loss when a structured decode flake yields None). REPRODUCED 2026-07-06 on develop with a minimal probe: scripted node declaring outputs=HypothesisSet returns None -> node_complete fires -> Each router crashes TypeError: NoneType object is not subscriptable.

THE BUG DEFEATS ITS OWN DESIGN: _wiring.py:66-69 — the comment above bus.get(root) explicitly anticipates 'a runtime-absent root surfaces as an empty/None collection below', and each_router (~:165) already has an empty_bypass path routing an empty collection downstream. But _collect_each_items navigates the dotted segments with getattr(obj, part) if hasattr else obj[part] and never guards obj is None — it crashes at :69 BEFORE returning the empty list that would trigger the bypass. The safety net exists; the navigation jumps over it. Latent sibling hole at :73 — list(obj) on a None root with zero segments raises the same way.

EXPECTED: a None/absent over source resolves to an empty collection -> each_router routes to empty_bypass -> downstream proceeds (fails-closed on 'no items'), exactly as the comment and bypass promise. No raw TypeError, and never a framework-internals stack trace that does not name the user's node or path.

FIX SHAPE (per existing design intent): break out of segment navigation when obj is None; treat missing mapping keys/attrs as None; return [] when the resolved obj is None. Guard :73 too. Emit a log.info (e.g. each_over_absent, fan_out=..., path=...) so an unexpected empty fan-out is diagnosable — silence would hide the Bug-2 class this often masks (see companion ticket for the None-output write-boundary question; the two are COMPLEMENTARY, not alternatives: this fix covers legitimately-absent upstream — untaken branch arm, skip_when — while the companion covers ran-and-violated-contract).

NOTE: _collect_each_items is the monopolized navigation rule shared by each_router AND flat_router (Each x Oracle fusion) — one fix covers both topologies; test both. TDD: minimal repro is a node declaring outputs=Foo returning None feeding | Each(over='node.items') — today TypeError, expected zero-item fan-out with the bypass taken. Also cover: absent root via untaken branch arm; dotted path where an INTERMEDIATE attr is None; consumer after the bypass still runs. Three-surface parity applies (map_over decorator form + programmatic Each).
close_reason: Guard _collect_each_items to fail-closed to [] on None/absent Each over-root (untaken branch/skip_when) or intermediate-None dotted attr, with each_over_absent log.info; each_router/flat_router now hit empty_bypass instead of crashing TypeError

title: Sweep verification for w74k.3.1
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on w74k.3.1
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" w74k.3.1`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (w74k.3.1)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update w74k.3.1 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add w74k.3.1 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for w74k.3.1
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show w74k.3.1` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/w74k.3.1/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" w74k.3.1
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (w74k.3.1)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update w74k.3.1 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update w74k.3.1 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/w74k.3.1/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add w74k.3.1 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the

title: Each: on_error='collect' partial-failure (typed EachFailure into the barrier) for .map fan-outs
description:
## What
Extend the Each fan-out modifier with on_error: 'raise' (current behavior, default) | 'collect'. With 'collect', make_each_redirect_fn (src/neograph/_oracle.py, the raw_fn.invoke wrapper — currently NO try/except) catches a per-item exception and writes a typed EachFailure{key, error_type, message} into the keyed barrier dict instead of aborting the run, so the barrier ALWAYS completes and consumers can assert set-equality (every planned key present as success-or-failure).

## Why
Requested by agent-stark stark-63q.26 (bounded research fan-out: 'one forced failure → typed Failed, no hang'). Today one throwing item aborts the whole .map run — the failure mode for any consumer fanning an agent sub-construct over external tools/APIs. agent-stark works around catchable faults with a Failed-as-normal-output union inside the sub-construct; only exceptions escaping the AGENT node still need this (the un-catchable remainder).

## Expectations after delivery
- Each(over=..., key=..., on_error='collect') → barrier dict contains EachFailure entries for thrown items, normal outputs for the rest; run completes.
- Default 'raise' unchanged — zero behavior change for existing consumers (piarch/derive_ensemble).

## Verification — integration & E2E
- Integration: a 3-item .map where item 2's sub-construct raises → barrier has 2 successes + 1 EachFailure{key='item2'}; run state completes; with on_error='raise' the same graph still aborts (regression).
- E2E: an agent-node sub-construct whose tool raises mid-loop → collected, not aborted.

## Acceptance
- Each accepts on_error with literal validation; 'collect' catches in the redirect fn and emits typed EachFailure keyed into the barrier; default unchanged; both paths covered by tests in tests/test_composition.py.

## Non-goals
- max_concurrency: already reachable via run(config={'max_concurrency': N}) passthrough — not part of this FR.
- item_timeout_s: no consumer AC requires it; file separately if ever needed.
notes:
FOLLOW-UP FIX (team-lead review): collect must not swallow GraphInterrupt/Command/cancellation.

- src/neograph/_oracle.py: added module-level 'from langgraph.errors import GraphBubbleUp'. Both each_redirect_fn and aeach_redirect_fn now re-raise GraphBubbleUp (umbrella base of GraphInterrupt + ParentCommand) BEFORE the broad 'except Exception as exc' collect path. asyncio.CancelledError is BaseException-only so it already escapes except Exception (left as-is). langgraph.errors is public API (passes the no-private-langgraph-imports guard); the except has 'as exc' so it is not the bare form the no-bare-except guard flags.

- New regression test tests/test_composition.py::TestEachOnErrorCollect::test_graph_interrupt_propagates_and_is_not_collected: collect-mode Each over a sub-construct whose inner node raises GraphInterrupt((Interrupt('need approval'),)). Asserts run() surfaces __interrupt__ (paused, propagated) AND no barrier value is an EachFailure (item2 not collected). Guard-verified: removing the 'except GraphBubbleUp: raise' block makes this test fail (interrupt swallowed into EachFailure, __interrupt__ absent). Note: without a checkpointer run() surfaces the bubble-up as a pause via result['__interrupt__'], not a raised exception -- test asserts the pause, which is the faithful behavior.

Gates re-run: ruff clean; tests/test_composition.py 80 passed (6 in TestEachOnErrorCollect); guard suites test_guards_sidecar_imports.py + test_guards_any_audit.py pass. Still NOT closed, NOT committed.
close_reason: Delivered: Each on_error='raise'|'collect' with typed EachFailure keyed into the barrier; default path unchanged; GraphBubbleUp (HITL/Command/cancel) re-raised, never collected. Three-surface parity + interrupt-propagation regression. Landed e6dbb00.
