title: gate_tools_when: deny is silently ignored — the gated tool runs anyway (approval checkpoint, not a gate)
description:
Found by independent verification of neograph-m6d3.4 (commit 43b5605). The gate node pauses correctly BEFORE the tools superstep (approve-before-side-effects holds, keystone green 4 ways), but the resume value is written to human_feedback (_wiring.py:781) and NEVER READ: grep shows zero routing consumers of HUMAN_FEEDBACK in src, and _wiring.py:794 adds an UNCONDITIONAL gate -> tools edge. Consequence: a user who resumes with a deny/reject payload gets the tool executed anyway. That is WORSE than no gate — it manufactures a false sense of a safety control. No deny test exists because deny is not implemented.

INVARIANT: a human gate that accepts a decision must honor the decision — approve routes to tools; deny must NOT execute the pending tool calls and must feed a denial back to the agent so the loop can continue reasoning (ToolMessage per pending tool_call, standard LangGraph review-tool-calls pattern), not crash or hang.

SCOPE (design decision first, then TDD): (1) define the resume contract — suggested {approved: bool, reason?: str} minimum; document whether edit-args is in scope or explicitly deferred; (2) gate -> conditional edge reading the resume decision: approve -> {node}__tools; deny -> back to {node}__agent with denial ToolMessages appended to neo_agent_messages so the LLM sees why; (3) failing tests FIRST: deny -> tool counter stays 0 AND the agent receives the denial and produces a final answer; approve path unchanged; both drivers; (4) docs: human-in-the-loop.mdx currently says approve-before-side-effects (accurate) — extend with the deny contract when built; until then the page must not imply deny works.

ANTI-BAND-AID: no in-body if-approved check inside the tools node (invisible to the checkpointer, wrong layer) — the decision belongs in Layer-1 topology (conditional edge), same as the rest of the agent cycle. Cite docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md.
design:
## Root Cause
_add_agent_cycle (_wiring.py:766-794) inserts a gate node on the router's tools arm. The gate interrupts BEFORE the tools superstep (approve-before-side-effects holds), and on resume writes the human decision to StateKeys.HUMAN_FEEDBACK. But nothing reads HUMAN_FEEDBACK for routing — line 794 is an unconditional edge gate_name -> names.tools. Deny is never implemented, so the tool always runs after resume.

## Fix Approach (minimal, Layer-1 topology)
Resume contract: {approved: bool, reason?: str} minimum. Edit-args EXPLICITLY DEFERRED (document as out of scope).

1. Replace the unconditional gate -> tools edge with a conditional edge:
   graph.add_conditional_edges(gate_name, gate_decision_router, path_map=[names.tools, names.agent])
   where gate_decision_router reads the resume decision from state: approved truthy -> names.tools; deny -> names.agent.
2. On DENY, append one denial ToolMessage per pending tool_call to neo_agent_messages_{field} so the LLM sees the rejection and can finalize (standard LangGraph review-tool-calls pattern). The pending tool_calls are on the last AIMessage in the messages channel. This synthesis belongs in the agent cycle (where msgs_key + pending tool_calls live), mirroring _agent_cycle._limit_messages — NOT an in-body if-approved check in the tools node (anti-band-aid; cite docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md).
3. Gate body must WRITE the decision to a routable channel (reuse HUMAN_FEEDBACK) AND, when deny, emit the denial ToolMessages on msgs_key. Because the gate needs msgs_key/field knowledge, build it via make_agent_cycle_bodies (agent-cycle layer) rather than inlining channel names in _wiring.py.

## Layer discipline
Decision-reading for routing = Layer-1 conditional edge (topology). Denial-message synthesis = Layer-2 agent-cycle body. No if-approved check inside the tools node body.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_tool_gating.py::TestToolGatingDenyKeystone::test_deny_does_not_run_tool_and_agent_finalizes (4 params: {run,arun} x {node,programmatic})
- All 4 FAIL: on resume with {approved: False}, side-effecting 'record' tool ran 1x (expected 0). 'DENY VIOLATION'.
- Root cause: the tool-gate's resume decision is written to HUMAN_FEEDBACK (_wiring.py:781) but never read for routing; _wiring.py:794 adds an UNCONDITIONAL gate -> {node}__tools edge, so any resume value (approve OR deny) falls through to the tools superstep and executes the pending tool.
## Trace-similar (same bug pattern elsewhere?)
Pattern category: a decision-bearing interrupt whose resume value is written to StateKeys.HUMAN_FEEDBACK but never READ for routing, followed by an unconditional downstream edge.

Two interrupt sites write HUMAN_FEEDBACK; NEITHER is read for routing anywhere in src (grep: zero routing consumers):
1. _wiring.py:781 — tool-gate (THIS bug, whq0). Contract IS to gate tool execution on the decision -> unconditional gate->tools edge is a real bug.
2. _wiring.py:823 — _add_operator_check (Operator modifier). Contract per modifiers.py:484 is 'pause graph for human review' = acknowledge-and-continue; the compiler continues linearly (compiler.py:487,544) regardless of decision. Operator does NOT promise to route on the decision, and human_feedback remains readable on the state bus for downstream nodes. So NOT the same bug — but it shares the write-and-never-read shape and would silently ignore a {approved: False} if a user expected it to skip. Noted, not filed: Operator's approve/deny semantics are a separate design question, out of scope for whq0.

No other unconditional-edge-after-decision-interrupt instances. whq0 is the only site where the gate's stated purpose (gate tool side effects) is contradicted by the topology.
## Codebase Disease Scan (whq0)

Pattern: a decision-bearing interrupt() whose resume value must gate downstream routing, but is followed by an UNCONDITIONAL edge that runs the gated work regardless of the decision.
Scan command: grep -rn 'interrupt(' src/neograph/ && grep -rn 'add_edge|add_conditional_edges' src/neograph/_wiring.py
Method: SYNTACTIC (exact-form enumeration of interrupt sites + their outgoing edges) — no fan-out needed.
Total instances found: 1 (the motivating site)

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | _wiring.py:780->794 | gate interrupt + unconditional gate->tools edge | MIGRATE | THE bug (whq0). Fix replaces 794 with a conditional edge reading the decision. |
| 2 | _wiring.py:822->827 (_add_operator_check) | operator interrupt + linear continuation | ALLOWLIST | Operator contract (modifiers.py:484) is pause-for-review = acknowledge-and-continue, NOT gate. Decision remains readable on the state bus (human_feedback). Not a gate promise -> not the disease. |
| 3 | hitl.py:56 (ask_human) | interrupt() passthrough inside a Layer-2 tool | ALLOWLIST | Resume value is returned to tool code (typed via resume_model), not a topology routing decision. N/A to this disease. |

Conclusion: the fix addresses the single MIGRATE instance. No other sites need the conditional-edge treatment.
## Architect Review (fix design)

1. Root cause correctness — LOW (correct). Verified: HUMAN_FEEDBACK written at _wiring.py:781, zero routing readers in src, unconditional edge at 794. Reproduction fails exactly as predicted (tool runs 1x on deny).

2. Fix minimality — LOW. Replacing one unconditional edge with a conditional edge + a deny message-emit is the minimal change. No IR/schema change; HUMAN_FEEDBACK channel already exists.

3. Architecture compliance — LOW. Matches three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md: routing decision = Layer-1 topology (conditional edge); interrupt already sits at a checkpointer-visible boundary node (sec 1.2 purity test); denial ToolMessage synthesis is node-boundary output built in the agent-cycle layer where msgs_key lives. No in-body if-approved check in the tools node.

4. Regression risk — LOW/MEDIUM. Approve path: existing TestToolGatingKeystone resumes {approved: True} and must stay green (conditional edge routes approved->tools). Verify no-gate path (else branch, line 795-799) is untouched. Operator/ask_human paths untouched.

5. FINDING (MEDIUM) — router must read a FRESH per-visit decision, NOT a persistent stale channel. HUMAN_FEEDBACK is a single overwritten channel; a multi-turn agent whose gate fires on turn 1 (approve) then does NOT fire on turn 3 would leave a stale 'approved' in HUMAN_FEEDBACK. The gate router must distinguish three cases on EACH visit: (a) gate fired + denied -> route to agent (deny msgs appended); (b) gate fired + approved -> route to tools; (c) gate condition falsy / did not fire -> route to tools (proceed). Recommend the gate body emit an explicit per-visit routing signal (or the router key off freshly-appended deny ToolMessages) rather than reading a persistent HUMAN_FEEDBACK that can go stale across turns. The fix atom MUST handle case (c) and the stale-across-turns case.

6. FINDING (MEDIUM) — fail-closed default. A gate is a SAFETY control: any resume value that is not explicitly {approved: True} (missing key, non-dict, malformed) should be treated as DENY, not approve. Make the approved-check explicit and fail-closed.

7. Test coverage — LOW/MEDIUM. Reproduction covers deny keystone (tool==0 + finalize) x {run,arun} x {node,programmatic}. Recommend the fix ALSO assert: (a) approve path still runs tool exactly once (existing keystone covers this); (b) a denial ToolMessage actually reaches the agent (assert the agent's message history contains a ToolMessage per pending tool_call after deny) so 'agent sees why' is pinned, not just inferred from finalization; (c) multi-turn stale-channel case if feasible.

## Verdict: PROCEED with two MEDIUM must-address items (fresh per-visit decision incl. case-(c); fail-closed default). No HIGH findings. Design is sound and minimal.
## Triage decision
Verdict: PROCEED to fix (no HIGH, no NEEDS_USER_INPUT). Two MEDIUM findings are concrete implementation requirements, not design ambiguities requiring human direction, so NOT NEEDS_REFINEMENT/NEEDS_USER_INPUT. Folded into the fix contract below. Proceeding to atom .7 (fix).

## Fix must-address (from review, binding on the fix atom)
- M5: gate router reads a FRESH per-visit decision. Handle all three cases each visit: approve->tools, deny->agent(+deny msgs), condition-did-not-fire->tools. Do NOT rely on a persistent HUMAN_FEEDBACK that goes stale across turns.
- M6: fail-closed — anything not explicitly {approved: True} = DENY.
- M7: add assertion that a denial ToolMessage (one per pending tool_call) reaches the agent after deny.
## Fix applied
Files:
- src/neograph/_agent_cycle.py: added make_tool_gate_bodies(node, gate_condition) + _gate_approved() helper. The gate body interrupts on a truthy condition; on resume, fail-closed: only {approved: True} approves. On DENY it appends one denial ToolMessage per pending tool_call to neo_agent_messages_{field} (answering the tool_calls so the LLM sees why + so the message history stays valid) and records HUMAN_FEEDBACK. gate_router reads a FRESH per-visit signal from the message channel: last msg is a ToolMessage (deny answered the calls) -> route to {node}__agent; else (approve/no-fire, tool_calls still pending) -> {node}__tools.
- src/neograph/_wiring.py: replaced the unconditional gate->tools edge with add_conditional_edges(gate_name, gate_router, [tools, agent]); gate body now comes from make_tool_gate_bodies (agent-cycle layer owns the message channel).

Addressed all review must-address items: M5 fresh per-visit decision incl. no-fire case; M6 fail-closed; M7 explicit denial-ToolMessage assertion.

## Verification
- Reproduction test TestToolGatingDenyKeystone (4 params: {run,arun}x{node,programmatic}) now PASS + M7 denial-message assertion.
- Approve keystone TestToolGatingKeystone unchanged/green.
- MUTATION verified: removing the denial-message append reintroduces the exact 'DENY VIOLATION: record ran 1x' failure across all 4 params (confirms the append is load-bearing; the routing edge alone is not — a ToolMessage has no tool_calls so the tools node no-ops regardless). Restored -> green.
- Full suite: 2372 passed (baseline 2368 + 4 deny params), 0 failed. Lint + mypy clean.
- Layer discipline: routing = Layer-1 conditional edge; denial synthesis = Layer-2 agent-cycle body; no in-body if-approved check in the tools node (three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md).
## Sweep Verification (whq0)
Re-scan command: grep -rn 'add_edge(gate_name|add_conditional_edges' src/neograph/_wiring.py (+ compiled-graph edge introspection)
Pre-fix instances: 1 (MIGRATE)
Post-fix instances: 0

| # | Content match | Pre-fix disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
|---|---------------|---------------------|----------------|----------|
| 1 | unconditional gate->tools edge (_wiring.py) | MIGRATE | REPLACED by add_conditional_edges(gate_name, gate_router, [tools, agent]); compiled gate now has 2 conditional edges (tools+agent), 0 unconditional | YES |
| 2 | _add_operator_check interrupt+linear | ALLOWLIST | unchanged (acknowledge-and-continue contract holds) | YES |
| 3 | ask_human passthrough (hitl.py) | ALLOWLIST | unchanged (tool-local resume, not topology) | YES |

## Structural guard (required: 1 MIGRATE row)
tests/test_guards_ir_compiler.py::TestToolGateRoutesConditionally — inspects COMPILED graph topology (not source text):
- POSITIVE: real gated graph routes to BOTH __tools and __agent, all conditional; asserts not _gate_is_diseased.
- NEGATIVE meta 1: hand-built unconditional gate->tools edge is flagged diseased.
- NEGATIVE meta 2 (would-be-missed): a CONDITIONAL gate edge with NO deny/__agent arm is still flagged (conditional alone is insufficient).
- N/A meta: ungated agent graph -> not diseased (guard never fires on ungated pipelines).
Guard mutation-verified on the REAL graph: reverting _wiring.py to the unconditional edge makes the positive guard FAIL ('gate has no deny (agent) arm'). Restored -> green. 4/4 guard tests pass.
## E2E verify
No external system involved (no adapter/API/serialization/protocol). The fix is HITL routing topology internal to the compiler + agent cycle.
However, the regression tests ARE end-to-end against the real engine: TestToolGatingDenyKeystone drives the real compile()/run()/arun() entrypoints against a real langgraph MemorySaver, exercising the actual interrupt -> checkpoint -> resume(Command) cycle (no engine mocking; LLM behavior via history-driven fakes only). Verified across both drivers {run, arun} and both API surfaces {@node, programmatic Node}. External-systems E2E: SKIPPED (N/A).

     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"

     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/pjqe/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" pjqe
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (pjqe)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update pjqe --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update pjqe --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/pjqe/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add pjqe codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Propagate RunnableConfig into tool .invoke in the ReAct loop (astream_events tool visibility)
description:
## What
neograph's agent/ReAct loop invokes tools WITHOUT the run's RunnableConfig: _agent_cycle.py:346 tool_fn.invoke(tc['args']) and :397 await tool_fn.ainvoke(tc['args']) — no config=config. Pass the node's config through so LangChain callbacks propagate and on_tool_start/on_tool_end appear in the compiled graph's astream_events.
## Why
Consumers (agent-stark) build live activity feeds over astream_events; today tool calls are invisible at the event stream (only the LLM/node events fire), so a UI can't show 'agent called search_graph(...)' live without scraping state. Relates to neograph-q8ec (custom stream events) — same goal, different mechanism.
## Verify
Integration: an agent node with a tool; drive compiled.astream_events(version='v2'); assert on_tool_start/on_tool_end fire with the tool name + args + result. Both sync and async tool paths.
## Acceptance
- tool .invoke/.ainvoke receive the node RunnableConfig; on_tool_start/end visible via astream_events; existing tool-loop tests green.
notes:
Fixed: threaded node RunnableConfig into tool execution at both agent-cycle call sites in src/neograph/_agent_cycle.py — tools_body line 351 (tool_fn.invoke(tc['args'], config=config)) and atools_body line 402 (await tool_fn.ainvoke(tc['args'], config=config)). _tool_loop.py did NOT need the fix: it no longer contains a tool-execution site (tool exec was moved into the agent cycle bodies); its .invoke/.ainvoke calls are all LLM calls via _CoercingToolWrapper. Core regression = config-capturing tool asserting the tool receives a non-None config at BOTH sync (run/graph.invoke) and async (graph.ainvoke) call sites — both RED before the fix (captured config was None), GREEN after. NOTE: an astream_events(v2) on_tool_start/on_tool_end assertion was NOT a valid RED test on its own — langchain_core 1.4.0 propagates callbacks via the var_child_runnable_config contextvar, so a real StructuredTool already fires those events without explicit config=. The explicit config= is still the documented-correct fix (contextvar propagation is fragile across thread/executor/context boundaries). Kept one astream_events test as an end-to-end visibility check.

Fake fallout (expected, reported): passing config= broke tool fakes whose invoke(self, args) had no config kwarg (real LangChain BaseTools accept config; the fakes modeled the old config-less contract). Updated FakeTool (tests/fakes.py) + inline tool fakes in tests/test_hitl.py, test_agent_subgraph_keystone.py, test_tool_gating.py, test_lint.py, test_composition.py, test_guards_ir_compiler.py, tests/modes/test_output_strategies.py, test_llm_internals.py to accept config=None, **kwargs. title: Sweep verification for neograph-p8wz
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-p8wz
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-p8wz`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-p8wz)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-p8wz --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-p8wz sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

description:

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-p8wz/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-p8wz
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-p8wz)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-p8wz --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-p8wz --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-p8wz/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-p8wz codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Retire hand-rolled engine-duplicating plumbing: neo_* strip tax and STREAM_CUSTOM flag (use the engine's own abstractions)
description:
The consumer-chair audit (2026-07-03) classified ~10 percent of the epic's code as category-4: re-implementation of signals/filters the engine already provides. Each instance exists because neograph hand-rolled a parallel mechanism instead of using a LangGraph abstraction. Design source: docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md.

THE INVARIANT (lead with this): when the engine offers an abstraction for a concern, neograph must use it; a hand-rolled parallel mechanism is a standing violation even when it works. The deliverable of this ticket is the DELETION of the hand-rolled mechanisms, not their improvement.

ITEM A — the neo_* strip tax (the root one). _strip_internals (now in _state_keys) and the stripping half of _finalize_chunk exist ONLY because framework keys (neo_schema_fingerprint, neo_node_fingerprints, neo_each_item, CONFIG_INPUT echo...) live in USER state channels and must be scrubbed at every exit (run/arun return, values-mode chunks, updates-mode chunks, sub-construct returns). LangGraph's OWN abstraction for this is schema separation: StateGraph(state_schema, input_schema=..., output_schema=...) — output filtering at the engine level. RESEARCH ATOM FIRST, these are the questions that decide feasibility: (1) does output_schema filter stream_mode=values chunks and updates chunks, or only invoke/ainvoke results? (2) do excluded-from-output channels still persist in checkpoints (fingerprints MUST persist — that is why they are in state)? (3) how does it interact with sub-construct isolated schemas and with get_state (auto-resume reads fingerprints back via channel_values)? If the engine filter covers the surfaces: declare output_schema excluding neo_* at compile time, then DELETE _strip_internals call sites and the stripping arm of _finalize_chunk (the helpers die or shrink to nothing; the four exit-point wraps in run/arun and the per-chunk strip disappear). If research shows a genuine engine gap (e.g. updates-mode not filtered), document the gap precisely in the ticket and keep ONLY the minimal residue, with a comment citing the gap.

ITEM B — STREAM_CUSTOM flag plumbing. progress.py's _custom_stream_active + the STREAM_CUSTOM config key set by the streaming verbs (_mark_stream_custom/_wants_custom in runner.py) re-implement a signal LangGraph already provides: get_stream_writer() returns a no-op writer when no custom-mode consumer is attached. Replace the flag plumbing with writer-presence detection for the warn-once; delete _mark_stream_custom/_wants_custom and the config key. Keep the warn-once behavior itself (that is Layer-2 value) — only the detection mechanism changes. Verify the no-op-writer semantics against the installed langgraph version first; if it cannot distinguish (e.g. returns a real writer under a non-custom stream), document and keep the flag with a citation.

ITEM C (minor, docs-only) — unconditional Operator adds nothing over raw interrupt_before; its value is the CONDITIONAL predicate form. One honest paragraph in the Operator docs saying so, steering users with static gate needs to interrupt_before via the facade.

ANTI-BAND-AID: no shims layered over the old mechanisms during migration — each item flips atomically behind its research answer. Audit step after A: grep for any remaining neo_-stripping logic outside the single residue site. Every existing pinning test (values/updates strip, custom/messages passthrough, prefix-strip invariant) must be RE-POINTED at the engine-level filter, not deleted — the behavioral contract (users never see neo_*) is unchanged; only its enforcement moves into the engine. Independent-review gate before closing.
design:
## Core Invariant
When the engine (LangGraph 1.2.4) offers a first-class abstraction for a concern, neograph must USE it by DECLARING at compile time (output_schema on StateGraph) rather than hand-wrapping the engine's runtime output — and any surviving hand-rolled residue must carry a written, cited engine-gap justification.

## Implementation Plan (reuse-first, evidence-scoped)
1. DECLARE, don't wrap (Item A core). In compiler.py:241 pass output_schema to StateGraph. Reuse the fields compile_state_model (state.py:96) already built — do NOT recompute 'user fields'. Build a Pydantic submodel from the state model containing every field whose name does NOT start with StateKeys.FRAMEWORK_PREFIX ('neo_'). This exactly mirrors _strip_internals (prefix-based), so node_id/project_root/human_feedback still surface (invariant test test_invariants.py:535 depends on it). input_schema STAYS UNSET (R1: it hard-filters the fingerprints run() seeds via initial input). Do this at BOTH the top-level compile and the recursive sub-construct compile (compiler.py:417) — the child's output_schema = its non-neo_ fields (surfaces sub.output).
2. DELETE the 4 dead strips atomically behind step 1: runner.py:509, runner.py:682, _subconstruct.py:169, _subconstruct.py:178. No shim overlap. The _strip_internals import in _subconstruct.py can go once both its uses are gone.
3. KEEP the 2 stream arms (runner.py:443 values, :447 updates) — engine gap: stream_mode=values/updates chunks are NOT filtered by output_schema in 1.2.4 (R1). Add a comment on each arm citing docs/design/langgraph-output-schema-research-2026-07-03.md (R1). _strip_internals stays alive for these two only.
4. Item B (STREAM_CUSTOM) — DOCUMENTED KEEP, not deletion (R4). Add a citation comment at progress.py:110 and the STREAM_CUSTOM def (_state_keys.py:58-64): get_stream_writer() returns the PRIVATE langgraph.runtime._no_op_stream_writer (config.py:196 / runtime.py:206) with no public sentinel, so the config flag is the robust discriminator. Leave _mark_stream_custom/_wants_custom/_custom_stream_active in place.
5. Item C (docs) — one honest paragraph in website/src/content/docs/node-api/modifier-kwargs.mdx: unconditional Operator adds nothing over raw interrupt_before; its value is the CONDITIONAL predicate form; steer static-gate users to interrupt_before via the facade. Run npm run build in website/.
6. Tests — RE-POINT (do not delete) the 4 dead-site pinning tests at the engine filter (contract unchanged, users still never see neo__): test_invariants.py:535, test_streaming.py:208, test_composition.py:532, test_composition.py:549, test_topologies.py:269. KEEP the _finalize_* stream-arm tests as-is. ADD: (a) a test that output_schema does NOT filter get_state()/channel_values (R2 auto-resume fingerprint read-back), (b) an arun batch-exit neo-free test symmetric to the sync one (guards the :682 deletion), (c) [refine .20] a sub-construct with TWO internal nodes producing the SAME output type asserting last-wins child return (guards multi-producer value-correctness).
7. Audit (anti-band-aid): after step 2, grep for any neo_-stripping logic outside the 2 stream arms + the single _strip_internals helper — must be zero. Independent-review gate before closing.

## Three-surface parity
Compile-layer change (state model -> output_schema) affects all three API surfaces identically; verify a run() through @node, declarative Node.scripted, and programmatic Node()|Modifier still yields neo_-free results (the composition + invariant tests already cover multiple surfaces).

## Refinement (neograph-8unp.20, 2026-07-03) — child output_schema reconciliation
AUTHORITATIVE: child output_schema = child state-model fields NOT starting with neo_ (SAME filter as top-level compile, step 1). This exactly mirrors today's _strip_internals(sub_graph.invoke(...)) then _scan_subgraph_output reverse-scan (last-wins across multiple same-type internal producers).
DO NOT declare child output_schema = 'exactly sub.output field' — that would collapse multi-producer channels and could change which value _scan_subgraph_output (_subconstruct.py:43, reverse-scan of ALL stripped values) returns. The research doc R3 verdict line has been corrected to match.
This is captured in step 1 (child = non-neo_ fields) and step 6(c) (multi-producer test).
notes:
2026-07-03 maintainer-approved framing for Item A (append verbatim into research/implement atoms):

THE KEYS STAY — THE STRIP DIES. The neo_* channels are NOT the disease. Group 1 (oracle gen_id/model, each_item, subgraph_input, loop counters/history, oracle collectors, agent-cycle messages/tool_log/budget) exists because one neograph definition compiles to MANY LangGraph nodes (Oracle = router + N generators + barrier; Each = router + workers + barrier; agent = agent/tools/parse cycle) and those synthesized nodes pass framework data between themselves through state channels — which is the engine's OWN mechanism for inter-node data. Group 2 (schema/node fingerprints) lives in state because checkpoints persist state — that is how versioning metadata durably attaches to a thread. Nobody removes or relocates the information.

The disease is that compile() never DECLARES which channels are framework-internal, so every exit surface is hand-wrapped: ~10 _strip_internals wrap sites (4 exits in run, 4 in arun, sub-construct return) + the stripping arm of _finalize_chunk per streamed chunk. That wrapping is the wrapper-owns-the-execution-path pattern this epic deleted everywhere else; the runner verbs cannot be thin while every one must remember to scrub.

INTERFERENCE vs USE (the distinction that makes this sound): interfering with the engine = intercepting/wrapping its RUNTIME behavior. Using the engine = DECLARING to it at compile time and letting it run untouched. StateGraph natively accepts input_schema / state_schema / output_schema; the engine itself filters invoke results down to output_schema — first-class mechanism for internal working channels (LangGraph's prebuilt agent hides its own step-tracking channels the same way). compile() already knows exactly which fields are user outputs (it built the state model) — declare output_schema = user fields, and enforcement moves from a runtime wrapper we own to a compile-time declaration the engine honors. Same user-visible contract; this is the same move as Operator being a compile-emitted boundary node rather than runtime interception.

RESEARCH QUESTIONS (empirical, against the installed langgraph — decide feasibility per surface):
R1. Does output_schema filter (a) invoke/ainvoke results, (b) stream_mode=values chunks, (c) stream_mode=updates chunks? Expectation: (a) yes, (b) verify, (c) probably NO (updates emits raw per-node writes — a synthesized barrier writing neo_oracle_* would appear). If (c) is unfiltered: a one-line residue survives for updates-mode chunks ONLY, commented as a cited engine gap — documented fallback, not a silent band-aid.
R2. Do channels excluded from output_schema still persist in checkpoints and surface via get_state channel_values? MUST be yes (auto-resume reads fingerprints back there; that path never goes through output filtering). Verify with a fingerprint round-trip.
R3. Sub-construct interaction: child isolated schema + parent type-scan read internal state directly — verify unaffected.
R4 (Item B): does get_stream_writer() return a detectable no-op when no custom-mode consumer is attached, distinguishing live-consumer from non-streaming driver for the warn-once? Verify against installed version; if indistinguishable, the STREAM_CUSTOM flag stays with a citation.

If research answers come back bad (e.g. values-mode chunks unfiltered), the strip STAYS and the outcome is a documented engine-gap justification where today there is an unexamined habit. Either way the mechanism ends up either the engine's, or ours WITH A WRITTEN REASON.
2026-07-03 RESEARCH COMPLETE — empirical, against langgraph 1.2.4. Full report: docs/design/langgraph-output-schema-research-2026-07-03.md. The ticket is RE-SCOPED by evidence:

R1: output_schema filters invoke/ainvoke ONLY; values/updates stream chunks (sync+async) are NOT filtered. CRITICAL: never declare input_schema — it is a hard input filter and silently drops the fingerprints run() seeds through the initial input; declare output_schema alone (keyword-only kwarg in 1.2.4).
R2: excluded channels persist in checkpoints AND get_state is unfiltered — auto-resume fingerprint read-back needs zero change.
R3: the sub-construct CHILD compile can declare output_schema (exactly sub.output field) — kills both strips in make_subgraph_fn.
R4: STREAM_CUSTOM CANNOT be replaced — get_stream_writer() never returns the public no-op sentinel in 1.2.4 (always a live closure); the only discriminator is a private freevars probe, more fragile than the flag. ITEM B RESOLVES AS DOCUMENTED KEEP, not deletion.
R5: managed values do not persist in checkpoints — do not fit fingerprints; output_schema is the right mechanism.

Reality correction: SIX strip sites, not ten (code already consolidated). IMPLEMENTATION SCOPE, final: (1) declare output_schema=user-fields at main compile + sub-construct child compile, input_schema stays unset; (2) DELETE 4 strips: runner.py:509 (run), runner.py:682 (arun), _subconstruct.py:169+:178; (3) KEEP 2 strips: _finalize_by_mode values arm (runner.py:443) + updates arm (:447), each commented citing the research doc (engine gap: streamed chunks unfiltered in 1.2.4); (4) Item B: keep STREAM_CUSTOM, add citation comment; (5) Item C unchanged (docs paragraph); (6) re-point existing pinning tests at the engine filter for the 4 dead sites (contract unchanged: users never see neo_*), keep stream-arm tests as-is; add a test that output_schema does NOT filter get_state (pins the auto-resume assumption against future langgraph upgrades).

title: ask_human(): typed mid-loop HITL ask — pure Layer-2 sugar over langgraph interrupt() + A.5 safety lint
description:
The namesake deliverable of neograph-m6d3, correctly scoped now that the mechanism has shipped. The capability EXISTS: raw langgraph.types.interrupt() inside an agent tool works through neograph today with exactly-once pre-interrupt tool execution (tests/test_agent_subgraph_keystone.py, both drivers). What is missing is ONLY the typed contract and its lint visibility. Design sources: docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md (purity test, Layer-2 definition); consumer-chair gap analysis 2026-07-03 (marginal value = typed resume validation + lint visibility + documented contract; capability contributes ZERO).

SCOPE IN (the whole ticket, ~4 files, ~250-350 LoC, no compiler/topology changes):
1. src/neograph/hitl.py — ask_human(payload: BaseModel, resume_model: type[BaseModel] | None = None). Body is a PASSTHROUGH: langgraph interrupt(payload.model_dump()) then resume_model.model_validate(returned) when resume_model given, else return the raw dict. Roughly 40-60 LoC including docstring. Export from neograph __init__.
2. Lint rule(s) in lint.py — the A.5 safety deliverable and the real prize: ask_human is a first-class marker the validator can SEE (raw interrupt inside an opaque tool callable is invisible to lint). New issue kinds: ask_human_in_mutating_node (ERROR or WARN: ask_human reachable from an act-mode node) and, if cheaply detectable, mutating-tool-precedes-ask ordering WARN (non-idempotent side effect before an interrupt in the same node can double-fire — the residual Level-B case; cite docs/design/durable-execution-replay-research-2026-07-02.md).
3. Tests: integration (typed payload pause -> resume -> tool receives validated ResumeModel; malformed resume raises at the boundary with a clear error, not deep in tool code); E2E reusing the keystone two-tool idempotency pattern but through ask_human; lint fixtures (tests/check_fixtures/should_fail/ask_human_in_act_node.py + a should_pass twin).
4. Docs: human-in-the-loop.mdx gains the mid-loop section with ask_human as the blessed path AND an explicit note that raw langgraph interrupt() remains supported.

SCOPE OUT — THE ANTI-REBOOT CLAUSE (this is the acceptance gate): the helper must contain ZERO execution logic. No interrupt mechanics, no resume plumbing, no Command handling, no checkpoint interaction, no topology or state-channel changes. If the implementation finds itself touching compiler.py, _wiring.py, _agent_cycle.py, runner.py, or state.py (beyond lint.py), it is rebuilding what m6d3 + LangGraph already deliver — STOP and re-read the keystone test. title: Agent-cycle: raise LangGraph recursion_limit to cover max_iterations*2 supersteps
description: Latent gap introduced by the inline agent cycle (neograph-m6d3.2). ReAct turns are now LangGraph SUPERSTEPS ({node}__agent + {node}__tools per turn), whereas the monolith ran the whole loop inside ONE superstep. LangGraph's default recursion_limit is 25, so an agent that legitimately loops beyond ~12 turns hits GraphRecursionError BEFORE the max_iterations guard (default 20) can force-finalize — i.e. the graceful forced-final edge is unreachable at the default max_iterations. Fix: set config['recursion_limit'] at invoke time (runner _prepare/_aprepare) to >= max(agent max_iterations)*2 + slack across the construct's agent/act nodes (config prep, not an engine verb — no 521j interaction). Not hit by current tests/examples (few turns, or max_iterations=3), but bites a real long-running agent. TDD: an agent that loops max_iterations>12 turns must force-finalize gracefully, not raise GraphRecursionError.
close_reason: Folded into m6d3.2 per leader decision. Runner _prepare/_aprepare now raise recursion_limit to a floor = 25 + sum over agent/act nodes of (max_iterations*2+3), only when below the floor (never clobbers a larger user value). CORRECTED understanding: a FLAT top-level agent does NOT crash at default (LangGraph's top-level invoke default is higher than 25); the real crash is a NESTED agent (sub-construct), where LangGraph applies default recursion_limit=25 to the child invoke — example 13's shipped shape. The raised top-level limit propagates into the child invoke, fixing it. Proven by test_forced_finalize_reachable_for_nested_agent_at_default_recursion_limit (run+arun) which fails without the floor (GraphRecursionError at ~turn 12) and passes with it. Full suite 2339 passed.

design:
## Core Invariant
An agent/act node's ReAct turns are REAL parent supersteps ({node}__agent / {node}__tools /
{node}__parse) with all mutable loop state in neo_-prefixed channels — so every payoff
(tool-gating, streaming, honest budgets) must be delivered by acting on those real nodes
and channels, NEVER by reintroducing in-node loop logic or leaking non-neo_ state.

## ORCHESTRATOR DECISION (neograph-8unp.21 refine): execute COHESIVELY (a+b+c+d in one chain).
The research's SPLIT recommendation below is preserved for the maintainer's future reorganization,
but this execution keeps m6d3.4 whole — the chain's review/triage/write-test gates supply the
design scrutiny and TDD the split was protecting. Item (a)'s API (`gate_tools_when=`) was confirmed
by architect review to be a sound conventional default (mirrors the existing `skip_when` Node-field
pattern) — NO maintainer API decision required. Item (d) = doc-only. Two refinements folded in below
(steps 3 and 6), superseding the prior orchestrator commitments.

## Scoping Recommendation: SPLIT (research's original recommendation — see decision above)
The four sub-items have fundamentally different natures:
- (a) tool-gating = a NEW public feature: new API surface + new wiring in _add_agent_cycle
  + resume-payload typing + should_pass/should_fail fixtures + 6-cell parity + review gate.
- (b) streaming = TEST-ONLY assertion riding on existing stream/astream verbs + real nodes.
- (c) honest budgets = mostly a TEST (budget already checkpointed per-turn); optional mypy
  narrowing.
- (d) A.5 lint = a near no-op reconciliation (the migration-lint was never built).
Bundling (a) with the verification items would let (a)'s real API design get shortchanged
under a "payoffs" framing. RECOMMEND: split into
  m6d3.4a — tool-gating HITL (the real feature: API + wiring + fixtures + 6-cell).
  m6d3.4b — payoffs verification + lint reconciliation: (b) astream turn-visibility test,
            (c) turn-granularity budget E2E across a checkpoint (+ decide mypy narrowing),
            (d) confirm/keep ask_human_in_mutating_node lint, correct doc line 341-342.
Rationale: (a) alone touches production wiring and public API and carries the parent's
Binding-Condition-1 risk (the forced-parse/router edge); (b)(c)(d) are low-risk
verification/cleanup that pair cleanly and unblock rsd1 docs. If the user prefers finer
grain, (d) can be its own trivial ticket, but (b)+(c) should stay together (same keystone
harness). Either way (a) MUST be its own task.

## Implementation Plan
### Item (a) — tool-gating HITL [its own task]
1. Design the API FIRST (record before coding): how does a user declare "gate tools on
   this agent node"? Recommended: a @node kwarg (e.g. gate_tools_when=<condition>) that
   maps to an Operator-like condition carried on the Node, since the user cannot name the
   synthesized {node}__tools. Decide the resume-payload contract (boolean-approve like
   Operator, vs a typed value that can rewrite tool args) — pin the typing.
2. REUSE the interrupt() body from _add_operator_check (_wiring.py:773-795), do NOT invent a

title: Branch-arm bare Nodes skip validation, IR-normalization, lint, and verify walks
description:
Adjacent to neograph-tdbb (which scopes to scripted-shim/DI/fingerprint collection via iter_nodes). The disease-scan for tdbb found the SAME _BranchNode-blind-spot in FIVE more hand-rolled construct.nodes walks that do NOT go through iter_nodes, so the tdbb iter_nodes fix does not reach them:

1. _construct_validation.py:128 (_validate_node_chain producer registration) — bare arm Nodes (forward.py true_only/false_only are bare Node objects) are never producer-registered or type-validated at the parent level. Sub-constructs in arms self-validate at their own Construct.__init__; bare arm Nodes do not.
2. _ir_normalize.py:226 — 'if not isinstance(item, Node): continue' skips _BranchNode, so oracle_gen_type / fan_out_param normalization never runs for arm nodes. An Each/Oracle @node placed directly in a branch arm would miss IR normalization.
3. lint.py:214 (_walk) — _BranchNode falls through the 'if not isinstance(item, Node): return' guard, so DI-binding + template-placeholder lint never inspects arm nodes.
4. verify.py:90/163 (_walk + _has_llm_nodes) — arm nodes skipped by the verify tree-walk.
5. runner.py:206 (adjacency builder) — arm nodes contribute no edges to the adjacency map.

Root cause is identical to tdbb: _BranchNode sentinels carry _BranchMeta.true_arm_nodes/false_arm_nodes that every non-arm-aware tree walk ignores. Scope decision needed: after tdbb makes iter_nodes descend, migrate these five walks to route through iter_nodes (uniform), OR give each its own arm descent. Anti-band-aid: prefer routing through the single iter_nodes source of truth. Note the DEDUP opportunity: state.py compile_state_model (state.py:102/126-241) already hand-rolls a CORRECT arm walk; once iter_nodes descends, that manual walk can likely be retired too.

Blocked-by: neograph-tdbb (land the iter_nodes descent first, then migrate these consumers).
design:
## Root Cause
Five (documented) + six (scan-found) hand-rolled construct.nodes tree walks visit only top-level items and short-circuit on _BranchNode via isinstance(item, Node)/(item, Construct) guards (or, at __main__.py:166, a hasattr('modifiers') guard the empty-ModifierSet sentinel passes but classify_modifiers finds nothing in). Arm contents (_BranchMeta.true_arm_nodes/false_arm_nodes) are reachable only via _neo_branch_meta, so they are invisible to: _construct_validation.py:128, _ir_normalize.py:226, lint.py:214, verify.py:90/163, runner.py:206, compiler.py:146/162/183, construct.py:170, __main__.py:165, _subconstruct.py:118. _wiring.py recursively _compile()s arm CONSTRUCTS (self-validating) but bare arm NODES go straight to make_node_fn, bypassing all compile-time guards.

## Fix Design (REFINED post-architect-review — VERDICT was NEEDS_REFINEMENT, 4 findings folded in)

### Primitives — home is _ir_branch.py (NOT construct.py) [FINDING 1, HIGH]
construct.py imports _validate_node_chain and normalize_ir from modules BELOW it; those modules would circular-import if they pulled the primitive from construct.py. _ir_branch.py already owns _BranchNode/_BranchMeta, is the neutral low-level IR home, and needs only item.nodes + _BranchNode + _neo_branch_meta.
- iter_with_arms(construct) -> Iterator[Node | Construct]: yield each item in construct.nodes; for each _BranchNode yield its arm items (true then false) IN PLACE OF the sentinel. ONE-LEVEL expansion — do NOT recurse into sub-constructs (arm Constructs yielded opaque so each caller's existing isinstance(item,Construct) recursion / _wiring recursive _compile handles them; recursing here would double-process).
- iter_item_slots(construct) -> Iterator[tuple[MutableSequence, int]]: yield (container_list, index) for every item slot incl. arm meta-list slots, so model_copy write-back targets the correct slot (top-level construct.nodes[i] OR meta.true_arm_nodes[j]/false_arm_nodes[j]).

### Read-only migrations (for item in construct.nodes -> iter_with_arms): sites 1,3,4,5,6,7,8,10,11.
### Write-back migrations (via iter_item_slots): site 2 (_ir_normalize) and site 9 (construct.py:170 llm_config/renderer inheritance).

### Known-limitation decisions [FINDINGS 2 & 3, MEDIUM]
- Site 1: registering conditional arm outputs as parent-scope producers is INTENDED (matches the state fields compile_state_model actually creates). Cross-arm leakage (false-arm node reading true-arm output) is NOT caught — not a regression (uncaught today); document in code comment + a pin test.
- Site 2: normalize_ir peer_field_names stays top-level-only for this fix; an arm Each reading an arm-SIBLING producer would misinfer fan_out_param. Document as a code-comment limitation (extending the peer set to arm producers is out of scope; no consumer needs it yet).

### state.py: LEAVE AS-IS + ALLOWLIST in the structural guard. Retiring its two arm walks needs re-expressing per-arm classify_modifiers (LOOP/ORACLE combos, loop-count fields) — file a separate low-priority follow-up, do NOT bundle.

### Test plan [FINDING 4, MEDIUM] — all RED before impl
- Keep the 5 existing RED tests (sites 1-5, true arm).
- Add RED per new site: 6 (bare arm Operator string cond unregistered -> ConfigurationError at compile), 7 (bare arm Operator + checkpointer=None -> CompileError 'requires a checkpointer' at COMPILE — highest-value), 8 (bare arm agent/act tool w/o factory -> CompileError at compile), 9 (bare arm LLM node inherits parent llm_config/renderer), 10 (CLI check auto-MemorySaver for arm Operator), 11 (sub-construct arm context node forwarded, not None).
- Add: idempotence (list(iter_with_arms(c)) == c.nodes when no _BranchNode); write-back-slot targeting (model_copy lands in meta.true_arm_nodes[j] AND meta.false_arm_nodes[j]); false-arm parity (extend _branch_parent to support false-arm placement — RED tests currently hardcode false_arm_nodes=[]); cross-arm-leakage limitation pin test.
- Structural guard (sweep-verify): every .nodes walk in src outside an allowlist must route through iter_nodes/iter_with_arms/iter_item_slots or be provably arm-aware. Model on tdbb TestIterNodesCoversBranchArms (behavioral pos/neg meta-test, NOT regex). Allowlist: state.py (documented), compiler.py:139 logging, loader.py spec-walks, testing.py codegen (neograph-gfoq), the primitives themselves, compiler.py:208 graph dispatch, iter_nodes.

### Core Invariant
Every walk over a Construct's node list that must observe conditionally-executed nodes routes through the single arm-descent primitive (iter_with_arms / iter_item_slots) or iter_nodes — no hand-rolled isinstance(item, Node/Construct) walk may silently skip _BranchNode arm contents.

## Triage (neograph-ala4.6): NEEDS_REFINEMENT -> refined inline (architect path was determinate, no user decision needed). Design above is the authoritative implementation plan for the fix atom.
notes:
## Reproduction (neograph-ala4.2)
- Failing test: tests/test_branch_arm_noniter_walks.py (5 tests, all RED)
  1. test_arm_node_input_type_mismatch_is_caught_at_assembly -- validation (_validate_node_chain): DID NOT RAISE on arm-node input type mismatch
  2. test_arm_each_node_gets_fan_out_param_normalized -- normalize_ir: arm Each node fan_out_param stays None (expected 'group')
  3. test_arm_node_di_binding_gap_is_linted -- lint._walk: arm FromInput binding never linted (0 issues)
  4. test_llm_node_in_arm_is_seen_by_has_llm_nodes -- verify._has_llm_nodes: returns False for arm-only LLM node
  5. test_arm_node_contributes_edge_to_adjacency -- runner adjacency: arm consumer contributes no seed->gate edge
- Root cause: Five hand-rolled construct.nodes walks short-circuit on _BranchNode sentinels because their isinstance(item, Node/Construct) guards do not recognize the branch sentinel, so nodes inside _BranchMeta.true_arm_nodes/false_arm_nodes are never visited. Identical root cause to neograph-tdbb (which fixed only the iter_nodes SoT walk).
## Trace-similar (neograph-ala4.3)
Bug pattern category: hand-rolled 'for item in construct.nodes' walk with an isinstance(item, Node)/(item, Construct) guard that short-circuits on _BranchNode, so bare arm Nodes (true_arm_nodes/false_arm_nodes) are skipped. Confirmed mechanism: _wiring.py:_add_branch_to_graph lowers arm CONSTRUCTS through a recursive _compile() (self-validating), but bare arm NODES go straight to make_node_fn -- bypassing every compile-time guard.

### Documented 5 (in ticket scope)
1. _construct_validation.py:128, 2. _ir_normalize.py:226, 3. lint.py:214, 4. verify.py:90/163, 5. runner.py:206. All reproduced RED in tests/test_branch_arm_noniter_walks.py.

### NEWLY FOUND same-pattern instances (NOT in original ticket scope)
6. compiler.py:146 -- Operator string-condition registration check (isinstance(item,(Node,Construct)) skips _BranchNode). A bare arm Node with Operator(when='unregistered-str') is never checked -> ConfigurationError not raised at compile.
7. compiler.py:161 -- has_operator checkpointer-requirement scan (top-level only). A bare arm Operator node -> has_operator False -> 'Operator requires a checkpointer' guard skipped -> runtime failure.
8. compiler.py:183 -- tool-factory registration check (top-level only). A bare arm agent/act Node with tools -> factory presence never validated -> runtime KeyError.
9. __main__.py:163 -- CLI 'neograph check' auto-MemorySaver supply, same has_operator top-level scan. Arm Operator -> no checkpointer auto-supplied -> false-negative check failure.
10. _subconstruct.py:118 -- runtime context-forwarding walk (for n in sub.nodes) within a sub-construct; a context node inside a branch arm of that sub-construct gets its context field forwarded as None.

### Recommendation
6-8 are the SAME compile-time-validation family as documented site 1 and share the identical arm-descent fix; strongly prefer folding them into this fix (anti-band-aid: one arm-descent primitive, all consumers). 9-10 are adjacent runtime/CLI instances -- architect atom (ala4.5) to decide fold-vs-file. Note: state.py (compile_state_model, compute_node_fingerprints) and compiler.py graph-build loop (208) and iter_nodes are ALREADY arm-aware -- they are the gold standard to mirror.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-ala4.4)

Pattern: a walk over a Construct's node list (`for _ in construct.nodes` / `.nodes`) whose isinstance(item, Node)/(item, Construct) guard short-circuits on _BranchNode, so bare arm Nodes in _BranchMeta.true_arm_nodes/false_arm_nodes are never visited.
Classification: SYNTACTIC/structural -- arm contents are reachable ONLY via _neo_branch_meta, so enumerating every .nodes walk AND every _neo_branch_meta access is provably complete (no semantic hiding places). Multi-agent fan-out not warranted.
Scan commands (reproducible):
  grep -rn 'for .* in .*\.nodes\|in construct\.nodes\|in self\.nodes\|in item\.nodes\|in sub\.nodes' src/neograph/*.py | grep -v 'arm_nodes\|for i in range\|lg_graph.nodes'
  grep -rn '_neo_branch_meta\|true_arm_nodes\|false_arm_nodes' src/neograph/*.py
Total .nodes-walk instances: 18 live walks (excl. loader spec-walks, emitted-code f-strings).

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | _construct_validation.py:128 | producer registration + type validation | MIGRATE | ticket site 1; RED test covers |
| 2 | _ir_normalize.py:226,228 | fan_out_param/oracle_gen_type inference + write-back | MIGRATE | ticket site 2; RED test; write-back into meta lists |
| 3 | lint.py:217 (_walk) | DI-binding + template lint | MIGRATE | ticket site 3; RED test |
| 4 | verify.py:91,163 | _walk + _has_llm_nodes | MIGRATE | ticket site 4; RED test |
| 5 | runner.py:206 | producer-consumer adjacency | MIGRATE | ticket site 5; RED test |
| 6 | compiler.py:146 | Operator string-condition registration check | MIGRATE | bare arm Operator condition never validated (found in trace-similar) |
| 7 | compiler.py:162 | has_operator -> checkpointer-required guard | MIGRATE | bare arm Operator skips checkpointer guard |
| 8 | compiler.py:183 | tool-factory registration check | MIGRATE | bare arm agent/act tools never validated |
| 9 | construct.py:170 | llm_config/renderer inheritance write-back | MIGRATE | bare arm LLM node misses parent llm_config/renderer inheritance (NEW -- not in trace-similar); write-back into meta lists |
| 10 | __main__.py:165 | CLI 'check' has_operator auto-MemorySaver | MIGRATE | arm Operator -> no auto-checkpointer -> false-negative check |
| 11 | _subconstruct.py:118 | runtime context forwarding within a sub-construct | MIGRATE | context node in an arm of the sub-construct forwarded as None |
| 12 | compiler.py:139,141 | compile_start logging node_names/modifiers | ALLOWLIST | display/telemetry only; no correctness impact |
| 13 | testing.py:72 (_collect_items) | test-scaffold codegen introspection | DEFER neograph-gfoq | tooling-only; arm nodes omitted from generated scaffolds |
| 14 | testing.py:90 (_collect_edges) | test-scaffold codegen introspection | DEFER neograph-gfoq | tooling-only; arm edges omitted from generated scaffolds |
| -- | construct.py:74 (iter_nodes) | leaf-node SoT walk | OK | already arm-aware (neograph-tdbb) |
| -- | compiler.py:208 | graph-build dispatch | OK | already dispatches _BranchNode -> _add_branch_to_graph |
| -- | state.py:100-102,309 | state model + node fingerprints | OK | already arm-aware (gold standard to mirror) |
| -- | loader.py:126,140,214,228 | YAML spec.nodes walk (pre-IR) | N/A | spec-level; _BranchNode arises only from forward/programmatic, never in a spec |
| -- | testing.py:194,202,519,524,530,541 | f-string-emitted code text | N/A | generated code, not a live IR walk |

MIGRATE count: 11 (sites 1-11). Scope note: sites 1-5 are the ticket's explicit scope; 6-11 are the same root-cause disease found by this scan. Anti-band-aid + gold-standard state.py already proves the arm-descent -- the fix should introduce ONE shared arm-descent primitive and route all 11 (plus retire state.py's/iter_nodes' hand-rolled copies where feasible). Architect atom to confirm final MIGRATE set (esp. whether 9/11 fold now or split).
## Proposed Fix Design (pre-review, neograph-ala4.5 input)
Primitive: add `iter_with_arms(construct) -> Iterator[Node | Construct]` in construct.py next to iter_nodes. It yields each item in construct.nodes AND, for each _BranchNode, yields its arm items (Node|Construct) in place of the sentinel; it does NOT recurse into sub-constructs (arm Constructs are yielded as Constructs so each caller's existing isinstance(item, Construct) branch handles them, incl. recursive _compile). One-level arm expansion = exactly the missing behavior.

Read-only migrations (swap `for item in construct.nodes` -> `for item in iter_with_arms(construct)`): _construct_validation(1), lint._walk(3), verify._walk+_has_llm_nodes(4), runner adjacency(5), compiler operator-condition(6)/has_operator(7)/tool-factory(8), __main__ CLI has_operator(10), _subconstruct context-forwarding(11).

Write-back migrations (need slot mutation, not just read): _ir_normalize(2) and construct.py:170 llm_config/renderer inheritance(9). title: Branch-arm nodes invisible to iter_nodes tree walks (scripted shims, DI, fingerprints)
description:
Discovered while fixing neograph-faf8. iter_nodes (construct.py:57) deliberately SKIPS _BranchNode sentinels, so nodes inside branch arms (_BranchMeta.true_arm_nodes / false_arm_nodes) are invisible to every iter_nodes-based tree walk: _collect_scripted_shims (compiler.py), _collect_required_di, and node/schema fingerprint collection. 

Concrete symptom: a scripted @node placed inside a branch arm sub-construct fails to compile with 'Scripted function <name> not registered' because its _scripted_shim PrivateAttr is never collected into the per-compile scripted dict. Declarative Node.scripted(fn=...) works only because its fn is registered via the global decoration registry / per-compile scripted= dict, not via shim collection.

This is distinct from neograph-faf8 (checkpointer/conditions threading into arm sub-construct compile, now fixed). This bug is about tree-walk coverage of branch arms.

Scope decision needed: is the right fix to make iter_nodes descend into _BranchNode arms (broad — affects lint, DI, fingerprints uniformly), or targeted per-consumer? iter_nodes skipping _BranchNode is currently documented/relied-upon behavior, so changing it needs an audit of all consumers. Anti-band-aid: prefer the uniform fix over patching only _collect_scripted_shims.

Repro: @node scripted sub-construct (construct_from_functions) with a port param, placed in a programmatic _BranchNode true arm, compiled.
design:
## Root Cause
iter_nodes (construct.py:57-68) walks construct.nodes and handles only Construct (recurse) and Node (yield); _BranchNode is skipped by design ('matching the prior walks' isinstance(Node) gate'). But _BranchNode carries _BranchMeta.true_arm_nodes / false_arm_nodes (list[Node | Construct]) that are real IR nodes. Three consumers walk iter_nodes and are therefore blind to arm contents:
  1. _collect_scripted_shims (compiler.py:255) -> arm @node shims uncollected -> 'not registered' at factory.py:61.
  2. _collect_required_di (compiler.py:271) -> arm DI params not surfaced in required-input validation.
  3. node/schema fingerprint collection (state.py compute_node_fingerprints) -> arm nodes excluded from checkpoint schema fingerprints.

## Fix Approach (uniform, anti-band-aid)
Make iter_nodes descend into _BranchNode arms: when item is a _BranchNode, iterate its branch_meta.true_arm_nodes + false_arm_nodes, recursing into Construct arm items and yielding Node arm items (same Node/Construct dispatch as the top level). This fixes all three consumers uniformly rather than patching only _collect_scripted_shims.

## Audit required (scope decision)
iter_nodes skipping _BranchNode is documented/relied-upon. Before changing, audit ALL iter_nodes callers to confirm descending is correct for each (shims YES, DI YES, fingerprints YES, lint placeholder checks — verify, validation walks use _construct_validation not iter_nodes — verify). Architect-review atom owns this scope call. Do NOT double-yield arm nodes that also appear elsewhere; _BranchMeta arms hold nodes that appear ONLY in that arm (per the field docstrings).
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_branch_arm_iter_nodes.py::test_node_subconstruct_in_true_arm_compiles_and_runs (and _false_arm_)
- Observed RED: ConfigurationError: [Node 'gate'] Scripted function 'gate' not registered (factory.py:61)
- Root cause: iter_nodes (construct.py:57) skips _BranchNode sentinels, so _collect_scripted_shims(parent) never collects the shim of a @node inside a branch arm; the recursive arm compile inherits the parent's incomplete _scripted_lookup (_wiring.py threads _scripted_lookup=scripted_lookup down, never re-collects) -> shim missing -> factory.py:61 raises.
- Confirmed mechanism: faf8 tests pass only because they used Node.scripted+explicit scripted= dict; the @node shim-collection path (_scripted_shim PrivateAttr) is the one iter_nodes-skip breaks. Same skip also starves _collect_required_di (DI) and fingerprint collection for arm nodes.
## Trace-similar (same bug pattern elsewhere)
Pattern category: IR tree-walks blind to _BranchNode arm contents.

THREE iter_nodes consumers share the EXACT blind spot (all fixed by making iter_nodes descend into arms):
1. _collect_scripted_shims (compiler.py:264) -- CONFIRMED broken (the repro): arm @node shims uncollected -> 'not registered'.
2. _collect_required_di (compiler.py:278) -- SAME walk: required FromInput/FromConfig params of arm nodes are not surfaced, so run(input=)/config missing a key an arm node requires escapes the required-input gate. Latent validation gap.
3. collect_llm_nodes (_llm_runtime.py:106, via iter_nodes) -- feeds check_llm_kwargs_or_raise (fail-loud 'LLM-mode nodes require runtime', _llm_runtime.py:141) AND lint. An LLM (think/agent/act) node in a branch arm with no runtime configured is invisible -> compile does NOT fail loud; it fails at runtime instead. Latent fail-loud gap.

SEPARATE walk, same disease, NOT fixed by the iter_nodes change:
4. compute_node_fingerprints (state.py:264) -- hand-rolls a shallow 'for item in construct.nodes' walk; a _BranchNode has neither .outputs nor .nodes so it is silently skipped (also does not recurse ordinary sub-constructs). Arm nodes get NO per-node fingerprint -> checkpoint auto-rewind cannot detect a changed arm node. Needs its own fix (fold into this ticket or file follow-up -- architect decides scope).

ALREADY arm-aware (correct; the contrast that proves the fix direction):
5. compile_state_model (state.py:102/126-127) -- explicitly iterates branch_meta.true_arm_nodes+false_arm_nodes; state fields DO cover arm nodes.
6. compute_schema_fingerprint (state.py:302) -- derives from state_model fields, so inherits arm coverage from #5.

DEDUP smell (file separately, out of bug-fix scope): #5 hand-rolls arm traversal that the uniform iter_nodes fix would make redundant -- two traversal idioms (one arm-aware, one not) is the drift that caused this bug. After iter_nodes descends, state.py manual arm walks could route through it.

Decision for architect atom: (a) uniform iter_nodes fix covers consumers 1-3; (b) confirm whether to fold the compute_node_fingerprints gap (#4) into this ticket or file a sibling; (c) file the state.py dedup (#5) as a separate refactor ticket, do not bundle.

title: Oracle merge barrier is single-path (no async twin) — LLM merge threadpooled under ainvoke
description:
Found by neograph-expi trace-similar (bug-triage neograph-wj8m.3). SAME disease as neograph-expi (single-path node-callable factory whose body invokes a blocking child), DIFFERENT instance — the Oracle merge barrier, not the sub-construct.

make_oracle_merge_fn (_oracle.py:383-427) returns a single sync merge_fn closure — no async twin, not RunnableLambda(afunc=...). Its body calls _merge_variants -> invoke_structured (_oracle.py:276, a SYNC LLM call) when the Oracle uses an LLM merge (merge_prompt/merge_model). group_merge_barrier (_wiring.py:261, the Each x Oracle fused merge) has the same shape via _merge_one_group -> invoke_structured. Both are added via graph.add_node with no afunc.

Consequence: under graph.ainvoke the Oracle/Each-Oracle merge barrier is threadpooled and its LLM merge runs on the sync path — blocks the event loop, violates the Phase-1 H2 invariant (async is driver-selected and must propagate through every nesting level). NOTE: the Oracle GENERATOR redirects ARE dual-path (make_oracle_redirect_fn/_oracle.py:90, make_eachoracle_redirect_fn/:135, make_each_redirect_fn/:461) — Phase 1a did those but missed the merge barrier.

Out of scope for neograph-expi (that fix is the sub-construct twin only; fixing the merge here would violate 'fix the bug only'). Needs its own dual-path fix: async merge twin awaiting ainvoke_structured (verify an async structured-invoke exists) + return RunnableLambda(merge_fn, afunc=amerge_fn); mirror in group_merge_barrier. TDD: thread-identity / gate-parking discriminator over graph.ainvoke of an Oracle-with-LLM-merge pipeline.
design:
## Root Cause
The Oracle GENERATOR redirects were made dual-path in Phase 1a (make_oracle_redirect_fn/_oracle.py:90, make_eachoracle_redirect_fn/:135, make_each_redirect_fn/:461), but the MERGE barriers were missed:
- make_oracle_merge_fn (_oracle.py:383-427) returns a single sync merge_fn; body -> _merge_variants -> _run_merge_prompt -> invoke_structured (sync LLM, _oracle.py). Added via _wire_oracle -> graph.add_node(merge_name, merge_fn, defer=True) with no afunc.
- group_merge_barrier (_wiring.py:261) -> _merge_one_group -> _merge_variants -> same sync invoke_structured. Added via graph.add_node(barrier_name, group_merge_barrier, defer=True) with no afunc.
Under graph.ainvoke both are threadpooled; the LLM merge runs on the sync path, blocking the loop (Phase-1 H2 invariant: async is driver-selected and must propagate through every nesting level). The scripted merge_fn path (_run_merge_fn) is pure Python (no I/O) — harmless if threadpooled — but the merge_prompt (LLM) path is the defect.

## Fix Approach (dual-path, mirrors _oracle.py redirects + Phase 1c ainvoke_structured)
1. Add async merge twins that await the async LLM seam:
   - _amerge_variants(...) mirroring _merge_variants, branching to an async _arun_merge_prompt that awaits _llm.ainvoke_structured (already exists, _llm.py:231). The _run_merge_fn (scripted) branch has no I/O; its async twin can call the same sync helper (or a thin await-nothing wrapper) — keep ONE merge algorithm, only the LLM seam differs (parity with invoke_structured/ainvoke_structured sharing _prepare/_finish).
2. make_oracle_merge_fn returns RunnableLambda(merge_fn, afunc=amerge_fn); amerge_fn awaits _amerge_variants. _wire_oracle passes the Runnable to graph.add_node (defer=True) unchanged.
3. group_merge_barrier: add async twin agroup_merge_barrier awaiting _amerge_one_group (async twin of _merge_one_group); wrap graph.add_node(barrier_name, RunnableLambda(group_merge_barrier, afunc=agroup_merge_barrier), defer=True).
4. Structural guard (sweep): pin make_oracle_merge_fn AND group_merge_barrier's factory to be dual-path (afunc present + drives ainvoke_structured), extending the neograph-expi GUARD C pattern.
NO band-aid: do not thread-offload; the merge must AWAIT the async seam so async selection propagates.

## Reproduction (neograph-45xo.2)
- Failing tests: tests/test_async_llm_tool.py::TestOracleMergeAsyncSeam (2 cells)
