Locks the three-layer principle (docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md sections 1 and 3.5) against drift, the way the H2 dual-path guard locks driver-selected async. Guard-first workflow: this guard is written to FAIL against any new violation and stays permanently.

THE INVARIANT: engine execution verbs on a compiled graph (.invoke/.ainvoke/.stream/.astream/.astream_events/.update_state/.get_state...) appear ONLY in (a) _compiled.py explicit delegations and (b) runner.py top-level verbs. Allowlisted exception: _subconstruct.py's wrapper-invoke (both drivers, post neograph-expi) — the documented LangGraph pattern for different-schema subgraph composition. LLM/tool .invoke/.ainvoke on BaseChatModel/BaseTool (Layer-2 node-internal cognition in _llm_*, _tool_loop, _oracle, node.run_isolated) is NOT an engine verb — the guard must discriminate by receiver, e.g. AST-scan for calls on objects flowing from compile()/CompiledStateGraph rather than naive method-name grep, or scope by module allowlist with a justification table like the existing guards.

Also guard the import direction: run-layer modules (runner) must not be imported from compile-layer modules (post neograph relocation ticket for _strip_internals, that inversion is gone — the guard keeps it gone).

Place in the existing structural-guard suite (test_guards_* conventions, allowlist + justification comments). Cite the design doc in the guard docstring.
close_reason: Added tests/test_guards_three_layer.py: AST structural guard locking three-layer principle (design doc §1/§3.5). Confines engine execution verbs (graph-only get_state/update_state/... + receiver-discriminated Runnable-shared invoke/ainvoke/stream/astream/astream_events/get_graph on graph receivers) to _compiled.py + runner.py, with _subconstruct.py wrapper-invoke allowlisted. Guards import direction (no compile-layer module imports neograph.runner). 11 tests + meta slip-tests; full guard suite 361 passed.

title: Relocate _strip_internals to a neutral module — kill the _subconstruct -> runner layer inversion
description:
Found by the three-layer audit (docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md section 2.5.3). _subconstruct.py:63 does a function-local 'from neograph.runner import _strip_internals' inside make_subgraph_fn (used at _subconstruct.py:117). _subconstruct is compile-layer (builds node callables); runner is the run layer — a compile-layer module reaching into the run layer, with the function-local import existing only to dodge the circular import the inversion itself creates. That dodge is the tell.

FIX: _strip_internals (runner.py:27) is a pure result-shaping utility (drops neo_* keys). Move it to a neutral low-level module reachable from both layers — _state_keys.py is the natural home (it already centralizes StateKeys). runner.py and _subconstruct.py both import from there; the function-local import becomes module-level; update the function-local-import allowlist guard accordingly.

SEQUENCING: this folds naturally into the q8ec runner-verbs refactor (the finalize/finalize_chunk extraction touches the same helper) — q8ec depends on this ticket so the relocation lands first on clean ground. Keep the existing pinning tests green (test_composition.py:617-626 passthrough, test_invariants.py:528 prefix-strip, guard test_guards_sidecar_imports.py:149).
close_reason: Moved _strip_internals to _state_keys.py (neutral leaf). runner.py and _subconstruct.py now import it at module level; the compile->run function-local inversion is gone. Removed the allowlist entry (allowlist shrank). Full suite 2242 passed.

title: Branch-arm sub-constructs compile with checkpointer=None while the main path threads the parent checkpointer
description:
Found by the three-layer audit (docs/design/three-layer-principle-2026-07-03.md section 2.5.2). _wiring.py:576 and _wiring.py:585 both compile branch-arm sub-constructs with checkpointer=None; the main sub-construct path threads the parent checkpointer (compiler.py:213 passes checkpointer=checkpointer into _add_subgraph). By the codebase's own theory — the main path threads it because it is needed — a sub-construct inside a branch arm has no persistence: an Operator interrupt inside it may fail or lose state, and crash recovery would re-execute the whole arm rather than resume inside it.

CAVEAT that makes this failing-test-FIRST: LangGraph may propagate the parent checkpointer to invoked subgraphs via config at invoke time, in which case the two paths coincidentally behave identically and the fix is to make the code CONSISTENT (and document which form is authoritative) rather than behavioral. Either outcome is informative.

TDD: branch arm containing a sub-construct with an Operator; run with a real file-backed SqliteSaver; interrupt; resume; assert the arm CONTINUES from the interrupt rather than restarting. Write the test before touching either call site. If the test passes as-is, the deliverable becomes consistency + a pinning test, not a behavior change.
close_reason: BEHAVIORAL bug confirmed via TDD (not consistency-only): an Operator sub-construct inside a branch arm failed to COMPILE with 'Operator modifier requires a checkpointer' because _add_branch_to_graph compiled arm sub-constructs with checkpointer=None (also dropped conditions=), while the main path (_add_subgraph) threads both. Fix: threaded parent checkpointer + condition_lookup into _add_branch_to_graph and both arm-sub-construct _compile call sites in _wiring.py (compiler.py passes them in). Now compiles, interrupts mid-arm, and resumes from the interrupt (pre-interrupt node runs exactly once). Test: tests/test_branch_arm_checkpointer.py (3 tests, real file-backed SqliteSaver, true+false arm + main-path parity). Verified RED without fix / GREEN with. Added ANY_ALLOWLIST entry for checkpointer:Any. Full suite 2245 passed. Filed neograph-tdbb for the independent iter_nodes/branch-arm shim-collection gap discovered en route (blocks @node sub-constructs in branch arms).

title: Sweep verification for neograph-w74k.2.7
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-w74k.2.7
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-w74k.2.7`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-w74k.2.7)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-w74k.2.7 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-w74k.2.7 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-w74k.2.7
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-w74k.2.7` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-w74k.2.7/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-w74k.2.7
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-w74k.2.7)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-w74k.2.7 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-w74k.2.7 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-w74k.2.7/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-w74k.2.7 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-scan:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Disposition table in notes covers every found instance AND records the exact reproducible scan command. For a semantic disease, `.claude/code-review/neograph-w74k.2.7/` exists (targeted-scan artifact). Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

   ```
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched

   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has

       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)


     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.

     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.

exists:

```bash

```


   ```
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |

   ```

     remaining instance

   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new

   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).

       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-w74k.2.3
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-w74k.2.3` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-w74k.2.3/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-w74k.2.3
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-w74k.2.3)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-w74k.2.3 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-w74k.2.3 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-w74k.2.3/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-w74k.2.3 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Sync run() + async scripted/raw body silently stores an un-awaited coroutine
description: Latent footgun surfaced during Phase 1b (neograph-w74k.2.2). ScriptedDispatch.execute (_dispatch.py:123, SYNC path) and raw_node_wrapper (factory.py:101) call the user body and return its result directly. If a user writes an 'async def' scripted/raw body but runs the graph via the SYNC driver run()/graph.invoke, self.fn returns a coroutine that flows UN-AWAITED into state — silent wrong behavior (a coroutine object where a model is expected). Phase 1b handles the ASYNC driver correctly (isawaitable-await); this is the sync-driver+async-body mismatch. DECISION NEEDED: reject an async body at compile-time when only sync run is used (hard — driver is chosen at call time, not compile time), OR warn/raise at runtime when ScriptedDispatch.execute sees isawaitable(result) under the sync path (cheap, fail-loud). Recommend: in the SYNC ScriptedDispatch.execute + raw_node_wrapper, if inspect.isawaitable(result): raise a NeographError('async body invoked under sync run(); use arun()'). Out of scope for 1b (async path); file for a later phase.
notes:
Fail-loud guard for async body under sync driver.

Fix (two SYNC call sites): after calling the user body, if inspect.isawaitable(result) -> raise ExecutionError (subclass of NeographError) instead of returning the coroutine into state.
- src/neograph/_dispatch.py ScriptedDispatch.execute (~L127): added isawaitable check + result.close() + raise. Imported ExecutionError.
- src/neograph/factory.py raw_node_wrapper in _make_raw_wrapper (~L102): same guard. Imported ExecutionError.
Async twins (ScriptedDispatch.aexecute, araw_node_wrapper) unchanged — they correctly isawaitable-await.

Error: ExecutionError.build('async node body invoked under sync run(); use arun()', node=<name>, hint='...Call arun(graph, ...) / graph.ainvoke instead of run() / graph.invoke.'). Message matches /arun/. Chose ExecutionError over bare NeographError as the most specific runtime subclass; pytest.raises(NeographError) still catches it. Also close() the rejected coroutine to suppress the 'never awaited' RuntimeWarning.

Tests (TDD red-first) in tests/test_async_dual_path.py::TestAsyncBodyUnderSyncRunFailsLoud:
- test_scripted_async_body_under_sync_run_raises (async @node scripted body via run() -> raises)
- test_raw_async_body_under_sync_run_raises (mode='raw' async body via run() -> raises)
- test_scripted_async_body_under_arun_still_works (positive regression via arun())
- test_raw_async_body_under_arun_still_works (positive regression via arun())
Verified red before fix (scripted silently returned coroutine; raw got opaque LangGraph InvalidUpdateError), green after.

Gates: ruff check src/ tests/ -> All checks passed. Full suite 2384 passed. Targeted async/scripted/raw/dispatch suites 40+483 passed. NOT closed, NOT committed per instructions.

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep

title: Refine neograph-w74k.1 plan per review (drift-guard soundness + delegation)
description:
Adjust the Phase-0 implementation plan using EXISTING research (do NOT re-research). Resolve the two MEDIUM architect findings on neograph-w74k.1:

MED-1 (drift-guard unsound): The specified guard 'assert ainvoke output == invoke output on identical fake state' is unsound. invoke() mutates scripted state (ReActFake._call_idx, StringArgsFake._call_idx, GuardFake._call_counter, StubbornFake._call_count, FakeTool.calls.append), so sequential calls advance the script -> false mismatch; and AIMessage has no value __eq__ so even stateless fakes fail raw equality. RESOLUTION: make the drift-guard STRUCTURAL (source/AST assert each fake's ainvoke body is a bare delegation to invoke with no response logic), matching the repo's tests/test_guards_*.py / test_structural_guards convention. Optionally add ONE executed asyncio.run(fake.ainvoke(...)) smoke assertion per finding LOW-3 so ainvoke is exercised, not merely inspected, in Phase 0 (async cell skips).

MED-2 (drop _impl indirection): Do NOT extract an _impl per fake. For all 8 deterministic fakes use 'async def ainvoke(self,*a,**k): return self.invoke(*a,**k)' and 'def abind_tools(self,*a,**k): return self.bind_tools(*a,**k)' (and _agenerate->_generate for StringArgsFake). invoke() itself becomes the single source of truth; drift is structurally impossible because ainvoke computes nothing. Reserve bespoke async bodies ONLY for the NEW awaitable-gated M1 primitive (plan step 5), which is async-native and EXEMPT from the sync-mirror drift invariant.

description:

a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-w74k.1`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used

     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test

       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-w74k.1
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-w74k.1` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-w74k.1/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-w74k.1
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-w74k.1)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-w74k.1 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-w74k.1/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a

```bash
bd label add neograph-w74k.1 codebase-scan:complete
```

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must

- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Expose agent-callable mid-node HITL interrupt (ask_human tool)
description:
## What
A first-class way for an agentic (mode='agent'/ReAct) node's tool to raise a TYPED human-in-the-loop interrupt MID-LOOP and receive the structured resume value — i.e. surface LangGraph's interrupt() from inside a tool/node, not only via the boundary-level interrupt_when/Operator that neograph exposes today.

## Why
Consumer (agent-stark) needs a research agent to pause mid-ReAct and ask the operator a decision ('found that person A left the company — remove / add-and-research / ignore?') then continue with the answer. Today neograph only supports interrupts AFTER a node (interrupt_when -> Operator -> interrupt(payload) -> human_feedback). LangGraph itself supports interrupt() inside a node/tool; neograph should expose it so consumers don't reach around the framework.

## Expectations after delivery
- An agent node's tool can call something like ask_human(payload: BaseModel|dict) that raises a typed interrupt and returns the operator's structured answer to the tool.
- The payload/resume contract is typed (consumer supplies the model), matching the existing human_feedback dict shape.
- Documentation of the replay-idempotency contract: on resume the node re-executes from the top, so any tool side effects before the interrupt must be idempotent.

## Verification — integration & E2E only
- Integration: a ReAct node whose single tool calls ask_human; run to the interrupt, assert the compiled graph pauses with the typed payload; resume with a structured answer; assert the tool receives it and the node completes.
- E2E: a two-tool research node that asks a mid-loop question, resumes, and produces its typed output — asserting no duplicate side effects across the interrupt (idempotency).

## Acceptance
- Public API to raise a typed interrupt from within an agent node's tool loop and receive the resume value.
- Boundary interrupt behavior unchanged; existing tests green.
- Docs cover the payload/resume typing and the replay-idempotency footgun.
- Discovered during agent-stark Layer-1 interaction-protocol design (ADR-0007); V1 uses boundary interrupts, this unblocks mid-research decisions in V2.

Design: docs/design/async-streaming-mcp-hitl-2026-07-02.md §6.4. Ships at LEVEL A (document the idempotency footgun; costly/mutating tool calls before ask_human re-execute on resume). Independent of async — interrupt/resume already works under run(); tool-exec site and dispatch have no broad except (GraphInterrupt propagates).
ADD Level A.5 lint (review M3): flag ask_human in an act-mode node (mutations) — and/or a mutating-tool call preceding ask_human in the same node. Converts 'document the footgun' into 'catch it', keyed on the existing agent(read-only)/act(mutation) mode distinction. Note: today's interrupt() lives in a dedicated micro-node (operator_check, no re-exec problem); ask_human deep in a fat agent node is categorically more dangerous.
Level B (true replay-safety) is DEFERRED — research delivered: docs/design/durable-execution-replay-research-2026-07-02.md (step- vs node-granularity; Level B = checkpoint-keyed step-memo layer in the tool loop, built only when a real consumer needs it and Phase 1 has landed). Level A->B compat: Level B must preserve results for tools idempotent under Level A.

title: Expose custom progress/domain stream events from nodes (LangGraph stream_mode=custom)
description:
## What
A neograph API for nodes to emit TYPED custom progress/domain events that surface through the compiled graph's stream — i.e. expose LangGraph's stream_mode='custom' / get_stream_writer() so a node can emit milestones like 'found new person Y -> fanning out research'.

## Why
Consumer (agent-stark) needs a progress channel for its UI (AG-UI/CopilotKit) that shows domain-level milestones, not just node-lifecycle/token events. Node lifecycle + tokens already come free from LangGraph astream_events on the compiled graph, but there is no neograph-sanctioned way for a node body/tool to emit a bespoke progress event. Without it, consumers must reach around neograph to LangGraph's writer, defeating the single-seam design.

## Expectations after delivery
- A node (scripted/think/agent) can emit a typed progress event (e.g. emit_progress(model)) that appears in the compiled graph's event stream with a stable, documented shape.
- Works alongside the existing cost_callback/telemetry without interfering with checkpoint schema fingerprinting.

## Verification — integration & E2E only
- Integration: a node emits N progress events; stream the compiled graph and assert all N appear with the typed shape, interleaved correctly with node lifecycle events.
- E2E: a small multi-node construct emitting milestones; assert a consumer can reconstruct stage progression from the stream alone.

## Acceptance
- Public emit-progress API usable from any node type; documented event shape.
- Events surface via the compiled graph's stream; existing streaming/telemetry unaffected; tests green.
- Discovered during agent-stark Layer-1 interaction-protocol design (ADR-0007) — the read-only progress channel for the operator UI.
notes:
## Now Phase 2 of epic neograph-w74k (async streaming) — re-scoped 2026-07-02
Design: docs/design/async-streaming-mcp-hitl-2026-07-02.md §6.2. Two pieces: emit_progress(model) [small] + the ASYNC streaming runner astream() [the missing, bigger piece — run() only does graph.invoke() today, discarding custom events]. Sync stream() is DROPPED (astream-only; review + maintainer decision).
HARD PART is the resume-stream protocol (review H3): a cross-cut with HITL (m6d3), NOT independent. One stream that carries progress -> pauses at an interrupt -> surfaces the payload to the UI -> resumes on the answer (astream <-> interrupt <-> astream). Named deliverable + typed contract + its own E2E.
Cancellation/cleanup (review H3, invariant §4.6): SSE disconnect mid-astream must cancel the run, dispose live MCP session, leave the checkpoint consistent — cancellation E2E required.
Guards: custom events never touch the schema fingerprint or any log/ToolInteraction. emit_progress under a non-streaming driver must warn (not vanish) — review L1.
DEPENDS ON Phase 1 (neograph-w74k.2, async foundation). Parallelizable with Phase 3.

1. GUARD-FIRST, before refactoring: pin the four weakly-pinned runner responsibilities with name-level tests — defensive input copy (entirely unpinned today: an in-place mutation would leak neo_* into the caller dict with zero test failure), CONFIG_INPUT stash/re-inject, fingerprint-injection ordering, preflight-DI ordering.
2. All twelve pre-engine responsibilities apply to streaming AS-IS. Auto-resume rewind is pure pre-flight config mutation and carries over free — CAVEAT: it must run inside _prepare, not lazily inside the generator, or the first chunk fires against the un-rewound checkpoint.
3. The genuinely NEW code: _finalize_chunk(chunk, stream_mode) — values: strip neo_*; updates: strip one level down (per-node deltas can carry fingerprints); custom/messages/debug: pass through UNTOUCHED. 5. Facade delegations in _compiled.py: stream (sync), astream_events, update_state/aupdate_state (HITL state-editing resume is impossible through the facade today — accidental omission per solid-grasp R6 history).
6. Add _prepare/_aprepare to the twin-guard tables (test_guards_async_dispatch, test_guards_meta) or co-location is unenforced.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-s1u4
description:
The fix for neograph-s1u4 typically eliminates an anti-pattern (raw access
where a helper exists, parallel implementation of a rule, etc.). This
atom forces a WHOLE-CODEBASE scan for that anti-pattern BEFORE the
fix is designed, so the fix addresses every instance — not just the
motivating site.

Distinct from trace-similar: that atom finds OTHER bugs of the same
shape. This atom finds INSTANCES of the disease pattern that the fix
introduces (or codifies) a helper for.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-s1u4` shows the `reproduce:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design's Fix Approach.
   Write a one-line spec — see task-execute.yaml::codebase-scan for
   examples.

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** (NOT just the file where the bug
   manifests). Choose the method by disease shape:
   - **SEMANTIC** (a rule re-implemented under different names; a helper
     bypassed): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted scan (3
     disease-scoped lenses + optional opus), which writes per-lens
     findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-s1u4/`:
     `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-s1u4`
     then merge the per-lens rows into the disposition table below.
   - **SYNTACTIC** (one exact literal / regex-able form): a single
     grep / AST scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out.

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-s1u4)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>
   ```

4. **Store the scan**:


title: Sweep verification for neograph-eoi8
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-eoi8
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-eoi8`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-eoi8)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-eoi8 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-eoi8 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.
acceptance_criteria: sweep:complete label added (the closure criterion — do NOT close this atom without it). Post-fix disposition table written. When >=1 MIGRATE row exists, a structural guard exists with positive + negative meta-tests (plus a regex-slip meta-test when the guard is regex-based); a zero-MIGRATE table records why the guard is N/A.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-eoi8
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-eoi8` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-eoi8/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-eoi8
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-eoi8)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-eoi8 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-eoi8 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-eoi8/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-eoi8 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

title: Sweep verification for neograph-f7nt
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-f7nt`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-f7nt --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash

```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.

  regressed.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-f7nt
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-f7nt` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-f7nt/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-f7nt
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-f7nt)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-f7nt --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-f7nt --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-f7nt/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-f7nt codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.

Every DEFER row points to a filed follow-up ticket.

title: Default output_strategy to json_mode (schema-in-prompt + auto-recovery) instead of structured
description:
Proposal: change the default LlmConfig.output_strategy from 'structured' to 'json_mode'.

WHY:
1. AGENT-MODE DOUBLE-GENERATION. With mode='agent' + output_strategy='structured', the ReAct loop first emits a free-form final answer to end the loop, THEN _call_structured makes a SEPARATE with_structured_output LLM call that re-generates the same object (_tool_loop.py:369-398: the 'structured' branch calls _call_structured; the 'json_mode'/'text' branch instead parses messages[-1] directly — no 2nd call). Observed in ox-troubleshooting-demo trace deal-4818-alice (77653beff70fc50a76649a5d5e427e77): GEN1 tool-call (8 tok) + GEN2 fenced JSON answer (232 tok) + GEN3 structured re-gen (227 tok, ~1.6s, ~$0.00094 ≈ 43% of the whole trace cost). The diagnosis is generated twice.
2. json_mode is functionally equivalent for the RESULT: inject schema into the prompt (already done via describe_type/BAML) -> llm.invoke -> parse -> auto-recovery with error feedback (_invoke_json_with_retry appends bad output + validation errors + full schema and retries). Same typed object, self-healing.
3. 'structured' requires a provider-compat shim (_llm_structured_compat.py) BECAUSE with_structured_output(include_raw=True) is polymorphic across providers (include_raw rejection, parsed=None, dict variants). json_mode is provider-uniform (plain invoke + parse), so defaulting to it removes reliance on that fragile surface.

TRADE-OFF (for maintainers to weigh): 'structured' uses provider-native CONSTRAINED DECODING — a stronger conformance guarantee for weaker models / providers that don't reliably emit valid JSON. json_mode relies on the model emitting parseable JSON (schema in prompt) + recovery. For capable models this is a win (cheaper, uniform, no double-gen); for weak models constrained decoding may be safer.

OPTIONS:
- (A) Flip the global default to json_mode; keep 'structured' as opt-in for constrained-decoding guarantees.
- (B) Narrower: keep 'structured' default for single-shot nodes, but in AGENT mode stop the redundant 2nd call — reuse/parse the ReAct final answer (i.e., agent mode effectively uses the json_mode tail). This kills the double-gen without changing conformance strategy for non-agent nodes.
Recommend deciding between (A) and (B); (B) is the minimal fix for the wasteful path, (A) is the broader simplification the reporter advocates.

Origin: ox-troubleshooting-demo; pairs with the tool-budget preamble (this repo, prior issue) as the efficiency/fewer-calls theme. Refs: _llm_config.py:36, _llm.py:142-145, _tool_loop.py:369-398, _llm_dispatch.py:_call_structured, _llm_retry.py:_invoke_json_with_retry, _llm_structured_compat.py.
design:

MEDIUM-1 — non-silent degradation (RESOLVED):
- After the change, output_strategy is INERT for agent/act nodes (always json_mode-tail parse of messages[-1]). Make it non-silent BOTH ways:
  (a) DOC: document at LlmConfig.output_strategy docstring (_llm_config.py:36) and agent-mode website docs that output_strategy only affects single-shot (think) nodes; agent/act nodes always parse the final ReAct turn as JSON.
  (b) WARN: emit a UserWarning ONCE when an agent/act node is built with output_strategy explicitly set (i.e., 'output_strategy' in llm_config.model_fields_set). Default/unset -> NO warning. Emit at a THREE-SURFACE-UNIFORM site (compile time / where agent/act ToolDispatch nodes are constructed), so @node, declarative, and programmatic all get it. Message: 'output_strategy=<x> is inert for agent/act node <name>; the final ReAct turn is parsed as JSON. output_strategy only affects single-shot (think) nodes.' No opt-out to keep _call_structured in agent mode (trade-off locked).

MEDIUM-2 — preserve neograph-0tid DSML guard (RESOLVED, simpler than feared):
- KEY FINDING: the with_structured_output compat polymorphism (include_raw TypeError fallback, Parsed/Raw/Failed) is ALREADY covered by DIRECT _call_structured unit tests at test_llm_internals.py:549 (test_fallback_succeeds_when_include_raw_raises_type_error) and :581 (test_result_correct_when_include_raw_supported). Those call _call_structured(...) directly and are UNAFFECTED (think path keeps _call_structured). So NO compat coverage is lost; no new think-path compat test needed.

  * test_llm_internals.py:2568 (neograph-0tid DSML recovery through invoke_with_tools, structured): CONVERT to an agent-mode DSML-recovery guard — final ReAct turn emits DSML/tool-call markup, the json_mode tail's recover_dsml (still present, _tool_loop.py:382) recovers it, assert recovered output.   * test_llm_internals.py:2650 (structured happy baseline through invoke_with_tools): CONVERT to agent-mode happy baseline — final turn emits valid JSON, parses directly (no re-gen).

title: Sweep verification for neograph-iyo2
description:
Confirm the codebase-scan disposition table is honored end-to-end and
a structural guard pins the disease pattern going forward.

Without this atom, a future PR could re-introduce the same pattern in
a new file and slip the existing guards (which are typically scoped to
cited files). This atom converts the local fix into a class-level fix.

## Precondition

- `codebase-scan:complete` label on neograph-iyo2
- Implementation atom closed

## Instructions

1. **Re-run the scan** from the codebase-scan atom. Use the EXACT same
   command recorded in bead notes. For a semantic disease scanned via
   the targeted mode, re-invoke it to regenerate the post-fix table
   mechanically instead of re-grepping by hand:
   `/dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<same disease spec>" neograph-iyo2`

2. **Compute the diff** between the Phase 1b table and current state:

   ```
   ## Sweep Verification (neograph-iyo2)

   Re-scan command: <same as Phase 1b>
   Pre-fix instances: <N from Phase 1b>
   Post-fix instances: <M>

   | # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
   |---|--------------------|--------------------|----|----|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | MIGRATE | now uses helper | YES |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | ALLOWLIST | unchanged | YES (false positive confirmed) |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | DEFER -> neograph-XXXX | unchanged | YES (deferred ticket open) |
   ```

   Every Phase 1b row must have:
   - MIGRATE rows: the post-fix state shows the helper is now used
   - ALLOWLIST rows: the instance is still there but the false-positive
     reason still holds (re-state it)
   - DEFER rows: the follow-up ticket exists, is open, and tracks the
     remaining instance

   NOTE: a MIGRATE fix shifts line numbers, so do NOT join Phase 1b and
   post-fix rows on `file:line`. Re-localize each row by its matched
   CONTENT (the `Form` column / matched text) and record the new
   location. The deterministic check is the instance-count diff
   (Pre-fix N vs Post-fix M); the per-row join is by content.

3. **Verify the structural guard exists**. When the disposition table
   has >=1 MIGRATE row, this atom REQUIRES that the implementation (or
   write-test) atom added a structural guard banning future instances
   of the disease pattern (modulo the allowlist). If the table has
   ZERO MIGRATE rows (everything ALLOWLIST/DEFER), no code changed, so
   the guard requirement is N/A — record why, and treat an
   all-ALLOWLIST architectural ticket as suspicious (see anti-patterns).
   The guard must:
     - Live in `tests/test_guards_*.py` (or equivalent)
     - Have at least one positive and one negative meta-test
     - If regex-based, include a "would-be-missed" case as a meta-test.
       Concrete failure mode: a `_neo_isolated_input` key slips a
       `^neo_`-anchored regex because of the leading underscore — the
       meta-test feeds that variant and asserts the guard still catches
       it. (A non-regex guard — AST-walk, import-graph — has no
       regex-slip case; positive + negative suffice.)

   Record the guard reference:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-iyo2 --append-notes "## Structural Guard
   - File: tests/test_guards_<name>.py
   - Class: TestNo<DiseasePattern>
   - Meta-tests: positive=<test_name>, negative=<test_name>, regex-slip=<test_name>"
   ```

4. **New instances detected** (the sweep found instances NOT in Phase 1b):
   - If the disposition table was incomplete, STOP. Re-do the scan
     properly. The Phase 1b artifact is the contract.
   - If the new instances were introduced BY this ticket (e.g. you
     refactored and accidentally re-introduced the pattern), FAIL.
     Re-implement.

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the post-fix table is complete AND the structural guard
exists:

```bash
bd label add neograph-iyo2 sweep:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "All Phase 1b rows had ALLOWLIST disposition" → suspicious. The
  ticket may not be doing real work. Re-examine.
- "Structural guard added but no negative meta-test" → the guard
  itself is a regex-slip risk. Add the meta-test.
- "Found new instances during sweep, dispositioned silently" → fail.
  Either the Phase 1b scan was incomplete (re-do it) or implementation
  regressed.

title: Codebase-wide disease scan for neograph-iyo2
description:
Architectural changes are local-only by default. This atom forces the
executor to look at the WHOLE codebase before designing the fix, so the
design phase addresses every instance of the disease pattern — not just
the motivating site.

Background: a Jun-2026 multi-agent code review surfaced 41 verified
findings (1 Critical, 10 High, 9 Medium) — overwhelmingly cases where a
canonical helper existed but the majority of call sites bypassed it,
because previous tickets fixed the motivating site only. This atom is
the structural counter-measure.

## Precondition

`bd show neograph-iyo2` shows the `research:complete` label.

## Instructions

1. **Identify the disease pattern** from the design field. Write it
   as a one-line spec: "What anti-pattern is this ticket eliminating?"
   Examples:
     - "raw getattr(state, X) on state instead of bus.get/get_required"
     - "f-string per-key field-name joins instead of output_field_name(...)"
     - "next(iter(x.values())) on outputs instead of normalize_outputs(x).primary"
     - "module-level mutable dict in src/<pkg>/"
     - "two-named alias for the same helper (e.g. _isinstance_safe / _is_instance_safe)"

2. **Scan the WHOLE codebase** for this pattern (NOT just the cited
   files in the ticket). Choose the method by disease shape:

   - **SEMANTIC disease** (logic re-implemented under different names, a
     canonical helper bypassed by hand-rolled variants — where one grep
     cannot find every variant): invoke the in-loop multi-agent targeted
     scan, which fans out 3 disease-scoped lenses (dedup / consistency /
     layering) + an opus elegance reviewer for architectural tickets and
     writes per-lens findings to `.claude/code-review/neograph-iyo2/`:

     ```
     /dev-practices:code-review --targeted "<one-line disease spec>" neograph-iyo2
     ```

     Then merge the per-lens rows into the single disposition table below.

   - **SYNTACTIC disease** (one exact literal / a single regex-able form):
     a single-executor scan is sufficient — do NOT fan out. Prefer
     structural tools over text grep when available:
     - **`ast-grep`** (`sg` / `ast-grep`, if installed): the preferred
       scan — matches code shape, not text, so it skips comments/strings
       and catches whitespace/formatting variants a regex misses.
     - **`.agent-index/`** (if present): consult it to enumerate the
       definitions / call sites to scan, instead of reading whole files.
     - Fall back to `grep -rn '<regex>' src/<pkg>/`, a `python -c "import
       ast; ..."` scan, or `git grep` only when ast-grep is unavailable.

     Whichever tool is used, record the EXACT reproducible command in the
     disposition table (`sweep-verify` re-runs it verbatim).

3. **Produce a disposition table** in the bead notes. Every instance
   found must appear:

   ```
   ## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-iyo2)

   Pattern: <one-line spec>
   Scan command: <exact command, reproducible>
   Total instances found: <N>

   | # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
   |---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
   | 1 | foo.py:42 | f"{x}_{key}" | MIGRATE | use output_field_name |
   | 2 | bar.py:101 | f"{x}_{key}" | ALLOWLIST | not a field-name join — base path concat |
   | 3 | baz.py:55 | f"{x}_{key}" | DEFER | scope explosion — file new ticket neograph-XXXX |
   ```

   Allowed dispositions:
   - **MIGRATE**: this ticket fixes the instance
   - **ALLOWLIST**: the instance is a false positive (the pattern matches but the semantic is different); the reason must be specific enough to justify
   - **DEFER**: out of scope for this ticket; a NAMED follow-up beads ticket is filed BEFORE this atom closes

   No row may be silently ignored. Every instance gets a disposition.

4. **Store the scan in the bead**:

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-iyo2 --append-notes "<disposition table above>"
   ```

5. **Update the design field** if the disposition table reveals scope
   changes (e.g. you initially planned to fix 1 site, the scan found 8):

   ```bash
   bd update neograph-iyo2 --design "<updated design covering all MIGRATE instances>"
   ```

## Gate: Add Label

ONLY after the disposition table is complete (every row has MIGRATE /
ALLOWLIST / DEFER + a reason) AND every DEFER row has a filed
follow-up ticket ID. For a SEMANTIC disease, the targeted scan's
artifact directory `.claude/code-review/neograph-iyo2/` MUST exist (it is
the structural proof the scan actually ran — the gate is not earned by a
hand-waved table):

```bash
bd label add neograph-iyo2 codebase-scan:complete
```

## Anti-Patterns

- "Disease pattern unclear, scope unbounded" → STOP. The pattern must
  be one-line specifiable. If you can't write the spec, the ticket
  itself is too vague.
- "Found instances but ignored some" → every row gets a disposition.
- "DEFER without filing the follow-up ticket" → defer requires a
  beads ticket ID to point at.
- Skipping this atom because "the cited files are obvious" → the
  point of this atom is what's NOT in the cited files.
