## Audit findings to incorporate (2026-04-10)

6a. This task needs a step-by-step migration plan:
Step 1: Add modifier_set: ModifierSet field to Modifiable (Node + Construct inherit)
Step 2: Rewrite __or__ to update modifier_set instead of appending to list
Step 3: Add computed property modifiers -> list[Modifier] from modifier_set (backward compat bridge)
Step 4: Rewrite .map() to use modifier_set.with_each()
Step 5: Rewrite has_modifier/get_modifier to delegate to modifier_set
Step 6: Update compiler.py logging (line 85-87) to log modifier_set.combo
Step 7: Update _BranchNode — it has modifiers=[] duck typing (forward.py:354). Either give it a ModifierSet(BARE) or keep a shim.
Step 8: Update 2 check fixtures that use modifiers=[...] syntax
Step 9: Remove computed property bridge (Phase 3 breaking change)

6c. _BranchNode.modifiers = [] is duck-typed. Under ModifierSet, _BranchNode needs modifier_set = ModifierSet() or a has_modifier/get_modifier shim that returns False/None.

- DIBinding dataclass: name, kind, inner_type, required, payload

- NodeOutput: wraps single value or multi-output dict. Same — not BaseModel-only.

2. Define ModeDispatch Protocol with typed execute()
3. Create 3 implementations: ScriptedDispatch, ThinkDispatch, ToolDispatch

title: Each/Oracle: single item failure crashes entire fan-out batch
description: When one item in an Each or EachOracle fan-out hits a retryable/transient error (e.g., 402 insufficient credits, 429 rate limit), the entire graph panics via _panic_or_proceed. All parallel items — including ones that could succeed — are killed. Should catch transient API errors per-item, mark that item as failed, and continue processing remaining items. Currently requires full re-run even if 14/15 items succeeded.
notes:
## Reproduce: CONFIRMED. One item RuntimeError kills entire fan-out batch. Test: test_each_item_failure_crashes_entire_batch. Fix requires per-item try/except in the node wrapper with sentinel results for failed items.
## Architect: NEEDS_USER_INPUT. This is a design decision: (1) wrap every Send-target in try/except, (2) add error_handling='continue' kwarg to Each, (3) use LangGraph RetryPolicy + custom error handler. Each approach has different tradeoffs for DX and debugging. Recommend approach 2: explicit opt-in via Each(on_error='continue') vs default 'raise'.
## Finding: LangGraph checkpoint already handles partial resume.
With checkpointer: run 1 dispatches 3 Send items. 'a' and 'b' succeed (checkpointed). 'bad' fails → panic. Resume: invoke(None, config) re-runs ONLY the failed 'bad' item. 'a' and 'b' results from checkpoint. All 3 succeed.

The fix is documentation + DX, not code:
1. Document: pass checkpointer= to compile() for fan-out resilience
2. Document: catch error, fix transient issue, resume with same config
3. Optional: add a helper like run_with_retry() that wraps this pattern
close_reason: Not a code bug: LangGraph checkpoint handles partial resume for Send failures. Needs documentation.

description: Triage and fix bugs through a reproduction-first workflow: reproduce -> trace similar -> architect review -> triage -> fix -> e2e verify -> commit. Each atom is self-contained -- findings stored in the beads task itself.
notes: ## Baseline: 1054 passed, 1 KNOWN failure (neograph-nwes reproduce test)

title: Architecture: single DI resolver (bouncer pattern) to eliminate cross-boundary bugs
description: Pattern 2 has 12 historical bugs, all from DI resolving differently across execution contexts. Root cause: 4 independent resolution paths (_resolve_di_value, _resolve_merge_args, _extract_input, scripted shim) each handle Loop unwrap, Each unwrap, config lookup independently. Fix: one canonical resolver that all paths delegate to. Validate once, trust downstream. The bouncer pattern.
notes:
## Research (2026-04-10)

### Findings
- 5 resolution functions + 2 inline patterns
- Loop unwrap duplicated across 10 sites with subtly different guards
- dict-to-list unwrap duplicated across 2 sites
- Config lookup duplicated across 2 sites

### Recommendation: Option C (extract helpers)
Two helpers: _unwrap_loop_value(val, expected_type) and _unwrap_each_dict(val, expected_type).
Replace all 10 Loop-unwrap sites and 2 dict-unwrap sites.
Zero test signature changes. Zero API changes.
Defined once, called everywhere. Missing call becomes obvious.

### Migration: zero breakage
No tests mock these functions. Option C changes no signatures.
close_reason: Shipped: _unwrap_loop_value + _unwrap_each_dict. 10 Loop unwrap sites + 2 dict unwrap sites unified.

title: Architecture: Hypothesis property-based tests for pipeline topology invariants
description: Pattern 3 has 10 historical bugs from dict-form × single-type × modifier combinatorial explosion. Manual test enumeration cannot keep up. Fix: Hypothesis generates random valid pipeline topologies (random modifier combinations, random I/O shapes) and asserts invariants: output matches declared type, no silent None, token count non-negative, compile+run round-trip succeeds. Runs on every CI push.
notes:
Research complete. Key findings:
- ModifierCombo enum has 10 valid combos (BARE, EACH, ORACLE, LOOP, OPERATOR, EACH_ORACLE, EACH_OPERATOR, ORACLE_OPERATOR, LOOP_OPERATOR, EACH_ORACLE_OPERATOR)
- Invalid combos: Each+Loop, Oracle+Loop (mutual exclusion)
- Node.scripted() needs register_scripted() for fn name
- compile() validates: LLM config, tool registrations, output_strategy, checkpointer for Operator
- compile_state_model creates typed state with reducers per modifier combo
- effective_producer_type: Each->dict[str,T], else->T
- classify_modifiers returns (ModifierCombo, dict)
- describe_graph returns Mermaid string
- Tests use register_scripted with lambda fns for scripted nodes
## Architect Review
- [LOW] Strategy should build from ModifierCombo enum to ensure exhaustive coverage. Using st.sampled_from(ModifierCombo) is the right approach.
- [LOW] Keep invariants simple for v1: (1) compile doesn't crash, (2) run produces non-None output, (3) output isinstance matches declared type. Add token/cost invariants in v2.
- [LOW] Use register_scripted with lambda fns returning model instances. Each test generates a unique registry key to avoid collisions.

Overall: ALL_LOW
close_reason: Hypothesis property tests: 4 invariants × 5 combos + 5 deterministic. 1231 tests pass.

title: Architecture: typed modifier spec (discriminated union) to eliminate composition bugs
description: Pattern 1 has 22 historical bugs, all from modifier combinations the compiler forgot to handle. Root cause: modifiers: list[Modifier] is a bag — any combination is syntactically valid. Fix: replace with a discriminated union (ModifierSpec) where each valid combination is a distinct type. Illegal combinations become unrepresentable. Compiler dispatch becomes a match statement. Inspired by Gemini analysis of whack-a-mole pattern.
notes:
## Research (2026-04-10)

### Findings
- 7 dispatch sites with 56 total has_modifier/get_modifier calls
- 10 valid Node combos, 8 valid Construct combos
- Option A (discriminated union): moderate disruption, maximum safety
- Option B (classify enum): minimal disruption, still allows invalid combos programmatically
- 210 pipe-syntax test uses survive unchanged, 2 direct modifiers= fixtures to update

### Recommendation: Option B first, Option A later
Option B is a safe stepping stone: add ModifierCombo enum + classify_modifiers() at each dispatch site. Uses match + assert_never. No API change. Then Option A in a future version replaces the list field entirely.

This avoids the risky API surface change while getting the exhaustive-match guarantee immediately.
## Architecture v2 feedback: eliminate Any from ModeDispatch protocol

The execute() method accepts Any input and returns Any output. This defeats type safety at the framework's core dispatch layer. The input/output types ARE known at compile time (node.inputs, node.outputs). The protocol should either:

1. Use BaseModel bounds: input_data: BaseModel | dict[str, BaseModel], return: same
2. Use TypeVar bound to BaseModel for generic dispatch
3. Use the node's declared types via a NodeSpec[I, O] generic that carries the types

Option 3 is the most type-safe but requires Node to be generic (Node[Claims, Report]). Python's type system supports this via Generic + TypeVar. The @node decorator already knows I and O from the function signature — it could produce Node[Claims, Report] at decoration time.

This is a design discussion for the architecture-v2 migration, not an immediate change.

title: inputs=list[X] (single-type) fails to extract from Each dict[str,X] producer
description: _extract_input in factory.py has two code paths for input extraction: dict-form inputs and single-type inputs. The dict-form path (line ~569) has logic to unwrap dict[str,X] into list[X] via list(values()). The single-type path (line ~578) does NOT have this unwrap — it uses _is_instance_safe which checks isinstance(dict_value, list) which is False. Result: inputs=list[X] (single type) for a downstream of Each receives None at runtime. Workaround: use inputs={'name': list[X]} (dict-form) instead. @node always generates dict-form inputs from the function signature, so this only affects surfaces 2 (Node.scripted) and 3 (programmatic Node). Fix: add dict-to-list unwrap logic to the single-type path, or document that list[X] consumers of Each producers must use dict-form inputs.
close_reason: Fixed: single-type path unwraps dict→list for Each producers

title: Each fan-in validation double-skip: fan_out_param + _each_skip_used both fire
description:
When a node has both fan_out_param set (from @node decorator) AND has_each=True, the _check_fan_in_inputs validator double-skips unmatched keys. fan_out_param skips the fan-out receiver at line 416, but _each_skip_used remains False, so line 422-424 allows ONE ADDITIONAL unmatched key to pass silently. A typo in inputs dict is never caught.

Repro:
  n = Node.scripted('consumer', fn='f', inputs={'claims': Alpha, 'item': Beta, 'mystery': Gamma}, outputs=Gamma)
  n = n | Each(over='claims', key='value')
  object.__setattr__(n, 'fan_out_param', 'item')
  producer = Node.scripted('claims', fn='f', outputs=Alpha)
  Construct('test', nodes=[producer, n])  # should raise ConstructError for 'mystery' but doesn't

Fix: initialize _each_skip_used = True when fan_out_key is not None (the fan-out receiver slot is already consumed by the explicit fan_out_param).

Location: src/neograph/_construct_validation.py line 414
Test: tests/test_obligation_r1r2.py::TestEachFanInValidationEdgeCases::test_fan_out_param_set_plus_each_skip_double_fires

title: _check_fan_in_inputs silently skips ALL unmatched keys when Each modifier present
description:
In _construct_validation.py:_check_fan_in_inputs (lines 421-422), when a node has an Each modifier, ALL unmatched input keys are assumed to be fan-out item receivers and silently skipped. But a node should have at most ONE fan-out item key. Extra unmatched keys (typos, stale references) pass validation silently.

Repro:
  extract = Node(name='extract', outputs=Claims)
  # 'clams' is a typo for 'extract' — should be caught
  verify = Node(name='verify', inputs={'clams': Claims, 'item': SingleClaim}, outputs=Result) | Each(over='extract.items', key='text')
  Construct(name='test', nodes=[extract, verify])  # No error raised

At runtime, the 'clams' parameter resolves to None (no upstream produces it), causing a silent data loss bug.

Fix: when has_each is True, count the number of unmatched keys. Allow at most one (the fan-out receiver). If fan_out_param is set, only skip that specific key. If fan_out_param is not set (programmatic API), allow at most one unmatched key as the inferred fan-out receiver and reject additional unmatched keys.
close_reason: Fixed: Each allows at most 1 unmatched fan-in key

title: invoke_with_tools double-counts tokens for json_mode/text strategy
description:
In _llm.py:invoke_with_tools (lines 707-731), when output_strategy is 'json_mode' or 'text', the final message's token usage is double-counted.

The json_mode/text path sets usage = getattr(last_msg, 'usage_metadata', None) where last_msg = messages[-1]. Then the message walk loop (lines 720-727) iterates ALL messages including messages[-1], summing their usage. Finally, lines 729-731 add 'usage' (from last_msg) AGAIN. This double-counts the final message's input_tokens and output_tokens.

The 'structured' strategy path does NOT have this bug because _call_structured makes a NEW LLM call (not in the messages list).

Repro: any agent/act mode node with llm_config={'output_strategy': 'text'} will report ~2x the actual token usage for the final ReAct message.

Fix: set usage=None after the json_mode/text parse since last_msg is already in the messages list.

title: _add_subgraph silently drops Operator modifier when Oracle or Each is present
description: In compiler.py _add_subgraph(), the Oracle branch (line 254-258) and Each branch (line 260-262) return immediately without checking for a co-existing Operator modifier. This means Construct | Oracle(...) | Operator(...) and Construct | Each(...) | Operator(...) silently drop the Operator — no interrupt check node is added to the graph. Compare with _add_node_to_graph() which correctly checks 'if operator:' after every modifier branch. Confirmed with live test: modifiers list shows [Oracle, Operator] but compiled graph has zero operator nodes. Fix: add 'if operator: last_name = _add_operator_check(graph, last_name, operator)' before returning from the oracle and each branches, mirroring lines 307-309 in _add_node_to_graph.
close_reason: Fixed: Operator chained after Oracle/Each in _add_subgraph

title: from_state in merge_fn doesn't unwrap Loop append-list
description:
When a @merge_fn has a from_state parameter that references a node with a Loop modifier, the resolver (\_resolve_merge_args line 418) reads the raw state field via getattr(state, pname, None). For Loop nodes, the state field is an append-list (list[T]) due to the append_list reducer. The resolver passes the full list to the merge_fn instead of unwrapping to the latest value ([-1]).

The validator (_construct_validation.py line 262-271) also doesn't account for Loop's effect on the state field type — it checks from_state param type against the node's declared output type, not the runtime append-list type.

Repro: Oracle node with merge_fn that has a from_state param referencing a Loop node. The merge_fn is annotated as expecting Context but receives list[Context] at runtime.

Fix: _resolve_merge_args should check if the from_state value is a list (append-list from Loop) and unwrap val[-1]. The validator should also use effective_producer_type or check for Loop modifier when validating from_state param types.

Related: _extract_input already handles this correctly on line 566 (unwraps loop-list fields for downstream consumers). The same logic is missing from _resolve_merge_args.

title: Loop + dict-form inputs: first iteration passes empty list instead of None for self-reference key
description:
## Bug

When a Node with Loop modifier has dict-form inputs (e.g. inputs={'refine': Draft, 'seed': Config}), the first iteration receives an empty list [] for the self-reference key instead of None.

## Root cause

In factory.py:_extract_input, the Loop re-entry check (line 506-545) only fires when own_val is a truthy list. On first iteration, own_val is [] (empty append-list from state initialization), which is falsy, so the check is skipped. Execution falls through to the fan-in dict path (line 556+), which reads the raw state field 'refine' and gets the empty list []. The unwrap check (line 566) doesn't fire because empty lists are falsy. So [] is passed to the user function as the value for the self-reference key.

## Impact

User code expecting Draft | None for the self-reference key on the first iteration gets [] instead. This causes AttributeError if the code tries input_data['refine'].text or similar attribute access. The user must add defensive checks for empty lists, which contradicts the typed contract.

## Reproduction

Node with inputs={'refine': Draft, 'seed': Config}, outputs=Draft, Loop modifier. On first iteration, input_data['refine'] is [] instead of None.

## Fix direction

In the fan-in dict path of _extract_input, when a Loop node reads its own append-list field and gets an empty list, it should return None for that key instead of the raw empty list. Add: if isinstance(value, list) and not value and node.has_modifier(Loop) and state_key == own_field: value = None
close_reason: Fixed: empty list [] treated as None on first iteration

title: cost_callback silently dropped when usage={} (empty dict is falsy)

title: _invoke_json_with_retry loses token usage from retry LLM calls
description: When max_retries>1 and retries happen, only the final attempt usage is returned. Retry LLM calls are invisible to cost_callback. If 2 retries fire, 2 calls worth of tokens vanish from cost tracking. Found by /test-obligations C-07.

title: Test gap: resume with fresh config (no _neo_input) — silent None for FromInput
description: Obligation R-04: run(resume=dict, config=has_configurable_no_neo_input). If user constructs a fresh config for resume instead of reusing the one from initial run(), _neo_input is absent and FromInput DI silently returns None. No error, no warning. Test should verify this scenario — either document the requirement to reuse config, or add a warning when _neo_input is missing on resume.

title: Test gap: Node(no param_res) + merge_fn simple DI not tested
description: Obligation W-13: lint _walk with a node that has NO DI params of its own but has Oracle with merge_fn that uses simple from_input/from_config (not bundled model). Currently only the bundled model variant (W-14) is tested. A regression that re-introduces the early return would break both, but a regression affecting only simple DI in the merge_fn section would not be caught.

title: lint() skips from_input_model/from_config_model validation for @merge_fn
description: lint.py lines 131-165 validate @merge_fn DI params but only check from_input and from_config scalar bindings. It does NOT check from_input_model or from_config_model (bundled Pydantic BaseModel params). This means a merge_fn with ctx: Annotated[PiarchCtx, FromInput] passes lint even if PiarchCtx fields are not available in config. The regular @node validation (lines 99-128) correctly handles both scalar and model bindings. Fix: mirror the model-bundled branch from the @node section into the @merge_fn section.
close_reason: Fixed: lint() checks from_input_model/from_config_model in merge_fn. Also fixed early return that skipped merge_fn check.

title: Test coverage: 88% → 100%
description: 440 uncovered lines across 18 modules. Three phases: Phase 1 (88→95%): ~50 trivial/easy tests for renderers, lint, decorators edge cases, conditions. Phase 2 (95→99%): ~30 medium tests for CLI subprocess, branch-arm Constructs, Each×Oracle compiler paths, ReAct tool_log. Phase 3 (99→100%): pragma no cover for ~15 genuinely untestable lines (LangGraph serde internals, AST exception paths).
close_reason: Coverage 88% → 98%. 12 modules at 100%. 981 tests. 57 remaining lines are edge cases in compiler/validation/forward/state.

title: Double DI marker (FromInput + FromConfig) silently picks first
description:
Annotated[str, FromInput, FromConfig] — both markers on the same param. The classifier silently picks the first one (FromInput) and ignores FromConfig. No warning about ambiguity.

Root cause: decorators.py _classify_di_params lines 284-292 — marker-matching loop breaks on first DI marker found.

Fix: Count DI markers in the Annotated args. If >1, raise ConstructError at decoration time.

Fixture: tests/check_fixtures/known_gaps/di_double_marker.py
close_reason: Fixed: double DI marker raises ConstructError

title: merge_fn DI bindings invisible to lint()
description:
lint() walks Construct.nodes but never inspects Oracle merge_fn functions. DI bindings in @merge_fn (e.g., Annotated[SharedResources, FromConfig]) are completely invisible to static validation. Production code (piarch/rw_ingestion.py) uses this pattern in 5 merge functions.

Root cause: lint.py _walk() only calls _get_param_resolutions on Node instances, never on merge_fn registry entries.

Fix: Extend _walk() — when a Node has an Oracle modifier with merge_fn, look up the function via get_merge_fn_metadata(), extract its param_res, and validate DI bindings. Extract existing DI-check logic into a _check_di_bindings() helper to avoid duplication.

Fixture: tests/check_fixtures/known_gaps/di_merge_fn_missing_config.py
close_reason: Fixed: lint() now checks merge_fn DI bindings

title: Sub-construct output boundary check doesn't fire for single-node sub-constructs
description: The output boundary check added in neograph-c4se doesn't catch the case where a single-node sub-construct declares output=TypeA but its only node produces TypeB. The check exists in _construct_validation.py line 192-212 but the producers list appears empty or the check doesn't fire for this specific case. Fixture at tests/check_fixtures/known_gaps/subconstruct_output_mismatch.py reproduces the issue.
close_reason: Already fixed by neograph-luzc (commit ff612b6). Boundary check now excludes input port.

title: Compile-time: validate output_strategy values
description: At compile(), for every LLM node with llm_config.output_strategy set, verify the value is in {structured, json_mode, text}. Currently raises ExecutionError at runtime.

title: Wrap Loop/branch condition calls in try/except
description: User-provided lambda conditions (Loop.when, branch op_fn) can crash on None input with AttributeError. Wrap condition(value) calls in compiler.py with try/except that converts to clear ExecutionError naming the condition and the None value.

title: Compiler should register output model types with LangGraph msgpack allowlist
description: When compiling a construct with MemorySaver checkpointer, LangGraph warns about unregistered types during checkpoint deserialization (on resume after interrupt). The compiler knows all node output types at compile time — it should collect them and pass to LangGraph via allowed_msgpack_modules. Currently produces hundreds of 'Deserializing unregistered type' warnings on resume. Types to register: all node output Pydantic models, their nested types (enums, sub-models), and framework types (NodeType, NodeStatus, GuaranteeType etc.).
design:
## Root Cause
LangGraph's JsonPlusSerializer defaults to _allowed_msgpack_modules=True (warn-and-allow). neograph's compile() passes the checkpointer through unchanged. with_msgpack_allowlist() is a no-op when _allowed_msgpack_modules is True. Result: every user Pydantic type triggers a warning on checkpoint deserialization.

## Fix Approach
In compile() (compiler.py), after compile_state_model(), collect all output types from the state model. Build an allowlist of (module, classname) tuples. Create a new JsonPlusSerializer with the explicit allowlist and replace the checkpointer's serde before passing to graph.compile(). Use LangGraph's _collect_from_type or walk Pydantic fields manually.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_pipeline_modes.py::TestMsgpackTypeRegistration::test_output_types_registered_when_compiled_with_checkpointer
- Root cause: compile() never modifies checkpointer's serde. _allowed_msgpack_modules stays True (warn-all mode).
## Trace Similar
Pattern: compile() passes checkpointer to graph.compile() but doesn't configure it.
Only one instance of this pattern: checkpointer.serde._allowed_msgpack_modules.
No other LangGraph serialization configuration gaps found in the codebase.
Sub-construct compilation (line 108) also threads the checkpointer but LangGraph handles sub-graph checkpoint scoping internally.
## Architect Review
Core invariant: compile() must configure all LangGraph internals that depend on type knowledge.
Approach: ALL_LOW — walk state model fields, collect (module, classname) tuples, create new JsonPlusSerializer.
Risk: Depends on LangGraph's _allowed_msgpack_modules private attr. Wrap in try/except to gracefully degrade if API changes.

description:

- Loop for draft→review→revise per section
- Sub-constructs (draft+review is isolated per section)
- Real PDF parsing
- Spec-driven pipeline

title: ForwardConstruct: Loop + branch composition fails (Construct.outputs vs .output)
description:
## Problem
When self.loop() produces a Construct that ends up in a branch arm (via the re-trace strategy), compile_state_model crashes with AttributeError because _add_output_field accesses .outputs (Node-only plural) but Construct has .output (singular).

## Reproduce
test_loop.py::TestForwardConstructLoop::test_loop_followed_by_branch_composes (currently xfail strict=True)

## Root cause
state.py _add_output_field and the branch arm node iteration in compile_state_model assume all items are Nodes. When self.loop() puts a Construct in the traced node list, the branch tracer can put it in _BranchMeta.true_arm_nodes or false_arm_nodes. The state builder then calls item.outputs (plural) on it, which doesn't exist on Construct.

## Fix approach
In state.py branch arm iteration, check isinstance(arm_node, Construct) and use .output (singular) instead of .outputs (plural). Same pattern as the existing sub-construct handling.

## Verification
Remove the xfail marker from test_loop_followed_by_branch_composes, test must pass.
design:
## Fix
1. state.py: in branch arm loop, check isinstance(arm_node, Construct). If Construct, handle same as sub_constructs section (use .output singular, apply modifier-aware field creation).
2. compiler.py _add_branch_to_graph: check isinstance(node, Construct). If Construct, use _add_subgraph() path (compile sub-graph, make_subgraph_fn) instead of make_node_fn.

Core invariant: Branch arms can contain both Nodes and Constructs — the same dispatch logic used at top-level (isinstance checks) must apply inside branch arms.
notes:
## Trace similar
Two crash sites when Construct appears in branch arm:
1. state.py:80-81 — _add_output_field(arm_node) accesses .outputs (Node-only)
2. compiler.py:507-513 — make_node_fn(arm_node) expects Node, not Construct

Both need isinstance checks to dispatch to Construct handling.
close_reason: Construct.outputs crash fixed, sequential loops fixed, sub-construct input extraction fixed. 2 xfails remain for loop+branch (neograph-477t).

notes:
## Similar Pattern Analysis
- if/else: Handled via re-trace (record_branch). Works correctly.
- for-loop over proxy attr: Handled via __iter__/record_iteration → Each fan-out. Works for map-over-items, NOT for cycles.
- for-loop over range(): Python-level iteration, nodes deduped. No cycle.
- while: Goes through __bool__/record_branch (treated as branch, not loop). No cycle.
- try/except: Dead-code limitation (v1). Documented.

- No other files attempt loop-to-cycle compilation. The gap is entirely in the tracer.
close_reason: Analysis complete. The tracer handles if/else (re-trace) and for-over-proxy (Each fan-out) but NOT iterative refinement cycles. The Loop modifier exists in modifiers.py and the compiler handles it. The gap is the tracer not detecting for/while and lowering to Loop.

title: Architect review of neograph-mwx3
description:
Review the proposed fix for correctness, minimality, and risk.

## Review Criteria

1. Root cause correctness
2. Fix minimality
3. Regression risk
4. Architecture compliance
5. Similar bug scalability
6. Test coverage sufficiency

Rate findings: LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH.
acceptance_criteria: Review written with rated findings and overall verdict.
notes:
## Architect Review

### 1. Root Cause Correctness: LOW risk
The root cause is clear and well-scoped: _Tracer.record() deduplicates by id(node), so repeated calls in a for-loop are no-ops. No back-edge is generated.

### 2. Fix Minimality: HIGH risk
There is no minimal fix. The tracer architecture doesn't support cycle detection. Options range from documenting the limitation (zero code change) to a significant tracer rewrite (AST or new tracing pass).

### 3. Regression Risk: HIGH
Any tracer change risks breaking existing for-loop-over-proxy (Each fan-out) and if/else (branch re-trace) support, both of which are tested and working.

### 4. Architecture Compliance: MEDIUM
The project chose re-trace over AST. Options A and B push against this. Option C (explicit annotation) is architecturally compatible.

### 5. Similar Bug Scalability: LOW risk
This is the only pattern affected.

### 6. Test Coverage Sufficiency: LOW risk
The failing test is clear and will catch the regression.

## Verdict: NEEDS_REFINEMENT
The fix requires a design spike. The tracer needs architectural changes to detect loop structure, and the interaction with branch re-trace needs careful design. Recommend filing a separate design task and marking the existing test as documenting a known limitation.
close_reason: Architect review complete. Verdict: NEEDS_REFINEMENT. The fix requires tracer architecture changes (loop detection + branch interaction). No minimal fix exists. Recommend documenting as known limitation + design spike for loop cycle support.

title: ForwardConstruct: for/while loops don't compile to graph cycles
description: ForwardConstruct traces forward() once symbolically and records node call order. Python for/while loops don't compile to LangGraph cycles — the tracer sees each node called once in the loop body but doesn't detect the loop structure itself. The test test_for_loop_compiles_to_cycle had a trivially-true assertion that hid this. Review only ran once. This is a known limitation — ForwardConstruct loop support requires cycle detection in the tracer.
design:
## Decision: Explicit loop primitive (JAX/TF model)

Python for/while loops cannot be detected by a tracer without AST inspection. AST locks us into Python and breaks TypeScript parity. Every major tracing framework (JAX, TF, Haiku, Flax) uses explicit loop primitives instead.

### API: self.loop()

```python
class Writer(ForwardConstruct):
    draft = Node.scripted('draft', ...)
    review = Node.scripted('review', ...)
    revise = Node.scripted('revise', ...)

    def forward(self, topic):
        d = self.draft(topic)
        d = self.loop(
            body=[self.review, self.revise],
            when=lambda r: r.score < 0.8,
            max_iterations=5,
        )(d)
        return d
```

### Loop types
- for (fixed N): self.loop(body=[...], max_iterations=N)(state)
- while (condition): self.loop(body=[...], when=lambda s: ..., max_iterations=N)(state)
- do-until: same — Loop already runs body at least once before checking

### Implementation
self.loop() returns a proxy that the tracer records as a sub-construct with Loop modifier. Maps 1:1 to the YAML spec format and to the programmatic construct | Loop() API.

### Why not AST
- Locks into Python (no TypeScript parity)
- Restricted Python subset (same pitfall as TorchScript)
- Two parsers to maintain long-term

### Why not pure tracing  
Every framework that tried (torch.trace, JAX raw) failed. The tracer sees duplicate node calls but can't extract loop semantics (condition, max_iterations, break predicate).
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_loop.py::TestForwardConstructLoop::test_for_loop_review_cycles_when_score_below_threshold
- Root cause: _Tracer.record() deduplicates by id(node) -- repeated calls to the same Node in a for-loop are no-ops. The tracer discovers loop-body nodes but does not detect the loop structure itself. No back-edge is generated, so the compiled graph is a linear chain (review runs once), not a cycle.
## Triage Result: NEEDS_REFINEMENT
- Failing regression test: tests/test_loop.py::TestForwardConstructLoop::test_for_loop_review_cycles_when_score_below_threshold (skip-marked)
- Root cause confirmed: _Tracer dedup prevents cycle detection
- Fix requires design spike: tracer architecture change for loop detection + Loop modifier lowering
- Loop modifier infrastructure (compiler, state, factory) already works
- All 7 triage atoms closed
## Resolution Path
Option C (explicit loop primitive) chosen. Language-agnostic, maps to YAML spec format. Python for/while in forward() documented as unsupported — use self.loop() instead.

title: _render_tool_result_for_llm ignores renderer parameter
design:
## Root Cause
_render_tool_result_for_llm accepts renderer param but unconditionally uses describe_value for Pydantic models. The renderer.render() method is never called.

## Fix Approach
In _render_tool_result_for_llm, check if renderer is not None first and use renderer.render(result) for both single models and lists. Fall back to describe_value only when no renderer is provided.
notes:

- Failing test: tests/test_renderers.py::TestRenderToolResultForLlm::test_renderer_used_for_pydantic_model
- Failing test: tests/test_renderers.py::TestRenderToolResultForLlm::test_renderer_used_for_list_of_models
- Root cause: _render_tool_result_for_llm (line 323) always calls describe_value(), never checks if renderer is not None

title: Oracle models= parameter + body-as-merge DX
description:
## Feature
Extend Oracle with models= parameter for multi-model ensemble. Body of @node IS the merge function.

See GitHub issue KonstantinMirin/neograph#1 for full design.

## Key changes
1. Oracle.models: list[str] | None field in modifiers.py
2. oracle_router injects neo_oracle_model per Send (round-robin)
3. Factory reads neo_oracle_model from state, overrides node.model
4. @node decorator: models= kwarg creates Oracle, registers body as merge_fn
5. Body-as-merge: when models= set, function body receives list[OutputType] at runtime
6. Info log when n % len(models) != 0

## Verification
- New test: models=['reason','fast','creative'] produces 3 variants merged by body
- New test: n=7 + 3 models → round-robin 3,2,2 with info log
- New test: body-as-merge receives list[OutputType]
- Existing Oracle tests still pass (backward compat)
design:
## Architecture
Option A: body-as-merge with models= on Oracle.
1. Oracle.models: list[str] | None. Validation: if models set, n = len(models) unless n also set.
2. oracle_router: Send(..., neo_oracle_model=models[i % len(models)]). Info log if n % len(models) != 0.
3. Factory produce/tool wrappers: read neo_oracle_model from state, use as model_tier override.
4. State model: neo_oracle_model: str | None field when any Oracle has models=.
5. @node decorator: models= kwarg. If models set without merge_fn/merge_prompt, register body as merge_fn.
6. Body-as-merge: function body receives list[OutputType] at runtime.
notes:
## Findings

### Oracle flow (injection points):
1. compiler.py:383-391 — oracle_router creates Send() with neo_oracle_gen_id per generator
2. factory.py:279-282 — scripted wrapper injects gen_id into config
3. factory.py:326-327 — produce wrapper uses model_tier=node.model (OVERRIDE POINT)
4. factory.py:391-403 — tool wrapper uses model_tier=node.model (OVERRIDE POINT)

### Implementation path:
- Oracle.models field in modifiers.py
- oracle_router injects neo_oracle_model=models[i % len(models)] into each Send state
- Factory wrappers (produce + tool) read neo_oracle_model from state, override model_tier
- State model adds neo_oracle_model field when any Oracle has models=
- @node decorator: models= kwarg creates Oracle, body-as-merge

### Body-as-merge:
- When models= set without merge_fn/merge_prompt, register the function body as the merge_fn
- The body receives list[OutputType] at runtime (not the upstream type)
- The decorator synthesizes a merge_fn name and registers it

### Core Invariant:
Oracle with models= is Oracle with per-generator model override — the existing fan-out/barrier/merge topology is unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented in a120656. Oracle models= + body-as-merge.

title: Each fan-out: dedup on duplicate keys with warning instead of crash
description:
Currently Each fan-out raises ExecutionError on duplicate keys. This is too strict — the LLM upstream may produce duplicates (e.g., same claim in two clusters). The framework should dedup by key (keep first), log a warning, and continue. The crash forces every consumer to dedup before fan-out, which is defensive boilerplate.

Current: raise ExecutionError('duplicate key R41')
Proposed: log.warning('each_duplicate_key', key='R41', kept_index=21, dropped_index=39) and skip the duplicate
design:
## Root Cause
Two locations raise ExecutionError on duplicate dispatch keys during Each fan-out:
1. compiler.py each_router guard (line 440-452) — pre-flight duplicate check before Send()
2. state.py _merge_dicts reducer (line 48-50) — reducer-time duplicate check

Both crash instead of deduping.

## Fix Approach
1. compiler.py each_router: On duplicate key, log warning with structlog (key, kept_index, dropped_index), skip the duplicate item (keep first). Continue dispatching only unique items.
2. state.py _merge_dicts: On duplicate key, log warning, keep existing value (first-write-wins = keep first).
3. Update 4 existing tests that assert ExecutionError to assert warning + dedup behavior instead.
notes:

- Failing test: tests/test_modifiers.py::TestEachDuplicateKeyDedup::test_dedup_keeps_first_and_warns_when_each_has_duplicate_keys_node_api
- Failing test: tests/test_modifiers.py::TestEachDuplicateKeyDedup::test_dedup_keeps_first_and_warns_when_each_has_duplicate_keys_programmatic
- Root cause: Two locations raise ExecutionError on duplicate keys — compiler.py:451 (each_router guard) and state.py:50 (_merge_dicts reducer). Both should dedup (keep first) and log warning instead.

title: Loop modifier: cyclical graphs for iterative refinement (0.3.0)
description:
Design research complete. neograph currently only supports DAGs. Cycles enable iterative refinement — the most common real-world agent pattern (draft→review→revise until approved).

## Recommended design: Loop modifier + ForwardConstruct while loops

Three API surfaces, same IR:

### @node decorator
@node(outputs=Draft, loop_when='needs_refinement', max_iterations=5)
def refine(draft: Draft) -> Draft: ...

### ForwardConstruct
def forward(self, topic):
    d = self.draft(topic)
    for _ in range(5):
        r = self.review(d)
        if r.approved:
            break
        d = self.revise(d, r)
    return d

### Programmatic
node | Loop(when='condition', max_iterations=5, reenter='earlier_node')

## Type safety challenge
Back-edge requires: node output compatible with reentry node input. Self-loop: outputs must be subtype of inputs. Multi-node: last node output must match reentry node input. The validator checks this at assembly time.

## Framework survey summary
- LangGraph: conditional back-edges via routing functions + recursion_limit
- Pydantic AI: implicit agent loop, model decides when to stop
- DSPy: assertion-driven retry (module-level, not topology)
- Temporal: plain while loops in workflow code
- Naiad: typed ingress/feedback/egress loop boundaries (academic, strongest type model)

## Implementation plan (7 steps)
1. Loop modifier in modifiers.py (when, max_iterations, reenter, on_exhaust, history)
2. Validator rule: loop output compatible with reentry input
3. effective_producer_type: Loop does not change output type
4. State compiler: neo_loop_count + optional neo_loop_history
5. Compiler: _add_loop_back_edge with conditional edge + iteration guard
6. @node kwarg: loop_when= and max_iterations= sugar
7. ForwardConstruct tracer: recognize for/while, emit _LoopNode sentinels

## Open questions
1. Self-loop accumulation: last-write-wins vs list? (propose: LWW default, history=True for list)
2. Multi-node validation: simple last→reentry check or full sub-chain? (propose: simple)
3. Nested loops: defer to Phase container for 0.4.0
4. Each+Loop composition: Loop wraps Each (entire fan-out re-executes)
5. Operator+Loop: Operator fires after loop exits (modifier ordering)

Deferred to 0.3.0 — not blocking the 0.2.x release.
design:
## Feature Design: Loop Modifier

### Loop class (modifiers.py)

class Loop(Modifier):
    when: str | Callable    # condition function or registered name. Returns True to continue looping.
    max_iterations: int = 10
    reenter: str | None = None  # back-edge target node name (None = self-loop)
    on_exhaust: Literal['error', 'last'] = 'error'
    history: bool = False   # collect iteration history in state

Validation in model_post_init:
- max_iterations >= 1
- when is str or callable

### State model (state.py)

When a node has Loop modifier:
- Add neo_loop_count_{field_name}: int = 0  (tracks current iteration)
- If history=True: Add neo_loop_history_{field_name}: list = []  (append reducer)

### Validator (_construct_validation.py)

New rule in _validate_node_chain:
- Self-loop: node.outputs must be compatible with node.inputs via _types_compatible
- Multi-node (reenter=X): last node's outputs must be compatible with reentry node's inputs
- Raise ConstructError('loop output type X not compatible with reentry input type Y') on mismatch

### Compiler (compiler.py)

New function _add_loop_nodes(graph, node, loop, prev_node, retry_policy):

For self-loop:
1. Add node function (graph.add_node)
2. Create loop_condition_fn(state) that:
   - Reads neo_loop_count, checks < max_iterations
   - Calls loop.when(state) or lookup_condition(loop.when)(state)
   - Returns node.name to continue loop, or next node/END to exit
3. graph.add_conditional_edges(node.name, loop_condition_fn)

For multi-node (reenter=X):
1. Add all nodes in the loop body normally
2. On the last node (the one with Loop modifier), add conditional back-edge to reenter node
3. The condition_fn checks neo_loop_count + loop.when

Iteration counter:
- The node wrapper increments neo_loop_count_{field_name} on each execution
- Compiler wrapper or factory wrapper handles the increment

on_exhaust='error': condition_fn raises ExecutionError when count >= max_iterations and when() still True
on_exhaust='last': condition_fn returns next/END when count >= max_iterations regardless of when()

### Factory (factory.py)

The existing _make_produce_fn / _make_tool_fn / _make_scripted_wrapper wrappers need to increment neo_loop_count when the node has Loop modifier. Add to _build_state_update:
- If node has Loop: update['neo_loop_count_{field}'] = current_count + 1
- If Loop(history=True): update['neo_loop_history_{field}'] = result

### @node decorator (decorators.py)

New kwargs: loop_when=, max_iterations=, loop_to=, on_exhaust=
Sugar that compiles to | Loop(...):

if loop_when is not None:
    loop_kwargs = {'when': loop_when, 'max_iterations': max_iterations or 10}
    if loop_to: loop_kwargs['reenter'] = loop_to
    if on_exhaust: loop_kwargs['on_exhaust'] = on_exhaust
    n = n | Loop(**loop_kwargs)
    _register_sidecar(n, f, param_names)

### __init__.py

Export Loop from neograph.

### Modifier composition order

Loop interacts with other modifiers:
- Loop + Operator: Operator fires after loop exits (last in modifier chain)
- Loop + Each: Each wraps Loop — each fan-out item loops independently
- Loop + Oracle: Not supported initially (raise ConfigurationError)

### Implementation sequence (7 subtasks)

1. Loop class in modifiers.py + export in __init__.py (schema only)
2. State model: neo_loop_count + neo_loop_history fields
3. Validator: back-edge type compatibility check
4. Compiler: _add_loop_nodes with conditional back-edge
5. Factory: loop counter increment in state update
6. @node decorator: loop_when= / max_iterations= / loop_to= kwargs
7. Integration test verification (make test_loop.py pass)

title: Conditional produce: skip_when= predicate to bypass LLM call
design:
## Architecture (from analysis session 2026-04-06)

### New Node fields (node.py)
```python
skip_when: Callable[[Any], bool] | None = None
skip_value: Callable[[Any], Any] | None = None
```
Same pattern as raw_fn, renderer, fan_out_param. Justified: programmatic API needs it too.

### Factory integration (factory.py)
Insert after _extract_input, BEFORE renderer and invoke_structured:
```python
input_data = _extract_input(state, node)
# skip_when check
if node.skip_when is not None and node.skip_when(input_data):
    skip_result = node.skip_value(input_data) if node.skip_value else None
    node_log.info('node_skipped', reason='skip_when')
    if skip_result is not None:
        return {field_name: skip_result}
    return {}
# renderer + invoke_structured follow...
```
Apply in _make_produce_fn AND _make_tool_fn (gather/execute). NOT in _make_scripted_wrapper (scripted nodes have Python control flow).

### @node decorator (decorators.py)
Add skip_when= and skip_value= kwargs, pass through to Node().

### Each interaction
skip_when receives one item at a time (via _extract_input's neo_each_item path). Per-item skip decision. Missing items = fewer keys in the dict reducer. Document this.

### Renderer interaction
skip evaluates BEFORE rendering. No point rendering if we skip.

### Tests (~8)
- test_produce_skip_when_true: skip fires, no LLM call, skip_value returned
- test_produce_skip_when_false: normal LLM call
- test_skip_when_no_skip_value: returns empty dict (pass-through skip)
- test_skip_when_with_each_fanout: per-item skip
- test_skip_when_gather_mode: skip before tool loop
- test_skip_when_programmatic_api: Node(..., skip_when=lambda x: True)
- test_skip_when_decorator_surface: @node(skip_when=...)
- test_skip_when_three_surfaces: all three API surfaces

### Files to modify
- src/neograph/node.py (2 fields)
- src/neograph/factory.py (_make_produce_fn + _make_tool_fn)
- src/neograph/decorators.py (kwarg passthrough)
- tests/test_e2e_piarch_ready.py (new TestConditionalProduce class)

### Core invariant
skip_when is evaluated after _extract_input but before renderer and LLM call. When it returns truthy, zero LLM tokens consumed. Existing nodes without skip_when are completely unaffected.

title: json_mode output schema: emit TypeScript-style notation instead of JSON Schema
description:
Sibling of neograph-ni6 (input rendering). This issue covers OUTPUT schema emission.

## The problem

Current json_mode output strategy relies on consumers to inject a JSON Schema into the prompt so the LLM knows what shape to return. piarch's bridge does this via:

    schema_str = json.dumps(output_model.model_json_schema(), indent=2)
    # Injected into prompt via 'common/json-instruction' template

JSON Schema is verbose. For a typical Pydantic model with 5-10 fields and some nesting, the JSON Schema representation is 300-800 tokens. BAML's insight: a TypeScript-style notation for the same schema is ~4x more token-efficient AND the LLM parses it more reliably.

## The BAML comparison

Same Resume model, two representations:

JSON Schema (current, ~400 tokens):
{
  '$schema': 'https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema',
  'type': 'object',
  'properties': {
    'name': {'type': 'string', 'title': 'Name'},
    'education': {
      'type': 'array',
      'items': {
        'type': 'object',
        'properties': {
          'school': {'type': 'string'},
          'graduation_year': {'type': 'integer'}
        },
        'required': ['school', 'graduation_year']
      }
    }
  },
  'required': ['name', 'education']
}

TypeScript-style (proposed, ~80 tokens):
{
  name: string
  education: [
    {
      school: string
      graduation_year: int
    }
  ]
}

5x reduction for the same information. BAML's docs and benchmarks claim the LLM parses the TypeScript form more reliably too — fewer parse failures, fewer schema drift errors.

## Proposed design

Add a new helper function to neograph:

    from neograph import describe_type

    describe_type(
        model: type[BaseModel],
        *,
        prefix: str = 'Answer in JSON matching this schema:',
        hoist_classes: Literal['auto', 'all'] | list[str] = 'auto',
        hoisted_class_prefix: str = 'type ',
        always_hoist_enums: bool = True,
        or_splitter: str = ' or ',  # NOT '|' — LLMs parse 'or' better
        indent: str = '  ',
    ) -> str

Behavior:
- Walks Pydantic model_fields recursively
- Emits TypeScript-style notation (string/int/float/bool primitives, [ ] for lists, { } for objects, enum members inlined)
- 'hoist_classes=auto' extracts repeated nested types as 'type Foo = { ... }' declarations before the main type — avoids repetition when the same sub-model appears multiple times
- 'or_splitter=" or "' for Union types (BAML's insight: LLMs read 'string or int' better than 'string | int')
- Reads Pydantic Field(description='...') metadata and emits as inline comments: '  name: string  // the person name'
- Handles Literal types as inlined enums: 'status: "active" or "inactive" or "pending"'

## Integration with output_strategy

Change json_mode strategy in neograph/_llm.py to use describe_type() instead of raw JSON Schema:

    # Before:
    schema_str = json.dumps(output_model.model_json_schema(), indent=2)

    # After:
    schema_str = describe_type(output_model)

This is a strategy-level change in neograph, not a consumer change. Consumers using json_mode get the improvement automatically.

Leave structured strategy unchanged (LangChain's with_structured_output uses the provider's native JSON Schema and that's fine — providers optimize for it).

Leave text strategy unchanged.

## Public helper

Expose describe_type() as a public helper (neograph.describe_type) so consumers who write custom prompts can use it directly. Example piarch use:

    @node(output=BRDocument, model='reason', prompt='br/write-document')
    def br_write(qualification: BRQualification) -> BRDocument: ...

    # In the prompt template:
    'Return a business rule matching this schema:\n{output_schema}\n\nBased on: {qualification}'

    # prompt_compiler:
    messages[0].content = messages[0].content.format(
        output_schema=describe_type(BRDocument),
        qualification=rendered_qualification,
    )

## IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: port from BAML

BAML's implementation is in Rust (baml/engine/baml-lib/jinja-runtime/src/output_format/types.rs) and is the best prior art. Port the algorithm to Python:

- Core type dispatch (primitive/list/object/enum/union)
- hoist_classes logic (auto-detect repeated types, emit as 'type Foo = ...' declarations)
- Field description inlining from Pydantic Field metadata
- or_splitter for unions
- always_hoist_enums behavior

Do NOT take BAML as a dependency — it's Rust-first with a Python client, designed for .baml file consumption. Use only as the reference implementation for the algorithm.

## Token savings estimate

For piarch's 60-80 models across 15 pipelines:

- Average JSON Schema per model: 400 tokens
- Average TypeScript notation per model: 80 tokens
- Average produce calls per pipeline run: 5
- Average pipeline runs per day during active iteration: 50

Savings: (400 - 80) × 5 × 50 = 80,000 tokens/day, or ~2.4M tokens/month.
At ~$0.5/1M input tokens (DeepSeek R1 rate), that's ~$1.20/month in savings. Small, but compounds with scale.

The real value isn't cost — it's prompt parse reliability. Fewer schema drift errors = fewer fallback-path executions = more deterministic outputs.

## Success criteria

1. describe_type(BRDocument) produces <100 tokens for models that currently emit 400+ tokens of JSON Schema
2. json_mode strategy automatically uses describe_type() instead of raw model_json_schema()
3. Public helper available as 'from neograph import describe_type'
4. Nested models with repetition get hoisted correctly ('auto' mode)
5. Pydantic Field(description=...) metadata is surfaced as inline comments
6. Union types use 'or' separator, not '|'
7. Enum Literal types are inlined as quoted strings
8. Round-trip test: LLM response parsed by Pydantic matches expected structure for complex models
design:
## Architecture (from plan session 2026-04-06)

### New file: src/neograph/describe_type.py
Public helper: `from neograph import describe_type`

```python
def describe_type(
    model: type[BaseModel],
    *,
    prefix: str = 'Answer in JSON matching this schema:',
    hoist_classes: Literal['auto', 'all'] | list[str] = 'auto',
    always_hoist_enums: bool = True,
    or_splitter: str = ' or ',
    indent: str = '  ',
) -> str
```

### Algorithm: two-pass recursive type walker
- Pass 1: _count_classes(model) — walk recursively, count occurrences in a dict
- Pass 2: _render_model_body(model, ...) — render, using references for hoisted classes

Type dispatch: str->string, int->int, float->float, bool->bool, None->null, list[X]->[X], dict[K,V]->object notation, Optional[X]->X or null, Union[A,B]->joined by or_splitter, Literal['a','b']->quoted values with or, BaseModel->recursive { field: type } blocks, Field(description=...)->// inline comment.

Handle circular models via visited set.

### Integration: json_mode auto-injects output_schema
- _llm.py:invoke_structured generates output_schema=describe_type(output_model) for json_mode
- _compile_prompt passes output_schema as new kwarg
- _accepted_params mechanism ensures old prompt_compilers that don't accept output_schema= just don't receive it (backward compat)

### Files to modify
- src/neograph/describe_type.py (NEW)
- src/neograph/_llm.py (_compile_prompt + invoke_structured)
- src/neograph/__init__.py (export)

### Tests (21 tests in 2 classes)
TestDescribeType (17): primitives, nesting, lists, dicts, optionals, unions, literals, enums, field descriptions, hoisting auto/all/explicit, recursion, empty model, token reduction comparison
TestJsonModeOutputSchema (4): json_mode passes output_schema, structured/text don't, backward compat

### Core invariant
describe_type is a pure function with no side effects. It walks Pydantic model_fields only. The json_mode integration is additive — existing prompt_compilers continue to work unchanged.
notes:
## Research note: BAML as a library dep is not viable

Investigated whether baml-py (Rust+PyO3, like pydantic-core) exposes the output_format renderer as a standalone Python function. Verdict: NO.

**Findings** (verified from baml-py canary branch):

- baml-py public API is entirely BAML runtime: BamlRuntime, FunctionResult, streams, media types, observability. No standalone schema renderer.
- TypeBuilder helper exists for dynamic type construction but has no .render() method returning schema string.
- Rust crate baml-lib/jsonish holds the algorithm but is not exposed via PyO3 bindings.
- BAML tracks this gap in issues #998 and #1403, shipped 'Modular API' (b.request/b.parse) but still requires .baml files + codegen.

**Why PyO3 being available doesn't help**:

pydantic-core is DESIGNED as a library primitive with a stable documented API. baml-py is DESIGNED as a runtime consumer of .baml files. Same tech (PyO3), fundamentally different API contracts. BAML chose to only expose the runtime, not the primitives.

**Implementation still means porting**:

- Port from baml-lib/jsonish Rust source (open, well-documented)
- ~200-400 lines of Python
- Algorithm is simple (type dispatch + recursion + hoisting)
- Performance is not critical (rendered <1KB per LLM call, not a hot loop)

**Optional upstream contribution**:

File an issue with BoundaryML asking to expose OutputFormatContent renderer as a standalone Python function. If shipped, our port becomes replaceable. Good open-source citizen move, benefits every other Python consumer.

title: FromInput[PydanticModel] — bundle multiple input fields into a typed context object
description: Scripted @nodes that need pipeline metadata (node_id, project_root, run config fields) currently repeat: node_id: FromInput[str], project_root: FromInput[str], shared: FromConfig[SharedResources] — 3 lines per node, ~20 nodes in piarch = 60 lines of boilerplate. Proposal: support FromInput[PydanticModel] where the model's field names map to config['configurable'] keys. Example: class RunCtx(BaseModel): node_id: str; project_root: str. Then: def my_node(upstream: X, ctx: FromInput[RunCtx]) -> Y: ... and ctx.node_id / ctx.project_root are populated from config automatically. Each field resolved independently via config[configurable][field_name].
close_reason: 6jd: FromInput[PydanticModel] and FromConfig[PydanticModel] now detected at decoration time and resolved at runtime by pulling each of the model's field names from config['configurable'], constructing the instance. Classifier walks call-stack frames to find locally-defined Pydantic model classes (needed under 'from __future__ import annotations'). Shared _classify_di_params + _resolve_di_value helpers extracted so both @node and @merge_fn use the same DI machinery. 4 regression tests in TestFromInputPydanticModel. 9zj: new @merge_fn decorator for Oracle merge functions with FromInput/FromConfig DI. Auto-registers via register_scripted for back-compat with Oracle(merge_fn='name') lookups. make_oracle_merge_fn in factory.py checks the @merge_fn registry first and calls with resolved DI args instead of legacy (variants, config) signature when a match is found. Plain (variants, config) merge_fn functions still work unchanged. 3 tests in TestOracleMergeFnDI covering bundled FromConfig, FromInput, and back-compat. 217/217 passing.

title: Oracle merge_fn — support @node-style dependency injection
description: Oracle's merge_fn is a plain function with signature (variants, config) -> output. It can't use FromInput/FromConfig parameter injection like @node does. Example pain: def _group_claims_merge(variants, config) needs to manually extract shared = SharedResources.from_runnable(config) and node_id = config.get('configurable',{}).get('node_id'). Should be: def group_claims_merge(variants: list[X], shared: FromConfig[SharedResources], node_id: FromInput[str]) -> Y. Either add a @merge_fn decorator, or let merge_fn reference a @node-decorated function that's called in merge context rather than as a topology node.
close_reason: 6jd: FromInput[PydanticModel] and FromConfig[PydanticModel] now detected at decoration time and resolved at runtime by pulling each of the model's field names from config['configurable'], constructing the instance. Classifier walks call-stack frames to find locally-defined Pydantic model classes (needed under 'from __future__ import annotations'). Shared _classify_di_params + _resolve_di_value helpers extracted so both @node and @merge_fn use the same DI machinery. 4 regression tests in TestFromInputPydanticModel. 9zj: new @merge_fn decorator for Oracle merge functions with FromInput/FromConfig DI. Auto-registers via register_scripted for back-compat with Oracle(merge_fn='name') lookups. make_oracle_merge_fn in factory.py checks the @merge_fn registry first and calls with resolved DI args instead of legacy (variants, config) signature when a match is found. Plain (variants, config) merge_fn functions still work unchanged. 3 tests in TestOracleMergeFnDI covering bundled FromConfig, FromInput, and back-compat. 217/217 passing.

title: Default llm_config on Construct — inherited by all produce nodes
description: Every produce node in piarch repeats llm_config={'output_strategy': 'json_mode'} because DeepSeek doesn't support with_structured_output. This should be settable once at Construct level: Construct('name', llm_config={...}, nodes=[...]). Produce nodes without explicit llm_config inherit the Construct's default. Explicit per-node llm_config wins over Construct default (merge, not replace).
close_reason: zf8: new construct_from_functions(name, [fn1, fn2, ...]) — takes explicit list of @node-decorated functions, same topo sort + validation + raw_fn attach as construct_from_module. Both construct_from_module and construct_from_functions accept llm_config= kwarg. 206/206 passing.

title: construct_from_functions() — build Construct from explicit function list

Add construct_from_functions('name', [fn1, fn2, fn3]) that takes an explicit list of @node-decorated functions and builds the Construct. Same topo-sort + validation as construct_from_module.

title: @node: cross-module composition + name-collision detection
description:
Part of epic neograph-4mx (@node production readiness).

## Problem

Two untested edge cases in `construct_from_module`:

### Case 1: Cross-module composition

A pipeline split across modules:

    # pipelines/stage_a.py
    @node(mode='scripted', output=RawText)
    def fetch() -> RawText: ...

    # pipelines/stage_b.py
    from pipelines.stage_a import fetch   # import the decorated Node

    @node(mode='scripted', output=Claims)
    def process(fetch: RawText) -> Claims: ...

    pipeline = construct_from_module(sys.modules[__name__])

Does this work? `fetch` should be in `vars(stage_b)` after the import, with a sidecar entry set at decoration time in stage_a. `construct_from_module(stage_b)` should find both nodes and wire them. In theory it works — in practice it's untested.

### Case 2: Name collision

Two modules both define a @node called `compute`:

    # pipelines/metrics.py
    @node(mode='scripted', output=Metrics)
    def compute(data: RawData) -> Metrics: ...

    # pipelines/stats.py
    @node(mode='scripted', output=Stats)
    def compute(data: RawData) -> Stats: ...

    # pipelines/combined.py
    from pipelines.metrics import compute as metrics_compute
    from pipelines.stats   import compute as stats_compute

    @node(mode='scripted', output=Report)
    def report(metrics_compute: Metrics, stats_compute: Stats) -> Report: ...

    pipeline = construct_from_module(sys.modules[__name__])

What happens?
- Both decorators set node_name='compute' (no awareness of import alias)
- `construct_from_module` walks `vars(combined)` and finds three entries: `metrics_compute`, `stats_compute`, `report`
- The field_name derivation: `attr.name.replace('-', '_')` = 'compute' for BOTH renamed imports
- The `decorated` dict collides: second-inserted wins, first is silently dropped
- `report`'s parameters reference `metrics_compute` and `stats_compute` (Python variable names), which don't match the field_name 'compute'
- ConstructError on both parameters (unknown param)

The user is stuck. No clear error message about the collision — just two 'unknown parameter' errors that don't hint at the root cause.

## Proposed fix

### For Case 1 (cross-module composition):

Write a test verifying it works. If it does, document the pattern in the `@node` docstring or example. If there's a bug in the walker, fix it (likely a one-liner — just need to ensure `_get_sidecar(attr)` still returns the correct entry for a Node imported from another module; since sidecar is keyed by `id(node)`, and the Node instance is the same across imports, this should work).

Test: `test_node_decorator_cross_module_composition`. Use `types.ModuleType` to build a fresh module, populate it with @nodes from ANOTHER fresh module via attribute assignment, verify `construct_from_module` finds them all and wires topology correctly.

### For Case 2 (name collision detection):

In `construct_from_module`, when walking `vars(mod)`, detect two Node instances with the same `field_name`:

    decorated: dict[str, Node] = {}
    collisions: dict[str, list[str]] = {}  # field_name -> [module-level attr names]

    for attr_name, attr in vars(mod).items():
        if isinstance(attr, Node) and _get_sidecar(attr) is not None:
            field_name = attr.name.replace('-', '_')
            if field_name in decorated:
                collisions.setdefault(field_name, [list of prior attr_name])
                collisions[field_name].append(attr_name)
            else:
                decorated[field_name] = attr

    if collisions:
        msg_lines = ['@node name collisions detected in module:']
        for field, attrs in collisions.items():
            msg_lines.append(f\"  '{field}' — bound to module attributes: {attrs}\")
        msg_lines.append('  fix: pass explicit name= to @node, or rename one of the functions')
        raise ConstructError('\\n'.join(msg_lines))

Also, the parameter lookup in the adjacency-build phase should use the module-level attribute name (e.g., `metrics_compute`), not just `field_name`, when a collision has been resolved via explicit `name=`. This requires additional bookkeeping — document it in the error message and let users fix by passing `@node(name='metrics_compute')`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Test `test_node_decorator_cross_module_composition`: one @node imported from module A into module B, second @node in B depends on it via parameter name, construct_from_module(B) wires them correctly and compile+run produces the expected output.
- Test `test_node_decorator_name_collision_raises`: two @node functions with the same `fn.__name__` in the same module walk, `construct_from_module` raises `ConstructError` with a message listing both colliding attribute names.
- Test `test_node_decorator_collision_resolved_by_explicit_name`: same setup but with explicit `@node(name='metrics_compute')` on one — assembly succeeds.
- Error message for collision includes: the colliding field name, both module-level attribute names, and the fix hint (pass explicit name=).
- Full suite stays green.

## Files to read

- `src/neograph/decorators.py:179-214` — current walker and adjacency-build
- `types.ModuleType` — how the existing tests build throwaway modules

## Non-goals

- Do NOT introduce a global @node registry across all modules — collisions should be scoped to one construct_from_module call.
- Do NOT auto-rename collided nodes — requires user action via `name=`.

title: @node: replace or augment 01b example with a fan-in showcase

## Problem

`examples/01b_scripted_pipeline_decorator.py` is a linear 3-node port of `examples/01_scripted_pipeline.py`. Same shape, same output, just uses `@node` syntax instead of `Node.scripted(...)` + `Construct(nodes=[...])`.

The actual selling points of @node are:
1. **Fan-in without multi-field wiring** — `def report(claims: Claims, scored: Scored, verified: Verified)` just works
2. **Refactor-safety** — rename a function, downstream parameter reference breaks at import time

None of these are visible in a linear 3-node chain.

title: @node: error messages point to construct_from_module call site, not @node decoration site
description:
Part of epic neograph-4mx (@node production readiness).

## Problem

When `construct_from_module` raises `ConstructError` for an invalid @node function (unknown parameter, self-dependency, cycle, fan-in type mismatch from neograph-8pt), the error's source location — rendered by `_source_location` in `_construct_validation.py` — points to the `construct_from_module(mod)` CALL SITE, not to the offending `@node`-decorated function.

This makes debugging painful in a module with dozens of @node functions:

    ConstructError: @node 'summarize' parameter 'max_items' does not match any @node in module 'my_pipeline'.
      available @nodes: [...]
      at my_pipeline.py:287    ← this is the `pipeline = construct_from_module(...)` line,
                                  NOT where `summarize` is defined

The user has to grep for `def summarize` to find the actual offender.

## Proposed fix

At `@node` decoration time, capture the function's source location via `fn.__code__.co_filename` and `fn.__code__.co_firstlineno`, and stash them in the sidecar alongside `fn` and `param_names`:

    _node_sidecar[id(n)] = (fn, param_names, fn.__code__.co_filename, fn.__code__.co_firstlineno)

When `construct_from_module` raises an error involving a specific @node, include that location in the error message:

    ConstructError: @node 'summarize' parameter 'max_items' does not match any @node ...
      available @nodes: [...]
      @node defined at my_pipeline.py:42        ← the actual function definition
      construct_from_module called at my_pipeline.py:287

Format: use `os.path.basename(filename)` for consistency with the existing `_source_location` output.

Apply to all construct_from_module errors that name a specific @node:
- Unknown parameter name
- Self-dependency
- Cycle detection (name the first-visited node in the cycle)
- (After neograph-8pt) Fan-in type mismatch
- (After neograph-q54) Any decoration-time error from the @node decorator itself already has a clean traceback since it raises during class loading — no change needed there

## Acceptance criteria

- Extend `_register_sidecar` signature: `_register_sidecar(n, f, param_names, source_file, source_line)`.
- Extend the sidecar tuple to include source location.
- New helper `_get_source_location(n: Node) -> tuple[str, int] | None` returning the stashed location.
- All `ConstructError` raises in `construct_from_module` that name a specific node include `at <basename>:<line>` for that node's definition.
- Update the existing `test_node_decorator_unknown_param_raises` to assert the error message contains both the function's source filename and a line number.
- New test `test_node_decorator_cycle_error_includes_source_location`: construct a two-@node cycle and assert both source locations appear.
- New test `test_node_decorator_error_filename_is_basename`: verify we emit `module.py:N` not an absolute path.

title: @node: test coverage for produce/gather/execute modes (LLM dispatch path)
description:
Part of epic neograph-4mx (@node production readiness).

## Problem

All six tests in `TestNodeDecorator` use `mode='scripted'`. The @node decorator's LLM-mode path (produce/gather/execute) is completely untested. Whether it actually works end-to-end — whether the LLM dispatch in `factory.py` correctly sees the `input`/`output`/`prompt`/`model` values set by the decorator — is theoretical.

This is a major gap because the Dagster-style example in the research report and the beads brief for neograph-dur BOTH showcase LLM-mode @node usage:

    @node(mode='produce', output=Claims, prompt='rw/decompose', model='reason')
    def decompose(topic: RawText) -> Claims: ...

If this path is broken, the @node decorator's marquee use case (inferred topology for LLM pipelines) doesn't exist yet.

## What to test

### Produce mode

`test_node_decorator_produce_mode_end_to_end`: Two `@node(mode='produce', ...)` functions chained via parameter names, configured with a fake LLM via `configure_fake_llm(lambda tier: StructuredFake(...))`. Run via `construct_from_module` + `compile` + `run`. Assert the expected structured outputs flow through.

`test_node_decorator_produce_mode_fan_in`: Fan-in pattern with 3 upstream produce nodes feeding a fourth produce node. Verify the fourth's `.input` is inferred correctly and the LLM receives the expected upstream value (the first parameter's value, per the current decorator's single-input contract).

### Gather mode

`test_node_decorator_gather_mode_with_tool`: A `@node(mode='gather', tools=[@tool-decorated fn], ...)` that uses the ReAct loop. Mirror `TestToolDecorator::test_tool_decorator_auto_registers`. Verify the tool is called and the final output is produced.

### Execute mode

`test_node_decorator_execute_mode_with_mutation_tool`: A `@node(mode='execute', tools=[...])` that calls a mutation tool. Mirror `TestExecuteMode::test_execute_with_tools`.

### Mixed mode pipeline

`test_node_decorator_mixed_scripted_and_produce`: A pipeline that combines a scripted @node (e.g., data fetch) with a produce @node (LLM processing). Verify end-to-end correctness. This proves both dispatches coexist under `construct_from_module`.

title: forward: Python 'if' conditional branching via Proxy.__bool__
description:
Add Python `if` support to `ForwardConstruct.forward()` tracing by intercepting `Proxy.__bool__`. This is the subtask that actually kills `Operator(when='string_key')` dispatch — it's what the epic is pointing at.

## Context

- Depends on the end-to-end compile integration.
- Design: `.claude/spikes/neograph-pub/design.md` — "How control flow maps" (if section) and "How the Proxy type works". Note the open question about re-trace vs exception-rewind; this subtask needs to pick one and document the choice.
- Prior art: torch.fx's `concrete_args` re-trace pattern. Read torch/fx/proxy.py `TraceError` handling before starting.

## Files

- `src/neograph/forward.py` — add branch interception to `Proxy` and branch-recording state to `Tracer`.
- Potentially new IR: `BranchConstruct` or a modifier that lowers to `graph.add_conditional_edges`. This subtask gets to decide; the decision goes in a doc-comment with rationale.
- `src/neograph/compiler.py` — new lowering path for the branch IR to LangGraph conditional edges.
- `tests/test_forward_construct_branching.py` — new test file.

## Signatures

Sketch — the implementer may refine:

```python
class Proxy:
    def __lt__(self, other): return _ComparisonProxy(self, '<', other)
    def __gt__(self, other): return _ComparisonProxy(self, '>', other)
    # __le__, __ge__, __eq__, __ne__ similarly
    def __bool__(self):
        tracer = _active_tracer()  # contextvar
        return tracer.record_branch(self)  # returns True first, then False on re-trace
```

Strategy to pick (document in design-note comment):
- **Re-trace**: `Tracer.record_branch` returns True, runs forward() to completion, then resets and re-runs with False for that branch id. torch.fx approach.
- **Fork-on-demand**: single trace, on __bool__ spawn a cloned tracer that explores both arms. More complex, handles nested branches symmetrically.
Pick one; explain why in the module docstring.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `forward()` with `if self.classify(x).confidence < 0.7: self.decompose(x)` compiles to a StateGraph with a conditional edge after `classify`, same topology as the declarative `classify | Operator(when='low_confidence')` equivalent.
2. Both arms of the branch run correctly at runtime (test with seed inputs that take each arm).
3. Nested `if` works (at least two levels deep).
4. `elif` / `else` work.
5. Predicate supports: attribute chains (`x.confidence`), numeric comparisons (`<`, `>`, `==`), and `and`/`or` between comparisons. Short-circuit semantics documented.
6. A predicate that references a non-proxy value (e.g. `if some_constant:`) still works — don't over-intercept.
7. Failure mode: a predicate that we can't represent (e.g. calls a user function on a Proxy) raises `TracerError` with a pointer to the `forward()` line.

## Out of scope

- `for` loops, `try/except`, `while` — separate subtasks.
- Branch depth > 4 (bail with a clear error; 4 is arbitrary but bounded to keep re-trace cost sane).
- Interaction with `Oracle` / `Each` modifiers on nodes inside branches.
close_reason: Python if branching via Proxy.__bool__ + re-trace strategy. _Proxy gains __getattr__ (child proxies for attribute chains), 6 comparison dunders returning _ConditionProxy, __bool__ delegating to tracer. Re-trace strategy: run forward() with all branches True, then re-run with each branch flipped to False, diff traces to identify true-only/false-only/shared nodes. _BranchNode sentinel in node list carries _BranchMeta (condition spec + arm nodes). Compiler gains _add_branch_to_graph lowering _BranchNode to add_conditional_edges with a runtime router that navigates state field + attribute chain and applies the comparison. Join node for convergence. State builder extended for branch arm nodes. 18 new tests in tests/test_forward_construct_branching.py. 187/187 passing.
