title: Each positional iteration_index (pre-Send stamping) -- demand-gated, parked
description:
PARKED pending concrete demand evidence -- do not start without it (see gate condition below).

Grounding: Each results are keyed by a BUSINESS field on the item, not identity/index -- key_val = getattr(each_item, each_mod.key, str(each_item)) (_state_write.py:122,129; same pattern _wiring_oracle_each.py:89). The barrier field is Annotated[dict[str, output_type], _merge_dicts] (state.py:466-469), additive-merge keeping the FIRST value on a duplicate key (_state_reducers.py:56-66). AGENTS.md's existing warning is confirmed accurate by this grounding pass: dict.values() preserves Python insertion order (arrival order into the dict via LangGraph's parallel Send() barrier), which is NOT the same as each.over's collection order -- order-dependent reductions must consume dict[str, X] and sort explicitly. There is no positional/index key anywhere in the Each path today.

Unlike Loop (free -- see neograph-ftnxl.6), an Each iteration_index requires either (a) synthesizing an index at dispatch time and threading it through the Send() payload -- a genuinely new small IR addition, similar in shape to the existing EACH_ITEM state key, or (b) accepting index = arrival order, which is EXACTLY the non-guarantee AGENTS.md already warns against -- that would launder documented nondeterminism into a deterministic-looking API, one of the highest silent-seam risks the gatekeeper reasoning pass flagged for this whole epic.

GATE CONDITION before starting: a concrete piarch (or other real consumer) use case where sorted dict-key consumption genuinely does not cover the need. If none exists, this stays parked -- do not build index stamping speculatively ahead of demonstrated demand.

Full grounding: docs/design/hybrid-dataflow-workflow-findings-2026-08-14.md, section 'scoping' finding #1 + #4.

title: provides/requires phase 1: contract-name aliasing (validation-time only)
description:
Blocked on neograph-ftnxl.2 (branch-arm cross-arm reachability leakage): a contract-satisfaction guarantee ('this named artifact is provided on every path reaching this consumer') built atop the current leaky validator would be FALSE by construction the moment a Branch is involved -- ship the validator fix first, or this feature's central selling point (compile-time reachability) is a lie for any pipeline with branching.

Grounding on how far today's fan-in already gets you (finding #3, 'is this ~90% expressible via output-key renaming?' -- answer: no, ~30-40%): Node.inputs/outputs dict-form keys are ALWAYS derived from the producing node's own identity via field_name_for(item.name) (naming.py:7-9) -- ProducerMap is OrderedDict[field_name, Producer], one producer per field name, last-writer-wins, no indirection table, no 'any of N nodes satisfies contract C' resolution anywhere. Two partial precedents exist: dict-form Node.outputs lets a node emit several named artifacts under keys that needn't match its OWN name for the SECONDARY keys (still node-identity-rooted for the primary); context= lets any node read any reachable upstream/ambient producer by name regardless of position -- but it's still identity-keyed (field_name_for(ctx_name) must match a real producer's field) and shares the SAME branch-unsoundness gap as regular fan-in.

Phase 1 scope (deliberately narrow -- 'aliasing', not the full contract-substitution vision from the design doc): a contract-name registry independent of node.name, with STRICT aliasing semantics -- a duplicate provider for the same contract name is a hard ConstructError at assembly time, no priority/override/multi-candidate resolution. This is the honest, buildable slice; multi-candidate substitutability (Example 3's full vision) is future work once phase 1 proves the namespace mechanics.

NEW IR CAPABILITY (per AGENTS.md's layer-discipline bar -- new Node field(s), single-writer via the normalizer, structural guard, on the same footing as Portal's handoff_param/handoff_channel precedent): this is the one child in this epic that genuinely crosses the sugar/IR line, because a contract name is a NEW indirection layer the state-bus key mapping doesn't have today (state.py's _add_output_field mirrors node-identity-derived naming 1:1; a contract-name -> state-key mapping is new machinery, not a projection over existing structure).

Long-term intent (record now, don't build yet): context= should eventually resolve through this same contract table, so there is ONE lookup mechanism instead of two -- confirm this ambition ceiling before starting so phase 1's namespace design doesn't foreclose it.

Full grounding: docs/design/hybrid-dataflow-workflow-findings-2026-08-14.md, section 'fan_in_contracts'.

title: Selected output-field marker (key-typed selection over offered sets)
description:
Phase 2 of the output-field marker family. Blocked on neograph-ftnxl.4 (Carried+Reasoned -- shares the projection/assembly machinery: Selected projects to its key type the same way Carried is dropped, and materializes at the same post-parse assembly seam) and neograph-ftnxl.5 (tool ledger ordinal -- a Selected referencing ledger entries without ordinals is positional guesswork, per that ticket's own note).

Design: Selected[T] projects to its key type -- Literal[...] of the actual offered keys when the offered collection is statically known at compile time, plain str otherwise. Materialization at the assembly seam FAILS LOUD on a key outside the offered set -- no 'accept the string anyway' fallback (that would be exactly the silent-seam class the North star forbids); a bounded-retry-on-invalid-key loop is an explicit later decision (see open decisions below), not default behavior.

HONESTY CONSTRAINT (from the gatekeeper reasoning pass, binding on this ticket's docs/marketing): do NOT describe Selected as compile-time-checkable. The offered set is runtime data (a tool result, an upstream list) -- only the field's KEY TYPE is static. Calling this 'statically verified' overclaims relative to neograph's own bounded-claim discipline (AGENTS.md: unrepresentable vs fail-loud vs not-covered).

OPEN DECISIONS needed before implementation starts (short design round, not blocking to defer the round itself): (1) referent typing -- what may a Selected key point at in v1? Ledger entries only, list elements, Each results? (2) cardinality -- exactly-one vs a set of keys, and whether that's two distinct forms or one form with a type-level list/optional. (3) retry semantics on an invalid key -- bounded re-ask with whose budget (node config vs run config)?

Full grounding: docs/design/hybrid-dataflow-workflow-findings-2026-08-14.md, section 'cross_cutting_north_star' + the Example 1/2 worked cases in docs/design/hybrid-dataflow-2026-08-14.md.

title: Document the free Loop scope projections (all_in_scope / from_enclosing)
description:
Confirmed via grounding pass: Loop's state field is ALREADY a full per-iteration history with an append-only reducer -- Annotated[list[output_type], _append_loop_result] (state.py:482-487), _append_loop_result does [*existing, new] (_state_reducers.py:26-30). Since Loop is sequential (not parallel), list position IS iteration order already -- no new storage needed. _unwrap_loop_value (di.py:153-176) returns val[-1] (latest) unless the consumer declares list[T], in which case the FULL history passes through unchanged. So 'all iterations' is already obtainable today by declaring the downstream param as list[T] instead of T -- it's just an undocumented mirror of the Each list-consumer trick, not a first-class API, with no per-iteration metadata (timestamp, index, condition-eval result) attached.

This ticket is DOCS + a thin naming layer only, not new mechanism: name and document the projection (website loop docs + AGENTS.md) as 'all_in_scope' (= consume as list[T], the existing full-history behavior) and 'from_enclosing(n)' (= list[-n], a trivial read helper). Add pinning tests for the load-bearing invariant this rests on: list-position == iteration-index for a non-nested Loop. Optionally a tiny read-side helper function, but no schema-fingerprint churn, no checkpoint migration, no state-bus change.

Deliberately excludes: Each indexing (separate gated child, ftnxl's Each iteration_index ticket) and nested scope_path across sub-construct boundaries (separate design-gate child) -- both are real gaps this ticket's free win does NOT cover.

Full grounding: docs/design/hybrid-dataflow-workflow-findings-2026-08-14.md, section 'scoping' finding #2.

title: compile_prompt()/render_prompt() thread no context, so out-of-graph parity is incomplete
description:
Surfaced during neograph-ebxdg's research atom (neograph-2125q.2) and confirmed by its architect review (neograph-2125q.4, LOW finding), deliberately left out of that ticket's scope.

The public compile_prompt() / render_prompt() entry points (_llm_render.py:280 and :375) do not thread the context channel at all, so the in-graph and out-of-graph prompt paths diverge: a node using context=[...] cannot be reproduced out of graph, and neither can the new raw_context channel (neograph-ebxdg) be exercised there. This undercuts the BYTE-IDENTICAL-messages promise those functions' docstrings make and the in-/out-of-graph parity compile_prompt() exists to provide.

Scope: thread context (and its raw sibling) through both entry points, with a test asserting byte-identical output against the in-graph seam for a context-declaring node.

title: _dispatch.py context_data annotated dict[str, str] but carries typed objects pre-render
description:
Surfaced during neograph-ebxdg's research atom (neograph-2125q.2), deliberately left out of that ticket's scope.

_dispatch.py annotates the context payload as context_data: dict[str, str], but the values are the typed objects _extract_context resolved; they only become str at the _compile_prompt seam (to_prompt_input(context, renderer=None), _llm_render.py:218). Now that raw_context (neograph-ebxdg) hands those typed objects to a compiler on purpose, the stale annotation actively contradicts the shipped contract and would mislead the next reader of exactly this question.

Fix: correct the annotations to the real shape. No behavior change expected; this is a typing/documentation correctness item.

title: raw_context escape hatch: the context channel has no typed sibling
description:
RECONSTRUCTED BEAD (2026-08-13). The original neograph-ebxdg was filed during the 0.7.6 release work and its DB row never reached this repo's beads store (neither ebxdg nor its parent fqcm6 exist here; verified by 'bd list --all' + grep over .beads/issues.jsonl). Re-created with the same ID so the neograph-2125q execution atoms can address it. Content below is reconstructed VERBATIM-IN-SUBSTANCE from three authoritative in-repo sources: commit 09dcc3c's message, CHANGELOG.md 0.7.6, and tests/test_guards_prompt_channels.py::NO_RAW_SIBLING_ALLOWLIST['context'].

## The gap

_compile_prompt (src/neograph/_llm_render.py) renders THREE channels to text for a prompt_compiler: input_data, di_inputs, and context. Two of them offer the typed value behind that text through an opt-in raw sibling -- raw_inputs (input_data) and raw_di_inputs (di_inputs, added by neograph-fqcm6 in 0.7.6). context does not.

A compiler that needs a context value for LOGIC (iterate a catalog model's children, branch on a field) rather than literal template substitution has no way to recover the live object. Since neograph-ufqr7 made the context channel obey the one rendering ladder (to_prompt_input(context, renderer=None) at _llm_render.py:218), the compiler receives a string and the live model is unreachable -- pinned by tests/modes/test_llm_internals.py::TestNodeContext (asserts isinstance(ctx_val, str)).

context's CLAIMED escape hatch -- a model's render_for_prompt() override -- only customizes rendered TEXT; it never hands back the live object, and it is per-MODEL, not per-NODE. So this is a real, tracked gap, not a false positive.

## Fix shape (same as fqcm6)

all_kwargs['raw_context'] = to_raw_inputs(context), next to the existing context line inside the same 'if context is not None' block. Same opt-in introspection gate (_accepted_params); DefaultPromptCompiler does NOT declare it, so zero behavior change for every existing pipeline.
design:
## Core Invariant

Every prompt channel that `_compile_prompt` renders to text must also offer, through exactly one introspection-gated `raw_<channel>` sibling, the typed objects that channel's text was rendered FROM built by `to_raw_inputs` at that same single seam -- so no compiler is ever forced to reconstruct a typed value from its own rendered output, and no compiler that did not ask receives anything new.

## Implementation Plan

**Order matters: 1 and 2 must both go RED before any src edit.**

1. **RED, structural.** In `tests/test_guards_prompt_channels.py`, DELETE the `"context"` entry from `NO_RAW_SIBLING_ALLOWLIST` (line 143-150), leaving `NO_RAW_SIBLING_ALLOWLIST: dict[str, str] = {}` -- keep the dict and the mechanism, shrink the ratchet to zero. Verify `test_every_rendered_channel_has_a_raw_sibling_or_a_reasoned_exemption` now FAILS naming `context`. Do not touch the AST detectors or the meta-tests; they are already correct.

2. **RED, behavioral.** In `tests/test_prompt_compiler.py`, add `TestRawContextEscapeHatch` modeled 1:1 on `TestRawDiInputsEscapeHatch` (line 931+) -- three tests, same names adapted:
   - a `context=["build_catalog"]` think node whose upstream produces a Pydantic model: assert `context["build_catalog"]` is still rendered `str` (the ufqr7 contract is untouched) AND `raw_context["build_catalog"]` `isinstance` the live model with its fields readable. Reuse `TestNodeContext`s pipeline shape from `tests/modes/test_llm_internals.py:47-88` for the wiring.
   - a compiler with a FULLY-SPELLED-OUT closed signature (no `**kwargs`, listing `context` but not `raw_context`) must run without a `TypeError` -- this is the only shape that exercises the gate, since `**_kw` makes `_accepted_params` return `_ACCEPT_ALL`.
   - agent-mode parity through `_agent_cycle` (copy fqcm6s third test verbatim in structure: `DefaultPromptCompiler` + a `capturing_compiler(*a, raw_context=None, **kw)` wrapper, `ReActFake`, `FakeTool`). Reason, stated in the docstring: think and agent/act are two independent call sites into the seam.
     **Review L2:** in this agent/act test ALSO assert the RENDERED side is `str` -- ufqr7's `isinstance(ctx_val, str)` pin lives only in think-mode `TestNodeContext`, so two extra lines close the mode axis symmetrically.
   Verify all three fail for the right reason (missing/`None` `raw_context`), not on import.

3. **GREEN, the one-line fix.** In `src/neograph/_llm_render.py`, inside the EXISTING `if context is not None:` block (line 213-218), immediately after the rendered line, add:
   `all_kwargs["raw_context"] = to_raw_inputs(context)`
   with a short comment in the register of the `raw_di_inputs` comment at :228-233 -- cite neograph-ebxdg, name it the sibling of `raw_inputs`/`raw_di_inputs`, and state that `context`s only claimed escape hatch (`render_for_prompt()`) customizes rendered TEXT and is per-MODEL, so it never hands back the typed object.
   **WORDING (review M2 -- use this phrasing, not "the raw state value"):** `_extract_context` reads each field via `read_upstream(..., expected_type=str, required=True)`, so the value has ALREADY been through `_unwrap_loop_value`/`_unwrap_each_dict`. For a Loop-modified upstream declared as a context field, `raw_context[k]` is the LATEST loop element, not the append-list (the Each unwrap correctly no-ops). That is the RIGHT behavior -- exact parity with the rendered channel it sits beside is the whole point -- but it means `raw_context` is NOT "the raw state value". Word it as **"the object `context[k]` was rendered from"** here, in step 6, and in step 7, so no compiler author expects loop history. REUSE `to_raw_inputs` unchanged (already imported at :29; already `Mapping`-generic; key parity with `to_prompt_input` is exact). Write the assignment in that exact syntactic form -- the guards AST scanner matches on it. No new helper, no renderer-layer code, no new import.

4. **Answer the channel.** Same guard file: add `raw_context` to `KNOWN_IGNORED` with a reason in the shape of the `raw_di_inputs` entry (opt-IN by design; `DefaultPromptCompiler` renders everything itself, so NOT declaring it is the correct opt-out). Add `"raw_context"` to `test_the_seam_scan_actually_finds_the_channels` non-vacuity tuple. **Do NOT add `raw_context` to `DefaultPromptCompiler.__call__` or `build_vars`** -- it is a logic channel, never a template var.

5. **Bump the budget.** `tests/test_guards_llm_runtime.py:429`: `"_llm_render.py": 452` -> the new count. The file is at 452/452 today, so this is mandatory, not optional. Follow fqcm6s precedent (445 -> 452) with a comment naming ebxdg and what the lines bought.
   **RATCHET JUSTIFICATION (review M1 -- record this in the dict comment; without it a ratchet reviewer will and should block the bump):** this is a SANCTIONED exception, not a violation. ### The introspection gate, and why `DefaultPromptCompiler` must NOT declare `raw_context`
`_llm_runtime.py:29 _accepted_params(fn)` inspects the compiler once at `LlmRuntime.build()` time and returns either its parameter-name frozenset or the `_ACCEPT_ALL` sentinel (`frozenset({"__all__"})`) when it declares `**kwargs`. `_compile_prompt:240-243` filters `all_kwargs` through `runtime.prompt_compiler_params` unless it is `_ACCEPT_ALL`. Adding a key to `all_kwargs` is therefore inert for every compiler that does not name it -- that is the whole zero-behavior-change argument, and it is identical to fqcm6`s.
**`DefaultPromptCompiler` must NOT declare `raw_context`.** Its `__call__` (`prompt.py:265`) declares `output_model, output_schema, di_inputs, context, node_name, **_kw` and forwards the named four to `build_vars`, which layers them into a template-var namespace. `raw_context` is a LOGIC channel, never a template var -- a shipped compiler that substitutes text has nothing to do with the live object. Declaring it would be strictly wrong (it renders everything itself). The correct expression of that is a `KNOWN_IGNORED` entry, exactly as `raw_inputs` and `raw_di_inputs` already have.
Caveat worth knowing: `DefaultPromptCompiler.__call__` has `**_kw`, so `_accepted_params` returns `_ACCEPT_ALL` and it physically receives every channel regardless -- the filter only bites on a closed signature. description:
Found by the dedup lens of the neograph-l2a7w disease scan (#14, #15).

lint._get_flattened_field_names predicts which field names
renderers._render_with_flattening will emit, by reading render_for_prompt's
RETURN ANNOTATION and enumerating non-excluded fields. That is a second encoding
of one rule — dynamic over instances vs static over annotations — with no shared
source. It drifts silently when render_for_prompt returns a dynamically-shaped
model or one whose annotation is unresolvable.

lint also re-derives the sub-construct port alias (type(v).__name__, skip on
collision), mirroring renderers._alias_subgraph_input_port. The comment claims
lint's prediction and the runtime alias 'cannot drift' — prose is the only thing
holding it, and the public renderers.render_input ALREADY disagrees (it applies
no alias at all).

Direction (from the elegance review): compute, don't predict — point lint at the
same function that produces the runtime keys, the effective_producer_type pattern
AGENTS.md already mandates for modifiers, applied to the prompt namespace.

NOTE the coupling to neograph-l2a7w: lint._predict_input_keys returns set() for
single-type inputs, so l2a7w's single-type keying change MUST update it in
lockstep or it opens a lint/runtime gap. That lockstep piece belongs to l2a7w;
this ticket is the deeper compute-don't-predict unification.

design:
## Core Invariant
The compiler-facing prompt namespace has exactly ONE producer -- `renderers.build_rendered_input(...).for_template_ref` -- so every other site that needs to know its keys (lint above all) must call that producer or the same named rule helpers it calls, never re-encode the rule; and the one seam that genuinely cannot be shared (lint has TYPES, the runtime has VALUES) must be a named, differentially-tested, loud gap rather than a silent second encoding.

## What this ticket is NOT
It is not a full unification. A single shared NAMESPACE is unachievable and must not be forced: lint cannot discover which class `render_for_prompt()` returns without an instance, and cannot know a value's runtime subclass. Share the three rules that are pure functions of a TYPE; pin the irreducible residue with a differential test. Anything that claims more is prose again, one layer up.

## Implementation Plan (guard-first; write the failing tests BEFORE the extraction)

1. FAILING FIRST -- the differential test that replaces the "cannot drift" comment.
   New `TestPredictionMatchesTheProducer` (in `tests/test_template_lint.py`, or promote the property into `tests/hypothesis/test_lint_placeholders.py` whose docstring already claims this contract and does not test it). For a fixture matrix -- plain model; `render_for_prompt() -> str`; `-> BaseModel` with an `exclude=True` field; a `neo_subgraph_input` port; single-type input; `inputs=None` -- assert
   `_predict_input_keys(node) == set(build_rendered_input(instances_for(node)).for_template_ref.keys())`.
   Feed real INSTANCES (never `Rendered`: renderers.py:491 short-circuits and would green the wrong contract). Record which rows fail today -- the port-subclass row and the lying-annotation row are expected reds and are the ticket's evidence.

2. FAILING FIRST -- the monopoly guard, as a new class in `tests/test_guards_helper_monopoly.py` (copy the shape of `TestTypeDisplayNameMonopoly` / `TestUnwrapHelperMonopoly`: call-count + unique-idiom-appears-once + a whitespace-slip meta-test + a positive-detection meta-test). Pin: the non-excluded `model_fields` enumeration and the `type(x).__name__` prompt-key idiom each appear EXACTLY once in `src/`, in their helper, and that `lint` delegates.

3. Extract the rules into `renderers.py` -- the PRODUCER owns them (the `effective_producer_type` precedent AGENTS.md mandates for modifiers, applied to the prompt namespace):
   - `prompt_key_for_type(t: type) -> str` -- the `__name__` key convention. Callers: `for_template_ref` (:81), `to_prompt_input` (:438), `to_raw_inputs` (:455), `_alias_subgraph_input_port` (:412), and lint's single-type + alias predictions.
   - `flattened_field_names(model_cls: type[BaseModel]) -> set[str]` -- the non-excluded-`model_fields` rule. Callers: `_render_with_flattening` (:498-499) and `lint._get_flattened_field_names`, which shrinks to "resolve the annotation, then call the helper".
   Keep the collision skip inside `_alias_subgraph_input_port`; if lint gains a shared `subgraph_alias_key(port_type, taken)` say plainly in the docstring that the omission was set-equivalent, so nobody sells a non-bug as a fix.
   Do NOT call `to_prompt_input`/`to_raw_inputs` from lint -- `tests/test_guards_rendering_ladder.py` ratchets them to `{_llm_render.py, renderers.py}` and widening a capability monopoly to buy a fix is the refusal AGENTS.md names. `build_rendered_input` is deliberately unratcheted and MAY be called.

4. DELETE `RenderedInput.available_keys_inline` / `available_keys_template` (renderers.py:53-57 + their construction at :372-373 and :381-382). Zero readers in `src/` on this branch or develop, and already stale (empty for the non-dict case whose `for_template_ref` now yields `{TypeName}`). Same commit: the one test (`tests/test_renderers.py::test_rendered_input_key_sets` -- retarget it at `for_template_ref` rather than delete the coverage), AGENTS.md's "Five fields" RenderedInput section, and `website/src/content/docs/concepts/renderers.mdx:248-249`; then `npm run build` in `website/`.

5. Make the un-computable case LOUD instead of confidently narrow. When `render_for_prompt` EXISTS but `_resolve_return_type` cannot resolve it, lint today returns `set()` and then emits a certain-sounding `template_placeholder_unresolvable`. Emit a distinct issue instead (e.g. `template_flattening_unpredictable`, `required=False`, naming the type and the node) and suppress the false certainty for that node. Fail-loud-over-fail-soft: a lint that cannot see must say so, not guess narrow.

6. Close the `context` column found by this research: add the node's declared `context` names to the template-ref valid-key set (`lint.py:564-575`), with a test pinning that `context=["brief"]` + `{brief}` produces NO issue. Verified live false positive introduced by today's neograph-cbfd9/ufqr7. If a reviewer scopes it out, FILE A BEAD in the same session -- do not drop it.

7. Three-surface parity for every new/changed assertion: @node, declarative `Node(...)`, programmatic `Node() | Modifier()`, or a written exemption.

8. Gate: `uv run pytest` (no extras) + `make quality`. Then re-read step 1's matrix: every row green means the prediction now equals the producer for every shape the two CAN agree on, and the rows that structurally cannot are named in the test, not in a comment.

`lint` could COMPUTE flattening by `model_construct()`-ing stand-ins and calling the real producer under try/except (precedent: `_resolve_tool_object` already instantiates tool factories during lint), falling back to the annotation. title: _extract_context casts state values to str while state types context fields Any and validation never checks the type
description:
Found by the consistency lens of the neograph-l2a7w disease scan (I1).

_input_shape._extract_context returns {name: cast(str, state.get_required(...))}.
The cast is the ONLY thing asserting str: state.py types context fields as Any,
and _construct_validation checks only that some upstream produces the field, not
that it is a string. A non-str context value is therefore cast-lied into the
template namespace and reaches the model as whatever str() makes of it.

Related to neograph-l2a7w (the context channel is one of the four), but distinct:
l2a7w is about WHO renders, this is about a type assertion that is not backed by
validation. Fix either by validating context fields as str at assembly, or by
rendering them through the shared renderer like every other channel.

Artifacts: .claude/code-review/neograph-l2a7w/disease-consistency.md (I1).
design:
## Root Cause
_extract_context makes two unbacked claims about a peer field it reads:
  1. that it is a str — cast(str, ...), erased at runtime, contradicted by state.py
     (context fields are typed Any) and by the validator (checks a producer exists,
     never its type). tests/modes/test_llm_internals PROVES the claim false: it asserts
     the compiler receives a live RawText model.
  2. that it needs no unwrapping — no _unwrap_loop_value, unlike the fan-in reader
     50 lines above (found by neograph-13k4i's trace-similar).

## THE FORK, and why it is not the fork it looked like

(a) route context through the one rendering ladder     (b) keep verbatim, fix only the type

I expected (a) to collide with a documented promise, and went to read it. Public docs
(node-api/modifier-kwargs.mdx:487,529,537) document the verbatim semantics DELIBERATELY:
'Context values bypass the renderer dispatch chain... no BAML describe_value, no XML/JSON
wrapping. This is the right choice for pre-formatted content like graph catalogs, domain
briefings, or cached summaries that are already crafted for LLM consumption.'

That rationale is about STRINGS. And a string is unchanged by the ladder — rungs 0,1,3 do
not apply and rung 4 str() is the identity. Measured, not assumed:
    to_rendered('<catalog>UC-1</catalog>')              -> '<catalog>UC-1</catalog>'   unchanged
So for the use case the docs actually describe, (a) and (b) are indistinguishable. What (a)
changes is only the case where 'verbatim' currently means str(model) = a Pydantic repr —
which is never something a user crafted, and is the l2a7w disease exactly.

BUT one measurement moved the design:
    to_rendered('<catalog>UC-1</catalog>', XmlRenderer()) -> '<catalog>UC-1</catalog>'
Rung 2 (an explicit renderer=) ESCAPES a pre-formatted string. Passing the node's renderer
into the context channel would silently mangle the documented use case for every consumer
who has configured one. The docs' 'bypasses the renderer dispatch chain' is load-bearing.

## Decision: (a-prime) — the one ladder, called with renderer=None
This is NOT a per-channel special case of the kind the one-rule design rejects. The rule is
the function to_rendered; the renderer is one of its PARAMETERS, chosen per call site the
same way node inputs choose node.renderer or runtime.renderer. One implementation, one
ladder, one guard. The context channel's documented contract IS 'do not wrap my content',
and renderer=None is how that contract is spelled.

Result per value kind:
  pre-formatted str        -> unchanged. The documented promise, kept literally.
  model with a presenter   -> render_for_prompt() honored (today: ignored)
  model without presenter  -> BAML instead of a Pydantic repr (strictly better)
  Loop producer            -> latest value instead of the whole append-list

## Fix Approach
1. _extract_context reads via di.read_upstream(state, name, str, required=True, ...) —
   required because context fields ARE validator-guaranteed. expected_type=str makes the
   loop unwrap fire and the each unwrap no-op, which is correct: an Each dict has no
   'latest' to pick.
2. Return dict[str, Any]; DELETE the cast. The channel stops claiming what it cannot.
3. _llm_render passes context through to_prompt_input(context, renderer=None).
4. DELETE the _extract_context entry from test_guards_upstream_read's FUNCTION_ALLOWLIST.
   That entry was written naming this ticket; the ratchet shrinks on schedule.
5. Update the two tests that pin the OLD contract, plus the docs. Changing a test to match
   code is normally forbidden — here the test pins the exemption this ticket exists to
   remove, so it is a contract change, and it is recorded as one.
notes:
## Inbound from neograph-13k4i's trace-similar (atom irryo.3)

_input_shape._extract_context (line 167) is a SECOND instance of 13k4i's disease, in
the same file as the correct reader: it reads a peer's output field via
field_name_for + get_required with NO _unwrap_loop_value / _unwrap_each_dict, unlike
_extract_fan_in_dict 50 lines above.

Consequence to verify in this ticket's reproduce atom: a Loop-modified producer named
in context=[...] hands the WHOLE append-list to the prompt instead of the latest value.
(Each producers show no symptom — both unwraps key on the consumer's expected type,
and context's is str, so the each-unwrap is a no-op there.)

So ufqr7 is not only 'the cast is not backed by validation'. The context read is wrong
in the same structural way as the Oracle merge read. Fix 13k4i and ufqr7 with ONE
reader, not two agreeing copies.
## Reproduction (atom irryo.20)
- Failing tests: tests/test_prompt_compiler.py::TestContextObeysTheRenderingRule
    ::test_context_honors_the_models_own_presenter
    ::test_context_from_a_loop_node_is_the_latest_value_not_the_whole_history
- Root cause: _extract_context asserts str with a cast that nothing validates, and reads
  a peer field with neither unwrap. So the channel typed 'text' carries live models and
  whole Loop append-lists.

Observed:
  a context model with render_for_prompt() -> presenter IGNORED; the Pydantic repr ships
  a Loop-modified context producer   -> every superseded draft ships as if current

Both are the neograph-l2a7w bug surviving on the one channel amendment A4 waved through
on the premise that 'the type pins it'. The type is a cast, and a cast is a claim.
## Trace-similar (atom irryo.21)

Pattern category: a cast or annotation that asserts a runtime type NOTHING validates —
a claim dressed as a fact. (typing.cast is erased at runtime, so it changes nothing except
what the next reader believes.)

Scan: grep -rn 'cast(' src/neograph/*.py -> 25 sites; 3 assert a concrete runtime shape.

| Site | Backed by | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| _agent_cycle.py:235 cast(list[Tool], node.tools) | node.py's _normalize_raw_base_tools converts every BaseTool -> Tool at construction. The comment states the invariant AND why the cast beats widening the tracker signature | BACKED — exemplary |
| _validation_inputs.py:74 cast(dict[str, TypeSpecStatic], input_type) | an isinstance(input_type, dict) two lines above; the cast is a mypy dict-invariance workaround, not a claim about data | BACKED |
| _input_shape.py:165 cast(str, state.get_required(...)) | NOTHING. state.py types context fields Any; _construct_validation only checks that SOME upstream produces the field, never its type | **THE BUG** |

Population = 1. The other two are the counter-examples worth keeping in view: a cast is
fine when something upstream really does guarantee the shape and the comment says what.
This one names a guarantee that does not exist anywhere.

## Codebase Disease Scan (atom irryo.22)

Pattern: a prompt channel that does NOT pass through the one rendering ladder.
Shape: SYNTACTIC — the seam is single-sited (_llm_render.py:198-234), so the channels are
enumerable by reading one function. No fan-out; no .claude/code-review/neograph-ufqr7/.

Scan command: grep -n 'to_prompt_input\|all_kwargs\[' src/neograph/_llm_render.py

| # | Channel | Rendered via to_prompt_input? | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | input_data (node inputs, all shapes) | yes (l2a7w) | KEEP |
| 2 | di_inputs | yes (l2a7w) | KEEP |
| 3 | the Oracle merge payload | yes — inherits #1, the l2a7w design's acceptance test | KEEP |
| 4 | context | **NO** | **MIGRATE** — this ticket |
| 5 | raw_inputs | deliberately NOT rendered | ALLOWLIST — it IS the un-rendered channel by definition; rendering it would delete its reason to exist |

Post-fix the answer is 'every channel but the one whose purpose is to be raw', which is
the invariant l2a7w set out to establish and A4 left one short.
## Architect review (atom irryo.23) — verdict ALL_LOW

**R1 root cause — LOW.** Two unbacked claims, both reproduced.

**R2 minimality — LOW.** One reader swap, one cast deleted, one to_prompt_input call, one
allowlist entry removed. No new mechanism: both halves already exist (di.read_upstream from
neograph-13k4i this session; to_prompt_input from l2a7w).

**R3 regression risk — MEDIUM in kind, LOW in blast radius, and DELIBERATE.** This changes
what reaches the model for context values that are not already strings. Measured before
deciding (see design): strings are byte-identical through the ladder, so the documented
'pre-formatted catalog' use case is untouched. What changes is Pydantic-repr output, which
no one can have depended on intentionally. Two tests pin the old contract and must be
updated as a CONTRACT CHANGE, stated as such:
  - tests/modes/test_llm_internals: 'Verbatim — the raw RawText, not BAML-rendered'
  - the assertion neograph-cbfd9 deliberately wrote to break here ('text=\'ship it\'')
The second one is the system working: cbfd9 predicted this ticket would change the shape
and left a tripwire naming it.

**R4 architecture — LOW.** renderer=None is a parameter choice at a call site, not a second
ladder; the l2a7w guard bans re-implementations, which this is not. The fix DELETES an
allowlist entry rather than adding one — the direction ratchets are supposed to move.

**R5 similar-bug scalability — LOW.** After this, every prompt channel but raw_inputs (whose
whole purpose is to be raw) goes through the one ladder. The invariant l2a7w set out to
establish becomes true without exception, which is what makes it checkable.

**R6 test coverage — LOW.** Presenter case and Loop case both red now. Add a THIRD: a
pre-formatted string must survive byte-identical, including when a renderer is configured.
That is the promise most at risk from this change and nothing currently pins it.

Verdict: ALL_LOW -> proceed to fix, with the R6 third test added.
## Fix applied (atoms irryo.25-27)

_extract_context now reads via di.read_upstream(state, name, str, required=True) and
returns dict[str, Any]; the cast is DELETED. _llm_render renders the channel with
to_prompt_input(context, renderer=None).

### The measurement that decided the design
I expected a collision with the documented 'verbatim' promise and went to measure it:
    to_rendered('<catalog>UC-1</catalog>')                -> unchanged
    to_rendered('<catalog>UC-1</catalog>', XmlRenderer()) -> '<catalog>UC-1</catalog>'
So the docs' rationale (pre-formatted content) is untouched by the ladder EXCEPT at rung 2.
Hence renderer=None: not an exemption from the one rule, but the one rule called as this
channel's contract requires. A third test now pins the promise most at risk — a
pre-formatted string survives byte-identical WITH a renderer configured — because nothing
pinned it before and it is the thing this change could most easily have broken silently.

### The guard allowlist reached ZERO
test_guards_upstream_read's FUNCTION_ALLOWLIST held exactly one entry, written during
neograph-13k4i naming THIS ticket as the one that deletes it. It is now empty. A ratchet
that never reaches zero is a backlog wearing a guard's clothes.

### Four tests pinned the old contract; all four are CONTRACT CHANGES, recorded as such
  tests/modes/test_llm_internals (x2), tests/test_composition (x1) — asserted the compiler
    receives a live model ('Verbatim — the raw RawText, not BAML-rendered')
  tests/test_prompt_compiler — the tripwire neograph-cbfd9 deliberately left, asserting
    the Pydantic repr and saying in place that ufqr7 would break it. It fired on cue.
Three of the four failed via l2a7w's own Rendered.__getattr__ ('text' on already-rendered
prompt text) rather than by silently asserting against an empty string — the loudness
bought two tickets ago is what surfaced this one's blast radius.

### Docs
node-api/modifier-kwargs.mdx (prose + the Rendered table row) and concepts/spec-format.mdx
now say what is actually true: never renderer-wrapped, still text, presenter honored.
Website builds, 45 pages.

Gate: 3132 passed / 0 failed (baseline 3114), mypy clean 82 files, ruff clean,
_llm_render.py back at its 445-line budget (trimmed the comment rather than raising the
budget), 23/23 keyless examples pass.
close_reason: Fixed in b10539c. Cast deleted, reads via read_upstream, rendered via to_prompt_input(renderer=None). Upstream-read guard allowlist now empty. Docs corrected.

title: Agent Spec export: outermost Construct's EndNode declares no outputs, so a third-party runtime's invoke() result is always empty
description:
Found during dgbqv.2's implementation (neograph-jn555.31, 2026-08-06), the COMPARE tier's own distinct finding (not a restatement of qtfof.6/.7/.8): the third-party pyagentspec AgentSpecLoader runtime completes without raising on the simplest scripted cells but returns an EMPTY outputs map, e.g. scripted-oracle-merge_fn-single: third-party = {}, neograph's own run(compile(...)) = {"ok": "done"} (terminal node "gen").

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed against the installed pyagentspec SDK source, pyagentspec/adapters/langgraph/_node_execution.py:256-291 EndNodeExecutor._update_status): the final invoke() result's 'outputs' key is built as {property_.title: outputs.get(property_.title, property_.default) for property_ in (self.flow_outputs or [])} -- i.e. it iterates over the EndNode's DECLARED outputs list. neograph's export (_agent_spec.py:619-622) builds end_props = _properties_for(construct.output) and only sets EndNode(outputs=end_props) when construct.output is not None. For the OUTERMOST Construct passed to compile()/run() directly (not used as a sub-construct item), construct.output is ALWAYS None by neograph's own design (only sub-constructs used as items need a declared boundary output type) -- so the outermost EndNode's outputs list is empty, flow_outputs is empty, and the third-party runtime's invoke() 'outputs' key is unconditionally {} regardless of what the graph actually computed.

This is invisible to both the WIRE tier (Flow.from_dict round-trip) and the reachability tier (control-graph shape only) -- neither executes the graph or inspects what a consumer would receive back. It is exactly the class of defect dgbqv.2's EXECUTE+COMPARE tiers exist to catch.

FIX DIRECTION (not yet designed): the outermost Construct's exported EndNode needs SOME declared outputs for a third-party consumer to receive anything -- likely derived from the terminal node(s)' own output type(s) (the same node(s) test_agent_spec_execute.py's terminal-node heuristic already identifies for the neograph-side comparison). Needs its own design pass: does this apply universally to every outermost Construct export, or only when the caller opts in (a new to_agent_spec() parameter)? Does it interact with the multi-exit-branch case (an outermost Construct can have multiple terminal nodes on different branches)?
design:
## Root Cause                                                               
                                                                            
_agent_spec.py:619-621 builds end_props = _properties_for(construct.output) 
and                                                                         
EndNode(outputs=end_props or None). For the OUTERMOST Construct             
construct.output                                                            
is always None by design, so end_props is empty -> pyagentspec's            
EndNodeExecutor                                                             
iterates an empty flow_outputs and a third-party invoke() returns {}        
unconditionally (failure mode (a)).                                         
                                                                            
Independently, NO DataFlowEdge ever feeds a synthetic EndNode, so whenever  
the                                                                         
EndNode DOES declare outputs the loader raises                              
Expected node '<name>__end' to have a value for property '<x>' (failure mode
(b)).                                                                       
                                                                            
**CORRECTED SCOPE (atom neograph-q14v5.39, empirically verified --          
supersedes**** this                                                         
****field's earlier text).** The earlier statement that mode (b) is specific
to the                                                                      
outermost Construct "because no parent exists to wire the peer edge a sub-  
flow item's                                                                 
parent normally provides" is FALSE. _emit_input_edges only ever targets real
construct ITEMS (input_targets_by_item_name[item_name]); a synthetic EndNode
is not                                                                      
an item at ANY nesting level, so no parent wires the inner one either. A    
NESTED                                                                      
sub-Construct with a declared output= -- the normal, validated way to use   
one --                                                                      
raises identically:                                                         
                                                                            
  Construct('outer', nodes=[head, construct_from_functions('sub',[inner1,   
inner2],output=B)])                                                         
  -> ValueError: Expected node `sub__end` to have a value for property `b`  
                                                                            
**The fix must therefore wire terminal-producer -> EndNode for EVERY****    
Construct                                                                   
****export, outermost AND nested, not only the outermost.**                 
                                                                            
## Fix Approach                                                             
                                                                            
Extract ONE shared boundary-wiring helper (declare the terminal producer's  
output                                                                      
Properties on the EndNode AND emit the real DataFlowEdge into it), used by  
every                                                                       
Construct export. Deliberately a new module, not an edit in place:          
tests/test_guards_file_size.py:73 pins "_agent_spec.py": 650 as an EXACT    
ceiling                                                                     
and the file is 650 lines today, so appending fails CI; and qtfof.11 /      
qtfof.12 are                                                                
both specified to reuse this same helper, so a shared module is the right   
shape                                                                       
regardless (AGENTS.md's ModifierCombo single-source-of-truth lesson).       
                                                                            
Mechanics, with the ticket's original reuse premises corrected (architect   
review                                                                      
neograph-q14v5.41, findings R3/R4/R5):                                      
                                                                            
• **Terminal producer set = DATA plane**: derive from construct.nodes[-1]   
via                                                                         
data_node_by_item_name (keyed by ITEM name). Do NOT derive it from exits[-1] --
those are control-plane SpecNodes and include an Operator's pause node and, 
for an                                                                      
empty arm, the BranchingNode itself, none of which produce a domain output. 
• **Edge emission**: reuse _emit_input_edges rather than writing a second   
emitter,                                                                    
but note it subscripts input_targets_by_item_name[item_name] directly and so
raises KeyError for a non-item. Register the EndNode under a synthetic key  
as                                                                          
[(end_node, False)] before the data-edge phase. Also note the EndNode is    
currently                                                                   
constructed AFTER that phase (:621), so its construction must be hoisted.   
• **Do NOT try to import the test-side terminal heuristic.**                
max(neograph_side, key=...) in tests/test_agent_spec_execute.py runs over a 
RUNTIME RESULT dict the exporter does not have. Parity with it is a property
to                                                                          
assert, not code to share.                                                  
• **Conformance must move in lockstep**: NARROW (do not delete) the         
outermost_end_node_unwired predicate in _agent_spec_conformance.py:104-110 --
tests/test_guards_agent_spec_conformance.py fails on a stale entry, and     
qtfof.12's gated-Portal shape still legitimately reaches that check. Note   
export_conformance() is public API.                                         
                                                                            
## BLOCKED -- two decisions required before implementing                    
                                                                            
• **R1: universal, or opt-in via a new **to_agent_spec()** parameter?**     
Review                                                                      
recommends UNIVERSAL (an opt-in default that still returns {} leaves the    
silent                                                                      
seam), but the blast radius covers every exported artifact and public       
export_conformance() output.                                                
• **R2: multi-exit branch -- what does ONE EndNode declare when arms        
terminate**** in                                                            
****different producers?** Union reintroduces mode (b); union-with-defaults 
trades one                                                                  
silent seam for another; requiring arm convergence (reusing                 
ArmScopedProducers.output_reachable_on_every_arm) + fail-loud is the only   
seam-free option but makes currently-exporting constructs start raising.    
                                                                            
See the full rated review in NOTES (atom neograph-q14v5.41).                

## MAINTAINER DECISIONS (2026-08-14)

R1: UNIVERSAL. Every to_agent_spec() call gets correct EndNode outputs automatically -- no opt-in parameter. An opt-in whose default still returns {} for callers who don't know to pass it leaves the exact silent seam this bug is about.

R2: FAIL-LOUD, require arm convergence. Reuse ArmScopedProducers.output_reachable_on_every_arm (the existing neograph-ftnxl.2 machinery) -- if a Construct's terminal producer set does not converge on every branch arm, raise ConfigurationError at export time rather than guessing (union reintroduces failure mode (b); union-with-defaults trades one silent seam for another). This makes constructs that export today start raising IF they have genuinely divergent per-arm terminal outputs -- acceptable per the north star (loud > silent).

Multi-exit-branch topology itself (a Construct with >1 terminal node on different branches, each independently reachable) is NOT permanently unsupported -- LangGraph's underlying graph model supports arbitrary branch/merge/branch-again topologies, and neograph itself has no structural reason to forbid it long-term. The fail-loud behavior here is a SCOPE BOUNDARY for the Agent Spec EXPORT PATH specifically (this ticket), not a statement that neograph can never represent multi-exit constructs. File a follow-up ticket for supporting multi-exit-branch Agent Spec export properly (e.g. a Flow with multiple EndNodes, or a documented convention) -- do not conflate with this fix.
notes:
## Merged from duplicate ticket neograph-qtfof.10 (2026-08-06)

Independently re-discovered and filed by the orchestrator after taking over dgbqv.2's implementation from a stalled agent (this ticket, qtfof.9, was filed by that same stalled agent shortly before being killed for inactivity -- its bd action had not yet synced into the orchestrator's context). Same root defect, complementary detail worth preserving:

qtfof.10 additionally noted the DataFlowEdge angle for the case where construct.output IS explicitly set on an outermost Construct: even then, the EndNode's declared outputs have zero DataFlowEdge feeding them (no parent exists to wire the peer edge the way a sub-flow item's parent would), so pyagentspec's AgentSpecLoader raises 'Expected node <end> to have a value for property <X>' rather than returning an empty dict. This is the SECOND failure mode of the same root cause (this ticket's case (a) is construct.output=None -> silently empty {}; the merged case (b) is construct.output set but unwired -> raises).

FIX DIRECTION addendum from qtfof.10: whatever fix computes end_props for the outermost Construct must ALSO wire a real DataFlowEdge from the terminal producer node(s) into the EndNode -- declaring the property alone (without the edge) only trades a silent empty-dict failure for a loud missing-property one, it doesn't make the third party's invoke() actually return the computed value. The SAME peer-edge wiring machinery a sub-flow item's parent provides needs to be applied to the EndNode itself when there's no parent to provide it.

Duplicate ticket neograph-qtfof.10 closed, referencing this ticket as canonical.
## Reproduction
- Failing tests: tests/test_agent_spec_execute.py::TestOutermostConstructEndNodeHasNoOutputs::test_third_party_invoke_returns_empty_outputs_for_a_simple_outermost_construct (mode a: construct.output=None -> silently {} vs expected {'ok': 'done'})
- Failing test: tests/test_agent_spec_execute.py::TestOutermostConstructEndNodeWithDeclaredOutputRaises::test_third_party_invoke_raises_when_outermost_output_is_declared_but_unwired (mode b: construct.output set but unwired -> raises ValueError: Expected node `qtfof9-mode-b__end` to have a value for property `ok`, but none was found)
- Both confirmed via uv run pytest, 2 failed, matching the ticket's predicted symptoms exactly.
- Root cause: _agent_spec.py's outermost EndNode gets end_props=_properties_for(construct.output) (always empty for a top-level Construct) and, even when output is set, no DataFlowEdge wires the terminal producer node(s)' output into it.
## Trace-Similar
Pattern category: 'a boundary Property list left empty because a sub-construct-only field defaults to None for the outermost Construct, causing a downstream pyagentspec node to have no data to work with.'

Checked the symmetric case: the outermost Construct's synthetic StartNode also gets start_props = _properties_for(construct.input), which is likewise always None/empty for a top-level Construct (same design reason). This is NOT the same bug, though it is related:
- EndNode: empty declared outputs means the loader either drops already-COMPUTED data (mode a) or raises (mode b) -- a real data-loss/crash defect, because the EndNode is an EXTRACTION point being read AFTER the graph ran.
- StartNode: empty declared inputs means the third party gets no type-casting/introspection metadata for what invoke() must be called with, but pyagentspec's StartNodeExecutor sources inputs directly from the caller's invoke() kwargs (not from a peer DataFlowEdge), so no data is silently dropped -- it is a documentation/introspection gap, not a correctness defect. Not filing a separate ticket: the same fix design pass (this ticket's open question about universality) should decide whether outermost StartNode also deserves declared inputs for symmetry, since it's a natural extension of the same design decision rather than an independent bug.

No other instance found: sub-construct items already get start_props/end_props from their declared input=/output= boundary (see _agent_spec.py comment above end_props, this was deliberately handled for sub-constructs already -- Loop self-feedback edge, Oracle variant fan-in). The gap is scoped exactly to the outermost Construct, matching the ticket's own framing ('a universal property of outermost-Construct export, not a per-shape defect' -- per test_agent_spec_execute.py's _compute_compare_exempt docstring).
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-qtfof.9)

Pattern: raw `edges_mod.DataFlowEdge(...)` construction bypassing the canonical peer-edge wiring closure (`_emit_input_edges`, _agent_spec.py:429-480), which is the single place item-to-item data wiring is currently centralized.
Scan command: grep -rn "DataFlowEdge(" src/neograph/*.py
Total instances found: 3 (1 is the canonical helper itself, 2 are candidate disease instances)

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | _agent_spec.py:476 | `edges_mod.DataFlowEdge(...)` inside `_emit_input_edges` closure | N/A (canonical) | This IS the canonical helper, not an instance of the disease. |
| 2 | _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:252 | `edges_mod.DataFlowEdge(...)` in Oracle variant fan-in (`_lower_oracle`) | ALLOWLIST | Genuinely different edge shape: N-variant-to-1-merge fan-in chain with prompt-flat-map routing (merge_orig_to_flat) that `_emit_input_edges` has no equivalent for -- not a duplicate, a specialization. |
| 3 | _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:444 | `edges_mod.DataFlowEdge(...)` in Loop self-feedback edge (`_lower_loop` body) | ALLOWLIST | Self-loop edge (source_node == destination_node) gated by `property_mod.property_is_castable_to`, a materially different compatibility check than `_emit_input_edges`'s translation-map routing. Not a duplicate. |

No MIGRATE or DEFER rows -- both non-canonical instances are legitimate specializations, not disease duplication.

## Actionable finding for the fix design (not this atom's job to implement)
The outermost EndNode fix should NOT add a 4th raw `DataFlowEdge(...)` site. `_emit_input_edges` is a LOCAL CLOSURE defined inside `to_agent_spec` (not a module-level helper), but it is defined BEFORE end_props is computed (~line 619) in the SAME function scope, so it is already in scope at the fix site. `_emit_input_edges(item_name, ...)` looks up `input_targets_by_item_name[item_name]`, which only has entries for real construct items today. The clean reuse path: register a synthetic entry `input_targets_by_item_name[<end-node-sentinel-name>] = [(end_node, iterated=False)]` before the closure is invoked for the EndNode's terminal-producer edges, then call `_emit_input_edges` exactly as every other consumer does -- this reuses translation/flat-map handling for free and adds zero new edge-construction sites. Whether the sentinel item_name needs a matching entry in `item_by_name` too (for the `_is_translation_eligible`/`_node_translation` lookups inside the closure) needs verification during implementation.
## Architect Review (neograph-qtfof.9)

1. Root cause correctness: LOW. Confirmed by 2 failing tests reproducing both predicted failure modes exactly, and independently verified against the installed pyagentspec SDK source (EndNodeExecutor._cast_values_and_add_defaults).

2. Fix minimality: LOW. The disease-scan's reuse path (register a synthetic input_targets_by_item_name entry for the EndNode, then call the existing _emit_input_edges closure) adds zero new DataFlowEdge construction sites.

3. Regression risk: MEDIUM -> resolved below. Making the outermost EndNode declare non-empty outputs is a wire-format change for every exported top-level Flow. Checked tests/test_agent_spec_export.py and test_agent_spec_flow_walk.py for any assertion that the outermost EndNode.outputs is empty/None -- found none. No existing test pins the current (broken) empty-outputs shape, so this is safe to change unconditionally.

4. Architecture compliance: LOW, contingent on following the disease-scan's reuse recommendation (no new duplicated edge-construction site).

5. Similar-bug scalability: LOW. trace-similar found no other instance of the same defect; disease-scan found no duplicate wiring logic elsewhere.

6. Test coverage sufficiency: MEDIUM -> resolved below (was the ticket's own open design question, now given a concrete recommendation rather than left open).

## Resolution of the ticket's open design question
'Does this apply universally to every outermost Construct export, or only opt-in? Does it interact with the multi-exit-branch case?'

RECOMMENDATION: Apply UNCONDITIONALLY (no new to_agent_spec() parameter) whenever the outermost Construct has exactly ONE terminal producer node -- this covers every existing GREEN compare-matrix cell and the overwhelming majority of real pipelines, and matches the existing sub-flow-item precedent (declared boundary props are unconditional there too, not opt-in). tests/test_agent_spec_export.py::test_multi_node_arm (the 'multi-node-arm' fixture) proves the codebase ALREADY has multi-terminal-node constructs (a _BranchNode with two arms both reconverging on one EndNode via control-flow edges) -- so the multi-exit-branch case is real, not hypothetical, and pyagentspec 26.1.2 explicitly REJECTS two same-titled outputs of different sources without disambiguation (_validate_outputs_with_same_name_do_not_exist, already referenced in _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py's Oracle fan-in comment) -- naively unioning divergent-type terminal properties across arms risks hitting that validator or silently producing a wrong schema.

Scope THIS ticket's fix to the single-terminal-node case (derive end_props from that one terminal node's output type, wire one DataFlowEdge). For the multi-exit-branch case, FAIL LOUD with a clear ConfigurationError at export time naming the construct and the divergent terminal nodes, rather than attempting a union -- and file a follow-up ticket for real multi-exit-branch EndNode output support (deferred, not silently dropped). This keeps the fix minimal and testable while turning the previously-open design question into a bounded, implementable scope.

## Overall verdict: ALL_LOW (the two MEDIUM risks are resolved above with concrete, actionable recommendations -- no unresolved question blocks the fix)
## Triage
Verdict: ALL_LOW. Clean review -- proceeding to fix.
## Similar-Pattern Trace (atom neograph-q14v5.39)

Pattern category: **a boundary node's declared I/O is derived from a field that is
None/absent at that boundary, and/or is declared with NO DataFlowEdge feeding it --
producing an exported artifact a third-party runtime either silently empties or hard-rejects.**

Four instances found. Instance 1 MATERIALLY CORRECTS this ticket's DESIGN field.

### 1. SAME BUG, wider scope: EVERY sub-Construct's EndNode is ALSO unwired (_agent_spec.py:619-622)
This ticket's DESIGN says failure mode (b) happens because "no parent exists to wire the
peer edge a sub-flow item's parent normally provides via _emit_input_edges/
data_node_by_item_name". **That premise is FALSE.** Nobody wires the inner EndNode either --
_emit_input_edges only ever targets `input_targets_by_item_name[item_name]`, i.e. real
construct ITEMS. The synthetic EndNode is never an item, at any nesting level.

Empirically confirmed (probe: outer=Construct([head, sub]), sub=construct_from_functions(
'sub',[inner1,inner2],output=B), run through the real pyagentspec AgentSpecLoader):

    RAISED: ValueError Expected node `sub__end` to have a value for property `b`,
            but none was found.

and the exported shape shows the hole directly:
    FlowNode sub        | in: []    | out: ['b']
      StartNode sub__start | in: [] | out: []
      ToolNode inner1      | in: [] | out: ['a']
      ToolNode inner2      | in: ['inner1:a'] | out: ['b']
      EndNode  sub__end    | in: ['b'] | out: ['b']    <-- declared, ZERO edges feeding it
    outer/sub data edges: [('inner1','a','inner2','inner1:a')]   <-- no *__end edge

So mode (b) is NOT specific to a manually-output-annotated outermost Construct: it fires for
EVERY sub-Construct with a declared `output=`, which is the NORMAL, validated, documented way
to use a sub-construct. **Fix scope consequence: the terminal-producer -> EndNode DataFlowEdge
must be emitted for EVERY Construct export (outermost AND nested), not only the outermost.**

Why nothing caught it: tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py builds ZERO nested sub-Construct cells
(every `construct_from_functions(nm, ...)` call at :247/:258/:288/:298/:308/:321/:332/:348/
:359/:370/:381 is the TOP-LEVEL cell construct). So the EXECUTE/COMPARE grid never exercises a
FlowNode sub-flow at all -- a real coverage blind spot, not an EXEC_EXEMPT sweep.

### 2. SAME SHAPE: an Each sub-flow's EndNode declares no outputs -> MapNode exposes none
`_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:303`: `end_node = nodes_mod.EndNode(name=f"{node.name}__each_end")`
-- no `outputs=`. pyagentspec's MapNode infers its OWN outputs from the inner EndNode, so:

    MapNode work | inputs: ['iterated_item:v'] | outputs: []

i.e. an Each-modified node exports a node that produces NOTHING a downstream consumer can
source a DataFlowEdge from. The asymmetry is explicit and documented in that same function:
the comment at :283-302 records that the StartNode's INPUT side was deliberately given
declared Properties for exactly this reason (neograph-hf505 / neograph-cbpyx). The EndNode's
OUTPUT side never received the symmetric treatment.
DISTINCT from neograph-qtfof.7, which is about the MapNode's `iterated_item` INPUT having no
DataFlowEdge. This is the MapNode's OUTPUT side. Do not conflate.

### 3. SAME SHAPE: Portal-operator gated mesh EndNodes (_agent_spec_portal.py:200-201)
`end_default` / `end_paused` are constructed with no `outputs=`, and the enclosing Flow at
:203-224 is built with NO `data_flow_connections=` argument at all. Same disease, third
construction site. Currently unexercised (the matrix has zero GREEN Portal cells --
conformance's `portal_mesh_unverified` records exactly that), but note the *gated* path
returns a **Flow**, not a Swarm, so it falls PAST `_flow_findings`' Swarm early-return into
`_check_outermost_end_node` -- the conformance classifier would flag it as this same bead.

`start_props = _properties_for(construct.input)`; outermost `construct.input` is always None by
