has no way to SUPPLY anything. Latent rather than active only because DI is not exported at all
(`grep -n "FromInput|FromConfig|_param_res|DIBinding" src/neograph/_agent_spec*.py` -> zero
hits), so today there is nothing to feed. Recording as the symmetric half of the same design
assumption; it is a separate, larger gap (DI has no Agent Spec representation) and should NOT
be folded into this fix.

### Already-known, correctly classified (no action)
`_agent_spec_conformance.py:104-110` already declares the `outermost_end_node_unwired`
predicate against this exact bead, and `_check_outermost_end_node` (:192-206) already detects
it post-export. The classifier is right; the exporter is wrong. Whatever fix lands must make
that predicate stop firing for the normal case, and `tests/test_guards_agent_spec_conformance.py`
asserts no stale predicate entry -- so retiring/narrowing it is part of the fix, not optional.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-qtfof.9) -- atom neograph-q14v5.40

**Pattern**: a synthetic Flow-BOUNDARY node (StartNode/EndNode) whose declared I/O is
derived from a field that is None at that boundary, and/or is declared with NO
DataFlowEdge feeding it -- yielding an exported artifact a foreign runtime either
silently empties ({} outputs) or hard-rejects ("Expected node X to have a value for
property Y").

**Classified SYNTACTIC, not semantic** -- deliberately, and this is the gate
justification. The disease has exactly one lexical form: a `StartNode(` / `EndNode(`
constructor call. pyagentspec boundary nodes cannot be produced any other way, so a
single grep is EXHAUSTIVE by construction, not merely a good sample -- there is no
"expressed differently" variant for a multi-agent semantic sweep to find. Per the
atom's own rule ("SYNTACTIC -> a single grep / AST scan is sufficient -- do NOT fan
out"), no targeted /dev-practices:code-review was invoked and no
.claude/code-review/neograph-qtfof.9/ artifact exists; the SEMANTIC-only artifact
precondition does not apply.

**Scan commands (exact, reproducible)**:

    grep -rn "StartNode(\|EndNode(" src/neograph/     # 7 hits -- every boundary node
    grep -rn "flow_mod\.Flow(\|Flow(" src/neograph/   # 3 hits -- every Flow assembly

**Total instances found: 7** (across all 3 Flow-assembly sites; the whole disease
surface is confined to src/neograph/_agent_spec*.py).

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | _agent_spec.py:621 | `EndNode(outputs=end_props or None)`, `end_props=_properties_for(construct.output)`; never fed by a DataFlowEdge | **MIGRATE** | The motivating site, BOTH failure modes. Scope is WIDER than the ticket states: per atom .39 this also breaks every NESTED sub-Construct with a declared `output=` (empirically: `ValueError: Expected node sub__end to have a value for property b`). Fix must cover outermost AND nested. |
| 2 | _agent_spec.py:620 | `StartNode(inputs=start_props or None)`, `start_props=_properties_for(construct.input)` | **ALLOWLIST** | The input-side mirror, but LATENT, not broken: DI (`FromInput`/`FromConfig`) has no Agent Spec representation at all (`grep -n "FromInput\|FromConfig\|_param_res\|DIBinding" src/neograph/_agent_spec*.py` -> zero hits), so there is nothing a caller could supply and nothing to wire. Closing it means designing DI export -- a strictly larger gap that must not ride along on this fix. |
| 3 | _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:302 | `StartNode(inputs=inner_inputs or None)` (Each sub-flow) | **ALLOWLIST** | Already CORRECT, and is the reference implementation for the pattern -- the input side was deliberately given declared Properties by neograph-hf505 / neograph-cbpyx. Nothing to migrate; it is what the other sites should look like. |
| 4 | _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:303 | `EndNode(f"{node.name}__each_end")` -- no outputs at all -> MapNode infers `outputs: []` | **DEFER** | **neograph-qtfof.11** (filed). Same disease, but carries an independent unresolved design question qtfof.9 does not: a MapNode's result is a fan-out COLLECTION, so whether the inner EndNode declares the inner node's bare Properties (or a list wrapper) must be settled against the pyagentspec SDK first. Distinct from qtfof.7 (that is the MapNode's INPUT side). |
| 5 | _agent_spec_portal.py:199 | `StartNode(name=...)` -- no inputs (gated Portal mesh Flow) | **DEFER** | **neograph-qtfof.12** (filed). |
| 6 | _agent_spec_portal.py:200 | `EndNode(...__end_default)` -- no outputs | **DEFER** | **neograph-qtfof.12** (filed). |
| 7 | _agent_spec_portal.py:201 | `EndNode(...__end_paused)` -- no outputs; enclosing Flow (:203-224) passes NO `data_flow_connections` at all | **DEFER** | **neograph-qtfof.12** (filed). The Portal tier is empirically unverified (zero GREEN Portal cells in the matrix -- exactly what the `portal_mesh_unverified` predicate records), so there is no executable evidence to fix against. Getting a Portal cell executable is a prerequisite, not part of this bug. |

Both DEFER tickets were filed with `discovered-from:neograph-qtfof.9` and both
explicitly require reusing the helper this fix lands rather than writing a parallel
implementation -- so the ratchet is one shared wiring rule, not four copies.
## Architect Review (atom neograph-q14v5.41)

Verdict: **NEEDS_USER_INPUT.** Two genuine, undetermined design decisions (R1, R2)
that the codebase does not answer and that change the artifact every consumer
receives. Everything else is tractable, but three of the ticket's own stated
"reuse this existing machinery" premises are FALSE as written (R3, R4, R5) and
would seed a parallel implementation if followed literally.

### 1. Root cause correctness -- **LOW** (confirmed, with one correction)
Re-verified against current code and the installed SDK. `_agent_spec.py:619-621` is
exactly as described: `end_props = _properties_for(construct.output)`, and
`EndNode(outputs=end_props or None)`. The pyagentspec side was re-confirmed live,
not read: mode (a) yields `{}` and mode (b) raises from
`.venv/.../pyagentspec/adapters/langgraph/_node_execution.py:161`
(`Expected node 'qtfof9-mode-b__end' to have a value for property 'ok'`). Both
repro tests fail today, no xfail, real third-party loader.

CORRECTION already recorded in atom .39: the DESIGN field's stated mechanism --
"no parent exists to wire the peer edge a sub-flow item's parent normally provides
via `_emit_input_edges`/`data_node_by_item_name`" -- is FALSE. `_emit_input_edges`
only ever targets real construct ITEMS; a synthetic EndNode is not an item at ANY
nesting level, so no parent wires the inner one either. Empirically a nested
sub-Construct with a declared `output=` raises the identical error
(`Expected node 'sub__end' to have a value for property 'b'`). The root cause is
right; the scope statement attached to it is not.

### 2. Fix minimality -- **MEDIUM**
Minimal in shape (declare + wire at one site) but NOT minimal in blast radius,
because it is universal-by-default over every exported artifact. Two constraints
bound how minimal it can actually be:

* **The file-size ratchet forbids the obvious edit.** `tests/test_guards_file_size.py:73`
  pins `"_agent_spec.py": 650` and the ceiling is EXACT, not a maximum
  (`ALLOWLIST[f] == len(splitlines())`); `_agent_spec.py` is 650 lines today, i.e.
  ZERO headroom. Per AGENTS.md, growth is "blocked and fixed in-PR, never deferred"
  -- so appending the wiring to `to_agent_spec` fails CI by construction. The fix
  MUST extract the boundary-wiring rule into its own module. This is a happy
  convergence rather than a tax: qtfof.11 and qtfof.12 are both specified to reuse
  the same helper, so a shared `_agent_spec_boundary`-style module is the design the
  ratchet was going to force anyway. Do not "solve" this by raising the number.
* **Sequencing.** The data-edge phase (~:558-593) runs BEFORE the EndNode is
  constructed (:621). Wiring INTO the EndNode requires either hoisting its
  construction above the phase or emitting the boundary edges after it. Small, but
  it is a real ordering constraint on any "just add a line" plan.

### 3. Regression risk -- **MEDIUM** overall
* Round-trip (import) side: **LOW, verified not assumed.** `loader.py:145` skips
  `StartNode`/`EndNode` outright, and `_agent_spec_node_import._inputs_from_data_edges`
  selects edges by `e.destination_node.name == dest_name` where `dest_name` is a
  reconstructed TOP-LEVEL item. New `terminal -> __end` edges therefore match no
  importer query and cannot manufacture a phantom `Node.inputs` entry.
* Conformance/public-API side: **MEDIUM.** `_agent_spec_conformance.py:104-110`
  declares the `outermost_end_node_unwired` predicate against this bead and
  `_check_outermost_end_node` (:192-206) detects it post-export. That predicate
  feeds `export_conformance()`, which is PUBLIC API (shipped a3844bd). Fixing the
  exporter changes public classifier output for essentially every construct, and
  `tests/test_guards_agent_spec_conformance.py` asserts no STALE predicate entry --
  so retiring or narrowing the predicate is part of this fix, not a follow-up.
  Note it must be NARROWED, not deleted: qtfof.12 (gated Portal) still legitimately
  produces output-less EndNodes and currently falls through to this same check.
* Artifact-shape side: **MEDIUM.** Every exported Flow gains EndNode Properties and
  at least one DataFlowEdge. Any WIRE/reachability/matrix assertion pinning exact
  node or edge counts will move.

### 4. Architecture compliance -- **LOW, if the shared-helper form is honoured**
Directly on point for AGENTS.md's ModifierCombo lesson (2026-07-27): the failure
mode to avoid is N consumers each growing their own copy of one rule. The scan found
exactly 3 Flow-assembly sites and 7 boundary-node sites -- a closed, enumerable
consumer set. One helper, three call sites, a structural guard enumerating them
(re-verified by re-running the grep, not copied) satisfies the discipline. Writing
the wiring inline at `_agent_spec.py:621` and leaving qtfof.11/.12 to reimplement it
later is the precise anti-pattern that lesson forbids.

### 5. Similar-bug scalability -- **LOW**
The disease surface is closed and enumerable (7 sites, disposition table above); a
shared helper plus a guard scales to all of them. The two DEFERs are deferred for
independent design reasons, not for want of a mechanism.

### 6. Test coverage sufficiency -- **MEDIUM**
The two repro tests cover only a LINEAR outermost construct. Uncovered and required:
* **The nested sub-Construct case** -- empirically broken today (atom .39) and NOT
  covered by any test. Root cause: `tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py` builds ZERO
  nested sub-Construct cells (every `construct_from_functions(nm, ...)` at :247/:258/
  :288/:298/:308/:321/:332/:348/:359/:370/:381 is the top-level cell construct), so
  the entire FlowNode sub-flow shape escapes the EXECUTE/COMPARE grid. A fix verified
  only against the two current repro tests would leave this broken.
* **The multi-exit-branch case** (see R2) -- no test exists in either direction.
* **Three-surface parity** (AGENTS.md): `to_agent_spec` consumes the IR, so the
  declarative `Construct(nodes=[Node(...)])` and programmatic `Node() | Modifier()`
  surfaces should each be exercised at least once, not just `@node`.
* **The COMPARE tier's own expected-value heuristic is fragile** and worth hardening
  while here: `terminal = max(neograph_side, key=lambda name: list(neograph_side).index(name))`
  is an elaborate spelling of "the last key of a dict", i.e. it assumes neograph's run
  result is insertion-ordered with the terminal node last. That assumption is exactly
  what a branchy or parallel graph breaks -- the same case R2 is about.

---

## Risk items requiring a DECISION (not silently picked)

**R1 -- Universal, or opt-in via a new `to_agent_spec()` parameter? [HIGH]**
Recommendation: **UNIVERSAL**, but flagged rather than assumed because the blast
radius is every exported artifact plus public `export_conformance()` output.
Argument for universal: an opt-in flag whose DEFAULT still returns `{}` from a
third-party `invoke()` leaves the silent seam in place for every caller who does not
know to pass it -- which AGENTS.md's north star calls an existential defect, not
deferrable polish. It also cannot be justified as backwards compatibility: at 0.x
with one downstream consumer, the project's stated policy is no compat shims.
Argument for opt-in: it is the only way to keep today's exact artifact bytes stable
for the WIRE/reachability/conformance suites. That is a testing convenience, not a
user-facing requirement. **Decide before the fix atom; do not let the fix pick.**

**R2 -- Multi-exit branch: what does ONE EndNode declare when arms terminate in
different producers? [HIGH]**
An Agent Spec EndNode has a single `outputs` list, but when the last item is a
`_BranchNode`, `exits[-1]` carries one exit per arm with potentially different
producers and different output types. Three options, none free:
 (a) **Union of all arm terminals.** Whichever arm did NOT run leaves its Properties
     unfed -- which REINTRODUCES failure mode (b) for every branchy graph. Confirmed
     against SDK source: the raise is only avoided when
     `property_.default is not pyagentspec_empty_default`.
 (b) **Union with defaults attached.** Avoids the raise, but a consumer can then not
     distinguish "this arm did not run" from "this is a genuine default value" -- a
     NEW silent seam, traded for the one being closed. Rejecting a fix that swaps one
     silent seam for another is the north star's explicit decision filter.
 (c) **Require arm convergence.** neograph ALREADY has this primitive:
     `ArmScopedProducers.output_reachable_on_every_arm` (`_validation_arms.py:54`,
     consumed at `_construct_validation.py:371-380`) is precisely "the declared output
     is produced on EVERY arm". The catch: it is only evaluated when
     `construct.output is not None` -- i.e. exactly not the outermost case this bug is
     about. Reusing it for the outermost would mean either synthesizing a declared
     output or extending the contract, and a non-converging outermost branch would
     then have to FAIL LOUD at export.
Recommendation leans (c) + fail-loud, as the only option that does not create a new
silent seam -- but it makes some currently-exporting constructs start raising, which
is a user-visible policy call. **Undetermined; needs the maintainer.**

## Corrections to the ticket's stated reuse plan (act on these regardless of R1/R2)

**R3 -- "Reuse test_agent_spec_execute.py's terminal-node heuristic" is not
actionable. [MEDIUM]** That heuristic is
`max(neograph_side, key=lambda name: list(neograph_side).index(name))` -- it operates
on a RUNTIME RESULT dict, which the exporter does not have and cannot obtain. There
is no shared primitive to reuse here; the export-side analogue is
`construct.nodes[-1]` plus `data_node_by_item_name`. Pursuing literal reuse would
mean importing test code into `src/`. Treat "parity with the test heuristic" as a
property to ASSERT, never as code to share.

**R4 -- `_emit_input_edges` is only PARTIALLY reusable. [MEDIUM]** It is a closure
inside `to_agent_spec` and its second line is
`for target_node, iterated in input_targets_by_item_name[item_name]` -- a direct
subscript, so an EndNode (never an item) raises `KeyError`. It also runs
placeholder-translation gating (`_is_translation_eligible(dest_item)`) that is
meaningless for a boundary node. It CAN be reused cleanly by registering the EndNode
into `input_targets_by_item_name` under a synthetic key `[(end_node, False)]` before
the data phase -- which is the right call, since it keeps one edge-emitting rule.
But "it is already reusable as-is" is not true, and a fix author who discovers the
KeyError under time pressure is one step from writing a second emitter. State the
synthetic-registration approach explicitly in the fix task.

**R5 -- `exits[-1]` is the CONTROL plane; the terminal PRODUCER set is the DATA
plane. [MEDIUM]** The ticket proposes deriving `end_props` from the same
`(from_node, from_branch)` pairs that feed the synthetic end control edges. Those are
SpecNodes, and for an Operator item the set includes the pause node, which produces
no domain output at all; for a `_BranchNode` it includes the branch itself when an arm
is empty (`_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:518-523`). The data source must come from
`data_node_by_item_name`, keyed by ITEM name -- a different map with different
membership. Conflating the two is a live way to wire an edge out of a node that has
nothing to give.
## RECONCILIATION: two agents walked this chain concurrently (2026-08-14)

Two agents (`bug-qtfof9` and this one) were spawned against the SAME atom chain
neograph-q14v5.38-.42 and executed it in parallel. Both sets of findings are above,
appended non-destructively -- nothing was lost -- but the ATOM CLOSE REASONS were
overwritten by whichever finished last, and the two runs DISAGREE on three points.
Read this section before trusting either close reason.

Where they agree: the root cause at `_agent_spec.py:619-621`, and that a real
DataFlowEdge into the EndNode is required, not just a declared property.

Where they diverge -- and why the differences are empirical, not stylistic:

1. **Atom .39 close reason says "No separate bug found."** That is contradicted by a
   live repro. A NESTED sub-Construct with a declared `output=` -- the normal,
   validated way to use one -- raises under the real pyagentspec loader:
   `ValueError: Expected node 'sub__end' to have a value for property 'b'`. Command

   section above. Consequence: the fix must cover EVERY Construct export, not only
   the outermost. A fix scoped to the outermost alone leaves this broken and passes
   both current repro tests while doing so.

2. **Atom .40 close reason describes scanning "3 DataFlowEdge() sites".** That scans
   the wrong surface. The disease is a BOUNDARY NODE declared without outputs and/or
   without a feeding edge, so the exhaustive surface is
   `grep -rn "StartNode(\|EndNode(" src/neograph/` -> **7 sites**, not 3. The
   DataFlowEdge-site scan cannot see the two additional broken boundary sites it
   misses: `_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:303` (Each sub-flow EndNode -> MapNode
   exports `outputs: []`, verified by probe) and `_agent_spec_portal.py:200-201`
   (gated Portal mesh, plus a Flow built with no `data_flow_connections` at all).
   Those are now filed as neograph-qtfof.11 and neograph-qtfof.12.

3. **Atoms .41/.42 closed ALL_LOW, resolving the multi-exit-branch question
   unilaterally as "fail-loud".** Fail-loud is also THIS review's leaning, so the two
   runs are close on the merits -- but it makes constructs that export today start
   raising, which is a user-visible policy change, and the parallel open question
   (R1: universal vs opt-in) additionally changes the output of `export_conformance()`,
   which is public API. This run's verdict is NEEDS_USER_INPUT specifically because
   those are product decisions a review cannot settle, and the orchestrator's brief
   for this chain was explicit that they must not be picked silently.

**Recommended state**: treat R1 and R2 (see this ticket's DESIGN field) as still
requiring a maintainer answer before neograph-q14v5.43 runs, and treat the fix scope
as all-Construct-exports rather than outermost-only regardless of how R1/R2 land.

title: Agent Spec reachability tests never validate branch labels (from_branch) -- a branch-relabeling bug is invisible to the whole matrix
description:
Found during dgbqv.2's architect review's elegance/architectural lens (2026-08-06), proven by controlled mutation: relabeling the loop arm's exit branch ('done' -> 'continue', producing a BranchingNode with two 'continue' successors and no 'done' successor -- unrunnable for any literal executor) was caught by exactly ONE test in the whole tree (test_the_loop_exits_through_the_check_nodes_done_branch), and only by luck of that test targeting a plain-loop pipeline specifically; the entire test_agent_spec_loop_operator.py module (including round-trip and compile-and-run) passed unaffected, because _walk (test_agent_spec_reachability.py:81-101) collapses edges into an unlabelled successor set, discarding edge.from_branch entirely. All 13 from_branch assertions in tests/ are against hand-picked single pipelines; ZERO run over the 100-cell GREEN matrix.

Real exposure: 100 GREEN cells x every BranchingNode = no branch-label coverage anywhere in the systematic test suite. This is exactly the reachability tier's own stated policy ('correct for ANY real Agent Spec runtime that walks edges literally') failing to be enforced for the one thing that actually needs label-awareness: knowing which branch fires.

Fix direction: add a generic 'every exported ControlFlowEdge.from_branch names a branch its own BranchingNode.mapping declares' assertion, run matrix-wide over GREEN cells -- this is a real coverage gap that survives even after dgbqv.2 lands (dgbqv.2's own EXEC_EXEMPT fallback rule can mask a bogus label, so this needs its own dedicated check, not just inherited coverage from dgbqv.2).
design:
# dgbqv.10 DESIGN (research atom h71a2.10)

## Core Invariant (one sentence)

Every `BranchingNode`'s outgoing edges, across the whole exported `Flow` AND every
nested sub-`Flow` (recursively), must carry `from_branch` labels that are **exactly**
`set(node.mapping.values())` — no duplicate label among the edges, none of the
mapping's declared labels missing — so a literal edge-walking executor can always
resolve exactly one outgoing edge per branch outcome.

**Correction to the ticket's own fix-direction wording**: the ticket says "names a
branch its own `BranchingNode.mapping` declares" and fxfk5's note says "a declared
KEY of that node's mapping". Both are imprecise. `mapping` is `{outcome -> label}`
(`_agent_spec_markers.py:59-77`); `edge.from_branch` is always the LABEL, i.e. a
**mapping VALUE**, not a key. For the loop check (`mapping={continue: continue, done:
done}`) and the plain branch node (`{true: true, false: false}`) key and value
coincide, which hides the distinction — but the Operator composite's mapping is
`{true: pause, false: default}` (`_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:636`), where
`from_branch` is always `pause`/`default`, never `true`/`false`. A check written
against `mapping` keys would silently never fire on any Operator/Portal-operator
BranchingNode. The check MUST be against `set(node.mapping.values())`.

**A second, more consequential correction, verified empirically (see "Verification"
below): a membership/subset check ("is `from_branch` one of the declared labels")
is NOT sufficient** — it does not catch the ticket's own motivating mutation. The
check must assert the outgoing multiset of labels equals the mapping's value-set
EXACTLY (no dup, none missing), not merely that each label is drawn from a valid set.

## 1. Which current assertions are blind, file:line

All five "pairs" sites use `edge_pairs(flow)` (the unlabelled `{(from, to)}`
projection, `tests/agent_spec_flow_walk.py:111-117`) to assert edges exist, with NO
`from_branch` check on the edge — except where a *separate* `arm_targets(...,
Branch.PAUSE)` call already covers one specific arm. Per site:

- **`tests/test_agent_spec_each_operator.py:145`** (`test_map_node_chains_into_the_operator_check`)
  - `("each_step", "each_step__operator_check") in pairs` — source is a `MapNode`,
    not a `BranchingNode`; no label exists to be blind to. N/A.
  - `("each_step__operator_check", "each_step__operator_pause") in pairs` — source
    IS the operator `BranchingNode`, but this specific edge's label is already
    checked by the very next line, `arm_targets(flow, "each_step__operator_check",
    Branch.PAUSE)`. NOT blind for this edge.
  - **Blind gap**: the check node's OTHER outgoing edge — the `Branch.DEFAULT`
    reconvergence edge (`each_step__operator_check -> <next node>`, wired by the
    caller in `_agent_spec.py:337`, `[(check, Branch.DEFAULT), (pause, None)]`) —
    has NO assertion anywhere in this file, labelled or not.

- **`tests/test_agent_spec_oracle_operator.py:138`** — identical shape/gap: the
  `Branch.PAUSE` arm is checked via `arm_targets`; the `Branch.DEFAULT` arm off
  `ensemble__operator_check` is never asserted.

- **`tests/test_agent_spec_loop_operator.py:146`** — TWO BranchingNodes are in
  play here (`refine__loop_check` AND `refine__operator_check`), and this is the
  site structurally closest to the ticket's own cited regression:
  - `("refine__loop_check", "refine__operator_check") in pairs` — source is the
    LOOP's own `BranchingNode` (mapping `{continue: continue, done: done}`,
    `_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:373-375`). **Genuinely blind**: no label
    assertion exists for this edge anywhere in the file. This is exactly the shape
    of the ticket's cited bug (a Loop check's exit edge going unlabelled/mislabelled).
  - `("refine__operator_check", "refine__operator_pause") in pairs` +
    `arm_targets(..., Branch.PAUSE)` — covered, same as above.
  - **Blind gap**: `refine__operator_check`'s `Branch.DEFAULT` arm — never asserted.

- **`tests/test_agent_spec_each_oracle_operator.py:148`** — same shape as
  each_operator/oracle_operator: `Branch.PAUSE` arm covered via `arm_targets`;
  `Branch.DEFAULT` arm off `fanned__operator_check` never asserted.

- **`tests/test_agent_spec_each_oracle.py:168`** (subflow variant) — checked: this
  pipeline has NO `Operator`/`Loop`/plain-branch modifier at all (grepped for
  `BranchingNode`/`_lower_operator`/`_lower_loop`/`Operator(` in the file: zero
  hits). Its exported flow contains **no `BranchingNode`**, so there is no label to
  be blind to. Converting its `edge_pairs` use to a labelled form would be a
  style-parity nicety only, not a coverage fix for this bug class. Do not spend the
  fix budget here.

## 2. What the labelled assertion should be — derivable from combo, no per-cell table

**No per-cell/per-shape expectation table is needed.** Every `BranchingNode`
construction site (`_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:373` loop,  `:500` plain
branch, `:634` operator, `_agent_spec_portal.py:187` portal-operator) stamps its own
`mapping` onto the node at construction time. The expected label set for ANY
BranchingNode, in ANY cell, of ANY shape, is available **reflexively** by reading
that node's own `.mapping.values()` — the exported Flow already carries its own
expectation. A matrix-wide check therefore never needs to know "this is a Loop cell
so expect {continue, done}"; it just asks each BranchingNode to grade itself against
its own declared mapping. This is why the fix is a single generic assertion, not N
per-shape assertions.

## 3. The structural property, matrix-wide, verified against real exported flows

**Property**: for every `BranchingNode` `n` in every `Flow` reachable via
`all_flows(top)` (top-level + every nested sub-Flow, both subflow spellings), let
`edges_from_n = [e.from_branch for e in flow.control_flow_connections if
e.from_node.name == n.name]`. Then `edges_from_n`, as a multiset, must equal
`set(n.mapping.values())` as a set — i.e.: (a) no two edges leaving `n` share a
label, and (b) every label `n.mapping` declares has exactly one edge leaving `n`
carrying it, and (c) no edge leaving `n` carries a label absent from
`n.mapping.values()`.

**Verified empirically against every real GREEN cell** (script run against
`tests/test_agent_spec_matrix.py`'s `GREEN`/`CELLS`/`build_cell` +
`tests.agent_spec_flow_walk.all_flows`, this session): 62 `BranchingNode`s found
across the 100 GREEN cells (recursing into subflows); **zero violations of the
above property today** — the codebase is currently clean, so this is a pure
coverage-adding test, not a pre-existing-bug fix.

**Verified the mutation is caught by this property and NOT by a weaker
membership-only check** (script run against GREEN cell `act-loop-single`,
mutating the loop-check's `done`-branch exit edge's `from_branch` from
`Branch.DONE` to `Branch.CONTINUE` in-memory post-export):
- Membership-only check (`from_branch in mapping.values()` per edge, no
  dup/missing check): **0 violations found** — the mutated edge's label
  (`"continue"`) is still a value the mapping declares, so a subset check is blind
  to it. This confirms the ticket's own literal fix-direction phrasing ("names a
  branch its mapping declares") is insufficient as stated and must be tightened to
  the exact-multiset form above.
- Exact-multiset check (this design's property): **1 violation found** —
  `refine__loop_check` reported both a duplicate label (`continue` appears twice)
  and a missing label (`done` appears zero times). Exactly the ticket's cited
  defect shape.

**Recommended placement**: a new test class in `tests/test_agent_spec_reachability.py`
(the existing "TOPOLOGY proof" module, already `@pytest.mark.parametrize("cell_id",
sorted(GREEN))`-driven via `TestEveryExportedFlowIsLiterallyExecutable` at line ~70),
e.g. `TestBranchingNodeEdgesMatchTheirOwnMapping`, following the exact same
parametrization pattern: build the cell, `to_agent_spec`, walk `all_flows`, assert
the property per BranchingNode, fail loud naming the node + expected vs actual label
sets. Read edges via the existing seam's single edge read (`branch_adjacency` from
`tests/agent_spec_flow_walk.py`, filtered locally by `from_node == n.name`) rather
than a new seam function — the property is a one-off local reduction over the
existing primitive, not a second edge-reading path, so it does not need to widen
`agent_spec_flow_walk.py`'s public API.

## 4. Core Invariant

See top of document (repeated for the record): every `BranchingNode`'s outgoing
edges, across the whole exported Flow and every nested sub-Flow, must carry
`from_branch` labels that are exactly `set(node.mapping.values())` — no duplicate
label, none missing — so a literal edge-walking executor can always resolve exactly
one outgoing edge per branch outcome.

## 5. The relabel mutation that must fail once the fix lands (acceptance evidence)

Take any GREEN cell whose pipeline includes a `Loop` modifier (e.g. `act-loop-single`,
or the dedicated fixture in
`tests/test_agent_spec_reachability.py::TestLoopEntersTheBodyBeforeTheCheck._pipeline`).
Export it, then mutate: find the `ControlFlowEdge` whose `from_node.name` ends in
`__loop_check` and whose `from_branch == Branch.DONE`, and rewrite its `from_branch`
to `Branch.CONTINUE`. Result: the loop-check `BranchingNode` now has two
`continue`-labelled outgoing edges and zero `done`-labelled ones — unrunnable for
any literal executor (per the ticket's own framing).

- The new matrix-wide `TestBranchingNodeEdgesMatchTheirOwnMapping` test (item 3)
  must go RED for that cell, reporting `refine__loop_check` (or the cell's
  equivalent check-node name) with a duplicate `continue` label and a missing
  `done` label. This is the primary, high-confidence acceptance evidence — verified
  by the script run in this research session.
- If `tests/test_agent_spec_loop_operator.py:146`'s `refine__loop_check ->
  refine__operator_check` pairs-assertion is converted to a labelled form (item 1's
  loop_operator.py gap), it must ALSO go RED for this same mutation when the
  mutated pipeline is the Loop+Operator combo.
- The `each_operator.py` / `oracle_operator.py` / `each_oracle_operator.py`
  DEFAULT-arm gaps (item 1) are a DIFFERENT latent blind spot (the Operator
  composite's own `Branch.DEFAULT` reconvergence edge, not the Loop's `done` arm)
  — closing them is real coverage but will NOT turn red under THIS specific loop
  mutation; they need their own DEFAULT-relabel mutation as separate acceptance
  evidence if the executor chooses to fix them too.
- `each_oracle.py:168` needs no mutation-based acceptance at all (item 1: no
  BranchingNode in that pipeline).

## Scope recommendation for the write-plan atom

Two independent, additive changes, do both:

1. **Primary (matrix-wide, no table, highest value)**: add
   `TestBranchingNodeEdgesMatchTheirOwnMapping` to
   `tests/test_agent_spec_reachability.py`, parametrized over `sorted(GREEN)` same
   as its sibling class, implementing the property in item 3.
2. **Secondary (the ticket's named 5 sites)**: convert the genuinely-blind
   BranchingNode-sourced edges in `each_operator.py`, `oracle_operator.py`,
   `loop_operator.py`, `each_oracle_operator.py` to labelled assertions (via
   `arm_targets(flow, from_name, Branch.X)`, already imported in these files) for
   both arms of each operator `BranchingNode` (PAUSE already done; add DEFAULT) and
   for `loop_operator.py`'s `refine__loop_check -> refine__operator_check` edge
   (add `Branch.DONE`). Leave `each_oracle.py:168` as-is (no BranchingNode present,
   not blind, not part of this bug class) — note explicitly in the PR/commit so a
   later pass doesn't "fix" a non-issue there.

design:
# dgbqv.9 DESIGN v2 -- post-review, supersedes "## Plan (h71a2.2)" and the ADDENDUM

This is the ONE authoritative API list and plan. Where the earlier plan or the ADDENDUM
disagree with this file, this file wins; the superseded names are listed at the bottom so an
executor cannot pick a stale one.

## Core Invariant
A test-side graph walk must see EVERY node and EVERY labelled edge the exported Flow actually
contains -- across both subflow spellings, preserving from_branch AND its multiplicity -- and
must be reachable from any test module without dragging the marker-reading importer
(from_agent_spec) into its import graph.

## R0 -- IMPORT PURITY IS ABSOLUTE (review finding, verified empirically)
tests/agent_spec_flow_walk.py imports NOTHING from neograph. Not even Branch.

PROOF this matters (run, not assumed):
    import neograph._agent_spec_markers   ->  'neograph.loader' in sys.modules == True
Importing ANY neograph submodule executes src/neograph/__init__.py, whose line 65 is
"from neograph.loader import from_agent_spec, load_spec". So a single Branch import would put
from_agent_spec back in the module's import graph and contradict the Core Invariant -- while
the AST guard shipping alongside would NOT catch it. Decided here rather than discovered later.

Consequences:
  - every branch parameter is a plain `str`
  - CALLERS pass Branch.CONTINUE / Branch.PAUSE / ... in from their own modules
  - the module mirrors src/neograph/_agent_spec_graph.py's zero-neograph-import discipline and
    keeps the always-importable (Tier-A) property tests/agent_spec_capabilities.py has
  - a test in the module's own suite asserts 'neograph' not in sys.modules after importing it
    in a subprocess -- the same shape as test_guards_agent_spec_core_purity.py, because the
    AST guard structurally cannot prove this

## API -- 9 functions, every one a primitive or a pure projection of the single edge read
    sub_flows(flow)             -> list[Flow]        reads BOTH .subflow and .subflows
    all_flows(flow)             -> list[Flow]        BFS closure over sub_flows
    walk(flow)                  -> (set[str], set[str])   reachable-from-start, can-reach-end
                                                     (keeps the existing NAME; move verbatim first)
    branch_adjacency(flow)      -> list[(str, str|None, str)]   THE single edge read
    edge_pairs(flow)            -> set[(str, str)]    projection of branch_adjacency
    successors_of(flow, name)   -> list[str]          projection
    arm_targets(flow, name, branch) -> list[str]      projection; branch is a plain str
    entered_nodes(flow)         -> set[str]           see R2
    inner_nodes(holder)         -> list[Node]         498gr's seam; routes through sub_flows

R1 -- branch_adjacency is LIST-valued, never a set. Multiplicity is load-bearing:
  test_agent_spec_export.py:783, :1138, :1201 assert len(back_edges) == 1
  test_agent_spec_export.py:1157 asserts len(self_edges) == 1
A set silently collapses duplicate (from, branch, to) triples and weakens all four.

R2 -- entered_nodes must assert a THREE-WAY BIND before returning, not merely uniqueness.
Verified: walk() seeds from the DECLARED flow.start_node.name, while the two entered sites
(reachability.py:165 and :223, byte-identical) compute successors of any node whose TYPE NAME
is StartNode. Different questions. pyagentspec's Flow.start_node is annotated Node, not
StartNode, so the spec permits a Flow whose declared start is not the StartNode. All three
neograph exporters happen to pass the same object today (_agent_spec.py:620/644,
_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:302/335, _agent_spec_portal.py:187/193), which is exactly why
a straight unification looks green AND is still a narrowing: the TYPE form catches a second
StartNode appearing; the start_node form catches the declared start drifting off it.
entered_nodes therefore asserts: exactly one StartNode-typed node exists AND flow.start_node
IS that node AND the result is its outgoing edge targets. Own step, reachability suite green
before and after.

R3 -- GUARD SCOPE: control_flow_connections + subflow/subflows ONLY. Explicitly NOT
data_flow_connections.
Reason (review HIGH): tests/test_guards_agent_spec_data_flow_reads.py (neograph-p0dn8, landed
this session) ALREADY governs every data_flow_connections read in tests/ under a DIFFERENT
rule -- must be the left operand of a BoolOp(Or) -- with a ZERO-entry allowlist. A second
guard with a second rule over the same attribute is the duplicated-source-of-truth shape
CLAUDE.md's Portal lesson bans, and it would silently un-defer the readers this ticket's
RISK/NON-GOAL refuses to fold in.
The rule stays ATTRIBUTE-READ (strictly more robust than iteration-expression), but it is
justified as FUTURE-PROOFING, not by citing phase5_reuse.py:174/185 -- those are data-flow
sites, and citing them is what dragged data-flow into scope. Checked: every
control_flow_connections site in tests/ today reads the attribute inside the iterating
expression, so no current control-flow site forces the stronger rule.
  -> drop data_edge_tuples from the helper set.
  -> file the phase5_reuse dedup as a follow-up that EXTENDS the p0dn8 guard, so the scan's
     DEFER row points at a bead rather than at prose.

R4 -- ALLOWLIST, published BEFORE the guard is written so it cannot be grown to fit.
The scan's ~9-entry ALLOWLIST column was grep-derived and over-counts: re-checked by hand, all
3 subflow hits in test_guards_branch_arm_walks.py, all 3 in test_guards_agent_spec_import_seam.py
and construct_item_roundtrip.py:39 are inside STRING LITERALS or DOCSTRINGS -- invisible to a
Load-context ast.Attribute rule, so they need no entry at all.
Honest projection, data-flow out of scope: 7 entries.
  export.py:192, :910, :961      isinstance(ControlFlowEdge)-filtered lists  <- NO owning ticket
  each_oracle.py:113             _inner_nodes            -> expires with 498gr
  each_oracle_operator.py:118    _inner_nodes            -> expires with 498gr
  placeholder_translation.py:270 singular .subflow       -> expires with 498gr
  export.py:1106                 singular .subflow       -> expires with 498gr
Every entry must record an OPEN owning bead OR a structural-forever reason, with a meta-test
asserting the ticket-bound ones name a bead that exists. 4 of 7 expire when 498gr lands.
DECIDE NOW (do not defer): the export.py isinstance trio is the only group with no owning
ticket and is therefore the seed of a frozen ratchet -- either give the module an
isinstance-safe projection they can use, or make them explicit permanent entries with a
written reason.

R5 -- DO NOT CLAIM THIS TICKET WIDENS COVERAGE. It does not, and the old VERIFICATION step was
vacuous. Deriving edge_pairs from branch_adjacency centralizes WHERE the label is dropped, not
WHETHER: all five migrated pairs sites still assert on unlabelled tuples, so a branch-relabel
mutation stays exactly as invisible as today. dgbqv.9 ENABLES dgbqv.10 -- it gives it exactly

## Risks & Edge Cases
- **R1 (highest): the entry-set unification is a behaviour change hiding inside a move.**
  `flow.start_node.name` and "edges whose `from_node` is a StartNode" are not the same
  question if a Flow ever carried a second StartNode. Collapsing them is the RIGHT call
  (one answer per question) but it must land as its own step with the reachability suite
  re-run, not smuggled into a bulk find/replace. Keep an explicit fail-loud assertion inside
  the helper that the declared `start_node` is the only StartNode, so the collapse is proven
  rather than assumed.
- **R2: set-vs-list drift.** Migrating the `pairs` sites onto a projection of a list-valued
  adjacency must keep `(src, dst) in pairs` semantics; the projection must be materialized
  (`set[tuple[str,str]]`), not a generator, or the 5 sites' `in` checks silently change cost
  and repeated use breaks.
- **R3: `_walk` regression risk.** Reimplementing `_walk`'s `successors` on top of the new
  branch-keyed builder changes a `KeyError`-on-dangling-endpoint into whatever the new
  builder does. `_walk` pre-seeds from `flow.nodes` and would KeyError on an edge endpoint
  absent from `flow.nodes`; a fresh `setdefault`-based builder tolerates it silently. That
  fail-loud behaviour is a FEATURE (a dangling endpoint is a real export defect) -- preserve
  the pre-seed, and prove it with a test, or the whole 100-cell GREEN matrix quietly weakens.
- **R4: the guard's allowlist size.** An attribute-read rule catches all 32 sites; after

title: Agent Spec export gap: LlmConfig with api_provider='None' not supported for think-mode cells
description: Found during dgbqv.2's architect review (neograph-jn555.28, 2026-08-06) while verifying AgentSpecLoader against the real exporter: think-bare-single fails to load with 'LlmConfig with api_provider=None is not supported'. A third, previously-unfiled Agent Spec export gap alongside neograph-qtfof.6 (BranchingNode missing DataFlowEdge) and neograph-qtfof.7 (MapNode missing DataFlowEdge). Needs its own investigation: what does neograph's export emit for a think-mode node's LlmConfig, and why is api_provider ending up None/unset in a way the third-party AgentSpecLoader rejects. Relevant to the project's stated full-interop design goal (see neograph-dgbqv.2's Design Decision note).
design:
## MAINTAINER DECISION (2026-08-14): Option (A) -- Fail-loud opt-in

Add an explicit to_agent_spec(construct, api_provider=...) parameter (no IR change). With nothing declared, export keeps emitting no api_provider and export_conformance() keeps reporting NEOGRAPH_ROUND_TRIP_ONLY. No EXISTING pipeline becomes portable without an author-side change; the 72 affected matrix cells do NOT green automatically -- they re-partition onto qtfof.6/.7 (per atom .30's empirical finding). The CHANGELOG / test_agent_spec_execute.py docstring promise that qtfof.8 landing widens COMPARE_CELLS needs correcting.

Rationale (maintainer, grounded in the project's own design): neograph deliberately decouples LLM configuration from the graph definition -- Node.model is an opaque tier string ('fast'/'reason'), never a full provider config; resolution happens at runtime through a registry/factory (llm_factory) into a pre-instantiated BaseChatModel. The graph layer intentionally never knows or stores which real provider backs a tier. Forcing the exporter to guess/assert a concrete api_provider (option B) would synthesize information the design deliberately keeps out of the graph layer, and risks silently routing a non-OpenAI pipeline to the wrong provider if loaded by a third party -- trading today's loud NotImplementedError for a silent wrong-provider seam. Option A is the only choice consistent with that design.

## Implementation Plan

1. RED first: failing test asserting to_agent_spec(construct) with no api_provider= keeps emitting no LlmConfig.api_provider (today's behavior, but now documented/intentional) AND export_conformance() reports NEOGRAPH_ROUND_TRIP_ONLY for the affected cells; a second test asserting to_agent_spec(construct, api_provider='openai') DOES emit it and the real pyagentspec AgentSpecLoader can then load+convert the LlmConfig (the currently-failing repro tests in tests/test_agent_spec_llm_config_api_provider.py, parametrized think-bare-single/scripted-oracle-merge_prompt-single/agent-bare-single/act-bare-single, should flip to use the new parameter and pass).
2. Add api_provider: str | None = None parameter to to_agent_spec() (find its exact signature site in _agent_spec.py), threaded down to wherever LlmConfig is constructed for think/agent/act mode cells (the _make_llm_config single-writer site, per the review's confirmed monopoly).
3. Correct the CHANGELOG.md / test_agent_spec_execute.py docstring claim that qtfof.8 landing widens COMPARE_CELLS unconditionally -- state it widens COMPARE_CELLS only when the caller opts in via api_provider=.
4. Docs: website Agent Spec export page, document the opt-in parameter and why neograph cannot infer a default (link to the LLM registry/factory design).
notes:
## Reproduction (neograph-q14v5.29)
- Failing test: tests/test_agent_spec_llm_config_api_provider.py::TestExportedLlmConfigIsConvertibleByAThirdPartyRuntime::test_the_third_party_runtime_can_convert_the_exported_llm_config
- Verified RED at HEAD: 4 failed in 0.87s (cells think-bare-single, scripted-oracle-merge_prompt-single, agent-bare-single, act-bare-single).
- Root cause: `_agent_spec_node_lowering._make_llm_config` (src/neograph/_agent_spec_node_lowering.py:328-332) constructs `SpecLlmConfig(name=..., model_id=node.model or 'default')` and never sets `api_provider`, so pyagentspec's bare-LlmConfig dispatch (adapters/langgraph/_langgraphconverter.py:1324-1342) falls through its only supported branch (`api_provider == 'openai'`) and raises NotImplementedError.

### Two manifestation points (a load-only test would false-green half the surface)
- think + Oracle merge_prompt lower to LlmNode -> adapter converts the config EAGERLY at `load_dict` -> fails at LOAD.
- agent/act lower to AgentNode -> conversion is LAZY -> the flow LOADS CLEANLY and fails at INVOKE.
This is why the repro drives cells through the harness's load-AND-invoke entry point (`run_via_agent_spec_loader`) rather than a bare `load_dict`.

### Empirically probed fix constraint (relevant to fix scoping)
Patching the exported LlmConfig to `api_provider='openai'` makes the adapter build a LIVE ChatOpenAI at conversion time: without credentials it raises `OpenAIError: Missing credentials`; with a dummy key it loads and then makes a real network call on invoke (401). So fixing qtfof.8 makes the export LOADABLE/CONVERTIBLE but cannot make think/agent/act cells EXECUTE in the offline gate -- do not scope the fix to greening EXECUTE-tier cells.
## Trace similar patterns (neograph-q14v5.30)

### 1. No duplicate instance of THIS bug -- single-writer discipline held
`grep 'LlmConfig(' src/neograph/_agent_spec*.py`: the exported (pyagentspec) LlmConfig has exactly ONE construction site, `_make_llm_config` (_agent_spec_node_lowering.py:328-332), with 3 callers -- :114 (LlmNode / think, incl. the Oracle per-variant model tier), :257 (`_make_agent` for agent/act), and _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:182 (the Oracle merge_prompt LlmNode). The defect is an INCOMPLETE FIELD SET in one helper, not a pattern copy-pasted across sites, so the fix is genuinely single-site. (Note the shadowing hazard: neograph's OWN `_llm_config.LlmConfig` is a different, unrelated type -- grep hits in _llm.py/_oracle.py/construct.py/_spec_schema.py are the IR type, not the export type.)

### 2. Not a langgraph-adapter quirk -- the gap is cross-runtime
The identical bare-LlmConfig 'dispatch on api_provider, only openai supported' block exists in pyagentspec's openaiagents (:105-112), crewai (:326-335), autogen (:220-224) and agent_framework (:261-270) adapters. An exported LlmConfig with api_provider=None is un-runnable under EVERY shipped Agent Spec runtime, not just the one the EXECUTE tier uses.

### 3. Empirical whole-matrix probe at HEAD (all 100 GREEN cells, load+invoke via the real loader)
  api_provider (qtfof.8) ......... 72 cells   <-- by far the largest gap
  iterated_item (qtfof.7) ........ 16
  branching_mapping_key (qtfof.6) . 8
  RUNS ............................ 4  (scripted-bare-{single,dict}, scripted-oracle-merge_fn-{single,dict})
ZERO unclassified failures -- there is no untracked sibling of this bug shape anywhere in the matrix. The same bug SHAPE (export omits a field a third-party consumer requires) is already fully enumerated by qtfof.6/.7/.8/.9; nothing new to file.

### 4. What is hiding BEHIND qtfof.8 (verified, not inferred) -- matters for fix-atom expectations
Re-ran the same 100-cell probe with `_make_llm_config` monkeypatched to emit `api_provider='openai'` (offline: dummy key + unroutable OPENAI_BASE_URL). Result: 0 api_provider failures, and the 72 cells redistribute as
  - qtfof.7 (iterated_item) widens 16 -> 40
  - qtfof.6 (branching_mapping_key) stays 8
  - 20 APIConnectionError (the expected live-LLM call; qtfof.8's fix cannot make these run offline)
  - 28 ValueError 'tool t_read/t_write ... does not appear in the tool registry'
So closing qtfof.8 will NOT green those cells; it re-partitions EXEC_EXEMPT onto qtfof.6/.7. Do not scope the fix to a green EXECUTE tier.

### 5. One TEST-HARNESS gap this unmasks (harness bug, not an export bug -- do not file as an export defect)
`agent_spec_loader_harness.server_tools` (tests/agent_spec_loader_harness.py:49-55) collects tools only from `node.tool`. An agent/act cell exports `AgentNode.agent.tools`, so `stub_registry` returns `['prod']` while the flow needs `['prod','t_read']` -- verified directly on agent-bare-single. That is the source of the 28 ValueErrors above. When qtfof.8 lands, `server_tools` must also walk `getattr(node,'agent',None).tools` or agent/act cells will fail for a spurious reason that looks like an export defect.

## Architect Review (neograph-q14v5.32)

### 1. Root cause correctness -- LOW
Verified empirically at BOTH manifestation points (LlmNode load-time, AgentNode invoke-time) against the real third-party adapter, and confirmed by reading pyagentspec's own source (adapters/langgraph/_langgraphconverter.py:1324-1342). The single writer `_make_llm_config` is proven a monopoly by import scan. Nothing speculative.

### 2. Fix minimality -- MEDIUM
The design lists three options and picks none, and the option set is incomplete. A fourth exists and may be the cheapest honest one: an explicit exporter parameter, `to_agent_spec(construct, api_provider=...)` (and/or `url=`), which needs NO IR change, adds no magic key to the free-form `provider_kwargs` dict, and puts the declaration at the boundary where portability is actually being requested. The fix atom must not start until ONE option is chosen -- 'minimal' currently points at option (a), which is the one finding #4 rejects.

### 3. Regression risk -- MEDIUM
Not from the emitted field (additive + Optional in pyagentspec's model). The risk is entirely in the mandatory sweep:
  - `export_conformance()` is SHIPPED PUBLIC API (neograph-ftnxl.1, in `__init__.__all__`); changing the `llm_config_missing_api_provider` predicate changes published verdicts and the CHANGELOG/website text that documents them.
  - `tests/fixtures/agent_spec_refactor_snapshot.json` pins `"api_provider": null` in many places. Regenerating a large snapshot fixture inside a bug fix is exactly where an unrelated regression hides unnoticed -- diff it field-by-field, do not bulk-accept.
  - `classify_load_failure`'s api_provider branch must be REMOVED, not left: an exemption branch for a closed gap silently swallows a regression of that gap.
  - Expect 28 'tool t_read/t_write not in the tool registry' ValueErrors to appear on agent/act cells (verified, atom .30 section 5). That is a pre-existing harness gap being UNMASKED, not a regression caused by the fix -- but a fix agent that does not know this will mis-triage it.

### 4. Architecture compliance -- HIGH
Option (a) (unconditionally emit `api_provider='openai'`) trades a LOUD failure for a SILENT WRONG one. neograph is deliberately provider-neutral below the model layer (llm_factory + BaseChatModel; `Node.model` is an opaque tier string -- 'fast' in the fixtures -- and neograph's own `LlmConfig` is `extra='forbid'` with no provider field). The exporter therefore has NO evidence for the claim it would be emitting. For an author on Anthropic / OpenRouter / Ollama the exported artifact would then LOAD cleanly and route to OpenAI with a foreign model_id: a silent seam where today there is a fail-loud NotImplementedError. AGENTS.md's north star is explicit that this inverts the product ('fail-loud over fail-soft'; 'a band-aid that leaves a silent seam is an existential defect, never deferrable polish').

That makes the real question a PRODUCT decision, not an implementation one, and it is the maintainer's:
  (A) **Honest / fail-loud default** -- add an opt-in channel (option b/c/d); with nothing declared the export keeps emitting no api_provider and `export_conformance()` keeps reporting NEOGRAPH_ROUND_TRIP_ONLY. Consequence: qtfof.8 'closes' by giving authors a way to be portable, but NO existing pipeline becomes portable without an author-side change, and the 72 affected matrix cells do NOT green (they re-partition onto qtfof.6/.7 -- verified in atom .30 section 4).
  (B) **Portable-by-default** -- guess 'openai' as the Agent Spec baseline and document it. The 72 cells stop failing on this gap, at the cost of the exporter asserting a provider it does not know.
The existing docs lean toward (B)'s expectation (CHANGELOG + tests/test_agent_spec_execute.py:53-56 promise COMPARE_CELLS widens 'as qtfof.6/.7/.8 land'), while the north star lands squarely on (A). That contradiction is what needs human direction. Recommendation if a tiebreak is wanted: (A) via option (d) -- an explicit `to_agent_spec(api_provider=...)` -- plus a docs correction to stop promising that qtfof.8 alone widens the executable set.

### 5. Similar-bug scalability -- LOW
Single-writer helper with a proven import monopoly; the sibling export gaps of the same SHAPE are already enumerated (qtfof.6/.7/.9) and the 100-cell empirical probe found ZERO unclassified failures. Fixing this one helper scales to all three call sites for free.

### 6. Test coverage sufficiency -- MEDIUM
`tests/test_agent_spec_llm_config_api_provider.py` genuinely reproduces (4 cells RED, both manifestation points, real third-party runtime, no xfail/skip). But its premise -- a construct that declares NO provider must nonetheless convert -- silently encodes answer (B). Under answer (A) the test is asserting the wrong contract and would stay red forever. Whichever answer is chosen, coverage needs:
  - the positive case restated against it (under (A): a node whose provider IS declared converts);
  - a companion test pinning that the UNDECLARED case still fails LOUD (under (A)) -- otherwise the fix could regress into a silent guess with nothing to catch it;
  - the offline fixture kept (dummy key + unroutable OPENAI_BASE_URL): a named provider makes the adapter build a live client, and the default gate must not reach a vendor endpoint.

### Verdict
Findings: 1 HIGH (architecture compliance -- the default-provider question is a product decision with a north-star conflict), 3 MEDIUM (fix minimality, regression risk, test coverage), 2 LOW.
**Overall: NEEDS_USER_INPUT.**
## Triage (neograph-q14v5.33) -- BLOCKED ON MAINTAINER
Verdict NEEDS_USER_INPUT (1 HIGH). neograph-q14v5.33 left OPEN; neograph-q14v5.34 (fix) must not start until the default-provider question in the review above is answered: (A) opt-in channel with a fail-loud default, or (B) emit api_provider='openai' by default. See neograph-q14v5.33's notes for the framing.
## Sweep Verification (neograph-qtfof.8)

Re-scan commands: grep -rnE 'LlmConfig\(|llm_config\s*=' src/neograph/ ; grep -rn 'pyagentspec.llms|from pyagentspec' src/neograph/

Pre-fix instances: 1 construction site (_make_llm_config, _agent_spec_node_lowering.py:333) + 3 delegating call sites (_lower_generation_step think-mode, _make_agent agent/act-mode, Oracle merge lowering) + 2 downstream consumers.
Post-fix instances: same 1 construction site (now threading api_provider through), same 3 delegating call sites (now all accept+forward api_provider=), same monopoly -- pyagentspec.llms.llmconfig imported at exactly this one place still.

| # | Phase 1b site | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | _agent_spec_node_lowering.py _make_llm_config (the construction site) | MIGRATE -- THE fix site | Fixed: api_provider: str | None = None parameter added, threaded from to_agent_spec(construct, api_provider=...) through _lower_construct_item -> _lower_oracle/_lower_item_body -> _lower_node -> _lower_generation_step/_make_agent -> _make_llm_config. Recursive sub-flow export (Portal mesh Swarm, nested Construct items) uses functools.partial(to_agent_spec, api_provider=api_provider) so nested exports inherit the same provider. | Verified: 8/8 tests pass in tests/test_agent_spec_llm_config_api_provider.py (4 opt-in-succeeds + 4 default-stays-honest); mutation-verified (removing api_provider=api_provider from the SpecLlmConfig(...) call reproduces all 4 opt-in-test failures) |
| 2-4 | 3 delegating call sites | (implicitly covered by fix) | All thread api_provider= now | Verified via the same 8 passing tests (all 4 LLM_BEARING_CELLS shapes: think, Oracle merge_prompt, agent, act) |

No new MIGRATE/DEFER rows found on re-scan. Monopoly still holds (single pyagentspec.llms import site).

## Structural Guard

Behavioral guard (the disease was a missing capability, not a duplicated pattern): tests/test_agent_spec_llm_config_api_provider.py, two classes -- TestExportedLlmConfigIsConvertibleWhenApiProviderIsSupplied (positive: 4 cells x api_provider='openai' -> loadable/convertible) and TestExportedLlmConfigStaysHonestByDefault (negative: 4 cells x no api_provider -> stays NotImplementedError, the intentional default). Mutation-verified as above.
## Fix Applied

Added `api_provider: str | None = None` to `to_agent_spec()`, threaded through the full lowering dispatch tree to `_make_llm_config`'s 3 call sites (_lower_generation_step for think-mode LlmNode, _make_agent for agent/act AgentNode, _lower_oracle's merge_prompt LlmNode). Used functools.partial to bind api_provider into the recursive export_flow callable (Construct-item sub-exports inherit it) rather than widening every _lower_* callable-typed parameter to also carry a scalar. Portal/Swarm export path untouched (no _make_llm_config call site there, confirmed by grep -- out of scope per the ticket).

Rewrote tests/test_agent_spec_llm_config_api_provider.py's original repro (which called to_agent_spec(construct) with no parameter and expected it to work -- that would have been Option B's behavior) into two classes: TestExportedLlmConfigIsConvertibleWhenApiProviderIsSupplied (api_provider='openai' -> works) and TestExportedLlmConfigStaysHonestByDefault (no api_provider -> keeps raising, the intentional permanent behavior).

Corrected the stale 'COMPARE_CELLS widens automatically as qtfof.6/.7/.8 land' claim in tests/test_agent_spec_execute.py -- qtfof.8's opt-in shape does NOT widen COMPARE_CELLS for the zero-arg export that tier exercises, unlike qtfof.6/.7's real-DataFlowEdge fixes. Added a CHANGELOG.md entry.

File-size ratchet: _agent_spec.py 650->662, _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py 646->649, both updated with justification.
API manifest regenerated (to_agent_spec signature changed) + website/reference/api.mdx's generated region regenerated + npm run build/test green (47 pages).

## E2E Verify

No additional e2e work needed.
## Sweep Verification (neograph-qtfof.8)

title: Agent Spec importer: loader.py hand-rolls the same 'is there an edge X->Y (optionally labelled L)?' predicate four times
description:
Found by dgbqv.2's codebase disease scan (2026-08-06), dedup lens row 20 (.claude/code-review/dgbqv.2/dedup.md).

src/neograph/loader.py repeats the composite-recognition predicate
  any(e.from_node.name == A and e.to_node.name == B [and e.from_branch == L] for e in flow.control_flow_connections)
at four sites: :112-114, :117-120, :198-204, :461-464.

This is the importer's 'never trust a marker -- confirm the structure' discipline, which is the CORRECT layer and correct behaviour; the defect is only that the predicate has no name and is spelled out four times, so the four copies can drift.

SRC-SIDE, so it explicitly cannot consume dgbqv.2's tests-side helper (layer discipline). Needs its own extraction: a private _has_control_edge(flow, src, dst, branch=None) in the Agent-Spec import layer, with all four recognizers routed through it.

Note :118 and :202 also spell the branch labels 'pause'/'continue' as raw literals -- see the branch-label-constants follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: One named edge-existence helper in the import layer; all four recognizers call it. Import behaviour unchanged (round-trip suites green).
notes:
## Prep (fwait.17)

CORRECTION to the ticket's site list -- the line numbers predate a landed move.
The ticket names four sites 'in src/neograph/loader.py' at :112-114, :117-120,
:198-204, :461-464. loader.py is now 413 lines: neograph-jtawq.10 (closed, this same
epic) moved the swarm-import cluster out. Re-derived by content:
  src/neograph/loader.py:113                 primary -> check          (no branch)
  src/neograph/loader.py:118                 check --pause--> pause    (branch)
  src/neograph/loader.py:199                 node -> nxt               (no branch)
  src/neograph/loader.py:203                 nxt --continue--> node    (branch)
  src/neograph/_agent_spec_swarm_import.py:284  agent -> check         (no branch)  <-- MOVED
So the fourth site is in a DIFFERENT MODULE now. This matters: the helper cannot be a
loader.py-private function, or the moved site cannot reach it and the duplication
survives the very fix meant to remove it.

Files to modify:
- NEW src/neograph/_agent_spec_graph.py (the helper's neutral home)
- src/neograph/loader.py (4 call sites)
- src/neograph/_agent_spec_swarm_import.py (1 call site)

Placement decision (checked for cycles, not assumed):
- _agent_spec_group_import.py would work cycle-wise (it does not import loader), but
  its concern is RECONSTRUCTION; this predicate is RECOGNITION. Wrong module.
- _agent_spec_markers.py is documented as the neutral both-sides module, but its
  concern is marker keys + the pyagentspec import guard. Mixing in a graph predicate
  muddies it.
- New _agent_spec_graph.py imports nothing from neograph, so it is cycle-free by
  construction and is the seed home for the further src-side Flow predicates b0y5s
  (branch labels) and 498gr (subflow descent) will want.

Ordering note: doing lp92e BEFORE b0y5s deliberately. b0y5s must replace the raw
'pause'/'continue' literals at loader.py:118/202; after this extraction those become a
single branch= argument per call site rather than two inline literals.

Approach: _has_control_edge(flow, from_name, to_name, branch=None) -> bool, returning
any(edge matches), with branch=None meaning 'any branch'. Route all five sites through
it. Behaviour must be identical -- round-trip suites are the proof.
## Execution (fwait.18)
Changes made:
- NEW src/neograph/_agent_spec_graph.py: _has_control_edge(flow, from_name, to_name,
  branch=None). branch=None means 'any branch'; a label additionally requires that arm.
  Imports nothing from neograph, so it is cycle-free and reachable from every
  import-side module.
- 4 loader.py sites + 1 _agent_spec_swarm_import.py site routed through it.
- NEW tests/test_guards_agent_spec_control_edge_predicate.py: AST guard allowing a raw
  iteration over X.control_flow_connections ONLY in _agent_spec_graph.py. Includes an
  allowlist-liveness test (the allowlisted module must still contain the walk, so the
  guard cannot pass because the thing it protects vanished) and a detection self-test.
  Scoped to src/ deliberately -- the ~20-25 test-side walks are dgbqv.9; folding them in
  would ship this guard pre-loaded with a 20-entry allowlist, i.e. a ratchet that never
  ratchets.

Sweep verified, not assumed: after the change every surviving
'control_flow_connections' in src/ is either a WRITE (exporter kwarg at
_agent_spec.py:648, _agent_spec_portal.py:197, _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:339) or
the helper itself. Zero remaining hand-rolled reads.

Non-vacuity PROVEN by controlled mutation: re-inlining the swarm-import site made the
guard FAIL naming _agent_spec_swarm_import.py:285. Reverted; green.

ONE EXISTING TEST FAILED and it was RIGHT: test_guards_ir_compiler.py::
TestNoTicketIdsInComments rejected '(neograph-lp92e)' in the new module's docstring --
the project bans bare parenthesized ticket IDs in src. Fixed my docstring rather than
the guard. (Dotted refs like '(neograph-jtawq.10' elsewhere do not match its regex,
which requires ')' right after a 3-5 char id -- so those are legitimately untouched.)

Quality check: PASS (4516 passed, 106 skipped, 0 failed; 4513 -> +3 new guard tests).

title: Guard G1 (Command construction monopoly) scans SRC_DIR.glob('*.py') -- non-recursive and src-only; widen to rglob
description:

tests/test_guards_assembly.py:120 iterates sorted(SRC_DIR.glob('*.py')) -- glob, not rglob. So src/neograph/testing/ and src/neograph/schemas/ escape the Command-construction monopoly entirely, as do tests/ and examples/.

NO LIVE BREACH TODAY (verified by AST sweep across src recursively, tests, and examples): every Command(...) construction inside src/ is in factory.py (14 sites: 281,291,304,308,351,356,364,372,424,426,921,926,935,940) or runner.py (2 sites: 257,464), exactly as _ALLOWED declares. title: Agent Spec: branch-label constants defined twice in src, and 'continue'/'done'/'true'/'false' have no constant at all
description:
Found by dgbqv.2's codebase disease scan (2026-08-06), consistency lens (.claude/code-review/dgbqv.2/consistency.md rows 108-110).

DUPLICATED DEFINITION: _DEFAULT_BRANCH = 'default' and _PAUSE_BRANCH = 'pause' are defined INDEPENDENTLY in two src modules:
  - src/neograph/_agent_spec_portal.py:39-40
  - src/neograph/_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:67-68
Neither imports the other, so a rename in one silently diverges the export from the importer. src/neograph/loader.py:118 already spells 'pause' as a raw literal, matching neither constant.

NO CONSTANT AT ALL for the loop/branch arm labels, which are spelled literally at their definition sites:
  - _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:377  mapping={'continue': 'continue', 'done': 'done'}
  - _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:504/516  mapping={'true': 'true', 'false': 'false'} and (arm, 'true')/(arm, 'false')
  - _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:390  from_branch='continue'
  - src/neograph/loader.py:202  e.from_branch == 'continue'
and re-typed across tests at test_agent_spec_export.py:769/842/913/914/1124/1187 and test_agent_spec_reachability.py:179/213.

FIX DIRECTION: single home in src/neograph/_agent_spec_markers.py (the existing neutral constants module both the export and import sides already import), with every construction and comparison site reading from there.

notes:
## Prep (fwait.11)

Files to modify:
- src/neograph/_agent_spec_markers.py (new single home for the 6 branch labels)
- src/neograph/_agent_spec_portal.py (delete its private duplicate pair)
- src/neograph/_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py (delete its duplicate pair; adopt constants)
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py (re-export block: repoint _DEFAULT_BRANCH/_PAUSE_BRANCH)
- src/neograph/loader.py (2 raw literals)
- tests: export.py (6), reachability.py (2)

Sweep re-derived by grep (ticket line numbers had drifted; content-keyed instead):
SRC duplicate definitions -- confirmed:
  _agent_spec_portal.py:40-41            _DEFAULT_BRANCH / _PAUSE_BRANCH
  _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:67-68 _DEFAULT_BRANCH / _PAUSE_BRANCH  (independent)

  _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:377   mapping={'continue': 'continue', 'done': 'done'}
  _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:390   from_branch='continue'
  _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:504   mapping={'true': 'true', 'false': 'false'}
  _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:516   (arm, 'true') / (arm, 'false')
  _agent_spec.py:265                     [(branch, 'done')]   <-- NOT in the ticket
  loader.py:118                          e.from_branch == 'pause'
  loader.py:202                          e.from_branch == 'continue'
TEST raw literals -- 8 sites, all in 2 files:
  test_agent_spec_export.py:780/853/924/925/1135/1198
  test_agent_spec_reachability.py:179/213
  (4 further sites in the *_operator tests ALREADY compare against _PAUSE_BRANCH --
   that is the target form.)

TRAP -- do NOT blanket-replace 'true'/'false': three src sites spell those strings
for entirely unrelated reasons and must stay untouched:
  _describe_value.py:97  BAML bool rendering
  conditions.py:47,49    condition-expression parsing
Only the branch-arm labels in the Agent-Spec lowering are in scope.

VOCABULARY NOTE (affects how many constants): at mapping={'true': _PAUSE_BRANCH}
the KEY is the BranchingNode mapping key (the condition OUTCOME) while the VALUE is
the branch LABEL. At :504 both spellings coincide ('true' -> 'true'). These are two
distinct roles that happen to share a spelling; the acceptance ('each branch label
defined exactly once') is about the LABEL. Plan: name the labels
_BRANCH_TRUE/_BRANCH_FALSE/_BRANCH_CONTINUE/_BRANCH_DONE alongside the moved

4. Extend tests/test_guards_agent_spec_markers.py with a branch-label check so the

## Execution (fwait.12)

FIRST ATTEMPT REJECTED BY THE FILE-SIZE RATCHET -- and the ratchet was right.
Six loose module constants meant every consumer needed up to 6 import lines, which
GREW two allowlisted files (_agent_spec.py 651->655, _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py
648->651). The ratchet's rule is explicit: 'If it GREW, do NOT just raise the number --
shrink the file in-PR; the ceiling may only follow a real shrink.' Raising the two
ceilings would have been the band-aid.

STRUCTURAL FIX (not a workaround): collapse the six labels onto ONE container class,
Branch, in _agent_spec_markers.py -- mirroring the existing StateKeys precedent in
_state_keys.py (fixed names as class attributes, single source of truth, pinned by a
structural guard). Each consumer now needs ONE import line instead of six, so both
files SHRINK below their old ceilings and the ceilings follow a real shrink:
  _agent_spec.py                    651 -> 650
  _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py  648 -> 646
Use sites read better too: Branch.CONTINUE says which vocabulary the string belongs to
in a way a bare _BRANCH_CONTINUE does not.

Changes made:
- _agent_spec_markers.py: new Branch container (DEFAULT/PAUSE/CONTINUE/DONE/TRUE/FALSE),
  carrying the outcome-vs-label note in its docstring.
- Deleted BOTH private duplicate pairs (_agent_spec_portal.py, _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py).
- Migrated 26 src use sites across _agent_spec.py (2), _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py
  (16), _agent_spec_portal.py (6), loader.py (2) -- including _agent_spec.py:265's
  [(branch, 'done')], which the ticket did not list.
- Migrated 12 test use sites across 6 files, incl. the 4 *_operator tests that already
  imported _PAUSE_BRANCH (repointed to Branch.PAUSE for one vocabulary, not two).
- tests/test_guards_agent_spec_markers.py: two new checks --
  test_branch_labels_are_defined_exactly_once (Branch holds the six values AND no src
  module re-defines any of the six RETIRED constant names) and
  test_no_raw_branch_label_literals_in_the_agent_spec_layer (no raw label literal on a
  from_branch/mapping line in the Agent-Spec modules).
- tests/test_guards_file_size.py: both ceilings lowered, same commit.

Scoping trap avoided: the raw-literal check is scoped to the Agent-Spec modules by
name. 'true'/'false'/'done'/'continue' are ordinary strings elsewhere in the tree
(_describe_value.py:97 renders bools, conditions.py:47/49 parses literals) -- a
tree-wide scan would be noise, and those sites are deliberately untouched.

PROCESS ERROR I made and caught: I did the bulk rename with a regex that included
'\bNAME, ' to strip names from import lists. That pattern also matched inside dict
literals and call arg lists, silently corrupting 6 sites -- 5 became syntax errors
(caught by ruff) but ONE did not: tests/test_agent_spec_reachability.py:179 became
'assert exits[0].from_branch == ("the loop's exit edge must...")', comparing the
branch against its own failure message. Syntactically valid, semantically dead -- a
green-looking test asserting nothing. Found by diffing EVERY changed line against
HEAD and reconciling removed-label-token counts against Branch.* use counts per file
(all 12 files now reconcile 1:1), not by reading the diff by eye. Lesson: a
green ruff/pytest run does not prove a mechanical rename was faithful.

Non-vacuity re-PROVEN after the Branch rework by two controlled mutations:

title: Agent Spec: tests re-type 'neograph/*' marker literals instead of importing _MARK_*; widen the markers guard to tests/
description:
Found by dgbqv.2's codebase disease scan (2026-08-06), consistency + layering lenses (.claude/code-review/dgbqv.2/).

src/neograph/_agent_spec_markers.py is the neutral single source for the wire marker keys, and tests/test_guards_agent_spec_markers.py pins their values. But that guard sets SCANNED to 7 SRC files only, and its docstring states it lives under tests/ (not scanned) so it may name the strings freely.

Consequence: 80 'neograph/' string literals under tests/, of which 32 are the guard's own intentional value pin (structurally exempt). The remainder are re-typed literals in modules that could import _MARK_*:
  - tests/test_agent_spec_export.py (~39, the largest holdout)
  - tests/test_agent_spec_refactor_snapshot.py (~5)
  - tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py (~3)
  - tests/test_agent_spec_import.py (~1)
  - tests/test_guards_agent_spec_lowering.py (~1)
12 other test modules already DO import _MARK_* -- that is the dominant, correct form.

WHY IT MATTERS beyond tidiness: a re-typed marker key that drifts is a SILENT no-match (the marker is simply unread and the node treated as foreign), not a loud failure. dgbqv.2's metadata-aware mini-executor reads these markers, so it is directly exposed.

FIX: migrate the holdouts to _MARK_* imports, then widen the guard's scan to tests/ with an explicit exemption for the guard module itself (which must re-type the literals to assert them).
acceptance_criteria: Non-guard test modules import _MARK_* rather than re-typing 'neograph/*'. test_guards_agent_spec_markers.py scans tests/ too, with a documented self-exemption, and fails on a newly re-typed literal.

- tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py

count is not the migratable count; three classes are literals that must STAY:

title: Agent Spec: assert every exported ControlFlowEdge.from_branch names a branch its own BranchingNode.mapping declares, matrix-wide over GREEN
description:
Found by dgbqv.2's codebase disease scan (2026-08-06), elegance lens (.claude/code-review/dgbqv.2/elegance.md, 'Residual after dgbqv.2 lands').

Even once dgbqv.2's mini-executor lands, one defect class stays uncovered: nothing checks that an edge's from_branch is a KEY of its own BranchingNode's mapping. If export emits from_branch='finished' on a node whose mapping is {'continue','done'}, the executor's own unmatched-key -> 'default' fallback (pyagentspec's rule) can MASK it whenever the fallback happens to route sensibly.

Orthogonal to the executor and cheap: one assertion on top of the branch-keyed adjacency builder dgbqv.2 introduces, parametrized over the GREEN matrix.

close_reason: Duplicate of neograph-dgbqv.10 (same mutation-tested branch-label coverage gap, filed independently by two paths from the same review). Detail merged into dgbqv.10's notes.

description:

The day any lowering picks a plural holder, all five go SILENTLY blind while _sub_flows keeps working.

notes:
Depends on neograph-dgbqv.9 landing first (the neutral shared graph-primitives module this ticket's fix routes through).
## Scope addition from neograph-dgbqv.9's whole-tree disease scan (2026-08-11)

The dgbqv.9 scan found a SECOND singular-only subflow reader this ticket does not list:
  tests/test_agent_spec_export.py:1106   subflows = [v.subflow for v in variants]

Unblocked by neograph-dgbqv.9 landing (commit 9824213), which supplied the seam:
tests/agent_spec_flow_walk.inner_nodes(holder), routing through sub_flows() so it reads BOTH
the singular .subflow and the plural .subflows spellings via the single _holder_flows helper.

Sites re-derived by grep (line numbers current as of 9824213):
  tests/test_agent_spec_each_oracle.py:113           def _inner_nodes  -> DELETE
  tests/test_agent_spec_each_oracle.py:136,164,165   3 call sites       -> inner_nodes(...)
  tests/test_agent_spec_each_oracle_operator.py:118  def _inner_nodes  -> DELETE (byte-identical)

  tests/test_agent_spec_export.py:1106                  [v.subflow for v in variants] singular-only
