title: Design question: expose Portal.conditions on the YAML spec surface as name->expression (deferred from 2j208)
description:
Surfaced by 2j208's architect review (finding 3c) and its refinement pass (neograph-jn555.58, 2026-08-06). 2j208 adds PortalSpec to the YAML spec surface but deliberately OMITS Portal.conditions (and Portal.scripted). This ticket records the omitted half that IS YAML-expressible, so the capability is deferred explicitly rather than dropped silently.

## What is actually lost today (corrected -- the review's own framing was wrong)

The review claimed that with scripted=None and conditions=None "a YAML-declared dispatch Portal can only ever emit flows built from LLM-mode nodes". That is FALSE. compiler.py:150-167 seeds both per-compile lookups INDEPENDENTLY of the kwargs:

- scripted_lookup = _collect_scripted_shims(construct) then .update(_decoration_registry.scripted); the explicit scripted= kwarg merges LAST (so it WINS).
- condition_lookup = dict(_decoration_registry.condition); the explicit conditions= kwarg merges on top.

So a YAML dispatch Portal's emitted flow still reaches every decoration-time registration (@node scripted shims, @merge_fn, inline interrupt_when conditions, anything passed to register_scripted / register_condition). The REAL narrowing is narrower and worth stating precisely: a YAML Portal cannot supply a portal-LOCAL callable registry -- one that (a) provides a callable that is not globally registered, or (b) OVERRIDES a global registration for just this one portal's emitted flow.

## The evaluation (finding 3c), resolved

The review suggested expressing conditions: as a list of registered names "resolved through parse_condition -- the SAME registry LoopSpec.when already uses". That premise conflates two different mechanisms:

- conditions.py:95 parse_condition(expr) is an EXPRESSION PARSER ("score < 0.8"), not a name registry. That is what _spec_loader.py:258 uses for LoopSpec.when.
- The actual condition NAME registry is _decoration_registry.condition (_runtime_registry.py), seeded into compile()'s condition_lookup.

Therefore:

- Option (a) conditions: [registered_name, ...] resolved via the name registry is VACUOUS -- compile() already seeds condition_lookup from _decoration_registry.condition, so re-passing those names adds exactly zero capability.
- Option (b) conditions: {name: "score < 0.8"} -- a mapping of name to condition EXPRESSION, each resolved by parse_condition -- IS genuinely new capability: a portal-local condition registry authored entirely in YAML. This is the option worth designing.

## Why it was deferred out of 2j208 rather than folded in

1. It is the only PortalSpec field that would NOT be a pure pass-through. 2j208's loader arm forwards spec.portal.model_fields_set by name, which is what buys model_fields_set parity with the programmatic form BY CONSTRUCTION. A transformed field is a deliberate exception to that property and needs its own justification.
2. Error mapping is undesigned. parse_condition raises a bare ValueError for a malformed expression; every other loader failure surfaces as ConfigurationError/ConstructError with a field path. Which one a bad portal condition expression should raise is an open call.
3. It is dispatch-mode-only, and 2j208 ships ZERO dispatch-mode YAML coverage (its fixtures are peer-mode meshes). Adding an untested dispatch-only field is precisely the defect 2j208's review finding 4 objects to.

Portal.scripted (dict[str, Callable]) is genuinely NOT YAML-expressible under any option and is out of scope here.

## Acceptance

- Decide whether option (b) is worth the exception to the pass-through property.
- If yes: PortalSpec gains conditions: dict[str, str] | None, resolved via parse_condition in the _apply_modifiers portal arm, with a decided error-mapping story, plus dispatch-mode YAML fixtures (which 2j208 does not add).
- Either way, keep website/src/content/docs/concepts/spec-format.mdx's stated restriction in sync with the outcome.
design:
## Core Invariant                                                           
                                                                            
Every PortalSpec field is a YAML-representable NARROWING whose value is     
assignable to the same-named Portal field -- not 'identical types' (already 
false in-tree: PortalSpec.output: str | None vs Portal.output:              
type[BaseModel] | str | None). conditions: dict[str, str] fails that        
narrowing test against Portal.conditions: dict[str, Callable] (not a        
superset), so it is the one field that would need its own transform arm --  
the exception a total-mirror comprehension exists to avoid.                 
                                                                            
## FINAL DECISION: DO NOT IMPLEMENT option (b). Close as a documented design
decision.                                                                   
                                                                            
This bead's history contains multiple flip-flopping research/design passes  
(visible in NOTES) that reached opposite conclusions without reconciling.   
The architect review (fe1d6.28, 2026-08-14) independently re-verified the   
'do not implement' reasoning against source (parse_condition call sites,    
condition_lookup seeding, Operator.when typing, PortalSpec/Portal field     
diff) and rated it [LOW] risk / correct: 'Option (b) does not buy the       
capability it appears to buy... a two-hop indirection around a one-hop gap.'
This is the FINAL, authoritative decision -- do not re-open without new     
evidence the review didn't already consider.                                
                                                                            
## Reasoning (unchanged from the reviewed pass)                             
                                                                            
Portal.conditions has exactly one consumer (_agent_spec_dispatch.py:143),   
feeding the emitted flow's condition_lookup. That emitted flow is loaded    
through the same _spec_loader, whose only spec path reaching                
condition_lookup is OperatorSpec.when (LoopSpec.when is parse_condition-ed  
at LOAD TIME, never consulting condition_lookup). So option (b) would add a 
portal-local name->expression registry solely to give a NAME to an          
expression so operator.when can reference it -- a two-hop indirection around
a gap that has a direct one-hop fix.                                        
                                                                            
## Implementation Plan (documentation + follow-ups, no PortalSpec change)   
                                                                            
1. Correct spec-format.mdx:156 (already partially updated by an earlier     
pass) and _spec_schema.py:73-76: drop the stale 'cannot be represented in   
YAML' framing, state scripted/conditions are Python-only CALLABLE registries,
and add: for a spec-emitted flow the condition half is reachable only       
through operator.when (loop.when is expression-parsed at load time).        
Acceptance: npm run build (in website/) green.                                             
2. File follow-up A (BLOCKING successor to this ticket, not a loose follow- 
up -- link it): OperatorSpec.when accept name-OR-expression like LoopSpec.  
when. Scope correction from the reviewed pass: this requires an IR-layer    
widening of Operator.when from str-only to str | Callable[[Any], bool] FIRST
(modifiers.py:578) -- the _agent_spec_group_import.py:284-296 dual-         
resolution exemplar yields a callable, which is not type-valid against      
today's str-only field. Acceptance items: (i) compiler.py:203's             
isinstance(op.when, str) guard must intentionally skip the new callable form --
state this, don't just discover it; (ii) _agent_spec_swarm_import.py:301-308
and _agent_spec_group_import.py:287 currently treat Operator.when as always-
a-name with no callable export form -- a YAML-authored expression Operator  
would not survive an Agent-Spec round-trip, must be addressed or explicitly 
scoped out; (iii) modifiers.py is an IR-layer edit -> three-surface parity  
testing applies.                                                            
3. File follow-up B: fix the latent bug (same defect as neograph-ijyjr) --  
_spec_loader.py:258/259 calls parse_condition(spec.loop.when)               
unconditionally, so a registered-NAME loop.when (the canonical form lint's  
loop_condition_unregistered rule enforces) dies with a raw ValueError       
instead of resolving. TDD: failing repro first. Reuses the same             
_agent_spec_group_import.py dual-resolution helper as A.                    
4. File follow-up C: add dispatch-mode (route: decide) YAML spec fixtures --
zero exist today (confirmed unchanged on re-check). Gates any future        
dispatch-mode spec-surface work; do not let this be deferred a second time. 
5. File follow-up D (LOW, from review): Node.gate_tools_when reads          
condition_lookup (_wiring.py:617) but has no spec-schema field at all --    
unreachable from YAML entirely. File alongside A/B/C rather than leaving    
unowned.                                                                    
6. Close neograph-t0ajj citing this decision, with an explicit note in the  
closing reason that follow-up A supersedes any research suggesting option   
(b) is 'non-vacuous' -- an inline expression needs no registry entry at all 
once A ships.                                                               
                                                                            
## Anti-band-aid clause                                                     
                                                                            
Do NOT re-open this decision without evidence beyond what the review already
independently verified. Do NOT let follow-up A's ticket description under-  
scope the IR widening as a drop-in reuse -- it requires the three-surface-  
parity + guard-scoping work item 2 lists.
notes:
## Findings (research atom neograph-fe1d6.26, 2026-08-14)

VERDICT: **DO NOT implement option (b).** It is a two-hop workaround for a
one-hop gap that lives somewhere else. Recommend documenting the decision and
closing, with three concrete follow-ups (below). Detail:

### 1. Blocker (1) is STRONGER than the ticket states -- the pass-through is now total, not model_fields_set

The ticket says 2j208's loader arm "forwards spec.portal.model_fields_set by
name". That is no longer accurate. Since neograph-dgbqv.6, `_spec_loader.py:275`
forwards EVERY declared field:

    kwargs = {name: getattr(spec.portal, name) for name in type(spec.portal).model_fields}
    item = item | Portal(**kwargs)

with an in-code comment stating this is safe precisely because "field names are
identical between PortalSpec and Portal, and BOTH default their knobs to None".
`_spec_schema.py:69-72` states the same as PortalSpec's contract: "mirroring
neograph._portal.Portal field-for-field (identical names, identical defaults
where one exists) ... gives YAML parity with the programmatic form BY
CONSTRUCTION".

So `conditions: dict[str, str]` would not merely be "the only non-pass-through
field" -- it is a field whose TYPE does not mirror `Portal.conditions:
dict[str, Callable]` (_portal.py:85), so it would **break the comprehension that
IS the pass-through**: the loop would hand a dict of strings to a field typed
dict of callables. It would require a special-case pop-and-transform inside the
one construct whose whole value is that it has no special cases.

### 2. Option (b)'s reachable surface is MUCH narrower than the ticket assumes -- this is the decisive finding

`Portal.conditions` is consumed at exactly ONE site:

    _agent_spec_dispatch.py:143
      compiled = compile_construct(sub, scripted=portal.scripted, conditions=portal.conditions)

i.e. it becomes the per-compile `condition_lookup` of the LLM-EMITTED flow. But
that emitted flow is a Spec dict loaded through the SAME `_spec_loader`, and the
spec surface has only two condition sites:

* `LoopSpec.when: str` -> `_spec_loader.py:258` `parse_condition(spec.loop.when)`
  -- converted to a CALLABLE AT LOAD TIME. `condition_lookup` is therefore NEVER
  consulted for a spec-loaded Loop (`_wiring.py:145` `_resolve_condition` sees a
  callable and returns identity).
* `OperatorSpec.when: str` (`_spec_schema.py:58-63`, docstring literally
  "Operator modifier with registered condition NAME") -> `_spec_loader.py:265`
  `Operator(when=spec.operator.when)` -- the string passes through unchanged and
  IS resolved against `condition_lookup` (validated `compiler.py:205`, resolved
  `_wiring.py:761`).
* `Node.gate_tools_when` also reads condition_lookup (`_wiring.py:617`) but has
  NO field in the spec schema at all, so it is unreachable from YAML.

**Conclusion: for a YAML/spec-emitted flow, `portal.conditions` is reachable
through `operator.when` and nothing else.** Option (b) would add a portal-local
name->expression registry whose sole purpose is to give a NAME to an expression
so that the emitted flow's `operator.when` can reference that name. That is a
two-hop indirection around a one-hop gap.

### 3. The REAL gap is a spec-schema asymmetry, not a Portal omission

`LoopSpec.when` accepts an expression; `OperatorSpec.when` accepts only a
registered name. If the capability "author a condition inline in YAML" is
wanted, the direct fix is to make `OperatorSpec.when` accept name-OR-expression
the same way, which:
  - is symmetric with LoopSpec rather than a Portal exception,
  - benefits EVERY YAML pipeline, not only dispatch-mode Portals,
  - keeps PortalSpec a total, exception-free field-for-field mirror,
  - and has an EXISTING in-repo precedent to reuse rather than invent:
    `_agent_spec_group_import.py:284-294` already does exactly this dual
    resolution (try `parse_condition`; on ValueError treat the string as a
    registry name and pass through for `compile()` to resolve). Its comment
    documents neograph-ijyjr, where assuming "expression" unconditionally broke
    the registry-name form.

### 4. Blocker (2) error-mapping precedent -- the ticket's premise is only mostly true

The ticket says "every other loader failure surfaces as
ConfigurationError/ConstructError with a field path". The ONE existing
`parse_condition` call site in the loader (`_spec_loader.py:258`) is BARE -- no

title: Portal mesh: mixed agent(trigger=tool)+think mesh silently converts think member to agent on re-import (two defects cancel)
description: Surfaced by dgbqv.5's architect review (neograph-jn555.37 triage, 2026-08-06). A legal mesh of one agent(trigger='tool') member + one think member exports handoff=OPTIONAL. On re-import, _swarm_trigger forces trigger='tool' onto EVERY member -- which _validation_portal.py:162-174 would normally reject (trigger=tool requires agent/act mode) -- except _agent_spec_node_import.py:216 hard-codes mode='agent' for markerless agents. So the think member silently becomes an agent member on round-trip. Two defects cancel to produce a working-but-wrong round trip: fixing EITHER side alone (the trigger-forcing OR the mode hard-code) turns a previously-working round trip into a ConstructError. Currently only a warnings.warn at loader.py:427 flags this (not fully silent, but easy to miss). Needs investigation: which side is the actual bug, and what's the correct fix that doesn't regress the other.
notes:
## Reproduce (d2ulr.11) -- REPRODUCED, and the root cause is on neither side the ticket names

REPRO (exact, run):
  mesh = [ Node(triage, mode=agent, tools=[]) | Portal(to=[scribe], trigger='tool', max_hops=4),
           Node(scribe, mode=think)           | Portal(to=[triage]) ]
  BEFORE: [('triage','agent','tool'), ('scribe','think','output')]
  export -> Swarm.handoff = HandoffMode.OPTIONAL
  AFTER:  [('triage-agent','agent','tool'), ('scribe-agent','agent','tool')]
The think member comes back as an AGENT member with trigger='tool'. Confirmed, with only a
best-effort warnings.warn to flag it.

THE TICKET'S FRAMING IS INCOMPLETE. It presents two cancelling IMPORT-side defects
(_swarm_trigger forcing the mesh trigger onto every member; _agent_spec_node_import
hard-coding mode='agent') and asks which is the real bug. Answer: NEITHER, on its own.
Inspected the exported Swarm's per-agent metadata directly:
  AGENT triage-agent metadata keys: ['neograph/prompt_spec']
  AGENT scribe-agent metadata keys: ['neograph/prompt_spec']
The EXPORT records only the prompt. The member's MODE and its PER-MEMBER TRIGGER are never
written to the wire at all -- _lower_portal_mesh_to_swarm builds each member with _make_agent
and stamps _MARK_PROMPT_SPEC only, bypassing the richer neograph/agent_spec marker the
non-mesh node lowering uses (which does carry mode/model/tools/gate_tools_when/context).

So the causal chain is: EXPORT destroys mode+trigger -> the importer has nothing to read ->
mode='agent' hard-code and mesh-level trigger-forcing are the only things it CAN do. Both
'defects' are downstream symptoms. This is why fixing either import site alone converts a
working round trip into a ConstructError, exactly as the ticket observed: it would make the
importer honest about information that is not there.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THIS SHAPE: the round trip is advertised as lossless for
neograph-exported specs. Here it is silently LOSSY -- a think member becomes an agent member,
which changes what the node DOES at runtime (a ReAct tool-call cycle instead of one
structured completion), not merely how it is labelled. The two defects cancelling is what
kept it out of sight.

CORRECT FIX DIRECTION (does not regress either side): stamp the per-member mode and trigger
on export, read them back per member on import, and keep today's behaviour as the FOREIGN
fallback (a Swarm with no neograph marker still maps HandoffMode -> mesh trigger and defaults
to agent mode). That fixes the true cause, leaves foreign-Swarm import untouched, and makes
the two import-side sites correct rather than merely cancelling.
Precedent for the shape already exists in-tree: SWARM_ENCODING's SUB_CONSTRUCT row carries
import_forced_trigger='output' -- a PER-CLASS trigger decision rather than a mesh-level one.
The fix generalises that idea from one hard-coded row to the member's own recorded class.
## Fix + verify (d2ulr.12-.19)

FIRST ATTEMPT WAS WRONG, AND THE EXISTING TESTS CAUGHT IT -- recorded because the wrong
reasoning is instructive. I first derived the trigger STRUCTURALLY from whether the member
has tools ('no tools -> no ReAct turn -> cannot be tool-triggered'), which would have worked
for foreign specs with no marker. Four existing tests went red. They were RIGHT: a
tool-triggered member may legitimately declare tools=[] because the transfer_to_<peer> tools
are SYNTHESIZED at compile time, not user-declared, so Agent.tools is a signal for 'has user
tools', NOT for 'can be tool-triggered'. Reverted in full rather than adjusted around.

That failure also settled the maintainer's question ('a spec without neograph annotation must
import correctly too'): it ALREADY does. A foreign Swarm's members genuinely ARE Agents, so
mode='agent' + the mesh-level HandoffMode inference is the correct reading for them. There is
no foreign signal that says 'this was a think node', because in a foreign spec it wasn't one.
The losslessness gap is therefore OURS alone, and the fix must not touch the foreign path.

THE FIX (root cause -- the EXPORT, not either import site the ticket named):
- NEW marker neograph/portal_member_spec, stamped per mesh member by
  _lower_portal_mesh_to_swarm, carrying {mode, trigger}. Swarm.handoff is mesh-level and
  pyagentspec's Agent carries no mode, so these two facts had NO wire representation at all.
- _reconstruct_swarm_mesh prefers the marker per member; absent it, the mesh-level inference

title: Portal mesh: tools_destinations omits exit_name even though on_exhaust='exit' can emit Command(goto=exit_name)
description: Surfaced by dgbqv.4's architect review (neograph-jn555.21 triage, 2026-08-06). Today's tools_destinations (built at _wiring.py:745's peer_targets, peers only, no exit_name) omits exit_name from a tool-triggered member's registered goto target set, even though _tool_handoff_to_command:356/364 can emit Command(goto=exit_name) on HANDOFF_END or on_exhaust='exit'. This looks like a real gap (LangGraph destination validation could reject the exit transition for a tool-triggered member on exhaust), but it was explicitly called out as OUT OF SCOPE for dgbqv.4's pure-plumbing-collapse commit -- do not silently fix it there. Needs its own investigation: is this reachable today, and if so does it actually break, or is there a compensating mechanism elsewhere?
notes:
## Reproduce (d2ulr.2) -- the ticket's OWN question answered, and the premise is FALSE

The ticket asked: 'is this reachable today, and if so does it actually break, or is there a
compensating mechanism elsewhere?' Both halves answered by experiment, not by reading.

STRUCTURAL GAP -- CONFIRMED in source:
  src/neograph/_wiring.py:709  parse_destinations = ctx.destinations_for(portal)
      -> its own comment says 'declared peers UNION {exit} for BOTH trigger kinds'
  src/neograph/_wiring.py:723  tools_destinations = ctx.resolved_peers(portal) + (agent,)
      -> peers + agent, NO exit_name
  src/neograph/factory.py:277  Command(goto=ctx.exit_name) on HANDOFF_END
  src/neograph/factory.py:289  Command(goto=ctx.exit_name) on on_exhaust == 'exit'
So a tool-triggered member's tools node CAN emit a goto to a node absent from its own
declared destination set. The asymmetry with parse_destinations is real.

REACHABLE -- PROVEN, not assumed. Built a two-agent trigger='tool' mesh whose fakes keep
issuing transfer_to_<peer> calls, with max_hops=1. With on_exhaust='error' it raises
  ExecutionError: Portal handoff exceeded max_hops (expected convergence within 1 hops)
from the tool-triggered path, which proves the budget branch in _tool_handoff_to_command IS
entered. With on_exhaust='exit' the same run completes normally -- i.e. the
Command(goto=exit_name) IS emitted and executed from a node that does not declare exit_name.

DOES IT BREAK? NO -- and this is where the ticket's premise ('LangGraph destination
validation could reject the exit transition') turns out to be FALSE for the pinned
LangGraph. Isolated minimal experiment, no neograph involved:
    g.add_node('a', a, destinations=('b',))   # a returns Command(goto='c')
    app = g.compile()   -> COMPILED OK
    app.invoke({})      -> {'x': 'c-ran'}
LangGraph validates destinations= NEITHER at compile time NOR at run time. It is METADATA
(graph rendering / static analysis), not an enforcement mechanism. That IS the 'compensating
mechanism elsewhere' the ticket hypothesised -- just not the kind it expected: nothing
compensates, nothing needs to, because nothing enforces.

TRIAGE CONSEQUENCE -- this is NOT a runtime bug and must not be reported as one:
- No failing runtime test can be written for it, because there is no runtime failure. A
  bug-triage 'reproduce' atom that demands a RED runtime test cannot be satisfied honestly
  here, and inventing one (e.g. asserting an exception that does not occur) would be fake.
- It IS a real defect of a lower kind: the declared graph misrepresents the actual control
  flow. A rendered diagram omits the tools->exit transition, any static analysis over
  destinations= is wrong, and it is inconsistent with parse_destinations which does include
  exit. If LangGraph ever adds enforcement, it becomes a silent break at that moment.
- Correct severity: downgrade from BUG to a correctness-of-declaration task. Fix is a
  one-liner (add ctx.exit_name to tools_destinations, mirroring destinations_for), and the
  regression test must assert the DECLARED SET -- the acceptance genuinely lives in the
  declaration, not in behaviour, so a structural assertion is the matching locus here rather
  than a substitute for a behavioural one.
## Fix + trace-similar + verify (d2ulr.3, .4, .7, .8)

FIX (one line of behaviour): _wiring.py tools_destinations now uses
ctx.destinations_for(portal) -- peers UNION exit -- instead of resolved_peers(portal),
matching the parse sibling. Plus the agent loopback, unchanged.

TWO INCORRECT CLAIMS IN THE CODEBASE, both corrected because both are what made this
defect exist and look scarier than it is:
1. _portal_route.py destinations_for's docstring justified EXCLUDING the tool member:
   collapsing 'would silently widen a tool-triggered member's declared goto target set,
   and destinations= is validation/rendering metadata no behavioral test asserts on'.
   Both clauses are false. The tools node genuinely emits Command(goto=exit_name), so
   declaring it is a CORRECTION not a widening; and a test now asserts it. Rewritten with
   the history, so the next reader does not re-derive the old rationale.
2. _wiring.py:358 claimed members are registered with destinations= 'so LangGraph
   validates the target set at compile time'. LangGraph does no such thing -- proven by
   isolated experiment. Corrected in place; this is the belief that framed dgbqv.7 as a
   potential runtime break.

TRACE-SIMILAR (d2ulr.3) -- swept every destinations= site in src/ against every
Command(goto=) emitter:
  _wiring.py:305  (approve_name, ctx.exit_name)          includes exit  OK
  _wiring.py:312  ctx.destinations_for(portal)           includes exit  OK
  _wiring.py:326  ctx.destinations_for(portal)           includes exit  OK
  _wiring.py:458  (exit_name, portal.error_handler)      includes exit  OK
  _wiring.py:592  parse_destinations                     includes exit  OK
  _wiring.py:587  tools_destinations                     WAS the only omission -- FIXED
tools_destinations was the single outlier in the codebase, not an instance of a wider
pattern. Systemic risk: LOW.

REGRESSION TEST: TestToolTriggeredToolsNodeDeclaresTheMeshExit in
tests/test_portal_tool_trigger.py. Asserts the tools node declares the SAME exit its parse
sibling declares, read through the public graph.get_graph() accessor (the same accessor the
neighbouring no-static-edge test uses). RED before the fix (AssertionError naming the
missing __handoff_exit_triage), GREEN after. Its docstring records WHY it asserts a
declaration rather than a runtime failure, so nobody later mistakes it for a weakened test.

FILE-SIZE RATCHET INTERACTION -- worth recording because it shaped the commit: the fix is
one line but the explanatory comments pushed _wiring.py from 773 to 783, and the ratchet
blocks growth (a ceiling may only follow a real shrink). Rather than raise it, the prose was
compressed back to land the file at exactly 773 with the corrections intact. The long-form
reasoning lives here and in the commit message, which is where the ratchet's own rules say
it belongs.

title: Design question: should Portal's max_hops/on_exhaust entry-only rule become value-based instead of model_fields_set-based?
description:
Surfaced by 2j208's architect review (neograph-jn555.45 triage, 2026-08-06). The entry-only-knobs rule for Portal (max_hops/on_exhaust only valid on the entry member) is currently encoded FOUR separate times by hand: _node_modifier_kwargs._build_portal_kwargs:187-206 (@node, None-sentinel conditional include), forward.py:989-992 self.handoff (entry-member-only application), loader.py:388-397 _reconstruct_swarm_mesh (idx==0 from portal_spec marker), and now a 4th in 2j208's YAML PortalSpec pass-through. All four exist because the rule is currently keyed on model_fields_set ("which fields did the author explicitly write") rather than on value ("is max_hops non-None").

Open question: would changing to a value-based sentinel (max_hops: int | None = None, default applied at READ time rather than construction time) let all four encodings collapse into one, and would it survive a model_dump/model_validate round trip (which the current model_fields_set-based rule does NOT, hence the bespoke marker handling in loader.py)?

This is a design question, not yet scoped as an implementation ticket. Needs its own design pass before work starts.
design:
# dgbqv.6 DESIGN v2 — value-based Portal knob sentinels (post-review)

Supersedes v1. All six review findings accepted; two were BLOCKING and would have broken
features landed this week. Every claim below re-verified in-tree by the orchestrator.

## Core Invariant (unchanged)
Authorial intent about a Portal knob must be carried by the knob's VALUE, so it survives every
boundary that reconstructs the object — never by `model_fields_set`, which is a property of
how an instance was CONSTRUCTED and does not travel.

## R1 (was BLOCKING) — the field list spans THREE declaration sites, not one
v1 listed only `Portal`. Verified:
    src/neograph/_portal.py         max_hops: int = 10 / on_exhaust: ... = "error" / trigger: ... = "output"
    src/neograph/_spec_schema.py:84-86   PortalSpec declares ALL THREE with the same eager defaults
    schemas/neograph-pipeline.schema.json:505-511   mirrors them as JSON-schema defaults
If PortalSpec keeps eager defaults while `_spec_loader.py:275`'s fields_set comprehension
collapses to a plain read, EVERY YAML non-entry member starts passing `max_hops=10`, which
under `is not None` trips the entry-only rule and breaks the YAML Portal support merged in
e85a0cc. All three sites convert in ONE commit, or none do.

## R2 (was BLOCKING) — forward.py's SIGNATURE defaults, not just its application site
`forward.py:974-975` is `max_hops: int = 10, on_exhaust: Literal[...] = "error"`. v1 changed
only the application (line ~1019). Left eager, the ForwardConstruct entry member always
carries an explicit 10 while a declarative entry carries None — so v1's own MANDATORY
three-surface parity test fails on the ENTRY member, and the Agent-Spec marker then differs by
surface. `self.handoff`'s params become `| None = None` too.

## R3 — SERIALIZATION SITES ARE A FIRST-CLASS CATEGORY THAT MUST READ RAW
Answers the open question this ticket was blocked on. `_agent_spec_portal.py:114`
(`"trigger": member_portal.trigger`) and the `_MARK_PORTAL_SPEC` dict (`max_hops`/`on_exhaust`
from `entry_portal`) are intent SERIALIZERS, not value consumers. Writing `effective_*` there
would round-trip an unset entry as explicitly-10 / explicitly-"error" — destroying exactly the
unset-ness this ticket exists to preserve, and reversing the losslessness neograph-dgbqv.8
(56eb106) fixed hours earlier.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GUARD: v1 said "nothing outside `_portal.py` reads the raw optional field
for a VALUE" and its guard banned precisely this read. Serialization/marker sites are
therefore a NAMED allowlist category with a written reason — decided here, not discovered
mid-implementation.
Downstream widening to verify: `_agent_spec_swarm_import.py:171` types `member_trigger` as
`Literal["output","tool"]` and reads `portal_spec["max_hops"]` as `int`; both widen to
`| None`. Check `tests/test_guards_agent_spec_markers.py` does not pin concrete marker values.

## R4 — the read-site count was WRONG, and this resolves the seam question
v1 claimed ~17 read sites incl. "factory.py x8". Verified false: `factory.py:214/215/283/284`
read `ctx.max_hops` / `ctx.on_exhaust` on **MeshContext** (`_portal_route.py:68-69`, typed
`max_hops: int`), NOT on a Portal.
So the default is APPLIED once, where MeshContext is built (`_portal_route.py:96-97`), from
`effective_*`. Then:
  * factory.py needs ZERO edits
  * MeshContext keeps `max_hops: int` — no Optional leaks into the runtime
  * the `on_exhaust == "exit"` quiet-fallthrough the decision note called "fail-loud by luck"
    is eliminated BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by discipline
`effective_*` on Portal is the right home for the default VALUE; `_portal_route.py`'s
MeshContext build is the right place to APPLY it. The only genuine arithmetic site is
`_recursion_budget.py:98` (`entry_portal.max_hops * per_hop`) — one call, not eight.

## R5 — trigger converts; dgbqv.8 is NOT at risk; one unnamed edit
Every trigger read verified. `_portal_member.py:95` classifies through `portal.is_tool_triggered`,
and `_agent_spec_swarm_import.py:225/231` passes a CONCRETE trigger for every member, so
SWARM_ENCODING / `import_forced_trigger` / PortalMemberClass are untouched.
The edit v1 missed: `_portal.py:106` `self.trigger == "tool"` must become
`self.effective_trigger == "tool"`. `None == "tool"` is False — the right answer BY ACCIDENT,
which is the very "correct by luck" pattern this ticket's read-time seam exists to remove.
After it, `trigger` has ZERO raw value-reads outside `_portal.py` (only the R3 marker write).

## R6 — the entry-only rule survives, but only after R1+R2
`getattr(portal, knob) is not None` preserves rejection for non-entry members. The decorator
surface is already safe (`_build_portal_kwargs`'s conditional-include yields None-for-unset, so
it degrades to a true pass-through). Import applies knobs only at `idx == 0`. The two surfaces
that could accidentally pass an explicit default and NEWLY trip the rule are YAML (R1) and
ForwardConstruct (R2) — which is why those two are blocking rather than cosmetic.

## Sequence (revised)
1. Guard (failing-first) + the RED behavioural test:
   `Portal.model_validate(Portal(to=['b']).model_dump())` raises today, must pass after.
   Guard categories: VALUE reads -> `effective_*` (allowlist `_portal.py`);
   SERIALIZER reads -> raw, allowlisted BY NAME with reason (R3).
2. `_portal.py`: three field types -> `| None = None`; `DEFAULT_*`; `effective_*` properties;
   `is_tool_triggered` -> `effective_trigger` (R5).
3. The 4 enforcement sites -> `is not None` (incl. `_portal.py:129`, which is what fixes the
   round trip).
4. `_portal_route.py:96-97` applies the defaults into MeshContext (R4). `_recursion_budget.py:98`.
5. `_spec_schema.py` + the JSON schema (R1); `forward.py` signature (R2).
6. The intent encodings collapse to pass-throughs; delete the now-false docstrings that
   justify them (`_build_portal_kwargs`'s "load-bearing, not cosmetic" paragraph is the main one).
7. Three-surface parity tests (@node / declarative / programmatic) + YAML + ForwardConstruct —
   R1/R2 mean the surface count that must agree is FIVE, not three.
8. Full gate incl. the Agent-Spec Portal round-trip suites; file-size ceilings in the same commit.

## R7 — THE TRAP: the import fallback must stay keyed on marker PRESENCE
From the review addendum; verified in-tree at `_agent_spec_swarm_import.py:217`, which is
`if member_spec is not None:` — presence-keyed today, and it MUST stay that way.

Once `trigger` can legitimately be None, the natural "tidy" is
    member_trigger = member_spec.get("trigger") or mesh_trigger        # WRONG
    # or:  if member_spec["trigger"] is not None: ...                  # WRONG
Either silently re-creates neograph-dgbqv.8's bug FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION: in a mesh where
ANY member is tool-triggered the exported `Swarm.handoff` is OPTIONAL, so a None trigger
falling through to `mesh_trigger` converts an UNSET think member into `trigger="tool"` — the
exact silent conversion dgbqv.8 was filed for and fixed in 56eb106.

REQUIRED regression test, named against dgbqv.8 so nobody re-tidies it later:
> a mesh of one agent member with `trigger="tool"` + one think member with trigger UNSET
> exports as HandoffMode.OPTIONAL and re-imports with the think member's Portal trigger
> still **None** — not "tool", and not "output"-by-materialization.
Assert on the VALUE being None. Do NOT assert via `model_fields_set` — the new guard bans it,
and asserting through the mechanism being retired would be self-defeating.

## R8 — why the marker must write RAW, stated precisely (tense matters)
The addendum's strongest argument is about the POST-change state, and the pre-change
measurement does not refute it — checked both:
    TODAY:  Portal(to=['x']) == Portal(to=['x'], trigger='output')  ->  True
            (both materialize trigger="output", so the distinction is invisible to __eq__)
    AFTER:  the first has trigger=None, the second "output"  ->  NOT equal
Pydantic `__eq__` compares field VALUES and ignores `model_fields_set`. So after the change,
writing `effective_*` into the marker makes export->import a NON-IDENTITY: the reconstructed
Portal differs from the original by a field value, and `tests/test_portal_parity.py` compares
Portal instances across surfaces. Raw write keeps it an identity; effective write turns it
into a fixpoint at the wrong point. Behaviour is identical either way (None -> effective ->
"output" at every read) — only fidelity differs, which is the whole ticket.

Mechanical consequences, same commit: `_agent_spec_swarm_import.py:171` `member_trigger`
widens to `Literal["output","tool"] | None`, as do the `Portal(trigger=...)` calls at :225/:231;
`portal_spec["max_hops"]` widens to `int | None`. Guard allowlists BOTH serializer sites by
name with the reason inline.
notes:
## Design-pass evidence (2026-08-11, orchestrator)

The ticket asks whether a value-based sentinel would collapse the four encodings AND whether
it would survive a model_dump/model_validate round trip, noting the current rule 'does NOT'.
Measured it rather than assuming, and the result is SHARPER than the ticket states.

A legal Portal cannot survive its own DEFAULT serialization:
    p = Portal(to=['b'])                  -> OK, model_fields_set == {'to'}
    Portal.model_validate(p.model_dump()) -> ConfigurationError:
        'Portal peer mode forbids max_depth'
Because model_dump() emits max_depth=None, and on re-validation the mere PRESENCE of the key
puts 'max_depth' into model_fields_set, which the peer-mode check reads as 'the author set
it'. The rule cannot distinguish 'explicitly None' from 'serialized default'.

    p.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)      -> {'to': ['b']}   round-trips fine.

So the current design carries an UNWRITTEN INVARIANT: every serialization path touching a
Portal must pass exclude_unset=True. Nothing enforces or documents it, and a plain
model_dump() anywhere produces a payload that cannot be loaded back.

NOT A LIVE BUG TODAY: swept src/ and tests/ -- nothing calls model_dump on a Portal (the
Agent-Spec export builds its own marker dict instead). So this is latent, not active. It is
also precisely WHY loader.py needs bespoke marker handling rather than just re-validating a
dumped Portal, which is the ticket's fourth encoding site.

FRAMING FOR THE DECISION: model_fields_set is being used as a proxy for authorial INTENT, but
it is a property of HOW AN OBJECT WAS CONSTRUCTED, not of its value -- so it cannot survive
any boundary that reconstructs the object (serialization, model_validate, and to a degree
model_copy). Every one of the four hand-rolled encodings exists to carry that intent across a
boundary where model_fields_set does not travel. That is the root cause; the four encodings
are the symptom.
## DECISION (maintainer, 2026-08-11): value-based sentinel, ALL FOUR fields together

Chosen over (b) keep model_fields_set + guard the exclude_unset invariant, and over (c) move
the knobs to the mesh. Portal is unreleased with one downstream consumer, so the breaking
change to its public field types costs nothing real.

SCOPE IS FOUR FIELDS, NOT TWO -- this is the binding part of the decision. _portal.py:154's
dispatch-mode check reads model_fields_set for ('max_hops', 'on_exhaust', 'name', 'trigger'):
  max_hops : int = 10                              -> int | None = None
  on_exhaust: Literal['error','exit'] = 'error'    -> Literal[...] | None = None
  trigger  : Literal['output','tool'] = 'output'   -> Literal[...] | None = None
  name     : str | None = None                     -> ALREADY value-based, no type change
Converting only some leaves model_fields_set for the remainder, i.e. TWO mechanisms where
there is now one consistent (if duplicated) one -- strictly worse than today. All four move
or none do.

CORRECTION to an earlier framing in this session: I first listed 'explicitly set to the
default becomes indistinguishable from unset' as a cost. That is WRONG for a None sentinel --
max_hops=10 explicit is still distinguishable from unset (None). Authorial intent survives as
a VALUE. That cost does not apply and should not be planned around.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY PAID:
1. 17 read sites across 7 src modules (factory.py x8, _portal_route.py x2, _recursion_budget.py
   x2, modifiers.py x2, _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py, _spec_loader.py, _wiring_loop.py) go
   from int to int|None. Defaults must be applied at ONE read-time seam, not per site.
2. The field type stops expressing 'a peer Portal always has a hop budget'; that invariant
   moves into the accessor.
3. Migration risk is mostly loud (current >= None -> TypeError) with ONE quieter case:
   on_exhaust == 'exit' reads False when None, falling through to the raise branch. Fail-loud
   by luck rather than design -- the read-time seam must remove that luck.

EXPECTED PAYOFF: the four hand-rolled encodings collapse to one, and
Portal.model_validate(p.model_dump()) starts working -- today it raises ConfigurationError
because dumped max_depth=None re-enters model_fields_set (measured, see the evidence note
above). The unwritten 'always dump with exclude_unset=True' invariant disappears rather than
needing a guard.
## Architect Review (96a70.4) — VERDICT: NEEDS_REFINEMENT

Direction is sound and NOT re-litigated. Six defects in the PLAN, two of which
break code that landed this week if implemented as written.

### F1 (BLOCKING) — PortalSpec is missing from the field-change list
`_spec_schema.py:85-86` declares `max_hops: int = 10` / `on_exhaust: Literal[...] = "error"`
on **PortalSpec**, and `schemas/neograph-pipeline.schema.json:505-511` mirrors them.
The plan collapses `_spec_loader.py:275`'s fields_set comprehension to "a plain field
read" — but with PortalSpec keeping EAGER defaults, every YAML **non-entry** member then
passes `max_hops=10`, which under `is not None` trips the entry-only rule at
`_validation_portal.py:264`. That breaks the YAML Portal support merged in e85a0cc.
PortalSpec's three fields (and the JSON-schema defaults) must convert in the SAME commit,
or the comprehension must not collapse. The design's field list covers only Portal itself.

### F2 (BLOCKING) — forward.py's own signature defaults, not just its application site
`forward.py:974-975` is `max_hops: int = 10, on_exhaust: Literal[...] = "error"`.
The plan only changes line 1019 ("pass None for non-entry members"). With the signature
defaults left eager, the ENTRY member always carries `max_hops=10` explicitly while a
declarative entry carries None — so the plan's own MANDATORY three-surface parity test
fails on the entry member, and the Agent-Spec export marker then differs by surface.
`self.handoff`'s params must become `| None = None` too.

### F3 (Q2 answered) — export MUST write RAW; the guard as scoped forbids that
`_agent_spec_portal.py:114` (`"trigger": member_portal.trigger`) and the `_MARK_PORTAL_SPEC`
dict (`max_hops`/`on_exhaust` from `entry_portal`) are intent SERIALIZERS, not value
consumers. Writing `effective_*` there makes an unset entry round-trip as explicitly-10 /
explicitly-"error" — losing exactly the unset-ness the whole ticket exists to preserve, and
reversing the losslessness dgbqv.8 (56eb106) just fixed. But the design states "nothing
outside `_portal.py` reads the raw optional field for a VALUE", and its guard bans precisely
this read. **Serialization/marker sites must be a named first-class category** (raw read
required, allowlisted with a written reason), not an exception discovered during
implementation. Downstream: `_agent_spec_swarm_import.py:171` `member_trigger` is typed
`Literal["output","tool"]` and `portal_spec["max_hops"]` is `int` — both widen to `| None`;
verify `tests/test_guards_agent_spec_markers.py` does not pin concrete marker values.

### F4 (Q4 answered) — the "17 read sites / factory.py x8" figure is wrong, and this
### resolves the seam question
factory.py:214/215/283/284 read `ctx.max_hops` / `ctx.on_exhaust` on **MeshContext**
(`_portal_route.py:68-69`, declared `max_hops: int`), NOT on a Portal. If
`_portal_route.py:96-97` populates MeshContext from `effective_*`, then **factory.py needs
zero edits**, MeshContext stays `int`, and the `on_exhaust == "exit"` quiet-fallthrough the
decision note flags as "fail-loud by luck" is eliminated BY CONSTRUCTION. So: `effective_*`
on Portal is the right home for the default VALUE; `_portal_route.py`'s MeshContext build is
the right place to APPLY it. The only genuine arithmetic site is `_recursion_budget.py:98`
(`entry_portal.max_hops * per_hop`) — one call. Re-derive the site count before sizing;
mypy exposure is far smaller than 17.

### F5 (Q1 answered) — trigger SHOULD convert; dgbqv.8 is NOT at risk, but one edit is unnamed
Verified every trigger read. The classifier is safe: `_portal_member.py:95` goes through
`portal.is_tool_triggered`, and `_agent_spec_swarm_import.py:225/231` passes a CONCRETE
trigger for every member (from the member marker or `_swarm_trigger`), so
SWARM_ENCODING/`import_forced_trigger` and PortalMemberClass are untouched. The one edit
the design does not name: `_portal.py:106` `self.trigger == "tool"` must become
`self.effective_trigger == "tool"` — `None == "tool"` is False, i.e. the RIGHT answer by
accident. That is the same "correct by luck" pattern the decision note demands the read-time
seam remove; leaving it raw would satisfy the tests and violate the design's own rationale.
Note also that after this, `trigger` has ZERO raw value-reads outside `_portal.py` (only the

## Architect Review (96a70.4) — ADDENDUM: ruling on the dgbqv.8 marker seam

Asked to rule precisely on `_agent_spec_portal.py:114` (`"trigger": member_portal.trigger`,
landed today in 56eb106) and its importer `member_trigger = member_spec["trigger"]`.

### (a) The marker MUST write the RAW field. Not the effective value.

Three independent reasons, any one sufficient:

1. **Pydantic equality is value equality.** Under the value rule `Portal(to=x)` and
   `Portal(to=x, trigger="output")` are NOT equal models (`__eq__` compares field VALUES;
   `model_fields_set` is not part of it). Writing the effective value makes export->import
   a non-identity: the reconstructed Portal differs from the original by a field value.
   `tests/test_portal_parity.py` compares Portal instances across surfaces — an
   effective-write turns a genuine round-trip into a fixpoint at the WRONG point.
2. **It reverses the ticket.** The whole change exists so intent travels as a value across
   reconstruction boundaries. The Agent-Spec marker IS that boundary. Writing the effective
   value there is the one place that would still destroy unset-ness — the exact failure
   mode, just relocated from `model_fields_set` to the wire.
3. **Effective buys nothing.** The importer feeds the value straight back into
   `Portal(trigger=...)`, and `None` -> `effective_trigger` -> `"output"` at every read. The
   operative behaviour is identical either way; only fidelity differs.

**Consequences to implement (all mechanical, all must be in the same commit):**
- `_agent_spec_swarm_import.py:171` `member_trigger: Literal["output","tool"]` widens to
  `| None`, as does the `Portal(trigger=member_trigger)` call at :225/:231.
- Same ruling for `_MARK_PORTAL_SPEC`'s `max_hops`/`on_exhaust` (`_agent_spec_portal.py`
  Swarm metadata) — raw, and `portal_spec["max_hops"]` widens to `int | None`.
- Therefore the plan's guard MUST allowlist these two serializer sites explicitly, with the
  reason written in the guard (see F3/F7 above). They are intent SERIALIZERS; a raw read is
  correct there and a raw read is a defect everywhere else. If the guard cannot express that
  distinction, the guard is wrong, not the export.

### (a-corollary) THE trap, and the test that must pin it

The fallback in `_agent_spec_swarm_import.py` is keyed on **marker PRESENCE**
(`if member_spec is not None:`), and it must STAY keyed on presence. Writing it as
`member_spec.get("trigger") or mesh_trigger` (or `if member_spec["trigger"] is not None`)
would be the natural "tidy" once the value can be None — and it silently re-creates
dgbqv.8's bug from the other direction: in a mesh where ANY member is tool-triggered the
exported `Swarm.handoff` is OPTIONAL, so a `None` trigger falling through to `mesh_trigger`
would convert an unset THINK member into `trigger="tool"`.

REQUIRED regression test (name it against dgbqv.8 so nobody re-tidies it):
> a mesh with one agent member `trigger="tool"` + one think member with trigger UNSET
> exports (HandoffMode.OPTIONAL) and re-imports with the think member's Portal trigger still
> None — not "tool", and not "output"-by-materialization.
Assert on the VALUE being None, not on `model_fields_set` (which the new guard bans).

### (b) `is_tool_triggered` — no None branch. One-token change, for a stated reason.

`_portal.py:106` is `not self.is_dispatch and self.trigger == "tool"`. `None == "tool"` is
False, so it is right today — but right by coincidence of the comparison operator, which is
the same "fail-loud by luck" the decision note says the read-time seam must eliminate.
Change it to `self.effective_trigger == "tool"`. Do NOT add an explicit
`if self.trigger is None: return False` — that would encode "None means output" a SECOND
time, one line away from `DEFAULT_TRIGGER`, which is the duplicated-source-of-truth disease
this ticket is removing. One default, one accessor, one comparison.

### (c) `portal_member_class` is unaffected — verified, and it is the desired class.

`_portal_member.py:73-95`: `is_tool_triggered` is consulted ONLY inside the
`mode in {"agent","act"}` branch. So:
- think/scripted member, trigger=None -> ATOMIC (or ATOMIC_OPERATOR) — trigger never
  enters the decision at all. Identical to today's trigger="output". Correct.
- agent/act member, trigger=None -> `is_tool_triggered` False -> AGENT_CYCLE_OUTPUT ->
  `SWARM_ENCODING[AGENT_CYCLE_OUTPUT].export_trigger == "output"` -> the mesh-level
  `mesh_handoff_mode` aggregation is unchanged. Correct, and it is the desired class: an
  unset trigger means the member routes by typed output.
No surprising class, no new class needed, no change to SWARM_ENCODING or
`import_forced_trigger` (SUB_CONSTRUCT still force-sets a concrete "output", which under
the value rule is a legitimate EXPLICIT value — the Construct member genuinely cannot be
tool-triggered, so recording that as an authored value rather than a default is right).

### (d) Second authority to document, or it will be "unified" later

After this change there are two per-member trigger facts on the export path with DIFFERENT
jobs: the raw marker (`member_portal.trigger` — authorial intent, may be None) and
`SWARM_ENCODING[...].export_trigger` (per-class canonical wire value, never None, feeds
`mesh_handoff_mode`). They will now visibly disagree in shape for an unset member. Write the
distinction into a comment at BOTH sites in this commit; otherwise a future reader collapses
them and silently reintroduces materialization at the marker.

Consequence: neograph.testing's auto-scaffolded test directory (test_modifiers.py, test_sync.py drift detection) silently produces NO modifier assertions and NO drift tracking for a Portal-modified node -- it is treated as unmodified. design:
# Design: Portal coverage in the neograph.testing scaffold (neograph-wvp7j)

Design pass, 2026-08-11. Scope: `src/neograph/testing/scaffold.py` only (the YAML
spec surface with the same disease is neograph-2j208's scope).

## The defect, restated precisely

`scaffold.py` hand-enumerates the modifier universe in FOUR places, and all four
stop at oracle/each/loop/operator:

1. `_node_info` (scaffold.py:67-70) — the per-node capture dict has no `portal` key.
2. `_gen_modifiers` (scaffold.py:236) — `modified = [n for n in nodes if n["oracle"] or n["each"] or n["loop"] or n["operator"]]`.
3. `_gen_sync` (scaffold.py:519-521) — the same 4-way disjunct builds `EXPECTED_MODIFIED`.
4. **Inside the GENERATED test file** — `_gen_sync` emits `has_mod = bool(item.modifier_set.oracle or ... or item.modifier_set.operator)` (scaffold.py:574-575). This one is worse than the other three: a generated suite is frozen at scaffold time, so even after scaffold.py is fixed, this emitted enumeration would rot again the day a sixth modifier lands.

Consequence: a Portal-modified node produces no modifier assertions, no
EXPECTED_MODIFIED entry, and — because the emitted `has_mod` is also partial —
the generated drift test can never fire "gained a modifier" for Portal. The
scaffold reports covering the construct while silently not covering it.

## Q1 — What a generated Portal assertion should assert

Portal is one modifier with two structurally different modes, discriminated
ONLY via `Portal.is_dispatch` (`_portal.py:80` — the declared single source of
truth; a structural guard already bans the inline `route == "decide"` literal
outside `_portal.py`). Generated code and scaffold code alike must read
`is_dispatch` / `is_tool_triggered`, never string-compare fields.

### Dispatch mode (`route="decide"`) — per-node assertions in test_modifiers.py

A dispatch Portal is a standalone linear node, never a mesh member
(`_portal_member.py` docstring). The per-node pattern the other four modifiers
use fits it exactly. Emit, following the oracle precedent (unconditional
asserts for required knobs, conditional for optional ones):

```python
portal = planner.modifier_set.portal
assert portal is not None
assert portal.is_dispatch
assert portal.spec_field == "spec"
assert portal.input_field == "dispatch_input"
assert portal.output is Summary            # __name__-rendered if a class, string literal if str
assert portal.max_depth == 3
assert portal.on_invalid == "raise"
# only if set:
assert portal.error_handler == "handle-bad-spec"
assert sorted(portal.scripted) == ["fn_a", "fn_b"]      # keys only — values are callables
assert sorted(portal.conditions) == ["done"]
```

All four required dispatch knobs (`spec_field`, `input_field`, `output`,
`max_depth` — enforced by `model_post_init`, `_portal.py:144-153`) are asserted
unconditionally. `scripted`/`conditions` registries are asserted by sorted key
list only; the callables cannot be value-asserted, and pretending to (repr of a
lambda) would be a fake assertion.

Capture caveat: `output` may be a class or a string. Render with the same
`__name__`-collapsing rule `_node_info` already applies to `outputs_name`
(scaffold.py:43-46, the neograph-wpzg/CON-01 fix) — a raw class repr is not
valid Python in generated source.

### Peer mode (`to=[...]`) — assertions live at MESH level (see Q2)

Per-member knobs: `to` (the declared successor set), `trigger`
(`output`/`tool`), `name` (mesh group, if set), and the member's
`PortalMemberClass`. Entry-only knobs: `max_hops`, `on_exhaust` — meaningful
only on `members[0]` (`_portal.py:65`), so asserting them per node on non-entry
members would emit default-value noise that LOOKS like coverage. They are
asserted once, on the entry, in the mesh test.

The `PortalMemberClass` assertion is the highest-value one: `portal_member_class(item)`
(`_portal_member.py:73`) is the ONE authority for "what kind of participant is
this", and it is exactly the axis on which silent lowering changes happen — a
member whose mode flips scripted→agent moves from ATOMIC to AGENT_CYCLE_OUTPUT
and compiles to a different runtime shape. A generated
`assert portal_member_class(member) is PortalMemberClass.ATOMIC` pins that with
one line and zero re-derived taxonomy.

## Q2 — Per-node dict vs mesh-level notion (the crux)

**The per-node dict is necessary but not sufficient. The scaffold needs a
mesh-level summary, collected through `_group_portal_members` — never a
re-derived grouping.**

Why per-node cannot express the mesh:

- **Entry identity is positional.** `members[0]` of a contiguous sibling run is
  the entry; the entry carries the budget knobs and is the only legal jump
  target (the north-star entry-port rule). No single node's dict knows whether
  it is first. Reordering two siblings changes the entry — a silent routing +
  budget change with zero per-node field difference. That is precisely the
  drift class test_sync exists to name.
- **Membership is a set property.** "Which nodes form mesh `name=X`, in what
  order" is the thing `_group_portal_members` (`_portal.py:175`) computes, and
  its docstring declares it the SINGLE grouping authority (validator, IR
  normalizer, and wiring collector all route through it). The scaffold
  re-deriving grouping inline would replant the exact duplicated-source-of-truth
  disease this ticket is about.
- **Mesh members need not be Nodes.** A SUB_CONSTRUCT member is a `Construct`
  with a portal; `_collect_items` routes Constructs into `subs` dicts that
  carry no modifier info at all. A node-keyed portal capture would silently
  drop sub-construct members — a second silent seam inside the fix.

Concrete design:

- `_node_info` gains a `"portal"` key (per-node capture: `is_dispatch`, mode
  knobs, `member_class` name) — parity with the other four slots, and it feeds
  the totality-fixed `modified` filter and `EXPECTED_MODIFIED`.
- New collector `_collect_meshes(construct) -> list[dict]`: walk
  `construct.nodes` (top-level items, Node OR Construct), keep items whose
  `portal_member_class(item)` is a mesh-member class (not `None`, not
  `DISPATCH`), group via `_group_portal_members`. Each mesh dict:
  `{"name": group_or_None, "members": [ordered names], "entry": members[0],
  "max_hops": entry.portal.max_hops, "on_exhaust": entry.portal.on_exhaust,
  "per_member": [{name, to, trigger, member_class}, ...]}`.
- `_gen_modifiers` emits one `TestPortalMesh...` class per mesh asserting:
  ordered membership against `_group_portal_members(...)` on the live construct
  (pins membership, order, and therefore entry identity and contiguity),
  entry budget knobs, and each member's `to`/`trigger`/`PortalMemberClass`.
- Split of responsibility: dispatch Portal → per-node test in `TestModifiers`;
  peer Portal → everything in the mesh test. This resolves the Node/Construct
  asymmetry (the mesh test looks members up by NAME in `construct.nodes`, so a
  sub-construct member gets identical treatment) and avoids duplicating peer
  assertions in two places.

Generated-code imports: the mesh test imports `_group_portal_members` and
`portal_member_class`/`PortalMemberClass`. Generated suites already import the

## Q3 — _gen_sync drift shape

Three changes, each with a named drift class it catches:

1. **`EXPECTED_MODIFIED` becomes total** (via the Q4 registry). Catches: Portal
   added to / removed from a node. This is the tier-drift analog for modifiers
   and today is silently blind to Portal.
2. **The EMITTED `has_mod` expression is replaced with
   `has_mod = bool(item.modifier_set.to_list())`** (`to_list` walks
   `_SLOT_RULES`, `modifiers.py:804` — total over the roster by construction).
   This makes generated suites total FOREVER, including against modifiers that
   do not exist yet: the frozen-at-scaffold-time enumeration is the one site
   the scaffold cannot patch retroactively, so it must not enumerate at all.
3. **Two new expected-blocks + drift tests:**
   - `EXPECTED_PORTAL_MESHES = {mesh_name_or_None: ("entry", "m2", ...)}` —
     compared against `_group_portal_members` output on the live construct.
     Catches: member added/removed, members reordered (entry changed),
     peer member flipped to dispatch (drops out of the grouping). These are
     routing-topology changes — exactly the "shape drift" tier test_sync
     owns (its existing checks are scripted↔LLM tier and modifier
     presence, never knob values).
   - `EXPECTED_DISPATCH = {...}` names — drift test asserts each still has
     `modifier_set.portal is not None and portal.is_dispatch`, and that no
     node OUTSIDE the set became dispatch. Catches: the peer↔dispatch mode
     flip, which rewrites the node's entire lowering (mesh member vs
     standalone Command-returning runtime).

   Knob-value drift (`max_hops` 10→6, `spec_field` renamed) deliberately stays
   in test_modifiers/mesh assertions, not sync — sync's contract is
   shape/tier-level, mirroring how it treats `mode` but not `prompt`.

## Q4 — Yes, the enumeration is the real defect. Recommendation: capture registry + totality guard

Adding a 5th disjunct fixes Portal and re-plants the disease for modifier six.
The root cause is that scaffold.py's modifier vocabulary has no structural tie
to the roster in `modifiers._SLOT_RULES` (the declared "adding a new modifier
means adding ONE row here" table, `modifiers.py:646-655`).

**Recommended:** a scaffold-local capture registry

```python
_MODIFIER_CAPTURE: dict[str, Callable[[ModifierSet, Node], dict | None]] = {
    "each": ..., "oracle": ..., "loop": ..., "operator": ..., "portal": ...,
}
```

- `_node_info` builds its modifier keys by iterating `_MODIFIER_CAPTURE`.
- Every "is this node modified" check derives from the registry keys
  (`any(n[slot] for slot in _MODIFIER_CAPTURE)`), so sites 2 and 3 stop being
  independent enumerations.
- A structural guard (failing-first, per project practice) pins totality:
  `set(_MODIFIER_CAPTURE) == {r.slot for r in _SLOT_RULES}`, plus an AST/grep
  ban on the inline `n["oracle"] or n["each"]`-style disjunct in scaffold.py.
  A sixth modifier without a capture entry now fails CI loudly instead of
  falling through silently. Same shape as the
  `test_guards_modifier_composition_completeness.py` precedent for
  `MODIFIER_KWARGS`.

**Rejected alternative — fully generic capture** (dump each modifier's
`model_fields` and assert everything): truly automatic, but emits meaningless
assertions — lambda reprs for `Operator.when`/`Portal.scripted`, entry-only
budget knobs asserted on non-entry members, mode-forbidden fields asserted at
defaults. That is the "reports covering without covering" failure this ticket
exists to refuse. Per-modifier emission knowledge (which knobs are assertable,
in which mode, at which level) is irreducible; the registry's job is to make
its ABSENCE loud, not to eliminate it.

**Tradeoff stated:** the guard is test-time, not import-time — a sixth
modifier's author sees a red guard, not a type error. Acceptable: it matches
every other totality ratchet in this codebase (`_COMBO_MAP` exhaustiveness,
`MODIFIER_KWARGS` completeness), and an import-time assert in scaffold.py would
punish every user import for a maintainer-only invariant.

Note: `PortalMemberClass` (dgbqv.3) does NOT replace this registry — it answers
"what kind of mesh participant", not "which slots exist". The registry keys on
`_SLOT_RULES`; the member-class taxonomy is the vocabulary INSIDE the portal
capture/emission, as Q1/Q2 use it.

## Architect Review (hb60o.4) — VERDICT: NEEDS_REFINEMENT

First independent review of the wvp7j design. The CORE of the design survives: I verified Q2s
crux claim against the real authority and it is CORRECT (see A3). Four concrete defects must be
fixed in the design before an executor touches code. None invalidate the approach.

### R1 (CRITICAL, design is silent) — RAW vs effective_* for the None-sentinel knobs

The design predates dgbqv.6 (6302f83). `Portal.max_hops` / `on_exhaust` / `trigger` are now
`X | None = None` (_portal.py:75-77) with `effective_max_hops` / `effective_on_exhaust` /
`effective_trigger` applying DEFAULT_* (_portal.py:104-123). The design never states which one a
generated assertion emits. RULING, concretely:

  CAPTURE the RAW field. EMIT the assertion ONLY when the raw field `is not None`.
  NEVER emit an `effective_*` assertion, and never emit a value for an unset field.

Three reasons, in force order:
1. `assert portal.max_hops == 10` for a mesh that never set it is the exact fake assertion this
   ticket exists to refuse — it reports covering an authorial decision that was never made.
2. It is WORSE than fake: it freezes a LIBRARY constant into a USER suite. Change
   DEFAULT_MAX_HOPS and every generated suite for a pipeline that never declared a budget goes
   red, attributing a neograph-internal change to the users pipeline. `effective_*` has the
   identical defect (`assert portal.effective_max_hops == 10` pins DEFAULT_MAX_HOPS through the
   users tests), so switching to effective_* does NOT fix it — only conditional emission does.
3. Conditional emission is already the established precedent in this exact function: _gen_modifiers
   emits oracle.merge_fn / merge_prompt only under `if o["merge_fn"]:` (scaffold.py:257-261).
   Portal knobs are the same shape; no new convention is needed.

Payoff: conditional-on-raw also catches the drift class effective_* cannot — an author ADDING an
explicit `max_hops=10` that happens to equal the default produces a NEW assertion line where none
existed. Under an effective_* rule that change is invisible.

Scope: applies to the mesh entry knobs (max_hops, on_exhaust) AND to the per-member `trigger`
(design Q1 lists it unqualified). Not an issue for dispatch mode: model_post_init (_portal.py:187)
forbids all four of max_hops/on_exhaust/name/trigger when route="decide". The designs mesh dict
already captures `entry.portal.max_hops` (raw) — so only the EMISSION rule is missing, not the
capture.

### R2 — _MODIFIER_CAPTURE: the registry as designed DOES duplicate the roster; derive it

Confirmed: _SLOT_RULES (modifiers.py:648-655) already carries all five slots incl. Portal, with
the "adding a new modifier means adding ONE row here" comment. The designs registry hand-writes
those five keys AGAIN and pins the duplication with a set-equality guard. That works, but it is
strictly worse than deriving:

    _CAPTURE_FNS = {"each": ..., "oracle": ..., "loop": ..., "operator": ..., "portal": ...}
    _MODIFIER_CAPTURE = {r.slot: _CAPTURE_FNS[r.slot] for r in _SLOT_RULES}

The roster then exists ONCE, and a sixth modifier without a capture is a loud KeyError at import
of neograph.testing.scaffold — not neograph — so the designs "punish every user import" objection
does not apply (a user install can never hit it; only a tree mid-refactor can).

WARNING THAT COMES WITH IT (and is the real finding): under derivation, the proposed
`set(_MODIFIER_CAPTURE) == {r.slot for r in _SLOT_RULES}` guard becomes VACUOUSLY TRUE. Do not
keep it in that form. Retarget the guard to non-vacuity: for each slot, build a node carrying that
modifier and assert its capture returns a non-None dict, AND assert `_node_info()`s returned dict
has a key per slot. Then mutation-test it (drop "portal" from _CAPTURE_FNS, confirm red) before
calling the guard done — project practice, and this guard is exactly the kind that can ship green
and empty.

The design also splits the table: it puts "the portal entry of _MODIFIER_CAPTURE" in the sibling
module while the registry presumably lives in scaffold.py. That re-plants the disease at half
scale. The registry and every capture fn must live in ONE module (see R4).

Guard 1b (the AST/grep ban on inline slot disjuncts) is under-specified and will be either vacuous
or over-broad as written. Concrete form that works: assert no line in testing/*.py matches
`modifier_set\.(oracle|each|loop|operator|portal)\s+or` and none matches
`n\["(oracle|each|loop|operator)"\]\s+or`. Both patterns are exactly the four real sites.

neograph.testing re-export; keep it as the optional follow-up ticket the design already names.
The alternative — having generated code re-derive the grouping to avoid the import — is the
disease, so the private import is the CHEAPER of the two.

so the file-split procedures heavier machinery is not required", and simultaneously that

fresh-file addition cannot lower it. Something existing MUST move out, which IS a cluster split.

Recommendation (also fixes R2s split-table defect): move the whole modifier-emission cluster —
_gen_modifiers plus the new _MODIFIER_CAPTURE registry, all five capture fns, _collect_meshes and
the portal/mesh emitters — into ONE sibling named for what it owns, `_scaffold_modifiers.py`, not
`_scaffold_portal.py`. The registry is not portal-specific; naming the module after Portal

### Steps 1-5 otherwise stand
Guard-first ordering, the heterogeneous 3-member peer fixture, and especially step 4s red half
(the same generated test_sync.py must FAIL against reorder / mode-flip / portal-removed variants,
