title: P10: export/import read PortalMemberClass -- replace loader.py's type-name Swarm-encoding check (depends on P9)
description:
Axis 3 of the former neograph-jtawq.1 (now closed, split three ways). Full detail: docs/design/
agent-spec-target-architecture-2026-08-03.md Sec 2 Pillar B5.

A two-way table mapping PortalMemberClass <-> Agent-vs-Flow member encoding, trigger axis <->
HandoffMode (via the existing _swarm_trigger inverse pair), entry knobs <-> _MARK_PORTAL_SPEC.
Replaces loader.py:373's `type(agent).__name__ == 'Flow'` type-name check and its hard-coded :380-384
rule. Depends on P9 (neograph-dgbqv.4) per the design doc's own stated phase order -- re-verify at
implementation time whether P10 could in fact start as soon as P7 alone lands (the doc lists them
sequentially but the technical dependency may only be on the PortalMemberClass enum itself, not on
P9's plumbing collapse); if so, loosen the dependency, but do not assume -- confirm by reading what
P10's implementation actually needs.

Swarm stays a documented LOSSY adapter (loader.py:411-442 warnings; _agent_spec_portal.py:158-170
exit-gate approximation) -- the runtime taxonomy (PortalMemberClass) is the authority; the Swarm
mapping is one table reading it, never the reverse.
design:
## Core Invariant

PortalMemberClass is the runtime taxonomy and the sole authority; the Agent-Spec Swarm encoding is ONE table that READS it in both directions, so the runtime never mirrors Swarm's shape and no consumer re-derives "Agent vs Flow", "trigger", or "HandoffMode" locally.

## Implementation Plan (corrected per architect review neograph-jn555.36, resolved in refine atom neograph-jn555.57, 2026-08-06; every location + ceiling below re-verified against HEAD 89d1784)

0. Re-derive locations by SYMBOL, not by line. jtawq.10 lands FIRST and moves loader.py:237-491 -- the entire import half of this ticket -- into `_agent_spec_swarm_import.py`. Re-read the home of `_reconstruct_swarm_mesh` / `_swarm_trigger` before touching anything. Verified at refinement time (pre-jtawq.10): type-name check `loader.py:362`, forced trigger `loader.py:373`, `_swarm_trigger` `loader.py:274-292`, export sites `_agent_spec_portal.py:93 / :121-126 / :147-151`, dispatch fail-loud `_agent_spec.py:295-303`.

1. New leaf table module `src/neograph/_agent_spec_swarm_encoding.py`. Imports ONLY `neograph._portal_member`, `neograph.errors` (verified a true leaf -- its only import is `from __future__ import annotations`) and stdlib. It must NEVER import pyagentspec at module level (core-purity guard): HandoffMode is carried by its STRING VALUE ('never'/'optional'/'always'), and the export side converts at its EXISTING function-local `from pyagentspec.swarm import HandoffMode, Swarm` (_agent_spec_portal.py:112) via `HandoffMode(<value>)` -- verified value-constructible (NEVER='never', OPTIONAL='optional', ALWAYS='always').

   TWO tables, because the two axes have DIFFERENT key spaces. This is a correction to the prior plan, which tried to hang the mode axis's `canonical` flag on rows keyed by PortalMemberClass -- impossible, since HandoffMode.ALWAYS has no PortalMemberClass row to live on.

   (A) `HANDOFF_MODE_TRIGGER: tuple[HandoffModeRow, ...]` -- the MODE axis, TOTAL over HandoffMode's three values. Frozen NamedTuple columns: `mode_value: str`, `trigger: Literal["output", "tool"]`, `canonical: bool`. Rows exactly: ("never","output",True), ("optional","tool",True), ("always","tool",False). This one table absorbs BOTH `_swarm_trigger`'s hand-written forward map and `_agent_spec_portal.py:121-126`'s hand-written inverse.

   (B) `SWARM_ENCODING: dict[PortalMemberClass, SwarmEncoding]` -- the MEMBER axis, TOTAL over the enum (all six: ATOMIC, ATOMIC_OPERATOR, AGENT_CYCLE_OUTPUT, AGENT_CYCLE_TOOL, SUB_CONSTRUCT, DISPATCH), with DISPATCH present as a real not-exportable row. Frozen NamedTuple columns:
      - `spec_class: Literal["Flow", "Agent"] | None` -- 'Flow' for SUB_CONSTRUCT, 'Agent' for the four node classes, None for DISPATCH.
      - `export_trigger: Literal["output", "tool"] | None` -- what this class CONTRIBUTES to the mesh handoff decision. 'tool' for AGENT_CYCLE_TOOL, 'output' for the other four exportable classes, None for DISPATCH.
      - `import_forced_trigger: Literal["output", "tool"] | None` -- whether reconstruction OVERRIDES the mesh trigger for this class. 'output' for SUB_CONSTRUCT (that IS loader.py:373's hard-code); None ("use the mesh trigger") for every other row.
      - `gated: bool` -- True for ATOMIC_OPERATOR only.
      - `exportable: bool` + `reason: str | None` -- False + a reason string for DISPATCH; True + None otherwise.
      - `canonical: bool` -- the spec_class-axis inverse selector; see step 2.

      REVIEWER NOTE, stated so this is not mistaken for a re-run of the finding-3 disease: `export_trigger` and `import_forced_trigger` are NOT two spellings of one relation. They answer different questions and neither is derivable from the other -- AGENT_CYCLE_TOOL exports 'tool' but on IMPORT takes the mesh trigger (None), while SUB_CONSTRUCT is 'output' on both. Only ONE of them (`export_trigger`) feeds handoff mode, and there is NO hand-written per-class handoff_mode column at all (step 3).

2. [resolves finding 2] The inverse must FAIL LOUD, never silently pick. Do NOT copy `modifier_names_for_combo` verbatim -- it is only correct because `_COMBO_MAP` is a BIJECTION. Both inverses here are many-to-one: {optional, always} -> 'tool', and {ATOMIC, ATOMIC_OPERATOR, AGENT_CYCLE_OUTPUT, AGENT_CYCLE_TOOL} -> 'Agent'. A `{row.col: row for ...}` comprehension is order-dependent last-wins -- a silent seam inside the very module built to remove silent seams.

   Write ONE generic `_derive_inverse(rows, value_of, key_of)` helper in the table module that groups rows by the target column, and per group:
      - exactly one row -> that row is the inverse image;
      - >1 rows with exactly one `canonical=True` -> that row;
      - >1 rows with >1 `canonical=True` -> raise `ConfigurationError` AT IMPORT TIME (a contradiction inside the table);
      - >1 rows with ZERO `canonical=True` -> the key is DELIBERATELY ABSENT from the derived inverse, and a lookup for it raises `ConfigurationError` naming the colliding members.

   That last rule is a deliberate correction to the review's own "REQUIRES exactly one canonical" suggestion: "at most one" lets the table state honestly that a direction is NON-invertible instead of forcing us to fabricate a canonical row for a question nothing asks.

   Apply the helper twice:
      - MODE axis over (A): trigger -> canonical mode. 'output' -> 'never' (sole row); 'tool' -> 'optional' (canonical over 'always'). This turns `_agent_spec_portal.py:126`'s existing PROSE comment ("OPTIONAL/ALWAYS are byte-identical there, so OPTIONAL is the canonical choice") into DATA.
      - spec_class axis over (B): 'Flow' -> SUB_CONSTRUCT (sole row, `canonical=True`). All FOUR 'Agent' rows are `canonical=False` ON PURPOSE -- the import path never recovers a PortalMemberClass from 'Agent' (it builds a Node and applies the mesh trigger), so crowning an arbitrary one (the prior plan guessed "likely ATOMIC") would invent data with no consumer AND would silently answer a question the encoding genuinely cannot answer.

   Module docstring must state the asymmetry: the table is TOTAL export-ward (every PortalMemberClass has a row) but only the SUB_CONSTRUCT / 'Flow' cell is invertible import-ward; asking the inverse for 'Agent' is a loud error, by design.

3. [resolves finding 3] There is NO hand-written per-class handoff_mode column (see step 1B). The table module instead exposes:
      - `handoff_mode_for_class(cls) -> str` = canonical-mode-for-trigger(`SWARM_ENCODING[cls].export_trigger`), routed through the ONE step-2 mode inverse. Never a second hand-typed dict.
      - `mesh_handoff_mode(classes: Iterable[PortalMemberClass]) -> str` -- the MESH-level aggregation `Swarm.handoff` needs. This function exists because `Swarm.handoff` is per-MESH while the encoding column is per-CLASS, so the combination rule must be NAMED and STATED rather than implicit. Precedence, verified against today's `any_tool` at `_agent_spec_portal.py:121-126`: **'optional' wins over 'never'** -- return the canonical mode for 'tool' if ANY member's `export_trigger` is 'tool', else the canonical mode for 'output'. Comment it with that provenance. DISPATCH must never appear in `classes` (a dispatch-mode Portal is not a mesh member -- `_portal_member.py`'s own docstring); raise rather than defaulting.
      - After this, `_agent_spec_portal.py` holds NO handoff-mode literal of its own: `handoff=HandoffMode(mesh_handoff_mode(member_classes))`.

4. Import side -- replace, do not wrap.
      - `type(agent).__name__ == "Flow"` becomes `type(agent).__name__ == SWARM_ENCODING[PortalMemberClass.SUB_CONSTRUCT].spec_class` (equivalently, a lookup through the step-2 spec_class inverse).
      - `member_trigger = "output"` becomes `SWARM_ENCODING[PortalMemberClass.SUB_CONSTRUCT].import_forced_trigger`.
      - `_swarm_trigger` becomes a thin read of the mode->trigger direction over table (A), KEEPING its existing normalization byte-for-byte (`handoff is True` -> tool; `False`/`None` -> output; `getattr(handoff, "value", handoff)` then table lookup). Do not change its fail-soft-on-unknown behavior in this ticket.
      - Everything else in `_reconstruct_swarm_mesh` untouched; the `member_trigger = mesh_trigger` Agent arm stays as-is -- `import_forced_trigger is None` for those rows IS the "use the mesh trigger" statement.

5. [resolves finding 4] Export side -- same tables, other direction, and NO rewiring of the dispatch raise.
      - `isinstance(member, Construct)` at `_agent_spec_portal.py:93` becomes `portal_member_class(member) is PortalMemberClass.SUB_CONSTRUCT`.
      - `any_tool` + the HandoffMode ternary (:121-126) is replaced by `HandoffMode(mesh_handoff_mode(...))` (step 3).
      - the `gated` comprehension (:147-151) selects on `SWARM_ENCODING[portal_member_class(m)].gated` (== ATOMIC_OPERATOR; equivalent by construction per `_validation_portal.py:144-154`).
      - DO NOT touch `_agent_spec.py:295-303`'s dispatch-mode fail-loud (inside the `PrimaryShape.PORTAL` arm). VERIFIED: that is the real site, NOT `_agent_spec_portal.py`, and `_agent_spec.py` is at its EXACT allowlist ceiling 651/651 (tests/test_guards_file_size.py:73) which step 8 does not budget. Rewiring it would additionally be (a) a layer inversion -- the generic item-lowering dispatcher importing a SWARM-specific encoding table -- and (b) would make `_agent_spec.py` an undeclared new PortalMemberClass consumer, turning the P7 census red. Instead EXTEND `TestDispatchModePortalFailsLoud` to assert the EXISTING raise is CONSISTENT with `SWARM_ENCODING[PortalMemberClass.DISPATCH].exportable is False` and its `.reason`: a DATA-consistency test, not a code rewire. If a future ticket rewires it anyway, it must budget the `_agent_spec.py` ceiling AND add it to MIGRATED in the same commit.

6. [resolves finding 1 -- MANDATORY per AGENTS.md's Portal-rollout lesson; BOTH sibling tables shipped one] NEW structural consumer guard `tests/test_guards_swarm_encoding_consumers.py`, written FAILING-FIRST, in the same shape as `tests/test_guards_combo_decomposition_consumers.py` (pure `ast`, no `re`, so it is exempt-by-construction from `tests/test_guards_meta.py`'s named-regex/slip-test discipline):
      (a) NO SECOND ENUMERATION. No file under `src/neograph` may reference `HandoffMode.<ATTR>` (attribute access on the enum) -- every mode value must come from the table. The sanctioned post-migration shape `HandoffMode(<str from table>)` is a CALL, not an attribute reference, so it passes by construction; say so in the docstring.
      (b) NO TYPE-NAME MEMBER-CLASS DISPATCH. No file under `src/neograph` may compare a `type(x).__name__` against the string literal `"Flow"` outside the table module. Precise by design: the five ALLOWLIST sites compare against "AgentNode"/"Swarm"/"FlowNode" -- spec-PRIMITIVE dispatch, the different question P7 also refused -- and stay untouched.
      (c) READS THE TABLE. Each declared consumer imports at least one table symbol AND actually uses the binding (a dead import must not satisfy the guard -- R-L3).
      (d) COMPLETENESS / ANTI-TAUTOLOGY. Derive the "touches this vocabulary" set from the FILESYSTEM and assert strict equality against the hand-written consumer inventory union {table module}. RE-DERIVE that inventory by a FRESH SWEEP at write-test time -- do NOT copy the disease-scan table (AGENTS.md's provisional-list lesson) -- and do NOT build the banned set by intersecting it with the declared set (the half-vacuous-intersection mistake flagged on 2j208's review); derive it structurally so a brand-new file growing the idiom fails loud even though it appears in no literal.
      Negative test REQUIRED: a synthetic `HandoffMode.ALWAYS` and a synthetic `type(x).__name__ == "Flow"` planted outside the table module must each trip the guard.

7. Shrink the P7 guard literals in the SAME commit (`tests/test_guards_portal_member_class_consumers.py`). Four EXACT literal edits (per the LOW finding -- DELETE, not "move"):
      - DELETE "loader.py" from `EXEMPT_FILES` (:118-133).
      - DELETE "loader.py" from `NO_DISCRIMINATOR_ATTR_SITES` (:188). Today those two CANCEL each other in the census `expected` (:370-371), so they must be removed together to keep it balanced once loader.py holds neither an axis-A site nor a classifier use post-jtawq.10.
      - ADD "_agent_spec_swarm_import.py" (jtawq.10's successor module) to `MIGRATED` (:83) -- it will import-and-USE a classifier symbol, satisfying assertion (b). loader.py must NOT go into MIGRATED; it would fail (b).
      - Account for the new `_agent_spec_swarm_encoding.py` in whichever literal the re-derived census requires (it references PortalMemberClass, so it cannot be silently absent -- most likely MIGRATED; confirm against assertion (b) at implementation time).

8. File-size ratchet. `loader.py` is at its EXACT ceiling (652/652 verified; `tests/test_guards_file_size.py:83`). This change must leave it net-shorter and LOWER the ceiling in the SAME commit -- or DELETE the entry entirely if jtawq.10 already dropped it under 500 (never lower it to a sub-500 number). `_agent_spec.py`'s 651/651 (:73) is deliberately NOT budgeted -- step 5 is what keeps that true. The new table module must land under 500 with no allowlist entry.

      (a) TOTALITY -- every `PortalMemberClass` member has a `SWARM_ENCODING` row, asserted by iterating the ENUM itself (not a literal list); and `HANDOFF_MODE_TRIGGER` is total over HandoffMode's values.
      (b) The SUB_CONSTRUCT forced-'output' rule survives a Swarm whose handoff is OPTIONAL.

      (e) The mixed-mesh cell pinned as DOCUMENTED-LOSSY by an explicit test AND (per finding 5) by a written invariant COMMENT IN THE TABLE MODULE ITSELF, not only in the test: "a mixed mesh (tool-triggered agent member + non-agent member) round-trips LOSSILY: export sets handoff=OPTIONAL, which forces trigger='tool' onto EVERY member on re-import; _validation_portal.py:162-174 would reject that on a think-mode member, and ONLY _agent_spec_node_import.py:216's markerless-agent mode='agent' hard-code prevents a ConstructError. The two defects CANCEL -- see neograph-dgbqv.8; do not fix either side without fixing the other."

notes:
## Findings (research atom neograph-jn555.34, 2026-08-06, against HEAD 89d1784)

### The reuse target already exists — do NOT build a parallel taxonomy
- REUSE `PortalMemberClass` / `portal_member_class` — src/neograph/_portal_member.py:53-96 (landed 23eb571, P7/dgbqv.3). It is already THE authority, and its own docstring (:79-81) pre-declares dgbqv.5's scope: a foreign pyagentspec object has no `.modifier_set`, returns `None`, and 'it is not this classifier's job to reconstruct a spec-shape mapping (neograph-dgbqv.5)'. So P10 does NOT extend the classifier — it adds a SEPARATE bridge-layer table that reads it.
- REUSE the table IDIOM the same wave already established: `ComboDecomposition` NamedTuple + `COMBO_DECOMPOSITION: dict[ModifierCombo, ...]` (src/neograph/modifiers.py:136-179), with the inverse DERIVED from the one table at definition time rather than hand-written a second time (modifiers.py:115-117 `modifier_names_for_combo`; jtawq.2's 'derive from a table field, not a predicate'). That is the exact shape B5 asks for.

### The six encoding sites the table must own (the actual disease surface)
IMPORT (loader.py, `_reconstruct_swarm_mesh` :327-433):
- :362 `type(agent).__name__ == "Flow"` — the member-kind read the ticket names.
- :373 `member_trigger = "output"` — the hard-coded rule (ticket says :380-384; STALE, see Risks).
- :274-292 `_swarm_trigger(swarm)`: HandoffMode value -> trigger, many-to-one ({never->output, optional/always->tool}), string-value compare (no pyagentspec import).
- :387 `member_trigger = mesh_trigger` — the Agent arm.
EXPORT (_agent_spec_portal.py, `_lower_portal_mesh_to_swarm` :43-210):
- :93-94 `isinstance(member, Construct)` -> `export_flow(member)` — the SAME member-kind question as :362, written a second way. Not caught by P7's guard (its node-vs-construct axis is deliberately not AST-decidable).
- :121-126 `any_tool` -> `HandoffMode.OPTIONAL/NEVER` — the canonical inverse of `_swarm_trigger`. Already reads the classifier (P7-migrated); the table absorbs the literal.
- :147-151 `gated` dict from `member.modifier_set.operator is not None` — exactly ATOMIC_OPERATOR (validation at _validation_portal.py:144-154 rejects Operator on agent/act and sub-construct members, so the two are equivalent by construction).
- Entry knobs are per-MESH, not per-class: `_MARK_PORTAL_SPEC` written at :128-133, read at loader.py:352 + applied entry-only at :388-397. The table covers the member axis; entry knobs stay a marker round trip.

### The two-way table, filled in (verified against code, total over the enum)
| PortalMemberClass | export encoding | import recognition | trigger | HandoffMode contribution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUB_CONSTRUCT | `export_flow` -> pyagentspec `Flow` | `Flow` | "output" (forced) | never |
| ATOMIC | `_make_agent` -> `Agent` | `Agent` | mesh trigger | never |
| ATOMIC_OPERATOR | `Agent` + name in `_MARK_PORTAL_OPERATOR_SPEC` + mesh-exit composite | `Agent` + gated marker | mesh trigger | never |
| AGENT_CYCLE_OUTPUT | `Agent` | `Agent` | "output" | never |
| AGENT_CYCLE_TOOL | `Agent` | `Agent` | "tool" | optional |
| DISPATCH | NOT exportable, fail loud (pinned: tests/test_agent_spec_construct_member.py:166-174) | n/a | n/a | n/a |
The class->encoding direction is a FUNCTION; encoding->class is NOT (four classes share `Agent`). What is a function on the import side is encoding -> member-kind + forced-trigger, which is all :362/:373 actually need. Keeping DISPATCH as a real row makes the table TOTAL, so consumers can stay exhaustive.

### Where it lives
A new leaf module (proposed `_agent_spec_swarm_encoding.py`) importing only `_portal_member` + stdlib, sitting below BOTH bridge sides per the target-architecture layer map (docs/design/agent-spec-target-architecture-2026-08-03.md:165-186). It must express HandoffMode by its STRING VALUE ('never'/'optional'), never by importing pyagentspec at module level — tests/test_guards_agent_spec_core_purity.py flags module-level imports only, and `_swarm_trigger` already compares string values (loader.py:290-292). The export side converts to the enum at its existing function-local `from pyagentspec.swarm import HandoffMode, Swarm` (_agent_spec_portal.py:112).

design:
## Core Invariant

"What kind of Portal mesh participant is this item" is answered in exactly ONE place, which
COMPOSES the existing authorities (_portal.py's is_dispatch / is_tool_triggered plus
COMBO_DECOMPOSITION / classify_modifiers) and discriminates Node-vs-Construct STRUCTURALLY --
no consumer re-derives the fact, no new Node/Construct import is created to obtain it, and no
existing single-source authority (grouping, legality, combo decomposition) is absorbed or
duplicated in the process.

## Implementation Plan

0. **Resolve the home first -- this is a real fork, not a formality** (see the NEEDS USER INPUT
   risk). modifiers.py sits at its exact 881-line ceiling, so the doc's stated home cannot take
   the code without turning tests/test_guards_file_size.py red, and "raise the number" is
   explicitly not a remedy. Default taken below: the design doc's OWN pre-authorized fallback --
   a new leaf module **src/neograph/_portal_member.py**, which imports classify_modifiers /
   primary_shape / PrimaryShape / COMBO_DECOMPOSITION from modifiers.py and Portal from
   _portal.py. It sits ABOVE modifiers.py and BELOW every consumer, so no cycle exists and
   structural discrimination is preserved by choice rather than forced by the DAG. Do NOT
   re-export it through modifiers.py -- even two lines trips the ceiling; consumers import from
   the new module and G-PMC pins the single authority regardless of file. If the maintainer
   instead wants the modifiers.py home, the same commit must shrink modifiers.py by at least the
   lines added (a split is not cleanly available -- see Risks).

1. **Write G-PMC FIRST, failing** (guard-first, per this repo's standing discipline), as
   tests/test_guards_portal_member_class_consumers.py, copied in shape from
   tests/test_guards_combo_decomposition_consumers.py -- MIGRATED / PENDING / TABLE_OWNER
   frozensets, AST symbol-use scan, mutation meta-tests, anti-vacuity tripwire. Seed MIGRATED
   from a sweep you run at that moment, not from this bead's census (which is itself declared
   provisional). PENDING must reach frozenset() before the task closes.
   Two guard clauses the doc specifies incorrectly and that must be written correctly here:
   (a) the import-discipline assertion is scoped to the CLASSIFIER FUNCTION's AST subtree, not to
   the whole module -- modifiers.py:399-400 already holds an allowlisted function-local
   Node/Construct import for Loop validation, so a module-wide assertion is unsatisfiable;
   (b) modifiers.py:818/:861 are exempt BY REASON (pair-legality, jtawq.3/P3 axis), recorded in
   the exemption literal with that reason, not silently omitted.

2. **Build the taxonomy** in the chosen module: enum PortalMemberClass with ATOMIC,
   ATOMIC_OPERATOR, AGENT_CYCLE_OUTPUT, AGENT_CYCLE_TOOL, SUB_CONSTRUCT, DISPATCH; and
   portal_member_class(item) -> PortalMemberClass | None, where None means "carries no Portal at
   all" so the enum stays closed over participants and match arms remain exhaustive under
   assert_never.

3. **Derive, never re-derive, inside the classifier**: read PORTAL membership through
   primary_shape / classify_modifiers (never an inline isinstance-on-Portal); read the mode axis
   through _portal.Portal.is_dispatch and .is_tool_triggered; discriminate node-vs-construct with
   getattr(item, "nodes", None) is not None, and read the agent/act axis with
   getattr(item, "mode", None) -- the exact duck-typing shape classify_modifiers uses at
   modifiers.py:169. Preserve compiler.py:284-286's Node-only DISPATCH invariant as a fail-loud
   check inside the classifier rather than letting it dissolve into a silent classification.

4. **Migrate the compile-side consumers**, one commit-coherent pass, each keeping its existing
   error messages and behavior byte-identical: state.py (delete the private _is_dispatch at
   :225-227; :239 member filter; :253-256 operator field; :266), compiler.py:278-286,
   _wiring.py:197 / :336-364 / :748, _construct_validation.py:249, and _validation_portal.py's
   six arms (:68, :130, :147-152, :166-168, :318, :345) -- the last of these must keep building
   its "sub-construct" vs "<mode>-mode" strings locally; the classifier supplies the verdict only.

5. **Migrate _recursion_budget.py:36-63 and :172** -- the consumer the ticket and the design doc
   both miss. _member_hop_cost becomes a match over PortalMemberClass, which is also the clearest
   demonstration that the taxonomy is the right abstraction (its four arms are the four classes).

6. **Migrate the bridge sites**: _agent_spec_portal.py:93, :122, and :218-228 (_is_portal_member
   collapses to one classifier call), plus loader.py:373's type-name derivation and the second
   import-side derivation at :488. Keep the Swarm mapping a thin two-way table reading the
   taxonomy -- per the design's Conflict Resolution 6, Swarm is a lossy adapter and never the
   authority. If the loader-side move proves to need the P9/P10 plumbing, migrate what is
   mechanical now and record the remainder against dgbqv.5 (P10) rather than half-landing it.

7. **Behavioral coverage, not just the guard**: add tests that pin the classification of each
   enum member through a real construct (atomic peer, Operator-gated peer, agent-mode peer,
   trigger="tool" agent peer, sub-Construct member, dispatch node, and a non-Portal node -> None),
   and prove no behavior changed at the migrated sites by keeping the existing Portal suites green
   (tests/test_example_portal.py, test_example_portal_dynamic_flow.py, the _validation_portal
   error-message assertions, and the recursion-budget tests).

8. **Close the ratchets in the same commit**: PENDING == frozenset(); update
   tests/test_guards_file_size.py only in the direction the ratchet allows (new module under 500
   with no entry; if modifiers.py shrank below 500 its entry is DELETED, never lowered);

description:
Pillar C steps (b)+(c) from docs/design/agent-spec-target-architecture-2026-08-03.md. The tier that
would have caught the rh5fb and s7zt3.15/.17 bug class -- reachability alone is NOT sufficient
(a734217's branch-flattening bug was fully reachable; only a walk that EVALUATES conditions sees a
missing decision).

(b) EXECUTE: a literal Agent-Spec mini-executor in tests/ -- the semantic extension of the
reachability BFS (test_agent_spec_reachability.py:81-113): walk ControlFlowEdges from StartNode,
evaluate BranchingNode conditions, pass values only via DataFlowEdges, iterate MapNode subflows.
Semantics pinned to _wiring's actual runtime (do-while entry, gate-after-body, pause reconvergence) --
exactly as the reachability suite's own docstrings already document (:35-38, :139-150, :185). Run over

(c) COMPARE: mini-executor outputs == real `run(compile(construct))` outputs. Immediately possible
ONLY for mode=scripted cells -- build_cell's `_llm_kwargs` gives think/agent/act cells a real model +
prompt, not scripted fakes (a prior probe's premise that they were already fakes was refuted during
the target-architecture audit -- do not re-assume it). LLM-mode GREEN cells enter an EXEC_EXEMPT
frozenset with per-entry reasons, partition-asserted against GREEN, shrink-only ratchet (same shape as
the combo-decomposition guard's PENDING pattern). Burn-down path: wire tests/fakes.py
(configure_fake_llm/StructuredFake/ReActFake) identically into both the mini-executor and the real
run() side.

own importer path -- independence from the forgiving marker-reader is the entire point of this tier;
its own possible wrongness is defended by (c)'s two-sided comparison.

blocker. Depends on P2 (this ticket) landing first -- the WIRE tier's cell registry is what EXECUTE

design:
## Core Invariant

The EXECUTE tier runs the exported Flow through a genuinely third-party, independently-authored runtime -- pyagentspec.adapters.langgraph.AgentSpecLoader, already installed via the pinned pyagentspec>=26.1.0,<27 dependency -- rather than code neograph's own team writes and could get wrong in the same way twice. Independence comes from AUTHORSHIP (Oracle wrote it, we didn't), not from hand-rolling a parallel walker. AgentSpecLoader consumes ONLY the exported Flow (plain pyagentspec data: nodes/edges/metadata) plus a tool_registry we supply (callables keyed by exported node/tool name) -- zero dependency on the neograph package -- so any disagreement between AgentSpecLoader's execution and neograph's own run(compile(construct)) on the same cell is a real defect in one of the two independently-authored sides, never a shared blind spot.

The metadata-awareness question (may the harness read neograph/* metadata) is a SEPARATE axis from "who builds/runs the graph": AgentSpecLoader builds and runs the graph purely from ControlFlowEdge/DataFlowEdge/BranchingNode topology -- it never reads neograph/* metadata (that is neograph's own private export annotation, meaningless to a third-party consumer). The executor is therefore metadata-BLIND by construction -- the STRONGER form of the "any real Agent Spec runtime" policy test_agent_spec_reachability.py's docstring already commits to, and more faithful to the project's stated full-interop design goal than either option in the original NEEDS_USER_INPUT fork.

## STATUS: prior mini-executor plan is SUPERSEDED (2026-08-06)

The original plan (a hand-rolled tests/agent_spec_mini_executor.py: _branch_adjacency, run_flow, EXEC_EXEMPT frozenset, an AST guard banning the mini-executor's own import graph) and its same-day AMENDMENT are DEAD. AgentSpecLoader eliminates the need for any hand-rolled walker -- it already handles BranchingNode/MapNode/ToolNode/AgentNode dispatch, loop semantics, and hop budgets as a real, tested, third-party implementation. Building a parallel one would be the exact duplicated-verification-surface anti-pattern the pivot exists to avoid.

## Design Decision (user, via orchestrator, 2026-08-06)

User's answer to the metadata-blind vs metadata-aware fork: 'when neograph imports, it should honor the metadata. when neograph exports, the agentspec should be 100% the same in execution as in neograph itself. Also, if one exports - with metadata, the 3rd party changes it and as long as it is a valid agentspec, it has to be imported back to Neograph. Of course, it might lose the awesome wiring abstractions like Oracle/Each etc but it should still be wired correctly, and executed correctly like a langgraph-based graph. that's the design goal: full interop'.

DECISION: mini-executor is METADATA-AWARE — it reads neograph/* metadata for branch/loop/each decisions (matching the recommended option), since neograph's own COMPARE tier must reflect neograph's own execution semantics. This resolves the immediate NEEDS_USER_INPUT block on the 66/100 cells.

BUT: the user's stated design goal is FULL INTEROP — a 3rd party (or a strictly-blind Agent Spec runtime) must still be able to wire and execute the exported Flow CORRECTLY using only ControlFlowEdge/DataFlowEdge, without understanding neograph/* metadata (losing neograph's abstractions like Oracle/Each is acceptable; losing correct execution is NOT). This means the two underlying gaps the research surfaced are REAL EXPORT-FIDELITY BUGS, not artifacts of an overly strict test harness:
1. BranchingNode's branching_mapping_key input has no DataFlowEdge — the decision lives ONLY in metadata (_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py:376-385, 634-641 for loop/operator respectively).
2. MapNode's iterated_item has no DataFlowEdge — the 'over' source lives ONLY in metadata (each_spec).

Per this decision, FILE two separate follow-up beads tickets (blocking neograph's stated 'full interop' design goal) tracking these as export-fidelity gaps: exported Flows should carry REAL DataFlowEdges for branch predicates and Each's 'over' source, not just metadata mirrors, so a metadata-blind runtime executes them correctly. This ticket (dgbqv.2) proceeds with a metadata-aware executor for now; the filed tickets are the path to eventually making the executor's own EXEC_EXEMPT/metadata-aware fallback unnecessary.

### Why C1 generalises `_walk` rather than adding a parallel helper

The plan's wording ("the ONE extension of `_walk`") should be read as **extend `_walk`**, not *sit beside it*.
The Portal retrospective's failure was N consumers independently answering "what does this decompose into";
substitute the noun and it is this situation verbatim -- N consumers independently answering **"what is this
Flow's successor relation"**. Two builders over the same `control_flow_connections`, that must agree forever
and are checked by nothing, is precisely the condition AGENTS.md forbids.

The drift is not hypothetical -- the two builders would differ on exactly the cases that matter:
- `_walk` pre-seeds from `flow.nodes` then does `successors[edge.from_node.name].add(...)`, so it **KeyErrors**
  on an edge whose endpoint is not in `flow.nodes`. A freshly-written helper will almost certainly use
  `setdefault` and **silently tolerate** it -- a divergence about whether a dangling-endpoint export is a defect.
- `_walk` collapses to a `set`, so **duplicate edges vanish**; a branch-keyed `dict[str|None, list[str]]`
  preserves them, and two successors under one label is a real ambiguity a literal executor must fail loud on.
- `from_branch is None` out of a `BranchingNode` is invisible to `_walk`, and is the single most likely export bug.

Each is a case where the reachability tier would prove reachability over a graph the executor does not walk.
**dgbqv.2's entire value proposition -- "a disagreement is a real defect in one of the two sides, never a
shared blind spot" -- is void if the two tiers disagree about what the graph IS.**

Decisive: the branch-keyed view is **strictly richer**. The unlabelled view derives from it in one line
(`{frm: {to for tos in by_branch.values() for to in tos} for frm, by_branch in adj.items()}`); the reverse
derivation does not exist. A second builder adds no expressible representation -- only a second chance to be wrong.

Cost: ~15 lines, proven by the existing 100-cell reachability tier. **Ordering:** land the extraction in the
SAME commit as the executor's first use -- a builder with one caller and no branch-consuming test is dead
weight the next reader inlines back.

neutral-module extraction that C4 makes mandatory. Everything else is ALLOWLIST or DEFER. Deliberately NOT
recommended: migrating the 5 `pairs` sites (proven futile), the 51 lookups / ~20 filters (pure churn), a
tests-side structural guard banning a second Flow-adjacency builder (with C1 done there are 2 consumers of

put the rule in the builder's docstring and file the guard when a THIRD consumer appears; recorded so a

`(flow.data_flow_connections or [])` (C10 -- the Each cells WILL hand it `None`); import `_MARK_*`, never
re-type a marker literal (C11); use the `type(n).__name__` string form (C9).

title: Agent Spec export: RemoteAgent silently re-exports as a plain scripted node (zero readers of _remote_agent_endpoint)
description:
Found by the multi-agent target-architecture audit (docs/design/agent-spec-target-architecture-2026-08-03.md,
ticket-ground-truth table + Sec 2 Pillar B6), re-verified 2026-08-04: `node._remote_agent_endpoint`
(written at src/neograph/_agent_spec_node_import.py:266-267, a `tuple[str, dict[str, Any]] | None`
PrivateAttr on Node, node.py:198) has ZERO READERS anywhere in src/neograph/ -- confirmed by grep.

CONSEQUENCE: neograph-pt85t (closed) correctly preserves a RemoteAgent's endpoint config on IMPORT
(from_agent_spec side) into that sidecar field. But nothing on the EXPORT side (to_agent_spec /
_agent_spec.py / _agent_spec_node_import.py's siblings) ever reads it back out. So importing an Agent
Spec Flow containing a RemoteAgent, then re-exporting the resulting neograph pipeline, silently
degrades the RemoteAgent into a plain scripted node -- the endpoint configuration is quietly lost, not
rejected. Under this session's maintainer-set policy for Agent Spec export ("a faithful, independently
executable program", the same policy that drove neograph-s7zt3.15/.17's fixes), this is a real bug: a
silent lossy re-export, not a documented limitation.

Also noted in the same audit: src/neograph/node.py:191-193's comment on the `_remote_agent_endpoint`
field says it is "stashed by loader.py" -- that's stale; the actual writer is
_agent_spec_node_import.py. Fix the comment in the same change.

FIX DIRECTION (per the target-architecture doc's Pillar B6 / Phase P11, "refined plan"): a
class-discriminator sidecar approach -- when exporting a Node that carries `_remote_agent_endpoint`,
reconstruct the appropriate pyagentspec RemoteAgent-family class (per-family attrs verified against
the actually-installed pyagentspec version) instead of falling through to the plain scripted-node
lowering, and fail LOUD (not silently) if the installed pyagentspec version's RemoteAgent shape has
drifted from what was captured at import time.

DEFINITION OF DONE (per the target-architecture doc): also touches the website's Agent Spec interop
docs page -- AGENTS.md requires a website content pass when an API surface's round-trip behavior
changes. RemoteAgent round-trip is a consumer-visible interop capability.

This is the ONE item the target-architecture doc identified as still keeping neograph-qtfof open --
all of qtfof's other children and dependencies are closed. Closing this ticket (or explicitly
descoping it) is what allows qtfof itself to close.
design:
## Root Cause
node._remote_agent_endpoint (a (agent_class_name, {attr: value}) PrivateAttr sidecar) is written exactly once, at _agent_spec_node_import.py:267, when _reconstruct_agent_node best-effort-imports a client-initiated RemoteAgent/A2AAgent/OciAgent AgentNode into a name-bound Node(mode='scripted', scripted_fn=name). Nothing on the export side ever reads that sidecar back: _lower_node -> _lower_generation_step (src/neograph/_agent_spec_node_lowering.py:164-173, 81-161) dispatches purely on node.mode, and the 'scripted / raw already rejected raw_fn upstream' fallback (154-161) unconditionally builds a bare ToolNode via _make_server_tool, with no branch checking node._remote_agent_endpoint. Confirmed by grep: zero readers of _remote_agent_endpoint anywhere under src/neograph/ besides the PrivateAttr declaration (node.py:198) and this single writer. Consequence: import -> re-export of a Flow containing a client-initiated RemoteAgent silently degrades it to a plain scripted node -- the endpoint configuration is quietly lost, not rejected.

## Fix Approach
Per the ticket's FIX DIRECTION (target-architecture doc Pillar B6 / Phase P11): in _lower_generation_step's scripted/raw fallback (or a new branch in _lower_node before it), check node._remote_agent_endpoint first. If set, reconstruct the appropriate pyagentspec RemoteAgent-family class (A2AAgent/OciAgent, keyed by the stored agent_class_name, with the stored per-family attrs) and emit an AgentNode wrapping it -- mirroring the shape _reconstruct_agent_node originally consumed -- instead of falling through to the ToolNode lowering. Verify per-family attrs against the actually-installed pyagentspec version and fail LOUD (ConfigurationError) if the installed SDK's RemoteAgent-family shape has drifted from what was captured at import time (e.g. a stored attr name no longer exists on the class), per the fail-loud-not-silent-drop policy already used elsewhere in this module (_reject_unrepresentable_fields). Also fix the stale node.py:191-193 comment claiming _remote_agent_endpoint is 'stashed by loader.py' -- the actual writer is _agent_spec_node_import.py. DoD also requires a website Agent Spec interop docs pass (AGENTS.md content-parity rule) since RemoteAgent round-trip is a consumer-visible interop capability.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py::TestRemoteAgentEndpointSurvivesReExport::test_a2a_agent_endpoint_is_lost_on_reexport
- Failure: AssertionError: expected the RemoteAgent endpoint sidecar to reconstruct an AgentNode wrapping an A2AAgent, got a bare 'ToolNode' -- the endpoint config was silently dropped on re-export
- Root cause: _lower_generation_step (src/neograph/_agent_spec_node_lowering.py:154-161) has a single scripted/raw fallback branch that unconditionally builds a ToolNode and never consults node._remote_agent_endpoint, so a Node reconstructed by the import-side best-effort RemoteAgent branch (_agent_spec_node_import.py:259-268, mode=scripted, sidecar set) re-exports as an indistinguishable plain scripted node.
## Similar Pattern Analysis
Bug pattern category: an export-side (Agent Spec) lowering function silently ignores an import-side sidecar field, causing a lossy round-trip instead of a fail-loud rejection.

Search performed: grepped every PrivateAttr sidecar on Node (node.py:195-198: _sidecar, _param_res, _scripted_shim, _remote_agent_endpoint) and Tool (tool.py:64: _bound_tool), and every write site under _agent_spec_node_import.py, _agent_spec_group_import.py, and loader.py's Agent-Spec import arms.

Findings:
- _sidecar/_param_res/_scripted_shim are the @node decorator sidecar (unrelated to Agent Spec import/export) -- they ARE read, by _construct_builder.py at assembly time. Not an instance of this pattern.
- Tool._bound_tool is intentionally NEVER re-serialized on export (documented Core Invariant at _agent_spec_node_lowering.py:215 -- a live callable cannot round-trip through Agent Spec). This is a deliberate, documented decision, not a silent bug.
- _remote_agent_endpoint (_agent_spec_node_import.py:267) is the ONLY sidecar written by the Agent Spec import path with zero export-side readers.
- _agent_spec_group_import.py and loader.py's swarm-import arms (jtawq.10 scope) do not stash any comparable sidecar field.

Conclusion: this bug pattern is ISOLATED to _remote_agent_endpoint. No other instance found; no additional beads tasks filed.
## Codebase Disease Scan (qtfof.5)

Pattern: an Agent-Spec EXPORT-side lowering/dispatch function that branches purely on node.mode (or an equivalent coarse discriminator) and does NOT consult a Node/Tool PrivateAttr sidecar that import-side code wrote for exactly this node — silently dropping node-specific state instead of reconstructing it.

Scan command (SYNTACTIC — single exact-shape branch point, confirmed by direct read + grep, no fan-out warranted):
  grep -n 'PrivateAttr' src/neograph/node.py src/neograph/tool.py
  grep -rn "node.mode ==" src/neograph/_agent_spec*.py
  (plus a full read of src/neograph/_agent_spec_node_lowering.py)

Total instances found: 1

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | src/neograph/_agent_spec_node_lowering.py:154-161 | `_lower_generation_step`'s scripted/raw fallback builds a bare ToolNode without checking node._remote_agent_endpoint | MIGRATE | This is the exact motivating bug — the fix (P11) adds the sidecar check here. |

Rationale for N=1: `_lower_generation_step` is the codebase's SINGLE per-node.mode dispatch function (already unified per its own docstring: 'the ONE validator, not two' anti-pattern CLAUDE.md bans). It has exactly three branches (think / agent-act / scripted-raw); only the scripted-raw fallback is the unconditional catch-all, and it is the only branch missing a sidecar check. There are only 4 PrivateAttr sidecars in the whole codebase (node.py: _sidecar, _param_res, _scripted_shim, _remote_agent_endpoint; tool.py: _bound_tool) — trace-similar (zcjqo.3) already confirmed the other 3 node sidecars ARE read at assembly time and _bound_tool is deliberately never re-serialized (documented Core Invariant). No other export-lowering module (_agent_spec.py, _agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py, _agent_spec_portal.py, _agent_spec_group_import.py) has a comparable mode-dispatch-with-fallback shape. No DEFER/ALLOWLIST instances; no follow-up tickets needed.
## Architect Review (atom neograph-zcjqo.5)

Verified against source: `_agent_spec_node_lowering.py` (full read), `_agent_spec_node_import.py:38-41,229-268` (`_REMOTE_AGENT_ENDPOINT_ATTRS`, `_reconstruct_agent_node`), `node.py:185-198`, and the installed pyagentspec SDK (`a2aagent.py`, `ociagent.py`, `remoteagent.py`, `_openaiagent.py`).

1. **Root cause correctness: LOW risk (confirmed correct).** `_lower_generation_step`'s scripted/raw fallback (lines 154-161) unconditionally returns `ToolNode`; `node._remote_agent_endpoint` is genuinely never read anywhere on the export path. The stale node.py:191-193 comment ('stashed by loader.py') is confirmed stale — the writer is `_agent_spec_node_import.py:267`.

2. **Fix minimality: LOW risk.** The natural fix point IS `_lower_generation_step`'s existing scripted/raw fallback (the codebase's single per-mode dispatch, per its own docstring) — a guarded `if node._remote_agent_endpoint is not None: ... else: <existing ToolNode path>` touches zero other call sites and changes behavior for exactly the one Node shape that carries the sidecar (every other scripted node has it `None` by construction).

3. **Regression risk: LOW.** Confirmed via PrivateAttr default — `_remote_agent_endpoint` is `None` unless set by the one import-side writer, so the new branch is unreachable for all existing scripted/raw nodes.

4. **Architecture compliance: LOW risk, compliant.** Reuses the single dispatch function rather than adding a second copy (avoids the 'one validator, not two' anti-pattern CLAUDE.md bans); the fail-loud-on-drift requirement matches the established `_reject_unrepresentable_fields` convention already in the same module.

5. **Similar bug scalability: LOW — confirmed isolated** by both trace-similar (zcjqo.3) and disease-scan (zcjqo.4): N=1, only `_remote_agent_endpoint` has this write-without-read shape.

6. **Test coverage sufficiency: MEDIUM — needs expansion beyond the single repro test.** Concrete gaps the fix/e2e-verify atoms must close:
   - Repro test only exercises `A2AAgent`; `OciAgent` (the other mapped family) has no test.
   - No test for the fail-loud `ConfigurationError` path when a stored attr name no longer exists on the installed SDK class (the ticket's explicit drift-detection requirement).
   - `pyagentspec.Component.name` is a REQUIRED field on `A2AAgent`/`OciAgent` but is NOT captured in `_REMOTE_AGENT_ENDPOINT_ATTRS` (only `agent_url`/`connection_config` for A2AAgent, `agent_endpoint_id`/`client_config` for OciAgent) — the export-side reconstruction must synthesize a `name=` (e.g. from `node.name`) or the pydantic construction will raise before the intended fail-loud check runs. Not a blocker, just an implementation detail the fix must not miss — no test currently pins it.

## Additional findings (not blocking, informational)

- **LOW, pre-existing scope note, not introduced by this fix**: `A2AAgent.session_parameters` (has a pydantic default) and `OciAgent.retry_policy` (defaults to `None`) are silently NOT captured by `_REMOTE_AGENT_ENDPOINT_ATTRS`, so even after this fix, a RemoteAgent with a customized `session_parameters`/`retry_policy` round-trips to the DEFAULT, not the original — a residual (smaller, pre-existing) lossy-round-trip gap on the IMPORT side that predates qtfof.5. Out of this ticket's stated scope (its FIX DIRECTION only covers the already-captured attrs), but worth a one-line caveat in the website docs pass so 'faithful, independently executable program' isn't overclaimed for these two optional fields.
- **LOW, confirms correct scope, no action needed**: a third concrete `RemoteAgent` subclass exists in the installed SDK (`pyagentspec._openaiagent.OpenAiAgent`), but it is NOT in `_reconstruct_agent_node`'s accepted `agent_type` set, so it already fails loud on IMPORT today (before this ticket) — `_remote_agent_endpoint` can never be set for it, so the export-side fix correctly needs no OpenAiAgent branch.
- The literal string "RemoteAgent" in `_reconstruct_agent_node`'s `agent_type in ("RemoteAgent", "A2AAgent", "OciAgent")` check is dead (pyagentspec's `RemoteAgent` is declared `abstract=True`, so `type(agent).__name__` can never literally be "RemoteAgent") — harmless, not worth changing in this ticket.

## Overall verdict: PROCEED WITH ADJUSTMENTS

The root cause and fix direction are correct and minimal. Before closing, the fix atom must (a) synthesize a valid `name=` for the reconstructed RemoteAgent instance, and the test-writing/e2e-verify atoms must (b) add an OciAgent round-trip test alongside the existing A2AAgent one, and (c) add a fail-loud drift test. No HIGH findings; one MEDIUM (test coverage) that gates test-writing, not implementation.
## Triage (atom neograph-zcjqo.6)

Architect review verdict interpreted as NEEDS_REFINEMENT (not ALL_LOW: one concrete MEDIUM finding on test coverage; not NEEDS_USER_INPUT: no ambiguous design question, the reviewer gave concrete actionable gaps). bug-triage.yaml has no separate refine atom, so refinement is folded directly into the fix atom's required scope:

1. Fix must handle BOTH A2AAgent and OciAgent RemoteAgent families (not just A2AAgent).
2. Fix must add a test for the fail-loud ConfigurationError path when the installed pyagentspec SDK's RemoteAgent shape has drifted from what was captured at import time.
3. Fix must ensure pyagentspec.Component.name (a required field on A2AAgent/OciAgent, not currently captured in _REMOTE_AGENT_ENDPOINT_ATTRS) is synthesized/captured so reconstruction doesn't fail before the drift check runs.

Proceeding to fix-qtfof.5 (neograph-zcjqo.7) with this expanded scope.
## Sweep Verification (atom neograph-zcjqo.8, retry)

Re-scan command (exact, from disease-scan notes):
```
grep -n 'PrivateAttr' src/neograph/node.py src/neograph/tool.py
grep -rn "node.mode ==" src/neograph/_agent_spec*.py
(plus a full read of src/neograph/_agent_spec_node_lowering.py)
```

Pre-fix instances: 1 (MIGRATE)
Post-fix instances: 0

| # | Phase 1b file:line | Phase 1b disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | src/neograph/_agent_spec_node_lowering.py:154-161 (_lower_generation_step fallback) | MIGRATE | Fallback now checks `node._remote_agent_endpoint is not None` at line 161 before falling through to ToolNode; reconstructs the RemoteAgent family via `_reconstruct_remote_agent()` (lines 189-229) instead of silently dropping the sidecar | yes -- confirmed by direct read of current source |

## Structural Guard

- File / Class: `tests/test_guards_agent_spec_llm_construction_sites.py::TestScriptedFallbackConsultsRemoteAgentSidecar` (new class, 4 tests)
- Mechanism: AST-based checker `_scripted_fallback_consults_sidecar()` walks `_lower_generation_step`'s source for an `if` test referencing `node._remote_agent_endpoint` that precedes/guards the `ToolNode(` fallback call
- Meta-tests: `test_real_source_consults_the_sidecar` (positive, real file), `test_negative_missing_sidecar_check_is_flagged` (negative -- synthetic fallback with no check), `test_negative_fallback_never_reached_is_flagged` (negative -- check present but fallback call absent, catches a differently-shaped regression), `test_positive_check_and_fallback_together_pass` (positive, synthetic minimal correct shape)
- Mutation-verified: temporarily removed the `if node._remote_agent_endpoint is not None:` branch from `_agent_spec_node_lowering.py` via Edit (not git) -- `test_real_source_consults_the_sidecar` failed as expected; restored via Edit, all 19 tests in the file pass again (confirmed identical to pre-mutation diff via `git diff`)
- Not regex-based (pure AST), so no regex-slip meta-test needed per the atom's own carve-out

## Quality gate note

Scoped verification (not full `make quality`): `tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py` + `tests/test_guards_agent_spec_llm_construction_sites.py` = 52/52 passed; ruff + mypy clean on all files this atom touched. A concurrent, unrelated in-flight atom (jtawq.9's write-test, actively editing `tests/test_guards_assembly.py` at the time of this atom's execution -- confirmed via `git diff --stat` showing 90 lines changed mid-edit) was contaminating full-suite `make quality` runs with 2 unrelated failures in `TestPortalDispatchRoutesThroughCanonicalGate` (jtawq.9's own target class, not touched by this fix). Those failures are NOT attributable to qtfof.5's fix or this sweep-verify atom. The epic-level finalize atom (neograph-zcjqo's 'Verify zero regressions vs baseline') will run the full gate once all concurrent work settles.
## E2E Verification (atom neograph-zcjqo.9)

Bug touches serialization/protocol behavior (Agent Spec RemoteAgent export/import round-trip), which per the atom's criteria would normally warrant E2E verification. However, there is no live external system in scope: RemoteAgent (A2AAgent/OciAgent) construction is pure typed-object construction against the REAL installed pyagentspec SDK classes (not mocked) -- agent_url/connection_config etc. are inert configuration data, no network call is made at construction time by either neograph or pyagentspec itself. The fix's tests (test_a2a_agent_endpoint_is_lost_on_reexport, test_oci_agent_endpoint_is_preserved_on_reexport, test_reexport_fails_loud_when_remote_agent_shape_has_drifted) already exercise the real pyagentspec SDK classes end-to-end for construction/validation -- this IS the closest available E2E verification for this bug's scope. No further live-system verification applies. E2E verification: SKIPPED WITH JUSTIFICATION (no live external system to reach; real-SDK-class construction already covered by fix tests).

title: @node registry Phase 3: enable strictness gate (_check_kwargs_against_shape) -- maintainer-gated
description:
Follow-up to neograph-jtawq.4 (closed after Phases 0-2 landed: Phase 0 pinning grid test, Phase 1 additive ModifierCombo-keyed registry, Phase 2 dispatch rewrite -- see docs/design/node-decorator-classify-dispatch-2026-08-04.md and neograph-jtawq.4's design field for the full refined plan and resolution log).

Phase 3 (originally 3b) is the ONE deliberately-deferred piece: enabling _check_kwargs_against_shape so a passed @node kwarg with no owning trigger raises ConstructError, instead of today's silent-accept. This is a REAL, user-visible strictness change (not zero-behavior-change like Phases 0-2), which is why the refined plan scoped it out of the main ticket's execute run.

## What Phase 3 does (from neograph-jtawq.4's design field)

- Add _check_kwargs_against_shape to src/neograph/_node_modifier_kwargs.py; call it from decorators.py for the FIRST time in this phase (it does not exist yet at all -- not added inert earlier).
- Compare each passed kwarg's value against inspect.signature(node).parameters[name].default (NOT is not None), so map_on_error='collect' (default 'raise', not None) is handled correctly.
- Newly-rejected inputs (today silently ignored, confirmed no test asserts success on these): max_iterations without loop_when; on_exhaust without loop_when/portal; map_on_error!=default without map_over; merge_model/merge_pre_process/merge_post_process/merge_fallback without an oracle trigger.
- should_fail fixtures per new pattern + should_pass twins; extend the Phase-0 grid (tests/test_guards_node_kwarg_grid.py) with dangling-satellite cases.

## MANDATORY before landing

rg piarch's constructs (piarch/src/derive_ensemble/constructs/) for the 4 dangling-satellite patterns above -- required, not optional. Either the gate comes back green (proving suite-neutrality) or it names the exact relying construct(s), which get listed and decided by the maintainer explicitly, never silently accommodated.

## Acceptance
- _check_kwargs_against_shape live and gated on; 4 new should_fail + should_pass fixture pairs; Phase-0 grid extended; piarch swept per the mandatory step above; ceiling bookkeeping on decorators.py/_node_modifier_kwargs.py re-verified with wc -l.
design:
## Core Invariant

A @node kwarg that cannot reach any modifier the derived ModifierCombo actually carries must fail loudly at decoration time and BEFORE any builder side effect fires -- and the set it is checked against must be DERIVED from _COMBO_MAP via the existing valid_kwargs(), never re-encoded as a second table of "which kwargs go with which shape".

## Implementation Plan

Guard-first. Every step reuses something that already exists; nothing here writes a new taxonomy.

1. **Red first: extend the grid with dangling-satellite cases** (tests/test_guards_node_kwarg_grid.py). Add a NEW parametrized test class alongside TestNodeKwargGrid -- do NOT widen TRIGGER_NAMES or ALL_SUBSETS (module-level `assert len(ALL_SUBSETS) == 32` at :90 pins the product). Parametrize the 4 unshadowed dangling patterns, each asserting `pytest.raises(ConstructError)`: `max_iterations=7` with no loop_when; `on_exhaust='last'` with neither loop_when nor portal; `map_on_error='collect'` with no map_over; each of merge_model / merge_pre_process / merge_post_process / merge_fallback with no oracle trigger. Derive the satellite->trigger ownership from MODIFIER_KWARGS rows rather than hand-listing, matching the file`s existing "expected outcome derived from _COMBO_MAP, never hand-listed" discipline. Run it, watch all cells FAIL (today they decorate successfully). Include one positive control asserting `map_on_error='raise'` on a bare node still succeeds -- that cell must be GREEN both before and after, and it is what pins the value-vs-default semantics.

2. **Add `_check_kwargs_against_shape` to src/neograph/_node_modifier_kwargs.py**, immediately after `valid_kwargs` (:312) so the reader meets the contract-computer and its one consumer together. Signature, resolving the circular-import constraint from the notes:

   ```
   def _check_kwargs_against_shape(
       kwargs: Mapping[str, Any], combo: ModifierCombo, *, node_label: str, defaults: Mapping[str, Any]
   ) -> None:
   ```

   Body: `passed = {k for k, v in kwargs.items() if v != defaults.get(k)}`; `invalid = passed - valid_kwargs(combo)`; on non-empty raise `ConstructError.build(f"kwarg(s) not valid for a {combo.name} node", node=node_label, found=", ".join(f"{k}=" for k in sorted(invalid)), hint=f"a {combo.name} node accepts: {sorted(valid_kwargs(combo) - IDENTITY_KWARGS)}")` -- the doc`s message shape (docs/design/node-decorator-classify-dispatch-2026-08-04.md:416-420), which is fine; only its passed-ness test was stale. Docstring must state (a) that value-vs-default supersedes the doc`s `is not None`, naming map_on_error as the only non-None default and therefore the only reason the distinction exists, and (b) that an explicitly-default value is indistinguishable from unset and stays accepted.

   `defaults` is a PARAMETER, not an internal `inspect.signature(node)` call: _node_modifier_kwargs cannot import decorators (decorators.py:99 imports it), and a function-local import would grow FUNCTION_LOCAL_IMPORT_ALLOWLIST, which tests/test_guards_sidecar_imports.py:58-60 forbids. If threading a mapping reads badly, the equivalent-and-also-acceptable variant is a keyword-only `signature_of: Callable` plus a module-level `@lru_cache` helper that does the inspect -- same no-cycle property, one line at the call site. Either way the defaults are DERIVED from the live signature; never a hand-written literal.

3. **Call it from decorators.py, exactly once, between :544 and :546** -- after `members = modifier_names_for_combo(combo)`, before `if "oracle" in members:`. Before-the-builds is required: _build_oracle_kwargs (_node_modifier_kwargs.py:116-133) fires a UserWarning and register_scripted, and a rejected node must not leave a shim behind. Pass `node` itself (or a cached default map derived from it) as the signature source -- resolved at call time from module globals, no cycle. Add the import to the existing `from neograph._node_modifier_kwargs import (...)` block at decorators.py:99. Re-run step 1`s test: green.

4. **Fixtures.** 4 new should_fail files in tests/check_fixtures/should_fail/, one defect each, ~15 lines, `# CHECK_ERROR:` regex on line 1 matching the gate`s message (copy the shape of should_fail/each_plus_loop_same_node.py): dangling_max_iterations.py, dangling_on_exhaust.py, dangling_map_on_error.py, dangling_merge_satellite.py. Use ONLY the 4 unshadowed patterns -- a fixture for `route=`/`max_hops=`/`map_key=` would assert the pre-existing pre-check message (decorators.py:265-310) and prove nothing about Phase 3.
