title: spec_types/loader: YAML NodeSpec/ConstructSpec has no 'portal' field -- Portal modifier unreachable from YAML pipelines
description:
Found during neograph-jtawq.4's architect-review refinement (2026-08-05). src/neograph/_spec_schema.py's NodeSpec (:76-94) and ConstructSpec (:97-115) declare oracle/each/loop/operator fields but NO portal field, and src/neograph/_spec_loader.py's _apply_modifiers (:237-268) has no 'if spec.portal is not None' arm to match. Confirmed via grep: zero hits for 'portal' anywhere in spec_types.py, and _spec_schema.py's two spec classes list only 4 of the 5 modifiers.

This means a YAML-defined pipeline (the declarative spec surface) cannot express a Portal mesh member at all today -- the only way to build a Portal-modified node is programmatically (Node|Portal(...)) or via @node(portal=...). Given Portal is a first-class modifier (ModifierCombo has PORTAL/PORTAL_OPERATOR entries, and the @node decorator, forward.py, and the Agent Spec import/export paths all support it), this is a real surface gap, not an intentional omission -- but it needs its own design pass (a PortalSpec schema shape, YAML wire format for to=/route=/max_hops=/on_exhaust=/trigger=, and the loader arm) rather than being folded into jtawq.4's decorator-only scope.

## Acceptance
- PortalSpec added to _spec_schema.py's NodeSpec/ConstructSpec
- _spec_loader.py's _apply_modifiers gets a portal arm
- should_pass/should_fail check fixtures + spec-loader tests covering a YAML-defined Portal mesh
design:
## Core Invariant

The YAML spec surface must be TOTAL over the modifier universe `_COMBO_MAP` defines, and a modifier reached through YAML must produce a `model_fields_set`-identical modifier instance to the programmatic `| Portal(...)` form -- because `_validation_portal.py:261-272` reads `model_fields_set` as behavioral input, so "which fields the author wrote" is semantics, not bookkeeping.

Clause 1 (field-name totality) is ratcheted by step 1. Clause 2 (`model_fields_set` parity) is ratcheted by step 2. Neither was ratcheted before this revision.

## Implementation Plan (revised per architect review, neograph-jn555.58, 2026-08-06)

Three of the four review findings were re-verified against current source during this refinement, and TWO of them turned out to rest on a factually wrong premise in the review itself. Those corrections are recorded inline below (finding 3) and in `neograph-t0ajj`. Read step 3 before quoting the old "LLM-mode nodes only" claim anywhere.

### 1. Guard first (TDD red) -- STRUCTURAL derivation, not intersection

Extend `tests/test_guards_modifier_composition_completeness.py::TestModifierKwargsRegistryIntegrity` with a sibling of `test_modifier_kwargs_row_names_equal_combo_map_modifier_universe` (:389).

Per review finding 1: do NOT derive the spec-side set as `set(NodeSpec.model_fields) & combo_map_universe`. An intersection is vacuous in the stray/stale direction -- a modifier dropped from `_COMBO_MAP` while its spec field lingers is intersected away and passes silently. The cited exemplar does not intersect; it derives `row_names` structurally.

Derive the spec-side set structurally instead. For each field on `NodeSpec` and on `ConstructSpec`, include its name iff the field's annotation is exactly `<Model> | None` where `<Model>` is a `BaseModel` subclass **defined in `_spec_schema.py` itself** (`Model.__module__ == NodeSpec.__module__`).

That predicate needs NO hand-typed exclusion list -- verified against current source:
- `llm_config: LlmConfig` is non-optional AND imported from `neograph._llm_config`, so it fails both halves.
- `ToolSpec` never appears as a bare field annotation, only inside `tools: list[str | ToolSpec]`, so it fails the shape test.

A hand-typed `exclude={"llm_config", "tools"}` would reintroduce the same duplicated-derivation disease this guard exists to prevent -- do not write one.

Assert the structurally-derived set EQUALS the live `_COMBO_MAP` key universe (`set().union(*_COMBO_MAP)`; the `frozenset()` BARE key contributes nothing). Assert it for BOTH classes. Field name to modifier key is identity today (`oracle`/`each`/`loop`/`operator` <-> `_COMBO_MAP` keys) -- assert that identity directly rather than introducing a mapping table.

Now a missing modifier block AND a stray/stale one both fail. Run it: must FAIL on `portal` missing from both classes.

### 2. Failing behavioral test + fixtures (still red), PLUS the model_fields_set parity ratchet

In `tests/test_spec_loader.py::TestLoadSpecModifiers` (:890) add `test_portal_mesh_from_spec`: a 2-member YAML mesh transliterated from `tests/check_fixtures/should_pass/portal_mesh_minimal.py` (entry with `portal: {to: [billing], max_hops: 6}`; peer with `inputs: {handoff: Handoff}` and `portal: {to: [triage]}`), loaded AND compiled AND run so the `Command(goto)` lowering is actually exercised.

Per review finding 2, in the SAME test additionally assert `model_fields_set` EQUALITY per member between each YAML-loaded `Portal` instance and the programmatic `Portal` built in `portal_mesh_minimal.py` (entry `{to, max_hops}`; peer `{to}`). One assert per member -- the cheap ratchet for Core Invariant clause 2. This matters because the plan adds a FOURTH independent hand-rolled encoding of the entry-only-knobs rule; the existing three are `_node_modifier_kwargs._build_portal_kwargs:187-206`, `forward.py:989-992`, and `loader.py:388-397`.

**Check fixtures must be spec-driven, and this is the first time that has been done.** Verified: `tests/test_check_fixtures.py` imports each fixture `.py` and scans `dir(mod)` for module-level `Construct` instances (`_try_compile`:137-140); ZERO existing fixtures call `load_spec` or mention YAML. So a fixture copied from `portal_mesh_minimal.py` would exercise the programmatic path and prove NOTHING about the YAML surface. Write each new fixture as an inline-YAML module instead:

```python
CONSTRUCT = load_spec(SPEC_YAML, project=PROJECT_YAML)   # module level
```

`load_spec(spec, project)` (`_spec_loader.py:39-66`) accepts YAML strings or dicts and returns a `Construct`, so the fixture is self-contained with no sidecar file. `_isolated_registries` clears `spec_types._type_registry` before exec, and `load_spec`'s own `load_project_types(project_dict)` repopulates it at exec time -- so passing `project=` is REQUIRED, not optional, for these fixtures.

Fixtures to add:
- `should_pass/spec_portal_mesh.py` -- the 2-member YAML mesh.
- `should_fail/spec_portal_max_hops_non_entry.py` -- `# CHECK_ERROR:` matching "entry-only". Raises at import (inside `load_spec` -> `Construct(...)` assembly), which the harness accepts.
- `should_pass/spec_portal_construct_member.py` -- the Construct-level mesh member, per finding 4 below.

### 3. Add PortalSpec to _spec_schema.py

Copy the `OracleSpec`/`LoopSpec` shape (`extra="forbid"`, field names IDENTICAL to `Portal`'s, same default as `Portal` wherever one exists). Cover both modes: peer (`to`, `route`, `trigger`, `max_hops`, `on_exhaust`, `name`) and dispatch (`spec_field`, `input_field`, `output`, `on_invalid`, `error_handler`, `max_depth`). `output` stays `str | None` -- `Portal` already resolves the string via `lookup_type` (`factory.py:795-797`, `state.py:270`). Add `portal: PortalSpec | None = None` to BOTH `NodeSpec` (:91-94) and `ConstructSpec` (:112-115).

Omit `scripted` and `conditions` (`dict[str, Callable]`, `_portal.py:73-74`).

**Finding 3, CORRECTED -- the review's premise was wrong, and so was the previous plan text.** Both the old notes ("clean, non-lossy restriction") and the review's counter-claim ("can only ever emit flows built from LLM-mode nodes") are false. Verified at `compiler.py:150-167`: both per-compile lookups seed INDEPENDENTLY of the kwargs --

- `scripted_lookup = _collect_scripted_shims(construct)` then `.update(_decoration_registry.scripted)`; the explicit `scripted=` kwarg merges LAST, so it WINS.
- `condition_lookup = dict(_decoration_registry.condition)`; `conditions=` merges on top.

So a YAML dispatch Portal's emitted flow still reaches every decoration-time registration (`@node` scripted shims, `@merge_fn`, inline `interrupt_when`, anything via `register_scripted` / `register_condition`). State the narrowing PRECISELY, in the plan and in the docs: a YAML Portal cannot supply a portal-LOCAL callable registry -- one that provides a callable not globally registered, or that OVERRIDES a global registration for just this portal's emitted flow. It is a real capability narrowing, fail-loud at the emitted flow's compile, not silent -- and it is much narrower than either earlier framing. Do not use the "non-lossy" wording, and do not repeat the "LLM-mode nodes only" wording either.

**Finding 3(c), evaluated and RESOLVED -- deferred to `neograph-t0ajj`.** The review proposed expressing `conditions:` as registered names "resolved through `parse_condition` -- the SAME registry `LoopSpec.when` already uses". That conflates two mechanisms: `conditions.py:95 parse_condition(expr)` is an EXPRESSION parser (`"score < 0.8"`), not a name registry, and the actual name registry is `_decoration_registry.condition`. Consequently option (a) `conditions: [registered_name, ...]` is VACUOUS -- `compile()` already seeds `condition_lookup` from that registry, so re-passing the names adds zero capability. Only option (b) `conditions: {name: "score < 0.8"}` (name -> expression, each parsed by `parse_condition`) is genuinely new. It is deferred OUT of this ticket, explicitly rather than silently, because: it is the only PortalSpec field that would not be a pure pass-through (breaking the step-4 property that buys `model_fields_set` parity by construction); its error mapping is undesigned (`parse_condition` raises a bare `ValueError`, unlike every other loader failure); and it is dispatch-mode-only while this ticket ships zero dispatch-mode YAML coverage, so it would ship untested -- the exact defect finding 4 objects to. `Portal.scripted` is not YAML-expressible under any option. Full analysis in `neograph-t0ajj`.

### 4. Add the arm to _spec_loader._apply_modifiers (:237-268)

Extend -- do not duplicate -- the one existing site. Forward EXACTLY the explicitly-written fields: iterate `spec.portal.model_fields_set` and pass those through by name, then `item = item | Portal(**kwargs)`. Field names are identical between `PortalSpec` and `Portal`, so this is a pure pass-through and gives field-for-field parity with the programmatic form BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a hand-maintained list -- and it is why unconditional default forwarding must be avoided (see Risks). Import `Portal` from `neograph.modifiers` alongside `Each`/`Loop`/`Operator`/`Oracle` (:28). Add NO loader-side validation: `Modifiable.__or__` delegates every duplicate/illegal-combo rejection to `ModifierSet.with_modifier`, and `Portal.model_post_init` enforces the peer-XOR-dispatch rules.

**Finding 4: `ConstructSpec.portal` must not ship with zero coverage.** Step 1's guard forces `portal:` onto `ConstructSpec`, so the sub-construct path gains a schema field regardless. It is materially different from the node path -- `_build_sub_construct:209-224` auto-wires sequential inputs, and a Construct mesh member has its own boundary I/O. Step 2's `should_pass/spec_portal_construct_member.py` covers it: a construct-level `portal:` block plus a node-level peer. Note the interaction that makes it work: `explicit_inputs` (:116-117, :209) makes any node with a declared `inputs:` skip the sequential auto-wiring, so declaring `inputs: {handoff: X}` is what keeps a sub-construct-level mesh from being clobbered.

### 5. Regenerate the committed JSON schema

Run `scripts/regen_schema.py` so `src/neograph/schemas/neograph-pipeline.schema.json` matches `Spec.model_json_schema()` byte-for-byte, or `tests/test_spec_loader.py:1296 test_pipeline_schema_in_sync` goes red. Same commit.

### 6. Update the docs to match the surface

Add a `#### Portal (dynamic handoff)` block to `website/src/content/docs/concepts/spec-format.mdx` next to the oracle/each/loop/operator sections (:94-126), showing the entry/peer split, the entry-only `max_hops`, and the `scripted`/`conditions` restriction **stated in the corrected form from step 3** (a YAML Portal cannot supply a portal-local callable registry that adds an unregistered callable or overrides a global one; globally registered scripted fns and conditions DO remain available to the emitted flow). Amend :152 to include `portal`. Run `npm run build` in `website/`. Add a CHANGELOG entry.

### 7. Gates

`uv run pytest` (bare), ruff, mypy -- i.e. `make quality`. Confirm step 1's guard (structural, not intersecting) and step 2's fixtures + `model_fields_set` parity asserts are GREEN. Re-run the `_COMBO_MAP`-consumer sweep BY GREP rather than trusting any list in this plan, per the 2026-07-27 Portal-rollout lesson.

## Recorded, NOT folded into this ticket

- `neograph-dgbqv.6` -- whether `model_fields_set`-as-semantics is itself the underlying defect. A `max_hops: int | None = None` sentinel with the default applied at READ time would collapse all four hand-rolled entry-only-knobs encodings into one and would survive a `model_dump`/`model_validate` round trip, which the current scheme does not. Do not attempt that redesign here.
- `neograph-t0ajj` -- exposing `Portal.conditions` as name -> expression on the YAML surface (finding 3c, evaluated above).

## Risks & Edge Cases

- **Unconditional default forwarding is the one way to get this wrong.** Any YAML mesh with >1 member fails assembly with "sets max_hops but it is entry-only" if `PortalSpec` defaults are forwarded. Write the multi-member `should_pass` fixture FIRST -- a single-member test passes either way and hides the bug.
- **Entry-member `inputs` divergence from the programmatic fixture.** `_build_node:171` falls back to `inputs = outputs` (single-type form) when `inputs:` is omitted, whereas `portal_mesh_minimal.py` leaves the entry's `inputs=None`. The single-type form skips fan-in validation and defers to a runtime isinstance scan, so it should behave, but the YAML mesh entry is NOT bit-identical to the Python fixture. Verify by compiling AND running, not just loading. Note this does not affect the step-2 parity assert, which compares the `Portal` modifier's `model_fields_set`, not the Node's `inputs`.
- **`to: []` terminal member.** `portal_construct_member.py` uses `Portal(to=[])` as the mesh terminal. An empty list is not None, so peer mode is still selected -- YAML `to: []` must round-trip. Worth one assert; a naive falsy check anywhere in the arm would silently drop the modifier.
- **`model_fields_set` does not survive a round trip.** Anything that `model_dump`s and re-validates a `PortalSpec` (or a `Portal`) loses the entry/peer distinction. Nothing in this plan does that, but do not introduce it -- it is the same defect `neograph-dgbqv.6` exists to question.
notes:
## Findings

**REUSE TARGET #1 -- the modifier arm shape already exists.** `_spec_loader.py:237 _apply_modifiers(item, spec)` is the ONE place all four existing modifiers are applied, for BOTH `NodeSpec` (via `_build_node`:186) and `ConstructSpec` (via `_build_sub_construct`:234). Adding Portal = one more `if spec.portal is not None:` arm + one `PortalSpec` model. There is NO second application site to keep in sync.

**REUSE TARGET #2 -- `Portal` needs NO new resolution machinery.** Every Portal field is already YAML-expressible as-is:
- `to`, `route`, `trigger`, `max_hops`, `on_exhaust`, `name`, `spec_field`, `input_field`, `on_invalid`, `error_handler`, `max_depth` are plain scalars/lists.
- `output` is ALREADY declared `type[BaseModel] | str | None` and the string form is resolved by `lookup_type` inside the runtime (`factory.py:795-797`, `state.py:270`) -- the SAME registry `_spec_loader` populates via `load_project_types`. So dispatch mode needs zero loader-side type resolution; pass the string through.
- ONLY `scripted` / `conditions` (`dict[str, Callable]`, `_portal.py:73-74`) are not YAML-expressible. They are optional (`= None`) and only feed `compile_construct(sub, scripted=..., conditions=...)` at `factory.py:868`, so omitting them from PortalSpec is a clean, non-lossy restriction (a YAML dispatch Portal emits flows that use only globally-registered building blocks).

**CRITICAL correctness rule -- conditional-include via `model_fields_set`.** `_validation_portal.py:261-272` enforces that `max_hops` / `on_exhaust` are ENTRY-ONLY, and it enforces it by reading `Portal.model_fields_set`. If the loader forwards PortalSpec defaults unconditionally, EVERY non-entry mesh member gets `max_hops` in its `model_fields_set` and every YAML mesh fails assembly. The codebase already has TWO precedents for exactly this:
- `_spec_loader.py:249-251` -- the oracle arm gates `merge_model` on `"merge_model" in spec.oracle.model_fields_set`.
- `_node_modifier_kwargs.py:187-206 _build_portal_kwargs` -- the @node builder, whose docstring states the invariant verbatim: conditional-include so `model_fields_set` matches the programmatic `| Portal(...)` form field-for-field, BECAUSE `_validation_portal` reads it.
The generalization that fits Portal.s 11 YAML-able fields without an 11-arm if-chain: forward exactly `spec.portal.model_fields_set` (Pydantic populates it only for keys the YAML author actually wrote). Field names are identical between PortalSpec and Portal, so it is a pure pass-through -- and it gives field-for-field parity with the programmatic form BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a hand-maintained list.

**Legality is inherited, not re-implemented.** `_apply_modifiers` composes with `|`, and `Modifiable.__or__` (`modifiers.py:329-335`) delegates every duplicate/illegal-combo rejection to `ModifierSet.with_modifier` -- the single legality gate collapsed in dcf0b4f. A YAML `portal:` + `each:` on one node therefore fails LOUD for free. Do NOT add loader-side pair validation. Arm ORDER within `_apply_modifiers` is also inert: `decorators.py:552-558` documents that ModifierSet uses typed slots, not an ordered list, so PORTAL_OPERATOR composes identically regardless of whether the portal arm precedes or follows the operator arm.

**Wire-format precedent for a declarative Portal already exists.** `loader.py:327-398 _reconstruct_swarm_mesh` builds a full peer mesh from a serialized (Agent Spec Swarm) form: entry = `nodes[0]`, `to=` peers per member, and the entry-only `max_hops`/`on_exhaust`/`route` read back from a marker and applied to `idx == 0` ONLY (`loader.py:388-397`). That is the exact semantic a YAML mesh must reproduce, and it confirms `pipeline.nodes` ORDER is what designates the entry.

**The YAML mesh needs no new wiring support.** `NodeSpec.inputs` already accepts the dict form (`str | dict[str,str] | None`, resolved at `_spec_loader.py:166-167`), so the reserved `handoff` input key is expressible today as `inputs: {handoff: Payload}`. `handoff_param`/`handoff_channel` are NOT set by the loader -- `_ir_normalize.py` is their sole writer, firing in `Construct.__init__` (same as `_reconstruct_swarm_mesh` relies on). Top-level `_build_construct` (:138-142) puts pipeline refs into one `Construct(nodes=[...])`, which IS the sibling-mesh shape. Inside a `ConstructSpec`, `explicit_inputs` (:116-117, :209) makes any node with a declared `inputs:` skip the sequential auto-wiring at :210-224 -- so declaring `inputs: {handoff: X}` is also what keeps a sub-construct-level mesh from being clobbered.

**Mandatory generated artifact.** `src/neograph/schemas/neograph-pipeline.schema.json` is asserted byte-for-byte against `Spec.model_json_schema()` by `tests/test_spec_loader.py:1296 test_pipeline_schema_in_sync`. Adding PortalSpec REQUIRES running `scripts/regen_schema.py` in the same commit or the gate goes red.

**The ratchet that should have caught this (anti-band-aid).** Nothing forces `_spec_schema` to be TOTAL over the modifier universe -- which is precisely why portal was omitted silently. The exemplar to copy is `tests/test_guards_modifier_composition_completeness.py:389 test_modifier_kwargs_row_names_equal_combo_map_modifier_universe`, which asserts `MODIFIER_KWARGS` row names == the union of `_COMBO_MAP` keys. The direct sibling guard -- NodeSpec/ConstructSpec modifier-block field names == that same universe -- makes a 6th modifier silently skipping the YAML surface structurally impossible. This is the CLAUDE.md "ONE shared table, every consumer reads it" rule applied to the spec surface, which the 2026-07-27 Portal-rollout lesson explicitly says must be re-verified by sweep rather than trusted from a list.

## Relevant Code

- `src/neograph/_spec_schema.py:27-64` -- OracleSpec/EachSpec/LoopSpec/OperatorSpec: the exemplar modifier-block models (all `extra="forbid"`, all field names IDENTICAL to the modifier class field names). PortalSpec copies this shape.
- `src/neograph/_spec_schema.py:91-94` and `:112-115` -- the two 4-of-5 modifier field blocks that must both gain `portal: PortalSpec | None = None`.
- `src/neograph/_spec_loader.py:237-268` -- `_apply_modifiers`: the single arm site. Line 249-251 is the `model_fields_set` conditional-include precedent to generalize.
- `src/neograph/_portal.py:33-172` -- Portal: field list (:61-77) and `model_post_init` (:108-172), which already enforces the peer-XOR-dispatch discrimination and every required/forbidden-knob rule. The loader adds NO validation of its own; a bad YAML combination raises ConfigurationError from here.
- `src/neograph/_validation_portal.py:261-272` -- the entry-only `max_hops`/`on_exhaust` check reading `model_fields_set`. THE reason unconditional forwarding breaks.
- `src/neograph/_node_modifier_kwargs.py:187-206` -- `_build_portal_kwargs`: the @node-side conditional-include builder, with the docstring stating the invariant.
- `src/neograph/loader.py:327-398` -- `_reconstruct_swarm_mesh`: declarative-form -> Portal mesh reconstruction; entry-only knobs applied at `idx == 0`.
- `tests/check_fixtures/should_pass/portal_mesh_minimal.py` -- the minimal legal mesh to transliterate into YAML (2 members, `Handoff(goto: str)` payload, entry has `max_hops=6`, peer declares `inputs={"handoff": Handoff}`).
- `tests/check_fixtures/should_pass/portal_construct_member.py` -- 3-member mesh incl. a Construct member and a terminal `Portal(to=[])`.
- `tests/test_spec_loader.py:890-994` -- `TestLoadSpecModifiers`: the per-modifier loader-test exemplar (each/operator/oracle) the portal test joins.
- `tests/test_spec_loader.py:1296-1314` -- `test_pipeline_schema_in_sync`: forces `scripts/regen_schema.py`.
- `tests/test_guards_modifier_composition_completeness.py:389-404` -- the totality-guard exemplar to copy for the spec surface.
- `website/src/content/docs/concepts/spec-format.mdx:152` -- "Sub-constructs support the same modifier blocks as nodes: `oracle`, `each`, `loop`, `operator`" -- the doc sentence that must gain `portal`, plus a new modifier section alongside :94/:107/:115/:126.

## Risks & Edge Cases

- **Unconditional default forwarding is the one way to get this wrong.** Any YAML mesh with >1 member fails at assembly with "sets max_hops but it is entry-only" if PortalSpec defaults are forwarded. Write the multi-member should_pass fixture FIRST -- a single-member test would pass either way and hide the bug.
- **Entry-member `inputs` divergence from the programmatic fixture.** `_build_node`:171 falls back to `inputs = outputs` (single-type form) when `inputs:` is omitted, whereas `portal_mesh_minimal.py` leaves the entry.s `inputs=None`. The single-type form skips fan-in validation and defers to a runtime isinstance scan, so it should behave, but the YAML mesh entry is NOT bit-identical to the Python fixture. Verify by compiling AND running the YAML mesh, not just loading it.
- **`to: []` terminal member.** `portal_construct_member.py` uses `Portal(to=[])` as the mesh terminal. An empty list is not None, so peer mode is still selected -- YAML `to: []` must round-trip. Worth one fixture/assert; a naive falsy check anywhere in the arm would silently drop the modifier.
- **Dispatch mode (`route: decide`) scope.** It IS expressible in YAML except `scripted`/`conditions`. Restricting PortalSpec to peer mode only would re-create the exact "partial surface" disease this ticket exists to remove, so the recommendation is to declare both modes and let `Portal.model_post_init` police the XOR. If the reviewer disagrees, the fallback is peer-only PLUS an explicit `extra="forbid"` rejection message naming dispatch as unsupported -- never a silent omission.
- **`PortalSpec.name` vs `NodeSpec.name`.** Portal.s mesh-group field is `name` (`_portal.py:67`). Inside the nested `portal:` block there is no ambiguity, and exact field-name parity is the invariant every sibling spec model holds -- so keep `name`, do not rename to `group`.
- **Docs contradiction (non-blocking).** `spec-format.mdx:6` already claims the spec expresses "the full topology -- nodes, modes, modifiers, wiring", which is false today for Portal. The doc over-claims rather than contradicting the code.s intent, so implementing the feature resolves it; no user input needed.
- **Sub-construct-level mesh is a second-order case.** `_build_sub_construct`:210-224 auto-wires sequential `inputs` for any member lacking an explicit `inputs:`, which would clobber a mesh nested INSIDE a ConstructSpec. Declaring `inputs: {handoff: X}` on each member opts out via `explicit_inputs`. Do not extend the auto-wiring to be Portal-aware -- that would be a band-aid; the explicit-inputs escape hatch already exists and is the documented mechanism.
- **File-size ratchet is not a concern.** `_spec_schema.py` is 140 lines and `_spec_loader.py` is 268 -- both far under the 500 cap; neither is in the ALLOWLIST and neither will approach it.
## Codebase Disease Scan (2j208)

title: Agent Spec export has TWO FlowNode construction sites, not one: _lower_oracle builds one inline outside _lower_item_body
description:
Found by the architect review of neograph-s7zt3.11 (Phase 8), 2026-07-31, verified against develop @ 51b7b6e. EXPORT-side, so out of scope for Phase 8 under the 2026-07-31 import-only scope decision.

THE FACT: it is widely asserted in this codebase's tickets and notes -- including neograph-s7zt3.11's own research findings and its Core Invariant wording -- that the Agent Spec EXPORT side absorbs the Node-vs-Construct difference in exactly ONE seam, _lower_item_body. That is NOT true. There are two FlowNode construction sites:

  src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:141  _lower_item_body                      (the seam everyone cites)
  src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:199  _lower_oracle, Construct-variant arm  (inline: FlowNode(name=variant_name, subflow=to_agent_spec(node)))

The second exists because an Oracle variant needs a DISTINCT name per variant, which the shared seam does not parameterize.

WHY IT MATTERS beyond tidiness: the single-export-seam claim is load-bearing in two places that are about to be written. Phase 8 plans an import-side guard phrased as mirroring the single export-side body seam -- a guard asserting a property of a mirror that the original does not have. And the Theme 2 dispatch redesign (neograph-jtawq.2) is meant to use the export/import asymmetry as its motivating example. Both need the accurate picture.

SCOPE: decide whether _lower_oracle:199 should route through _lower_item_body with the name parameterized, or whether a per-variant distinct name is a genuine second case that deserves to stay separate and be DOCUMENTED as such. Either outcome is acceptable; what is not acceptable is leaving the codebase asserting one seam while having two.

Fix the inaccurate claims wherever they appear once decided (the Core Invariant wording in neograph-s7zt3.11, and any guard docstring that repeats it).
notes:
## DECISION (2026-07-31): YES collapse it -- but NOT in Phase 8. Verified approach below.

The maintainer asked directly whether we remove this duplication or not, and why. Answering with a probe rather than an opinion.

### Is it collapsible? YES -- verified

The two sites differ ONLY in name and metadata:
  _lower_item_body:141   FlowNode(name=item.name,    subflow=to_agent_spec(item))
  _lower_oracle:199      FlowNode(name=variant_name, subflow=to_agent_spec(node), metadata=variant_metadata)

_lower_oracle cannot simply CALL the seam wholesale, because for a Node it must go to
_lower_generation_step (per-variant model tier), not _lower_node -- so the seam's own
Node/Construct dispatch is already resolved by the caller and the seam's Node branch is
wrong for it. But inside the Construct arm the collapse works. Probed:

  body = _lower_item_body(sub)          -> FlowNode name=sub subflow=Flow
  body.model_copy(update={'name': 'sub__variant_0', 'metadata': {...}})
                                        -> FlowNode name=sub__variant_0, metadata applied

### THE TRAP -- this is why it is not a one-liner

model_copy SHARES the subflow object (probe: subflow_same_obj = True). The current inline
code calls to_agent_spec(node) FRESH on every loop iteration, so the export emits N
DISTINCT sub-Flow objects, one per variant. Phase 7's landed pattern is explicitly 'N
FlowNodes wrapping FRESH to_agent_spec() calls'. A naive hoist-once-then-copy would emit
ONE shared Flow referenced N times -- different component identity in the exported spec.
That is a BEHAVIOUR change wearing a refactor's clothing, exactly what the file-split
procedure's refusal 2 forbids.

CORRECT SHAPE: call _lower_item_body(node) INSIDE the loop (fresh subflow each iteration)
and model_copy only to stamp name/metadata. Cost is one extra model_copy per variant.

### Why NOT in Phase 8 (neograph-s7zt3.11)

1. Export is OUT of Phase 8's scope by the maintainer's 2026-07-31 decision. This is
   export-side.
2. Phase 8 already absorbed one scope addition -- the HIGH-1 boundary restoration -- which
   was justified because it is a defect IN the seam being built and would be replicated
   fivefold. This is neither: it is a thin, currently-correct duplication that harms
   nothing today.
3. It is not test-free. The freshness caveat above means it needs a test proving N
   DISTINCT subflows are still emitted, so it cannot ride the existing suite unchanged.

### What Phase 8 DOES owe, and is already carrying

Phase 8 must not repeat the false one-seam claim. Its rewritten Core Invariant and its
step 9 guard docstring both now state the export side has TWO sites. That obligation is
discharged regardless of whether this ticket is ever done.

### Residual risk if this is never done

Low but real: a change to how a Construct body lowers (a new FlowNode field, a change to
the subflow export) must be applied at both sites or they drift. Cheap mitigation if the
collapse is deferred indefinitely -- a structural guard that every FlowNode( construction
in _agent_spec.py passes subflow=to_agent_spec(...), which pins the shape without forcing
the merge.

title: ModifierSet: three encodings of pair legality collapse to one gate function (_validate_slot_set)
description:
CONFIRMED 2026-08-05 per docs/design/agent-spec-target-architecture-2026-08-03.md (Pillar A2,
ticket-ground-truth table): this is the ONE jtawq theme whose original 2026-07-29 diagnosis still
matches current code almost exactly -- re-verify line numbers with a fresh grep before starting (the
audit's own citations are already a few lines off in places, e.g. the ":694-696 'ONE row'" comment
claim), but the shape of the problem is real and unchanged.

THREE independent encodings of "which modifier pairs are legal" exist in modifiers.py today, kept in
sync only by a code comment admitting the hazard (:802-806):
1. `_SLOT_RULES` (excludes list, :727-754)
2. FIVE hand-coded `model_post_init` arms (:791-812) -- exist because Pydantic's `model_copy` SKIPS
   `model_post_init` (:856-860), so direct construction and the `with_modifier`/pipe path need
   separately-maintained enforcement
3. The Portal(is_dispatch)+Operator dynamic rule, duplicated VERBATIM at :818-822 and :857-865

Plus 5 additional hand-written per-slot enumerations, including BOTH `classify_modifiers` code paths
(:181-191, :199-215). The "Unknown modifier type" expected-list (:838) is stale -- it omits Portal.

THE FIX: extract a module-level `_validate_slot_set(slots) -> None`: present-name frozenset in
`_COMBO_MAP` -> pass; else raise the pair-specific `ConstructError` from a new `_CONFLICT_DIAGNOSTICS`
table (never a raw `KeyError`); then run `_DYNAMIC_RULES` (the Portal.is_dispatch+Operator instance-
dependent check, which correctly CANNOT be a static table entry -- it depends on Portal's `route`
VALUE, not just modifier presence). `model_post_init`'s five arms + the duplicated dynamic rule
collapse to ONE call. `with_modifier` KEEPS `model_copy` (do not route it through the constructor --
verified this would flip pipe-path rejections from `ConstructError` to Pydantic `ValidationError`, a
real behavior change, refused) but calls `_validate_slot_set(prospective_slots)` first, preserving the
pipe-path's `ConstructError` shape exactly. `_SlotRule.excludes` is deleted; the field set, `combo`'s
has-set, `to_list`, BOTH `classify_modifiers` paths, and the stale "Unknown modifier type" list all
derive from one roster instead of being separately hand-maintained.

Canonical error phrasing = the already-pinned direct-construction-path order ("Cannot combine Portal
and X", tests/modifiers/test_portal.py:222-230) -- breakage shrinks to docstring updates in
test_portal.py, test_portal_operator_approval.py:17-20, test_forward_parity.py:836, and the
fusion-guard rationale prose.

NEW GUARD (G-SLOT, 4 assertions, doc Sec 6): (i) totality -- every 2-subset of roster slot names is in
_COMBO_MAP union dom(_CONFLICT_DIAGNOSTICS), domains disjoint; (ii) AST ban on 'Cannot combine'
string literals outside the tables; (iii) ModifierSet field names == roster; (iv) both
classify_modifiers paths + to_list iterate the roster. Extends (does not contradict)
TestNoRedundantValidation (test_guards_assembly.py:1423) -- that guard's "ModifierSet only" rule
strengthens to "_validate_slot_set only".

Full detail and the conflict-resolution reasoning (why NOT to route direct construction through
with_modifier for symmetry) is in the design doc.
design:
## Core Invariant

Which modifier sets are legal — and *why* an illegal one is illegal — is decided in exactly
ONE function (`_validate_slot_set`, reading `_COMBO_MAP` + `_CONFLICT_DIAGNOSTICS` +
`_DYNAMIC_RULES`), which BOTH construction paths call; neither path's exception shape changes
(direct construction stays `ValidationError`-wrapped, the pipe path stays bare
`ConstructError`), because a pure-refactor is never allowed to become a behavior change.

## Implementation Plan

1. **Shrink the existing roster, don't build a new one.** Delete `_SlotRule.excludes` and the
   `excludes` tuples from all five `_SLOT_RULES` rows (modifiers.py:681-754), leaving
   `(mod_type, slot, label)`. Delete `_km_conflict` (:718-724) — canonicalization makes the
   "whichever landed second" trick obsolete. Keep the field name `mod_type`
   (`tests/test_forward_parity.py:851` reads it). Keep row ORDER each/oracle/loop/operator/
   portal — `to_list` derives from it and its order is observable.

2. **Build `_CONFLICT_DIAGNOSTICS: dict[frozenset[str], tuple[str, str]]`** (message, hint),
   module-level, immediately after `_SLOT_RULES`. Exactly five entries, reusing the existing
   message/hint constants verbatim so the pinned phrasings survive byte-for-byte:
   `{each,loop}` → `_EACH_LOOP_CONFLICT`; `{oracle,loop}` → `_ORACLE_LOOP_CONFLICT`;
   `{portal,each}`/`{portal,oracle}`/`{portal,loop}` → the "Cannot combine Portal and X on the
   same item" + `_PORTAL_HINT` strings currently inline at :749-751. These five plus
   `_COMBO_MAP`'s five legal pairs are exactly the 10 = C(5,2) 2-subsets (G-SLOT(i) totality).

3. **Build `_DYNAMIC_RULES`** as a tuple of `(predicate, message, hint)` triples — data, not
   raising callables, so the literals stay inside a table for G-SLOT(ii). One row today:
   `lambda slots: slots["portal"] is not None and slots["operator"] is not None and
   slots["portal"].is_dispatch` → the existing "Cannot combine Portal (dispatch mode) and
   Operator on the same item" + its hint, verbatim (the `match="dispatch mode"` assertions at
   `tests/modifiers/test_portal.py:180,:188` depend on this). Predicate reads
   `Portal.is_dispatch` — never an inline `route == "decide"` (banned by
   `test_guards_assembly.py:179-190`).

4. **Extract `_validate_slot_set(slots: Mapping[str, Modifier | None]) -> None`**, module-level,
   after the two tables. Body: build `present = frozenset(name for name, v in slots.items() if
   v is not None)`; if `present in _COMBO_MAP`, skip to step (c). Else (a) look for the first
   2-subset of `present` in `_CONFLICT_DIAGNOSTICS` and raise
   `ConstructError.build(message, hint=hint)` — this makes 3+-modifier supersets report the
   pair that actually explains them; (b) if no pair explains it, raise a generic
   `ConstructError.build("Invalid modifier combination", found=str(sorted(present)), ...)` —
   NEVER a KeyError. (c) run `_DYNAMIC_RULES` in order, raising the first triple whose
   predicate is True.

5. **`model_post_init` collapses to one call** (modifiers.py:789-822): replace all five arms
   plus the dynamic rule with
   `_validate_slot_set({r.slot: getattr(self, r.slot) for r in _SLOT_RULES})`. Pydantic keeps
   wrapping the raise in `ValidationError` — that is the established, tested convention
   (`tests/modifiers/test_portal.py:213-219`), preserved deliberately.

6. **`with_modifier` keeps `model_copy`** (:824-866). Order: (a) roster lookup by
   `isinstance(mod, r.mod_type)` — unchanged; (b) unknown-type raise, with `expected=` now
   derived as `", ".join(r.label for r in _SLOT_RULES)` (fixes the stale :839 list that omits
   Portal); (c) the duplicate-slot arm — unchanged, it cannot move into the gate (a name-set
   loses slot occupancy); (d) NEW: build `prospective = {r.slot: getattr(self, r.slot) for r in
   _SLOT_RULES} | {rule.slot: mod}` and call `_validate_slot_set(prospective)`; (e)
   `model_copy`. Delete the excludes loop (:852-854) and the duplicated dynamic rule
   (:857-865). The pipe path still raises bare `ConstructError` — verified: routing it through
   the constructor instead would flip it to `ValidationError`, and is REFUSED.

7. **Derive the five (really seven) enumerations from the roster**, all inside modifiers.py:
   `ModifierSet.combo`'s has-set (:776-787); `to_list` (:868-881); `classify_modifiers`
   fast path (:181-191) and fallback path (:199-215, keyed by `get_mod(r.mod_type)`);
   the unknown-type `expected=` list (step 6b); and — beyond the ticket's named five, same
   disease, same file — `Modifiable.has_modifier` (:414-426) and `get_modifier` (:428-440).
   Those last two compare by IDENTITY, so derive as `r.mod_type is modifier_type`, not
   `isinstance`, to preserve semantics exactly. Do NOT touch `_COMBO_MAP`'s own literal
   (`TestComboMapMonopoly` counts it).

8. **Write G-SLOT failing-first**, new file `tests/test_guards_slot_set.py` (the doc allows a
   `test_guards_assembly` extension, but that file is already ~1500 lines and a fresh file
   keeps the four assertions discoverable). (i) totality: every 2-subset of
   `{r.slot for r in _SLOT_RULES}` is in `_COMBO_MAP` ∪ `dom(_CONFLICT_DIAGNOSTICS)`, and the
   two domains are disjoint; (ii) AST ban on the literal `Cannot combine` in `src/neograph/`
   outside the two table assignments — copy the `_decide_literal_comparisons` structure at
   `tests/test_guards_assembly.py:165-205`, with the f-string-aware `_string_fragments` helper
   from `tests/test_guards_function_local_imports.py:487-500`, plus positive and
   docstring-negative slip meta-tests; (iii) `set(ModifierSet.model_fields) == roster slots`,
   AND `{row.name for row in MODIFIER_KWARGS} == roster slots` (pins the seventh enumeration
   in `_node_modifier_kwargs.py:236-267` without merging it — it lives on a different axis);
   (iv) both `classify_modifiers` paths and `to_list` iterate `_SLOT_RULES` (AST: the function
   body references the roster name and contains no per-slot attribute chain).

9. **Amend `TestNoRedundantValidation`'s docstring** (`tests/test_guards_assembly.py:1423-1429`):
   "ModifierSet.model_post_init is the structural gate" → "`_validate_slot_set` is the
   structural gate; `model_post_init` and `with_modifier` are its two thin callers." Extends,
   does not contradict — no assertion changes.

10. **Update the four affected docstrings only** (no assertion edits are needed — verified by
    grep that no test matches on "... and Portal"): `tests/modifiers/test_portal.py` :6-10,
    :130, :208-211 (the "pipe path reads `_SLOT_RULES` excludes / direct path uses hard-coded
    pairwise checks" prose is now false — both call one gate);
    `tests/test_portal_operator_approval.py:17-20`; `tests/test_forward_parity.py:836`; and the
    fusion-guard rationale prose. Then re-derive `wc -l src/neograph/modifiers.py` and lower
    `tests/test_guards_file_size.py:84`'s exact ceiling in the SAME commit.

**Anti-band-aid clause.** If any step forces a widening — a new entry in
`FUNCTION_LOCAL_IMPORT_ALLOWLIST`, a carve-out in G-SLOT(ii), a `.get()` fail-soft on
`_COMBO_MAP`, or a `# type: ignore` — the step is wrong as scoped. Take the smaller change and
report it rather than buying the collapse with a loosened ratchet. In particular: do NOT
unify the two exception shapes, and do NOT route `with_modifier` through the constructor.
notes:
## Findings (research atom yf2ar.18, 2026-08-05 — fresh grep against develop, modifiers.py = 881 lines)

**Diagnosis re-verified, citations accurate.** Unlike the ticket's caveat, every line
citation in the 2026-07-29 audit checks out against today's file: `_SLOT_RULES` :727-754,
`model_post_init` arms :791-812, dynamic rule duplicated :818-822 + :857-865, `model_copy`
:856-860, `classify_modifiers` paths :181-191 / :199-215, stale "Unknown modifier type"
expected-list :839 (says "Each, Oracle, Loop, or Operator" — omits Portal), and the
":694-696 ONE row" comment claim is exactly at :694-696. Nothing to re-scope.

**Three empirical verifications (run, not assumed) — all three confirm the design doc:**
1. `ModifierSet(each=Each(...)).model_copy(update={"loop": Loop(...)})` returns an ILLEGAL
   set with no error. `model_copy` really does skip `model_post_init`. This is WHY parity
   needs a shared function rather than one gate.
2. Direct `ModifierSet(each=..., loop=...)` raises pydantic `ValidationError`
   (`isinstance(e, ConstructError)` is **False**); `with_modifier` raises `ConstructError`
   (True). Routing the pipe path through the constructor for "symmetry" is a REAL behavior
   change — the doc's refusal (Conflict 1/6) is correct and must be honored.
3. **Pipe-path phrasing is order-dependent today**: `| Portal() | Each()` →
   "Cannot combine Each and Portal on the same item"; `| Each() | Portal()` →
   "Cannot combine Portal and Each on the same item". Canonicalizing to the direct-path

title: node() decorator: replace the 5-branch flat-kwarg dispatch with a ModifierCombo-keyed registry (design complete, ready for /execute)
description:
FULLY DESIGNED as of 2026-08-04 -- see docs/design/node-decorator-classify-dispatch-2026-08-04.md
(three rounds of adversarial verification within the same session; every citation spot-checked
against the working tree by the maintainer independently, not just accepted from the design pass).
This description supersedes the stale 2026-07-29 framing below the line (kept for history; the file's
line numbers there predate the 3ffdg split wave and no longer resolve).

CURRENT VERIFIED STATE (2026-08-04): node() has 32 parameters (confirmed by AST parse, not estimate).
decorators.py is 671 lines (its exact ceiling in tests/test_guards_file_size.py:79). The decorator(f)
closure (:242-637, ~396 lines) applies modifier sugar via 5 ad hoc if/elif branches (:490-618) that
each test raw kwargs directly and pipe a modifier inline -- no shared classification, no declared
per-shape contract. Confirmed: Operator composes orthogonally with everything (its branch is a bare
`if`, not `elif`); Oracle+Loop and Oracle+Portal are NOT rejected at the top of the function today and
fall through to the pipe layer's ConstructError one layer down (loud, not silent, but message-
inconsistent vs the four pairs that ARE rejected with kwarg-named errors at decoration time).

THE DESIGN (full detail in the doc; summary here so the ticket is self-contained):

1. A registry keyed by the EXISTING `ModifierCombo` enum (modifiers.py) -- explicitly NOT a second,
   decorator-local taxonomy of "node kinds" (that would reintroduce the exact disease
   docs/design/modifier-combo-single-source-of-truth-2026-07-27.md diagnosed). 5 new rows
   (`MODIFIER_KWARGS`, one per modifier: which of the 32 kwargs trigger/configure it) derive the
   12 shapes' legal-kwarg contracts through `modifier_names_for_combo` -- the sanctioned membership
   reader, re-stating nothing `_COMBO_MAP` already owns.
2. `derive_combo(kwargs)` computes which modifier names the kwargs imply, then reads `_COMBO_MAP`
   (the one validity authority) via `combo_for_modifier_names`.
3. `_check_kwargs_against_shape` validates every passed kwarg belongs to the derived shape's declared
   contract -- new, strictly stronger validation than today (see "behavior changes" below).
4. BUILD step -- this went through two real design iterations, both maintainer-driven:
   - First iteration copied compiler.py's `match COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[combo].primary:` dispatch
     shape. REJECTED on re-examination: compiler.py is choosing ONE graph-topology algorithm
     (genuinely mutually exclusive), the decorator is piping COMPOSABLE modifier objects (genuinely
     not mutually exclusive -- EACH_ORACLE is two modifiers at once). Copying that shape forced an
     artificial mutual-exclusivity assumption and required carving Each+Oracle fusion out as a
     special pre-match case -- a shape that does NOT generalize to any future multi-modifier
     combination without another hand-written carve-out.
   - FINAL shape: five independent, unconditional membership checks against the SAME `members`
     value already validated in step 3 (`if "oracle" in members: n = _build_oracle_node(...)`, etc.,
     fixed order oracle/each/operator/loop/portal reproducing today's exact pipe sequence). Reads as
     a narrative ("this shape -> this specific named modification") per the maintainer's explicit
     ask, AND composes correctly for arbitrary future multi-modifier combos with ZERO new code
     beyond one `if "x" in members:` line -- no carve-out, ever.
5. Because the applied set and the validated set are now the SAME value, the original design's
   runtime `_assert_shape_applied` safety net is PROVABLY REDUNDANT (argued, not asserted, in the
   doc's Sec 5) and dropped -- not kept as defensive padding.
6. Naming: legal/illegal -> valid/invalid throughout (maintainer correction: not this codebase's or
   the field's vocabulary). "Arm" -> "branch" throughout (maintainer correction: software
   architecture doc, not an anatomical one).
7. Layering: registry lives in `_node_modifier_kwargs.py` (decorator layer), NOT `modifiers.py` --
   4 concrete reasons in the doc (AGENTS.md's explicit layer-discipline rule naming modifiers.py as
   off-limits for @node features; the IR-side "abstract roles" already exist as the modifier
   classes' own Pydantic fields; the import direction already runs decorator->IR, matching
   compiler.py's own consumption of the same names; modifiers.py is already at its file-size
   ceiling).
8. Reuse audit (maintainer asked explicitly): `is_each_oracle_fused` has nothing to share with this
   design -- its docstring states it exists for a consumer standing inside a COLLAPSED
   `PrimaryShape.EACH` match branch (compiler.py's shape), a question that doesn't arise once fusion
   is just two independent checks both firing. No third combo-validity error path exists to unify
   (grepped: only modifiers.py has that wording) -- the 3 remaining differently-worded messages
   (pipe-layer/classifier/decorator) differ in vocabulary ON PURPOSE, each naming what its own
   surface saw; homogenizing would erase real information for zero deduplication of already-
   centralized validity logic. `classify_modifiers` is already the natural external-audit mechanism
   with no new code needed (an existing test, tests/decorator/test_fanout_oracle.py:1191, already
   audits decorator output exactly this way).
9. VALUE-THREADING GAP FOUND (maintainer's own catch, verified real, not hypothetical): today's
   suite verifies modifier COMPOSITION (was Each/Oracle/Loop/Portal attached) but for Loop and
   Portal specifically, NEVER verifies that a passed kwarg VALUE actually reached the built modifier
   instance. Census (2026-08-04): Each has over/key asserted (map_on_error never); Oracle has
   models/n/merge_fn asserted ONCE in a body-as-merge edge case (ensemble_n->n, merge_model, the
   three hooks never); Operator has `when` asserted; Loop has ZERO value assertions anywhere on any
   surface (test_edge_cases.py:160-168 passes max_iterations=5 and asserts only has_modifier(Loop));
   Portal has ZERO assertions on the @node path (test_portal.py:105-110 only tests the programmatic
   Portal(...) constructor directly, never the portal= kwarg sugar). The new grid test (below) closes
   this by asserting value fidelity for every one of its 32 cases, not just modifier presence.

STRICTNESS IS NOT ZERO-BEHAVIOR-CHANGE, NAMED EXPLICITLY (Sec 4 of the doc): today several invalid
kwarg combinations are silently accepted and the value evaporates (`max_iterations` without
`loop_when`; `on_exhaust` without an owning trigger; `map_on_error='collect'` without `map_over`;
4 Oracle satellite kwargs without an Oracle trigger). Under the design these become decoration-time
ConstructErrors naming the kwarg and the shape -- a real, isolated, separately-gated behavior change
(Phase 3b), not smuggled into the zero-behavior-change phases (0-2).

NEW STRUCTURAL GUARDS (all failing-first, full spec in doc Sec 6):
- tests/test_guards_node_kwarg_grid.py -- NEW. Enumerates all 2^5=32 kwarg-trigger subsets, expected
  outcome derived from _COMBO_MAP (never hand-listed), asserting BOTH which modifiers attach AND
  that specific passed values (max_iterations, ensemble_n, etc.) actually landed on the built
  instances. This is the test that would have caught neograph-s7zt3.10 before it shipped, plus the
  value-threading gap above. Lands in Phase 0 against the CURRENT code (must pass); non-vacuity
  proven by Edit-mutation (reinsert the old early return, watch it fail; revert).
- tests/test_guards_modifier_composition_completeness.py RULE 1 -- EVOLVES (same commit as the
  branch rewrite) to scan apply_node_sugar's new shape: exactly one return; every membership check
  reads `"<name>" in members` (never a re-derived raw-kwarg condition); every declared modifier name
  is checked. RULE 2 (_agent_spec.py) is untouched -- correct there because export lowering
  genuinely dispatches on shape, unlike the decorator.
- Registry integrity guards (same file): _COMBO_MAP round-trip bijectivity; MODIFIER_KWARGS
  row/universe totality; the anti-flat-explosion ratchet (every node() kwarg must appear in exactly
  one row's triggers/satellites or IDENTITY_KWARGS, so a 33rd kwarg added without declaring its
  owning shape fails CI); field_map honesty (every renamed field is real on the modifier class).

PHASED BUILD PLAN (each phase separately shippable, guard-first -- full detail in doc Sec 7):
Phase 0 (pin current behavior via the new grid test, no src change) -> Phase 1 (registry, additive,
zero-behavior-change) -> Phase 2 (dispatch rewrite, zero-behavior-change, collapses 5 sidecar
re-registration sites to 1) -> Phase 3a (complete the kwarg-named vocabulary for the 2 currently-
inconsistent pairs, message re-sourcing only) -> Phase 3b (enable the new strictness, maintainer-
gated, grep piarch's constructs for reliance on today's leniency first).

REFUSAL-CRITERIA CHECK (doc Sec 8): no capability monopoly widened (G1/G3 untouched); modifiers.py
untouched (all @node vocabulary stays in the decorator layer per AGENTS.md); no second taxonomy
introduced; every behavior change is enumerated, phase-isolated, and gated.

STATUS: design complete and twice re-verified by independent citation spot-checks (line numbers,
function names, test file contents all confirmed against the working tree, not merely accepted).
Ready for /execute. No further design work identified as of 2026-08-04.
design:
## Core Invariant

The valid @node kwarg contract for any modifier shape is DERIVED from ModifierCombo/_COMBO_MAP (the one existing IR-layer validity/composition authority), never re-guessed post-hoc from which kwargs happened to be non-None and never re-encoded as a second decorator-local taxonomy -- so the set of modifiers VALIDATED and the set of modifiers APPLIED are provably the same value, making the s7zt3.10 silent-drop bug class structurally unrepresentable rather than merely re-guarded.

## Implementation Plan (REFINED 2026-08-05, atom neograph-hy268.12, resolves the architect review's 5 MEDIUM + 4 LOW findings — see notes for the finding-by-finding resolution log)

Re-verified against the live tree. 4 phases now (3a folded into Phase 2 — see Finding 5 resolution). Full original rationale/rejected-alternatives: docs/design/node-decorator-classify-dispatch-2026-08-04.md — this plan supersedes that doc's Sec 7 phasing where they conflict.

### Phase 0 -- pin current behavior, no src change (UNCHANGED from original plan)

Add tests/test_guards_node_kwarg_grid.py: enumerate all 2^5=32 subsets of the five modifier-trigger kwarg groups, expected outcome derived from _COMBO_MAP (never hand-listed), asserting BOTH which modifiers attach AND that specific passed kwarg VALUES actually landed on the built modifier instances. Must pass against decorators.py's CURRENT 6-branch chain as-is. Non-vacuity proof: Edit-mutation (reinsert old early-return, watch {each,operator} fail; drop max_iterations from loop kwargs, watch {loop} fail; revert both). Commit.

### Phase 1 -- registry, additive, ZERO decorators.py line-count change (REVISED: Finding 1 + Finding 6/LOW)

In src/neograph/_node_modifier_kwargs.py: add ModifierKwargs NamedTuple, the 5-row MODIFIER_KWARGS tuple, IDENTITY_KWARGS, valid_kwargs(combo), derive_combo(kwargs). Anti-flat-explosion ratchet wording corrected to match doc Sec 6.3.3: every node() kwarg (via inspect.signature(node), excluding fn) appears in >=1 row's triggers/satellites or IDENTITY_KWARGS -- NOT 'exactly one' (on_exhaust is a documented shared satellite of BOTH loop and portal; 'exactly one' is unsatisfiable and a guard-first implementer following the old wording writes a guard that can never pass).

Write tests/test_guards_modifier_composition_completeness.py's new registry-integrity checks FIRST (failing until tables exist): _COMBO_MAP round-trip bijectivity; MODIFIER_KWARGS row-set == _COMBO_MAP's modifier-name universe; the corrected >=1-row anti-flat-explosion ratchet; field_map honesty.

Finding-1 resolution -- the Phase-1 audit (originally 'migration scaffold inside decorator(f), cross-checking derive_combo against the built node at the existing exit') is moved OUT of decorators.py entirely: decorators.py is at its EXACT file-size ceiling (671, test_guards_file_size.py:79, which asserts strict equality in both directions) and Phase 1 must not touch it. Instead the Phase-1 audit runs from the TEST SUITE: a new test (same file as the grid, or a sibling) calls node(**each of the Phase-0 grid's 32 kwarg subsets), then independently calls derive_combo(the same kwargs) and asserts it equals the built node's actual modifier_set.combo -- verifying the registry classifies identically to today's live branches WITHOUT decorator(f) importing or calling anything from _node_modifier_kwargs.py yet. decorators.py's line count and ALLOWLIST entry (671) are UNCHANGED after Phase 1. Gate: bare uv run pytest.

### Phase 2 -- dispatch rewrite + kwarg-named vocabulary completion, ceiling updated IN THIS COMMIT (REVISED: Findings 1, 2, 5)

Finding-2 resolution (sugar_kwargs provenance) -- add ONE line as the FIRST statement in node()'s body (before caller_ns = sys._getframe(1).f_locals, which itself is currently the first statement): `sugar_kwargs = {k: v for k, v in locals().items() if k != 'fn'}`. At function entry, locals() contains EXACTLY node()'s 32 parameters (31 kwargs + fn) and nothing else -- captured before caller_ns or any other local exists, so no pollution. decorator(f) references sugar_kwargs via closure, the same mechanism it already uses for map_over/loop_when/etc. This IS the kwargs: Mapping[str, Any] that apply_node_sugar/derive_combo consume -- not a hand-written dict literal (which would relocate rather than remove the flat enumeration, per the finding). The Phase-1 anti-flat-explosion guard's inspect.signature(node) universe and this locals()-derived sugar_kwargs are BOTH anchored to node()'s actual signature, so they cannot drift apart from each other by construction.

Extract _build_operator_kwargs and _build_loop_kwargs into _node_modifier_kwargs.py (mirroring the 3 existing builders). Add 5 named _build_star_node functions. Replace decorators.py's 6 branches with: combo = derive_combo(sugar_kwargs, node_label=node_label); members = modifier_names_for_combo(combo); then 5 independent, unconditional membership checks in fixed order oracle/each/operator/loop/portal (verified order-inert: ModifierSet stores typed slots per modifiers.py:757-771, not an ordered list -- architect-review CONFIRMED SOUND, re-verify against live line numbers when implementing). Collapse the 5 sidecar re-registration sites to ONE terminal call (verified safe -- nothing between the pipes reads the sidecar; architect-review CONFIRMED). Move _apply_eager_oracle_gen_type to one end-of-chain call (verified inert -- oracle_gen_type_for reads only modifier_set.oracle + node.outputs; architect-review CONFIRMED).

Finding-5 resolution (message-ordering / side-effect delta, folds the original Phase 3a into Phase 2) -- calling derive_combo unconditionally on sugar_kwargs would, for the two currently-gapped invalid pairs (oracle-kwargs+loop_when, oracle-kwargs+portal), raise the GENERIC 'Invalid modifier combination' message via combo_for_modifier_names BEFORE _build_oracle_kwargs ever runs -- silently dropping the body-as-merge UserWarning + register_scripted side effects that fire today (today these side effects DO fire, because the oracle branch's pipe succeeds first and the pipe-layer ConstructError only fires later when the loop/portal pipe is attempted). To keep this a NAMED, deliberate change rather than a smuggled one: land the two new kwarg-named pre-check clauses (originally scoped as 'Phase 3a') in decorators.py's EXISTING pre-check block (:243-295) in THIS SAME Phase-2 commit -- same style as the 4 already there (oracle-kwargs+loop_when; oracle-kwargs+portal). These clauses fire BEFORE derive_combo is ever reached, so: (a) derive_combo/combo_for_modifier_names never observes an invalid combo on the @node path in practice (defense in depth, not the enforcement mechanism), (b) oracle kwargs are never built for these 2 invalid pairs -- matching the pattern of the 4 pairs ALREADY guarded this way today, (c) the message becomes kwarg-named (the one deliberate, explicitly-called-out message improvement bundled with this commit -- 'Phase 2 is the phase that owns this message change' satisfies the review's 'no phase changes a message unless it owns message changes' mandate). Add the 2 new should_fail check fixtures + 2 new @node-path message assertions (test_loop.py/test_portal.py currently have ZERO @node-path assertions for either pair -- only programmatic-surface assertions exist) in this same commit.

Retarget tests/test_guards_modifier_composition_completeness.py RULE 1 in the SAME commit (goes silently vacuous otherwise -- architect-review CONFIRMED). New invariants: exactly one return in apply_node_sugar; every membership-check block tests membership against members (never a re-derived raw-kwarg condition); the membership-checked name-set equals MODIFIER_KWARGS' row-name set. RULE 2 untouched.

Ceiling bookkeeping (Finding 1, continued): decorators.py's line count changes in THIS commit (elif chain replaced by shorter registry-driven dispatch: net shrink expected even after adding the 2 new pre-check clauses + the 1-line sugar_kwargs capture). Re-measure with wc -l and update tests/test_guards_file_size.py's ALLOWLIST entry to the EXACT new count IN THIS SAME COMMIT -- never deferred to a later phase.

Gate: tests/test_node_sidecar_contract.py, tests/decorator/, tests/modes/, tests/modifiers/, tests/test_loop.py, tests/test_portal.py (new assertions), then full uv run pytest.

### Phase 3 (was 3b) -- enable the contract check, real strictness, maintainer-gated (REVISED: Findings 6/7/8 LOW)

Add _check_kwargs_against_shape to _node_modifier_kwargs.py and call it from decorators.py for the FIRST time in this phase (Finding-7 resolution: it is NOT added inert in Phase 2 -- apply_node_sugar's Phase-2 flow reads identically without it, so introducing it only when it does something avoids a called-but-no-op stub sitting in a shipped phase).

Finding-8 resolution (map_on_error default semantics): _check_kwargs_against_shape must compare each passed kwarg's value against inspect.signature(node).parameters[name].default -- NOT is not None -- so map_on_error='collect' (whose declared default is 'raise', not None) is correctly treated as 'not passed' only when it equals its default, and flagged only when the caller explicitly set a non-default value without an owning trigger (map_over).

Newly-rejected inputs (today silently ignored, confirmed no test asserts success on these): max_iterations without loop_when; on_exhaust without loop_when/portal; map_on_error!=default without map_over; merge_model/merge_pre_process/merge_post_process/merge_fallback without an oracle trigger.

should_fail fixtures per new pattern + should_pass twins; extend the Phase-0 grid with dangling-satellite cases.

BEFORE landing: rg piarch's constructs (piarch/src/derive_ensemble/constructs/) for the 4 dangling-satellite patterns -- required, not optional -- full gate; either green (suite-neutral) or names the exact relying test(s) for the maintainer to decide explicitly.

Ceiling bookkeeping: re-measure decorators.py and _node_modifier_kwargs.py post-change; update or delete the decorators.py ALLOWLIST entry per the exact-ceiling rule.

Finding-9 resolution (_assert_shape_applied removal justification, was doc Sec 5's 'provably redundant'): restate as 'covered exhaustively by the Phase-0 grid's 32 membership assertions across every shape' -- NOT 'provably redundant' or 'would compare a value against itself'. The two sides (kwargs -> derive_combo -> _COMBO_MAP vs the actually-piped ModifierSet -> .combo) are computed by genuinely DIFFERENT code, so a hypothetical future builder degenerately returning n unpiped stays representable in principle; the Phase-0 grid's exhaustive coverage is what makes dropping the runtime assert defensible, not a structural proof.

Update AGENTS.md's @node sections to describe the registry. Close neograph-jtawq.4 citing docs/design/node-decorator-classify-dispatch-2026-08-04.md AND this refined plan.

## Reuse Decision (Finding 4)

_spec_loader.py's _apply_modifiers (:237-268) stays SEPARATE from the new @node registry -- not extracted into one shared applier. Reason: the two appliers have genuinely different input provenance. _apply_modifiers reads TYPED Pydantic sub-model presence (spec.oracle/spec.each/spec.loop/spec.operator, each a distinct schema-validated class whose own field set is the validity contract) parsed from YAML via _spec_schema.py. The new registry reads FLAT co-occurring kwargs on a single Python function call and must DERIVE which modifier(s) they imply via ModifierCombo/_COMBO_MAP -- a classification problem _apply_modifiers does not have (a YAML spec already states exactly which modifier sub-blocks are present; there is nothing to infer). Unifying them would force one of the two into an unnatural shape for no dedup of actual validity logic (both already terminate at the same modifiers.py classes). The spec loader's missing Portal arm (confirmed: _spec_schema.py's NodeSpec/ConstructSpec declare oracle/each/loop/operator but NO portal field -- Portal is unreachable from YAML pipelines today) is filed as its own follow-up: neograph-2j208.
