title: ComboDecomposition: add a derived, guarded fused field so is_each_oracle_fused stops being independently re-called at 7 sites
description:
RESCOPED 2026-08-04 -- the ticket's original framing (a 6-file "shape-dispatch visitor" spanning
_agent_spec.py, loader.py, modifiers.py, compiler.py, state.py, _oracle.py) was investigated by the
16-agent architecture audit and EXPLICITLY REJECTED. Do not re-propose a visitor/strategy
unification -- see "REJECTED IDEA" below before touching this ticket.

CURRENT GROUND TRUTH (docs/design/agent-spec-target-architecture-2026-08-03.md, ticket-ground-truth
table + Pillar A1; re-verified fresh 2026-08-04, do not trust older line numbers):

Most of this theme's original scope is ALREADY LANDED via `COMBO_DECOMPOSITION`
(modifiers.py:132-146) + its consumer ratchet (tests/test_guards_combo_decomposition_consumers.py,
PENDING == frozenset()). runner.py and factory.py hold ZERO combo vocabulary -- strike them from any
future span estimate.

THE LIVE RESIDUAL (this ticket's actual remaining scope, narrow and fully designed already):
"is this combo an Each x Oracle fusion" has THREE independent spellings today, none of them a field
on `ComboDecomposition` (the one table everything else reads for combo meaning):
  1. `is_each_oracle_fused(mods)` (modifiers.py:288) -- a predicate over modifier INSTANCES.
  2. `modifier_names_for_combo(combo)` (modifiers.py:254) -- table-derived, self-described as "the
     ONLY sanctioned way" to ask combo membership, yet a SEPARATE spelling from #1.
  3. loader.py:558's `dict.fromkeys(names, True)` shim feeding #1 -- a third, ad hoc spelling.

`is_each_oracle_fused` is called independently at 7 sites across 6 files (re-verified 2026-08-04,
grep `is_each_oracle_fused(` across src/neograph/):
  compiler.py:548, _state_write.py:90, loader.py:558, _subconstruct.py:103, _agent_spec.py:227,
  state.py:400 (case-guard: `case PrimaryShape.EACH if is_each_oracle_fused(mods):`), state.py:462
  (inline). No `assert_never` or guard trips if a second fused combo is ever added -- the exact
  "silent divergence" shape this codebase's other single-source-of-truth fixes exist to close.

WHY THE FUSED/PLAIN DISTINCTION MUST EXIST AT ALL (so nobody "fixes" this by deleting it): most of
the 7 consumers only need `COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[combo].primary == PrimaryShape.EACH` -- a fused node
IS basically an Each node for their purposes (state-field shape, etc). Only compiler.py's actual
graph-topology construction needs the finer distinction, because the topology genuinely differs:
plain Each is a fan-out+barrier, fused Each x Oracle is a different M x N Send-based topology
(_add_each_oracle_fused). Folding EACH_ORACLE down to primary=EACH for the common case and giving
only the topology-builder an extra orthogonal question is the RIGHT shape. What's wrong is only HOW
that extra question is currently answered (a free-floating function, re-called 7 times) instead of a
guarded field on the table those same 7 call sites already hold.

THE FIX (Pillar A1 in the target-architecture doc, full detail there):
1. Add `fused: bool` to `ComboDecomposition` (modifiers.py), computed AT DEFINITION from the
   existing sanctioned membership function `modifier_names_for_combo` -- not hand-set per row.
2. A partition guard (new test, alongside tests/test_guards_combo_decomposition_consumers.py)
   asserting, for every ModifierCombo: `decomp.fused == ({'each','oracle'} <= modifier_names_for_combo(combo))`
   -- so the field and the function it's derived from can never silently drift apart.
3. Migrate the 7 call sites above to `decomp.fused` (they already do `decomp =
   COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[combo]` to get `.primary`/`.has_operator` a few lines earlier in most cases --
   this becomes a one-line, coherent edit per site, not a new lookup).
4. `is_each_oracle_fused` either goes away or becomes a thin, table-backed helper -- decide which at
   implementation time based on whether any call site still needs the instance-level (not name-level)
   signature.
5. Also fold in: normalize compiler.py's `mods.get('operator')` postlude reads to `decomp.has_operator`
   for spelling uniformity (same commit, same guard file).

REJECTED IDEA -- do not resurrect: the original description's "candidate shape-dispatch visitor
design question" (unifying compiler.py/_agent_spec.py/loader.py/_wiring.py/runner.py's construct-tree
traversal idioms into one visitor). Investigated and rejected in
docs/design/agent-spec-target-architecture-2026-08-03.md Sec 3, Conflict 4: the per-shape arm bodies
bind genuinely divergent tuples (export's 7-tuple _LoweredItem vs compiler graph mutations vs loader
items vs state field dicts); the export/import dispatch mirror is DOCUMENTED and deliberate on both
sides; a visitor would be a SECOND parallel dispatch mechanism -- the disease, not the cure.
Consumers stay exactly where they are; only the FACTS they consult (this ticket: the fused bit)
centralize.

RELATED, NOT THIS TICKET'S SCOPE: the neograph-jtawq.4 (node() decorator redesign, fully designed,
see that ticket) explicitly investigated and declined to import is_each_oracle_fused at all -- its
design is independent of whether/how this ticket resolves. Fixing this ticket does not block or get
blocked by jtawq.4.

DEPENDENCY STATUS: neograph-s7zt3.11 (Phase 8), the prior blocker, is CLOSED. This ticket is
unblocked. Per the target-architecture doc's phased plan this is "P4" -- ordered after P1-P3
(bookkeeping, the wire oracle, the ModifierSet slot-legality gate) but the ordering constraint is
about a shared file-size ratchet sequencing, not a hard technical dependency; verify against the
target-architecture doc's Sec 4 table at implementation time since phase numbers may have shifted if
other phases already landed.
design:
## Core Invariant

"Is this ModifierCombo an Each x Oracle fusion?" is answered by exactly ONE authority -- a
`fused` column on `COMBO_DECOMPOSITION` derived at definition from `_COMBO_MAP` via
`modifier_names_for_combo` -- and every consumer READS it; no consumer, no second table, and no
free-floating predicate re-derives fusion from modifier presence.

## Implementation Plan

Guard-first (write each guard/test red before the production edit). Every step below EXTENDS an
existing table, guard, or test class -- nothing new is invented.

1. **Hoist, don't duplicate.** Move `modifier_names_for_combo` (modifiers.py:254-272) above
   `COMBO_DECOMPOSITION` (:132). It reads only `_COMBO_MAP` (:87-101), so this is a pure move.
   Correct its docstring sentence "COMBO_DECOMPOSITION cannot answer this" -- with `fused` it
   partially can. Keep it line-neutral (see ratchet, step 8).

2. **Extend `ComboDecomposition` with `fused: bool`** and rebuild `COMBO_DECOMPOSITION` as a
   comprehension over a `(primary, has_operator)` base map, with
   `fused = frozenset({"each", "oracle"}) <= modifier_names_for_combo(combo)`. Derived at
   definition, never hand-set per row (this is the doc's Sec 3 conflict-2 resolution). Nothing
   outside modifiers.py constructs `ComboDecomposition` (verified), so no other call site breaks.

3. **Derive `SUB_CONSTRUCT_UNSUPPORTED_COMBOS`** (modifiers.py:148-150) from the new column
   instead of hand-typing the two fused combos -- it is a fourth spelling of the same fact.
   `tests/test_combo_decomposition.py:95` already pins the identity, so it is the ready-made
   red/green check. Net line shrink.

4. **G-FUSE partition guard** -- extend `TestComboDecompositionTable` in
   `tests/test_combo_decomposition.py`, copying `test_has_operator_is_true_exactly_for_operator_combos`
   (:56) and reusing the `_COMBO_TO_NAMES` inversion idiom (:133) so the expectation is DERIVED,
   never re-typed: `for combo, decomp: assert decomp.fused == ({"each","oracle"} <= names[combo])`.
   Do NOT put it in test_guards_combo_decomposition_consumers.py (an AST census file, wrong home
   despite the doc's line 403).

5. **Migrate all 7 call sites to `decomp.fused`.** Each already holds `combo`; four already hold
   `decomp`. compiler.py:548 and _agent_spec.py:227 keep reading `mods["each"]`/`mods["oracle"]`
   for the INSTANCES inside the fused branch -- only the TEST moves. loader.py:547-558 loses the
   `dict.fromkeys(names, True)` shim and its 8-line comment outright. state.py:400 becomes
   `case PrimaryShape.EACH if decomp.fused:` and :462 `if decomp.fused:` -- both strictly
   line-neutral (state.py sits at 499/500).

6. **DELETE `is_each_oracle_fused`** (modifiers.py:288-306). Step 5 leaves it with zero callers;
   it is not in `neograph/__init__.__all__`. Rewrite `TestIsEachOracleFused`
   (tests/test_combo_decomposition.py:114-221) against the column. -- GATE: confirm the
   NEEDS USER INPUT item in the notes first; if the c265k guard's premise is to be preserved
   instead, stop at a thin table-backed predicate and skip only step 6.

7. **Rewrite `tests/test_guards_each_oracle_fusion_predicate.py`, do not delete it.** Its R1/R2/R3
   open-coding scanners and their ~30 meta-tests remain the ratchet that stops the fusion test
   from being re-inlined. Changes: assertion (a) widens to include modifiers.py (no owner
   exemption once the predicate is gone); assertion (b) is re-anchored on meta-test liveness --
   the precedent that guard itself sets for R3 ("its meta-tests, not its offender count, are what
   prove it is not a dead scanner"); assertion (c)'s `FUSION_READERS` is replaced by a census of
   `decomp.fused` readers, or retired with its rationale moved to the G-FUSE docstring. Update
   the module docstring to name the new authority.

8. **Ratchet bookkeeping, same commit.** Re-derive `wc -l src/neograph/modifiers.py` and LOWER
   `tests/test_guards_file_size.py:84` to the exact new count (the net effect must be a shrink --
   ~21 lines freed by step 6 against a few added by step 2). Re-check `state.py` is still < 500.
   Never raise a ceiling.

9. **Optional / scope-check A1(d) before doing it** -- see notes: `operator = mods.get("operator")`
   binds an instance and cannot become `decomp.has_operator`. If kept in scope, limit it to the
   two `if operator:` guards (compiler.py:513, :632, passing `mods["operator"]` to
   `_add_operator_check`) plus the `any("operator" in ...)` scan at :212-213, and re-derive
   G-OP's exemption literal by grep rather than copying the doc's provisional six-file list.

10. **Gate:** full `uv run pytest` (bare -- no `--extra`) + `make quality`. Guards to watch
    specifically: `test_guards_file_size`, `test_guards_combo_decomposition_consumers`,
    `test_guards_each_oracle_fusion_predicate`, `test_combo_decomposition`,
    `test_agent_spec_each_oracle`. Three-surface parity is not at risk (no IR field added, no
    behaviour change) -- the change is a pure re-spelling of one internal fact.
## Maintainer-Requested Architecture Decision (fresh study, 2026-08-05)

DECISION: delete-and-rewrite-guard. `is_each_oracle_fused` is deleted; `fused: bool` lands on
`ComboDecomposition`; `tests/test_guards_each_oracle_fusion_predicate.py` is REWRITTEN (never
deleted) in the same commit, keeping R1/R2/R3 and all meta-tests. This section is the explicit
authorization the architect review's HIGH finding said was missing.

### The factual record (all re-verified against develop, not taken from prior notes)

1. Timeline: COMBO_DECOMPOSITION landed 2026-07-27 (035da38, s7zt3.4); its 7-consumer migration
   2026-07-28 (a0bc59d, s7zt3.7); c265k's predicate + 673-line guard 2026-07-28 (babf728). The
   guard was written WITH full knowledge of the table -- its docstring cites COMBO_DECOMPOSITION
   and the fold-to-EACH decision. So the maintainer's hypothesis ("the 2026-08-04 redesign
   superseded the guard's premise") is FALSE as a factual claim: c265k's stance was a deliberate,
   contemporaneous design position, not staleness. jtawq.4 itself deliberately stayed independent
   (node-decorator-classify-dispatch-2026-08-04.md:473-476 verified the predicate had "nothing to
   share"). The decision below is made on the merits, not on recency.

2. Extensional equivalence is PROVEN, not assumed: classify_modifiers derives combo and mods from
   the same non-None slots via _COMBO_MAP (total over legal sets, fail-loud otherwise), so
   `is_each_oracle_fused(mods) == ({"each","oracle"} <= modifier_names_for_combo(combo))` at
   every reachable site. The guard's "modifier-PRESENCE read, deliberately NOT a decomposition
   question" distinction is intensional only -- it names no observable difference in this
   codebase.

3. The smoking gun that the predicate's signature is WRONG, not merely duplicative:
   loader.py:548 calls `is_each_oracle_fused(dict.fromkeys(names, True))` -- fabricating a fake
   instance dict from a name set purely to ask a name-level question through an instance-level
   signature. A caller that has to counterfeit its argument's type to use "the single authority"
   is direct evidence the authority has the wrong shape. Fusion is a fact about the COMBO
   (EACH_ORACLE is fused regardless of which Each/Oracle instances are attached); every fused
   branch that needs instance data reads mods["each"]/mods["oracle"] separately and continues to.

4. The guard's "must NOT be added to TABLE_SYMBOLS" clause protected against a DIFFERENT move
   than jtawq.2 makes. Its stated harm: adding the predicate FUNCTION to the sibling census would
   drag every presence-only reader into that guard's equality. jtawq.2 adds a FIELD on
   COMBO_DECOMPOSITION -- an already-tracked symbol needing no new TABLE_SYMBOLS entry (verified
   in research + architect pass). The specific harm the docstring feared cannot occur under this
   design. What remains of the c265k stance is one rationale sentence ("COMBO_DECOMPOSITION
   cannot answer this", modifiers.py:261) that becomes provably false the moment the field
   exists -- and keeping a provably-false claim as a guard-enforced doctrine IS the
   duplicated-source-of-truth antipattern AGENTS.md's Portal-rollout lesson names as binding:
   any fact about a ModifierCombo must live in the one table, never re-derived at N sites.

### Why delete rather than keep-and-shrink

- Keep-and-shrink leaves FOUR live spellings (predicate, modifier_names_for_combo subset, loader
  shim, hand-typed SUB_CONSTRUCT_UNSUPPORTED_COMBOS) whose agreement is coincidental, unpinned,
  and per-site. The ticket's entire value is unrealized.
- A thin table-backed predicate wrapper is the WORST option: it also turns guard assertion (b)
  red (the architect verified R1 matches only ast.BoolOp; a `.fused` attribute read or subset
  compare is not one), so it forces the same guard rewrite while keeping two authorities. Once
  the rewrite is unavoidable either way, deletion strictly dominates.
- Protection is not weakened: the disease c265k actually kills is open-coded co-presence
  spellings, and the rewrite keeps R1/R2/R3 + ~30 meta-tests intact. Assertion (b) re-anchors on
  meta-test liveness -- the precedent c265k's own docstring sets for R3 ("its meta-tests, not its
  offender count, are what prove it is not a dead scanner"). Assertion (c) becomes a census of
  `decomp.fused` readers (or retires into G-FUSE's docstring). The rewritten guard bans exactly
  what the old one banned, plus re-inlining against the new authority.

### Strongest counter-argument, and why it loses

The guard is 7 days old, green, deliberate, and written with the table in full view; overturning
recent deliberate decisions invites thrash, and "presence vs decomposition" could be defended as
a real conceptual boundary (instance-level facts vs type-level facts). It loses because the
boundary, examined site-by-site, protects nothing: all 7 callers hold `combo` in scope (four
already index COMBO_DECOMPOSITION on the same or adjacent line), zero callers need instance data
for the TEST itself, and the one caller without instances (loader) has to forge them. A
conceptual distinction that no call site exercises, that is extensionally equal everywhere, and
that forces one caller to counterfeit its argument is not a boundary worth a 673-line doctrine --
it is rationale prose that overreached its operational content. The scanners were the substance;
they survive.

### Binding riders (from the architect review, adopted as part of this decision)

- G-FUSE partition guard must derive its expectation from the enum NAME
  (`{"EACH","ORACLE"} <= set(combo.name.split("_"))`), mirroring test_combo_decomposition.py:56,
  NOT from modifier_names_for_combo (which would be X == X against the production derivation).
- Do NOT derive SUB_CONSTRUCT_UNSUPPORTED_COMBOS from `fused` (step 3 as written): the concepts
  are coincidentally equal today and neograph-rh5fb shows the unsupported-set growing
  independently. Keep it hand-written; ADD the intentional-coincidence pin
  (`SUB_CONSTRUCT_UNSUPPORTED_COMBOS == {c for c,d in COMBO_DECOMPOSITION.items() if d.fused}`)
  so divergence fails loud instead of being silently redefined.
- Fix the ~9 stale rationale comments (compiler.py:544-547, modifiers.py:261-262, loader shim
  comment, etc.) in the same commit -- enumerate by grep, not by this list.
- Drop step 9 (operator-spelling normalization): compiler.py has zero ratchet headroom and it is
  spelling-only churn. File separately if still wanted.
- Delete the now-orphaned `Mapping` alias in modifiers.py (architect-verified F401 on deletion).

DECISION: delete-and-rewrite-guard
notes:
## STILL BLOCKED on Phase 8 -- confirmed, not inherited (2026-07-31)

Re-checked when the blanket Phase 8 gate was lifted from siblings .1, .4, .5. This child STAYS blocked, and for a narrower and now-verified reason.

Phase 8 was re-scoped to Agent Spec IMPORT only. Its working set is loader.py -- which is squarely inside this theme's span (this ticket covers the construct-tree traversal idiom shared by compiler.py, _agent_spec.py, loader.py and others, with divergent per-shape bodies). Phase 8 will additionally hoist the FlowNode-to-Construct recursion into ONE named import-side seam, which is precisely a change to how this theme's dispatch works on the import side.

So the original 'do NOT start early' instruction still holds, but the reason is now specific: Phase 8 changes the import-side dispatch shape this theme is meant to unify. Starting first would design against a shape that is about to move.

What CHANGED and is worth folding in when this starts: the export side of Phase 8 turned out to be already item-kind-agnostic (_lower_each / _lower_oracle / _lower_operator / _lower_construct_item all handle a Construct today -- verified empirically, not assumed). The import side is where the asymmetry lives. That asymmetry -- one clean export seam (_lower_item_body) versus an inlined-and-duplicated import path -- is the concrete instance of this theme's thesis and should be its motivating example.

EXCEPTION to record: _lower_loop is NOT item-kind-agnostic. Loop on a Construct with DIFFERING boundary types fails at export (neograph-rh5fb). Do not treat 'export is uniform' as universal when planning this theme.
## Findings (research atom yf2ar.10, 2026-08-05 -- all line numbers re-verified fresh against develop)

**REUSE TARGET (do not build anything new):** `COMBO_DECOMPOSITION` (modifiers.py:132-146) +
its `ComboDecomposition` NamedTuple (:114-131). `modifier_names_for_combo` (:254-272) depends
ONLY on `_COMBO_MAP` (:87-101) -- verified -- so it can be hoisted above the table with zero new
dependencies, which is what "derive `fused` at definition" needs.

**The partition guard already has an exemplar -- copy it, do not invent a new file.**
`tests/test_combo_decomposition.py:56` (`test_has_operator_is_true_exactly_for_operator_combos`)
and `:61` (`test_primary_agrees_with_combo_map_modifier_semantics`) are EXACTLY the shape G-FUSE
needs, including the anti-tautology idiom (`_COMBO_TO_NAMES = {combo: names for names, combo in
_COMBO_MAP.items()}`, :133). The `fused` partition test belongs in `TestComboDecompositionTable`
there. NOTE a divergence to settle: the ticket says "new test alongside
test_guards_combo_decomposition_consumers.py"; the target-arch doc line 403 says "in
test_guards_combo_decomposition_consumers.py". Neither fits -- that file is an AST consumer
census, not a table-contract file. Recommend test_combo_decomposition.py.

**Step 4 of the ticket ("decide whether the predicate survives") resolves empirically to DELETE.**
The doc's A1(c) assumes some sites are "genuine mods-in-hand reads" that cannot reach the table.
Verified false: ALL SEVEN call sites already hold `combo` in local scope, and four of them index
`COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[combo]` on the SAME or an adjacent line:
- compiler.py:532 `combo, mods = classify_modifiers(node)` -> :548 test
- _agent_spec.py:225 `decomp = COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[combo]` -> :227 test (one line apart)
- loader.py:547 `decomp = COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[combo]` -> :558 test
- state.py:399 -> :400 (case guard); state.py:455 -> :462
- _state_write.py:85 `match COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[combo].primary` -> :90
- _subconstruct.py:94-95 `sub_combo` + `COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[sub_combo].primary` -> :103
`is_each_oracle_fused` is NOT in `neograph/__init__.__all__` (verified: 0 hits) -- internal, no
public-contract cost to deleting. No website/api-manifest reference.

**A FOURTH fusion spelling the ticket does not count:** `SUB_CONSTRUCT_UNSUPPORTED_COMBOS`
(modifiers.py:148-150) is the hand-typed frozenset `{EACH_ORACLE, EACH_ORACLE_OPERATOR}` -- i.e.
"the fused combos", re-typed. Once `fused` exists it should be DERIVED from it (its own test,
test_combo_decomposition.py:95, already asserts exactly that identity). Derives cleanly and is a
net line SHRINK, which the ratchet below makes valuable.

**Current vs deprecated pattern.** Current (post-neograph-tjpn4 / s7zt3.10): a consumer holds
`decomp = COMBO_DECOMPOSITION[combo]`, matches `decomp.primary`, closes with `assert_never` --
see _agent_spec.py:212-240 and its documented import mirror loader.py:540-570. Deprecated: any
hand-written `combo in (X, Y)` / `combo == ModifierCombo.X` chain -- already eradicated
(`PENDING == frozenset()`). Fusion is the last fact still answered outside the table.

## Relevant Code
- `src/neograph/modifiers.py:114-146` -- `ComboDecomposition` + `COMBO_DECOMPOSITION`; the table
  to extend. Nothing outside this file constructs `ComboDecomposition` (grep-verified), so a
  third field is contained. Its 12 rows are POSITIONAL literals, so "derived at definition"
  means restructuring to a comprehension over a `(primary, has_operator)` base map.
- `src/neograph/modifiers.py:254-272` -- `modifier_names_for_combo`, "the ONLY sanctioned way to
  ask combo membership". Its docstring claims "COMBO_DECOMPOSITION cannot answer this" -- that

title: Portal dispatch: PortalMemberClass taxonomy + routing-plumbing collapse + export/import table (3 axes, corrected scope)
description:
RESCOPED 2026-08-05 per docs/design/agent-spec-target-architecture-2026-08-03.md (Pillar A3/B4/B5,
ticket-ground-truth table + Sec 4 phased plan P7/P9/P10). Original framing's line-count estimate
(_wiring.py:703-1038 + factory.py:109-719, ~1182 lines) is DEAD -- both files have since moved (817 /
949 lines as of the audit; re-derive with `wc -l` before starting, per every jtawq child's standing
instruction). The bigger correction: the ticket's premise ("design the missing agent-cycle
abstraction") is stale -- that abstraction ALREADY EXISTS (`_wire_agent_cycle_body`, _wiring.py:
557-681, already shared by both the linear agent/act path :684-702 and the Portal mesh path :783-792).
Routing DECISIONS are also already single-sourced (`_portal_route_to_command` factory.py:225-310,
`_tool_handoff_to_command` :313-371).

The real remaining scope decomposes into THREE independent axes (do not re-propose a shape-dispatch
visitor spanning these -- see neograph-jtawq.2's own note on why that idea was investigated and
rejected; the axes below stay separate, each reading a shared vocabulary rather than merging into one
mechanism):

AXIS 1 -- member-class taxonomy (Phase P7). "What kind of Portal mesh participant is this item" is
independently re-derived by isinstance/mode/is_dispatch checks across 7 src files (_wiring.py:197,748;
_validation_portal.py x3; _construct_validation.py:249; _agent_spec_portal.py x2; compiler.py:280;
modifiers.py:818,861) plus an 8th way in loader.py (`type(agent).__name__ == 'Flow'`, :373). Fix: a
`PortalMemberClass` enum + `portal_member_class(item)` classifier living in modifiers.py beside
`classify_modifiers` -- NOT in `_portal.py` (whose raw is_dispatch/is_tool_triggered discriminators at
:80-106 stay the single source for THEIR OWN axis; the classifier composes them). CRITICAL layering
constraint, resolved concretely in the doc, do not re-derive casually: modifiers.py sits BELOW
node.py/construct.py in the import DAG (construct.py:33, node.py:73 import it at module level;
modifiers.py sees ConstructItem only under TYPE_CHECKING, :43) -- so the classifier MUST discriminate
node-vs-construct STRUCTURALLY (the duck-typing pattern classify_modifiers already uses, modifiers.py:
169) rather than via a module-level import (hard cycle) or a function-local import (grows
FUNCTION_LOCAL_IMPORT_ALLOWLIST -- refused, same as neograph-jtawq.4's resolved layering question).
Migrate: state.py's private `_is_dispatch` (:225-227), compiler.py:280's arm-selection branch,
_wiring.py:333-425's inline if/elif chain, loader.py:373's type-name derivation.

AXIS 2 -- routing-plumbing collapse (Phase P9, depends on Axis 1 landing first). A frozen
`PortalRouteSpec` (channel_key/count_field/payload_field/route_field/valid_targets/max_hops/
on_exhaust/exit_name/entry_name) + a `MeshContext` built once in `_add_portal_mesh`, collapsing 4
copy-pasted closure-param blocks (_wiring.py:305-331 -> :342-396, :749-777) and 10 kwarg-threaded
route-call sites (8x `_portal_route_to_command` factory.py:184,203,481,498,567,584,686,703; 2x
`_tool_handoff_to_command` :658,672) into thin per-class adapters keyed by PortalMemberClass. PURE
plumbing collapse -- no restructuring of the sync/async twin pairs (that's neograph-jtawq.6, out of
scope here), no change to hop-budget/approval accounting. Read-side only: touches nothing that writes
`handoff_param`/`handoff_channel` (guard G3 untouched).

AXIS 3 -- export/import read the same vocabulary (Phase P10, closes this ticket). A two-way table
mapping PortalMemberClass <-> Agent-Spec-vs-Flow member encoding, trigger axis <-> HandoffMode,
replacing loader.py:373's type-name check and its hard-coded :380-384 rule. Swarm stays a documented
LOSSY adapter (loader.py:411-442 warnings; _agent_spec_portal.py:158-170 exit-gate approximation) --
the runtime taxonomy is the authority, Swarm's encoding is one table reading it, never the reverse.

Full detail, conflict resolutions, and the exact guard specs (G-PMC consumer ratchet) are in the
design doc -- read it before starting, do not re-derive from this summary alone.
notes:

title: Accept an optional caller correlation_id, logged on every framework line and attached to the trace
description:
Split out of neograph-s65y2 by its architect review (atom neograph-ehuks.4, finding #4). s65y2 delivers the run_id<->trace_id join; this is the ticket's option 3, which is a DIFFERENT capability.

## The ask (verbatim intent from s65y2)
Accept an optional caller `correlation_id` that is logged on every framework log line and attached to the trace, WITHOUT replacing `run_id`. This lets a caller stamp ITS unit of work (an Inspect sample id, an eval arm, an epoch) into neograph's own log lines — something callers cannot do today because they do not own neograph's logger. s65y2's own note calls this 'the most general' of the three options: even with the join in place, callers still need their unit of work on the framework's lines.

Downstream is working around it with `structlog.contextvars`, which works only if the host app configured `merge_contextvars` in its processor chain — a caller who does not know to add it gets nothing, silently.

## Why it is separate
It adds PUBLIC config surface (a documented `correlation_id` key), which per AGENTS.md drags in website/docs updates. s65y2 already carries a dependency-floor bump plus three config-carrier migrations; bundling made one unreviewable commit.

## Implementation sketch (both halves land on primitives that already exist)
- LOGS: bind it in `_execute._run_id_binds` — the single site building the structlog bind dict, consumed by both node-lifecycle twins. Same edit point s65y2 uses for trace_id.
- TRACE: forward via `config['metadata']['langfuse_session_id']` (or `langfuse_trace_attributes`) — keys the LangChain handler already honors, so no new langfuse surface. Verified present in the SDK.
- Explicitly NOT making `run_id` caller-settable; s65y2's reasoning for framework-minting stands.

Depends on s65y2 landing first (shares the bind site).
notes: CITATION FIX 2026-08-05 (workflow triage): the implementation sketch's '_execute._run_id_binds' does not exist (grep returns zero hits) -- the actual function is _identity_binds at src/neograph/_execute.py:41-63 (builds {run_id, trace_id} bind kwargs, consumed by both node-lifecycle wrapper twins at :110/:164). Mechanism described is accurate, only the identifier name was wrong (likely drifted between sketch-writing and s65y2's actual landing under a different name).

title: Agent Spec export topology: Operator/Loop check-node bypasses the body, pause node has no outgoing edge, fused Each variants have no inbound control edge
description:
Found by the architect review of neograph-s7zt3.10 (atom neograph-nmyw7.4, 2026-07-29), probed at HEAD. PRE-EXISTING -- not introduced by Phase 7.

For an OPERATOR item the top-level incoming control edge is 'prev_primary -> {name}__operator_check', BYPASSING the body node entirely, and the pause InputMessageNode has no outgoing edge. Plain LOOP already has the same shape (primary = the check node). In the Each x Oracle fused subflow, 'StartNode -> merge' is the single start edge, so the variant nodes have no inbound control edge.

This round-trips FINE through neograph's own loader, because that loader recognizes structure via the neograph/* markers plus a structural confirmation walk -- it never executes the Flow's control edges. But a FOREIGN Agent Spec runtime executing the exported Flow literally would skip the body node / the variant nodes, and would dead-end at the pause node.

So the exported Flow is a faithful neograph SERIALIZATION but not a faithful neograph PROGRAM. Decide which the export is contracted to be, then either fix the topology or document the boundary explicitly (and say so on the website's Agent Spec page).

DO NOT let any new Phase 7/8 fixture assert foreign-executable semantics the export does not have -- that is the trap this ticket exists to keep visible.
notes:
DECISION (2026-08-03, maintainer): policy is "a faithful, independently executable program" -- an exported Flow must be correctly executable by any real Agent Spec runtime (e.g. WayFlow), not merely round-trippable through neograph's own marker-reading importer. Maintainer: "I don't know how the read can be any different at all" -- consistent with the project's stated north star (anything that compiles to LangGraph must be representable in Agent Spec) and with the explicit rejection, throughout this epic, of "we don't support it" answers that turn out to be reuse failures rather than real limits.

This makes the current topology (Operator/Loop check-node bypassing the body, pause node dead end, fused Each variants with no inbound control edge) a real bug, not an acceptable documented boundary. Needs actual control-edge rewiring for OPERATOR, LOOP, and fused EACH_ORACLE export so a naive edge-walking executor reaches the body node, the pause node has a real continuation, and the fused variants have a real inbound trigger edge.
close_reason:
All THREE topology gaps fixed with a real control-edge rewiring, plus a fourth found by the same walk.

MECHANISM: _lower_construct_item's single 'primary_node' (which served as BOTH the incoming-edge target and the outgoing-edge source) is split into an ENTRY node and a list of (from_node, from_branch) EXITS. to_agent_spec chains every exit of item N to the entry of item N+1, and terminates every exit of the last item at the EndNode.

1. Operator body bypass -- the composite now keeps the ARM's entry (the body it guards) and appends the gate to the arm's EXITS, mirroring _wiring._add_operator_check's 'node -> check'. Pre-fix the body had NO inbound edge at all: unreachable.
2. Pause node dead end -- the composite exits on BOTH (check, DEFAULT_BRANCH) and (pause, None), reconverging on the successor. That IS the runtime resume path (the interrupt fires inside the check node, so the human's answer resumes there and falls through), not an invented one.
3. Fused Each x Oracle variants -- fixed at the root, in _lower_oracle: the variants are now CHAINED (variant_0 -> ... -> variant_n-1 -> merge) instead of all pointing at the merge, so each has an inbound edge. This fixes the un-fused top-level ORACLE identically (same defect, same shared function). Chain not ParallelFlowNode because pyagentspec forbids two subflows exposing the same output title, which N Oracle variants do by construction; the variants are independent, so sequential is a valid topological order.
4. (found by the reachability test) LOOP was exported as a while-do -- entered at the check -- while neograph's Loop is a DO-while. Now entered at the BODY and exited via the check's 'done' branch.

TESTS: new tests/test_agent_spec_reachability.py (104 tests). The headline is a literal BFS/co-BFS control-edge walk parametrized over the WHOLE mechanically-derived GREEN matrix (82 of 104 were RED before the fix), recursing into every sub-Flow, asserting every node is reachable from the StartNode AND can reach an EndNode. Plus targeted do-while-entry and pause-reconvergence tests. Two pre-existing tests that pinned the buggy shape were rewritten to the correct topology.

FILE-SIZE RATCHET: the fix grew _agent_spec.py past its 981 ceiling, so the modifier lowerings (_lower_item_body/_lower_oracle/_lower_each/_lower_loop/_lower_operator) were extracted to a new src/neograph/_agent_spec_modifier_lowering.py (486 lines, no allowlist entry needed) with to_agent_spec injected as export_flow -- the same device _agent_spec_portal.py already uses. _agent_spec.py: 981 -> 652, ceiling lowered.

GOLDEN: tests/fixtures/agent_spec_refactor_snapshot.json -- 22 of 37 cells changed (all 16 ORACLE, 3 LOOP, 3 OPERATOR); in every one of the 37, the change is confined ENTIRELY to control_flow_connections (asserted by the patch script). Documented as the third sanctioned modification.

GATE: 4249 passed, 4 skipped; ruff clean; mypy clean on all 126 source files.

REMAINDER FILED: neograph-s7zt3.17 -- a DIFFERENT, pre-existing defect found by this walk. to_agent_spec uses iter_with_arms, which DROPS the _BranchNode sentinel, so a ForwardConstruct branch exports as a straight line and a foreign runtime runs BOTH arms unconditionally. Reachable and live, so the new walk passes on it -- reachability is necessary, not sufficient.

title: run_isolated mutates the caller's config dict (copy-not-mutate violation in node.py)
description:
node.py's run_isolated (CITATION FIXED 2026-08-05 -- was cited :478-480, now confirmed at :427-429
after an intervening refactor, neograph-3ffdg.18 commit f922e42; code and defect unchanged):

  config = config or {"configurable": {}}
  if "configurable" not in config:
      config["configurable"] = {}

The second branch ASSIGNS into a caller-owned dict rather than building a fresh one. Every other
framework site honours copy-not-mutate via _config_carrier._with_configurable (see its module
docstring: the fresh-dict rule exists so a caller re-invoked per superstep is idempotent).

Impact is low -- run_isolated is a testing/inspection tool and the mutation only inserts an empty
dict -- which is why it was dispositioned DEFER rather than folded into neograph-s65y2 (a different
concern: not identity, not the carrier idiom that ticket reuses).

Fix: config = {**(config or {}), "configurable": {**(config or {}).get("configurable", {})}} or route
through _with_configurable.

Found by the codebase disease scan in atom neograph-ehuks.3.

## THREE more sites in the same family (CORRECTED 2026-08-05 -- was "two more sites", workflow
triage found a third, pre-existing at ticket-creation time, just never counted)

config.setdefault("configurable", {}) MUTATES the caller's config dict -- same copy-not-mutate
violation, different spelling. Current locations (re-verified 2026-08-05, citations were also stale --
was runner.py:256/567, now):
  • runner.py:154 -- configurable = config.setdefault("configurable", {}), inside _prepare_new_input
  • runner.py:646 -- config.setdefault("configurable", {})["checkpoint_id"] = rewind_checkpoint_id,
    inside sync _auto_resume_from_divergence
  • runner.py:679 -- THE SAME statement inside the async twin _aauto_resume_from_divergence -- this
    is the previously-uncounted third site, confirmed present since before this ticket was filed
    (git show 946da8e, predates ticket creation)

Deliberately NOT folded into s65y2: that ticket migrated the re-inlined MERGE idiom
({**config, 'configurable': ...}), a distinct sub-pattern. The setdefault mutation is this bead's
concern, and s65y2's guard (TestConfigCarrierIsTheOnlySite, tests/test_guards_llm_runtime.py:2405-2440)
does not cover it -- its detector requires a ** splat, confirmed by reading the detector. Whoever picks

title: Agent Spec round-trip: Loop/Operator registered-NAME conditions don't round-trip (expression conditions do)
description:

title: spec_types._structural_type_name hash collision: distinct list-item types with same field name synthesize the SAME class
description:
Discovered while implementing neograph-e3b4j's docs example (examples/31_agent_spec_each_oracle_loop.py).

spec_types.py's _structural_type_name computes a registry key as tuple(sorted((p.title, str(getattr(p, 'type', None))) for p in props)) -- but pyagentspec's own Property.type field appears to carry only the bare JSON-schema type keyword (e.g. 'array'), NOT the nested item schema. So two DIFFERENT Pydantic models each with a single field named 'items' -- one 'list[str]', the other 'list[SomeNestedModel]' -- hash to the IDENTICAL 'AgentSpecType_<hash>' registry key and get reconstructed as the SAME synthesized class. In a single process reconstructing BOTH shapes (e.g. two independent panels in one script, first Bag(items: list[Tagged]) then Claims(items: list[str])), the SECOND reconstruction silently reuses the FIRST's cached class, causing a real pydantic ValidationError when data shaped for the second type is validated against the first's schema (e.g. 'items.0: Input should be a valid dictionary, got str').

WORKAROUND used in e3b4j's example: avoid reusing the SAME field name ('items') across independently-reconstructed types that end up in the same process/registry lifetime -- Claims' field was renamed 'items' -> 'claims'.

FIX: _structural_type_name's signature must be genuinely structural for LIST/nested types too -- likely needs to recurse into Property.items (or whatever pyagentspec exposes for array item schemas) rather than only using the bare top-level type keyword, so list[str] and list[SomeModel] hash differently even when the field name coincides.
design:
## Root Cause
_structural_type_name's per-field signature (str(getattr(p, 'type', None))) is not genuinely structural for container types -- it stops at the bare top-level JSON-schema keyword and never looks at ListProperty.item_type / DictProperty.value_type / ObjectProperty.properties / UnionProperty.any_of.

## Fix Approach
Added _property_type_signature(prop), a recursive structural signature that walks into item_type (list), value_type (dict), properties (object), and any_of (union), falling back to the bare type keyword for primitives. _structural_type_name now hashes (title, _property_type_signature(prop)) pairs instead of (title, bare-type-str) pairs. Kept the two functions in lockstep via a docstring cross-reference (both live in spec_types.py, no split needed).
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing tests written: tests/test_agent_spec_types.py::TestStructuralTypeNameDistinguishesListItemTypes (test_list_of_str_and_list_of_model_with_same_field_name_hash_differently, test_reconstructing_both_shapes_in_one_process_does_not_collide)
- Root cause: CONFIRMED exactly as reported. _structural_type_name's signature used str(getattr(p, 'type', None)) which for a ListProperty is just the bare keyword 'array' -- never recursing into ListProperty.item_type. Bag(items: list[Tagged]) and Claims(items: list[str]) both produce sig=(('items','array'),), hashing to the SAME AgentSpecType_<hash>. register_type's idempotency check (_fields_match) only compares FIELD NAMES (not types), so it silently treats the second reconstruction as 'same schema' and reuses the FIRST-registered class -- reproducing the reported pydantic ValidationError exactly.
## Trace Similar Patterns
Found ONE related-but-distinct sibling: register_type's _fields_match (spec_types.py:45-47) has the SAME shallow-equality disease at a DIFFERENT site -- it compares field NAMES only, never TYPES. My _structural_type_name fix prevents the hash from colliding for the qtfof.4 repro (so _fields_match never even gets exercised with mismatched types for THIS bug), but any caller using register_type() with an EXPLICIT (non-structural) name -- e.g. loader.py's agent_spec_properties_to_types(props, name=<caller-supplied>) -- could still trip the same silent-reuse failure mode independently. Filed as a separate follow-up: neograph-wqb5t (does NOT block this bug's fix, since qtfof.4's specific repro path is fully fixed by the _structural_type_name recursion).

No other instances of the shallow-signature disease (str(getattr(p, 'type', None)) or field-name-only equality) found elsewhere in src/neograph/.
## Codebase Disease Scan (qtfof.4)
Disease pattern (SYNTACTIC): a Property-type signature/hash-key derivation using only the bare top-level str(getattr(p, 'type', None)) keyword, without recursing into item_type/value_type/properties/any_of.

Re-scan command: grep -rn 'getattr(.*, .type., None)' src/neograph/*.py

| # | Site | Disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
|---|------|-------------|-----------------|----------|
| 1 | _structural_type_name (spec_types.py) | MIGRATE | now delegates to _property_type_signature (recursive) | Yes -- 2 regression tests + full suite (3473 passed) |

No other site derives a Property-based hash/signature key. The related _fields_match shallow-equality disease (field NAMES only, different code shape -- not a signature/hash function) is a SEPARATE site, already filed as neograph-wqb5t in trace-similar.
## Architect Review (qtfof.4)

1. Root cause correctness: CONFIRMED via direct repro -- both new tests failed with the exact collision described (identical AgentSpecType_ hash, ClaimsRebuilt is BagRebuilt) before the fix.
2. Fix minimality: LOW risk. Adds one new recursive helper function (_property_type_signature) and changes _structural_type_name's one-line signature tuple to call it -- no signature/API change to any public function.
3. Regression risk: LOW. For primitive (non-container) properties, _property_type_signature returns str(getattr(prop, 'type', None)) -- IDENTICAL to the old inline expression -- so existing structural names for primitive-only models are byte-for-byte unchanged (same digest). Only container/nested types (list/dict/object/union) get a richer signature, which can only SPLIT previously-colliding names apart, never merge previously-distinct ones (a stronger signature is a refinement, never a coarsening).
4. Architecture compliance: PASS. Confined to spec_types.py, reuses the existing _import_agent_spec_property_classes() helper (no new import surface), no IR/validator changes.
5. Similar bug scalability: covered by trace-similar (03k9k.30) and disease scan (03k9k.31) -- one related sibling (_fields_match, different shape of the same underlying shallow-equality theme) filed separately as neograph-wqb5t, correctly NOT bundled into this fix's scope.
6. Test coverage sufficiency: PASS. Covers both the unit-level signature-hash test AND the full end-to-end reconstruction scenario from the bug report (two panels, same process, second reconstruction must not corrupt). Full suite green: 3473 passed, 0 failed.

VERDICT: ALL_LOW -- fix proceeds to commit.
## Sweep Verification (qtfof.4)

Re-scan command: grep -rn 'getattr(.*, .type., None)' src/neograph/*.py
Pre-fix instances: 1 (_structural_type_name's bare-keyword signature)
Post-fix instances: 0 bare-signature sites remain (delegates to recursive _property_type_signature)

| # | Site | Disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
|---|------|-------------|-----------------|----------|
| 1 | _structural_type_name (spec_types.py) | MIGRATE | delegates to _property_type_signature | Yes -- mutation-verified, full suite 3473 passed |
| 2 | register_type._fields_match (different disease shape: field-name-only equality, not a hash signature) | DEFER | filed neograph-wqb5t | N/A -- separate bug, separate fix scope |

## Structural Guard
- File: tests/test_guards_spec_types_structural_signature.py (new file)
- Class: TestStructuralTypeNameUsesRecursiveSignature
- Meta-tests: test_structural_type_name_delegates_to_recursive_signature_helper + test_signature_helper_recurses_into_list_and_dict_item_types (positive), test_meta_guard_catches_the_disease_pattern_if_reintroduced (negative)
- 3/3 tests pass
## E2E Verification
Acceptance locus is real pyagentspec Property construction + pydantic model reconstruction/validation (in-process, no external service). test_reconstructing_both_shapes_in_one_process_does_not_collide exercises the full real path (model_to_agent_spec_properties -> loader._agent_spec_props_to_type -> real pydantic instantiation+validation of both shapes) end-to-end, matching the exact scenario from the bug report. No further e2e verification needed.
close_reason: Fixed: _structural_type_name now hashes a recursive Property-type signature (via new _property_type_signature helper) instead of the bare top-level type keyword, so list[str] and list[SomeModel] under the same field name never collide. Mutation-verified, full suite green (3473 passed).

title: RemoteAgent import: preserve endpoint config (Node has no metadata field)
description: Deferred from neograph-aa5gq gap 3. The design said 'stash endpoint shape in metadata[_MARK_REMOTE_AGENT]' so a RemoteAgent/A2AAgent import could later re-export its endpoint. But Node has NO metadata field, and adding one is an untested IR change with allowlist ramifications, so aa5gq's implementer left _MARK_REMOTE_AGENT defined (guard-required) but did NOT preserve the endpoint — the best-effort import produces a name-bound scripted Node + warning only, dropping the A2AConnectionConfig/endpoint. This meets aa5gq's acceptance (best-effort is explicitly lossy + warned) but means a RemoteAgent cannot round-trip its endpoint. Decide: add a Node IR field (metadata/sidecar) to carry the endpoint, or accept permanent lossiness and document it. Cite src/neograph/loader.py::_reconstruct_agent_node + docs/design/agent-spec-ratification-2026-07-13.md §3b.
design:
## Refined Plan (post-review)

Core Invariant: the sidecar must carry enough information to reconstruct the EXACT original agent class on export -- a lossy round-trip that silently drops class identity or captures None for a mismatched attribute name is itself a silent seam.

Resolution to MEDIUM 1 (class discriminator): extend the sidecar payload from tuple[str, Any] to a 3-tuple (or small dataclass) additionally carrying the agent CLASS name/type (RemoteAgent | A2AAgent | OciAgent) -- import already dispatches on this type (loader.py:213), so export must know which one to reconstruct. Before hardcoding agent_url/connection_config as the two captured attributes, verify these attribute names are correct for ALL THREE families against the actually-installed pyagentspec classes (not assumed) -- OciAgent in particular may use different attribute names (e.g. endpoint/agent_endpoint_id); capture per-family attribute names explicitly rather than a blind two-field getattr that could silently produce None for a mismatched family.

Resolution to MEDIUM 2 (scope split): pt85t's acceptance is import-side best-effort capture only. Descope the NEW export-side AgentNode+RemoteAgent lowering branch and its round-trip test OUT of this task -- file/confirm they belong to the downstream v2 epic (neograph-qtfof) that pt85t already blocks. pt85t's own scope becomes: (1) capture the endpoint + class discriminator in the sidecar on import, (2) a test asserting the sidecar carries the correct endpoint + class for each of the 3 agent families, (3) NO new export lowering branch in this task.

Resolved (LOW): _MARK_REMOTE_AGENT stays a write-intended-but-not-yet-read marker after this task (the sidecar, not the marker, carries the round-trip data for now) -- document this explicitly rather than implying the marker itself closes the round-trip; the follow-up doc-sync for ratification §3b stays a separately-filed bead per the original research.
notes:
## Findings
- **Reuse target: the existing PrivateAttr sidecar mechanism on `Node`** (`src/neograph/node.py:264-266`: `_sidecar`, `_param_res`, `_scripted_shim`), NOT a new public `Node.metadata` field. CLAUDE.md's own rationale for the sidecar pattern is a direct answer to this task's dilemma: 'the sidecar carries a Callable... which can't go through Pydantic schema validation without `arbitrary_types_allowed` on every downstream consumer. PrivateAttr bypasses schema while staying on the Node instance.' A RemoteAgent endpoint (`agent_url: str`, `connection_config: A2AConnectionConfig` — external `pyagentspec` types, per `tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py:522-527`) is exactly this shape: opaque, non-Pydantic-native, only needed by one export path, never touched by the compiler/validator/state layers.
- Adding a **public** `Node.metadata` field (what the ratification doc literally proposes, see NEEDS USER INPUT below) would be the 'untested IR change with allowlist ramifications' the task warns about: it would need to thread through `_construct_validation.py`'s no-Any boundary guards (`test_guards_any_audit.py`), the `IR_FIELDS`/`ALLOWED_PREPOP` single-writer guard (`tests/test_guards_llm_runtime.py:1018`, though that guard currently only tracks `fan_out_param`/`oracle_gen_type`/`handoff_param`/`handoff_channel` — a new field's writer-discipline would need its own guard or an extension of that one), and `model_copy`/pipe/deepcopy preservation tests (`test_node_sidecar_contract.py`). A PrivateAttr sidecar avoids ALL of this — it is bypassed by the same guards by design (it's not part of the pydantic schema), and `model_copy` already preserves `__pydantic_private__` for free (confirmed pattern, same file, same section).
- **Current (deprecated-by-omission) state**: `_MARK_REMOTE_AGENT = "neograph/remote_agent"` is defined in `src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:72` and pinned by `tests/test_guards_agent_spec_markers.py:108` (`test_marker_constants_pin_the_exact_wire_values`) but is **never referenced anywhere else in `src/`** (`grep -rn "_MARK_REMOTE_AGENT" src/neograph/*.py` returns exactly one line — its own definition). It's a guard-required placeholder with no producer or consumer yet.
- The best-effort import path (`src/neograph/loader.py:213-227`, `_reconstruct_agent_node`) currently drops the endpoint entirely: it emits a `warnings.warn` and returns `Node(name=..., mode="scripted", inputs=..., outputs=..., scripted_fn=spec_node.name)` — no trace of `agent.agent_url` / `agent.connection_config` survives.
- **Export-side gap, not just import-side**: even if the endpoint were captured on import, there is currently NO path in `_lower_node` (`src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:171-206`) that re-exports a `mode="scripted"` Node as an `AgentNode` wrapping a `RemoteAgent`/`A2AAgent` — `_lower_node` only ever emits `ToolNode` for scripted/raw nodes (the trailing branch, `_agent_spec.py:200-206`). So 'round-trip' requires BOTH a new import-side capture point AND a new export-side dispatch rule (something like: scripted Node with the sidecar populated -> AgentNode+RemoteAgent, instead of -> ToolNode). This is strictly larger than 'add one field' — it's a new lowering branch.
- Concrete external shape to capture (from the existing test fixture, `tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py:522-527`): `A2AAgent(name=..., agent_url: str, connection_config: A2AConnectionConfig, outputs=...)`. `agent_url` and `connection_config` are the two fields that would need to survive on the sidecar.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/loader.py:191-227 -- `_reconstruct_agent_node`, the exact best-effort branch (lines 213-227) that currently drops the endpoint; this is where a new PrivateAttr write would go (mirroring how `_sidecar`/`_param_res` get set at construction time, e.g. `decorators.py`'s `node._sidecar = (...)` pattern).
- src/neograph/node.py:258-266 -- the sidecar PrivateAttr block + its docstring; the exemplar to copy (add a fourth PrivateAttr here, e.g. `_remote_agent_endpoint: Any | None = PrivateAttr(default=None)`, following the exact same comment convention).
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:171-206 -- `_lower_node`, the export dispatch by `node.mode`; would need a new branch checking the sidecar before falling through to the `ToolNode` default, and would re-attach `metadata={_MARK_REMOTE_AGENT: ...}` on export using the already-defined marker constant.
- src/neograph/_agent_spec.py:62-72 -- the centralized marker-constant block (`_MARK_AGENT_SPEC`, `_MARK_REMOTE_AGENT`, etc.) -- single source of truth for wire-format strings; any new marker usage MUST reference these constants, never re-inline the literal (enforced by `tests/test_guards_agent_spec_markers.py`'s offender scan).
- tests/test_agent_spec_roundtrip.py:492-559 -- `TestRemoteAgentBestEffortImport`, the current best-effort-import-with-warning test; a future round-trip test would extend this class (or add a sibling) asserting the endpoint survives on the sidecar and re-exports correctly.
- tests/test_guards_llm_runtime.py:1018-1110 -- `IR_FIELDS`/`ALLOWED_PREPOP` single-writer guard; relevant ONLY if the public-field option is chosen (it would NOT need updating for a PrivateAttr, which is the reuse argument for that option).
- docs/design/agent-spec-ratification-2026-07-13.md:95-101 (§3b) -- the original design intent ('The endpoint/auth-shape rides in metadata for re-export') that this task is reconciling against the fact that `Node` has no `metadata` field.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- NEEDS USER INPUT: docs/design/agent-spec-ratification-2026-07-13.md:99 says the endpoint 'rides in metadata for re-export', implying a `Node.metadata` dict field was assumed to already exist or would be trivially added. It does not exist (confirmed: no `metadata` field in `src/neograph/node.py`'s `Node` class). The doc is silent on the sidecar-vs-public-field tradeoff and predates the discovery that this is genuinely underspecified. This is not a contradiction to silently resolve — the ratification doc is the authoritative design record; if the sidecar approach is chosen, the doc's §3b wording should be updated to reflect the mechanism actually used (a follow-up doc-sync task, not blocking this research).
- If the PrivateAttr sidecar is chosen, it must be set at construction time in `_reconstruct_agent_node`'s best-effort branch (Pydantic `PrivateAttr` cannot be passed as a constructor kwarg the way public fields can, so the pattern is `node = Node(...); node._remote_agent_endpoint = (agent.agent_url, agent.connection_config); return node` — consistent with how `decorators.py` sets `_sidecar`/`_param_res` post-construction).
- The export-side gap (no `AgentNode(agent=RemoteAgent(...))` lowering branch exists yet) means this task, even once 'solved', only unlocks IMPORT-side capture. A full round-trip additionally needs an export-side task — scope this explicitly rather than silently expanding pt85t.
- `A2AConnectionConfig` (and the broader `RemoteAgent`/`OciAgent` family) are external `pyagentspec` SDK types, optionally imported (guarded the same way `_import_agent_spec_flow_classes`/`_import_agent_spec_import_classes` gate all `agent_spec` imports in `loader.py`/`_agent_spec.py`) — storing them on a PrivateAttr is safe (PrivateAttr bypasses Pydantic schema validation entirely, so no `arbitrary_types_allowed` ConfigDict change is needed, unlike a public field would require).
## Codebase Disease Scan (pt85t)
Pattern: a defined-but-never-wired 'reserved for future' _MARK_* constant in _agent_spec.py (dead marker, same category as _MARK_REMOTE_AGENT).
Scan command: `for m in _MARK_MODE _MARK_AGENT_SPEC _MARK_TOOL_SPEC _MARK_REMOTE_AGENT _MARK_MODIFIER _MARK_GROUP_ID _MARK_VARIANT _MARK_ORACLE_SPEC _MARK_EACH_SPEC _MARK_LOOP_SPEC _MARK_OPERATOR_SPEC _MARK_BRANCH; do grep -rn "$m" src/neograph/*.py | grep -vc "= \"neograph/\""; done`
