title: [SPIKE] Portal+Operator: human-approval gate on a dynamic handoff (D4 v2, wrapper/approval-node interrupt)
description: v1 makes Keymaker+Operator ILLEGAL (D-NO-OPERATOR-COMBO/D4): the Operator postlude (_add_operator_check, _wiring.py:939-961) is bypassed by a Command(goto)-returning member. v2 path: raise interrupt() INSIDE the keymaker wrapper before returning the Command — a wrapper-level gate, not a postlude node. Deferred from KEYMAKER v1 (epic neograph-t1f7z). Cite: docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md + docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md.
design:
SPIKE GOAL: prove that Portal+Operator (human approval on a handoff) is buildable WITHOUT re-invoking the member's LLM on resume, and land the design. Closing this de-risks the 7t7tf ratification of Command(goto) by proving the D4 cost is temporary, not permanent.

CORE INVARIANT: the approval pause must sit ON the dynamic (Command(goto)) path, never on a statically-appended edge — because a Command(goto)-returning member routes straight to its target and never traverses an appended static edge (that is the D4 bug itself).

ROOT CAUSE (why v1 cut the combo): Operator wires via _add_operator_check (_wiring.py:1082) which does graph.add_edge(node_name, check_name) — a STATIC edge from the guarded node to a `{node}__operator` interrupt node. A Portal member returns Command(goto=peer), LangGraph follows the goto, and the static node->check edge is never traversed. The approval node is wired, looks correct, and silently never fires.

RECOMMENDED SHAPE (approval-node-on-the-dynamic-path, NOT naive in-wrapper):
- NAIVE (reject): call interrupt() inside make_portal_fn right before returning the Command. Simple but WRONG: LangGraph re-runs the interrupted node from the top on resume, so the member's LLM/tool calls re-fire (double model spend, possibly different answer).
- CLEAN (target): the Operator-guarded member computes its handoff and routes THROUGH a tiny dedicated approval node —
    member returns Command(goto="<member>__approve", update={proposed_target: target, ...})
    the approval node is the ONLY place interrupt() lives; on approval it returns Command(goto=approved_target); on rejection it routes elsewhere / stays.
  Resume then re-runs ONLY the cheap approval node, not the LLM member. The approval sits on the live routed path (member -> approve -> target), so the goto cannot skip it.

WHY Command(goto) HELPS HERE: the same "route through a node I name at runtime" power that makes mode (b) possible is exactly what lets us splice the approval node into the live path. This is an argument FOR the 7t7tf Command(goto) decision, not against it.

ACCEPTANCE (spike deliverables):
1. A runnable proof: an Operator-guarded Portal member pauses at the proposed handoff, surfaces the proposed target as the interrupt payload, resumes via Command(resume=<decision>), and routes to the approved target — with a checkpointer + thread_id.
2. PROVE the LLM/tool work does NOT re-execute on resume (assert the member's model/tool fake is called exactly once across pause+resume). This is the crux the naive shape fails.
3. Decide + document: does this stay illegal-at-assembly with a nicer error, or become a first-class `Portal + Operator` composition? If first-class, what does the surface look like (@node(portal=[...]) + Operator; or an explicit approve= kwarg on Portal)?
4. If landed: lift the D4 assembly ban for this specific composition; keep the ban for any shape that can't satisfy invariant #1.
notes:
## LangGraph HITL mechanics (grounding for the spike)
- Primitive: langgraph.types.interrupt(payload). Calling it inside a node RAISES GraphInterrupt, which bubbles up and PAUSES the graph; state is checkpointed (REQUIRES a checkpointer + thread_id). The payload is surfaced to the caller as the interrupt value (what the human sees).
- Resume: graph.invoke(Command(resume=<value>), config). LangGraph RE-ENTERS the interrupted node and re-runs it FROM THE TOP; this time interrupt() RETURNS <value> instead of raising, so the node continues past it.
- THE RE-RUN TRAP: everything before interrupt() in that node executes again on resume. For an LLM/agent member this means the model + tool calls re-fire unless the interrupt is isolated in a node that does no expensive work. Same class as the durable-execution replay problem (see docs/design/durable-execution-replay-research-2026-07-02.md).
- neograph already wraps this: hitl.py::ask_human (:56) is a pure passthrough over interrupt(payload.model_dump()); Operator's operator_check (_wiring.py:1094-1099) calls interrupt(should_pause) and returns {HUMAN_FEEDBACK: human_input}. The agent/act ReAct cycle already interrupts at a TURN BOUNDARY with turn-boundary idempotency (_wiring.py:1003,1040) — that idempotency pattern is prior art for keeping pre-interrupt work exactly-once and may be the reusable mechanism for the approval node.

## Linkage
- Informs (does NOT hard-block) 7t7tf: the Command(goto) ratification is cleaner to accept once this spike proves the D4 combo-cut is temporary. Cross-referenced there.
- Prior art to reuse: agent/act turn-boundary idempotency (_wiring.py:1003+), hitl.py passthrough, _add_operator_check structure.
- Code refs: _wiring.py:1082 _add_operator_check (the static-edge bug), _wiring.py:732 _wire_portal_mesh / factory.py make_portal_fn (where the approval-node routing would splice in), hitl.py ask_human, _wiring.py:1094 operator_check.
- Design docs: docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md, docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md (D4), renamed-construct note on 07inf.
## Prep (wyymi.2, 2026-07-14)
Code read: factory.py:103 make_portal_fn (_to_command emits Command(goto) after inner runs — the splice point), _wiring.py:723 _add_portal_mesh (members registered with destinations=; approval node would be added here per guarded member), _wiring.py:1082 _add_operator_check (the static-edge D4 bug), modifiers.py _SLOT_RULES + ModifierSet._validate (reciprocal Portal x Operator ban, fixture portal_operator_combo.py), hitl.py ask_human, _wiring.py:1035+ tool-gate prior art (gate node = only interrupt site, approve/deny routing — the EXACT shape the design recommends), tests/test_checkpoint_portal.py (SqliteSaver + interrupt/resume conventions).

## Plan (spike scope = acceptance 1-3; 4 is conditional on landing the feature)
- Files to ADD: tests/test_spike_portal_operator_approval.py (runnable proof), docs/design/portal-operator-approval-gate-2026-07-14.md (decision doc).
- Approach: build the CLEAN shape as a LangGraph-level proof mirroring make_portal_fn mechanics — a counted member returns Command(goto='member__approve', update={proposed target}); a dedicated approval node is the ONLY interrupt() site and on resume returns Command(goto=approved_target). File-backed SqliteSaver + thread_id; assert (a) pause surfaces proposed target as interrupt payload, (b) Command(resume=decision) routes to approved target, (c) member callable ran EXACTLY ONCE across pause+resume (the crux the naive in-wrapper shape fails — also prove the naive shape re-runs, as contrast). Sync + async.
- Decision to document (#3): recommend FIRST-CLASS Portal+Operator in v2 — Operator on a mesh member means 'splice {member}__approve onto the dynamic path' (wiring change in _add_portal_mesh + a make_portal_approval_fn in factory.py, G1-compliant); ban stays until implemented. Implementation = separate feature bead under 07inf.
- Core Invariant (from bead): approval pause sits ON the Command(goto) path, never a statically-appended edge.
## Execution (wyymi.3, 2026-07-14)
- Deliverable 1+2 (runnable proof + exactly-once crux): tests/test_spike_portal_operator_approval.py — 4 tests, all passing against real file-backed SqliteSaver/AsyncSqliteSaver. Clean shape: pause surfaces {proposed_target} as interrupt payload; Command(resume='approve') routes to approved target, 'reject' routes to mesh exit; member body executed EXACTLY ONCE across pause+resume (sync + async). Contrast test PROVES the naive in-wrapper interrupt re-runs the member (called 2x) — the D4 rejection is now empirical, not theoretical.
- Deliverable 3 (decision): docs/design/portal-operator-approval-gate-2026-07-14.md — first-class Portal+Operator in v2, surface = reuse Operator as-is (member | Portal(to=[...]) | Operator(when=...)), no approve= kwarg. Ban STAYS until implemented.
- Deliverable 4 (conditional): not landed here by design — implementation filed as neograph-kdr1u (discovered-from this spike) with the 6-step sketch + anti-band-aid clause. 7t7tf cross-referenced with the spike outcome.
- Quality check: PASS (3276 passed, ruff + mypy clean)

title: Portal: ForwardConstruct self.handoff(members=[...]) builder
description: v2 fast-follow. ForwardConstruct is exempt in v1 (D-FORWARD-EXEMPT): a runtime mesh has no static dataflow for the tracer. Add a self.handoff(members=[...], route=..., max_hops=...) builder copying self.interrupt (forward.py:1283). Nothing in v1 IR blocks it. Deferred from KEYMAKER v1 (epic neograph-t1f7z). Cite: docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md + docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md.
design:
## Refined Plan (post-review)

Core Invariant: self.handoff's emitted IR must be BYTE-FOR-BYTE identical to the declarative mesh IR (Construct(nodes=[member | Portal(...), ...]), no nesting) -- ForwardConstruct is a thin recorder, not a second IR shape.

Resolution to MEDIUM 1 (flatten): for each member, build 'bare_node | Portal(...)' and tracer.record() it DIRECTLY into the ForwardConstruct's own _ordered list (forward.py:413) -- do NOT wrap members in a Construct(...) and do NOT call record_construct(). This keeps the final construct's nodes list identical to examples/28_portal_swarm.py's demo_surface_parity target, with no extra subgraph boundary for Command(goto=<peer>) to cross.

Resolution to MEDIUM 2 (entry-only kwargs): build Portal kwargs CONDITIONALLY per member to satisfy _check_portal_mesh's entry-only validator (_validation_portal.py:194-205): the entry member (first recorded, or an explicit entry= kwarg) gets Portal(to=to[entry], max_hops=max_hops, on_exhaust=on_exhaust); every non-entry member gets Portal(to=to[name]) with NO max_hops/on_exhaust keyword passed at all (passing even the default would put it in model_fields_set and trip the validator).

Committed concrete signature: self.handoff(members=[self.a, self.b], to={'a': [...], 'b': [...]}, max_hops=..., on_exhaust=..., entry=None) -- 'to' keyed by member name, mirroring Portal.to 1:1 (never resurrect 'peers='). Scope v1 to a terminal/whole-graph mesh (self.handoff has no proxy output/input, per D-FORWARD-EXEMPT); mid-pipeline mesh embedding is explicitly out of scope, documented in the method's docstring.
notes:
## Findings
- **Reuse target (builder shape)**: `_ModifierWrapCall` + `_InterruptCall` (`src/neograph/forward.py:978-1137`) and `_ForwardSelf.interrupt()` (`forward.py:1281-1298`) are the exact pattern to copy for `self.handoff(...)`: a thin `_ForwardSelf` method that captures the tracer and returns a small `_XxxCall` object; `_ModifierWrapCall` already handles both the bare-node-target and list-of-nodes-target forms (`_materialize`, `forward.py:1083`), building either `Node | modifier` or `Construct(nodes=[...]) | modifier` depending on target shape — this is the SAME form-awareness `self.ensemble`/`self.interrupt` already give for Oracle/Operator, so Portal gets it for free structurally.
- **The modifier to attach is the existing `Portal` class** (`src/neograph/modifiers.py:600`, renamed from Keymaker per neograph-1t0zh) — NOT a new IR capability. Mode (a) peer-routing fields: `to: list[str] | None`, `route: str = 'goto'`, `max_hops: int = 10` (entry-member-only), `on_exhaust: Literal['error','exit']`. `Portal.is_dispatch` is the sole mode discriminator (never inline `route == 'decide'`).
- **Key structural difference from self.interrupt/self.ensemble that self.handoff must account for**: Operator/Oracle wrap ONE dataflow edge (proxy in -> proxy out); Portal wires a MESH where every member independently declares its OWN `to=` peer list (see `examples/28_portal_swarm.py` demo 1: each `@node(portal=[...])` sets its own peers) and there is NO proxy chain between members (D-FORWARD-EXEMPT: 'every member is simultaneously producer and consumer of the mesh channel'). So `self.handoff(members=[...])` cannot reuse the proxy-threading half of `_ModifierWrapCall.__call__` (there's no single input proxy to consume) — it only needs the ASSEMBLY half: collect self.<x> Node refs into the tracer's `_ordered` list (via `tracer.record`, forward.py:413) each already carrying (or here-attached) its own `Portal(to=...)`, in a call that is NOT __call__'d with a proxy the way self.interrupt(...)( proxy ) is — it is closer to a batch-record than a wrap.
- **Declarative/programmatic precedent for the mesh IR shape to reproduce**: `examples/28_portal_swarm.py` demo 4 (`demo_surface_parity`, lines 238-268) — `Node.scripted(...) | Portal(to=[...], max_hops=...)` per member, then `Construct(name, nodes=[member1, member2])` with NO edges between them (Portal owns the runtime routing, not the static DAG). This is the exact IR the ForwardConstruct builder must emit.
- **Reserved-key / IR facts already shipped, nothing new needed here**: `Node.handoff_param`/`Node.handoff_channel` are written ONLY by `_ir_normalize.py` (single-writer, guard G3, `IR_FIELDS` in `test_guards_llm_runtime.py`); `Command(` construction is monopolized in `factory.py`/`runner.py` (guard G1). The ForwardConstruct builder only needs to emit `Node | Portal(...)` — the normalizer + compiler + factory already do the rest, exactly as for `@node(portal=...)` and declarative `Portal(...)`.
- **Current vs deprecated naming**: the design docs (dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md, keymaker-decision-log) still say 'Keymaker' / 'peers=' / 'self.handoff(members=[...], ...)' — these are the PRE-RENAME names. Current shipped names are `Portal`, `to=` (not `peers=`), `portal=` (the @node kwarg, not `peers=`). The task's own bead title uses 'self.handoff' as the METHOD name (kept — 'handoff' is the reserved mesh-channel input key, per D-RESERVED-KEY, and reads naturally as a verb: 'self.handoff(...)'), but its kwarg `members=` should very likely become `to=` per-member peer lists, matching `Portal`'s own field name — do not resurrect `peers=`.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/forward.py:978-1137 -- _ModifierWrapCall + _EnsembleCall + _InterruptCall: the exemplar builder-call pattern (form-aware target, _materialize to Construct|Node + modifier, dedup via tracer occurrence counter)
- src/neograph/forward.py:1281-1298 -- _ForwardSelf.interrupt(): the exact method-shape to copy for self.handoff (capture tracer, return a _XxxCall)
- src/neograph/forward.py:413-425 -- _Tracer.record()/record_construct(): how nodes/sub-constructs get appended to _ordered; self.handoff's assembly-only path (no proxy in/out) should call these directly rather than going through _NodeCall.__call__
- src/neograph/modifiers.py:600-660 -- Portal class (to/route/max_hops/on_exhaust fields, is_dispatch discriminator, model_post_init mode validation) -- the modifier to attach unchanged
- examples/28_portal_swarm.py:238-268 (demo_surface_parity) -- canonical declarative/programmatic mesh IR: Node | Portal(to=[...]) per member, Construct(nodes=[...]) with no static edges between mesh members -- this is what the ForwardConstruct builder must reproduce
- examples/28_portal_swarm.py:94-121 -- @node(portal=[...], max_hops=...) per-member decorator sugar -- shows max_hops/on_exhaust are set on the ENTRY member only, others default
- docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md:133-142 -- D-FORWARD-EXEMPT judgment call, the origin decision text (pre-rename: 'peers=', 'self.handoff(members=[...], ...)')
- docs/design/portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md:176-182 -- restates D-FORWARD-EXEMPT as the origin of neograph-a37vk; 'nothing in v1's IR blocks it'
- docs/design/keymaker-design-review-2026-07-13.md:134-136 -- independent-review AGREE on D-FORWARD-EXEMPT, stronger than the di_inputs analogy (genuinely no static dataflow to thread)

## Risks & Edge Cases
- **members= vs to= per-member ambiguity (design decision needed, not a doc contradiction)**: the design docs never fully specify self.handoff's signature (it was explicitly deferred as fast-follow with no API sketch). Implementer must decide how each member's peer list is supplied -- e.g. `self.handoff(members=[self.triage, self.billing], to={'triage': ['billing','technical'], 'billing': []}, max_hops=6, on_exhaust='error')`, applying `Portal(to=to[name], max_hops=max_hops if name==entry else default, on_exhaust=...)` per member. This mirrors Portal's own field names 1:1 (max_hops only meaningful on the entry member, matching the @node sugar's existing rule) rather than reinventing.
- **max_hops-only-on-entry validation already exists in Portal/its validator** (`_validation_portal.py`, `_check_portal_mesh`) -- do not re-validate in the builder; let the existing mesh-assembly validation catch a misconfigured builder call at compile time, same as declarative/@node surfaces.
- **Proxy-tracer dataflow**: self.handoff members are NOT threaded through proxies (no `(result)` call like self.interrupt(...)(result)) since D-FORWARD-EXEMPT establishes there is no static dataflow. The builder call itself (not a returned callable requiring __call__) should likely just record the members directly, unlike every other self.X() builder in this file which returns a callable expecting a proxy argument. This is a genuine shape difference from the _ModifierWrapCall family -- flag for implementer, don't force-fit the proxy-call convention.
- **Three-surface parity claim in the review ('AGREE... parity rule fully satisfied') was made BEFORE self.handoff existed** -- it argued ForwardConstruct's ABSENCE was acceptable, not that a future self.handoff would trivially reuse the interrupt/ensemble shape. Don't over-read 'parity satisfied' as implying self.handoff must look identical to self.interrupt; it only means the exemption itself doesn't break the parity rule.
## Codebase Disease Scan (a37vk)
Pattern: a self.<modifier> ForwardConstruct builder method that bypasses _Tracer.record()/record_construct() (the single recording mechanism) or collides in name with an existing self.X method.
Scan command: `grep -n "def [a-z_]*(self" src/neograph/forward.py`
Total instances found: 0 collisions -- no existing self.handoff method; all existing self.X builder methods (self.interrupt at :1281, plus ensemble/loop/each per class definitions) are the only builder-shaped methods on _ForwardSelf

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | forward.py:1281 (self.interrupt) | _ForwardSelf builder method | ALLOWLIST | exemplar to copy, not a conflict |
| — | (no self.handoff exists yet) | N/A | N/A | greenfield addition, confirmed no naming collision |

N/A overall -- this is a new-feature research scan (self.handoff doesn't exist yet), confirming a clean addition point with the correct exemplar (self.interrupt) to copy per the design field's note that this needs a genuinely different (non-proxy) call shape.
## Architect Review

- [MEDIUM] Finding: The plan contradicts itself on the load-bearing flatten-vs-nest question, and one branch VIOLATES the stated Core Invariant. Step 1 + the Findings say 'collect self.<x> Node refs into the tracer _ordered list (via tracer.record)' — i.e. flatten each member directly into the ForwardConstruct's own construct. Step 4 says 'Emit the mesh as a Construct(name=..., nodes=[member | Portal(...)]) ... record_construct(sub)' — i.e. a NESTED sub-construct. Since ForwardConstruct IS-A Construct (forward.py:135) and its final nodes come from tracer._ordered (forward.py:504-506), record_construct-ing a wrapper yields Construct(nodes=[Construct(nodes=[triage|Portal, billing|Portal])]) — one nesting level deeper than the declarative demo_surface_parity target Construct(nodes=[triage|Portal, billing|Portal]) (examples/28_portal_swarm.py:255-260). That is NOT the 'IDENTICAL IR' the Core Invariant demands, and it inserts a LangGraph subgraph boundary that Command(goto=<peer>) must now cross (only partially supported per commit 481ee34 'cross-subconstruct mesh via parent-scoped bubble-up'). Suggestion: pin the approach decisively to FLATTEN — for each member build 'bare_node | Portal(...)' (bare node from the _NodeCall._node the self.<name> lookup returns, forward.py:1158-1164) and tracer.record() it directly into _ordered; do NOT wrap in a Construct and do NOT call record_construct. Then the ForwardConstruct's own nodes list contains the members directly, byte-for-byte with declarative. The step-5 parity test is the right forcing function and would catch the nested variant — keep it, and assert node-list equality at the outer level (not one construct deep).

- [MEDIUM] Finding: Naive per-member Portal construction will trip the entry-only validator. _check_portal_mesh (_validation_portal.py:194-205) rejects ANY non-entry member whose Portal has max_hops OR on_exhaust in model_fields_set — and Portal is a Pydantic model, so passing on_exhaust='error' (even the signature default) to a non-entry member's Portal() puts it in model_fields_set and raises 'on_exhaust ... is entry-only'. Step 3's pseudocode 'Portal(to=to[name], max_hops=..., on_exhaust=...)' per member would therefore fail assembly for every declarative-equivalent 2+ member mesh. Suggestion: build kwargs conditionally — entry gets Portal(to=to[entry], max_hops=max_hops, on_exhaust=on_exhaust); every non-entry member gets Portal(to=to[name]) with NO max_hops/on_exhaust passed at all. Entry = the member recorded first (validator's entry is node_members[0], the first in construct order), so the builder must record the entry member first (honor an explicit entry= kwarg by reordering).

- [LOW] Finding: self.handoff's signature is still marked 'design decision needed' (Risks section) though the plan already proposes the right shape. Suggestion: just commit to self.handoff(members=[self.a, self.b], to={'a': [...], 'b': [...]}, max_hops=..., on_exhaust=..., entry=None) with 'to' keyed by member name (mirrors Portal.to 1:1; do NOT resurrect peers=). No further design input needed.

- [LOW] Finding: Mid-pipeline mesh embedding (threading the mesh's output into a downstream forward() node) is undefined — self.handoff records directly and returns no proxy, so there is no dataflow handle for anything after it. Suggestion: explicitly scope v1 self.handoff to a terminal / whole-graph mesh (matching demo_surface_parity, where the mesh IS the graph) and say so in the docstring; defer mid-pipeline embedding.

Reuse/soundness check (survives attack): the plan correctly reuses Portal unchanged (modifiers.py:600), the single validation path _check_portal_mesh (which DOES recurse per-level, _construct_validation.py:346-348), and _Tracer.record (forward.py:413) — no reinvention, no new IR field, no new Command site. The D-FORWARD-EXEMPT no-proxy call shape is correctly identified as a genuine departure from the _ModifierWrapCall family. No naming collision (scan confirmed 0). Those parts are sound.

## Core Invariant

A routing decision made inside an isolated sub-construct that names a parent-level Portal peer must reach that peer as a BOUNDARY-PORT handoff on the parent mesh -- never by the parent graph reaching into the sub-construct's interior, and never by the sub-construct's isolated invoke() mutating parent control flow directly. Command( construction stays inside the existing G1 monopoly (factory.py/runner.py only). See docs/design/do0d9-parent-scoped-bubbleup-2026-07-23.md for the full ratified doc -- this field is a summary pointer, not a duplicate; read the doc for the resolved Q1-Q7 checklist, the rejected alternatives, and the spike.

## STALE: the previous Implementation Plan below (8 steps, written 2026-07-14/16) is SUPERSEDED

It described the literal `Command(graph=Command.PARENT, ...)` mechanism, which was spiked and PROVEN DEAD (2026-07-15, see NOTES) -- do not follow steps 3/4 below, they describe a mechanism that does not work. Kept only for history; the CURRENT implementation plan is docs/design/do0d9-parent-scoped-bubbleup-2026-07-23.md §3.1 (What do0d9 actually builds -- the delta), which lists the 5 Node-typed sites to extend (post-independent-review corrections applied 2026-07-23):

1. `factory.py` -- new `make_portal_subgraph_fn` (sibling of `make_portal_fn`), wraps `make_subgraph_fn`'s sync/async twins, pipes the returned update through the EXISTING `_portal_route_to_command`. Sole new Command(-adjacent site; already inside the G1 monopoly.
2. `_validation_portal.py` -- relax the blanket `isinstance(member, Node)` rejection (`:86-95`) to admit a Construct member whose declared `.output` matches the mesh payload type. MUST also fix `member.outputs` (`:104`) to route through `_declared_output(member)` (Construct has no `.outputs` field) -- this will AttributeError otherwise. The reserved-`handoff`-key check (`:241-252`) operates on a Node-only-narrowed list and should stay Node-scoped by design (a Construct's boundary port is `.input`/`.output`, not a fan-in `inputs` dict).
3. `_ir_normalize.py` (guard G3, single-writer for `handoff_channel`) -- `:264` and `:280` both `isinstance(item, Node)`-gate and currently EXCLUDE a Construct mesh member; must be extended so a Portal-carrying Construct member is collected into `portal_members` and gets a `handoff_channel` key threaded to it (via the SAME `_add_subgraph` recursive-compile-kwarg channel as `checkpointer`/`runtime`/`scripted_lookup` -- not a new field on Construct).
4. `_wiring.py` -- `_contiguous_portal_mesh`'s collection loop and `_add_portal_mesh`'s `members: list[Node]` typing / `entry_label_map` (keyed off `member.mode`, which Construct lacks) both need a Construct-aware branch dispatching to `make_portal_subgraph_fn` instead of `make_portal_fn`.
5. Fixtures + example: should_pass/should_fail check-fixtures for a cross-boundary peer reference (valid + invalid target), and a runnable example mirroring 28/29's Portal showcase pattern.

Acceptance for closing do0d9: the design doc's mechanism implemented across all 5 sites above, PLUS a real end-to-end test proving an ACTUAL `Construct` object sitting inside a `Portal` member list routes correctly (the design doc's own spike used a plain `@node` wrapper hand-invoking the sub-construct, which does NOT exercise sites 2-4 above -- see design doc §8 finding 5). Three-surface parity per AGENTS.md; ForwardConstruct stays exempt (D-FORWARD-EXEMPT, inherited unchanged, until neograph-a37vk gives it a handoff builder).

## Findings
- REUSE TARGET (v1 lowering to extend, not re-derive): Portal mesh lowering already produces `Command(goto=...)` at ONE construct level — `make_portal_fn` (src/neograph/factory.py:103-207) builds the wrapper, `_add_portal_mesh` (src/neograph/_wiring.py:723-789) wires `add_node(member.name, member_fn, destinations=...)` with a pass-through `__handoff_exit_<entry>` re-join node. D-MESH-LEVEL's ratified rationale ("Lower to Command(goto) so v2 cross-boundary needs no re-lowering", decision log table row) means do0d9 extends THIS wrapper/factory, not a new lowering mechanism.
- REUSE TARGET (mesh-assembly validation cluster): `_check_portal_mesh` in src/neograph/_validation_portal.py:40-254 is the SINGLE place mesh rules live (per AGENTS.md's single-sited-validation-cluster discipline). The CURRENT v1 rule that do0d9 must relax/extend is the shape check at lines 86-95: `if not isinstance(member, Node): raise ConstructError(...'Portal mesh member is a Construct'..."mesh members must be sibling Nodes (D-MESH-LEVEL)")`. do0d9 turns this hard rejection into a validated cross-boundary case instead of ripping it out wholesale — v1's "same-level sibling Node" rule still holds for the SAME-LEVEL mesh; do0d9 adds the NEW case (a peer reference that crosses INTO or OUT OF a sub-construct boundary).
- REUSE TARGET (sub-construct boundary machinery): `_add_subgraph` (src/neograph/compiler.py:438-497) + `make_subgraph_fn` (src/neograph/_subconstruct.py:57-207) are the existing single-typed-entry/output boundary-port machinery (Construct.input/output, construct.py:113-123) that any cross-boundary addressing must hook into, per the ratified portal-addressability doc (docs/design/portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md) mechanism 1 (entry-label map) framing.
- CRITICAL ARCHITECTURE FINDING (the actual hard part of do0d9, not yet resolved by any doc): neograph's sub-construct compilation is NOT LangGraph's native subgraph-as-node nesting. `make_subgraph_fn`'s `subgraph_node`/`asubgraph_node` (src/neograph/_subconstruct.py:182-199) call `sub_graph.invoke(sub_input, config=config)` — a plain, isolated, top-level Pregel invocation from inside a RunnableLambda that the PARENT adds as an ordinary node — NOT `parent_builder.add_node(name, compiled_child_graph_object)` (the native form LangGraph's own subgraph docs assume). LangGraph's `Command.PARENT` bubble-up mechanism (verified in installed langgraph 1.x: `.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/langgraph/pregel/_retry.py:544-631`, `_io.py:56-59`) works by an inner node's Pregel task-loop catching `cmd.graph == Command.PARENT`, rewriting it to the checkpoint-namespace-derived parent segment (`_checkpoint_ns_for_parent_command(ns)`), and RE-RAISING as a bubble exception that the enclosing Pregel task loop (one level up) catches again, repeating until `cmd.graph` matches the CURRENT graph's own namespace. This bubble is namespace-string-driven (`config['configurable'][CONFIG_KEY_CHECKPOINT_NS]`), not object-identity driven, so it MAY already work through neograph's isolated-invoke wrapper (config is passed through unmodified at src/neograph/_subconstruct.py:150/188/198, and nothing in neograph catches/swallows an exception around the `sub_graph.invoke`/`ainvoke` call — grep confirmed zero `except` blocks there). But this has NEVER been exercised in this codebase (zero hits for `Command(graph=` / `graph=Command.PARENT` in tests/ or src/) and is genuinely uncertain without an empirical spike, because `sub_graph.invoke()` is its own fresh top-level Pregel run (own recursion_limit, own stream_mode) rather than a task dispatched BY the parent's own Pregel scheduler — whether LangGraph's `Pregel.invoke()` entry point respects and threads an INCOMING checkpoint_ns from config to continue the parent's namespace (vs. resetting to a fresh root namespace) is the crux unresolved question.
- Command construction monopoly: guard G1 (`TestCommandConstructionMonopoly`, tests/test_guards_assembly.py) restricts `Command(` construction to factory.py and runner.py ONLY — any new Command.PARENT emission must land in one of those two files, not _wiring.py or _subconstruct.py.
- The design doc (docs/design/portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md) explicitly scopes mechanism 1 (entry-label map) as WITHIN one compile() level, and calls out do0d9's Command.PARENT mechanism as the deliberately-separate cross-boundary case (see "A note on lowering substrate" + mechanism-1 section) — confirms do0d9 is not expected to reuse mechanism 1 verbatim, just to keep the two textually separate, which the doc already does.
- CURRENT vs DEPRECATED: no deprecated pattern here — this is a net-new capability layered onto the still-current v1 mesh machinery (Portal, formerly Keymaker; the rename is already complete, use Portal/handoff terminology throughout, never 'Keymaker' except when quoting the historic banner-preserved docs).

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/_validation_portal.py:86-95 -- the CURRENT hard `ConstructError` for a Construct mesh member (D-MESH-LEVEL v1 rule); do0d9 must extend this function (not inline elsewhere) to admit the validated cross-boundary case.
- src/neograph/factory.py:103-207 (`make_portal_fn`) -- the exemplar same-level `Command(goto=...)` lowering incl. fail-loud invalid-target (`ExecutionError`) and hop-budget accounting; the pattern any cross-boundary `Command(graph=Command.PARENT, goto=...)` wrapper should mirror for consistency (same channel-key/hop-count conventions).
- src/neograph/_wiring.py:723-789 (`_add_portal_mesh`) + :697-720 (`_contiguous_portal_mesh`) -- mesh wiring/collection walk; a cross-boundary member would need either a new collection rule here or a parallel `_add_portal_mesh_cross_boundary`-style helper, kept in this file (compiler-layer, matches Command-construction-adjacent placement even though guard G1 restricts literal Command( to factory.py/runner.py).
- src/neograph/_subconstruct.py:182-199 -- `subgraph_node`/`asubgraph_node`: the isolated `sub_graph.invoke()` call with NO exception handling around it; the mechanism whose Command.PARENT-bubble-compatibility is the open empirical question above.
- src/neograph/compiler.py:438-497 (`_add_subgraph`) -- sub-construct compile entry, fail-loud `sub.input is None` check; the existing boundary-port machinery to extend.
- src/neograph/_state_keys.py:126-145 (`StateKeys.handoff_payload`/`handoff_hops`) -- reuse verbatim for any cross-boundary channel/counter naming; no new state-key scheme per AGENTS.md's `neo_`-prefix discipline.
- tests/test_guards_assembly.py (`TestCommandConstructionMonopoly`, guard G1) -- pins where `Command(` may be constructed; extend/verify against, don't bypass.
- docs/design/portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md -- ratified Core Invariant doc (see notes above); cite verbatim, don't re-derive.
- docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md -- D-MESH-LEVEL entry (verbatim: "Peers = sibling Nodes at same construct level; sub-construct member / Command.PARENT cross-boundary = ConstructError. Lower to Command(goto) so v2 cross-boundary needs no re-lowering.") is the direct origin/justification for do0d9; do not re-derive.
- docs/design/dynamic-handoff-research-2026-07-13.md:112-130,536-556,620-642,769-774 -- deepest existing research on Command.PARENT semantics + langgraph-swarm's `create_handoff_tool` precedent; read before designing the cross-boundary wrapper.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- The single biggest risk: do0d9 could be implemented as "just add graph=Command.PARENT to the wrapper" without first spiking whether neograph's isolated-invoke sub-construct architecture actually propagates LangGraph's checkpoint-namespace bubble-up correctly. If it does NOT propagate (e.g. `sub_graph.invoke()` resets checkpoint_ns to a fresh root), the mechanism will silently do nothing OR raise a LangGraph-internal error ("no parent graph") at runtime with no compile-time signal — a genuine SILENT SEAM the North-star invariant explicitly forbids. Recommend an isolated LangGraph-only (no neograph IR) spike FIRST: two nested `StateGraph`s where the child is invoked via a wrapping RunnableLambda exactly like `_subconstruct.py` does, one inner node returns `Command(graph=Command.PARENT, goto=<parent_peer>)`, and confirm empirically whether the parent-level goto fires. This determines whether do0d9 is (a) a straightforward wrapper extension, or (b) requires first migrating the relevant sub-constructs to LangGraph's native `add_node(name, compiled_child_graph)` nesting (a much bigger architectural change, likely needing its own decomposition/bead).
- Symmetric case ambiguity: "cross-subconstruct mesh" could mean (i) a peer INSIDE a sub-construct routing OUT to a parent-level peer (Command.PARENT literally as named), (ii) a parent-level peer routing INTO a sub-construct's entry (this is arguably mechanism-1's entry-label map territory, not Command.PARENT), or (iii) two sibling sub-constructs at the SAME parent level acting as whole-Construct mesh members (peer = a Construct, not a Node — currently rejected by the isinstance(member, Node) check). The bead title says "Portal: cross-subconstruct mesh via Command.PARENT" but the decision log's D-MESH-LEVEL phrasing ("sub-construct member... cross-boundary") is ambiguous between (i) and (iii). Needs disambiguation before implementation — likely (i) is the literal Command.PARENT case and (iii) is a separate, simpler "whole-Construct-as-mesh-member" extension that does NOT need Command.PARENT (it could lower to a same-level Command(goto=<subconstruct's field_name>) since sub-constructs already compile to ordinary nodes at the parent level via `_add_subgraph`). NEEDS USER INPUT: confirm which of (i)/(ii)/(iii) — or "all three" — do0d9's acceptance criteria actually require; the bead body's one-liner is a design pointer, not a spec.
- Async: `_subconstruct.py` has dual sync/async twins (`subgraph_node`/`asubgraph_node`); any Command.PARENT-bubble compatibility must be verified on BOTH `sub_graph.invoke` and `sub_graph.ainvoke` paths (Phase-1 H2 invariant: async must propagate through every nesting level) — do not spike only the sync path.
- Checkpointer interaction: `_add_subgraph` threads `checkpointer=checkpointer` recursively into the child `compile()` call (compiler.py:474-482) — if a bubble-up path requires checkpoint_ns continuity, the presence/absence of a real checkpointer (vs None) on the child compile may change behavior; the spike should test both with and without a checkpointer.
- No existing test/example exercises `Command(graph=...)` or `Command.PARENT` anywhere in this repo (grep confirmed zero hits in tests/ and src/) — there is no prior art within neograph to copy; the langgraph-swarm precedent (external library) is the closest analog, cited in dynamic-handoff-research-2026-07-13.md:150.
SPIKE FINDING (2026-07-15): Command(graph=Command.PARENT) does NOT propagate through neograph's isolated sub_graph.invoke() sub-construct compilation. Standalone LangGraph-only spike, both handling strategies: (a) wrapper CATCHES the raised ParentCommand -> escape is swallowed, the static successor edge fires, the parent-level peer never runs (SILENT SEAM — North Star forbidden); (b) wrapper lets it PROPAGATE -> uncaught exception, outer Pregel does NOT interpret it as routing. Command.PARENT is a NATIVE subgraph-nesting feature; neograph deliberately uses isolated invoke for state hygiene, so the parent graph has no structural knowledge of the child. Zero Command(graph= usages existed in the repo — this path was never exercised.

D-MESH-LEVEL FALSIFIED: the v1 'lower to Command(goto) so v2 cross-boundary needs no re-lowering' forward-compat claim was based on an untested assumption. The lowering (Command(goto) vs path_map) was never the blocker; the propagation mechanism is.

RE-SCOPE (design-first): do0d9 is NOT literal Command.PARENT. Mechanism = neograph-native parent-scoped bubble-up — the sub-construct wrapper CATCHES the escape intent (explicit, not silent), reads its target, and writes it onto the parent mesh channel (StateKeys.handoff_payload) so the parent mesh routes on it via the normal Portal path. This preserves isolated-invoke state hygiene and is Mechanism 2 (mesh-transparent-exit, ozrct) extended across the boundary. REJECTED alternative: switch sub-construct compilation to native LangGraph subgraph-as-node nesting — trades the state-isolated boundary-port invariant for one feature. do0d9 now needs a design step (spike done -> design -> implement) before implementation; it must NOT proceed through disease-scan/review/implement as an impl task.
## Scope decision (2026-07-16, user-directed)
The literal Command.PARENT shape (i) is a PROVEN SILENT SEAM: spiked and confirmed it does not propagate through neograph's isolated sub_graph.invoke() wrapper -- catching it swallows the escape, letting crashes propagate uncaught. This falsifies D-MESH-LEVEL's 'lower to Command(goto) so v2 needs no re-lowering' bet. Recorded in docs/design/portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md (Mechanism 1 section, 2026-07-15 correction) so the disproven mechanism does not propagate to whoever implements this next.

do0d9 is RE-SCOPED: a neograph-native parent-scoped bubble-up. The wrapper catches the escape intent and writes it onto the parent mesh channel (StateKeys.handoff_payload) for the parent mesh to route on -- NOT literal Command(graph=Command.PARENT,...). Shape (iii) (whole-Construct same-level mesh members) and shape (ii) (parent-peer routing into a sub-construct entry) are explicitly NOT this bead's scope -- (ii) belongs to the entry-label-map mechanism (mechanism 1 in the addressability doc).

title: Portal: named meshes (>1 mesh per construct level)
description: v1 allows one mesh per construct level (D-SINGLE-MESH) because two disjoint meshes make the reserved 'handoff' input key ambiguous. Add named meshes so the reserved key can be disambiguated per mesh. Deferred from KEYMAKER v1 (epic neograph-t1f7z). Cite: docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md + docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md.
design:
## Refined Plan (post-review)

Core Invariant: a construct that validates must lower EXACTLY as validated -- grouping (which members belong to which named mesh) must be computed by exactly ONE shared helper, never three independently-inferred groupings across validator/normalizer/compiler that could silently diverge.

Resolution to MEDIUM (mandatory shared helper): the grouping helper is MANDATORY (not 'if practical') at all three consumer sites: _validation_portal.py (mesh validation), _ir_normalize.py (handoff_channel writer), and _wiring.py (mesh collector/compiler walk). Place it in an import-safe NEUTRAL module reachable by all three without an import cycle (verify against test_guards_assembly.py's import-DAG guard before picking a location -- modifiers.py next to the Portal class is the natural home since all three sites already import Portal-related symbols from there). The helper defines BOTH the group key (Portal.name, or a synthesized default) AND the None-handling rule (all name=None members belong to one default group) in exactly one place. Add a structural guard test (following this file's existing AST/grep-based guard conventions) pinning that grouping is computed ONLY via that helper -- not re-derived inline at any of the three sites.

Resolved (LOW): reserved-key disambiguation is grouping-based (not a handoff_<meshname> syntax change), per design doc S3.3 -- each node belongs to at most one mesh, so grouping alone disambiguates the reserved 'handoff' key. Add a model_post_init check rejecting name= on a dispatch-mode Portal (is_dispatch=True, not a mesh member) with a should_fail fixture.

Runtime test requirement: the multi-mesh test must explicitly assert non-interference of the two meshes' hop counters AND distinct exit-node names -- 'falls out for free' from the shared grouping is a claim to PROVE, not assume.
notes:
## Findings
- Current state: Portal enforces D-SINGLE-MESH — exactly ONE mesh (one connected component under the peer relation) per construct level. Enforced in `src/neograph/_validation_portal.py` (`_check_portal_mesh`), which today:
  - collects ALL Portal-modified (non-dispatch) siblings at a level into one `members` list (no grouping key),
  - requires them CONTIGUOUS in `Construct.nodes` (single `lo..hi` span, :121-130),
  - requires ONE connected component reachable from `members[0]` (entry) via the undirected peer relation (:169-192) — this is the literal D-SINGLE-MESH check; two disjoint components today raise "two disjoint Portal meshes at one construct level".
  - runs uniform-payload / route-field / reserved-key / entry-only-knob checks over that single `members` list.
- The reserved `handoff` inputs key ambiguity (the reason D-SINGLE-MESH exists) is concrete in the IR normalizer, NOT the validator: `src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py:257-273` collects ALL Portal members at a level into one `portal_members` list and computes ONE `handoff_channel = StateKeys.handoff_payload(field_name_for(portal_members[0].name))` — i.e. it blindly takes the FIRST Portal member across the whole level as "the" entry and stamps that single channel key onto every Portal member at the level. With two disjoint meshes this is actively wrong (members of the second mesh would get the first mesh's channel key), which is exactly why the validator forbids the scenario today rather than leaving it to silently misroute.
- Compiler-side mesh detection is ALSO single-mesh-shaped: `_contiguous_portal_mesh` (`src/neograph/_wiring.py:700-725`) walks forward from an entry while `classify_modifiers(item)[0] == ModifierCombo.PORTAL` (any Portal member, no name/group distinction) and stops only at a non-Portal item or a dispatch-mode Portal. Two named meshes placed back-to-back with NO plain node between them would currently be silently glommed into one `members` list by this collector — a second gap to close, not just the validator.
- State-key generation (`StateKeys.handoff_hops` / `StateKeys.handoff_payload`, `src/neograph/_state_keys.py:129-146`) is already keyed by an arbitrary `field_name: str` (currently always the mesh entry's producer field) — no format change needed for named meshes; it already supports parameterizing by whatever field the normalizer chooses to pass, so two distinct entries naturally get two distinct field names TODAY. The only thing missing is a GROUPING key (a mesh name) so the normalizer/validator/compiler agree on which Portal members belong to which mesh, instead of assuming one global group.
- `Portal` (`src/neograph/modifiers.py:600-670`) has NO `name=` field today. Confirmed via direct read — this task is fully unstarted, no partial work exists.
- Design doc explicitly scopes this as v2, deferred from KEYMAKER v1 T8 consolidation: `docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md` §3.1 (D-SINGLE-MESH judgment call, lines 166-172) and `docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md` line 235 ("D-SINGLE-MESH | One mesh per construct level ... Named meshes = v2 | SHIPPED | Ratify; named meshes filed").
- Most recent related Portal work (current-way precedent to copy the STYLE of, not the content): `docs/design/do0d9-parent-scoped-bubbleup-2026-07-23.md` (cross-subconstruct mesh via parent-scoped bubble-up, landed 2026-07-23, commit 481ee34) — shows the sanctioned pattern for extending `_validation_portal.py` / `_ir_normalize.py` / `_wiring.py` together as one coherent change, keeping the single-writer invariants (G1 Command monopoly, G2 StateKeys centralization, G3 handoff_param/handoff_channel sole-writer in `_ir_normalize.py`) intact rather than adding a second mechanism.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/_validation_portal.py:40-260 (`_check_portal_mesh`) -- the single mesh-assembly validator; the exemplar to EXTEND (group by mesh name, run existing per-group checks, add a NEW cross-group rule: peers must resolve within the SAME named group) rather than rewrite.
- src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py:239-295 (`normalize_ir`, the `portal_members` collection + single `handoff_channel` computation at :257-273) -- must become per-named-group (one `handoff_channel` per group, keyed off that group's own entry), still the sole writer of `handoff_param`/`handoff_channel` (G3).
- src/neograph/_wiring.py:700-725 (`_contiguous_portal_mesh`) -- compiler-side contiguous-run collector; must stop the run at a mesh-NAME boundary in addition to today's non-Portal/dispatch-mode stops, or two adjacent named meshes will be merged.
- src/neograph/_wiring.py:790+ (`_add_portal_mesh`) -- per-mesh lowering (Command(goto), destinations=, exit node); called once per detected mesh already (see compiler.py:243-277 walk) — should need only the entry-detection fix above, not new lowering logic, since it already lowers exactly the `members` list it's handed.
- src/neograph/compiler.py:243-277 -- the mesh-aware compile walk (dispatches `_add_portal_mesh` once per detected contiguous mesh via `meshed: set[int]` bookkeeping); already loops, so multiple meshes at a level should fall out for free ONCE `_contiguous_portal_mesh` correctly bounds each group.
- src/neograph/_state_keys.py:129-146 (`StateKeys.handoff_hops`/`handoff_payload`) -- already parameterized by `field_name`; reuse as-is per named group's entry field, no signature change needed.
- src/neograph/modifiers.py:600-670 (`Portal` class) -- add the new `name: str | None = None` field here (mirrors how `route`/`max_hops` etc. already live as plain fields); `None` should mean 'the level's single/default mesh' so existing single-mesh pipelines keep working with zero change (back-compat via a synthesized default group key, e.g. the level's first-seen Portal member's node name, or a fixed sentinel).
- docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md:153-260 (§3 runtime contract) -- the mesh/reserved-key/channel design section this task revises; the reserved-key rationale in §3.3 is the exact ambiguity this task resolves.
- docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md:130-140,235 -- D10 (channel-read-side, entry-keyed) and the D-SINGLE-MESH ledger row this task closes.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Reserved-key disambiguation is grouping-based, not naming-based: since a node belongs to at most ONE Portal group, the reserved `inputs={'handoff': T}` key does NOT need to change syntactically (no 'handoff_<meshname>' key) — the normalizer just needs to know WHICH group a member is in to stamp the right `handoff_channel`. Confirm this reading with the maintainer if the fefar bead intends a syntax change to the reserved key itself; the design doc's phrasing ("disambiguated per mesh") is consistent with grouping-based disambiguation, but double-check before implementing.
- Back-compat default group key: existing single-mesh pipelines set no `name=`; the implementation must synthesize a stable default group (e.g. all `name=None` Portal members at one level form the implicit default group) so current examples/tests (28_portal_swarm, test_keymaker.py-equivalent suites) do not need updating.
- Cross-group peer validation is a NEW rule not present today: a peer named in `to=[...]` that exists as a sibling but belongs to a DIFFERENT named mesh must be a `ConstructError" (today the validator only checks 'peer exists as a sibling' + 'peer is Portal-modified' + implicitly enforces same-mesh via the single-mesh-only connected-component check). title: Portal: agent/act mesh members
description: v1 rejects agent/act members at assembly (D-MEMBER-MODES) because they compile to a multi-node ReAct cycle (_agent_cycle.py) whose terminal hop needs separate plumbing to emit the mesh Command(goto). Wire the terminal-hop handoff so LLM-swarm members can be full agents. Deferred from KEYMAKER v1 (epic neograph-t1f7z). Cite: docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md + docs/design/keymaker-decision-log-2026-07-13.md.
design:
## Core Invariant
Runtime routing operates on BOUNDARY PORTS, never region interiors (docs/design/portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md): an agent/act mesh member's Portal-visible identity is its single declared entry (`{member.name}__agent`) and single reconverging exit (`{member.name}__parse`), never the interior `{member.name}__tools`/loopback nodes — every Command(goto=...) that targets this member, from any peer OR from the mesh's own static entry edge, MUST resolve through the entry, and every Command(goto=...) this member emits MUST originate from the exit, keeping the class of broken states (a jump into a ReAct cycle's interior) permanently unrepresentable, exactly like Portal already guarantees for atomic members.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Extract, don't duplicate, the Command-emission logic.** In `src/neograph/factory.py`, lift `make_portal_fn`'s inline `_to_command` closure (lines ~168-204) into a standalone, reusable factory.py-local function (e.g. `_portal_route_to_command(update, state, *, payload_field, route_field, valid_targets, channel_key, count_field, max_hops, on_exhaust, exit_name, node_name, entry_name)`), called from both the existing atomic-member wrapper AND the new agent/act path below. This keeps 100% of the budget/target-validation/channel-write logic single-sourced. G1 (`TestCommandConstructionMonopoly`) already forces this to live in factory.py — do not move it to `_wiring.py`/`_agent_cycle.py`.

2. **New factory.py function wraps the ReAct cycle's parse-body callables.** Add `make_portal_agent_cycle_fn(node, portal, entry_field, exit_name, *, max_hops, on_exhaust, entry_name, runtime, tool_factory_lookup) -> dict` in factory.py that: imports `make_agent_cycle_bodies` from `neograph._agent_cycle` (module-level import is safe — no reverse dependency exists), calls it to get the agent/tools/parse sync+async pairs + router, and returns a dict shaped like `_add_agent_cycle`'s `parts` PLUS Command-wrapped parse callables (parse_sync/parse_async wrapped so their returned update dict is piped through `_portal_route_to_command` before being returned). The agent/tools nodes and the 3-way router are UNCHANGED (reused verbatim — Mechanism 2 only touches the exit node).

3. **Extend `_wiring.py`'s mesh wiring via ONE shared helper, not a copy.** In `_add_portal_mesh` (`_wiring.py:723-788`), branch per member on `member.mode in ('agent','act')`. **COMMITTED (refine, neograph-vihe7.29): do not copy `_add_agent_cycle`'s ~95 lines wholesale.** Factor the shared agent/tools/router/loopback wiring (identical between the non-mesh and mesh cases) into ONE internal helper parametrized by `(parse-body builder, destinations=)`, called by BOTH `_add_agent_cycle` (non-mesh, plain dict return) and the new mesh path (Command-wrapped parse body + `destinations=` set on the `{member}__parse` add_node call, per LangGraph's requirement that any Command-returning node declares `destinations=`, mirroring the atomic member's `graph.add_node(member.name, fn, destinations=...)`). Only the parse node's registration (Command-wrapped body vs plain dict) and the `destinations=` argument diverge — every other line (agent/tools node registration, gate_tools_when arm, 3-way router, tools->agent loopback) is identical between the two callers.

4. **Build the entry-label map (Mechanism 1) scoped to the mesh**, as a DX-peer-name -> LangGraph-entry-node-name dict, computed once before the per-member loop: atomic members map to themselves (`member.name -> member.name`), agent/act members map to their cycle entry (`member.name -> f'{member.name}__agent'`). Use this map for (a) every OTHER member's `destinations=` tuple and Command `goto=` target resolution, AND (b) **the mesh's own static entry edge** — `_add_portal_mesh`'s `prev -> entry.name` wiring (`_wiring.py:783-786`) MUST ALSO resolve through this same map when the ENTRY member itself is agent/act (its real LangGraph node is `{entry}__agent`, not `entry.name`); this is not a separate mechanism, it is the same map applied to the entry as well as every peer. The agent/act member's own registration name stays `{member.name}__agent` (LangGraph node identity), while its DX-facing name for routing purposes is `member.name`. Build this as a plain local dict for nnds9's scope (mesh-local, not a graph-wide compiled artifact like schema_fingerprint — that graph-wide generalization is left as a code-comment pointer for do0d9/a37vk to pick up, not built here, to avoid scope creep beyond 'unlock agent/act members').

5. **Relax (narrow, don't delete) the D-MEMBER-MODES rejection.** In `src/neograph/_validation_portal.py`'s `_check_portal_mesh` (lines 96-104), remove the blanket `member.mode in ('agent','act')` rejection. Every other existing rule in the same function (uniform payload via `_declared_output`, route-field type/Literal check, dict-outputs-forbidden, contiguity, peer existence, single-mesh-per-level, entry-only `max_hops`/`on_exhaust`, reserved `handoff`-key typing) already reads `Node.outputs`/`Node.modifier_set` mode-independently and needs NO changes — confirm this with a should_pass fixture mixing agent+scripted members before touching anything else (guard-first: write the fixture, watch it fail against the OLD rejection, then remove the rejection). **The should_pass fixture set must include BOTH shapes: (a) a scripted entry + agent/act peer (tests peer-resolution through the entry-label map) AND (b) an agent/act ENTRY + scripted peer (tests the static entry-edge resolution from step 4b) — testing only (a) structurally dodges the entry-is-agent case (refine, neograph-vihe7.29).**

6. **Runner recursion-limit floor — concrete formula (refine, neograph-vihe7.29).** `runner.py`'s `_ensure_agent_recursion_limit` currently sums one `agent_cost` per agent NODE (via `iter_nodes`) plus `max_hops` per mesh — this budgets K hop-supersteps but an agent/act mesh member re-entered K times via mesh hops actually costs up to `K * (max_iters * 2 + overhead)` supersteps (each hop re-runs the full agent<->tools loop before the parse node ever emits its Command). **Pin the floor as: for each agent/act mesh member, multiply that member's per-cycle agent_cost by the mesh's max_hops (instead of adding a flat max_hops count), and add this to the existing floor calculation.** This gives the implementer a concrete formula and lets the checkpoint test in step 7 assert the floor is sufficient rather than guessing.

7. **Tests, guard-first per AGENTS.md convention:**
   - **CORRECTED TARGET (refine, neograph-vihe7.29): retire `tests/test_portal_validation.py:249` `test_agent_member_rejected`** (a unit test pinning the OLD D-MEMBER-MODES rejection) — invert it to assert the agent/act member now succeeds, or delete it if superseded by the new should_pass fixture. (The plan previously named a nonexistent check-fixture path `tests/check_fixtures/should_fail/portal_agent_member_rejected.py` — no such file exists; `test_agent_member_rejected` is the real pin to retire.)
   - New `should_pass/portal_agent_mesh_member.py` fixture(s): per step 5, BOTH the scripted-entry+agent-peer AND agent-entry+scripted-peer shapes.
   - `tests/test_portal_validation.py` (or wherever mesh runtime tests live): new runtime test proving an agent/act member routes correctly (Command(goto) lands on the peer's real entry node, not a nonexistent bare name), the exit node reconverges identically to an atomic member's exit, the static entry edge resolves correctly when the entry is agent/act, and `gate_tools_when` composes with mesh membership.
   - New checkpoint test extending the existing Portal checkpoint suite: an agent/act member's hop spans multiple supersteps but is still resumable; hop counter persists correctly (only incremented once per COMPLETED hop, at the parse/Command-emission point, not per ReAct turn); recursion floor from step 6 is sufficient for a multi-hop agent/act mesh run (does not hit LangGraph's recursion_limit before max_hops exhausts).
   - Structural guard: extend or add a guard asserting no new `Command(` construction site outside `factory.py`/`runner.py` (G1 already covers this — just confirm the new code lands there, no new allowlist entry needed).

8. **Docs:** update `docs/design/dynamic-handoff-2026-07-13.md`'s D-MEMBER-MODES entry with a forward-pointer to this task's resolution (historical record stays; **must keep the literal string 'D-MEMBER-MODES' present, per tests/test_portal_addressability_doc.py:102 which asserts on it (refine, neograph-vihe7.29)** — mark it resolved/superseded the same way D-LOWERING-DISSENT was marked RATIFIED in portal-addressability-2026-07-15.md), and the website Portal docs page (`website/src/content/docs/concepts/portal.mdx`) to remove/update any 'agent/act members not supported' caveat if one exists.

## Refinement applied (neograph-vihe7.29, 2026-07-16)
Per architect review (neograph-vihe7.12, NEEDS_REFINEMENT): (1) step 4 now explicitly resolves the static mesh-entry edge through the entry-label map when the entry itself is agent/act, and step 5's fixture set now covers that case; (2) step 7 retargeted from a nonexistent check-fixture to the real pin test_agent_member_rejected, and step 8 now preserves the literal 'D-MEMBER-MODES' string per the doc-assertion test; (3) step 6 now states a concrete recursion-floor formula instead of flagging without specifying; (4) step 3 now commits up front to one shared wiring helper instead of copy-then-maybe-merge.

Its `_finish_and_shape`/parse_body (_agent_cycle.py:761-822) currently returns a plain state-update dict; it is the ONE place that needs to additionally emit `Command(goto=...)` for a mesh member.

This must be extracted into a reusable, non-closure helper in factory.py (still factory.py, per G1) and called from BOTH make_portal_fn's atomic wrapper and a new agent/act-cycle wrapper — do not re-derive the ExecutionError / budget-check logic a second time.

Building it as the shared graph-level artifact (not a nnds9-local ad hoc dict) directly serves the sibling tasks neograph-do0d9 (cross-construct Command.PARENT) and neograph-a37vk (self.handoff builder needs a stable name to target) per the doc's explicit framing — reuse across all three, don't reinvent per-task.

This means the new agent/act-terminal-hop Command emission MUST be built as a factory.py function (e.g. wrapping the parse-body callables that make_agent_cycle_bodies already returns), never inlined into _agent_cycle.py's parse_body itself or into _wiring.py's _add_agent_cycle. factory.py does not currently import _agent_cycle (only _wiring.py does) — a new module-level or function-local import from factory.py -> _agent_cycle is safe (no reverse import exists, checked by grep).

## Relevant Code

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Entry-node identity mismatch: if the entry-label-map mechanism is skipped and a naive implementation uses member.name directly as the Command(goto=) target for an agent/act peer, LangGraph will raise (no node named '{member.name}' exists -- only '{member.name}__agent' does) or, worse, silently mis-route if a differently-named node happens to collide. ## Findings

### (a) forward.py DRY-02 - Investigation Result: **LIVE BUG CONFIRMED**

The tracer/runtime type-view divergence IS a live bug for Oracle-modified nodes inside ForwardConstruct.

**Evidence:**
-  (lines 364-382) handles Oracle gen_type override: when `node.oracle_gen_type` is set, it returns `node.oracle_gen_type` (the per-variant type generators produce), NOT the post-merge type
- `forward.py` tracer runs at compile-time via `_trace_forward` during `ForwardConstruct.__init__`
- All 11 tracer sites use `normalize_outputs(_declared_output(x)).primary` which returns the POST-MERGE type (what merge_fn outputs), not the gen_type
- Oracle's gen_type override is ONLY applied at runtime via ThinkDispatch._resolve_primary_output

**Divergence example:**
```python
class MyPipeline(ForwardConstruct):
    gen = Node(mode="think", outputs=Claim, prompt="gen", model="fast")
    best = self.ensemble(self.gen, n=3, merge_fn="combine")  # Oracle sets gen.oracle_gen_type
    def forward(self, topic):
        variants = self.gen(topic)  # tracer infers Claim (post-merge type)
        return self.best(variants)   # but runtime produces Claim[] (gen_type)
```

**Recommendation:** Share `_dispatch._resolve_primary_output` rather than extract a module-private helper. Import check: `forward.py` already imports `_construct_validation` from `neograph._construct_validation`, adding an import from `neograph._dispatch` is layer-legal (dispatch is a peer module, no cycles). The neutral home for a shared helper would be `_normalize.py` (already exports `_declared_output`, a selector used by both layers).

design:
## Core Invariant
The three-layer engine-verb guard classifies .invoke/.ainvoke/.stream/.astream on a compile(...)-bound receiver as an engine call regardless of variable name — no compile-layer module may schedule engine execution and evade detection by naming the compiled graph something without 'graph'.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Add evasion meta-test FIRST** (anti-band-aid clause — TDD for guard hardening):
   - In tests/test_guards_three_layer.py, add `TestEngineVerbsConfinedToEngineSurface` method:
     - Name: `test_meta_compile_bound_to_innocent_name_is_flagged`
     - Synthetic source: `"g = compile(pipeline)\ng.invoke(state, config=c)"` (or similar)
     - Assertion: `_scan_engine_verbs(source)` must contain `("invoke", "shared")`
   - This meta-test MUST FAIL on current implementation, proving the blind spot exists

2. **Broaden _receiver_is_graphlike with provenance tracking** (~15 lines AST):
   - Add helper before `_scan_engine_verbs`:
     - Function `_compile_assignments(source: str) -> set[str]`
     - Parse AST with `ast.parse(source)`
     - Walk `ast.Assign` nodes where `value` is `ast.Call` with func.name == "compile"
     - Return set of target names (the left-hand side identifiers)
   - Modify `_receiver_is_graphlike(expr)`:
     - First check existing token-based logic (keep for speed path)
     - If no 'graph' token, check if receiver is `ast.Name` whose id is in compile-assigned set
     - Requires passing the compile-names set through OR building a closure that captures it
   - Alternative: modify `_scan_engine_verbs` to collect compile-names once per module, then filter calls

3. **Verify EXPECTED_ENGINE_SURFACE still matches exactly**:
   - After broadening, run `TestEngineVerbsConfinedToEngineSurface::test_engine_surface_matches_expected_exactly`
   - Must pass unchanged — confirms real engine surface is stable, detector didn't drift

4. **Audit step** (verification that blind spot was not exploited):
   - Run `grep -rnE '= *compile\(' src/neograph/*.py` to list all compile(...) assignments
   - Cross-reference against `grep -rnE '\.(invoke|ainvoke|stream|astream)\(' src/neograph/*.py` receivers
   - Confirm no compile-and-invoke pair exists outside runner.py/_compiled.py/_subconstruct.py
   - caller/payload in _agent_cycle.py are LLM/tools (Layer-2), correctly exempt

**Touch scope**: Only tests/test_guards_three_layer.py — no production code changes.

title: Unify forward.py _discover_node_attrs onto _classify_member (third member-collection site)
description: ForwardConstruct._discover_node_attrs (src/neograph/forward.py:157-170) is a third isinstance(Node)-only collection site with the same Construct-blind shape as the neograph-xv9ay disease. Deferred from the xv9ay disease scan because it is NOT a silent drop today: a Construct class attribute fails LOUD at class-definition time (Pydantic non-annotated-attribute error, verified 2026-07-10), and final membership is fixed by forward() tracing, not the attr walk. Once _classify_member exists in _construct_builder.py (xv9ay fix), evaluate whether ForwardConstruct attr discovery should adopt it — which would amount to sub-construct support in ForwardConstruct class bodies (a feature decision, not a bug). Scan artifacts: .claude/code-review/xv9ay/.
design:
## Core Invariant (reworded per review)
ForwardConstruct pipeline membership is fixed by forward() tracing, never by the class-attr walk — _discover_node_attrs is a name->Node lookup table feeding the tracer, deliberately EXEMPT from _classify_member; the exemption is safe only while a non-Node pipeline object in a class body fails LOUD (PydanticUserError via ignored_types=(Node,)) instead of silently dropping.

## Implementation Plan (REFINED: Option B — exempt-by-design, ratified by review verdict NEEDS_REFINEMENT)
1. Pin the loud failure with a behavioral test in tests/test_forward.py: a ForwardConstruct subclass with a Construct class attribute raises PydanticUserError at class-definition time. This is a guard-existing-behavior test (passes immediately — sanctioned refactor shape); it turns the exemption into a contract: if ignored_types ever widens without membership work, this test fails.
2. Docstring the exemption in _discover_node_attrs (forward.py) with a cross-ref to _member_select.py: attr-set -> trace contract; sub-pipelines enter a forward() trace via self.each()/self.loop()/self.ensemble(), not class attrs.
3. Record the exemption in TestMemberSelectionPredicateMonopoly's docstring (tests/test_guards_assembly.py) so future disease scans stop re-flagging forward.py:192.
4. No behavior change, no new feature, no website docs change.
Option A (full adoption) intentionally rejected: the disease (silent drop) does not exist here; adoption would ship an unrequested edge-case-heavy public feature redundant with self.each()/self.loop() with zero demand evidence.
notes:
## Findings
- PRECONDITION SATISFIED: _classify_member EXISTS. It lives in src/neograph/_member_select.py:39 (not _construct_builder.py as the bead text says -- it was EXTRACTED from _construct_builder.py per the module docstring; _construct_builder.py:33 now imports _bucket_members from it). No sequencing blocker.
- The reuse target is _member_select.py: _classify_member (THE single membership predicate, returns _MemberKind: DECORATED_NODE / PLAIN_NODE / SUB_CONSTRUCT / ARTIFACT-when-output-is-None) + _bucket_members (THE sole skip/warn/raise policy site, parameterized source='module'|'list'). Guard TestMemberSelectionPredicateMonopoly (tests/test_guards_assembly.py:1715) bans isinstance(x, Node/Construct) classification outside _classify_member -- but its scan scope is ONLY _construct_builder.py + _member_select.py; forward.py is currently outside the guard.
- Current third site: ForwardConstruct._discover_node_attrs (src/neograph/forward.py:182-194) -- reverse-MRO walk collecting isinstance(attr, Node) only. NOT a silent drop today, RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-11 by live repro: a Construct class attribute raises PydanticUserError 'A non-annotated attribute was detected' at class-DEFINITION time, because model_config ignored_types=(Node,) (forward.py:147) covers only Node.
- KEY STRUCTURAL FINDING: adopting _classify_member in _discover_node_attrs is meaningful ONLY together with extending ignored_types to include Construct. Without that, Pydantic raises before discovery ever runs, so the SUB_CONSTRUCT/ARTIFACT branches would be unreachable dead code -- pure cosmetic churn. Therefore adoption == the feature 'sub-construct support in ForwardConstruct class bodies', exactly as the bead frames it (feature decision, not bug).
- The downstream chain ALREADY supports Construct members: _Tracer._ordered is list[Node | Construct]; _Tracer.record_construct exists (forward.py:392, used by self.loop()/self.each() deferred builders since e9zse wave, commits a2834d6/d208f55); _Proxy._neo_source is typed Node | Construct | None; _trace_forward returns list[Node | Construct]; Construct.__init__ validation + compiler.py three-way dispatch already handle sub-constructs from the trace. The ONLY gaps are (a) Pydantic class-body acceptance, (b) discovery predicate, (c) _ForwardSelf.__getattr__/_NodeCall which today wrap only Node and call tracer.record (dedup + loop-tagging) not record_construct (no dedup, no loop-tag).
- xv9ay scan artifacts (.claude/code-review/xv9ay/disease-consistency.md Instance 3, disease-dedup.md site 3) explicitly deferred this site with: 'Flag it so the xv9ay fix consciously decides whether ForwardConstruct joins the unified member predicate or stays exempt-by-design; do not fold it into the same change blind. No repro written (no evidence forward sub-construct-as-attr is a supported/used shape).'
- Current vs deprecated: nothing deprecated here; the e9zse self.each()/self.loop()/self.ensemble() surfaces (June commits) are the CURRENT way sub-pipelines enter a forward() trace. Class-attr sub-constructs would be a second entry path for the same capability -- the feature-decision question is whether that redundancy is worth the symmetry with construct_from_module (which now collects sub-constructs post-xv9ay).

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/_member_select.py:39 (_classify_member) and :64 (_bucket_members) -- the monopoly predicate + policy site to REUSE; module docstring pins the layer (assembly/DX, same as _construct_builder; do NOT push into IR).
- src/neograph/forward.py:147 -- ignored_types=(Node,) model_config; the loud-fail gate that must widen to (Node, Construct) if the feature ships.
- src/neograph/forward.py:182-194 -- _discover_node_attrs, the site to migrate.
- src/neograph/forward.py:1127-1133 -- _ForwardSelf.__getattr__ returns _NodeCall(node_attrs[name], tracer); needs Construct awareness if feature ships.
- src/neograph/forward.py:382-394 -- _Tracer.record (dedup via _seen + loop-body Each-tagging) vs record_construct (neither); must be reconciled for repeat calls / bare-for loop bodies over a class-attr sub-construct.
- tests/test_guards_assembly.py:1715 -- TestMemberSelectionPredicateMonopoly; extend its scanned-paths set to forward.py as the guard-first step.
- tests/test_forward.py (~67 tests) -- where new behavior tests go; tests/check_fixtures/should_fail + should_pass -- every new validation rule needs fixtures per AGENTS.md.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Decision risk (for architect atom vgfwk.4): adopt-as-feature vs exempt-by-design-with-documentation. Both are defensible; the epic title says 'forward.py unify' which leans adopt, but the bead itself says feature decision. Researcher recommendation below in design.
- ignored_types with a BaseModel subclass: Pydantic's ignored_types is documented for arbitrary classes; verify it accepts a BaseModel subclass value (Construct) without schema side effects -- smoke-test in the regression atom before building on it.
- ARTIFACT policy: with ignored_types widened, a Construct(output=None) class attr no longer fails loud via Pydantic -- _classify_member's ARTIFACT branch becomes the loud gate. A class body is a promise (like source='list'), so policy should raise, but the policy must live in _member_select (the sole policy site), not inline in forward.py -- add a class-body source kind or a small policy helper there, or the monopoly guard's spirit is violated.
- record_construct has no _seen dedup and no _loop_body_nodes tagging: calling the same sub-construct attr twice would duplicate membership; calling it inside a bare for-loop body would silently NOT Each-wrap. Either unify record/record_construct semantics or loudly reject sub-construct calls in loop bodies for v1.
- Proxy naming: out_of_{name} and _over_path_for_proxy use field_name_for(source_node.name); confirm a sub-construct's output surfaces in parent state under field_name_for(construct.name) so downstream proxy consumption wires correctly (composition tests in test_composition.py are the reference).
- Doc surface: website ForwardConstruct docs + AGENTS.md would need the new shape documented if the feature ships (verifiable-docs remark plugin will build-fail on bad refs; run npm test in website/).
## Codebase Disease Scan (gtzkd)
Disease spec: membership CLASSIFICATION of arbitrary objects into pipeline members via private isinstance ladders outside _member_select._classify_member (the xv9ay disease). Shape: SYNTACTIC re-verification — the June xv9ay ticket already ran the full 3-lens multi-agent scan (.claude/code-review/xv9ay/); this atom re-swept src/neograph/*.py for isinstance(x, Node/Construct).

|---|---|---|

Post-fix expectation: zero collection-time ladders outside _member_select; guard TestMemberSelectionPredicateMonopoly scan scope extended to forward.py enforces it.
## Architect Review (vgfwk.4, independent)

Research verified against code: guard scan scope = BUILDER+SELECT only (forward.py out of scope, confirmed test_guards_assembly.py:1715+); tracer record() has _seen dedup + loop-body tagging while record_construct() has NEITHER (forward.py:382-394); _discover_node_attrs is isinstance(Node)-only (182-194); ignored_types=(Node,) (147); _classify_member lives in _member_select.py:39 (research correctly re-sourced it). Live repro CONFIRMS the load-bearing 'fails loud today' claim: a Construct instance as a non-annotated ForwardConstruct class attr raises PydanticUserError 'A non-annotated attribute was detected' at class-def time, and widening ignored_types to (Node, Construct) is the necessary gate — so adoption == the feature, exactly as framed.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: REJECT Option A as the default. The motivating disease (silent sub-construct DROP) does NOT exist at this site — it fails loud today (repro'd). So the correctness pressure behind xv9ay is absent here; the only pull toward A is code-symmetry. A ships a NET-NEW public API surface (class-attr sub-constructs in forward bodies) that is REDUNDANT with the CURRENT sanctioned entry path self.each()/self.loop()/self.ensemble() (e9zse wave) — reuse-over-reinvention cuts against a second way to do the same thing. No demand: the xv9ay scan itself recorded 'no evidence forward sub-construct-as-attr is a supported/used shape', and sole-downstream piarch has no cited need. Cost is NOT a small delta — the plan's own risks list 5+ genuine edge cases (record/record_construct reconciliation for dedup + loop-body tagging, _NodeCall/_ForwardSelf Construct-awareness, UNDEFINED bare-for-loop-over-subconstruct semantics, proxy out_of_{name} naming confirmation, ARTIFACT policy routing). Suggestion: adopt Option B (exempt-by-design: keep isinstance(Node), docstring cross-ref to _member_select, pin the loud failure, note the exemption in the guard). If piarch later needs class-attr sub-constructs, revisit A then — non-blocking.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: the Core Invariant conflates TWO different questions and, as written, forecloses Option B (makes B a self-inflicted invariant violation). _discover_node_attrs is a PRE-DECLARATION name->Node lookup feeding the proxy/tracer machinery; FINAL membership is fixed by the TRACE (_Tracer._ordered), NOT the attr walk — the bead's own notes say 'final membership is fixed by forward() tracing, not the attr walk.' Forcing that lookup to delegate to _classify_member ('the membership predicate') is a category error. Suggestion: reword the invariant so attr-discovery-for-tracing is explicitly distinct from member-classification, carving out the documented forward.py exemption — otherwise the invariant and the two-option framing contradict each other.

- [LOW] Finding: gate label 'codebase-scan:complete' is ABSENT on gtzkd (only 'research:complete' present), so the atom's hard-check fails — but the '## Codebase Disease Scan' disposition table IS present and vgfwk.3 is CLOSED, so the scan was substantively done; this is a bookkeeping miss, not a bypass. - [LOW] Finding: bead DESCRIPTION/DESIGN text still says _classify_member lives in _construct_builder.py; it was extracted to _member_select.py (research corrected this). Suggestion: propagate the correction into the refined plan so the implementer targets the right module.
