title: MCP prompts: consume server prompt templates (prompts/list + prompts/get) as a neograph prompt source
description:
CORE INVARIANT: a server-provided MCP prompt template (prompts/get) can back a neograph node prompt — closing the THIRD MCP primitive (tools DONE, resources DONE, prompts MISSING).

WHY: MCP defines three primitives — tools (mcp_tool_factories/session), resources (FromResource/resource_reader), and PROMPTS. neograph maps the first two and ignores the third. A server shipping a curated prompt template cannot feed neograph prompt_compiler today.

SCOPE: a battery helper (e.g. mcp_prompt_source(server, name)) that fetches a server prompt via prompts/get and adapts it into neograph prompt-source / template loading, with the prompt declared arguments bound from node inputs / di_inputs. Offline-at-build like the singular tool factory (deferred connect) where feasible.

ANTI-BAND-AID: route through the EXISTING prompt-source / prompt_compiler seam — do NOT add a second prompt-resolution path. An MCP prompt is just another source feeding the same compiler; the inline/template-ref key rules and lint coverage still apply.

ACCEPTANCE: a demo-server prompt template renders into a node prompt and drives a fake-LLM node end to end; arguments bind from node inputs; it flows through the normal prompt_compiler (no bypass); keyless via fakes. NOT 0.6.0-gating.
design:
## Core Invariant
A server-provided MCP prompt is consumed as a neograph prompt SOURCE that feeds the UNCHANGED DefaultPromptCompiler + lint(template_resolver) seam -- the MCP client stays consumer-owned strictly inside the returned loader closure (nmb2), and neograph core gains ZERO second prompt-resolution path.

## Implementation Plan (REFINED per architect review neograph-5jrd0.54)
1. ADD a demo-server prompt: in examples/_mcp_demo_server.py add one pure-passthrough `@mcp.prompt() def crm_brief(deal_context: str) -> str` so placeholder-echo yields a real `{deal_context}` template. Keep it PLAIN FastMCP.
2. REUSE the transport primitives from src/neograph_mcp/_client.py (StdioServer/HttpServer, _client_for, _resolve_token_no_config, _run_sync, TokenProvider) -- import verbatim.
3. BUILD `mcp_prompt_source(server_key, spec, *, token_provider=None, stdio_token_arg='token', timeout=30.0) -> Callable[[str], str | None]` — **[REVISED] NO name= parameter: the returned loader uses its INCOMING template argument AS the MCP prompt name** (matching the directory loader's {template}.md name->text contract; load_template passes the NODE's declared prompt name). One compiler backs N MCP-backed nodes; a prompt the server doesn't declare returns None (loader contract: None -> not found, fail-loud upstream). Signature mirrors _client_for(server_key, spec, token) explicitly (the cited exemplar).
4. Structurally copy mcp_resource_fetcher: create the MultiServerMCPClient INSIDE the closure (deferred connect, zero network at construction); open `async with client.session(server_key)`; list_prompts (paginated) to read declared arg NAMES; get_prompt(template, arguments={a: '{'+a+'}' for a in declared}) — placeholder-echo; concatenate returned messages' TEXT into one template string. **[REVISED] MEMOIZE (name->text) in the closure BY DEFAULT** (load_template fires per-superstep; a server prompt template is stable within a run) — lint+compile don't double-connect. Bridge async->sync with _run_sync.
5. **[REVISED] Docstring MUST document**: (a) MCP-backed lint(template_resolver=...) performs a LIVE get_prompt round-trip (lint is otherwise offline; no offline way to read declared args) — memoization means one connect serves lint+compile; (b) role-collapse: get_prompt messages' role structure is dropped (pure-template passthrough only) and non-TextContent blocks raise a typed error; (c) brace-collision: a server template carrying literal {..} (JSON examples) fails loud at compile — inherent to brace templating.
6. EXPORT mcp_prompt_source via neograph_mcp __init__ __all__. No change to src/neograph.
7. Acceptance: a demo-server prompt renders into a node prompt and drives a fake-LLM node end-to-end (template arg = node's declared prompt name); arguments bind from node inputs via the normal compiler; lint(template_resolver=mcp_prompt_source(...)) validates placeholders (live, memoized); keyless via fakes where possible, demo-server for the E2E. NOT 0.6.0-gating.
notes:
## Findings

### REUSE TARGET (primary): the DefaultPromptCompiler loader seam + lint template_resolver seam
- `DefaultPromptCompiler(loader=...)` already accepts a `Callable[[str], str]` (name->raw-template-text) — `TemplateLoader = str | Path | Callable[[str], str]` (src/neograph/prompt.py:133). This IS the 'prompt source' seam the task names. The MCP helper should RETURN such a loader closure; DO NOT write a second prompt-resolution path. `load_template` (prompt.py:166) calls `self.loader(template)`; the returned text then flows through the UNCHANGED `build_vars`->`render_inputs`->`substitute` chain, so node inputs + di_inputs bind the `{arg}` placeholders (build_vars di_inputs base-layer rule at prompt.py:178-210). No bypass.
- The SAME loader closure doubles as `lint(construct, ..., template_resolver=...)` (src/neograph/lint.py:255,260 — signature `Callable[[str], str | None]`, name->template text). Passing the mcp_prompt_source closure as template_resolver gives the mandated lint coverage for free — the template-ref `{var}` column validates the MCP arg placeholders against predicted node input keys.
- compile() already threads prompt_compiler through unchanged (src/neograph/compiler.py:63,69). Nothing in neograph core changes.

### REUSE TARGET (transport plumbing): src/neograph_mcp/_client.py + _session.py primitives — import verbatim, do NOT reinvent
- `StdioServer` (_client.py:63) / `HttpServer` (:76), `_client_for` (:104), `_resolve_token_no_config` (:128), `_run_sync` sync->async bridge (:143), `TokenProvider` (:55). The prompt loader is a name->text SYNC callable but MCP get_prompt is async, so `_run_sync` is exactly the bridge already used for build-time tool discovery.
- EXEMPLAR to copy structurally: `mcp_resource_fetcher` (_client.py:449) — a builder that returns a closure owning a consumer-held `MultiServerMCPClient` created strictly INSIDE the closure (the nmb2 invariant), opened via `async with client.session(server_key)`, McpError re-raised after the context closes. mcp_prompt_source mirrors this shape exactly but calls list_prompts/get_prompt instead of read_resource.
- Raw session prompt API: `session.list_prompts()` -> Prompt(name,title,description,arguments[PromptArgument(name,description,required)]); `session.get_prompt(name, arguments: dict)` -> GetPromptResult(description, messages[PromptMessage(role, content)]). Pagination pattern already solved in `McpSession._ensure_listing` (_session.py:253). langchain adapter also exposes `load_mcp_prompt` / `client.get_prompt` (langchain_mcp_adapters/prompts.py) but the RAW session is preferred here (the battery already prefers raw session for resource_fetcher to avoid the adapter's content rewrites).

### Mechanism: placeholder-echo to recover a template from a server-side-rendered prompt
- MCP has NO 'get raw template' call — get_prompt(name, args) renders SERVER-SIDE. To obtain text carrying neograph `{arg}` placeholders (so DefaultPromptCompiler.substitute binds them from node inputs/di_inputs), the loader calls list_prompts to read the declared argument NAMES, then get_prompt(name, arguments={arg: '{'+arg+'}' for arg in declared}) — the server echoes the placeholder tokens back into its template, and the assembled message text carries `{arg}` for the normal compiler. This is what makes 'declared arguments bound from node inputs' land through the existing seam rather than a bypass.

### Public surface + export
- New symbol goes in src/neograph_mcp/_client.py (or a new _prompt.py) and is exported via src/neograph_mcp/__init__.py `__all__` (:50). neograph_mcp is the [mcp] battery package (pyproject extra name is `mcp`; examples use `mcp-examples`). Naming policy: __all__ is the contract; underscore-prefix is advisory.

### Demo server gap
- examples/_mcp_demo_server.py (346 lines) has NO `@mcp.prompt` yet — only @mcp.tool/@mcp.resource. Add one PURE-passthrough f-string prompt (e.g. `@mcp.prompt() def crm_brief(deal_context: str) -> str: return f'...{deal_context}...'`) in the resources section (~line 311) so placeholder-echo works. FastMCP `@mcp.prompt` decorator confirmed available (mcp 1.28.x).

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/prompt.py:133,136,166,178 -- DefaultPromptCompiler + loader seam + build_vars di_inputs base-layer; the REUSE target, unchanged.
- src/neograph/lint.py:255,260 -- lint(template_resolver=) seam; feed it the same mcp_prompt_source closure for template-ref lint coverage.
- src/neograph/compiler.py:63,69 -- compile(prompt_compiler=) threads through unchanged.
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:449 (mcp_resource_fetcher) -- the closure-returning builder to copy structurally (client owned inside closure, McpError re-raise-after-close).
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:63,76,104,128,143,55 -- StdioServer/HttpServer/_client_for/_resolve_token_no_config/_run_sync/TokenProvider to import verbatim.
- src/neograph_mcp/_session.py:253 (_ensure_listing) -- paginated tools/list pattern to mirror for prompts/list.
- src/neograph_mcp/__init__.py:50 -- __all__ export point for the new mcp_prompt_source symbol.
- examples/_mcp_demo_server.py:~311 -- add the @mcp.prompt template here.
- tests/test_mcp_battery.py:225 (test_compile_lint_and_arun_through_the_battery) and :539 (e2e typed) -- exemplars for the acceptance test: compile+lint+drive-with-fake end-to-end. Fake LLM via tests.fakes.configure_fake_llm/build_test_compile_kwargs; a think node (StructuredFake) is simpler than the agent ReActFake here.
- tests/test_mcp_examples_e2e.py -- keyless stdio-subprocess harness; a new example (2?_mcp_prompt*.py) auto-discovers into its runner.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- PASSTHROUGH LIMITATION (call out in docstring): placeholder-echo only works for server prompts that are pure templates. A server prompt that USES arg values (e.g. read_table_schema(table_name)) will run against the literal token '{table_name}' and misbehave. For value-substituting server prompts the escape hatch is a scripted node using McpSession + get_prompt with REAL values (not this loader). Document that mcp_prompt_source targets pure-template server prompts.
- SYNC/ASYNC: load_template is sync; get_prompt is async -> bridge with existing _run_sync (_client.py:143), which already handles the running-loop case via a worker thread. A network get_prompt fires per node-prompt compile (per superstep); mirror the tool-factory per-superstep-connect precedent, optionally add a one-shot closure cache for the (name->text) result since a server prompt template is stable within a run.
- nmb2 INVARIANT (do NOT reopen): the MultiServerMCPClient/session must be created and owned strictly INSIDE the returned loader closure; neograph core never holds it. tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py scans src/neograph only — keep the helper in neograph_mcp.
- Arg-name mapping: MCP declared argument names become neograph template-ref keys, so they must match predicted node input keys (upstream outputs / flattened / framework extras / di_inputs param names). Lint's template-ref column enforces this exactly — no new lint rule needed.
- Three-surface parity note: prompt-source is a compile-time seam (prompt_compiler/loader), NOT an IR-level Node change, so the three-API-surface parity rule does not apply; the helper is orthogonal to @node vs declarative vs programmatic.
## Codebase Disease Scan (uagu7)
Pattern: a SECOND prompt-resolution path bypassing DefaultPromptCompiler + lint(template_resolver) seam.
Scan command: grep -rn 'DefaultPromptCompiler|prompt_compiler|class.*PromptCompiler' src/neograph/prompt.py src/neograph/lint.py
Total instances found: ONE compiler seam — DefaultPromptCompiler (prompt.py:136) + lint(prompt_compiler=) (lint.py:262). No competing resolver.

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | src/neograph/prompt.py:136 | DefaultPromptCompiler(loader=) | ALLOWLIST (reuse target) | THE single seam — uagu7 adds mcp_prompt_source as a LOADER feeding this compiler, not a 2nd resolver; inline/template-ref + lint rules still apply |

No MIGRATE — uagu7 is net-new (a loader source) routed through the existing seam. Clean. SYNTACTIC scan sufficient.
## Architect Review (neograph-5jrd0.44)

Independent adversarial review of the research + plan for consuming an MCP server prompt (prompts/list + prompts/get) as a neograph prompt SOURCE through the DefaultPromptCompiler(loader=) + lint(template_resolver=) seam. Verified claims against src/neograph/prompt.py, node.py, lint.py, and src/neograph_mcp/_client.py/_session.py/__init__.py.

CORE INVARIANT HOLDS: the loader-closure IS the existing seam (prompt.py:133,174-176,247) — no second prompt-resolution path. build_vars di_inputs base-layer (prompt.py:201) binds {arg} placeholders unchanged. nmb2 client-ownership preserved (helper lives in neograph_mcp; the ownership guard scans src/neograph only). mcp_resource_fetcher (_client.py:449) is a faithful structural exemplar. Placeholder-echo is sound WITHIN the documented pure-template scope. No HIGH.

FINDINGS:
- [MEDIUM] Hardcoded name= breaks the loader name->text contract. load_template(template) passes the NODE'S declared prompt name (node.py:172, prompt.py:247) to loader(template). The plan's mcp_prompt_source(..., name='crm_brief') pins the MCP prompt name and (per step 3) calls get_prompt(name, ...) IGNORING the incoming template arg. Consequence: one DefaultPromptCompiler cannot back two nodes with two different MCP prompts, and a node declaring prompt='X' silently receives the pinned prompt. The single-node acceptance test will NOT surface this. Suggestion: use the incoming template arg AS the MCP prompt name (drop name=, matching the directory loader's {template}.md contract) — or keep name= only as a fail-loud assertion that template == name.
- [MEDIUM] lint(template_resolver=mcp_prompt_source(...)) makes lint perform a LIVE network get_prompt round-trip. lint() is otherwise a static/offline check; the plan feeds it the same deferred-connect closure, so linting now requires a live MCP server. title: First-class production auth: OAuth 2.1 / client-credentials / JWT token_provider helpers
description:
CORE INVARIANT: a production consumer gets refresh/expiry-handling OAuth identity for an HttpServer by passing a battery helper to token_provider=, not by hand-rolling httpx.Auth.

WHY: token_provider returns a bare bearer string today; OAuth 2.1 / client-credentials / on-behalf-of / JWT flows exist ONLY as hand-rolled httpx.Auth in example 23 appendix. The MCP SDK ships the httpx.Auth providers (OAuthClientProvider / ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider / PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider) — wrap them so consumers get token refresh + expiry for free.

SCOPE: battery helper(s) (e.g. oauth_token_provider(...)) producing a token_provider/httpx.Auth wired into HttpServer bearer path, minting + refreshing per-run identity from config. Cover client-credentials at minimum; document on-behalf-of / JWT.

ANTI-BAND-AID: reuse the SDK httpx.Auth providers — do NOT re-implement OAuth token exchange/refresh. neograph carries identity from config to the transport; it never parses or stores the token (stays out of state/checkpoint/fingerprint, per the existing invariant).

ACCEPTANCE: an HttpServer against a demo OAuth-guarded endpoint authenticates via the helper; token refresh on expiry works without a reconnect; the token never appears in state/checkpoint; docs cover the three flows. NOT 0.6.0-gating.
design:
## Core Invariant
A production consumer gets refresh/expiry-handling OAuth identity by attaching an SDK-built httpx.Auth to the transport (HttpServer.auth -> the adapter connection dict), and neograph_mcp only CARRIES that Auth from config to the adapter -- it never parses, stores, or refreshes the token itself (the token stays out of state/checkpoint/fingerprint).

## Implementation Plan
1. EXTEND HttpServer, not a new seam: add `auth: httpx.Auth | None = None` to the frozen dataclass (src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:76-82). httpx is already transitive under the mcp extra.
2. WIRE the single choke point: in `_connection` (_client.py:88-101) add `if isinstance(spec, HttpServer) and spec.auth is not None: conn['auth'] = spec.auth`. This lights up all three surfaces (tool factories, resource fetcher, mcp_session) for free -- do NOT touch the surfaces individually. Precedence: if both `auth` and a bearer `token` are present, the httpx.Auth wins (an Auth manages its own Authorization header); document that token_provider is for stdio/static-bearer, auth for OAuth flows.
3. SHIP thin battery constructors that WRAP the SDK providers (reuse, never re-implement token exchange/refresh). Suggested surface in src/neograph_mcp (new _auth.py or in _client.py), exported via __init__.__all__:
   - `client_credentials_auth(server_url, client_id, client_secret, *, scopes=None, auth_method='client_secret_basic') -> httpx.Auth` -> wraps ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider with a fresh in-memory TokenStorage. (Covers the mandated client-credentials case.)
   - `private_key_jwt_auth(...)` / `oauth_client_provider(...)` -> wrap PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider / OAuthClientProvider (document on-behalf-of / interactive OAuth 2.1; can be thinner/doc-first).
   Each helper reads its client_id/secret from run config where per-run identity is needed, or takes them directly for static app identity. Prefer names ending in `_auth` returning httpx.Auth over the bead's misleading `oauth_token_provider` (see NEEDS USER INPUT in notes).
4. PROVIDE a minimal in-memory TokenStorage (implements mcp.client.auth.TokenStorage: get/set tokens + client_info) created per helper call, never persisted -- this is the structural guarantee the token never reaches state.
5. FUNCTION-LOCAL imports for mcp.client.auth.* and jwt-dependent providers (keep module import light; keep the fail-loud extra check in __init__ authoritative).
6. TEST (copy tests/test_mcp_battery.py TestHttpServerSmoke + _demo_http_server pattern): stand up a minimal OAuth token endpoint fixture (Starlette, mirroring _demo_http_server) that issues a short-lived token and returns one 401 to force a refresh; assert (a) an HttpServer(auth=client_credentials_auth(...)) authenticates, (b) refresh-on-expiry succeeds WITHOUT rebuilding the client/session, (c) the client_secret/token never appears in state/checkpoint/fingerprint. Gate the whole class behind the mcp extra like the existing http tests.
7. DOCS: update the appendix in examples/23 (or a new example) + website mcp-client/mcp-integration pages to show HttpServer(auth=client_credentials_auth(...)) and document all three flows (client-credentials at depth; on-behalf-of / private-key-JWT by reference). Run `npm run build` in website/ after.
8. GATE the API shape (step 1/3 naming) on the NEEDS USER INPUT resolution before landing: confirm HttpServer.auth (transport seam) is the accepted API vs overloading token_provider.
notes:
## Findings (dp-researcher, neograph-5jrd0.34)

REUSE TARGET (do not re-implement OAuth): the mcp SDK 1.28.x ships the httpx.Auth providers already installed under the `mcp` extra:
- `mcp.client.auth.OAuthClientProvider` (interactive OAuth 2.1 / auth-code+PKCE)
- `mcp.client.auth.extensions.client_credentials.ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider(server_url, storage, client_id, client_secret, token_endpoint_auth_method='client_secret_basic'|'client_secret_post', scopes=None)`
- `...client_credentials.PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider(server_url, storage, client_id, assertion_provider)`
- `...client_credentials.RFC7523OAuthClientProvider`, `JWTParameters`, `SignedJWTParameters`, `static_assertion_provider`
All subclass `httpx.Auth` (MRO: Provider -> OAuthClientProvider -> httpx.Auth). They mint AND refresh tokens internally via the httpx auth_flow (401 -> refresh -> retry in the SAME httpx client, i.e. WITHOUT a reconnect). pyjwt 2.13 is present transitively (client_credentials does `import jwt`).

THE SINGLE WIRING CHOKE POINT: `_connection(spec, token)` in src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:88-101 builds the langchain-mcp-adapters connection dict for EVERY surface. All three consumer surfaces route through `_client_for` -> `_connection`:
- tool factories: _client.py:276 (_make_tool_factory)
- resource fetcher/replayer: _client.py:495 / :505
- mcp_session: _session.py:235
The adapter's `StreamableHttpConnection` TypedDict (langchain-mcp-adapters 0.3.0) ALREADY accepts an `auth` key (verified: keys include 'auth'). So threading an httpx.Auth requires touching ONE builder, not the three surfaces.

CURRENT (string) vs NEW (httpx.Auth) identity paths:
- CURRENT: `token_provider` (TokenProvider = Callable[..., str|Awaitable[str]], _client.py:55) returns a BARE bearer string, resolved once per superstep (_resolve_token, _client.py:114) and stamped into `headers['Authorization'] = f'Bearer {token}'` (_client.py:96-97). A fresh client is built each superstep, so a token change here IS a reconnect. This path stays for stdio (tool-arg identity) and simple static bearers. NOT deprecated.
- NEW: an httpx.Auth lives IN the transport's httpx client and refreshes per-request. This is the ONLY path that satisfies the acceptance 'refresh on expiry without a reconnect'.

GUARD BOUNDARY (favorable): tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py scans `src/neograph` ONLY. The battery lives in `src/neograph_mcp`, which is ALLOWED to `import mcp` / httpx / hold client lifecycle. New helper code belongs in src/neograph_mcp/_client.py (or a new src/neograph_mcp/_auth.py), exported via src/neograph_mcp/__init__.py __all__ (the facade is the public contract per AGENTS.md naming policy).

TokenStorage: `mcp.client.auth.TokenStorage` is a Protocol (get_tokens/set_tokens/get_client_info/set_client_info). The SDK ships NO in-memory impl -> the battery must provide a tiny in-memory TokenStorage (per-run, never persisted; keeps the token out of neograph state/checkpoint by construction).

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:76-82 -- `HttpServer` frozen dataclass (url, headers). Add `auth: httpx.Auth | None = None` here; it is the natural home for transport identity.
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:88-101 -- `_connection`: the single builder. Add `if spec.auth is not None: conn['auth'] = spec.auth`. Covers all three surfaces at once.
- src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:104-111 -- `_client_for`: unchanged; already the shared client constructor.
- src/neograph_mcp/__init__.py:35-61 -- facade; add the new helper(s) + HttpServer stays exported. Public iff in __all__.
- examples/23_mcp_client_selective_binding.py:453-488 -- APPENDIX B: the hand-rolled PerRunBearer httpx.Auth this task graduates; explicitly names the three SDK providers to wrap. This is the spec-in-prose.
- tests/test_mcp_battery.py:594-653 (TestHttpServerSmoke) + _demo_http_server fixture (:137-156) + _demo_http_server_spec (:166-169) -- the EXEMPLAR http-integration test to copy for an OAuth test class.
- pyproject.toml:43-47 -- the `mcp` extra (mcp>=1.28,<2, langchain-mcp-adapters>=0.3). pyjwt already transitive; confirm no new pin needed for PrivateKeyJWT before adding one.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- NEEDS USER INPUT: the bead Core Invariant says the consumer wires OAuth 'by passing a battery helper to token_provider='. But `token_provider` returns a STRING resolved once per superstep, and a per-superstep client rebuild IS a reconnect -- so it structurally CANNOT satisfy the acceptance 'refresh on expiry WITHOUT a reconnect'. The httpx.Auth must live in the transport (HttpServer.auth / connection['auth']). Recommended resolution: add `HttpServer(auth=httpx.Auth)` and treat 'token_provider=' in the invariant as loose shorthand for 'the neograph identity seam'. Confirm the API shape (new HttpServer.auth field) before implementing. Corollary: the suggested name `oauth_token_provider` is misleading (it returns an httpx.Auth, not a token string) -- prefer `oauth_client_credentials(...) -> httpx.Auth` (or an `oauth_auth` family).
- Acceptance requires a 'demo OAuth-guarded endpoint'. The current examples/_mcp_demo_server.py is plain FastMCP that only ECHOES the Authorization header (bearer_identity) -- it runs NO OAuth token endpoint and enforces nothing. The SDK providers do RFC-8414 metadata discovery + a token-endpoint round-trip + 401-triggered refresh, so a faithful test needs a minimal OAuth token server (short-lived token + one 401 to prove refresh-without-reconnect). This is the largest lift; a Starlette token-endpoint fixture (mirroring _demo_http_server) is the likely shape. Scope the demo-server work explicitly.
- Token-never-in-state invariant holds by construction ONLY if the in-memory TokenStorage is created per-run inside the consumer factory and never written to config that enters state. Add a test asserting the token/secret never appears in checkpoint/state/fingerprint (mirrors existing 'token never enters state' pins).
- Three-surface note: this is a neograph_mcp battery, NOT a core IR change, so the @node/declarative/programmatic three-surface parity rule does not apply; the parity that DOES apply is the three neograph_mcp surfaces (tool factories, resource fetcher, mcp_session) -- all covered free by wiring `_connection`.
- client_credentials extension imports `jwt` (pyjwt) at module top; a bare `import` of the helper without pyjwt would fail. Gate the client_credentials import function-locally and keep pyjwt pinned in the mcp extra if PrivateKeyJWT/RFC7523 helpers are shipped.
## Codebase Disease Scan (27h3s)
Pattern: per-surface auth/header wiring instead of the single _connection choke point.
Scan command: grep -rn 'def _connection|conn\[|headers|Authorization|auth' src/neograph_mcp/_client.py
Total instances found: auth-header construction is ALREADY single-sited at _connection (:88-100); _client_for (:111) routes all 3 surfaces through it.

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:88-100 | _connection builds conn['headers']/Authorization once | ALLOWLIST (reuse target) | already the single choke point — 27h3s adds conn['auth'] HERE (design step 2), lighting all 3 surfaces at one site; no per-surface duplication exists |

No MIGRATE — the centralization the ticket wants already exists; 27h3s extends it in place. BLOCKED pending token_provider= vs HttpServer.auth transport decision (NEEDS_USER_INPUT).
## Architect Review (neograph-5jrd0.36)

Gate hard-check PASS: research:complete + codebase-scan:complete both present. All load-bearing research claims verified against code: _connection (_client.py:88) is genuinely the single choke point (tool factory :276, resource fetcher :480/:497, mcp_session _session.py:235 all route through _client_for->_connection); StreamableHttpConnection TypedDict DOES accept an auth key; OAuthClientProvider/ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider/PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider/TokenStorage all present and subclass httpx.Auth; per-superstep fresh-client rebuild (=reconnect) confirmed by the module docstring + _client_for building a new MultiServerMCPClient each call.

- [HIGH] Finding: The flagged token_provider= vs HttpServer.auth contradiction is REAL and CORRECTLY framed. token_provider is typed Callable[...,str|Awaitable[str]] returning a bare bearer string, resolved ONCE per superstep before the client is built and stamped into a header (_client.py:96-97,122). Refresh-on-expiry-without-reconnect structurally requires the httpx.Auth object to live inside the persistent httpx client and intercept 401s via auth_flow -- a string returned by token_provider cannot do this. The ticket Core Invariant literally says "pass a battery helper to token_provider=", which is structurally unsatisfiable for the stated acceptance. Suggestion: This is a genuine HIGH because the resolution (a) adds a new PUBLIC field auth to the frozen public HttpServer dataclass and (b) rewrites the ticket-author-stated Core Invariant. The design already picked the correct approach (HttpServer.auth) and step 8 gates on it -- user should CONFIRM the API shape (new HttpServer.auth transport field + reframed invariant + renaming the misleading oauth_token_provider to an *_auth family returning httpx.Auth) before landing. Not open-ended; a confirm-this-shape gate.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: Undefined precedence when both seams are set. token_provider (a param to mcp_tool_factories/mcp_tool_factory) and HttpServer.auth are INDEPENDENT seams both feeding _connection(spec, token). A consumer can set HttpServer(auth=...) AND pass token_provider=... -> _connection would set BOTH conn["headers"]["Authorization"] (from token) AND conn["auth"]. Design step 2 merely ASSERTS "httpx.Auth wins" relying on undocumented httpx header-vs-auth precedence, not enforced in the wiring. Suggestion: enforce mutual exclusivity (raise a clear error if a bearer token and spec.auth both resolve for the same HttpServer), or at minimum skip stamping headers["Authorization"] when spec.auth is set, so precedence is code-guaranteed rather than httpx-behavior-dependent. Add a test pinning the chosen precedence.

- [MEDIUM] Finding: Demo OAuth-server fixture is underspecified in plan step 6 vs the risks note. Step 6 says "minimal OAuth token endpoint fixture (mirroring _demo_http_server)", but the SDK ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider does RFC-8414 metadata discovery (/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server) BEFORE the token round-trip. A naive copy of _demo_http_server (which only echoes the Authorization header, enforces nothing) will fail at discovery, not at the token endpoint. Suggestion: the fixture must serve BOTH the discovery document AND the token endpoint (+ a one-shot 401 to force refresh). This is the largest lift; scope it as discovery-endpoint + token-endpoint, and verify whether the provider also needs client_info from TokenStorage.get_client_info for the client-credentials path.

- [LOW] Finding: Reuse posture is sound -- plan correctly wraps SDK providers rather than re-implementing OAuth, extends the existing single choke point in place (disposition table has no MIGRATE, correctly), and lives in src/neograph_mcp (outside the src/neograph guard scope). No net-new primitive that duplicates an existing one. With future annotations in _client.py, auth: httpx.Auth | None annotation needs no runtime httpx import; the isinstance(spec, HttpServer) guard in step 2 needs no httpx import either.

Overall: NEEDS_USER_INPUT
## Triage (neograph-5jrd0.37): NEEDS_USER_INPUT — blocked for maintainer. 1 HIGH: token_provider= (bare string) cannot do refresh-without-reconnect; needs httpx.Auth on HttpServer.auth (design already picked this) — but it adds a public field + reframes the ticket invariant. Awaiting shape sign-off.
## MAINTAINER DECISION (2026-07-10): APPROVE HttpServer.auth + reframed invariant. Add auth: httpx.Auth | None to the frozen HttpServer dataclass; wire at the single _connection choke point (lights all 3 surfaces); ship SDK-wrapping helpers (client_credentials_auth, ...). Precedence: auth wins over bearer token when both set. token_provider stays for stdio/static-bearer. title: Decorator parity: expose Oracle.merge_model and Loop.history as @node kwargs (merge_model=/loop_history=)
description: Under neograph-fsoss (doc bug), the architect found the website documented @node(merge_model=) and @node(loop_history=True) as first-class @node kwargs, but neither was EVER wired into the decorator (git -S/-G over decorators.py = empty; docs added ahead of impl in 07475e1). Both features exist ONLY on the programmatic modifiers: modifiers.Oracle.merge_model (str='reason') and modifiers.Loop.history (bool). fsoss fixes the DOCS to the programmatic surface. THIS bead tracks the product decision: should @node forward these two for three-surface parity? decorators.py already forwards loop_when/max_iterations/on_exhaust -> Loop(**kwargs) and ensemble_n/models/merge_fn/merge_prompt/hooks -> Oracle(**kwargs); adding loop_history->Loop(history=) and merge_model->Oracle(merge_model=) is small but requires three-surface parity tests + re-documenting the @node form. Decide: wire-for-parity (then re-add the @node-kwarg docs) vs keep programmatic-only.
design:
## Core Invariant
The @node decorator is pure sugar over the IR: any forwarded kwarg must map 1:1 onto an existing modifier field via the existing pipe sites with modifier defaults preserved (forward only when explicitly set) — no new IR, factory, or state capability, no @node-specific logic below decorators.py, and IDENTICAL semantics to the programmatic modifier (no decorator-only validation the modifier itself does not perform).

## Implementation Plan (REFINED per architect review — Option A ratified, all three kwargs)
1. decorators.py node() signature: add merge_model: str | None = None, loop_history: bool = False, map_on_error: Literal['raise','collect'] = 'raise'.
2. _build_oracle_kwargs: accept merge_model; include in oracle_kw ONLY when not None (conditional-include pattern; Oracle's 'reason' default stays authoritative). SILENT-IGNORE semantics with merge_fn — identical to programmatic Oracle (review ruling: decorator-only fail-loud would re-introduce validation asymmetry; the previously cited decorators.py:203 precedent was the merge_fn+merge_prompt check, not hooks).
3. Loop path (decorators.py:622-630): loop_kwargs['history']=True when loop_history set; raise ConstructError if loop_history without loop_when (decorator-level pairing guard, precedent: map_over-requires-map_key — the kwarg would otherwise be silently dead since no Loop is composed at all).
4. Each path: thread map_on_error to BOTH Each construction sites (decorators.py:561 fusion + :570 plain), conditional-include only when != 'raise'. Name keeps the map_ prefix per map_over/map_key.
5. Tests (TDD): decorator surface asserts composed Oracle carries merge_model / Loop carries history / Each carries on_error; loop_history runtime accumulation reuses existing plumbing (_state_write.py:135-142, state.py:238); loop_history-without-loop_when raises. ForwardConstruct self.loop() is structurally EXEMPT from history (Construct-level ban modifiers.py:263-267) — document the exemption.
6. Fixtures: should_fail (loop_history without loop_when, CHECK_ERROR regex) + should_pass (all three new kwargs in use). NO merge_model+merge_fn fail fixture (silent-ignore ruling).
7. Docs: re-add @node-kwarg forms — oracle-ensemble.mdx:223, node-api/modifier-kwargs.mdx, reference; add map_on_error. npm run build + npm test in website/.
notes:
## Findings

### Current @node forwarding (the reuse target for either option)
- Oracle kwargs: `_build_oracle_kwargs` (src/neograph/decorators.py:155-230) builds oracle_kw from ensemble_n/models/merge_fn/merge_prompt + 3 merge hooks. Applied at decorators.py:543-595 (`n = n | Oracle(**oracle_kw)`, two call sites: map_over branch + plain branch). merge_model is ABSENT.
- Loop kwargs: decorators.py:622-630 builds `{when, max_iterations, on_exhaust}` and pipes `n | Loop(**loop_kwargs)`. history is ABSENT. Note the conditional-include pattern: on_exhaust only forwarded when not None (preserves the modifier's Pydantic default).

### What the two fields actually do
- `Oracle.merge_model: str = 'reason'` (modifiers.py:422). Consumed ONLY on the merge_prompt (LLM-judge) path: _oracle.py:280 and :368 pass `model_tier=oracle.merge_model` to the merge invoke. With merge_fn it is silently ignored — Oracle.model_post_init validates hooks-vs-merge_fn but does NOT validate merge_model-vs-merge_fn.
- `Loop.history: bool = False` (modifiers.py:571). Node-level only: Construct|Loop(history=True) raises ConstructError (modifiers.py:263-267, pinned by tests/test_loop.py:410). When true, state.py:237 adds `neo_loop_history_{field}` (Annotated[list, _concat_reducer]) and _state_write.py:133-142 appends each iteration's result (key via StateKeys.loop_history, _state_keys.py:130). Framework-internal (neo_ prefix) — read back via graph.get_state(config).values, requires a checkpointer.

### Surface coverage today (the asymmetry)
- merge_model: programmatic Oracle ✓, ForwardConstruct `self.ensemble(..., merge_model=)` ✓ (forward.py:1219/1245), spec loader ✓ (loader.py:263-265, forwards only when in model_fields_set), spec schema ✓ (_spec_schema.py:36). **@node is the ONLY surface missing it.**
- Loop.history: programmatic Node|Loop ✓ (only legal form). ForwardConstruct `self.loop()` (forward.py:1150) does NOT expose it — structurally CANNOT: FC loops build a sub-construct, and Construct-level history raises. @node's loop_when path is a Node-level self-loop — exactly the supported shape — so @node is the only OTHER surface where history could legally live.

### Docs post-fsoss (already corrected to programmatic-only)
- website/src/content/docs/walkthrough/oracle-ensemble.mdx:223 explicitly says merge_model 'is not a @node kwarg' — must be re-edited if we wire.
- website/src/content/docs/node-api/modifier-kwargs.mdx:588-597 documents Loop(history=True) as the programmatic modifier + neo_loop_history_{node} readback.
- concepts/spec-format.mdx:99 + reference/api.mdx:395 document merge_model on spec/Oracle.

### Downstream consumer (piarch)
- Zero uses of merge_model or Loop.history anywhere in piarch/src (grep confirmed). Heavy Oracle use (ensemble_n=3, Oracle(n=3, merge_prompt=...)) but always default merge tier; the one Loop mention is a comment. No demand pressure either way.

### Option A — wire for parity
- merge_model: add `merge_model: str | None = None` param to node(); in _build_oracle_kwargs include `oracle_kw['merge_model'] = merge_model` only when not None (same conditional-include pattern as on_exhaust / loader.py:263). Closes the only-surface gap. Design point for architect: mirror Oracle (silently ignore with merge_fn) vs fail loud at the decorator like the hooks validation at decorators.py:203 — recommend fail loud, consistent with '@node validates eagerly'.
- loop_history: add `loop_history: bool = False`; forward `loop_kwargs['history'] = loop_history` only when True. Legal by construction (Node-level self-loop). ForwardConstruct stays exempt (structural, documented).
- Cost: ~10 lines decorators.py, parity tests (decorator surface in tests/decorator/test_fanout_oracle.py + tests/test_loop.py), re-add @node-kwarg docs in oracle-ensemble.mdx + modifier-kwargs.mdx + node-api reference, website npm build.

### Option B — keep programmatic-only
- Docs already consistent post-fsoss; zero consumer demand; @node kwarg surface already large (~20 params). But leaves merge_model as the one Oracle field with 3-of-4 surface coverage, and the 'kwargs mirror the Oracle modifier fields 1:1' claim (forward.py docstring) already true elsewhere — the asymmetry invites the exact doc drift fsoss just fixed.

### Recommendation (ratification to architect atom)
Wire both (Option A). merge_model is a straight parity hole — every other surface has it and the forwarding helper + conditional-include pattern already exist. loop_history is legal precisely and only on the @node self-loop shape. Both are additive, default-preserving, no behavior change for existing pipelines. The recurring failure mode here is docs/surface drift; symmetric surfaces are cheaper than remembering exemptions.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/decorators.py:155-230 — _build_oracle_kwargs: THE reuse target for merge_model forwarding
- src/neograph/decorators.py:543-595, 622-630 — Oracle pipe sites (x2) + Loop kwarg assembly (loop_history goes here)
- src/neograph/modifiers.py:422, 571, 263-267 — field definitions + Construct-history ban
- src/neograph/_oracle.py:280, 368 — merge_model consumption (model_tier, merge_prompt path only)
- src/neograph/_state_write.py:133-142 + src/neograph/state.py:237 + _state_keys.py:130 — history runtime plumbing (already complete; no IR/factory change needed)
- src/neograph/loader.py:263-265 — 'forward only when explicitly set' exemplar
- src/neograph/forward.py:1150 (loop, no history — exempt), 1219-1259 (ensemble, has merge_model)
- tests/decorator/test_fanout_oracle.py, tests/test_loop.py:410-423, tests/modifiers/test_oracle.py — where parity tests belong
- website: walkthrough/oracle-ensemble.mdx:223, node-api/modifier-kwargs.mdx:588-597 — docs to re-edit if wiring

## Risks & Edge Cases
- merge_model + merge_fn: Oracle silently ignores it. If wired, decide decorator-level fail-loud (recommended, mirrors hooks check at decorators.py:203) vs mirror-the-modifier. If Oracle itself gains the validation instead, that's an IR change requiring three-surface tests.
- loop_history naming: existing loop kwargs are loop_when (prefixed) but max_iterations/on_exhaust (unprefixed). Docs bug used loop_history; keep that name — bare 'history' as a @node kwarg is too generic.
- Three-surface parity rule: FC's self.loop() is structurally EXEMPT from history (Construct-level ban) — state the exemption in the test docstring per CLAUDE.md's parity rule. self.ensemble already has merge_model, so Oracle parity is complete under Option A.
- Do NOT default merge_model='reason' in the node() signature — use None + conditional include, or a decorator default would mask future Oracle default changes (same rationale as loader.py:263 comment).
- If Option B is ratified: no code change, but consider a should_fail-style guard or doc note preventing re-documentation of the phantom kwargs (fsoss recurrence).
## Codebase Disease Scan (d5pvl)
Disease spec: modifier fields reachable programmatically but not forwarded as @node kwargs (three-surface parity drift, the shape that caused the fsoss doc bug). Shape: SYNTACTIC — diffed model_fields of Oracle/Loop/Each/Operator vs inspect.signature(node).

| Modifier field | @node kwarg today | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| Oracle.merge_model | MISSING | MIGRATE (this ticket) |

title: Cross-linking depth: dotted Type.member refs link to the exact field anchor, not just the type section
description:
CORE INVARIANT: a dotted `Type.member` reference in prose links to that MEMBER's anchor inside the type's rendered reference section (a per-field id), not merely to the type's section heading — and the member anchor is manifest-derived + slug-stable, so it never dangles.

WHY: Stage B already VALIDATES dotted `Type.member` refs against the manifest (HARD tier: a missing member fails the Astro build), but it AUTOLINKS them to the TYPE's anchor (`#node-model`), dropping the reader at the top of the section rather than at the field. Once kec0k renders per-symbol field TABLES, each field row is a natural link target. This closes the 'cross-link to methods/members' half of the maintainer's goal (the RAMP mechanism links Message.field to the field, not just the message).

DEPENDS ON kec0k: the field tables + their stable per-field anchors must exist to link to. This ticket has two halves:
1. GENERATION (kec0k-adjacent): kec0k's field-table rows must emit a stable, manifest-derived per-field anchor (e.g. id='node-model-outputs' or slug('Node.outputs')). Settle the anchor scheme so it (a) cannot collide with a symbol anchor and (b) is reproducible by the plugin from manifest field data alone. If kec0k does not already emit field anchors, that emission is part of THIS ticket.
2. RESOLUTION (plugin): teach remark-api.mjs to resolve a validated `Type.member` ref to the field anchor when the type is fielded and the member is a field; fall back to the type anchor (current behavior) when there is no field-level anchor (e.g. a method/callable member with no row). Never emit a link to a non-existent field anchor (dead-anchor-proof, same discipline as the symbol path).

ANTI-BAND-AID: the member anchor must be COMPUTED from the manifest field name, not hand-authored per ref. A prose ref and the rendered field row derive the SAME anchor from the SAME manifest field, so they cannot drift.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A prose `Node.outputs` (and `Tool.name`, `ToolInteraction.typed_result`, etc.) emits a resolving <a href=...#node-model-outputs> in website/dist/, landing on the field row.
- The field anchor is manifest-derived and slug-stable (github-slugger of the rendered row == the plugin-computed target).
- Mutation-proven: renaming a manifest field (regen) moves BOTH the row anchor and the link target in lockstep; a ref to a removed field still fails the build (existing HARD-tier behavior preserved).
- Members with no field row (callables/methods) gracefully fall back to the type anchor — no dead links.

NOT 0.6.0-gating. The most advanced cross-linking step; do it AFTER symbol-level linking (kec0k) and the coverage capstone (wqzel) prove out.
design:
## Core Invariant
A dotted `Type.member` prose ref and the rendered field row it links to derive the SAME anchor -- `{type_anchor}-{field_name}` -- from the SAME manifest field, so the link can never dangle: the plugin emits a field anchor ONLY when the type's heading is present on the page, and render_reference_sections() emits the field row's <span id> for every manifest field, keeping emission and resolution in manifest-driven lockstep (the byte-for-byte freshness guard enforces it).

## Implementation Plan
1. GENERATION -- scripts/gen_api_manifest.py: change _reference_field_table(fields) -> _reference_field_table(fields, anchor); append a self-closing `<span id="{anchor}-{f['name']}" />` to each row's Field cell (`| \`{name}\`<span id="{anchor}-{name}" /> | ... |`). render_reference_sections() (:544) passes entry['anchor'] as the second arg. Field names are lowercase snake_case identifiers so `{anchor}-{name}` is github-slugger-stable with no member slugging.
2. GENERATION -- regenerate the api.mdx GEN:reference-sections region by hand-pasting the new render_reference_sections() output between the sentinels (no injector script; main() only writes JSON). This is the LOCKSTEP move with step 1.
3. RESOLUTION -- website/plugins/remark-api.mjs:143-147: when `fields.some(f => f.name === member)` AND `headings.has(typeAnchor)`, emit `url: ${REF_PAGE}#${typeAnchor}-${member}` (was `#${typeAnchor}`). Preserve: the headings.has(typeAnchor) gate (dead-anchor proof), the resolved-but-undocumented early-return (line 149), and the non-field-member build-fail (line 153, HARD-tier preserved). Members with no field row keep falling back to the type anchor path -- but for a fielded owner every validated member IS a field, so the type-anchor fallback is the graceful default for the never-a-field case.
4. GUARD (TDD, write first) -- add to tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py: (a) every rendered field row emits a <span id="{anchor}-{field}"> and no field anchor collides with any symbol anchor; (b) every field name is a lowercase identifier (fails loud if a future uppercase field breaks slug==name). Update the freshness guard expectation by regenerating (step 2).
5. PLUGIN TEST -- website/plugins/remark-api.test.mjs: tighten test (a) to assert the EXACT field anchor '#lintissue-kind' (not just includes('#lintissue')); add a mutation-style test that a field member resolves to {type}-{field} and a non-field member still throws (HARD-tier preserved). Run `npm test` in website/.
6. VERIFY -- npm run build in website/ (HARD-tier validation runs here); grep dist/reference/api/index.html for id="node-model-outputs" and confirm a prose Node.outputs emits <a href=...#node-model-outputs>. Run uv run --extra dev pytest tests/test_guards_api_manifest.py.

## Anti-band-aid
The member anchor is COMPUTED (`{anchor}-{name}`) on BOTH the render side and the plugin side from the same manifest field name -- never hand-authored per ref. Renaming a manifest field regenerates the row's <span id> and the plugin recomputes the target in the same breath; a ref to a removed field still hits the existing HARD-tier build-fail. No per-ref anchor table, no drift seam.
notes: ## Findings (research neograph-41t30.2) ### Field-anchor scheme DECISION: `f"{type_anchor}-{field_name}"` via explicit self-closing - kec0k's field-table rows emit PLAIN markdown cells (`| \`name\` | type | req | default |`) with NO id today. Verified in dist/reference/api/index.html: only headings carry ids (blobresult, node-model, node-function); field rows have none. So per-field anchors do NOT exist yet -> emitting them is part of THIS ticket (GENERATION half). - Anchor value = `{type_anchor}-{field_name}` (e.g. Node model anchor node-model + outputs -> node-model-outputs; matches the acceptance example exactly). type_anchor = the symbol's manifest `anchor` (already collision-free + kind-namespaced by _disambiguate_anchors). - SLUG-STABILITY PROVEN: every field name across BOTH manifests (core + mcp) is a lowercase snake_case identifier (verified: 0 non-snake fields). slug() lowercases + strips specials + collapses whitespace; underscores survive. If MDX chokes on the span-in-cell, fallback idiom: place the immediately BEFORE the row or wrap differently -- but the span-in-Field-cell is the standard MDX anchor idiom and expected to work. - mcp-manifest fielded owners (StdioServer/HttpServer/McpCallResult) have NO heading on api.mdx -> plugin's headings.has(typeAnchor) gate is false -> they stay INERT (no dead field anchor). Scan: grep backticked `Type.member` refs across docs; check generator for existing field anchors; locate remark-api.mjs dotted resolution. title: Stage D: run live-model doc snippets against tests/fakes.py instead of skipping (recover design step 5/6 coverage)
description: tests/test_docs_snippets.py currently seeds each page's execution namespace with acc={} and SKIP-marks the ~10 live-model snippets (test-skip: live-model...). The Core Invariant's safety half holds (no executed snippet hits a real LLM), but design steps 5/6 intended pipeline-running snippets to EXECUTE against tests/fakes.py (configure_fake_llm / build_fake_llm_kwargs) so their pipeline-construction API is drift-checked, not skipped. Enhancement: seed configure_fake_llm per page (patching the llm factory) as the initial module_globals, then remove the live-model skip markers whose only obstacle was the missing fake, and confirm each runs green. Recovers drift-detection coverage on the ~10 live-model snippets without any real API key. Keep genuinely non-runnable fragments/async skipped. Report the new collected/skipped/executed numbers.
design:
## Core Invariant
No Stage-D-executed snippet ever reaches a real LLM/API key, AND the collected
python-block count is a clean partition (collected == executed + skipped) with
zero silent drops — recovering drift-coverage on a live-model block means MOVING
it from the skipped bucket to the executed bucket by neutralizing its factory at
the _get_llm seam, never by weakening that partition or the block-count pins.

## Implementation Plan
1. Add an offline-LLM seam fixture to tests/test_docs_snippets.py that REUSES the
   install_fake_llm two-site pattern (src/neograph/testing/fakes.py:704): patch
   BOTH neograph._llm._get_llm and neograph._tool_loop._get_llm. The patched
   function calls the ORIGINAL _get_llm; on SUCCESS return its result unchanged
   (preserves testing.mdx's inline FakeLLM -> zero behavior change to the 75
   already-green blocks); on EXCEPTION (quick-start's os.environ KeyError) return
   a generic offline double. Wire it into test_docs_page_python_snippets_execute
   via a `monkeypatch` param, installed once before the per-page block loop, so
   the seed is uniform per page (skipped blocks never invoke it -> inert).
2. Build a SMALL generic double reusing StructuredFake shape: on
   with_structured_output(model).invoke() return _build_instance(model); tolerate
   bind_tools (return self) for think/agent parity. _build_instance recurses
   model.model_fields filling required fields by type default (str->"", list->[],
   dict->{}, int->0, float->0.0, bool->False, Optional/None-able->None, nested
   BaseModel->recurse, Enum->first member, Literal->first arg). No per-node output
   knowledge — works for any think snippet. Keep it in this test module (test-only).
3. Remove ONLY the two genuinely-recoverable `test-skip: runs a live-model...`
   markers: quick-start.mdx:98 and :122. Do NOT touch the other 8 markers — they
   are non-runnable for reasons unrelated to the fake (forward-ref fragments /
   langfuse-extra imports). Reuse the existing _skip_reason/_SKIP_RE; add NO new
   regex (PROC-2 stays N/A).
4. Run `uv run --extra dev pytest tests/test_docs_snippets.py -q -s`; confirm the
   coverage line reports 373 collected − 296 skipped = 77 executed and all tests
   green (the two quick-start pages now execute their think pipeline against the
   generic double). The computed partition assertion and the checkpoint-resume=3 /
   migrating-prompt-compilers=8 pins are unaffected (block counts unchanged).
5. In the return/report: state the recovered coverage is 2 of the nominal 10, and
   raise the NEEDS USER INPUT decision on whether to (a) re-label the remaining 8
   `live-model` markers to their true reason and/or (b) make those doc pages
   self-contained — both are docs (Stage A/C) edits beyond this test-only task.

title: Public neograph_mcp API to CALL a federated MCP tool from a node/tool (client/session), not just bind 1:1
description:
## What
Add a PUBLIC neograph_mcp API to CALL a federated MCP tool from inside a node/tool body (a client/session), not just BIND one tool 1:1 as an lc_tool. Today the public surface is `mcp_tool_factory` / `mcp_tool_factories` (bind one federated tool as a callable lc_tool) + `mcp_resource_fetcher`. There is no way for a scripted composite tool to issue N calls to federated primitives (e.g. `search_crm_objects` then `get_crm_objects` xM) and assemble the result. Expose a minimal client/session: connect to an HttpServer/StdioServer spec with a token_provider, call `tool_name(**args)`, get the typed/structured result, close — reusing the same transport + rename + token machinery `mcp_tool_factory` already has internally.

## Why
agent-stark's `hubspot_comms(domain)` is a COMPOSITE over HubSpot's MCP CRM primitives (resolve company by domain → fetch associated notes/emails/calls/meetings → flatten to a typed list). ADR-0014 wants it federated behind the gateway with NO second HubSpot code path (user decision 2026-07-09, agent-stark stark-8ok). That is impossible with bind-one-tool factories: a composite must ISSUE the primitive calls itself. This is the same "MCP plumbing belongs in neograph, max-reuse its public API, file neograph-* gaps rather than hand-roll in agent-stark" pattern that produced neograph-g2jg (the offline-at-build + rename gaps the 54.4 GATE surfaced). Without this, agent-stark would hand-roll an MCP client — exactly what the seam forbids.

## Expectations after delivery
- A public neograph_mcp client/session (added to `__all__`) that a node/tool can use to call a federated tool by name with args + a token_provider, returning the structured result (rehydrated, same as mcp_tool_factory's rename path).
- agent-stark's composite `hubspot_comms` can compose over federated HubSpot CRM primitives with zero hand-rolled MCP transport.
- Offline-at-build preserved (deferred connect), consistent with mcp_tool_factory.

## Verification — integration & E2E only
- Integration: against a local sample MCP peer exposing 2+ primitives, the client connects (deferred), calls each primitive by name with args, and returns the structured result; token_provider identity rides on the call; a transport failure surfaces as a typed error (not a hang). Reuse neograph's existing MCP test fakes/peers.
- E2E: a composite node calls 2 federated primitives through the client and assembles a result — driven through neograph's normal node execution, asserting the assembled output (not internals).

## Acceptance
- Public client/session API exported from neograph_mcp; documented; offline-at-build.
- Integration tests green against a sample multi-primitive peer; token_provider honored.
- agent-stark stark-8ok can unblock its composite on this API (no hand-rolled MCP client in agent-stark).
design:
## Design (session 2026-07-10, adversarially reviewed — APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES, all folded in)
Full design: docs/design/mcp-session-api-2plcl-2026-07-10.md (authoritative; read it before implementing).

## Core Invariant
The MCP session is consumer-owned and battery-scoped: created ONLY inside src/neograph_mcp (never src/neograph — nmb2 guard untouched), ZERO network I/O at construction (connect defers to __aenter__), and its lifetime is <= one node/tool invocation (enter/exit in the same task, never stored in state/checkpoints). Identity is minted ONCE at __aenter__ via the existing _resolve_token machinery.

## API (public, via neograph_mcp.__all__)
mcp_session(server_key, spec, *, token_provider=None, config=None, stdio_token_arg='token', timeout=30.0) -> McpSession (async cm) with .call(tool_name, args) -> McpCallResult(content: list[dict], structured: dict|None, .text) and .tool_names(); McpToolCallError on isError=True (carries structuredContent). New module src/neograph_mcp/_session.py (~150 lines), reusing _connection/_client_for/_resolve_token*.

## Non-negotiables from the adversarial review (empirically probed)
1. Recursive single-leaf ExceptionGroup unwrap at BOTH __aenter__ and __aexit__ (connect failures arrive as nested ExceptionGroups; multi-leaf propagates as-is).
2. timeout=30.0 ships in v1 (NOT deferred): asyncio.timeout on connect + call_tool(read_timeout_seconds=...) per call — hung-initialize stdio hangs forever, silent-accepting HTTP stalls 300s without it.
3. PREREQUISITE: demo-server tool annotations -> dict[str, Any] (FastMCP emits NO structuredContent for bare '-> dict'/'-> list'); re-run tests/test_mcp_examples_e2e.py after.
4. Content conversion replicated locally against PUBLIC types (adapter block table incl. ResourceLink->file — get_deal exercises it); do NOT import the adapter's private _convert_call_tool_result. content is ALWAYS a list.
5. Paginated tools/list cursor loop for lazy stdio token-arg injection; minted token overrides caller-supplied arg.
6. No rename param on the call path (deliberate deviation from ticket wording — caller passes the gateway-namespaced name; discovery via tool_names()).

## Deliverables
_session.py + exports; tests in test_mcp_battery.py (offline-at-build; 2 primitives over ONE session with token echo; HttpServer bearer leg; refused-port/hung-server/isError typed-error trio; structured fidelity; E2E composite via compile()+arun()); example 26_mcp_composite_session.py; website mcp-client.mdx section (bind vs compose).

## Implementation Plan (validated — atom neograph-5hwbb.2)

CITES docs/design/mcp-session-api-2plcl-2026-07-10.md (authoritative; §-refs below).
Validated 2026-07-10 against current source; the doc is implementable as written.
The Core Invariant above stands unchanged. Naming: use `output_model=` (+ optional
`parse=`), NOT `output=` — §4bis supersedes §4.1's `output=` for battery-wide
consistency with `_wrap_output_model`/`resource_reader` (confirmed landed in
src/neograph_mcp/_client.py via neograph-wmmhc).

1. New module `src/neograph_mcp/_session.py`. Import langchain_mcp_adapters + mcp +
   langchain_core + pydantic ONLY (battery import guard bans langgraph + neograph
   run-layer modules; nothing else). REUSE `_connection`/`_client_for`/`_resolve_token`/
   `_resolve_token_no_config` from `_client.py` — do not re-derive transport/token glue.
2. `mcp_session(server_key, spec, *, token_provider=None, config=None, stdio_token_arg='token',
   timeout=30.0) -> McpSession` stores args only, ZERO network I/O (mirror
   TestLazySingleToolFactory offline-at-build proof, test_mcp_battery.py:308).
3. `McpSession.__aenter__`: mint token (`_resolve_token(tp, config)` if config is not None
   else `_resolve_token_no_config(tp)`), `_client_for(server_key, spec, token)`, enter
   `client.session(server_key)` (adapter client.py:124, auto_initialize=True) inside
   `asyncio.timeout(timeout)`. Wrap in a RECURSIVE single-leaf `_unwrap_single` (descend
   BaseExceptionGroup while len==1); same helper at `__aexit__` (§4.2, §9). This is NEW
   code — the mcp_resource_fetcher catch-in-scope trick does NOT cover connect-time
   nested groups.
4. `McpSession.call(tool_name, args=None, *, output_model=None, parse=None)`:
   `session.call_tool(name, args or {}, read_timeout_seconds=timedelta(seconds=timeout))`
   (mcp ClientSession.call_tool, confirmed sig). Convert `CallToolResult` LOCALLY:
   - Check `result.isError` FIRST -> raise `McpToolCallError` (convert `.content` via the
     local block table, carry `.structuredContent`). The session OWNS this raise (no
     adapter wrapper on this path — differs from `_wrap_output_model`).
   - Replicate the content-block table from adapter tools.py:175-223 using PUBLIC
     `langchain_core.messages.content.create_{text,image,file}_block` (do NOT import the
     adapter's private `_convert_mcp_content_to_lc_block`/`_convert_call_tool_result`).
     Include the ResourceLink image/* vs file branch and both EmbeddedResource arms.
     `content` is always a list.
   - `output_model` path: mirror `_wrap_output_model` (client.py:190-232) EXACTLY —
     `parse(structured) if parse else output_model.model_validate(structured)`; copy its
     missing-structuredContent `ValueError` message verbatim; let `ValidationError`
     propagate. `output_model=None` returns the full `McpCallResult`.
5. stdio identity: on first `call()` when spec is StdioServer and a token was minted, run a
   PAGINATED `list_tools()` (cursor loop over `ListToolsResult.nextCursor`), cache each
   tool's declared arg names from `Tool.inputSchema['properties']` (NOT `tool.args` — see
   notes Risk 1), inject `stdio_token_arg` into `args` when declared (minted token
   OVERRIDES caller value). Factor a shared `_declares_arg(declared_names, arg_name)` helper
   used by BOTH the session and a refactored `_inject_stdio_token` (helper takes a name-set,
   not a tool object). `tool_names()` triggers the same cached paginated listing on either
   transport.
6. Dataclasses/exception: `@dataclass(frozen=True) McpCallResult(content: list[dict],
   structured: dict|None)` + `.text` property; `McpToolCallError(Exception)` carrying
   server_key, tool_name, converted error content, structuredContent.
7. Export `mcp_session`, `McpSession`, `McpCallResult`, `McpToolCallError` through
   `src/neograph_mcp/__init__.py` import block AND `__all__` (public contract).
8. Tests in tests/test_mcp_battery.py mirroring TestTypedOutputModel/TestHttpServerSmoke
   (§7): offline-at-build; 2 primitives (crm_search + get_deal) over ONE session with
   same-`acting_as` echo; HttpServer bearer leg; typed-error trio (refused port ->
   unwrapped ConnectError; hung stdio -> TimeoutError at ~timeout via a 1-line sleep-server
   fixture; isError -> McpToolCallError); structured fidelity + `output_model` rehydration
   (crm_search) + missing-structuredContent ValueError (get_deal); E2E composite via
   compile()+arun(). Guards stay green unchanged.
9. Example 26 `examples/26_mcp_composite_session.py` (auto-discovered by
   tests/test_mcp_examples_e2e.py `examples/2?_mcp_*.py` glob, `--extra mcp-examples`) +
   website mcp-client bind-vs-compose section (§8).

The §4bis `output_model=` BOUND-TOOL work is a SIBLING bead (neograph-wmmhc) and is
ALREADY LANDED — this atom's scope is the SESSION API only.

## Research validation (atom neograph-5hwbb.2)

Validated the authoritative design doc (docs/design/mcp-session-api-2plcl-2026-07-10.md)
against CURRENT source after sibling neograph-wmmhc landed. Verdict: design is
ACCURATE and IMPLEMENTABLE as written; only naming (`output=` -> `output_model=`)
and a few line-number citations need the noted refresh. No blocking staleness.

### Findings — reuse targets (all confirmed present, src/neograph_mcp/_client.py)
- `_connection` (client.py:88) / `_client_for` (:104) — transport dict + MultiServerMCPClient, reuse as-is.
- `_resolve_token` (:114, config path) / `_resolve_token_no_config` (:128, no-config path) — reuse as-is; session mints via `_resolve_token` when `config is not None` else `_resolve_token_no_config`, exactly as §4.2 states.
- `_inject_stdio_token` (:160) — the declares-check semantics to MIRROR (not call directly; see Risk 1).
- Persistent-session precedent: `mcp_resource_fetcher` fetcher/replayer (:460/:477) already do `async with client.session(server_key) as session:` then `session.read_resource(...)` / `session.call_tool(real, args or {})`. This is the EXACT pattern the session API generalizes. The replayer already returns `list(getattr(result,'content',None) or [])` — precedent that `.content` is a list.
- wmmhc ADDED (confirmed): `ParseFn` type alias (:60), `_wrap_output_model` (:190), and `output_model=`/`output_models=`/`parse=`/`parses=` params on `mcp_tool_factory`/`mcp_tool_factories`. The session's typed-result path MUST reuse this exact wrap/validate/fail-loud pattern and naming.

### The `_wrap_output_model` pattern to align with (client.py:190-232) — THE typed-result contract
- Signature the session's `call(..., output_model=, parse=)` must match: `parse: ParseFn | None`, `output_model: type[BaseModel] | None`.
- Validate: `parse(structured) if parse is not None else output_model.model_validate(structured)`.
- Missing structuredContent -> `ValueError` with this EXACT message shape: "MCP tool '{name}' was declared with output_model={Model.__name__} but the server returned no structuredContent. The server tool likely has a bare '-> dict' / '-> list' return annotation; use '-> dict[str, Any]' or a Pydantic return type so FastMCP emits structuredContent." Copy this message.
- isError: on the SESSION path there is no adapter wrapper, so the session must check `CallToolResult.isError` ITSELF and raise `McpToolCallError` BEFORE the output_model/missing-structuredContent branch (design §4.2 "isError beats output"). This DIFFERS from `_wrap_output_model`, whose isError is raised upstream by the adapter — the session owns the isError raise.

### Adapter facts (langchain-mcp-adapters 0.3.0 — confirmed installed)
- `MultiServerMCPClient.session(server_name, *, auto_initialize=True)` — async cm, client.py:124, yields an initialized `ClientSession`. auto_initialize default True means the initialize handshake fires inside `__aenter__` (bound by `asyncio.timeout`).
- Content-conversion table lives in `_convert_mcp_content_to_lc_block` (tools.py:175-223), called by `_convert_call_tool_result` (tools.py:226). REPLICATE this table; do NOT import either private symbol. Full table confirmed:
  - TextContent -> `create_text_block(text=...)`
  - ImageContent -> `create_image_block(base64=..., mime_type=...)`
  - AudioContent -> `NotImplementedError`
  - ResourceLink: if mimeType startswith 'image/' -> `create_image_block(url=..., mime_type=...)` ELSE -> `create_file_block(url=..., mime_type=...)`  (design table simplified to 'file block'; the image/* branch exists — get_deal's links are application/json => file block)
  - EmbeddedResource: TextResourceContents -> text block; BlobResourceContents image/* -> image block(base64), else -> file block(base64)
- The block constructors `create_text_block/create_image_block/create_file_block` are PUBLIC: `from langchain_core.messages.content import ...` (verified importable). The adapter itself imports them from there. Battery import guard does NOT ban langchain_core, so this import is allowed.
- HTTP 300s stall class CONFIRMED: sessions.py builds `httpx.Timeout(timeout_seconds, read=sse_read_timeout_seconds)` (construction at sessions.py:354, not :56-57 as the doc cites — :56-57 are the CONSTANTS `DEFAULT_STREAMABLE_HTTP_TIMEOUT=30` / `..._SSE_READ_TIMEOUT=300`). Values still 30/300; the 300s read-stall hang is real. Minor stale citation only.

### mcp SDK 1.28.1 facts (confirmed)
- `ClientSession.call_tool(name, arguments=None, read_timeout_seconds: timedelta | None = None, ...) -> CallToolResult`. Design's `read_timeout_seconds=timedelta(seconds=timeout)` is correct.
- `CallToolResult` fields: `meta, content, structuredContent, isError`. All three the design relies on exist.
- `ClientSession.list_tools(cursor: str | None = None, ...) -> ListToolsResult`; `ListToolsResult` fields `meta, nextCursor, tools`. Cursor pagination loop confirmed (§4.2).
- `mcp.types.Tool` fields include `name, inputSchema, outputSchema, ...`. On the RAW session path declared args come from `Tool.inputSchema['properties']` — NOT `tool.args` (that is langchain BaseTool). See Risk 1.
- Content block types (`TextContent, ImageContent, AudioContent, EmbeddedResource, ResourceLink`) all importable from `mcp.types`. Also `TextResourceContents, BlobResourceContents` for EmbeddedResource arms.

### Demo server state AFTER wmmhc (examples/_mcp_demo_server.py — confirmed)
- `crm_search(query, token='anon') -> CrmSearchResult` (Pydantic: query, hits: list[DealHit], acting_as, bearer_identity) => structuredContent. THE typed round-trip fixture; a client-defined model rehydrates it.
- `kb_lookup`, `crm-perplexity_research`, `update_deal` -> `dict[str, Any]` => structuredContent.
- `get_deal(deal_id, token='anon') -> list` => content-only (1 TextContent + 2 ResourceLink blocks, application/json). Doubles as (a) the missing-structuredContent ValueError fixture and (b) the ResourceLink->file-block conversion fixture. §7.2/§7.5 assertions all satisfiable.
- Token echo: every tool stamps `acting_as` (stdio `token` arg) and `bearer_identity` (http Authorization header) — both observable on ONE call, so §7.2 (same acting_as across 2 calls over one session) and §7.3 (bearer over http, token arg untouched) are directly assertable.

### Guards (confirmed non-blocking)
- tests/test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py: `SRC_DIR = .../src/neograph` (line 26) — scans src/neograph ONLY. A new `src/neograph_mcp/_session.py` is OUTSIDE its scope; the battery owns sessions legitimately (it already does in mcp_resource_fetcher). No change needed there.
- Battery import guard `TestMcpBatteryImportsNoEngineSurfaces` (same file, :107): bans `langgraph` + `neograph.{runner,compiler,factory,_agent_cycle,_tool_loop,_dispatch,_execute}` imports in src/neograph_mcp. `_session.py` may import langchain_mcp_adapters + mcp + langchain_core + pydantic freely — none are banned. Stay clear of the listed neograph run-layer modules.

### Test conventions to mirror (tests/test_mcp_battery.py)
- `@requires_mcp` = `pytest.mark.skipif(not _HAS_MCP, ...)` (:44). `_demo_stdio_server()` (:99) returns `StdioServer(command=sys.executable, args=[str(DEMO_SERVER)])`.
- `_demo_http_server(state_file)` context manager (:137) yields a URL; `_demo_http_server_spec(url)` -> HttpServer (:166). `TestHttpServerSmoke` (:604) is the HTTP-leg exemplar.
- Offline-at-build exemplar: `TestLazySingleToolFactory.test_construction_is_zero_network_and_returns_a_coroutine_function` (:308) builds against a BOGUS unreachable spec and asserts no raise. Mirror it: `mcp_session(...)` against a bogus spec must construct without any connect.
- Typed-output exemplars to copy for the session's output_model path: `TestTypedOutputModel` (:397) — `_client_crm_models()` fixture (:381) defines a CLIENT-side model (independent of the server's), asserts `.model_validate` round-trip, the missing-structuredContent ValueError (get_deal), the ValidationError propagation, and the E2E BAML-render (:539). Session tests should mirror this class structure.
- Run: `uv run --extra dev --extra mcp pytest tests/test_mcp_battery.py`; examples E2E: `tests/test_mcp_examples_e2e.py` (add example 26, auto-discovered by the `examples/2?_mcp_*.py` glob, needs `--extra mcp-examples`).

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Risk 1 (adapter shape mismatch on the stdio declares-check): `_inject_stdio_token` (:160) reads declared args from langchain `tool.args`. The SESSION path has NO langchain BaseTool — it works with raw `mcp.types.Tool` from `list_tools()`, whose declared args live in `Tool.inputSchema.get('properties', {})`. The design's §4.3 "factor so `_inject_stdio_token` and the session use one helper" is achievable ONLY if the shared helper takes a SET of declared arg names (computed per-path: `set(tool.args or {})` for the factory, `set((t.inputSchema or {}).get('properties', {}))` for the session) rather than a tool object. Implementer must extract a `_declares_arg(declared_names, arg_name)`-style helper, not reuse `_inject_stdio_token` verbatim.
- Risk 2 (isError ownership differs from the factory path): on the factory/bound path the adapter raises `_MCPToolExecutionError` for isError before neograph sees it. On the SESSION path neograph calls `session.call_tool` directly and gets a `CallToolResult` with `isError=True` (no exception) — the session MUST inspect `.isError` and raise `McpToolCallError` itself, converting `.content` via the local table, and BEFORE the output_model branch. This is new code with no factory-path analogue to copy; §4.2 specifies it correctly.
- Risk 3 (naming, already resolved in the doc/ticket): design §4.1/§4.2 write `output=`; §4bis + ticket note (2) SUPERSEDE it to `output_model=` for battery-wide consistency with `_wrap_output_model`/`resource_reader`. Implementer uses `output_model=` (+ optional `parse=`). Not a contradiction — the doc self-corrects in §4bis/§379.
- Risk 4 (ExceptionGroup unwrap): design mandates a RECURSIVE single-leaf `_unwrap_single` at BOTH `__aenter__` and `__aexit__`. The `mcp_resource_fetcher` precedent (catch McpError in-scope, re-raise after the `async with`) is a DIFFERENT technique for a different shape and does NOT cover the connect-time nested ExceptionGroup — the session needs the new recursive unwrapper. Python 3.12 `BaseExceptionGroup` is available (repo runs 3.12). The doc marks these *(probed)*; re-probing live is out of scope for this validation, but the stack versions (adapters 0.3.0 / mcp 1.28.1 / httpx 0.28.1) are byte-for-byte what the doc probed against — confirmed via importlib.metadata.
- Risk 5 (line-citation drift, non-blocking): doc cites `tools.py:175-283` (correct region), `client.py ~125` (correct: session at :124), `sessions.py:56-57` (constants correct; the httpx.Timeout construction is now :354). Cosmetic only.
- NOT a risk: no new sibling changes to _client.py beyond wmmhc's output_model work (file mtime 2026-07-10 11:31 matches the wmmhc landing). `__init__.py` `__all__` currently exports StdioServer/HttpServer/ToolFactory/mcp_tool_factories/mcp_tool_factory/mcp_resource_fetcher — the session symbols (`mcp_session`, `McpSession`, `McpCallResult`, `McpToolCallError`) must be ADDED to both the import block and `__all__`.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-2plcl)

Pattern: hand-rolled MCP session/client plumbing (MultiServerMCPClient / client.session() / get_tools() / raw session.call_tool()) OUTSIDE the neograph_mcp battery's own helpers — code that should route through the battery's public API instead of re-implementing transport/session/token. SYNTACTIC disease (greppable) — single-executor grep, no semantic fan-out, no .claude/code-review artifact needed.

Scan command (reproducible):
  grep -rn "MultiServerMCPClient\|\.session(\|\.get_tools(\|\.call_tool(\|load_mcp_tools" src/ examples/ tests/

Total instances found: ~40 across 8 files. Bucketed (representative rows):

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | src/neograph_mcp/_client.py:107,111,186,260,466,481,482 | MultiServerMCPClient/get_tools/client.session/call_tool | ALLOWLIST | this IS the battery — the legitimate OWNER of the plumbing (nmb2: session owned inside the battery, never src/neograph). The new _session.py adds to this owner. |
| 2 | examples/23_mcp_client_selective_binding.py:432-475 | MultiServerMCPClient/get_tools in `# ...` comments | ALLOWLIST | Appendix A/B — the DOCUMENTED hand-rolled escape hatch (pedagogical), all inside comments, not live code. |
| 3 | examples/24_mcp_resources_from_resource.py:178-183, 399-403 | client.session()+session.call_tool() to build a get_deal tool + arm_email_expiry | ALLOWLIST | hand-rolls to preserve RAW resource_link blocks (string uris, the shape the ref-lift scans). The new mcp_session.call() CONVERTS blocks via the adapter table (resource_link -> file block), so it does NOT serve this raw-block need — this is a distinct requirement, not a bypass of the session API. Confirmed by reading _make_get_deal_tool (:172-199). No current session-API consumer shares this need (agent-stark hubspot_comms wants STRUCTURED results, not raw blocks) -> not a DEFER, genuinely out of scope. |
| 4 | examples/13b_mcp_tools.py:6,28,66; examples/_mcp_demo_server.py:57 | load_mcp_tools / MultiServerMCPClient in prose/comments | ALLOWLIST | documentation prose, not live hand-rolling. |
| 5 | tests/test_mcp_examples_e2e.py:72-274 (many) | MultiServerMCPClient + get_tools/session/call_tool | ALLOWLIST | E2E HARNESS asserting TRANSPORT-level behavior directly (per-operator identity, expiry self-heal, resource reads) — test infrastructure that verifies the raw adapter, not production code that should use the session API. |
| 6 | tests/test_mcp_battery.py:4; test_mcp_async_factory.py:73; test_guards_mcp_session_ownership.py:12-78 | prose/comments + the ownership guard's own regex/meta-tests | ALLOWLIST | prose + the guard that ENFORCES this very invariant. |
