title: Oracle over an agent/act node with multiple upstream inputs OR dict-form outputs: bundle-port synthesis
description: Follow-on to neograph-qot6 (single-producer input-port synthesis, landed). qot6 auto-wraps Oracle-over-agent when the agent has ZERO or ONE upstream producer (single-type inputs, or a single-key dict-form fan-in) -- the value maps cleanly onto the single-value subgraph boundary (neo_subgraph_input). Two sub-cases stay fail-loud: (1) MULTIPLE distinct dict-form upstream producers -- the single-value boundary can't carry N values; needs a synthesized 'packer' node in the parent that bundles the N upstreams into one port model, plus an 'unpacker' inside the sub-construct (or a prompt-var mapping) so the agent still sees the original keys. (2) dict-form (multi-output) agent OUTPUTS -- the sub-construct has a single output boundary port. Both are genuinely ambiguous (prompt variable surface for the bundle) so were left fail-loud with precise ConstructErrors. See src/neograph/_fan_agent.py::_unsupported_reason and docs/design/fan-over-agent-node-2026-07-07.md.
notes: 2026-07-07 verification note for this seat (Wave 8): the shipped qot6 agent-fan tests assert merged-N (wiring) but NOT that each isolated cycle SAW the upstream value — the verifier's echo probe (scratchpad/probe_qot6.py pattern: prompt_compiler renders upstream into the message, echo fake reflects it, merge concatenates) proved value delivery manually. When this seat touches the fan tests, COMMIT that echo-style value-delivery assertion for the single-type, dict-form, and DI shapes so the property is pinned, not probe-only.
close_reason: Bundle-port synthesis. (1) Oracle over agent with MULTIPLE dict-form producers now supported via packer-port synthesis: wrap_fan_over_agents takes scripted_lookup; _expand_agent_node returns [packer, wrapped_sub] for multi-producer. Synthesized parent packer bundles N upstreams into a _NeoAgentPort_* model; inner per-key unpacker nodes re-expose the ORIGINAL producer names inside the sub-construct so the agent's dict-form fan-in + prompt-var surface is unchanged. Scoped to Oracle; Each/Loop multi-input stay fail-loud (precise error). (2) Dict-form multi-output agent OUTPUTS kept fail-loud by design (single output boundary + undefined N-way merge of secondary outputs would silently drop declared outputs) - sharpened message + should_fail fixture. Moved oracle_over_agent_multiple_inputs.py should_fail->should_pass; added oracle_over_agent_multi_output.py should_fail. WAVE-8 value-delivery pins committed: TestOracleOverAgentValueDelivery asserts each isolated cycle SAW its upstream value for single-type/dict-form/DI shapes (echo prompt-compiler+echo ReAct fake+concat merge); TestOracleOverAgentMultiInputBundle asserts BOTH bundled values reach each cycle. @node-surface multi-input parity test added. title: Optional per-run cache for FROM_RESOURCE fetch on the agent/act async path (avoid per-superstep re-fetch)
description: Follow-on to neograph-3q6j (async di_inputs twin). If per-turn resource re-fetching becomes a cost concern, cache the fetched value for the duration of one run. NOTE: this is gated on the SAME missing prerequisite as neograph-m6d3.8 — there is no sound per-run cache key (no framework-minted run_id threaded through config; thread_id is absent without a checkpointer and stable across resume). Build only atop a sound per-run key AND a real cost-driven consumer. Relates to neograph-3q6j; shares the run_id-threading prerequisite with neograph-m6d3.8.
close_reason: Per-run FROM_RESOURCE fetch cache on the agent/act async path. _ainject_di_inputs (_dispatch.py) now resolves each FROM_RESOURCE binding through _run_cache.aget_or_build, keyed on StateKeys.RUN_ID (same primitive as m6d3.8): the awaited fetch happens ONCE per run and is reused across the ReAct cycle's supersteps; a resume re-mints RUN_ID -> cache miss -> refetch. Copy-not-mutate idempotence preserved (resolved value still stashed into a fresh config copy). TDD-first tests in tests/test_agent_cycle_run_cache.py (TestPerRunResourceFetchCache): fetcher called ONCE across a multi-turn arun (was 6, RED->GREEN) and refetched on resume (life-1=1, life-2=2) via file-backed AsyncSqliteSaver. title: Oracle/Each over an agent/act node WITH upstream inputs: input-port synthesis
description: Follow-on to neograph-m6d3.6 (fan-over-agent auto-wrap). title: hgpt v2b: manifest-driven hydration + layered expiry (read -> replay producing_call -> fail loud) + templated URIs
description: Child 4 of neograph-hgpt per docs/design/hgpt-refined-design-2026-07-06.md. FromResource(ref=)/manifest-driven + RFC-6570 templated URIs (borrows v1a interpolation). LAYERED EXPIRY: (1) resources/read on ref.uri; (2) on -32002 REPLAY ref.producing_call and read the fresh link; (3) fail loud ResourceExpiredError(ref, node). Silent staleness is worse than failure. HARD GATE: replay is only legal for idempotent producers — depends on the tool-idempotency annotation ticket; refuses non-idempotent producers loudly (purity test: a read may replay, a mutation may not). Also surfaces ttl_ms when servers ship SEP-2549. Risk mitigations from the design: FromResource(text) carries max_bytes failing loud at node entry before the blob reaches a prompt; lint fails loud when a node hydrates a kind no upstream producer emits (flat servers fall back to v1a readers — R1 and R2 cover each other's gaps). Depends on v2a.

title: Tool idempotency annotation (idempotent=True on Tool/resource_reader) — the replay-safety gate for manifest re-derivation
description: Spun out of hgpt-refined-design-2026-07-06.md Risk 1 (also the field survey's open question 4). Replaying a producing tool call to re-derive an expired resource is only safe for idempotent/read-only tools — replaying an act-mode producer double-mutates. Add an idempotent: bool = False (or side_effect: Literal[read, mutate]) annotation to the Tool spec + resource_reader (readers default idempotent=True); hydration replay (hgpt v2b) gates on it and refuses non-idempotent producers with a typed error. Also useful independently: lint can warn when an act-mode node's tools are all-idempotent (mode probably should be agent), and future Level-B step-memo journaling would key on it. Small, self-contained, blocks hgpt v2b.
close_reason: Implemented: idempotent: bool = False on Tool + resource_reader (default True); NonIdempotentReplayError typed error exported; lint act_mode_all_idempotent_tools WARN. TDD, all green (2578 passed, ruff+mypy clean).

title: Trace span hygiene: name node runnables (kill node_wrapper spans) + attach node metadata to the engine's own callback spans (GH issue 4, gap-2 re-scoped)
description:
From GitHub issue 4 gap-2, RE-SCOPED by empirical probe (2026-07-06, scratchpad cb_span_probe.py): the issue claimed the graph structure is invisible to tracing backends and proposed native OTEL spans — REFUTED: LangGraph already fires on_chain_start/on_chain_end per node to any config.callbacks handler, so a Langfuse/OTEL-bridge handler already gets the full DAG tree. What the probe DID expose is hygiene debt in what those engine spans look like: every node emits a child span literally named node_wrapper (neograph's internal factory wrapper name leaking into every consumer's trace tree), and the engine spans carry none of the rich attributes neograph already computes into structlog (mode, input/output types, duration, token usage).

SCOPE (Layer-2/compile-time only — enrich the ENGINE's spans, never emit parallel ones): (1) name the wrapper runnables so traces read as the user's node names — RunnableLambda accepts a name (or .with_config(run_name=...)); apply at the factory/make_node_fn sites AND the agent-cycle bodies, oracle redirects, subgraph fn, gate/operator/parse nodes (audit every add_node callable for its trace name; the m6d3 cycle nodes should read {node}__agent/{node}__tools/{node}__parse which they may already via add_node names — verify which layer wins); (2) attach metadata: run_name/tags/metadata via .with_config on the wrapper — node mode, declared output type, neograph node id — so callback backends index them; token usage stays on the LLM child spans where LangChain puts it; (3) verify with the probe pattern: handler captures names+metadata, asserts no node_wrapper anywhere and user node names present; (4) confirm zero cost when no callbacks attached (with_config is static — no runtime branching).

NON-GOAL (locked by the companion observe= ticket's rejection): no neograph-emitted OTEL spans, no tracer dependency, no wrapping of engine scheduling. The structlog events stay as-is (they serve log consumers; this ticket serves trace consumers via the engine's own channel).
notes: DONE (wave B, not committed). Added src/neograph/_trace.py: named(runnable, name, *, mode, output_type, node_id) -> late STATIC .with_config(run_name/tags/metadata) binding. run_name overrides the leaking inner wrapper __name__ so engine callback spans read as the user node name; metadata carries neograph_node/neograph_mode/neograph_output_type; tag neograph:node. Applied at: factory.make_node_fn (both returns, full metadata), compiler._add_subgraph (subgraph_fn, mode=subgraph), _wiring._add_arm_nodes (arm subgraphs), _wire_oracle (gen+merge), _wire_each (fan), _add_each_oracle_fused (redirect + group_merge_barrier), _add_agent_cycle (3 ReAct bodies). make_subgraph_fn keeps its bare dual-path RunnableLambda return (async guard pins it) — naming applied at add_node sites instead. Guard-first probe tests/test_trace_span_hygiene.py: FAILED 4/7 pre-fix (node_wrapper/subgraph_node leak), PASS 7/7 post-fix. Covers scripted/think/agent + branch + subgraph; asserts no wrapper-name leak, node names present, metadata attached, static-binding zero-cost. Token usage untouched (stays on LLM child spans). No native OTEL/tracer dep (NON-GOAL respected). mypy/ruff clean.

title: Intermittent neo_agent_* leak: async-resume results + cross-test-file channel pollution (two manifestations, likely one root cause)
description:
Two independent verifiers observed neo_agent_* channels escaping containment, both intermittent/order-dependent — likely one root cause in how agent-cycle state channels interact with the pjqe output_schema filtering and/or state-model caching:

MANIFESTATION 1 (runtime, observed once, not reproduced after): on a cold first arun in a fresh session, TestBudgetAcrossCheckpoint [arun] FAILED with neo_agent_budget_greedy / neo_agent_messages_greedy / neo_agent_tool_log_greedy leaked into the RESUMED arun result. Passed on 40+ subsequent runs (isolation, full file, full suite). Consistent with the residual gaps runner.py:442-447 documents for langgraph 1.2.4 output_schema filtering — but batch ainvoke SHOULD be filtered per R1, so a cold-path leak suggests the output-schema model or channel registration has an ordering/caching dependency.

MANIFESTATION 2 (test infra, reproducible): running test_agent_subgraph_keystone.py and test_hitl.py in the SAME pytest process trips the keystone no-leak guard (test_agent_subgraph_keystone.py:238) with a neo_agent_* channel from the OTHER file's pipeline — cross-file pollution. Also the probable identity of the transient 2-failures observed in a full-suite run raced against concurrent pytest processes on 2026-07-04 (passed clean twice after).

TRIAGE DIRECTION: reproduce M2 first (deterministic: same-process file pair), trace WHERE the foreign channel enters (registry? compile_state_model cache? add_messages channel registration keyed globally instead of per-compile?), then evaluate whether M1 is the same mechanism surfacing at runtime under a cold import order. The per-compile registry decision (project memory: architecture decisions 2026-05) says compile-scoped registries are the norm — check whether agent-cycle channel synthesis honored that. Fix must be structural (scoping), not a test-ordering band-aid; the keystone no-leak guard and the item-c no-leak assertion both stay as-is (they caught this — they are working).
design:
## Root Cause
NOT a neograph defect on the current tree. Exhaustive investigation refutes every structural hypothesis (per-compile channel scoping is correct; output_schema filters batch invoke/ainvoke including add_messages reducer channels; no global channel state; auto-resume returns the filtered invoke). The M1/M2 sightings were transient (both verifiers saw them pass immediately after) — most consistent with a langgraph 1.2.4 cold-path quirk, not a scoping bug.

## Reproduce-atom deviation (documented, not rationalized)
The bug-triage reproduce atom's strict acceptance is 'a FAILING test'. No failing test is possible: the behavioral symptom does not reproduce and the structural hypotheses are refuted, so there is no disease to guard against either. Fabricating a red test would violate test integrity. Instead the reproduce artifact is a DETERMINISTIC PASSING guard (TestCrossCompileChannelIsolation) that pins the per-compile channel-scoping invariant so a future regression is caught deterministically.

## Fix Approach
Keep-open. The only remaining action is the maintainer's architectural call on whether to add a belt-and-suspenders _strip_internals net on the batch run()/arun() exits (M1 as cited engine-gap) — a partial reversal of pjqe Item A. Not done autonomously because the bug is unreproducible and pjqe was a deliberate recent decision by the same maintainer.
notes: 2026-07-06 team-wave re-verification: TestCrossCompileChannelIsolation (2 params run/arun) GREEN in 0.29s. No production change per keep-open decision; guard confirmed present + committed. Remains OPEN as P3 sentinel pending maintainer's belt-and-suspenders _strip_internals call.
close_reason: DELIBERATE CLOSE per the y5ux Wave-4 disposition rule (fix-or-deliberate-close; keep-open limbo disallowed). Not reproducible: exhaustive structural refutation 2026-07-04 (per-compile channels, output_schema filtering re-confirmed vs R1 research, auto-resume path); independent verifier stress runs 2026-07-07: M2 file-pair 16/16 across repeated+reversed orderings, M1 2/2, isolation guard 2/2. The belt-and-suspenders _strip_internals question was ALREADY DECIDED 2026-07-04: NO — a defensive strip would destroy the detection signal. STANDING ALARM: TestCrossCompileChannelIsolation + the keystone no-leak guard + item-c no-leak assertion remain permanently; ON NEXT SIGHTING reopen at P2 and capture the full result dict + exact import/collection order immediately.

title: Optional within-run live-handle reuse for the agent cycle (§5 two-lifetime)
description: Deferred per the m6d3.2 fork decision. The inline agent cycle rebuilds the LLM client once per superstep (correct for a stateless message-history LLM). §5's within-run reuse would cache the live LLM/tool handle across the cycle's supersteps WITHIN one run (matching the monolith's build-once-per-execution) for performance. NOT built in m6d3.2: there is no reliable per-run cache key for run() without a checkpointer (no thread_id), and a wrong key is the hidden-bug landmine the architect flagged. Build only if a real consumer needs the perf, and only atop a sound per-run key (e.g. after a run_id is threaded through config). Must invalidate on resume (fresh process re-mints), preserving the two-lifetime rule.
notes:
2026-07-07 INVESTIGATION (Wave-1 team, exec-m6d38): NOT DOABLE SOUNDLY YET — no code changes made.

Evidence:
- grep 'run_id' src/ -> ZERO hits. No framework-minted per-run identity is threaded through config.
- thread_id only in runner.py (docstrings + resume logic ~412/691/700-704); user-supplied only, meaningful only with a persistent checkpointer.
- config['configurable'] keys enumerated at _state_keys.py:54-88 (_neo_input, _neo_di_inputs, _neo_stream_custom, node_id, project_root) — none is a stable-per-run, invalidated-on-resume identity.
- thread_id fails BOTH soundness halves: (1) absent without a checkpointer (bare run()); (2) SAME id reused on resume (runner.py:700-704), so keying a live-handle cache on it reuses a stale handle across fresh-process resume = the two-lifetime violation the architect flagged. Current per-superstep rebuild (_agent_cycle.py:148-164) is documented correct-on-resume.
- No consumer: only m6d3.8 mentions within-run handle reuse; no piarch request.

BLOCKED on: a framework-minted per-run identity in config['configurable'] (e.g. StateKeys.RUN_ID = '_neo_run_id'), minted fresh in runner._prepare/_aprepare per execution and NOT persisted into the checkpoint (fresh-process resume re-mints it, satisfying two-lifetime rule §5). Only atop that key can the live LLM/tool handle be cached across the inline agent cycle's supersteps. ALSO still gated on a real consumer requesting the perf. When BOTH hold, implement TDD-first (failing test: handle reused across supersteps within one run AND re-minted on resume).
close_reason: Within-run live LLM/tool handle reuse for the inline agent cycle. Added src/neograph/_run_cache.py (per-run cache keyed on StateKeys.RUN_ID: config-only, stable within a run, re-minted on resume -> cache miss -> rebuild; bounded LRU; no-RUN_ID -> never caches). Wired the LLM client + tool-instance builds in _tool_loop.py (_build_loop_preamble, _prepare_tool_loop, _aprepare_tool_loop) through get_or_build/aget_or_build. TDD-first tests in tests/test_agent_cycle_run_cache.py (TestWithinRunLlmHandleReuse): llm_factory built ONCE across a multi-turn run's supersteps (was 6, RED->GREEN), and rebuilt on resume (life-1=1, life-2=2) via file-backed SqliteSaver. Near-dup helper guard allowlist updated for the get_or_build/aget_or_build twin. Full suite: 2641 passed.

title: Generalize fan-target from fan_name to (entry_node, exit_node) so Each/Oracle can wrap an inline agent cycle
description: Follow-up to the agent-as-subgraph INLINE decision (binding condition 3). Today _wire_each/_wire_oracle Send to exactly ONE node and defer the barrier on [fan_name]; an inline agent/act node expands into a multi-node region ({node}__agent/{node}__tools/{node}__parse), which cannot be the single Send target. m6d3.2 ships a COMPILE-TIME ERROR ('Each/Oracle over an agent/act node not supported') + should_fail fixture as the safe stopgap. This ticket is the principled fix: generalize the fan target abstraction from a single fan_name to an (entry_node, exit_node) pair so Each/Oracle (and Loop) can wrap a multi-node region. When done, the compile-time error from m6d3.2 is removed and its should_fail fixture moves to should_pass. Blocked until the inline expander (m6d3.2) lands.
notes: 2026-07-07 RE-SCOPED + DELIVERED (Wave-1 team). The prescribed inline (entry,exit) fan mechanism was proven ARCHITECTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for N>1: LangGraph Send isolates only the first superstep, so an agent's shared ReAct reducer channels (neo_agent_messages_*) merge fanned branches (minimal repro in docs/design/fan-over-agent-node-2026-07-07.md). Replaced deliverable 1 with AUTO-WRAP: a compile pre-pass (_fan_agent_wrap.wrap_fan_over_agents, classifier _fan_agent.is_supported_fan_over_agent) rewrites a supported fan-over-agent Node into an isolated single-node sub-construct routed through the EXISTING subgraph fan path. Shipped: Oracle over a self-contained agent/act node (three-surface tested); m6d3.2 blanket compile error removed; oracle_over_agent_node fixture moved should_fail->should_pass. Hard cases FAIL-LOUD (assembly-time ConstructError) with follow-up beads: Each-over-agent=neograph-1h8c, Loop-over-agent=neograph-gk3e, agent-with-upstream-inputs=neograph-qot6, plus a residual arm-nested CompileError. DECISION taken autonomously (user AskUserQuestion timed out): base-case + fail-loud (option 1). If fuller coverage was wanted, reopen or prioritize the 3 follow-ups. All green: 2578 passed, ruff+mypy clean.
close_reason: Re-scoped to auto-wrap (inline mechanism proven impossible) and delivered: Oracle-over-self-contained-agent works, compile error removed, fixture moved. Hard cases fail-loud + follow-ups filed (1h8c/gk3e/qot6). See notes + docs/design/fan-over-agent-node-2026-07-07.md.

title: Thread RunnableConfig into tool invocations (tool_fn.invoke/ainvoke) for callback propagation
description: Surfaced in Phase 1f observability scan (neograph-w74k.2.6). _tool_loop.py invokes tools without config: sync :462 'tool_fn.invoke(tool_call["args"])' and async :691 'await tool_fn.ainvoke(tool_call["args"])' — neither passes config=config, so LangChain callbacks/tracers attached via config['callbacks'] do NOT propagate INTO tool execution. This is a SYMMETRIC pre-existing gap (both sync and async omit it), NOT introduced by the async work — so out of scope for Phase 1f (which requires only that async preserves sync's observability parity, which it does). Fix: thread config into both tool_fn.invoke/ainvoke so tool spans nest under the run trace. Low priority; do together for both surfaces to keep parity.

title: ARCH: relocate _BranchNode out of forward.py (DIP inversion — compiler/state/_wiring import it UP from the DX layer)
description: Split out from neograph-8cqd (Option A scope was kept to the declared-output selector + TS-justification scrub). Finding from the DDD + SOLID three-lens review (docs/design/ir-item-dispatch-{ddd,solid-grasp}-2026-06-04.md): _BranchNode is a core-IR concept but is DEFINED in the DX-layer forward.py (class _BranchNode(Modifiable), forward.py:350) and imported UPWARD by compiler.py:44, state.py:16, _wiring.py. That is a DIP inversion / bounded-context leak. Relocate _BranchNode to a neutral low-level IR module (e.g. a new _ir_branch.py or alongside the IR protocols) so the lower layers no longer import from forward.py. Add/extend an import-DAG guard. Behavior-preserving; guard-first. Out of scope: any ConstructItem-protocol widening (that remains gated on a 4th item type per neograph-8cqd S9.4).
design:
## Core Invariant
_BranchNode and its _BranchMeta/_ConditionSpec are core-IR concepts owned by a neutral low-level module (_ir_branch.py); the compiler/state/wiring layers import them from there and NEVER import from the DX layer forward.py -- dependency points DX -> IR, never IR -> DX.

## Fix Approach
Relocate _ConditionSpec + _BranchMeta + _BranchNode to a new src/neograph/_ir_branch.py (runtime deps: modifiers.Modifiable/ModifierSet; Node/Construct under TYPE_CHECKING). forward.py imports them back; compiler.py/state.py/_wiring.py repoint to _ir_branch. Guard-first: add an import-DAG guard banning forward imports from the lower layers (RED now, GREEN after). Behavior-preserving.
notes:
## Findings
- _BranchNode defined at forward.py:350 (DX layer). Imported UPWARD by compiler.py:44, state.py:16, _wiring.py:35 (all `from neograph.forward import _BranchNode`). That is the DIP inversion: lower compiler/state/wiring layers depend on the DX layer.
- Those 3 modules import ONLY _BranchNode and access branch._neo_branch_meta.condition_spec via attributes (no direct import of _BranchMeta/_ConditionSpec).
- _BranchNode (forward.py:350) deps: Modifiable, ModifierSet (modifiers.py, IR layer), and _BranchMeta (annotation only -> stringized via `from __future__ import annotations`).
- _BranchMeta (forward.py:337) deps: _ConditionSpec + list[Node|Construct] (annotations).
- _ConditionSpec (forward.py:311): pure frozen dataclass; deps are annotations only (Node|Construct|None, Any).
- _BranchPoint/_BranchTrace (forward.py:321/331) depend on forward-internal proxies (_ConditionProxy/_Proxy) -> STAY in forward.py.
- Other modules referencing _BranchNode (construct.py, _normalize.py, _validation_types.py, modifiers.py) do so ONLY in comments/docstrings -- no real imports/isinstance. No changes needed there.
- Cycle check: modifiers.py runtime-imports only _dev_warnings + errors (node/construct under TYPE_CHECKING) -> a new _ir_branch importing modifiers has no cycle. Node/Construct referenced only as TYPE_CHECKING annotations in _ir_branch.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/forward.py:311-364 -- _ConditionSpec, _BranchMeta, _BranchNode (move these three).
- src/neograph/compiler.py:44, state.py:16, _wiring.py:35 -- repoint imports to _ir_branch.
- src/neograph/modifiers.py:190 Modifiable, :545 ModifierSet (runtime deps of _BranchNode).
- src/neograph/_ir_protocols.py -- references _BranchNode in docstring only.
- tests/test_guards_assembly.py:305 TestAssemblyClusterImportDAG + _parse_neograph_imports helper (extend / add a guard here).

## Plan
1. New module src/neograph/_ir_branch.py: `from __future__ import annotations`; import Modifiable, ModifierSet from modifiers; TYPE_CHECKING import Node, Construct; define _ConditionSpec, _BranchMeta, _BranchNode.
2. forward.py: delete the 3 classes; add `from neograph._ir_branch import _BranchMeta, _BranchNode, _ConditionSpec`.
3. compiler.py / state.py / _wiring.py: `from neograph.forward import _BranchNode` -> `from neograph._ir_branch import _BranchNode`.
4. Update test imports of _BranchNode from forward if any.
5. Guard-first: add import-DAG guard asserting compiler/state/_wiring (and other lower layers) do NOT import `forward`.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- get_type_hints on the moved dataclasses would need Node/Construct resolvable; add TYPE_CHECKING import (annotations are stringized, so no runtime need). Low risk -- these are internal sentinels.
- Behavior-preserving: pure relocation; isinstance(_BranchNode) identity unchanged (single class, single new module). No public API change (_BranchNode is private).
- Three-surface parity: _BranchNode is produced only by forward.py (ForwardConstruct branch tracing); declarative/programmatic do not create it. Refactor does not change behavior on any surface; full suite + test_forward.py cover it.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-9epk)
Disease: a lower compiler/IR-layer module importing UP from the DX layer forward.py (DIP inversion / bounded-context leak).

Scan command (SYNTACTIC -- single grep, no fan-out):
  grep -rn "from neograph.forward import\|import neograph.forward\| forward\." src/neograph/ | grep -v "forward.py:"
Total forward-import sites: 4 (+1 comment).

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | _wiring.py:35 | from neograph.forward import _BranchNode | MIGRATE | repoint to _ir_branch |
| 2 | compiler.py:44 | from neograph.forward import _BranchNode | MIGRATE | repoint to _ir_branch |
| 3 | state.py:16 | from neograph.forward import _BranchNode | MIGRATE | repoint to _ir_branch |
| 4 | __init__.py:48 | from neograph.forward import ForwardConstruct | ALLOWLIST | package facade re-exports the PUBLIC DX class; the top-level __init__ sits above all layers -- legitimate, not a DIP inversion |
| 5 | conditions.py:18 | comment mentioning forward.py | ALLOWLIST | comment, not an import |

Only the 3 _BranchNode imports are the disease; all fixed by relocation. No DEFER rows.

title: examples/observable_pipeline.py: undeclared langfuse dependency
description:
## Symptom

`examples/observable_pipeline.py` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'langfuse'`.

## Root cause

The example imports `langfuse` for tracing demonstration but the dep is undeclared in `pyproject.toml`.

## Suggested fix

Add `langfuse` to the `[dependency-groups].dev` block (same pattern used for `langchain-openai` and `python-dotenv` recently).

## Affected scope

Single example.
design:
## Root Cause
examples/observable_pipeline.py imports langfuse, which is not in pyproject [dependency-groups].dev -> uninstalled -> ModuleNotFoundError.

## Fix Approach
Add "langfuse" to [dependency-groups].dev in pyproject.toml (same pattern as langchain-openai/python-dotenv), run uv sync so it installs. The structural guard then passes.
notes:
## Reproduction (structural disease -- no behavioral test)
- Failing structural guard: tests/test_guards_examples.py::TestExampleImportsAreDeclared::test_example_third_party_imports_are_importable

- observable_pipeline.py:24 `from langfuse.langchain import CallbackHandler` (+ :135 `from langfuse import get_client`).
- Root cause: langfuse is not declared in pyproject [dependency-groups].dev, so it is not installed -> ModuleNotFoundError at import.
- Scan of all example third-party import roots: only langfuse is missing (dotenv/langchain_core/langchain_openai/langgraph/pydantic/structlog/yaml all importable).

Result: langfuse is the ONLY missing one (examples/observable_pipeline.py). All others importable: dotenv, langchain_core, langchain_openai, langgraph, pydantic, structlog, yaml.
No other instances; no separate beads filed.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-b6hm)
Pattern: example third-party import not declared/installed.
Scan command (SYNTACTIC -- AST import-root collection + find_spec; no fan-out):
  collect roots via ast over examples/*.py + examples/**/*.py, exclude stdlib + local sibling stems, run importlib.util.find_spec on each.
Total third-party roots: 9; missing: 1.

| # | Module | File | Disposition | Reason |
|---|--------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | langfuse | examples/observable_pipeline.py | MIGRATE | add to [dependency-groups].dev |
| 2 | dotenv/langchain_core/langchain_openai/langgraph/pydantic/structlog/yaml | various examples | ALLOWLIST | already installed/declared (find_spec OK) |

No DEFER rows. Structural guard already authored in the reproduce atom (TestExampleImportsAreDeclared) -- it is the sweep artifact for this structural disease.
## Architect Review (neograph-b6hm)
1. Root cause correctness [LOW]: undeclared dep; find_spec confirms langfuse uninstalled. Correct.
2. Fix minimality [LOW]: add one line to [dependency-groups].dev + uv sync. No code change.

## Fix Applied
pyproject.toml [dependency-groups].dev += "langfuse>=3.0" (resolved 4.0.6) and "langchain>=1.0".
- langchain was a TRANSITIVE requirement: examples/observable_pipeline.py imports `from langfuse.langchain import CallbackHandler`, and langfuse.langchain raises ModuleNotFoundError("install langchain") if langchain is absent. So both deps are needed for the example to import.
- uv sync installed langfuse + langchain (+ otel/protobuf transitives); also bumped langgraph 1.1.6 -> 1.2.4 transitively. Full suite green on 1.2.4 (2123 passed).

title: vs_langgraph/03_map_reduce inline lambda assumes data is list[Pydantic]; gets BAML-rendered string
description:
## Symptom

`examples/vs_langgraph/03_map_reduce.py` fails at the `merge_jokes` node with:

```
AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'items'
  File ".../examples/vs_langgraph/03_map_reduce.py", line 123, in <lambda>
    "\n".join(f"- {j.items[0]}" for j in data if j.items)
```

## Root cause

The example's inline lambda assumes `data` is `list[Claims]` (Pydantic instances with `.items` attribute). The example pre-dates neograph's auto-BAML-rendering pattern — when written, prompt_compilers received raw Pydantic objects. neograph now BAML-renders upstream output to a STRING before the compiler sees it; iterating with `.items` on a string crashes.

## Suggested fix

Rewrite the lambda to operate on the rendered string OR migrate to the canonical pattern with `${variants}` placeholder substitution. The example demonstrates Map-Reduce side-by-side with LangGraph — fix should preserve the comparison purpose.

## Affected scope

Only this example.
design:
## Root Cause
Oracle merge_prompt passes prompt_compiler input_data = a dict {variants: [Jokes,...], **upstream}. The example lambda iterates data directly, walking dict keys (strings) -> .items AttributeError.

## Fix Approach
In examples/vs_langgraph/03_map_reduce.py run_neograph prompt_compiler, change the merge branch from iterating data to iterating data[variants] (the list of Jokes variants). Scoped to this one example.
notes:
## Reproduction
- Failing test: tests/test_example_map_reduce.py::TestMapReduceExampleNeoGraphPath::test_neograph_map_reduce_returns_a_joke
- Confirmed FAILS: AttributeError "str object has no attribute items" (matches ticket).
- Root cause (precise): the Oracle merge step calls the prompt_compiler with input_data = a DICT {variants: [<variant models>], ...}, not list[Pydantic]. The example lambda iterates data directly (for j in data), walking the dict KEYS (strings like variants); .items on a str raises. The ticket BAML-rendered-string phrasing is imprecise -- data is a dict.
- Fix: read data[variants] in the merge branch.
## Trace-similar (other instances of the same bug pattern)
Pattern = an inline/custom prompt_compiler for an Oracle merge_prompt that iterates input_data directly assuming list[Pydantic], when the merge actually passes input_data = a dict {variants: [...], **upstream}.

Scan: grep -rnE "for [a-z]+ in data|in data if|merge_prompt" examples/ + manual review of each merge_prompt compiler.

OTHER INSTANCE FOUND:
- examples/observable_pipeline.py:73-82 (merge-claims branch). Comment literally says "input_data is a list of Claims from Oracle generators"; does for claims in input_data: claims.items -> iterates dict keys -> AttributeError. Same bug. LATENT behind bug b6hm (file currently dies at import: ModuleNotFoundError langfuse). Will fix in the iu05 fix atom (same disease, trivial); b6hm separately adds the langfuse dep.

SAFE (no manual data iteration):
- examples/20_oracle_merge_hooks.py: inline merge_prompt with ${numbered_variants} placeholder -> neograph auto-substitutes.
- examples/03_oracle_ensemble.py: inline merge_prompt with ${tagged_claims} placeholder.
- examples/lead-outreach/pipeline.py: merge_prompt=pick_best via make_template_prompt_compiler (_shared.py), which handles the {variants:...} dict via safe_substitute (single-key dict also exposed as ${input}); pick_best.md uses ${input}. No crash.

No separate bead filed; observable_pipeline fix folded into iu05 (same bug). b6hm cross-referenced.
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-iu05)

Pattern: an Oracle merge_prompt prompt_compiler that iterates its data/input_data parameter DIRECTLY (for X in data) assuming list[Pydantic], when the Oracle merge passes input_data = a dict {variants: [...], **upstream}. Iterating the dict yields its keys (strings) -> attribute access on a str crashes.

Scan command (SYNTACTIC -- single grep, no fan-out):
  grep -rnE "for [A-Za-z_]+ in (data|input_data)\b" examples/
Total raw hits: 5; disease instances: 2.

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | vs_langgraph/03_map_reduce.py:127 | for j in data (gen-expr, merge prompt_compiler) | MIGRATE | the bug; fixed in fix atom |
| 2 | observable_pipeline.py:76 | for claims in input_data (merge-claims branch of prompt_compiler) | MIGRATE | same bug, latent behind b6hm langfuse import; fixed in fix atom |
| 3 | 05_subgraph_composition.py:48 | input_data.scored (scripted node body) | ALLOWLIST | scripted @node receives the real typed model, not the variants dict; attribute access, not a merge compiler |
| 4 | 05_subgraph_composition.py:65 | for claim in input_data.items (scripted node body) | ALLOWLIST | scripted node, typed input |
| 5 | 10_full_pipeline.py:146 | for claim in input_data.items (scripted node body) | ALLOWLIST | scripted node, typed input |

No DEFER rows. SYNTACTIC -> single grep sufficient; no multi-agent fan-out, so .claude/code-review/neograph-iu05/ not required.
Distinguisher: disease instances are MERGE prompt_compilers (signature (template, data)) iterating the bare data param; ALLOWLIST hits are @node bodies (no template param) accessing their typed input. The sweep guard keys on this (template-param + bare-data iteration).
## Architect Review (neograph-iu05)
Scope: contained example bug; no core-IR/layering implications (contrast yi0n). Inline review.

1. Root cause correctness [LOW]: Confirmed empirically -- Oracle merge passes input_data = {variants: [Jokes,...]} (a dict); the example iterates the bare dict -> keys (str) -> .items AttributeError. Correct.
2. Fix minimality [LOW]: read data[variants] (the list of variants) in the merge branch. Minimal, scoped to the 2 affected examples (03_map_reduce + observable_pipeline merge-claims).
3. Regression risk [LOW]: example-only change; behavioral runtime test (fake LLM) guards 03; AST guard (sweep) covers both.
4. Architecture compliance [LOW]: aligns with the documented merge contract (input_data has a variants key; templates use ${variants}). The fully-canonical alternative is to drop the inline compiler and use a ${variants} template-ref placeholder, but the inline custom compiler is INTENTIONAL here (mirrors the hand-wired LangGraph comparison). Minimal data[variants] fix preserves the comparisons pedagogy -- preferred over rewriting to ${variants}.
5. Similar-bug scalability [LOW]: observable_pipeline (2nd instance) fixed in same atom; sweep adds an AST guard.
6. Test coverage [LOW/MEDIUM]: 03 has a behavioral fake-LLM runtime test. observable_pipeline is gated by b6hm (langfuse import) so it cannot get a runtime smoke test yet; the AST guard covers it statically. Acceptable.

VERDICT: ALL_LOW -> proceed to fix (data[variants], both examples). No refinement.
## Fix Applied
- examples/vs_langgraph/03_map_reduce.py: merge prompt_compiler now iterates data["variants"] (was: for j in data).
- examples/observable_pipeline.py: merge-claims branch now iterates input_data["variants"] (was: for claims in input_data); same bug, latent behind b6hm.
Regression test tests/test_example_map_reduce.py runs example 03 with a fake LLM: RED before (AttributeError), GREEN after.
Quality gate: pytest 2114 passed, ruff clean, mypy clean.
Note: two ruff F541 (placeholder-less f-strings) exist in examples/ but are pre-existing and outside the project lint gate (src/+tests/ only); not introduced here.
Meta-guards caught two issues during the fix (now resolved): unused pytest import (F401) and an inline-regex violation of TestRegexGuardsHaveSlipMetaTests (refactored the yi0n guard to be regex-free).
## Sweep Verification (neograph-iu05)
Re-scan command: grep -rnE "for [A-Za-z_]+ in (data|input_data)\b" examples/
Pre-fix disease instances: 2; Post-fix: 0.

| # | Phase 1b content | Disposition | Post-fix state | Verified |
|---|------------------|-------------|----------------|----------|
| 1 | vs_langgraph/03_map_reduce merge gen-expr | MIGRATE | now iterates data["variants"] (Subscript) | YES |
| 2 | observable_pipeline merge-claims for-loop | MIGRATE | now iterates input_data["variants"] (Subscript) | YES |
| 3 | 05_subgraph_composition:48 | ALLOWLIST | scripted body, input_data.scored (Attribute) | HOLDS |
| 4 | 05_subgraph_composition:65 | ALLOWLIST | scripted body, input_data.items | HOLDS |
| 5 | 10_full_pipeline:146 | ALLOWLIST | scripted body, input_data.items | HOLDS |

## Structural Guard
- File: tests/test_guards_examples.py
- Class: TestExampleMergeCompilerReadsVariants
- AST-based (regex-free): identifies prompt_compilers by signature (first param template/tmpl/t + a data param) and flags iteration of the BARE data param via either a for-statement OR a comprehension generator. Reading data["variants"] (Subscript) or data.attr (Attribute) is not flagged; scripted @node bodies (no template param) are exempt.
- Meta-tests: positive comprehension form; would-be-missed for-statement form (the observable_pipeline shape); negative subscript form (the fix); negative scripted-node-body form (05/10 exemption).
- All 5 pass; real-example scan green post-fix.
- Note: TestRegexGuardsHaveSlipMetaTests forced the yi0n guard to be regex-free; this guard is also regex-free.
## E2E Verification (real OpenRouter)
examples/vs_langgraph/03_map_reduce.py runs clean end-to-end: 3 Oracle generators + pick-best merge (prompt=pick-best, strategy=structured) complete with no AttributeError. NeoGraph path returned: "Why do programmers prefer dark mode? Because light attracts bugs!" LangGraph path also returned a joke.

title: ARCH: loader.py:230 auto-fan-in assigns raw prev_node.outputs as input type (dict-form upstream mismatch)
description: Found by neograph-my84 codebase disease scan (DEFER row). loader.py:230 (_load_construct auto-inputs wiring) sets inputs_dict[prev_field] = prev_node.outputs for each prior node in a YAML sub-construct. When prev_node.outputs is dict-form, this (a) assigns a dict where a single type is expected (same class as neograph-my84 part 1), AND (b) keys the fan-in entry by prev_field, but a dict-form producer registers per-key fields prev_field_{key} (the base prev_field is not itself a producer). So normalize_outputs(prev_node.outputs).primary alone is insufficient — the KEY must also map to the per-key producer field (output_field_name(prev_field, primary_key)). Needs its own analysis + a should_fail/should_pass fixture for a dict-form upstream in a YAML sub-construct. Deferred from neograph-my84 (which scopes to forward.py + the 4 primary-field micro-pattern sites) because this requires validator-wiring semantics verification beyond a .primary swap. Low confidence any current YAML pipeline hits dict-form sub-construct auto-wiring.
design:
## Core Invariant
Sub-construct auto-fan-in must wire each upstream producer to the EXACT state-bus field the validator registers, via the monopolized normalize_outputs/primary_output_field helpers -- so a dict-form producer maps to {prev}_{primary_key}: primary_type, never the raw outputs dict at the base field.

## Fix Approach
loader.py:230 -> inputs_dict[primary_output_field(prev_field, prev_node.outputs)] = normalize_outputs(prev_node.outputs).primary. Import both from neograph._normalize. Behavior-preserving for single-type (the only YAML-reachable form today); correct for dict-form. Test via direct _build_sub_construct call with a synthesized dict-form node (YAML cannot express dict-form outputs).
notes:
## Findings
- loader.py:227-231 (_build_sub_construct auto-fan-in): for each prior node in a YAML sub-construct it does inputs_dict[prev_field] = prev_node.outputs. Two defects when prev_node.outputs is dict-form:
  (a) assigns the raw dict where a single type is expected;
  (b) keys by the BASE prev_field, but the validator registers a dict-form producer ONLY at output_field_name(prev_field, key) (per-key), never the base field -> fan-in finds no producer.
- REACHABILITY: NodeSpec.outputs is typed `str` (_spec_schema.py:84) and _build_node sets outputs = lookup_type(str) (loader.py:175) -> a YAML-spec node can NEVER have dict-form outputs. So this branch is currently UNREACHABLE via load_spec. The bug is latent/defensive (confirms the ticket DEFER note). No current YAML pipeline can hit it.
- Validator producer registration (_construct_validation.py:195-208): dict-form Node -> producers[output_field_name(field, key)] per key; single-type/Construct -> producers[field]. Fan-in (_check_fan_in_inputs) looks up producers by the inputs-dict KEY. So the auto-wired key MUST equal the registered producer field.
- Monopolized helpers (_normalize.py): normalize_outputs(outputs).primary = primary type (single type for both forms); primary_output_field(base, outputs) = base for single-type, output_field_name(base, primary_key) for dict-form. These already exist and are the single source of truth.

## Relevant Code
- src/neograph/loader.py:226-231 -- the buggy auto-fan-in assignment (fix site).
- src/neograph/_normalize.py:58-125 -- normalize_outputs / primary_output_field (use these).
- src/neograph/naming.py:12 -- output_field_name(base, key).
- src/neograph/_construct_validation.py:188-220 -- producer registration (per-key for dict-form).
- src/neograph/_spec_schema.py:84 -- NodeSpec.outputs: str (reachability root cause).
- tests/test_spec_loader.py -- spec-loader test patterns (~26 tests).

## Fix shape
Replace inputs_dict[prev_field] = prev_node.outputs with:
  inputs_dict[primary_output_field(prev_field, prev_node.outputs)] = normalize_outputs(prev_node.outputs).primary
Behavior-IDENTICAL for single-type (primary_output_field->prev_field, primary->the type); correct for dict-form.

## Risks & Edge Cases
- Cannot write a pure-YAML should_fail/should_pass (NodeSpec.outputs is str). The test must drive _build_sub_construct directly with a synthesized all_nodes containing a dict-form-output Node -> assert the later node`s inputs wires {SUBGRAPH_INPUT: input, output_field_name(prev, key): primary} and the Construct compiles. RED before (raw dict / wrong key -> ConstructError), GREEN after.
- Keep auto-wiring to the PRIMARY output only (matches single-type heuristic); secondary dict keys are not auto-exposed.
- Three-surface parity: this is loader-only (YAML surface); declarative/@node/programmatic do not auto-wire inputs, so parity N/A here (note in test).
## Codebase Disease Scan (neograph-z3ie)
Disease: fan-in / producer-field auto-wiring that uses raw Node.outputs instead of the monopolized primary_output_field (field name) + normalize_outputs(...).primary (type). Drift here mismatches the per-key producer fields the validator registers for dict-form outputs.

Scan command (SYNTACTIC + manual classification; small, no fan-out):
  grep -rnE "\.outputs\b" src/neograph/ | (exclude _normalize/_declared_output/primary_output_field/docstrings)

| # | File:line | Form | Disposition | Reason |
|---|-----------|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | loader.py:230 | inputs_dict[prev_field] = prev_node.outputs (auto-fan-in) | MIGRATE | THE bug; fix uses primary_output_field + .primary |
| 2 | _wiring.py:324 | output_model = node.outputs (oracle merge arg) | ALLOWLIST | passed to _merge_variants/invoke_structured which normalize dict-form internally (first key = primary) |
| 3 | compiler.py:512 | make_oracle_merge_fn(..., node.outputs, ...) | ALLOWLIST | merge fn normalizes internally (CLAUDE.md) |
| 4 | _validation_modifiers.py:41,119 | output_type = node.outputs (modifier validation) | ALLOWLIST | validation reads raw type; effective_producer_type handles modifier effects |
| 5 | _ir_normalize.py:72,170 | state builder per-key + gen-type compare | ALLOWLIST | builder already emits {base}_{key} per dict key (correct); :170 is oracle gen-type inference, not fan-in |
| 6 | _dispatch.py:261 | docstring/gen-type override | ALLOWLIST | not fan-in wiring |

Only loader.py:230 is the fan-in-field disease. neograph-my84 already swept forward.py + the 4 primary-field micro-pattern sites and DEFERRED this one (this ticket). No DEFER rows remain after this fix.

title: ARCH-DECOMP-1: split _construct_validation.py (1005L) by validation concern
description:
## Architectural invariant

`src/neograph/_construct_validation.py` (currently 1005 LOC, the synthesis's "hardest code in the repo, and it's correct") is decomposed by validation concern into ≥3 focused modules. Each module owns ONE validation rule family. No module exceeds ~400 LOC. The split preserves every existing rule behaviorally — this is reshape, not rewrite.

## Why this is filed (and why it's P3)

The Jun-2026 multi-agent review explicitly praised this file's CORRECTNESS while flagging its size as a smell. Post-ARCH-SWEEP, the codebase is structurally coherent; the only remaining "is it too big?" anxieties (per a Jun-2026 maintainer audit) point at three files of which this is the largest. NOT a release blocker — the file works and is well-tested. But the decomposition is the cheapest plausible 1000→400 LOC win on the whole project.

## Phase 1 — Code archaeology

Read `_construct_validation.py` in full. Inventory every top-level function + class. Categorize each as belonging to ONE of:

- **Type compatibility** (`_types_compatible`, `_unwrap_optional`, PEP-604 helpers, `_MISSING` sentinel, ForwardRef resolution)
- **Fan-in validation** (`_check_fan_in_inputs`, `_check_item_input`, producer registry walk)
- **Fan-out / Each path resolution** (Each path navigation, list-element compatibility, dotted-path walk)
- **Context validation** (the recursive `_validate_node_chain` + `ambient_producers` + sub-construct depth)
- **Loop self-edge** (`validate_loop_self_edge`, output/input back-edge compat)
- **Merge hooks** (`_validate_merge_hooks` — Oracle hook arity/type checks)
- **Naming / field-name helpers** (small utilities)

Some functions cross categories — note which. Output the inventory as a table in bead notes.

## Phase 1b — Codebase-wide disease scan

Disease pattern: "Validation rule helpers OUTSIDE `_construct_validation.py` that duplicate or shadow rules that should live in it." Scan for any validation logic in `node.py`, `modifiers.py`, `construct.py`, `_ir_normalize.py`, `_construct_builder.py`. Disposition table per the molecule.

This is also the input to deciding split boundaries — if e.g. modifier validation is already cross-referenced from `modifiers.py`, the split should preserve the seam.

## Phase 2 — Target design

Propose the new module layout. Strawman (validate during architect review):

- `src/neograph/_validation/__init__.py` (re-exports for `construct.py`'s single import call site)
- `src/neograph/_validation/_types.py` — type compatibility primitives
- `src/neograph/_validation/_fan_in.py` — fan-in producer registration + match
- `src/neograph/_validation/_fan_out.py` — Each path resolution + list-element checks
- `src/neograph/_validation/_context.py` — recursive walk + ambient_producers
- `src/neograph/_validation/_loop.py` — loop self-edge
- `src/neograph/_validation/_merge_hooks.py` — Oracle hook validation
- `src/neograph/_validation/_walker.py` — the top-level `_validate_node_chain` orchestrator (the only thing `construct.py` calls)

Single import boundary: `construct.py` imports `from neograph._validation import _validate_node_chain, ConstructError`. Internal module relationships private to the package.

Test files split in lockstep — `tests/test_validation.py` (currently slimmed-down post-`e8jg`) becomes the orchestrator-level test; per-rule tests already live in `test_fanin_validation.py`, `test_context_validation.py`, `test_construct_validation_merge_hooks.py` from the earlier split. Confirm no new test files needed.

## Phase 3 — Iterative elegant solution

Apply SOLID rigorously. Iterate until ALL of:

- No new module exceeds 400 LOC.
- Every function lives in exactly ONE module (no duplication across the split).
- `construct.py` has exactly ONE import line from the new package.
- Existing per-rule tests need at most their import line updated.
- The walker (top-level `_validate_node_chain`) is < 100 LOC — it's an orchestrator, not a rule-carrier.

## Phase 4 — Anti-band-aid clauses

- NO copying a function into a new module and leaving the original "for compat." Move = delete from old + add to new.
- NO `from neograph._validation._foo import *` star-imports in the `__init__.py`. List exports explicitly.
- NO module that ends up < 100 LOC — that's over-splitting. Merge sibling concerns if a candidate module is too thin.
- The validation BEHAVIOR must not change. Any test diff outside import updates is a red flag.

## Phase 5 — Sweep verification

- Re-run the Phase 1 inventory against the new layout. Every function from the original 1005-LOC file is in exactly one new module.
- `wc -l src/neograph/_validation/*.py` → all ≤ 400.
- `grep -rn "from neograph._validation" src/neograph/` → only `construct.py` appears outside the package itself.
- Run the full test suite — zero behavioral diffs.
- Add structural guard `TestValidationPackageBoundary`: AST-scan asserting `_validate_node_chain` and `ConstructError` are the only public names exported from `neograph._validation`.

## Phase 6 — Independent review

Opus reviewer evaluates:
1. Is the split boundary architecturally honest, or did the executor draw lines just to hit the LOC target?
2. Did the test suite catch every behavioral edge during the move?
3. Is the package `__init__.py` minimal (single import seam) or did it accumulate convenience re-exports?
4. Would the next contributor adding a new validation rule know which sub-module to put it in?

Verdict ELEGANT, confidence ≥85.

## Acceptance

- `_construct_validation.py` deleted; replaced by `neograph._validation` package (≥3 modules, none >400 LOC)
- `construct.py` imports unchanged in semantics (one line)
- All existing tests pass; test-file imports updated only as needed
- Structural guard pins the package boundary
- Independent reviewer ELEGANT ≥85
design:
## Core Invariant
Validation BEHAVIOR is byte-identical to the 1005-LOC original — every rule fires on exactly the same inputs producing the same ConstructError messages and locations; only file boundaries and the import seam change (reshape, not rewrite).

## Target module layout (4 files: 3 new sub-modules + slimmed orchestrator)
Flat peer modules per the neograph-3zai precedent (NO sub-package). Dependency DAG leaf -> root (architect-verified acyclic):

1. _validation_types.py (~220 LOC) — LEAF. _types_compatible, _extract_list_element, _resolve_field_annotation, _MISSING, _fmt_type, _source_location; shared vocab Producer / ProducerMap / NodeItem / _is_construct_like; effective_producer_type. Imports ConstructError/NeographError from neograph.errors DIRECTLY (never from _construct_validation). No intra-cluster deps.
2. _validation_inputs.py (~350 LOC) — consumer input satisfaction: _check_item_input (dispatcher) + _check_fan_in_inputs + _check_each_path (Each fan-out) + _build_no_producer_error + _suggest_hint. Imports _validation_types. fan_out_candidates stays FUNCTION-LOCAL (real cycle via _ir_normalize->_sidecar->_di_classify->_construct_validation).
3. _validation_modifiers.py (~210 LOC) — modifier-triggered rules: validate_loop_self_edge + validate_loop_construct + _validate_merge_hooks. Imports _validation_types + modifiers.
4. _construct_validation.py (slimmed ~180 LOC) — ORCHESTRATOR: _validate_node_chain + ValidationMode (KEEP HERE — cv.ValidationMode guard at test_guards_assembly.py:1340) + explicit (non-star) RE-EXPORT block: ConstructError, _validate_node_chain, _types_compatible, effective_producer_type, validate_loop_self_edge, validate_loop_construct, ValidationMode, Producer, ProducerMap. get_merge_fn_metadata stays FUNCTION-LOCAL in the orchestrator.

Boundary rationale (architect-accepted, honest): _validation_inputs is one concern (single dispatcher routes fan-in vs Each). _validation_modifiers groups by trigger axis (fired from |/Oracle) — mildly grab-bag but serviceable; the ticket anti-thin-module clause (standalone fan_out ~105 / loop ~90 breach the 100-LOC floor) forces the merge. 4 files, not the strawman 7.

## Implementation Plan
1. (write-test atom) Author structural guard TestValidationModuleBoundary in test_guards_assembly.py: (a) line-cap (all cluster files <=400) + symbol-location table (each func in its target module, absent from orchestrator), (b) SEAM: only _construct_validation.py is imported by files OUTSIDE the cluster {_construct_validation, _validation_types, _validation_inputs, _validation_modifiers}; intra-cluster imports allowed, (c) no `from neograph._construct_validation import *` and no `import *` within cluster. Include negative meta-tests like TestConstructBuilderSplit. VERIFY IT FAILS pre-refactor (modules do not exist yet).
2. Create _validation_types.py; move type primitives + shared vocab + effective_producer_type + _source_location. Import ConstructError from neograph.errors.
3. Create _validation_inputs.py; move fan-in + Each-path + error builder + hint. Keep fan_out_candidates function-local.
4. Create _validation_modifiers.py; move loop self-edge + loop construct + merge hooks.
5. Slim _construct_validation.py to orchestrator + ValidationMode + explicit re-export block (keep get_merge_fn_metadata function-local). DROP dead _location_suffix — the SINGLE non-move-only diff; call it out explicitly in the commit body so the move-only reviewer does not trip.
6. Update guards IN THE SAME COMMIT as the move:
   - LOAD-BEARING: test_producers_collection_keyed_by_field_name (test_guards_assembly.py:1349) — relocate scan target to the cluster (keep the SAME assertion: OrderedDict[str, Producer] present AND list[Producer] absent). Without this CI goes RED (the ProducerMap alias leaves _construct_validation.py).
   - OPTIONAL HARDENING (not coverage-preserving — no cast(Any) exists anywhere): broaden test_no_cast_any_in_validator scan to the cluster. Do NOT block on it.
   - ADD _validation_types.py / _validation_inputs.py / _validation_modifiers.py to ANY_AUDIT_MODULES — needs ZERO new ANY_ALLOWLIST entries (Cluster-5 already on TypeSpecStatic per 86r1).
   - RELOCATE (not grow) the fan_out_candidates function-local-import allowlist entry: _construct_validation.py -> _validation_inputs.py (test_guards_sidecar_imports.py:100). get_merge_fn_metadata entry STAYS; modifiers->validate_loop_* entries UNCHANGED.
7. (sweep) wc -l cluster <=400; grep proves single import seam; run TestNoRedundantValidation post-move; full suite GREEN with ZERO non-import test diffs (re-exports keep all test imports valid).

title: ARCH-DECOMP-2: audit testing.py (640L) + forward.py (889L) for helper-monopoly bypasses
description:
## Architectural invariant

`src/neograph/testing.py` (640 LOC) and `src/neograph/forward.py` (889 LOC) are audited for the same "canonical helper exists, majority of call sites bypass it" disease pattern that ARCH-3 (`neograph-gf9g`) closed in the runtime IR layer. Every bypass found is migrated, allowlisted, or deferred per the codebase-scan disposition discipline. New helper monopolies discovered in these two files get structural guards with full meta-test coverage. Outcome: either a meaningful LOC reduction (10-20% per file) or a documented finding that "these files are minimum-viable size for what they do."

## Why this is filed (and why it's P3)

Two of the three remaining files >700 LOC (`_construct_validation.py` is the third, addressed in its own ticket). The Jun-2026 sprint closed runtime-layer helper monopolies (ARCH-2/3/4). These two files were OUT OF SCOPE of that sprint but live in the same codebase and may carry the same disease. The audit is preventive — surface the diseases now, fix what's contained, file the rest.

NOT a release blocker. Pure architectural housekeeping.

## Phase 1 — Code archaeology

For EACH of the two files separately, inventory:

**`testing.py` (640 LOC)** — likely concerns:
- Fake LLM infrastructure (`StructuredFake`, `TextFake`, `ReActFake`)
- Test compile-kwargs builders (`build_test_compile_kwargs`, `build_fake_llm_kwargs`)
- Test-side registries (`register_scripted`, `register_condition`, `register_tool_factory` test helpers)
- Mock state/config builders
- Convenience exports
Output: list of top-level functions/classes, grouped by concern, with LOC per concern.

**`forward.py` (889 LOC)** — likely concerns:
- `ForwardConstruct` base class
- `_Proxy` symbolic-tracer (the heaviest piece)
- `_BranchNode` sentinel
- Path-parse utilities (`out_of_<node>` and similar — MED-02 in synthesis flagged `_Proxy` `out_of_<node>` path parse duplicated at lines 286, 421)
- Loop/if/try tracing
- Compilation hooks
Output: same grouping format.

## Phase 1b — Codebase-wide disease scan

Disease pattern (per file): "Inline repetition of logic that should live in a single helper within this file." Specifically scan FOR:

1. **In `testing.py`:**
   - Repeated patterns across `*Fake` classes that should be a base class or mixin
   - Repeated kwarg-bundle construction across `build_*_kwargs` helpers
   - Test-side registry init/clear logic duplicated across test files (cross-file scan)

2. **In `forward.py`:**
   - The MED-02 finding (path-parse duplicated at lines 286, 421) — verify currency, migrate if still present
   - Repeated `_Proxy` attribute access / setattr patterns
   - Repeated tracer-frame construction across `_BranchNode` variants

Both files: cross-reference against `_state_bus.py` / `_ir_normalize.py` / `_oracle.py` patterns. Is there a runtime-layer helper either file could be consuming but isn't (e.g., `snapshot_state`, `output_field_name`, `normalize_outputs.primary`)? Disposition table per finding.

## Phase 2 — Target design

For each file, one of three outcomes:

(a) **Migration plan** — a list of helper monopolies to introduce + MIGRATE rows to apply. Estimated LOC delta. New structural guards required.

(b) **Decomposition plan** — split the file into 2-3 focused modules along the concern lines from Phase 1. Same shape as the `_construct_validation.py` ticket but smaller.

(c) **"Minimum-viable" finding** — document that this file is already as small as it can honestly be. Cite the inventory and explain why each chunk pulls weight. Close the ticket as INFO-ONLY with the analysis attached.

Outcome (c) is acceptable but only after Phase 1b shows zero meaningful disease instances. Don't manufacture work.

## Phase 3 — Iterative elegant solution

Apply SOLID + DRY. Iterate until ALL of:

- Every MIGRATE row from Phase 1b is applied OR explicitly DEFERRED with a filed follow-up.
- If decomposition was chosen (outcome b), no new file exceeds 400 LOC.
- New helpers (if any) have ONLY THE NEW SITE'S CALL SITES — no existing call sites left bypassing the helper.
- If outcome (c) was chosen, the bead notes contain a clean rationale-per-chunk that a future maintainer can read.

## Phase 4 — Anti-band-aid clauses

- NO collapsing the five fake LLM classes into one branching function (the Jun-2026 architectural review explicitly rejected this — they encode five real LLM contracts).
- NO collapsing the three API surfaces' tracing logic in `forward.py` (same review rationale).
- NO "rename for tidiness" diffs that don't actually reduce duplication or improve clarity. If the file is already at minimum size, accept it.
- NO migrating MED-02's `_Proxy` path-parse to a helper that ONLY `_Proxy` consumes — extraction only earns its keep if the helper has ≥2 distinct consumers OR the original code was provably error-prone.

## Phase 5 — Sweep verification

- Re-run all Phase 1b scans. Every row has a verified disposition (migrated / allowlisted / deferred).
- If outcome (a) or (b): new structural guards added with positive + negative + regex-slip meta-tests.
- If outcome (c): bead documents "no structural guard needed because no helper monopoly was introduced."
- `make quality` green. Zero behavioral diffs in the test suite (these files are not behavior-bearing in the same way as runtime code, but tests must still pass).

## Phase 6 — Independent review

Opus reviewer evaluates:
1. Did the audit honestly find diseases, or did the executor manufacture finds to justify the ticket?
2. If outcome (c) was chosen, is the "minimum-viable" rationale convincing per-chunk, or hand-waved?
3. For any new helper, does it have ≥2 real consumers TODAY (not "for future use")?
4. Did the executor avoid the anti-pattern of "rename helpers for tidiness without reducing duplication"?

Verdict ELEGANT, confidence ≥85.

## Acceptance

- Per-file inventory + Phase 1b disposition table in bead notes.
- One of three outcomes shipped: migration (with LOC delta + new guards), decomposition (with module layout + guards), or documented "minimum-viable" closure.
- All existing tests pass.
- Independent reviewer ELEGANT ≥85.
- If decomposition chosen, the resulting files all ≤ 400 LOC.

title: decorators.py: consolidate oracle_gen_type eager-write + fix mid-file import
description:
From code review of 185c322 (synthesis.md DRY-04 + LR-06 + CON-01/PP-L3). Clean up the @node decoration-time oracle_gen_type pre-population path.

## DRY-04 + LR-06: extract the eager-write, optionally via model_copy
The 3-line block is copy-pasted verbatim at decorators.py:572-577 (Each x Oracle branch) and :608-611 (Oracle-only branch):
    gen_type = oracle_gen_type_for(n)
    if gen_type is not None:
        n.oracle_gen_type = gen_type
Extract a single helper (e.g. _apply_eager_oracle_gen_type(n: Node) -> Node) called from both branches. While consolidating, address LR-06: the block mutates n.oracle_gen_type DIRECTLY rather than via model_copy, deviating from the IR-layer immutability convention. It is pre-existing and currently safe (the Node is freshly created, not yet shared), but routing the single helper through model_copy (return n.model_copy(update={'oracle_gen_type': gen_type})) makes the eager write consistent with the rest of the IR layer and removes the only direct-Node-mutation in the decoration path. Verify the returned/rebound Node is used by both call sites (the Each x Oracle branch returns n; the Oracle-only branch falls through — handle both).

## CON-01 / PP-L3: move the mid-file import to the header block
decorators.py:104 places 'from neograph._ir_normalize import oracle_gen_type_for' after the register_* function defs, in the middle of the file. It works only because E402 is globally ignored — but that ignore is for cycle-breaking deferred imports, and this is NOT a cycle (_ir_normalize imports no DX modules). Move the import into the top alphabetical from-neograph header block (e.g. after the _construct_validation import at :68). Confirm no import cycle is introduced (import neograph still succeeds).

## Acceptance
- Single eager-write helper, called from both @node branches, no verbatim duplication.
- Eager write goes through model_copy (no direct n.oracle_gen_type = assignment in decorators.py) — verify the new guard's ALLOWED_PREPOP allowlist still matches (decorators.py may then write oracle_gen_type via model_copy dict-literal instead of attr-assign; update the guard/allowlist if the write form changes).
- Import in the header block; E402 no longer relied upon for it.
- make quality green (incl. the sole-writer guard and the bare-node test_fanout_oracle.py:621 assertion still pass).
notes:
## Research (atom dzbf.8)

### Core Invariant
The decoration-time eager oracle_gen_type pre-population is a SINGLE named operation; it produces a new Node (IR-immutability), and the inference rule stays owned by oracle_gen_type_for.

### Two eager-write sites (decorators.py)
- Site 1 Each×Oracle (~571-575): _register_sidecar(n); gen_type=oracle_gen_type_for(n); if gt: n.oracle_gen_type=gt; return n.
- Site 2 Oracle-only (~600-608): same block, then FALLS THROUGH to operator/interrupt + context handling that keeps using n.
Both are verbatim duplicates (DRY-04). Both mutate n.oracle_gen_type directly (LR-06).

### Findings
- Node is NOT frozen (model_config has no frozen=True) — direct attr mutation works; it is safe here because n is a fresh local (not yet shared). LR-06 is pre-existing + low risk.
- EMPIRICAL: n.model_copy(update={'oracle_gen_type': T}) PRESERVES the sidecar (_get_sidecar(copy) is not None == True). So switching to model_copy does NOT drop the sidecar — the fan-out branch's 're-register after | Each' comment is belt-and-suspenders / specific to the | pipe path, not a model_copy limitation.
- Sole-writer guard: after switching to model_copy(update={'oracle_gen_type':...}), decorators.py writes oracle_gen_type via a DICT-LITERAL key (still detected by _scan_ir_field_writes) -> ALLOWED_PREPOP {decorators.py: {oracle_gen_type}} stays valid. No guard change needed.
- CON-01: import 'from neograph._ir_normalize import oracle_gen_type_for' is mid-file (decorators.py:104), relying on E402 (meant for cycle breaks; this is not a cycle). Move to the header from-neograph block.

### Plan
1. Add _apply_eager_oracle_gen_type(n: Node) -> Node helper: gen_type = oracle_gen_type_for(n); return n if None else n.model_copy(update={'oracle_gen_type': gen_type}).
2. Site 1: return _apply_eager_oracle_gen_type(n). Site 2: n = _apply_eager_oracle_gen_type(n) (rebind before fall-through).
3. Move the oracle_gen_type_for import to the top from-neograph block; verify no cycle (import neograph OK).
4. Gate: bare-node test_fanout_oracle.py:621 (oracle_gen_type on a bare decorated node) MUST stay green; sole-writer guard green; make quality green.

### Risk
- Site 2 rebind: subsequent fall-through code must use the rebound n (not a stale reference). Verify.
- @node fusion path test (test_each_oracle_fusion_infers_gen_type_from_merge_fn) must stay green.
## Architect Review (atom dzbf.8 validation)

Verdict: plan is sound and behavior-preserving. All five questions resolved LOW.

### Q1 model_copy vs direct mutation -> DECISION: model_copy
- [LOW] LR-06. Both are functionally safe (Node is not frozen; n is a fresh local). Choose model_copy for IR-immutability consistency: it makes the eager write the ONLY write form in decorators.py that matches _ir_normalize's idiom, and removes the last direct-Node-mutation in the decoration path. Churn is one helper + two call sites -- trivial. The sidecar-preservation finding (empirically verified) removes the only real objection to model_copy. Direct mutation would be the lazy call; model_copy is the right one.

### Q2 Site 2 rebind -> [LOW] verified safe
- Traced decorators.py:604-645. After Oracle, the block does: n = n | Oracle(...); _register_sidecar(n,...); _set_param_res(n,...); then the eager write; then fall-through to interrupt_when (n = n | Operator), loop_when (n = n | Loop), and 'return n'. ALL downstream uses are 'n | Modifier' reassignments or '_register_sidecar(n,...)' -- every one reads the current binding of n. No stale alias is captured: no closure closes over the pre-copy n, and the _register_sidecar(n) call that PRECEDES the eager write stores a reference to the OLD n, but model_copy preserves _sidecar onto the new n (empirically verified), and the subsequent | Operator / | Loop re-register on the rebound n anyway. The Oracle-only-with-no-interrupt/loop path returns the rebound n. SAFE. Rebind 'n = _apply_eager_oracle_gen_type(n)' is correct.
- Note: Site 1 (Each x Oracle) is 'return _apply_...(n)' immediately, no fall-through -- trivially safe.

### Q3 import move -> [LOW] no cycle
- _ir_normalize imports only _normalize, _sidecar, naming, node -- none import decorators at module level. The two decorators-importing edges in the chain (node.py:374, _sidecar.py:101) are function-local deferred imports, so they do not participate in module load. decorators -> _ir_normalize is a clean DX->IR edge. Confirmed E402 is the only reason the mid-file form compiles; moving to the top from-neograph header block (after _construct_validation at ~:68) introduces no cycle. 'import neograph' + direct import smoke-tested OK.

### Q4 sole-writer guard -> [LOW] stays green, no guard change
- _scan_ir_field_writes detects dict-literal keys: model_copy(update={'oracle_gen_type': gen_type}) is an ast.Dict with key 'oracle_gen_type', matched at guards line ~4288-4294. ALLOWED_PREPOP {decorators.py: {oracle_gen_type}} already permits it. The attr-assign form (current) and the dict-literal form (proposed) are BOTH detected and BOTH allow-listed. No guard/allowlist edit needed. test_no_direct_attr_assignment guard is _construct_builder-scoped only, does not touch decorators.py.

### Q5 TDD -> guarding existing behavior is sufficient; no new test required
- This is a pure behavior-preserving refactor. The eager write is already guarded by test_fanout_oracle.py:621 (Site 1, Each x Oracle: asserts fused.oracle_gen_type is Claims) and test_each_oracle_fusion_infers_gen_type_from_merge_fn covers the same Site 1. Site 2 (Oracle-only) eager write is exercised by the test_oracle_body_merge / param_resolutions tests in the same file. RECOMMENDATION: before refactoring, confirm there is an EXISTING assertion that an Oracle-ONLY (no Each) bare decorated node carries oracle_gen_type -- Site 1 is covered, but if no test pins Site 2's oracle_gen_type on the returned node, add one failing-first assertion (bare @node with ensemble_n+merge_fn, NO map_over, assert .oracle_gen_type is T). That is the one coverage gap worth closing to make the rebind regression-proof. Otherwise existing guards suffice.

Decision: model_copy (route the single helper through n.model_copy(update={'oracle_gen_type': gen_type})).
Overall: ALL_LOW
## Triage (atom dzbf.10)
Verdict ALL_LOW. Decision: model_copy (sidecar preservation verified; only direct-Node-mutation in the decoration path removed). Proceed. Architect's required test gap: add a Site 2 (Oracle-only, NO map_over) bare-node test asserting .oracle_gen_type is T on the decorated node directly — test_composition.py:1686 does NOT cover it (asserts post-assembly where normalize_ir re-derives). title: _ir_normalize type precision + Protocol hygiene (narrow Any, audit scope, runtime_checkable)
description:
From code review of 185c322 (synthesis.md MED-03 + CON-02 + PP-L1 + PP-L2). Tighten the new module's typing and Protocol usage.

## MED-03: narrow the inference return type
src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py:96 oracle_gen_type_for returns 'Any | None' but only ever yields a Pydantic model class or None. The Any is contagious — it switches off mypy at the assignment sites decorators.py:575/609 and the normalizer. Narrow to 'type[BaseModel] | None'. The value originates from _sidecar.infer_oracle_gen_type (also Any | None) — narrow that too, or add a cast at that boundary. (Note: the broad Any is currently consistent with _sidecar/_normalize precedent; this ticket intentionally improves the precedent for the IR-field path.)

## CON-02: bring _ir_normalize under the IR Any-discipline
_ir_normalize.py is an IR-layer module (imported by construct.py, writes IR fields) but is NOT in TestNoAnyInIRPublicAPIs' ANY_AUDIT_MODULES (test_structural_guards.py ~2195). After MED-03's narrowing, add _ir_normalize.py to ANY_AUDIT_MODULES, allowlisting any genuine user-type boundaries (e.g. IrNormalizer.apply -> dict[str, Any], which carries user Pydantic types) with the one-line-reason ANY_ALLOWLIST convention. Consider adding _normalize.py too for the same reason, or explicitly document why the normalized-view helpers stay exempt.

## PP-L1: drop unused @runtime_checkable
IrNormalizer is decorated @runtime_checkable but nothing does isinstance(x, IrNormalizer). Drop the decorator, or add a comment if it is retained intentionally for downstream consumers.

## PP-L2: document the deliberate predicate/inference redundancy
_OracleGenTypeNormalizer.applies_to re-checks the oracle/merge_fn guard that oracle_gen_type_for also performs. This is the intentional GRASP predicate/inference split — do NOT collapse it (applies_to must stay cheap; apply recomputes). Add a one-line comment noting the redundancy is deliberate so a future 'DRY cleanup' doesn't merge them and call the inference inside applies_to.

## Acceptance
- oracle_gen_type_for and (if needed) infer_oracle_gen_type return type[BaseModel] | None.
- _ir_normalize.py in ANY_AUDIT_MODULES with justified allowlist entries.
- @runtime_checkable removed or documented.
- applies_to redundancy documented.
- mypy + make quality green.
notes:
## Prep
Files: src/neograph/_ir_normalize.py, tests/test_structural_guards.py (ANY_AUDIT_MODULES + ANY_ALLOWLIST). _sidecar.infer_oracle_gen_type stays Any|None (it can return any introspected type; narrowing it would over-promise) — narrow at the oracle_gen_type_for boundary with cast instead.

Plan:
1. MED-03: oracle_gen_type_for -> type[BaseModel] | None. Import BaseModel (pydantic) + cast (typing). Return cast('type[BaseModel]', gen_type). gen_type sourced from infer_oracle_gen_type (Any) — cast is the honest boundary (the merge_fn's list[T] element is intended to be a BaseModel subtype; not statically provable). Node.oracle_gen_type field is type[BaseModel]|None so this aligns the assignment sites.
2. PP-L1: drop @runtime_checkable from IrNormalizer (nothing isinstance-checks it); remove now-unused runtime_checkable import. Protocol structural typing for list[IrNormalizer] is unaffected.
3. PP-L2: one-line comment in _OracleGenTypeNormalizer.applies_to noting the oracle/merge_fn guard is deliberately duplicated with oracle_gen_type_for (predicate/inference split; do not collapse).
4. CON-02: add '_ir_normalize.py' to ANY_AUDIT_MODULES. After MED-03, the only remaining public Any is IrNormalizer.apply -> dict[str, Any] (heterogeneous model_copy update dict: str fan_out_param + type oracle_gen_type) — allowlist it with that reason. Document that _normalize.py stays out of scope (pre-existing normalized-view helper; separate effort) to avoid scope creep.

Gate: make quality (mypy must stay green after the narrow; the Any-audit guard must pass with _ir_normalize in scope).
## Execution
- MED-03: oracle_gen_type_for -> type[BaseModel] | None (cast at the infer_oracle_gen_type boundary; infer_oracle_gen_type left Any|None since it can return any introspected type). decorators.py assignment sites now type-check precisely.
- PP-L1: dropped @runtime_checkable from IrNormalizer + removed the unused import. list[IrNormalizer] structural typing unaffected.
- PP-L2: added comment in _OracleGenTypeNormalizer.applies_to explaining the deliberate guard duplication (predicate/inference split; don't collapse).
- CON-02: added _ir_normalize.py to ANY_AUDIT_MODULES; allowlisted IrNormalizer.apply:return (heterogeneous model_copy update dict). Documented _normalize.py stays out of scope. Verified the guard actually scans _ir_normalize (empty-allowlist probe flags apply->Any; oracle_gen_type_for no longer flagged).

description: P3. _construct_builder.py mixes: DI param classification, scripted shim registration, modifier wrapping, port resolution, fan-out param detection, sub-construct binding. title: bha9 follow-up: add version: Literal['1'] field to Spec for forward-compat
description:
Follow-up to neograph-bha9 (commit 739009b). Reviewer agent caught that the design promised a `version: Literal['1']` field on `Spec` for forward-compat versioning ('spec_version: 2 gates allowed fields'), but it was dropped silently in the implementation.

## Scope

Single-field addition to `src/neograph/_spec_schema.py`:

```python
class Spec(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    version: Literal['1'] = '1'  # NEW
    types: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    construct: ConstructSpec
```

## Behavior

- Default to '1' so existing specs without an explicit version field continue to load.
- Adding `version: 2` to a future spec without updating Spec would raise pydantic.ValidationError -- the 'forward gate' that motivated this in the design.
- `Spec.model_json_schema()` now exports the version constraint, visible to IDE / docs consumers.

## Tests

- `test_spec_without_version_loads_with_default_1` -- backward compat
- `test_spec_with_explicit_version_1_loads` -- forward compat
- `test_spec_with_unknown_version_2_raises` -- gate works

## Related

- Update `scripts/regen_schema.py` if it pins the schema -- new field will surface, drift test (`test_pipeline_schema_in_sync`) will fail until the on-disk schema is regenerated.
- No piarch migration needed; default value preserves existing behavior.

## Effort

~30 min. One field + 3 tests + schema regeneration.
notes:
